Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister on Saturday amid nationwide student protests over the alleged NEET paper leak. He said the decision was aimed at safeguarding students' futures and preventing what he described as "anti-national forces" from exploiting the large-scale youth protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Saturday said Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation reflects the Bharatiya Janata Party's commitment to placing the interests of the nation, students, and youth above political office.
In a post on social media, Shah said, "For BJP workers, the country, our youth, and students are far more important than any position. Today, the resignation of Union Education Minister Shri @dpradhanbjp ji from his post exemplifies this very principle."
Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister on Saturday amid nationwide student protests over the alleged NEET paper leak. He said the decision was aimed at safeguarding students' futures and preventing what he described as "anti-national forces" from exploiting the large-scale youth protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
Shah said the Narendra Modi-led government respects the concerns of the country's youth and remains committed to introducing stringent reforms to prevent examination paper leaks.
"The Modi government respects the sentiments of the country's youth and is committed to implementing the necessary reforms against paper leaks. The decisions taken by Modi ji to ensure strict punishment for those guilty of paper leaks are commendable," Shah said.
He added that he was confident the government's measures would ensure justice for students who had successfully cleared the NEET examination.
Highlighting Pradhan's tenure as Education Minister, Shah credited him with driving key reforms, including the implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP), expanding examinations in regional languages, strengthening PM SHRI Schools, promoting digital education, advancing skill development, and improving industry-academia collaboration.
He also praised Pradhan's efforts to make the examination system more inclusive and student-centric.
"His tenure is a testament to his dedication to the resolve of making India a developed nation," Shah said.

headline: NEW DELHI: The opposition on Saturday hailed the youth protesters after Union education minister
full_text:
NEW DELHI: The opposition on Saturday hailed the youth protesters after Union education minister 
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following massive student demonstrations demanding his resignation over the alleged NEET (UG) paper leak and other education-related issues.
The resignation came ahead of the third round of talks between the government and the Cockroach Janta Party (
CJP), an online satirical platform spearheading the protests at Jantar Mantar, Delhi's designated site for public demonstrations.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge credited both the students and the "united opposition."
"India's âStudents' Echoâ has finally reached the threshold of the arrogant power. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
This is the victory of our millions of youth who raised their voices on the streets across the country to fix the education system. This is the victory of truth and the defeat of Mr. Modi's stubbornness. This is the victory of all those families who lost their blood, their children, because this government is corrupt. This is the victory of the united opposition, who raised their voices from Parliament to the streets in the interest of the students.
 Now it is Mr. Modi's turn to apologize to our young generation and to take strict action against those who unleashed lathis, batons, and pellet guns on them," Kharge wrote on X.
"Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation; Modi-Shah are not invincible...They too will go!" Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut posted on X.
AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal described it as a "big win for democracy."
"Congratulations to the entire country on Dharmendra Pradhanâs resignation. Big win for democracy," Kejriwal said in a video message on X.
Here's who said what:
Manoj Jha (RJD MP): "First setback for Modi government, thanks to the resolve of our youths and students."
Kunal Ghosh (TMC MLA): "He (Pradhan) should have done it earlier... BJP was trying to protect him. This is the victory of the people and students who were protesting... This is the victory of the whole country."
Bhupender Singh Hooda (ex-Haryana CM): "Better late than never. This should have come earlier. There wouldn't have been so much damage. The young generation across the country has lost faith in exams, so the entire system should change. A new system should be introduced... The demand for Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as Education Minister wasn't just from Congress alone; it was from the youth of the entire country."
Shashi Tharoor (Congress MP): "The resignation of the Education Minister is an acknowledgment that accountability in a democracy cannot be indefinitely evaded. It comes after weeks of determined, peaceful voices raised by students, parents and citizens across the country who refused to be ignored."
Manish Sisodia (AAP leader): Dharmendra Pradhan did not voluntarily submit his resignation. The nation's children, the nation's students, secured Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. If this had been a voluntary resignation, it should have happened when the NEET paper leak occurred...The country needs a massive education revolution."
Sharad Pawar (NCP-SP chief): "In response to the insistent demand of the protesters, the Union education minister has finally resigned today. This fight, which stood firmly against oppression without fear and forced the government to accept moral responsibility against injustice, is a symbol of the power of democracy. This is a major victory for the unity of the youth power in the country."
Akhilesh Yadav (SP chief): "This is a big victory for the youth, but people from all political parties should learn from this that in the future, the examinations will have to be strengthened so that no papers are leaked and avenues for employment and jobs will have to be opened for the youth."

headline: NEW DELHI: BJP leader Pralhad Joshi on Saturday was appointed as the new Union education minister, hours after
full_text:
NEW DELHI: BJP leader Pralhad Joshi on Saturday was appointed as the new Union education minister, hours after 
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned.
Pradhan resigned taking moral responsibility for the NEET-UG paper leak controversy that triggered weeks of nationwide student protests. His resignation was accepted by President Droupadi Murmu.
A press release by Rashtrapati Bhavan read: "The President of India, as advised by the Prime Minister, has accepted the resignation of Shri Dharmendra Pradhan from the Union Council of Ministers, with immediate effect, under clause (2) of Article 75 of the Constitution of India. Further, as advised by the Prime Minister, the President has directed that Shri Pralhad Joshi, Cabinet Minister, be assigned the charge of the Ministry of Education, in addition to his existing portfolio.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
"
After being appointed as education minister Pralhad Joshi said he accepted the additional charge of the education ministry with 'a sense of duty and humility' and pledged to work under the guidance of PM Modi to further strengthen the country's education system.
"I accept this responsibility with a sense of duty and humility. I am thankful to the Prime Minister. In the last 12 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, many historic achievements have been made. 
In the last four to five years, Dharmendra Pradhan also implemented the National Education Policy, and several important initiatives were undertaken. The country has made significant progress in the new education system. Under the guidance of the Prime Minister, I will work to the best of my ability and fulfil my responsibilities with dedication," Joshi said.
Joshi, the Lok Sabha MP from Karnataka's Dharwad constituency also hold the portfolios of new and renewable energy and consumer affairs, food and public distribution. A five-time MP, he has previously served as the Union minister for coal, mines and parliamentary affairs.
As the minister for new and renewable energy, Joshi has been leading the Centre's efforts to expand clean energy capacity, with a focus on achieving 500 GW of renewable and non-fossil fuel energy capacity by 2030 and net-zero emissions by 2070.
He has overseen key initiatives including the National Green Hydrogen Mission, PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, PM-KUSUM scheme and offshore wind energy projects, while pushing for annual bids for 50 GW of renewable energy capacity and other policy measures to boost the sector.
His appointment comes at a crucial time as the education ministry implements sweeping reforms following the 
NEET-UG controversy, including the restructuring of the National Testing Agency (NTA), stricter anti-paper leak measures and a shift to computer-based testing for NEET from 2027.

His resignation comes after sustained demonstrations led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), student organisations and opposition parties, which had made his removal from the Union Cabinet the central demand of the agitation....Read More
Entry gates for all metro stations are now open, DMRC said. The Internet is back in the Jantar Mantar area as the CJP called off their protest.
Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Friday hit back at critics questioning his decision to end his 26-day hunger strike, asking why he needed a "character certificate" for his commitment to the students' movement. His remarks came even as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) held a second round of talks with the Centre, which has reportedly given written assurances on some of the protesters' key demands.
Union Minister JP Nadda had said that the Centre will hold the third round of talks with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Sunday afternoon after discussions within the government on the protesters' demands.
Despite Wangchuk ending his indefinite fast shortly after midnight on Thursday, the atmosphere at Jantar Mantar remained charged. The protest site continued to draw large crowds, with people waiting between 50 and 100 minutes in a serpentine queue stretching up to Janpath Metro station on Tolstoy Marg. As reported by HT earlier, delegations of lawyers, farmer unions, NGOs and groups from neighbouring states arrived through the day carrying banners and placards in support of the agitation.
Meanwhile, 18 metro stations in Delhi will remain closed on Saturday as authorities tighten security amid the ongoing protests.
Wangchuk responds to criticism
In a video message shared on social media, Wangchuk dismissed allegations that he had compromised with the government by ending his fast.
"After 26 days of fasting for the sake of students, losing 11 kilograms of body weight in which I have also lost muscle mass and my organs and brain reached the verge of irreversible damage, and doing all this in the scorching heat of Delhi after coming from the bitter cold of Ladakh, do I have to seek a character certificate from anyone about how sacred my fast was, about whose hands I broke it at, or whether I made a deal or not?... Shame on a country that produces such minds, from which such vile thoughts spring.”
The educationist and activist reiterated that there was no deal with the government. He said his foremost concern during negotiations was ensuring that students participating in the protests were protected from violence and legal action.
He also explained why he did not insist on Union education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation during the talks, saying preventing cases against protesters was the immediate priority. Wangchuk added that he believed Pradhan would eventually resign.
Why Wangchuk ended the 26-day hunger strike
Wangchuk said he agreed to end the fast only after the Centre provided written assurances and because he feared an imminent crackdown on protesters.
"Last night around midnight, I was told the ministers had agreed to give the assurance in writing. I was in a hurry because the situation in Delhi was such; there was apprehension that a major crackdown could happen. I was watching reports and was reminded of September 24, 2025, when police and CRPF personnel mercilessly fired at the youth of Ladakh. I was afraid something similar could happen here. I felt that if I ended my fast and appealed for peace, perhaps the situation could be diffused," he said.
The activist had been on an indefinite hunger strike since June 28 after joining the CJP-led agitation demanding accountability over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, reforms in the education system and the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
CJP says government responded positively
Following a second round of discussions with Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, CJP leaders said the Centre had shown "significant in-principle agreement" on several demands while further talks would continue, reported news agency ANI.
CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said the party placed four key demands before the government, including compensation for families of students who allegedly died by suicide because of the examination system and withdrawal of FIRs against peaceful protesters.
Nadda, according to the CJP, told the delegation that another round of discussions would be held.
Why are people protesting at the Jantar Mantar?
The protests, led by the Cockroach Janta Party, are centred on allegations of irregularities in the NEET examination, demands for reforms in the examination system, accountability over the alleged paper leak and the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
CJP's key demands
- Resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
- ₹1 crore compensation for families of NEET aspirants who died by suicide.
- No prosecution of peaceful protesters.
- Prosecution of police officials allegedly involved in excesses against protesters.

headline: Around 2.25 pm, as soon as the news of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation broke, Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement, shouted jubilantly.
full_text:
Around 2.25 pm, as soon as the news of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation broke, Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) movement, shouted jubilantly.
Jantar Mantar protest updates on July 25, 2026
He then grabbed a microphone, walked to the front of the stage and addressed the thousands gathered at Jantar Mantar protest site: “We have done it.”
With his fists closed and raised in the air, he declared, “Dharmendra Pradhan has resigned. It was said that resignations do not happen in this government. Even the world will bow if there is a person to make it happen.”
The protest site erupted in celebration. Protesters hugged one another, broke into tears, and danced to patriotic Bollywood songs as chants of victory echoed through the crowd and slogans like “Haar gaye, haar gaye, Tanashah haar gaye [dictator has been defeated]” reverberated across the venue.
For many students who had spent days braving rain, heat, and sleeping on roads while demanding accountability, the announcement was more than a political development. It was an emotional affirmation that their voices had finally been heard.
Despite the resignation, which was one of the major demands, the crowd at Jantar Mantar continued to swell as people wanted to celebrate the “historic victory”.
Dozens gathered in front of the main stage to take selfies, while long queues were seen outside the entrance of the venue as thousands of people continued to stream in to the protest site.
Inside the protest site, slogans of “Inquilab Zindabad” and “Bharat Mata ki Jai” filled the air. Some also chanted “Jang abhi bhi jaari hai, E20 ki baari hai” (the fight is not over, E20 is the next target) even as organisers repeatedly appealed to the gathering to maintain peace.
As A.R. Rahman’s ‘Vande Matram’ played from the stage, people sang along, as Mr. Dipke waved the national flag from the centre of the stage. People continued to celebrate as “Chak De! India” blared from the stage.
People distributed “Melody” chocolate in celebration, an apparent reference to Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifting the confectionery to the Italian Prime Minister earlier this year. Mr. Dipke, who had been unwell, soon left the area.
At around 6 p.m., CJP spokespersons Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das returned after meeting Union Ministers and announced that “we have won”, triggering another round of applause.
About half an hour later, Mr. Ranka urged people to disperse peacefully as the protest had been called off. “We will meet you soon,” he said, as both of them left the area.
While many people started to leave, hundreds continued to pour in to celebrate, forcing the volunteers to close the entries to the protest site. Thousands of people who were still coming to the protest site gathered at the Sansad Marg leading to Connaught Place.
By 8:30 pm, workers had started to dismantle the main stage. But, still people climbed on it to click selfies, amid chants of “Vande Bharatam” and fluttering of national flags.
Protesters divided
However, not all protesters agreed with the decision to call off the agitation.
Kuldeepak Yadav, 29, from Firozabad, Uttar Pradesh, who said he had been at the protest site since it began, was of the opinion that it would have been difficult to continue the protest after the government had agreed to the three core demands. “If we continue the protest, a lot of people who are originally associated with the movement may distance themselves,” he said.
But Vrutika, 17, from Mumbai, who had joined the protest a day earlier with her father, had a different take. “The protest should continue seeking the Prime Minister’s resignation. There are many pressing issues, such as price rise, financial distress, and lack of regard for the Constitution,” the Class XII student said.
“I came here to fight for education and also my rights,” she added.

headline: Sarnath becomes India's 45th Unesco World Heritage Site, PM calls it a proud moment
full_text:
Sarnath becomes India's 45th Unesco World Heritage Site, PM calls it a proud moment
The ancient Buddhist site Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh has been inscribed on the Unesco World Heritage List, becoming India's 45th World Heritage Site during the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea.
India's ancient Buddhist site of Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh was on Saturday inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List during the 48th session of the Unesco World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea.
Unesco announced the decision in a post on X, saying, "New inscription on the Unesco World Heritage List: Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath, India."
The inscription makes Sarnath India's 45th site on the Unesco World Heritage List.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the recognition and described it as "a proud moment for every Indian."
"A proud moment for every Indian! Delighted that Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh has been inscribed on the Unesco World Heritage List," PM Modi said in a post on X.
The Prime Minister said Sarnath has a deep connection with Lord Buddha, whose timeless message of wisdom, compassion and harmony continues to inspire the world.
"This recognition celebrates India's profound civilisational and spiritual heritage. It will also inspire more people across the world to come to Sarnath and connect with the ideals of Lord Buddha," he said.
Located around 10 kilometres from Varanasi, Sarnath is one of the most significant pilgrimage sites for Buddhists across the world. It holds a unique place in history as the site where Gautam Buddha delivered his first sermon.
The decision to inscribe Sarnath on the World Heritage List was taken during the ongoing 48th session of the Unesco World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea.
In August 2025, Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat informed the Lok Sabha in a written reply that India had submitted a dossier titled "Ancient Buddhist Site, Sarnath" to the Unesco World Heritage Centre for the 2025-26 nomination cycle.
The World Heritage Committee is one of the two bodies that govern the Convention for the Protection of the World's Cultural and Natural Heritage.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah also welcomed the development, saying, "Our cultural pride soars even higher today as Sarnath in Uttar Pradesh has been included in the Unesco World Heritage List."
Calling it an endorsement of India's ancient heritage associated with Lord Buddha, Shah said the recognition would take the Buddha's luminous wisdom to more people and inspire them to embrace the ideals of peace and enlightenment for a better world.
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India's timeless civilisational heritage continues to receive global recognition.
"Sarnath's inscription on the Unesco World Heritage List is a proud moment for every Indian and a shining reflection of Uttar Pradesh's glorious spiritual and cultural legacy," he said, adding that Uttar Pradesh welcomes the world to experience this eternal heritage.

As the student protests over paper leaks spread across different States and snowballed into a major political crisis for the Narendra Modi government, Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as the Education Minister on Saturday (July 25, 2026), prompting the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) to call off the protests at Jantar Mantar, which had become the epicentre of the agitation for the past 36 days.

President Droupadi Murmu accepted Mr. Pradhan’s resignation on the Prime Minister’s advice and appointed Pralhad Joshi as the new Education Minister, a communique from the Rashtrapati Bhavan said in the evening.
In his resignation letter addressed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, posted on X, Mr. Pradhan said he was resigning on his own account, so that “anti-national” elements do not exploit the situation created by the protests.
As soon as the news of the resignation broke in the afternoon, protesters at Jantar Mantar erupted in joy. “We have done it,” CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke told the jubilant crowd.
Thank you all, says Wangchuk
Activist Sonam Wangchuk, whose hunger strike gave momentum to the protests, termed it a victory of democracy, peace, patience, and perseverance. “Congratulations CJP, Gen Z of the nation, and thank you all citizens for shedding fear and the fear of fear, and rising up from every corner of the nation,” he posted on X.
The resignation came moments before Union Ministers J. P. Nadda and Jitendra Singh met CJP spokespersons Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das for talks to end the protests.
Govt. assurance
At a joint press conference with the Ministers, the CJP spokespersons said they are calling it off in “good faith” as the government had agreed to their two demands: ₹1 crore to the families of all students who died by suicide because of NEET paper leaks and no action against any of the student protesters.
Mr. Nadda said the government will give “honourable compensation” within rules to the families of the students who died by suicide after the NEET test was cancelled and ensure withdrawal of all FIRs registered against the protesters.
“As far as their [CJP] charter for broader education reforms is concerned, we will deliberate upon and engage with them,” Mr. Nadda said at a press conference.
PM should apologise: Congress
Congratulating the students on their victory, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said removal of Mr. Pradhan is a “symbolic” but huge step in rebuilding the education system.
The Opposition leader, however, said there are still two more demands: anyone who beat up the students should be held accountable and that the Prime Minister should apologise to the students.
“It is also a signal to other parts of society, farmers, labourers, poor people, anybody whom this regime is attacking and oppressing, there is wisdom and courage in standing up. Daro mat (don’t fear). Let’s get rid of this regime,” Mr. Gandhi said.
In a post on X, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said: “Prime Minister Narendra Modi should apologise to youth. There should be strict action against those who unleashed lathis and pellet guns.”
With the first week of the Monsoon Session of Parliament washed out over the Opposition’s insistence on Mr. Pradhan’s resignation, the government is now expecting both Houses to function.
Three police personnel injured
Amid the jubilation at Jantar Mantar, there were also tense moments, as three senior police officials were injured in stone-throwing close to the protest site, at the intersection of Tolstoy Marg and Sansad Marg. However, the police personnel quickly restored order by using tear gas and resorting to a mild lathi-charge.
Sources said the government had come around to the view on Friday evening that it would be necessary for Mr. Pradhan to resign in order to end the protests, which appeared to be spreading across the country.
With Delhi University set to open soon and protests spreading to tier-II cities, discretion was considered the better part of valour, the sources added.
Mr. Pradhan received much support from his Cabinet colleagues, with Defence Minister Rajnath Singh posting on X that the former had contributed to public service and the creation of an inclusive, future-ready India.
Mr. Pradhan is the second Union Minister in Mr. Modi’s tenure to resign following a public controversy. The first was M. J. Akbar, who stepped down as the Minister of State for External Affairs in 2018 after sexual harassment allegations surfaced against him during the #MeToo movement.

headline: Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday as Union education minister, taking moral responsibility for the NEET-UG paper leak controversy that has shaken the country's examination system, sparked mass student protests and triggered political confrontat...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: 
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday as Union education minister, taking moral responsibility for the NEET-UG paper leak controversy that has shaken the country's examination system, sparked mass student protests and triggered political confrontations.
In his resignation letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Pradhan said he had dedicated more than four decades to students, teachers and education reform.
He said the government had acted immediately after irregularities surfaced in the NEET-UG examination held on May 3, including cancelling the test, ordering a 
CBI probe and deciding to hold a fresh examination. He also said the test would be conducted in computer-based mode from next year.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
Pradhan said that he had tried from the first day to ensure that no meritorious student suffered because of what he described as an examination mafia. He said the unrest at Jantar Mantar and across the country had saddened him and that he was resigning to prevent anti-national forces from exploiting the situation and to protect the unity of the country.
Also Read | 
Dharmendra Pradhan resigns as Union education minister amid massive student protestsThe Odisha-born BJP leader had served as education minister since 2021 and was reappointed after the BJPâs victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha election.
Cockroach Janta Party chief spokesperson Saurav Das said the party had been called for third round of talks and would stay until a written commitment was made. He described the expected outcome as a 'huge victory'.
Click here to follow live blog updatesHere are the key events that led to the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan:Leak sparks outrage
The crisis began after allegations of a paper leak in the NEET-UG 2026 examination, which was held on May 3. Investigators later said a question set described as a 'guess paper' had circulated among students weeks before the test and that many questions closely matched the actual paper.
The National Testing Agency cancelled the exam on May 12 and the government referred the case to the Central Bureau of Investigation for a full probe. The exam, which is used for admission to undergraduate medical and dental courses, had been taken by nearly 22.79 lakh students. The cancellation marked the first full scrapping of 
NEET in its 13-year history.
Also Read | 
Watch: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke falls on stage after being told Dharmendra Pradhan has resignedThe government later announced that the re-examination would be held on June 21 and that no fresh registration would be required. It also said fees already paid would be refunded and that the exam would be shifted to online mode from 2027.
CBI widens probe
The CBI widened its investigation rapidly, carrying out searches at dozens of locations across several states and tracing the alleged source of leaked Physics, Chemistry and Biology questions. The agency said it had identified a network of accused persons, coaching links and middlemen involved in circulating the questions.
Among those arrested were a Latur-based doctor, Dr Manoj Shirure and a Pune-based physics faculty member, Tejas Harshadkumar Shah. Investigators said Dr Shirure helped three students access leaked Chemistry questions, while Shah allegedly passed on Physics questions obtained from another accused already in custody.
Earlier, the CBI had also arrested a Chemistry lecturer, PV Kulkarni, whom it described as a key figure in the leak. The agency said he had conducted special coaching sessions at his residence in Pune, where questions and answers were dictated and later matched the actual NEET paper.
Protest movement grows
The exam controversy soon became a major student movement. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a satirical youth-led campaign, began protests at Jantar Mantar on June 20, demanding Pradhanâs resignation and accountability over paper leaks and other examination irregularities.
The agitation gathered pace after climate activist Sonam Wangchuk joined the protest and began an indefinite hunger strike. His deteriorating health drew wide attention on social media and his later hospitalisation further fuelled public anger. He eventually ended his 26-day hunger strike after receiving written assurances from the government.
The CJP said the movement would continue until Pradhan resigned. Its leaders also demanded compensation for the families of students who died by suicide, withdrawal of FIRs against peaceful protesters and a written guarantee that no such cases would be filed in future.
Centre shifts strategy
The Centreâs response changed over time. At first, several BJP leaders dismissed the protests, but the government later opened negotiations and announced a series of measures to calm the situation.
PM Modi said paper leaks were not an ordinary matter and announced fast-track courts to ensure swift punishment for those involved. He also said the government had acted to make sure that nearly 22 lakh students did not lose an academic year.
The Union Cabinet later approved amendments to anti-paper-leak law, proposing a maximum jail term of 10 years, a fine of up to Rs 10 crore and a higher minimum sentence. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said the Bill would be brought to Parliament soon.
At the same time, the National Testing Agency began a major internal overhaul, terminating 47 officials and recruiting new personnel in cybersecurity, digital forensics and test-centre operations. Officials said the changes were aimed at restoring confidence and tightening examination security.
Talks remain deadlocked
Even as the government expanded its response, its talks with the CJP remained unresolved. A second round of discussions between Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh and CJP representatives ended without a breakthrough. The CJP said the Centre had sought time until Saturday afternoon to respond to its main demand for Pradhanâs resignation.
The group said the other two major demandscompensation for bereaved families and withdrawal of cases against peaceful protesters had been accepted in principle. But it insisted that any further meeting must be held at a neutral venue, such as the Constitution Club of India, rather than a ministerâs residence.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi renewed his attack on the government, accusing Pradhan of presiding over a collapse of the education system. He also joined opposition leaders in paying tribute to students who died by suicide over the controversy and accused the Centre of using force against peaceful demonstrators.
Opposition steps up pressure
As protests spread across the country, opposition parties intensified their demand for Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, accusing the Centre of failing to protect the integrity of competitive examinations.
Parliament witnessed repeated disruptions as INDIA bloc MPs insisted that the education minister step down before any discussion on the NEET controversy could begin.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi emerged as one of the strongest critics of the government, calling Pradhan 'a symbol of the collapse of our education system' and saying, "He has to go." He also said students were making three key demands: the education minister's removal, action against those responsible for the alleged pellet gun use and lathi-charge on protesters, and an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi to the affected youth.
The opposition also organised protests and candlelight marches in solidarity with students and families affected by the alleged paper leak and exam-related suicides.
Rahul Gandhi later brought before the media a protester whom he claimed had suffered pellet gun injuries during the Jantar Mantar demonstration, alleging that the government had falsely denied using pellet guns against protesters. "His eye has suffered damage, and he has lost his vision," Gandhi said, while accusing the Centre of attacking the future of the country's youth instead of addressing their concerns.
Courts and Parliament
The Supreme Court agreed to hear petitions over alleged excessive police action against protesters. The court also clarified that reports saying it had refused to hear the matter were false.
Parliament too was paralysed repeatedly as opposition MPs pressed for Pradhanâs resignation before any debate could begin. The government said it was ready for discussion without preconditions and accused the opposition of blocking parliamentary proceedings.
Meanwhile, Delhi Police warned that those directly involved in violence during the protests could face passport cancellation. The warning came after clashes near Jantar Mantar left several police personnel and protesters injured.
What the resignation means
Pradhanâs resignation is the biggest political consequence so far of the NEET controversy. It follows weeks of criticism over repeated exam irregularities, the handling of protests and the governmentâs initial response, which opponents said was too slow and dismissive.
The CBI probe into the alleged leak has widened across several states, with arrests made and searches carried out in multiple cities. The case has also prompted the government to push a tougher anti-paper leak law, while the National Testing Agency has begun a major overhaul of its staffing and security arrangements.

headline: 'Dharmendra Pradhan resigned under no pressure,' says BJP leader; urges parents not to send students to ‘such protests’
full_text:
'Dharmendra Pradhan resigned under no pressure,' says BJP leader; urges parents not to send students to ‘such protests’
Dubey praised Pradhan’s long association with the education sector and highlighted his role in introducing major reforms
BJP MP Nishikant Dubey on Saturday defended Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation as India's education minister, saying the decision was not taken under any pressure but was a personal choice.
He praised Pradhan’s long association with the education sector and highlighted his role in introducing major reforms, including the National Education Policy (NEP) and changes in the higher education and examination systems.

Dubey said, “Dharmendra Pradhan did not resign under any pressure. He is a senior BJP leader who rose through the ranks of the ABVP and worked extensively in the education sector, bringing major changes such as the new education policy, universities, and examination systems. He took this decision on his own.”
He also urged parents to discourage their children from participating in such protests, saying, “I also appeal to parents not to push their children into such protests.”
Pradhan resigns
Education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday, after weeks of massive student protests in Delhi seeking his resignation over exam irregularities, particularly the NEET-UG paper leak.
Pradhan announced his resignation from the post on X. He said that he was taking the decision keeping the future of students in mind. "...To ensure that anti-national elements are not benefitted by the situation at Jantar Mantar and across the country, that the nation remains united, students in India do not get tangled in legal complexities and focus on their studies and their career, I have tendered my resignation to the Prime Minister...," the letter reads.
The development comes a day after spokespersons from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), the Abhijeet Dipke-led outfit that has been leading the protests, met union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh.
After the meeting, the CJP had said that the government had sought day's time to decide on Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.
CJP withdraws protest
The CJP ended its over a month-long protest on July 25, announcing that all of its demands have been accepted by the government. “Cockroach Janta Party withdraws its nationwide agitation with immediate effect. All demands of the Cockroach Janta Party have been accepted by the government,” the outfit said in a tweet.

-All FIRs by Central govt and NDA-ruled states will be withdrawn, and no action will be taken against anyone involved in these protests in the future.

headline: Dharmendra Pradhan, who stepped down as Union education minister on Saturday after a five-year tenure, leaves behind an education system more standardised, digitally connected and centrally regulated than the one he inherited â but also questions ove...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: 
Dharmendra Pradhan, who stepped down as Union education minister on Saturday after a five-year tenure, leaves behind an education system more standardised, digitally connected and centrally regulated than the one he inherited â but also questions over examination credibility, institutional autonomy, data privacy and the Centreâs capacity to implement reforms on such a large scale.
Pradhan, the longest-serving education minister in Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs cabinet, held the portfolio from July 7, 2021, to July 25, 2026. Until 2024, he was also minister for skill development and entrepreneurship.
His tenure was less about announcing a new education policy â the National Education Policy had been approved in 2020 â and more about constructing the machinery required to put it into operation.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
The defining theme was standardisation and portability: common entrance examinations, transferable academic credits, permanent student identification numbers, comparable assessment standards and an attempted umbrella regulator for higher education.
The Common University Entrance Test, introduced in 2022, sought to replace differing Class XII board cut-offs with a common admission platform for central universities. 
It also dramatically expanded the role of the National Testing Agency, whose functioning and credibility later became one of the biggest challenges of Pradhanâs tenure.
The National Credit Framework, Academic Bank of Credits and four-year undergraduate programmes were designed to allow students to accumulate and transfer credits, pursue multidisciplinary courses and enter or leave programmes without losing their academic record.
APAAR, envisaged as a permanent academic identity for every student, sought to link school, university and skill qualifications through DigiLocker and the credit bank. While intended to ease mobility, it triggered concerns over consent and protection of childrenâs data.
In school education, the ministry released curriculum frameworks for the foundational stage and school education, operationalising the NEPâs 5+3+3+4 structure. PM SHRI was launched to upgrade more than 14,500 existing government schools as models of NEP implementation, while PARAKH was established to develop common assessment standards and bring greater comparability among school boards.
Other big-ticket measures included the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, One Nation One Subscription for access to research journals, PM-USHA funding for state universities, permission for foreign universities to open campuses in India and the establishment of IIT campuses abroad.
Pradhan also pushed Indian-language textbooks, multidisciplinary education, vocational integration and apprenticeship programmes, drawing on the overlap between his education and skill-development portfolios.
The proposed replacement of UGC, AICTE and NCTE with an umbrella regulatory architecture remained unfinished. Implementation also met resistance from some states over language, curriculum and centrally sponsored schemes.
Ultimately, the sharpest contradiction of the Pradhan years lay in national testing. Common examinations were meant to deliver fairness and uniformity, but paper leaks, cancellations and administrative failures raised doubts about whether centralisation had moved faster than institutional capacity.

headline: Longest mobile internet shutdown in Delhi's history eases as CJP withdraws protest
full_text:
Longest mobile internet shutdown in Delhi's history eases as CJP withdraws protest
With the seventh extension that came on Saturday, mobile internet in the area remained repeatedly suspended for five days.
Delhi witnessed its longest internet shutdown during the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest demanding the resignation of (now former) education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. On Saturday morning, the government issued a seventh order extending the suspension of mobile internet services around Jantar Mantar until 12 midnight.
However, people in and around the affected area said mobile internet services were restored shortly after Pradhan announced his resignation on X and the CJP called off its protest, saying the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government had agreed to its demands.
The restoration came well before the scheduled midnight deadline for the suspension. Despite the restoration, telecom service providers (TSPs) had not received any formal order revoking the suspension until late Saturday evening, said people aware of the matter.
In the last five days, it was only on July 21 when the government did not issue a suspension order. With the seventh extension that came Saturday, mobile internet in the area remained repeatedly suspended for five days, making it the longest such disruption recorded in the national capital.
Also Read | Jantar Mantar protest: Delhi Police FIR includes charge of attempt to murder
A timeline of shutdowns
The shutdown began on July 20, when the government directed TSPs, including Airtel, Reliance Jio and Vodafone Idea, to suspend mobile internet services from 10 am to 6 pm in parts of central Delhi around Jantar Mantar. A second order followed on July 22, directing operators to suspend services from 6 pm until 6 am the next morning.
On July 23, the government first extended the suspension from 9.30 am to 4.30 pm before issuing another order extending it until midnight. On Friday, authorities again suspended mobile internet until noon before issuing a sixth order extending the shutdown till 12 midnight. On Saturday, a seventh order further extended the suspension till 12 midnight.
The orders require telecom companies to suspend mobile internet services within a 1.5-km radius of the protest site. Affected areas include Janpath Market near Connaught Place, Le Meridien, Shangri-La hotel, the National Media Centre and the Indian Women’s Press Corps office.
Digital rights organisation SFLC.in also challenged the internet shutdown orders before the Delhi High Court, arguing that the suspension of mobile internet services in parts of central Delhi during the July 2026 protests was unlawful.
A history of shutdowns
While Delhi has seen internet shutdowns before, they have been shorter and linked to specific law-and-order situations.
One such instance was in December 2019, during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), when mobile internet services were suspended for several hours in parts of the capital. The shutdown was ordered by Delhi Police, which is empowered to direct telecom operators to suspend services under the temporary telecom suspension rules.
Another instance of internet shutdown occurred during the farmers’ protests in 2021. In January 2021, the government suspended mobile internet services in adjoining areas of Delhi. The suspension was later extended at some of the Delhi border protest sites, including Singhu, Ghazipur and Tikri, as the farmers’ agitation continued.
Unlike the 2019 and 2021 disruptions, the current shutdown was extended through multiple consecutive government orders over several days.
The repeated internet suspensions pushed protesters to look for alternative ways to communicate. Some turned to apps such as Bitchat Mesh, which do not depend on mobile internet. Instead, the app creates a Bluetooth-based mesh network that connects nearby users, allowing messages to be exchanged without an internet connection.
The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the Home Ministry, also issued a notice to GitHub under section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act, directing it to remove URLs hosting BitChat, said the messaging app’s founder Jack Dorsey on X on Friday.

headline: All about Pralhad Joshi: BJP's 'blue-eyed boy' now in charge of education ministry after Pradhan quits
full_text:
All about Pralhad Joshi: BJP's 'blue-eyed boy' now in charge of education ministry after Pradhan quits
Pralhad Venkatesh Joshi is currently the Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, as well as New and Renewable Energy.
After President Droupadi Murmu on Saturday accepted the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as education minister, senior BJP leader Pralhad Joshi has been given the additional charge of the Education Ministry.
The development came just hours after Pradhan announced that he had submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Who is Pralhad Joshi?
Pralhad Venkatesh Joshi is currently the Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, as well as New and Renewable Energy. Along with these portfolios, he will now also oversee the Education Ministry.
Also read | Here's the last time a Union minister resigned under Modi govt because of protests
Joshi returned to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Cabinet in 2024. A five-time Member of Parliament, he is regarded as one of the BJP's trusted leaders and is often described as the "blue-eyed boy" of the party's top leadership.
Political journey
Born in November 1962 into a traditional North Karnataka Brahmin family, Joshi entered national politics after being elected to the 14th Lok Sabha in 2004.
Also read | Pralhad Joshi gets education ministry charge as Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation accepted
He became associated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) at a young age and later rose through the ranks of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
His electoral journey began in 1996 when he was elected to the Karnataka Legislative Assembly. Eight years later, he entered Parliament after winning the Dharwad-Hubballi Lok Sabha seat in 2004. Since then, he has retained the constituency in every general election, securing victories in 2009, 2014, 2019 and 2024.
Rise within the BJP
Joshi's active participation in parliamentary debates, particularly on development, infrastructure and education, strengthened his position within the BJP. His growing influence earned him the reputation of being one of the party high command's most trusted leaders.
In 2019, he joined Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Cabinet as Union Minister for Parliamentary Affairs, Coal and Mines. He returned to the Union Cabinet in 2024.
Faced challenge in 2024 Lok Sabha election
Despite his strong political standing, Joshi's latest electoral battle was not without hurdles. He faced opposition from sections of the influential Lingayat community in Karnataka, with Lingadishwar seer emerging as a key challenger through his followers.
Dispute resolved before election
The differences were eventually resolved with the intervention of senior leaders, including former chief minister BS Yediyurappa.
Dharwad city BJP block president Tippana Majjagi said the misunderstanding between the two sides had been settled.
A key face in Karnataka BJP
Over the years, Joshi has remained one of the BJP's most prominent leaders from Karnataka. Despite political challenges and criticism, he has continued to retain his electoral base and remains an influential figure within both the state unit and the party's national leadership.

headline: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party leaders on Saturday met Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar after the protest against the NEET paper leak at Jantar Mantar was called off following education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and the fulfi...

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party leaders on Saturday met Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar after the protest against the NEET paper leak at Jantar Mantar was called off following education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and the fulfilment of the remaining demands.
While speaking to reporters after the meeting, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das said they had made it clear that the party would take legal action against every official who used excessive force against students during the July 20 march.
"There was no specific agenda for the meeting... The discussion took place in a very cordial atmosphere. Senior officers, including the Special Commissioner of the Delhi Police, were also present.

"We will initiate legal proceedings against all such police and RAF personnel very soon. We have also launched a website, and when we begin this legal action, we will not only file complaints but also seek the registration of FIRs.

"It was a good meeting. We discussed everything that has happened over the past few days. What happened on the 20th was very unfortunate. However, we also recognise that there had been consistent cooperation from the Delhi Police," he said.
"We acknowledged that as well. We hope this marks the beginning of a new chapter. All our demands have been accepted, including the withdrawal of the FIRs and the assurance that no new FIRs will be filed. All's well that ends well, and we sincerely thank the youth of this country," he added.

headline: ‘Police are everywhere’: Sonam Wangchuk's wife questions heavy deployment at Medanta
full_text:
‘Police are everywhere’: Sonam Wangchuk's wife questions heavy deployment at Medanta
Angmo's post comes after Wangchuk shared a video late Friday night questioning whether he needed a “character certificate” after 26 days of hunger strike.
Scientist and activist Sonam Wangchuk's wife Gitanjali Angmo questioned the heavy deployment of police in the hospital where he is admitting, claiming that the authorities are deciding who “may or may not meet him”.
Angmo shared a picture from the hospital on Saturday showing several police officers standing in the lobby of Medanta Hospital in Gurugram where Wangchuk is currently admitted after Delhi high court's order.
He was earlier taken to Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital by Delhi police amid his hunger strike in support of students demanding education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. ‘Police are everywhere’
In the post shared by Angmo, she questioned the heavy deployment of police at Medanta Hospital and said that “police are everywhere”.
“At both Safdarjung and now Medanta, police are everywhere. At the main gate. The reception. The lifts. Outside @Wangchuk66’s ICU. They decide who may or may not meet him. If the Court has clarified that he is not under detention, then under what authority is this happening?” she questioned.
“In an enlightened democracy, is the role of the police to protect citizens and uphold the law, or to control citizens on behalf of those in power? These are questions every Indian should be asking,” she added.
The official Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) handle also drew attention to Angmo's post.
Angmo's post comes after Wangchuk also shared a video late Friday night questioning whether he still needed a “character certificate” after 26 days of hunger strike, following allegations of a “deal” with the government.
In a 22-minute long tell-all video posted on his YouTube handle, Wangchuk alleged ill-treatment via police occupation at Safdarjung Hospital and refusal to let him go after a High Court order granted him permission to shift to a private facility of his choice.

A clip in the video showed Wangchuk trying to get away from Safdarjung Hospital but being denied exit by cops positioned on the hospital floor. The confrontation turned aggressive as Wangchuk lay on the ground, refusing to move from the spot.
“Arrest me. Why are you forcing... people, this is torture. Now arrest me if you want, you understand? Arrest me, arrest me. You can stop me wherever, let the nation know how,” he can be heard saying angrily in the video taken and uploaded by an aide from his team as cops try to chase him down the hospital corridor.
“It is digitally everywhere. The world knows except you. The world knows,” he says in reference to the Delhi High Court order allowing him to be transferred to Medanta Hospital.
In his YouTube video, Wangchuk also addressed questions regarding why he dropped education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation as well as the manner in which he broke his fast by saying that he feared a violent government crackdown similar to the one seen in Ladakh during his last hunger strike. He emphasised that his priorities in this instance were to ensure legal impunity for all students who are protesting peacefully.
Police, hospital authorities clarify
Officials have clarified that the video was recorded at Safdarjung Hospital on July 21, the day of the High Court order. "This is from July 21 July, the day when the court informed Sonam's family that he can be moved to Medanta hospital," an official said.
“He was trying to leave for Medanta hospital, but was not allowed, as we were waiting for the court orders to come to us first and hence we were stopping him,” the official clarified as the reason for attempts to block Wangchuk's exit.
Safdarjung Hospital cited a similar reason by stating that all preparations were in place to handover Wangchuk to the medical team at Medanta Hospital as soon as the High Court order officially reached them.
"The video was reportedly recorded before the hospital administration received the written order of the high court. At that time, Mr Wangchuk insisted on leaving the hospital based on information available in the media," the hospital's statement said, as per PTI report.
“It is pertinent to note that Mr Wangchuk was handed over to the team of doctors from Medanta Gurugram on the same day at 6:40 pm, immediately after the written order was received by the hospital."
Currently, Wangchuk is under recovery at Medanta Hospital. The CJP has vowed to continue its nationwide protests until Pradhan's resignation. Representatives from the party are scheduled to have another round of talks with Nadda and Singh in the afternoon. Track CJP protest LIVE updates here

headline: Ayodhya donation theft: UP to propose 3-IPS panel for new SIT to Supreme Court
full_text:
Ayodhya donation theft: UP to propose 3-IPS panel for new SIT to Supreme Court
Uttar Pradesh is set to place the names of three senior IPS officers before the Supreme Court for a new SIT in the Ayodhya temple donation case. The move follows the court's insistence on a team that conducts the probe itself rather than merely supervising it.
The Uttar Pradesh government is set to submit a panel of three senior IPS officers before the Supreme Court on Monday for the constitution of a new Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe the alleged theft and misappropriation of donations at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple in Ayodhya.
The matter is scheduled to come up for hearing before the apex court, which had earlier directed the state government to constitute an SIT headed by a senior IPS officer to ensure an independent and effective investigation into the alleged embezzlement of devotees' donations.
According to sources, the state government is likely to propose the names of Inspector General (IG), Lucknow Range, Kiran S, Deputy Inspector General (DIG), Ayodhya Range, Somen Verma, and Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), Ayodhya, Gaurav Grover for the new SIT. The proposed team is expected to function under the leadership of IG Kiran S and submit its findings to the Supreme Court.
The proposed panel marks a change from the existing SIT. Earlier, the committee included Lucknow Divisional Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant and Special Secretary (Finance) Neel Ratan Kumar. Under the revised proposal, the two civil officers have been replaced by senior IPS officers in line with the Supreme Court's observations.
The Supreme Court, while hearing a batch of petitions on July 20 seeking a fair, impartial and time-bound investigation into the alleged embezzlement, had questioned whether the existing SIT was directly investigating the case.
Responding to the Bench, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Uttar Pradesh government, had informed the court that the investigation was being carried out by the Uttar Pradesh Police, while the SIT was only supervising the probe.
Expressing dissatisfaction with the arrangement, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant directed the state government to obtain instructions on constituting an SIT that would itself conduct the investigation. The Bench suggested that the team be headed by a senior IPS officer, such as the IG of the Lucknow Range, who was already a member of the existing SIT.
The matter is being heard by a bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohan in a batch of petitions seeking an independent probe into the alleged embezzlement of donations made by devotees at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple.
The allegations relate to an FIR registered over the alleged diversion of temple donations. Police have arrested all eight persons named in the case, including the official responsible for counting cash donations at the temple's pilgrim facilitation centre. The accused have been booked under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita on charges including criminal breach of trust, cheating and criminal conspiracy. Investigators suspect the alleged fraud was carried out over a period of time through manipulation of the temple's donation collection and accounting process.
The Supreme Court is expected to consider the panel proposed by the Uttar Pradesh government during Monday's hearing and take a call on the constitution of the new SIT.

headline: NEW DELHI: It must qualify as a striking case of maximising one's returns on meagre capital. Disproportionate to its marginal presence in Parliament and anaemic strength on the ground, Left parties successfully leveraged AISA, SFI and AISF, which hav...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: It must qualify as a striking case of maximising one's returns on meagre capital. Disproportionate to its marginal presence in Parliament and anaemic strength on the ground, Left parties successfully leveraged AISA, SFI and AISF, which have active units in Delhi, to pressure govt to give into the demand of getting Dharmendra Pradhan to resign as education minister.
In fact, AISA members, president Neha Bora and Manish Kumar and Ameen Amitoj, despite having no prior association with Abhijeet Dipke, sat on a 23-day hunger strike in solidarity with the students.
The victory of their student outfits, which made common cause with those sections of Gen Z, who are usually not receptive to their "class warfare" trope, could act as a compensation of sorts for the Left in an electorally bleak season, marked by routs in Kerala and West Bengal.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
Earlier, in another instance of them successfully using their tactical intelligence, the Left, through its farmers' wings, influenced the protests in Punjab against farm sector reforms laws enacted by Modi govt, which had to junk them.
If AISA, SFI and AISF were a vocal presence throughout the protest, their mother outfits CPI(ML), CPM and CPI, in that order, complemented the effort on the ground by goading the opposition to support the CJP-led protests.
According to Left functionaries, who have been part of the demonstrations, when the Left-aligned students groups joined the students' protest led by CJP, they were drawn into the fold organically and not perceived as people just jumping in for credit as these students have been raising issues around the flaws in the examination system and the challenges through their unions.
All 15 MPs belonging to the Left joined the students to protest the police action against them during the march to Parliament on July 20. They also ensured there was no dilution of the demand for Pradhan's resignation.
CPI(ML) general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya agreed that the success of the protests has given the Left a fillip. "This movement has re-energised ongoing struggles across the country for democracy, justice, and the defence of the Constitution." He called upon INDIA bloc to carry the energy, resolve, and democratic spirit of this movement into Parliament and intensify the struggle for affordable and quality education for all.
CPM general secretary M A Baby said Pradhan's resignation was the first step. "Congratulations to Abhijeet Dipke and CJP, to SFI, AISF, AISA, and lakhs of students and young people for their courage and determination which has won this historic victory. We demand comprehensive reform: scrap NTA! Take back NEP!" CPM said.
"It is a rare moment of democratic accountability, achieved not through the goodwill of an arrogant govt, but through the sustained struggle of students and youth across the country. The students' movement has defeated the arrogance of BJP and compelled the Modi-Shah regime to answer for its failures," CPI general secretary D Raja said.

headline: 21 is the new political age: Revanth Reddy seeks lower age to contest MLA, MP polls
full_text:
21 is the new political age: Revanth Reddy seeks lower age to contest MLA, MP polls
A Revanth Reddy said Telangana will move a resolution to lower the minimum age for contesting Assembly and Lok Sabha elections to 21. He presented it as a push for stronger youth representation and wider student participation in national politics.
In a major political pitch aimed at empowering India's youth, Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Saturday announced that his government would move a resolution in the State Assembly urging the Centre to reduce the minimum age to contest Assembly and Lok Sabha elections from 25 years to 21 years.
Addressing a massive Gen Z rally in Hyderabad, Revanth Reddy said the time had come to give young Indians a greater role in shaping the country's future. "If a 21-year-old can become an IAS officer, contest local body elections, and even serve the nation through the civil services, why can't they contest Assembly and Parliament elections?" he asked.
The Chief Minister said the Telangana government would convene a special session of the Assembly and Legislative Council in the first week of August to pass a resolution seeking the constitutional amendment. He added that Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge would pursue the issue in Parliament.
Making a strong case for lowering the age limit, Revanth Reddy cited former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi's decision to reduce the voting age from 21 to 18 through the 61st Constitutional Amendment and PV Narasimha Rao's 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, which enabled 21-year-olds to contest local body elections. He also referred to countries such as Germany, the United Kingdom and Singapore, where younger leaders are allowed to contest elections at an earlier age.
The Chief Minister said Gen Z accounts for nearly 30 per cent of India's population but has less than one per cent representation in Parliament. "India's future lies in the hands of its youth. The country's legislatures must reflect that reality," he said.
Revanth Reddy also praised the nationwide Gen Z movement over the alleged NEET paper leak, claiming it had compelled the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. He demanded that the Centre withdraw cases filed against protesting students and provide compensation to the families of students who allegedly died by suicide in connection with the controversy.
Calling the movement a victory for India's youth rather than any political party, the Chief Minister urged young people to continue their fight for justice and greater representation. "This tsunami of youth must not stop here. The voice of Gen Z should be heard from Jantar Mantar to Parliament," he said.

headline: All Delhi metro stations now open as CJP withdraws protest, curbs ease in capital

In a relief for commuters, the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) announced on Sunday morning that all network stations are now open and operational. This comes as the students protests, led by Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) in the national capital, came to an end on Saturday evening after Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.

Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister after days of student protests in the national capital. He announced his resignation, saying that the developments of the past 10 days had "saddened" him deeply and that the issue was "not a matter of personal prestige."

headline: Dharmendra Pradhan steps down, Gen Z steps up
full_text:
Dharmendra Pradhan steps down, Gen Z steps up
Minister Pralhad Joshi gets additional charge of education, BJP leaders rally behind Pradhan after he resigns.
A 36-day stir by students achieved a landmark victory on Saturday as education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following weeks of sweeping protests that brought central Delhi to a halt, energised a moribund Opposition, and heralded the entry of a new generation of young people into politics.
The sprawling sit-in in Delhi’s historic Jantar Mantar was called off hours after the resignation was announced by the minister on X with leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) saying the government had accepted two other demands – compensation of ₹1 crore to the kin of every student who died by suicide following irregularities in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test, and the withdrawal of all first information reports against students who undertook a massive march to Parliament earlier this week.
“We have won. Gandhi has won. Ambedkar has won,” CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said from the makeshift stage in Jantar Mantar as news trickled into the heavily barricaded site.
This is the first time that a popular street protest has forced the resignation of a Union minister in the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government’s three terms. Union consumer affairs minister Pralhad Joshi was given additional charge of the education ministry.
Also read: Fear of losing Gen Z, poll math forced BJP's hand in Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
Celebrations erupted soon after as young men and women – many of them Gen Z -- waved the Tricolour, climbed barricades and broke into impromptu jigs as makeshift loudspeakers belted out Bollywood favourites. Many briefly interrupted festivities to stand in attention and loudly sing along to the national anthem and Saare Jahan Se Acha, before unfurling their banners and posters featuring memes and slogans hitting out at the government.
“Our generation did it. We showed them that you cannot call us terrorists, hit us, and go scot free,” said Nachiket Malhotra, 22.
Pradhan – one of the seniormost ministers in the Cabinet who was a part of the council of ministers since Prime Minister Narendra Modi swept to power in 2014 and the longest serving education minister in almost two decades – announced his dramatic resignation on X.
In his two-page note in Hindi, the minister said he was disturbed to see the events of the past 10 days, and said he had resolved to not let the youth get ensnared in the web of confusion.
“Considering the situation at Jantar Mantar and across the country-with the aim of preventing anti-national forces from exploiting it, preserving national unity, ensuring that not a single Indian student’s future gets entangled in legal complexities, and allowing our children to devote their time to studies and focus on building their careers-I have submitted my resignation to prime minister,” he said.
“It is not a matter of individual prestige for me,” he added.
Rashtrapati Bhavan accepted his resignation even as senior ministers and Bharatiya Janata Party leaders rallied behind him. “His contribution to public service has been inclusive, future-ready, and aligned with the aspirations of a New India,” defence minister Rajnath Singh said on X.
Hours later, CJP representatives Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das met Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh – for the third time in as many days – and announced later that the government had accepted all their demands. The two sides will again meet after four weeks to discuss broader reforms in the examination system, the CJP said.
Also read: NEET can’t continue as a make-or-break exam
“The CJP declares that we withdraw the agitation in good faith and understanding that the agreed-upon terms will be executed within the agreed-upon timeline,” Das said at a joint press conference with Nadda and Singh.
“As the government accepted all our demands after 36 days of protests, we appeal to everyone to peacefully withdraw from protest sites and go home,” Ranka said.
Das said they have shared a draft of the demands with the government and the government will share a written guarantee by Tuesday. There was no word on the demand for an apology from the government over clashes on July 20.
Nadda said the CJP representatives came to the meeting with a written draft on cases filed during the July 20 agitation. Delhi Police have filed at least 15 FIRs in connection with the protest when tens of thousands of young people broke barricades, braved tear gas shells and batons to march to Parliament.
Nadda said the government also discussed demands of no retaliatory measures against agitators, compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who died, and a five-point CJP charter.
Also read: New paper leak bill prescribes 2-month window for probes, speedy trials
“After the discussion, the first point was that no action should be taken and no FIRs should be filed. If any FIRs have already been registered, whether by the Delhi Police or in BJP-ruled states, it will be withdrawn,” Nadda said, adding that the government agreed to give “honourable compensation within the rules” to the families of NEET suicide victims.
“All our demands have been accepted by the government,” Das said. Nadda said the government will provide to CJP copies of FIRs registered.
The announcements drew a dramatic denouement to the sweeping protests that were birthed by a controversial comment by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant describing unemployed people and dubious degree holders earlier this year.
“I thank CJI Surya Kant ji for calling us cockroaches. If you had not called us cockroaches, I would not have returned to India. If you hadn’t called us cockroaches, the youth would not have been on the roads,” Dipke said at Jantar Mantar to cheers.
The CJP first garnered millions of followers on social media before launching an indefinite sit-in protest on June 20 demanding the resignation of Pradhan over repeated question paper leaks – including one earlier this year. After days of tepid crowds, the movement was galvanised by the hunger strike and forcible removal of activist Sonam Wangchuk last week.
Crowds swelled through the weekend and by Monday morning, columns of people –– many of them students, first-time agitators and young professionals –– had defied a steady drizzle and police barricading to join what became the largest street protests in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s third term. Over 100 protesters and 129 security personnel were injured. One protester remains in the ICU.
Over the past week, crowds swelled and spilled beyond the confines of Jantar Mantar as thousands of young people poured into central Delhi, despite the longest spells of internet shutdown and metro station closure in Delhi, scores of barricades that sparked traffic snarls across the Capital, and controversial police detention from roads over protesters carrying posters or pepper spray. Tensions sporadically flared at the site, most dramatically on Wednesday night when clashes between protesters and police led to injuries to five agitators and five police personnel.
As the storm of Gen Z protesters grew, the government’s efforts to break the impasse kicked into overdrive. Nadda and Singh convinced Wangchuk to break his fast, Modi made a rare personal appeal to young people on Instagram and promised a stringent new bill – which will come before Parliament on Monday – to tackle paper leaks, and the National Testing Agency fired top officials. The police continues to be under fire over allegations of excess force used to scatter crowds on July 20; the Supreme Court is set to hear two appeals on Monday even as four people have alleged that the security forces used pellet guns on them – an unprecedented occurrence in the Capital.
But on Saturday afternoon, as an avalanche of people – many of them school students, many first-time protesters who had never stepped outside campuses before, many who travelled a night or more to be there – thronged Jantar Mantar, the jubilation around their achievement had washed away the bitterness. “Everyone thought we were lazy, we don’t know anything beyond Instagram or our phones,” said Nikita Joshi, 19. “Today, our generation raised its voice.”
