headline: WhatsApp puts multiple accounts in India under review, blocks app access for 24 hours
full_text:
WhatsApp puts multiple accounts in India under review, blocks app access for 24 hours
Affected users said they were unable to use the Meta-owned messaging app despite receiving no prior warning.
Multiple WhatsApp users, including several in India, reported on Monday evening that their accounts had been placed "under review" for up to 24 hours. The app temporarily blocked access to all features of the instant messaging platform, PTI reported.
The issue occured around 8 pm, Indian time. Affected users said they were unable to use the Meta-owned messaging app and hadn't received any prior warning.
What users saw
Users whose accounts were affected were shown the following message on the app: "Account in review. Date requested: 3 Aug 2026. Your account activity and device info is being checked to make sure it follows our terms of service. We will notify you of the result typically within 24 hours."
The review notice also included links to information on "How to use WhatsApp responsibly" and "About stolen phone and accounts."
During the review period, users reported being unable to access WhatsApp's messaging and calling features.
ALSO READ | After a decade in the US, Adobe executive relocates to Bengaluru to be closer to family
A user wrote on X, "WhatsApp has placed several accounts under investigation for 24 hours. WhatsApp suddenly put several users' accounts under investigation on Monday evening. As a result, they were unable to use the app's features for 24 hours. This step has left people frustrated in India and several other places, and they also lodged their complaints on social media."
Another user on X wrote, “WhatsApp has banned my account for absolutely no reason. Has anyone else experienced this? Any idea what the next steps are?”
WhatsApp's response
A WhatsApp spokesperson acknowledged that the company's automated systems could occasionally make mistakes while enforcing its policies.
ALSO READ | WhatsApp's biggest calling update is here: You can now make audio and video calls on WhatsApp Web
"We are always working to stay ahead of those trying to abuse our service and ban accounts to help keep other users safe. Sometimes we get this wrong and if we do, we try to fix it as quickly as possible to get people back to chatting," the spokesperson told PTI.
WhatsApp did not specify how many accounts were affected or whether the issue was linked to a technical glitch or an automated enforcement action. The company said it worked to correct cases where legitimate accounts are mistakenly flagged and restore access as quickly as possible.

headline: 2 losses, 1 win: BJP election scorecard days after Gen Z delivered a setback to Modi govt
full_text:
2 losses, 1 win: BJP election scorecard days after Gen Z delivered a setback to Modi govt
The biggest setback for the BJP came from Bihar, where Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar by 19,324 votes in Bankipur.
The BJP had a mixed day, at best, in the assembly bypolls on Monday. The saffron party won only one of the three seats that went to polls, all of them in states it rules.
It lost the high-profile Bankipur seat in Bihar and failed to wrest Datia in Madhya Pradesh, though the BJP held on to Manjalpur in PM Narendra Modi's home state of Gujarat.
The results came days after the Centre was put under pressure -- and the education minister had to be replaced -- over protests that saw massive participation of youth in Delhi against repeated examination paper leaks. Track election results live here
Bankipur loss hands Prashant Kishor first win
The biggest setback for the BJP came from Bihar, where Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor defeated BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar by 19,324 votes in Bankipur.
The BJP had held the seat since 1995.
The bypoll was held after BJP national president Nitin Nabin resigned from the assembly upon moving to the Rajya Sabha.
This was Kishor's first election victory since entering politics and gave Jan Suraaj its first MLA. The party had failed to open its account in the 2025 Bihar elections.
ALSO READ | From Jan Suraaj's zero to Bankipur victory: What changed for Prashant Kishor in Bihar within months
During the campaign last week, Kishor said Jan Suraaj already changed Bihar's political debate despite not being in power.
RJD's vote share also dropped sharply. Its candidate, who had polled more than 46,000 votes in the last assembly election, got fewer than 15,000 votes this time.
BJP loses Datia
The BJP also lost the Datia assembly bypoll in Madhya Pradesh, with Congress candidate Ghanshyam Singh defeating BJP's Ashutosh Tiwari by 6,016 votes.
The Congress retained the seat, which it had won in the 2023 elections.
BJP holds Manjalpur
The BJP's only win came from Gujarat, where it comfortably retained the Manjalpur Assembly seat.
BJP's Satendrabhai Patel defeated Congress candidate Bhikhabhai Rabari by a margin of over 30,000 votes.
ALSO READ | 'Bankipur won't become Bengaluru overnight': Prashant Kishor after big win in Bihar
Opposition steps up attack
The Opposition was quick to target the BJP after the results.
Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav linked the defeats to public anger over paper leaks, unemployment, inflation and corruption. Calling the verdict the “beginning of change”, he said it showed the “unity of the youth and the outrage of their guardians”.
He added that "even the BJP's safest and most traditional seats won't be able to save them from defeat now" and described the outcome as the “double defeat of the double-engine government”.
“Bhagwan ko nachane ka ahankaar rakhne walon ko Bhagwan ne hi nacha diya. (Those who believed they could make God dance have instead been humbled by God Himself),” the SP chief said.
AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal also took a swipe at the BJP over the bypoll results.
READ ALSO | 'BJP just lost its president's seat': Kejriwal on Prashant Kishor's big debut win in Bihar's Bankipur
Congratulating Prashant Kishor on his debut win, Kejriwal said, “The BJP has lost even the seat of its national president.”
He claimed the BJP's “ground has completely shifted” and blamed the result on issues such as “fund theft, paper leaks, E20” and growing public dissatisfaction with the Narendra Modi government.
"The arrogance is breaking down. The people of the country have given a signal of change," he added.
Results come after Jantar Mantar protests
The bypoll results came days after the Centre took a beating from non-stop GenZ-driven protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar over exam paper leaks and education reforms.
The agitation, led by the satirical digital front Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), began over the NEET paper leaks before ballooning into a mass movement on education, jobs and governance.
ALSO READ | 'Withdraw FIRs now': CJP to BJP after top court clarifies order on protest-linked cases
After over a month of protests and hunger strikes, the Centre opened talks with CJP leaders. Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan was forced to resign on June 25, and the government announced a series of measures, including examination reforms, discussions on preventing future paper leaks and compensation for families of students who died by suicide following exam paper leaks.
The CJP later ended its protest, saying the government accepted its key demands.
Kishor on CJP's impact
Last week, Kishor said the popularity of the CJP was an example of public frustration with the BJP growing day by day.
“The so-called party is being talked about because within no time of it hitting the Internet, nearly two crore people have signed up,” he told reporters.
“It must be understood that there is public distress which has led to so many people associating themselves with the party. Problems like unemployment, corruption, price rise and non-availability of gas and fertilisers have created a situation in which so many people are endorsing this campaign.”
Asked if the campaign could influence future elections, he said, “That remains to be seen. But the response to the campaign should have the government concerned. It is indicative of a trust in the system giving way to anxiety.”

headline: Parliament panel summons Meta, X, Google, Snapchat over digital safety, meeting at 4pm today
full_text:
Parliament panel summons Meta, X, Google, Snapchat over digital safety, meeting at 4pm today
The panel will examine measures to protect women, children and citizens' data privacy, besides reviewing how social media platforms comply with government rules
The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology summoned representatives of major social media platforms Meta, X, Snapchat, and Google to appear before the panel today at 4 PM.
The meeting of Parliament's Committee on Information Technology and communications was scheduled to convene to evaluate the broader framework of online safety. The discussions primarily focused on three core areas: ensuring the digital safety of women and children, safeguarding the data privacy of farmers, rural residents, laborers, and general citizens, and assessing how social media platforms comply with government rules governing law and order.
Also read: Govt summons Meta’s global head after PM Modi's Facebook reel removed
Announcing the summons earlier, BJP MP and chairperson of the Parliamentary Standing Committee Nishikant Dubey outlined the specific areas of inquiry for the digital platforms.
"On 3 August 2026 at 4 PM, our Parliamentary Committee on IT and Communication has summoned Meta (Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp), X (Twitter), Snapchat, and Google," Dubey stated.
"How will the privacy of women, children, farmers, rural folks, laborers, and the general public be protected? How do these companies ensure the government's public order?" he added.
The development follows an incident involving Meta, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Facebook video addressing action against examination paper leaks was briefly removed from the platform before being restored.
In a statement, a Meta spokesperson said, "The content was removed in error and has since been restored," attributing the removal to a technical error.
Also read: ‘Removed in error’: Meta on blocking PM Modi's video on Facebook
The video, released on July 23, marked Prime Minister Modi's first direct address to Gen Z during the 36-day-long Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led agitation over the NEET-UG 2026 examination irregularities.
In the address, the Prime Minister assured students that the government would strengthen the legal framework against paper leaks, including setting up Special Fast-Track Courts and introducing stricter punishment through fresh legislation. The Centre subsequently introduced the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, proposing imprisonment of up to 10 years, enhanced monetary penalties and Special Fast-Track Courts for offences under the Act.
The student agitation was called off on July 25 after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned. The Centre also reached an understanding with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and activist Sonam Wangchuk to withdraw cases against protesters, prevent police intimidation and bring stronger anti-paper leak legislation.

headline: RSS chief Bhagwat to address Gen Z at Mumbai event, Aaditya Thackeray takes a ‘suddenly’ dig
full_text:
RSS chief Bhagwat to address Gen Z at Mumbai event, Aaditya Thackeray takes a ‘suddenly’ dig
The interaction will take place in Mumbai during an event commemorating the 15th anniversary of India's International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN).
Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh chief Mohan Bhagwat is scheduled to interact with Gen Z students from over 100 cities across the country on Thursday (August 6), days after the student protests at Jantar Mantar. The youth-led demonstrations forced the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as the Union education minister.
The interaction between the youth and RSS chief Bhagwat, 75, will take place in Mumbai during an event commemorating the 15th anniversary of India's International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN), according to a press release.
Over 2,000 high school students are expected to be present during the inaugural ceremony of IIMUN's Annual Championship Conference, which will be held at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC). Gen Z and Gen Alpha are demographic groups, segregated according to their birth years — those born from 1997 to 2012 come under the Gen Z umbrella, those from 2013 to 2025 are considered to be Gen Alpha. Gen Z made up a major part of the recent student protests.

The IIMUN, founded by Rishabh Shah in 2011, organises 108 conferences and thousands of civic engagements and community interventions ever year, according to the press release. These are largely led entirely by youths aged 15-24 for students aged 11-19.
“IIMUN is a public affairs platform dedicated to uniting the world by spreading the idea of Bharat and sensitising tomorrow's leaders, today. headline: Politics often comes wrapped in familiar assumptions. With the BJP, the ruling party at the Centre, now also in power in a majority of states, either alone or in alliance, one might expect a degree of sameness in the profiles of Indiaâs chief ministe...
full_text:
Politics often comes wrapped in familiar assumptions. With the BJP, the ruling party at the Centre, now also in power in a majority of states, either alone or in alliance, one might expect a degree of sameness in the profiles of Indiaâs chief ministers. Yet the Association for Democratic Reforms reports show a more varied picture. The countryâs CMs come from different social strata, age groups, educational backgrounds and economic profiles, even within their own parties. There is no single formula for political ascent.That is what makes the comparison between ADRâs 2025 and 2026 reports more revealing than either report viewed alone. The 2025 study examined 30 chief ministers, since Manipur was then under Presidentâs Rule. The 2026 report covers 31, after the return of a chief minister in the state. More importantly, the occupants of the chief ministerâs office changed in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Bihar and West Bengal.
South pulls the wealth map
The combined assets declared by Indiaâs chief ministers rose from Rs 1,632 crore in the 2025 report to Rs 3,660 crore in 2026. Average assets more than doubled from Rs 54.42 crore to Rs 118.07 crore. The number of billionaire chief ministers rose from two to four.
In 2025, N Chandrababu Naidu, with assets of Rs 931.84 crore, and Pema Khandu, with Rs 332.57 crore, were the only billionaire chief ministers. Siddaramaiah was a distant third with Rs 51.94 crore. A year later, Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar is the clear number one with Rs 1,413.8 crore, while cine star and Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay declared assets of Rs 648.86 crore. Together, these four account for approximately Rs 3,327 crore, or 90.9% of the assets declared by all 31 chief ministers. The remaining 27 account for only around Rs 333 crore between them.
Analysing the assets held by CMs
A geographical cut makes the imbalance sharper. Using a broad four-zone grouping, not an ADR classification, the South has only six of the 31 CMs but accounts for roughly Rs 3,059 crore, or about 83.6% of all declared CM assets in 2026. That is because three of the four billionaire CMs, Shivakumar, Naidu and Vijay, are from southern states. So the South, in a way, lives up to the larger-than-life CM personalities. Naidu is a veteran politician who has survived many ebbs to rise again and regain his lost glory. D K Shivakumar finally got rewarded after a power tussle with Siddaramaiah, and Vijay was the new kid on the block who broke through the DMK-AIADMK binary, while also ticking the box of another cine star to become CM of Tamil Nadu. So the profiles of these billionaire CMs could not be more different.East and the Northeast together have the largest number of CMs in this grouping, 12, but account for about Rs 495 crore, helped substantially by Khanduâs declaration. North and Central India together have 10 CMs but only around Rs 75 crore in declared assets, while the West has three CMs and around Rs 31 crore.
Same party, different worlds
The party-wise picture is just as uneven. The BJP has 17 chief ministers in the 2026 list, but they are far from a single economic bloc. Its richest CM is Pema Khandu, with Rs 332.57 crore in declared assets. Its poorest is West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari, with about Rs 85.88 lakh. That is a nearly 387-fold gap within the same party.The Congress spread is smaller in headcount but sharper in scale. Of its four CMs, Shivakumar alone accounts for Rs 1,413.8 crore. At the other end is Kerala CM V D Satheesan, with Rs 6.66 crore. Revanth Reddy, at Rs 30.05 crore, and Himachal Pradesh CM Sukhvinder Singh, at Rs 7.82 crore, sit far below Shivakumarâs level. In effect, Congressâs CM asset profile is overwhelmingly shaped by one leader.This is why the average can mislead. A calculation based on individual entries puts the 2026 median at only around Rs 8.23 crore, barely higher than the 2025 median of about Rs 8.02 crore.Total declared liabilities rose from roughly Rs 242 crore in 2025 to nearly Rs 505 crore in 2026, though the number of CMs declaring liabilities of Rs 1 crore or more remained unchanged at 11. Khandu led the 2025 liability table with Rs 180.28 crore. In 2026, Shivakumar moved to the top with Rs 265.07 crore, followed by Khandu and Himanta Biswa Sarma.
Younger leaders, uneven party trend
The leadership profile also became younger. In 2025, 12 of the 30 chief ministers were in the 51-60 group. By 2026, that number had risen to 17. The number aged 61 or above fell from 10 to six. The 41-50 category remained unchanged at eight.
India now has younger CMs
The average reported age declined from 58.8 to 56.7, though the median remained 56. The shift reflects the exit of several older CMs, including Siddaramaiah, Pinarayi Vijayan, Nitish Kumar, M K Stalin and Mamata Banerjee. The ages are those recorded when election affidavits were filed, not necessarily current ages. So the actual decline is much sharper because the 2025 calculation accounted for many outgoing CMsâ 2021 affidavits.Here again, parties differ internally. Congressâs four CMs are tightly bunched. Revanth Reddy is 56, Sukhvinder Singh 58, Shivakumar 60 and Satheesan 61. The BJPâs spread is wider. It has Pema Khandu at 44 and Manik Saha at 70, with several CMs clustered in their 50s. In other words, the Congress CM cohort is smaller and more middle-aged, while the BJPâs larger pool stretches from younger leadership to older veterans.There was a reversal on gender. The 2025 report listed two women among 30 chief ministers. The 2026 report lists only one among 31. Mamata Banerjeeâs exit from the CM roster left Delhiâs Rekha Gupta as the sole woman in the group.
Degrees stay broadly stable
Many of the politicians are products of student politics. They may not have worked professionally, but they still believed in the inherent importance of formal education. In 2025, 25 of the 30 CMs were graduates, professional graduates, postgraduates or doctorate holders. In 2026, the number remained 25, despite the larger group. The proportion with graduate-level qualification or higher slipped slightly, from about 83% to 81%.Within parties, the BJP shows the widest educational spread. Its CM list includes doctorate holders such as Mohan Yadav, Himanta Biswa Sarma and Samrat Choudhary, but also leaders listed as Class 10 pass, diploma holders, graduates, professional graduates and postgraduates. Congressâs four CMs are more compact educationally: Shivakumar and Sukhvinder Singh are postgraduates, Revanth Reddy is a graduate and Satheesan is a graduate professional.
Cases rise, but cluster in five names
The criminal-record figures worsened modestly. In 2025, 12 of 30 chief ministers, or 40%, had declared criminal cases; 10 had cases classified by ADR as serious. By 2026, 14 of 31, or 45%, had declared criminal cases; 11 had serious cases.The combined number of declared cases rose from 187 to 195. The burden remained concentrated. Revanth Reddy continued to head the list with 89 cases, followed by Suvendu Adhikari with 29, Shivakumar and Naidu with 19 each, and Keralaâs V D Satheesan with 18. Five chief ministers accounted for 174 of the 195 cases, or 89.2%.
Criminal cases against CMs
Three of Congressâs four CMs are among the top five by declared cases: Revanth Reddy, Shivakumar and Satheesan. Among BJP CMs, Adhikari carries the highest declared case load, while several BJP chief ministers have no declared criminal cases. Geography shows a similar concentration, though for different reasons. The six southern CMs together account for 147 declared cases, driven mainly by Revanth Reddy, Shivakumar, Naidu and Satheesan. East and the Northeast account for 38 cases, led by Adhikari. North and Central India account for six, while the West accounts for four. It is perhaps not a coincidence that many of the CMs with high case loads were opposition leaders for a significant time.
Thus, criminal cases need to be treated with caution. A low case count may not strictly be a virtue; it may just be a case of friendly police administration. Disclosures arenât the only way to understand the nature of a politician. But they are an important starting point, particularly when compared over the years, to understand how the seat of power remains the same, but the nature of those who occupy it changes, perhaps as an inevitable reflection of the realities of the times.

headline: CJP eyes next chapter after NEET agitation, announces nationwide listening tour
full_text:
CJP eyes next chapter after NEET agitation, announces nationwide listening tour
The Cockroach Janta Party will also hold a two-day strategy meeting in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Wednesday and Thursday to finalise its future roadmap. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, spokespersons and organisational leaders will be in attendance.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Monday unveiled plans for a nationwide listening tour to connect with young people across India as it looks to build on the momentum of its agitation against the NEET paper leak.
In a statement posted on X, the outfit announced a two-day strategy meeting in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Wednesday and Thursday to finalise its future roadmap. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, spokespersons and organisational leaders will be in attendance.
According to the party, the discussions come after days of consultations with a broad cross-section of stakeholders, including around 50 volunteers who played a key role in the Jantar Mantar agitation.
As part of the nationwide listening tour, the CJP said it would reach out to volunteers across the country to understand the aspirations and concerns of young people before deciding its next course of action.
It said the outreach programme is aimed at engaging with a generation that has become "hopeful and optimistic" following what it described as the success of its campaign, which led to the resignation of former Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, ending the two-month agitation.
"The defeat of this arrogant government at the hands of the youth shows that when young people come together, they can achieve anything," CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said.
"Our team is working to put together the best possible path forward to channel the expectations of our youth into meaningful action," he added.
The party said it would announce further details, including the schedule and format of the nationwide listening tour, in the coming days.
The outreach is expected to shape CJP's organisational and political strategy as it seeks to build on the momentum generated by the anti-NEET movement.

headline: Continued political activities by deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from Indian territory “could harm” bilateral relations, the Government of Bangladesh conveyed to India on Monday (August 3, 2026) through Humayun Kobir, the Foreign Aff...
full_text:
Continued political activities by deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina from Indian territory “could harm” bilateral relations, the Government of Bangladesh conveyed to India on Monday (August 3, 2026) through Humayun Kobir, the Foreign Affairs Adviser to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
Mr. Kobir met with Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi in Dhaka after Ms. Hasina’s August 5 ‘homecoming’ media event was announced here by the Foreign Correspondents Club.
“Adviser Kobir mentioned that such activities could harm the positive progress of bilateral relations between the two countries. The Indian High Commissioner assured that the matter would be duly considered, necessary inquiries would be made and efforts would be made in this regard,” the official news agency of Bangladesh UNB reported.
The meeting took place in the Prime Minister’s Office in Tejgaon, Dhaka, UNB said.
The report added that Dhaka expects India to ensure that no one, including Ms. Hasina, used “Indian territory to make political statements or conduct any activities aimed at creating instability within Bangladesh”.
The Indian High Commission, in a statement, said that the discussion between Mr. Trivedi and Mr. Kobir focused on “mutual interests” and “mutual benefits”.
“High Commissioner reiterated India’s intent to work positively with the Government of Bangladesh to advance the developmental aspirations of the peoples of India and Bangladesh,” said the Indian High Commission in a message.
Ms. Hasina, who has been based here since fleeing Dhaka on August 5, 2024, has given multiple telephonic and emailed interviews over the past three months expressing her desire to return to Bangladesh by the end of the year.
Earlier, on Sunday, the Foreign Correspondents Club announced that the media event featuring an audio message from Ms. Hasina would be held on August 5 and that the event titled ‘Sheikh Hasina’s Homecoming’ would also feature her son Sajeeb Wazed Joy and several top functionaries of the Awami League.
Waeil Awwad, the club’s president, told The Hindu on Monday (August 3, 2026) that the event remains on track.

If you look at the viewership algorithm of the BJP, Congress, Samajwadi Party, and Aam Aadmi Party, the viewership is only 23 million. If Zuckerberg does not give it, then the safe harbour protection under Section 79 should be withdrawn from him."Dubey also raised concerns over the handling of child sexual abuse material and other objectionable content on social media platforms.He said, "CSAM (Child Sexual Abuse Material) is another issue. During the committee meeting, several members posed tough questions to Meta officials. Meta officials apologized, stating that the PMâs video was removed due to an error. headline: Zuckerberg apology sought over PM Modi video takedown, Meta faces panel heat
full_text:
Zuckerberg apology sought over PM Modi video takedown, Meta faces panel heat
A parliamentary panel has sought answers from Meta over why a PM Modi video disappeared from Facebook for hours. The episode has now raised questions over accountability, safe harbour and platform moderation.
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg should personally apologise for the temporary removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's video from Facebook, Parliamentary Standing Committee on Information Technology chairman Nishikant Dubey said on Monday after a meeting with representatives of the social media giant.
Speaking after the more than three-hour meeting, Dubey said Meta had acknowledged that Modi's video remained unavailable on the platform for about five hours, from 12.30 am to 5 am.
"They themselves admitted that the video was taken down for five hours. This is a very serious matter and an apology must come from Zuckerberg's side," Dubey said, according to PTI.
He also warned that if Zuckerberg did not apologise, the government should consider withdrawing Meta's safe harbour protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act.
The provision protects intermediaries from liability for third-party content under certain conditions.
WHY WAS PM MODI'S VIDEO REMOVED?
The meeting was convened after a Facebook post by Modi on action against paper leaks was briefly removed from the platform.
Meta had earlier attributed the incident to a technical glitch, apologised and restored the post. However, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology described the explanation as "inadequate".
Sources said the parliamentary panel has asked Meta to submit a written response within 10 days.
During the meeting, several BJP MPs questioned Meta representatives over who authorised the removal of the Prime Minister's video and sought clarity on who was responsible.
Members also raised concerns over alleged algorithmic bias, arguing that objectionable material remained available on the platform while "genuine" content was removed.
META OFFICIALS EXPRESS REGRET
According to sources, Meta representatives expressed regret over the incident and indicated that they were willing to apologise before the committee.
BJP members, however, argued that the matter went beyond an apology and called for accountability to be fixed, with legal action to be considered if warranted.
Opposition MPs on the committee took a different position, arguing that social media platforms must preserve space for dissent in a democracy.
They also cautioned against treating criticism of the government as anti-national content.
GOOGLE, X, YOUTUBE ALSO APPEAR
The meeting was part of the parliamentary panel's broader examination of the regulation of social and digital platforms.
Apart from Meta representatives, Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, MeitY Secretary S Krishnan and officials from Google, X, YouTube and Snapchat also appeared before the committee.
The episode has put fresh focus on how major social media platforms moderate political content and the extent of accountability they should face when posts by public figures are removed, even temporarily.

headline: ‘Zuckerberg intends to destabilise India’: Parliament panel chief demands apology from Meta boss over PM post row

‘Zuckerberg intends to destabilise India’: Parliament panel chief demands apology from Meta boss over PM post row
Highlighting the removal of PM Modi's content, Nishikant Dubey said this was “not the first time” Meta had done this.
BJP MP Nishikant Dubey on Monday questioned Meta chief executive officer (CEO) Mark Zuckerberg's “intention”, days after the brief removal of one of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's videos on Facebook. Dubey, who is also the chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications & IT, further demanded an apology from Zuckerberg himself after a meeting of the panel.
Highlighting the removal of PM Modi's content, Dubey said this was “not the first time” Meta had done this. “If you recall, Zuckerberg himself made a statement in January regarding the 2024 elections and later apologised. “Our committee has said two things and has clearly stated that the apology should come from Zuckerberg. If Zuckerberg does not give it, then the safe harbour protection under Section 79 should be withdrawn from him,” the BJP MP from Godda said.

Dubey said child sexual abuse material (CSAM) was another issue with the the platform. “YouTube also has that content. Meta also has that content, and they do not remove content related to child abuse,” Dubey alleged, adding that content “related to women” is not removed.

headline: Congress retains Madhya Pradesh's Datia seat; BJP loses bypoll after candidate switch
full_text:
Congress retains Madhya Pradesh's Datia seat; BJP loses bypoll after candidate switch
At the end of all 15 rounds of counting, Singh secured 66,757 votes, while Tiwari polled 60,741 votes.
The Congress on Monday retained the Datia assembly seat in Madhya Pradesh, with the party candidate Ghanshyam Singh defeating his nearest rival Ashutosh Tiwari of the BJP by 6,016 votes in the byelection marked by differences in the saffron camp over the choice of candidate.
At the end of all 15 rounds of counting, Singh secured 66,757 votes, while Tiwari polled 60,741 votes. Azad Samaj Party candidate Damodar Yadav secured third position by bagging 22,527 votes, District Election Officer and Datia District Magistrate Swapnil Wankhade told PTI.
A total of 21 candidates were in the fray, including Ghanshyam Singh and Ashutosh Tiwari.
At one point, Singh's lead of 12,607 votes over his nearest rival appeared unassailable, but the BJP nominee managed to close the gap to an extent in the last rounds.
The byelection was necessitated after a Delhi court in April this year sentenced sitting Congress MLA Rajendra Bharti to three years' imprisonment in a cheating case, leading to the termination of his Assembly membership.
"This verdict marks the beginning of the end of the BJP," Ghanshyam Singh told reporters.
In Bhopal, celebrations broke out at the state Congress headquarters with party workers distributing sweets.
A total of 21 candidates contested the by-election, which saw a healthy 71.44 per cent voter turnout, though the main fight was between Congress' Singh and Tiwari of the ruling BJP.
Then-Congress nominee Bharti had defeated BJP candidate and former state Home Minister Narottam Mishra in Datia by over 7,700 votes in the 2023 Assembly elections.
For the by-election, the BJP denied a ticket to Mishra and instead fielded Tiwari.
Ghanshyam Singh expressed confidence that the Congress will form the next government in Madhya Pradesh in 2028, adding that the party was working to see Rahul Gandhi become the next Prime Minister.
He said his priority would be to promote communal harmony in Datia and end political vendetta.
"I will work to end gambling and betting rackets in the constituency," he said.
State Congress President Jitu Patwari described it as a victory for the people of Datia, a clarion call for the 2028 assembly elections, and the result of the collective efforts of Congress leaders.
Patwari told reporters in Bhopal that Datia voters have exposed the corruption, terror, and arrogance of the BJP-led government.
He said the people of Datia have laid the foundation for change and the BJP's departure.

headline: 251-foot Tricolour Kanwar steels the spotlight during Kanwar Yatra in Haridwar
full_text:
251-foot Tricolour Kanwar steels the spotlight during Kanwar Yatra in Haridwar

headline: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat to interact with 2,000 teenagers in Mumbai on August 6 amid growing youth assertiveness
full_text:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat to interact with 2,000 teenagers in Mumbai on August 6 amid growing youth assertiveness
NEW DELHI: Days after saying that the era of unquestioned obedience was over and young people now sought reasons and logic, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat will interact with nearly 2,000 teenagers in Mumbai on August 6, bringing him face to face with the generation he has urged elders to engage through dialogue rather than commands.The students, aged between 15 and 19, will come from schools and colleges across more than 100 cities. The interaction will be held at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre as part of the 15th anniversary programme of Indiaâs International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN), a youth-led organisation.
The event comes against the backdrop of growing youth assertion in the country, with students increasingly using social media and street protests to demand answers from governments and institutions. The recent agitation over irregularities in NEET-UG and other examinations has also brought questions of transparency, accountability and the role of young people in public debate to the centre stage.Bhagwat did not refer to any particular agitation while speaking recently about changing relations between generations. He had said that, unlike in the past, children today expect reasons, examples and explanations and must be engaged through regular conversation.
The Mumbai interaction will, therefore, be watched for the issues raised by students and whether the session allows them to directly question the RSS chief on education, leadership, nation-building and social change.IIMUN founder Rishabh Shah said the gathering was aimed at creating a dialogue between senior leaders and young people.
âLeadership is not only about guiding the next generation, but also listening to it. At this critical juncture in Indiaâs journey, we need this dialogue more than ever before,â Shah said.Bhagwatâs address will mark the opening of the organisationâs annual championship conference, where students will debate national and international issues. This yearâs theme is âThe Role of Youth in Uniting the World, the Indian Wayâ.
Manash Pratim Gohain is a seasoned journalist with over two decades at The Times of India, where he has built a rich body of work spanning education policy, politics, and governance. Renowned for his incisive coverage of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, accreditation reforms, and skilling initiatives, he has also reported on student politics, urban policy, and social movements. His political reportageâboth reflective and news-drivenâadds depth to his writing, bridging policy with public impact. Through his 2,500 articles and related outlets, he has emerged as a trusted voice in national discourse, particularly in linking education reform to broader societal change.

headline: NEW DELHI: Indiaâs one more wetland, Glaw Lake of Arunachal Pradesh, has entered the global list of protected wetlands as a Ramsar site. It is the countryâs 101st such site and the stateâs first to join the elite club for additional care and conserva...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Indiaâs one more wetland, Glaw Lake of Arunachal Pradesh, has entered the global list of protected wetlands as a Ramsar site. It is the countryâs 101st such site and the stateâs first to join the elite club for additional care and conservation.Located within the Kamlang Tiger Reserve and Wildlife Sanctuary, Glaw Lake is a pristine freshwater lake in the Eastern Himalayas and a biodiversity hotspot. The lake is fed by perennial mountain streams and is surrounded by lush vegetation, supporting rich floral diversity.âEvery new Ramsar site strengthens our resolve to protect nature while securing the future of communities that depend on these invaluable ecosystems,â said Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav while announcing the development on X on Monday.The Glaw Lake wetland has over 150 tree species and 49 orchid species recorded within the site and its catchment, underscoring its ecological significance and surrounding landscape.âFrom 26 Ramsar sites in 2014 to 101 today, this remarkable journey reflects our unwavering commitment to environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable development,â said Yadav.
Globally, there are nearly 2,600 such designated wetlands under the Ramsar Convention.
India has the highest number of such wetlands in Asia and third highest in the world after the UK (176) and Mexico (144).Wetlands are land areas covered by water, either temporarily/ seasonally or permanently. These are critical ecosystems that play a significant role in supporting biodiversity, and providing various ecosystem services such as flood control, water supply, food, fibre and raw materials.
Vishwa Mohan is Senior Editor at The Times of India. He writes on environment, climate change, agriculture, water resources and clean energy, tracking policy issues and climate diplomacy. He has been covering Parliament since 2003 to see how politics shaped up domestic policy and Indiaâs position at global platform. Before switching over to explore sustainable development issues, Vishwa had covered internal security and investigative agencies for more than a decade.

headline: Gurugram: When Haryana BJP’s newly appointed state president Dr Archana Gupta rolled out her list of office-bearers this week, one pattern stood out—several party leaders who had been denied poll tickets or had openly expressed their ire against the ...
full_text:
Gurugram: When Haryana BJP’s newly appointed state president Dr Archana Gupta rolled out her list of office-bearers this week, one pattern stood out—several party leaders who had been denied poll tickets or had openly expressed their ire against the senior leadership found themselves accommodated.
The list, cleared with the concurrence of BJP’s national president Nitin Nabin, names eight state vice-presidents, three general secretaries, nine state secretaries, four office-bearers handling treasury and administration, four in charge of media and IT, six morcha presidents and two cell in-charges.
The most striking name on the list is of Bhavya Bishnoi, son of former MP Kuldeep Bishnoi and grandson of former Haryana chief minister Bhajan Lal, who has been made a state vice president.
The Bishnois were at the centre of a public row just months earlier. In April, Rajya Sabha MP Rekha Sharma, addressing a meeting ahead of the Panchkula mayoral election, alleged that BJP candidate Sham Lal Bansal had lost the same seat years ago because of “badmaashi” by then CM Bhajan Lal and his men. Kuldeep and Bhavya reacted sharply and Sharma later apologised.
Since then, Kuldeep Bishnoi’s proximity to Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Saini has been visible, though he skipped Saini’s event at Guru Jambheshwar University in Hisar last month.
Earlier, in 2024, Kuldeep Bishnoi and his supporters had targeted former CM Manohar Lal Khattar in Hisar during the Lok Sabha campaign, after Khattar seemed to accuse Bhajan Lal, without naming him, of promoting corruption. Kuldeep was also passed over by the party for a poll ticket.
Bhavya Bishnoi’s own political run has had its share of setbacks.
Kuldeep fielded his son instead of contesting himself in the 2019 Lok Sabha election from Hisar, where he finished third. In 2022, when Kuldeep quit the Congress for the BJP, he fielded Bhavya for the bypoll in Adampur—a seat he himself had vacated and which Bhavya won comfortably.
In 2024, the father-son duo was denied the Hisar Lok Sabha ticket, which went instead to Khattar’s preferred candidate Ranjit Singh—who went on to lose the seat and later quit the BJP.
Another name on the list, Sunita Duggal, has had a similarly turbulent run with ticket allocations.
A former Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer, Duggal resigned from government service ahead of the 2014 elections after being assured a Lok Sabha ticket from the Sirsa (SC) seat. The BJP instead gave the seat to Kuldeep Bishnoi’s Haryana Janhit Congress.
Duggal was then made to work the Pataudi assembly constituency for months, only for the ticket to go to Bimla Chaudhary. She was finally fielded from Ratia at the last minute and lost narrowly to the Indian National Lok Dal’s Ravinder Baliala.
In the 2019 Lok Sabha polls, Duggal won the Sirsa seat by a margin of over three lakh votes, defeating Congress’s Ashok Tanwar.
But in 2024, the BJP dropped her again—this time in favour of Tanwar himself, who had joined the BJP after stints with the Congress, Trinamool Congress and AAP. Tanwar lost to Congress’s Kumari Selja.
Duggal, fielded once more from Ratia, lost to Congress’s Jarnail Singh.
Now, one of the men who defeated Duggal now figure alongside her on Gupta’s list. Ravinder Baliala, who beat her in 2014, joined the BJP in 2019 and has been named a state vice president.
Also on the list is Deepak Mangla, who won the Palwal assembly seat in 2019 after losing it to Congress’s Karan Singh Dalal in 2014, but was denied a ticket in 2024 when the party fielded Gaurav Gautam instead. Mangla has now been named a state vice president.
Latika Sharma, who won the Kalka assembly seat on a BJP ticket in 2014 before losing it to Congress’s Pardeep Chaudhary in 2019, had a public argument with the party in 2024 when it denied her a ticket in favour of Shakti Rani Sharma, wife of former minister Venod Sharma. Latika Sharma had broken down in front of party workers at the time, alleging injustice. She, too, has now been made a state vice president.
The remaining vice presidents are sitting MLA Laxman Yadav, and longtime party workers Jawahar Saini of Jind and Ashok Gujjar of Kaithal.
Also Read: No LS ticket, not in star campaigners’ list — Kuldeep Bishnoi on political margins after joining BJP
Other office-bearers
The other office-bearers on Gupta’s list are general secretaries Gopal Sharma (Faridabad), Satyaprakash Jarawta (Gurugram) and Ved Phulla (Fatehabad).
The nine state secretaries are Madan Chauhan (Yamunanagar), Harvinder Kohli (Gurugram), Amarpal Rana (Jind), Pratibha Suman (Rohtak), Meena Chauhan (Karnal), Nagendra Sharma (Rohtak), Vikas Dahiya (Sonipat), Ravi Batan (Kurukshetra) and Gurpreet Kaur (Ambala).
Ajay Bansal (Rohtak) is state treasurer, Narendra Gupta (Faridabad) co-treasurer, Hariprakash Yadav (Jhajjar) office secretary and Rameshwar Chauhan (Yamunanagar) co-office secretary.
Further, Dr Sanjay Sharma (Ambala) is chief spokesperson, Bhupeshwar Dayal (Sonipat) is media coordinator, Aditya Chawla (Yamunanagar) is IT coordinator and Sombir Kataria (Jhajjar) is social media coordinator.
Morcha presidents are Akshit Dahiya (Sonipat)—Yuva Morcha, Richa Pahwa (Yamunanagar)—Mahila Morcha, Mahesh Chauhan (Gurugram)—Kisan Morcha, Sunil Sain (Dadri)—OBC Morcha, Ajay Khundia (Rohtak)—SC Morcha and Dr Avnit Vadaich (Kurukshetra)—Minority Morcha.
The cell in-charges are Mukesh Gaur (Bhiwani) and Manish Yadav (Gurugram).

headline: BJP is hopeful that DMK's bubbling anger with Congress will help its bid to win over the party's support for its key legislative measures, especially delimitation, in Parliament
full_text:
BJP is hopeful that DMK's bubbling anger with Congress will help its bid to win over the party's support for its key legislative measures, especially delimitation, in Parliament
NEW DELHI: DMK Sunday mounted a furious pushback against Rahul Gandhi's describing any support to govt's widely speculated move to revive the bill to increase Lok Sabha's strength, coupled with delimitation of constituencies, as a betrayal of Tamil Nadu amid buzz in political circles that the regional party may come around to backing the measure.A day after Rahul, during his visit to Tamil Nadu, said any party supporting the constitution amendment bill in Parliament will be a 21st century Ettappan, a historical figure reviled for treachery, senior DMK MP Dayanidhi Maran came out with a blistering retort. "These are the people who traded our trust in them for mere ministerial berths," he said, lashing out at "poisonous snakes" which sell trust to "buy" power, a reference to Congress's decision to snap ties with DMK and TVK.Maran's strongly worded rejoinder captured the lingering sense of betrayal within the Dravidian party over Congress's swift embrace of its rival after the national party went to the poll as DMK's ally and was fully backed by the latter on all key issues, including Rahul's leadership, in national politics through its years in office.BJP is hopeful that DMK's bubbling anger with Congress will help its bid to win over the party's support for its key legislative measures, especially delimitation, in Parliament, even though govt has so far not taken any official step to revive the bill that was defeated by a united Opposition in the last session.
DMK has anyway indicated its openness over the issue, saying it will take a call after studying the bill and insisting that the proposed law should not harm south India's interests.Rahul's comments are also a nod to the acknowledgement in Opposition camp of the possibility of DMK revising its stand on a bill which, opposition parties have alleged, will allow BJP-led governing alliance to reconfigure constituencies to its advantage for the 2029 Lok Sabha poll.
Targeting Rahul, Maran added, "Those who come to Tamil Nadu and stay silent about Cauvery rights are traitors. Those who only talk about irregularities in the exam, rather than insisting on completely abolishing NEET are traitors. Those who condemn BJP's horse-trading but ignore TVK's disgusting horse-trading are merely continuing that betrayal."

The suspension followed allegations of anti-party activities during the Datia by-election campaign. Congress candidate Ghanshyam Singh submitted a written complaint to party president Mallikarjun Kharge and senior leaders, accusing Bharti of colluding with BJP leaders and attempting to sabotage the party’s prospects.
“Bharti was working in collusion with BJP leaders and had received funding from the BJP. An attempt was made to harm the Congress party by distributing money among voters through Bharti’s supporters,” Singh alleged.

Kerala floods: Death toll rises to 15, 7 missing as heavy rain continues
NEW DELHI: Chief minister VD Satheesan on Monday said that the death toll in rain-related incidents across Kerala has risen to 15 as heavy rainfall continued to batter the state and rescue operations intensified.Addressing a press conference after reviewing the flood situation with senior officials, Satheesan said 316 relief camps were functioning across Kerala, sheltering 11,018 people displaced by flooding and landslides.
He said Kottayam reported three deaths, including two in the Poonjar assembly constituency and a child who drowned after falling into a water tank. Ernakulam recorded two deaths, while one person each died in Idukki and Muvattupuzha. Four people died in Malappuram, two in Kollam and one each in Kannur and Kozhikode.The chief minister said seven people were still missing. Two each are missing in Kollam and Kannur, while one person each is untraceable in Malappuram, Idukki and Muvattupuzha.Satheesan announced Rs 10,000 as funeral assistance for the families of those killed in rain-related incidents. He also said people returning home from flooded relief camps would receive Rs 10,000 as immediate assistance.
The chief minister directed the Agriculture Department to submit a proposal to revise crop compensation, saying the current relief was inadequate. According to preliminary estimates, 165 hectares of agricultural land have been damaged, affecting 3,596 farmers.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued rain alerts for all 14 districts in the state. Orange alerts are in place for Kasaragod, Kannur, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Malappuram, Ernakulam, Idukki, Kottayam, Alappuzha and Pathanamthitta, while Palakkad, Thrissur, Kollam and Thiruvananthapuram remain under a yellow alert.The weather office has forecast isolated heavy rainfall accompanied by gusty winds of up to 60 kmph.Authorities have urged people living in low-lying and riverside areas to remain alert as water levels in major rivers continue to rise. Residents in landslide-prone hilly regions have also been advised to move to safer locations if necessary.
District collectors have declared a holiday for educational institutions in 12 districts, including professional colleges, due to the heavy rain.The ban on fishing along the Kerala, Karnataka and Lakshadweep coasts also remains in force because of rough sea conditions.In Pathanamthitta district, rising water levels in the Pamba river have raised concerns after recent flash floods. Authorities have warned that the Moozhiyar Dam may be opened if water levels continue to rise and have asked residents along the riverbanks to stay prepared for evacuation.The Kerala government said it remains fully prepared to handle any emergency and urged people to strictly follow advisories issued by the state and district administrations. It also said financial assistance would be provided to families of those killed and to people who lost their homes and livelihoods.

headline: Prashant Kishor rules out alliances after Bankipur win, says BJP voters backed him
full_text:
Prashant Kishor rules out alliances after Bankipur win, says BJP voters backed him
Prashant Kishor won the Bankipur bypoll and ruled out joining any political alliance in Bihar. The result gives Jan Suraaj its first Assembly seat and sharpens pressure on the BJP-led government.
Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor on Monday ruled out joining any political alliance after his victory in the Bankipur Assembly bypoll in Bihar, saying his party's alliance would be with the people of the state.
Kishor defeated BJP's Neeraj Kumar by 18,953 votes in his electoral debut, winning 63,203 votes against Kumar's 44,250. The victory gives Jan Suraaj its first seat in the Bihar Assembly and ends the BJP's run in the constituency, which it had held since 1995.
"We shall have no alliance. Our alliance shall be with the people of Bihar. You should see that the people of Bankipur have voted for us, giving up on established parties," Kishor told reporters after the result.
Asked whether he would reconsider his earlier decision to contest elections without an alliance, Kishor said he would not.
'BJP, CONGRESS, RJD VOTERS BACKED US'
Kishor credited his victory to support from voters and workers who were unhappy with their respective parties, including the BJP, Congress and RJD.
"I would like to thank my active supporters as well as those who backed me in the by-election, despite not being with Jan Suraaj. I received support from people in BJP, Congress and RJD, who were unhappy with the state of affairs in their party," he said.
Kishor had described the Bankipur bypoll as a "referendum" on the BJP-led government in Bihar. He also suggested that the atmosphere created by recent Gen Z protests may have contributed to the result.
"The atmosphere created by Gen Z protests" might have played a role, he said, but added that there was little evidence of a large turnout among young voters in Bankipur.
"There is nothing to show that young electors had voted in large numbers in Bankipur. It is unfortunate, but that is the reality," Kishor said.
Turnout in the July 30 bypoll was below 35 per cent.
KISHOR CALLS RESULT A REJECTION OF SAMRAT CHOUDHARY
Kishor also claimed that the mandate was primarily against Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary.
He said the verdict was a mandate "against whom I have nothing personal, but who is detested by educated people of Bihar because of criminal antecedents and lack of qualifications".
Kishor called the result a wake-up call for Prime Minister Narendra Modi and said that if Choudhary's selection was linked to his Kushwaha caste, he should be replaced by someone from the same community with a "cleaner background".
Choudhary, who joined the BJP less than a decade ago and became the party's first leader to head a government in Bihar, congratulated Kishor in a post on X and described the contest as "the grand festival of democracy".
BJP LEADER BLAMES GROWING DISSATISFACTION
A senior BJP leader attributed the defeat to growing dissatisfaction among the party's traditional upper-caste support base.
"Prashant Kishor struck all the right notes. He tapped into the growing dissatisfaction among the upper castes by raising issues like the death after suspected rape of a NEET aspirant and the police encounter of Bharat Tiwari," the leader said on condition of anonymity.
The leader also said remarks by BJP figures had compounded the problem, referring to Patna Sahib MP Ravi Shankar Prasad's comment that Bankipur was a seat "we can win even if a dog or a cat was fielded as the BJP candidate".
"The Gen Z protests highlighted our weakening support among the youth, especially the upper castes, who have been our core base. They had been unhappy over the controversial UGC regulations and, now, they have begun to feel that we are taking them for granted," the BJP leader said.
OPPOSITION SEES BJP DEFEAT
Leaders of INDIA bloc parties stopped short of congratulating Kishor but described the result as a setback for the BJP.
CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya called it "an emphatic victory against the BJP" and said the result, coming against the backdrop of the Jantar Mantar protests, indicated "a welcome shift in public mood".
Congress spokesperson Suman Kumar Mallick said Bankipur voters had sent a message against "the arrogance of power and autocracy".
"If Parliamentary elections are held today, Modi government will definitely be voted out," he said.
RJD spokesperson Chitaranjan Gagan, whose party candidate Rekha Gupta finished third, said the key point was that the BJP had lost.
"We are not dejected and will work with renewed vigour to ensure the overthrow of the NDA from Bihar as well as the Centre," he said.
Veteran socialist leader Shivanand Tiwary, meanwhile, called on the INDIA bloc to approach Kishor.
"Prashant Kishor's energy and organisational abilities have been there for all to see. The INDIA bloc must approach him. The victory in Bankipur must be viewed in a larger perspective," Tiwary said.
Recalling the student protests, Tiwary said the recent demonstrations at Jantar Mantar, across Bihar and elsewhere were far bigger than the 1974 movement, adding that today's student activists were showing "far superior acumen" than in his time.
JAN SURAaj GETS FIRST ASSEMBLY SEAT
The Bankipur victory marks Jan Suraaj's first electoral success after the party drew a blank in last year's Bihar Assembly election.
Kishor, who gave up political consultancy in 2021, has now entered the Bihar Assembly as an elected representative and secured a victory over a BJP candidate in a constituency the party had held for three decades.
He said he would not make "tall promises" such as turning Bankipur into Bengaluru, but promised to work towards improving the constituency and said changes would be visible within a few months.
The bypoll was necessitated after fifth-term MLA Nitin Nabin resigned from Bankipur following his election to the Rajya Sabha after being elevated as the BJP's national president.
With Jan Suraaj opening its account in the Bihar Assembly, Kishor's first electoral victory has also set the stage for a new political force in the state, even as he maintains that the party will continue to contest without alliances.

headline: India approved just one Chinese FDI proposal worth ₹1 crore, while clearing 13 applications from Hong Kong worth ₹610.42 crore in the last financial year, according to official data.
full_text:
India approved just one Chinese FDI proposal worth ₹1 crore, while clearing 13 applications from Hong Kong worth ₹610.42 crore in the last financial year, according to official data.
These approvals are important as investments from countries sharing a land border with India have been subject to prior government approval since April 2020 under Press Note 3 of the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).
The measure was introduced to curb opportunistic takeovers and acquisitions of Indian companies during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Overall, the government has approved 63 FDI (foreign direct investment) proposals worth ₹10,292.67 crore, or $1.18 billion, during April 2025-March 2026, according to the DPIIT data.
Singapore emerged as the largest source of approved FDI proposals in value terms, with five proposals worth ₹3,259.88 crore ($382.52 million) receiving clearance.
This was followed by the UK, where five proposals worth ₹2,477.67 crore ($283 million) were approved, and Thailand, which received approval for two proposals worth ₹1,600 crore (about $180 million).
In March, the government eased Press Note 3 of April 2020. Under that, it stated that investors with non-controlling LBC (land border countries) beneficial ownership of up to 10% would be permitted under the automatic route, according to the applicable sectoral caps, entry routes, and other conditions.
However, it was clarified that the relaxed FDI norms will not apply to entities registered in China/Hong Kong or other countries sharing land borders with India.
Countries that share land borders with India are China, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Bhutan, Nepal, Myanmar, and Afghanistan.
India has never received significant investments directly from China. China ranks 23rd, accounting for only 0.32% of total FDI equity inflows into India between April 2000 and March 2026, at $2.51 billion (₹16,162.25 crore).
On the other hand, Hong Kong was at 15th position with only a 0.62% share ($4.91 billion or ₹31,220.30 crore) in the total FDI equity inflow reported during that period.
Like 2025-26, India had approved only one Chinese FDI proposal in 2024-25 also. It was valued at ₹28.71 crore ($3.44 million). In that fiscal, a total of 82 proposals were approved under the government route, involving a total investment of ₹39,758 crore ($4.72 billion).
From Hong Kong, 11 proposals worth ₹1,225.28 crore ($146.51 million) received approval in 2024-25.

'Bangladesh uprising that was taken over by Jihadis': What CJP protest reminded Taslima Nasreen of
Taslima Nasreen said she was concerned about such movements due to what happened in Bangladesh after the 2024 student protest.
Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen said on Sunday that while she did not follow the student protest at Jantar Mantar, a small clip of it reminded her of the 2024 student uprising in Bangladesh that led to the ouster of then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
She said that the 2024 Bangladesh protests “fooled” people because it looked like the students were protesting against the quota system, it was later found out that “jihadis (Islamic fundamentalists)” were behind it.
"It was like that. That student movement in Bangladesh fooled us. Because we thought the students wanted to abolish the quota system. Sheikh Hasina had also agreed to their demands, but ultimately the government fell. Later, we found that jihadis (Islamic fundamentalists) were behind that movement. The fallout has not been good for Bangladesh. Jihadis have taken over power there," Nasreen was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.

She added that she was concerned about such movements due to what happened in Bangladesh after the 2024 student protest.
‘Want Hasina to return to Bangladesh’
Nasreen also backed ousted former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who is in living in exile in India, and said that she was against the ban on her party Awami League back in their home country.
"No political party should be banned. The manner in which Awami League's Sheikh Hasina was forced to leave the country is questionable. It was not right to ban the Awami League. It was a move against democracy," she said.

“I want the ban to be lifted as soon as possible. The party should be allowed to participate in the elections, and I want Hasina to return to Bangladesh,” she added.
Awami League was banned in Bangladesh in 2025 by the country's interim government under anti-terrorism legislation. The author also said that workers of Hasina's party have faced violence in Bangladesh since then.

Nasreen herself was forced to leave Bangladesh in 1994 after she faced death threats from radical religious groups over her writings and religious views. She has been living in exile in India since 2004.
In 2007, she was forced to leave Kolkata as well due to violent protests over her writings.
On Friday, she came back to Kolkata after almost two decades of being forced out of the city. “I can’t believe that I am in Kolkata now. I was driven out in 2007. Initially I had thought that I will be able to return. Kolkata is a progressive city. But as years passed, I had a feeling that I may never be able to return. But then Osman Gani Mallik of Secular Mission invited me to Kolkata. He made all the arrangements,” she said after returning in an interview to a television channel.

Today, children from ordinary families are receiving facilities that are even better than those available in many private schools, he said.
The school at Kidwai Nagar has been completed at a cost of Rs 10.62 crore, while the school at Miller Ganj has been completed at a cost of Rs 3.48 crore."No freebie or concession cards can eliminate poverty or other social maladies in the state, but education is the key that can pull people out of this vicious cycle by raising their standard of living. Therefore, the government is tirelessly making efforts to improve the standard of education and empower the common people," Mann said.

headline: A day before the result of the recently held by-election to Madhya Pradesh’s Datia Assembly seat, the Congress suspended former MLA Rajendra Bharti — whose disqualification necessitated the bypoll — from the party’s primary membership.
full_text:
A day before the result of the recently held by-election to Madhya Pradesh’s Datia Assembly seat, the Congress suspended former MLA Rajendra Bharti — whose disqualification necessitated the bypoll — from the party’s primary membership.
The suspension comes days after the Congress candidate for the bypoll, Ghanshyam Singh, accused Mr. Bharti of trying to sabotage his campaign and colluding with the Bharatiya Janata Party. Mr. Bharti, however, alleged that Mr. Singh had been colluding with senior BJP leader and former State Home Minister Narottam Mishra, who was denied the ticket by the ruling party.
“With the approval of the president of the All India Congress Committee (AICC), Mallikarjun Kharge Ji, Rajendra Bharti, former MLA from Datia, is hereby suspended from the primary membership of the Indian National Congress with immediate effect,” Harish Chaudhary, Congress general secretary in-charge of Madhya Pradesh, said in a statement.
Bypoll to the Datia Assembly seat was held on July 30 and the votes will be counted on August 3. The constituency recorded a voting turnout of 71.44%, as per the Election Commission.
The bypoll was necessitated following the disqualification of Mr. Bharti in April due to his conviction in a bank fraud case.
The BJP fielded debutant Ashutosh Tiwari, after snubbing former State Home Minister Narottam Mishra who represented the seat for three consecutive terms until his defeat to Mr. Bharti in the 2023 Assembly polls. The Congress fielded Mr. Singh, a member of the erstwhile Datia royal family and former MLA from neighbouring Sewda Assembly seat.
Towards the end of campaigning days in Datia, Mr. Bharti and Mr. Singh levelled allegations against each other, including about receiving funding from BJP leaders. Mr. Singh also accused Mr. Bharti of not supporting his campaign in the bypoll.
Speaking to The Hindu, Mr. Bharti’s son Ankit Bharti said, “Ghanshyam Singh has been very close to Narottam Mishra for several years and has worked against Congress candidates in the past. Even for this election he has received funding from Narottam as he is also working against BJP because he did not get the ticket. But he [Mr. Singh] has alleged that my father has received funding from the BJP to support their candidate [Mr. Tiwari].”
Mr. Bharti and Mr. Mishra have been political rivals for more than a decade with the former ending the BJP leader’s three-term tenure as Datia MLA in the 2023 election.
A leader close to Mr. Bharti also said he “had a role” in the BJP’s decision to deny Mr. Mishra the ticket.

headline: The Lok Sabha on Monday (August 3, 2026) passed a Bill to increase the sanctioned strength of judges in the Supreme Court without any discussion as persistent protests by Opposition members over the police action against protesting students at Jantar...
full_text:
The Lok Sabha on Monday (August 3, 2026) passed a Bill to increase the sanctioned strength of judges in the Supreme Court without any discussion as persistent protests by Opposition members over the police action against protesting students at Jantar Mantar and the alleged chadhawa chori (theft of offerings) at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya continued to disrupt proceedings.
Two other legislations — the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026, and the Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026 — were introduced amid sloganeering in the afternoon.
Parliament Monsoon Session Day 11 highlights
The House was adjourned repeatedly during the day as Opposition members trooped into the Well raising slogans and displaying placards, forcing Speaker Om Birla to suspend proceedings first till noon, then till 2 p.m., before adjourning the House for the day following the passage of the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026.
At the Business Advisory Committee (BAC) meeting, sources told The Hindu that Congress deputy leader Gaurav Gogoi, Chief Whip Kodikunnil Suresh and Samajwadi Party MP Dharmendra Yadav demanded that Home Minister Amit Shah make a statement in the House on the police crackdown on protesters and that the government initiate a discussion on the alleged embezzlement of funds at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, during which Prime Minister Narendra Modi could intervene.
The BAC allotted three hours each for discussion on the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill and the Indian Statistical Institute Bill, and five hours for the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill. However, there was no discussion on taking up the proposed amendments to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA).
The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill replaces an ordinance promulgated earlier this year to raise the sanctioned strength of the apex court from 34 to 38 judges, including the Chief Justice of India. A statutory resolution moved by Opposition members seeking disapproval of the ordinance was rejected by voice vote.
Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal briefly introduced the Bill, but with protests continuing, it was passed by voice vote without debate. The government has argued that increasing the court’s strength is essential to address mounting pendency. As of January 1, the Supreme Court had 92,101 pending cases. The legislation says the additional judges would also enable the Chief Justice of India to constitute Constitution Benches more regularly. Five judges have already been appointed following the promulgation of the ordinance.
Amid the disruptions, the House also introduced the Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026, and the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026.
The Indian Statistical Institute Bill seeks to repeal the 1959 Act governing the institution and incorporate it as a statutory body corporate with the President as its Visitor and a Board of Governors as its principal executive body. It also provides for an Academic Council headed by the Director to strengthen governance, research and academic autonomy while expanding the institute’s role in statistics, data science and allied disciplines.
The Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, introduced by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, seeks to replace the colonial-era 1891 law by recognising electronic, digital, virtual and cloud-based banking records as admissible evidence in courts. It also provides for digital authentication of records and empowers the Centre to extend the law to other financial sector entities. Both Bills were introduced by voice vote after Opposition members who had submitted notices opposing their introduction did not press their objections.

Row over Udhayanidhi's 'double-meaning' remark on Trisha, TVK MLA says disgusting
A clip of the incident has since circulated widely on social media, with critics accusing the DMK leader of making an inappropriate, double-meaning reference to Trisha.
DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin has come under fire after a viral video from a Cauvery protest in Thanjavur showed him making a remark involving actor Trisha that critics described as a double entendre.
TVK MLA Rhevanth Charan condemned the comment as “disgusting” and unacceptable, accusing the DMK leadership of lowering political discourse and resorting to provocation.
Addressing a rally on the Cauvery issue, Udhayanidhi was interrupted by chants of "Trisha, Trisha" as he criticised Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay.
“Not even a drop of Cauvery water has been received. But has the Chief Minister opened his mouth about it? No. He is only concerned with filing “false cases” against the DMK,” Udhayanidhi was heard saying in a video that has gone viral.
As the chants continued, he paused, smiled and made a remark that many interpreted as an innuendo about actor Trisha, Vijay's co-star and close friend, amid longstanding social media speculation about their relationship.
“Whether the water reaches anywhere else or not, it should reach there,” before smiling and clarifying that he was referring to the Cauvery.
TVK MLA, BJP SLAM UDHAYANIDHI
Reacting to the viral video, Charan called the remark “absolutely disgusting” and said such comments against anyone were unacceptable. He alleged that the episode reflected the DMK’s political culture and declining standards.
Charan also claimed that the protest had failed to gain traction and accused the party of turning to “cheap provocation” to attract attention on social media.
He warned that continued “arrogance and indecency” would further erode the DMK’s public relevance.
"This is precisely why the people of Tamil Nadu rejected you and confined you to the position you are in today. Even by Arivalayam’s already abysmal standards, this is a new low," he said.
The Tamil Nadu unit of the BJP, too, criticised the Leader of Opposition over his remark, calling it “disgusting, obscene, vulgar and shameful."
State BJP spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy also criticised former CM MK Stalin for remaining silent and demanded Udhayanidhi’s arrest, saying legal action would enhance Chief Minister Vijay’s credibility.
TVK URGES WOMEN'S PANEL TO ACT
The ruling party has written to the National Commission for Women (NCW) seeking action against Udhayanidhi. Calling the remarks "deeply troubling," the TVK said the language "normalises the objectification and verbal harassment of women in public spaces," "severely degrades the decorum expected of public figures," and sets "a dangerous precedent" for the treatment of women in public life.
TVK urged the NCW to take formal cognisance of the speech and rally footage, issue a notice seeking an explanation and an unconditional public apology. It also called for the DMK leader to be booked for public obscenity and outraging the modesty of women.

headline: A seat for JSP's 'school bag': Why Prashant Kishor's Bankipur win is a warning for both BJP and RJD
full_text:
A seat for JSP's 'school bag': Why Prashant Kishor's Bankipur win is a warning for both BJP and RJD
Kunal Varma / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 04, 2026, 07:54 IST
