The Bombay High Court directed social media platforms to remove allegedly defamatory deepfakes linking Nitin Gadkari and family to E20.
NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Wednesday granted interim relief to Union minister Nitin Gadkari, directing social media intermediaries, including Meta, to take down defamatory deepfakes, AI-generated images and other posts linking him and his family to the government's E20 ethanol-blending programme. The court described the flagged material as âvile and abusiveâ.Granting interim relief, the Bombay High Court on Wednesday directed intermediaries, including Meta, to take down deepfakes, AI-generated images and other posts falsely linking Union Minister Nitin Gadkari and his family to the E20 fuel controversy, describing the content as "vile and abusive."
The order was passed by Justice Arif Doctor on Wednesday in Gadkari's suit against Meta Platforms, X, Google/YouTube, the Union ministry of electronics and information technology, the department of telecommunications and unidentified users.The court observed that the material cited by Gadkari was âabsolutely vileâ and abusive, and said such content should not be available on public platforms accessible to young people."One such transcript appears on instagram reel. There are other content. The material which plaintiff seeks to pull down, I can only say that the same is absolutely vile abusive. Such material should have no place on public platform, which is accessible to everyone including young," the court said in its interim order, as reported by Bar & Bench.
The court said Gadkari had made out a case for ad interim relief. Meta and Google, which appeared before the court, agreed to remove the material identified in Exhibit C of the plaint. âTheir statement is accepted,â the court said.The case concerns posts, reels and videos that Gadkari alleged contained manipulated images and videos, including AI-generated âdefamatory contentâ and âdeep fake contentâ. The material allegedly attributed personal responsibility to the Union minister for the E20 programme and suggested that he and his family had derived âundue pecuniary benefitsâ from ethanol blending.According to the plea, some posts referred to Gadkari's son, Nikhil Gadkari, and his association with CIAN Agro Industries & Infrastructure Limited, which is involved in manufacturing ethanol and other products. The allegations sought to link that association to purported financial benefits from the E20 programme.
Gadkari has denied the allegations.The suit also referred to social media content blaming the minister for introducing or mandating E20 petrol and alleging that ethanol-blended fuel had caused damage to vehicles. Gadkari argued that the posts insinuated corruption, conflict of interest and abuse of office.The court's interim directions apply to the material identified in the proceedings, rather than constituting a blanket finding on all online criticism of the minister.The matter will come up for further hearing after four weeks, when the court is expected to consider the case further.

headline: ‘Posts against Nitin Gadkari vile, defamatory. Take them down’: Bombay HC amid E20 row
full_text:
‘Posts against Nitin Gadkari vile, defamatory. Take them down’: Bombay HC amid E20 row
The high court also asked the platforms to come up with a framework to take down such content without court intervention every time.
The Bombay high court on Wednesday directed Meta, X, Google and other social media platforms to take down defamatory posts and AI-generated deepfake videos allegedly targetting Union minister Nitin Gadkari and his family members over the ethanol-blended petrol (EBP) programme.
The high court also asked the platforms to come up with a framework to take down such content without court intervention every time.
A single-judge bench of Justice Arif Doctor said the content against Gadkari was “vile” and “abusive”. “The material which the plaintiff seeks to pull down, I can only say that the same is absolutely vile and abusive. Such material should have no place on a public platform, which is accessible to everyone, including young," he said.
Justice Doctor said if any further abusive material or deepfakes are found, the same shall be communicated to the defendant. “In the event there is a grey area, they will have liberty to move court,” the bench said and posted the matter after four weeks for further hearing.
Gadkari moves Bombay HC
Gadkari had approached the court over the posts that claimed he and his family financially benefited from the EBP programme. In his petition, filed through advocate Sandeep S Ladda, the Union minister said the social media posts falsely suggested that he and his family received undue financial benefits from the programme, “insinuating corruption, nepotism, conflict of interest, abuse of official position, misuse of governmental authority and other acts of impropriety.”
Gadkari argued that the content is ex facie false, fabricated, baseless, malicious, misleading, unsubstantiated and devoid of any factual foundation. “It contains abusive and derogatory language, scandalous remarks, false accusations and manipulated audio-visual material intended to falsely attribute statements and conduct to the plaintiff,” he said. The plea added that the defamatory content consists of profane, vulgar and abusive language directed at him and sought ₹11 crore in damages.

The developments come amid growing backlash over the EBP, introduced to reduce crude oil imports. The programme has been accelerated since 2021, with ethanol produced from sugarcane, rice and maize being blended with petrol. India achieved its target of 20% ethanol blending (E20) five years ahead of its original 2030 deadline.
Motorists have complained that E20 fuel is reducing mileage and causing engine corrosion in older and non-compliant vehicles. Gadkari and the government have rejected such claims, dismissing them as social media misinformation.
Gadkari approached the high court after Bharatiya Janata Party’s Nagpur social media cell convener, Shishir Arun Tripathi, lodged a police complaint last month over videos and posts circulating “baseless and objectionable claims” about the Union minister and E20 fuel that could “mislead the public, confuse citizens and disturb peace”.

headline: New Delhi: With the Congress slamming the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) almost on a daily basis, the possibility of its senior leader Shashi Tharoor sharing a stage with the Hindu organisation’s chief Mohan Bhagwat at an event in Mumbai was bound...
full_text:
New Delhi: With the Congress slamming the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) almost on a daily basis, the possibility of its senior leader Shashi Tharoor sharing a stage with the Hindu organisation’s chief Mohan Bhagwat at an event in Mumbai was bound to raise eyebrows. But Tharoor has now put that speculation to rest, clarifying that while both he and Bhagwat will be attending events organised by the International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN), there will be no shared stage.
The clarification comes after questions were raised across social media over Tharoor’s participation in the event by IIMUN, a youth organisation that conducts leadership and civic engagement programmes for students. The speculation gathered significant traction, given the Congress’s long-standing differences with the RSS, and because Tharoor has, at times, differed from the party’s official stand. Responding to the criticism, Tharoor also made it clear that the event was not being organised by the RSS, and that Bhagwat’s and his presence is on separate days.
“It is not RSS-led. It’s a student movement that invites educationists and thought leaders of all backgrounds to address students. I believe in freedom of expression and will chair their Board meeting and events on 7th & 8th. Mr Bhagwat will meet them on 6th when I am in Delhi for Parliament,” Tharoor wrote on X.
Bhagwat is scheduled to interact with young participants on 6 August at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC) in Mumbai. The event marks the 15th anniversary of IIMUN and the opening of its annual Championship Conference, news agency ANI reported.
Bhagwat’s participation has also drawn political criticism from Opposition parties. Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray ) leader Aaditya Thackeray took a swipe at those seeking to engage with Gen Z and Gen Alpha, questioning where they were when young protesters were facing police action.
“Suddenly everyone who wants to interact with Gen Z and Gen Alpha, and some who have taken it on themselves to preach ‘culture’ to them via social media, the simple question to all of them is… Where were you when they were facing AK-47s, lathis with rusted nails, electric shock guns and electric barricades, tear gas and when women were manhandled in the name of ‘law and order’?” Thackeray said on X.
He also questioned why they had not stepped in when young people were detained while leaving for peaceful protests or arrested.
This will not, however, be Bhagwat’s first interaction with young people through the organisation. He was among the participants in leadership development sessions hosted at the IIMUN headquarters in June.
More than 2,000 students between the ages of 15 and 19, representing schools and colleges from over 100 cities across the country, are expected to attend the gathering. Bhagwat’s interaction will centre on the theme, ‘The Role of Youth in Uniting the World, the Indian Way’.
The four-day conference, being held from 6 -9 August, is aimed at bringing young participants, including members of Gen Z and Gen Alpha, into direct conversations with senior figures from different fields.
IIMUN founder Rishabh Shah said the interaction comes at an important time and stressed the need for senior leaders to listen to younger voices. “Leadership is not only about guiding the next generation, but also listening to it. At this critical juncture in India’s journey, we need this dialogue more than ever before,” Shah said.
“I am grateful to Shri Mohan Bhagwat ji for accepting our invite to address this gathering at this critical juncture,” he added as per the press release reported by ANI.
Founded by Shah in 2011, IIMUN describes itself as a public affairs platform aimed at preparing young people for leadership. The organisation says its programmes now span 275 cities across India and 40 countries.
Tharoor himself has a longstanding association with IIMUN and is a member of its advisory board, which includes former Chief Justice of India D.Y. Chandrachud, industrialists Ajay Piramal, Deepak Parekh and Nadir Godrej, filmmaker Karan Johar and athlete P.T. Usha, among others.
While the presence of both Tharoor and Bhagwat at IIMUN, events had sparked speculation, their schedules will not overlap as per plan. Bhagwat will interact with the students on 6 August, when Tharoor says he will be in Delhi for Parliament. The Congress leader will chair IIMUN’s board meeting and attend its events on 7 and 8 August.
(Edited by Nardeep Singh Dahiya)

NEW DELHI: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju on Wednesday met Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi in an effort to end the continuing deadlock in Parliament, as disruptions in the Monsoon Session forced another adjournment of the Lok Sabha.According to PTI sources, Rijiju held a nearly 50-minute meeting with Rahul Gandhi in the latter's Parliament office. Senior Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also attended the meeting, which focused on the ongoing impasse in Parliament and the proposed Delimitation Bill.
According to ANI sources, Rijiju sought to know the opposition's stand on the Delimitation Bill during the discussions.There is no move at present to introduce either the Delimitation Bill or the Women's Reservation Amendment Bill in a special Parliament session after Independence Day, government sources told PTI. They added that Union home minister Amit Shah will speak on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026.The meeting came after the Lok Sabha was adjourned till 2 pm as Opposition members continued sloganeering over several issues, including the alleged police action against students during the July 20 protest at Jantar Mantar. The Opposition has also been demanding statements from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah in Parliament.
Since the Monsoon Session began on July 20, the Lok Sabha has not completed a single Question Hour. Five Bills have been passed without discussion amid repeated disruptions.As soon as the House assembled on Wednesday, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla urged members to return to their seats and allow Question Hour to proceed."Sloganeering, whether inside or outside the House, is not good for democracy. By showing placards and sloganeering you are lowering the dignity of the House," Birla told Opposition members.He added that several MPs had expressed concern that important questions could not be taken up because of repeated disruptions.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosted a breakfast meeting with 37 BJP MPs at his residence as part of his interactions with parliamentarians during the Monsoon Session. According to ANI sources, the Prime Minister shared personal experiences and held informal discussions with the MPs.
Earlier in the day, Opposition MPs, including Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, marched from the Gandhi statue at Prerna Sthal to Makar Dwar in Parliament, protesting against Union home minister Amit Shah over the alleged police action against CJP protesters on July 20, the alleged Ayodhya Ram Mandir donation embezzlement and other issues.

headline: Mumbai: In what comes as a major relief for Union Road Transport & Highways Minister and senior BJP leader Nitin Gadkari, the Bombay High Court on Wednesday directed the social media platforms Meta, X Corp and Google LLC to take down defamatory posts...
full_text: Mumbai: In what comes as a major relief for Union Road Transport & Highways Minister and senior BJP leader Nitin Gadkari, the Bombay High Court on Wednesday directed the social media platforms Meta, X Corp and Google LLC to take down defamatory posts vis-a-vis the circulation of alleged defamatory and AI-generated deepfake content about him on the Internet related to E20 ethanol-blended petrol. "These posts, on the face of it, are abusive, vile, and obscene. Such material should have no place on a public platform, which is accessible to everyone, including the younger generation,” observed Justice Arif Doctor.Several social media posts have appeared against Gadkari on Meta platforms Facebook and Instagram, microblogging site X and Google in the recent past over the issue of E20 ethanol-blended petrol, which the government is pushing.Justice Doctor also questioned the online platforms on whether they had any mechanism to take down such posts without the person having to approach the court. “The platforms ought to take down such posts voluntarily,” the court said..Bombay High Court allows Nitin Gadkari to sue over deepfake, defamatory content.Besides, the court noted that if similar posts are uploaded in the future, Gadkari can approach the platforms directly, which should then act promptly.The High Court order came in relation to a civil suit filed by Gadkari against alleged defamatory and AI-generated deepfake content about him on the Internet related to E20 ethanol-blended petrol.Gadkari was represented by advocate Sandeep Ladda.Gadkari had clarified that the ethanol-blending programme and the E20 policy are administered by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, and not by him personally.It may be recalled that last week, Justice Abhay Ahuja had allowed Gadkari's plea seeking leave under Clause XII of the Letters Patent, a procedural requirement that enables the High Court to entertain a civil suit despite issues of territorial jurisdiction.According to him, the defamatory and deepfake content had been made publicly accessible by the defendants, including to users in Mumbai, and hence it gives territorial jurisdiction to the Bombay High Court to hear the matter.Ladda pointed out that social media platforms are being misused to damage reputations, while there is no adequate system in place to prevent such misuse.

Narottam Mishra skips BJP meet held to discuss Datia assembly bypoll defeat
A two-member committee is expected to be formulated to examine the reasons of BJP's defeat in the assembly bypoll.
Senior Madhya Pradesh BJP leader and former home minister Narottam Mishra skipped a BJP review meeting on Tuesday convened to analyse the party’s defeat in the Datia assembly bypoll, triggering speculation over his role in the electoral setback and his standing within the party.
The meeting, said people aware of the matter, was held at CM Mohan Yadav’s residence in Bhopal a day after Congress candidate Ghanshyam Singh defeated BJP’s Ashutosh Tiwari by 6,016 votes in the bypoll.
Mishra’s absence drew attention as he was in Bhopal when the meeting took place. The BJP had made the Datia contest a prestige battle, deploying at least 12 ministers, including a deputy CM, six MPs and several senior leaders during the campaign.

NEW DELHI: Centre Tuesday told Supreme Court that while the proposal to shift NEET from pen-and-paper mode to computer-based mode is under consideration, the final decision will be taken only after getting the report of the Nandan Nilekani-led high-powered task force set up to overhaul India's public examination systems.
In an affidavit, govt briefed SC on measures taken to make the exam foolproof, including stringent penal provisions against use of unfair means and setting up of task force. It was responding to a plea by All India Medical Association seeking a more secure NEET following this year's paper leak.
Govt said: "Migration from pen-and-paper mode to a computer-based mode, whether in single-stage or two-stage exam on the pattern of JEE, is presently under consideration by all stakeholders." The final approach, it added, would be adopted after considering the task force's recommendations.
It said NTA has migrated seven of its eight major exams to computer-based testing. NEET (UG) remains its only major pen-and-paper exam.

headline: India has firmly denied any role in Sheikh Hasina's forthcoming media address, while Dhaka expresses skepticism, worried that the address may jeopardize diplomatic ties. Meanwhile, Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has received an invitation...
full_text:
India has firmly denied any role in Sheikh Hasina's forthcoming media address, while Dhaka expresses skepticism, worried that the address may jeopardize diplomatic ties. Meanwhile, Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has received an invitation to the Brics summit from India, but he may encounter domestic backlash concerning the extradition of Hasina. To date, Bangladesh has not officially responded to the Brics invitation.
Ahead of former Bangladeshi PM Sheikh Hasinaâs media address, the Indian govt sought to distance itself from the event and said New Delhi doesnât endorse any views that may be expressed at the event. However, Dhaka, which had raised the issue with Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi on Monday, remains unconvinced as diplomatic sources said allowing Hasina to make a political speech might rock an already unsteady relationship.Hasina, who has announced she plans to return to Bangladesh in Dec despite the death sentence awarded to her, is scheduled to virtually address a media event at the Foreign Correspondentsâ Club on Wednesday evening.The ministry of external affairs said the interaction was being organised by a private media entity. âGovt has no involvement whatsoever in it. Neither does it endorse any views that may be expressed at the forum,â spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said. The ministry recently told a parliamentary committee that while providing refuge to Hasina, India had strictly adhered to the principle that no political activity was directed against any other country from Indian soil.
The Indian government also confirmed that Bangladeshi PM Tarique Rahman had been invited by India for the Brics summit that it will host in Sept. While PM Narendra Modi had earlier invited Rahman to India for a bilateral visit, govt said the invitation on this occasion was for a Brics outreach session and in Rahmanâs capacity as the current chair of Bimstec.While Bangladesh aspires for Brics membership and has already received support from Russia and China for its candidature, Rahman will likely be wary of any domestic fallout of travelling to India amid the unresolved Hasina extradition issue. Jamaat-e-Islamiâs ascendancy as the primary opposition party may also restrict Rahman from soft-pedalling the Hasina issue. Dhaka has not yet formally accepted or declined the invitation that was extended by Modi to Rahman for Brics.

headline: Former J&K Chief Minister and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) evening held protest in Srinagar on the eve of seventh anniversary of abrogation of Article 370 and said the way the BJP looted the Ram ...
full_text:
Former J&K Chief Minister and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) evening held protest in Srinagar on the eve of seventh anniversary of abrogation of Article 370 and said the way the BJP looted the Ram Temple, is the same way it looted the special status from people of J&K.
Terming August 4 as “the darkest night in J&K’s history”, Ms. Mufti said, “Neither Pakistan nor China granted Article 370 and 35A to J&K but it was the Indian Constitution. However, the BJP used the brute majority to snatch Article 370 from J&K. We are an alive nation and will keep fighting for it,” said Ms. Mufti.
She said Ambedkar’s constitution was first diluted for J&K but people of the country stayed silent. “However, people are getting to know how the BJP was treating the Constitution,” she said.
Carrying the Indian flag on one hand and erstwhile J&K State’s separate flag in another hand, Ms. Mufti said, “Article 370 provided a protection of J&K’s land. identity and jobs.”
She also demanded the release of youths of J&K from the jails in and outside the Union Territory. “People are dying on both sides of Kashmir. In Muzaffarabad and Rawalakot, Kashmiris are dying. We saw a police constable killed recently on this side of Kashmir. It was followed by hundreds of arrests of locals. Houses were also demolished. A house, where the militant is not living anymore, was also demolished. Our two labourers were also killed,” said Ms. Mufti.
Meanwhile, the PDP alleged that Ms. Mufti’s daughter Iltija Mufti was “heckled by the police” during a protest in Srinagar. Later, PDP supporters also raised slogans, demanding return of Article 370 and 35A.

J&Kâs governing NC said it would hold peaceful protests to demand the restoration of statehood while PDP said its demonstrations would seek the restoration of Article 370 and the release of political prisoners.
âOn this day, I would just say they (Centre) should fulfil their promise. They promised the people of J&K and the entire country that statehood would be restored after elections and delimitation. Both have been done,â NC chief Farooq Abdullah said.
BJP spokesperson Sajid Yousuf Shah said the party would take out a Tiranga rally from Lal Chowk, adding the abrogation of Article 370 had changed the mood in J&K.

headline: Madhya Pradesh air ambulances, launched in 2024, served 159 people, 32 had BJP links
full_text:
Madhya Pradesh air ambulances, launched in 2024, served 159 people, 32 had BJP links
Only 13 have paid for the service -- those without an Ayushman card and being flown to a hospital outside the state have to pay for it according to the scheme.
Madhya Pradesh’s PM (Prime Minister) Shri Air Ambulance Service launched in May 2024 has benefited 159 patients; 32 of them are either leaders of the Bharatiya Janata Party or their friends or relatives.
Of the 159, only 13 have paid for the service -- those without an Ayushman card and being flown to a hospital outside the state have to pay for it according to the contours of the scheme -- including a BJP leader and his relatives/friends.
The scheme comes under the health department and health minister Rajendra Shukla said people haven’t paid for the service because the government sometimes pays on humanitarian grounds.
What air ambulance operator said
The service is provided by Flyola, a private company that offers on-demand custom flight solutions. It handles operations via a 24-hour non-scheduled facility at the Bhopal Airport State Hangar.
Also read: ‘Resignations part of politics’: Karnataka CM Shivakumar on MLAs’ threats over cabinet expansion
The company’s director corporate affairs, Monika Tiwari, said, “ We own 22 aircraft, and two of them -- a helicopter and a six-seater plane -- are reserved for air ambulance services. We get approval from the health department, which checks whether the beneficiary is an Ayushman cardholder or not. We airlift non-Ayushman cardholders only upon reference from the CM’s office or as special cases involving accidents. We are trying to save lives. Until May, we were getting approvals offline, but now we are getting them online. We are providing quick service to every patient.”
₹36 crore spent on air ambulance in 2 years
In all, the state has spent ₹36 crore on the service till July 7, according to commissioner of the health department S Dhanraju.
HT has reviewed documents on the scheme and spoken to 119 of the 159 beneficiaries.
At least 44% of the beneficiaries (70) were from the Rewa division — Rewa, Sidhi, Singrauli, Mauganj, Satna and Maihar districts — the home turf of health minister Rajendra Shukla. “I am proud that most of the beneficiaries are from my region,” he said.
The 13 who paid for the service include BJP leader Ram Sajjan Shukla and businessmen from Indore, Bhopal, Ujjain, Rewa and Jabalpur; all paid ₹5-10 lakh each.
Also read: Complaint against Noida teen who ‘abused’ PM Modi at NEET protest dropped
Contours of the air ambulance scheme
Individuals affected by road accidents, industrial mishaps, or natural disasters can be flown to government or private hospitals within and outside the state for free, according to the scheme.
“Ayushman card holders are eligible for free transportation to government and Ayushman-affiliated hospitals, regardless of the location. For those who do not possess an Ayushman card, the service provides free transport to government hospitals only within the state, while transport to medical facilities outside the state is available at contracted rates,” read the service guidelines.
The service requires a recommendation of the district’s chief medical health officer. The contracted rate is ₹2.35 lakh per hour for a helicopter and ₹3.90 lakh per hour for a six-seater air ambulance. Of the 119 beneficiaries, 95 were airlifted within the state; 55 were taken to government hospitals — eight to the state government hospital and 47 to AIIMS Bhopal — and 40 were shifted to private hospitals.
‘No one asked for money’
Of the 64 people flown to other states, 31 were non-Ayushman card-holders, and 11 did not respond on whether they have Ayushman cards. Of the 31, only seven paid for the service, while seven other are special accident cases. Beneficiaries, who were flown outside the state and were required to pay, said nobody asked them for money.
Former minister and MLA Gaurishankar Bisen said, “I felt pain in my chest so I was airlifted to Medanta hospital in Gurugram. No money was demanded from me, so I didn’t pay anything.” The BJP MLA from Garoth Chandan Singh said. “My son was ill and the government made arrangements for an airlifting him to Ahmedabad. No one asked for any money.”
Suneet Makin, son of petrol pump owner and businessman Rakendra Kumar Makin from Satna, gave the same reason for not paying. “My father was admitted to a hospital in Rewa. Health minister Shukla helped us in airlifting him to Delhi for a problem in the heart valve,” he said.
Ghanshyam Tripathi, whose friend was flown to a private hospital in Bhopal from Rewa, said, “The service was provided free of cost on the recommendation of chief minister (Mohan Yadav) as I am his guru (teacher).”
HT found three individuals — businessman Madhu Wadhwani of Rewa, Umesh Gupta from Rewa, and former MP Ram Vilas Das Vedanti — were never airlifted but the company was paid for the trips. Health minister Shukla explained the company charges a fixed amount and once it is booked, the charges are applicable whether the service is used or not.
Wadhwani and Vedanti’s families said they died before being airlifted, while Gupta’s family refused transfer after seeing the condition of the plane, the family said. Tripathi also complained of the plane’s poor condition. “The oxygen cylinder was unlocked (when it was not in use) and most of the equipment was rusted. Nobody was ready to travel with him but I mustered courage and travelled to a private hospital in Bhopal,” he added.
Shukla agreed that the air ambulance fleet do not comprise new planes but added they have all the facilities. “Their engines are in good condition. It (the service) is serving the purpose effectively.”
To be sure, there are Ayushman card holders who have benefited from the scheme.
A resident of Rewa, Ramvati Gupta was airlifted twice, first from Rewa to Bhopal and then Bhopal to Delhi, said, “This service gave me a second life. I can’t thank the government in words for providing air ambulances.”
A resident of Chhatarpur, 49-year-old Meena Sahu, suffering from acute pancreatitis, was airlifted in the presence of BJP MLA Lalita Yadav. Her son Sumit Sahu said, “I never thought that my mother would be airlifted for treatment. I contacted BJP MLA Yadav and she helped without any delay.”
In at least three cases, the Air Ambulance Service was used for organ donation. In the first case, the heart and liver of Baliram Kushwaha were transported to Bhopal and Indore from Jabalpur; in another instance, Satendra Singh’s heart was transported from Indore to Bhopal.
When asked why many of the beneficiaries were BJP leaders or their relatives, Shukla said some people might have used it under the CM’s special discretionary fund. “In many cases, ministers, MLAs and former ministers got special funds from the CM’s Swekchanudan,” he said. CM’s Swekchanudan is a special fund used by the CM to provide quick financial grant for medical emergencies and natural disasters.
Shukla said some business persons have also benefited. He added that local public representatives provided this service on humanitarian grounds to small business owners and other non-Ayushman card holders. “Later, all these cases get Cabinet’s approval. Many have paid for the service too.”

I have closely tracked three assembly elections, three Lok Sabha elections, leadership transitions in MP while exposing governance lapses, tender irregularities, and flawed policy rollouts. headline: Resignation a part of politics: DKS over legislators’ threats
full_text:
Resignation a part of politics: DKS over legislators’ threats
Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Tuesday issued a stern warning to disgruntled Congress legislators threatening to resign after being overlooked in the cabinet expansion, saying if they resign, it will be accepted “within a few minutes
Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Tuesday issued a stern warning to disgruntled Congress legislators threatening to resign after being overlooked in the cabinet expansion, saying if they resign, it will be accepted “within a few minutes.”
The remarks came a day after some Congress MLAs expressed displeasure and offered to resign after missing out on a ministerial berth following the long-awaited cabinet expansion that saw 19 ministers getting inducted. Notable among the disgruntled legislators were Indi MLA Yashvantharayagouda V Patil, who submitted his resignation from the assembly, and Belur Gopalakrishna, who also offered to step down after being overlooked.
“Resignations are a part of politics. No one can stop those who want to resign. If they want the party and a political future, they should stay. If there is a party, everything else follows,” Shivakumar told reporters in Bengaluru. “When I was denied a ministerial berth during the tenures of Dharam Singh and Siddaramaiah, I could have resigned too. Didn’t G Parameshwara (deputy CM) and I remain patient?... One needs to have patience.”
Asserting that the party is more important, Shivakumar said, “If anyone gives resignation, within a few minutes I’m going to accept.”
Urging the disgruntled legislators to be patient and wait for their opportunity, the chief minister said posts in state-run boards and corporations will be filled up soon.
“Those party men and legislators who were earlier appointed as members and heads of boards and corporations were told that their tenure will be for 2.5 years. It is already delayed. I will first ask our workers to resign from the posts and fill up those posts afresh, then I will speak to MLAs one by one,” he added.
Shivakumar was sworn-in as the chief minister along with 13 ministers on June 3, following Siddaramaiah’s resignation as CM on May 28. The sanctioned strength of Karnataka’s council of ministers is 34, including the CM. After the Monday’s expansion, the cabinet now has one vacant berth.
Shivakumar also dismissed any internal rift in the party after Siddaramaiah’s absence from the swearing-in ceremony on Monday. Some party insiders claimed that the former CM was unhappy with the party high command ignoring several of his recommendations while finalising the cabinet expansion.
“There is a feeling among his (Siddaramaiah’s) supporters that his views were not given the weight they deserved. That is what is being discussed inside the party,” a senior party leader said, declining to be named.
Shivakumar, however, said Siddaramaiah was not dissatisfied with the cabinet exercise.
Meanwhile, the BJP continued to attack the ruling Congress over the cabinet composition and absence of women in the council of ministers.
“Priyanka Gandhi Vadra delivered long speeches under the slogan ‘Main Ladki Hoon, Main Lad Sakti Hoon’. But where are the women in your own Congress Cabinet?” senior BJP leader and member of the legislative council CT Ravi said, alleging the Congress failed to match its rhetoric on women’s representation.
- ABOUT THE AUTHORArun DevArun Dev is an Assistant Editor with the Karnataka bureau of Hindustan Times. A journalist for over 10 years, he has written extensively on crime and politics.

headline: Nitish Kumar meets PM Modi after big BJP upset in Bihar's Bankipur bypoll
full_text:
Nitish Kumar meets PM Modi after big BJP upset in Bihar's Bankipur bypoll
The JD(U) is a key ally of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance and the two parties run a coalition government in Bihar.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday met former Bihar chief minister and JD(U) president Nitish Kumar, a day after the BJP failed to retain its stronghold of Bankipur in the bypoll, the first election after Kumar stepped down as CM. The seat earlier held by BJP’s national president Nitin Nabin has been wrested by Jan Suraaj Party’s Prashant Kishor.
According to people aware of the details, the agenda for the first meeting between the PM and Kumar, after he became a Rajya Sabha MP, was largely confined to “Bihar’s development, the roadmap for the future of the state and the alliance.”
The JD(U) is a key ally of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance and the two parties run a coalition government in Bihar.
“The meeting was about issues related to the development of Bihar. The former CM discussed some issues that needed attention and sought support for the state…it was largely about development and infrastructure enhancement,” said a person privy to the meeting of the two leaders.
Also Read | Paper leaks, caste factors: What led to BJP loss in Bankipur and Datia?
The person quoted above said “some political issues” were discussed but declined to comment on whether the bypoll results were specifically addressed by the two leaders.
While the PM’s office put out a photograph of the meeting, Kumar who was accompanied by JD(U) working president and MP Sanjay Jha and Union minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh in a post on ‘X’ said, “Today, I had the courtesy of a meeting with the Honourable Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji in his office chamber at Parliament House...”
Post the meeting, a BJP leader responding to a question on the implications of the bypoll for the alliance said, “Both the BJP and the JD(U) will assess the result of the bypoll although the Jan Suraaj winning the seat has more grave implications for the Rashtriya Janata Dal whose candidate (Rekha Kumari) forfeited her security deposit (for failing to win at least one-sixth of the total votes polled)...”
While the BJP on Monday attributed the loss to a raft of issues, the JD(U) for its part has been largely silent.
On Tuesday, a JD(U) leader said the emergence of a new outfit in Bihar’s polity dominated by caste will ring an alarm for the established parties particularly the BJP, which banks on a wider coalition of castes and does not have a stronghold in terms of electorate. He said the party will also have to “consider the acceptability” of CM Samrat Choudhary among the electorate and its own votebank.

headline: Supreme Court urged prompt action against cyber fraudsters, while noting a reduction in incidents. Authorities were directed to expedite decisions on a 'kill switch' for phones. Monies transferred to mule accounts will be placed on hold by banks. Vic...
full_text:
Supreme Court urged prompt action against cyber fraudsters, while noting a reduction in incidents. Authorities were directed to expedite decisions on a 'kill switch' for phones. Monies transferred to mule accounts will be placed on hold by banks. Victims will receive recovered amounts expeditiously after investigations conclude. New directives aim to enhance cyber crime grievance redressal mechanisms.
NEW DELHI: Despite 75% reduction in cyber-crime and digital arrest incidents, Supreme Court continued to push authorities for prompt action against cyber fraudsters by issuing a slew of directives Tuesday, including an expeditious decision on a 'kill switch' in phones to prevent these crimes and placing on hold monies transferred to mule accounts.Attorney general R Venkataramani told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that number of complaints on national cyber crime portal had gone down from 1,23,672 in 2024 to 16,377 in 2026 (as of June 30). Besides, an Rs 18 crore has been restored to around 36,000 cyber fraud victims, he said in a status report.While appreciating the progress made in the matter, which the court is monitoring after taking suo motu cognisance on Oct 16 last year, bench directed Reserve Bank of India to formally "adopt and circulate formal standard operating procedure within four weeks detailing the action to be taken by banks for placing temporary hold on amounts and accounts in mule accounts linked to cyber fraud".Accepting a suggestion of amicus curiae N S Nappinai, SC also directed states, UTs and law enforcing agencies to take steps for expeditious adoption and operationalisation of grievance redressal and money restoration modules of home ministry, which should be given adequate publicity to enable victims to take required remedial measures.CJI-led bench directed "all adjudicatory authorities, including RBI ombudsman, consumer fora, courts and law enforcing authorities - to ensure that amounts recovered from fraudsters are disbursed to victims of digital arrest expeditiously".
It asked RBI to file a status report on this aspect by Sept 16, the next date of hearing.Even as CBI continues investigations into digital scams, the court asked agency to examine AG's suggestion for lowering the present threshold of Rs 10 crore for taking up investigations into cases where the same gang of scamsters are involved.
"The proposal concerning a time-based 'Kill switch' for audio and video calls may be examined by ministry of information and technology, Department of Telecom and Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) in consultation with telecom intermediaries and a brief note on technical feasibility, efficacy, safeguards and alternatives be placed on record," the bench said.It asked Inter-Departmental Committee (IDC), which coordinates with various departments for steps to prevent digital arrest and cyber crime offences, to issue necessary directives on setting up of cyber crime grievance redressal mechanism and restoration of defrauded amounts to victims.

headline: Supreme Court tightens rules to curb 'digital arrests', RBI to frame SOPs to deal with mule bank accounts
full_text:
Supreme Court tightens rules to curb 'digital arrests', RBI to frame SOPs to deal with mule bank accounts
The RBI has been asked to prepare a comprehensive SOP for dealing with bank accounts opened or used to receive and transfer proceeds of cyber fraud.
The Supreme Court on Tuesday stepped up its oversight of the country’s battle against the growing menace of “digital arrest” scams, issuing a fresh set of nationwide directions aimed at plugging systemic gaps in cyber fraud investigations, speeding up the restoration of victims’ money and strengthening preventive mechanisms. Among its key directions, the court asked the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to frame within four weeks a standard operating procedure (SOP) for dealing with mule bank accounts used to launder proceeds of cyber fraud, directed all states to operationalise cyber fraud grievance redressal and money restoration systems, called for the adoption of the e-Zero FIR mechanism across the country, and asked the Centre to examine a shared liability and victim compensation framework for victims of digital arrest scams.
The directions were passed by a bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant hearing a suo motu case initiated to monitor the country’s response to digital arrest frauds, where fraudsters impersonate police officers, CBI officials, judges or other government functionaries to extort money from victims through prolonged video calls and psychological intimidation.
The bench, also comprising justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, was considering the fourth status report submitted by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the Union home ministry, along with notes filed by Attorney General R Venkataramani and senior advocate NS Nappinai, the amicus curiae assisting the court.
ALSO READ | Supreme Court proposes no fuel for uninsured vehicles, seeks Centre's plan
Vigilance remains essential: SC
While noting that the government’s coordinated efforts have led to a significant decline in reported cases, the bench emphasised that sustained vigilance remained essential and that institutional mechanisms had to be further strengthened. “The trend is certainly encouraging…but continued monitoring remains indispensable,” observed the bench while referring to the decline in complaints.
According to the status report, complaints relating to digital arrest scams on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal have fallen from 123,672 in 2024 to 58,249 in 2025 and further to 16,377 till June 30 this year. The reported amount lost to such frauds has also reduced substantially.
Venkataramani told the court that the law enforcement response had also improved considerably. Over 36,000 cases have been investigated, while more than ₹18 crore has been restored to victims through the government’s money restoration mechanism. High-value digital arrest cases continue to be investigated by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), while other complaints are handled by state police forces.
A ‘kill switch’
At the same time, the court took note of submissions made by Nappinai that digital arrest frauds continue to evolve despite the fall in numbers. She suggested that the government examine a technological “kill switch” under which messaging platforms such as WhatsApp could automatically terminate unusually long video calls or display warning pop-ups to users where calls continue for six to twelve hours, a common feature in digital arrest scams.
Accepting that the proposal deserved examination, the bench directed the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and I4C, in consultation with intermediaries, to study the technical feasibility, safeguards, possible alternatives and use cases of imposing time-based restrictions on audio and video calls, and place a report before the court.
RBI asked to prepare SOPs within four weeks
One of the most significant directions issued on Monday concerned RBI. The central bank has been asked to prepare and circulate, within four weeks, a comprehensive SOP for dealing with mule accounts –– bank accounts opened or used to receive and transfer proceeds of cyber fraud and money laundering. The SOP will also be circulated to the registrar generals of all high courts.
The court also directed all states, Union territories and law enforcement agencies to operationalise without delay the grievance redressal module and the money restoration module developed under the home ministry’s January 2, 2026 SOP for handling cyber fraud complaints through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and Cyber RMS. States have also been directed to create public awareness about these mechanisms so that victims can seek quicker relief.
Recognising that victims frequently approach courts seeking de-freezing of bank accounts or recovery of money, the bench asked the registrar generals of every high court to inform all courts and adjudicating authorities dealing with cyber fraud matters about the grievance redressal mechanism. At the same time, it clarified that using this mechanism would not prevent any person from pursuing statutory or constitutional remedies before courts.
The court also sought greater transparency in measuring the effectiveness of the recovery mechanism. It directed that the next status report should include state-wise and bank-wise data on complaints registered, complaints disposed of, restoration orders issued, successful restorations and the amount restored.
Noting that only 14 states have so far operationalised State Cyber Crime Coordination Centres and that the e-Zero FIR mechanism is functional in only 19 states, the bench directed the remaining states to notify their coordination centres within four weeks and adopt the e-Zero FIR system in consultation with I4C. The central agency has been asked to assist states in implementing these measures.
The bench further directed authorities to ensure expeditious disposal of matters relating to freezing of bank accounts arising from cyber-enabled financial frauds, an issue that frequently delays recovery of funds for victims and businesses alike.
The Inter-Departmental Committee (IDC), which is coordinating the government’s response to digital arrest scams, has also been directed to intensify nationwide awareness campaigns on cyber frauds, the grievance redressal and money restoration mechanisms, cyber security measures and procedures available for recovery of defrauded money. The court also recommended that all State Legal Services Authorities undertake public awareness drives on preventing digital arrest scams.
In another important direction, the bench asked the IDC to consult banks and technology intermediaries on introducing technological safeguards to prevent digital arrest scams, improve recovery of money, facilitate investigations and ensure compliance with legal obligations.
The court also accepted Nappinai’s suggestion that victims require greater institutional support beyond existing legal remedies. It directed the IDC to examine and discuss a proposal for introducing a shared liability and victim compensation framework for digital arrest scams, potentially paving the way for a structured compensation mechanism for victims.
On the investigative front, the court took note of the CBI’s progress in handling organised cyber fraud networks. The status report records that the agency has registered 10 digital arrest cases and several connected matters. In one investigation alone, the CBI identified 238 victims, traced 67 first-layer bank accounts, tracked transactions worth nearly ₹80 crore and carried out searches at 93 locations spread across 16 states.
The bench also asked the IDC to continue examining whether the existing ₹10 crore threshold for mandatory CBI investigation should be lowered and whether multiple frauds committed by the same organised network should be aggregated for determining the threshold for central investigation.
The matter will next be heard on September 16, when the Centre is expected to file a fresh consolidated status report on compliance with the court’s directions.

headline: Big change in UPI policy? Payments above ₹2,000 may carry a fee. What we know
full_text:
Big change in UPI policy? Payments above ₹2,000 may carry a fee. What we know
The bill seeks to remove the provision that prevents banks and payment service providers from charging a fee, including MDR, on notified electronic payments.
A major policy change might be headed towards the free Unified Payments Interface (UPI), with Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman introducing the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha.
UPI, one of the world's largest real-time payment interfaces, processed 23.6 billion transactions worth ₹29.9 trillion in July, as per official data.
The bill intends to further amend the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, the Income-tax Act, 2025, and the Finance Act, 2026.
ALSO READ | HT Insight: India’s UPI revolution’s becoming a global export
While amendments have been proposed to different parts of the bill, the aim remains the same -- making India a more attractive and predictable place for global capital, manufacturing, and businesses to come to and remain in the nation, news agency PTI reported, citing finance ministry sources.
What's key for UPI?
Regarding a policy change in UPI, the main focus among the proposed amendments is the amendment to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
The bill seeks to remove the existing legal provision that prevents banks and payment service providers from charging a fee, known as the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), on notified electronic payments.
MDR is a fee that merchants pay to banks and payment service providers for processing digital transactions.
Relevant changes have been sought in Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, and Section 269SU of the Income Tax Act, requiring large businesses with a turnover exceeding ₹50 crore to accept payments via specific electronic modes, including BHIM-UPI QR codes and RuPay debit cards.
So far, no bank or payment system provider has imposed any charge on anyone, either directly or indirectly, for using the electronic modes of payment prescribed under Section 269SU of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
The latest amendment bill, however, proposes to expand the scope of what could be notified under modes of payment that attract no charges.
While no charge on UPI payments would be imposed immediately, the bill does give the government the flexibility to introduce MDR at any time.
The proposed amendments may result in the Centre setting an MDR fee below 0.5 per cent, which would apply to transactions above ₹2,000, Moneycontrol reported, citing sources. But this charge may be valid for merchants with an annual turnover above ₹1.5 crore.
This means that consumers may not have to pay any additional charges, and small businesses may also continue to enjoy the UPI facility free of cost.
Another option is that an MDR would be determined based on transactions above a certain limit, Reuters reported.

However, no final decision has been made on the rate or the transactions that would be covered under this amendment.
Why was there no fee on UPI payments?
In December 2019, the Centre issued a circular to clarify that, based on Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2007, no charges, including MDR, shall be applicable on or after January 1, 2020, on the payment made through prescribed electronic modes.
The prescribed modes are:
- Debit Card powered by RuPay
- Unified Payments Interface (UPI) (BHIM-UPI)
- Unified Payments Interface Quick Response Code (UPI QR Code) (BHIM-UPI QR Code)
According to a March 2026 report from the Standing Committee on Finance, the objective of zero MDR was to make digital transactions more affordable and widely accessible.

The committee was told by the Department of Financial Services that the policy aimed to encourage wider acceptance of UPI and RuPay payments, including by smaller businesses.
However, it noted that the absence of a fee was making the UPI ecosystem "financially unstable." The committee observed that a structural funding gap was impacting long-term infrastructural investment.
The committee observed that while government schemes are necessary to democratise digital payments in Tier 3-6 cities, it urged DFS to explore a self-reliant, tiered revenue model.
"The Committee would like to emphasise that establishing a viable revenue mechanism is critical to ensuring the UPI ecosystem achieves financial sustainability without perpetually straining the government exchequer," the report stated.

headline: Assam floods death toll reaches 95 as 1.6 lakh affected in 14 districts
full_text:
Assam floods death toll reaches 95 as 1.6 lakh affected in 14 districts
Assam's flood situation worsened on Wednesday, with six more deaths and a sharp rise in affected people. The expanding deluge has damaged villages, crops, livestock and infrastructure across 14 districts.
The flood situation in Assam worsened on Wednesday, with the death toll in this year’s deluge rising to 95 and the number of affected people increasing to more than 1.6 lakh across 14 districts, according to an official bulletin.
The Assam State Disaster Management Authority said six people died in the last 24 hours. The number of affected people also went up sharply from more than 1.22 lakh across five districts on Tuesday to over 1,60,600 across 14 districts on Wednesday.
According to the ASDMA bulletin issued in the evening, two people each drowned in floodwaters in Sivasagar and Biswanath districts, while one person each died in Golaghat and Morigaon. With these deaths, the total number of people killed in this year’s floods has risen to 95.
The authority’s daily flood report said people were affected in Biswanath, Charaideo, Darrang, Dhemaji, Golaghat, Jorhat, Kamrup Metropolitan, Karbi Anglong, Lakhimpur, Nagaon, Sivasagar, Sonitpur, Tinsukia and Udalguri districts. Sivasagar was the worst-hit district with more than 57,000 people affected, followed by Golaghat with 34,000 and Jorhat with 25,000.
The administration has been operating 105 relief camps and relief distribution centres in six districts, where 44,523 affected people are being looked after at present. In the last 24 hours, the authorities distributed 528.44 quintals of rice, 126.72 quintals of dal, 73.21 quintals of salt and 2,519.64 litres of mustard oil among flood victims.
The ASDMA said 563 villages are under water and 16,951.76 hectares of crop area have been damaged across the state. Floodwaters have also damaged embankments, roads, bridges and other infrastructure in different districts. The Dhansiri river was flowing above the danger level at Numaligarh. The floods have also affected 35,025 domestic animals and poultry across Assam, while 8,529 more have been washed away.
Overall, the flood situation in Assam deteriorated further on Wednesday, with deaths rising, more districts coming under the impact of the deluge, and damage reported to villages, crops, infrastructure and livestock.

headline: Karnataka Council chair row: Basavaraj Horatti says Shivakumar asked him to resign
full_text:
Karnataka Council chair row: Basavaraj Horatti says Shivakumar asked him to resign
Council Chairman Basavaraj Horatti said Chief Minister D K Shivakumar asked him to resign. He said only the House can decide the post, sharpening a fresh constitutional row.
Karnataka Legislative Council Chairman Basavaraj Horatti on Tuesday said Chief Minister D K Shivakumar had called him and asked him to resign from the post. Horatti said he would discuss the matter with BJP and JD(S) leaders before taking a decision.
He also said the chairman of the Legislative Council and the Speaker of the Assembly can be chosen only by the House, and not by the high command of a political party. His remarks came after the Congress high command approved Saleem Ahmed as its nominee for chairman of the state Legislative Council and Umashree for deputy chairperson.
The approvals were conveyed in a letter sent to Shivakumar on Monday, along with the list of ministers who were sworn in the same day. The party also cleared the names of G S Patil as its nominee for the post of Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and A S Ponnanna for deputy speaker.
"The chief minister called me and requested that I resign and cooperate to prevent embarrassment, as the party has sent the name (for the new chairman).... I will discuss this with opposition leaders and decide," Horatti told reporters. Horatti, an eight-time MLC, has his current term till July 2028.
Questioning the announcement by the party, Horatti said, "This is probably for the first time I have seen a party declaring the chairperson of the legislative council. I'm not sure how they are doing it. It is not good in democracy." He said the chairman of the council and the speaker of the assembly could only be elected by the House.
Explaining the process for his removal, Horatti said, "To remove the chairman, ten members must give 14 days' advance notice, to move the no-confidence motion. Based on the discussion in the House the matter will be decided," and added that the decision of the House was supreme in the matter.
He also said no chairperson had been made to resign since 1956 and that all had completed their terms. According to Horatti, there were no grounds to remove him.
In the 75-member Legislative Council, the Congress has 38 members, the BJP 24 and the JD(S) 6. There is one Independent member and one chairman, while five seats are vacant. The row over Horatti's continuation has come after the Congress named its candidates for the top posts in both Houses.

headline: 'Grave security threat': CJP's Saurav Das raises SOS after YouTubers enter his house
full_text:
'Grave security threat': CJP's Saurav Das raises SOS after YouTubers enter his house
In a series of posts on X, Saurav Das, one of the faces of the recent protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, called it a “grave security threat” to his family.
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das on Wednesday accused certain YouTubers and media channels of invasion of privacy, alleging that “15-20 of such people have broken” into his house.
In a series of posts on X, Das, who was one of the faces of the recent anti-NEET paper leak protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, called it a “grave security threat” to his family.
“#SOS: Certain YouTubers and media channels have broken into my house and are showing the visuals from inside. It’s not just an invasion of my privacy but also a grave security threat for me and my family. If anti-social elements attack me at my residence as a result of this, these YouTubers and their troll handlers who are coordinating this will be directly responsible! @DelhiPolice,” Das wrote on one of the posts.
In another post on X, Saurav Das said that “15-20 such people had descended" on his house on Wednesday morning while he was in Maharashtra for the two-day CJP meet.
“Some have been camping outside since last night. These videos have now activated goons, a grave security threat for everyone living in the house. I am currently in Maharashtra for CJP’s two-day meeting,” he added.
Saurav Das says Sonam Wangchuk to continue as CJP mentor
Before the two-day meet began in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Saurav Das said that environmentalist and education activist Sonam Wangchuk will continue to be their mentor and that they will seek his advice.
Das further said they will push for the withdrawal of FIRs against students who took part in the recent protests led by the CJP against the NEET paper leak and other exam irregularities.
"We are talking with government representatives on this issue," he said.
Das also said they are working to provide legal and medical assistance to protesters injured in recent student agitations across the country.
Abhijeet Dipke backs Jharkhand protest
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke on Wednesday declared support for protesting students in Jharkhand, stating that the youth movement will operate as a "pressure group" to demand institutional accountability.
Talking to reporters ahead of the CJP's meeting in his hometown, Dipke said the CJP members will travel to Jharkhand to back job aspirants, who have been staging an indefinite sit-in at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi since July 29.
"People have lost faith in the judiciary, politics, media and the Election Commission. Our agitation received nationwide support. As the agitation grew, the support was not merely limited to education issues; it was also about these institutions. Hence, to bring accountability in these institutions, there is a need for a public pressure group," Dipke said.
A large number of job aspirants have been staging a protest in Ranchi, demanding that the alleged irregularities in the JPSC and other recruitment examinations be investigated by an independent panel of retired HC judges from outside Jharkhand.
Asked whether he will support the protest in Jharkhand, Dipke said, "We will definitely go to Jharkhand, we will stand with them and support their every demand in the agitation."

headline: France offers to build 94 of 114 Rafale jets in India under Rs 3.25-lakh crore deal
full_text:
France offers to build 94 of 114 Rafale jets in India under Rs 3.25-lakh crore deal
A key feature of the offer is the local production of 94 jets in partnership with Indian industry. The government is now examining the technical and commercial aspects of the bid, including indigenous weapons integration and technology transfer.
France has submitted its detailed technical and commercial proposal to India for the proposed acquisition of 114 Rafale multirole fighter aircraft, marking a key step forward in one of the country's biggest defence procurement programmes. Estimated to be worth around Rs 3.25 lakh crore, the government-to-government deal is currently being evaluated by the Ministry of Defence's Acquisition Wing and the Indian Air Force (IAF), defence sources said.
The proposal follows India's Letter of Request (LoR) sent to France in May this year and places strong emphasis on local manufacturing, technology transfer and greater indigenous content.
A major highlight of the French proposal is the plan to manufacture 94 of the 114 Rafale jets in India through a domestic industry partner. The production programme is expected to involve Dassault Aviation along with leading French defence firms MBDA, Safran and Thales.
The project is expected to significantly boost India's aerospace manufacturing ecosystem, with substantial opportunities for Indian companies such as Tata, Larsen & Toubro and other domestic defence manufacturers. Industry participation under the programme could generate business worth around Rs 1.6 lakh crore, according to sources.
INDIGENOUS WEAPONS, LOCAL CONTENT UNDER SCRUTINY
The Indian side is expected to closely examine the French proposal for provisions related to the integration of indigenous weapons systems, particularly variants of the Astra beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile, into the Rafale platform.
Officials will also assess the level of indigenisation offered under the deal, in line with the government's push to strengthen domestic defence manufacturing and reduce dependence on imported military equipment.
CRITICAL FOR IAF'S COMBAT STRENGTH
The acquisition is aimed at addressing the Indian Air Force's declining squadron strength, which has been affected by the phased retirement of ageing MiG fighter aircraft and delays in the induction of indigenous platforms such as the LCA Mk1A and the upcoming LCA Mk2.
The Rafale was selected by the Defence Ministry in 2012 after a lengthy global competition and has since emerged as one of the IAF's frontline combat aircraft.
The Defence Acquisition Council cleared the proposal for procuring 114 Rafale jets around five months ago, following a capability enhancement review initiated by Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh after he assumed office in 2024.
INDIA'S RAFALE FLEET SET TO GROW
The Indian Air Force and the Indian Navy have already placed orders for 62 Rafale aircraft. If the proposed acquisition goes through, India's Rafale fleet will increase to 176 aircraft.
The Indian Navy has also expressed its intent to induct 31 additional Rafale-M fighter jets for carrier-based operations, which could eventually take the total number of Rafales in Indian service to more than 200.

A sense of belonging and mutual respect is needed for dialogue to take place. We need to recognise and respect each other. Only then can a meaningful dialogue happen, where we understand their concerns and they understand our perspective," Bhagwat said.
Describing today's youth as more honest than previous generations, he added, "I believe today's younger generation, Gen Z and Gen Alpha, is more honest than the existing generation. This generation should have honesty towards the nation, a spirit of patriotism, and a commitment to service."
Bhagwat reiterated his faith in young people even while acknowledging that he did not know the complete facts behind the recent confrontation between police and protesters.
"I will trust Gen Z blindly," he said. Referring to reports of the use of tear gas and pellet guns during the protests, Bhagwat said conclusions should not be drawn without verified information.
"If I had to believe, I will believe Gen Z. But we do not know the reality. Both of us are conversing on the basis of information available through reports. There have also been reports of some anti-social elements in this movement. But we cannot talk without authentic information," he said.
'WILL NEVER SAY GEN Z SHOULD NOT PROTEST'
Calling protest an integral part of democracy, Bhagwat said dialogue was essential to address genuine grievances.
"Protest is also one of the means of dialogue. Democracy is a way to make consensus after discussion. Grievance is genuine, and a lot has to be improved in our nation's education system. So dialogue is important," he said.
Drawing a contrast with previous generations, Bhagwat said today's youth are more willing to question authority.
"We never used to question authorities, but Gen Z and Gen Alpha question authority and want logical answers, that too with love," he said.
The RSS chief said he would never discourage young people from protesting. "I will never say that Gen Z should not protest, but there should also be a way given in democracy. We need to see that if youth is shouting, it is not for opposing but for improvement," he said.
He added that there were shortcomings in the system that needed to be rectified and that student protests seeking reforms should be viewed as a legitimate democratic exercise.
'A LEADER CREATES MORE LEADERS, DOESN'T SEEK THE SPOTLIGHT'
Bhagwat also outlined what he called the qualities of a true leader, saying leadership was not about delivering speeches, winning elections or standing in front of people, but about working quietly, sharing success and nurturing future leaders.
Referring to a Sanskrit verse, the RSS chief said an ideal leader should possess knowledge, recognise and appreciate the strengths of others, share success, fame and material gains with colleagues, and display courage like a warrior when faced with challenges.
"Real leaders are those who lead from behind. They work from within," Bhagwat said.
Rejecting the conventional notion of leadership, he added, "Leadership is not about standing before people, making speeches or winning elections. I do not see myself as a leader. I see myself as a worker."
Bhagwat said the ultimate purpose of leadership was not to build followers but to create more leaders.
"The purpose of leadership is to lead people towards light. The purpose of leadership is to create leaders. It is not to lead by myself. My leadership should create leaders," he said.
EDUCATION IS SOCIETY'S RESPONSIBILITY
The RSS chief devoted a significant part of his address to education, saying it should not become a commercial activity.
"Education is not a commercial business. Community help can improve the education system. The financial burden of education is huge. We need to be vigilant, active and assess the system regularly. We also need to train our teachers. It is not just the government's responsibility to educate, but a social responsibility," he said.
Backing a long-standing demand for greater public investment, Bhagwat said allocating six per cent of the national budget to education remained relevant.
"Demand for a 6% budget allocation for education is old. But only the government does not run schools. We as an organisation also strive hard for education and learning. There should be a social spirit awakening for education," he said.
LAW ALONE CAN'T FIX SOCIAL MEDIA
Bhagwat also spoke about the influence of social media, saying legislation alone could not solve the problem of misinformation.
"It is necessary to change the attitude. Only law enforcement is not enough. We need to change role models," he said.
He urged influencers with millions of followers to act responsibly and stressed the need to verify information through authentic sources.
"If something is banned, there will always be loopholes. So banning alone cannot be the solution," he said.
Questioning why violent content attracts greater engagement online, Bhagwat said, "Gen Z does not subscribe to violence, then why does violent content receive more likes? It needs to be thought about and analysed."
BHAGWAT ON TIES WITH PAKISTAN, CHINA
Speaking on national security and international conflicts, Bhagwat said citizens should support the government's decisions during crises while maintaining a humanitarian outlook.
"In times of conflict, we have to go with what the government does. Pakistan and China are two examples. The Indian solution is to hold back differences while dealing with conflicts. Permanent hatred is not the solution," he said.
"It is not that Pakistanis are wholeheartedly our enemies, and not even all Indians. Humanity has to be one," Bhagwat added.
ON LGBTQ, SAME-SEX COMPANIONSHIP
Bhagwat said members of the LGBTQ community were an integral part of society and deserved accommodation.
"They are also part of our society, and we have a tradition to accommodate them," he said.
However, he distinguished marriage from companionship, saying marriage was a social institution rather than merely an arrangement for two people to live together.
"Marriage is not a convenience to just live together, but it is a unit of society. Families create good citizens. We need to have some system first. If existing systems are disrupted without creating new systems, there will be consequences," he said.
Emphasising that social norms shape legislation, Bhagwat said, "Law does not dictate society, but society dictates law."
He added that while he did not support same-sex marriage, society should evolve a framework to recognise same-sex companionship.
"We have to devise a system where not same-sex marriage, but same-sex companionship should be accommodated," Bhagwat said.
Bhagwat's remarks come amid a wider debate over student-led protests, police action and the role of democratic dissent, with the RSS chief arguing that India's younger generation should be engaged through dialogue rather than suspicion.

RSS chief disagrees with anti-national tag for youth protesters; says if Gen Z is shouting, it is because they face problems that must be resolved; calls for law allowing same sex couples to stay together, not marry
Gen Z’s grievances are genuine and need to be addressed, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh Sarsanghchalak Mohan Bhagwat said on Thursday (August 6, 2026). Speaking days after the massive youth protest at Jantar Mantar, the RSS chief said that protest is a way of dialogue in a democracy, and that it should be used to evolve a consensus.
He was participating in an interview at an event organised by India’s International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN), a youth-run nonprofit, at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre.
Disagreeing with the tag of “anti-nationals” slapped on the young protestors by some people, Mr. Bhagwat said that Gen Z was, in fact, much more honest than his generation. “They are not anti-national. They are our own next generation. They have to be addressed with that relation. There has to be love,” he said.
‘Protest should aim for consensus’
Emphasising that the goal of an agitation should be to create consensus, he said that the current generation of youth was markedly different from the previous generations. “When we were Gen Z, we listened to what our elders told us. Now, Gen Z asks questions. They want logical answers. They want love too. This should be there,” he said.
“In a democracy, debate is important. We get so many new opinions. They together form a total view of the truth. Debate should happen. The methods have been laid out in the Constitution by Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar. We too have to see that if Gen Z is shouting, they are doing so due to problems. We need to resolve the issues they face,” he added.
Law for same sex couples
The event’s organisers said that the questions Mr. Bhagwat was asked — on topics ranging from LGBTQI rights, women’s empowerment, social media use, and educational reforms, to India’s relations with Pakistan and China, reservation policies, climate change, and unemployment — were collected from members of Gen Z and Gen Alpha. The interview was moderated by IIMUN’s Rishabh Shah, who was cheered by the crowd when he asked questions about youth being labelled as anti-national, empowerment of women within the RSS, and the Sangh’s stance on same sex marriages.
Mr. Bhagwat called for a law to allow same sex companions to stay together, though not in the form of a marriage. “LGBTQIs are a part of our community. But in our community, marriage is not a convenience created for two persons to stay together. It is an institution. Family is the unit of society where the next generation is trained by their relations,” he said.
“That is also an ancient system running. If we disturb an existing system, and we don’t have new systems, that will create a conflict. We can’t mix these things. Prepare a system which can accommodate all these people. But the manner has to change. In this situation, same sex companions can stay together, we have to devise some system and form a law for that. That law should be acceptable to the society,” he added.
‘Education is not a business’
Asked about the lathi charge against youth protesters in Delhi last month, Mr. Bhagwat said that he trusted the Gen Z, but that complete information about the incident will have to be known before he could comment.
He emphasised the importance of self-discipline regarding young people’s use of social media. Asked about educational reforms, he said that education should not be treated like a commercial business. “It is a necessity of life. Its structure should be such that it should be accessible to all,” he said.
‘Permanent hatred not a solution’
When Mr. Bhagwat was asked if the reservation policy was still relevant, he said that Babasaheb Ambedkar’s thoughts on it should be followed, adding that the policy itself was not wrong, but that the intention behind its implementation should be pure. “Those who wield the sword are holding it wrongly,” he said.
On India’s relations with Pakistan and China, he said that civilian interactions and ties should be continued during peacetime. “In times of conflict, we have to go with our government. But that should not sever ties which are already there. China says, for 2000 years, Bharat has given them some values. These ties cannot be severed. They can be put on hold during conflict. But after the resolution of conflict, we have to pick up from where we left. Permanent hatred is not the solution,” he said.
