Bombay HC convicts Tarun Tejpal of raping colleague in 2013, sentences him to 10-yr RI
Panaji, The Bombay High Court on Thursday convicted former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal of raping a colleague in 2013, setting aside his acquittal by a Goa sessions court five years ago, and sentenced him to ten years' rigorous imprisonment.
Justices Neela Gokhale and Amit Jamsandekar of the HC's Goa bench initially said Tejpal shall surrender within two weeks, but following a request from his lawyers, the court extended the time to four weeks.
The court, while imposing the minimum punishment, said the incident occurred 13 years ago, and Tejpal has since then not committed any other offence.
"Both parties may have moved on in life now," it observed.
The court also imposed a fine of ₹10,21,000 on Tejpal, which would be paid to the victim.
It said, "The victim having suffered sexual assault would be handed over the entire fine amount."
While Tejpal pleaded for leniency, claiming he was a "political victim" and the father of two daughters, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Goa government, demanded the maximum punishment to send a strong message that "no means no".
"We set aside the trial court order of acquittal. The respondent stands convicted," the bench said.
Tejpal said he will move the Supreme Court against the HC's order.
He has been convicted under sections 376 , 354 and 354 of the Indian Penal Code.
The bench sentenced Tejpal to ten years' rigorous imprisonment under section 376 , one year under section 354 and three years under section 354. All sentences would run concurrently, it said.
Tejpal, who was present in court, sought leniency, claiming that he was a "political victim" and the father of two daughters.
"I am 62 years old today. I am a father of two daughters. I have a wife. I am a political victim. My lawyers have also asked me to urge the court to show leniency," he told the court.
Tejpal's lawyer Aabad Ponda, while seeking the minimum punishment, also urged the court to suspend the sentence and conviction for at least 10 weeks so that they could file an appeal in the Supreme Court.
Tejal later told reporters that he will move the apex court against the HC order.
"We will be appealing against this order. We feel the order is wrong. We will be moving to the Supreme Court against the order," he said.
The case relates to allegations by a former junior colleague that the veteran journalist sexually assaulted her inside a hotel elevator during the ThinkFest event in Goa in November 2013.
After he was acquitted by the trial court in 2021, the Goa government challenged the verdict in HC.
Tejpal's lawyer Ponda said, "He has been on bail since trial and has not ever violated any of the conditions imposed on him. He is a senior citizen."
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, however, said Tejpal deserved the maximum punishment of life sentence considering his "brazen" attitude towards the victim and also for later portraying her as behaving normally after the alleged incident.
"The convict was in a position of dominance over the victim. The victim was not just a colleague but also a friend of his daughter. The convict has shown no remorse," Mehta said.
He repeated the offence the next day, and then during the trial and now before the HC questioned the victim's behaviour by saying that she behaved normally, he said.
"The punishment should commensurate the act. It is high time to send a clear message that no means no. That deterrent message needs to be sent out," Mehta said.
During the hearing on the state's appeal, Mehta had argued that the sessions court committed a serious error by assessing the complainant's conduct based on preconceived notions of how a victim of sexual assault should behave.
There is no universal standard governing the reaction of a survivor, as responses differ depending on an individual's education, personality, social background and circumstances, the Solicitor General had said.

headline: New Delhi: Gen Z should not be branded as anti-national if they participate in an agitation, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat said Thursday while addressing a youth conference in Mumbai, adding that protesting is a way of buildin...
full_text:
New Delhi: Gen Z should not be branded as anti-national if they participate in an agitation, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat said Thursday while addressing a youth conference in Mumbai, adding that protesting is a way of building consensus.
Responding to a question about concerns that protesters may be labelled “anti-national”, Bhagwat said he does not endorse the term. “I want to make it clear that if Gen Z engages in any agitation, they are not anti-national. They are our own people; they are our next generation. Gen Z vagerah aise hee mai toh ye baatein nahi maanta…A sense of belonging and mutual respect is needed for dialogue to take place. We need to recognise and respect each other. Only then can meaningful dialogue happen, where we understand their concerns and they understand our perspective.”
“I believe today’s younger generation, Gen Z and Gen Alpha, is more honest than the existing generation and honest appeal of patriotism and service works with them,” he added, as he addressed Gen Z and Gen Alpha attendees at a conference on ‘The Role of Youth in Uniting the World, the Indian Way’, organised by India’s International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN) in Mumbai.
“If I had to choose one generation to trust, I would place my trust in Gen Z,” he further said.
The RSS chief’s remarks come days after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protests—which originated in Delhi’s Jantar Mantar and spread across the country—ended on 25 July after former education minister Dharmendra Pradhan submitted his resignation, which was the protesters’ key demand in connection with the NEET paper leak and subsequent student suicides.
The BJP has also embarked on an outreach programme to connect with Gen Z across states, conducting small-scale programmes that are being addressed by local leaders. The outreach was initiated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi himself, when he began posting reels addressed to the youth while the Jantar Mantar protest was still ongoing.
Asked if he agreed that if dialogue had started earlier, the matter wouldn’t have escalated, Bhagwat said: “When something happens that shouldn’t happen, it means there was a lapse somewhere. Whose fault it is or what happened is a separate matter, but there certainly was a shortcoming. It will be corrected; it should be corrected. That’s what I believe.”
Bhagwat’s comments also come at a time when the Modi government has faced intense criticism over use of force against protesting students, especially at Jantar Mantar and in Bihar.
Specifically asked about the lathi-charge and pellet gun firing, he said, “We need to first understand what happened and why it happened. We need to examine the reasons behind it. I do not have all the information required to give a complete opinion on this issue, and I do not think you have the complete details either. We need to look into where exactly the problem lies.
He added: “At this moment, I cannot say what happened or who was right or wrong, because I do not have complete information. You are sharing what you have read, and I am also going by what I have read…However, if I am asked to place my faith in someone, I would place my faith in Gen Z.”
‘Gen Z’s grievance is genuine’
“A protest is also a way of dialogue. We are sitting here and discussing, and if we understand each other’s perspectives, that is good. Otherwise, a debate will continue. If you or I are facing a difficulty and the solution is in your hands or mine, but it is not being resolved, then I may raise my voice and say that I will bring you there and ask you to resolve it because it is urgent,” Bhagwat said.
The RSS chief further said that in a democracy, protests are also a way of building consensus. “Lots of views come together, and consensus evolves after discussions. That discussion may happen through dialogue. However, due to various reasons, if a concern is not heard, one may move towards agitation. But all these steps should be taken to evolve a consensus, not to create divisions.”
Bhagwat added that Gen Z’s grievances are genuine. “As far as Gen Z is concerned, what happened recently, their grievance is genuine. A lot needs to be done in India’s education system, and it is not being done.”
“…when we were their age, we were habituated to accepting whatever the elders said, we never questioned them. Now, Gen Z and Gen Alpha questions, they want logical answers and love…In democracy, this is the method. They call it ‘debate’ in English, we call it ‘shastrarth’. There is no debate there but there are two sides—‘poorv’ and ‘uttar’. We look at all aspects and everyone has their own perspective, so a new dimension comes to light in every subject. So, we get so many opinions and counter-opinions, they together form a total view of the truth. This should indeed happen,” he further said.
Bhagwat said that he won’t say that Gen Z should not protest, but there are methods to how and what is to be done in a democracy. “Those who drafted the Constitution, the speeches of Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar, have indications on the same. This should be looked at. We too should see that Gen Z is not raising its voice to oppose, they are doing this because they have some issues and that should be rectified. Agitation should not be against me or you, but for system correction…”

headline: 'Gen Z are our own, protesting doesn't make them anti-national': Mohan Bhagwat
full_text:
'Gen Z are our own, protesting doesn't make them anti-national': Mohan Bhagwat
“When we were of their age (youth), we would listen to our elders. We never used to question. Now, the Gen Z wants logical answers,” he said.
Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat on Thursday said that if Gen Z is protesting, they aren't anti-nationals but “our own people”.
Addressing an event in Mumbai, Bhagwat said that Gen Z is not like the previous generation, which did not question elders, and that it wants logical answers.
“When we were of their age (youth), we would listen to our elders. We never used to question. Now, the Gen Z wants logical answers,” he said.
"If Gen Z is protesting, they are not anti-nationals. They are our own people, our next generation... I do not believe Gen Z is like that... I think the new generation - the Gen Z and Gen Alpha - is more honest than our existing generation, and the honest appeal of patriotism and service works with them," he added.
His remarks came against the backdrop of the recent Jantar Mantar protests in Delhi against the NEET paper leak, which was largely joined by Gen Z students.
Talking about the police action on the students at the protest on July 20, Bhagwat said he does not know why the police resorted to lathi charge and pellet guns.
“Why did the lathi charge happen? Why are pellet guns used? We need to study the reasons,” he said.
Bhagwat also backed comprehensive reforms in the education system, saying one or two reforms are not enough.
“I'll tell you, two or three are needed. Education is not a business, and we need to provide education to all. We need to work on fee structures," he said, while backing a demand for the share of education in India's budget to be increased to six per cent.
“Public participation is important in education, from school development to quality education. Focus on teachers' training. We are giving education to educate people, not for business,” he said while elaborating on the needed reforms.
What Mohan Bhagwat said on Pakistan, China
Bhagwat said conflicts between countries should not permanently damage bilateral relations. He asserted that nations such as Pakistan and China should not be viewed as India's "wholehearted enemies". He said disputes may temporarily put ties on hold, but should not bring them to an end.
"In times of conflict, we should not spoil bilateral ties. They can be put on hold till the issue is resolved, but they cannot be severed. Conflicts may halt ties, but they should not end them. It is not that Pakistan and China are whole-heartedly our enemies. State politics also plays a role," he said.
Bhagwat also said people should stand with the government during times of conflict, while stressing that humanity ultimately transcends political divisions.
"During conflict, we are with the government, but we also know that sometimes we have to become one. Humanity is one," he said.

headline: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay urges PM Modi to fast-track Godavari-Cauvery link
full_text:
Tamil Nadu CM Vijay urges PM Modi to fast-track Godavari-Cauvery link
Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi to expedite the Godavari-Cauvery-Gundar river linking project. He said the project is vital for Tamil Nadu's water security and deserves national importance status.
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Thursday urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to speed up the implementation of the Godavari-Cauvery-Gundar river linking project and declare it a project of national importance.
In a letter to the Prime Minister, he sought direct intervention to ensure long-term drinking water and irrigation security for southern India.
Vijay said Tamil Nadu has an inherent surface water deficit and depends on neighbouring states for more than 30 per cent of its water needs.
He said the proposed river link was the most significant long-term opportunity to increase the state's surface water resources and address the growing demand for drinking water and irrigation.
In his letter, the Chief Minister said, "Groundwater resources have also been exploited to critical levels, with several regions continuing to experience over-exploitation despite the sustained regulatory and conservation measures undertaken by the state government."
He added, "The Godavari-Cauvery-Gundar Link represents the most significant long term opportunity for augmenting Tamil Nadu's surface water resources. It is of vital importance to redress the growing needs of drinking water and irrigation for the population in Tamil Nadu."
He also said, "The southern districts of Tamil Nadu, particularly Pudukkottai, Sivagangai, Ramanathapuram and Virudhunagar, are chronically water-scarce and highly drought-prone".
Vijay said the most sustainable way to meet the growing water needs of these regions would be the implementation of the Godavari-Cauvery-Vaigai-Gundar link project, which would allow the transfer of surplus floodwaters from water-surplus basins to water-deficit regions.
He said, "The National Water Development Agency (NWDA) has prepared the Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the Godavari-Pennar-Palar-Vellar Link as phase one of the larger project."
He added, "This component is envisaged to benefit Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu," but noted that "the alignment covered by the DPR presently terminates a few kilometres upstream of the Cauvery River".
Urging quick action, he said, "Therefore, may I request that the project of inter-linking of Godavari-Cauvery-Gundar rivers which is a project of national importance be taken up on a priority basis."
He added, "I am confident that this project can be achieved and differences between states can be resolved through constructive consultation and cooperative federalism, keeping in view the larger national interest and I request that, considering the strategic importance and far-reaching socio-economic benefits of the project, Godavari-Cauvery-Gundar Link Project be taken up on a fast-track basis and may be given the status of a project of national importance".
The Chief Minister also said a dedicated special purpose vehicle with the participation of the Centre and the beneficiary states could be considered to ensure coordinated implementation, assured funding and timely completion.
He said, "It's early execution would benefit the people and farming communities of Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka" and assured that the Tamil Nadu government would extend all necessary cooperation for the project's speedy and successful implementation.
In his closing appeal, Vijay asked the Prime Minister to direct the Ministry of Jal Shakti and the NWDA to speed up consultations with stakeholder states, help build an early consensus on pending issues, finalise the DPR for extending the link up to the Kattalai Barrage across the Cauvery, accord priority to the project, implement it as a national project on a fast-track basis, consider setting up a dedicated special purpose vehicle, and declare it a project of national importance.

headline: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke kicks off nationwide 'Kya Bolti Public' campaign to gauge public concerns
full_text:
CJP's Abhijeet Dipke kicks off nationwide 'Kya Bolti Public' campaign to gauge public concerns
Dipke said the campaign's first focus would be education, arguing that rising school and college fees have made quality education unaffordable for families.
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Thursday announced a nationwide public outreach campaign, Kya Bolti Public, saying the initiative aims to understand 'people's issues'.
Dipke said the campaign's first focus would be education, arguing that rising school, college and coaching fees have made quality education unaffordable for many families.
He was addressing a press conference after the conclusion of the CJP's core team meeting in his hometown Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra. The core team had been holding talks at Dipke's residence since Wednesday.
Also Read | CJP forms National Working Committee to better outreach. See members' list here
"Education reform will be our first issue that we are going to take up. We believe education has become unaffordable in the country. Annual fees are in the range of ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh for Class 1, over and above the donation money," he said.
Questioning how middle- and lower-income families manage such costs, Dipke said, "From where the families bring the money who do not have that much income."
Also Read: Between placards and Parliament: What a ‘pressure group’ is, and where Abhijeet Dipke’s CJP fits
Dipke flags soaring education costs
He further alleged that escalating college and coaching fees were pushing families into debt and said the party wanted to ease that financial burden.
"College fees and coaching fees are also becoming too high, bringing families into the burden of loans. We want to free families from this. The parents should not feel burdened if they want to give higher education to their children," he said.
Dipke also cited BR Ambedkar while stressing that education should remain accessible.
"It is a fundamental right, according to Dr BR Ambedkar, but in the last few years, it has turned as education is a fundamental business to gain business," he said.
Dipke said the response to the recent Jantar Mantar protest went beyond concerns over NEET or the education system, and reflected growing public anger against the political system.
"The response to the Jantar Mantar protest was not limited to NEET or for the education system per se. It was against the entire system created in the last few years," he said.
He alleged that people were increasingly losing faith in democratic institutions, claiming that voters often see elected representatives switch parties after elections.
He also questioned the neutrality of the judiciary, alleging that rulings increasingly favour the ruling party while ordinary citizens struggle to get timely hearings.
"The judicial decisions are coming and have created questions about their neutrality. The way more decisions come in the favour of ruling parties, a common man does not get early hearing, he continues to get dates. In contrast, when a big businessman approaches court, he gets urgent hearing and quick verdict," he said.
Dipke further alleged that courts acted swiftly in matters involving political parties but were slow to deliver justice in cases involving ordinary citizens.
"The court immediately gives a verdict on splitting parties and induction of MLAs from one party to another, but the same court does not have time when the common man wants justice. This has created a big question on the integrity and neutrality of the courts," he said.a

Jharkhand govt reaches out to protesting students, stalemate continues
The Jharkhand students protests are demanding for a proper probe into irregularities in the 14th JPSC Civil Service Examination.
The state government on Wednesday, reached out to the protesting students at Jaipal Singh Stadium to initiate a dialogue, but by late evening, the students had not decided whether to hold talks with the government or pursue a different course of action.
Students’ spokesperson Piyush Kumar Singh said a decision would be made possibly by late night.
Student delegation deliberates

We could not decide whether to accept a closed-door meeting or not. Later we held a Tiranga March and remained busy with other activities. headline: ‘Hemant Soren unfit for office’: Students seek Jharkhand CM's resignation amid protest, plan state assembly gherao

‘Hemant Soren unfit for office’: Students seek Jharkhand CM's resignation amid protest, plan state assembly gherao
The student protest in Jharkhand has entered Day 13 and as protestors continue their hunger strike, they have called for the resignation of Hemant Soren.
As the protests in Jharkhand continue over alleged irregularities in the JPSC and JSSC CGL recruitment tests, students have now called for the resignation of chief minister Hemant Soren.
This demand comes as the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha chief met with governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar to brief him about the ongoing row regarding the JPSC recruitment process.
“The governor termed the alleged irregularities a matter of grave concern. He stated that the commissions should function in a manner that leaves no room for doubt regarding their transparency and credibility,” said a statement issued by the Lok Bhavan.
As reported by HT earlier, Soren has assured the governor that the state government is committed to ensuring justice for the protesting students and will look into the case.
Students call for Soren's resignation, says govt 'unresponsive'
As the protest and hunger strike continue in Ranchi, students have called for the resignation of Hemant Soren and alleged that the state government has been “unresponsive.”
Speaking to ANI, protesting student Rahul Kranti stated that despite the students' readiness for talks, the state government appears unresponsive to their demands.
"We are ready for talks. However, judging by the government's actions and what we are hearing through the media, it still does not appear to be taking a positive approach toward our demands. The government continues to say that it is investigating the matter through its own agencies. If that is the case, what is the objection to ordering a CBI inquiry?" Kranti told the news agency.
“We now demand the Chief Minister's resignation, as he is unfit for the office he holds. It has been so long since he returned from Bengaluru, yet he has taken no cognisance of the situation,” a protestor told news agency ANI.
The students have also stated that their plan for a gherao of the state assembly will proceed as scheduled on August 10.
Kranti also added that the students will be sending their own delegation for talks with the government, after officials reached out for dialogue.
"Initially, we wanted the government's delegation to come to the protest site. However, since there has been no positive response from the government on that front, we have decided to send our own delegation for the discussions," he told ANI.
HT reported that the state government has reached out to the students for a dialogue.
Students’ spokesperson Piyush Kumar Singh told HT that representatives from the government met the students on Wednesday afternoon.
“State government’s representatives came to talk to us in the afternoon. They offered a meeting with the state government and asked us to send a five-member delegation. We could not decide whether to accept a closed-door meeting or not," Singh said, adding that the students will soon decide who decide its representatives for the dialogue.
Amid this stalemate, students have carried out a Tiranga March, reiterating their demand for Soren's resignation.
“We are undertaking this Tiranga march, demanding the resignation of Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren, so that the selling of exam papers and jobs can be stopped... Our demand is that whatever talks (government) will happen will happen in front of the media,” a protestor told news agency ANI.
'Health is deteriorating'
Students have been on a hunger strike for three days, with many stating their health has started to deteriorate.
"My health is deteriorating. I feel dizzy if I try to stand up. I try to speak as little as possible," a protestor told ANI.
"The chief minister is like our guardian. When children remain hungry, a guardian also feels pain. We hope he will listen to our grievances. We want action and justice, not just assurances," said another protester to news agency PTI in an emotional appeal to the JMM leader.
Jharkhand Krantikari Loktantrik Morcha (JKLM) leader Devendra Nath Mahto is also on an indefinite hunger strike. Mahto, who has become the leading face of the Ranchi movement, consumed water on Wednesday after an interaction with activist Sonam Wangchuk.
"You have taken a big step by keeping your life at stake, but water and salt should be taken. Our purpose is to awaken the soul of the government, not to commit suicide," Wangchuk told the student leader.
The student leader and others will continue their hunger strike until the state government takes action on the alleged exam and recruitment irregularities.

headline: Govt amends rules to debar pharma firms submitting fake or fabricated data
full_text:
Govt amends rules to debar pharma firms submitting fake or fabricated data
The Union health and family welfare ministry called the amendments a significant step towards strengthening the integrity of the regulatory system
Union health and family welfare ministry has notified amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, empowering the licensing authority to debar further applications by pharmaceutical manufacturers that submit fake or fabricated data for the evaluation of the quality, safety, and efficacy of drugs.
An applicant submitting fabricated data earlier faced actions such as rejection of applications or cancellation of licenses. With the amendments, they would be debarred from filing further applications with the concerned regulatory authority, either in states or at the Centre as applicable, for a specified period.
In a statement issued on Thursday, the ministry called the amendments a significant step towards strengthening the integrity and transparency of the drugs regulatory system. It added that in addition to existing enforcement provisions under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, the newly notified provisions empower the licensing authority to debar further applications by entities submitting fake or fabricated data in support of their applications.
This will apply to all applications filed under various provisions of the Drugs Rules, 1945.
The ministry said due process has been prescribed through the issuance of show-cause notices before any punitive action is taken. There is also a provision for appeals.
The ministry said sound scientific data submitted by applicants forms the basis for regulatory evaluation of the quality, safety and efficacy of drugs. “Submission of fake or fabricated data compromises the integrity of the regulatory process, casts aspersions over the quality of drugs and may pose serious risks to public health.”
The ministry said the amendments are intended to deter misconduct, strengthen accountability among applicants and ensure that approvals of drugs are backed by reliable and scientifically valid evidence.
The government has amended the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1945, to introduce stricter norms to ensure quality and safety of drugs being manufactured in India.
The ministry said the fresh notification is in line with the government’s efforts to strengthen the regulatory framework in accordance with global best practices. “It aims to promote those drug manufacturers and distributors who are compliant with the regulatory framework and endeavours to deal with any reported instances of malpractice,” said the health ministry. “It complements the ongoing regulatory reform in the pharmaceutical domain with a renewed focus on enhancing oversight, promoting ethical practices and ensuring that unscrupulous entities are adequately penalised.”

The campaign will involve CJP representatives across the country to seek people's views on the issues they face and understand what they think about the present political and social situation. âDuring the âKya Bolti Publicâ campaign, we will get to know what people think of the present situation in the country and what the issues they face are,â he said."For now, CJP will be a pressure group because what India needs right now is a pressure group," he clarified.He said the organisation's work would extend beyond education-related issues and focus on wider concerns around governance and democratic institutions.
"Whether it is the political system, the judiciary, the media, or the Election Commission, the reality is that people have lost faith in all these institutions," Dipke said.He added that CJP wanted to build public pressure to restore accountability and neutrality in these institutions, adding that "the political system today, in my opinion, is in a very bad state".Unemployment is another issue the organisation plans to take up nationally. "Unemployment is a major problem, we will make it a nationwide issue," Dipke said.He also said CJP would work on education reforms and criticised the rising cost of education. "Education has remained unaffordable since schooling. Education is used for making profits. But we want to change it," he said.Dipke further stated that young people would be a key focus of the nationwide campaign, noting that 60 per cent of India's population is below the age of 35. He said unemployed youngsters had also participated in CJP's protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi last month.The organisation had led protests over the NEET paper leak and other alleged examination irregularities. Dipke described the resignation of former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan as a major outcome of the agitation. "Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is the biggest achievement of the students' agitation," he said.
The two-day core committee meeting also focused on expanding CJP's grassroots presence across states, strengthening its organisational network and preparing for the nationwide youth outreach campaign.Dipke rejected speculation that CJP was preparing to enter electoral politics, saying the organisation had no immediate plans to become a political party. Instead, it would seek to build a nationwide citizens' movement around transparency, accountability and institutional reforms.
He also expressed support for students protesting over alleged examination irregularities in Jharkhand and said CJP members, including its leadership, could visit the state if required.The CJP founder also called for efforts to restore the credibility of the media, making it another focus of the organisation's broader campaign.

headline: The Bombay High Court on Thursday (August 6, 2026) convicted Tarun Tejpal, former editor of Tehelka magazine, in a 2013 sexual assault case and sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment.
full_text:
The Bombay High Court on Thursday (August 6, 2026) convicted Tarun Tejpal, former editor of Tehelka magazine, in a 2013 sexual assault case and sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment.
The Goa Division Bench of Justice Neela Gokhale and Justice Amit Jamsandekar set aside the trial court’s 2021 judgment that had acquitted Tejpal. Terming the ruling “perverse”, the Bench said that the trial court fell for the notion that a sexual assault complainant must be a “perfect victim” and conduct herself in a certain way to appear credible.
The court ordered Tejpal to surrender within two weeks but extended it to four weeks on a request.
In its 81-page judgment, the court expressed disapproval about the way the defence highlighted the complainant’s personal life, and noted that it found it surprising that the trial court “remained silent and allowed the defence to harass and humiliate her during the cross examination”.
Tarun Tejpal case - a timeline
The court said that the prosecution had established its case “beyond every reasonable doubt” and the victim too had stood firm in her testimony.
The trial court had proceeded with the notion that a sexual assault complainant must behave in a stereotypical manner, the court said.
“The ‘perfect victim’ concept, more formally known as an ‘ideal victim’, described an unspoken cultural archetype where a person is fully believed, sympathised with and granted legitimacy only if they exhibit absolute vulnerability, complete innocence and total passivity,” the court said. When a victim does not fit the description, the trauma is devalued, it added.
The Bench heard arguments on the quantum of sentence from both sides on Thursday. While Solicitor-General Tushar Mehta requested the court to award the maximum sentence, senior advocate Abad Ponda, representing Tejpal, appealed for leniency, stating that this was Tejpal’s first offence and he was 62 years old.
Issues of sexual assault: the Tehelka case
“The accused in this case has shown no remorse whatsoever. He repeated the alleged act the very next day. His attitude was extremely brazen,” Mr. Mehta said before the Bench. He argued that the court’s perspective on the case would be important, as the accused could not be given the benefit simply because the victim was mature.
Mr. Mehta urged the court to send a clear message that “no means no”, regardless of the person involved. He requested the court to consider the deterrent effect while deciding the sentence.
Mr. Ponda submitted that the incident occurred in 2013 and that the appeal had been pending since 2022. He stated that Tejpal had been on bail and had not violated any bail conditions. He informed the court that Tejpal’s passport was deposited with the authorities. Mr. Ponda urged the court to stay the conviction order and grant eight weeks’ time for Tejpal to surrender. He said that Tejpal wished to challenge the High Court order in the Supreme Court.
“Please consider putting a stay on this order for a few weeks. Let me be given an opportunity to approach the Supreme Court,” Mr. Ponda said on behalf of Tejpal. He assured the court that Tejpal was not going to flee from the law.
Tejpal, with permission from the court, addressed the Bench. “For the last 13 years, we have been working to bring facts and truth to light. Obviously, that holds no significance today. I am a father to two daughters, and I have a family. All I want to say is that we now have the option to appeal in a higher court... My lawyer has asked me to appeal to the court for leniency in sentencing,” he said.
The Bench stated that it had heard Mr. Ponda’s submission that the accused had no other criminal cases pending against him and that this was his first offence. The court noted that Tejpal had stated that he was a victim of political vendetta. It observed that Mr. Mehta had argued that the defendant was acting as a guardian to the victim and therefore deserved the maximum sentence.
Mr. Ponda said that Tejpal had complied with court directions and had been present at every hearing. He stated that despite being acquitted by the trial court, he never travelled abroad. Mr. Mehta urged the court to take the accused into custody immediately. He said that after that, if Tejpal wished, he could seek bail in a higher court.
The court convicted Tejpal under Sections 376(2)(f), 376(2)(k), 354A, and 354B of the Indian Penal Code and also imposed a fine of ₹5 lakh under Section 376(2)(f). Under Section 376(2)(k), the court awarded 10 years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine of ₹5 lakh. Under Section 354, the Court sentenced him to one year of rigorous imprisonment and a fine of ₹10,000. Under Section 354A, the Court imposed one year of rigorous imprisonment and a fine. Under Section 354B, the Court awarded three years of imprisonment and a fine of ₹3,000. The sentences will run concurrently.
The six-month custody period previously served by the accused will be taken into account, the Court said. The Bench noted that there were no complaints of misbehaviour or misconduct against Tejpal in prison.
(With inputs from PTI)

headline: Amid protests and a walkout by Opposition members demanding the presence of Union Home Minister Amit Shah in the House, the Rajya Sabha on Thursday (August 6, 2026) considered and returned the Appropriation Bill, 2026 that allows the expenditure of a...
full_text:
Amid protests and a walkout by Opposition members demanding the presence of Union Home Minister Amit Shah in the House, the Rajya Sabha on Thursday (August 6, 2026) considered and returned the Appropriation Bill, 2026 that allows the expenditure of around ₹ 54,067 crore, incurred during the 2022-23 financial year.
Replying to a brief discussion on the Bill, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said the excess expenditure arose under two heads and had already been examined by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC). She noted that the demands formed part of the PAC’s 39th Report, which was presented to the Lok Sabha in April this year.
Parliament Monsoon Session: Follow LIVE updates on August 6, 2026
Ms. Sitharaman said an excess demand of ₹196.44 crore stemmed from a court order relating to the Ministry of Railways, while the larger demand of ₹53,871 crore was towards debt repayment.
Responding to a demand for greater financial assistance to Jammu and Kashmir, the Finance Minister said the Union government bears the entire salary and pension of Jammu and Kashmir Police, amounting to approximately ₹13,000 crore annually.
“We paid back the entire debt of Ladakh and after taking care of readjustments, restructured J&K’s debt. Also, for the years 2024-25 and 2025-26, an additional amount of ₹5,000 crore each year has been given, over and above the revised estimates of their budgets, just to make sure the urgent requirements of the J&K administration [are met] and it is not left without anybody’s support,” Ms. Sitharaman said, hailing the decision to abrogate Article 370, which was done seven years ago.
Earlier, the House witnessed disruptions and had to be adjourned for an hour when it met after lunch at 2.15 p.m. The Opposition walked out demanding that Union Home Minister Amit Shah must come to the House and apologise for the police action on protesting students.

headline: Kerala grants state honours to flood rescue hero Rajesh R, who died saving stranded farmer
full_text:
Kerala grants state honours to flood rescue hero Rajesh R, who died saving stranded farmer
Rajesh R, a swimming and disaster rescue instructor, drowned after providing his life jacket to an old farmer he was rescuing.
The Kerala government on Wednesday accorded state honours to Rajesh R, a swimming and disaster rescue instructor who drowned while rescuing a man during the recent floods in Cherupuzha in Kannur district.
Chief minister V D Satheesan visited Rajesh’s family at their home in Kalliyoor, Thiruvananthapuram, and offered his condolences.
He later told reporters after the cabinet meeting that the government would fund the completion of Rajesh’s under-construction house.
On August 1, Rajesh and his associates, Shibin and Jithin, volunteered for a rescue mission after learning that S Benny (61), a farmer, was stranded on his farmland between a river and dense forests along the Kerala-Karnataka border in Meenthully near Cherupuzha.

While escorting Benny to safety through the river, Rajesh handed over his own life jacket after noticing that the farmer was struggling against the strong current.

The CM described Rajesh’s death as “truly heartbreaking.”
“His ultimate sacrifice and selfless love for humanity will forever be remembered,” he said.

headline: New Delhi: Over four weeks after quitting the Trinamool Congress (TMC), the 20 rebel Members of Parliament (MPs) of the party who had merged with the Tripura-based Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) find themselves on a sticky wicket.
full_text:
New Delhi: Over four weeks after quitting the Trinamool Congress (TMC), the 20 rebel Members of Parliament (MPs) of the party who had merged with the Tripura-based Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) find themselves on a sticky wicket.
While they have gone on the warpath with Trinamool chairperson Mamata Banerjee at the cost of inviting brickbats from their own constituents for supporting the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the latter does not seem to be willing to fully embrace them.
Twenty of the 28 TMC parliamentarians had broken away from the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress in mid-June in the aftermath of the party’s humiliating defeat in the West Bengal Assembly elections. Even in the West Bengal Assembly, 60 of the 80 TMC legislators led by Ritabrata Banerjee split from the party and claimed to be the “real TMC.”
The rebel MPs led by Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar met Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on 14 June and sought recognition as a separate parliamentary group. The Mamata Banerjee camp also wrote to Birla on 10 June, urging him to not recognise any separate faction within the party, and pressed for the disqualification of the rebel MPs under the anti-defection law.
Nearly two months since both factions wrote to Birla, sources in the Lok Sabha Secretariat told ThePrint that the Speaker is yet to deliver a ruling. “No decision has been taken in the matter,” the source said. In fact, the Lok Sabha website still lists all 28 MPs, including the 20 rebels, as TMC MPs.
The Speaker’s delay in giving a ruling has led to an air of uncertainty in the rebel camp. Sources speak of the fear of some dissident MPs leaving if the air is not cleared about their status.
Though the rebel MPs have merged with NCPI, they support the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance. A majority of the rebel group also attends NDA parliamentary party meets.
Trouble seems to be brewing. At least three MPs from the rebel camp – Khalilur Rahaman from Jangipur, Yusuf Pathan from Baharampur and Abu Taher Khan from Murshidabad –vented their feelings by skipping the NDA meeting on 4 August. This was the second time in two months that the three MPs skipped the NDA meeting.
Speaking to reporters in Parliament on 4 August, Abu Taher Khan said that he will not join the BJP. ThePrint also reached out to six of the MPs from the rebel faction, including Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, Sudip Bandopadhyay, Abu Taaher Khan, Yusuf Pathan and Khalilur Rahaman, but all refused comment.
While the rebel group merged with NCPI to avoid disqualification under the anti-defection law, several MPs from the camp have expressed their willingness to join the BJP. But resistance from its own leaders and party rank-and-file seems to be holding the BJP back.
On 4 June, days before he was appointed West Bengal’s Finance Minister, Swapan Dasgupta in a post on social media platform X, cautioned his party to be wary of “false friends”. “I shed no tears for the TMC’s self-destruction. My only hope is that the political culture of the vandals does not start contaminating the West Bengal BJP. We in the BJP have to be always wary of false friends who are today cosying up to us because they need to wash away their past sins. The detox of Bengal cannot be left incomplete.”
The rebel MPs are also facing heat in their constituency and outside for aligning with the BJP. On 7 July, when one of the rebel MP Sayani Ghosh went to Baruipur to meet the family of an 11-year-old rape and murder victim, she was greeted with chants of “traitor”.
Poll panel silent
Even the Election Commission of India (ECI) is silent on the matter of 60 MLAs who have split from the Mamata Banerjee-led party and claim to be the real TMC. Both factions have also met the election commissioner and submitted letters making competing claims. While the rebel camp has staked claim to the TMC’s name and symbol, the Mamata Banerjee faction has urged the ECI not to recognise the former. The ECI has also not given any decision in the matter yet.
Leaders from the Mamata Banerjee camp have urged the Election Commission multiple times – the last was four days back – to give a ruling. “They (ECI) seem to be under pressure,” a leader from the Mamata Banerjee camp told The Print on condition of anonymity.
A leader from the Mamata Banerjee camp told ThePrint that the rebel MPs and MLAs have not only violated the 10th schedule of the Constitution that deals with disqualification but also the TMC’s constitution that bars party leaders from electing the party’s chairperson till five years after they are elected.
“Mamata Banerjee was elected the TMC chairperson in 2022 by member delegates for a term of 5 years. How can the rebel MLAs elect Arup Roy as the chairperson when Mamata Banerjee continues to hold the position?” the leader, who did not want to be named, said.

'Convey sentiments': Rajya Sabha Chairman tells Kiren Rijiju after opposition demands Amit Shah's presence

NEW DELHI: Parliament proceedings remained disrupted on Thursday as opposition parties continued to demand the presence of Union home minister Amit Shah over the police action against student protesters at Jantar Mantar. The Lok Sabha was also repeatedly adjourned amid the continued uproar.Amid the repeated disruptions, Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan asked Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju to "echo the sentiments" and demand to the home minister.
As the Rajya Sabha reassembled, the Chairman attempted to take up the Question Hour, but opposition members continued sloganeering. He repeatedly urged protesting MPs to maintain order and assured them they would get an opportunity to raise their concerns.The Chair then allowed leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge to speak. However, members of the Treasury benches objected, triggering a heated exchange between the ruling and opposition members.Kharge reiterated the opposition's demand that Amit Shah address the House on the police action against protesters and said the opposition was ready for a discussion."We only raise genuine questions concerning the country and its 140 crore people.
We are asking the Home Minister and the Prime Minister to come to the House. We request the Chair to direct the Home Minister to come and give a statement. We are ready to discuss it," Kharge later posted on X."In this very House, Arun Jaitley ji himself said that disruption is a part of Parliamentary Democracy. You can raise any questions that is relevant to the proceedings. But here, when we are asking genuine questions, they are escaping," he added.Responding to the demand, Rijiju said Kharge had not cited any rule while making the request and could not decide which minister should reply on behalf of the government."The leader of the opposition did not quote any rule, cannot give direction to the Chair, only make requests, cannot dictate. New Congress members not learning anything because their leadership not giving them a chance", Rijiju told Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge in Rajya Sabha.Following the exchange, the Rajya Sabha Chairman directed Rijiju to convey the sentiments of the opposition to the home minister."Now i request you to consider his request. Kharge requested the presence of home minister in the house. You represent him. As a parliamentary affairs minister you can echo the sentiments to the home minister," the RS Chairman said.
Outside Parliament, Kharge said the Chairman had asked the Parliamentary affairs minister to ensure Amit Shah came to the House and made a statement."This is a simple request, and it is well within the government's control. Why they are not present is still unknown. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha told the Parliamentary affairs minister that the home minister should come to the House and speak on this incident. Rijiju alone does not have the authority to resolve the issue. He only conveys the matter, and then the issue fizzles out," Kharge said."When I raise a point of order, I am not allowed to speak. We want the House to run peacefully, and for that, the Home Minister should make a statement in the House. Instead of asking students to seek forgiveness, the government should apologise to the students and their families," he added.Asked whether the opposition would continue its protest, Kharge said the next course of action would depend on the government's response.
"It depends on when the Home Minister comes to the House and what statement he makes. Even the Prime Minister should come to the House and apologise. Such a serious incident has taken place, and yet the Home Minister has not made a statement," he said."We are raising the students' cause. We have written to our allies as well. Wherever there is an issue concerning students, we will raise it and stand with them," he added.The Rajya Sabha witnessed multiple adjournments during the day as opposition members continued sloganeering. Proceedings were first adjourned within 30 minutes of the House assembling, and later again till 2.15 pm and subsequently 3.15 pm with normal business repeatedly disrupted.

NEW DELHI: Air India's recent severe turbulence incident is now under a "thorough investigation" by the directorate general of civil aviation (DGCA), civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said on Wednesday.Naidu said the Air India flight from Phuket to New Delhi experienced severe turbulence for "four to five minutes", leaving several passengers injured and some crew members with spinal and neck injuries.At least 17 people, including four cabin crew members, were injured after the aircraft suddenly lost around 300 feet in altitude during the midair turbulence.

The moment the plane was landed, it was put in a separate hangar. The data recorder, the voice recorder, everything is in the possession of DGCA. They will thoroughly investigate how and why this incident happened. Only when we have the facts in front of us, we are going to make it public," he said.The minister said medical teams attended to passengers and crew immediately after the flight landed in Delhi.
"The moment the flight landed in Delhi, the medical assistance team immediately attended to them. All first aid and medical assistance that needed to be provided was done at the airport itself. There were some passengers and crew members who were observed to need more medical assistance, they were shifted to Medanta Hospital and also Fortis Hospital," Naidu added.He said seven passengers admitted to Medanta Hospital on Monday were discharged after undergoing medical examinations."Spinal Injuries Centre, Fortis Centre - two passsengers were admitted yesterday. They both were also discharged but four crew members were admitted in Fortis where I also personally visited along with Ministry Team and DGCA Team. We interacted with crew members also. They have been very brave, even after that incident happened for 5 minutes and they were prone to certain injuries, the plane had to travel for 1 more hour. Even through that hour, the crew members provided all the assistance that was required. So, it was very brave of the women, the crew members who were on the flight," he said.The Airbus A320neo, operating as flight AI2379 from Phuket to Delhi on Tuesday, was carrying 137 passengers and eight crew members. Following the turbulence, 13 passengers and four crew members sustained injuries and were taken to hospitals for medical evaluation.
An Air India spokesperson said on Tuesday, "Earlier today, Air India flight AI2379 operating from Phuket to Delhi experienced a sudden loss of altitude during cruise. After the momentary event, the aircraft continued normally and landed safely in Delhi at 11:07 hrs IST."The DGCA is now investigating the incident to determine the cause of the severe midair turbulence.
Abhishek Mishra is a Digital Content Producer at The Times of India, working with the news desk. He writes with a keen eye on foreign policy, defence developments, and the shifting currents of geopolitics-and yes, Indian politics always finds a way onto his radar too.

headline: Air India turbulence lasted 5 minutes, crew members suffered spinal injuries: Minister
full_text:
Air India turbulence lasted 5 minutes, crew members suffered spinal injuries: Minister
An Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi encountered severe mid-air turbulence, briefly losing around 300 feet in altitude and leaving 17 people injured on Thursday.
The mid-air turbulence that hit an Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi on Tuesday lasted nearly five minutes, leaving some crew members with spinal and neck injuries, Civil Aviation Minister K Rammohan Naidu said as he shared fresh details about the incident.
The Airbus A320neo, operating as flight AI2379, experienced a sudden loss of around 300 feet in altitude while cruising on Tuesday. The aircraft, carrying 137 passengers and eight crew members, continued its journey and landed safely at Delhi airport at 11.07 am.
Speaking at a briefing in New Delhi, Naidu said the turbulence lasted around four to five minutes and praised the cabin crew for continuing to assist passengers despite suffering injuries themselves.
"The plane had to travel for one more hour and even through that hour, the crew members provided all the assistance required. It was very brave... I would like to thank them for the bravery they have shown," Naidu said.
When asked about the extent of the injuries, the minister said a couple of crew members suffered spinal injuries, including injuries near the tailbone and neck, and had been advised rest by doctors.
A total of 13 passengers and four cabin crew members were taken to hospital following the incident. Air India said on Wednesday that all 13 passengers had since been discharged, while the four crew members remained under medical care.
"As of Wednesday evening, all 13 passengers who were admitted to hospital following the incident involving Air India flight AI2379 from Phuket to Delhi on August 4 have been discharged. Four crew members remain under medical care and continue to receive treatment," the airline said in a statement.
The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has launched an investigation into the incident, with the aircraft's Flight Data Recorder and Cockpit Voice Recorder secured for detailed examination.
According to a senior DGCA official, the pilot reported a severe injury to one cabin crew member, an injury to another and minor injuries to some passengers following the sudden loss of altitude.
"Air India A320 aircraft VT-EXO operating flight AI2379 (Phuket-Delhi) experienced loss of approximately 300 feet in altitude during the flight," the official said.
Air India had earlier said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss of altitude during cruise but continued to operate normally after the "momentary event" and landed safely in Delhi.
Following the incident, Naidu, Civil Aviation Secretary Samir Kumar Sinha and DGCA Director General Vir Vikram Yadav visited Fortis Hospital in Delhi to enquire about the condition of those injured.
The aircraft has since been moved to a hangar as investigators examine the circumstances surrounding the sudden altitude loss. Air India has said it is cooperating with the investigation and has also informed the aircraft manufacturer.

headline: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat at an interaction with 'Gen Z' in Mumbai
full_text:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat at an interaction with 'Gen Z' in Mumbai
NEW DELHI: Calling Gen Z and Gen Alpha more "honest" than adults RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Thursday rejected attempts to brand protesting youngsters "anti-national," and said they have "an honest feeling of patriotism." He described protest as a legitimate form of democratic dialogue and said their questions must be answered with logic, affection and a sense of belonging.By the end of the freewheeling exchange, the 75-year-old had also picked up a new expression from his young audience â âclock itâ â and tried it out before the cheering crowd, adding a lighter finish to a conversation that ranged from student protests and reservation to social media, LGBTQ rights and relations with Pakistan and China.
The interaction, held as part of IIMUNâs 15th anniversary celebration in Mumbai, was driven by questions from Gen Z and Gen Alpha delegates on issues ranging from education and jobs to reservation, social media and the right to protest.âI feel that this new generation â Gen Z and Gen Alpha â is more honest than our existing generation. There is an honest feeling of patriotism and service in them,â Bhagwat said, adding, âThey are not anti-national.
They are our own people, our next generation,â . The exchange came against the backdrop of recent Gen Z-led protests over examination irregularities, education and jobs.Bhagwat said young people today were unlike earlier generations that often accepted what elders told them without question. âThey ask questions. They want logical answers, and along with that, they want affection,â he said.âI feel this new generation â Gen Z and Gen Alpha â is more honest than our existing generation. The honest impulse of patriotism and service is stronger in them,â he added.Bhagwat said protest should not be treated as the opposite of dialogue. âProtest is also a way of dialogue,â he said, describing it as a democratic means of building consensus. An agitation, he added, should seek to correct the system rather than target individuals or deepen divisions.Asked about allegations of lathi-charge and pellet firing on young protesters, Bhagwat said he did not have enough verified information to reach a conclusion. âI place my trust in Gen Z,â he said.Bhagwat backed the longstanding demand to allocate 6% of the Budget to education, saying, âThe demand is justified. It should be implemented.â He also argued that education should not be treated as a commercial business.Turning to social media, Bhagwat warned against trusting content without checking authentic sources, particularly when technology could produce fake images, voices and videos. Influencers and public figures, he said, must recognise their responsibility because lakhs of people may imitate them.Turning to affirmative action, he said reservation must continue as long as social discrimination remained. âThose who have received its benefit and whose condition has improved should give up that benefit for others,â he said. Bhagwat also referred favourably to sub-categorisation so that the benefits reached those still left behind, and blamed politics for creating âbad bloodâ over a measure intended to promote social unity.The discussion also moved to LGBTQ rights. Bhagwat said the community was part of society and must be accommodated, but favoured wider debate on a legal framework for same-sex companionship rather than an immediate change to the institution of marriage.He also said people-to-people relations with Pakistan and China could be paused during war or terrorism but should not be permanently severed. âPermanent enmity is not the solution,â he said.The discussion also turned to jobs, with Bhagwat arguing that employment should not be reduced to salaried or government work. Entrepreneurship, skilled work and self-employment were equally valid, he said, calling for the restoration of "shram pratishtha", or dignity of labour. Society, he added, must stop ranking occupations as high or low and accord equal respect to anyone earning honestly, whether through farming, manual work, private employment, government service or a small enterprise.
Asked why the RSS remained a male organisation despite describing women as equal partners in nation-building, Bhagwat said men and women were âequal and complementaryâ and should receive the same training and opportunities. He said the Rashtra Sevika Samiti functioned independently with the RSSâs support, while women working in public organisations were invited to the Akhil Bharatiya Pratinidhi Sabha and participated in its decision-making process. He also indicated that organisational integration could be considered if the womenâs organisation itself sought it.
Manash Pratim Gohain is a seasoned journalist with over two decades at The Times of India, where he has built a rich body of work spanning education policy, politics, and governance. Renowned for his incisive coverage of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, accreditation reforms, and skilling initiatives, he has also reported on student politics, urban policy, and social movements. His political reportageâboth reflective and news-drivenâadds depth to his writing, bridging policy with public impact. Through his 2,500 articles and related outlets, he has emerged as a trusted voice in national discourse, particularly in linking education reform to broader societal change.

headline: As the Narendra Modi government explores the possibility of bringing in a constitutional amendment Bill to carry out a fresh delimitation exercise, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) may consider extending support if the government revises the legis...
full_text:
As the Narendra Modi government explores the possibility of bringing in a constitutional amendment Bill to carry out a fresh delimitation exercise, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) may consider extending support if the government revises the legislation bringing in three essential changes to the Bill that reached the Lok Sabha in April.
There is a freeze on seats based on the 1971 Census which ends after the latest Census that is expected to be completed in 2027. The DMK wants this constitutional freeze to remain for another 25 years, while amending the Constitution to introduce a 50% blanket increase in the Lok Sabha seats for all States, which was verbally promised by Home Minister Amit Shah when the legislative package aimed at bringing about delimitation was brought in Parliament in April.
Additionally, the party wants a Schedule of the number of seats that each State will have in the legislative package, as per sources in the DMK. A top DMK leader said that the government has not yet approached them on the issue either “formally or informally”. The party maintains that it will take a final call only once the form and substance of Bills are known.
These conditions come amid renewed efforts from the government to reach out to the Opposition, with Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju speaking to Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi again on Thursday. “I had a productive conversation with Rahul Gandhi. I have made a request on a few specific issues and also discussed other matters. We expect continuous communication and coordinated action with the Congress and other Opposition parties,” Mr. Rijiju said.
The Parliamentary Affairs Minister had also met Mr. Gandhi at the latter’s office in Parliament on Wednesday, during which the Congress leaders are also said to have reiterated their opposition to any constitutional amendment to carry out the delimitation exercise.
Though the government doesn’t have the two-thirds majority yet to push through a constitutional amendment, the political situation has changed since April 17, when the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill was defeated on the floor of the House. The numerical strength of the INDIA bloc has since vastly changed.
In the present 540-member Lok Sabha, the two-thirds majority mark is 360, and if 22 Lok Sabha members of the DMK vote for the Bill, the government’s strength would go up to 346. While the government would still be short of 14 MPs, the threshold changes if there are abstentions during the proceedings. If the government brings the Bill to the Rajya Sabha, it will find it easier to reach the two-thirds majority mark. In the Rajya Sabha, if all 244 members are present during voting, the government needs 164 votes. The BJP-led National Democratic Alliance currently has 158 MPs.
Mr. Shah had earlier said that once it is assured of the numbers, the government would once again bring the constitutional amendment Bill to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha to 850 seats in order to implement the 33% reservation for women after fresh delimitation.
Since April, the government has secured the support of 20 rebel Trinamool Congress MPs, who are now part of the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) and six Shiv Sena MPs who had switched sides from the Uddhav Thackeray faction to the Eknath Shinde-led faction.
On Friday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be hosting the NCPI and Shiv Sena MPs for a breakfast meeting.
In anticipation of the delimitation and the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment (FCRA) Bills coming up next week, the Congress is all set to issue a three-line whip, asking its members to be present in Parliament next week.
Meanwhile, the Lok Sabha continued to be disrupted over the Opposition protests regarding police action against students.
Speaker Om Birla started the proceedings in the morning by commemorating the anniversaries of the bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki and members stood in silence to pay tribute to the victims.
Thereafter, Opposition MPs began raising slogans, demanding the presence of Mr. Shah in the House over the police action against student protesters on July 20. Some members were also seen displaying placards.

Six deaths reported: Two each in Sivasagar and Biswanath districts, and one each in Golaghat and Morigaon. (Photo: PTI)
NEW DELHI: The death toll from the devastating floods in Assam rose to 95 after six more people died, while more than 1.6 lakh people remained affected across 14 districts, officials said on Thursday.According to the Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA), six deaths were reported on Wednesday, two each in Sivasagar and Biswanath districts, and one each in Golaghat and Morigaon.
Sivasagar continues to be the worst-affected district, accounting for 50 of the 95 deaths reported so far.
Sivasagar continues to be the worst-affected district. ( Photo: ANI)
Neighbouring Charaideo has recorded 21 fatalities, followed by Jorhat (9), Golaghat (5), Dhemaji (3), Karbi Anglong (2) and Biswanath (2). One death each has also been reported from Sonitpur, Kamrup Metropolitan and Morigaon.The floods have affected over 1,60,600 people in Biswanath, Charaideo, Darrang, Dhemaji, Golaghat, Jorhat, Kamrup Metropolitan, Karbi Anglong, Lakhimpur, Nagaon, Sivasagar, Sonitpur, Tinsukia and Udalguri districts.Sivasagar alone has around 57,000 affected residents, followed by Golaghat (34,000) and Jorhat (25,000).
The number of affected people has risen sharply from 1.22 lakh in five districts reported on Tuesday.
Cars lie partially submerged in mud and silt washed along floodwater of the swollen Dikhow River (PTI Photo)
Authorities have set up more than 100 relief camps and relief distribution centres across six districts, where 44,523 people are currently taking shelter.Floodwaters have submerged 16,951.76 hectares of cropland, while embankments, roads, bridges and other public infrastructure have suffered extensive damage in several parts of the state.Union health and family welfare minister J P Nadda, who was deputed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, visited the flood-hit Nepalikhuti area along the Assam-Nagaland border in Sivasagar district on Wednesday, one of the regions worst affected by the latest wave of floods that began on July 19.Later in the day, Nadda chaired a high-level review meeting with Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and senior state officials to assess the flood situation and review ongoing relief, rehabilitation and healthcare measures.
JP Nadda and Himanta Biswa Sarma inspect flood-ravaged Assam (PTI)
"I have visited the flood-hit Nepalikhuti area. Along with CM Sarma, I have witnessed the scale of devastation. The damage is so huge that it will take time (for normalcy to return)," Nadda told reporters after interacting with flood-affected families.
"The Central Government and the State Government have stood with complete sensitivity and utmost promptness beside every flood-affected family. We are continuing the relief and rehabilitation efforts with full commitment. I assure everyone that there will be no lapses of any kind in the relief and rescue operations. Teams of Central Government representatives are conducting extensive assessments of the flood damages, and all kinds of financial assistance are being extended," he added.Nadda is scheduled to visit Yazali in Arunachal Pradesh on Thursday to inspect areas affected by flash floods and interact with affected residents. During the visit, Nadda will chair a review meeting with state government officials to assess the health situation and review ongoing relief and rehabilitation efforts in the region.The visit is part of his three-day tour of the Northeast from August 4 to 6.

headline: Jantar Mantar protest: Rahul Gandhi defends students, blames Shah for violence on students
full_text:
Jantar Mantar protest: Rahul Gandhi defends students, blames Shah for violence on students
Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi, flanked by five young activists who are facing harassment after the students protests at Jantar Mantar, criticised Union home minister Amit Shah and said, “Complaining about the education system, which is a flawed system, a collapsing system, a useless system, is not a crime
Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi, flanked by five young activists who are facing harassment after the students protests at Jantar Mantar, criticised Union home minister Amit Shah and said, “Complaining about the education system, which is a flawed system, a collapsing system, a useless system, is not a crime.”
After the five activists narrated their ordeals—including police atrocities, pellet injuries, online harassment and trauma, Gandhi said, “Complaining about the education system, which is a flawed system, a collapsing system, a useless system, is not a crime. If anything, the system needs to be changed; it needs to be corrected. That is all they were asking for. They were not doing violence, they were not being aggressive, they were not being nasty. They were beaten, assaulted and threatened,” he said.
Directing his critique at the top leadership, Gandhi alleged that the government lacked the moral courage to face questions directly, pointing fingers squarely at the Union Home Minister.
“They are young people who are standing here, in front of India’s press. But Amit Shah and the Prime Minister don’t have the courage to stand here. The person who is responsible for this violence, the person who had the pellet gun fired into this young lady, is Amit Shah - the Home Minister of India. He does not have the decency to come to Parliament; he does not have the decency or the courage to comment on what has happened,” said Gandhi.
Gandhi also raked up the issue of the 15-year old girl who had to publicly apologize for abusing the PM. “Forcing them first, sending goons to their house, forcibly demanding an apology of a 15-year-old girl and then accepting that apology is complete nonsense. We do not accept it. We want an education system that works, we want exam leaks to stop and we want the future of this country to be respected and protected,” Gandhi said.
Speaking about their harassment, Riya Ahir, who stopped a police van in Mumbai, said, “According to the media, I stopped the bus, but I am the girl who prevented the students from being forcibly arrested. The children I stood up for are now standing up for me,” she said, adding that she is yet to get a copy of the FIR she filed against harassment.
Jharkhand resident Nutan Toppo alleged that she sustained direct injuries from pellet fire during the July 20 protest at Jantar Mantar. Fahranaz and Muskan raised serious allegations regarding police excesses, communal profiling, and unprovoked baton charges by security personnel during peaceful assembly.
Fahranaz from Uttar Pradesh alleged police excesses during the demonstration. “Police goons were brutally beating me. The police said I was in a bus. He made us sit and asked us to make a separate list because he is a traitor to the country,” she alleged. Bharat Banait said, “I have never seen such a dark day in my life as what happened that day. Those whose heads were broken had their legs broken.”
Gandhi again blamed Shah for the violence against students. “There are only two possibilities: One, he did not know that this violence was being carried out on the children, in which case he is incompetent. Two, he ordered the shooting of the pellet gun and the violence on these children. It means he is culpable. Either way, he is responsible,” Gandhi added.

headline: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju met Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) in an effort to break the parliamentary deadlock, with the two sides discussing the proposed delimitation Bill and th...
full_text:
Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju met Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) in an effort to break the parliamentary deadlock, with the two sides discussing the proposed delimitation Bill and the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment (FCRA) Bill, 2026.
Amid speculation that the government could convene a three-day session after Independence Day to push through the women’s reservation Bill and the delimitation Bill, Mr. Rijiju told The Hindu that “there is no such proposal”.
Sources said Mr. Rijiju did not raise any proposal to extend the ongoing Monsoon Session or convene a Special Session during the nearly 50-minute meeting with Mr. Gandhi. Instead, he sought the Congress leader’s views on the party’s stand on delimitation, they said.
According to sources, Mr. Gandhi conveyed to Mr. Rijiju that a statement by Home Minister Amit Shah on the police action against students who protested against the NEET paper leak and a discussion on the alleged theft of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya were non-negotiable if the House was to function.
The Congress leaders also reiterated their opposition to any constitutional amendment to carry out the delimitation exercise, sources added.
The meeting, held in Mr. Gandhi’s Parliament office, was attended by Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal, deputy leader in the Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi and Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra.
The government’s outreach came on a day when Opposition MPs held a symbolic march within the Parliament complex, questioning Mr. Shah’s continued absence from the House.
Both Houses witnessed repeated disruptions before being adjourned for the day.
The Wednesday (August 3) meeting was the second between Mr. Rijiju and Mr. Gandhi in the past 10 days. The Parliamentary Affairs Minister had also spoken to the Congress leader over the telephone on Tuesday (August 4) night as part of the government’s efforts to secure Opposition cooperation during the remainder of the Monsoon Session.
Sources said Mr. Shah was expected to reply to the debate when the FCRA Bill comes up for discussion and passage. “The LoP has made it very clear that they cannot bring the FCRA Bill in this form,” Mr. Venugopal told reporters after the meeting.
“Now you see, the mood of Narendra Modi will change within a minute. If the Indian Opposition says something, he will not listen, but this kind of diktat is coming from foreign country, they will now...,” he added, when asked about U.S. Congressman Riley M. Moore’s social media post criticising the FCRA.
The Bill is considered contentious because it empowers a government-appointed authority to take over foreign-funded assets of organisations whose FCRA registration ceases, a provision that the Opposition says gives the Centre sweeping powers over NGOs and religious institutions.
However, there was no clarity on whether the delimitation Bill would be introduced during the current session, which is scheduled to conclude on August 13. Sources also ruled out, for now, the possibility of a Special Session immediately after Independence Day.
The government is understood to be assessing the political support available for reviving the delimitation Bill, a Constitution amendment Bill requiring a two-thirds majority in Parliament. It could not muster the required numbers when it attempted to move the legislation during the Budget Session.
Since the Monsoon Session began on July 20, the Lok Sabha has failed to transact Question Hour even once because of repeated disruptions. Five Bills have been passed without debate as the Opposition has pressed for discussions on the NEET paper leak, the police action against protesting students and the alleged theft of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, while demanding statements from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Mr. Shah.

headline: Former Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman and veteran Congress leader P.J. Kurien on Thursday (August 6, 2026) urged Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla to “perform the duty of directing” Union Home Minister Amit Shah to be present in the House and respond to the qu...
full_text:
Former Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman and veteran Congress leader P.J. Kurien on Thursday (August 6, 2026) urged Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla to “perform the duty of directing” Union Home Minister Amit Shah to be present in the House and respond to the questions raised by the Opposition members.
In a letter to the Speaker, Mr. Kurien said that as a citizen of the country, he was disappointed over the “non-functioning” of the House and its “failure” to ensure the accountability of the government and avoid the “consequent stalemate”.
Noting that the Lok Sabha was not functioning for about one week because the Union Home Minister was “not coming to the House to respond to the questions of his department raised by the Opposition members”, he said in a democracy, the Opposition had an equally important role to play as the ruling party.
Constitutional duty
He said the government was accountable to Parliament and it was the constitutional duty of the Opposition to ensure accountability. It was the constitutional duty of the Speaker to protect the rights of members in their effort to ensure accountability, said Mr. Kurien, adding that if the Union Home Minister “evaded” Parliament continuously, he was “failing to perform his constitutional duty”.
“In such a situation, Hon’ble Speaker, being the custodian of the House, has the duty to intervene to save Parliament from being defunct and to avoid stalemate. It is the duty of the Hon’ble Speaker to direct the government that the Home Minister has to be present in the House and give a reply to questions about his department,” he said.
Mr. Kurien said the presiding officers had on umpteen occasions given such directions and that it was the precedent and practice of the House. “Can I request the Hon’ble Speaker to perform the duty of directing the Home Minister to be present in the House or asking the government to ensure his presence in the House. With all humility I do so,” he added.
