headline: ₹557.51 crore spent on PM Modi’s trips to 77 countries since 2021: Govt
full_text:
₹557.51 crore spent on PM Modi’s trips to 77 countries since 2021: Govt
Government told Parliament PM Modi’s visits to 77 countries since 2021 cost ₹557.51 crore and resulted in 316 agreements across key sectors.
A total of ₹557.51 crore has been spent on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visits to 77 countries since 2021, including ₹74.59 crore on trips to 12 nations this year, according to information provided by the government in Parliament on Thursday.
The highest expenditure during this period was recorded in 2025, when the PM’s visits to 23 countries cost ₹187.83 crore, figures provided by minister of state for external affairs Pabitra Margherita in the Rajya Sabha showed. He was responding to a question from Aam Aadmi Party MP Sanjay Singh and CPI MP V Sivadasan.
According to details provided by Margherita in a written response, the figures for 2026 did not include expenses incurred on a visit to France in June for the PM to attend an outreach session of the G20 Summit and hold bilateral meetings, as the “compilation of bills is still underway”.
Margherita noted in response to questions from the MPs that the total foreign direct investment (FDI) received by India between April 2021 and December 2025 was $381.8 billion.
He said the PM’s trips between 2021 and 2026 resulted in the signing of 316 agreements — including government-to-government pacts and MoUs between government institutions, research bodies, and universities — in fields such as defence, trade, investment, nuclear energy research and development, healthcare, renewable energy, space, sports, and culture.
Of all the trips this year, the PM’s visit to Norway in May for a bilateral meeting and to attend the India-Nordic Summit was the most expensive, costing the exchequer ₹17.46 crore. This was followed by visits to Israel in February ( ₹11.92 crore), Seychelles in June ( ₹8.22 crore), and Sweden in May ( ₹6.32 crore).
Expenditure on other trips this year included ₹5.57 crore for a visit to Malaysia in February, ₹1.97 crore for a visit to the United Arab Emirates (UAE), ₹3.6 crore for a visit to the Netherlands, ₹4.23 crore for a visit to Italy (all in May), ₹4.77 crore for a visit to the Slovak Republic in June, ₹3.87 crore for a visit to Indonesia, ₹1.18 crore for a visit to Australia, and ₹5.43 crore for a visit to New Zealand (all in July).
“High level visits by the Prime Minister are established means of fostering closer relations with foreign countries and promoting India’s engagements at bilateral, regional and global levels,” Margherita said in his reply.
“These visits, and the understandings and agreements concluded therein, facilitate the strengthening of partnerships across a wide range of sectors, including technology, innovation, trade and investment, defence and energy cooperation, and resilient supply chains, among others.”
Of the visits to 23 countries in 2025, the five most expensive were to France ( ₹25.59 crore), Brazil ( ₹17.72 crore), the US ( ₹16.54 crore), Saudi Arabia ( ₹15.54 crore), and China ( ₹10.6 crore).
The PM visited 17 countries in 2024 at a total cost of ₹109.51 crore, with the five most expensive trips being to the US ( ₹15.33 crore), Italy ( ₹14.36 crore), Russia ( ₹10.75 crore), Poland ( ₹10.1 crore), and Singapore ( ₹7.75 crore).
There were visits to 11 countries in 2023 that cost a total of ₹93.63 crore, with the most expensive trips being to the US ( ₹22.89 crore), Japan ( ₹17.19 crore), France ( ₹13.74 crore), and Papua New Guinea ( ₹8.58 crore).
The PM’s visits to 10 countries in 2022 cost a total of ₹55.83 crore, with the most expensive trips being to Germany ( ₹14.47 crore), another visit to Germany ( ₹9.44 crore), and Japan ( ₹8.68 crore).

headline: India, China to use diplomatic, military channels to resolve outstanding border issues: MEA
full_text:
India, China to use diplomatic, military channels to resolve outstanding border issues: MEA
The representatives of both the countries met and engaged in what the MEA described as “frank” discussions and reviewed the situation along the LAC.
India and China on Thursday agreed to continue using existing diplomatic and military channels to address outstanding issues and prevent misunderstandings and miscalculations along the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
The two sides held what the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) described as "frank" discussions, reviewing the situation along the LAC. They also underscored that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral ties.
The discussions took place during the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC) in New Delhi on August 6.
Also Read: 2026 could be landmark year for India-EU ties, courtesy China, US and Russia
The Indian delegation was led by Sujit Ghosh, Joint Secretary (East Asia) in the Ministry of External Affairs, while the Chinese side was headed by Hou Yanqi, Director General of the Department of Boundary and Oceanic Affairs at China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
As a follow-up to the outcomes of the 24th Special Representatives (SR) talks, the two sides held detailed discussions on boundary delimitation, border management, mechanism-building and trans-border cooperation.
India also reiterated the need for an early meeting of the Expert Level Mechanism on trans-border rivers and stressed the importance of sharing technical details related to upstream projects.
Also Read: 'Ties can't be severed, they can be on hold during conflict': Mohan Bhagwat's China-Pakistan example
35th WMCC meet
The 35th WMCC meeting was held in Beijing on May 27, 2026, where the two sides reviewed the situation along the India-China border and expressed satisfaction with the progress made in maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas.
They noted that the stable situation had facilitated gradual progress towards the normalisation of bilateral relations.
India-China ties
The India-China relationship continues to face challenges, particularly over the long-standing border dispute. Tensions have persisted as China has repeatedly laid claims to territories that India considers part of its own.
In his most recent comments, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reacted strongly to China repeatedly raising sovereignty issues in official readouts of bilateral meetings, saying the Indian side hasn’t violated China’s sovereignty, whereas Beijing continues to illegally occupy territories in the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir and has built projects in these regions.
Jaiswal was responding to a Chinese readout of a meeting between external affairs minister S Jaishankar and his counterpart Wang Yi, which contended that the Indian leader had assured the Chinese side about respecting China’s sovereignty, including on issues such as Taiwan and Tibet. People familiar with the matter said Jaishankar had made no such comments, HT reported earlier.
“Let me say that the external affairs minister said that when it comes to sovereignty issues, it is actually India that should be and is raising them,” Jaiswal said in response to a question at a regular media briefing.
“India does not violate China’s sovereignty in any manner and has been consistent, but China is in illegal occupation of Indian territories in Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh since 1963, where India’s right is officially acknowledged even by China,” he said.
“Also, there are Chinese projects in territories in Jammu and Kashmir that belong to India, and we object to that,” Jaiswal said, referring to projects implemented by China in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) as part of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) and in the occupied Shaksgam Valley.
Jaishankar-Wang meet
India's external affairs minister S Jaishankar met his Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi on the margins of Asean-related meetings in the Philippines capital of Manila last month.
Jaishankar emphasised the Indian position that a stable and cooperative relationship “can best be developed on the basis of mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity” to contribute to a multipolar Asia and a multipolar world.
“Peace and tranquillity in the border areas is obviously the prerequisite for normal ties. Since October 2024, both sides have engaged to ensure that important objective. This will continue to need our constant attention,” he said, referring to the understanding reached by the two sides in 2024 to end the face-off on the LAC that took bilateral relations to a six-decade low.

headline: ‘Freedom fighters took bullets, you fear eggs?’: SC refuses to entertain Mahua Moitra’s plea

‘Freedom fighters took bullets, you fear eggs?’: SC refuses to entertain Mahua Moitra’s plea
Faced with the court’s disinclination to grant relief, senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Moitra, sought permission to withdraw the petition.
The Supreme Court on Friday refused to entertain Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra’s plea seeking permission to join police interrogation through video conferencing in a case over her allegedly provocative Facebook posts, telling her that having “taken the plunge into politics”, she could not shy away from appearing before investigators merely because she feared eggs being hurled at her.
“You are a member of Parliament? Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs? When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest? These are applications that should not come before this court at all,” a bench of justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu remarked while declining to interfere with an order of the Calcutta high court directing Moitra to appear before the investigating officer in person.
Faced with the court’s disinclination to grant relief, senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Moitra, sought permission to withdraw the petition. The bench dismissed it as withdrawn.
The case arises out of an FIR registered in June at Hogalbaria police station in West Bengal’s Nadia district on a complaint by BJP leader Hirak Bhattacharya, accusing Moitra of making provocative remarks capable of hurting religious sentiments and disturbing communal harmony. The FIR was registered under alleged offenses related to promoting social and religious enmity, outraging religious beliefs, and making statements that cause public mischief.
What is the complaint about?
The complaint relates to two videos uploaded by Moitra on Facebook after a group of BJP women workers allegedly gathered outside the Krishnanagar district sessions court carrying eggs and tomatoes, claiming they would throw them at the MP if she appeared in connection with an earlier case.
Also Read | Parliament Showdown: Mahua Moitra Presses Amit Shah Over Protest Crackdown
In the first video, Moitra said she would lodge a police complaint against the women seen outside the court with eggs and, if the police refused to register her complaint, she would approach the courts, including the Supreme Court.
In another video posted the following day, she said she would name all the women in an FIR and allegedly remarked that instead of throwing eggs openly, they should do so while “wearing a burqa” so that no one would recognise them. The videos went viral on social media, prompting the BJP leader to lodge the complaint alleging that her remarks were intended to inflame communal tensions.
Last month, the Calcutta HC granted Moitra interim protection from coercive action on her plea seeking quashing of the FIR but directed her to cooperate with the investigation by appearing before the investigating officer on August 14.
Before the Supreme Court, Sankaranarayanan submitted that while Moitra was willing to cooperate with the investigation, she should be permitted to do so through video-conferencing because she apprehended a hostile crowd outside the police station.
'Fear mob attack': Mahua on seeking virtual appearance
When the bench asked why she could not appear physically, counsel said the police station was located in her own constituency and that she feared another mob confrontation.
“I have a legal right under law. The requirement as per the police notice is to be at the police station in my own constituency. Last time I went there, two things happened. First there were threats that eggs would be thrown, and the second time eggs were actually thrown,” Sankaranarayanan submitted.
The bench, however, refused to accept the contention, pointing out that the high court had already directed Moitra to cooperate with the investigation.
“Read paragraph 18 of the impugned order. If you do not appear, then face the music before the High Court. If you are aggrieved thereafter, then come,” the bench observed.
In paragraph 18 of its July 21 order, the high court had given liberty to the state to come back to the court in case Moitra “does not co-operate with the Investigating Agency to take forward the investigation and if she does not obey the notices issued in connection with the aforesaid criminal prosecution.”
To be sure, the impugned high court order had specifically asked the police authorities to ensure that Moitra “shall not be subjected to egg pelting or any other form of harassment.”

Akali Dal sources confirmed to ThePrint that a possible coming back together of the former partners was the agenda of the meeting. However, details of the discussion have not yet been made public.
A one-on-one meeting between the two leaders has happened after several years. The Akalis and the BJP remained political partners for over three decades before parting ways in 2020 following the controversy over the three central farm laws.
Sources further said that Badal was called for a meeting by the PM within days of the former having met Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini regarding a possible pre-poll alliance. Badal, along with senior Akali leaders Daljit Singh Cheema and Balwinder Singh Bhundar, had met Saini some days ago asking him to take up the matter—as in-charge of the BJP in Punjab—with the party leadership.
Saini, sources added, was instrumental in getting Badal an audience with the PM on the matter.
In March this year, Union Home Minister Amit Shah had during his rally in Moga ruled out the possibility of any bonding with the Akalis.
Moreover, PM Modi had during his visit to Jalandhar last month attacked the Akalis, along with other opposition parties in his speech. The negative reference to the Akali Dal had almost ruled out the possibility of the two parties coming together before the elections.
‘Anyone can go meet PM, We will contest all seats alone’
Reacting to the meeting, state BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon said that as far as the Punjab BJP is concerned, it is making preparations to contest all 117 assembly seats in the state and there was no possibility of a tie-up. “Anyone can go and meet the PM. We are going to contest alone on all seats,” he told mediapersons Friday.
On the other hand, some senior BJP leaders including former chief minister Capt Amarinder Singh and former state party chief Sunil Jakhar had made it clear that the BJP will benefit electorally if it were to come back with SAD.
During a recent visit to Punjab, BJP president Nitin Nabin had said that a decision regarding the alliance would be taken at an appropriate time.
The seat sharing formula followed before the break-up had the Akalis in the dominant position. For the Lok Sabha elections, Akalis fought 10 of the 13 seats while the BJP fought on 3. In the assembly elections, the BJP fought on 23 seats while the Akalis fought on 94 seats.
After breaking away in 2021, the two parties contested the 2022 Punjab assembly elections and the 2024 Lok Sabha elections independently. In the assembly elections, the Akalis won three seats and the BJP won two. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP failed to win any seats in the state, while the Akali Dal managed to secure only one.
Sources in the BJP told ThePrint that the state leadership was divided over the decision regarding a tie-up. However, everybody was on the same page that in case the two parties come together for the elections, the BJP will not be the junior partner. Sources added that the Akalis will have to give more or an equal number of seats to the BJP.
Akali Dal sources told ThePrint that issues related to the division of seats would come up only after an in-principle decision of a tie-up is agreed to by the Prime Minister. They said that the question of seat-sharing depended on the winnability of candidates but the Akalis are ready to give almost 35 seats to the BJP for the assembly elections.
AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal reacted to the meeting quoting a popular Bollywood number of the yesteryears. “Na na karte pyaar tumhi se kar baithe…(we kept saying no, no but finally we fell in love).”
“Are the chanda chor (temple donation thief) and beadbi (sacrilege) parties coming together?” he posted on X.

headline: NEET paper leak chargesheet reveals how CBI tracked 13 accused
full_text:
NEET paper leak chargesheet reveals how CBI tracked 13 accused
The CBI chargesheet before a Delhi court details how investigators tracked and arrested the NEET-UG paper leak accused. It shows deleted chats, leaked PDFs and alias-based coordination formed the backbone of the conspiracy.
The CBI has told a Delhi court in its chargesheet in the NEET paper leak case how it made a series of arrests in the investigation. The agency said 13 accused are currently in judicial custody.
According to the chargesheet, the alleged conspiracy was uncovered through forensic imaging of mobile devices, which helped recover deleted WhatsApp chats and PDF documents containing the leaked questions. The document sets out the sequence of arrests made by the agency in May.
The agency began its action on May 13 with the arrests of Mangilal, Dinesh and Vikas Biwal in Rajasthan. Their mobile phones contained leaked PDFs that had been received through Telegram on April 29. On the same day, the CBI also arrested Yash Yadav in Gurugram and Shubham Khairnar in Nashik.
The chargesheet said Khairnar used the alias "Ap Broker" on WhatsApp to hide his identity and was found to have coordinated the distribution of leaked chemistry questions. Another arrest on May 13 was Dhananjay Lokhande in Pune. He allegedly tried to destroy his phone to remove evidence before he was caught.
Manisha Sanjay Waghmare was arrested in Pune on May 14. After questioning those arrested, the agency arrested the alleged mastermind, PV Kulkarni, from Latur on May 15.
This was followed by the arrest of Manisha Mandhare from Pune on May 16. Shivraj Motegaonkar, founder of a coaching centre in Latur, was arrested on May 17.
The final arrests in the case were made on May 22 and May 26. Manisha Sanjay Havaldar was arrested from Latur on May 22, while Tejas Shah and Dr Manoj Shirure were arrested from Pune and Latur respectively on May 26.
NEET-UG is conducted by the NTA for medical aspirants. On May 12, the NTA cancelled the NEET-UG held on May 3 for admissions to medical courses amid allegations of a paper leak, and a re-examination was held on June 21.
Education minister Dharmendra Pradhan later resigned over the NEET paper leak row following the protests. The chargesheet now places on record the order in which the CBI tracked and arrested those accused in the case.

headline: India maps 27 key Arunachal locations after China's repeated renaming attempts
full_text:
India maps 27 key Arunachal locations after China's repeated renaming attempts
The exercise was carried out in consultation with the Arunachal Pradesh government and is intended to ensure accurate identification of these places and improve public awareness, a statement said.
India on Friday formally marked 27 locations and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh on the official maps of the Survey of India, a move that comes amid repeated attempts by China to rename places in the border state.
According to an official statement, the exercise was carried out in consultation with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh and is intended to ensure accurate identification of these places and improve public awareness.
"The Government of India, in consultation with the State Government of Arunachal Pradesh, has marked a total of twenty-seven (27) locations/geographical features situated in Arunachal Pradesh on the official maps of the Survey of India, along with their standard names," a Home Ministry statement said.
"The objective of formally marking these on the Survey of India's map of Arunachal Pradesh is to facilitate their precise identification and foster greater awareness among the general public," it added.
The development comes against the backdrop of China periodically releasing lists of so-called standardised names for places in Arunachal Pradesh, which Beijing refers to as Zangnan.
New Delhi has consistently rejected these exercises, maintaining that they have no bearing on India's sovereignty over the state.
India has repeatedly described the Chinese renaming exercise as "vain and preposterous" and asserted that it will not change the "undeniable" reality that Arunachal Pradesh "was, is, and will" remain an integral part of India.
Among the places formally identified on the Survey of India map is Longju, located along the Line of Actual Control. Longju was one of the earliest flashpoints in India-China border tensions when Chinese forces entered the area in 1959. Nearby Maja village in Upper Subansiri district has also been included.
The notified locations include several strategically important high-altitude passes such as Dzo La, Riza La and Pukur La. Thag La, where one of the opening battles of the 1962 India-China war took place, has also been formally marked on the official map.
Jairampur in Changlang district, an important logistics hub that supports movement of security forces towards eastern Arunachal Pradesh and the Myanmar frontier, is among the identified locations.
Other places listed include Sambho Sarovar, a high-altitude lake, Bara Kundun, Chhota Kundun, Dhan Bari, Pritnagar, Teritnagar, Ramnagar and Jaswant Garh, which houses the memorial of 1962 war hero Jaswant Singh Rawat on the Tawang road. Villages such as Sagar, Padma, Jyotinagar and Baisakhi have also been marked.
The list further includes Sher-e-Thapa Memorial, which commemorates 1962 war hero Trilok Singh Thapa, along with Chhota Ropuk, Bara Ropuk, Shivaji Nagar, Sunpura, Kamlang Nagar and Buddhamandir.

headline: India issues names for 27 Arunachal locations in response to China’s renaming moves
full_text:
India issues names for 27 Arunachal locations in response to China’s renaming moves
India on Friday issued standard names for 27 places and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh located along the Line of Actual Control (LAC)
India on Friday issued standard names for 27 places and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh located along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), a move officials described as a riposte to China’s efforts to rename dozens of locations in the state in recent years.
Among the places included in the list is the border village of Longju, which has been controlled by China since 1959 but falls within the Indian claim line, officials said on condition of anonymity. The move is aimed at reinforcing India’s absolute sovereign and legal jurisdiction over these territories.
An official statement from the Union home ministry said the Indian government, in consultation with the government of Arunachal Pradesh, “identified a total of 27 places or features in Arunachal Pradesh, by standard place and feature names on the official maps of Survey of India (SoI)”.
“Identifying them formally on the Survey of India map of Arunachal Pradesh is aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public at large,” the statement said.
The home ministry said the locations identified on the Survey of India map include 21 land areas, four passes, a lake, and a monument. The land locations are Longju, Maja, Bisa, Bara Kundun, Chhota Kundun, Dhan Bari, Pritnagar, Buddhamandir, Jairampur, Teritnagar, Ramnagar, Jaswant Garh, Sagar, Padma, Jyotinagar, Baisakhi, Chhota Ropuk, Bara Ropuk, Shivaji Nagar, Sunpura, and Kamlang Nagar.
The passes are Dzo La, Riza La, Pukur La, and Thag La, and the list included Sambho Sarovar lake and Sher-e-Thapa Memorial.
An official familiar with the development said: “There has been a lot of ambiguity regarding the maps. China uses this to give fictitious names to Arunachal Pradesh’s territories, which are part of sovereign India.
“Putting these 27 locations on the Survey of India map provides clarity, makes our claim status strong and strengthens the official documentation of geographical features.”
Over the past few years, China has repeatedly announced its own “standardised names” for dozens of places in Arunachal Pradesh as part of its claims on Indian territory. China refers to Arunachal Pradesh as “south Tibet”, and there have been instances of Chinese authorities issuing stapled visas to residents of Arunachal Pradesh.
In November 2025, India registered a strong protest after a woman from Arunachal Pradesh was detained by Chinese authorities at Shanghai airport on the grounds that her Indian passport was invalid.
The officials said identifying a place on the Survey of India map gives administrative and governance value to it, as mapped places are easier to reference in land, revenue, and census records, infrastructure planning, and border road construction.
They also said the move is aimed at discrediting China’s efforts to assign “fictitious names” to places in Arunachal Pradesh.
In April this year, after China assigned names to 23 locations in Arunachal Pradesh, the external affairs ministry said such attempts to manufacture “baseless narratives” would not alter the reality and could even hit efforts to normalise bilateral relations.
External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at the time that India categorically rejected “any mischievous attempts by the Chinese side to assign fictitious names to places which form part of the territory of India”. He added, “China should refrain from actions which inject negativity into relations and undermine efforts to create better understanding.”
Jaiswal said such moves by China, aimed at introducing false claims, cannot alter the “undeniable reality that these places and territories, including Arunachal Pradesh, were, are, and will always remain an integral and inalienable part of India”.
China’s ministry of civil affairs — which is responsible for standardising the names of geographical features in “south Tibet” — had issued a notification renaming the 23 locations, including rivers, mountains, and towns.
In the past too, India has rejected China’s moves to rename dozens of locations in Arunachal Pradesh, including towns, rivers, and geographic features, arguing that such actions will not change the reality. China has resorted to such renaming exercises in 2017, 2021, 2023, and 2024, usually during periods of strained relations.
India and China are currently normalising their relations, which plummeted to an all-time low due to a military standoff on the LAC that began in 2020 and lasted more than four years. As part of this process of normalisation, the two countries have held talks aimed at resolving their long-standing border dispute.

headline: National Handloom Day: Govt showcases India’s tribal textile heritage through RISA

National Handloom Day: Govt showcases India’s tribal textile heritage through RISA
The event showcased several GI-tagged tribal textiles including Kotpad Cotton, Tussar Silk, Eri Silk, Muga Silk, Toda embroidery and Dongria embroidery.
On National Handloom Day 2026, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs and TRIFED showcased traditional weaves, embroidery and crafts under the RISA: Timeless Tribal initiative in New Delhi.
The event, organised at the RISA Flagship Store at the State Emporia Complex on Baba Kharak Singh Marg, highlighted tribal textiles not only as products of cultural heritage but also as repositories of indigenous knowledge, traditional skills and sustainable practices passed down through generations.
The event was inaugurated by Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs (STA).
As per a press statement issued by the Ministry, she emphasised the importance of creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for tribal communities through stronger market linkages, enabling them to establish a distinct presence in the niche textile segment and meet the evolving aspirations of a wider clientele. She further highlighted that tribal textiles embody generations of indigenous knowledge, cultural identity and sustainable practices, and reiterated that initiatives such as RISA provide an important platform for preserving these traditions while expanding market access and creating enhanced livelihood opportunities for tribal artisans across the country.
The inauguration was followed by a panel discussion on “What Makes Tribal Weaves Timeless?”, in which eminent personalities from academia, textiles, design, and crafts shared their thoughts and opinions. The discussion focused on how traditional knowledge can be preserved while introducing contemporary design and creating new market opportunities for tribal artisans.
The session was moderated by Smt. Asha Baxi, Founding Faculty and former Dean, National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT). The distinguished panel comprised Smt. Jaya Jaitly, renowned craft revivalist and Founder of Dastkari Haat Samiti, Shri Gaurav Jai Gupta, Founder and Creative Director of Akaaro, Shri Gaurang Shah, Textile Artist, Shri Ramesh Menon, Founder of Save the Loom and Ms Anju Modi, Fashion Designer.
The event showcased several GI-tagged tribal textiles from across India, including Kotpad Cotton, Tussar Silk, Eri Silk, Muga Silk, Toda embroidery and Dongria embroidery. Collections by leading Indian designers, including Shri Abu Jani Sandeep Khosla, Ms Anju Modi, Shri Manish Tripathi, Shri Gaurav Jai Gupta and Ms Sameera Dalvi, featuring textiles sourced directly from tribal weavers, were also displayed.
RISA also showcased specialised handicrafts, including Longpi Pottery (Manipur), Turtuk Brass Cutlery (Ladakh), Warli Art (Maharashtra), and the world-renowned Dokhra Art (Chhattisgarh).
At the event, tribal master artisans were felicitated, while visitors were given a curated walkthrough of tribal textiles and live demonstrations of Warli and Gond art on tribal textiles.

headline: Marking National Handloom Day, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday paid tribute to the State's weaving community, describing handloom artisans as preservers of India's cultural heritage and emphasising their role in carrying forw...
full_text:
Marking National Handloom Day, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday paid tribute to the State's weaving community, describing handloom artisans as preservers of India's cultural heritage and emphasising their role in carrying forward traditions that have been passed down through generations.Addressing a gathering in Lucknow after presenting the Sant Kabir State-Level Handloom Awards, the Chief Minister congratulated artisans across the State and linked the occasion to India's freedom movement."Today is National Handloom Day. I congratulate all the artisans across the state on Handloom Day. It was on this very day, August 7, 1905, that India's freedom struggle received a new direction," Adityanath said.He recalled that August 7 commemorates the launch of the Swadeshi Movement, which encouraged Indians to embrace indigenous products and reject foreign goods during the freedom struggle. According to the Chief Minister, the movement not only strengthened the spirit of self-reliance but also boosted confidence in India's traditional industries, particularly handloom weaving.The Chief Minister said the handloom sector is more than an economic activity.
It represents India's identity, craftsmanship and cultural continuity. He stated that every handwoven fabric carries the story of the artisan behind it and reflects centuries of skill, patience and creativity.Uttar Pradesh is home to several renowned handloom traditions, including the Banarasi silk saree, Chikankari embroidery of Lucknow, Bhadohi carpets and handwoven textiles from Mau, Tanda and Mubarakpur. These crafts provide livelihoods to thousands of weaving families and contribute significantly to the state's economy and exports.Adityanath said recognising artisans through state-level awards is an effort to encourage excellence while inspiring younger generations to preserve traditional crafts. He added that supporting weavers through government initiatives, better market access and modern technology is a priority.
National Handloom Day is observed every year on August 7 to commemorate the Swadeshi Movement launched in 1905. The day celebrates India's rich handloom heritage and honours millions of weavers whose craftsmanship continues to keep traditional textile arts alive despite changing market trends and industrialisation.

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Friday criticised RSS chief Mohan Bhagwatâs recent remarks on Gen Z and Gen Alpha, saying young Indians do not need his âcertificateâ or endorsement.Speaking to reporters outside Parliament, the Congress general secretary and Wayanad MP said, âThey don't need a certificate from RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat ji.â
Priyanka also said home minister Amit Shah appeared to be 'afraid' and questioned his absence from Parliament. Referring to alleged police excesses against students protesting over the July 20 paper leak issue, she said Shah should "come, give a statement, what is the issue with that. Something wrong happened, so take responsibility."
Her remarks came a day after Bhagwat interacted with members of Gen Z and Gen Alpha during a session at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC) in Mumbai. The outreach has drawn criticism from Opposition leaders, who have questioned the RSS' engagement with younger generations.Priyanka Gandhi's remarks followed a wider political response to Bhagwat's interaction. Bhagwat's interaction with young participants has therefore become a point of political debate, with Congress and SP leaders using the outreach to question the RSS' approach to India's youth.

headline: Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla criticises Opposition for stalling House proceedings
full_text:
Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla criticises Opposition for stalling House proceedings
Birla urged members to follow parliamentary decorum and said that democracy could be strengthened through discussion and dialogue.
Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Friday appealed to Opposition members to allow the House to proceed as protests over the NEET paper leak and alleged theft of Ram temple donations continued in the House.
Birla urged members to follow parliamentary decorum and said that democracy could be strengthened through discussion and dialogue.
However, as the protests continued, the Lok Sabha was adjourned till 12 noon.
Also Read: Lok Sabha proceedings adjourned for the day after passing Appropriation Bill
Addressing the lower house of Parliament, Birla said, The entire world, not just India, recognizes the contributions of the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi. This is why the world draws inspiration from him. You should also take inspiration from him. To empower and strengthen democracy within the country, engage in discussions, dialogues, and express your thoughts here. Question Hour is an important time."
Birla invoked the contributions of Mahatma Gandhi and the views of BR Ambedkar, saying that members should express their views through discussions in the House.
"Baba Saheb Ambedkar proposed the idea that if democracy is to be empowered and strengthened in the country, then discussion and dialogue are the way forward. I urge you every time, but your conduct is not in accordance with parliamentary decorum. You should reflect on this. The House is meant for discussion, dialogue, and especially during Question Hour, for the important questions of the honorable members. I urge you to let Question Hour proceed. You do not want the House to function. This behavior and conduct of yours is not appropriate. Please sit in your seats and let the Question Hour proceed. The House proceedings are adjourned until 12:00 PM today," he further said.
The Lok Sabha is scheduled to take up The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026 and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 for consideration and passing, according to the Revised List of Business.
Minister of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Jitan Ram Manjhi will move the Bill to further amend the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006, as passed by Rajya Sabha.
The House will also take up the Kashmiri Pandits (Recourse, Restitution, Rehabilitation and Resettlement) Bill, 2025.

headline: 'Fake News': MEA rejects report that India approached Israel for defence pact after Pak-Saudi-Turkey deal
full_text:
'Fake News': MEA rejects report that India approached Israel for defence pact after Pak-Saudi-Turkey deal
A Turkish media outlet, citing unnamed Pakistani sources, claimed India sought a defence pact with Israel to counter the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia-Turkey alliance
The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Friday dismissed as ‘fake news’ a viral claim that India had approached Israel to sign a defence pact in response to the recently announced Pakistan-Saudi Arabia-Turkey security agreement.
The claim was circulated by Turkish media outlet Straturka and amplified on social media. Citing unnamed Pakistani sources, the report alleged that India had requested Israel to enter into a defence pact to counter the trilateral agreement.
Fact-checking the claim, the MEA's Fact Check division shared a screenshot of the report and labelled it ‘fake news.’
"We caution against such malicious posts on social media platforms which use AI to create fake content!" the MEA Fact Check wing said in a post on X.
Saudi, Pakistan, Turkey sign defence deal
The clarification comes hours after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed the "Mecca Joint Defence Agreement", a strategic pact aimed at boosting military cooperation and collective security among the three countries.
According to Pakistan's foreign ministry, the agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence and states that "any armed attack against any one of the three States shall be regarded as an attack against them all." The pact also envisages deeper defence cooperation across multiple sectors.
Also Read | India reacts to Turkey-Pakistan-Saudi defence deal: 'Closely following the development'
Responding to the development earlier on Friday, the MEA said India was monitoring the agreement closely.
Addressing a weekly media briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, "This is also a development that we are closely following, and we shall keep you updated."
Netanyahu dials PM Modi
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Israeli counterpart Benjamin Netanyahu spoke over the phone on Thursday, discussing ways to further strengthen the India-Israel Special Strategic Partnership and reviewing cooperation across a range of sectors.
Speaking at the MEA's weekly media briefing on Friday, spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the call was initiated by the Israeli side. "During the conversation, it was discussed as to how we can further strengthen this bond, this friendship that we have with Israel across various sectors," Jaiswal said, underscoring the strong bilateral relationship between the two countries.

headline: Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren on Friday said his government was ready to continue dialogue with protesting JPSC and JSSC aspirants and was committed to introducing reforms to address their concerns over recruitment examinations.
full_text:
Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren on Friday said his government was ready to continue dialogue with protesting JPSC and JSSC aspirants and was committed to introducing reforms to address their concerns over recruitment examinations.
Speaking to reporters, Soren said the government had already established a communication channel with the students. “We have already specified a channel of communication. We are ready to talk. The government is keen to understand the issues faced by every student. We are now trying to take the students’ wishes beyond the confines of Jaipal Singh Stadium,” he said.
The protests are centred on alleged irregularities in JPSC, JSSC CGL and other competitive examinations, with students demanding greater transparency and accountability in the recruitment process.
Protesting JPSC and JSSC aspirants on Friday said state cabinet ministers acknowledged that several of their demands, including the cancellation of allegedly irregular examinations, were genuine during the first round of talks held in Ranchi.
Student leader Rajesh Prasad said the discussions were conducted in a cordial atmosphere and that the delegation had explained the basis of each demand in detail. “A 10-member delegation went for a meeting with the 4 Ministers. The discussion began in a cordial atmosphere, like speaking with one’s family. We listed all our genuine demands before the Ministers. We told them in detail the basis of the demands. They listened to us very carefully, and they said that our demands are genuine. The demand for CGL-JPSC (cancellation) is genuine,” he said.
Prasad said the ministers assured the delegation that the demands would be presented to Chief Minister Hemant Soren with due sensitivity.
Representatives of protesting JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand on Friday said their agitation would continue indefinitely after the first round of formal talks with a state government delegation failed to provide a definitive timeline for addressing their demands.
The meeting was held at the State Guest House in Ranchi between a five-member government delegation and a 10-member delegation of protesting students. The protests have been continuing at Jaipal Singh Stadium over alleged irregularities in the JPSC, JSSC CGL and other competitive recruitment examinations.
Student leader Ravindra Paswan said the ministers listened patiently to the delegation’s concerns but did not announce any immediate action plan. “Our 10-member delegation had the first meeting with the Govt delegation today. We listed out our main demands and explained them in detail. The Ministers listened to us carefully and assured that they would deliberate on our main demands. We said that until our main demands are met, our protest will continue,” he said.
Paswan added that the lack of a specific timeframe was the main reason the protests would continue. “We have not been given a time frame, but we have made it clear that the Govt should meet our genuine demands at the earliest. We will continue our protest until our demands are met,” he said.

The JPSC JSSC Reform Manch on Friday said protesting students had formed an 11-member delegation to negotiate with the Jharkhand government and demanded that all future discussions be held in the presence of the media.
According to the Reform Manch, the delegation comprises eight student representatives, one lawyer and two technical experts. The students argued that previous discussions held behind closed doors had failed to produce any meaningful resolution.
A meeting between a five-member state government delegation and a 10-member delegation of protesting aspirants was held at the State Guest House in Ranchi, where the students reiterated their demands regarding alleged irregularities in JPSC, JSSC CGL and other competitive examinations.
Representatives of protesting JPSC and JSSC aspirants on Friday said their agitation would continue indefinitely after the first round of talks with a state government delegation failed to produce a definitive timeline for addressing their demands.
Student leader Piyush Kumar said the proposed “Vidhan Sabha gherao” on August 10 would go ahead as planned. “Our proposal for ‘Vidhan Sabha gherao’ on 10th August continues to be. We are going ahead with this on 10th August. Until the last of our demands is met, the protest will continue,” he said.
He said a 10-member delegation had presented the students’ key demands in detail during the meeting and that ministers had assured them the issues would be considered. However, the protesters decided to continue their agitation until concrete action was taken.
The protests are being held at Jaipal Singh Stadium in Ranchi over alleged irregularities in JPSC, JSSC CGL and other competitive examinations.
Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Lok Sabha MP Nishikant Dubey on Friday said he would push for a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) inquiry into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in Jharkhand, asserting that officials responsible for administrative lapses must be held accountable.
Speaking to reporters, Dubey said the issue would be raised forcefully in Parliament because it concerned the future of students in the state. “We are raising this issue in Parliament. This matter concerns the future of the children of Jharkhand. We will try to get a CBI inquiry conducted into it. Jharkhand is a major source of revenue for the Congress,” he said.
The BJP MP added that a thorough investigation would be ensured through legal action, student pressure or public protests. “It is a question of Jharkhand’s students’ future. We will ensure a proper investigation is conducted whether prompted by court intervention, student pressure, or student protests so that no one dares to commit such an act again in the future,” Dubey said.
The protesters have maintained that their movement is centred on ensuring transparency and accountability in Jharkhand's recruitment process. They have demanded cancellation of the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission Civil Services Preliminary Examination, alleging irregularities in the conduct of the recruitment exercise.
Along with scrapping the examination, the demonstrators are seeking an independent investigation either by the Central Bureau of Investigation or by a panel of retired High Court judges from outside Jharkhand. Protesters have also called for comprehensive reforms in both the Jharkhand Public Service Commission and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission, arguing that repeated allegations of irregularities have severely undermined confidence among job aspirants preparing for government recruitment examinations.
In a key development in the protest against alleged irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) recruitment exams, agitating students on Friday dropped two journalists and a lawyer from the delegation set to hold talks with the state government.
The protesters have instead finalised a 10-member delegation consisting exclusively of student representatives. The members are Ravindra Paswan, Piyush Kumar, Rajesh Prasad, Neetu Kujur, Ankit Raj, Kartik Soren, Shalu Kumari, Ravindra Kumar Ravi, Anand Kumar and Ankit Kumar.
What began as a student protest over alleged examination irregularities has now developed into one of Jharkhand's biggest political controversies. The agitation has spilled into the Monsoon Session of the Assembly, with opposition parties staging demonstrations, demanding a CBI inquiry and accusing the government of failing to address students' concerns. On the other hand, the state government has reiterated that it remains open to dialogue while continuing the CID investigation. Hunger strikes, Assembly protests, planned marches and calls for recruitment reforms have kept the issue at the centre of public debate. With thousands of aspirants continuing their indefinite sit-in and opposition parties promising to intensify their campaign, the controversy is likely to remain one of the most closely watched developments in Jharkhand politics until a negotiated resolution or concrete government action emerges.
The recruitment examination controversy echoed inside the Jharkhand Assembly as BJP legislators staged a demonstration on the premises during the Monsoon Session. Opposition members carried placards bearing slogans such as "Stop selling students' future" and "Recommend a CBI probe into irregularities in JPSC examination". Several legislators also raised slogans against the Hemant Soren government, accusing it of failing to protect the interests of job aspirants. The protest disrupted the political atmosphere outside the Assembly as the opposition attempted to keep pressure on the government over the issue. The Assembly demonstration mirrored the continuing student agitation outside, highlighting how the recruitment controversy has evolved into a major political flashpoint in the state.
BJP leader Babulal Marandi intensified his attack on the state government by alleging that investigating agencies were attempting to shield those responsible for the alleged irregularities instead of conducting an impartial investigation. Addressing reporters outside the Assembly, he claimed the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) were protecting the government and the accused. "The investigating agencies are trying to cover up the matter. Whether it's the CID or the ACB, both agencies in Jharkhand are solely focused on protecting the government and the criminals," Marandi alleged. His remarks came amid opposition demands for an independent CBI investigation into the recruitment controversy. The government has not accepted these allegations and maintains that the ongoing CID investigation is proceeding according to law.
The hunger strike remained at the centre of the agitation as six protesters continued their indefinite fast demanding justice for job aspirants. Among them is JLKM leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been fasting for several days and recently agreed to consume water after social activist Sonam Wangchuk appealed to him over the phone. Protesters say they were forced to adopt the extreme step after repeated appeals to the government failed to produce meaningful action. Student leaders argue that the alleged irregularities have severely damaged public confidence in the recruitment system. They insist that only an independent investigation and sweeping reforms in Jharkhand's recruitment bodies can restore trust among thousands of aspirants preparing for government jobs.

headline: 3 NTA experts named in CBI's NEET paper leak probe chargesheet, may face life term if proven guilty
full_text:
3 NTA experts named in CBI's NEET paper leak probe chargesheet, may face life term if proven guilty
The chargesheet names Manisha Gurunath Mandhare, Prahalad Kulkarni and Manisha Sanjay Havaldar.
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has chargesheeted three National Testing Agency (NTA) subject experts engaged in setting the NEET UG 2026 examination paper, alleging criminal breach of trust as public servants and other offences in connection with the alleged paper leak case.
The chargesheet names Manisha Gurunath Mandhare, Prahalad Kulkarni and Manisha Sanjay Havaldar. The agency has invoked Section 316(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, relating to criminal breach of trust by a public servant, provisions of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, and other provisions of the BNS.
According to the CBI, conviction under Section 316(5) of the BNS carries punishment of life imprisonment or imprisonment up to 10 years along with a fine.
The agency further stated that offences under Section 11 of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 carry punishment of seven to 10 years' imprisonment and a minimum fine of ₹10 crore, if proved.
The CBI has charge-sheeted Manisha Gurunath Mandhare, under Section 316(5) of BNS, 2023, alleging that as a public servant/subject expert for NEET UG 2026, she committed criminal breach of trust by removing NTA's proprietary confidential material from its premises. The confidential question material entrusted to her constituted property of NTA.
Further, under Section 317(2) of BNS, 2023 for dishonestly received leaked physics questions from co-accused Manisha Sanjay Havaldar, knowing that it was property obtained through criminal breach of trust from NTA, and retained them.
According to the chargesheet, Mandhare has also been booked under Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(a) of the Prevention of Corruption Act for allegedly dishonestly misappropriating confidential NTA question papers for monetary gain.
The CBI has further invoked Section 10 read with Sections 3, 4 and 5 of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, alleging that she leaked confidential questions, colluded with others and provided leaked material and unauthorised tutoring to candidates before the examination.
Section 11 of the Act has also been invoked for her alleged involvement in organised criminal activity relating to the public examination.
Prahalad Kulkarni has been chargesheeted under Section 238 of the BNS, with the CBI alleging that he intentionally destroyed original question notes supplied to candidates after becoming aware of the offence. He has also been booked under Section 316(5) of the BNS on allegations that he removed confidential NTA question material entrusted to him as a subject expert.
The agency further alleged that Kulkarni dishonestly misappropriated confidential question papers for monetary gain.
CBI has further invoked Section 10 read with Sections 3, 4 and 5, as well as Section 11 of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, alleging that he leaked questions, colluded with others, facilitated unauthorised tutoring and participated in organised criminal activity.
The third subject expert, Manisha Sanjay Havaldar, has also been chargesheeted under Section 238 of the BNS on allegations that she intentionally destroyed original question notes shared with co-accused persons and candidates after becoming aware of the offence.
The CBI has further booked Havaldar under Section 316(5) of the BNS, alleging that she removed confidential NTA question material from official custody, thereby committing criminal breach of trust as a public servant.
She has also been chargesheeted under Section 13(2) read with Section 13(1)(a) of the Prevention of Corruption Act for allegedly dishonestly misappropriating confidential NTA question papers for monetary benefit.
The agency has additionally invoked Section 10 read with Sections 3, 4 and 5, along with Section 11 of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, alleging that Havaldar leaked questions for monetary gain, colluded with others, provided leaked material and unauthorised tutoring to candidates prior to the examination, and participated in organised criminal activity.

headline: Exclusive: DMK clears stance on delimitation bill amid buzz as Vijay calls MPs' meet
full_text:
Exclusive: DMK clears stance on delimitation bill amid buzz as Vijay calls MPs' meet
Amid strong buzz that the DMK has softened its stance on the delimitation bill, much to the unease of the INDIA alliance, Udhayanidhi Stalin clarified that the party had opposed the exercise from the very start.
At a time when the Centre has signalled its intention to reintroduce the delimitation bill, which it has linked to the implementation of women's reservation, the issue has become the latest flashpoint in Tamil Nadu. Amid buzz that the DMK has softened its stance on the bill much to the unease of the INDIA bloc, Udhayanidhi Stalin clarified to India Today that the party had opposed delimitation from the very beginning and "will continue to do so".
With differing voices emerging on the key issue, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay has called a meeting with state MPs to discuss the proposed delimitation exercise. So far, the DMK had not presented a stern stance on the bill amid talks of its revival. It had led to unease in the opposition, especially the Congress.
Rahul Gandhi, in a veiled swipe at the DMK, described the supporters of the bill as "21st-century Ettappans" - a term used in Tamil Nadu as a metaphor for a traitor.
DMK CLARIFIES ON DELIMITATION AMID BUZZ
A united opposition had defeated the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill in April, which proposed lifting the freeze on expanding the number of Lok Sabha seats.
However, much water has flown down the Cauvery since DMK supremo MK Stalin burnt a copy of the bill as a symbolic protest. The DMK exited the INDIA bloc at the national level after the Congress ditched the party to support Vijay's TVK in Tamil Nadu.
The delimitation bill seeks to redraw constituencies based on the 2011 Census. It will see the total number of Lok Sabha seats rising from 543 to 850.
Clearing the DMK's stance on the bill, Udhayanidhi said, "The DMK has always opposed delimitation. We will continue to oppose it in the future."
"This is not a new issue. The Centre is presenting it as if it has surfaced for the first time," the Leader of the Opposition in the Tamil Nadu Assembly told India Today.
Significantly, the clarification came hours after a report in The Hindu claimed the DMK has indicated it might support the delimitation bill if three changes were incorporated. With 22 MPs in the Lok Sabha and eight in the Rajya Sabha, the DMK is the fifth-largest constituent in Parliament.
The DMK has demanded that the 1971 Census and not the 2011 exercise should remain the basis for delimitation of the Lok Sabha for the next 25 years.
The party has also sought a blanket 50% increase in the Lok Sabha seats for all states. This was verbally promised by Union Home Minister Amit Shah when the bill was brought in Parliament in April.
Thirdly, according to the report, the DMK wants the bill to include a state-wise list showing how many seats each state will have following the proposed delimitation exercise.
Udhayanidhi's clarification on the DMK's position comes against the backdrop of the report.
THE DELIMITATION MUDDLE FOR TAMIL NADU
Now, why is Tamil Nadu opposed to the delimitation exercise?
The key argument of parties in Tamil Nadu and southern states is that linking the delimitation exercise to population would unfairly benefit the North, where population growth has been higher. The southern states have historically performed better in population control.
The South fears it will lead to a smaller increase in seats than the northern states, where the BJP wields influence. This will not only result in the South losing its voice in Parliament, but it may also lose out on tax devolution.
The five southern states - Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Telangana - account for around 24% of the population.
Now, let's understand the math.
Presently, Tamil Nadu has 39 Lok Sabha seats. Its share in Parliament is 7.2%. If the strength of each state is increased by 50%, as demanded by the DMK and other parties, Tamil Nadu will have 59 seats.
WHY UNIFORM INCREASE WON'T SOLVE PROBLEM
Even then, a uniform increase in Lok Sabha seats will substantially enhance the political weight of larger states, most of which are in the north.
This was very well portrayed by Kerala MP Shashi Tharoor via a salary analogy on X in his reply to Andhra Pradesh MP Chandrababu Naidu.
"Say your salary is Rs 2 lakh, and your driver's is Rs 20,000. A 50% increase will take your salary to Rs 3 lakh and that of your driver's to Rs 30,000. The percentage increase is the same - but aren't you much better off than your driver?" Tharoor said in a post in June.
Now, let's apply the same logic to Lok Sabha seats. A 50% increase will take Uttar Pradesh's representation from 80 MPs to 120. But a similar increase will take the number of MPs from Kerala to 30 from 20. This, in fact, takes the gap in MPs between UP and a southern state like Kerala from 60 to 90.
CM VIJAY CALLS MEETING OF MPs
Meanwhile, Chief Minister Vijay will hold a meeting with MPs from the state on Saturday to discuss the proposed delimitation bill and its potential impact on the state. Vijay had previously called the Centre's delimitation exercise a "biased move" and vehemently opposed it.
The meeting will be attended by both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs from Tamil Nadu. The move by Vijay to engage with parties across the political spectrum earned praise from Congress MP Manickam Tagore.
"Over the past 12 years, I have seen five chief ministers as MPs. However, this is the first time I have seen a Tamil Nadu Chief Minister take the step of personally inviting MPs from all parties for a consultation, without any political differences," Tagore tweeted.
"Everyone must stand together so that Tamil Nadu speaks with one voice in Delhi against the oppression of the BJP-led Centre," he further said.
Congress MP and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has already conveyed to Union Minister Kiren Rijiju that the delimitation bill was "not acceptable" to the opposition.
The timing of the meeting is crucial, with the DMK and the TVK being at loggerheads recently. The dramatic arrest of Udhayanidhi earlier this week over alleged vulgar remarks against actor Trisha, a close friend of Vijay, further added to the bad blood.
With the DMK having the largest number of MPs from the state, it is expected that the party would influence the outcome of the meeting.
(With inputs from Anagha)

headline: New Delhi: A day after Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat endorsed the role of Gen Z in the recent Cockroach Janta Party-led protests, BJP MP and actor Kangana Ranaut sought to make amends, calling them India’s ‘biggest strength’.
full_text:
New Delhi: A day after Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat endorsed the role of Gen Z in the recent Cockroach Janta Party-led protests, BJP MP and actor Kangana Ranaut sought to make amends, calling them India’s ‘biggest strength’.
Her latest remarks marked a sharp climbdown days after the Member of Parliament from Himachal Pradesh’s Mandi referred to “young Hindu women” who took part in the CJP protests as “generation gutter”. Some wanted to imitate independent career women without earning their freedom or accepting accountability, she had said.
On Friday, Kangana said it was wrong to judge an entire generation based on the actions of a few individuals. “Gen Z is a part of the government. Our government has been in power for so long due to the mandate of Gen Z. It is not true that only those 10-15 people who abuse during protests represent Gen Z.” She further cited the example of students protesting alleged irregularities in government recruitment exams in Jharkhand.
“Today, the students sitting and protesting in Jharkhand are conducting themselves peacefully and responsibly. Many young people from the country who have returned with medals have dedicated them to the Prime Minister and to the nation…there are only a handful of people who are damaging the image of Gen Z,” she said.
Earlier, the BJP leader had also accused student protesters of glorifying “drugs, drinks and endless body counts”. She even termed videos from the Jantar Mantar as “puke-inducing”.
Kangana made the latest remarks while accusing the Opposition of creating a ‘ruckus’.
“You can see the kind of ruckus the Opposition is creating and the extent of the loss the public is suffering; they are obstructing all the government’s work and refusing to give their consent for any of the bills that were to be introduced,” Ranaut said.
Her comments come a day after Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat addressed Gen Z and Gen Alpha attendees at a conference on ‘The Role of Youth in Uniting the World, the Indian Way’, organised by India’s International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN) in Mumbai.
At the event, Bhagwat said they should not be branded as anti-national if they take part in an agitation. The RSS chief’s remarks come days after the CJP-led protests—which originated in Delhi’s Jantar Mantar and spread across the country—ended on 25 July after the resignation of then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, which was a key demand.
Bhagwat during the interaction in Mumbai also termed protest as a way of dialogue and consensus-building. His comments were in sharp contrast to the reactions of some BJP leaders including Lok Sabha MP Nishikant Dubey, who alleged that “foreign forces hijacked the students’ outrage and anti-national forces were driving the movement”.
Dubey had also questioned sources of funding of the CJP-led protests.
On Friday, Ranaut praised Bhagwat’s views and said it is heartening that the youth are connecting with Indian culture. “Mohan Bhagwat ji is highly respected and we have had the opportunity to listen to his wisdom and experiences many times. We are very happy that the youth of the country, who are connected with us and represent our culture, are emerging as ambassadors of our heritage. This is a matter of great joy,” she said.

headline: AIADMK's boycott clouds CM Vijay's bid for united Tamil Nadu front on delimitation
full_text:
AIADMK's boycott clouds CM Vijay's bid for united Tamil Nadu front on delimitation
The AIADMK and the DMK will not attend Chief Minister Vijay's all-party meeting on delimitation in Tamil Nadu. Their absence exposes divisions over the Centre's proposed seat redraw linked to the 2011 Census.
The AIADMK has decided not to participate in Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay's all-party meeting on delimitation scheduled for Saturday, dealing a setback to efforts to present a united political front against the Centre's proposed constituency redrawing exercise.
The DMK has also decided to boycott the meeting, further exposing divisions among the state's major political parties over the issue.
The meeting was convened by Chief Minister Vijay to bring together Members of Parliament from Tamil Nadu and discuss a common strategy against the Centre's proposed delimitation exercise, which has emerged as a major political flashpoint in the state.
The latest development comes amid growing political debate over reports that the Centre is considering reintroducing the delimitation bill alongside the implementation of women's reservation.
The proposed legislation seeks to redraw parliamentary constituencies based on the 2011 Census and increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the current 543 seats to around 850.
WHY SOUTH INDIAN STATES OPPOSE DELIMITATION BILL?
Political parties across southern India, particularly in Tamil Nadu, have consistently opposed such an exercise if it is linked to population figures.
They argue that states which successfully implemented population control measures would be penalised with relatively fewer parliamentary seats, while northern states with higher population growth would gain a larger share of representation.
The issue had already triggered friction within the Opposition alliance after speculation that the DMK had softened its stand on the proposed legislation.
However, Tamil Nadu's Leader of Opposition, Udhayanidhi Stalin recently clarified that the DMK had opposed delimitation "from the very beginning" and would continue to do so.
The Congress had also expressed concern over the reported shift, with Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi taking a veiled swipe at supporters of the proposed legislation by referring to them as "21st-century Ettappans"—a term commonly used in Tamil Nadu to describe a traitor.
The proposed delimitation bill had earlier failed to secure passage after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill was defeated in Parliament in April.
'DELIMITATION MIGHT REDUCE SOUTH INFLUENCE'
Opponents argue that delimitation based on the 2011 Census would disproportionately increase parliamentary representation for northern states while reducing the political influence of southern states, which have recorded lower population growth over the past decades.
They also contend that a reduced share of Lok Sabha seats could eventually weaken the South's bargaining power in Parliament and affect issues such as tax devolution and allocation of central resources.
With both the AIADMK and the DMK staying away, Vijay's meeting is set to proceed without the participation of two of Tamil Nadu's largest political parties, underscoring the complex political equations surrounding the contentious delimitation debate.

headline: 'Our internal matter': India rebuffs US lawmakers’ criticism of FCRA bill
full_text:
'Our internal matter': India rebuffs US lawmakers’ criticism of FCRA bill
Lawmakers from US have criticised the proposed changes to the FCRA on the grounds that they could hit Christian organisations and other civil society groups.
India on Friday pushed back against criticism by American lawmakers of proposed changes to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA), saying this is an internal matter and pointing out that even the US has regulations to control the flow of foreign funding.
Lawmakers from the Democratic and Republican parties in the US have criticised the proposed changes to the FCRA on the grounds that they could hit Christian organisations and other civil society groups by preventing access to foreign funding and lead to their assets being seized.
External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told a regular media briefing that the proposed changes to the FCRA are an internal legislative issue that can be decided only by India’s Parliament.

“We have seen the comments [critical of the proposed changes]. Legislative matters concerning India are our internal affairs, on which decisions are taken by the Parliament of our country,” Jaiswal said.
“I would also like to point out that there are several nations, including the United States, which regulate the flow of foreign funds.”

US lawmakers' criticism of planned changes to FCRA
Several influential US lawmakers have criticised the planned changes to the law in recent days. Senator James Risch, who heads the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, described the proposed amendments as “deeply concerning”.
Republican Congressman Riley Moore, in a recent social media post, claimed that the proposed amendments to the FCRA would “permit government takeovers of churches and religious charities”. He added, “This is a clear attack against Christians. If this bill proceeds in this way, it would be a point of major concern in our bilateral relationship with India.”
Risch also said the US would not “hesitate to call out countries who violate the internationally recognised human rights of Christians and other religious groups around the world”.
Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026
The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, has been introduced in the Lok Sabha but is yet to be taken up for discussion. The bill states that when FCRA licences aren’t renewed, foreign contributions and assets of an entity will “provisionally” go to a “Designated Authority” notified by the government. If the entity cannot secure a fresh registration within a prescribed period, the foreign contributions and assets will vest permanently with the authority, which will use them for public purposes.

Union home minister Amit Shah has met chief minister Lalduhoma of Mizoram, a Christian-majority state, and representatives of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of India (CBCI) to discuss concerns about the proposed changes to the FCRA and assured them that the proposed law will not apply retrospectively.
The CBCI has expressed concerns that the proposed changes can “affect charitable institutions that have served poor and vulnerable communities for decades”. It sought safeguards to ensure that existing rights, legally acquired assets, and ongoing charitable activities are protected.

NEW DELHI: The protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Thursday, with students demanding action over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, while political pressure on the Hemant Soren government intensified.The protest, launched on July 25 under the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch at Ranchi's Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, has grown into one of Jharkhandâs largest student-led movements in recent years. headline: New Delhi: The Congress Thursday accused the government of weakening Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), alleging that faculty appointments made under Vice-Chancellor Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit violated mandatory University Grants Commission (UGC) re...
full_text:
New Delhi: The Congress Thursday accused the government of weakening Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), alleging that faculty appointments made under Vice-Chancellor Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit violated mandatory University Grants Commission (UGC) regulations.
The allegations were made by Congress media and publicity department chairman and Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera, who claimed the appointments were part of a larger effort by the Centre to undermine the university.
In a post on X, Khera alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was “anti-education” and had deliberately sought to weaken JNU.
“It is clear that Modi is anti-education. That’s why the destruction of JNU has long been one of his pet political projects. And appointing Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit as Vice Chancellor despite her proven record of ‘moral turpitude’ was part of that project,” he said on X.
Khera alleged that since Pandit took charge in February 2022, JNU had recruited “at least five associate professors and two professors in violation of mandatory UGC regulations”.
“With over 220 faculty appointments made during her tenure, the actual scale of the irregularities could be far greater,” he said.
“At least two serving teachers were appointed as professors through direct recruitment, bypassing the standard promotion process,” he added on X.
Khera also questioned the silence of Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, both JNU alumni.
“Both the Finance Minister and the External Affairs Minister are JNU alumni. It is a shame that they have acted as mute bystanders while the integrity of their alma mater has been systematically undermined,” he said.
The Congress has repeatedly taken on JNU V-C Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit since she assumed office in February 2022. It initially opposed her appointment, pointing to a past disciplinary inquiry, and has since raised objections over faculty recruitment, administrative decisions, the handling of student protests and disciplinary measures on campus. Most recently, the party demanded action against Pandit over her remarks on caste and the UGC’s equity regulations.
The criticism coming from the Congress is part of the wider accusation that the BJP-led Centre has increasingly interfered in the functioning of public universities.
ThePrint has reached out to V-C Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit on call, whatsapp and through her secretary. This report will be updated if and when she responds.

headline: Akal Takht panel seeks Punjab compliance report before anti-sacrilege talks
