headline: ‘Ask the mother who the father is’: Tamil Nadu BJP chief’s remark on CM Vijay sparks row
full_text:
‘Ask the mother who the father is’: Tamil Nadu BJP chief’s remark on CM Vijay sparks row
BJP leader Nainar Nagendran sparked controversy by targeting Chief Minister Vijay's mother, leading to criticism from political leaders.
Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagendran has triggered a political controversy after allegedly making a personal remark about the mother of Chief Minister Vijay.
Speaking at an event at the BJP’s state headquarters Kamalalayam on Saturday, Nagendran appeared to target Vijay while responding to the actor-turned-politician’s recent political remarks.
“When people search for a father in the House and cannot find him, they should ask the mother at home to know who the father is,” Nagendran said, according to news agency PTI.
Also Read: Trisha Krishnan sits with Vijay's parents as she attends Independence Day event in Chennai. Watch
The remark drew sharp criticism from political leaders, who accused the BJP state chief of crossing the limits of political discourse and making a derogatory personal comment.
According to local media, a complaint has been filed against Nagendran at the DGP Office.
What Vijay said in Assembly
Nagendran’s remarks came in response to a “kutti kathai” (short story) narrated by Vijay in the Assembly. Vijay had used the story to take a swipe at DMK president MK Stalin after the DMK’s defeat in the April 2026 Assembly election, making an apparent reference to the whereabouts of an opposition leader’s “father” following Stalin’s electoral defeat in the Kolathur Assembly constituency. Vijay’s remarks had earlier drawn criticism from several political parties.
Responding to Nagendran’s comments, Minister A Rajmohan condemned the BJP leader’s remarks, describing them as “uncivilised and inappropriate” for someone holding a senior political position.
Rajmohan said Vijay had advised his colleagues to maintain civility in politics even when faced with provocation or personal attacks.
Former Tamil Nadu BJP president K Annamalai also criticised Nagendran, saying the state BJP chief had crossed the boundaries of political decency and civility.
In a post on X on Saturday, Annamalai said it was “highly condemnable” that political speeches were vulgarising Tamil Nadu’s political arena.
He said political differences and criticism of government policies were part of democratic politics, but targeting a leader’s family members, particularly their mother, was unacceptable.
Annamalai described such remarks as “low-quality” and “third-rate” politics, and said such conduct should not be encouraged among Tamil Nadu’s younger generation.
He also said political leaders should not set an example of such behaviour for children in the state.

headline: Jharkhand protest: Students demand CM Hemant Soren's resignation, ask Congress to ‘withdraw support’

Jharkhand protest: Students demand CM Hemant Soren's resignation, ask Congress to ‘withdraw support’
The protesters announced that they will burn effigies of Soren and Rahul Gandhi on Sunday. They also said that they will gherao the CM's residence on August 20.
Students protesting against alleged job and exam irregularities have demanded Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren's resignation, accusing Congress and JMM of playing politics.
According to a report by news agency PTI, the students have also demanded that Congress withdraw support from the JMM-led coalition if the Jharkhand CM does not listen to them.
The protesters announced on Saturday that they will burn effigies of Soren and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on August 16. The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch also said that it will gherao the CM's residence on August 20.
Deep Dive
The students have been protesting over alleged irregularities in examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC. They were demanding cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination.
Hemant Soren's assurance
Hemant Soren, on Saturday, assured that the state government was working to ensure transparency in examinations, especially those conducted by bodies such as the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).
"For me, the youth of the state are very important to me and their faith in us. We have decided to bring changes in the system. Transparent examination will be ensured," Soren said while addressing the gathering at a state-level Independence Day celebration.
He said that the state government has initiated "Chhatron Ki Baat - Chhatron Ke Sath" and sought their suggestions to improve the education system. He said that students' contributions remain crucial to establishing a "good education system".
The Jharkhand CM told the youth to have faith in the state government and assured that "talent will not be allowed to go to waste due to mafia". He also said that transparent examinations will be ensured in the future.
"I want to urge the youth that their dreams will be protected. I want to assure that talent will not be allowed to go to waste due to the mafia. This is a serious challenge before the nation. For me, the youth of the state are very important to me and their faith on us. We have decided to bring changes in the system. Transparent examination will be ensured," Soren said.
Congress leader backs Soren
Congress leader Rajesh Thakur Hemant Soren's remarks on alleged irregularities in the JPSC-JSSC recruitment process, saying the Chief Minister had acknowledged the issue and assured students that steps would be taken to address it.

headline: What is PM Modi's 'Saptadhara' plan to achieve Viksit Bharat: Explained
full_text:
What is PM Modi's 'Saptadhara' plan to achieve Viksit Bharat: Explained
PM Modi said India must emerge as a trusted hub in global supply chains and stressed the need for Indian manufacturers to compete on cost, quality and scale.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday unveiled a seven-point ‘Saptadhara’ reform framework to accelerate India's journey towards becoming a Viksit Bharat by 2047, calling for sweeping changes in manufacturing, agriculture, technology, infrastructure, defence, the green and blue economy, and India's global influence.
Addressing the nation from the Red Fort on Independence Day, Modi said India needed a new set of streams of strength to drive its development journey, drawing a parallel with the ancient reference to the ‘Sapta Sindhu’, or seven rivers.
Follow live updates related to Independence Day here.
“Today, I would also like to recall that era when the nation knew, understood, and heard of India's prowess in the form of the 'Sapta Sindhu'. Now, to build a Viksit Bharat, we need a new current. Today, from the ramparts of the Red Fort, I invoke the 'Saptadhara' of strength before the nation,” Modi said.
Deep Dive
“In the coming 5 to 7 years, what could not be achieved in the last 5 to 7 decades, through the prowess and power of this Saptadhara, we will give the nation new heights, new momentum, and the capability to surpass new goals,” he added.
The seven streams outlined by Modi are Manufacturing Power; Agriculture and Food Processing; Technology and Innovation; Gati Shakti; Defence Shakti and Aatmanirbhar Defence; Green Economy and Blue Economy; and India's Soft Power.
ALSO READ | PM Modi announces free online coaching for competitive exams in Independence Day speech
1. Manufacturing Power
Modi said India must take its manufacturing sector to a new level and become a trusted hub in global supply chains.
“When I speak of the Saptadhara, the first stream of strength is manufacturing power,” Modi said.
He called for the entire value chain, from components and design to finished products, to be developed within India. He said Indian manufacturing must compete globally on cost, quality and scale, with zero-defect and precision manufacturing becoming India's identity.
2. Agriculture & Food Processing
The second stream focuses on agriculture and food processing, with the aim of positioning India as a global food powerhouse.
Modi linked the sector to India's export ambitions and the need to create greater value from agricultural production. He also highlighted the government's efforts to protect farmers from volatility in global fertiliser prices.
He said a bag of urea that costs around ₹3,000 in the international market is being provided to Indian farmers for ₹300. Similarly, DAP, which he said costs around ₹5,000 in the global market, is being provided at ₹1,350.
3. Technology & Innovation
Technology and innovation form the third stream of the Saptadhara, with Modi positioning them as key drivers of India's future growth.
The focus is on strengthening India's technological capabilities and ensuring that innovation becomes an important engine of the Viksit Bharat journey.
4. Gati Shakti
The fourth stream is Gati Shakti, centred on building world-class, high-speed connectivity and infrastructure.
Modi said seamless connectivity would be critical to India's economic expansion, helping goods, services and people move faster while strengthening the country's infrastructure and competitiveness.
5. Defence Shakti & Aatmanirbhar Defence
The fifth stream is Defence Shakti and Aatmanirbhar Defence, aimed at strengthening India's national security through self-reliance.
Modi's emphasis on defence self-reliance comes amid his broader argument that countries are increasingly seeking to secure their own strategic resources and supplies.
He said resources ranging from petrol and diesel to fertilisers, medicines and technology chips were being “weaponised” globally. In such an environment, he argued, India's push for self-reliance had become increasingly important.
6. Green Economy & Blue Economy
The sixth stream combines the green economy and blue economy, focusing on sustainable growth across India's land and maritime sectors.
Modi also highlighted the potential for India's vast coastline and fishing communities to benefit from expanding global trade opportunities.
He cited India's free trade agreements and said sectors such as seafood could use greater access to international markets to increase exports.
7. India's Soft Power
The seventh stream is India's soft power, reflecting the country's ambition to expand its global cultural and diplomatic influence.
He said India had entered into FTA agreements with nearly 40 countries since 2014 and urged Indian businesses, particularly MSMEs, to seize the opportunity to take Indian products to global markets.
“Every Indian product must reach global markets,” Modi said, while stressing that Indian products would need to meet global standards on quality and price.
‘Reform Express’ to accelerate Viksit Bharat journey
Modi said achieving the goal of a developed India by 2047 would require a change in India's work culture, thinking and pace of execution.
“We will have to reform our traditional systems. We will have to reform our thinking. We will have to reform the way we set our goals. And therefore, my dear countrymen, we will have to move forward with a clear direction,” he said.
Calling the initiative a “Reform Express”, Modi said the next five to seven years would be crucial.
“The work that was not done in the past five to seven decades has to be completed in the coming five to seven years,” he said.
The Prime Minister expressed confidence in India's youth, women, farmers and workers, saying their energy and capabilities would be fully harnessed for nation-building as India works towards the Viksit Bharat@2047 goal.

headline: ‘His health is priority’: Jharkhand Congress leader defends police stopping Mahto from Tiranga Yatra
full_text:
‘His health is priority’: Jharkhand Congress leader defends police stopping Mahto from Tiranga Yatra
Jharkhand Congress leader Kumar Raja accused the BJP of trying to politicise the issue and said the party was “playing politics over dead bodies”.
Jharkhand Congress leader Kumar Raja on Saturday defended the decision to stop student leader Devendra Nath Mahto from leaving Sadar Hospital in Ranchi to participate in a Tiranga Yatra, saying his health should take 'priority over political point-scoring'.
Raja accused the BJP of trying to politicise the issue and said the party was “playing politics over dead bodies”, news agency PTI reported.
“BJP is a party that plays politics over dead bodies; they are uneducated and boorish,” Raja said, reacting to the controversy over Mahto being stopped at the hospital.
Deep Dive
Mahto, who has been on an indefinite hunger strike since August 2, entered the 14th day of his protest on Saturday. He was admitted to Sadar Hospital after a Ranchi Vidhan Sabha Gherao march turned chaotic, with police using lathicharge, tear gas and water cannons against protesting students.
Raja said talks between the government and the protesting students were underway and that officials were regularly monitoring Mahto’s health.
“Consider this individual: he has been on a hunger strike for 11-12 days, and talks with the government are ongoing. The government is sensitive to the situation; officials are visiting him regularly. We, too, are meeting him because we are concerned about Devendra's health,” he told ANI.
“If he were to step out in his current medical condition, he could face serious complications. For us, his health is a higher priority than scoring political points. The BJP is trying to politicize this issue,” Raja added.
Heavy police deployment outside hospital
Earlier on Saturday, Mahto alleged that a heavy police deployment had been placed outside his hospital room after he expressed his desire to participate in the Independence Day flag-hoisting and Tricolour March at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, the main protest site.
“After expressing my desire to participate in the flag hoisting and Tricolour March organised at the protest site, Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, a heavy police force has been deployed outside my room in the Sadar Hospital. What kind of freedom is this, after all?” Mahto posted on X.
“Are we not even free to hoist the Tricolour and participate in the Tricolour March in our own country? Despite the difficult circumstances, I want to join this program in a peaceful manner,” he said.
Jharkhand student protest
Thousands of students have been protesting at the stadium over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission.
Meanwhile, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren said the state government was committed to ensuring transparency in examinations.
“For me, the youth of the state are very important to me and their faith in us. We have decided to bring changes in the system. Transparent examination will be ensured,” Soren said at a state-level Independence Day event.
Soren also said the government had launched “Chhatron Ki Baat - Chhatron Ke Sath” to seek students’ suggestions on improving the education system.
Student leader Ravinder Paswan said protesters would focus on celebrating Independence Day and would refrain from raising their demands with the government on the occasion.

full_text:
Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been undergoing treatment at Ranchi Sadar Hospital, has slammed the police for stopping him when he tried to take part in the Tiranga Yatra organised by the protesting students on the occasion of 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026.
Mr. Mahto, who is leading the faction of JPSC-JSSC Nyay Manch, has been on a hunger strike for the past 14 days in support of the demands raised by the students over alleged irregularities in the recruitment examination in Jharkhand.

When the police did not allow him to leave the room where he was admitted, an altercation took place between police personnel and Mr. Mahto. The JLKM leader alleged that he sustained an injury to his chest while being stopped and jostled by the police. Mr. Mahto also alleged that the police assaulted and beat up his associates who came to rescue him.
He also shared the footage of the altercation on his official social media account.
“For 14 days, I have been on a hunger strike, and today the police tried to push and forcefully stop me along with my companions. The police also assaulted my people who were with me. Despite being hungry for several days, I stand firm for my rights and the voice of the people. They cannot silence our voice by stopping us in this manner,” Mr. Mahto wrote on X.
Police action ‘raises serious questions’
He further said, “Despite being on a hunger strike for 14 days, the way the entire police force came down aggressively just for expressing a desire to hoist the national flag and participate in the Tiranga Yatra raises several serious questions on this day of Independence. During this time, my people were also brutally beaten and thrashed to the ground. Is this the free India we gained from the sacrifices of Lord Birsa Munda and Bhagat Singh? Is this the form of India that Subhas Chandra Bose, Khudiram Bose, Chandrashekhar Azad, Mahatma Gandhi, and Baba Saheb Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar dreamed of?”
After the alleged assault, Mr. Mahto, along with his people, sat down on dharna right outside his room.
“Until I am allowed to leave from here, I will keep sitting right here. I will not even get my treatment done, and I will stay here to raise my concern. My fight is for the rights of the people and for justice. They (Police) cannot silence my voice by stopping me,”Mr. Mahto said.
Later, he spoke to his party supremo and MLA Tiger Jairam Mahto over a video call and narrated his ordeal, how he was stopped by the police and allegedly assaulted.
“The answer will be sought from the government on the floor of the House. On the 80th Independence Day in free India, why was a protester, who has been on a hunger strike for 14 days, prevented from hoisting the flag? Why was he stopped from joining the Tiranga Yatra? And why is he not being given the freedom to seek treatment as per his own wish? The answer to all these questions will be sought from the government on the floor of the house,” Mr. Mahto said in the post later in the day.

headline: NEW DELHI: A political row erupted on Saturday over the rendition of the full version of Vande Mataram at the Congress's Independence Day event, with the BJP accusing grand old party's former chief Sonia Gandhi of objecting to the national song and t...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: A political row erupted on Saturday over the rendition of the full version of Vande Mataram at the Congress's Independence Day event, with the BJP accusing grand old party's former chief Sonia Gandhi of objecting to the national song and the opposition party rejecting the allegation.The BJP shared video footage from the Congress's event at Indira Bhawan and alleged that Sonia questioned party workers while Vande Mataram was being played. Congress, however, said there was no attempt to stop the full rendition and that Sonia was merely asking for a chair for party president Mallikarjun Kharge, who had been standing for some time.
BJP spokesperson Gopal Krishna Agarwal, sharing the footage on X, accused the Congress of showing disrespect towards the national song. "The scene that has come to light today on Independence Day is utterly shameful."He said, "Sonia Gandhi's objection during the rendition of India's national song, 'Vande Mataram', and her questioning of Congress workers as to why it was being played exposes the Congress party's mindset."Agarwal said Vande Mataram represented more than a patriotic song, calling it a symbol of India's freedom struggle and national consciousness.
"Is this the same Congress that lays claim to the legacy of the nation's freedom struggle?" he asked.He also alleged that the Congress's alleged approach towards the national song reflected the party's "Emergency mindset"."The people of the country have rejected this mindset and will continue to reject it," he said.
Congress rejects BJP's allegation
The Congress dismissed the BJP's claim and maintained that the full version of Vande Mataram was sung at its Independence Day programme.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh cited the party's historical association with the song and referred to a 1937 meeting of the Congress Working Committee in Calcutta, attended by several prominent leaders of the freedom movement."On October 28, 1937, in Calcutta, a meeting of the Congress Working Committee was held in the presence of Mahatma Gandhi, Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, Jawaharlal Nehru, Govind Ballabh Pant and C Rajagopalachari, and on the advice of Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore, they decided that the initial stanzas of Vande Mataram would be sung at the Congress sessions," Ramesh said.Ramesh said Tagore had advised Nehru and Bose that the opening portions of the song should be used at Congress gatherings."Tagore gave the advice to Nehru and Bose that the first few paragraphs of Vande Mataram should be used, he said."We have been singing those lines in every session since them, our Seva Dal sings it, our workers sing it, there is no controversy over that," Ramesh said."He stressed that the complete version was sung at Saturday's event and said the issue had already been debated extensively in Parliament."This was discussed in Parliament for 16 hours. We put forward our views. I narrated the whole history around it which the prime minister and the home minister did not know. I informed MPs of the context in which the Vande Mataram decision was taken," Ramesh said.
"But today, at Indira Bhawan, the full version was sung, there is no question of a controversy over it," he added.Asked specifically about the BJP's allegation that Sonia had tried to stop the full rendition, Ramesh offered a different explanation for what was seen in the video."As the Congress president was standing for a long time, Soniaji was asking for a chair for him," he said.
BJP escalates attack
BJP spokesperson R P Singh also targeted Sonia over the controversy, questioning her alleged opposition to the national song."Why does Antonio Maino Ji hate Vande Mataram so much? When Vande Mataram was being sung, Antonio Maino Ji reportedly became so angry that she allegedly got agitated and asked her party workers to stop it. Why such hatred for Vande Mataram?"The row over Vande Mataram comes shortly after Parliament passed legislation dealing with disrespect towards the national song. The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, was passed by the Lok Sabha through a voice vote on July 30, a day after the Rajya Sabha cleared it.The legislation grants Vande Mataram a status on par with the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana.

headline: New Delhi: In his shortest Independence Day address in the past four years, Prime Minister Narendra Modi made a major outreach to the youth, stressing that the greatest beneficiaries of ‘Viksit Bharat (Developed India)’ will be the country’s youth.
full_text:
New Delhi: In his shortest Independence Day address in the past four years, Prime Minister Narendra Modi made a major outreach to the youth, stressing that the greatest beneficiaries of ‘Viksit Bharat (Developed India)’ will be the country’s youth.
The Prime Minister’s outreach to the young generation, including Gen Z, was amply clear as he mentioned the words ‘youth’, ‘young’ and ‘younger’ 43 times in his 75-minute speech. He used the term ‘youth’ 20 times, ‘young’ 22 and ‘younger’ once in his speech.
“When I speak of a ‘Viksit Bharat’, when I speak of taking the country forward at a rapid pace, who is the greatest beneficiary of all these efforts? Who is the greatest force driving these efforts? If there is one, it is the youth of my country, the youth power of the country,” the PM said Saturday.
His speech packed with announcements for the young generation assumes significance, especially against the backdrop of the protest that took place across the country, particularly in New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak and concerns about the integrity of other competitive exams.
The BJP and the Modi government faced flak over the condition of India’s overall education system and the lack of job opportunities for the youth. The protest finally concluded with the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan in July, but it also led to growing concerns within the party about its inability to connect with the aspirations of the youth.
In fact, the party had faced criticism from several quarters including from RSS ideologues such as Ratan Sharda, who severely criticised the BJP’s media team, including its IT cell, over its handling of the protests in New Delhi, pointing out that they had no idea about youth anger because they are not in touch with ground realities.
For the BJP that came to power riding high on the success of social media and WhatsApp, advice came from the PM himself as he directed his Cabinet ministers to become more active on Instagram, post reels, and use interactive sessions to connect with the youth—something he did himself to reach out to the protesting youth.
The PM, in his Independence Day speech, announced free online coaching classes for competitive examinations, showcasing it as a way to ease financial burden on poor and middle class families. In another outreach to the youth, Modi announced a programme to train one crore young people in AI skills over the next year.
Moving beyond Gen-Z, the PM extended his outreach to even children from Gen Alpha and announced a nationwide talent hunt for identifying sports talent.
It comes as the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which spearheaded the Jantar Mantar protest, has taken the shape of a pressure group and has launched the ‘School Thik Karo” campaign.
The campaign was launched after scores of Gen Alpha students across several states launched protests demanding better school infrastructure including clean water, functional toilets, roads, teachers among others.
Experts point out that the youth outreach announced by Modi shows that the government is thinking seriously about the growing youth discontent.
“The fundamental offerings and youth outreach announced by Prime Minister Modi in his Independence Day speech show one thing quite clearly: the government is thinking seriously about growing youth discontent,” said Sayantan Ghosh, political analyst and author.
He called the emphasis on AI infrastructure, online tuition for competitive examinations and job creation as important.
“The problem is that these themes have appeared repeatedly in election manifestos, government budgets and policy promises across states. Employment, education infrastructure, online learning and, increasingly, AI have become recurring features of political messaging. The real question is not what is being promised, but how much of it is actually being implemented,” he added, pointing out that the speech did not sufficiently address the question of accountability.
“The larger question is whether youth discontent will be viewed merely as an issue of jobs, education and technology, or whether the government is willing to understand it as a deeper demand for accountability and responsiveness.”
However, many like Yashwant Deshmukh, founding director of CVoter,
pointed out that it will also depend on whether these announcements help generate employment, something which has been a major concern for the youth.
The announcements, he said, were expected especially after the Jantar Mantar protest.
“The kind of anger the youth had expressed as long as these announcements practically result in generating jobs, and new opportunities, it will definitely have some impact. However, if it remains rhetorical and on papers, then the issues will remain the same and so will be the concerns of the youth,” Deshmukh said.
The Mood of the Nation tracker has been highlighting that inflation and unemployment are major concerns and need to be resolved, he said.
“If every year these issues are coming up, then surely there is something wrong,” he added.
Social scientist and political analyst Badri Narayan pointed out that PM Modi doesn’t want to leave any room for uncertainty amongst the youth and is reaching out to even the section that was questioning the party.
“This is a positive step and we must welcome it. The BJP’s core support has traditionally come from the youth, and there has been some confusion among the young people, rather amongst a section, that the party is now trying to address which is what his speech indicates,” Narayan said.
He further said that while Modi’s popularity among the youth remains strong, he is also reaching out to the segment that had begun to question the party.
“We should welcome this effort, as it aims to rebuild trust and dispel the doubts that had arisen. A certain narrative has been created, and he does not want to leave any room for uncertainty among young voters about the BJP.”
However, Congress leader Pawn Khera termed the announcements as “too little, too late and too desperate”.
“Today’s grand announcements are just another Modi-era pipe dream with no real implementation plan. This is a desperate attempt to recover the government’s lost legitimacy by dangling fancy announcements before the youth,” he said.
“Free online coaching and AI sound impressive. But this government has a terrible record of last-mile delivery. During COVID, millions of students were left behind because they lacked smartphones, devices, electricity or reliable internet needed for online classes.”
Khera said these same students — those from marginalised backgrounds who most need support to complete their education in an increasingly extractive and exploitative system — are likely to be left behind again under this fresh push for online coaching and AI.
“In reality, BJP is a party of the rich, for the rich. It neither understands nor cares about the interests of the poor and marginalised,” he said.
Author and researcher Chandrachur Ghose said the PM’s address to the youth had two components.
“Firstly, reiteration of all the policies and programmes of the past decade to emphasise how these have opened new horizons in terms of productive opportunities,” he said.
“The second component was to present to the youth a picture of a whole new world of opportunities-expansion of infrastructure, focus on spotting talent in specific areas and providing training and development with definite goals. These opportunities would be in the form of integration with the new economy, deployment of new technologies and involvement in national service.”
Ghose pointed out that a few words on addressing systemic weaknesses would have given the picture of a promising future, a more solid grounding, but perhaps the speech from the Red Fort was not quite the occasion for it.
“The promises were finely balanced not to appear as an effort to counter the grievances of a section of students and youth, but to portray that despite the problem areas a promising future is waiting for them,” he said.
(Edited by Tony Rai)

headline: Addressing the nation from the ramparts of Red Fort on its 80th Independence Day, just days after massive youth protests rocked the capital, Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s speech included a seven-point economic reform plan and an outreach to Gen Z yo...
full_text:
Addressing the nation from the ramparts of Red Fort on its 80th Independence Day, just days after massive youth protests rocked the capital, Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s speech included a seven-point economic reform plan and an outreach to Gen Z youth, promising AI skilling programmes and free online coaching in an attempt to address post-globalisation anxieties. He also warned the country about the threat of “dimagi Naxals” — intellectual or ideological Naxals — in society, even after the eradication of armed left wing extremism.
At the first Independence Day that saw Vande Mataram preceding the national anthem, the Prime Minister directly addressed challenges facing the youth, from employment worries to the incursion of of Artificial Intelligence in everyday life.
More than one crore youth will be provided AI skills in a “mission mode” drive over the coming year, he said. India’s digital public infrastructure will be used to provide free online coaching to students wishing to take various competitive exams, and there will be a nationwide sports talent hunt among children between five and 15 years of age ahead of the 2036 Olympic Games, he added.
Mr. Modi recalled that, when he had first promoted his ‘Make in India’ initiative, advocates of globalisation had reacted as though it was heresy. In the current global economy, however, every country is thinking for itself, he pointed out.
‘Identify, isolate intellectual Naxals’
This acknowledgement of GenZ anxieties that spilled over into the recent Jantar Mantar protests was, however, spiked by a warning about “intellectual Naxals”.
“For years, people with a Maoist ideology had established themselves in the corridors of power and influenced policymaking, including as advisors on government committees. We have succeeded in eliminating armed Naxalites from the forests and freeing the country from that grave threat, but these ideological Naxalites are waiting for opportunities,” Mr. Modi said. “They are trying to revive the paths of violence and anarchy, and are making various attempts to drag society in the wrong direction. We must identify these ideological Naxalites and isolate them. At the same time, we must connect the country’s young generation with the mainstream effort to build a developed nation,” he added.
Freedom’s Progress Through the Years
He announced a full review and restructuring of civil defence infrastructure. “The nature of warfare is changing. There is no guarantee that wars will now be fought only along the borders,” the Prime Minister said. “A new form of warfare is emerging... Attacks can target a refinery, the banking sector, or a data centre. Infrastructure can be destroyed and factories can be targeted. We had announced Mission Sudarshan Chakra, [a multi-layered defence infrastructure system, with AI and cybersecurity components] last year, and work on it is going on rapidly,” he added.
“The nature of warfare is changing. There is no guarantee that wars will now be fought only along the borders. A new form of warfare is emerging... attacks can target a refinery, the banking sector or a data centre. Infrastructure can be destroyed and factories can be targeted. We had announced Mission Sudarshan Chakra (a multi-layered defence infrastructure with AI and cybersecurity components) last year (2025), and work on it is going on rapidly,” the PM said. A full review and restructuring of the way the civil defence infrastructure functioned would be undertaken, he also announced.
Economic reforms
A large part of the Prime Minister’s speech was devoted to what he termed ‘Saptadhara’ or the seven economic streams where his government was committed to reforms for growth. This includes manufacturing power with emphasis on quality; agriculture and food processing; technology and innovation as evidenced by the opening of the private sector for space exploration, and operationalisation of seven or eight semiconductor plants in the next year or two; the PM GatiShakti plan for multi-modal connectivity; enhanced domestic capabilities in armament production; a green and blue economy, with a coastline changed for full utilisation and increased energy storage; and the projection of India’s soft power, including via yoga, tourism, and animation.
The government has targeted the creation of 100 GW of nuclear energy capacity by 2047, Mr. Modi said, adding that five new reactors will be made operational in the next six to seven years.
Mr. Modi praised the government’s handling of the economy through several global crises. “After beating the COVID-19 pandemic, there was conflict and war everywhere. People had begun fearmongering. Many said there would be no vaccines, no one would be saved. They said no one would get fuel, diesel, fertilizer; people spread all kinds of rumours, and some people derived pleasure in this fearmongering,” he said. “However, despite these challenges, we have followed the spirit of ‘Nagrik Devo Bhava’ (the citizen is equivalent to God), and our preparations have helped us,” he added.

headline: NEW DELHI: More than 75 years of the Constitution coming into force, the derogatory practice of witch-hunting that targets defenceless women due to prejudice, suspicion, superstition and irrational fear, continues in the country, the Supreme Court la...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: More than 75 years of the Constitution coming into force, the derogatory practice of witch-hunting that targets defenceless women due to prejudice, suspicion, superstition and irrational fear, continues in the country, the Supreme Court lamented while upholding life term for two who murdered a woman in a tribal village of Odisha in Feb 1998.A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and N V Anjaria said the facets of the case had a disturbing impact on the court as a defenceless woman was branded a practitioner of witchcraft and was brutally assaulted in front of her daughter. âWhat effect it must have had on the daughter of the deceased who had to witness her mother being killed in the most brutal way,â the bench wondered.Writing the judgment, Justice Mishra said the malady of with-hunting continues to plague sections of our society, where prejudice, superstition, and irrational dear supersede the rule of law and constitutional morality.âThe brutality associated with witch-hunting extends far beyond the act of killing; where victims mostly women are subjected to torture, beatings, sexual violence and social ostracization. In such a situation, superstitious beliefs or fears are given precedence leading to vulnerable women becoming victims of collective hostility,â he said.IN Feb 1998, in the remote village of tribal inhabited Sundergarh district, one Manobodha Naikâs daughter died, and family members claimed that she died because of witchcraft practice of one Puni Naik.
Hearing this Udai Oram dragged Puni Naik to Naikâs house and with his associate, mercilessly assaulted her with sticks leading to her death. The trial court had convicted the duo in 2002, but the Orissa HC took two decades to uphold the conviction and life sentence.
Justices Mishra and Anjaria said, âSometimes in the most difficult situations, it often becomes an easy escape to blame a woman for the acts she did not commit, thus reflecting a deeply rooted social prejudice that often seeks scapegoats rather than solutions. In such situations, what can be given an ascendency is âreasonâ for reason is the only virtue that stands as a bulwark against collective irrationality.âSC said the Constitution guarantees equality, promotes fraternity and envisages citizens to adopt scientific temperament to rid the society of derogatory practices against women. âDespite this, practices such as witch-hunting continue to persist within a few sections of our society. A Constitutional democracy such as ours cannot survive; wherein such derogatory practices continue to elude the principles of rule of law and Constitutional morality,â it said.

headline: IPS Nupur Prasad, who led Sushant Singh Rajput CBI probe, to get President's Medal
full_text:
IPS Nupur Prasad, who led Sushant Singh Rajput CBI probe, to get President's Medal
Senior IPS officer Nupur Prasad has been selected for the President's Medal for Distinguished Service. The honour highlights her high-profile CBI tenure, including supervision of the Sushant Singh Rajput death probe.
Senior IPS officer Nupur Prasad, who supervised the CBI investigation into the death of actor Sushant Singh Rajput, has been selected for the prestigious President’s Medal for Distinguished Service this year.
Prasad, a 2007-batch AGMUT-cadre IPS officer, recently completed her tenure with the Central Bureau of Investigation and returned to the Delhi Police. She is currently serving as Joint Commissioner of Police in the Economic Offences Wing.
The award citation describes Prasad as an “accomplished officer” and a leader known for “versatility, integrity and institutional vision”. It highlights her work across the Delhi Police, CBI, West Bengal and Arunachal Pradesh, including several high-profile investigations and major policing initiatives.
ROLE IN SUSHANT SINGH RAJPUT DEATH PROBE
Prasad’s role in the Sushant Singh Rajput investigation was among the most prominent assignments of her CBI tenure.
Rajput, 34, was found dead at his Bandra residence in Mumbai on June 14, 2020. The Mumbai Police initially registered an accidental death case and investigated the circumstances surrounding his death.
The case took a major turn after Rajput’s father, K K Singh, filed an FIR in Patna against actress Rhea Chakraborty and others, alleging abetment to suicide, financial wrongdoing and harassment.
Following the legal and political controversy surrounding the jurisdiction of the investigation, the CBI took over the case in August 2020.
The investigation continued for nearly five years and involved examination of witnesses, scrutiny of medical and forensic evidence and investigation of allegations of murder, abetment to suicide and other suspected wrongdoing.
The case generated intense public and media scrutiny, with several theories circulating on social media and television, including allegations of poisoning and strangulation.
In March 2025, the CBI filed closure reports before courts in Mumbai and Patna, stating that its investigation had found no evidence of foul play, abetment to suicide or criminal conspiracy in Rajput’s death.
DISTINGUISHED POLICING CAREER
The President’s Medal citation highlights Prasad’s work across several challenging assignments.
As the first DCP of Shahdara, she was tasked with establishing the district’s policing framework from the ground up. During her tenure, she led action against drug networks and gambling operations and worked to make Anand Vihar a “snatching-free zone”.
As DCP, North District, Prasad oversaw security arrangements for major events, including Delhi University elections and Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort.
She also spearheaded community-oriented initiatives, including women’s self-defence training, hygiene camps in collaboration with the Ladli Foundation, youth skill-development programmes and drug de-addiction initiatives with SPYM.
Her career also includes significant assignments outside Delhi. In West Bengal, she handled security arrangements during the 2011 Assembly elections and the Ganga Sagar Mela.
As Superintendent of Police in Arunachal Pradesh, she worked to restore inter-tribal peace and dismantle extortion networks.
CONTRIBUTIONS TO POLICING REFORMS
During her CBI tenure, Prasad supervised some of the agency’s significant cases, including the AgustaWestland investigation and the Sushant Singh Rajput death case.
She also contributed to the CBI Crime Manual 2020 and the agency’s Vision Document. She was associated with preparations for the Interpol General Assembly 2022 and the G20 Cyber Conference.
After returning to the Delhi Police, Prasad introduced the MyKase software for trial monitoring while serving in the Economic Offences Wing.
She also contributed to the Bureau of Police Research and Development’s National Police Mission, Micro Mission.
PRESIDENT’S MEDAL FOR DISTINGUISHED SERVICE
The President’s Medal for Distinguished Service is among the highest service honours conferred on police personnel.
Prasad’s selection recognises a career spanning investigation, law-and-order policing, community outreach, institutional reform and assignments in some of the country’s most challenging security environments.
Her supervision of the Sushant Singh Rajput investigation remains one of the most high-profile assignments of her CBI tenure, with the agency ultimately concluding that there was no evidence of foul play in the actor’s death.

headline: A Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) event meant to commemorate the horrors of Partition turned into an unexpected display of the party’s internal fault lines in Gurugram on Friday, with Union Minister of State for Planning and MP Rao Inderjit Singh public...
full_text:
A Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) event meant to commemorate the horrors of Partition turned into an unexpected display of the party’s internal fault lines in Gurugram on Friday, with Union Minister of State for Planning and MP Rao Inderjit Singh publicly objecting to the programme being projected as a “community-specific” event and questioning why local leaders had not been invited.
The State-level Vibhajan Vibhishika Smriti Diwas programme at Sector 29 brought together BJP national president Nitin Nabin, Union Minister Manohar Lal and Haryana BJP president Archana Gupta. But the spotlight soon shifted from Partition remembrance to the politics within the Haryana BJP.
Taking the microphone, Mr. Singh made it clear that he was unhappy with the way the event had been organised. “People from various parts have come to this event. I think local people have not been invited today. I object to this,” he said, before thanking Ms. Gupta for inviting Mr. Nabin and turning the programme into a party event rather than allowing it to remain, in his words, a programme of a “specific community”.
Draws comparisons
Mr. Singh then directly addressed Mr. Nabin, welcoming him, while pointedly questioning whether he himself would have been invited had the national president not attended. The Gurugram MP drew comparisons with other BJP leaders. If such a programme were held in Panipat, he asked, would Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Bhatia not be invited? And if it were held in Karnal, would local MP Manohar Lal not be invited?
He also took a swipe at Mr. Lal, recalling that Haryana had been the first State to have a Punjabi Chief Minister and stressing that Mr. Lal had become the Chief Minister with the support of people from all communities.
Invoking Gurugram’s political history, Mr. Singh recalled that Dharambir Gaba, the city’s first Punjabi MLA, had won four times – not merely on Punjabi votes, but with support across communities.
“Most of those unsettled from Pakistan came to Haryana, and the people of Haryana welcomed them,” Mr. Singh said, underlining that Partition’s legacy belonged to the people of the entire State rather than any one community.
However, Mr. Singh’s address was stopped midway.
Sources in Mr. Singh’s office said the Minister had not received a formal invitation from the organisers, the Vibhajan Vibhishika Smriti Nyas. According to the sources, when the Chief Minister’s Office contacted Mr. Singh on Thursday afternoon to confirm his participation, his staff pointed out that no formal invitation had been received. The issue reportedly prompted administrative intervention. Ms. Gupta subsequently called Mr. Singh, informed him about Mr. Nabin’s presence and invited him to the programme.
An invitation letter issued by the organisers and shared by Mr. Singh’s office did not list the local MP’s name. An invitation issued by the local administration, however, did mention him as a guest of honour.
Convenor Bodhraj Sikri told The Hindu that the invitation letter from the district administration was forwarded to Mr. Singh on Thursday evening.

Armed Naxals are gone, but 'intellectual Naxals' still lurking; we must be vigilant: PM Modi
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said armed Naxalism had been curbed but warned that people with Maoist thinking were still present in different parts of the country and needed to be "identified, and isolated".Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the 80th Independence Day, PM Modi said the country had successfully weakened armed Naxalism but needed to remain alert against what he called "dimagi Naxals"."We need to identify these dimagi naxal, isolate them, and bring the youth together for a developed country," PM Modi said.PM Modi said Naxalism and Maoism had destroyed the aspirations of young people and kept large parts of the country under the grip of violence for decades. He also paid tribute to security personnel who lost their lives fighting the insurgency.
"Naxalism, Maoism destroyed the dreams of lakhs of youth. It stole the sons of numerous mothers, crushed the dreams of numerous mothers. This naxalism had kept a large part of India and population as a hostage for 4 decades with the barrel of a gun, they had destroyed the Constitution," PM Modi said.He said more than 3,500 security personnel had been killed while protecting citizens from Naxal violence.
"More than 3,500 security personnel were martyred while protecting the people of the country. More police personnel were killed than soldiers in war, police personnel had to put their lives on the line so that people can get security. This naxalism had covered the country in blood. In 2014, when you gave us the opportunity we had decided that we will rid the country of naxalism, and today I am happy to announce that naxalism does not have even the strength for breathing," the Prime Minister added.
PM Modi warns against âdimagi Naxalsâ
PM Modi drew a distinction between armed Naxals and people he described as "dimagi naxal", alleging that the latter continued to look for opportunities to promote violence and push the country in what he called the wrong direction."For years, people with Maoist thinking were there in public life, even in government committees this thinking had affected various institutions and initiatives. My dear countrymen, we have been able to curb and free the country from 'hathariya naxal' (armed naxal). Even if these naxals are gone, but the 'dimagi naxal' (people with naxal thinking), are looking for an opportunity, looking to see ways of violence, and trying to drag the country to a wrong path. We need to identify these dimagi naxal, isolate them, and bring the youth together for a developed country," PM Modi said.PM Modi said areas that were once affected by Naxal violence were now witnessing development, with the Tricolour representing progress and government initiatives flying in regions where armed insurgency had previously held sway."In the 21st century, it is imperative that we eliminate the decades-old challenges that have held the country back. Naxalism and Maoism have destroyed the future of millions of young people. They have snatched away the young sons of countless mothers and shattered the dreams of families across the country. For nearly four decades, Naxalism had held large parts of India and a huge section of its population in its grip, ruling through the barrel of a gun and tearing the Constitution to shreds. More than 3,500 of our police and security personnel sacrificed their lives while protecting ordinary citizens. Naxalism had turned the land red with blood."
âNaxalism is breathing its lastâ
PM Modi said the government had decided to eliminate Naxalism after coming to power in 2014 and claimed that armed Maoist violence no longer had the strength to sustain itself."When you gave us the opportunity to serve in 2014, we resolved on that very day to free the country from Naxalism.""Today, I am happy to say that Naxalite and Maoist violence no longer has the strength to sustain itself and is breathing its last. We are moving towards completely eliminating it. In areas where the bullets of Naxalites once rang out, where the soil was once stained with blood, today the same Naxal-affected regions are witnessing the tricolour of development, trust and endeavour flying high as they move towards becoming Naxalism-free."
PM Modi recalls challenges faced by India
During his Independence Day address, PM Modi also referred to challenges India faced over the past several years, including the Covid-19 pandemic and conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia."In the last 20-12 years, we have faced many dangers. As soon as we emerged from Covid, there was news of wars that started to arise from Ukraine side and West Asia. An atmosphere of tension prevailed. God knows what all the predictions the predictors made!," he said.
PM Modi said attempts were also made to create fear among citizens through rumours over the availability of vaccines, petrol, diesel and fertilisers.The remarks formed part of PM Modi's wider Independence Day address, in which he outlined the government's priorities and India's development ambitions as the country moves towards the goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047.

headline: Former Trinamool Congress MLA Nirmal Ghosh was mobbed outside a police station on Friday (August 14, 2026). A day back, he was arrested from Odisha for his alleged involvement in the ‘hurried’ cremation of the RG Kar rape and murder victim’s dead bod...
full_text:
KOLKATA
Former Trinamool Congress MLA Nirmal Ghosh was mobbed outside a police station on Friday (August 14, 2026). A day back, he was arrested from Odisha for his alleged involvement in the ‘hurried’ cremation of the RG Kar rape and murder victim’s dead body.
Mr. Ghosh was attacked right outside the Khardah Police Station as he was being escorted by the police to produce him at the Barrackpore Court in North 24 Parganas. He was wearing a helmet, but he was still subjected to physical attack, some threw eggs and muck, sticks, bricks, some also threw kicks and slaps. Many protestors carried garlands made of shoes.
The police tried to cover his head with a helmet to avoid any injuries during the transit. Mr. Ghosh was mobbed with “chor, chor“ (thief, thief) slogans outside the Barrackpore Court.
He was sent to 8 days police custody. He has also been accused in another case for allegedly stealing lottery prize money.
“Police promptly arrested the accused from another State. I appreciate the CP Barrackpore for their work,” Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Friday (August 14, 2026).
Commenting on the attack, Trinamool MLA Kunal Ghosh condemned the incident. “This cannot happen. How can the police allow this? The arrested person has not been convicted,“ Mr. Kunal Ghosh said. He also accused the police of being complacent in the attacks.
Nirmal Ghosh aide attacked
A former Trinamool councillor, Sanjib Mukherjee, a neighbour of the RG Kar victim in Panihati area, was also subjected to similar treatment. He was also being taken to court because he was allegedly present during the cremation of the victim’s body and was also known to be a close aide of Mr Ghosh. Mr. Mukherjee was also arrested on Thursday (August 14, 2026).
Mr. Ghosh, a former MLA from Panihati, also served as the chief whip of the Mamata Banerjee government. His son, Tirthankar Ghosh had fought the Assembly polls from Panihati and lost to the mother of the RG Kar victim Ratna Debnath.
Series of attacks on leaders
The attack on Mr. Ghosh is among the series of attacks that many Trinamool leaders have been subjected to in the past three months. After the Trinamool’s loss in the 2026 Assembly elections to the BJP, many of their current and former leaders, MLAs, former Ministers, and Councillors have been mobbed. Angry masses have raised slogans against them, hurled eggs, bricks, many were heckled, and some were also thrashed in public since May 4.
Among the top leaders, Trinamool chairperson and former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, general secretary Abhishek Banerjee, MLA Kunal Ghosh, and many others have come under attack. Mr. Abhishek Banerjee was one of the first leaders, who was showered with eggs and physically abused by the mob, after which the attacks have been consistent on the others.
Trinamool Congress leaders have repeatedly blamed the BJP for these attacks. However, BJP leadership has denied all such allegations.
The Calcutta High Court had also raised questions about the role of the State’s administration and the police for not being able to ensure the safety of the leaders.

headline: Cockroaches, expired food: Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart face Maharashtra FDA crackdown
full_text:
Cockroaches, expired food: Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart face Maharashtra FDA crackdown
Maharashtra's FDA has suspended 14 licences after statewide inspections found food safety lapses at quick-commerce facilities and other establishments. The drive also triggered notices, seizures, FIRs and a warning to food businesses to meet prescribed hygiene and storage standards.
Maharashtra’s Food and Drug Administration has launched a major crackdown on food businesses after a statewide inspection drive uncovered serious hygiene, storage and food safety violations at quick-commerce facilities, hotels, restaurants and other establishments.
The FDA inspected 86 establishments linked to online food delivery platforms on August 13, suspending 14 food business licences with immediate effect. Five licences were linked to Blinkit, five to Zepto, two to Instamart, while one each belonged to Bhagwati Store and Swinsta ENT Pvt Ltd.
The action came after inspectors found expired food products, poor temperature control, pest infestations, unhygienic storage, inadequate waste disposal and serious lapses in personal hygiene at several facilities.
14 LICENCES SUSPENDED AFTER STATEWIDE INSPECTIONS
Alongside the licence suspensions, the FDA issued 60 improvement notices and ordered one establishment to immediately halt business operations.
The inspections examined storage conditions, temperature control, cleanliness, pest control, hygiene of food handlers, FIFO and FEFO practices, food safety records and the display of FSSAI licences.
Officials said suspension action was taken against establishments where serious non-compliance was detected.
EXPIRED FOOD, COCKROACHES AND COLD-CHAIN FAILURES
At a Zepto facility in Pune’s Lohegaon area, inspectors found food products stored beyond their declared “Use By” dates. The facility also failed to follow FIFO and FEFO practices and had unhygienic storage, inadequate pest control and serious personal hygiene deficiencies.
The FDA said the company’s response during the hearing was unsatisfactory.
At Swinsta ENT Pvt Ltd in Warje Jakat Naka, Pune, inspectors reported cockroach infestation, inadequate cold-chain maintenance for frozen products, temperature-control problems and serious hygiene and pest-control deficiencies.
BLINKIT FACILITIES FLAGGED IN MUMBAI
A Blinkit facility in Malad West was found operating with a chiller-room temperature of 6 degrees Celsius, above the prescribed level.
The FDA also found that around 40 food handlers had not undergone medical examinations and that the required records were unavailable. Several workers were reportedly not wearing headgear, aprons or gloves.
Inspectors further flagged disorganised storage, damaged and rusted racks, inadequate segregation of vegetarian, non-vegetarian, cooked and dairy products, along with shortcomings in training and food safety supervision.
At another Blinkit facility in Ghatkopar, inspectors found inadequate drainage and waste-disposal arrangements, poor temperature control for frozen products and unprotected lighting fixtures in an unpacked-food storage area.
The establishment scored just 34 out of 74 marks, or 46 per cent, and was declared non-compliant.
ZEPTO, INSTAMART UNITS ALSO FOUND NON-COMPLIANT
At Zepto’s Mulund facility, inspectors reported inadequate waste disposal, temperature-control failures, lighting problems, poor cleanliness and inadequate separate storage facilities. The FSSAI licence was also not prominently displayed.
The facility scored 81 out of 180 marks, or 45 per cent, and was declared non-compliant.
A reinspection of Zepto’s Gola Unit in Goregaon also found deficiencies in temperature control, lighting, food storage, personal hygiene facilities and cleanliness. Despite scoring 98 out of 142 marks, or 70 per cent, the unit was still classified as non-compliant.
At an Instamart facility in Andheri, food packets were found stored directly on the floor. Inspectors reported inadequate storage space, congestion, temperature-control deficiencies and problems with lighting, cleanliness and personal hygiene.
The facility scored 76 out of 140 marks, or 55 per cent, and was declared non-compliant.
At Zepto’s Lokhandwala facility, the FDA additionally found inadequate temperature control for perishable food, no ante-room for frozen products, poor warehouse layout and improper segregation of food, non-food items and hazardous substances. The facility scored 65 out of 140 marks, or 47 per cent.
DELIVERY RIDERS ALSO UNDER FDA SCANNER
The crackdown extended beyond warehouses and stores to delivery operations.
At a Blinkit store in Karad, Satara district, officials checked 125 two-wheeler delivery riders and found that they lacked identity cards and medical fitness records.
The FDA also found that the principal food business’s FSSAI licence was not displayed on delivery carts, bags or boxes. The firm was directed to stop business activity involving two-wheeler deliveries until the deficiencies were rectified.
MILK PRODUCTS, BAKERY ITEMS SEIZED
The statewide drive also resulted in significant seizures of food products.
The FDA seized 698 kg of milk and milk products valued at around Rs 34,302. Another 1,270 kg of food items, including milk products, bakery products and edible oil, valued at approximately Rs 1,29,762, was seized.
The regulator said the total value of seized goods involving other food items and banned products stood at around Rs 46,89,603.
The drive also led to 10 FIRs over the sale, distribution and transportation of banned products such as pan masala and gutkha. Nine people were arrested and banned stock worth Rs 46,76,631 was seized.
109 HOTELS, RESTAURANTS AND DHABAS INSPECTED
The FDA also inspected 109 hotels, restaurants and dhabas as part of the wider crackdown.
Officials issued 49 improvement notices and suspended four food establishment licences. A total of 15 raids were conducted during the special drive.
BOLLYWOOD CAFE FACES ACTION OVER HYGIENE LAPSES
The FDA also conducted a special inspection at Bollywood Cafe, Studio Number 13, located in Dadasaheb Phalke Chitranagari, Film City, Goregaon.
Inspectors found serious shortcomings in cleanliness and food safety standards. The condition of utensils and the premises was found unsatisfactory, while a large-scale fly infestation was reported.
The kitchen was found with dirty water, accumulated dirt and food residue. Officials also found food being prepared on rusty and unhygienic food-contact surfaces.
The department directed the cafe management to immediately rectify the violations and strictly comply with prescribed food safety and hygiene standards.
The FDA said penal action was being initiated under Section 69 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
FDA WARNS FOOD BUSINESSES
The Maharashtra FDA said the action against quick-commerce establishments and other food businesses was taken under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the rules and regulations framed under it.
The regulator has warned food business operators involved in selling and delivering food through online platforms to strictly comply with prescribed standards for food safety, hygiene, storage and handling.

headline: The Nagaland Baptist Church Council (NBCC) has opposed the Centre’s order to play or sing the revised version of Vande Mataram, the National Song, at official events to mark India’s 80th Independence Day.
full_text:
GUWAHATI
The Nagaland Baptist Church Council (NBCC) has opposed the Centre’s order to play or sing the revised version of Vande Mataram, the National Song, at official events to mark India’s 80th Independence Day.
The church body’s opposition follows the Naga Students’ Federation’s call to ensure that schools and other educational institutions do not send their students to participate in the Independence Day programmes. The students’ body also said students who decline to sing Vande Mataram “on grounds of conscience or religious beliefs” should not face disciplinary action or discrimination.
In a statement on Thursday (August 13, 2026) evening, the NBCC said it was against any directive or practice that seeks to compel citizens, particularly Christians, to sing Vande Mataram. It maintained that patriotism should arise from willing participation and a shared love for the nation rather than compulsion.
At the same time, the church body called upon all stakeholders to express their positions peacefully and constructively, cautioning that disagreement over national symbols or patriotic practices should not become a source of communal tension or social division.
The NBCC said it fully respects national symbols, patriotic sentiments, and the constitutional values of India. However, it insisted that matters concerning faith, conscience, religious conviction, and deeply held identity require “the highest degree of sensitivity, wisdom, and respect.”
“National unity cannot be strengthened by compelling citizens to participate in an expression that, for reasons of faith or conscience, they may not be able to embrace,” the NBCC said, reminding the Centre that India was a plural and diverse nation.
“India’s unity will be strongest when every citizen, irrespective of faith, community, culture, or conviction, can say with confidence that there is a rightful place for them in the nation and that their conscience will be respected,” it added.

headline: A firing incident involving armed civilian members of the Village Defence Guards (VDG) left one dead and another injured in Jammu division’s Udhampur district on Friday (August 14, 2026).
full_text:
A firing incident involving armed civilian members of the Village Defence Guards (VDG) left one dead and another injured in Jammu division’s Udhampur district on Friday (August 14, 2026).
Preliminary reports suggest that a scuffle broke out among the VDG members, trained to fight against terrorists, in Udhampur’s hilly pocket of Pancheri area. Initial information suggests that one VDG member, Surjeet Singh, a resident of Sasri Damnot, fired upon two civilians.
One civilian, identified as Baldev Singh was left dead in the firing incident and another civilian, identified as Romesh Singh, was critically injured. The injured was shifted to a hospital in the district.
Officials said the firing incident was being investigated. A police team assessed the spot where the incident took place and “will prepare a report soon”, officials said. Initial investigation suggests that the firing could be the result of an “altercation”. However, the officials said the police were “still in the process of establishing the cause of the firing”. Meanwhile, the accused was on the run, officials said.
Second incident in two years
This is the second such incident in the past two years in the Jammu region. A woman was left dead in Kishtwar’s Chatroo area after a VDG opened fire in 2025. Two VDG members were kidnapped and killed by terrorists in Kishtwar in 2024.
Earlier known as Village Defence Committees, the civilian armed groups were first constituted in Jammu and Kashmir in 1995 in 10 districts of the Jammu region. The move was made after multiple terrorists carried out the killings of members of minority communities till 2006. Later, it was disbanded. However, after the Dangri attack in Rajouri in 2023, which left six civilians dead and injured 15 others, the Centre decided to revive these groups and renamed them as VDGs. Hundreds of locals in the Jammu region have been imparted armed training in automatic rifles by the security forces in the past three years.
Before 2006, around 26,567 locals were recruited into VDCs in the Jammu region. According to official figures, 160 criminal cases involving VDC members were filed in the Jammu region.

headline: Vande Mataram row: Amit Shah attacks Sonia Gandhi, Congress hits back, cases filed
full_text:
Vande Mataram row: Amit Shah attacks Sonia Gandhi, Congress hits back, cases filed
The development came days after Parliament passed a bill that makes any insult to the national song a punishable offence.
The controversy surrounding Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s alleged objection to the singing of the entire Vande Mataram song during the party’s Independence day celebrations snowballed into a full-blown political feud on Sunday, with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) staging protests across the country and registering complaints against the senior opposition leader.
The Congress has denied the allegation that attempts were made by Sonia to stop the singing of the full version of the national song at the AICC headquarters on Saturday. The party said Sonia was only asking for a chair for Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge as he was standing for a while.
The development came days after Parliament passed a bill that makes any insult to the national song a punishable offence. The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, was passed by a voice vote in the Lok Sabha on July 30, a day after it was approved by the Rajya Sabha. The law grants status to Vande Mataram on par with national anthem Jana Gana Mana.
Also Read | 'Vande Mataram echoing from Red Fort for first time': PM Modi leads 'historic moment' at Independence Day
Shah targets Congress
Deep Dive
The controversy broke out on Saturday when BJP national general secretary (organisation) B L Santhosh shared a video of the Congress’s event on X. "Mother, son and national president (of the Congress) seem to be upset by the rendering of full Vande Mataram,” he wrote on the micro-blogging site.
On Sunday, Union home minister Amit Shah said the Vande Mataram song was sung at the Red Fort and all other places where flag hoisting was held after 80 years of Independence.
"Thousands of people faced bullets and lathis and were jailed for singing Vande Mataram," he said, referring to the use of the revolutionary slogan during the freedom struggle. "We all saw it on television. Sonia ji, 140 crore (people) are watching you. The people of the country will never forgive you for your sin... If there is any shame left, you should fold your hands and apologise to Bankim Babu's immortal spirit and the people," he added.
The Vande Mataram song was written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.
Also Read | Complaint filed against Sonia, Rahul Gandhi over disrespect to Vande Mataram
Shah was addressing a public event at Chittorgarh, Rajasthan, when he made the remarks. He alleged the Congress had forgotten 'Vande Mataram' due to vote-bank politics.
At a press conference in the national capital, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said the alleged opposition to the Vande Mataram song pointed towards a mindset of a "dimagi Naxal ecosystem".
"Can any patriot, can any Indian who believes in the Constitution of India, respects the Tricolour of India, respects India's freedom fighters and believes in India's sovereignty and integrity, ever get angry at the invocation of Vande Mataram on Independence Day?" he said.
He also said the Congress government in Kerala crossed all limits by completely removing Vande Mataram from the Independence Day celebrations.
Bankim Chandra’s descendant joins protest
BJP MLA Sumitro Chatterjee, a fifth-generation direct descendant of Bankim Chandra, sought an “unconditional apology” from Sonia.
In a letter to the Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson, the MLA from Naihati in West Bengal said the incident had deeply hurt the sentiments of the people of the eastern state, and appealed to her to introspect.
West Bengal CM attacks Congress
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari also said the incident had deeply offended the people of the state, where Bankim Chandra is revered as "Sahitya Samrat".
"Yesterday was Independence Day. During the event at the Congress headquarters in Delhi, when Vande Mataram was being sung, Sonia Gandhi expressed her displeasure at singing the full version. The entire country witnessed this on live telecast," Adhikari told reporters in Kolkata.
He accused the Congress leadership of trying to explain away the episode and said video footage would establish what happened. "As Chief Minister, I feel that insulting Vande Mataram is an insult to Bankim Chandra himself. I strongly condemn this," he said.
Congress refutes allegation
The Congress denied the BJP's allegation that Sonia showed disrespect to the national song or attempted to stop the singing of its full version.
The party maintained that there was no attempt to interrupt the rendition and that Sonia was only asking for a chair for Kharge, who had been standing for some time.
Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh slammed Shah as someone who insulted B R Ambedkar on the floor of the Rajya Sabha on December 17, 2024, and who belongs to an ideology that did not see fit to unfurl the Tricolour at its organisation's headquarters till January 2002.
"A man who insulted Dr Ambedkar on the floor of the Rajya Sabha on Dec 17, 2024. A man who belongs to an ideology that did not see fit to unfurl the tiranga at its headquarters till Jan 2002. A man who orchestrated the Delhi Police's brutalities on peacefully protesting youth,” he said on X.
“Such a man is now demanding an apology from the Congress to divert attention away from the real issues of the day and away from the colossal failures of his and his Sahib's," he added.
Congress's media and publicity department head Pawan Khera said when lathis rained down for chanting "Vande Mataram", it was the Congress that had sounded the bugle of freedom through this song. "At that time, people associated with the Sangh either fled with their tails tucked between their legs or wagged their tails to please their British masters," he said.
Several Congress leaders also shared on social media Ramesh's speech in the Rajya Sabha on December 10, 2025, during a debate marking 150 years of Vande Mataram. Participating in the debate, Ramesh had accused the BJP of distorting history and insulting freedom fighters who sacrificed their lives for the country.
Complaints filed, protests held across country
Multiple protests broke out and complaints were registered against Sonia across the country on Sunday.
A complaint was filed with the Delhi Police seeking registration of an FIR against Sonia and Rahul Gandhi over alleged obstruction during the singing of Vande Mataram. The complaint, filed by an advocate, was submitted at the IP Estate police station on August 16.
The complaint alleged that Sonia made gestures after the initial portion of the National Song had been sung, which the complainant claimed appeared to indicate an objection to its continuation. It also referred to a video in which Rahul is allegedly heard saying, "We are not singing Vande Mataram."
In Bengaluru, the BJP Yuva Morcha (youth wing) lodged a complaint at the Malleshwaram police station regarding the alleged insult and sought legal action. The Yuva Morcha also staged a protest near BJP state headquarters in the Karnataka capital.
In the police complaint, the Yuva Morcha said the song played an important role in the freedom struggle and is presently the national song of India. It is required by the law of our land to be accorded the same respect as our national anthem, "Jana Gana Mana”, they said.
The BJP also held a protest outside the Congress office in Srinagar. The party’s West Bengal unit held protest rallies in Kolkata and Siliguri.
In Manipur, more than 50 BJP workers, holding the national flag and posters of Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, raised slogans and played the song on loudspeakers outside the Congress Bhavan.

headline: Bangladesh says PM will not visit India until Hasina extradited
full_text:
Bangladesh says PM will not visit India until Hasina extradited
Sheikh Hasina faces the death penalty in Bangladesh after being convicted of crimes against humanity, and Dhaka has repeatedly requested her extradition.
Bangladesh said on Sunday that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman would not visit India until New Delhi extradited Sheikh Hasina, the Bangladeshi former premier who fled during a 2024 uprising.
The countries have had a strained relationship since deadly anti-government protests brought down Hasina's government and prompted her to escape to neighbouring India, where she remains.
She faces the death penalty in Bangladesh after being convicted of crimes against humanity, and Dhaka has repeatedly requested her extradition.
Speaking to reporters on Sunday, foreign ministry official A.K.M. Shahidul Karim played down media speculation about a possible trip by Rahman to India next week.
"We are of the view that a propitious environment needs to be created for the visit," Karim told reporters.
"To this end, we have urged the Indian authorities to expedite their efforts to extradite Sheikh Hasina and other fugitives."
India has said Bangladesh's extradition request is "under examination".
Rahman took office in February and has since visited Malaysia and China, departing from the tradition of Bangladeshi leaders heading to India for their first overseas trip.
India's High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Trivedi, met Rahman last week, fuelling speculation over a possible breakthrough.
Officials from Bangladesh and India have been in contact in recent weeks about the possibility of a visit by Rahman, Karim said.
"But the process has been vitiated by Sheikh Hasina's open media interactions, despite her being a convict in crimes against humanity."
Hasina, a former pro-democracy leader whom critics said grew increasingly autocratic during her 15-year rule, vowed this month that she would return to Bangladesh in December even if it meant imprisonment.
Karim also said the government would pursue a "Bangladesh First" foreign policy rooted in sovereignty and non-interference while seeking mutually beneficial ties with India and other countries.

headline: NEW DELHI: National Testing Agency (NTA) on Sunday acknowledged that the UGC-NET papers in English, Commerce and Sociology had multiple errors and repeated questions, and said the defects were too extensive to be addressed simply by dropping question...
