Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
On China, Jaishankar said India should continue doing business with Beijing while developing the domestic strength needed to compete with it
NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Saturday offered a candid assessment of a rapidly changing global landscape, warning that growing geopolitical and economic tensions are creating new challenges for countries and businesses. He also stressed that India must remain engaged with the world's major economies while strengthening its own industrial and economic capabilities.Speaking at the Economic Times World Leaders Forum 2026, Jaishankar said the emerging global environment required countries to reduce vulnerabilities, broaden their economic options and prepare for disruptions rather than rely on assumptions of stability.
He framed his assessment around three defining features of the present world order: competition, conflict and the growing use of economic and strategic leverage. To navigate these pressures, he proposed a four-part approach centred on reducing risks, diversifying partnerships and sources, addressing market distortions and maintaining a margin of safety.On China, Jaishankar said India should continue doing business with Beijing while developing the domestic strength needed to compete with it. He said greater self-reliance, industrialisation and manufacturing capacity would allow India to engage China more confidently rather than disengage from it.
"We have to do business with the entire world. That includes China too. But it is important we deal with them confidently."Jaishankar said India-China relations had gone through a difficult period between 2020 and 2024 because of the border situation, but both countries had an interest in maintaining stable ties. He also said India needed to make up for decades of shortcomings in building its manufacturing and industrial base."So I think a stronger, more self-reliant India, a more industrialised India, a more manufacturing India will be able to actually compete with China as it will with other major countries of the world."
Jaishankar's 3Cs view of the world
"It's not a very comforting answer I'm going to give," Jaishankar said while describing how he sees the world today.He said the world had become increasingly competitive, with countries and policymakers pursuing their interests to a point where competition could turn into conflict."I think what we've seen particularly in the last year or so, but I would really describe it as a growing trend. It looks increasingly competitive," he said, adding that countries and policymakers were pushing their interests "to a point where you actually have conflicts."He pointed to the Russia-Ukraine conflict and the conflict in West Asia as major examples, noting that one had entered its fifth year while there was still no clear "light at the end of the tunnel" for the other.Jaishankar said competition was no longer confined to traditional geopolitical rivalry, with economic and strategic tools increasingly being "weaponised"."This is a world increasingly characterised by choke points," he said, explaining that such a choke point emerges when "a country or a set of countries have established dominance" in a particular field and are prepared to use that dominance to exert pressure.According to Jaishankar, such leverage can "inflict pain" on others, while countries exercising it may believe they are sufficiently insulated from the consequences.
The 4Ds response
Jaishankar then outlined what he described as a response to these challenges."If I declare the problems in terms of Cs, maybe I move an alphabet beyond," he said, presenting derisking as his first and "biggest mantra"."Derisking will be my biggest mantra," Jaishankar said, stressing that the principle applied not only to businesses but also to politics and strategy.His second D was diversification."The more partners, the more sources that you have, clearly extending that you derisk," he said, arguing that countries and businesses should avoid excessive dependence on a small number of partners or sources.The third was dealing with distortions. Jaishankar pointed to disruptions in energy, fertiliser and shipping markets linked to conflicts and the emergence of choke points.For his final point, he urged businesses and policymakers to move beyond the traditional principle of "Trust and Verify"."Today I say 'Distrust and Diversify'," he said, arguing that planning should take into account the possibility that "things may not go right".He also warned against excessive reliance on just-in-time supply chains and the assumption that the lowest cost should always determine economic decisions."Don't let your supply chain really be just in time anymore; don't assume that your lowest cost will be the determinant," he said, stressing the importance of building a "margin of safety".
India-China ties need stability
Turning to China, Jaishankar said India's engagement with Beijing should ultimately help modernise the Indian economy and strengthen domestic capabilities, even as trade and other economic interactions continue."But for us, the interaction is the purpose of it is finally to modernise our economy and to develop our capabilities, but even as we do so, obviously there will be trade, there will be other economic interactions with them."He said India and China had experienced a particularly difficult phase between 2020 and 2024."I think we went through a particularly bad patch between the summer of 2020 and the autumn of 2024, and that was primarily an outcome of the situation in the border"However, he said both countries remained major economies and markets for each other, and that greater cooperation could be possible if relations remained stable and moved in a more cooperative direction.At the same time, Jaishankar said India had to address the weaknesses created by decades of inadequate industrialisation."We stand our ground as we have stood in the border. We develop our strengths, which unfortunately, as I said, from the 1960s for half a century, we did not do.""We have to make up for the shortcomings and you know the the mistakes of the past, and and that is really what we are hoping to do."Jaishankar said building a stronger manufacturing base would be central to India's ability to compete with China and other major economies.
India has raised Chinese visa concerns
Jaishankar also acknowledged concerns among Indian businesses over difficulties obtaining Chinese business visas, saying the government had taken up the issue."So, in seeing those stories about business visa issues, which our businessmen have been facing, yes, we have seen it, and I want to say, I mean, for those of you who may have an interest or who may have been affected, we have taken it up as well."At the political and strategic level, he said both India and China had an interest in maintaining stable relations."I would also say, at a political level, at a strategic level, they, you know, it's both of us have an interest in maintaining a certain, you know, I would say stable relationship here."Jaishankar cautions against US-China 'G2' narrativeJaishankar also urged caution over the idea of a US-China "G2", saying the relationship between Washington and Beijing remained fundamentally competitive despite areas of cooperation."I think people use that term. I would advise you to treat it with some caution, because the fact is, if you look at the US-China relationship, I think at its heart it's a fundamentally competitive relationship."He said the two countries could still cooperate in some areas and remain largely indifferent to each other in others.
"But as is often the case, it can also be collaborative in certain matters. It can be indifferent in certain sectors."He added that the US and China would not necessarily compete on every issue, in every geography or at every point in time."So it is not that they will compete on every issue and every geography and every time flight."Jaishankar concluded that the uncertainty confronting governments and businesses represented a broader shift in the global environment."I think this is the reality of the world. It applies to national policymakers; it applies to enterprise decisions," Jaishankar said, concluding: "I think it is a realistic picture."

headline: India-Bangladesh ties must serve mutual interest: S Jaishankar
full_text:
India-Bangladesh ties must serve mutual interest: S Jaishankar
On Pakistan-US relations, Jaishankar said the two countries have a "long history" of ties. He said that while India has, to a large extent, developed its own relationship with the United States, Pakistan stands apart for a different reason.
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Saturday said any relationship can work only if it meets the test of "mutual interest", as he spoke about the current state of India’s ties with Bangladesh. He also described Pakistan as a "unique" country, saying no other nation uses "terrorism so systematically" and in such a sustained way to attack and pressure a neighbour.
Speaking at the Economic Times World Leaders Forum, Jaishankar addressed questions on ties with Bangladesh and Pakistan-US relations. His remarks on Bangladesh came amid continuing uncertainty over the much-anticipated visit of Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to India, even as both sides are learnt to be continuing back-channel talks to explore the possibility of the trip in the next couple of weeks.
Declining to respond directly to a question on Dhaka’s demand that India extradite former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, Jaishankar said, "What I can tell you is, for any relationship to work, it has to meet the test of mutual interest. It has to work for us."
He added that ties between neighbours cannot be one-sided. "I am not expecting neighbours to only do what is in my interest. There has to be a reasonable degree of my recognising and respecting what is in their interest, just as I expect them also to do so," Jaishankar said.
"It is when you get that landing point, that common ground, relationships work smoothly," he said, adding that "mutuality" of interests underpins overall engagement.
The Ministry of External Affairs announced earlier this month that India has invited Rahman for a bilateral visit as well as to attend the outreach session of the upcoming BRICS summit in New Delhi. Rahman’s expected visit is seen as important for rebuilding bilateral ties, which saw a severe downturn after the collapse of the Hasina government two years ago.
India-Bangladesh relations came under fresh strain after Hasina held a virtual media interaction in New Delhi on August 5. Following the event, Dhaka reiterated its demand for her extradition and sought to link it with Rahman’s planned trip to India.
India later sought to distance itself from the event, saying New Delhi neither played a role in it nor endorsed Hasina’s comments. The Bangladesh foreign ministry reacted sharply and said the country was "outraged" that the interaction was allowed to take place despite Dhaka conveying its concerns to New Delhi over the likely impact on bilateral relations.
On Pakistan-US relations, Jaishankar said the two countries have a "long history" of ties. He said that while India has, to a large extent, developed its own relationship with the United States, Pakistan stands apart for a different reason.
"Now, to a large extent, we have developed our own relationship with the United States, but here is the point: Pakistan is unique not because it is a neighbour of India. We have other neighbours. Other countries have problems between them," he said.
"It is unique because in this day and age, there is no other country which uses terrorism so systematically and in such a sustained manner to attack and pressurise another neighbour, and that has an impact on public opinion in this country," he said.
Jaishankar added, "I am a minister of a democratic polity. I cannot be impervious to what is the public opinion of my country." In his remarks, he underlined that ties with neighbours must rest on mutual interest and common ground, while reiterating India’s concerns over Pakistan’s use of terrorism.

headline: PM Modi meets BJP’s newly formed team at party headquarters in Delhi
full_text:
PM Modi meets BJP’s newly formed team at party headquarters in Delhi
PM Modi arrived at the BJP headquarters on Saturday evening, shortly after the party passed a resolution on the honour and historic legacy of 'Vande Mataram'.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday met the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)’s newly formed team under national president Nitin Nabin at the party headquarters in Delhi.
PM Modi arrived at the BJP headquarters on Saturday evening, shortly after the party passed a resolution on the honour and historic legacy of 'Vande Mataram' and announced a nationwide campaign to raise awareness about the National Song's history and significance.
Deep Dive
The Prime Minister was greeted by party president Nitin Nabin. In a video shared by the news agency ANI, Modi and Nabin can be seen posing with the entire team of office-bearers who were recently named to various posts.
The 65-member team announced on August 17 comprises 51 new faces, including Kavita Patidar, K Surendran, Manoj Tigga, and Sandeep Pathak. In the overhaul, key names that were given responsibilities include former Rajasthan chief minister Vasundhara Raje and former Union minister Smriti Irani.
Nitin Nabin's youth push
In a meeting with the new team earlier in the day, BJP chief Nitin Nabin asked the newly appointed office-bearers to prioritise “Yuva Samvad”, or continuous engagement with young people.
According to a report by India Today, the BJP plans to launch major youth outreach initiatives in the coming days. Discussions focused on devising an effective campaign to reach people aged 14 and above.
The party has begun constituting dedicated teams comprising senior leaders from across the country. The Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha has been tasked with helping form and mobilise these teams.
Former national office-bearers will also be given a key role in the outreach programme, the report added.
The Vande Mataram resolution
BJP on Saturday passed a resolution opposing the Congress Working Committee’s decision to reaffirm its 1937 resolution and restrict the singing of Vande Mataram to its first two stanzas at party programmes, while seeking to uphold the National Song’s historical legacy.
The resolution stated that the legacy of the National Song cannot be “reduced to the calculations of contemporary vote-bank politics.”
A statement issued by the party said it regards Vande Mataram as the National Song of Bharat, an expression of reverence for Bharat Mata, a mantra of the freedom struggle and an immortal symbol of India’s national consciousness.
The party resolved to “uphold the honour, dignity, legacy and national status of the complete Vande Mataram as the National Song of Bharat and as an immortal symbol of India’s national consciousness and freedom struggle… To affirm the constitutional and statutory status of Vande Mataram as established by the Constituent Assembly’s 1950 pronouncement and reinforced by Parliament’s 2026 amendment extending statutory protection to the National Song equivalent to that accorded to the National Anthem,” the resolution said.
Lashing out at the Congress for refusing to sing all stanzas of the National Song, the BJP said it will reject every attempt to subordinate the National Song to communal pressure, political appeasement, or narrow vote-bank considerations.
The CWC earlier decided to abide by its 1937 resolution on Vande Mataram and sing only two stanzas of the National Song, instead of its full rendition, at all party events.
“…To remind the Congress that a resolution of its Working Committee cannot override the constitutional institutions or laws of the Republic of India, and that a political compromise of 1937 cannot be elevated above the constitutional settlement of 1950 and legislation enacted by Parliament in 2026….To expose before the people of Bharat the historical and political context in which the truncation of Vande Mataram took place, including the objections raised by the Muslim League and the subsequent politics of communal and separatist demands,” the resolution said.

headline: ‘My husband made scapegoat’: Wife of Indian captain held in UK over ‘Russia shadow fleet’ case
full_text:
‘My husband made scapegoat’: Wife of Indian captain held in UK over ‘Russia shadow fleet’ case
Ritu Pant said her husband sounded devastated when she first spoke to him after his arrest, “He was broken and he was just crying.”
"My husband was made the scapegoat," Ritu Pant said, defending her husband, Ajay Pant, the Indian captain of an oil tanker seized by British commandos in the English Channel.
The 38-year-old captain is facing sanctions charges in Britain over allegations that the vessel he was on was part of Russia’s shadow fleet, but his wife told news agency AFP that he was doing his job and was “at the wrong place at the wrong time".
British authorities reportedly allege that the tanker is linked to Russia’s so-called shadow fleet — ships often operating through complex ownership and insurance arrangements that are accused of helping Moscow move oil despite sanctions imposed following its invasion of Ukraine.
The merchant navy officer from Uttarakhand's Nainital is accused of breaching sanctions and could face up to 10 years in prison if convicted.
What the British side claims
MV Smyrtos, the oil tanker that was captained by Pant, was stopped on June 14 in an operation involving British commandos who descended from a helicopter onto the vessel. The mission was the first of its kind led by Britain and was described by then-prime minister Keir Starmer as a “blow to Russia”.
The vessel had left Russia’s Ust-Luga port on June 5 and was sailing towards Egypt’s Port Said, according to MarineTraffic. It was carrying roughly 98,000 tonnes of oil when British forces intercepted it.
Pant, who was the vessel’s captain, is accused of having knowledge of the cargo. Prosecutors have described him as the “master of the ship” and argued that his awareness of the cargo is central to the sanctions case.
His wife, however, said a captain's job is primarily to ensure that the cargo reaches its destination safely. “The master's responsibility in any vessel is to just get the cargo safely to its destination,” she said, AFP reported.
His defence has argued that he was acting on instructions from the vessel’s owner and had no role in determining the commercial arrangements surrounding the cargo.
Wife says ‘he was broken, crying’
Pant has remained in British custody after being denied bail. For his family back in India, the circumstances of his arrest have been difficult to comprehend.
Ritu said her husband sounded devastated when she first spoke to him after his arrest. “He was broken and he was just crying,” she said.
“He didn't know what had happened to him... He just said, ‘I am in jail, please take me out’," she was quoted as saying by AFP.
Just days before his arrest, he had spoken to her about the dangers at sea after Indian sailors were killed around the Strait of Hormuz amid the conflict in the Middle East.
“He said that the sea is becoming very difficult now,” Ritu said. “I was just praying, and telling him that, 'just be calm, be careful and just keep contacting us'.”
Now, his mother Deepa is appealing to the Indian government to intervene.
Pant is the only crew member from the ship to face charges. The other 24 sailors have largely been sent back to their home countries, while the Smyrtos remains anchored off the southern English coast.
His trial is due to begin on December 15.
Case and its implications
Anwar Sadat of the Indian Society of International Law said the case presented “complex” legal issues. The prosecution is also being closely watched because it is believed to be the first instance in Europe of sanctions-related criminal charges being brought against a tanker captain rather than focusing only on the vessel or its owners.
David Hammond of Human Rights at Sea International said the outcome could have consequences beyond Pant himself.
“The case carries implications far beyond the fate of a single ship, its cargo or its master,” he wrote in an analysis for Lloyd's List Intelligence.
The issue carries particular weight for India, which has more than 3,20,000 seafarers working across the global merchant shipping industry.
Govt keeping close watch
The Indian government has been keeping a close watch on the case through the Indian High Commission in London, according to a statement released in June.
In a letter to Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, the High Commission shared an update on Pant’s case, according to an official release reported by news agency PTI.
Indian officials first established contact with Pant through the prison’s telephone system on June 19. During the conversation, Pant said he was in good health, had access to medical care and was regularly in touch with his wife.

British commandos seized the oil tanker Smyrtos in the English Channel and charged its captain, Ajay Pant. The case has raised questions over sanctions enforcement and the vulnerability of seafarers.
The Indian captain of an oil tanker seized by British commandos in the English Channel has been made a scapegoat, his wife told AFP, as he awaits trial in Britain on sanctions-related charges.
Ajay Pant, 38, has been charged with sanctions offences carrying a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison. His trial is scheduled to begin on December 15.
“My husband just became the scapegoat,” Ritu Pant, 36, told AFP in her first interview since his arrest in June. “He was at the wrong place at the wrong time.”
British commandos fast-roped from a helicopter on June 14 to intercept the sanctioned oil tanker Smyrtos, which was captained by Pant.
The vessel is allegedly part of Russia’s shadow fleet, a network of ships with opaque ownership and insurance arrangements that Moscow is accused of using to evade oil sanctions imposed after its invasion of Ukraine.
According to MarineTraffic, the Smyrtos sailed from Russia’s Ust-Luga port on June 5 and passed through the Baltic Sea, with Egypt’s Port Said listed as its destination. As it crossed the English Channel, British commandos intercepted the vessel. Then-prime minister Keir Starmer described the operation as “a blow to Russia”.
Pant’s wife said her husband was a victim of the circumstances and was struggling in custody after being denied bail.
“He was broken and he was just crying,” she told AFP, recalling their first phone call after his arrest. “He didn't know what had happened to him... He just said, ‘I am in jail, please take me out’.”
‘SIMPLY FOLLOWING ORDERS’
Prosecutors allege Pant was the “master of the ship” and knew about its cargo, which consisted of around 98,000 tonnes of oil. Pant’s lawyer told a court that the captain was “simply following orders” as an employee of the vessel’s owner. His wife has also maintained that his responsibility was to safely transport the cargo to its destination.
The case raises complex legal questions and could become an important test as European countries intensify action against Russia’s shadow fleet.
It is believed to be the first case in Europe in which sanctions-violation charges have been brought against a ship’s captain rather than only the vessel or its owners.

India’s Foreign Ministry has said its consular officials visited Pant to enquire about his wellbeing. Pant is the only sailor from the vessel to have been charged. Most of the other 24 crew members have since been repatriated.
The Smyrtos remains anchored off England’s southern coast.
The case has also raised concerns among seafarers about being caught between geopolitical powers, according to Steve Yandell, coordinator of the seafarers’ section of the International Transport Workers’ Federation.
India, with more than 320,000 seafarers, is a major contributor to the global merchant shipping workforce.

headline: Mahua Moitra moves High Court against arrest warrant issued by Nadia court
full_text:
Mahua Moitra moves High Court against arrest warrant issued by Nadia court
Mahua Moitra has moved the Calcutta High Court against an arrest warrant issued by a Krishnanagar court in a remarks case. The plea centres on her claim that parliamentary duties and a pending exemption application were overlooked before the warrant was issued.
Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra on Friday moved the Calcutta High Court challenging an arrest warrant issued against her by a local court in Nadia district over allegedly objectionable remarks.
The Judicial Magistrate of the 3rd Court in Krishnanagar had issued the warrant on Wednesday after noting that Moitra had failed to appear before the court despite repeated summonses. She has been directed to appear before the court by August 28.
The matter was mentioned before a division bench of the High Court headed by Justice Debangshu Basak, with Moitra seeking an urgent hearing. The bench allowed the request and directed that the matter be listed for hearing on Monday.
WHY WAS THE ARREST WARRANT ISSUED?
The Krishnanagar court had summoned Moitra to appear on multiple dates. The court said her repeated failure to comply showed a lackadaisical approach and left it with “no other option” but to issue an arrest warrant.
Moitra, however, has argued that she could not appear because she was attending Parliament and that her exemption application had not been decided before the warrant was issued.
She said the first two summonses required her to appear on August 4 and 12. She was attending Parliament on both dates, while her lawyer could not appear because the Krishnanagar court was under a boycott by the local Bar Association.
Moitra said the third summons directed her to appear on August 18, a day after the lawyers’ boycott was withdrawn. She was still in Delhi, she said, while her counsel appeared before the court and filed an exemption application under Section 228 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).
According to Moitra, the judge instead directed her to appear personally the following morning. Her lawyer later sought a decision on the exemption application, saying she could not travel from Delhi to Krishnanagar at such short notice.
The court then issued the arrest warrant, she said.
WHAT IS THE CASE AGAINST MOITRA?
The case stems from a complaint filed by Chaina Nandi and five others, who described themselves as “peace-loving, law-abiding citizens and housewives”.
The complainants alleged that Moitra made objectionable and derogatory remarks about Union Home Minister Amit Shah, personnel of the Indian Armed Forces and certain Hindu religious beliefs and symbols.
They specifically alleged that she made objectionable remarks concerning the “Tulsi Mala”, a religious symbol worn by many Hindu devotees.
The complainants said the remarks hurt their religious sentiments and those of others who hold the symbol in high regard.
Moitra has now challenged the arrest warrant before the Calcutta High Court, which will hear the matter on Monday.

headline: Why Revanth Reddy was denied clearance for US visit: Centre explains
full_text:
Why Revanth Reddy was denied clearance for US visit: Centre explains
Reddy is expected to return home on August 23 after completing the UK leg of a two-nation tour.
Telangana chief minister and Congress leader A Revanth Reddy was denied political clearance for a planned visit to the US because the purpose and programme of the trip did not conform with established norms, the external affairs ministry said on Friday.
Centre denies US political clearance to Telangana CM’s visit
Reddy left for a 10-day visit to the UK and the US this week. He is now expected to return home on August 23 after completing the UK leg of the tour, for which political clearance was granted. The Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) in Hyderabad said he was denied permission to go to the US because of a “political angle”.
When external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal was asked about the matter at a regular media briefing in Delhi, he replied: “The visit of chief ministers, as indeed of other dignitaries, is assessed by the ministry of external affairs in order to accord political clearance.”
Also read: Revanth Reddy cancels US visit as Centre denies clearance due to lack of 'political angle'
MEA says proposed US programme did not meet clearance norms
He added: “The programme proposed in such cases should be appropriate to the office held and the purpose of the visit. In this particular case, that was not so in respect of the US, and therefore, the clearance was denied, not given.”
Jaiswal pointed out without elaborating that political clearance was granted for Reddy’s visit to the UK.
In the past, the BJP-led central government has denied clearance for foreign visits by chief ministers from non-NDA parties such as Trinamool Congress’s (TMC) Mamata Banerjee and Aam Aadmi Party’s (AAP) Arvind Kejriwal.
Also read: MEA on no permit for Telangana CM Revanth Reddy's US trip: Event wasn't appropriate to CM’s office
Reddy alleges political angle, says youth interests should be above politics
Reddy alleged during his tour of the UK that there was a “conspiracy” by the Centre and noted that issues such as youth development should be above politics. He pointed out that the only purpose of his visit was to bring the world’s best institutions to Telangana as part of the country’s New Education Policy and said: “They would have been an answer to our youth’s aspirations to get education, skills and training from the best Ivy Leagues and top global institutions.”
Reddy added, “I have always believed we should all think beyond politics and elections when it comes to nation-building and the future of the youth.”

Telangana plans to continue global education outreach
Reddy was accompanied by the “TelanganaRising” delegation for his visit, and he planned to travel to Boston and New York. He instructed state government officials to continue the US trip to sign agreements with leading educational institutions such as Harvard and MIT. The government’s TelanganaRising initiative, he said, would continue to focus on building the state’s economic and human-resource capabilities irrespective of political hurdles.
“My resolve and endeavour to make Hyderabad one of the top global cities, where any common Indian can get education and certificates from Harvard and Oxford, or an MIT and LBS or LSE, is because while most leaders have wanted to send their children abroad, I want to bring the world’s best to India,” he said.

NHRC directs Punjab govt to probe allegation against CM's wife of demanding ₹5 cr to suppress rape case
New Delhi, The NHRC has issued a notice to the Punjab government and its police chief over a complaint alleging that Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's wife demanded ₹5 crore to suppress a rape case, officials said on Saturday.
The National Human Rights Commission directed the authorities to inquire into the allegation and submit an action taken report within two weeks.
No immediate reaction was available from the Punjab government.
"The complainant alleged that a retired judge publicly stated that a demand of ₹5 crore was made in connection with a rape case, allegedly involving the wife of the chief minister of Punjab," the proceedings dated August 21 read.
An NHRC official said the Commission has taken cognisance of the allegation of the complainant that the wife of Chief Minister Mann sought ₹5 crore to suppress a rape case. According to the complaint, the allegation has been levelled by a former Punjab judge, the official said.
The complaint, filed by Legal Rights Observatory , raised concerns that such "interference" could compromise the victim's right to dignity, safety, fair investigation and access to justice, they said.
The complainant has requested independent verification of the allegation, preservation of evidence, and "impartial inquiry into any attempt to dilute or influence the investigation", and emphasised that a rape victim's right to justice must remain "above influence, status, or position".
The allegation prima facie seems to be a violation of the human rights of the victim, an NHRC bench presided over by its member Priyank Kanoongo said after taking cognisance of the matter under Section 12 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, according to the proceedings.
"The registry is directed to issue a notice to the chief secretary of the Punjab government, and the DGP of Punjab, with directions to 'get the allegations made in the complaint inquired into, and to submit an action taken report within two weeks for perusal of the Commission'," the bench said.
"Let a copy of this proceeding be also transmitted to the Joint Secretary, Women Safety Division, Ministry of Home Affairs, New Delhi, for information," it said.

“…To remind the Congress that a resolution of its Working Committee cannot override the constitutional institutions or laws of the Republic of India, and that a political compromise of 1937 cannot be elevated above the constitutional settlement of 1950 and legislation enacted by Parliament in 2026….To expose before the people of Bharat the historical and political context in which the truncation of Vande Mataram took place, including the objections raised by the Muslim League and the subsequent politics of communal and separatist demands,” the resolution said.
Earlier, Union home minister Amit Shah had dubbed the Congress resolution as anti-national and designed to foster vote-bank politics.

To counter the opposition’s claims that some faiths have reservations about the stanzas with religious imagery, the BJP said it will recall and disseminate Mahatma Gandhi’s testimony that Vande Mataram had become an “anti-imperialist cry” and that he associated it with “the purest national spirit,” demonstrating its larger national meaning beyond the literary or religious context of particular stanzas.
The party will undertake a nationwide campaign to take the history, meaning, national significance and glorious legacy of Vande Mataram to every corner of Bharat.
“…To educate and mobilise the people, especially the younger generation, so that the complete six-stanza National Song and its history are not forgotten and future generations understand the sacrifices, struggles and patriotic awakening with which Vande Mataram is inseparably associated,” the resolution said.
The party urged citizens to remember that the words Vande Mataram were once “powerful enough to frighten an empire.”

headline: Manan Mishra's BCI tenure under SC challenge: Plea seeks removal, fresh elections and term limits.
full_text:
Manan Mishra's BCI tenure under SC challenge: Plea seeks removal, fresh elections and term limits.
NEW DELHI: A day after Bar Council of India (BCI) chairman Manan Kumar Mishra said he would not resign from the post, a petition has been filed in the Supreme Court challenging his decade-long tenure. The plea seeks his removal, fresh elections and reforms to the rules governing the Chairman's term.The plea, filed by advocate Yogamaya MG through advocate Deepak Prakash, challenges the legality of Mishra's prolonged tenure and contends that Rule 12(2) of the BCI Rules prescribes a two-year term for the Chairman and Vice-Chairman, or until cessation of membership, whichever is earlier.
The petitioner has also challenged an April 21, 2025 Gazette notification that purportedly extends Mishra's tenure until 2030, arguing that an administrative notification cannot override the statutory framework governing the BCI.The plea has urged the apex court to quash the notification and direct the BCI to withdraw or rescind it."Although Rule 12(2) prescribes a two-year tenure, no meaningful restriction exists upon repeated re-election. Consequently, the office has remained with the same individual for nearly twelve years," the petition stated.It further argued that such prolonged concentration was "prima facie inconsistent with the representative scheme embodied in Section 4(1)(c)", under which every State Bar Council contributes to the composition of the BCI.
"A national institution representing the entire legal profession should not permit its highest office to remain concentrated indefinitely in one individual or a narrow regional grouping," the petition stated.Among its reliefs, the plea seeks Mishra's removal, fresh elections within a time-bound period under independent supervision, and the introduction of a cumulative cap on the number of years a person can serve as BCI Chairman.The petitioner has also sought a cooling-off period and a transparent rotational mechanism to give representatives from different States and regions an opportunity to head the BCI.The plea further asks the Supreme Court to constitute an independent committee headed by a former Supreme Court judge or former Chief Justice of a High Court. According to the petition, the committee could be assisted by an auditor nominated by the CAG, along with financial and technical experts.The petitioner has also raised concerns over the functioning and finances of the BCI Trust, "PEARL-FIRST", and the financial affairs of the All India Bar Examination. It has sought an independent inquiry and a time-bound audit of statutory funds, examination receipts, institutional receipts, Trust finances, vendor contracts and related party transactions.The petition traces Mishra's tenure as BCI Chairman to 2012. It states that although he briefly demitted office in 2014, he returned as Chairman in November that year and has remained in the post since. Mishra was elected unopposed again in March 2025, which the petitioner claims was his seventh consecutive term.The plea also refers to Mishra becoming a Rajya Sabha member after being nominated by the BJP in 2024. It clarifies that the petitioner does not contend that political affiliation, by itself, makes Mishra ineligible, but raises concerns about the perception of institutional neutrality."Petitioner does not seek the removal of any individual merely because of political affiliation or personal disagreement with any office bearer," the plea stated."The challenge is directed against structural illegality, alleged concentration of institutional control, prolonged concentration of statutory power, violation of mandatory statutory provisions governing tenure and elections, arbitrary exercise of regulatory authority, absence of transparency and accountability, and failure to preserve the representative democratic character contemplated under the Advocates Act, 1961," it added.
The petition comes a day after Mishra rejected calls for his resignation following a protest by lawyers outside the BCI office in New Delhi."I have served as the Chairman of the Bar Council of India for 12 to 14 years because I was elected. Manan Mishra represents 25 lakh lawyers; he will not step down simply," Mishra said.
He also defended the BCI's handling of the NALSAR University controversy, calling the students' boycott of the Chief Justice of India "deeply objectionable".Mishra said the BCI withdrew an order against the students within 15 minutes. He also said around 15 students had gathered outside the BCI office demanding his resignation.The controversy followed a BCI order on August 13 directing State Bar Councils not to enrol NALSAR University's 2026 graduating batch amid a student campaign linked to recent judicial developments and the invitation to CJI Surya Kant to their convocation. After criticism, the BCI permitted enrolment and withdrew the proceedings, saying most students were innocent. CJI Kant later termed the order "absolutely unnecessary", upheld the students' right to protest and barred punitive action against NALSAR students or faculty.

headline: Were Gandhi, Nehru anti-national? Kharge jabs Amit Shah over Vande Mataram row
full_text:
Were Gandhi, Nehru anti-national? Kharge jabs Amit Shah over Vande Mataram row
Speaking to reporters in Kalaburagi, Mallikarjun Kharge defended the Congress's practice of singing the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram, saying the shorter version was agreed upon in 1937 by national leaders including Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, Subhas Chandra Bose and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
Congress president and Rajya Sabha Leader of the Opposition, Mallikarjun Kharge, on Saturday hit back at Union Home Minister Amit Shah over the row surrounding Vande Mataram, questioning the Centre's decision to call the Congress's position “anti-national” and an instance of 'appeasement politics.'
Speaking to reporters in Karnataka's Kalaburagi, Kharge defended the Congress's practice of singing the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram, saying the shorter version was agreed upon in 1937 by national leaders including Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, Subhas Chandra Bose and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
Kharge said the Congress had followed the decision for nearly 90 years and questioned why the issue was being raised now. “If we sing as per what they said — are we Desh Drohis (anti-national)?” he asked, questioning whether the leaders who backed the two-stanza version would also be considered “anti-national”.
Kharge said the Congress had never opposed Vande Mataram and that the party and its Seva Dal had been singing it for years. He also drew a comparison with the national anthem, Jana Gana Mana, saying its original five stanzas are not all sung today.
He accused the BJP and the Narendra Modi-led government of using the issue to pursue “politics of polarisation”. Taking a swipe at Shah, Kharge asked why a decision on singing the full version had not been taken earlier despite Shah having served as home minister for years.
Kharge also criticised those targeting Nehru and other leaders of the freedom struggle, saying the focus should instead be on education, employment, inflation, investment and improving the lives of the poor.
Separately, Kharge criticised the Centre for denying political clearance to Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy's proposed visit to the US. He said such visits were aimed at attracting investment and creating jobs and should not be blocked for political reasons.
Kharge said Telangana and Andhra Pradesh have a large diaspora in the US and that chief ministers often travel abroad to meet potential investors and encourage them to set up businesses and industries. He alleged that the Centre was deliberately preventing Reddy from travelling and said investment brought to a state ultimately benefits the country through economic activity and job creation.

headline: Supreme Court plea seeks removal of BCI chief Manan Kumar Mishra, fresh election
full_text:
Supreme Court plea seeks removal of BCI chief Manan Kumar Mishra, fresh election
A plea in the Supreme Court seeks BCI chief Manan Kumar Mishra’s removal, challenging his tenure extension and seeking a probe into BCI finances and fresh elections.
A petition has been filed in the Supreme Court seeking the removal of Manan Kumar Mishra as Chairman of the Bar Council of India (BCI) and challenging the notification extending his tenure for a five-year period, even though BCI Rules cap the chairman’s tenure at two years.
The plea, filed by advocate MG Yogamaya, also seeks an interim direction to set up an independent administrative committee to run the affairs of the BCI in the event of his removal. It further demands the constitution of an independent, judge-headed committee to examine the finances and appointments made by the BCI.
The petition comes against the backdrop of the recent controversy surrounding Mishra’s decision to refuse enrolment to NALSAR University of Law’s graduating batch following the controversy over their reported objection to having Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant at their convocation ceremony.
Mishra directed all state bar councils not to enrol the students but later withdrew his order while initiating an inquiry into allegations that some teachers and outsiders had instigated the students. However, the BCI chairman got a rap from the CJI himself, who questioned what business he had to issue such a directive. The episode ended on August 15, when Mishra issued an apology letter, sincerely regretting his words or actions that may have hurt the students in any manner.
Following this episode, lawyer bodies demanded Mishra’s removal, followed by protests by lawyers outside the BCI office.
The plea states that it is not directed against the removal of any individual but challenges structural illegality, alleged concentration of institutional control, prolonged concentration of statutory power, violation of mandatory statutory provisions governing tenure and elections, arbitrary exercise of regulatory authority, absence of transparency and accountability, and failure to preserve the representative democratic character contemplated under the Advocates Act, 1961.
It questions the uninterrupted continuation of Mishra at the helm of the regulating body overseeing the legal profession and legal education in the country, citing Rule 12(2) of the BCI Rules, which caps the chairman’s tenure at two years. Contrary to this, it questions the continuation of Mishra from 2014, followed by a Gazette notification in April 2025 extending his term to 2030. The notification also extends the term of the BCI vice chairman, whose continuation has also been challenged.
The petition said, “The issues raised transcend the personal continuance of Respondent No. 3 (Mishra) and concern the constitutional integrity of a statutory regulator exercising extensive coercive, disciplinary, educational and financial powers over the legal profession.”
The petition has also sought a probe into the BCI Trust “PEARL-FIRST” and All India Bar Examination finances and sought the conduct of a fresh election in a time-bound manner under the supervision of the court.

headline: Panama-flagged cargo ship sinks off Odisha coast, 2 survivors rescued, 22 missing
full_text:
Panama-flagged cargo ship sinks off Odisha coast, 2 survivors rescued, 22 missing
A Panama-flagged cargo ship carrying 24 crew members sank after communication was lost off Odisha, prompting a major Coast Guard-Navy rescue operation as the search for survivors continues.
A Panama-flagged bulk carrier carrying 24 crew members sank in the Bay of Bengal, around 240 nautical miles from Odisha's Paradip coast, on Saturday, triggering a major search-and-rescue operation by the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) and Indian Navy.
The vessel, MV Ocean Winner (IMO 9145530), was carrying 20 Chinese, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi crew member, according to the ICG. Its last port of call was Paradip and its next scheduled port was Singapore.
The ICG has so far confirmed that two survivors have been rescued from two liferafts, while the search continues for the remaining 22 crew members.
COMMUNICATION LOST WITH MV OCEAN WINNER
The ICG's Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) in Sri Vijaya Puram received information at 11:48 am from a company associated with the vessel about the loss of communication with MV Ocean Winner.
The company also requested search-and-rescue assistance, the ICG said.
The bulk carrier was carrying iron ore from Odisha and was bound for Singapore.
TWO SURVIVORS RESCUED
Following the alert, the MRCC diverted MT Aisopos, a commercial vessel that was operating in the vicinity, to search for MV Ocean Winner or liferafts and render assistance.
MT Aisopos recovered two survivors from two liferafts at around 8 pm, according to the ICG.
The condition of the rescued crew members was not immediately available.
THREE ICG SHIPS DEPLOYED
The Indian Coast Guard and Indian Navy have launched a coordinated search-and-rescue operation to locate the remaining crew members.
ICG ships Varad and Anmol have been deployed for the search, while Vijit has been sent from Sri Vijaya Puram to augment the operation.
Other vessels in the area are also being coordinated with as authorities continue efforts to locate survivors and liferafts.
SEARCH CONTINUES FOR 22 CREW
MV Ocean Winner had 24 crew members on board when it sank — 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar nationals and one Bangladeshi national.
With two survivors rescued so far, the search continues for the remaining 22 crew members.
The exact circumstances that led to the sinking of the vessel have not yet been established. Further details about the ship's condition before it sank and the status of the missing crew members are awaited.

headline: NEW DELHI: Sikh leaders and families affected by the 1984 anti-Sikh riots staged a protest outside Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's residence in New Delhi on Saturday, demanding an apology over remarks by some Congress leaders describing former party l...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Sikh leaders and families affected by the 1984 anti-Sikh riots staged a protest outside Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's residence in New Delhi on Saturday, demanding an apology over remarks by some Congress leaders describing former party leader Sajjan Kumar as a "hero" and "role model".The protest, led by Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee (DSGMC) president Harmeet Singh Kalka and general secretary Jagdeep Singh Kahlon, took place amid heavy police barricading outside Gandhi's residence at 5, Sunehri Bagh Road.A DSGMC leader questioned whether the Congress endorsed the remarks made about Kumar, who was convicted in a case linked to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots."After Sajjan Kumar's death, the kind of statements given by Congress leaders saying Sajjan Kumar is our hero are objectionable. Rahul Gandhi has to clarify today whether Sajjan Kumar is their hero," the leader said.Referring to Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda's remarks, the DSGMC leader sought an apology from Gandhi and the party."Forty-two years later, the wounds of our families have been reopened. Our sentiments have been hurt. Rahul Gandhi and Congress leaders must acknowledge and apologise," he said.The DSGMC had earlier said the protest followed what it described as the Congress "once again allegedly referred to Sajjan Kumar, accused in the killings of thousands of Sikhs, as a role model".

headline: Rahul Gandhi calls Manusmriti's women's subordination norm a shame
full_text:
Rahul Gandhi calls Manusmriti's women's subordination norm a shame
Rahul Gandhi told a youth outreach programme that women belong to themselves, not male relatives. He said reducing women to identities tied to men diminishes their individuality and place in the country.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday said that women belong to themselves and not to their fathers, husbands or sons, terming as shameful the Manusmriti's norm that a woman should remain under the authority of male relatives at every stage of her life.
India's biggest strength is the “70 crore unique journeys, unique imagination, unique dreams” of its women, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha said while speaking at his party's youth outreach programme, 'Chhatron Ki Goonj', here.
'THESE WORDS ARE A SHAME'
“I would like to quote here the Manusmriti, which says clearly that in childhood a female must be subject to her father, in youth she belongs to her husband and, when her lord is dead, she belongs to her sons. A woman must never be independent. These words are a shame. These words should not have been spoken,” Gandhi said.
Women are the country's biggest asset, he said, adding that they should stand for themselves and believe in themselves.
“You belong to nobody, except yourself. You have a relationship with your father, brother, husband, your son, but you do not belong to them, and you belong to yourself,” Gandhi said.
'BREAK THE CAGE'
Gandhi said he had come to the city not to lecture or discuss politics, but to allow young people to express what they felt and discuss their ideas. The programme was held on the grounds of a local college, where young women were present in large numbers.
Calling on the audience to “break the cage”, Gandhi told the youth that every individual is unique and has their own dreams and vision.
“You are unique, you are special, you are an individual, and you have your own dream and vision,” he said.
WOMEN ARE INDIA'S BIGGEST ASSET
Explaining why he considered women a greater asset of the country, Gandhi said, “My logic is that women are by nature more sensitive, more gentle, more compassionate and more forward-looking than men.”
Women were often confined to three identities; daughter, wife or mother, the Congress leader said, adding that while there was nothing wrong with these relationships, these could not be their only identity.
Women become professionals and sportspersons and are active in several fields, but their identities are often defined through their relationships with men, Gandhi pointed out.

headline: 'You don't belong to anyone else, but yourself': Rahul Gandhi's message to young women
full_text:

Edited by: Vijaya Srivastava / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 22, 2026, 21:58 IST

Rejecting the idea of 'manusmriti', he asserted that a woman belongs to no one but herself.
NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday described Indiaâs 70 crore women as the countryâs âbiggest assetâ, saying they are more forward-looking than men and have a crucial role in shaping the nationâs future. He also invoked the idea of women's autonomy and said that a woman should have the exclusive ownership of her own life.Speaking at the fourth event of 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' at the AISSMS College Ground in Pune, Maharashtra, he invoked a verse from the Manusmriti and contrasted it with his call for the empowerment and autonomy of women.
Rejecting the idea of women being liable to other men, he asserted that a woman's exclusive ownership belongs to herself. While acknowledging that the relationships in a womanâs life are important, he stressed that they do not determine her identity or ownership.Speaking on the central theme of the evening, âbreak the cageâ, Rahul Gandhi called on the audience to recognise the individuality that sets each person apart and to resist the pressures that seek to confine them to predetermined identities or expectations. He said the most important message he wanted people to take away from the evening was a simple but powerful one: âEvery single one of you is unique in this universe.
âElaborating on the idea, Rahul Gandhi stressed that individuality is not merely about being different from others, but about recognising oneâs own worth and identity. âYou are unique. You are special. You are an individual,â he told the audience. He emphasised that every person has a distinct way of looking at the world, a different set of aspirations and the ability to imagine a life beyond the boundaries imposed on them.Rahul further connected this sense of individuality to the freedom to dream and choose oneâs own path. âAnd you have your own dream, your own vision for your life,â he said. The emphasis, he suggested, was not simply on having dreams, but on having the freedom to define those dreams for oneself rather than allowing society, circumstances or established notions of what one âshouldâ be to determine them.Through the theme of âbreak the cageâ, the LoP framed personal freedom as the ability to step outside these limitations and acknowledge that no individual should be reduced to a role, label or identity prescribed by others. His message was that recognising oneâs uniqueness is the first step towards claiming the freedom to shape oneâs own future, pursue oneâs aspirations and live according to oneâs own vision of life.
Rahul Gandhi attacks Manusmriti
Rahul Gandhi launched a sharp attack on the Manusmriti over its treatment of women, criticising the textâs prescription that women should remain under the authority of male relatives throughout their lives. He contrasted the idea with his call for womenâs autonomy, arguing that a womanâs identity and freedom should not be defined by her relationship with her father, husband or sons.Quoting from the Manusmriti, Rahul Gandhi said, âI (would) like to quote here the Manusmriti, which says clearly that in childhood a female must be subject to her father, in youth she belongs to her husband and, when her lord is dead, she belongs to her sons. A woman must never be independent.âCalling the words unacceptable, Rahul Gandhi added, âThese words are a shame. These words should not have been spoken.â He said the country should instead recognise women as individuals with their own aspirations and agency, describing Indiaâs 70 crore women as its âbiggest strengthâ because of their â70 crore unique journeys, unique imagination, unique dreamsâ.His remarks framed the debate around womenâs independence as a broader question of individual freedom, with Rahul arguing that women should have the right to define their own identities and determine the course of their lives rather than be treated as belonging to male relatives.
Event follows political storm, clashes
The event follows a political storm and clashes between student organisations. The programme was preceded by a midnight clash between the NSUI and ABVP at the COEP Technological University hostel.It happened after ABVP claimed that female students were being forced to attend the event. Meanwhile, Congress leaders countered the claims, saying two female students, who had earlier expressed their support for the event, were threatened and confined inside the hostel.BJP has also accused Congress of paying influencers and manufacturing crowds for the event. Meanwhile, Congress has alleged that the ruling establishment was attempting to disrupt Rahul Gandhiâs student outreach.
NSUI-ABVP clash erupts at COEP hostel
Tensions escalated on Friday night when NSUI and ABVP members clashed at the COEP hostel campus ahead of the LoPâs interaction. Police resorted to a lathi charge to control the situation, while several injured activists were taken to Sancheti Hospital.According to police sources cited in the material, the Shivajinagar Police registered cases against 50 to 60 people, including six named NSUI and Youth Congress activists, following a complaint by an ABVP member.The confrontation reportedly centred on student participation in LoP Rahul Gandhiâs programme. NSUI activists said they were responding to distress calls from female students, while ABVP alleged that Congress-linked workers were forcibly encouraging hostellers to register for the event.
Congress alleges female students were intimidated
Congress leaders accused ABVP workers of entering the girlsâ hostel and intimidating students who had expressed support for the event.Congress spokesperson Atul Londhe alleged that a female student was cornered and forced to apologise on camera. NSUI state president Sagar Salunke claimed that students had called the organisation for help and alleged that CCTV cameras had been switched off before NSUI members arrived.Salunke also alleged that students, including orphaned students, had been pressured to record videos praising the college administration. The case registered by police followed a complaint from 21-year-old student Malhar Nilesh Patil, who alleged that a studentâs video statement had been recorded under pressure at the hostel.
Pawan Khera alleges conspiracy to disrupt event
Congress leader Pawan Khera alleged that there had been a conspiracy to disrupt LoP's Pune programme, claiming that the response among young people had rattled those in power.Khera linked the controversy to the issues female students were expected to raise with Rahul, including alleged diversion of scholarship funds. He accused ABVP workers of intimidating students and said the incident reflected an attempt to keep women away from public decision-making.He also invoked Puneâs history as the city where Savitribai Phule pioneered womenâs education, arguing that the theme of the event was particularly relevant to the city.
BJP calls event âPaise Ki Goonjâ
The BJP launched a separate attack on the programme, accusing the Congress of paying influencers to mobilise attendance and promote Rahul Gandhiâs event on social media.BJP Maharashtra spokesperson Navnath Ban alleged that influencers were being offered Rs 30,000 to Rs 35,000 each, along with travel expenses, and claimed that the overall expenditure could reach Rs 9 crore to Rs 10 crore if around 3,000 people were paid.Ban dubbed the programme âPaise Ki Goonjâ instead of âChhatron Ki Goonjâ and demanded an investigation into the source of the alleged funds. BJP leader Keshav Upadhyay separately accused Rahul Gandhi of using student issues as a political platform.
Congress hits back, says BJP ârattledâ by youth response
The Congress rejected the BJPâs allegations and accused it of trying to create obstacles to LoP Rahul Gandhiâs programme because of his growing support among young people.Maharashtra Congress spokesperson Sachin Sawant claimed that the BJP was particularly apprehensive about Rahul's appeal among Gen Z and alleged that authorities and ABVP members had attempted to disrupt the programme.
NCP (SP) leader Mahesh Tapase also criticised the BJP, saying there was no reason to oppose a programme focused on issues affecting students and young people.
What is âChhatron Ki Goonjâ about?
Rahulâs Pune interaction with female students is centred on student and youth concerns, with issues such as paper leaks, unemployment and the education system expected to feature in the programme.The Congress has sought to position the initiative as a platform for students to directly raise their concerns, while the BJP has characterised it as a political campaign by the Leader of the Opposition. The Pune event, therefore, has begun against the backdrop of an escalating political battle over who controls the narrative around student and youth concerns.

headline: Over 900 people face FIRs following clashes during Jharkhand protests
full_text:
Over 900 people face FIRs following clashes during Jharkhand protests
Jharkhand police have filed fresh FIRs after violent clashes with protesting job aspirants in Giridih and Hazaribag. The cases have intensified the row over recruitment exam irregularities and the state's handling of student anger.
Three FIRs have been registered against 39 named people and more than 900 unidentified people following clashes during protests by job aspirants in Jharkhand’s Giridih and Hazaribag, officials said on Sunday.
The protests over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations turned violent when demonstrators attempted to burn effigies of Chief Minister Hemant Soren.
The cases come a day after Ranchi police registered three FIRs against 14 named and 200 unidentified people for allegedly obstructing government work and clashing with police.
FIR AGAINST 718 IN HAZARIBAG
In Hazaribag, Korra police registered an FIR against 18 named people and 700 unidentified people over violence during an attempt to burn Soren’s effigy on August 21.
Hazaribag Sadar DSP Rupak Kumar Singh said the case was registered based on a complaint by Sadar Circle Officer Ashutosh Kumar.
Eight police personnel were injured in the clash, Korra police station officer-in-charge Nemdhari Rajak said. They included four sub-inspectors serving as officers-in-charge of the Korra, Lohsinghna, Sadar and Bada Bazar police stations.
The accused have been booked under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to assault on police personnel, obstruction of public servants and unlawful assembly.
No arrests or detentions have been made so far. Police are examining CCTV recordings and other video footage to identify those involved.
TWO CASES FILED IN GIRIDIH
Two FIRs were registered at Giridih Town police station over clashes on Friday and Saturday.
Thousands of students had gathered at Gandhi Maidan on Friday to burn an effigy of the Chief Minister as part of their protest against alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. A scuffle broke out when police attempted to intervene.
The first FIR was registered on a complaint by ABVP activist Anish Rai against JMM leaders and workers. Eleven people, including JMM district president Sanjay Singh, were named, while 20 others remained unidentified.
The second case was registered on a complaint by Sadar Circle Inspector Manoj Kumar Singh. Around 10 people were named and 200 others unidentified.
Police accused them of attempting to block traffic at five locations, clashing with personnel while trying to burn the Chief Minister’s effigy and using abusive language against him.
PROTESTERS ALLEGE HARASSMENT
The JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch accused the state government of targeting its members through multiple FIRs.
Manch leader Piyush Kumar Singh said he, Kunal Prata Singh and Ravindra Prasad had been named in cases registered in both Ranchi and Hazaribag.
“How can we be present at both places simultaneously?” Singh asked.
Jharkhand Leader of the Opposition Babulal Marandi demanded the withdrawal of cases against the students.
“If the government does not withdraw the FIRs, the youth should not be afraid of jail. Fill up the jails,” Marandi said.
Former JNU Students’ Union president and SFI national joint secretary Aishe Ghosh also criticised the police action.
“The students have legitimate demands, and the government should listen to them. There is always room for dialogue. FIRs and intimidation against the student community should not happen,” Ghosh said during an SFI-led march.
POLICE ISSUE ADVISORY
Jharkhand Police on Sunday asked organisers to obtain prior permission for demonstrations, processions, rallies and public meetings. They also appealed to students and the public not to believe rumours.
The protests have intensified after the Jharkhand High Court stayed state government notifications cancelling several recruitment exercises and appointments.
On Friday, the court stayed notifications cancelling the appointments of Child Development Project Officers and candidates recruited through the JSSC-CGL examination.
A day earlier, it stayed notifications cancelling the 11th and 13th JPSC examinations and the appointments of food safety officers.
Student leaders have accused the government of deceiving job aspirants through its recruitment-related decisions.

headline: CPI(M) accuses ED of ‘politically targeting’ Pinarayi Vijayan in money laundering case
full_text:
CPI(M) accuses ED of ‘politically targeting’ Pinarayi Vijayan in money laundering case
CPI(M) state secretary M V Govindan alleged that the ED was conducting the investigation with an ulterior political motive.
The CPI(M) on Sunday accused the ED of "politically targeting" Leader of Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan in the CMRL money laundering case.
The Left party organised a meeting in Kozhikode following the Enforcement Directorate's money laundering probe into Vijayan's daughter Veena T and Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited.
Also Read | Former CM Vijayan says his hands clean; denies hawala dealings
Speaking at the event, CPI(M) state secretary M V Govindan alleged that the ED was conducting the investigation with an ulterior political motive and claimed that the probe against Veena was aimed at targeting the former CM and his son-in-law, MLA P A Muhammed Riyas.
"Politics is the only game being played to turn this into a case without any evidence. That is the politics we strongly oppose," he said.
Also Read | Vijayan alleges harassment, politically motivated transfers of public servants under UDF govt
Govindan said the ED's practice of issuing press releases during an ongoing investigation was unusual.
"What the ED is doing here is a strange stance. That strange stance comes in the form of press releases. Conducting an investigation, twisting and elaborating on matters that have no basis or evidence, and propagating them as if major evidence has been found to create a smokescreen," he said.
He alleged that nothing was found during searches conducted at the residences of Vijayan and Riyas on May 27.
Also Read | Rahul Gandhi vs Pinarayi Vijayan: Is the INDIA bloc cracking after LoP's ‘hug’ remark?
Govindan alleged that the ED had made little progress in the CMRL case and said the latest searches were an attempt to create a new narrative.
He was referring to searches conducted last week at nine locations, including the residences of people associated with Riyas.
"What did you get? You issued a press release saying, 'We got it.' What did you get? Apart from issuing a press note to create suspicion, you have received nothing," he said.
Govindan alleged that those questioned during the searches were intimidated and claimed that the ED was attempting to create a new line of investigation by referring to 'hawala'.
He alleged that the ED was now targeting Riyas because he was Vijayan's son-in-law.
"But now, it is not just Vijayan. You are trying to frame Muhammed Riyas-a CPI(M) State Secretariat member, former minister and MLA-just because he is Vijayan's son-in-law. We will face that attempt politically as well," he said.
Govindan defended CPI(M) leaders and workers whom he said were being targeted in connection with the searches.
He referred to the long-pending SNC-Lavalin case involving Vijayan, which was investigated by the CBI, and alleged that the ED would similarly prolong the present case for decades.
Govindan said the CMRL-related case would be dealt with by the company and reiterated that the CPI(M) would oppose what he described as political targeting of its leaders and workers.
He said the meeting was organised as part of a political campaign to explain to the public that such alleged attempts by the ED would not be accepted by society.
Govindan alleged that the ED did not examine the facts before initiating investigations.
"The case is being initiated with a political target in mind. Usually, the facts of a case are examined, and based on that, everything else follows. But in ED cases, that is absent. They declare the target. After declaring that target, the investigation follows," he said.
Govindan alleged that the BJP was using the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, with the help of the ED, to target political leaders, particularly those from opposition parties.
"There are no cases against BJP leaders under the law. Upon checking, nearly 95 per cent were against opposition party leaders. Not a single one was against a BJP member. One cannot say that they are people who haven't carried out money laundering," he said.
He alleged that the BJP spent more than ₹4 crore during the Kerala Assembly election in priority constituencies as part of its campaign and claimed that the money was unaccounted for.
The ED did not initiate any probe, he said.
"The present ED is not a truthful agency that the people of India can rely on. They are adopting a partisan and political stance," he said.

Govindan defended CPI(M) leaders and workers whom he said were being targeted in connection with the searches. Referring to the long-pending SNC-Lavalin case involving Vijayan, which was being investigated by the CBI, he alleged that the ED would similarly drag on the present case for decades.
He said the CMRL-related matter would be dealt with by the company and repeated that the CPI(M) would oppose what he described as political targeting of its leaders and workers. According to him, the meeting was part of a political campaign to explain to the public that such alleged attempts by the ED would not be accepted by society.
Govindan alleged that the ED did not examine the facts before starting investigations. "The case is being initiated with a political target in mind. Usually, the facts of a case are examined, and based on that, everything else follows. But in ED cases, that is absent. They declare the target. After declaring that target, the investigation follows," he said.
He further alleged that the BJP was using the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, with the help of the ED, to target political leaders, especially those from opposition parties. "There are no cases against BJP leaders under the law. Upon checking, nearly 95 per cent were against opposition party leaders. Not a single one was against a BJP member. One cannot say that they are people who haven't carried out money laundering," he said.
Govindan also alleged that the BJP spent more than Rs 4 crore during the Kerala Assembly election in priority constituencies as part of its campaign and claimed that the money was unaccounted for, while the ED did not begin any probe. "The present ED is not a truthful agency that the people of India can rely on. They are adopting a partisan and political stance," he said.
The CPI(M) used the Kozhikode meeting to repeat its charge that the ED's probe in the CMRL case was politically driven, with Govindan alleging that the agency was targeting Vijayan, Veena and Riyas while using searches, press notes and fresh claims to build suspicion.

headline: Deepender Hooda makes U-turn after backlash over Sajjan Kumar 'role model' remark
full_text:
Deepender Hooda makes U-turn after backlash over Sajjan Kumar 'role model' remark
Asked by reporters in Gurugram on Sunday whether he had called Sajjan Kumar a role model, Deepender Hooda said, “I did not use the words.”
Facing backlash over his alleged remarks describing former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar as a "role model", Rohtak Congress MP Deepender Hooda on Sunday denied using the phrase and expressed regret if his comments hurt anyone's feelings.
Kumar, a controversial former Congress MP who was serving two life sentences in connection with the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, died at the age of 80 on Thursday.
Also Read | Sajjan Kumar row: Punjab Congress distances itself from Hooda’s ‘irreparable loss’ remark
Hooda on Sajjan Kumar's death
Deep Dive
While condoling Kumar's death, Hooda had described it as a "loss to the country's political landscape" and praised the former MP's "connect with people and contribution to Delhi's development".
The remarks triggered criticism from within the Congress, with senior Haryana Congress leader Kuldeep Sharma writing to party president Mallikarjun Kharge and seeking Hooda's removal from the Congress Working Committee (CWC) for "extolling the virtues" of Sajjan Kumar.
Hooda's comments also drew sharp reactions in Punjab, where the SAD, BJP and AAP accused the Congress of having an "anti-Sikh mindset".
Asked by reporters in Gurugram on Sunday whether he had called Kumar a role model, Hooda said, "I did not use the words, nor did I harbour any such sentiment."
He added, "These words are being put in my mouth by those who wish to play politics by undermining the spirit of brotherhood. I had no intention of hurting anyone's feelings; those who know me are aware that I never harboured any intent to cause hurt to anyone."
Also Read | Punjab Congress distances itself from Deepender’s remarks on Sajjan
Statement being ‘distorted’: Hooda
Hooda later posted a video on X seeking to clarify his remarks on Sajjan Kumar.
"For the past two days, I have observed that my statement is being distorted and presented out of context. An English word – 'role model' – is being attributed to me, which I never uttered, nor did I ever intend to convey any such meaning.
"I had absolutely no intention of hurting anyone. And I could never even imagine causing hurt to our brothers in the Sikh community," Hooda said.
He added, "Nevertheless, the Sikh community is like family to us. If anyone's feelings have been hurt, I express my regret as your brother. My intention or objective was never to cause anyone pain."
Hooda, who ended the video with "Waheguru Ji Ka Khalsa, Waheguru Ji Ki Fateh", called the Sikh community a glorious part of the nation and said, "I take pride in a community whose sacrifices for us can never be forgotten."
"Whether it is the defence of our borders or the struggle for Independence, we take pride in the sacrifices the Sikh community has made for the nation; we share a bond akin to family. Whenever the need arose, we always stood together like brothers – that is the nature of our relationship," he said.
"During the recent farmers' agitation (against the now repealed farm laws), when our farmer brothers arrived from Punjab, I was among the first to reach out and stand with them. We have always stood together in every struggle," Hooda said.
"On the events of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, we stand with the Sikh community in their fight for justice. They deserve justice, and no guilty person should be spared," Hooda said in the video.
AAP MLA on ‘wounds of 1984’
The clarification came after AAP MLA from Punjab Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal on Saturday said the wounds of the 1984 anti-Sikh massacre remained alive in the hearts of Sikhs and described Hooda's remarks as deeply hurtful.
"If a senior Congress leader calls Sajjan Kumar his role model, it raises serious questions about the mindset and politics of the party," Dhaliwal said.
Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon had also criticised Hooda's remarks on Friday, saying the wounds of the "horrific and painful" 1984 Sikh massacre remained unhealed even 42 years later.
"At such a sensitive time, describing a key convict in the 1984 anti-Sikh riots as a role model was a condemnable attempt to rub salt on the wounds of the victim families and reopen their painful memories," Dhillon said.
Punjab Congress president Amrinder Singh Raja Warring sought to distance the state unit from Hooda's remarks, saying they may have reflected his "personal views".
Another Congress leader and former Punjab chief minister, Charanjit Singh Channi, on Saturday described Kumar as a "murderer of Sikhs" and a "traitor".
"He conspired to have Sikhs killed... Far from being a role model, even uttering his name is a sin. If such people become role models, the country will be destroyed," Channi said.
