headline: Supreme Court to hear plea on Aug 24 seeking CBI probe into Jharkhand JPSC exam
full_text:
Supreme Court to hear plea on Aug 24 seeking CBI probe into Jharkhand JPSC exam
A plea seeks a CBI probe into alleged Jharkhand Civil Services exam malpractice, calling for an impartial inquiry into the entire examination process.
The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear on Monday a plea seeking an independent, time-bound probe by the CBI into alleged malpractices in the Jharkhand Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination.
A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana is likely to take up the petition filed by activist Harisharan Devgan, through advocate Satyam Singh Rajput, for hearing.
"The present writ petition under Article 32 of the Constitution of India is being preferred in public interest seeking urgent intervention of this court in relation to serious and substantial concerns regarding the integrity, fairness, transparency and credibility of the Jharkhand Combined Civil Services Preliminary Competitive Examination–2025, conducted by respondent no. 2–Jharkhand Public Service Commission pursuant to Advertisement No. 01/2026 on April 19, 2026," it said.
Also Read | Ranchi police files FIR against JPSC-JSSC protest leaders over Aug 21 police-students clash
The plea has also sought transfer of the investigation from the state CID to the CBI to ensure an impartial probe into public officials and examination agencies.
"The petitioner submits that the controversy cannot appropriately be examined merely as a dispute concerning individual candidates or isolated instances of alleged malpractice.
"The allegations require examination of the entire examination chain, including preparation and printing of question papers, coding, storage, transportation, distribution, conduct of the examination, collection and custody of OMR sheets, scanning, coding and decoding, evaluation, storage and access to electronic examination data, generation of the result and publication thereof," it said.
It has also sought direction to immediately secure all physical and digital evidence, including original and candidate-held OMR carbon copies, CCTV footage, and server audit logs, to prevent tampering.
Also Read | A father's legacy, a son’s government: The symbolism in Jharkhand protesters carrying Shibu Soren's portrait
"The petitioner is conscious that the mere existence of allegations or public protests cannot, by itself, justify cancellation of an examination. The petitioner, therefore, does not seek cancellation merely on the basis of media reports or allegations.
"The principal relief sought is for an independent, impartial, comprehensive and time-bound investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation, so that the nature, extent, mechanism and impact of the alleged irregularities may be objectively determined," it said.
It further added that the consequential question whether the preliminary examination can safely be relied upon must thereafter be determined on the basis of objective and scientifically verifiable evidence.
Also Read | Jharkhand protesters threaten to gherao CM Soren's residence, demand his resignation
The petitioner said he raises a constitutional question concerning whether a public recruitment examination conducted by a constitutional authority has retained the minimum degree of fairness, transparency, reliability and institutional integrity necessary for its result to constitute the lawful basis for public appointments.

headline: Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan has accused the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government of surrendering to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Sangh Parivar on issues including the Waqf law.
full_text:
Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan has accused the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government of surrendering to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Sangh Parivar on issues including the Waqf law.
Inaugurating a seminar on ‘Waqf law and UDF surrender’ organised by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] here on Sunday evening, Mr. Vijayan pointed out that the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government that he led had not appointed two non-Muslim members to the Waqf Board. In contrast, he said, the UDF government told the High Court that there was no legal impediment to such appointments.
Mr. Vijayan questioned why the government should allow non-Muslims to be appointed to a Muslim religious institution. He alleged that such a move reflected a communal mindset and warned that similar interventions could later target institutions of other religions.
He also criticised the UDF over the singing of Vande Mataram, alleging that the decision to sing its full version at the new government’s swearing-in ceremony reflected a surrender to the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) agenda.
Mr. Vijayan said the Congress had no clear position on the issue and was aligning with RSS policies in States it governs and at its party headquarters.
Minister’s stance
He also questioned Waqf Minister N. Samsudheen’s position on the Waqf law and asked why he had not opposed the provision allowing non-Muslim members on Waqf Boards.
Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama secretary Umar Faizy Mukkam also criticised the UDF government at the seminar. He alleged that the government had supported BJP leader Shone George’s position before the High Court in the Waqf case.
Mr. Faizy claimed that the government’s stand would allow even RSS members to be appointed to the Waqf Board. He alleged that the government was opposing the inclusion of Umar Faizy and K.S. Hamza on the board and said it was willing to compromise a religious law to keep them out.
Mr. Faizy praised Mr. Vijayan for not appointing non-Muslim members to the Waqf Board during his tenure as Chief Minister.
Former Haj Committee chairman C. Mohammed Faizy and former Higher Education Minister K.T. Jaleel also attended the seminar.

headline: New Delhi: Putting women’s rights and empowerment at the centre of his fourth ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ address in Pune Saturday, Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi called out what he described as the “Manusmriti mindset”, whic...
full_text:
New Delhi: Putting women’s rights and empowerment at the centre of his fourth ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ address in Pune Saturday, Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi called out what he described as the “Manusmriti mindset”, which, he said, keeps women under the control of men. He also took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks on last month’s Cockroach Janta Party-led protest.
Referring to the PM’s video post on social media after the protests, where he “forgave” the ones who abused him, Gandhi said, “My question to you is that at Jantar Mantar, boys also abused and girls also abused. But the prime minister is saying that he felt a ‘cultural shock’ because the girls were also abusing. If boys abuse, there is no problem. For them, it is allowed. But if a girl abuses, it is a cultural shock. It doesn’t look good.”
Gandhi also cited remarks by RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and BJP leader Manohar Lal Khattar. “Mohan Bhagwat ji says that rape happens in India but does not happen in ‘Bharat’, Khattar ji says that 80 percent of rapes happen because of women.”
He went on to question why women were not treated as equals in society, saying that they had been reduced to three identities—“daughter, wife and mother”. He stressed on the need for women to be able to have independence and ambition without being controlled by men.
Referring to the Manusmriti, Gandhi said, “In childhood, a female must be subject to her father. In youth, she belongs to her husband. When her lord is dead, she belongs to her sons. A woman must never be independent.” He said that it is a “shame”, and that women should belong to no one but themselves.
He further called women India’s “biggest asset”, urging them to break the ceiling.
“People ask me, ‘What is India’s biggest strength?’ You get many answers. Somebody will say our economy, somebody will say our military, somebody will say our medical system, somebody might even say our people. But I am very clear on what is India’s biggest strength, our biggest asset, and that strength is 70 crore unique journeys, unique imaginations, unique dreams that the women of India are living,” he remarked.
“Women are by nature more sensitive, gentle, compassionate and forward-looking than men. That is why I believe India’s young and older women are its biggest asset.”
Gandhi then spoke about the different ways in which women are controlled by society, including violence, and restrictions on their opportunities and time. He said 4.5 lakh girls are killed every year before they are born, while 80 percent of women face harassment and 29 percent face physical violence. He added that six percent of women are raped and claimed that 99 percent of sexual violence cases go unreported because of social stigma.
He also said that safety concerns have a cascading effect on women’s education and employment. “Fifty percent of women are denied opportunities for education or employment in the name of safety… 84 percent of women need their family’s permission to take up employment. Women earn 25 percent less than men, and do not get promotions easily and only eight percent own land.”
Gandhi also spoke about how many girls are not allowed to step out of their homes on their own. “Sixty percent of our girls cannot go out of the house alone. If they have to go outside the house, they have to go with somebody.”
He also highlighted the unequal burden of household work, saying that women aged between 15 and 29 spend an average of 5.5 hours a day on household work, compared to around 30 minutes spent by men.
During the programme, several women students and competitive exam aspirants also shared their personal experiences with Gandhi, highlighting the pressures they face at home, in education and at work.
Tejwini, a fashion technology student from a small village, spoke about being pressured by her family to get married, instead of continuing her education. “I decided that no, I will work and study,” she said.
Gyaneshwari, who has completed her master’s degree from Jamia Millia Islamia, spoke about the pressure she faced over her education, career and her share in family property. “It’s not my right? It’s like, I am asking for the property.”
A tribal woman also raised concerns over the hunger strike by tribal students in Pune and the condition of tribal ashram schools, to which Rahul responded that he would join her in her agitation. “Call me there, I will come and sit with you,” he told her.
Concluding the programme, Gandhi called on women to challenge patriarchy and fight for their place in society.
“Patriarchy suppresses you, scares you, threatens you, controls you. Together, we have to finish this patriarchy. Be loud, be proud, and fight for your space in society,” he remarked.

headline: PM Modi pushes social media outreach with new BJP office-bearers
full_text:
PM Modi pushes social media outreach with new BJP office-bearers
PM Narendra Modi met the BJP's newly appointed national office-bearers and urged them to stay active on social media. The emphasis came as the party prepared to expand youth outreach and review election strategy.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday urged the BJP’s newly appointed national office-bearers to remain active on social media and use digital platforms to strengthen the party’s engagement with the youth.
Modi spent nearly four-and-a-half hours with the new team at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi, marking their first meeting since BJP president Nitin Nabin announced the 65-member organisational team on August 17.
PM MODI FOCUSES ON YOUTH CONNECT
During the interaction, Modi congratulated the newly appointed office-bearers and extended his best wishes to them. He advised the leaders to maintain an active presence on social media to connect with young people and ensure the party’s message reaches a wider youth audience.
The Prime Minister also held informal discussions over tea with the office-bearers, with some leaders sharing their ideas and perspectives. A group photograph was taken with the newly appointed team.
Modi later joined the office-bearers for a meal prepared using millets, adding an informal touch to the lengthy interaction.
BJP STEPS UP ‘YUVA SAMVAD’
The Prime Minister’s emphasis on social media comes as the BJP prepares to intensify its “Yuva Samvad” initiative, aimed at sustained engagement with young people.
Earlier in the day, Nabin chaired a meeting of the new office-bearers where the party discussed its organisational strategy, upcoming Assembly elections, grassroots mobilisation and communication of government initiatives.
According to sources, the BJP is planning major youth outreach programmes targeting people aged 14 and above, including members of Gen Z and Gen Alpha.
The party is also forming dedicated teams of senior leaders from across the country for the outreach drive. The Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha has been tasked with helping constitute and mobilise these teams, while former national office-bearers are also expected to play a key role.
PM MODI HOLDS SEPARATE MEETINGS
Modi also held separate meetings with Nitin Nabin, BL Santosh and Shivkumar during his visit to the party headquarters.
In his meeting with Nabin, the Prime Minister discussed the names being considered for the BJP Parliamentary Board. The names of the new members are expected to be announced soon.
BJP REVIEWS ELECTION PREPARATIONS
The meeting also focused on preparations for upcoming Assembly elections and strengthening the BJP’s organisation at the grassroots level.
Nabin is scheduled to chair another organisational review meeting at the BJP headquarters extension at 10 am on Sunday. State BJP presidents, organisational general secretaries and state in-charges from across the country are expected to attend.
The meeting will review preparations for elections in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab and other poll-bound states, besides discussing party programmes and broader organisational issues.
PM MODI HAILS NEW ORGANISATIONAL TEAM
After the meeting, Modi posted on X that organisational meetings were about new ideas and perspectives aimed at strengthening the party and deepening its connect with the people.
The new 65-member team includes prominent figures such as former Union minister Smriti Irani and RSS national executive member Ram Madhav, who have returned to key organisational roles.
BJP PASSES VANDE MATARAM RESOLUTION
The BJP also passed a resolution condemning the Congress Working Committee’s decision to sing only the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram at party events.
The resolution said the BJP would not accept any compromise on the honour and legacy of the national song for “political convenience or appeasement”.
“A political compromise of 1937 cannot be elevated above the constitutional settlement of 1950 and legislation enacted by Parliament in 2026,” the BJP president said.

headline: 2 rescued, 22 missing after China-bound iron ore vessel sinks off Odisha coast
full_text:
2 rescued, 22 missing after China-bound iron ore vessel sinks off Odisha coast
Two of the 24 crew members aboard the ship were rescued from life rafts, while an intensive search is underway for the remaining seafarers,
Twenty-two seafarers are missing in deep sea, while two have been rescued after a Panama-flagged cargo ship MV Ocean Winner carrying more than 72,000 tonnes of iron ore fines from Odisha to China sank in the Bay of Bengal, about 230 nautical miles off the eastern coast, officials said on Sunday.
Two of the 24 crew members aboard the ship were rescued from life rafts, while an intensive search is underway for the remaining seafarers, officials said.
The vessel left Paradip Port on Friday after loading iron ore fines and was bound for China. It reportedly sank in deep waters on Saturday after contact was lost. The crew comprised 20 Chinese nationals, three from Myanmar and one Bangladeshi national, officials said.
The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) in Sri Vijaya Puram (formerly Port Blair) activated a search-and-rescue operation after receiving a distress alert and losing contact with the vessel.
Indian Coast Guard ships and a Navy maritime surveillance aircraft have been deployed, while merchant vessels in the area have been alerted to assist in the search.
“MRCC Sri Vijaya Puram initiated a swift SAR effort following a distress alert and loss of contact with MV Ocean Winner, nearly 230 NM South East off Paradip,” Coast Guard spokesperson Commandant Amit Uniyal said. “Diverted via international safety net, MT AISOPOS successfully rescued two survivors from life rafts.”
The rescued crew members were being brought to the mainland for medical treatment. “We are yet to verify their nationalities,” said the spokesperson. He said rough sea conditions in the Bay of Bengal were hampering the search.
The cause of the sinking has not been established. Authorities are expected to examine whether adverse weather, sea conditions, problems involving the cargo, mechanical failure or other factors contributed to the incident. The loss of the vessel from tracking systems before it sank is also likely to form part of the investigation.
Ports, shipping and waterways minister Sarbananda Sonowal expressed concern over the incident, saying all agencies were coordinating the search and rescue efforts. “Deeply concerned by the unfortunate incident involving MV OCEAN WINNER off the coast of Odisha,” Sonowal said in a social media post.
The MV Ocean Winner, built in 1998, had a deadweight capacity of about 72,928 tonnes, according to available vessel details.
The incident occurred during the southwest monsoon, when rough seas and heavy weather can pose risks to vessels carrying bulk cargoes.
Paradip is one of India’s major ports for bulk commodities and handles large volumes of iron ore, coal and other mineral cargoes. Bulk carriers regularly sail from the port to international destinations across the Bay of Bengal.
The sinking recalls earlier accidents involving bulk carriers carrying iron ore from Indian ports.
In September 2009, the Mongolian-flagged MV Black Rose sank a few kilometres from Paradip after developing a hole in its hull. The vessel was carrying about 23,847 tonnes of iron ore and 920 tonnes of furnace oil.
In another incident that year, the Vietnam-flagged MV Vinalines Mighty developed a serious stability problem while carrying about 24,500 tonnes of iron ore from Paradip and sent an SOS after beginning to tilt. A major accident was eventually averted.
In 2009, during the monsoon, the MV Asian Forest capsized after loading iron ore fines at Mangalore Port on India’s west coast. The vessel sank after cargo liquefaction caused it to lose stability.

headline: The fates of 22 crew members aboard a Panama-flagged bulk carrier that sank in the Bay of Bengal off Odisha remained unknown even after 24 hours of intensive search and rescue operations by the Indian Navy and the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) on Sunday (...
full_text:
The fates of 22 crew members aboard a Panama-flagged bulk carrier that sank in the Bay of Bengal off Odisha remained unknown even after 24 hours of intensive search and rescue operations by the Indian Navy and the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) on Sunday (August 23, 2026).
According to the latest reports from the Navy and the ICG, two Chinese crew members of the ill-fated M.V. Ocean Winner, which was carrying iron ore from Odisha, were rescued, even as Navy ships and aircraft continued to search for the remaining crew.
Ocean Winner (IMO 9145530), with 24 (20 Chinese, three Myanmarese, and one Bangladeshi) crew onboard, had left Paradip Port late on August 20, 2026.
The ICG said that 36 hours after the ship’s departure, the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) received information that communication with the vessel was lost. It also received a request for a search and rescue operation.
The Eastern Naval Command said on X that it responded to the distress alert by deploying the P8I surveillance aircraft in coordination with MRCC, Sri Vijaya Puram. “The Indian Navy aircraft located a geographically dispersed liferaft in the area and soon coordinated with MT Aisopos, which was transiting nearby, with a request for the merchant vessel to render assistance. By late evening on August 22, MT Aisopos had rescued two of the 24 crew members from the liferafts,” the Navy said.
The Navy said it continues to coordinate with the ICG in the operation to find the remaining crew.
“Sustained monitoring and focused aerial search by Indian Navy P8I MR aircraft led to the successful detection of two floating liferafts and oil slick near the reported position,” the Navy posted on X.
According to Equasis, a global merchant shipping database, Ocean Winner was a 28-year-old vessel that could carry around 73,000 tonnes of cargo. Built in 1998, it was 225 metres long and 32.26 metres wide, and was in its end-of-life period. Periodic inspections by national authorities uncovered several deficiencies. The last inspection by Bangladesh authorities in Chittagong this June reported three deficiencies, including in the ship’s magnetic compass.
Ocean Winner was covered by Protection and Indemnity insurance that would compensate for the loss of life. The insurance is up-to-date, starting from August 1, 2026. The ship has changed hands many times, starting with Greek ownership. The current owner is located in Fujian, China.

headline: Rahul Gandhi calls for ‘end to patriarchy’ at Pune event after PM Modi’s ‘cultural shock’ remark

Rahul Gandhi calls for ‘end to patriarchy’ at Pune event after PM Modi’s ‘cultural shock’ remark
Rahul Gandhi also targeted PM Narendra Modi and played a video of him referring to abusive language used by girls during the agitation at Jantar Mantar.
Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on Saturday highlighted several issues concerning women’s safety, rights and social control, and lashed out at “Manusmriti mindset”, while addressing the Pune leg of the “Chhatron Ki Goonj” campaign that he said was dedicated to “daughters of the nation”.
Interacting with students at his outreach programme in Pune, Gandhi said women belonged to themselves and not to their fathers, husbands or sons, and slammed the Manusmriti’s prescription that a woman should remain under the authority of male relatives at every stage of her life.
He also targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi and played a video of Modi referring to abusive language used by girls during the agitation at Jantar Mantar over paper leaks and wondering how “daughters” could use such language, calling it a cultural shock.
Deep Dive
The Congress leader said both boys and girls had used abusive language at Jantar Mantar, but the Prime Minister said he felt a cultural shock because girls used such a language. “If boys abuse, there is no problem and it is allowed, but if a girl abuses, it is a cultural shock,” the Congress leader commented.
He also referred to an old statement by RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat that rape happens in “India” and not in “Bharat”, and former Haryana chief minister M L Khattar’s alleged comment that 80% of rapes happen because of women.
“So this is a mindset, and this fight is against this mindset,” Gandhi said.
“What is the mindset? That a girl has a place, she should be locked in a cage, she should be controlled, she should not work, and boys should get full freedom... if they want to abuse they can abuse, if they want to work they can work... We do not want such Hindustan,” he added.
Women and girls are India’s strength, its foundation and its future, Gandhi said, adding, “patriarchy suppresses you, scares you, threatens you, controls you.”
“Together we have to finish this patriarchy -- smash the patriarchy! And my message to you, simple message: Be loud, be proud, and fight for your space in society.”
Manusmriti and presnet-day violence
Earlier, referring to the Manusmriti, Gandhi quoted a verse from the ancient text which says a woman must obey her father in her childhood, in youth she belongs to her husband, and when he is dead, she belongs to her sons. “These words are a shame. These words should not have been spoken,” the Congress leader said.
Women are the country’s biggest asset, he said, adding that they should stand for themselves and believe in themselves.
“You belong to nobody, except yourself...” he added.
The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha further listed “three forms of violence against women -- physical violence, violence through denial of opportunities, economic violence”.

Gandhi said 400,500 female foeticides take place every year, 80% of women encounter harassment, 29% endure physical violence, and 6% face rape.
He claimed 99% of incidents of sexual violence are not reported because of social stigma.
Tribal protest and female susceptibility
During the programme, Sharayu Chopde, a Maharashtra Public Service Commission aspirant told Gandhi that women candidates suffer more because of exam-related malpractices, as they have a “deadline” and face pressures of marriage and family.
She asked for Gandhi’s support for MPSC candidates in Pune who were seeking re-examination following a recent paper leak. Gandhi said he would discuss the matter.

Gandhi replied, “Call me there, I will come and sit with you.”

headline: BJP president Nitin Nabin on Sunday (August 23, 2026) held a meeting with the party’s office-bearers to discuss a range of organisational matters, especially the strategy for high-stakes Assembly elections due in some States next year, including Utta...
full_text:
BJP president Nitin Nabin on Sunday (August 23, 2026) held a meeting with the party’s office-bearers to discuss a range of organisational matters, especially the strategy for high-stakes Assembly elections due in some States next year, including Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat, sources said.
The crucial meeting was attended by the newly-appointed office-bearers of the party, presidents of its State units and other key functionaries. Those in-charge of the BJP State units were also present at the meeting held at the BJP headquarters here, according to the sources.
BJP national general secretary (organisation) B.L. Santhosh was also present at the meeting, which delved into measures to strengthen grassroots outreach and youth connect, especially in the States where elections are due next year, the sources said.
There was no official word from the BJP on what transpired in the meeting.
Assembly polls are due in Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Goa, Himachal Pradesh and Gujarat in 2027. The BJP is in power in five of these poll-bound States, except Punjab and Himachal Pradesh. While the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) currently rules Punjab, the Congress is in power in Himachal Pradesh.
"It is a crucial meeting to discuss a range of organisational matters with prime focus on the party's preparations and strategy for the upcoming elections in States next year," a source told PTI.
This comes a day after Mr. Nabin held his first meeting with all newly appointed national office-bearers of the party. Former office-bearers of the BJP's national team were also present.
Modi’s interaction
In another meeting presided over by the BJP chief on Saturday (August 22, 2026), party State unit presidents and organising secretaries were also present. After the day-long meeting concluded on Saturday (August 22, 2026), Prime Minister Narendra Modi also visited the BJP headquarters and interacted with all 67 newly appointed national office-bearers of the party. The Prime Minister's meeting lasted for more than five hours.
"Organisational meetings are all about new ideas and perspectives aimed at strengthening the party and deepening the connection with the people. Great interaction with fellow party colleagues and the new organisational team," Mr. Modi said in a post, sharing pictures from his meeting with the party leaders.
Sources said Mr. Modi listened to each of the office-bearers and gave "vital suggestions".
"During the interaction with the newly appointed office-bearers, the Prime Minister listened to each of them very attentively and offered guidance through his suggestions along the way. Mr. Modi urged the new office-bearers to increase outreach and connect with the youth, emphasising the need to stay grounded and engage in greater on-the-ground activity," a source told PTI.
The BJP national office-bearers’ meeting on Saturday (August 22, 2026) also passed a resolution, condemning the Congress for its decision to sing just two stanzas of Vande Mataram at its events, and vowed to protect the "dignity and the national status" of the full version of the national song.
In a 10-point resolution passed at the meeting, the ruling party also asserted that it will launch a nationwide campaign to spread the significance of Vande Mataram and reminded the Congress that a resolution of its working committee cannot override the constitutional institutions or laws of India.
The BJP also resolved to educate and mobilise people, especially the younger generation, so that all six stanzas of the national song and its history are not forgotten, and future generations understand the "sacrifices, struggles and patriotic awakening with which Vande Mataram is inseparably associated".
"A political compromise of 1937 cannot be elevated above the constitutional settlement of 1950 and legislation enacted by Parliament in 2026," the party stated in the resolution.

headline: Sajjan Kumar row: Punjab Congress distances itself from Hooda’s ‘irreparable loss’ remark
full_text:
Sajjan Kumar row: Punjab Congress distances itself from Hooda’s ‘irreparable loss’ remark
Protests erupted outside Rahul Gandhi's residence, with Sikh leaders demanding apologies and condemning supportive remarks about Kumar.
Punjab Congress president Amrinder Singh Raja Warring and party MP Charanjit Singh Channi have distanced themselves from party colleague Deepender Singh Hooda’s remarks describing Sajjan Kumar’s death an “irreparable loss”.
Controversial former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar, who was serving two life sentences in connection with the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, died at the age of 80 on August 20.
Condoling his death, Hooda, the Congress MP from Rohtak, had said that Kumar’s death was a “loss to the country’s political landscape” and praised his “connect with people and contribution to Delhi’s development”.
Also Read | Sajjan Kumar, convicted for role in 1984 riots , dies
The remarks triggered sharp reactions from his party colleagues Warring and Channi, with Warring saying that Hooda’s comments may be his “personal view”, stressing that for many, the wounds of the riots were still fresh.
“No person whether a Sikh or a non-Sikh can forget the pain and trauma of 1984. Despite the passage of so much time, the trauma runs deep in people’s minds,” he said.
Channi called Kumar a disgrace to humanity. “Far from being a role model, even uttering his name is a sin...He should have been shot publicly.”
The former CM, in a video posted on X on Saturday, called Kumar a “murderer of the Sikhs” and a “traitor”. “If such people become role models, then country will be destroyed,” he added.
“He should have been shot publicly in a chowk. He died in jail while serving sentence,” Channi said.
The remarks triggered protests by Sikh leaders and families affected by the 1984 violence outside Rahul Gandhi’s residence in New Delhi on Saturday. The protesters, led by Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee president Harmeet Singh Kalka and general secretary Jagdeep Singh Kahlon, demanded an apology from Gandhi and Congress leaders.
Also Read | ‘Dying in jail is not enough’: 1984 survivors react to Sajjan’s death
A DSGMC leader said, “After Sajjan Kumar’s death, the kind of statements given by Congress leaders saying Sajjan Kumar is our hero are objectionable. Rahul Gandhi has to clarify today whether Sajjan Kumar is their hero.” “Forty-two years later, the wounds of our families have been reopened. Our sentiments have been hurt. Rahul Gandhi and Congress leaders must acknowledge and apologise,” he said.
The Delhi High Court sentenced Kumar to life imprisonment in 2018 for the killing of five Sikhs and burning of a gurdwara. He received another life term in 2025 in a separate murder case.

headline: NSA Ajit Doval to visit China for border talks ahead of Xi Jinping’s India trip
full_text:
NSA Ajit Doval to visit China for border talks ahead of Xi Jinping’s India trip
Ajit Doval is expected to meet his counterpart for the Special Representatives mechanism, Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi on Tuesday.
National security adviser Ajit Doval is expected to visit China on Monday for a meeting of the Special Representatives on the boundary issue, which is part of efforts by the two sides to normalise ties, people familiar with the matter said on Sunday.
Doval is expected to meet his counterpart for the Special Representatives mechanism, Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi, on Tuesday, the people said on condition of anonymity. This will be the 25th round of talks under the mechanism, established in 2003 to work out a framework for resolving the dispute over the 3,488-km border.
Doval’s visit assumes greater significance as it comes ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s expected trip to India next month to participate in the BRICS Summit in New Delhi. Though both sides have not made an official announcement in this regard, Xi is expected to join the summit to be held during September 12-13, the people said.
This will be Xi’s first visit to India in seven years. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Xi last met in August 2025 on the margins of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in China.
Also Read I However you measure it, China’s job market is weak
Talks against recent Arunachal Pradesh standoff
The talks between the Special Representatives is being held against the backdrop of a recent standoff between Indian and Chinese troops in the Arunachal Pradesh sector of the Line of Actual Control (LAC). External affairs minister S Jaishankar reiterated at a media conclave on Saturday that the state of the border will determine the course of the overall India-China relationship.
“I think we went through a particularly bad patch between the summer of 2020 and the autumn of 2024, and that was primarily an outcome of the situation in the border areas,” Jaishankar said, referring to a military face-off in the Ladakh sector of the LAC that lasted more than four years and took bilateral ties to a six-decade low.
After the two sides reached an understanding on ending the face-off in Ladakh in October 2024, Xi and Modi met in Russia and agreed on measures to normalise ties and address the border dispute. Though the two sides have taken steps such as reviving the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, resuming direct flights and easing visa restrictions for Chinese nationals, there has been no forward movement on de-escalation on the LAC.
Also Read I A bolder India on China border
Last round of Special Representatives' talk
At the last round of Special Representatives’ talks in New Delhi a year ago, the two sides reiterated the “importance of maintaining peace and tranquillity” on the border to promote the overall development of ties.
According to an Indian readout issued at the time, the Special Representatives agreed on the need for a “political perspective” while working on a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable framework for settling the boundary question in line with the Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question of 2005.
They also agreed to set up an expert group under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) on India-China Border Affairs to “explore early harvest in boundary delimitation”, and a working group under the WMCC to advance effective border management.
They further agreed to create general-level mechanisms in the eastern and middle sectors of the border, in addition to the existing general-level mechanism in the western sector.
Also Read I China to be India's main long-term competitor in multiple fields: Army ex-chief Naravane
There has been no word from both sides on what, if any, progress has been made on these matters.
The latest meeting of the WMCC, held in New Delhi on August 6, saw the two sides having detailed exchanges on “boundary delimitation, border management, mechanism‑building and trans‑border cooperation” as a follow-up to the last round of talks between the Special Representatives, according to an Indian readout.

headline: DMK calls for overhaul after poll setback: Age caps, 2-term limit, 110 organisational districts

DMK calls for overhaul after poll setback: Age caps, 2-term limit, 110 organisational districts
The DMK plans a major organizational overhaul following its setback in the April 2026 elections. New rules include age caps and term limits for posts.
The principal opposition DMK unveiled a structural overhaul in its organisation on Saturday, fixing strict age caps and limiting term for party posts following its electoral setback in the April 2026 assembly election.
The party’s executive committee, which met at Anna Arivalayam —the DMK state headquarters —with its president M K Stalin in the chair, passed crucial resolutions to radically restructure the organisation setup.
Under the new blueprint, the DMK will expand its organisational districts from 78 to 110, with each district broadly mapped across two Assembly constituencies to ensure localised administration.
Also Read | Focus on young blood, mandatory two-term limit: DMK’s overhaul to bounce back after poll defeat
The standalone post of “city secretary” in major urban centers such as Coimbatore and Tambaram has been completely abolished. Instead, urban zones will be redrawn by voter density - Chennai Corporation Area Committees will average 40,000 voters, while other corporations will average 30,000 voters per committee.
Once the party president formally releases the boundary maps for the 110 revamped districts, district executive committees must convene within 15 days under headquarters oversight to execute the transition.
The executive committee passed nine crucial resolutions to radically restructure its organisational setup.
Aiming to professionalise party operations and foster generational succession, the leadership has introduced strict age caps, a mandatory two-term limit across all posts, and a massive expansion of organisational districts.
Also Read | Vijay treating Assembly like ‘cinema set, delivering punch dialogues’: Stalin attacks Tamil Nadu CM
A resolution that was passed fixed the maximum age at 45 years for branch secretary, 50 years for ward municipal corporation, 60 years for area/union/ town panchayats and a cap of 70 years for district secretary. It limited holding the term of office to two for them all.
According to members in the party, the organisational overhaul will reduce the existing territorial powers of the current 77 district secretaries, and also drastically reduce the term in office.
Nearly 10 to 13 district secretaries are likely to be axed if the cap on age limit is enforced. They may be transitioned into non-administrative state-level or zonal-level responsibilities in the party, making way for young leaders.
There are currently 13 DMK district secretaries aged over 70. They are, Kancheepuram South secretary K. Sundar(72), Ranipet secretary R Gandhi (80), Tiruvannamalai South secretary E V Velu (75), Villupuram North secretary Gingee K S Masthan (71), Salem East secretary S R Sivlingam (75), Erode South secretary S Muthusamy (77), Thanjavur North secretary Sakkottai K Anbazhagan (72), Pudukkottai South secretar S Regupathy (76), Madurai City secretary Thalapathy (70), Theni South secretary N Ramakrishnan (77), Virudhunagar secretary K K S S R Ramachandran (77), Thoothukudi South secretary Anitha R Radhakrishnan (74), Tirunelveli West secretary R Avudaiyappan (81).

Meanwhile, Branch Committees will be formed in Chennai, Coimbatore, Madurai, Tiruchirappalli, and Salem corporations, and in other corporations wherever necessary, to strengthen the Ward Committees.

headline: 'Standard policy for VVIP visits': MEA sources on alleged ‘no questions request’ during PM Modi-Trump meet

'Standard policy for VVIP visits': MEA sources on alleged ‘no questions request’ during PM Modi-Trump meet
The government on Monday clarified that discussions about arrangements for a leader's public appearance are a “normal practice”.
The government on Monday clarified that discussions about arrangements for a leader's public appearance are a "normal practice" and part of the "stand policy for VVIP visits."
"Discussions regarding arrangements for public appearances of leaders are normal practice ahead of any VVIP visit. In this regard, the Indian side communicated its standard practice for such visits," MEA sources told HT.
“Delegations when meeting US President are wary about his unpredictable behaviour, as may be seen from his interactions with President of South Africa, UKraine etc. Thus, the cautious approach by India,” the sources added further.
Deep Dive
This clarification from the Ministry of External Affairs comes after US ambassador to India Sergio Gor alleged that India had "specifically requested" that no questions be taken from media during a bilateral meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump.
PM Modi met with President Trump on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in France.
During this, the two leaders held a joint press conference, during which Gor stated that the Indian government had stated that no questions will be taken from the media.
“I told the president, I said, the Indians prefer no questions. He said, sure, no problem. So the meeting starts, the press comes in, there must have been 50 cameras, the president is sitting here, the prime minister is sitting there, they both speak for a few minutes. As soon as they get done, the first thing the president does, he looks up at the camera and says, any questions?” Gor claimed, adding that the remark “opened everything up”.
The US ambassador said that “a 45-minute press conference” followed, and that “everything was on the table.”
What happened at the G7 summit?
During the meeting with Trump at the G7 Summit, PM Modi raised the issue of safety of seafarers amid increased ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz due to the ongoing conflict between the US and Iran.
"Lakhs of Indian seafarers operate in maritime sector; I believe that their security is equally important,” PM Modi told Trump.
Trump added that the US will "be there for India."
“If anybody attacks that man (pointing to Modi), we're gonna be there. Now, if there's a new leader, I'm not sure," Trump added further. The US President also hinted at a visit to India in the future.

Here is what happens once the draft electoral rolls are published.Following the publication of the draft electoral rolls, the claims and objections phase of the SIR begins. This phase allows people to verify their details in the draft rolls, fix exclusions and ensure their names are in the final list that will be published on October 27.The window to file claims and objections will be open from August 24 to September 23. If citizens need to fix their voter status, they must submit the correct form based on the specific situation.Form 6: Use this for the inclusion of a new voter registration (if you are a first-time voter or your name has been deleted from the rolls).Form 6A: Use this for the inclusion of an overseas voter registration (for non-resident Indians).Form 7: Use this for the deletion of a name (to report deceased or permanently relocated voters etc).Form 8: Use this for shifting of residence, correction of entries, replacement of EPIC, or marking of PWD (persons with disabilities). .Karnataka SIR | Name listed in ASDDO? headline: With the removal of over 1.07 crore names, Karnataka’s electorate shrunk to 4.46 crore voters when the draft electoral rolls were published on Monday as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). An overwhelming number of the missing names were ma...
full_text:
With the removal of over 1.07 crore names, Karnataka’s electorate shrunk to 4.46 crore voters when the draft electoral rolls were published on Monday as part of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). An overwhelming number of the missing names were marked ‘absent, shifted, duplicate, dead, and others’ (ASDDO).
Announcing the figures at the end of the enumeration phase, Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) V. Anbu Kumar said the electorate comprised over 2.22 crore males, 2.24 crore females, and 2,871 others. Voters can check their names on the CEO’s official website at https://voters.eci.gov.in/download-eroll?stateCode=S10
The CEO said a special campaign will be conducted in areas reporting high ASDDO numbers, where voters will be assisted in filling Form 6 (for inclusion). The dates for the campaign are yet to be announced by the CEO’s office.
As many as 43.81 lakh notices will be served on voters whose enumeration forms contained logical discrepancies or those who could not be mapped. Notices may also be issued if a complaint is filed against a voter or if the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) has reason to suspect that a voter is ineligible.
With the enumeration phase ending, voters are likely to face the same problems they encountered with the ASDDO list. Just as people remained unaware that their names were in the ASDDO list until 12 days before the enumeration phase ended, they now have no way of knowing whether they will receive a notice until one is actually served. “We only have numbers on how many people will receive notices, and the names will not be known until the notice is generated,” the CEO said.
However, the entire process — from an ERO generating a notice to it being served — is to be completed within just seven days. This could become a major hurdle, especially for voters living in another district or city while remaining registered in their native constituency, as the voter must attend the hearing in person.
There is, so far, no online option to check whether a person is likely to receive a notice. The CEO reiterated that names will be known only after a notice is generated.
The process has now placed the burden of saving one’s vote squarely on the voter. Unlike the enumeration phase, when Booth Level Officers (BLOs) were instructed to hand over enumeration forms to voters and a family member above the age of 18 could fill them on the voter’s behalf, BLOs, during this stage, can serve notices on anyone available at the address. The notice will also carry a QR code to submit one of the 11 documents online, but the voter alone must appear for the hearing.
This could pose challenges for sections of voters such as senior citizens, single mothers, women in general, labourers and persons with disabilities, among others.
For instance, within Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) limits alone, 40,307 voters are above the age of 85, while 829 are above 100. More than 21,400 voters are persons with disabilities.
More polling stations
Following the enumeration phase, the number of polling stations across Karnataka increased after rationalisation. Each polling station will now have up to and not more than 1,200 voters, and where a polling station had more voters, they were shifted to another polling station within a two-kilometre radius, the CEO said. This has resulted in the addition of 1,873 polling stations across the State.
Voters unable to find their names in their current polling station or booth list have been advised to search using their EPIC details, where the updated polling station will be reflected if rationalisation has taken place. They may also check two polling stations before and after their current one.
Regarding notices on logical discrepancies and unmapped status, EROs have been vested with full powers to take a decision. If aggrieved by an ERO’s decision, a voter can appeal to the DEO/DC within 15 days. If the response remains unsatisfactory, the voter can appeal to the CEO, the final appellate authority, within 30 days of the first appeal.
While the draft electoral rolls were published at 12 p.m. on Monday, people struggled throughout the day to view and download the rolls, particularly the English versions. While voters were able to access the website, after downloading the rolls, files repeatedly threw up errors such as “error” and “file corrupted.”

headline: Tarun Tejpal must surrender, seek exemption before appeal is heard: Goa tells SC
full_text:
Tarun Tejpal must surrender, seek exemption before appeal is heard: Goa tells SC
Senior advocate Kapil Sibal insisted that the requirement to surrender did not apply since the high court had given him four weeks to surrender
Former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal must surrender or secure an exemption from the Supreme Court before his appeal against his conviction and 10-year jail term in the 2013 sexual assault case can be heard, the Goa government told the Supreme Court on Monday.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Goa government, made the submission before justice Alok Aradhe, who was considering Tejpal’s appeal in the chamber list, where matters are taken up for preliminary or procedural consideration before being placed before a regular bench.
“The existence of the appeal is dependent on either filing a certificate that he has surrendered or, alternatively, he will have to pray to Your Lordships to allow an exemption from surrendering. These are the two options,” submitted Mehta, stressing the seriousness of the case.
Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Tejpal, opposed the state’s submission, arguing that the requirement to surrender did not apply in the present case as the Bombay High Court at Goa had granted him four weeks to surrender while declining to stay his conviction.
“This general rule does not apply because this is a case where stay has been granted by the high court, so there is no question of applying this rule,” contended Sibal.
He argued that Tejpal was still protected by the high court’s order and therefore there was no reason to insist that he surrender before his appeal was heard. “Why must I go to jail when I am protected?” asked Sibal, urging the court to list the appeal for hearing on August 31.
“If this court says no stay, I will have to go to jail. Allow me to argue the appeal and seek interim protection. If this court says we don’t think it is a case for bail, then I am inside,” he added.
Justice Aradhe, after hearing the submissions, said he would pass an appropriate order.
Tejpal approached the Supreme Court on August 20, challenging the August 6 judgment of the Bombay High Court at Goa that overturned his acquittal by the trial court and convicted him on two counts of aggravated rape. The high court sentenced him to 10 years’ imprisonment and imposed a fine of ₹10 lakh in all.
The high court, at Tejpal’s request, granted him four weeks to surrender before the jail authorities, although it rejected his plea to stay his conviction. He is therefore required to surrender in the first week of September.
The Goa government has separately approached the Supreme Court seeking enhancement of the sentence to life imprisonment. The state has not challenged the conviction but has argued that the 10-year sentence is grossly disproportionate to the gravity of the offences.
The government has also challenged the high court’s direction that the sentences for the two aggravated rape offences run concurrently, arguing that the alleged assaults took place on successive days and involved separate criminality.
Tejpal, in his appeal, has denied the allegations and challenged the high court’s findings that led to his conviction. He has argued, among other things, that the prosecution case was inconsistent with CCTV footage and questioned the circumstances in which the allegations emerged.
The case dates back to November 2013, when a junior female colleague accused Tejpal of sexually assaulting her twice in an elevator at a hotel in Goa during the Tehelka THiNK festival. Tejpal was arrested later that month and released on bail in July 2014.
The trial court acquitted him in May 2021 but high court reversed the acquittal on August 6 this year, holding that the trial court’s appreciation of the evidence was “not only unreasonable but perverse” and that the judge relied on preconceived notions while assessing the complainant’s testimony.

headline: Tarun Tejpal must surrender before challenging rape conviction, Goa govt tells SC
full_text:
Tarun Tejpal must surrender before challenging rape conviction, Goa govt tells SC
Former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal challenged his 10-year rape conviction before the Supreme Court. Goa told the court his appeal depends on surrendering or seeking exemption from surrender. Kapil Sibal argued Tejpal need not surrender as the High Court's stay remains in force.
Former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal has challenged in the Supreme Court the Bombay High Court's verdict overturning his acquittal in the 2013 rape case and sentencing him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment. During the hearing, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Goa government, argued that the maintainability of Tejpal's appeal depends on either him filing a certificate confirming his surrender or seeking an exemption from surrender before the court. “These are the two options,” Mehta said.
The arguments took place before a bench headed by Justice Alok Aradhe, with Tejpal's counsel Kapil Sibal and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, presenting opposing arguments.
Tejpal has challenged the Bombay High Court's verdict overturning the trial court's decision to acquit him and sentencing him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment. The Supreme Court heard his plea.
Mehta urged the court to consider the maintainability of Tejpal's appeal in this context.
Kapil Sibal argued that the rule does not apply in this case because the High Court has already granted Tejpal relief from surrender. Therefore, he said, there was no question of applying the rule. The High Court had given Tejpal four weeks to surrender, until the first week of September.
Sibal said, "Suppose the court refuses to grant a stay, then I will have to go to jail. But when the High Court itself has granted a stay and that order is still in force, why should I surrender? In such a situation, what is the point of surrendering first and then filing an appeal?"
Referring to an earlier Supreme Court case, Mayuram Subramanian Srinivasan vs CBI, Tushar Mehta said the matter could also be viewed from another perspective. The special court had suspended the sentence and granted relief for a certain period. Whether or not that relief should be extended is a matter of the court's discretion. However, he said, in their view, it would be subject to the provisions of Order XXI Rule 13A of the Supreme Court Rules.
Mehta argued that the provisions of Section 389 of the CrPC and the Supreme Court Rules are independent provisions and must be considered on their own terms.
Sibal said, "Despite my request, submissions and arguments, if this court says that this is not a bail matter, I am ready to go to jail. This is my regular appeal and the relief is still in force."
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta interjected, saying, "You have been incorrectly briefed. This is not an SLP."
Sibal responded, "This is an extension of criminal appellate jurisdiction."
After hearing arguments from both sides, Justice Alok Aradhe said, "This is a criminal appeal. We will pass an order on it."
Sibal said that listing the matter for the 31st would cause no prejudice to anyone. He added that whatever the complainant had said did not match the CCTV footage.
"Justice should be done. We have said what we had to say. The court can now pass an order," Sibal said.

headline: Manipur is awaiting a decision from New Delhi regarding the upcoming Census exercise, which remains in limbo in the State amid the demand by several Meitei and Naga civil society groups for a National Register of Citizens (NRC) to be compiled first. ...
full_text:
Manipur is awaiting a decision from New Delhi regarding the upcoming Census exercise, which remains in limbo in the State amid the demand by several Meitei and Naga civil society groups for a National Register of Citizens (NRC) to be compiled first. With the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI) yet to spell out the future course of action, a government source said a review of the situation is likely to be held in the coming days.
On Monday (August 24, 2026), following a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by the Kangleipak Students Association (KSA), the High Court of Manipur constituted a Special Division Bench comprising Chief Justice M. Sundar and Justice A. Guneshwar Sharma to hear the matter on August 25 at 2 p.m. In a notification issued on Monday (August 24, 2026), the court said the Special Division Bench would sit exclusively to hear the PIL.
The first phase of the Population Census 2027, House Listing and Housing Census (HLO), is scheduled to be held in Manipur from September 1 to September 30.
The training of enumerators, mostly government school teachers, has been halted in the State due to opposition and protests by several civil society groups. Enumerators are required to visit each household for door-to-door enumeration and record details in a specific app on their personal phones.
The self-enumeration portal, which allows respondents to enter their details independently, was scheduled to go live on August 17, but is yet to become operational. “A decision from the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is awaited. The RGI office will assess the situation and there will be some clarity soon,” said a State government official.
In 2011, the Census exercise could not be carried out in at least 103 villages in Chhattisgarh and 260 villages in West Bengal due to violence associated with Left Wing Extremism (LWE).
Delimitation anxiety
Though the Census is not an exercise to determine citizenship and counts all individuals irrespective of nationality, there is anxiety among a section of people in Manipur that the next delimitation exercise, which will redraw the boundaries of electoral constituencies, may take into account the latest Census data in a manner that could disadvantage the Meiteis and small tribal communities. Manipur has three major communities: the Meiteis, the Nagas, and the Kuki-Zo people.
At least 14 civil society groups representing Meiteis, Pangals (Meitei Muslims), and the Kom and Rongmei tribes, among others, are in Delhi to seek an audience with the Union government. The group also has representation from those displaced from their homes as a result of the ethnic violence between the Kuki and Meitei communities that started on May 3, 2023.
The group met officials of the MHA, Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs Kiren Rijiju and BJP president Nitin Nabin.
Former Manipur Chief Minister N. Biren Singh, who met Union Home Minister Amit Shah in New Delhi last week, said people are apprehensive that the “presence of illegal immigrants in the State has affected demographic imbalance” and that while people are not against the Census, they want the NRC first.
The Congress party on August 20 sought the postponement of the Census exercise in Manipur, citing continuing violence and the displacement of thousands of people.
Kuki-Zo Council calls for Census
The Kuki-Zo Council (KZC), on the other hand, said that to rebut the “falsehoods and propaganda surrounding our population and demographic status during the Manipur conflict, an impartial Census is essential to establish facts and dispel unfounded claims”.
The KZC also welcomed delimitation to ensure fair representation based on verified demographic data. Regarding the NRC, the KZC said it was a national exercise and that there was no provision for any community or State government to unilaterally initiate or conduct a separate NRC in a particular State at its own discretion.
During the HLO phase, enumerators will collect information relating to housing conditions, household details, available amenities and assets possessed by households through a structured questionnaire comprising 33 notified questions. This phase of the Census forms an essential foundation for evidence-based planning and formulation of welfare and development programmes. The actual headcount will be done during the Population Enumeration phase, the second phase, which will be conducted in February 2027. In the second phase, for the first time, respondents will be asked to state their nationality along with their religion and the place and date of birth of both their parents.

headline: ‘Birthright to denounce India’s heritage’: Yogi Adityanath slams Rahul Gandhi over Manusmriti remarks
full_text:
‘Birthright to denounce India’s heritage’: Yogi Adityanath slams Rahul Gandhi over Manusmriti remarks
UP chief minister Yogi Adityanath said Rahul Gandhi should be accountable to the country as the Leader of Opposition.
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday hit out at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on Manusmriti, accusing him of denouncing India's traditions and heritage and saying he had "ruined" his role as the Leader of Opposition.
Addressing an event in Raebareli to mark the 222nd birth anniversary of 1857 revolt leader Rana Beni Madhav Baksh Singh, Adityanath said Gandhi should be accountable to the country as the Leader of Opposition.
Yogi Adityanath vs Rahul Gandhi
"Rahul ji the country does not have any expectations from you as an individual. But as the Leader of Opposition in India's Parliament, the country's highest panchayat, you are accountable to the country's democracy," he said.
"You have taken an oath on the Constitution and, after taking that oath, you consider it your birthright to denounce India's traditions and heritage. When you go outside Uttar Pradesh, you defame and insult Uttar Pradesh, and when you go outside India, you insult India," he said.
Raebareli is the Lok Sabha constituency represented by Gandhi. His mother and former Congress president Sonia Gandhi represented the seat for two decades before opting for a Rajya Sabha seat in 2024.
Also Read | Rahul Gandhi calls for ‘end to patriarchy’ at Pune event after PM Modi’s ‘cultural shock’ remark
Yogi Adityanath on Rahul Gandhi's Manusmriti remarks
Referring to Gandhi's comments on Manusmriti, Adityanath said the Congress leader should read ancient Hindu texts to understand Manu's place in Indian tradition.
"You comment on Manu, Ram or India's heritage. If you want to know about Manu, read the Atharvaveda, Shatapatha Brahmana and Matsya Purana (religious texts). You will get all the information," he said.
Gandhi, during an interaction with girl students in Maharashtra on Saturday, had criticised the "Manusmriti mindset", urged students to "smash the patriarchy" and said women belonged to themselves, not to their fathers, husbands or sons.
Adityanath questioned Gandhi's call for women to break free from the "bondage" of Manusmriti, asking why he wanted to “lead India's children and young generation towards a situation where a mother or another person later has to feel ashamed and apologise?”
Adityanath also referred to the recent Jantar Mantar protest, alleging that a young woman had used abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi before later withdrawing her remarks and apologising.
Also Read | Rahul attacks Modi’s ‘cultural shock’ remark, says India must smash patriarchy
BJP, Congress trade barbs over Rahul Gandhi's Pune event
Adityanath's remarks came amid a wider political row over Gandhi's interaction with students in Pune on Saturday.
The BJP and Congress traded charges on Sunday over Gandhi's 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' programme, with the BJP dismissing it as a "political comedy show", while the Congress accused the ruling party of being rattled by Gandhi's growing appeal among young people.
Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis also criticised Gandhi, accusing him of hypocrisy over women's empowerment while opposing the Women's Reservation Bill in Parliament. He described the Congress as a directionless party of "show-offs and loudmouths" seeking television relevance.
BJP Maharashtra vice-president Keshav Upadhye also targeted the event, alleging that Gandhi delivered generic political rhetoric instead of addressing students' concerns and claiming that attendees had been brought in college buses to manufacture a crowd.
"Rahul Gandhi's Pune event was yet another political comedy show," Upadhye said in a statement. "While searching for Manuwad, the Congress should first look in the mirror."

headline: Putin assures India of fuel, fertilisers amid disruptions over West Asia crisis
full_text:
Putin assures India of fuel, fertilisers amid disruptions over West Asia crisis
Jaishankar said PM Modi hopes that President Vladimir Putin would attend the Brics Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday assured India of supplies of energy and fertilisers amid disruptions caused by the West Asia conflict, even as external affairs minister S Jaishankar highlighted the need to address the growing imbalance in two-way trade that has soared to $50 billion.
Putin’s expected meetings with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on the margins of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Kyrgyzstan this month and on the sidelines of the Brics Summit in New Delhi in September figured in a meeting between the Russian leader and Jaishankar in Moscow. Jaishankar is in Russia to co-chair a meeting of the Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation (IRIGC-TEC).
Putin pointed out that bilateral trade has increased this year, after declining slightly in 2025, and said Russia is increasing fertiliser supplies to India. He noted that any important issues had figured in the IRIGC-TEC meeting and said: “One of these issues is not only energy – it is, of course, the supply of fertilisers…We are doing everything to resolve this issue for Indian farmers, for agriculture. We are increasing these supplies and are ready to do so further.”
Also Read | Russian President Vladimir Putin expresses hope to meet PM Modi soon as he hosts EAM S Jaishankar
The two sides are also making progress on cooperation in nuclear energy and high-tech, Putin said.
Jaishankar said Modi hopes Putin will attend the Brics Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13. “Prime Minister Modi looks forward to meeting you at the SCO Summit and also hopes that you will have the opportunity to come to the Brics Summit and host this annual summit,” Jaishankar was quoted as saying by state-run TASS news agency.
He also handed over a personal message from Modi to Putin. People familiar with the matter said Putin is expected to attend the Brics Summit, along with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. The summit is expected to focus on global economic and political challenges, and expanding multilateral cooperation among Brics member states.
While co-chairing the IRIGC-TEC meeting with Russia’s first deputy prime minister Denis Manturov, Jaishankar pointed out that a more than four-fold increase in bilateral trade in goods — from $13 billion in 2021-22 to nearly $60 billion in 2025-26 — had been “accompanied by a significant widening of the trade imbalance” from $6.6 billion to more than $50 billion.
Also Read | EAM Jaishankar to visit Russia, co-chair key trade and economic commission
“Addressing this imbalance is today one of our foremost priorities. Progress on market access, removal of tariff and non-tariff barriers, strengthening payment mechanisms and stronger business-to-business engagement will be critical for addressing this imbalance and achieving our shared objective of $100 billion in bilateral trade by 2030,” Jaishankar said at the start of the meeting.
Jaishankar made three proposals for the next phase of the India-Russia economic partnership – focusing on implementation and outcomes to prioritise deliverables and solving problems, strengthening engagement with businesses by aligning institutional mechanisms with industry priorities, identifying bottlenecks and improving policy responses, and exploring new possibilities to address the needs of de-risking and diversifying.
The discussions between Jaishankar and Manturov also encompassed cooperation in trade, investments, energy, fertilisers, nuclear energy, connectivity, technology, space and mobility of professionals. The two sides also reviewed the progress in discussions between India and the Eurasian Economic Union on a free trade agreement.
Manturov said Rosatom’s involvement in building the Kudankulam nuclear power plant in Tamil Nadu could be the basis for expanding cooperation in nuclear energy, including the “creation of new power generation facilities in India, including small-scale ones, as well as the localisation of equipment and nuclear fuel production”.
Russia also sees potential for new joint projects in the extraction and processing of non-ferrous and rare earth metals, Manturov said. Russia and India are also discussing cooperation in space exploration, including manned spaceflight, rocket propulsion and satellite navigation, he said.
The prototype of a high-speed electric train jointly produced by India and Russia will be assembled by the end of the year, after which serial production is expected to begin, Manturov announced at the meeting. “Within this framework, the flagship project in transport engineering — the development and production of the Vande Bharat electric trains — is systematically developing,” he said.
Also Read | Russia tests readiness for new round of military mobilization
In March 2023, a consortium led by Russia’s Transmashholding won a $6.5-billion tender for the development, production and 35-year service of 1,920 Vande Bharat electric train cars.
Manturov also prioritised cooperation in energy security, including the supply of oil, petroleum products and coal, as well as joint investment projects in hydrocarbon production and processing. Russia is currently among the top two suppliers of energy to India.
Russian energy minister Sergei Tsivilev described India as a key partner for the country’s fuel and energy sector, while deputy prime minister Alexander Novak noted that Moscow is interested in Indian investments in the Russian oil and gas sector, and developing a distribution network involving Russian companies in India.
Manturov also noted that tourist flows between Russia and India had increased by 8% in the first half of 2026, with more than 25,000 Indian tourists visiting Russia. Around 50,000 Russians also visited India, he said. Referring to labour migration, he said Russia and India are focusing on expanding the legal framework to create stable and transparent conditions for attracting workers.
The number of Indian students in Russia has also grown to almost 40,000, Manturov said. Support for talented children and youth can be a new vector of cooperation between the two countries, he added.
