headline: ‘CAA citizenship hearings will be over soon’: Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari says 23,000 certificates already issued
full_text:
‘CAA citizenship hearings will be over soon’: Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari says 23,000 certificates already issued
Suvendu Adhikari had said on August 1 that all pending applications for citizenship under the CAA in the state would be disposed of within the next six months.
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday said that hearings of applications for citizenship under the CAA will soon be over, and so far the state has issued certificates to 23,000 people out of 2.30 lakh applicants.
Addressing a press conference at the state secretariat 'Nabanna', Adhikari said the hearings related to citizenship under the CAA would be completed expeditiously, and certificates would be issued soon.
The CAA or the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, seeks to grant Indian citizenship to refugees belonging to six communities, who had sought shelter in India before December 31, 2014, due to religious persecution in three neighbouring countries - Pakistan, Bangladesh and Bangladesh. The six communities are Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians.
"We will complete the hearings quickly through the district magistrates. Out of the 2.30 lakh cases, 23,000 have received certificates and 2.07 lakh are still pending," Adhikari told a press conference.
He added that those who had not yet applied for citizenship under CAA would also be able to do so and stated that the process for Hindu refugees who came from Bangladesh, citing religious persecution, would be expedited.
"We will complete the hearings quickly and issue certificates to Hindu refugees who came from Bangladesh because of religious persecution," the chief minister said.
Adhikari also sought to reassure members of the Matua community and other Hindu refugees who had been waiting for CAA certificates for a long time that they will receive their certificates from him.
"The Government of India has entrusted this responsibility to me," the CM said.
Adhikari had said on August 1 that all pending applications for citizenship under the CAA in the state would be disposed of within the next six months.
On the law-and-order front, Adhikari on Monday announced that a provision of a new legislation would come into force from Monday and warned that those damaging government property would not be spared.
The CM was apparently referring to the West Bengal Public Safety and Control of Anti-Social Activities Bill, 2026, which was passed by the assembly in July. The legislation, popularly referred to as the anti-goonda bill, was brought with the stated objective of curbing anti-social activities and strengthening preventive action by the police and administration.
"From today, a part of the anti-goonda law has come into effect in West Bengal. No one will be spared if government property is damaged," he said.
Adhikari further said those found responsible for damaging public property would be liable to pay three times the cost of the damage, along with interest. He also warned of swift action in cases involving attacks on police personnel.
The Assembly had also passed amendments to the West Bengal Maintenance of Public Order Act alongside the anti-goonda legislation. The measures include provisions relating to preventive detention and stricter action involving property of persons accused of anti-social activities.
The chief minister's remarks on public property came against the backdrop of earlier incidents of violence and damage to government assets during protests against the CAA in parts of Murshidabad and other areas of the state.
Incidentally, the Bengal CM has repeatedly maintained that his government would adopt a zero-tolerance approach towards attacks on police personnel and damage to public property.

headline: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA), led by Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, has launched a crackdown on Mumbai's leading eateries over hygiene violations. Licences of nine outlets in the city have been suspended, including five restaurant...
full_text:
The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA), led by Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, has launched a crackdown on Mumbai's leading eateries over hygiene violations. Licences of nine outlets in the city have been suspended, including five restaurants linked to the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) offering various cuisines. The action follows similar raids and licence suspensions at other high-profile venues in Mumbai, such as the CCI, Goregaon Sports Club, and Radio Club, as authorities target establishments failing to maintain required hygiene standards.
Ahead of the festive season, onion prices have begun to soar alongside sugar price hikes. The average retail price of onions has increased by forty-five percent compared to last year and nineteen percent from last month. The government clarified that seasonal demand in August and September, along with weather conditions and supply chain disruptions, contributed to the surge. Unseasonal rain has particularly impacted onion supplies from Maharashtra. To cool down soaring retail prices and stabilize supply, the government is bringing in onion shipments using the Kanda Express.
Sugar prices in India have surged nearly 40% within a month, rising from 48 rupees per kilogram in July to 62 rupees, threatening to raise costs during the upcoming festive season. In response, the Modi government has decided to import sugar and capped stock limits for bulk buyers at 15 days to curb hoarding. While Maharashtra farmers claim they are not benefiting from the price rise, the government attributes the shortage to crop disease and water scarcity, denying that ethanol diversion caused the spike.
The Jammu and Kashmir State Investigation Agency has reopened multiple cases involving the killings of Kashmiri Pandits, including the 1998 Wandhama massacre in Ganderbal, where 23 Kashmiri Pandits were shot dead by terrorists. Other cases being probed include the murders of SKIMS nurse Sarla Bhat, author Sarvanand Cole Premi, BJP leader Tikalal Taplu, and Judge Neelkanth Ganju. Raids have been conducted across the Kashmir Valley to track terror associates. Meanwhile, displaced Kashmiri Pandits working under Prime Minister packages face fresh threat letters from terror outfits like Lashkar, prompting authorities to bolster security in Shopian. The community has demanded that probes be expedited so those responsible are brought to justice.
Pakistan is attempting to expand the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, signed recently between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey, by inviting Iran and Bangladesh into the alliance. The proposed expansion aims to build an Islamic security framework under Pakistan's nuclear umbrella, despite longstanding regional rivalry between Saudi Arabia and Iran. Meanwhile, Pakistan's Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir arrived in Tehran to mediate between Iran and the United States ahead of potential US economic sanctions. Wearing civilian attire during meetings, Munir's visit is viewed as part of diplomatic efforts following communications involving US President Donald Trump and Pakistani leadership.

headline: A few hours of rainfall once again brought Delhi NCR, particularly Gurugram, to a complete standstill. Several parts of the millennium city experienced severe waterlogging, flooded roads, and heavy traffic chaos, leaving numerous vehicles stranded. T...
full_text:
A few hours of rainfall once again brought Delhi NCR, particularly Gurugram, to a complete standstill. Several parts of the millennium city experienced severe waterlogging, flooded roads, and heavy traffic chaos, leaving numerous vehicles stranded. The severe disruption has drawn attention to Gurugram's rapidly crumbling urban infrastructure despite its high per capita income. The incident underscores growing concerns over urban planning and the quality of infrastructure across Indian cities during heavy monsoon spells.
A fire broke out in the neonatal intensive care unit of District Women's Hospital in Amravati, Maharashtra, after a ventilator reportedly exploded around 3:30 AM on Monday. Out of thirty-nine newborns present in the ICU, staff rescued thirty-six babies, while three newborns lost their lives. Six critically affected newborns were transferred to a nearby super speciality hospital for treatment. Following the incident, the Maharashtra government ordered a high-level probe and announced five lakh rupees in financial aid for the victims' families. The tragedy has raised serious questions regarding hospital safety standards and infrastructure in smaller towns.
Former Indian cricket captain Kapil Dev commented on the joint letter written by 21 international cricket captains to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif concerning jailed former cricketer and Prime Minister Imran Khan. Dev stated that international players are supporting a friend whose cricketing skills they admired. He emphasized that they do not know the law of Pakistan, but are appealing on humanitarian grounds for proper facilities and medical care for a prisoner who served as a top cricketer and prime minister. Dev remarked, "We want he should get the best treatment what as we are asking for," clarifying that they are making a request rather than demanding a reply.
The Tamil Nadu government has put the proposed second greenfield airport for Chennai at Parandur on hold. The decision was announced after concerns were flagged over the site's wetlands and runway construction feasibility. Originally planned across 5,746 hectares at an estimated cost of 27,400 crore rupees, the project faced years of protests from farmers alongside environmental concerns. The government is now searching for an alternative location that causes minimal damage to agricultural land. However, halting the project has triggered a political debate over potential delays, even as capacity pressures mount at the existing Chennai International Airport due to rising passenger traffic and high-value cargo movement.
A major political conflict has erupted between the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Congress following remarks by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi during his 'Chhatro Ki Goonj' outreach program in Pune. Discussing women's safety and patriarchy, Rahul Gandhi quoted the Manusmriti, claiming it promotes the suppression of women and accusing the BJP and RSS of attempting to keep women caged. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath criticized Gandhi for insulting Indian cultural heritage, while BJP MP Dr. Sudhanshu Trivedi alleged the comments reflect a foreign, Marxist agenda to divide society. BJP leaders further questioned Congress's stance on women's rights regarding practices like triple talaq, Sharia, and the hijab, while Congress representative Pankhuri Pathak defended Gandhi's dialogue with young women. In international developments, Pakistan Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir visited Tehran regarding a proposed Joint Defense Agreement involving Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Turkey, Iran, and Bangladesh. Meanwhile, in Jammu and Kashmir, the State Investigation Agency reopened key Kashmiri Pandit murder cases, including the 1998 Wandhama massacre.

full_text:

TN CM Vijay announces 3 free LPG cylinders, expands free bus travel for women
NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday announced a set of welfare measures in the state Assembly, including three free cooking gas cylinders a year for eligible beneficiaries and an expansion of the fare-free bus travel scheme for women.Under the cooking gas scheme, the amount for the three cylinders will be credited directly to the bank accounts of eligible beneficiaries.Vijay announced the launch of the Vetri Payanam scheme, expanding the existing fare-free bus travel programme for women across the state.
Under the scheme, women will be allowed to travel free of charge on Express, LSS and Deluxe government buses operating in metropolitan and urban areas. For inter-district travel, the benefit will cover ordinary-fare government buses in mofussil and hilly areas.The scheme will come into effect from October 2, marking the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. Vijay said there would be no income ceiling or restriction on the number of trips under the programme. Transgender persons will also be eligible for free travel.
"No riders like income ceiling or number of trips for women to avail fare-free bus travel," Vijay added.
Vijay had earlier outlined several welfare measures in his election manifesto, including six free LPG cylinders a year for every family, up to 200 units of free electricity, a monthly assistance of Rs 2,500 for women below the age of 60, and family health coverage of up to Rs 25 lakh.

headline: 3 free LPG cylinders, bus travel scheme amped: TVK chief Vijay's big announcements for women
full_text:
3 free LPG cylinders, bus travel scheme amped: TVK chief Vijay's big announcements for women
The free LPG cylinders will be offered to women heads of households under a scheme called ‘Annapoorani Super Six, said Tamil Nadu CM and TVK chief Vijay.
Tamil Nadu chief minister and TVK supremo C Joseph Vijay on Monday made major announcements aimed at women in the state assembly, including the expansion of free bus travel scheme and three free LPG cylinders annually for households.
The free LPG cylinders, reportedly carrying an estimated annual budgetary outlay of ₹4,000 crore, will be offered to women heads of households under a scheme called ‘Annapoorani Super Six.
Chief minister C Joseph Vijay said the LPG offer under 'Annapoorani Super Six' is expected to benefit 1.3 crore families, adding that the scheme will be implemented from Pongal (in January).
Deep Dive
Expanding the free bus travel initiative, Vijay said the scheme meant for women will cover state-run buses, express, as well as deluxe buses. “No riders like income ceiling or number of trips for women to avail fare-free bus travel,” said Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) chief Vijay in assembly.
The 'Annapoorni Super Six scheme'
Addressing the assembly, the chief minister stated that the Annapoorni Super Six scheme will cover households with an annual income not exceeding ₹2.5 lakh, economically weaker sections, families of small and marginal farmers, and families of differently-abled persons, according to news agency ANI.
The cost of the cooking gas cylinder will be reimbursed and directly credited to the bank accounts of the female heads of families upon booking and delivery based on the official billing from oil marketing companies.
Chennai's 2nd airport plan dropped, for now
The chief minister also announced that his government would drop the plan to establish Chennai's second airport at Parandur, saying the project would affect agricultural land and disrupt the livelihoods of farmers and residents.
Speaking in the assembly, Vijay said Chennai's Meenambakkam airport, operated by the Airports Authority of India (AAI), currently has the capacity to handle 30 million passengers annually. He said a new airport was needed considering the city's growing requirements, industrial development and increasing cargo transportation.
However, the chief minister said the new airport should be located at a place where agricultural land and residential areas are minimally affected, ANI news agency reported.

Rai also hit back at the criticism by drawing a comparison with BJP leaders. headline: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders have questioned the remarks made by the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on the Manusmriti and women’s rights. BJP MP Nishikant Dubey quoted two verses from the text that emphasise respect fo...
full_text:
Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders have questioned the remarks made by the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on the Manusmriti and women’s rights. BJP MP Nishikant Dubey quoted two verses from the text that emphasise respect for women, while Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma accused Mr. Gandhi of using women’s empowerment as a pretext to target Hinduism.
Mr. Sarma also asked how often the Congress leader had spoken against what he described as “patriarchal and medieval practices that persist under Sharia”.
During an interaction with female students in Maharashtra on August 22, 2026, Mr. Gandhi spoke against the “Manusmriti mindset”, called on students to “smash patriarchy”, and said women belonged to themselves, not to their fathers, husbands or sons.
On social media platform X, the Congress party shared a photograph of him with an attributed quote: “The Manusmriti states that a woman must never be independent. But I believe women should be independent. You may have relationships with your father, brother, husband, or son, but you do not belong to them. You belong to yourself.”
Responding to the post the same day, Mr. Dubey tagged a message to Mr. Gandhi’s X handle, saying: “Reading the Manusmriti may not be possible for you, @RahulGandhi ji. This is a shloka from the Manusmriti; read, understand, and speak. Because of the English language, do you know nothing about India’s Vedas, Puranas, scriptures, Ramayana, and Mahabharata?”
Mr. Dubey mentioned two verses from the Manusmriti, along with translations that read: “Where women are respected and worshipped, the gods reside; where they are not respected, all work and noble deeds bring no results.”
On Monday (August 24, 2026), Mr. Sarma posted on X: “Rahul Gandhi is no champion of women’s rights. He is simply a Hindu baiter, using the cause of women’s empowerment as a convenient smokescreen to target and discredit Hindu Dharma.”
“Consider this: how many times has he spoken with the same outrage against patriarchal and medieval practices that persist under Sharia? Never. While Sharia is foundational to Islamic jurisprudence, Manusmriti has no comparable scriptural authority in Hindu Dharma. It is not even a universally binding code for Hindus,” Mr. Sarma said.
“Yet ask yourself: how many times does Rahul Gandhi attack the Manusmriti, and how many times does he attack Sharia with the same fervour? The enduring strength of Hinduism lies in its unique ability to evolve, reform and adapt with time – as it has for millennia and as it will for eternity,” he said.
“Every Hindu must therefore ask: what is Rahul Gandhi’s real intent – championing women’s rights, or using them as a pretext to malign Hindu Dharma? Cong[ress] rhetoric on women’s rights rings hollow when measured against its own record. They betrayed our mothers and sisters by reversing the effect of the Shah Bano judgment,” Mr. Sarma added.
Stating that the Congress opposed the law against ‘Triple Talaq’, he alleged that just to “cling to power in Karnataka”, Mr. Gandhi had ensured “not a single woman found a place in the State Cabinet”.
“So here is a simple challenge to Rahul Gandhi: If women’s equality truly comes before politics, will he unequivocally support a Uniform Civil Code that guarantees equal rights irrespective of religion? Or will his idea of ‘women’s rights’ continue to begin and end with attacking Hinduism?” Mr. Sarma said.

headline: CM Vijay says plan for 2nd airport for Chennai at Parandur to be dropped, new location to be proposed
full_text:
CM Vijay says plan for 2nd airport for Chennai at Parandur to be dropped, new location to be proposed
A new airport for Chennai will be proposed at a location where there is no opposition from the people, Chief Minister Vijay said.
The Tamil Nadu government has officially announced that the proposed plan for a second airport for Chennai at Parandur will be dropped. Parandur, located about 60km from west of Chennai, has seen long-drawn protests against the airport proposed by the previous MK Stalin government.
Chief Minister Vijay on Monday said a new airport will be proposed at a location where there is no opposition from the people. The new location will be decided after a careful study of technical feasibility by expert teams, he said.
ALSO READ: Fissures emerge between Left and TVK over Tamil Nadu’s anti-protest circular
Deep Dive
Vijay said the decision to cancel the project was taken to prevent relocation of a large number of people and protect agricultural land in the area. He also slammed the previous DMK government for picking the largely populated area.
Protests against Parandur airport
Former chief minister M K Stalin had, on August 2, 2022, announced the plan to build a second airport at Parandur at an estimated cost of ₹20,000 crore. The airport was expected to have an annual capacity of 10 crore passengers.
Soon after the announcement by the state government in 2022, residents of Parandur and its nearby villages staged protests for over a year against the then DMK regime claiming that the greenfield project would affect their livelihood.

In January 2025, Vijay who was the President of Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam joined the protest at Parandur and extended his party’s support to the agitating villagers.
Vijay announces LPG scheme
The Tamil Nadu CM also announced a major LPG scheme in the Assembly. “Under the Annapooranai Super Six scheme, free LPG cylinders will be provided to every household in Tamil Nadu from Pongal onwards, beginning January 14. The Tamil Nadu government will credit the amount for three cylinders directly into consumers’ bank accounts," said Vijay.
An amount of ₹4,000 crore will be allocated every year for the scheme which will benefit 1 crore 30 lakh families.
“Families with an annual income of less than ₹2.5 lakh, small and marginal farmers’ families, families with differently abled members and other vulnerable sections will benefit from the scheme," he said.

headline: Chennai: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay-led TVK government has decided to scrap the proposed greenfield airport project at Parandur in Kancheepuram district, planned by the previous DMK government as Chennai’s second airport. Vijay told the assembly ...
full_text:
Chennai: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay-led TVK government has decided to scrap the proposed greenfield airport project at Parandur in Kancheepuram district, planned by the previous DMK government as Chennai’s second airport. Vijay told the assembly Monday the decision has been taken to safeguard agricultural lands and the livelihoods of farmers and residents.
“I stand firmly with the people protesting against the airport to be established in Chennai’s Parandur and the surrounding villages. In order to safeguard the villages, the Parandur airport will be scrapped,” Vijay said in a statement in the House under Rule number 110.
Rule 110 allows ministers to make statements on matters of public importance in the assembly, with the Speaker’s consent, without an immediate debate on the statement.
DMK members staged a walkout after being denied an opportunity to speak on the announcement. Party leader and former chief minister MK Stalin, under whose term the project was approved. called the TVK government’s decision a “devastating blow to the employment dreams of Tamil Nadu’s youth”, saying it would hand a “jackpot” to competing states.
Vijay recalled visiting Ekanapuram and nearby villages on 20 January 2025, when he met the protesters. He had also voiced his disapproval of the project at his first public meeting in Vikravandi in October 2024.
“To fulfil the promise I made to the people to protect their lands, the steps taken to establish a new airport in Parandur will be abandoned by the TVK government,” he told the assembly,
The government will identify alternative sites around Chengalpattu and other areas in Kancheepuram, where impact on farmland and residential areas is minimal. The government will form expert teams to conduct technical feasibility studies to set up the new airport, he said.
Meanwhile, the existing Chennai airport in Meenambakkam will be expanded with a fifth terminal on the northwestern side. The expansion is expected to add significant passenger capacity to the current 30 million passengers per year.
The government remains committed to the Hosur airport project, subject to Defence Ministry clearance on airspace restrictions.
As per the TVK-led government’s instructions, land acquisition for Parandur has been stalled. and a decision is yet to be made on the already acquired land. Around 1,700 acres of land had already been acquired by March this year.
Stakeholders have emphasised the need for a second airport in Chennai due to growing passenger traffic, industrial expansion and capacity constraints at Meenambakkam.
While multiple sites were examined over the last 20 years, it was in 2022 that the then DMK government shortlisted four locations including Padalam, Thiruporur, Pannur and Parandur, after obtaining a feasibility report.
The Airports Authority of India narrowed it to Pannur and Parandur. In August 2022, Parandur was selected.
The project envisaged acquiring roughly 5,000–5,700 acres across 13 villages, with plans of dual parallel runways for simultaneous take off and landing, three terminals and handling up to 100 million passengers annually planned at an estimated cost of around Rs 27,400 crore. It was positioned to support the industrial corridor and improve connectivity.
However, the villagers opposed it.
The Civil Aviation Ministry granted in-principle approval in April 2025 and the state gave it special project status under the Tamil Nadu Land Consolidation for Special Projects Act to ease acquisition.
Residents of Ekanapuram began an indefinite agitation on 16 December 2022, which continued for over 1,000 days.
Vijay had also extended support and met the protesters in 2025.
The reasons for their objections included the displacement of more than 1,000 families, loss of fertile multi-crop agricultural land, impact on wetlands and water bodies, disruption of canal systems linked to Chennai’s flood management, and uncertain livelihoods.
After the TVK assumed power, ministers reiterated the party’s unchanged stand that a second airport is needed, but not at the cost of agricultural land and water bodies.
And Monday, Vijay formally announced the scrapping of the project. The decision drew sharp criticism from the opposition DMK.
Also read: Joyalukkas says 1-paisa bid for Tamil Nadu’s gold ring scheme is welfare support, not profit move
‘Jackpot for competing states’
Former chief minister MK Stalin called the scrapping of the Parandur project an irreversible setback for Tamil Nadu’s growth.
“The announcement made today by the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu to drop the Parandur International Airport project will set the State’s development back by several years. Tamil Nadu’s interests cannot be mortgaged for petty political considerations. An announcement of such far-reaching importance being made under Rule No. 110, shutting out any opportunity for debate or even for members to voice their views, is deeply troubling,” he wrote on X.
Stalin further said that Tamil Nadu leads the country across sectors, from electronics exports to automobiles and stated that a world-class airport in its capital is not merely desirable, but absolutely essential.
“Rejecting such a vital project is not change. It is a massive disappointment. The site was carefully selected after evaluating all available alternatives, and the land acquisition process has been almost completed. With several stages of preparatory work and approvals already completed, we had drawn up plans to ensure that construction could begin at a rapid pace once we returned to office. If the new government now starts all over again, identifies another location and goes through the entire process before work can even begin, Tamil Nadu’s growth trajectory itself will DROP,” he said on X.
Dropping Parandur is not Change. It's an irreversible setback for Tamil Nadu's growth
The announcement made today by the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu to drop the Parandur International Airport project will set the State’s development back by several years. Tamil Nadu’s… pic.twitter.com/QHZdVdK21L
— M.K.Stalin (@mkstalin) August 24, 2026
The decision would push the state to the bottom of the table in terms of attracting investments, he said, adding the announcement is nothing short of a jackpot for competing states. “Without industrial growth, economic targets of one trillion USD or 1.5 trillion USD are simply impossible to achieve. Taken without foresight, planning or consultation, this decision by the TVK government is a devastating blow to the employment dreams of Tamil Nadu’s youth.”
DMK leader and former Industries Minister TRB Raja called it an extremely sad day for Tamil Nadu.
“Years of hard work and intense planning to give Chennai the dual-runway Greenfield airport it desperately needs have been sacrificed at the altar of politics. Industry experts understand the stakes. Investment promotion agencies in neighbouring states will now quietly rejoice, saying: ‘Tamil Nadu has shot itself in the foot’,” he wrote on X.
He further added that Chennai’s growth and that of Tamil Nadu’s will now face a serious hurdle. “We most urgently need a truly world-class international airport capable of handling large aircraft, with two operational 4,000m+ parallel runways. I find it extremely difficult to believe that the very officers who worked so hard on this project supported this decision. They know better than most that there is no better alternative option given the environmental and aviation concerns.”
TRB Raja further said that the consequences of quashing the project would go far beyond just an airport and said that industrial growth has been compromised for plain politics.
“The entire industrial corridor from Poonamallee to Kanchipuram, which accounts for nearly 41% of India’s electronics exports, could have received a massive boost. Better port connectivity, reliable water infrastructure for industry and direct global air connectivity could have boosted this region and TN into one of the world’s most important manufacturing hubs, creating at least a million new jobs over time.”
Former minister Thangam Thennarasu and other DMK leaders also echoed concerns about economic damage, potential flight of industries to Andhra Pradesh, and the undoing of careful technical evaluation that led to Parandur’s selection. DMK members staged a walkout in the Assembly after being denied an opportunity to speak on the announcement.
Meanwhile, Confederation of Real Estate Developers’ Associations of India (CREDAI) Chennai, which has been pushing for a second airport in Tamil Nadu, said it respects the government’s position and its sensitivity to the concerns of farmers, but it views this decision as a setback that further delays the city’s quest for a world-class airport.
Any large land acquisition will inevitably face farmer and environmental challenges, but these concerns must be balanced against the state’s development interests, said the industry body that represents real estate developers and builders.
“Connectivity remains central to Chennai’s growth story. However, we have slipped to sixth position in passenger traffic, with Kolkata overtaking us. Peer cities are moving decisively on aviation infrastructure Bengaluru and Hyderabad continue to expand and plan additional airport capacity, while the Delhi-NCR and Mumbai regions have added new airports alongside their existing ones. Chennai has historically competed with these cities for investment, industrial relocation and talent, and sustained momentum on airport infrastructure will be important to protect that competitive position,” a statement from CREDAI said.
CREDAI Chennai urged the government to fast-track the selection and finalisation of an alternative site without delay. The association also welcomed the interim step of expanding Meenambakkam, including the proposed new terminal capacity, but cautioned that this expansion has severe constraints.

Why Vijay rejected Parandur

Tamil Nadu's interests cannot be mortgaged for petty political considerations," Stalin said.He also called the decision a setback to employment opportunities for Tamil Nadu's youth.
DMK warns of economic fallout

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday (August 24, 2026) in Raebareli hit out at the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of denouncing India’s traditions and heritage.
“Rahul Gandhi has taken an oath to uphold the Constitution, yet considers it his ‘birthright’ to criticise India’s traditions and heritage.”
“Rahul Gandhi goes outside Uttar Pradesh and defames and insults the State and goes outside India to insult the country. The Indian Army fights enemies on the borders, while Rahul Gandhi asks soldiers for proof. His party, Congress, has questioned the existence of Lord Ram in Ayodhya,” said Mr. Adityanath, addressing a gathering during a commemorative ceremony held on the 222nd birth anniversary of Avadh Kesari Rana Beni Madhav Baksh Singh, the icon of the First War of Independence of 1857.
Reacting to Mr. Gandhi’s remarks on Manusmriti, the U.P. CM said that as the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, Mr. Gandhi is expected to demonstrate accountability towards democracy and the Constitution. “If you want to understand Manu, you should read the Atharvaveda, Shatapatha Brahmana and Matsya Purana,” he said.
“No person goes through life without receiving care and protection from women in the form of a mother, sister, wife or daughter. India’s tradition concerning relationships between men and women, he said, needs to be understood in its broader context rather than viewed selectively,” added the U.P. CM.
Mr. Adityanath urged young people that should not to go in a direction that could later force their parents or families to apologise; the CM was referring to alleged abusive remarks against the Prime Minister at Jantar Mantar.
“The Prime Minister is not merely an individual but a constitutional institution of India. Therefore, he said, using abusive language against the Prime Minister amounts not only to insulting an individual but also to insulting the institution and the country,” said Mr. Adityanath.
The U.P. CM further accused Mr. Gandhi of allowing “urban Naxals” to damage the future of the present generation and questioned why he wanted to destroy India’s heritage and jeopardize the country’s future.
“The country had expected Rahul Gandhi, as Leader of Opposition, to play a positive and responsible role, but he completely distanced himself from his responsibilities. Amethi and Raebareli had supported the Gandhi family for decades. Still, the same family had also created an identity crisis for the region,” he siad.
“The Congress had shown greater interest in naming monuments and institutions after one family than in honouring great freedom fighters such as Rana Beni Madhav Baksh Singh, Lala Chand Sonekar and the valiant Veera Pasi linked to the region, honoring the country’s real heroes had never been a priority for the Congress,” alleged Mr. Adityanath.
The U.P. CM accused the Congress for consistently weakened democratic institutions. “Congress had difficulty accepting national heroes such as Veer Savarkar, Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. The Port Blair airport had been named after Veer Savarkar during the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government but was later renamed by a Congress government,” he said.
The U.P. CM stressed that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government had worked to establish due respect for freedom fighters and other national figures. “Along with the construction of the grand Ram Temple, he said, figures such as Maharishi Valmiki, Goswami Tulsidas, Nishadraj and Mata Shabari had also been accorded due honour,” he said.
In his address, the U.P. CM paid tribute to icons of independence movement, Mangal Pandey, Dhan Singh Gurjar, Nana Saheb, Tatya Tope, Rani Lakshmibai, Veera Pasi.
“The first phase of work on the Rana Beni Madhav Baksh Singh memorial had been completed. The total sanctioned budget was ₹21 crore, while approximately ₹25 crore had been spent. For the second phase, we will install statues of Veera Pasi and his associates at the memorial,” he said.

headline: FDA suspends licenses of restaurants in Mumbai Cricket Association premises over 'hygiene' issues
full_text:
FDA suspends licenses of restaurants in Mumbai Cricket Association premises over 'hygiene' issues
The five MCA outlets facing the Maharashtra FDA action are the Permit Room, Pavilion, Mediterranean, Oriental Swing, and Clubway & Pastry Counter.
The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the food licences of five outlets at the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) premises over alleged hygiene issues, including violations of food safety norms, flagging deficiencies in food handling, storage, refrigeration, and sanitation.
The action comes as the FDA, under Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, intensifies inspections of food establishments across Maharashtra to ensure compliance with food safety and hygiene requirements.
As part of its statewide drive, the FDA has suspended the licences of 11 food establishments, including the five outlets at MCA, news agency PTI reported on Monday.
The FDA inspected 45 hotels, restaurants, eateries and dhabas during the drive, issued improvement notices to 33 establishments and conducted 25 raids, according to a press note.
The five MCA outlets facing action are the Permit Room, Pavilion, Mediterranean, Oriental Swing, and Clubway & Pastry Counter. The FDA inspected the outlets on August 20 and found various deficiencies related to hygiene, food handling, storage, refrigeration and sanitation.
What the FDA found at the MCA premises
According to the FDA release, inspectors found ice accumulation in a kitchen refrigerator at the Permit Room, along with an unclean, slippery floor near the kitchen entrance, inadequate temperature control, deteriorated raw materials, and deficiencies in food storage and handling.
The outlet also lacked food-grade conformity certificates for food-contact packaging material and did not conduct regular checks of cooking oil.
The Pavilion faced action after inspectors found ice accumulation, unclean refrigerator components, poor segregation of food items in cold storage, inadequate refrigeration calibration, improper thawing of frozen food, and shortcomings in cooling and storage practices.
At Mediterranean, the FDA found inadequate sanitisation of food equipment, improper cooling, poor portioning practices, inadequate thawing of frozen food, deficient temperature controls and shortcomings in the handling of raw materials and packaging.
The Oriental Swing outlet was found to have an improperly calibrated refrigeration system, an unclean kitchen floor, damaged plaster or paint on part of the kitchen ceiling, inadequate sanitisation and deficiencies in temperature control and oil-quality checks.
At the Clubway & Pastry Counter, the FDA found inadequate work space, improper storage of raw food, a lack of gloves for a food handler, and inadequate measures to prevent dust, dirt, and insects from entering the food preparation area.
Other eateries that faced action
Besides the five MCA outlets, the statewide action included Lenexis Foodworks in Mahim, CafÃ© Cadell in Shivaji Park, China Town Fast Food Centre in Mulund, Morya Misal in Warje and Saoji Upahar Gruh in Nagpur.
The FDA suspended the registration of China Town Fast Food Centre with immediate effect after finding excessive use of artificial colour and MSG, repeated use of highly oxidised cooking oil, cockroach infestation, unhygienic food storage, a risk of cross-contamination between vegetarian and non-vegetarian food and inadequate drainage.
The FDA also suspended the licence of Morya Misal in Pune after finding artificial colouring in food, and storage and use of expired food products.

headline: Manipur: 1 CRPF personnel injured, 2 houses burnt by unknown armed individuals
full_text:
Manipur: 1 CRPF personnel injured, 2 houses burnt by unknown armed individuals
The gunfight broke out after two houses belonging to separate communities were set ablaze by an unidentified group of people
One Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel sustained a bullet injury during a gunfight between security forces and unidentified armed individuals in the Taphou area of Manipur’s Senapati district on Monday, officials said.
The gunfight broke out after two houses belonging to separate communities were set ablaze by an unidentified group of people, triggering tension in the area. One of the two houses belonged to a Kuki family while the other belonged to the Poumai community (a sub-community of the Naga community).
The CRPF personnel sustained a bullet injury to his leg during the exchange of gunfire and was evacuated to a nearby hospital for treatment. Officials said additional security forces have been deployed in the area to control the situation. A group of villagers have evacuated as well.
The reason for the attack was not immediately known.
According to a video clip circulating on social media, following the incident, locals from the area blocked National Highway 2 (Imphal-Dimapur) at Senapati headquarters. Protestors were seen blocking the highway with burning tyres and debris.
The Taphou Kuki Village Authority condemned the burning of a Kuki house and described the incident as “highly deplorable, inhuman and unacceptable”.

The village authority urged the district administration and police to take immediate and appropriate action to investigate the incident, identify those responsible and ensure that justice is delivered in accordance with the law.
The village authority has served a 24-hour deadline for the culprits involved in burning the Kuki house to claim responsibility and resolve the issue according to community law.
Tension between the Naga and Kuki communities has been simmering in the area since the twin ambush carried out at two different locations on May 13 -- one at Noney district and other at Kangpokpi district. Four persons including three church leaders and one Naga man was killed in the two incidents.
On the same day, 48 civilians belonging to Naga and Kuki-Zo were kidnapped by both the groups in retaliatory tension. Later, nearly after a month of captivity all the hostages were set free however. Six Naga men, however, were found dead near Kharam Vaiphei (Kuki village) in Kangpokpi district.
The case has been under investigation by National Investigating Agency (NIA) and as a part of the investigation four individuals including a couple have been arrested in the month of July on two separate occasions.

SC issues notice to Centre, CBI on plea for CBI probe into JPSC exam 'irregularities'
New Delhi, The Supreme Court on Monday issued notices to the Centre and the state government on a plea seeking an independent, time-bound probe by the CBI into alleged malpractices in the Jharkhand Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination.
A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought a response from the Union of India, the Jharkhand government, the Jharkhand Public Service Commission, CBI and others.
Senior advocate Manan Kumar Mishra, appearing for the petitioner, submitted that the plea seeks a CBI inquiry or an inquiry by a former judge of this court.
The top court was hearing a petition filed by activist Harisharan Devgan, through advocate Satyam Singh Rajput.
"The present writ petition under Article 32 of the Constitution of India is being preferred in public interest seeking urgent intervention of this court in relation to serious and substantial concerns regarding the integrity, fairness, transparency and credibility of the Jharkhand Combined Civil Services Preliminary Competitive Examination 2025, conducted by respondent no. 2 Jharkhand Public Service Commission pursuant to Advertisement No. 01/2026 on April 19, 2026," it said.
The plea has also sought transfer of the investigation from the state CID to the CBI to ensure an impartial probe into public officials and examination agencies.
The petitioner submitted that the controversy cannot appropriately be examined merely as a dispute concerning individual candidates or isolated instances of alleged malpractice.
"The allegations require examination of the entire examination chain, including preparation and printing of question papers, coding, storage, transportation, distribution, conduct of the examination, collection and custody of OMR sheets, scanning, coding and decoding, evaluation, storage and access to electronic examination data, generation of the result and publication thereof," it said.
It has also sought direction to immediately secure all physical and digital evidence, including original and candidate-held OMR carbon copies, CCTV footage, and server audit logs, to prevent tampering.
"The petitioner is conscious that the mere existence of allegations or public protests cannot, by itself, justify cancellation of an examination. The petitioner, therefore, does not seek cancellation merely on the basis of media reports or allegations.
"The principal relief sought is for an independent, impartial, comprehensive and time-bound investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation, so that the nature, extent, mechanism and impact of the alleged irregularities may be objectively determined," it said.
The petition said the consequential question: Whether the preliminary examination can safely be relied upon? must be determined based on objective and scientifically verifiable evidence.
The petitioner said he raises a constitutional question concerning whether a public recruitment examination conducted by a constitutional authority has retained the minimum degree of fairness, transparency, reliability and institutional integrity necessary for its result to constitute the lawful basis for public appointments.

Addressing a programme in Raebareli, Gandhi’s parliamentary constituency, the chief minister said he had recently come across a statement by the Congress leader in Maharashtra, where Rahul Gandhi had reportedly urged women to break free from the “shackles of Manusmriti”.
“As the Leader of the Opposition in Parliament, you are accountable to democracy. You have taken an oath on the Constitution. But you consider abusing India’s heritage your birthright,” Yogi said. “You insult Uttar Pradesh when you travel outside the state and insult India when you go abroad. You seek proof from the soldiers of the Indian Army.”
The chief minister further accused Rahul Gandhi and the Congress of indirectly encouraging elements opposed to the country in India’s fight against terrorism. “Your party questioned the existence of Lord Ram. Your commitment to democracy can be understood from the Emergency,” Yogi said.
Taking on Rahul Gandhi over his comments on Manusmriti, Yogi said, “If you want to understand Manu, read the Atharvaveda and the Matsya Purana. I want to ask whose life has not, in some form, been protected, nurtured or shaped by a woman as a mother, sister, wife or daughter?”

What Rahul said
Speaking at the ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event in Pune on Saturday, Gandhi said that women belong to themselves and not to their fathers, husbands or sons. He termed as shameful the Manusmriti’s assertion that a woman should remain under the authority of male relatives at every stage of her life.
“I would like to quote the Manusmriti here, which clearly says that in childhood, a female must be subject to her father, in youth, she belongs to her husband and when her husband is dead, she belongs to her sons. A woman must never be independent. These words are shameful. These words should never have been spoken,” Gandhi said.
Referring to Gen Z protests at Jantar Mantar, Chief Minister Adityanath further said a young woman had used objectionable language against the Prime Minister and later apologised for it, with her parents also acknowledging that she had made a mistake. “Why do you want to ruin India’s present generation at the hands of urban Naxals? Why do you want to play with India’s future?” Yogi asked.
The chief minister also targeted the Gandhi family, saying that while Raebareli had continued to support them, the family had created an ‘identity crisis’ for the region. “When you insult India’s institutions and make derogatory remarks against the Prime Minister, you are insulting an institution of India. The prime minister is not merely an individual, the office represents an institution of the country,” he said.
“If these institutions are put in the dock, every citizen of India will eventually be put in the dock. When you use abusive language against the prime minister, you insult India and create an identity crisis for the present generation,” Yogi added, urging Rahul Gandhi to refrain from such “irresponsible conduct”.
Yogi targets Congress’s UP leadership
The chief minister did not stop at Rahul Gandhi, taking a swipe at the Congress’s Uttar Pradesh leadership. “This is their history, the history of the Congress’s state president. When a mafia don (referring to Mukhtar Ansari) murdered his brother, this person did not testify against the criminal. “He bowed before the very man who had brutally killed his brother. The situation changed only when the government intervened and crushed that mafia element. Otherwise, these people had turned the state into a mafia-dominated region, creating an identity crisis,” he added.

headline: TMC moves Supreme Court over delay in disqualification decision on 20 rebel MPs; hearing on August 25
full_text:
TMC moves Supreme Court over delay in disqualification decision on 20 rebel MPs; hearing on August 25
TMC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee, in a plea before the top court, has sought an expeditious decision on the same by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla.
The Trinamool Congress on Monday approached the Supreme Court against the delay in deciding on the disqualification of 20 rebel MPs, who have aligned themselves with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI).
TMC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee, in a plea before the top court, has sought an expeditious decision on the same by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, news agency PTI reported.
According to the Supreme Court website, the plea has been listed for a hearing on August 25 by a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.
The 20 rebel MPs, who had split from the TMC, want to merge with the nondescript Nationalist Citizens Party of India, which supports the National Democratic Alliance. 19 of these MPs had on June 14 submitted a petition to Lok Sabha Speaker Birla, seeking recognition of their merger with NCPI. The next day, MP Rachana Banerjee submitted a similar letter. The merger has not yet been approved.
TMC seeks directions for Speaker to decide on disqualification of rebel MPs
Abhishek has, in his plea, challenged the alleged delay in deciding the disqualification proceedings initiated against the MPs. He has sought directions for the Lok Sabha Speaker to decide the disqualification petitions in accordance with the anti-defection provisions of the Constitution, according to the PTI report.
The TMC general secretary had earlier submitted separate petitions against the 20 MPs and urged the Speaker to dispose of them urgently. Abhishek had also met with Birla on August 12 over the issue after sending a written reminder on July 27.
Also Read | Bengal's new world order, 100 days on
The 20 rebel MPs of TMC have sought recognition of their merger with the Tripura-based NCPI. They have since been treated as an NCPI group in the Parliament and participated in NDA parliamentary activities.
However, the TMC has maintained that the MPs were elected on their party symbol and their decision to align with another party amounts to voluntarily giving up membership of TMC, thus attracting disqualification under the anti-defection law.
TMC rebels still awaiting status
TMC rebel leaders, both in West Bengal Assembly and Parliament, are waiting for a decision on their official status. In the Assembly, the Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction of 62 legislators have split from the party. However, there is still no official clarity on the timeline of resolution of their issues, official said, according to an earlier HT report.
While Abhishek has submitted a plea before the SC, officials said that the process of recognition of NCPI might be lengthy. They said it might depend on some external factors -- including a pending case in the Supreme Court filed by Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray against the Election Commission’s decision to recognise the Eknath Shinde-led faction as the real Shiv Sena. The Sena case is reportedly being watched closely by the poll body, which has not yet decided if the Ritabrata-led faction in Bengal Assembly is the real TMC.

headline: TMC moves Supreme Court against delay in disqualification of 20 rebel MPs
full_text:
TMC moves Supreme Court against delay in disqualification of 20 rebel MPs
The bench, comprising CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana, has agreed to hear Abhishek Banerjee's plea challenging the Speaker's failure to take a final decision on the disqualification petitions.
The Trinamool Congress (Mamata Banerjee faction) has approached the Supreme Court against the delay by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla in deciding its petitions seeking the disqualification of 20 rebel MPs. The plea, filed through TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee, will be heard by a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Tuesday.
The bench, comprising CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana, has agreed to hear Banerjee's plea challenging the Speaker's failure to take a final decision on the disqualification petitions.
The TMC has said that the 20 MPs have engaged in activities against the party and later merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI). Banerjee has argued that the MPs should face action under the anti-defection law.
WHAT TRINAMOOL SAYS
According to the petition, Banerjee has repeatedly met Speaker Om Birla since June 2026 and submitted written complaints concerning the conduct of the 20 MPs. However, he has claimed that no satisfactory action has been taken on the complaints.
The plea also raises questions over the status of the rebel MPs within Parliament. It claims that the Speaker has not formally recognised the rebel group as a separate entity, even though the seating arrangements of the MPs in the House have been changed.
The petition alleges that while the MPs describe themselves as members of NCPI outside the House, they continue to identify themselves as members of the All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) inside Parliament.
TMC INVOKES ANTI-DEFECTION LAW
Banerjee has argued that the conduct of the MPs warrants action under the anti-defection law. The plea challenges the delay in deciding the disqualification petitions and seeks the Supreme Court's intervention on the issue.
The TMC has also relied on previous Supreme Court judgments, including the 2023 Subhash Desai case, to argue that Speakers should decide petitions concerning defections within a reasonable, time-bound period.
The petition cites the principle that such matters should ordinarily be decided within three to four months, rather than being kept pending indefinitely.
SC HEARING ON TUESDAY
The Supreme Court's CJI-led bench will hear the matter on Tuesday. The proceedings will bring before the apex court the TMC's allegations regarding the 20 MPs, the pending disqualification petitions and the Speaker's handling of the matter.
The case has been filed directly against the alleged delay in taking a decision on the petitions submitted before the Lok Sabha Speaker, with Banerjee seeking judicial intervention over the issue.

headline: 17-year-old gangraped in MP’s Pachmarhi; 3 arrested: Police
full_text:
17-year-old gangraped in MP’s Pachmarhi; 3 arrested: Police
According to police, the incident occurred on August 19, but the survivor lodged a complaint on Sunday night
Three people were arrested on Monday in connection with alleged rape of a 17-year-old girl in Madhya Pradesh’s Pachmarhi, police said.
Police identified the accused as Hariom, Gypsy driver, and two hotel staff Pawan Bansal and Abhishek Vanshkar.
According to police, the incident occurred on August 19, but the survivor lodged a complaint on Sunday night.
Narmadapuram additional superintendent of police Abhishek Rajan said, “The victim, a school student in Pachmarhi, was standing at the bus stand with a friend on August 19 afternoon. The accused offered them a lift in a Gypsy and took them to a forest near the South Scout Guide Centre.”
According to police, the accused gangraped her and her friend to the vehicle when he resisted.
“After the rape, they dropped both students back at the bus stand and threatened them with death if they revealed the incident. The girl stopped attending school, and her health deteriorated. Her sister noticed unusual behaviour and after counselling, learned of the ordeal. The family then approached the police late Sunday night,” said the ASP.
A medical examination of the survivor has been conducted, police said.
Police said that the accused confessed to the crime during interrogation. They have been booked under sections 70(2) (gang rape), 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 351(3) (criminal intimidation), and 3(5) (common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with provisions of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

headline: ‘Open-ended questions misleading’: Kharge, Rahul Gandhi write to PM Modi, flag caste census concerns
full_text:
‘Open-ended questions misleading’: Kharge, Rahul Gandhi write to PM Modi, flag caste census concerns
Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi said the same caste could have different names, sub-castes and spellings in different parts of India.
Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi have objected to the proposed method of collecting caste details in Census 2027. Their concerns were raised in a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
The Population Census 2027 will include caste counting for the first time since Independence. Kharge, Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, and Rahul Gandhi, his Lok Sabha counterpart, said the government’s decision to use open-ended questions to record caste details could create confusion.
Reliable caste data was essential for framing social justice policies and assessing the socio-economic status of different communities, the leaders said. “Your government has chosen the method of recording caste information in the census using open-ended questions, which is misleading,” the letter read.
ALSO READ | Caste among 40 questions notified for the second phase of the Census 2027
The leaders said the same caste could have different names, sub-castes and spellings in different parts of India. If people from the same caste are recorded under different names, one caste could end up being counted as several different groups.
“This will result in millions of castes in the country, rendering the entire data obtained from the caste census useless,” the letter said.
Kharge and Rahul Gandhi said this could lead to incorrect estimates of the size of different communities. This could also affect decisions on education, jobs, government planning and social justice schemes, they said.
The proposed census would not give an accurate figure for the total OBC population because the questionnaire does not include the term “backward class”, the leaders wrote in the letter.
ALSO READ | SP turns to booth-level caste data ahead of 2027 assembly polls
Kharge, Rahul suggest caste list
The Congress leaders suggested using a fixed list of castes through a drop-down option instead of allowing people to enter caste names freely.
They said such a list could be prepared using existing government lists, including the Socially and Educationally Backward Classes list and information from the Anthropological Survey of India.
They cited the caste surveys conducted in Telangana and Bihar, saying both used caste lists. Copies of the caste lists from the Telangana Caste Survey-2024 and Bihar Caste Survey-2022 were attached to the letter.
“We do not accept this method of conducting a caste census,” Kharge and Rahul Gandhi said.
They asked the government to cancel the current questionnaire and prepare a new one after consulting political parties, experts and the public.
They said the new method should ensure that the number of people belonging to each caste and community is recorded correctly.
ALSO READ | How will the 2027 Census count caste? Number Theory
Caste census in India
One of the most important parts of this Census is the caste enumeration, which will take place for the first time in independent India. Caste was counted during the British period but this practice was later stopped.
The Census has continued to separately count Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs). The population of other communities, including Other Backward Classes (OBCs), was not separately counted.
The demand for a caste census has mainly come from OBC groups and political leaders. So, how will the 2027 Census count caste apart from SCs and STs? Here is what we know so far.
The challenge of counting OBC sub-castes
A key question is whether the government has a complete list of all OBC sub-castes. There is no single nationwide list. There are 2,479 entries in the Central OBC list, while states have their own lists. The total number is therefore much higher.
For example, Tamil Nadu has 182 OBC entries on the Central list but 252 entries on its state list. The Mandal Commission identified 3,743 communities as OBCs.
Why detailed data matters
Government surveys have already given broad estimates of India's caste composition. The NFHS 2019-21 estimated the population share of SCs, STs, OBCs and others at 22%, 9%, 42% and 27%.
The PLFS 2025 gave similar figures: 20%, 9%, 46% and 24%. The Bihar caste survey released in 2023 also broadly matched these estimates.

headline: Maharashtra's cab drivers move Bombay HC over Marathi language rule; seek immediate stay on govt notice
full_text:
Maharashtra's cab drivers move Bombay HC over Marathi language rule; seek immediate stay on govt notice
The Maharashtra government has announced a month-long statewide drive to assess drivers' Marathi language skills.
Four cab drivers, who are working with mobile cab aggregator apps, have moved the Bombay High Court challenging the Maharashtra government's Marathi language rule.
The state government has announced a month-long statewide drive to assess drivers' Marathi language skills. This comes after Maharashtra transport minister Pratap Sarnaik on August 12 notified the rule that drivers of passenger transport vehicles must have a working knowledge of Marathi to communicate effectively with commuters.
The petition by the cab drivers, which was filed through advocate Vivek Shukla, will be mentioned tomorrow (August 26) before the Chief Justice for urgent directions, Bar and Bench reported. It seeks an immediate stay on the government notification to prevent challenges to nearly 9.65 lakh drivers across Maharashtra.
What does the plea say?
The plea submitted by the four cab drivers argues that the rule regarding compulsory knowledge of Marathi violates their fundamental rights under Articles 14 (right to equality), 19 (freedom to carry on trade and profession) and 21 (right to life) of the Constitution.
It says that the rule is ultra vires the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, which does not prescribe any language requirement for driving licences, according to the Bar and Bench report.
“The parent Act (Motor Vehicles Act) confers no power upon the State Government to prescribe working knowledge of any language as a qualification for a driver, as a condition of a badge, or as a condition of a permit, and confers no power to suspend or revoke a badge on such a ground,” the petition states. It argues that the language rule “manufactures a new disqualification and a new ground of suspension” which had not been enacted by the Parliament.
Commuters face issues as drivers protest rule
Meanwhile, commuters in Mumbai faced problems while travelling as autorickshaw drivers went on a strike to oppose the new rule. Commuters struggled to reach railway stations and their workplaces as autorickshaws refused to ply in Bandra, Kandivali, Govandi, Vakola, Kurla, Andheri and Santacruz, according to an earlier HT report.
After videos circulating on social media showed demonstrations in a few locations in Mumbai, Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis stepped in to address the issue. Fadnavis said the objective behind the government drive was not to make the drivers experts in the language, but to ensure that they could communicate in the local language for work, PTI news agency reported.
This comes even as regional transport offices across Maharashtra issued notices to 331 autorickshaw and taxi drivers, including 139 in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), for failing to demonstrate working knowledge of Marathi, according to the PTI report.

headline: Did India hit Kirana Hills? Ex-CDS explains what happened during Op Sindoor
full_text:
Did India hit Kirana Hills? Ex-CDS explains what happened during Op Sindoor
Former CDS General Anil Chauhan also revealed that India cleared further strikes on Pakistani military targets even after Islamabad reached out for talks, with Sargodha among them.
Former Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan has addressed speculation over whether India struck Kirana Hills near Pakistan's Sargodha during Operation Sindoor, saying a loitering munition searching for radars may have hit one of the hills after failing to find its intended target.
Kirana Hills, around 10 kilometres north of Sargodha, has long been associated with Pakistan's nuclear infrastructure. Questions over whether India had targeted the area emerged after Pakistani media showed images of smoke rising from the hills during the military confrontation.
"We had deployed loitering munitions around Sargodha ahead of India's strikes on Pakistani airbases to hunt for radars," the former CDS said at an event organised by the Vivekananda International Foundation.
Chauhan explained that such a munition could remain airborne for around two hours while searching for a target. If it failed to find one, it would eventually come down.
"It must have come and hit one of those hills. So that could be one of the reasons... even Pakistani media showed some kind of images in which there was smoke coming out of Kirana Hills," he said.
Chauhan's remarks suggest that any impact at Kirana Hills was not a deliberate strike on the area or its nuclear facilities.
LOWER AIRSPACE WAS PART OF INDIA'S STRATEGY
The use of loitering munitions around Sargodha was part of India's broader decision to exploit the lower airspace during Operation Sindoor.
Chauhan described this as a "third option", distinct from the land-based response after the Uri terror attack and the large air package used following Pulwama.
"During Operation Sindoor, we decided to use a third option, that is, to exploit the lower airspace. That means it would have kept the threshold of conflict low. It would have assured success and then there would have been an element of surprise," he said.
The lower air envelope can be used by drones, loitering munitions, attack helicopters and other low-level platforms.
SARGODHA STRIKE CLEARED EVEN AFTER PAK SOUGHT TALKS
Chauhan also revealed that India cleared further strikes on Pakistani military targets even after Islamabad reached out for talks, with Sargodha among them.
He said Pakistan contacted India seeking talks when the Air Chief asked him whether the Indian Air Force should strike Sargodha.
"Once the Pakistanis had picked up the phone and said they wanted to talk at about 10 AM, the Air Chief asked me whether he should strike Sargodha. I said, 'Go ahead'," Chauhan said.
He then asked the Air Chief to identify two more targets.
"I said, could you please identify two more targets? So, one of the targets he identified was Skardu. We gave a yes, but after some time, the weather there turned bad, and they had to change over to Bholari," he said.
Chauhan said India's escalation strategy ensured it would deliver the final strike. "The last strike or the winning note will always be delivered by us and not by the Pakistanis," he said.
The remarks shed light on India's escalation strategy during Operation Sindoor, including its decision to retain the option of further strikes even after Pakistan sought talks.
PAKISTAN 'BLIND' ABOUT RESULTS OF ITS STRIKES
Chauhan also said Pakistan did not know whether its strikes had hit their intended targets and tried to obtain commercial satellite imagery until around May 12 to find evidence of damage.
"They were actually after 10th also till about 12th they were trying their best to obtain images so that they have some evidence," he said.
Chauhan said commercial satellite imagery was available from both US and Chinese companies. Pakistan, he said, also tried other Chinese satellite sources but failed to find evidence that its strikes had hit targets.
"But since they are not able to hit any target, they got no evidence," he said.
WHY INDIA HAD THE EDGE
Chauhan attributed India's success during Operation Sindoor to better situational awareness, battlefield transparency and coordination between the Army, Navy and Air Force.
"If I had to list out a couple of reasons for India's victory, I would say that we had better situational awareness, better battlefield transparency because we are better networked," he said.
He said the three services had access to a common operational picture, helping them make better decisions. They also worked on a unified plan instead of taking individual capability deficiencies before the political leadership.
"We have seen in the past, sometimes in front of political leadership, people bring out the kind of deficiencies that they have. This particular operation stands out... in which all three services and I, right from day one, did not bring any of these kinds of deficiencies," Chauhan said.
The former CDS also credited clear political direction for giving the military operational freedom. "The second thing I could attribute to victory was... clear political direction, which gave us a free hand to plan operations," he said.
REVISITING OPERATION SINDOOR
India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7, 2025, following the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people.
In the initial phase, the armed forces struck nine sites linked to terrorist groups in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir.
The strikes used precision and standoff weapons, allowing Indian aircraft to engage targets without flying deep into Pakistani airspace.
The operation later expanded after Pakistan launched military actions against India, prompting the Indian Air Force to strike Pakistani military infrastructure, including airbases and radar facilities.
The confrontation ended through direct military-to-military communications via the Directors General of Military Operations after Pakistan reached out for a ceasefire on the morning of May 10, 2025.
