headline: Hyderabad: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy defended his plans to meet New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani during a proposed trip to the United States—to which the Centre denied political clearance last week.
full_text:
Hyderabad: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy defended his plans to meet New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani during a proposed trip to the United States—to which the Centre denied political clearance last week.
Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Friday that the Centre had denied clearance for the US leg of Reddy’s overseas trip, stating that the proposed programme was “not appropriate” for his office. Apart from businesses, Reddy had also indicated he may meet elected officials in the US, ThePrint had reported.
“Mamdani is an elected leader; he is not an anti-social element. Also, the High Commission in any city in the USA is supposed to facilitate my visit if I want to meet them wherever I travel,” he said Monday in response to a media query on his intention to meet the New York City Mayor.
At a press conference at the state Secretariat, Reddy displayed a letter sent by the Telangana government to the MEA, saying that his visit’s aim was to “meet key stakeholders, prestigious world-class universities, sports institutions, and potential strategic partners”.
“My objective was to make Telangana a sports and education hub by bringing in investments from top universities in the UK and USA. My visit was part of the road show for the Telangana Rising Global Investors Summit to be held in December. By denying permission for my tour, Prime Minister Modi is still acting like the leader of Gujarat and not as PM of the country,” he said.
Reddy also contrasted the decision with the Centre’s permission to Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel for his visit to the US and Canada to promote the ‘Vibrant Gujarat’ investors summit.
Divisions within party
Revanth Reddy returned from London early Monday after visiting Oxford and Cambridge universities, besides attending All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) legislator Akbaruddin Owaisi’s daughter’s wedding.
The chief minister was to leave for the US from London and return to Hyderabad only on 30 August, but instead had to cut short his trip after the MEA’s decision.
The Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) slammed the move as “partisan” rather than a matter of administrative protocol.
Those in public office, including chief ministers, state ministers and MPs, require what is called political clearance from the MEA before they travel abroad for official purposes.
In case of chief ministers, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) must submit the proposed reason for the trip along with the schedule of meetings they wish to undertake.
Reddy’s press conference with five other ministers and at least three advisers beside him also drew attention as it came amid tensions within Telangana Congress.
Ministers Uttam Reddy, Seethakka, Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy, Bhatti Vikramarka and Tummala Nageswara Rao were seen sitting beside the chief minister as he addressed the media.
However, political observers questioned the unexpected show of unity as none of his cabinet colleagues condemned the sharp remarks by fellow minister Konda Surekha’s daughter against the chief minister.
“The body language of the ministers did not seem very encouraging. Peace is surely to have been brokered, but the ice is still to break,” Kalyan Chandra, a political analyst, told ThePrint.
Sources in the Telangana Congress added that at least 42 elected legislators and MLCs were called by the CM’s advisor Vem Narendra Reddy on Friday to attend a press conference convened by MLAs to seek Konda Surekha’s ouster from the state cabinet.
However, with only 18 MLAs and MLCs attending the press conference and none of the ministers condemning the remarks, talks of a rift between the old Congress and “Revanth’s TDP Congress” resurfaced.
Political tensions in the state escalated after Konda Sushmita, daughter of veteran Congress leaders Konda Surekha and Konda Murali, made controversial comments at Geesukonda, Warangal on 19 August.
The comments, made during her mother’s birthday celebrations, were over Revanth Reddy’s choice of an MLA candidate for the 2028 assembly elections.
The dispute over candidate selection for the Parkal assembly constituency arose after CM Revanth Reddy recently voiced his support for the sitting MLA Revuri Prakash Reddy.
Sushmita, a member of the Congress party who does not hold any official position, launched a direct attack on the state’s leadership.
She declared herself the party’s MLA aspirant and accused the chief minister of developing an “arrogant” attitude and favouring Telugu Desam leaders over Congress leaders.
The dispute triggered an open war between the two camps in the Congress, prompting the party’s disciplinary committee to issue a showcause notice to Surekha.
Political observers said the silence of the All-India Congress Committee (AICC) and the state cabinet exposed the differences among ministers.
While the MLAs’ press conference is being seen as Revanth’s “show of strength”, AICC President Mallikarjun Kharge’s meeting with Surekha is seen as a support for the Backward Classes leader who has a strong political base in Warangal.
TPCC President Mahesh Kumar Goud’s absence from the MLA’s press conference led to speculation that the former confidant of Revanth was now no longer in the CM’s camp.
“That only 18-20 MLAs showed up has not gone unnoticed. The AICC surely is using the Konda Surekha issue to assess if Revanth Reddy still commands a favourable image within the party and if the cabinet is with him,” said Kalyan Chandra.
(Edited by Sugita Katyal)

headline: Ahead of talks in Beijing on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) between National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi, Hu Shisheng, a leading Chinese strategic affairs scholar on South Asia, said the focus of both countries would b...
full_text:
Ahead of talks in Beijing on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) between National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi, Hu Shisheng, a leading Chinese strategic affairs scholar on South Asia, said the focus of both countries would be on “institutionalising stability” even as “structural differences” in the relationship remained.
Also Read | Eyes on Xi visit, ‘early harvest’ as Doval heads to Beijing
India and China will on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) hold the 25th round of talks between the Special Representatives (SRs) on the boundary question. Mr. Doval and Mr. Wang, who is also a member of the Politburo, will also take stock of relations ahead of next month’s expected visit to India by Chinese President Xi Jinping for the BRICS Summit, his first visit in seven years.
“On the border, I would expect the immediate focus to be less on a dramatic settlement and more on institutionalising stability. The priority is to prevent misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC, strengthen military and diplomatic communication, and turn last year’s idea of an ‘early harvest’ into an operational process,” Mr. Hu, who is Director of the South Asia Institute at the China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations (CICIR) in Beijing, told The Hindu.
He was referring to an agreement at last year’s 24th round on establishing an Expert Group under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) on border affairs to explore “early harvest on boundary delimitation”.
“The two WMCC meetings this year have discussed delimitation, so there has been procedural progress, but there is still no public indication of a concrete sectoral delimitation agreement,” Mr. Hu said. “The realistic next step would be to operationalise the Expert Group, agree on its mandate, timetable and criteria for identifying relatively less contentious sectors, rather than expect an immediate breakthrough on the boundary itself.”
The broader challenge facing the two SRs, he said, was whether both sides “can work out a sustainable modus vivendi that avoids confrontation, keeps differences manageable, and preserves space for cooperation”.
Mr. Hu said the timing of Mr. Doval’s visit, before the September 12 BRICS Summit in New Delhi, added significance to the visit with Mr. Xi expected to visit India.
“Both sides have a strong incentive to keep the border stable and create a favourable political atmosphere for possible leader-level interaction,” he said, adding that he viewed maintaining stability on the border, achieving “concrete and operational progress” on “early harvest” outcomes, and creating favourable conditions for the BRICS Summit as immediate priorities for the border talks.
Also Read | China’s media slams India’s move of formally naming 27 places in Arunachal Pradesh
At the strategic level, he added, Mr. Doval’s visit would help “clear potential obstacles ahead of the BRICS Summit and lay the groundwork for possible leader-level engagement.” He said ensuring no unexpected border incident before the summit, setting the political tone and identifying deliverables for a possible leaders’ meeting, and coordinating the handover of the BRICS agenda from India to China, which takes over as chair next year, would be three essential issues on the table.
The view in Beijing, as in Delhi, is that the normalisation in relations since the October 2024 meeting between Mr. Modi and Mr. Xi is likely to remain gradual and measured.
“As for the broader normalisation, I would describe it as strategic risk management rather than strategic realignment,” Mr. Hu said. “Recent difficulties in India-U.S. relations may give New Delhi greater incentives to diversify its strategic options, while the relative stabilisation of China-U.S. ties reduces some of the external pressure on China-India relations. But the structural differences between China and India have not disappeared. What we are seeing is an attempt to build a more stable form of competitive coexistence – keeping the border peaceful, restoring practical cooperation, and expanding coordination through BRICS and the Global South without pretending that strategic competition no longer exists.”

NEW DELHI: Chaotic scenes unfolded in Biharâs Patna on Tuesday as protesting students clashed with police during a massive protest over alleged irregularities in the 70th BPSC examination.The protest was met with a heavy police deployment, with barricades erected to stop the students from marching.Police also used water cannons as protesters attempted to push past the barricades.Later, the Samrat Choudhary-led government claimed it had addressed âalmost all issuesâ raised by the students. The protesters, however, said several long-standing demands remained unresolved and continued their agitation.The students marched from Gandhi Maidan towards Raj Bhavan.The protesting students also broke the barricades in bid to gherao chief minister's residence.The protest has also brought into focus delays in recruitment examinations, the proposed format of the Teacher Recruitment Examination-4 (TRE-4), alleged paper leaks and demands for greater transparency in Bihar's recruitment system.
Govt says students' issues have been addressed
Bihar education minister Mithilesh Tiwari said the government had resolved the issues raised by the students and maintained that its doors remained open for further dialogue.
"All the issues over which the students were staging a sit-in have been resolved. It is not as if the student agitation was the sole reason for this; it is the government's very intent to resolve the problems faced by our youth in a timely manner. We have addressed every issue raised by the youth. I was surprised to hear a person who has never even taken a board exam offering suggestions on examinations. That is why I would say to Tejashwi Yadav to enroll in a Bihar government school, pass the tenth-grade exam, and then come back to offer us suggestions on examinations," Tiwari said.The minister said that almost all the demands had been met and invited students to approach the government with any remaining concerns."We have met almost all the students' demands. For any students who wish to convey further points to the government, the doors for dialogue remain wide open. Let the students come, talk, and get their issues resolved; the government belongs to them," he said.However, the protesters said their concerns had not been fully addressed and that problems related to the education system, examination paper leaks and delayed recruitment continued.
'Do you need 1,800 years?' Students question recruitment delays
Protester Vikas Bhatt said the students were demanding improvements in Bihar's education system and action against repeated examination paper leaks."Our demand is that the education system in Bihar be improved. We are raising issues regarding the frequent exam paper leaks in the state. Look at the recruitment for librarians, it hasn't happened for 18 years; do you need 1,800 years? Whenever we stage a protest, they simply offer assurances and leave it at that. How can things go on like this? Three recruitment drives were announced through the BSSC, but it has been three years. We have repeatedly besieged the BSSC commission, demanding that the exam dates be announced. Despite this, they keep asking for 15 days' time. Apart from the BPSC, there isn't a single commission in Bihar that issues an annual calendar," Bhatt said.The students are demanding the cancellation of the 70th BPSC examination over allegations of irregularities and paper leaks.The agitation has also centred on the proposed TRE-4 examination. Students have opposed the proposal to conduct the examination in two phases across Bihar and are demanding that it be held in a single phase.They have also sought the immediate release of the official TRE-4 advertisement.
Students break through barricades during Raj Bhavan march
As the protest continued, students marched from Gandhi Maidan towards Raj Bhavan. Some protesters broke through police barricades and attempted to move towards the restricted area.Police used water cannons to disperse the crowd, while several protesters were detained.DSP Kamakhya Narayan Singh said the police would not allow the protesters to enter the restricted area, although he expressed hope that the ongoing talks between students and senior officials would lead to a resolution."We will stop them; we won't let them proceed further. However, the dialogue has been positive, and we hope the students will agree. They have raised several issues with the senior officials, and the outcome has been positive. So, I expect the turnout to be lower and that they will agree. If they don't, we will stop them right here. We won't allow them to enter the restricted area," Singh said.Congress leader Sushil Kumar, who was present at the protest site, said the government had failed to give assurances on several key demands."We want to state clearly that a single-stage examination must be implemented for TRE 4.0 at all costs, and negative marking should be abolished. There are numerous other issues as well, regarding the BPSC, BSSC, Sub-Inspector recruitment. The government has offered no assurances on any of these points. We have urged the Chief Minister to hold a dialogue; he should invite our delegation for talks. We have been on a hunger strike for nine days, yet no one is willing to listen to us. Just imagine, had the government engaged in dialogue, this situation would not have arisen. We are heading towards the Chief Minister's residence; the Chief Minister should hold talks, and our delegation will go there for the discussion," Kumar told news agency ANI.
JD(U) says govt is serious about students' concerns
JD(U) leader Shravan Kumar said the Bihar government was taking the concerns of students and job seekers seriously and was acting according to established rules and legal provisions."The government is taking the demands and concerns of students and job seekers seriously. Everything is being done for them in accordance with established rules, laws, and provisions. Bihar is the first state in the country to have made such large-scale recruitments across government departments," Kumar said.He also pointed to the government's employment target for the 2025-2030 period and urged young people not to be influenced by the opposition."It is Nitish Kumar's resolve to provide 10 million (1 crore) jobs and employment opportunities to the people of Bihar between 2025 and 2030. Recruitments are taking place in every sector, and vacancies are being announced in every department. I urge our youth to exercise patience and not fall for the opposition's ploys; they are not going to provide jobs. They merely intend to exploit your hard work and sweat to further their own political interests. Beware of them," he added.
Tejashwi writes to Samrat Choudhary
Meanwhile, Bihar leader of opposition Tejashwi Yadav has written to chief minister Samrat Choudhary over the ongoing BPSC row, urging the government not to ignore the students' demands and to hold talks for an early resolution.Tejashwi has demanded that TRE-4 be conducted as a single examination across the state. He has also sought an end to what he described as discrimination against Hindi-speaking candidates in the BPSC Civil Services Main Examination and interview.The RJD leader has further demanded complete transparency in all competitive examinations, including those for Sub-Inspector, Constable, BSSC and BPSC recruitments.Among his other demands are a high-level independent inquiry into alleged irregularities in past examinations, strict action against recruitment mafias and time-bound schedules for all pending tests.He has specifically called for clear timelines for the BSSC Intermediate, CGL, ASO, BSO, Librarian and Accountant recruitment examinations.RJD scion Tejashwi remark also followed BPSC official's "dog-barking" remark. Bihar LoP also called for action for his remark referring to students.
Bihar launches monthly student support camps
Amid the continuing protests, the Bihar government on Tuesday launched the monthly 'Vidyarthi Sahyog Shivir' or student support camps to address students' grievances.
The camps will be organised at educational institutions on the fourth Tuesday of every month, chief minister Samrat Choudhary said in a social media post."The Bihar government is launching Vidyarthi Sahyog Shivir starting today to ensure prompt resolution of students' grievances. These camps will be organised at educational institutions on the fourth Tuesday of every month," Choudhary wrote.The camps will allow students to raise their grievances directly with the concerned government officials. Students will also be able to register complaints online and track their status through the portal and Helpline 1100.The government's announcement comes as the student protest continues in Patna's Gardanibagh area, with the two sides offering sharply different views on whether the protesters' demands have been addressed.

headline: Elephant walks, dogs bark: BPSC official's remark draws student ire in Bihar
full_text:
Elephant walks, dogs bark: BPSC official's remark draws student ire in Bihar
Bihar Public Service Commission Examination Controller Rajesh Kumar Singh made a controversial remark while addressing allegations around the 70th BPSC examination. The comment has intensified attention on student protests over the exam and the proposed TRE-4 process.
Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) Examination Controller Rajesh Kumar Singh’s controversial remarks have sparked a fresh row amid ongoing protests by job aspirants in the state, which has received support from the opposition.
Speaking to the media while responding to allegations of irregularities and a purported paper leak, Singh said, “Hathi chale bazaar, kutta bhaunke hazaar” (An elephant walks through the market while a thousand dogs bark).
The remark drew an immediate backlash from protesting students, who erupted into fresh sloganeering, chanting “Shiksha Mantri chor hai” (The Education Minister is a thief) and raising slogans against Singh and his comments.
The remark came at a time when students have been staging a protest at Patna's Gardanibagh, demanding the cancellation of the 70th BPSC examination over alleged irregularities and paper leakage.
The protesters are also opposing the proposed Teacher Recruitment Examination – Fourth Phase (TRE-4) process. They have been demanding the release of the TRE-4 advertisement and have objected to the proposal to conduct the examination in two phases.
During the media interaction,Singh was responding to questions about demands raised by protesting candidates, including the allegation that the recruitment process puts Hindi-medium aspirants at a disadvantage.
Dismissing the concerns, he challenged the protesters to approach the courts. “I want to ask all those who have problems — why do you not move the court?” he said, before adding, “As far as the Commission is concerned, I would like to quote the proverb — Hathi chale bazaar, kutta bhaunke hazaar.”
The remark, which compares an elephant moving through a marketplace unfazed by a thousand barking dogs, quickly became the focus of the protest. Singh was heard asking reporters to ignore the reference, but the clip was soon aired by news outlets and widely circulated on social media.
RJD working president and Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav, who learnt about the remarks when he reached Gardani Bagh, where the protest was underway, hit out at Singh. He demanded an apology from the BPSC official and urged the Samrat Choudhary government to take strict action against him.
Several aspirants at the protest said Singh’s remarks showed how the authorities viewed their demands. “The BPSC official’s remarks are proof that in the eyes of the authorities, our worth is not more than that of stray dogs,” some protesters were heard saying.
Rohini Acharya, Yadav’s estranged elder sister, also shared the video on X, describing Singh’s remarks as “derogatory” and “undignified”.
Singh later sought to clarify his comments in a brief video statement. “I had merely uttered a proverb, but my words were twisted out of context. Nonetheless, if I have offended anybody, even unwittingly, I express regrets,” he said.

Rape convict Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh walked out of the Sunaria jail in Rohtak on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) morning on a 21-day furlough, sources said. It is the 17th time he has moved out of the prison since his conviction in August 2017.
Ram Rahim is serving a 20-year jail term for raping two of his disciples and is currently lodged in the Sunaria jail in Haryana's Rohtak.
He will stay at his Sirsa-headquartered Dera during the furlough period, sources said.
The preacher has been granted furlough an unusually high number of times since his conviction. This is his third release this year alone.
He was granted a 30 and 40-day parole in May and January, respectively.
He stepped out of prison on a 40-day parole in August 2025, a 21-day furlough in April 2025, and a 30-day parole in January 2025, ahead of the Delhi Assembly election in February 2025.
He walked out of prison on a 20-day parole on October 1, 2024, days before the October 5, 2024 Haryana Assembly election.
In August 2024, Ram Rahim was granted a 21-day furlough. He was also permitted a three-week furlough from February 7, 2022, barely two weeks before the Punjab Assembly election that year.
Sikh organisations, including the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee, have criticised the recurring relief provided to Ram Rahim.
In March, the Punjab and Haryana High Court acquitted Ram Rahim in the 2002 murder case of a journalist, seven years after he was convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment in the case by a special Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) court.
In May 2024, the HC overturned another special CBI court order and acquitted Ram Rahim and four others in the 2002 murder of the sect's former manager, Ranjit Singh.
The Sirsa-headquartered Dera Sacha Sauda has a huge following in Haryana, Punjab, and Rajasthan. In Haryana, the largest number of followers are from districts, including Sirsa, Fatehabad, Kurukshetra, Kaithal, and Hisar.

headline: Rape convict Gurmeet Ram Rahim walks out of prison on 21-day furlough
full_text:
Rape convict Gurmeet Ram Rahim walks out of prison on 21-day furlough
Gurmeet Ram Rahim, the self styles Godman, was convicted of raping two women disciples.
Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh walked out of the high-security Sunaria jail in Haryana’s Rohtak early Tuesday after being granted a 21-day furlough. This is his 17th temporary release since 2020.
Ram Rahim, who is serving sentences in separate cases of rape and murder, left the jail at around 6.05 am amid security arrangements. He has now left for Sirsa based Dera headquarters, HT has learnt.
The latest furlough comes less than two months after he returned to Sunaria jail on June 26 on completion of a 30-day parole.
Ram Rahim convicted of rape
The Dera chief was lodged in Sunaria jail in August 2017 after being convicted in the rape case involving two women followers. He was subsequently convicted in other cases, including the murder of Sirsa-based journalist Ram Chander Chhatrapati.
With Tuesday's release, Ram Rahim has now been granted parole or furlough on 17 occasions during his imprisonment. His repeated temporary releases have frequently triggered questions and criticism, particularly over the frequency of the relief granted to a convict serving sentences in serious criminal cases.
Earlier this year, Ram Rahim was granted 40 days of parole in January. He was again released on a 30-day parole in May and returned to the Rohtak jail on June 26 after completing the period of his temporary release.
The latest 21-day furlough once again brings the controversial Dera chief out of jail. His repeated parole and furlough releases have remained a subject of public and political debate ever since his conviction nearly nine years ago.
Ram Rahim’s 17 temporary releases since 2020
According to official prison records for convict 8647/C, Ram Rahim has been granted 17 temporary releases since 2020, including his latest 21-day furlough:
1st release — October 2020: 1 day
2nd — May 2021: 12 hours to visit his mother
3rd — February 2022: 21 days
4th — June 2022: 30 days
5th — October 2022: 40 days
6th — January 2023: 40 days
7th — July 2023: 30 days
8th — November 2023: 21 days
9th — January 2024: 50 days
10th — August 2024: 21 days
11th — October 2024: 20 days
12th — January 2025: 30 days
13th — April 2025: 21 days
14th — August 2025: 40 days
15th — January 2026: 40 days
16th — May 2026: 30 days
17th — August 2026: 21 days
Why is he out of prison so often?
Ram Rahim’s repeated temporary releases are governed by the Haryana Good Conduct Prisoners (Temporary Release) Act, 2022.
Under the rules, eligible convicts can be granted up to 70 days of parole and 21 days of furlough in a calendar year, subject to the applicable conditions and approval by the competent authority.

full_text:
A day after heavy rain left several parts of Gurugram waterlogged and caused massive traffic jams, residents and Opposition leaders stepped up their criticism of the Haryana government and local administration, questioning the lack of preparedness and the recurrence of the crisis every monsoon.
The Opposition targeted the BJP government over the city’s recurring waterlogging problems. Rohtak MP Deepender Hooda pointed at the city’s soaring property prices, arguing that greater attention should have been given to drainage infrastructure years ago. “Gurugram, where last week an entrepreneur bought a penthouse flat for ₹271 crore, if even 12 years ago such a budget had been properly allocated for rainwater drainage, we wouldn’t have to feel this ashamed in front of our next generation,” Mr. Hooda posted on social media.
Congress leader and former Gurugram Rural district women’s president Sheilza Bhatia said the waterlogging crisis was not a new phenomenon. “Everyone knows where the water accumulates, which roads get blocked, and which areas are worst affected. So why does the same problem occur every year?” she said. She also questioned the silence of Gurugram MP Rao Inderjit Singh. “Today, Gurugram is asking you just one question—when Gurugram was drowning, where were you?” she wrote.

headline: India didn't target Pakistan's Kirana Hills; loitering munition hit it inadvertently: Ex-CDS Anil Chauhan
full_text:
India didn't target Pakistan's Kirana Hills; loitering munition hit it inadvertently: Ex-CDS Anil Chauhan
Ex-CDS Gen Anil Chauhan says Indian loitering munition likely hit Kirana Hills after failing to find a radar target near Sargodha within its loiter time.
Former Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan on Tuesday said that India did not target Pakistan's Kirana Hills nuclear facility during last year's Operation Sindoor, but an Indian loitering ammunition inadvertently hit it.
Chauhan explained that a lot of loitering munitions were sent at Sargodha, which is just 10 km north of Kirana Hills. He said one of those munitions must have come and hit the Kirana Hills nuclear facility after not finding a target.
"Before those strikes, we had sent a lot of loiter ammunition at Sargodha, and Kirana Hills is 10 km north of Sargodha. So the loiter ammunition was looking for radars, which were in and around Sargodha, and it has got a lifetime. It will loiter for about two hours, and if it doesn't find a target, it will come and hit somewhere. It must have come and hit one of those hills,'' General Chauhan was quoted by ANI as saying.
The Kirana Hills is a vast rocky mountain range and a designated area under the Pakistan ministry of defence in Sargodha district. Locally referred to as the “Black Mountains” due to its brownish terrain, it stretches between the township of Rabwah and the city of Sargodha.
Former Director General of Air Operations, Air Marshal AK Bharti, had said on May 12 last year that the Indian armed forces did not target the nuclear facility at Kirana Hills in Pakistan.
Responding to a query during a press conference at the time, Bharti said, “Thank you for telling us that Kirana Hills houses some nuclear installation. We did not know about it. And we have not hit Kirana Hills, whatever is there.”
What happened?
India had launched Operation Sindoor on May 7 2025, in response to the deadly terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir's Pahalgam region on April 22, that left 26 people dead. The operation, launched by the tri-services, targeted terror infrastructure located in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK). Over 100 terrorists were killed in these strikes, according to the government.
In the following days, the Indian armed forces hit back at Pakistan's attempted retaliatory strikes. On May 10, the Pakistani army reached out to its Indian counterpart, leading to a ceasefire understanding between the two neighbours.
Immediately after the operation, as well, heavy speculations and social media chatter had claimed that India had struck the Mushaf Airbase in Sargodha, reportedly linked to underground nuclear storage beneath the Kirana Hills. The Air Force denied targeting the facility, both then and now.

headline: UP to give 1 lakh govt appointment letters in next six months: Adityanath

UP to give 1 lakh govt appointment letters in next six months: Adityanath
Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday said the state government will provide appointment letters to one lakh youths over the next six months.
Addressing an appointment letter distribution programme here, he said more than 9.3 lakh youths had been provided government jobs by his government through a transparent and non-discriminatory process since 2017.
"It gives me pleasure to say that during this period, our government has succeeded in providing government jobs to more than 9,30,000 youths of Uttar Pradesh, and no one can raise a question over even a single appointment," he said.
The CM was speaking at an event where appointment letters were handed over to 3,446 technical assistants and 126 market secretaries. Agriculture Minister Surya Pratap Shahi and Minister of State for Agriculture Baldev Singh Aulakh were also present.
Adityanath said the government had ensured recruitment on merit while following reservation rules and without discrimination.
Without naming former chief minister and Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav and his uncle Shivpal Yadav, Adityanath targeted the previous government, alleging that before 2017, whenever a recruitment advertisement was issued, a "chacha-bhatija" duo and the "entire Mahabharata family" would go across the state for "vasooli".
"Young people kept wandering, results did not come and ultimately courts had to stay the cases. Their time and age were wasted ," he said.
The CM alleged that the fault lay not with the youths but with "corrupt" officials, boards and commissions and politicians involved in the recruitment system at that time.
"We had said from the first day that this government would work with a zero-tolerance policy towards crime and criminals. We would also break the back of the copying mafia and mafias sitting in various institutions," he said.
Adityanath said his government had seized and recovered proceeds from the properties of mafias and made recruitment more transparent.
"Today, while giving appointment letters to more than 3,400 agricultural technical assistants and market secretaries, I want to assure the youth of the state that in the next six months note it we are going to provide one lakh government appointment letters every week in different stages," he said.
He said recruitment examinations had been completed and the result process was under way, asking commissions and boards to reduce timelines.
"We do not want a situation where a young person has to be provoked because he has appeared for an examination but the result has not come," he said.
Adityanath also attacked the previous government over examinations, alleging that the education system had been weakened and copying was encouraged for "cheap popularity".
"Today, we conduct the Uttar Pradesh Board examination in 14 days and get its results in the next 14 days," he said, adding that around 56 lakh students appear for the examinations.
He said the government had reduced the examination period from around six months to one month and ensured "copy-free" examinations and timely results.
The CM said recruitment processes should be completed within six months of requisition, with advertisements issued within a month and examinations and results completed in the following months.
He claimed that the 9.3 lakh government jobs had contributed to Uttar Pradesh's "demographic dividend" and helped in tripling the state's economy and per capita income.
"Now youths are getting appointment letters without transactions and without recommendations. Their dreams are getting wings, which was not possible before 2017," he said.
Adityanath alleged that the previous government "played with the lives" of youths and distributed jobs through "bandarbant" and money.
He said Uttar Pradesh, earlier described as a "BIMARU state", had now entered the country's top three economies by linking its young population with development.
BIMARU was an acronym used in the 1980s for the states of Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan to describe their backwardness.

headline: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is developing a technology-driven command-and-control system for India’s land borders that will integrate surveillance inputs from the field through a network of command centres stretching from forward areas to New ...
full_text:
The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is developing a technology-driven command-and-control system for India’s land borders that will integrate surveillance inputs from the field through a network of command centres stretching from forward areas to New Delhi, according to a senior government official.
The initiative, part of a new border management policy, is aimed at strengthening monitoring and response capabilities in border regions where physical fencing is not feasible, such as the 3,488-km border with China, which remains un-demarcated at several points from Ladakh to Arunachal Pradesh. A pilot project will start soon from the Pakistan border, the official added.
Home Minister Amit Shah had earlier announced a four-pronged border security strategy, which involves border guarding forces, local population, State police and technological solutions.
“There will be several small command centres along the land borders that will be linked to the field headquarters and further to Delhi headquarters. The live feed will help the border guarding forces to monitor and also save the resources, reducing the need for physical patrolling,” said the official.
Faster responses
The “smart border” architecture for all of India’s land frontiers would integrate artificial intelligence, sensors, surveillance systems and unified command-and-control centres to strengthen border security and enable faster responses to threats, the official said.
India shares 15,106.7 km land border with seven countries.
“The proposed framework is designed to bring together surveillance inputs from multiple technologies, including cameras, sensors, image-processing tools, drones and other monitoring systems, to create a common operational picture for agencies deployed along India’s borders,” said the official.
The system was envisaged as an integrated platform where information gathered on the ground could be transmitted quickly to command-and-control centres, allowing authorities to respond more effectively to infiltration attempts, smuggling networks and other security challenges, said the official.
Addressing the growing threat from drones, particularly for smuggling and reconnaissance, has emerged as a major focus area, particularly along the Pakistan border.
According to the official, border-management technologies would be tailored to local conditions rather than deployed uniformly. India’s land borders traverse deserts, mountains, riverine stretches, forests and densely populated areas, requiring customised solutions for different terrains and operational requirements, the official added.
“No two borders are the same. Just like the China border, which cannot be fenced, there are riverine stretches along the Bangladesh border, which are flood-prone. No fence can be put there. We are moving towards a concept where physical presence is not always required,” said the official.
On July 9, Mr. Shah addressed the first ever Land Border Districts’ Superintendents of Police Conference–2026. The meeting was attended by Superintendents of Police (SPs) of 119 border districts of 17 States and Union Territories, which share land border with Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan, China and Myanmar.
At the meeting, States were asked to submit their suggestions by December and the quadrangular security grid, which involves border communities and the local police, will be finalised in the next 1.5 years.

headline: The Centre is closely monitoring the situation arising from a flash flood in Nepal, amid concerns that rising water levels could affect areas along the India-Nepal border, particularly in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) sa...
full_text:
The Centre is closely monitoring the situation arising from a flash flood in Nepal, amid concerns that rising water levels could affect areas along the India-Nepal border, particularly in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) said on Wednesday (August 26, 2026).
Follow LIVE updates from the Nepal flash floods on August 26, 2026
Union Home Minister Amit Shah said the Government of India was maintaining a close watch on developments after reports of devastation caused by floods in Nepal. He also spoke with the Chief Ministers of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh to review preparedness measures in areas that could potentially be affected.
In a post on X, Mr. Shah expressed condolences to those affected by the disaster. “The devastation caused by the floods in Nepal is deeply tragic. My condolences are with the families who have lost loved ones in this disaster. The Government of India stands with Nepal in this hour of crisis,” he said.
High alert
He added that local administrations, rescue agencies and the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) had been placed on high alert in vulnerable border districts. “I spoke with the Chief Ministers of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh regarding the disaster in Nepal. In border areas likely to be affected, the local administration and rescue teams, along with the NDRF, have been placed on high alert,” Mr. Shah said.
According to an advisory issued by the Central Water Commission (CWC), a sudden rise in the water level of Trishuli river at Furke Khola in Nepal, about 160 kilometres from the Indian border, has been reported. The increase is suspected to have been caused by a flash flood or a glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) event near the Nepal-China border, a statement by NDRF said.
The CWC has warned that the impact of the floodwaters could travel downstream through the Gandak river system and reach parts of India.
Precautionary measures
State governments in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have initiated precautionary measures, including evacuation where necessary and support for communities living in areas close to the India-Nepal border. The Centre has advised both States to remain vigilant and continue close monitoring of the evolving situation.
Officials from the MHA, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), Ministry of Jal Shakti and Ministry of Defence are engaged in continuous monitoring of the situation.
As per CWC, the water levels in reservoirs on the Nepal side are receding and that the situation remains under control, the MHA said adding that there is currently no cause for panic.
The MEA and the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu have issued emergency helpline numbers for Indian nationals seeking assistance or information. Those requiring help may contact the embassy helplines at +977 985 131 6807 and +977 970 910 7500.

Those calling from abroad can give a missed call to +91 80690 09900 or contact +91 80690 09901. Those who want to reach the control room at the Tamil Nadu House in New Delhi can contact 92895 16712.
The 57 pilgrims went to Nepal on a tour organised by a Kumbakonam-based company in tie-up with a Nepal-based company. They landed in Nepal a few days ago and were heading towards the Tibet border as part of their travel plan when the mishap took place. Divided into three groups, they travelled in three buses to Tibet border, sources said.
Nepal floods: PM Modi speaks to Balendra Shah, offers humanitarian assistance
“Along with them, two others from Maharashtra too joined them. The incident happened around 8 a.m. today. Occupants of one of the vehicles took refuge on top of a hill,” a source coordinating rescue efforts said, adding that it is not immediately known as to what happened to the occupants of the other two vehicles.
While about 21 of them managed to get shelter at a Nepal border police outpost, the status of others was yet to be ascertained, according to an official spokesperson of the travel company. Meanwhile, the Thanjavur, Tiruvarur and Mayiladuthurai district administrations have started collecting the addresses and other details of the tourists from their respective districts and were perusing the condition of tourists with the Central government, official sources said. 11 persons from Chidambaram and Bhuvanagiri in Cuddalore district are among the pilgrims from Tamil Nadu who have been stranded in Nepal.
Founder of Isha Foundation Sadhguru Jaggi Vasudev on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) evening said that of the 21 groups who are part of their sojourn, 495 people have already returned safely, while 743 people were currently in Tibet, 148 people were in Nepal, and 77 people were at the immigration center and three volunteers in Timure, Nepal.
“All of us, including the volunteers and support teams are deeply anguished and are doing our utmost to assist in the rescue. There has been no official information on the whereabouts of any of the people who were at the immigration office. We are working with the authorities to see if we can get to the location and stand ready to be part of the rescue efforts, regardless of the risk involved,” he said in the post.
T. Sugumar (71) of Mayiladuthurai, whose wife, S. Manimekalai (64), had gone on a tour on Sunday (August 23, 2026) from Chennai to Kailash, said that his wife had communicated on Wednesday (August 26, 2026), saying that she was safe somewhere near the Nepal border. There were 19 others, along with Ms. Manimekalai, who travelled in the same vehicle on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) before the incident was reported.
“The call from my wife came around 11 a.m. to our daughter, saying that she and others were safe, said Mr. Sugumar. Where she was staying could not be known immediately. She could not be contacted thereafter, he further said.
Another traveller from Mayiladuthurai district was Pushpalatha (60) of Kazhukaanimattam. Her relative Ramesh said Ms. Pushpalatha made a WhatsApp call in the morning saying that she was safe. After the incident was reported, we called the official helpline number to be told that Pushpalatha was safe, Mr. Ramesh said.
A couple Rathinakumar (65) and Poonguzhali (61) of Mayiladuthurai had also gone for the Kailash tour on Sunday. “We got a call and a message from my uncle who had accompanied my parents during the tour saying that they were all safe after the landslide got reported”, said R. Arun Bharat Ram - the son of Rathinakumar and Poonguzhali.
My parents called my sister thereafter to say that they were all safe in a camp, Mr. Arun Bharat Ram said, adding that his parents had embarked on a 14-day tour. “We could not contact them later because of communication problems, he said.

Over 50 Tamil Nadu pilgrims stranded after flash floods at Nepal-China border
More than 50 pilgrims from Tamil Nadu are stranded after flash floods hit the Bhote Koshi River near the Nepal-China border; rescue efforts are underway.
More than 50 pilgrims from Tamil Nadu who had travelled to Nepal are stranded following a flash flood in the Bhote Koshi River upstream that killed at least nine people in Nepal and Tibet, washed away villages and damaged infrastructure on Wednesday, officials said.
The stranded group comprises pilgrims from Thanjavur, Kumbakonam and Mayiladuthurai districts. They were travelling in three cars when the flash flood occurred around 8am, officials said.
Also Read: Bihar steps up preparedness as flash flood in Nepal kills several, destroys villages
Deep Dive
A travel agent who organised the trip from Kumbakonam said some of the pilgrims managed to take refuge at an Armed Police Force outpost in Timure, about 150 km north of Kathmandu. However, he was unable to contact them due to a lack of mobile connectivity following the incident.
Tamil Nadu government officials are currently engaged in coordinated efforts to rescue the stranded pilgrims, officials said.
A round-the-clock toll free helpline was released by the Tamil Nadu government to assist the stranded people. “Within India 1800 309 3793, overseas (missed call) +91 80 6900 9900. They can also contact +91 80 6900 9901”, an official release said.
Those require assistance can also contact Tamil Nadu House, Delhi control room 92895 16712, it said.
Major casualties were feared in Nepal and Tibet. Videos showed crumbling homes in the floodwaters and floating cars as authorities urged people on the banks of the Bhote Koshi River to move to higher ground.
The Bhote Koshi River is a headwater tributary of the Kosi River system, which enters northern Bihar in Supaul after flowing through Nepal. Authorities in Bihar feared a sudden surge in water flow into the Gandak River.
The official said that teams of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) were being mobilised to handle any emergency. In Bihar, officials have identified areas such as Jhandu Tola, Bin Toli, Chakdahwa and Kailashnagar as vulnerable areas.
Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay said in a statement that he has instructed senior officials of the Tamil Nadu government at the Tamil Nadu House in Delhi to take all the necessary measures to swiftly rescue those hailing from Tamil Nadu missing in this disaster and to provide all required assistance to those affected.
Steps are being expedited to gather information about the people from Tamil Nadu through the ministry of external affairs of India and the Indian Embassy in Nepal ensuring their safety, he said
“Emergency telephone numbers have been announced to enable Tamils stranded in Nepal or their relatives in Tamil Nadu to reach out if they seek help” he added.

At least 105 Indians missing after flash floods

"A preliminary agency-wise record received from tourism and travel companies has identified 384 travellers, including 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali nationals, who were reported missing from the affected areas," said Nepal Tourism Board said.

headline: India rejects ‘politically motivated, malicious references' in UN panel's rights report
full_text:
India rejects ‘politically motivated, malicious references' in UN panel's rights report
Ministry of External Affairs, in a statement, said India had participated in the review in a “spirit of constructive engagement”.
India on Wednesday rejected what it called “politically motivated” and “highly malicious” references in a UN committee’s report on alleged racial discrimination in the country, saying the observations contained sweeping generalisations and unsubstantiated allegations.
“India rejects any politically motivated highly malicious references in the report with all the contempt that it deserves."
Responding to media queries on the UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination (UNCERD) press release following India’s 11th periodic review under the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (ICERD), the Ministry of External Affairs said in a statement that India had participated in the review in a “spirit of constructive engagement” and reaffirmed its unwavering commitment to combating racial discrimination.
The statement added that India had highlighted its constitutional safeguards, legal framework, pluralism and efforts to protect disadvantaged communities during the review.
“During the review, we highlighted India’s constitutional safeguards, robust legal framework, pluralism and sustained efforts to protect disadvantaged communities.”
The ministry of external affairs stressed that the inter-ministerial delegation led by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta had already rejected the “sweeping generalisations, unsubstantiated allegations, or tendency to exceed the Convention’s mandate” during the review meeting.
"While we will respond to the Committee's observations through the established procedure, the inter-Ministerial delegation, which was led by the Solicitor General of India, Shri Tushar Mehta, had already rejected the sweeping generalisations, unsubstantiated allegations, or tendency to exceed the Convention's mandate during the review meeting," the MEA stated.
It added that India would respond to the committee’s observations through the established procedure. The Indian Mission in Geneva has also issued a detailed statement following the CERD review.
What prompted India's response
MEA’s response came after the UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination raised concerns over reports of “large-scale violations” by law enforcement personnel against ethnic and ethno-religious communities, Indigenous and Tribal Peoples, including Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes, particularly Dalits, as well as non-citizens.
The recent review, held on August 11-12, covered India’s 12th and 21st combined periodic reports submitted to CERD in 2023. The discussions covered issues including the implementation of ICERD, progress among marginalised groups, and measures to address prejudice and intolerance, according to a statement by the Permanent Mission of India in Geneva, news agency ANI reported.
The Indian delegation highlighted the country’s diversity, constitutional safeguards, affirmative action, judicial remedies, democratic accountability and public policies aimed at promoting equality, dignity and opportunity for all citizens, the statement said.
In its statement, MEA stressed that India had played a leading role in negotiating and drafting ICERD in the 1960s.

Rahul Gandhi said the government was using batons and water cannons on students instead of hearing them, alleging AK-47 firing on protesters in Siwan.
Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday condemned the alleged use of an AK-47 against protesting students in Bihar over demands related to the BPSC examinations.
In a post on X, Rahul said that instead of listening to the students' demands, the government was using batons and water cannons against them. He added that police in Siwan had also allegedly opened fire with an AK-47 at protesters.

"The controversy over BPSC exams is not of today. Students have been on the streets for a long time over the recruitment process, exam pattern, delays, and transparency. But instead of answering, what is the government doing? It's wielding batons and water cannons. It's taking students into custody. In Siwan, there was even firing with an AK 47 on protesters," Rahul said.
Rahul further alleged that the BJP government was using the police as a weapon to evade accountability, adding that the use of such force would not stop students from raising questions.
"The students of Bihar will keep asking questions. And now, it's not just answers they want - they demand accountability," Rahul added.
What happened on Tuesday and why are students protesting in Bihar?
Tensions escalated in Patna on Tuesday as police deployed water cannons to disperse students marching towards Raj Bhavan and the chief minister's residence to protest against the 70th Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) examination and demand its cancellation.

Leader of Opposition in Bihar assembly Tejashwi Yadav alleged that the government, under pressure from the opposition and criticism over its handling of student protests, "might stop the use of firing but would not give up lathi-charge."
"The government will not engage in dialogue with students and youth fighting for transparency in the examination system and for jobs and education. Instead, it will get arrogant officials to insult them and have the police brutally lathi-charge peaceful protesters," the RJD leader said in a statement.
Chirag Paswan mediates between students and CM
Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) chief and Union minister Chirag Paswan said , later in the day, that he presented demands of the students before Bihar chief minister Samrat Chowdhary.
On Tuesday, Paswan visited the protest site in Patna and extended his support to the BPSC aspirants. He also criticised the police action on protesters marching towards Raj Bhavan and the Chief Minister's residence, demanding the cancellation of the 70th BPSC examination.

Upon reaching Patna today, I immediately went to the protest site and reached out to the students, listening seriously to their problems and demands."

headline: New Delhi: Days after the BJP and Union minister J. P. Nadda distanced themselves from the ‘purification’ controversy related to Congress national president Mallikarjun Kharge’s rally venue in Haldwani, Uttarakhand BJP president Mahendra Bhatt defend...
full_text:
New Delhi: Days after the BJP and Union minister J. P. Nadda distanced themselves from the ‘purification’ controversy related to Congress national president Mallikarjun Kharge’s rally venue in Haldwani, Uttarakhand BJP president Mahendra Bhatt defended the ritual saying “the place was polluted with slogans”.
A ‘shuddhikaran’ (purification) ceremony was held at the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani after a rally was addressed by Kharge on 8 August that had not only created a political stir in Uttarakhand, but nationally too.
Nadda, while responding to Kharge in the Rajya Sabha, had condemned the ‘shuddhikaran’.
Bhatt, while speaking to reporters on the sidelines of a Rakshabandhan event in Mussoorie, said the criticism over the ritual was being exaggerated by the opposition Congress merely for petty political gain as they don’t have any issue to raise.
Bhatt, while explaining the incident, stressed that the sanctity of a religious and cultural venue should be respected by all.
“Those who have no real issues raise matters that only damage and divide society. Kharge-ji’s rally (was) held in Haldwani. The Ramlila Ground there was defiled. Imagine at a place where there is a Ram temple, slogans were raised that should not have been raised. The place was polluted, and then it was purified,” Bhatt reasoned.
The BJP MP also accused the Congress of unnecessarily linking the controversy to Scheduled Caste politics.
“I can say that Congress members are making a mockery of their own leader; they have turned Kharge-ji into a subject of ridicule. Kharge-ji himself must surely realise that the incident which took place in Devbhoomi that day should not have happened,” he added.
Bhatt said the situation which unfolded during the rally and the slogans raised were not in keeping with the decorum of Ramlila Maidan.
The BJP state president also said that the cleanliness and purification of a religious site or an event venue should not be turned into a subject of political controversy. He also accused the Congress in Uttarakhand of raising issues that divide society.
A video of the ‘purification’ ceremony had gone viral on social media, with one of the organisers claiming that certain political slogans should not have been raised there. The ”purification’ ceremony was held at the site of the rally by members of the Shri Ram Sena a few days later.
Kharge had raised the matter in the Rajya Sabha and had demanded that those who carried out a ‘shuddhikaran’ at Haldwani’s Ramlila Ground after his rally be booked under the Untouchability Act and arrested.
Kharge had claimed that he had not referred to any particular community or religion in his speech.
Nadda, who is also the Leader of the House in Rajya Sabha, had distanced the BJP from the ceremony, pointing out that the party did not support such activities.
He had also assured Kharge that the incident would be investigated and said the BJP national president would look into the matter.
“It is a matter of great regret for all of us that your sentiments were hurt,” Nadda said.
(Edited by Viny Mishra)

headline: BJP MP Rao Inderjit Singh blames Congress era for Gurugram rain chaos, pitches tunnel fix
full_text:
BJP MP Rao Inderjit Singh blames Congress era for Gurugram rain chaos, pitches tunnel fix
BJP MP Rao Inderjit Singh said underground tunnels, similar to those built for the metro, should be constructed along the routes of the old drains.
BJP MP Rao Inderjit Singh has blamed development during the Congress era for Gurugram’s recurring waterlogging.
The ex-Congress minister said construction over old drainage routes worsened the problem and suggested building underground tunnels along old drainage routes to carry rainwater towards the Yamuna.
“We are still dealing with the consequences of this development that happened during the Congress era today,” he told reporters on Wednesday. “Waterlogging has been occurring in Gurugram for years. The main reason is that development has taken place over the old, traditional drains that used to carry water from the hills to the Yamuna,” Singh said.
He said underground tunnels, similar to those built for the metro, should be constructed along the routes of the old drains.
“The only way to fix this now is to construct underground tunnels, similar to those built for the Metro, along the paths of the old drains to channel the water through those original routes,” he said.
ALSO READ | After children stranded in rain, admin sets new safety protocol
Singh described the current measures as a temporary fix. “What we are doing right now is essentially a 'band-aid' solution. It offers some relief, but if we block the water in one place, it finds a way out elsewhere. The government is working on this, and we are arranging the necessary funds,” he said.
Inderjit Singh's Congress era
Rao Inderjit Singh himself was part of the Congress government during much of the period he blamed for Gurugram’s infrastructure woes. He began his political career with Congress in 1977, served as a Haryana minister, and later became a Union minister in the UPA government.
He won the Gurgaon Lok Sabha seat on a Congress ticket in 2009 before joining the BJP in 2014.
Deep Dive
Sinkhole opens up in Gurugram
His remarks came after a section of the service road at IFFCO Chowk caved in on Tuesday, creating a 10-foot-by-10-foot sinkhole following the collapse of a master sewer line.
The sinkhole opened on the Delhi-Jaipur side of the road. Traffic police barricaded the damaged stretch, while the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) closed both service lanes.
ALSO READ | Gurugram’s rain woes: IFFCO Chowk road caves in, dry taps, flood water recedes slowly
The cave-in came a day after heavy rainfall caused major waterlogging and traffic congestion across Gurugram. Several major roads and intersections were inundated, severely disrupting movement. By Wednesday morning, floodwater receded from most areas.
Traffic congestion was reported on Tuesday evening after the two service lanes were closed. Vehicles were subsequently diverted, officials said.
GMDA starts repair work
The GMDA said a master sewer line connecting Ambience Mall and Rajiv Chowk runs beneath or alongside the affected road.
GMDA executive engineer Bhim Arya said repairs would begin on Wednesday and an inspection would be carried out to establish why the sewer line collapsed.
NHAI said preliminary findings suggested that a leak or failure in the sewer line may have caused soil erosion, leading to the cave-in. The agency has asked GMDA to complete repairs urgently, calling the sinkhole a safety risk.
The cave-in came amid fresh disruptions to water supply in several Gurugram sectors, including 46, 48, 49, 50, 52, 56, 57 and 58 to 76, following damage to water and sewage pipelines.

NEW DELHI: New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has said he does not support a planned event featuring RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat at Madison Square Garden, while noting that the city may not have the legal authority to stop the private gathering.Bhagwat is scheduled to address around 5,000 members of the Indian diaspora at the iconic New York venue on August 29. His visit to the United States is part of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh's centenary-year global outreach programme."I don't support the rally, but I don't know if the city has any jurisdiction on cancelling a private event,â Mamdani said at a news conference on Tuesday.Mamdani was responding to questions about the RSS, the proposed event and protests against Bhagwat's appearance. He said the vision of India that he was taught by his family and the one that he grew up being very familiar with was that of "a pluralistic society, of a secular republic that believed in the belonging of each and every person who was from India".Mamdani said he was opposed to what he described as an increasingly exclusionary political movement.âAnd it has been incredibly troubling to see the rise of a movement that is predicated on an exclusionary vision of any country, frankly, and so it is one that I find myself in deep opposition to, not only as an Indian-American but also as the Mayor of a city that believes deeply in the belonging of each and every person, no matter their colour, their creed, their religion, their faith, wherever they're from,â Mamdani said.

New York mayor Zohran Mamdani opposed the event on Wednesday, even as he agreed that the New York City administration may not have the authority to cancel it.

headline: India not a ‘dharamshala’, says Amit Shah; cites threats from infiltrators
full_text:
India not a ‘dharamshala’, says Amit Shah; cites threats from infiltrators
Amit Shah said only citizens had the right to live in the country and infiltrators posed a threat to India’s security, economy and demographics.
Union home minister Amit Shah on Tuesday reiterated that India was “not a dharamshala”, saying only citizens had the right to live in the country and that infiltrators posed a threat to India’s security, economy and demographics.
“This country is not a dharamshala (charitable rest house); only citizens of the country have the right to live here,” Shah said, speaking at the valedictory session of the National Security Strategy conference of the Intelligence Bureau (IB), attended by chiefs of central agencies and state police forces.
Shah's take on India's security policy
Stressing that infiltrators threatened the country’s “security, economy and demographics”, the home minister said: “Over the past eight months, after visiting all states sharing land borders, we have shared a document outlining a four-pronged approach to border security with the states. Our goal is to make the country free of infiltrators in a very short period.”
Shah said India’s security policy had to be framed against the backdrop of global instability, insecurity around energy and resources, supply-chain disruptions, rising radicalisation and the warfare of cyber misinformation. A strong internal security apparatus, he said, was a prerequisite for a developed India. “If India is to emerge at the forefront in every field, its internal security will have to be further strengthened.”
Also Read I Use trial in absentia for fugitives hiding abroad: Amit Shah at security brass meet
Over the two-day NSS conference, intelligence agencies and security forces discussed infiltration, real-time intelligence-sharing against terror groups, and the dismantling of their logistics and funding networks, among other national security matters.
Similar comments from the past
Shah made similar remarks in Lok Sabha on March 27 while replying to the debate on the Immigration and Foreigners Bill, 2025. On that occasion, he had said India was “not a dharamshala where anyone can come and stay for any purpose”, arguing that Parliament had the right to bar those who posed a threat to national security, and that sensitive locations and army establishments along the borders could not be left open to all. Those who came legally to contribute to India’s prosperity were welcome, he had said, but illegal entrants would be dealt with strictly.
The Supreme Court too used phrasing when on May 19, a bench of justices Dipankar Datta and K Vinod Chandran declined to intervene in the detention of a Sri Lankan Tamil national facing deportation after a seven-year sentence under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. “Is India to host refugees from all over the world? We are struggling with 140 crore. This is not a dharamshala that we can entertain foreign nationals from all over.”
Also Read I ‘Let panel work’: SC on plea seeking Amit Shah, Delhi Police chief’s role in protest case
Attacking previous governments, Shah on Tuesday said had they anticipated the problems of narcotics, Naxalism and insurgency in the northeast before they became enormous challenges, “the country would not have had to suffer their consequences for decades.” He said the challenges in the country’s three internal security hotspots had been eliminated, and credited state police forces, central agencies and the central armed police forces (CAPFs).
Asking officers to look for trends over the next 15 to 20 years, Shah said they should identify problems that might arise and work out strategies to prevent them. He also directed state police forces to implement the Narcotics Control Vision document 2026-2029 on the ground and work on the “three Ds — Detect, Disrupt and Destroy” — to achieve a drug-free India.

headline: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) in Lucknow said the State government will provide appointment letters to one lakh youths over the next six months.
full_text:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) in Lucknow said the State government will provide appointment letters to one lakh youths over the next six months.
Mr. Adityanath added that more than 9.3 lakh youths had been provided government jobs by his government through a transparent and non-discriminatory process since 2017.
“The government has provided government jobs to more than 9.3 lakh youth in a transparent manner without discrimination over the last nine years. In Uttar Pradesh, one lakh jobs were once only an imagination, but we are going to hand over government job appointment letters to one lakh youth within the next six months. The process of declaring results is underway,” said Mr. Adityanath, addressing a function at Indira Gandhi Pratishthan.
In the function, he handed over appointment letters to 3,446 newly selected Technical Assistants (Group-C) and 126 Mandi Secretaries in the Agriculture Department under Mission Rozgar through the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC).
Mr. Adityanath urged newly selected candidates that since the government has provided transparent appointments, they should also use this opportunity for the benefit of the State, future generations, and the country. Honest discharge of duty is the theory of “Nation First.”
The Chief Minister further added, “our commissions and boards are effectively ensuring that appointment letters are issued to deserving candidates based on merit through a transparent recruitment process, free from discrimination and in accordance with reservation policies. This is praiseworthy. The selection of the most qualified candidates allows the entire state to harness their energy.”
The Chief Minister told officials of the recruitment commissions and boards, “there is no government interference in your operations. If we have granted you autonomy, then it is imperative to deliver results promptly. The declaration of results should not exceed six months after a requisition is received. Advertisements should be issued within one month, followed by examinations conducted within the subsequent two months. Streamline the process to ensure that the youth can channel their energy effectively. When we advance with the vigor of youth, positive outcomes will ensue.”
Hailing the transparent recruitment over the last nine years as an achievement of the double-engine government of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the CM accused the previous Samajwadi Party (SP) government of neglecting youths.
“Before 2017, as soon as advertisements were issued, the chacha-bhatija (uncle-nephew) duo and the Mahabharat clan would set out for collections. Youth kept wandering, but results never came. Ultimately, the Hon’ble Court had to stay the process. The time and age of youth were wasted,” he said.
“Young people who failed to get jobs were considered unworthy, but the fault was not of the youth. The fault lay with politicians sitting in the government machinery and dishonest people sitting in commissions and boards. Our government had said that we would break the backbone of the copying mafia and also bring their patrons to the ground. We got mafia properties confiscated and recovered money from them,” the CM added..
Mr. Adityanath said that after becoming Chief Minister in 2017, he directed officials of the Board of Secondary Education to conduct examinations and declare results within one month.
“When the response was negative, I told them, ‘Leave your chairs; I will get it done within a month.’ Today, examinations for 56 lakh candidates of the U.P. Board are completed within 14 days, and results are declared within the next 14 days. Earlier, examinations that started in February continued until the scorching heat of June. Now, examinations are conducted without copying, and results are declared on time. Universities have also been directed to bring reforms. Educational institutions should prepare themselves for students’ skilling, careers, and employment,” he added.

headline: 130+ Indians, 37 NRIs out of reach as Nepal floods toll mounts, Bihar, UP on alert: What is happening?
full_text:
130+ Indians, 37 NRIs out of reach as Nepal floods toll mounts, Bihar, UP on alert: What is happening?
Around 133 Indian nationals and 37 NRIs are among the foreigners missing and out of contact after a flash flood in the Bhote Koshi River in Nepal's Rasuwa.
Nepal has been witnessing massive flash floods since morning, with 95 dead so far, hundreds more missing, homes, cars and other establishments swept away in districts near rivers, and people separated from families.
Around 133 Indian nationals and 37 NRIs are among the foreigners authorities are unable to get in touch with after a flash flood in the Bhote Koshi River in the Rasuwa district of Nepal. Follow live updates here.
"A preliminary agency-wise record received from tourism and travel companies has identified 384 travellers, including 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali nationals, who were reported missing from the affected areas," said Nepal Tourism Board, as quoted by news agency AFP.
As Nepal deals with the flood chaos, Indian states Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have also stepped up vigil, with the possibility of a sudden rise in the Gandak and Narayani rivers' water due to the flash floods in the neighbouring country.
100+ Indians, 37 NRIs out of reach
According to the Nepal Tourism Board, around 133 Indian nationals and 37 NRIs are among the foreigners out of contact amid the flash floods. At least 59 of the Indians were pilgrims for the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra, PTI reported, citing Samrat Tours and Travel agency.
HT has learnt that the owner of a travel group has confirmed that 35 NRIs from a group of 47 people who left Kathmandu on Tuesday for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra are not reachable.
“They were staying at different hotels in Rasuwa. The 47 also include my staff and guests from Russia, Canada, US and UK. We spoke to them around 8 am today. We have lost touch after that. They were supposed to cross the Nepal-Tibet border today,” Sagar Pandey, owner of Himalayan Glacier Adventures said.
Also Read: Terrifying clips capture Nepal floods fury; buildings, people vanish in seconds
The 133 Indians are part of the 348 travellers out of contact since the flash floods hit Nepal. According to Reuters, 93 Nepalis, three US citizens, 17 Malaysian nationals, 12 British citizens, four South Africans, and one person each from Australia and the Netherlands. are also missing.
The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu has issued emergency numbers for assistance and information related to Indian nationals - 977 985 131 6807 or 977 970 910 7500.
Notably, at least 67 army personnel posted near the Nepal-China border are also among those with whom contact is yet to be established.
Why Nepal saw huge deluge today
Parts of Nepal and Tibet witnessed torrential floods on Wednesday morning. While roads, bridges, houses, and power projects were destroyed in Nepal, a mudslide hit Gyirong Port, a major land crossing with neighbouring Tibet.
According to Reuters, it is suspected that the floods were triggered by an earthquake striking the region and causing an ice-rock avalanche on the Lhende Khola river, which runs through both Nepal and Tibet.
Despite massive devastation in Nepal, the danger may not have passed yet. Authorities have reportedly warned that a second flood may occur since a blockage is still lodged upstream on the Lhende Khola river.
UP and Bihar on alert
Parts of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are on alert amid raging floods in Nepal.
There is a possibility in a sudden rise in water levels of the river Gandak in Bihar, and six teams of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) are on standby in border villagers of Bihar, HT has learnt. Districts such as Muzaffarpur, Gopalganj, Motihari, West and East Champaran and Siwan are likely to be impacted depending on water level and its flow when it reaches Bihar.
"We are in touch with Nepal authorities and tracking the water flow to India," NDRF officials said.
In Uttar Pradesh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directed the administrations of Maharajganj and Kushinagar districts to take all necessary measures to deal with any potential emergency. According to PTI, an official statement from Adityanath's office expressed concerns over the Nepal floods and said they could cause the water levels to surge in the Gandak and Narayani rivers in the neighbouring districts.
