headline: New Delhi: After Penguin Random House India Friday said that it is “not the publisher” of Sonia Gandhi’s upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, in India, Congress has alleged that the Narendra Modi government is “pressuring publishers”.

New Delhi: After Penguin Random House India Friday said that it is “not the publisher” of Sonia Gandhi’s upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, in India, Congress has alleged that the Narendra Modi government is “pressuring publishers”.
Senior party leader and former Rajasthan Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot has claimed that Penguin India was pressured to remove the portions related to Prime Minister Modi, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and the “occupation of Indian territory by China during Modi’s rule”.
“Penguin Worldwide is ready to publish Smt. Sonia Gandhi ji’s upcoming book worldwide in its original form, but Penguin Random House India wants changes made to launch it in India. After all, what is the reason or what pressure is there that what is being published across the world cannot be published in India?” he wrote in a post on X.
“This is the murder of democracy,” he remarked. “Why is this truth being hidden from the people of India? Will the Modi government alter even the facts by pressuring publishers?”
He added: “Smt. Sonia Gandhi ji’s life is an example of sacrifice and dedication. The integrity and dignity with which she has served the country is exemplary. Suppressing the book of Smt. Sonia Gandhi ji, a person of such stature, a senior leader of the nation, and former Leader of the Opposition, under pressure is tantamount to the murder of freedom of expression.”
Penguin Worldwide is ready to publish Smt. Sonia Gandhi ji's upcoming book worldwide in its original form, but Penguin Random House India wants changes made to launch it in India. After all, what is the reason or what pressure is there that what is being published across the…

As a publisher, it is both our prerogative and our responsibility to fact check and provide authors with recommendations that are in the best interests of their books.”
The publisher further called it a “normal part of the publishing process”. It added, “Throughout the relevant discussions, Penguin Random House India’s position was that we remained willing and keen to publish the book. We will not comment further on confidential discussions with the author.”

Gandhi’s 544-page memoir was set to be released in hardcover on 10 November, publisher Alfred A. The book offers a deeply personal account of Gandhi’s life, relationships and experiences, including her journey alongside husband Rajiv Gandhi and her years in public life.

headline: After Nepal says no to foreign help, India to send tunnel rescue team ‘on request’
full_text:
After Nepal says no to foreign help, India to send tunnel rescue team ‘on request’
External affairs minister S Jaishankar said that NDRF personnel may be sent if Nepal requires it and that two planes of relief materials have already gone.
As India continues to extend helping hand to flood-ravaged Nepal, external affairs minister S Jaishankar on Friday said that a team of tunneling experts is being sent as nearly a hundred people are stranded in a hydropower tunnel. This comes amid Nepal government denying help from foreign countries saying that its security agencies are capable of handling the rescue operation.
Jaishankar was speaking to the media after meeting group of 21 people who returned to Delhi from flood-ravaged Nepal on Friday. The minister said that a team of NDRF personnel may also be sent if Nepal requires it, adding that two planes of relief materials have already gone and third one will be sent on later in the day.
Track live updates on Nepal floods
What Jaishankar said
“The main thing is that in one place where there is a hydroelectric project, there could be possibility of people who may be a tunnel. So, we are sending a team to help with the experts in tunneling. Also, they need some bailey bridges, so we are sending bridges. These are bridges that can be quickly put together along with a team. There may be some medical teams also going out there. If they require NDRF people to go, we will send them. We have given them that option. Two planes of relief supplies have already gone out there and third plane will be taking off today,” Jaishankar said.
Deep Dive
While 85 Indians were rescued in Nepal on Friday, 315 still remain out of contact, Jaishankar noted. “We are still very much focused on contacting all the Indians who are there,” he said, adding that those who were evacuated and safely sent to India were thankful to Nepalese army.

Jaishankar further added that he spoke to Nepal's foreign minister on Friday morning as India remains focused on helping the flood-ravaged Nepal in the relief and rescue of people.
“We have given them a range of support offers, they are evaluating it. Whatever they feel is appropriate, they will pick up for their needs. Right now, the main thing is that in one place where there is a hydroelectric project, there could be possibility of people who may be a tunnel. So, we are sending a team to help with the experts in tunneling,” he said.
“Also, they need some bailey bridges, so we are sending bridges. These are bridges that can be quickly put together along with a team. There may be some medical teams also going out there. If they require NDRF people to go, we will send them. ”
MEA says help being sent
The ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal also said this earlier during the weekly MEA briefing. “As requested by the Nepal, we are preparing to send a Tunnel rescue team, for which a recce team is being flown in first to assess the equipment required etc. A medical team is also being sent. In addition, we have also offered Bailey bridges along with their associated technical teams so that connectivity can be restored quickly in the affected parts of Nepal. One Bailey bridge is already in Nepal and can be deployed for relief efforts," Jaiswal said.
Nepal rejects foreign help
Nepal has turned down offers from several countries to send search and rescue teams after devastating flash floods hit towns and villages near the China border. Nepal's Balen Shah-led government said on Friday that its security agencies are capable of handling the rescue operation.
At least 547 people have died and over 1,500 remain missing since Wednesday. Rescuers are searching through mud and debris, while newly formed barrier lakes raise fears of more flooding.
“The offer for help is natural. Our security agencies are doing the search and rescue operation. For now we don’t require such help,” Lok Bahadur Chhetri, spokesperson for Nepal’s foreign ministry, said, news agency Reuters reported.
The government has received requests from India, China, the US, UK, Japan, South Korea, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh to allow their search and rescue teams to assist with the operation.
The official said the decision was influenced by Nepal’s experience during the 2015 earthquake, when the arrival of a large number of foreign rescue teams created coordination challenges. headline: The Defence Ministry has simplified export and licensing norms to help Indian defence manufacturers access global markets faster.
full_text:
The Defence Ministry has simplified export and licensing norms to help Indian defence manufacturers access global markets faster.
Under the revised Defence Export Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), stakeholder consultation [with Ministries and government agencies concerned] has been dispensed with for exports of non-lethal defence items to most destinations. Safeguards, however, will continue to apply to sensitive countries. The requirement has also been removed for exports of all items for international tenders and exhibitions, allowing Indian companies to participate in overseas opportunities more expeditiously.
One-time approval
The Ministry’s Department of Defence Production has also overhauled the Open General Export Licence (OGEL) framework, which provides eligible exporters a standing, one-time authorisation to self-generate export authorisations for multiple consignments of specified defence items without seeking separate approval for every shipment.
Three existing OGEL SOPs covering major platforms and equipment, parts and components, and intra-company transfer of technology have been consolidated into a single framework.
The validity of OGEL has been increased from two to three years, reducing the frequency of renewals and associated compliance requirements. Its country coverage has also been expanded from 41 to all countries, except negative and sensitive nations, and those subject to United Nations Security Council sanctions or arms embargoes.
More items
A new provision has been introduced for Indian companies having long-term contracts or agreements with foreign original equipment manufacturers (FOEMs). An OGEL can be granted for eligible items for the particular FOEM, with validity aligned with the underlying contract or agreement, subject to prescribed conditions.
The range of items eligible for export under OGEL has also been expanded. The revised framework permits civil-end-use exports of specified parts and components of small-calibre arms and protective equipment, widening the scope for legitimate international business.
The reforms are intended to reduce routine procedural requirements while retaining safeguards for sensitive items, technologies, and destinations. The Ministry said the measures would particularly benefit Indian defence manufacturers, including micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), by helping them respond faster to international tenders and exhibitions, and reducing repetitive authorisation requirements.
The measures come amid a record growth in India’s defence manufacturing and exports. Defence production reached an all-time high of ₹1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26, while exports touched a record ₹38,424 crore during the financial year.

headline: Not accurate: Penguin India on reports it pulled plug on Sonia Gandhi's memoir
full_text:
Not accurate: Penguin India on reports it pulled plug on Sonia Gandhi's memoir
Penguin India said it is not the publisher of Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging' and said reports suggesting it decided against publishing the book because the Congress leader declined editorial changes were inaccurate.
Penguin Random House India has pushed back against reports that it dropped Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s much-anticipated memoir after she rejected editorial changes and deletions sought by the publisher.
In a statement shared on its X page on Saturday, the publishing house said it is not the publisher of 'Belonging: A Journey of Love in India' and said reports suggesting it decided against publishing the book because Gandhi declined editorial changes were inaccurate.
"Any suggestion that Penguin Random House India decided not to publish ‘Belonging’ because the author declined editorial changes does not accurately reflect the circumstances," the company said.
The clarification follows a report by The Indian Express that Penguin Random House India had pulled out of publishing the memoir after Gandhi rejected proposed changes and deletions to part of the manuscript.
Penguin India, in its statement, said fact-checking manuscripts and making editorial recommendations are a normal part of the publishing process.
"As a publisher, it is both our prerogative and our responsibility to fact check and provide authors with recommendations that are in the best interests of their books," it said.
The publisher added that during the discussions, its position was that it remained "willing and keen to publish the book".
The memoir, expected to offer a detailed account of Gandhi’s life, was originally announced for release in the US by Alfred A Knopf, which is owned by Penguin Random House. The book was scheduled for release November 10, 2026, with an initial print run of 100,000 copies.
'Belonging' traces Sonia Gandhi’s journey from her childhood in post-war Italy to her life in India after her marriage to Rajiv Gandhi. It also chronicles her years as the daughter-in-law of then-Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
The memoir covers Gandhi’s eventual entry into politics after years of resisting pressure to take the plunge. It also recounts her decision in 2004 to decline the prime minister’s post after the Congress-led alliance won the general election.
In a statement by Knopf earlier, the Congress MP said the book offers readers a perspective on the social and political changes she witnessed during more than six decades in India. She described India as "the beautiful country of my belonging".
The book has attracted considerable attention because Gandhi has largely stayed away from writing a conventional autobiography. She has previously authored and edited books, but people who have worked on the memoir have described it as "her most personal and definitive account of her life".
Knopf has described Belonging as a memoir about “love, family” and India, calling Gandhi one of the world’s most prominent women leaders.
However, Penguin India's clarification leaves the precise status of the book’s India publication unclear, with the Express report claiming that several top publishers are now vying for the rights.

headline: The Delhi Police Special Cell arrested a young couple from the city for allegedly working for Pakistan-based intelligence operatives and helping an ISI-backed espionage network procure Indian SIM cards and recruit people for reconnaissance of cantonm...
full_text:
The Delhi Police Special Cell arrested a young couple from the city for allegedly working for Pakistan-based intelligence operatives and helping an ISI-backed espionage network procure Indian SIM cards and recruit people for reconnaissance of cantonment areas, officials said on Friday (August 28, 2026).
The accused, identified as 25-year-old Md. Sahil, a resident of Sarai Kale Khan, and his 21-year-old wife, Sameera, were recruited through social media and provided logistical support to Pakistani handlers, the police alleged. Two mobile phones containing incriminating conversations with Pakistani intelligence operatives were recovered from them.
The Special Cell alleged that Sahil came into contact with a Pakistani agent on Instagram in 2024 through Sameera, and that the agent subsequently introduced the couple to a Pakistan-based intelligence operative, who the police said cultivated them and offered financial incentives to work for the network.
The couple was allegedly tasked with providing logistical support to the network in Delhi, recruiting more individuals for espionage and carrying out field operations.
The police said Sahil and Sameera procured eight Indian SIM cards in 2024 and 2025, and sent them to Pakistan through Dubai. They were paid ₹30,000 by their Pakistani handlers for the SIM cards, officers said.
The numbers were subsequently activated on WhatsApp in Pakistan, after which the Pakistani operatives allegedly used them to enter Indian WhatsApp groups and gather information. The accounts were also used to approach Indians to obtain sensitive information, police said.
Sahil was assigned the additional task of recruiting people to conduct reconnaissance of cantonment areas at different locations in India, police said, adding that he was also asked to provide details of Army personnel whose court-martial proceedings were pending before a tribunal.
The probe
The Special Cell said the investigation began after its Northern Range unit received information about an ISI-backed Pakistani intelligence network operating in Delhi-NCR. The information was developed further, leading investigators to identify individuals providing logistical support to the network.
Sahil was arrested first, and forensic analysis of his mobile phone revealed incriminating chats with Pakistani agents, police said. During interrogation, he disclosed the alleged involvement of Sameera, leading to her arrest.
The forensic examination of the couple's mobile phones purportedly revealed conversations between them and their Pakistani handlers. The police said their questioning had also provided details about the functioning of the network and the manner in which Pakistan-based operatives coordinated with individuals in India through social media and encrypted communication platforms.
Sahil, born in 2001, has a BA degree from the Indira Gandhi National Open University and had worked with a lawyer while planning to pursue a bachelor’s in law. He left the job in June 2025 and has been unemployed since then. Sameera, born in 2005, completed her Class 12 in Delhi and later pursued a BA through correspondence. She was working at a call centre in Noida before her arrest.

headline: Shashi Tharoor's vocab lesson amid flak over 'drama' remark on Nepal floods
full_text:
Shashi Tharoor's vocab lesson amid flak over 'drama' remark on Nepal floods
A single word sparked backlash against Shashi Tharoor over his Nepal flood post. The Congress leader has now explained why he used "drama" and admitted he regretted the choice.
Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Friday clarified his use of the word "drama" in a post on the Nepal flash floods, saying he had used it in the sense of "a state, situation or series of events involving intensely clashing forces". He also said he regretted choosing a word that could be so easily "misinterpreted".
The clarification came a day after Tharoor faced criticism on social media for saying he had been "blissfully unaware of the drama that had taken place in the hills" while referring to the disaster in Nepal. Several users called the wording insensitive and questioned his choice of words.
In a post on X, the Thiruvananthapuram MP said, "For all those fulminating in outrage about my use of the word 'drama' in my first tweet from Nepal, the word does not only mean something theatrical. It is also defined as 'a state, situation or series of events involving intensely clashing forces'." He added, "That's the sense in which I intended it. But I do regret the choice of a word that could be so easily misinterpreted."
Tharoor's remarks came after his Thursday post on the Nepal flash floods drew sharp reactions online. In that post, he had said, "Took off for Kathmandu yesterday, blissfully unaware of the drama that had taken place in the hills and caused such catastrophic damage."
He also wrote, "A severe, sudden flash flood struck northern Nepal's Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, causing widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Global warming and/or an earthquake in Tibet may have caused a large chunk of a glacier to break off and fall into the valley below, experts surmise."
Tharoor had said he learnt on arrival about the loss of life and that some 2,000 or more people were estimated to be missing. He said raging floodwaters had destroyed at least 19 motorable bridges, washed away roughly 40 kilometres of the Betrawati Rasuwagadhi highway, and heavily damaged eight operational hydropower projects.
He had also said, "I fully support the Indian government's immediate pledge of relief assistance. Nepal needs all the help it can get." In the same post, he added, "My heart goes out to the victims and their loved ones, who include large numbers of Indian tourists, including a hundred performing the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra. Prayers for the missing; may they be rescued soon."
Despite that broader message, many users focused on his wording. One user said, "Was nature's fury a 'drama'? How can you be so insensitive in your choice of words? What good is knowing the dictionary if you don't know what to say when? Your 'sympathy' seems like the drama here!"
Another wrote, "Sir, you are Shakespeare of Indian English. Is the usage of the word DRAMA in the second sentence of the first para appropriate?" A third user called it a "poor choice of words for someone with such a rich vocabulary".
Another post said, "Mr Exasperating Farrago -- Is this 'drama'?" while one more user wrote, "Drama?? You are a wordsmith, and this is what you came up with?"
Tharoor has now defended the intended meaning of the word while accepting that it could be misunderstood, after his post on the Nepal flash floods triggered a backlash and debate over his choice of language.

headline: Hi5, smiles and more: PM Modi's day out with children on Raksha Bandhan
full_text:
Hi5, smiles and more: PM Modi's day out with children on Raksha Bandhan
Narendra Modi celebrated Raksha Bandhan with schoolgirls and students at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg, where they tied rakhis and exchanged high-fives. The images and social media posts placed the festival interaction within a broader push for informal digital outreach to younger audiences.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated Raksha Bandhan with schoolgirls and students at his official residence at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg, on Friday, sharing moments of interaction, smiles and high-fives with the young visitors.
In a post on Instagram, PM Modi shared glimpses of the celebrations and captioned them, “Hi5, smiles and more during today’s Raksha Bandhan celebrations at 7, LKM.”
The visuals showed the Prime Minister engaging with the students in an informal and relaxed setting as they marked the festival. The event featured young students in school uniforms, including some dressed in NCC cadet attire, tying rakhis around PM Modi’s wrist as a symbol of affection and protection.
PM Modi was seen seated among the students and interacting directly with them.
Traditional Raksha Bandhan items, including a ceremonial bowl, were also visible during the celebrations.
In several moments, the Prime Minister exchanged high-fives with the young participants and smiled as he interacted with them.
A NEW WAY FOR GENZ OUTREACH?
The interaction can be viewed as another avenue for PM Modi to connect with younger audiences, particularly GenZ, through informal and relatable engagements.
The use of candid interactions, high-fives and social media-friendly visuals also reflects how political communication is increasingly moving beyond formal public meetings and traditional political events.
The outreach comes amid a broader emphasis on engaging younger audiences through digital platforms and more informal interactions.
While the Prime Minister's post did not explicitly describe the Raksha Bandhan celebration as a GenZ outreach initiative, the participation of school students and the manner in which the interaction was presented online could contribute to building a more youthful and approachable public image.
Earlier, PM Modi extended his greetings to people on Raksha Bandhan, wishing them happiness, prosperity and success. In a post on X, he said he hoped the festival would preserve the bond of love, affection and mutual trust symbolised by Raksha Bandhan, and remain “forever unbreakable”.
Raksha Bandhan celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters. Sisters traditionally tie colourful rakhis after applying tilak, while brothers offer gifts and reaffirm their support. The festival is observed on the full moon day of Shravana, generally in August, and is primarily celebrated in India and Nepal.

Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) leader Amit Thackeray on Thursday warned auto-rickshaw and taxi drivers against misbehaving with passengers or insisting that they speak only in Hindi, saying those found troubling commuters could face retaliation.
Thackeray's remarks came after the Maharashtra government on Thursday gave auto-rickshaw, taxi and cab drivers one year to learn functional Marathi, according to news agency ANI.

headline: In a first, CM Vijay ditches his chair, sits with ministers in Tamil Nadu Assembly
full_text:
In a first, CM Vijay ditches his chair, sits with ministers in Tamil Nadu Assembly
Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay moved from his designated chair and sat beside ministers in the Tamil Nadu Assembly. The unusual shift came amid a discussion on officials' presence in the House and broke with established seating practice.
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay broke with a long-standing Assembly convention on Thursday when he moved away from his designated chair and sat alongside ministers in the front row during the afternoon session of the state Assembly.
Vijay's move drew attention as chief ministers traditionally occupy a separate chair positioned close to the Speaker's seat. Ministers sit separately in the front row alongside the Chief Minister, with their positions generally determined by seniority.
The Opposition occupies the row facing the treasury benches.
The Leader of the Opposition and leaders of various legislature parties are seated according to their numerical strength in the 234-member House, with members of their respective parties seated behind them.
During Thursday's afternoon proceedings, Vijay casually left his designated chair, located to the right of Speaker JCD Prabhakar, and took a seat between ministers KA Sengottaiyan, who is also the Leader of the House, and Aadhav Arjuna.
A source said it was unusual for a chief minister to move from the chair specifically designated for the post and sit in a seat meant for a minister.
While ministers and legislators occasionally change seats for brief conversations with colleagues, the source said such a move by a chief minister was perhaps unprecedented.
The Chief Minister had attended government events earlier in the day before arriving at the Assembly for the afternoon proceedings.
OPPOSITION RAISES ISSUE OF OFFICIALS' PRESENCE
Earlier on Thursday, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin raised concerns over the absence of department secretaries from the Assembly when members discussed important issues.
Udhayanidhi referred to discussions surrounding the Karur stampede and recalled that during the previous DMK government, former Chief Minister MK Stalin and senior bureaucrats, including the Chief Secretary and department secretaries, were present in the House when the issue was discussed.
He said the same level of administrative presence was missing during the current Assembly session.
Responding to the Opposition leader, Aadhav Arjuna said department secretaries were present in an adjoining "war room" and were taking notes from the speeches and issues raised by legislators.
Speaker JCD Prabhakar agreed with Udhayanidhi's suggestion and said senior officials would be asked to remain present in the Assembly during proceedings.
The exchange came amid discussions on the functioning of the House and the coordination between the political leadership and senior government officials.
Vijay's unusual seating shift later in the day, meanwhile, became one of the notable moments of Thursday's Assembly proceedings, departing from the traditional seating arrangement followed by successive chief ministers.

headline: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Thursday announced that the government has decided to give autorickshaw and taxi drivers one year to learn “functional Marathi”.
full_text:
Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Thursday announced that the government has decided to give autorickshaw and taxi drivers one year to learn “functional Marathi”.
The Chief Minister made the announcement after a delegation of representatives of autorickshaw and taxi drivers, led by Haji Arfat Shaikh, met him.
“They requested one year’s time. The State government has accepted their demand. No action will be taken against the during this period. Marathi classes will be organised and study material will be provided to help migrant drivers learn functional Marathi. They have come forward and are willing to learn. Therefore, it was necessary to give them time,” Mr. Fadnavis said.
Facing backlash
The move comes days after the Transport Department headed by Shiv Sena Minister Pratap Sarnaik carried out a checking drive and issued notices to drivers who failed a Marathi test.
The State government faced backlash by a section of drivers, especially ahead of the 2027 Assembly election in Bharatiya Janata Party-ruled Uttar Pradesh. Maharashtra hosts a large workforce from U.P. across major economic hubs like Mumbai, Pune, and Nashik.
Mr. Fadnavis said the representatives shared the concerns of drivers. “They support the decision to learn functional Marathi, but said people of different age groups are in the profession. Many of them left studies years ago. In such a short span, it is difficult for them to learn the language. They have made an elaborate plan to learn functional Marathi in one year. So, the State government will help them learn it,” he said.
The government had announced in April that non-Marathi drivers must attain basic proficiency in the State’s official language and set August 15 as the deadline. Marathi classes were then organised for the drivers in the interim period.
Meanwhile, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde lauded Maharashtra Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik for the bid to bring and implement the decision. He said that 1.60 lakh non-Marathi people learnt the language because of this initiative. He also said that 15,000 to 20,000 auto and taxi drivers were certified in Mumbai alone.

Valmiki scam: Karnataka minister B Nagendra resigns; breaks down on camera

B Nagendra broke down during a press conference while announcing his decision
NEW DELHI: Karnataka planning and statistics minister B Nagendra resigned from the state cabinet on Friday amid mounting pressure over the alleged Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation scam.He also broke down during a press conference while announcing his decision.Nagendra stepped down within 25 days of assuming office after being re-inducted into the cabinet on August 3. He said he had tendered his resignation to chief minister D K Shivakumar."Today I am voluntarily tendering my resignation as the minister," an emotional Nagendra told reporters.
He said he had taken the decision with a heavy heart to ensure that the party leadership was not embarrassed.Nagendra alleged that he was being targeted as part of a conspiracy and said the BJP could not intimidate him through central investigating agencies."They (BJP) can't scare me with ED, CBI," Nagendra said.He also alleged that "Manuwadis", in an apparent reference to the BJP, were targeting him because they did not want a tribal person in the country to grow."Manuwadis targeted me as they didn't want a tribal person in the country to grow," he alleged.
Nagendra also challenged the BJP to defeat him in Ballari in the "court of public opinion". He said he was prepared to resign as an MLA and face elections if the BJP was ready to take him on.The resignation marks the second time Nagendra has stepped down from the cabinet over the controversy. He had earlier resigned as tribal welfare minister in June 2024 when the issue first surfaced.
Pressure after cabinet re-induction
Nagendra was re-inducted into the Karnataka cabinet on August 3 and given the planning and statistics portfolio. His return triggered fresh demands from the BJP and JD(S) for his removal over the alleged diversion of funds from the state-run corporation.Earlier on Friday, Nagendra had said he would meet chief minister D K Shivakumar and discuss the matter in detail."If a situation arises where my actions cause embarrassment to the party, then I will..." he had said, alleging that the developments were part of a "conspiracy".The opposition BJP and JD(S) had been protesting his re-induction into the cabinet and alleging his involvement in the alleged Rs 89 crore scam.The two parties had also staged repeated protests inside and outside the Karnataka legislature during the recent monsoon session, which was curtailed by three days and adjourned sine die on August 24 amid continued disruptions.The BJP and JD(S) had planned a foot march from Raichur to Ballari from September 1 to 10, demanding Nagendra's resignation.
What is the Valmiki Corporation case?
The controversy dates back to May 2024, when P Chandrasekharan, then an accounts superintendent with the Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation, died by suicide and left behind a six-page note alleging irregularities and unauthorised transfers of corporation funds.
Subsequent investigations found that Rs 89.63 crore had been transferred from a corporation account to a Union Bank of India account and later moved to multiple other accounts, triggering a major political controversy.Nagendra, who was tribal welfare minister when the issue surfaced, resigned from the cabinet in June 2024.He had previously rejected reports that he would resign and maintained that the allegations against him were "politically motivated". Just two days ago, he had dismissed media reports claiming that he had offered to step down.His resignation on Friday came amid renewed political pressure on the Congress government over the alleged Valmiki Corporation scam.

Arjuna told the Court that the X post made by DMK’s IT Wing was “ex facie false” and highly defamatory. The post, shared by the DMK IT Wing’s official X handle, claimed that John Britto, an accused in a narcotics case involving the alleged smuggling of banned substances worth ₹258 crore, was related to Arjuna.
Arjuna has denied having any connection with the accused.

Arjuna has further sought directions to Stalin and the DMK IT Wing to issue unconditional apologies in both Tamil and English through their social media accounts, as well as widely circulated Tamil and English newspapers and television channels. headline: Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force and other police teams are actively working to identify four assailants who allegedly shot dead Haryanvi singer and YouTuber Ankit Balyan in Shamli, after tracing their escape route to Haryana with the help of CCTV fo...
full_text:
Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force and other police teams are actively working to identify four assailants who allegedly shot dead Haryanvi singer and YouTuber Ankit Balyan in Shamli, after tracing their escape route to Haryana with the help of CCTV footage, officials said on Friday (August 28, 2026).
Sources said CCTV footage from several locations in Shamli, Loni in Ghaziabad, Delhi and Sonipat have captured four men fleeing on two motorcycles after the shooting.
Promoting his 'Baby Badmash' song released last month, Ankit Balyan sang a few of its lines, including, "Murder maar de sadak ke upar (murder on the road)" to his Instagram followers in a video. Hours later, he was shot dead in a manner eerily resembling the setting described in the song.
Balyan was leaving a gym in the Kotwali area of Shamli around 6.45 p.m. on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) when four assailants travelling on two motorcycles opened fire on him. He sustained critical injuries and was declared dead at a community health centre, police said.
A resident of Banti Kheda village in Shamli, Balyan had made a name for himself in the Haryanvi music industry. His YouTube channel had over 3.68 lakh subscribers, and his songs - heavily featuring guns, fights and SUVs, and with lyrics invoking themes of violence, defiance and rivalry - often drew millions of views.
Some of his popular numbers include "Bhari Court Mein Goli Marenge", "Body Builder", "PTI", and "Ek Khtola Jail Ke Bhitar".
Entry into politics
However, a career in music was not always Balyan's plan. His brother Kapil told mediapersons that the singer played state-level kabadi until 2013-14 and had participated in competitions in Delhi, Bhopal and other places. He had to quit the sport after suffering a leg fracture and later joined a gym.
It was around 2022 that Balyan began pursuing his passion for Haryanvi music. Over the years, he worked for more than 50 songs as a singer, lyricist and music composer. He remained active through music videos and social media and had about 4.97 lakh followers on Instagram as well, with his account displaying the tagline 'Yudhay Krit Nishchaya' (determined to fight), fitting with his song lyrics and musical genre.
His final Instagram post was uploaded about two hours before he was shot dead on Wednesday. In the video, Balyan is seen sitting in his car and singing a Haryanvi song with the line, "Murder maar de sadak ke upar".
Police are examining the activity and timeline of his social media accounts.
Balyan was working on more than 20 new Haryanvi songs, which were scheduled to be released next month. His family said he was also preparing to contest the district panchayat member election from his village and planned to try his luck in Bollywood.
Balyan is survived by two elder sisters and a younger brother.
He lived between Rohtak, Sonipat and Delhi's Khajuri Khas for his music work and had offices at all three places. He usually visited his village once every one or two months, locals said.
The killing triggered protests, with the victim's family and others blocking a road in Shamli and demanding the immediate arrest of the attackers.
The blockade has since been cleared, Mr. Bhaskar said, adding that the family was cooperating with the investigation.
Balyan's last rites were performed in his native village Banti Kheda after the post-mortem on Thursday.
The killing has drawn criticism from the Samajwadi Party and Congress, which have targeted the BJP-led Uttar Pradesh government over the law and order situation.

headline: Javelin missile explained: How anti-tank system India is buying uses ‘fire-and-forget’ tech to destroy armoured targets
full_text:
Javelin missile explained: How anti-tank system India is buying uses ‘fire-and-forget’ tech to destroy armoured targets
The anti-tank missile system is currently used by the US Army and Marine Corps as well as several international customers.
India has signed the letter of offer and acceptance with the United States to purchase the Javelin anti-tank guided missile system through its foreign military sales process. This comes nine months after the US State Department approved the possible sale, reportedly worth $45.7 million, to the Indian Army following New Delhi’s request.
The missile system is produced by the Javelin Joint Venture, a partnership between RTX and Lockheed Martin, and is currently used by the US Army and Marine Corps as well as several international customers. It is designed to be used against a wide array of targets, including armoured vehicles and fortified positions.
US ambassador to India Sergio Gor hailed the move as one which would further deepen bilateral defence cooperation.
All you need to know about the Javelin system
📌 What is the Javelin weapon?
The Javelin system is an advanced, medium-range, fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missile. According to the Lockheed Martin website, it is one of the world's “premier” shoulder-fired anti-armor system.
📌How does it work?
The anti-tank missile system automatically guides itself to the target after launch, allowing the gunner to take cover and avoid counterfire, according to the manufacturer. The soldiers or marines using it can reposition immediately after firing, or reload to “engage another threat.”
The weapon uses an arched top-attack profile, climbing above its target for improved visibility, and then strikes where the armor is weakest, according to Lockheed Martin. To fire, the personnel has to place a cursor over the selected target, following which the Javelin command launch unit sends a lock-on-before-launch signal to the missile.
📌Key features and other details
• Javelin is a single man-portable fire-and-forget medium-range antitank weapon system designed to defeat all known and projected threat armor. It can be fired in top or direct attack modes.
• It was developed and produced for the US Army and Marine Corps by the Javelin Joint Venture between Lockheed Martin in Orlando, Florida and Raytheon in Tucson, Arizona.
• The highly lethal medium-range Javelin has been in full-rate production since 1994, and made its 50,000th delivery in 2021, according to the Lockheed Martin website.
• Lockheed Martin specified that the anti-tank missile system's fire-and-forget capability provides “superior survivability” by enabling the operator to immediately relocate after firing.
• The anti-tank weapon is a platform-employed precision weapon system, and can defeat “all known and projected armor on the battlefield”, including main battle tanks and softer targets. Its soft-launch design allows the system to be fired safely from enclosed structures, including buildings and bunkers.
What did US ambassador Gor say on the agreement?
US ambassador Sergio Gor on Friday said the agreement “reflects a defense partnership that is growing deeper, more capable, and more consequential.”
“The Javelin agreement demonstrates the depth of US support for the Indian Army and creates new opportunities for our defense industries to work together. We see tremendous potential for future cooperation that strengthens the defense industrial bases of both countries,” Gor added.
Gor made the announcement on X, saying the purchase, “highlighted by” US secretary of war Pete Hegseth at the May 2026 Shangri-La Dialogue, was a “great step forward in the US-India defense relationship and opens the door to co-production possibilities.” He further said that the engagement between Washington and New Delhi was “at record high levels.”

headline: India sets sights on US Javelin anti-tank missile system. What is it?
full_text:
India sets sights on US Javelin anti-tank missile system. What is it?
One of the most famous anti-tank weapons in the world, the Javelin missile system uses fire-and-forget technology. It will be a potent addition to India's arsenal after last year's Operation Sindoor.
India plans to buy the US-made shoulder-fired Javelin anti-tank guided missile system (ATGM), US ambassador to India Sergio Gor announced on Friday, signalling further deepening of defence ties between Delhi and Washington. Calling it "big news", Gor asserted that it would open the door to co-production possibilities of Javelin missiles.
"Big news! India plans to buy the battle-tested Javelin anti-tank system... This is a great step forward in the US-India defence relationship and opens the door to co-production possibilities. The engagement between our two nations is at record-high levels," Gor tweeted.
The Indian army has signed a Letter of Offer and Acceptance (LOA) for the purchase of the Javelin missiles under emergency procurement. The development comes months after Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and his US counterpart Pete Hegseth signed a 10-year framework to deepen bilateral defence relations.
The deal, which will be through the Foreign Military Sales (FMS) route, will allow the armed forces to bypass the convoluted and long procurement process for contracts.
India's interest in the American FGM-148 Javelin system, however, is not new. Issues like technology transfer and local production have repeatedly stalled India's plans to procure one of the most famous anti-tank weapons in the world. In fact, talks have been ongoing since 2010.
WHAT IS JAVELIN ANTI-TANK MISSILE SYSTEM?
Jointly manufactured by Raytheon and Lockheed Martin, Javelin is a man-portable, fire-and-forget missile system. This means the operator does not have to manually guide the weapon to the target.
The missile system, which costs around $178,000, locks onto the target's heat signature before launch using its infrared seeker.
What makes the Javelin exceptional is its ability to strike tanks from above, where their armour is the weakest. Modern tanks are basically designed to survive frontal attacks. After being fired, the missile climbs to an altitude of 150 meters, and then dives onto the target from above.
Imagine a war scenario where battle tanks are pitted against Javelin missiles. A battle tank costs around $4 million. An infantry soldier carrying a Javelin system on his shoulder can destroy that tank in under 15 seconds.
Also consider the cost - the total Javelin system, including the command launch unit, costs a fraction of the target it's designed to kill. This is what makes the FGM-148 Javelin one of the most sought-after infantry weapons of the 21st century.
WHY IS IT KEY FOR INDIA'S ARMED FORCES?
When inducted, the Javelin missile system will undoubtedly be a potent addition to India's weaponry, especially following the hostilities with Pakistan last year.
In fact, the Indian Army's requirement for an advanced ATGM emerged in the early 2000s. Then, the Army was using the ageing French-origin Milan-2T and Soviet-era 9M113 Konkurs-M systems. While both were reliable, they were no match for third-generation ATGMs like Javelin.
The missile system was inducted by the US armed forces in the mid-1990s. Since then, it has evolved through several variants. While the base model has a maximum range of 2,500 metres, the more advanced FGM-148F system can fire missiles up to a range of 4,750 metres.
When the Indian forces ultimately acquire the Javelin system, it will bring to a close one of the longest-running defence procurement chapters in recent years.

headline: Delhi ‘spy couple’ sent SIM cards to Pakistan. ISI used them to enter Indian WhatsApp groups

Delhi ‘spy couple’ sent SIM cards to Pakistan. ISI used them to enter Indian WhatsApp groups
The cops seized two mobile phones that the couple used, which they say contain incriminating chats with their handlers in the network.
The Delhi Police's special cell on Friday said it busted a Pakistani intelligence operatives-led espionage module, based in Pakistan and backed by the country’s Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), by arresting a Delhi couple in their 20s, who had been working for it for two years.
According to the investigators, the arrested couple, identified as 25-year-old Mohammad Sahil and his 21-year-old wife Sameera, allegedly procured Indian SIM cards and sent them to Pakistan via Dubai for the module's use. Investigators said the Pakistani intelligence operatives used the cards to activate and operate WhatsApp from Pakistan and become members of groups in India to collect sensitive and classified information related to Indian defence.
Police said Sahil, an Indira Gandhi National Open University graduate, worked with a lawyer and planned to pursue a law course. In June 2022, he left the job and has been unemployed since. Sameera, who completed her BA course through correspondence, worked at a call centre.
The cops seized two mobile phones that the couple used, which they say contain incriminating chats with their handlers in the network.
Deputy police commissioner (special cell) Narra Chaitanya said the couple was allegedly tasked with recruitment in India for reconnaissance of cantonments and to share details of Indian Army personnel facing court-martial.
How was the module busted?
The Delhi Police's special cell, which tracks terrorist outfits and over-ground workers and sleeper cells providing logistical support, was tipped off about the ISI-backed network in Delhi and the National Capital Region.
The information was developed, and the special cell discovered that the module had recruited some in Delhi for logistical support and to procure SIM cards. The cell found WhatsApp was being used on these numbers from Pakistan to collect sensitive information.
DCP Chaitanya said the investigators identified the module's members and arrested Sahil, a resident of South Delhi’s Sarai Kale Khan.
"Forensic analysis of his mobile phone helped us find his incriminating chats with Pakistani agents,” Chaitanya said.
The couple contacted on Instagram
Sahil was found to have been allegedly in contact with a Pakistani agent on Instagram through his friend Sameera, who later became his wife. The agent allegedly introduced Sahil and Sameera to a Pakistani intelligence operative.
“Gradually, the operative cultivated Sahil and Sameera and convinced them to work for the network for financial gains. Sahil and Sameera were asked to extend logistical support to the network in Delhi and recruit more individuals for espionage and field operations,” DCP Chaitanya said.
₹30,000 for 8 SIM cards
Police said the couple was allegedly paid ₹30,000 for sending eight Indian SIM cards to Pakistan via Dubai in 2024 and 2025.
“WhatsApp accounts were activated on these numbers in Pakistan, and the network succeeded in joining some Indian WhatsApp groups for gathering information. These accounts were used to approach Indians to collect sensitive information,” said a second officer.
What interrogation reveals
DCP Chaitanya said the couple’s interrogation revealed the network's modus operandi and provided crucial insights into its structure and functioning.
"The operation uncovered significant details about Pakistan-based handlers and the method they used to coordinate with the over-ground workers/sleeper cells through encrypted communication platforms." He said the operation foiled espionage activities.

NEW DELHI: Two cabinet ministers - Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi - in the Narendra Modi-led government sparred over the issue of reservation on Saturday and sought each other's resignation.The controversy began after Hindustani Awam Morcha (Secular) president and Union minister Jitan Ram Manjhi's son, Santosh Kumar Suman, sought a review of the quota policy, backing the sub-categorisation of the Scheduled Castes (SCs) and the Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the reservation regime.âI think the purpose of reservation has not been served. The concept of creating the Mahadalit category with 18 of the 22 Dalit caste groups has been defeated due to the wide gap among the beneficiaries. The Extremely Backward Classes (EBC) category was created out of the other backward castes (OBCs), and the same was true for the concept of economically weaker sections (EWS) among the upper castes,â Suman had said.âHow can it be wrong to ask which sections have benefited from reservation and to what extent, and which people standing at the very bottom of the social ladder remain deprived of it? Why is no DM or SP from the Musahar community, which has 4 percent population in Bihar? A comparative study is needed.
Why will one section get 8 percent and another 80 percent among the beneficiaries?â he added.Chirag counters HAMThe remarks, however, did not sit well with another NDA ally, Chirag Paswan. The Union minister of food processing industries said that if Manjhi and his son want sub-quotas and a creamy layer within SC reservation, then the Union minister should resign."People ask, 'Why isn't there a 'creamy layer' provision?' Well, let them give it up, then - let them stop availing the benefits of reservation," Chirag said."If Jitan Ram Manjhi feels these measures should be implemented, should he not resign first? Let him introduce the 'creamy layer' concept - after all, he would fall under that category too, wouldn't he? He should resign, and his son - who is present here - should resign as well," he added.He also asserted that the basis of reservation lies in social factors and discussing it from an economic perspective "goes against the Constitution.""The basis is social - specifically, the issue of untouchability within society," he said.How Manjhi respondedLater in the day, Jitan Ram Manjhi slammed his cabinet colleague, accusing him of not caring about poor people."People will end up being deprived of the benefits of reservation because of this stance. However, we maintain that this division is essential in the broader public interest."Since he (Chirag) does not want to look after the interests of our poor people, he should resign," he added.SC-ST quota rowThe controversy stems from a 2024 Supreme Court judgment that allowed states to sub-classify Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) to ensure that the benefits of reservation reach the more backward groups within these categories.
It also asked governments to devise suitable criteria to bar the âcreamy layerâ among SCs and STs from availing reservation.The Centre, however, told the Supreme Court in an affidavit that the creamy layer principle cannot be extended to SCs and STs. It said the principle currently applies only to Other Backward Classes (OBCs)."It has nowhere specifically been held that the principle of creamy layer is applicable to SCs and STs. The reference made to the concept of creamy layerâ¦ appears to be the general observation with regard to reservation in respect of OBCs (Other Backward Classes)/SEBCs (Socially and Educationally Backward Classes)."

The development comes at a time when the reservation debate is back at the centre of politics amid anti-quota protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
The slugfest between the two Bihar leaders erupted earlier this week when Manjhi's HAM backed sub-quotas for SCs and STs within the existing reservation system. Manjhi's son and Bihar minister Santosh Kumar Suman said a review was needed to ensure that reservation benefits reach the most vulnerable and historically marginalised communities.
"We are not talking about ending reservation. We are talking about making reservation more just, effective and ensuring that it actually reaches those who are deprived," Suman said.
WHAT IS THE CONTROVERSY ABOUT?
Both Paswan's LJP (Ram Vilas) and HAM(S) are allies of the NDA in Bihar as well as at the Centre. Manjhi belongs to the Mushahar group, among the most backward Dalit groups.
The HAM has claimed that the benefits of Dalit reservation have remained concentrated among a few communities, including Paswans and Ravidas, while several other communities remain underrepresented. Suman has pointed out that not a single person from his Mushahar community has become an IAS officer.
The controversy has its roots in a 2024 Supreme Court judgment.
In a big verdict that year, the Supreme Court allowed states to sub-classify SCs and STs to ensure quota benefits to more backward castes in these groups.
Last month, a petition was filed in the Supreme Court demanding exclusion of socially and economically advanced individuals from reservation benefits. It argued that affluent families within the SC and ST categories were monopolising reservation benefits.
Citing the 2024 judgement, the plea said four of the seven judges on the Constitution bench suggested extending the creamy layer principle to these groups.
However, the Centre, in an affidavit before the Supreme Court, said the concept of creamy layer cannot be extended to SCs and STs. The principle has been applied only to OBCs.
'JITAN RAM MANJHI SHOULD RESIGN FIRST'
Countering HAM, Chirag Paswan asserted that if the party wanted sub-quotas and a creamy layer within SC reservation, then Manjhi and Suman, both being ministers, should resign.
"Those asking why there should not be a creamy layer should first give up the benefits of reservation. If Jitan Ram Manjhi believes in the creamy layer concept, he should first resign. His son should resign too," Paswan told reporters.
Paswan, whose party has always opposed sub-quotas, underlined that all communities within SCs have remained united. He said the Constitution does not provide for SC reservation to be determined on economic grounds.
Explaining his opposition, Paswan said introducing sub-quotas or a creamy layer within SC reservation could undermine the very purpose of social justice.
"Otherwise, the way society will be divided, the fight for social justice will lose its meaning. Dalits would continue to face discrimination," Paswan said.
"If they still want a creamy layer based on economic criteria, then he (Manjhi) should be the first to step aside," he further said.

headline: Red Fort blast: Delhi court takes cognisance of NIA’s 7,500-page chargesheet
full_text:
Red Fort blast: Delhi court takes cognisance of NIA’s 7,500-page chargesheet
The Red Fort blast took place on November 10 last year, wherein a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device exploded near the Lal Quila Metro Station
A Delhi court on Saturday took cognisance of the 7,500-page Red Fort bomb blast case chargesheet filed by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in May and fixed the matter for scrutiny of documents for September.
The cognisance was taken by Special Judge Prashant Sharma of Rouse Avenue Courts. A detailed order on cognisance is yet to be passed by the judge.
The Red Fort blast took place on November 10 last year, wherein a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device exploded near the Lal Quila Metro Station, killing at least 11 persons and injuring several others.
The explosion took place amidst a slow-moving traffic at the junction, causing wide-spread damage to nearby properties and vehicles.
Investigations later found that one Umar-un-Nabi, a doctor originally from Jammu and Kashmir, was allegedly inside the explosives-laden vehicle that detonated near the Red Fort.
A day later, the NIA registered a case under section 16 and 18 of Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and section 3 and 4 of the Explosive Substances Act.
Till December last year, the agency arrested nine persons for allegedly conspiring and providing technical and logistical support to Nabi to carry out the attack.
Also Read:Delhi HC denies default bail to Red Fort blast accused Jasir Bilal Wani
Some of the accused persons arrested in the blast case were allegedly linked to the Al-Falah University in Faridabad, where they either worked or taught.
NIA has so far filed two chargesheets before the court, which attributed the incident to a conspiracy, allegedly coined “Operation Heavenly Hind” that had purportedly been in preparation since 2022.
Last month, the NIA filed a supplementary chargesheet, naming three more persons, taking the total accused persons to 13.
The agency said that Nabi was the prime accused who masterminded the entire attack with a network of “radicalised individuals,” including doctors, facilitators and logistics provider, allegedly behind executing the terrorist blast.
The court has set the next date of hearing for September 9 when compliance under section 230 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which pertains to supply of chargesheet and other related documents to the accused, will take place.
The prosecution was represented by special public prosecutor Madhav Khurana and advocate Trisha Mittal.
The court last month allowed the NIA to dispose off the body parts of the Red Fort bomb blast deceased victims and alleged suicide bomber Nabi, with dignity and in line with their religious customs.
The court was ruling on an application moved by the federal agency, seeking to dispose off the body parts they collected from the spot of the bomb blast as part of case evidence.
The federal agency told the court that the body parts were gradually decomposing and were lying with the forensics unit.
The prosecution argued that their evidentiary value in the case had been adequately utilised through forensic analysis and hence, there was no need for further preservation.
The court order said, “The NIA should dispose off the biological body parts of the deceased and the accused with full human dignity and as per their religious belief.”

headline: AIMIM expels Telangana MLC Mirza Rahmath Baig; asks him to resign from post
full_text:
AIMIM expels Telangana MLC Mirza Rahmath Baig; asks him to resign from post
The party has not officially disclosed the grounds for Baig’s expulsion. It is also not immediately known whether he was served any prior notice
The All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) on Saturday expelled its Telangana state legislative council member Mirza Rahmat Baig with immediate effect and directed him to resign from his MLC post, amid allegations of sexual harassment on a minor girl.
In a post on the party’s X handle after midnight, AIMIM joint secretary SA Hussain Anwar announced: “Mirza Rahmath Baig has been expelled from AIMIM with immediate effect. He must immediately submit his resignation to the chairman of the legislative council,” he said.
The party, however, has not officially disclosed the grounds for Baig’s expulsion. It is also not immediately known whether he was served any prior notice or the action followed a specific complaint against him.
Baig represents the Hyderabad local authorities’ constituency in the Telangana legislative council and has nearly three years remaining in his current term. He could not be reached for his comment, as he is currently away on an Umrah pilgrimage.
Telangana legislative council chairman Gutha Sukhender Reddy said he did not receive Baig’s resignation. “I have not received any resignation from Rahmat Baig so far,” he said, adding that AIMIM leaders indicated that they would meet him on Friday evening but did not do so.
Also Read:AIMIM corporator held in TCS-linked BPO harassment case
The expulsion came a day after reports that Baig approached the Cyber Crime Police, alleging that unidentified persons were threatening and blackmailing him and demanding money by claiming they would release deepfake and morphed photographs and videos involving him. The police are investigating the complaint.
The contents of the alleged video have not been disclosed by the police, and neither the police nor AIMIM confirmed details circulating on social media. However, a party functionary, who refused to be quoted, said the video allegedly showed him with a minor girl.
Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Telangana president N Ramachander Rao demanded a comprehensive investigation into allegations of sexual harassment of a minor girl. In a statement, he said the allegations were “extremely serious” and warranted a thorough investigation.
He alleged that the issue was not a routine matter and that a deeper probe could potentially expose large-scale irregularities. He claimed that the allegations surfaced some time ago and questioned why action against Baig had been delayed.
“When such serious sexual harassment allegations have now surfaced, why are the Congress and BRS maintaining silence?” he asked.
Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) Hyderabad city unit president Nitin Nandekar demanded that AIMIM disclose the complete reasons for Baig’s expulsion. He alleged that Baig misused his position to intimidate local activists and municipal officials in the Goshamahal area.
Nandekar said the AIMIM leadership should not treat the episode as a routine resignation and insisted that the people of Goshamahal had a right to know the reasons behind the action and the former MLC’s conduct while in office.

headline: Kharge 'purification' row: Rahul demands FIR, BJP hits back with anti-Dalit jibe
full_text:
Kharge 'purification' row: Rahul demands FIR, BJP hits back with anti-Dalit jibe
Rahul Gandhi demanded an FIR over an alleged purification ritual after Mallikarjun Kharge's Haldwani rally, calling it untouchability. The BJP denied involvement, accused Congress of exploiting Dalits, and said religious groups performed the ritual after provocative slogans at the rally.
The row over an alleged purification ritual at the venue of Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge’s rally in Haldwani has taken a sharp political turn, with the BJP and the Congress trading allegations over discrimination against Dalits.
The confrontation intensified after Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi demanded an FIR under the SC/ST Act against those responsible. The BJP hit back, accusing Gandhi and the Congress of having an “anti-Dalit and feudal” mindset.
RAHUL GANDHI DEMANDS FIR
Addressing a press conference at the Congress headquarters on Saturday, Gandhi said the alleged ritual amounted to untouchability and reflected the “BJP-RSS mindset”. He claimed that no action had been taken even 20 days after the incident.
“The incident reflects the mindset of the BJP-RSS people who continue to practise untouchability. They do not want Dalits to progress, live with respect and become successful,” Gandhi said.
He asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi to ensure that a case was registered against those responsible.
Gandhi also accused Uttarakhand BJP president Mahendra Bhatt of defending the ritual and questioned Modi’s silence.
“PM Modi states that he belongs to every caste and is the prime minister of the country, but his party chief in Uttarakhand defends ‘shuddhikaran’,” he said.
Gandhi warned that the Congress would pursue action against those responsible even if the BJP governments at the Centre and in Uttarakhand failed to act.
BJP HITS BACK AT CONGRESS
The BJP accused the Congress of using Dalits for political gain and said Gandhi had no moral right to speak about their rights.
“Rahul Gandhi has no moral right to speak about Dalits. The Congress has only used Dalits for political benefit,” the party said.
The ruling party invoked the Congress’s treatment of BR Ambedkar and former Deputy Prime Minister Jagjivan Ram to question its record on Dalit rights.
“Babasaheb Ambedkar was conferred the Bharat Ratna only when a BJP-supported government was in power,” the party said.
The BJP also questioned why Kharge was not present in the room when Priyanka Gandhi Vadra filed her nomination papers for the 2024 Wayanad Lok Sabha bypoll.
Citing its government’s efforts over the past 12 years to honour Ambedkar and his legacy, the BJP said it did not need to prove its commitment to Dalits to the Congress.
WHAT HAPPENED IN HALDWANI
Kharge addressed a Congress rally in Haldwani on August 8. He alleged that BJP-RSS workers conducted a “shuddhikaran”, or purification ritual, at the venue two days later because he is a Dalit.
Kharge raised the issue in the Rajya Sabha on August 13. The Congress described the ritual as an act of untouchability and demanded action under the SC/ST Act.
“There were lakhs of people present at the time. I did not name any community or religion. I only spoke about the problems faced by the people there. But after my speech, BJP workers performed a havan,” Kharge had said.
However, Girish Chandra Pandey, the main organiser of the ritual, denied that it was linked to Kharge’s caste.
Pandey claimed that liquor bottles, paan stains, urine and wrappers had been found at the venue after the rally. He said the site was cleaned before a yajna was conducted to restore its sanctity.
“The purification ritual was performed to restore the sanctity of the place. We cleaned up the filth left behind on the stage and rendered the site fit for a yajna,” Pandey said.
He accused political parties of exploiting the event and said Gandhi did not have complete information about what had happened.
ROW WIDENS INTO BJP-CONGRESS CLASH
Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami denied the involvement of BJP workers in the ritual.
“No BJP worker was among those people who carried out the purification. But does anyone in Uttarakhand know what Mallikarjun Kharge’s caste is?” Dhami said.
He claimed that provocative religious slogans had been raised at the Congress rally and that some religious organisations conducted the purification programme in response.
Accusing Kharge of “lying”, senior BJP leader Ravi Shankar Prasad said the Modi government had respected Dalits, protected constitutional safeguards for reservation and introduced development programmes for the community.
The Congress, however, rejected the BJP’s defence and maintained that the ritual amounted to caste discrimination.
Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said describing the ritual as “shuddhikaran” or “safai” did not change the nature of the act.
“Performing a ‘purification’ ritual following the presence of a prominent Dalit leader is an act of untouchability,” Tharoor said.
Congress leader Jairam Ramesh alleged that such incidents repeatedly occurred in BJP-ruled states because those responsible enjoyed the support of the top leadership.
“Such audacity only comes when there’s backing from the top. Otherwise, what is the reason for such incidents recurring repeatedly in BJP-ruled states?” Ramesh said.

headline: 'Congress misleading Dalit community': BJP rejects Rahul's claim of Kharge's insult in Haldwani purification ritual
full_text:
'Congress misleading Dalit community': BJP rejects Rahul's claim of Kharge's insult in Haldwani purification ritual
Uttarakhand minister Khajan Das said BJP had no connection with the incident and accused the Congress of “attempting to mislead” the Dalit community.
The Bharatiya Janata Party on Saturday dismissed Congress's claims of a “purification” ritual being held at Ramlila Ground in Uttarakhand's Haldwani after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge addressed a public meeting there.
Uttarakhand minister and BJP leader Khajan Das said the party had no connection with the incident and accused the Congress of “attempting to mislead” the Dalit community, ANI news agency reported.
The controversy erupted after Kharge addressed a Congress rally at Ramlila Maidan in Haldwani on August 8. Members of a right-wing group later reportedly conducted a purification ritual at the ground, which was criticised by the leaders of Congress party.
Rahul asks PM to order FIR over purification row
Congress MP and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi earlier today demanded that Prime Minister Narendra Modi order an FIR to be filed against those involved in the “shuddhikaran” or purification of the Ramlila ground. Rahul further played a purported video showing the BJP’s Uttarakhand chief supporting shuddhikaran, and sought “justice” for the Congress president.
Kharge had, at the Congress Working Committee meeting on August 19, raised the issue of the purification ritual and lamented that some party leaders didn’t take it up, according to an earlier HT report.
‘BJP has nothing to do with it…’: What Uttarakhand minister said
Uttarakhand minister Das said there was no intention to insult Kharge, while adding that the BJP completely disassociated itself from the incident. “I wish to state that there was no such intention; the Bharatiya Janata Party dissociates itself from this entirely. The BJP has nothing to do with it,” ANI cited Das saying.
He further alleged that the Congress was “spreading rumours and attempting to mislead the Dalit community”. The Uttarakhand minister further stated that if an organisation had conducted a “havan” or purification ritual at the Ramlila Ground, “that is their own affair.”
“However, spreading such misinformation is not right,” Das said.
‘Shows the BJP and RSS’ mindset’: Rahul
While demanding for an FIR to be filed against those who had conducted the ritual, Rahul claimed that the BJP's Uttarakhand unit chief had said that “shuddhikaran was the right thing to do.” He said this was an “illegal act.”
“This shows the BJP and RSS’ mindset. They don’t want a Dalit to become prosperous and live respectfully,” Rahul said, while urging PM Modi to order an FIR under the SC/ST act. The Scheduled Castes and Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act came into force in 1995 to prevent atrocities and violence against the vulnerable sections. It has been amended to impose stricter punishment.
Also Read | BJP leader slams Rahul Gandhi's remarks on Manusmriti, files complaint
“We are not asking for anything impossible. According to the Constitution this is a crime. We are seeking justice for the Congress president,” the Lok Sabha LoP asserted. Rahul also raised a larger question of atrocities and violence faced by Dalits in India, and pointed to how Dalit students are made to clean toilets in schools and barred from drinking water from the village well or in tea shops.
He alleged that a shuddhikaran had followed after Union minister Jitin Ram Majhi visited a temple. “This is done by the BJP and RSS and this is a crime according to the Constitution. Shuddhikaran is another name for untouchability. Which is illegal but BJP practises it,” Rahul alleged.

A special court on Saturday (August 29, 2026) has taken cognisance of a chargesheet filed by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in connection with the explosion near Red Fort in New Delhi on November 10, 2025 which killed 14 people and injured dozens.
According to the NIA’s 7,500-page chargesheet, filed in May, the explosion was allegedly orchestrated by a terror module led by a group of doctors who had been searching for a suicide bomber for nearly a year. Dr. Umar-un-Nabi, named as the prime accused, allegedly drove the explosives-laden vehicle that detonated in the national capital.
The probe
The agency subsequently arrested 11 people accused of facilitating the attack by providing logistical support, sheltering suspects and attempting to destroy evidence. It is alleged that the accused had links to Ansar Ghazwat-ul-Hind, an organisation the NIA has described as an offshoot of Al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent.
In July, a supplementary chargesheet was also filed against three more accused, including an absconding paediatrician alleged to be a founding member of the terror module. With this, the number of people chargesheeted in the case has risen to 13.
The matter is scheduled for next hearing on September 9.

headline: Three mobile phones, Wi-Fi equipment, and ₹31,000 in cash were seized from the cell of Aftab Ahmed Ansari, the mastermind of the 2002 American Centre attack in Kolkata, who is serving a life term at the Presidency Correctional Home, officials said on...
full_text:
Three mobile phones, Wi-Fi equipment, and ₹31,000 in cash were seized from the cell of Aftab Ahmed Ansari, the mastermind of the 2002 American Centre attack in Kolkata, who is serving a life term at the Presidency Correctional Home, officials said on Saturday (August 29, 2026).
Senior officials from the West Bengal correctional services said the items were seized during a surprise search operation at the Presidency jail on August 23, following intelligence inputs that Ansari was allegedly using a mobile phone and had internet access.
“Three smartphones including an iPhone, three SIM cards, two routers, a Wi-Fi hotspot device, a pen drive, an OTG adapter, and wireless earbuds are among the electronic communication devices seized by our staff,” a senior officer said, adding that an investigation is underway to probe the potential involvement of jail staff.
The jail authority has lodged a case against Ansari at the Hastings police station. Investigators are also attempting to ascertain whether phone calls were made to Ansari’s contacts outside the country.
American centre attack
Ansari was a key member of the Dubai-based Asif Reza Commando Force, a wing of the Pakistan-based terrorist group Harkat-ul-Jehad-i-Islami. He was sentenced to life imprisonment in 2014 for the January 22, 2002, attack outside the American Centre in Kolkata, where two motorcycle-borne gunmen used AK-47 rifles to kill five police personnel and injure 20 others.
Saturday’s development follows the suspension of the superintendent of the Presidency jail, M. Kajur, and the chief controller, Dipta Gharai, by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on May 15. The suspensions occurred after a police search recovered 23 mobile phones and over 30 SIM cards allegedly used illegally by inmates.
