headline: ‘Memoir or fiction?’: BJP targets Sonia Gandhi’s book as Congress alleges govt pressure
full_text:
‘Memoir or fiction?’: BJP targets Sonia Gandhi’s book as Congress alleges govt pressure
Penguin Random House India clarified it is not publishing Sonia Gandhi's memoir, ‘Belonging.’
Penguin Random House India's decision not to publish Sonia Gandhi’s memoir in India has triggered a political slugfest between the BJP and Congress. While Congress has alleged “pressure” from the government and a “threat to freedom of expression”, BJP has challenged the claims and questioned the contents of the book.
BJP leader Mukhtar Abbas Naqvi said, “Whether the book written by Sonia Gandhi is a memoir or fiction is a matter to be decided between the author and the publisher. If a work labelled as a memoir turns out to be fiction, the publisher will certainly assess that before making a decision. I feel that if you attempt to politicise a work presented as a memoir, questions will inevitably be raised.”
Gandhi’s book deal with Penguin Random House India fell through after she refused to make changes or deletions of references to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)’s ideological fount, and Chinese intrusions, HT reported earlier.
Deep Dive
BJP National Spokesperson CR Kesavan said, “The attempts by Congress leaders to spin stories and manufacture a false narrative of fear over the release of Smt. Sonia Gandhi’s memoir are not merely ironic, they are glaringly hypocritical.”
Also Read: Exclusive: Penguin India sought cuts to Modi, RSS, China portions in Sonia Gandhi's memoir
Citing the late K Natwar Singh’s 2014 autobiography One Life Is Not Enough, Kesavan said excerpts from the book “clearly states how uneasy and uncomfortable the Nehru-Gandhi family was about his account of certain events in May 2004, before the UPA Government was sworn in.”
He said, “Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra decided to meet him before his book release to discuss it, this sudden visit coming after eight and a half years! Why was Sonia Gandhi so apprehensive about what Shri. Natwar Singh would write in his book?”
Drawing a parallel with the current controversy, Kesavan asked, “The moot point in the context of Smt. Sonia Gandhi’s memoirs is: which portions of her memoir warranted fact-checking and why so?”
He added, “For Congress leaders who are farcically saying that some are afraid of the memoirs contents, they should explain to the nation the real reason why the Congress first family is nervous and jittery to make public the 51 carton boxes of Nehru’s correspondence, which include his letters to Edwina Mountbatten.”
Congress alleges pressure
Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi said, “Penguin India is more than happy to publish ‘Exam Warriors’ and several books on RSS. No doubt there are those in the BJP government who have now become afraid of a book being being read by the people of India.”
Congress MP Dr Akhilesh Prasad Singh said, “It is clear that no publisher, whether Penguin or anyone else, can influence an author or pressure them to remove or include specific content. That is evident, and perhaps that is why Sonia Gandhi declined as well. We all understand the reason behind this.”
He added, “During the previous session of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, Rahul Gandhi himself raised the issue regarding Naravane’s book, which was effectively being suppressed, prevented from being read, by the government; it is likely the same kind of pressure at play here. That is why this is happening.”
Rajasthan Congress leader Ashok Gehlot said, “Penguin Worldwide is ready to publish Smt. Sonia Gandhi ji's upcoming book worldwide in its original form, but Penguin Random House India wants changes made to launch it in India. After all, what is the reason or what pressure is there that what is being published across the world cannot be published in India?”
Gehlot said Sonia Gandhi’s life was “an example of sacrifice and dedication” and that “the integrity and dignity with which she has served the country is exemplary.”
He added, “Suppressing the book of Smt. Sonia Gandhi ji, a person of such stature, a senior leader of the nation, and former Leader of the Opposition, under pressure is tantamount to the murder of freedom of expression.”
“The real issue is that pressure was put on Penguin India to remove the portions related to Modi, the RSS, and the occupation of Indian territory by China during Modi's rule. This is the murder of democracy,” Gehlot alleged.
“Why is this truth being hidden from the people of India? Will the Modi government alter even the facts by pressuring publishers?” he asked.
Also Read: Penguin India says never wanted to drop Sonia Gandhi's memoir: ‘Was willing and keen’
What Penguin said
Penguin Random House India on Friday said it had been “keen to publish” Sonia Gandhi’s memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love throughout “the relevant discussions” but said it was its “prerogative and responsibility” to fact-check authors.
The company clarified that it is not the publisher of the book in India, days after American publisher Alfred A Knopf, an imprint of Penguin Random House, announced that Belonging would release on November 10.
The statement came after a report in The Indian Express claimed that the publisher backed out after Gandhi refused “editorial changes” to the manuscript.
“Penguin Random House India is not the publisher of Belonging in India. Any suggestion that Penguin Random House India decided not to publish Belonging because the author declined editorial changes does not accurately reflect the circumstances,” the company said.
“As a publisher, it is both our prerogative and our responsibility to fact check and provide authors with recommendations that are in the best interests of their books. This is a normal part of the publishing process. Throughout the relevant discussions, Penguin Random House India's position was that we remained willing and keen to publish the book,” it said.
The company added that it would not comment further on “confidential discussions with the author”.

headline: New Delhi/Gurugram: Three BJP MPs were reprimanded by party chief Nitin Nabin for visiting the family of former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar, who was convicted in a 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, to offer their condolences on his death.
full_text:
New Delhi/Gurugram: Three BJP MPs were reprimanded by party chief Nitin Nabin for visiting the family of former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar, who was convicted in a 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, to offer their condolences on his death.
Kamaljeet Sehrawat, Ramvir Singh Bidhuri and Yogender Chandolia visited Kumar’s residence and met members of his family.
The BJP has found itself in a bind as the gesture is in sharp contrast over its long-held position on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. On Friday, it had termed the visit by the three leaders as a personal one.
Kumar was convicted in the 1984 anti-Sikh riots case and was serving two life terms for his role in the riots. He died on 20 August in New Delhi at the age of 80. With the Punjab elections all set to take place next year, the visit has the capacity to snowball into a major controversy, party leaders told ThePrint.
ThePrint reached out to Chandolia, Sehrawat and Bidhuri for a comment and the report will be updated once they respond.
According to sources, H.S.Phoolka, advocate and former Member of the Punjab Assembly, expressed his strong displeasure on the visit of the BJP MPs.
“Strongly condemn visit of 3 MP’s Kamaljeet Sehrawat, Ramvir Singh Bidhuri and Yogender Chandolia to mass murderer Sajjan Kumar’s residence to offer condolences on his death,” Phoolka had posted on X on August 28.
“This when #BJP has always supported our quest for justice against this culprits and supported us in ensuring that he stays in Jail. Sympathy should be reserved for victims and their families-many of whom live the horror of those days even till now. I call for the boycott of these 3 MPs.”
According to sources, the central leadership of the party is quite upset especially as it comes months before the Punjab elections. Sources within the party said that Nabin expressed displeasure over the visit.
“It seems like the three acted on their own without the party’s approval. With the Punjab elections just around the corner, this may snowball into a major issue. The party is mindful of that and which is why the three leaders were summoned,” said a senior party leader.
Phoolka reacted to the action taken by Nabin. “Greateful to @NitinNabin ji for taking a strong stance on the issue. This is what leadership should look like, as opposed to the hypocrisy of the Congress all these years. BJP has fought for this issue as their own for 40 years, starting from ……..#1984SikhGenocide,” he posted.
Kumar was a towering leader within the Jat community that has significant electoral and political power across rural Haryana as well as Delhi.
He represented the erstwhile Outer Delhi Lok Sabha constituency multiple times/ The South, West and North-West Delhi Parliamentary constituencies were carved out of this seat. “Naturally the BJP MPs felt the need to at least offer their condolences as it is culturally important for the segment,” said a leader.
The three BJP leaders who visited Kumar’s residence belong to these three constituencies. While Kamaljeet Sehrawat represent West Delhi parliamentary constituency, Bidhuri is the MP from South Delhi and Chandolia from North West Delhi.
After West Bengal, the BJP has set its eyes on Punjab where it will contest all 117 Assembly seats in the upcoming elections.
BJP general secretary (organisation) B.L.Santosh, who was on a two-day visit to the state to review organisation work, expressed confidence of BJP doing well.
Recently Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda’s remarks on Kumar’s death had put him in the middle of a controversy. The BJP MPs’ visit has added another layer to the row.
The three were present at Kumar’s final bhog ceremony.
“In our Haryanvi society, and the outer Delhi area shares the same culture, it is considered important for political leaders to visit a family whenever there is a death, to do ‘mokhan‘, to offer condolences,” the above-mentioned leader said.
“I remember people whose ‘mokhan‘ I missed telling me to my face that I did not even bother to come when someone in their family died. In our times, a political leader could skip a wedding in his constituency, but he did not dare skip a ‘mokhan‘.”
Hooda had also drawn sharp criticism from the Sikh community and from within his own party.
A senior political leader told The Print that there was no doubt Deepender’s father Bhupinder Singh Hooda had a close association with Sajjan Kumar, who was a frequent visitor to the senior Hooda’s Delhi residence during his years as Haryana chief minister.
The leader said that even after Sajjan Kumar could not contest elections because of his case, and his brother Ramesh Kumar became MP from the seat between 2009 and 2014, the family too enjoyed proximity with Hooda and with several other Jat leaders from Haryana.
It is this old association, and not any recent political calculation, that explains why the Hoodas found themselves under the scanner the moment Sajjan Kumar died, the leader said.
BJP national spokesperson and Sikh leader R.P.Singh said that the three MPs should have avoided the visit and that they have been reprimanded by the top brass is in line with the BJP’s ideology.
“Rajniti se badi samaaj niti hoti hai (Social policy is greater than politics). I had pointed out that they should not have gone in the first place. Kumar was convicted in the carnage which claimed thousands of lives. It is because of PM Modi that the SIT was formed in 2015 to reinvestigate the closed cases related to the riots,” he told ThePrint.

headline: New Delhi: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi Saturday stepped up his attack on the BJP and RSS over the ‘shuddhikaran’ performed at Haldwani’s Ramlila Maidan after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge addressed a ral...
full_text:
New Delhi: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi Saturday stepped up his attack on the BJP and RSS over the ‘shuddhikaran’ performed at Haldwani’s Ramlila Maidan after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge addressed a rally there, calling it an act of untouchability and demanding an FIR under the SC/ST Act.
“This is a crime. According to the Constitution of India, this is a crime,” Gandhi said at a press conference Saturday afternoon.
Kharge had addressed the Congress’s ‘Vijay Shankhnaad’ rally at the Ramlila Maidan in Haldwani on 8 August. The Congress has objected to the purification ritual at the venue two days later. Gandhi also referred to remarks by Uttarakhand BJP president Mahendra Bhatt defending the exercise.
“Who does this? Only BJP and RSS people do this,” Gandhi said.
He said the Congress wanted those responsible to face legal action. “Our demand is that, as soon as possible, an FIR should be registered in Uttarakhand against the people who carried out the purification,” Gandhi said.
Gandhi said the incident should not be viewed merely as an issue concerning the Congress president, but as an example of the discrimination faced by Dalits.
“This is not Kharge ji’s issue. This is the issue of every Dalit person in India, from the smallest child to the oldest person,” he said.
He also referred to other instances involving Dalit leaders. “Here, our Rajasthan CLP people go to temples, BJP leaders carry out purification. And an example from their party—Bihar Chief Minister Manjhi ji, he goes to a temple, and there too purification takes place,” Gandhi said.
Rahul Gandhi linked the Haldwani episode to an alleged wider pattern of caste discrimination, citing the treatment of Dalit children in schools, restrictions on access to water and separate cups at tea stalls.
“Even today, in schools, Dalit children are made to clean toilets. They are made to sweep and mop. At wells, Dalits are not allowed to drink water,” he said.
“At tea shops, look at this, two kinds of cups are used. One is a glass cup, a reusable cup, which can be washed. And the other is a paper or plastic cup, which is thrown away,” Gandhi said. “The plastic one, the paper one is for Dalits, and the glass one is for other people.”
He also spoke about attacks on Dalits during wedding processions.
“And finally, on the wedding day, which should be a day of happiness, thousands of Dalits in India, when they ride horses and go in the wedding procession, they go wearing helmets. Stones are thrown at them, they are attacked, threatened, beaten,” he said.
“The louder the voice, the more successful the Dalit person is, the more strongly he is attacked,” Gandhi added.
Gandhi described the political contest in the country as a fight between two competing ideologies.
“Look, there is a fight going on in the country between two ideologies. One is the Constitution of India; Ambedkar ji’s Constitution, Gandhi ji’s, Jawaharlal Nehru ji’s, Sardar Patel ji’s Constitution. And the second is the ideology of the BJP and RSS,” he said.
He said the purification at Haldwani reflected what he described as the BJP-RSS mindset towards Dalits.
“They do not want Dalits of this country to progress. They do not want Dalits of this country to live with respect and be successful,” Gandhi said.
The controversy had already spilled into Parliament 13 August, when Kharge raised the Haldwani incident in the Rajya Sabha. Kharge said a ‘havan’ had been performed at the Ramlila Maidan after his rally and spoke of the pain and humiliation caused by the alleged ‘shuddhikaran’ of the venue.
BJP president J. P. Nadda, responding to Kharge, said the BJP did not support such practices and that the matter would be looked into, with action to follow if anyone was found responsible for the ‘shuddhikaran’.
The issue subsequently took a sharper political turn after Uttarakhand BJP president Mahendra Bhatt defended the ritual, saying the venue had been “defiled” by slogans.
Rahul Gandhi said the Congress would pursue action against those responsible for the ‘shuddhikaran’ even if the BJP did not act.
“Even if BJP doesn’t do it, we are going to get it. He is not going to escape. I guarantee you, the entire Congress Party is not going to let that man escape,” he said.
“We have taken a decision that we want our President to get justice in Uttarakhand,” he added
“Our issue is that the Congress President should get justice,” Gandhi reiterated.

NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on slammed the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA), warning of contempt action against officials after the department refused to lift the suspension of food licences of five restaurants at the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) premises despite a fresh inspection finding them 88% compliant with food safety rules.âTired of scolding the department and officers,â the division bench of Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad said the FDA had taken a âpedantic instead of pragmatic viewâ despite the courtâs earlier direction to reconsider the matter. Accepting the undertaking, the court said the restaurants could reopen since the latest inspection had found them compliant. âThere is no provision in the law that prohibits the same,â the bench observed.The court recalled that it had, during the previous hearing, specifically directed FDA officials to apply their minds and take a pragmatic approach to the licence issue.âHowever, despite clearly saying this, the FDA has disobeyed our order and taken a pedantic view instead of a pragmatic view. headline: NEW DELHI: Zurich Airport has prepared itself for a longer takeoff roll at Noida Airport before the traffic here takes off. Multiple factors like the last-minute pullout by on of the three launch airlines; Delhi's IGI Airport operating way below its ...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Zurich Airport has prepared itself for a longer takeoff roll at Noida Airport before the traffic here takes off. Multiple factors like the last-minute pullout by on of the three launch airlines; Delhi's IGI Airport operating way below its existing and still expandable capacity and Noida International Airport's (NIA) connectivity woes with Delhi have meant a much lower than originally expected air traffic at the new hub that stated operations on June 15. Zurich Airport International AG is NIA's primary developer and concessionaire.Zurich Airport has said in its outlook for NIA: "Slower ramp up expected due to challenging geo political environment with near time performance remaining subject to elevated uncertainty. Route network will continue to expand with international services expected to follow. Strong confidence in the long term growth potential and attractive fundamentals of the Indian aviation market."It said NIA saw 104 flights and 25,000 passengers in June. This rose to 1,044 flights and 77,000 passengers in July. The airport's HY 16 EBIDTA loss is estimated about $3 million.IndiGo is the biggest operator at NIA, with Akasa having a few flights. Air India Express, which was to be the third launch airlines, had pulled out due to mounting losses of AI group. Setting up a new base means incurring significant expense, something AI wanted to avoid at this time.
The going was never going to be easy for NIA, the first second airport to open in an Indian urban conglomerate without either the pre-existing hub operating to capacity (like Mumbai CSMIA); being constrained (like Goa Dabolim) or the older one shutting down (like Bengaluru HAL, Hyderabad Begumpet and Visakhapatnam when Bhogapuram opens in a couple of months). The new airports in Hyderabad and Bengaluru are almost as far as Delhiites find NIA to be but travellers simply didnât have any option but to trudge the distance. Delhi, Gurgaon, Noida and Ghaziabad, however, have an option thatâs closer, better connected and more affordable multi modal transport.When it was coming up amid the boom post Covid boom in air travel, NIA was expected to have a tough time till 2030 when IGIA was to saturate by reaching its peak capacity of about 13-14 crore passengers annually (CPA). IGIA currently has a capacity of 11 CPA and handled less than 8 crore passengers last year.
Delhi Airport handles about 1,300 flights daily, way short of the 1,550 seen during the heady days of G20.So NIA would have to compete to get traffic with peak traffic hour slot availability being its USP to attract airlines. But it opened at a time when Indian carriers are reeling under the triple impact of finding lucrative western routes become unviable for them due to closure of Pakistan airspace for them since last April, US-Iran war sending oil prices flaring and the rupee weakening. As a result, they are cutting flights.

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Saturday attacked the Bharatiya Janata Party and Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh over a recent 'suddhikaran' or 'purification' ritual held at a venue in Uttarakhand where Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge had addressed a rally.Calling the practice "another name for untouchability", Rahul alleged that such an act was a crime under the Constitution.Addressing a presser at Congress headquarters in Delhi, the Rae Bareli MP said the country was witnessing a political contest between the ideology of the Constitution and that of the BJP and RSS.
"Our CLP leader in Rajasthan visits a temple, and BJP leaders perform a 'purification' ritual. Congress President Kharge ji, who has dedicated his entire life to the country and the Constitution, goes to the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani to deliver a speech, and a purification ritual is performed there. Who does this? It is the people from the BJP and RSS," Rahul said.
"Only BJP and RSS members do this, and it is a crime. Under India's Constitution, this is a crime, a criminal activity. 'Purification' is actually just another name for untouchability. Untouchability was outlawed, yet BJP members practice it openly," he added.Former Congress president said the ritual suggested that Dalits were "unclean" and should not be touched.
"When they perform this purification, they are effectively saying that Dalits should not be touched, that Dalits are unclean, and this constitutes a crime under the Indian Constitution," he said.Rahul also said the larger political contest in the country was between two opposing ideologies."A fight is under way in the country between two ideologies. The politics currently playing out in India is between these two ideologies," Rahul said.He also spoke about alleged caste-based discrimination and said Dalits continue to face discrimination despite constitutional safeguards."For thousands of years, Dalits in this country have been subjected to atrocities and violence. While the Constitution made this illegal, even today, Dalit children in schools are made to clean toilets and sweep and mop floors," he said."Just think about the impact this has on the minds of the future generation: children see some of their peers sweeping, while those doing the sweeping see others who do not have to do so. The plastic or paper cups are for Dalits, while the glass ones are for others," he alleged."This is the reality of India. This is the reality of Uttar Pradesh, the reality of North India, and you can see this in cities and villages," Rahul added.
The Haldwani controversy relates to a Congress rally held at Ramlila Maidan on August 8, ahead of the 2027 Uttarakhand assembly elections. Members of a right-wing group later performed a purification ritual at the venue, drawing criticism from Congress leaders.

headline: Over 17 days after tribal students began a hunger strike in different parts of Maharashtra, the State Government on Saturday (August 29, 2026) accepted all their demands. A delegation of tribal students walked out of Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis’...

Over 17 days after tribal students began a hunger strike in different parts of Maharashtra, the State Government on Saturday (August 29, 2026) accepted all their demands. A delegation of tribal students walked out of Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis’ residence, ‘Varsha,’ on Saturday (August 29) afternoon, stating that they were satisfied with the meeting after the government provided them with a time-bound schedule for implementing key demands, including the pending recruitment for 12,500 positions for tribals.
“We thank Rahul Gandhi, Rohit Pawar, Yashomati Thakur, and other leaders. This was the first time that the tribal students’ demands were heard on a national platform,” said tribal students’ leader Suraj Iccharam Kokani.
Tribal Affairs Minister Ashok Uike met with the protesting students late at night on Saturday (August 29) to present a copy of the written assurances. The students subsequently announced the suspension of their agitation, stating that they would resume it if their demands were not fulfilled within the given time frame. The Minister then offered juice to the protesting students.
Elaborating on the demands accepted by the government, he said that the students were assured that their demands would be fulfilled in three months. “As per the directions of the Supreme Court, we will complete the recruitment drive. In three months, the number of vacancies will be ascertained. In the next three months, recruitment to those positions will take place. The recruitment under PESA will also be done. For the safety and security of ashram shaalas (residential tribal schools), measures will be taken after the third party audit,” he said.
Government officials told The Hindu that an independent recruitment drive will be held if needed to adhere to the timeline of six months for filling up the positions. This was the main demand of the protesting students.
The meeting held by the Chief Minister was attended by seven student representatives from Nagpur, Pune, and Nandurbar. Students had been protesting for over 14 demands, including better infrastructure in tribal schools and hostels, the completion of pending recruitment drives, and the uploading of caste validity committees’ judgments on the website, among others. Officials stated that they had provided the students with written assurances, along with a timeline. The students said they received a copy of two new GRs regarding their demands.
The other key demand was action against bogus adivasis who had claimed government jobs on fake tribal certificates. The Chief Minister said that action against such bogus job-holders will start immediately. “As per the government rule, those selected for government jobs under the ST category have to submit their caste validity certificates within six months. But despite failure to do so, no action has been taken against them for 10 years,” said Mr. Kokani.
The government gave written assurance to the students about the safety and security measures in tribal residential schools to address the infrastructure gaps in them, starting hostel mess in the next three months and stopping the DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) allowance for food, a study of their demand for rise in fund allocation, plugging the loopholes in the central kitchen system and reviewing the existing schools under the scheme to draw tenders for clusters in a scientific way to avoid logistic challenges, new SOPs for the administration of the private aided ashram schools, expansion of SWAYAM scheme which will now be applicable for all courses for 11th standard students at taluka level too. The government also said that it will ensure that candidates produce their caste validity certificates before receiving their final appointment letters in the future.

headline: SC to hear plea seeking mandatory disclosure of ethanol content in petrol on Aug 31
full_text:
SC to hear plea seeking mandatory disclosure of ethanol content in petrol on Aug 31
New Delhi, The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear a petition on August 31 seeking a directive to the Centre and others to ensure mandatory and uniform labelling on every dispensing nozzle at petrol pumps, disclosing the exact percentage of ethanol in petrol.
According to the apex court's causelist of August 31, the plea would come up for hearing before a bench comprising Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale.
The petition, filed by Narendra Kumar Goswami, has also sought a direction that every fuel invoice should specifically and legibly state the percentage of ethanol in the petrol sold.
"Direct the respondents to prepare and publish within a stipulated time an official, public, vehicle-wise compatibility database searchable by manufacturer, model, engine type and year of manufacture, indicating the suitability or otherwise of various ethanol blends for each vehicle," the plea said.
It has also sought constitution of an independent expert committee comprising representatives from the ministries of petroleum and natural gas, road transport and highways, the Bureau of Indian Standards and others, including independent automobile engineers, to examine and submit a public report on real-world vehicle compatibility of E20 across the existing fleet.
The plea said the committee should also submit a report on the impact on fuel efficiency, engine longevity and maintenance costs, warranty and insurance implications, the net environmental footprint, including tail-pipe emissions and water consumption associated with ethanol production, and food-security and feed-diversion concerns allegedly arising from the blending programme.
"Direct the respondents to frame a national consumer disclosure protocol for all ethanol-blended petrol, in consultation with the Central Consumer Protection Authority and the Bureau of Indian Standards," it said.
It also sought directions to the concerned authorities to place before the apex court all policy files, technical studies, compatibility reports, safety standards, consumer advisories and records of public consultation that support the compulsory roll-out of E20.
The plea called on authorities to formulate and publish within a time-bound period a transparent transition framework for legacy and non-compatible vehicles, including consideration of designated availability of lower ethanol petrol wherever technically, economically and logistically feasible, together with a reasoned decision supported by expert material and public consultation.

headline: A drone suspected to be from Pakistan was spotted hovering over forward areas along the Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch district, prompting security forces to launch a search operation in the area early Saturday, officials said.
full_text:
A drone suspected to be from Pakistan was spotted hovering over forward areas along the Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch district, prompting security forces to launch a search operation in the area early Saturday, officials said.
The drone was spotted in the Behrooti village area of Balakote in the Mendhar sector late Friday (August 28, 2026) evening, and it moved towards the Mangalnar-Dabrote side near the border before returning to Pakistan, the officials said.
They said Army troops guarding the LoC intensified surveillance and launched a search operation at first light to determine whether it had dropped or carried any suspicious material.
Officials further said that the search operation is still underway and added that security forces remained on heightened alert along the border.
At the same time, police, along with Army and paramilitary forces, have been engaging in a massive search operation in the vast forested districts of Udhampur, Kathua and Rajouri following information about suspicious movement, they added.
According to officials, the joint search operation took place at Khuban, Nagain, Khtrail, Godu Falal, Padetar, Chor Mottu, Kia, Kheba, Bhed, Marta, Joffar, and the adjoining areas in the Udhampur-Kathua forest belt on Friday (August 28) evening and is still underway.
In Rajouri, another search operation was launched in Gaibas, Mithiyani, Mogla and Narla after villagers informed about the movement of two suspected armed persons, believed to be terrorists.
Officials said there have been no contact with any suspected persons so far.

headline: In the wake of the devastating flash flood that severely impacted Nepal’s power infrastructure, Kathmandu has asked India to give the requisite approvals for the transmission of electricity to Nepal earlier than usual, senior officials in the Union P...
full_text:
In the wake of the devastating flash flood that severely impacted Nepal’s power infrastructure, Kathmandu has asked India to give the requisite approvals for the transmission of electricity to Nepal earlier than usual, senior officials in the Union Power Ministry said on Saturday (August 29, 2026).
“Nepal has asked that India advance import approvals, starting from September this year, in view of the generation deficits caused by this disaster. The concerned authorities are processing the requests,” an official said. According to officials, India is willing to provide any additional power that Nepal may need.
Nepal usually imports electricity from India during the winter months, starting around October, as power generation is typically low in the Himalayan country during the freezing winter months. Conversely, the country exports its excess hydropower to India during the summer. According to official data, India imported 3,299 million units (MUs) of power from Nepal in fiscal year 2025-26 and exported 1,451 MUs to it.
Transmission of electricity across India’s borders requires mandatory clearances from the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), among others.
India ‘capable of absorbing shortfall’
According to an internal assessment, Nepal’s electricity generation capacity has declined by about 550 megawatts because of the infrastructural damage induced by the flood.
Officials said that this resulted in the cross-border power flow to India reducing by approximately 400 MW from earlier peaks of 950 MW to 1,000 MW. However, the officials assured that India was not foreseeing any requirement to make alternative arrangements to compensate for the shortfall.
“We do not foresee any requirement for exceptional emergency procurement or alternative arrangement to balance domestic demand,” an official said, adding, “India’s vast national grid capacity and robust generation reserve margins are capable of absorbing a temporary shortfall of 400 MW seamlessly without disrupting grid stability or retail supply."
The flash flood in the Nepal-Tibet border regions has killed about 675 people, authorities in Nepal said on Saturday. The country’s meteorology department has, meanwhile, warned of fresh rainfall and thunderstorms in the affected areas.

headline: This is BJP-RSS mindset: Rahul Gandhi slams 'shuddhikaran' after Kharge event
full_text:
This is BJP-RSS mindset: Rahul Gandhi slams 'shuddhikaran' after Kharge event
Rahul Gandhi hits out at BJP and RSS over the 'shuddhikaran' (purification) ceremony held at Mallikarjun Kharge's Haldwani rally venue, calling it a "crime" and saying an FIR under the SC/ST Act should be registered against those responsible.
Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday launched a blistering attack on the BJP and RSS over an alleged ‘shuddhikaran’ (purification) ritual held at the site of party president Mallikarjun Kharge’s rally in Uttarakhand’s Haldwani, calling it “another name for untouchability” and demanding action under the SC/ST Act.
Addressing a press conference at Indira Bhavan in Delhi, Gandhi said the incident exposed what he described as the “BJP-RSS mindset” towards Dalits and accused the ruling establishment of remaining silent despite what he called a criminal act.
“This act violates the SC/ST Act. Performing a ‘purification’ ritual is a crime. Yet, no action has been taken. Therefore, we demand that an FIR be registered immediately against those who carried out this purification ritual in Uttarakhand,” Gandhi said.
The controversy erupted after an alleged purification ceremony was held at Haldwani’s Ramlila Ground following Kharge’s August 8 Congress rally. Uttarakhand Congress chief Ganesh Godiyal had alleged that the Shri Ram Sena carried out the ritual because Kharge is a Dalit and asked police to examine whether any law was violated.
Gandhi said the incident was not merely about Kharge but reflected the discrimination faced by Dalits across the country. “Purification is actually just another name for untouchability. Untouchability was outlawed, yet BJP members practise it openly,” he alleged.
He said the message conveyed by such an act was that Dalits were “unclean” and should not be touched.
Gandhi then widened his attack, asking what such discrimination could mean for Dalit children if a senior leader such as Kharge could be subjected to it.
“If such a thing can be done against a senior person like Mallikarjun Kharge, imagine what can be done to a four-year-old in a school,” he said.
He cited alleged instances of Dalit children being made to clean toilets, sweep floors and perform other menial tasks in schools. He also referred to discrimination at village wells and tea stalls, claiming Dalits in some places are served disposable cups while others are given reusable glasses.
“This is the reality of India. This is the reality of Uttar Pradesh, the reality of North India, and you can see this in cities and villages,” Gandhi said.
‘FIGHT BETWEEN TWO IDEOLOGIES’
Gandhi framed the Haldwani controversy as part of a much larger political battle between the Constitution and the ideology of the BJP-RSS.
“A fight is underway in the country between two ideologies. On one side is the Constitution of India, the Constitution of Ambedkar, Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Sardar Patel. On the other is the ideology of the BJP and RSS,” he said.
Gandhi said both the Centre and the Uttarakhand government had a responsibility to ensure justice for Kharge.
“We are demanding justice for the Congress president. Give the Congress president justice in Uttarakhand. It is the duty of the central and state governments to ensure that Kharge gets justice,” he said.
Gandhi, however, said the Congress would continue to pursue the matter even if the BJP government did not act. “Even if BJP does not do it, we will get it done. Entire Congress party will not let that man escape either today or tomorrow,” he said.
He said the next step was now with the authorities and warned that the party would respond if no action was taken. “If action is taken, we will welcome it. If action is not taken, there will be a reaction,” Gandhi said.
He also criticised the Prime Minister for not speaking or acting on the issue. “The fact that the Prime Minister is neither speaking nor acting is a reflection of his ideology; we have no interest in that,” he said.
Gandhi further alleged that the BJP’s Uttarakhand state president had committed an illegal act by supporting the alleged purification ritual and called for action against him.
Earlier this month, Kharge had raised the issue in the Rajya Sabha, seeking cases under the law against untouchability against those involved in the alleged act and demanding their arrest.
Leader of the House and Union minister JP Nadda had said the BJP did not endorse such activities and assured that the incident would be investigated.

headline: PM Modi heads to Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan with security, connectivity on agenda
full_text:
PM Modi heads to Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan with security, connectivity on agenda
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic for bilateral talks and the SCO summit. The trip underscores India's push for a secure, connected Central Asia and a region free of terrorism.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said he was looking forward to advancing India’s vision for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), anchored in security, connectivity and opportunity, and to working with fellow member countries for a region free from terrorism. Ahead of his two-nation visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic from August 29 to September 1, he said the trip would advance the shared pursuit of peace, stability and prosperity.
PM Modi also said he was confident that the visit would strengthen India’s strategic partnerships in Central Asia and deepen its civilisational connect with the region. Officials said he will address the SCO summit and highlight India’s priorities of security, connectivity and opportunity, besides holding bilateral meetings with SCO leaders on the sidelines.
In his departure statement, PM Modi said, “India has been an active and constructive member of the SCO since 2017. I look forward to advancing India’s vision for the region, anchored in Security, Connectivity and Opportunity, and to working with fellow members for a region free from the scourge of terrorism, separatism and extremism, which continue to threaten peace and stability in our neighbourhood and beyond.”
At the invitation of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, PM Modi will visit Tashkent on August 29-30 for a State Visit to Uzbekistan.
Referring to ties between the two countries, he said the India-Uzbekistan strategic partnership had seen significant advancement in recent years. “I look forward to my discussions with President Mirziyoyev on further deepening our cooperation in trade and investment, digital connectivity, defence, energy, and on advancing our shared visions of ‘Viksit Bharat’ and ‘Yangi Uzbekistan’,” he said.
During the visit, PM Modi will also go to the Shastri Memorial and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies, which he described as a tribute to the close cultural and people-to-people ties between the two countries.
From Tashkent, PM Modi will travel to Bishkek at the invitation of Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov to take part in the 26th SCO Summit, which marks 25 years of the organisation.
“I also look forward to meeting President Zhaparov and other SCO leaders, and to attend the Opening Ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games, a celebration of the rich living heritage of Central Asia that India holds in deep respect,” he said.
The visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic will combine bilateral engagement with participation in the SCO summit, with PM Modi set to push India’s focus on security, connectivity and opportunity while seeking closer ties with Central Asia.

headline: ‘They will kill me’: Woman, newborn die after delivery in MP's Rewa; video shows she was screaming for help
full_text:

Nursing staff were seen trying to restrain and pacify her, while one staff member was heard asking, “Have you gone mad?” Kalpana died shortly afterward.
A 25‑year‑old woman died allegedly during her first delivery at Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital (GMH), in Rewa along with her unborn child, in a case that has triggered outrage after a disturbing video of the woman surfaced.
The woman, identified as Kalpana Mishra, a resident of Baikunthpur village, was seen hours before her death walking out of the ward, crying, screaming, and pleading for help. In the video, she was seen telling her mother that if this kind of treatment continues, they will kill her.
Nursing staff were seen trying to restrain and pacify her, while one staff member was heard asking, “Have you gone mad?” Kalpana died shortly afterward.
In response to the video, the dean Dr Sunil Agrawal suspended two doctors Dr Sonal Agrawal from the department of obstetrics and gynecology and Dr Nidhi Pandey from the department of anesthesiology along with two nursing staff.
Hospital superintendent Dr Rahul Mishra said, “The woman’s condition was poor from the beginning. She had undergone check‑ups only twice during her pregnancy at a private hospital and may have suffered from high blood pressure, which caused panic.”
Kalpana’s father, Ramsharan Mishra, said, “The daughter was active until shortly before her death. She was neither in a coma nor on oxygen support. She died because of negligence in the treatment.”
He demanded action against the hospital administration. An inquiry has been ordered to know the cause of death.

full_text:

Security forces along the Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu and Kashmir have been put on high alert after fresh aerial activity originating from across the border was detected in the Poonch district.According to inputs from Army sources cited by news agency ANI, an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) from Pakistan was detected at around 8:05 pm on Friday.The drone was spotted hovering over the general area of Behrooti village in the Balakote area of Poonch's Mendhar sector, which falls under the operational area of responsibility of the 22 Jammu and Kashmir Rifles (22 JAK RIF).
Drone tracked towards Mangalnar-Dabrote axis
Military personnel tracked the UAV as it manoeuvred towards the Mangalnar-Dabrote side near the border before returning to Pakistan.Alert troops immediately logged the intrusion, following which the entire forward sector was placed under tight aerial and ground surveillance.Security forces launched the search operation at first light on Saturday in adjoining forward areas to check for any possible dropping of contraband or arms.Monitoring along the border remains active, and further official updates are awaited.
Similar drone sightings reported along border
The latest incident comes amid heightened security concerns along the India-Pakistan border and follows other suspected drone sightings reported in Jammu and Kashmir in recent weeks.
Earlier this month, security forces launched a search operation after a suspected Pakistani drone was spotted over forward villages along the International Border in Jammu and Kashmir's Kathua district.The BSF and Jammu and Kashmir Police conducted searches to ensure that no weapons, explosives or other material had been dropped.A suspected Pakistani drone was also spotted in Rajouri's Sunderbani sector last month, after which security forces carried out a search operation but found nothing suspicious.Earlier in June, Army personnel opened fire after spotting a Pakistani drone over forward posts in the Balakote sector of Poonch, forcing it to retreat towards Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.
Turkish military flights raise concerns
Notably, the latest incident also comes days after an unusual increase in Turkish military transport flights to Pakistan raised concerns in Indian defence circles.Open-source flight trackers recorded a surge in Turkish C-130 Hercules and A400M aircraft flights between August 19 and 21, with the planes landing at Pakistani air bases, including Nur Khan, Masroor and Murid.There was speculation in defence circles that the flights may have carried military hardware, including unmanned aerial systems and air-defence equipment, although neither Pakistan nor Turkey officially confirmed the nature or cargo of the operations.
Search operations underway in Udhampur, Kathua and Rajouri
Separately, security forces are carrying out massive search operations in the forested districts of Udhampur, Kathua and Rajouri following information about suspicious movement, according to news agency PTI.In Rajouri, another search operation was launched in Gaibas, Mithiyani, Mogla and Narla after villagers reported the movement of two suspected armed persons, believed to be terrorists.No contact with any suspected persons had been established so far, officials said.The latest incident in Poonch comes as security forces continue to maintain heightened surveillance along forward areas of Jammu and Kashmir.

headline: Suspected Pakistan drone spotted near LoC in Poonch; Jammu and Kashmir on high alert
full_text:
Suspected Pakistan drone spotted near LoC in Poonch; Jammu and Kashmir on high alert
Security forces are searching nearby areas for any weapons, contraband or other material that the drone may have dropped, and to prevent further incursions.
A drone, suspected to have originated from Pakistan, was spotted hovering over forward areas along the Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch district. Security forces launched a search operation early Saturday, officials said.
The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) was detected around 8:05 pm on Friday in the general area of Behrooti village in the Balakote area of Mendhar sector, PTI reported. The drone was observed moving towards the Mangalnar-Dabrote axis near the border before returning towards Pakistan, according to officials.
Army troops deployed along the LoC immediately increased surveillance in the forward areas.

LoC on high alert
Security forces have been placed on high alert following the aerial activity, with the search operation still underway, ANI reported.
Forces are searching nearby areas for any weapons, contraband or other material that the drone may have dropped, and to prevent further incursions.
ALSO READ | Indian Army downs Pakistani drone after crossing LoC in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch
Search operations in Udhampur, Kathua, Rajouri
The drone activity comes amid multiple search operations being conducted by security forces in the forested areas of Jammu and Kashmir following inputs about suspicious movement.
Police, along with the Army and paramilitary forces, launched a joint search operation across several areas of the Udhampur-Kathua forest belt on Friday evening.
The operation covered Khuban, Nagain, Khtrail, Godu Falal, Padetar, Chor Mottu, Kia, Kheba, Bhed, Marta, Joffar and adjoining areas.
Security personnel continued combing the dense forest areas as part of efforts to verify the inputs and rule out the presence of any suspected persons.
In Rajouri, another search operation was launched in Gaibas, Mithiyani, Mogla and Narla after villagers reported the movement of two suspected armed men believed to be terrorists.
Officials said there had been no contact with the suspected persons so far and search operations were continuing.
Army shot at Pakistani drone
Earlier this year, Indian Army troops opened fire at a Pakistani drone after it briefly crossed the LoC into Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch district, officials said.
The drone was spotted near a forward post in the Digwar area on March 1. Troops fired more than a dozen rounds in an attempt to bring it down, but the drone escaped the firing and returned to Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), according to officials.
A search operation was subsequently launched in the area to check whether the drone had dropped weapons or narcotics.

headline: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman invited global investors to set up manufacturing bases, and technology and innovation centres in India, urging them to leverage talent and opportunity to build for the world.
full_text:
Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman invited global investors to set up manufacturing bases, and technology and innovation centres in India, urging them to leverage talent and opportunity to build for the world.
Addressing a high-level Business Roundtable with leading investors and business leaders in Chicago on Friday (August 28, 2026), Ms. Sitharaman highlighted India’s broad-based growth, reform momentum and expanding opportunities for long-term investment.
Ms. Sitharaman emphasised that India’s investment proposition rests not on any single sector, but on the convergence of scale, growth, talent, infrastructure, technology, and sustained reform over the past decade.
“The policy environment is increasingly focused on enabling businesses to invest, manufacture, innovate and expand,” she said at the roundtable organised by India’s Consulate General in Chicago in association with U.S.-India Strategic Partnership Forum.
The Finance Minister invited global partners to co-develop, co-produce and build for global markets.
She urged them not to consider India merely as a market to serve, but as a platform from which to build for the world — whether as a manufacturing base, technology and innovation centre, consumer market or destination for long-term infrastructure investment — leveraging India’s engineering talent, manufacturing scale and technology ecosystem.
The focus of the meeting was “Manufacture in India — for India and for the world”, with opportunities across manufacturing, AI & digital, financial services, infrastructure, food processing, defence and advanced technologies.
“As global companies reassess supply chains and capital allocation, India offers not only scale as a market, but increasing depth as a long-term investment and operating platform,” Ms. Sitharaman said.
The Minister said India’s Digital Public Infrastructure such as Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, ONDC and India Stack, has created platforms at population scale.
“The next opportunity is to build higher-value businesses in AI, engineering, analytics, product development, semiconductors and electronics, with India’s Global Capability Centres increasingly becoming global innovation hubs,” she said.
Ms. Sitharaman said GIFT City was emerging as an international financial centre connecting global capital with Indian opportunities.
With 1,250 registered entities as of June 2026, it offers opportunities across banking, fund management, reinsurance, aircraft and ship leasing, sustainable finance and other cross-border services, Sitharaman said, inviting global institutions to explore GIFT City as a gateway to India’s financial ecosystem.
She said with global supply chains being reconfigured, India offers a compelling combination of a large domestic market and globally competitive manufacturing capabilities.
The focus is moving beyond assembly towards deeper component manufacturing, engineering and advanced technologies, supported by targeted policy measures including production-linked incentives, the Minister said.
Ms. Sitharaman said India’s infrastructure build-out — from dedicated freight corridors and railway modernisation to electrification and high-speed rail — offers opportunities across engineering, technology, materials, specialised equipment and long-term institutional capital.
She said the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund provides a commercially driven platform for global investors to participate in this opportunity.
Ms. Sitharaman said India’s agricultural base, rising incomes and changing consumption patterns are creating opportunities across food processing, automation, packaging, logistics and cold chains, with potential to build businesses serving both Indian and global markets.
The Finance Minister said through initiatives such as Atmanirbhar Bharat and iDEX, India is building domestic capabilities in drones, autonomous systems and other advanced technologies.
Ms. Sitharaman is on a six-day visit to the U.S. and is scheduled to attend the G-20 Finance Ministers’ meeting in Asheville in North Carolina and visit New York.

headline: PM Modi gets Uzbekistan's highest state honour, Order of Oliy Darajali Do‘stlik
full_text:
PM Modi gets Uzbekistan's highest state honour, Order of Oliy Darajali Do‘stlik
PM Narendra Modi thanked his "brother" President Shavkat Mirziyoyev for the honour, saying India and Uzbekistan will work together for the welfare of humanity.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi was on Sunday conferred the ‘Order of Oliy Darajali Do‘stlik’, Uzbekistan’s highest state honour, by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, in recognition of the deep and enduring ties between India and Uzbekistan.
This happened during PM Modi's two-day state visit to the Central Asian country.
The prestigious honour was presented to PM Modi in Tashkent as the two leaders held delegation-level talks to expand cooperation between India and Uzbekistan across several key areas.
Deep Dive
Last year, Uzbekistan conferred the same award on Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, the President of Kazakhstan. Other notable leaders who have gotten the award are Turkmenistan President Serdar Berdimuhamedov, the chairman of the People's Council of Turkmenistan Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow, and United Nations secretary general António Guterres.
What PM Modi said
Prime Minister Narendra Modi thanked his "brother" President Shavkat Mirziyoyev for the honour, saying India and Uzbekistan will work together for the welfare of the Global South and humanity.
Expressing gratitude for the warmth extended to him and his delegation during his two-day State visit, PM Modi said the visit would remain memorable for him.
"My friend, the father of the economic revolution in Uzbekistan, who has served as a role model across this entire region in scaling new heights of development- this two-day visit of mine will always be remembered," PM Modi said.
"The warmth with which my delegation and I were welcomed made us feel right at home, and for this, I express my deepest heartfelt gratitude to the President," he added.
Reflecting on the honour, PM Modi said the words used by President Mirziyoyev captured India's heritage, its spirit of universal brotherhood and the efforts of its 1.4 billion people.
"The words you just used for me and the generosity you expressed--I believe you have captured in very few words India's thousands-of-years-old heritage, the identity of an India that lives by the spirit of universal brotherhood (Vishwa Bandhutva), and the enterprise of 1.4 billion fellow citizens," he said.
"I may only be a medium for all your words, but the true recipients are my thousands-of-years-old heritage, and the perseverance and hard work of 1.4 billion countrymen- they are the true deserving bearers of this honour," PM Modi added.
Calling the award a moment of "immense pride", the Prime Minister highlighted the significance of the word "Dostlik", meaning friendship, and said it reflected the core sentiment of India-Uzbekistan relations.
"Being conferred with Uzbekistan's highest award is a moment of immense pride for me. And you used a word with which the people of India are also very familiar--'Dostlik'," he said.
"'Dostlik' means friendship. This single word exquisitely captures and expresses the sentiment that lies at the very core of relations between India and Uzbekistan," PM Modi said.
PM Modi said the honour belonged not only to him but to the people of India, and dedicated it to the longstanding friendship and shared heritage between the two countries.
"This honour does not belong to just one individual; it belongs to 1.4 billion people of India. On behalf of all the people of India, I express my sincere gratitude to the people of Uzbekistan, its government, and my friend, the Honourable President," he said.
"I accept this highest honour with utmost humility and humbly dedicate it to the centuries-old friendship and our shared heritage between both nations," he added.
The Prime Minister also credited President Mirziyoyev's leadership and friendship with India for the steady strengthening of bilateral ties, noting that the relationship has now been elevated to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
"Excellency, under your visionary leadership and your friendship toward India, our relations have grown consistently stronger. They continue to successfully scale new heights at every step. As a result, our ties have today been elevated to the new level of a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership," PM Modi said.
PM Modi said the honour also carried a greater responsibility and assured the people of Uzbekistan that India would remain committed to the friendship between the two countries.

headline: India, Uzbekistan upgrade ties, eye $5billion trade, uranium supply deal
full_text:
India, Uzbekistan upgrade ties, eye $5billion trade, uranium supply deal
India and Uzbekistan set a bilateral trade target of USD 5 billion annually by 2030, up from the present of over USD 1 billion.
India and Uzbekistan on Sunday raised their ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership, set a target of $5 billion in annual trade by 2030 and agreed to work for the long-term supply of uranium during talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent.
Uzbekistan was the first stop in Modi’s two-nation tour, which will also take him to Kyrgyzstan to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit. This was Modi's fourth visit to Uzbekistan, which he described as being at the heart of India's engagement with Central Asia.
The talks between the two leaders focused on enhancing cooperation in trade and investment, defence and security, infrastructure, critical minerals, innovation, AI, pharmaceuticals, digital public infrastructure including India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI), agriculture and education.
Also read: PM Modi Kyrgyzstan Visit highlights: PM lands in Kyrgyzstan, will take part in SCO Summit in Bishkek
Deep Dive
Follow live updates on PM Modi's Uzbekistan visit here.
‘Stronger India-Uzbekistan ties force for peace’
“India and Uzbekistan share a deep convergence of perspectives and aspirations,” Modi told a joint media interaction, speaking in Hindi. “A stronger India-Uzbekistan partnership will be a powerful force for peace, progress and prosperity in Central Asia.”
He noted that the two sides were elevating their ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership on the 15th anniversary of their strategic partnership.
Also read: Uzbekistan introduces 30-day visa-free regime for Indian citizens during PM Modi's visit
“Our bilateral trade has crossed $1 billion. We have now set a target of $5 billion in bilateral trade by 2030. To achieve this, we will systematically address issues related to market access, connectivity, banking and payment systems,” Modi said.
At the start of his talks with Mirziyoyev, Modi outlined several steps the two sides planned to take to deepen their relationship. “We will also establish a long-term arrangement for the supply of uranium,” he said.
Sibi George, secretary (West) in the external affairs ministry, told reporters later that the two sides had “positive discussions” on a long-term arrangement for the supply of uranium to India. “We are closing in to the signing of an agreement very shortly,” he said without giving details.
Modi said the two countries will also establish a coordination council led by the foreign ministers to provide direction to all aspects of cooperation, and elevate an existing joint commission from the level of secretaries to the ministerial level.
India ‘reliable strategic partner’: Uzbek Prez
Mirziyoyev described India as a “reliable strategic partner” and noted that New Delhi’s voice and influence in global affairs has grown. Joint ventures between the two countries have increased seven-fold and there are now 14 direct flights every week, he said.
“We are aiming to advance cooperation in sectors such as energy, culture, critical minerals, pharmaceuticals, jewellery and agriculture,” Mirziyoyev said.
“We will prepare roadmaps for each of these sectors. Specific teams from India will come here, and our teams will travel to India, enabling us to clearly define our objectives in these fields,” he added.
Mirziyoyev said the introduction of a 30-day visa-free regime for Indian citizens will make a significant contribution to developing tourism and business exchanges.
Key outcomes from PM Modi's visit
PM Modi pointed out that the close defence and security cooperation between the two sides “reflects the deep mutual trust that underpins our relationship”. The two countries will promote direct linkages, co-production and co-development between their defence industries, he said.
“We believe that terrorism, extremism and separatism pose serious challenges to the entire region,” Modi said. “Our shared resolve to adopt a policy of zero tolerance towards them has been, and will continue to be, unwavering.”
Also Read : PM Modi gets Uzbekistan's highest state honour, Order of Oliy Darajali Do‘stlik
The leaders witnessed the exchange of 11 agreements covering areas such mining, culture, education and tourism. A memorandum of understanding (MoU) between India's ministry of mines and Uzbekistan's ministry of mining industry and geology will focus on cooperation in mineral resources, including rare earths.
An MoU between the ministries of finance of India and Uzbekistan will establish an Economic and Financial Dialogue, while another MoU focuses on cooperation in higher education and scientific research. The external affairs ministry and the Cultural Heritage Agency of Uzbekistan finalised a letter of intent for conserving and restoring the ancient buddhist sites of Fayaz Tepa and KaraTepa at Termez.
India announced a grant of $1 million for afforestation in the Aral Sea region, while India's NPCI International Payments Ltd (NIPL) signed a commercial agreement with Uzbekistan’s National Interbank Processing Centre JSC (NIPC) to enable Indian UPI apps of to scan national QR codes for merchant payments in Uzbekistan. George described this agreement as the first step towards greater inter-operability between the digital payment eco-systems of the two countries.
Also read: Putin to meet PM Modi on August 31 at SCO Summit; talks to continue at BRICS Summit
Mirziyoyev conferred the Oliy Darajali Do’stlik Order, Uzbekistan’s highest honour for foreign leaders, on Modi for his contribution to strengthening the friendship between the two countries. Modi dedicated the award to the 1.4 billion people of India and said the two sides will work jointly to protect the interests of the Global South.
Late on Sunday night, Modi arrived in Kyrgyzstan, where he will participate in the SCO Summit and to hold bilateral meetings with leaders such as Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Abhijeet Dipke said that Mohan Bhagwat had earlier said that the protesting Gen Z should not be called anti-nationals but PM Modi came up with ‘dimagi naxal’.
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Sunday said the BJP believes it has become bigger than the RSS. Dipke, who led the Jantar Mantar protest against alleged irregularities in the NEET exam, said the ruling party should heed what Sangh chief Mohan Bhagwat has been saying.
The former political communication strategist made the remarks in reply to a reporter's question about the RSS chief's statement in New York. Bhagwat had said that if any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslims in Bharat, he will not remain a Hindu.
''I have been saying this from the beginning that the BJP should listen to Mohan Bhagwat. After being in power for 12 years and having so many agencies in its hands, the BJP is thinking that it has grown bigger than the RSS," Dipke was quoted by news agency PTI as saying.
He pointed out that Bhagwat had earlier said that the protesting Gen Z should not be called anti-nationals.
"But the PM (Narendra Modi) came up with a new word, 'Dimagi Naxal'. It clearly shows that the PM is not listening to Mohan Bhagwat,'' Dipke added.
The Boston University graduate said that while the RSS chief talks about inclusivity and not disrespecting children, the PM uses such words. “This doesn't look good," he said.
"They should at least listen to Mohan Bhagwat, who is their mentor... they (BJP) are in power because of the RSS,'' Dipke added.
Dipke on Sonam Wangchuk's ‘not saints’ remark.
Asked about activist Sonam Wangchuk's statement in an interview with a YouTube channel that, in his assessment, the CJP leaders have political ambition and are “not saints”, Abhijeet Dipke asserted that the statement was being distorted.
"He was asked whether Sourav (Das) and Ashutosh (Ranka) have any ambitions. Wangchuk said that we are talented and good leaders and have not been corrupt till now. We have run the agitation honestly. He has spoken good things about us," Dipke said.
Dipke pointed out that Wangchuk was later asked what would happen in future. But, he said, nobody can predict what a person will do in the future.
"Even I cannot tell. I tell people repeatedly not to have blind faith in anyone because we do not know, there is no guarantee what any person will do in future," he said.
Notably, Sonam Wangchuk, who sat on a hunger strike at Jantar Mantar, asserted in the interview that it was not wrong to have a political ambition.

headline: Tamil Nadu police arrests couple in Manipur for murder of woman found dismembered in Delhi-bound train
full_text:
Tamil Nadu police arrests couple in Manipur for murder of woman found dismembered in Delhi-bound train
Through forensic examination and DNA analysis, the body was identified as that of 38-year-old Hayathun Nisha, a native of Odisha
Police on Saturday on late Saturday arrested 22-year-old M Manik Uddin Laskar and his wife, Bhagabati Maji alias Ayesha Begum (21) from Manipur’s Jiribam district in connection with the murder of a woman whose dismembered body was discovered in a red trolley suitcase aboard a Delhi-bound train earlier this month, police said on Sunday.
“A joint team of Tamil Nadu police assisted by Manipur police arrested Manik from inter-village road of Lalpani to Rasidpur, Jiribam district of Manipur on August 28, while the co-accused Bhagabati was arrested on the next day from Kashimpur village, of the same district,” an official statement said. The two accused were suspected to be in hiding and taking shelter in Jiribam area, police said.
On August 5, passengers travelling on a Tamil Nadu Express train noticed a foul smell emanating from a red trolley suitcase in an unreserved compartment after the train reached Agra. Railway police were immediately alerted. They opened the suitcase and recovered the headless and dismembered body of a woman.
The Tamil Nadu railway police at the Puratchi Thalaivar Dr MG Ramachandran Central Railway Station (Chennai Central Railway Station) were informed about the incident, along with the Agra railway police. A detailed probe was then conducted.
After monitoring over 350 surveillance videos, the police team identified a couple who were seen carrying the suitcase at Chennai Central Railway Station.
The Puratchi Thalaivar Dr MG Ramachandran Central Railway Station or the Chennai Central Railway Station is one of the major gateways in Tamil Nadu, where lakhs of passengers arrive and travel to various locations across the country every day.
Meanwhile, it emerged that a complaint was filed last week at the Guduvancherry police station by the deceased’s son, reporting that his mother was missing.
A detailed investigation by the railway police, led by superintendent of police P Rajan, along with a team from Guduvancherry police, led to a raid at a rented house on Mosque Street in Guduvancherry on August 23, where additional body parts of the victim were recovered.
Police found that the body parts were kept in a large cooking vessel in the house. Through forensic examination and DNA analysis, the body was identified as that of 38-year-old Hayathun Nisha, a native of Odisha.
Police said the two suspects were staying at the residence and had known the victim for several years.
The Guduvancherry police later converted the case from a missing-person case into a murder case and began looking for those involved in the crime and the motive behind the murder.
Multiple special teams were formed to identify the suspects. Late on Saturday, a Tamil Nadu police team nabbed Manik Uddin Laskar and his wife, Bhagabati Majhi, from Manipur.
Manik Uddin Laskar is a resident of Dakshin Krishnapur, Sonabarighat, in Assam’s Cachar district, while his wife, Bhagabati Majhi, is from Radhpur in Odisha’s Kendujhar district.
Police said that after placing the red trolley suitcase on the Tamil Nadu Express train on August 3, the couple fled to Manipur.
Following their arrest on Saturday, police said the couple will be produced before a magistrate’s court in Manipur and brought to Chennai after obtaining a transit warrant for further investigation.

headline: Nearly a month after a woman was murdered in Chennai and her dismembered body parts were found inside an abandoned trolley bag on board the Tamil Nadu Express at Agra Cantonment, the Guduvanchery police have arrested a couple from Manipur in the case...
full_text:
Nearly a month after a woman was murdered in Chennai and her dismembered body parts were found inside an abandoned trolley bag on board the Tamil Nadu Express at Agra Cantonment, the Guduvanchery police have arrested a couple from Manipur in the case.
The arrested — Manik Uddin Laskar and Bhagabati Majhi — are being brought to Chennai after obtaining a prisoner of transit warrant from the judicial magistrate of Jirbham district in the northeastern State. A senior officer of the Tambaram Police Commissionerate said the team was expected to reach Chennai on Sunday night. “Only after the suspects are brought to the city and interrogated the entire the murder plot could be found,” the officer said.
The police had arrested the couple on Saturday in connection with the murder of a 38-year-old woman in Guduvanchery, whose decomposed and dismembered body parts were found stuffed inside a trolley bag aboard the Chennai-New Delhi Tamil Nadu Express at Agra earlier this month. While Laskar hails from Dakshin Krishnapur, Sonabarighat, in Assam’s Cachar district his wife Bhagabati Majhi is from Odisha.
The murder came to light on August 5, when the body was found in the rear general compartment of the Tamil Nadu Express in Agra. The Agra Railway Police launched an investigation.
After being informed, the Government Railway Police at the Chennai Central railway station and the Railway Protection Force examined CCTV footage from Platform 4 and spotted a man and a woman carrying a suspicious trolley bag and boarding the train. Their movements led investigators to Guduvanchery, where they identified a rented house on Masuthi Street in which the couple had allegedly been staying with another woman. The deceased was later identified as Hayathun Nisha, 38, wife of Jahhur Khan and a native of Jagatsinghpur in Odisha. She stayed in Guduvanchery and worked at a private firm.
The police found Laskar and Bhagabati had gone missing. During the investigation, the police also recovered body parts from a cooking vessel on the premises. Tambaram City Police Commissioner Prem Anand Sinha formed a special team to trace the suspects. A senior police officer said the team travelled to a remote and difficult-to-access area of Manipur in search of Laskar. The team stayed in the area for more than a week and tracked his movements before locating him. “The area was remote, we could not move around much during the day, and it was also raining there. The team camped for more than a week and eventually traced the accused,” the officer said.
The police said the motive for the murder would be established only after the couple was brought to Tambaram and questioned.
