headline: India rejects Court of Arbitration's Indus Waters Treaty award: ‘Illegally constituted, has no jurisdiction’
full_text:
India rejects Court of Arbitration's Indus Waters Treaty award: ‘Illegally constituted, has no jurisdiction’
The MEA said the Hague-based court has no jurisdiction to pronounce on India’s sovereign decisions and that the treaty will remain in abeyance.
India on Monday rejected the Permanent Court of Arbitration’s (PCA) order setting aside its decision to suspend the Indus Waters Treaty with Pakistan, saying it had never recognised the existence of the “illegally constituted” court in The Hague.
The Indian government also rejected the court order on interim measures prohibiting New Delhi from building certain structures of the Ratle hydroelectric project in Jammu and Kashmir.
“India’s decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance remains in force,” the external affairs ministry said in a statement that rejected the Court of Arbitration’s awards.
Also Read | Hormuz to Indus: The new water weapon isn't scarcity. It's uncertainty
India held the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance as part of a package of punitive diplomatic and economic measures unveiled in April 2025 in response to the Pahalgam terror attack, which was carried out by a proxy for Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT). Pakistan, which has said any denial of its share of waters of cross-border rivers will be considered an act of war, approached the court in The Hague in March this year to determine the status of the water-sharing treaty.
The external affairs ministry described the “so-called Court of Arbitration” as illegally constituted and said: “This so-called Court was constituted by the World Bank in patent breach of the terms of the Treaty and India categorically rejects its so-called award, just as it has firmly rejected all prior pronouncements by this illegally constituted body.”
India has “never recognised the existence in law of this illegally-constituted and so-called Court of Arbitration”, and has always said the “very establishment of this alleged arbitral body constitutes a grave violation of the Indus Waters Treaty”, the statement said.
“Accordingly, India has never appeared before this body and has refused to take any cognisance of its earlier pronouncements,” it said.
The Court of Arbitration has “no jurisdiction whatsoever to pronounce on India’s sovereign decisions” and its “pronouncements, now or in the future, will have no effect on India’s actions in connection with the projects being undertaken by India”.
Also Read | ‘India could use water as weapon’: Pakistan minister warns amid Indus Water Treaty row
Since it suspended the treaty, the Indian side has stepped up work on several hydropower projects in Jammu and Kashmir that Pakistan opposed under the provisions of the 1960 pact. Among these are the Ratle and Kishenganga hydropower projects, over which Pakistan had sought the formation of a court of arbitration.
In a statement, the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) said that the court considered the meaning of India’s decision to suspend the treaty, “finding that it could only be a claim that the Indus Waters Treaty is either suspended or terminated”.
The court examined the potential grounds on which India can suspend or terminate the treaty, including grounds cited by New Delhi in its public statements. “In a unanimous decision, the Court found that none of these grounds could justify suspension or termination of the Treaty. Accordingly, the Indus Waters Treaty remains fully in force, and India must observe its obligations under the Treaty, including those relating to the design and operation of its hydro-electric projects on the Western Rivers,” the court said in a press release.
The Indus Waters Treaty, brokered by the World Bank, allocated the western rivers – Indus, Jhelum, Chenab – to Pakistan, and the eastern rivers – Ravi, Beas and Sutlej – to India. It also allowed each country certain uses of the rivers allocated to the other.
In its order on interim measures, the court considered Pakistan’s request for limiting construction works at the Ratle hydropower project pending a neutral expert’s decision on whether the project’s design complies with the treaty.
“In a unanimous decision, the Court decided to impose measures prohibiting India from concreting the RHEP dam wall and power intake structure above certain levels until 90 days after the Neutral Expert’s final decision, which is expected in July 2027,” the PCA press release said.
“The Court also imposed a reporting measure relating to the RHEP Construction Schedule until shortly after the Neutral Expert’s final decision,” it said.
The court also declined to grant two other measures requested by Pakistan – one that India would bear the risk of having to discontinue, modify or dismantle components of the Ratle hydropower project, and another that India should return to “full compliance” with the treaty pending the court’s decision on Pakistan’s application related to the status of the pact.
The court further said its decisions will be published on PCA’s website after completing a process with the two countries to “identify confidential information for redaction”.
The court of arbitration was chaired by Sean D Murphy of the US and its other members are Wouter Buytaert of Belgium, Jeffrey P Minear of the US, Awn Shawkat Al-Khasawneh of Jordan, and Donald Blackmore of Australia.
In July 2023, the court ruled it was competent to take up Pakistan’s case after rejecting India’s objections to its competence.
While Pakistan initially sought the appointment of a neutral expert to address objections to the Kishenganga and Ratle projects in 2015, it unilaterally retracted this request in 2016 and sought a court of arbitration. In 2016, the World Bank appointed both a neutral expert and the court of arbitration.
India attended meetings convened by the neutral expert till the treaty was suspended in 2025. It completely stayed away from proceedings of the court of arbitration, which it never recognised.
The proceedings before the neutral expert in relation to the Kishenganga and Ratle hydropower projects are ongoing, and the latest work programme issued by the expert envisages circulation of the final decision around July 16, 2027, the press release said.
The court said that while India did not participate by making written or oral submissions during proceedings, it took into account India’s positions on the issues “to the extent they could be discerned from India’s statements and conduct outside of these proceedings (including Indian government communications to Pakistan and to the neutral expert, and public statements made by Indian officials)”.
The court further noted that it looked “extremely seriously” into India’s allegation that “Pakistan’s sponsorship of cross-border terrorism had impeded its utilisation of rights” under the Indus Waters Treaty. “However, the Court found that even if India’s allegation was assumed to be true, they would not establish a material breach of the Treaty by Pakistan,” the press release said.
The treaty “does not address terrorism or the use of force and expressly indicates that it governs only the rights and obligations of the Parties with respect to the use of the waters of the Indus Rivers System”. The court said it “did not find evidence that the alleged terrorism had impeded India’s ability to construct its HEPs on the Western Rivers and instead noted that India has built and is building many such HEPs”.

headline: Goa nightclub fire case: SC junks owners' bail pleas, orders surrender in 2 weeks
full_text:
Goa nightclub fire case: SC junks owners' bail pleas, orders surrender in 2 weeks
The Supreme Court upheld the cancellation of bail for three co-owners of a Goa nightclub where 25 people died in a fire. The ruling requires them to surrender within two weeks and pushes the trial court to speed up charges.
The Supreme Court on Monday refused to interfere with a Bombay High Court order cancelling the bail of the three co-owners of a Goa nightclub where a fire killed 25 people and injured more than 50 on December 6 last year.
A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu dismissed the petitions filed by Saurabh Luthra, Gaurav Luthra and Ajay Gupta, the co-owners of Birch by Romeo Lane in Arpora, North Goa.
The top court upheld the High Court's August 18 order, directed the trio to surrender within two weeks, and asked the lower court to expedite the trial by speeding up the framing of charges. The case relates to the blaze at the nightclub, which is alleged to have been operating without proper licences and safety measures.
Appearing for the Luthra brothers, senior advocates Abhishek M Singhvi and Siddharth Dave told the court that the case was not one of direct intentional offence and was at best one of alleged negligence. Dave said there was no act on the part of the Luthra brothers that led to the killings.
He told the court, "Section 304, part II (of IPC) is wholly and can never be applied to this case. There is no act of mine which has caused death. Maximum, if the prosecution wants to succeed in this case, then it can be under Section 304A (causing death by negligence)."
Justice Datta then asked Singhvi how many people had lost their lives in the restaurant. Singhvi replied that 25 people had died and submitted that the high court judgment suffered from two basic errors. He also said several other co-accused had been granted bail in the case.
Senior advocate Shyam Divan, appearing for Gupta, said his client had only a 10 per cent share in the business and had nothing to do with the incident.
Additional Solicitor General SV Raju and standing counsel Surjendu Sankar Das, appearing for the Goa government, opposed the petitions and said the high court had already directed the trio to surrender within two weeks. While dismissing the petitions, the bench said that the three had two weeks from Monday to surrender.
The Luthra brothers had left for Phuket in Thailand shortly after the fire, after which an Interpol Blue Corner Notice was issued against them. They were detained by Thai authorities in Phuket on December 11 following the intervention of the Indian mission, which was in close touch with the Thai government.
A Delhi court later granted Goa Police a two-day transit remand on December 16, 2025 after they were brought back to India.
In its August 18 order, the Bombay High Court had set aside the bail granted to the trio by a trial court in April this year. The high court said the trial court had failed to properly consider the material collected during the investigation and had erred in saying the offence was not as heinous as murder or dacoity.
It noted that the restaurant was allegedly operating without licences, that the structure was unauthorised, and that the accused and their partners allegedly knew the risks of holding fire displays indoors without adequate safety measures.
The High Court also referred to allegations that forged documents were used to obtain licences and said there were no adequate fire safety installations or emergency measures, leaving many victims unable to escape. It had, however, said the accused were free to apply for bail again after surrender, and that such pleas would be considered by the trial court on their own merits and in accordance with law.
With the Supreme Court declining to grant relief, the three co-owners of the Goa nightclub must now surrender within two weeks, while the trial court has been asked to move faster on framing charges in the case arising from the fire that killed 25 people.

headline: Hours after the Permanent Court of Arbitration at The Hague said the Indus Waters Treaty remains "fully in force" and called on India to “observe its obligations”, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) rejected this, saying that the “very establishm...
full_text:
Hours after the Permanent Court of Arbitration at The Hague said the Indus Waters Treaty remains "fully in force" and called on India to “observe its obligations”, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) rejected this, saying that the “very establishment of this alleged arbitral body” itself was a “grave violation” of the treaty.
“This so-called Court was constituted by the World Bank in patent breach of the terms of the Treaty, and India categorically rejects its so-called award," the Ministry said on Monday (August 31, 2026).
It went on to say that India has “never recognised the existence in law of this illegally-constituted and so-called Court of Arbitration, and has consistently maintained that the very establishment of this alleged arbitral body constitutes a grave violation of the Indus Waters Treaty”.
“Accordingly, India has never appeared before this body and has refused to take any cognisance of its earlier pronouncements,” said the Ministry.
India had placed the Indus Waters Treaty “in abeyance” following the Pahalgam terror attack on April 22, 2025, and the MEA, in its response on Monday (August 31, 2026), reiterated its position. “India’s decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance remains in force," it said.
The MEA also said that “this so-called Court of Arbitration has no jurisdiction whatsoever to pronounce on India’s sovereign decisions”, and said that the court’s pronouncements, “now or in the future, will have no effect on India’s actions in connection with the projects being undertaken by India".
Pakistan’s plea
Earlier, the arbitration body, considering Pakistan’s plea, examined the reasons under which India placed the treaty “in abeyance” and said that “none of these grounds could justify suspension or termination of the Treaty”.
Issuing an "award" on the ‘Status of the Indus Waters Treaty and Order on Interim Measures concerning the Ratle Hydro-Electric Plant (RHEP)', the Permanent Court of Arbitration said, “Accordingly, the Indus Waters Treaty remains fully in force, and India must observe its obligations under the Treaty, including those relating to the design and operation of its hydro-electric projects on the Western Rivers.”
It had also considered Pakistan’s plea on imposing measures on India regarding the RHEP, saying, “In a unanimous decision, the Court decided to impose measures prohibiting India from concreting the RHEP dam wall and power intake structure above certain levels until 90 days after the Neutral Expert’s final decision, which is expected in July 2027.”
The Court of Arbitration is chaired by Prof. Sean D. Murphy of the United States and comprises Prof. Wouter Buytaert of Belgium, Prof. Jeffrey P. Minear of the United States, Judge Awn Shawkat Al-Khasawneh of Jordan, and Dr. Donald Blackmore of Australia.

headline: Should move from endless war to end of war, PM Modi tells Russian Prez Putin
full_text:
Should move from endless war to end of war, PM Modi tells Russian Prez Putin
Modi made the remarks when he met Putin on the margins of SCO Summit, their first in-person engagement since the India-Russia Summit in New Delhi last December
Russia should move from “endless war towards the end of war”, Prime Minister Narendra Modi told President Vladimir Putin on Monday, nudging the Russian leader yet again to end the more than four-year-old conflict that has had an adverse impact on the global community.
Modi made the remarks when he met Putin on the margins of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in the Kyrgyz capital of Bishkek, their first in-person engagement since the annual India-Russia Summit in New Delhi last December. India hasn’t publicly criticised Russia’s invasion of Ukraine but has backed dialogue and diplomacy to find a resolution.
The two leaders met against the backdrop of increased tensions over Russian and Ukrainian attacks on merchant vessels in the Black Sea that have killed at least five Indian seafarers. The impact of the attacks in the Black Sea on maritime trade and the safety of Indian seafarers figured in the discussions, the external affairs ministry said.
“Every day spent perpetuating war pushes humanity backwards, and every step taken towards peace fills the whole of humanity with new hope and enthusiasm. We must move from endless war towards the end of war, which is very necessary for the well-being of humanity,” Modi said in televised opening remarks at the meeting with Putin.
“A peaceful resolution of all issues as soon as possible is the call of humanity, and this is also India’s message. The land of Gandhi and Buddha has one message — the path of peace,” he said, speaking in Hindi.
Modi noted that he and Putin had always discussed the Ukraine issue at all their meetings, and India “supports all efforts for peace and will continue to do so in future”.
The remarks were largely in line with those made by Modi in past engagements with Putin — at their meeting following the start of the Ukraine conflict in Samarkand in September 2022, Modi had said that “today’s era is not of war”, while at a meeting in Moscow in July 2024, Modi had pointed out that “no solution to any conflict is possible on the battlefield”.
Modi and Putin are set to meet again within less than a fortnight when the Russian leader travels to New Delhi to participate in the Brics Summit to be held during September 12-13. Modi referred to Putin as “my friend” and said all Indians were eager to welcome him and his delegation as the visit will “strengthen bilateral relations and empower discussions and cooperation within Brics”.
The two leaders also reviewed various aspects of bilateral relations, including cooperation in trade, investment, and energy and fertiliser security. Modi referred to Putin’s visit to India for the annual bilateral summit last December and said the meeting had taken economic cooperation to new heights.
“It is a matter of great satisfaction that our cooperation is continuously moving towards new heights and we are working together for the benefit of the people of both countries,” Modi said. “Moving forward while keeping national interests above all else is what we both believe in and this will be our root formula in the future too.”
Putin said Russia-India relations have become stronger because of the bilateral special and privileged strategic partnership. “This is undoubtedly facilitated by your personal attention to the development of the Russia-India relations, as well as by the close personal friendship that has developed between us,” he said.
Putin also noted that bilateral trade turnover increased by 2.6% in the first half of 2026 after a slight decline last year. India is “among the leaders” in terms of foreign students in Russia, as the number of Indian students increased seven-fold over the past decade and now stands at almost 40,000, he said.
The discussions between the two leaders covered key areas of cooperation such as defence, energy, mobility of workers, innovation, space, fertilisers and people-to-people contacts. They also discussed regional and global issues, including the “conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region which have impacted maritime trade and the safety and security of Indian seafarers”, the external affairs ministry said.
Modi and Putin agreed to strengthen the bilateral special and privileged strategic partnership, which has registered significant growth and “shown resilience in the backdrop of geopolitical uncertainties”.
Foreign secretary Vikram Misri acknowledged at a media briefing after the meeting that the growing imbalance in two-way trade and the need to expand Indian exports to Russia had figured in the discussions. He pointed out that Modi had shared a paper with Putin at last year’s annual summit that detailed market access-related issues faced by Indian products and non-tariff barriers.
“I am glad to report that, with the cooperation of our Russian friends, we’ve had significant progress on that front and market access has improved significantly in several areas of interest, including meat exports, marine products exports, dairy exports as well,” Misri said.
Both sides will work to increase access to Russian markets and diversify the trade basket to address the growing trade deficit, he said.
Misri responded to a question on the problem of Indian nationals being recruited into the Russian Army to fight in the war in Ukraine by saying that the Indian embassy in Moscow is monitoring the situation to ensure the release and repatriation of these citizens.
He noted that a total of 227 Indians had so far been recruited into the Russian military and 139 were discharged while 51 had died. “We are in discussions with the Russian side to ensure that any cases that remain are discharged at the earliest so that we can return these people to their families,” he said.

headline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday (August 31, 2026) met Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Bishkek and said the world “must move from endless war to an end of war for the benefit of humanity”.
full_text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday (August 31, 2026) met Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Bishkek and said the world “must move from endless war to an end of war for the benefit of humanity”.
The External Affairs Ministry said the two leaders discussed conflicts in West Asia and in the Black Sea region, where, in recent months, Indian seafarers have been attacked by both Russian and Ukrainian forces.
“Had extensive discussions with President Putin. Discussed the full range of the India-Russia Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership. It is gladdening to see significant progress across various sectors in recent years. Focus areas for India-Russia friendship remain energy, innovation, space, fertilisers, and people-to-people linkages,” said Prime Minister Modi.
In a statement, the Ministry said, “They also shared perspectives on key regional and global issues of mutual interest, including the conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region which have impacted maritime trade and the safety and security of Indian seafarers. The Prime Minister reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy were the way forward in resolving conflicts.”
The upcoming BRICS summit featured prominently in the discussion, and Mr. Modi said he “looks forward to welcoming President Putin in India for the 18th BRICS summit on 12-13 September”.
The Bishkek meeting between Mr. Modi and Mr. Putin featured in talks during External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar’s visit to the Kremlin on August 24, 2026, when Mr. Putin had indicated that he would meet Prime Minister Modi in Kyrgyzstan and also at the BRICS summit in Delhi.
“This time, our meeting is taking place on the eve of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit – an organisation that works to deepen contacts among the countries of the Global South and East, promotes the region’s socioeconomic and cultural development, and contributes to building a just multipolar world,” said President Putin in his remarks, reminding that next year will mark the 80th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between New Delhi and Moscow.
Mr. Putin noted that the number of Indian students in Russia has increased almost seven-fold in a decade, and currently 40,000 Indians are studying in Russia.
President Putin said trade and economic cooperation between Russia and India is showing positive trends, with trade turnover increasing by more than 2%. He noted the growth in tourist exchanges between the two countries, with a 16% increase in 2025.

headline: Anna Hazare admitted to Mumbai hospital's ICU with acute dehydration, kidney issue
full_text:
Anna Hazare admitted to Mumbai hospital's ICU with acute dehydration, kidney issue
Hazare, who was admitted to the Bombay Hospital, is in the intensive care unit (ICU) under Dr Gautam Bhansali.
Social activist Anna Hazare was hospitalised on Monday following viral infection, acute dehydration and kidney issues.
Hazare, who was admitted to the Bombay Hospital, is in the intensive care unit (ICU) under the care of Dr Gautam Bhansali.
The veteran Gandhian activist was brought to the hospital in a cardiac ambulance, along with caretakers from his village. Dr Bhansali said Hazare's tests were underway, following which further treatment will be determined.
Hazare rose to prominence nationally through the India Against Corruption movement in 2011. Before that, he was known across Maharashtra for his social and anti-corruption work.
As recently as last month, Hazare told a group of Indian Police Service (IPS) probationers that India's youth represent its future and that integrity and selfless service are essential qualities for nation-building.
The group of 20 IPS probationers from different states, who underwent training at Hyderabad's Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy, visited Hazare's native village, Ralegan Siddhi, in western Maharashtra's Ahilyanagar district in late July to study its watershed development and rural transformation model.
Anna Hazare on CJP protest
Speaking about the Cockroach Janta Party protest, Anna Hazare emphasised that peaceful agitation and democratic dialogue are the only ways to address public grievances.
"Any issue gets resolved through dialogue. Dialogue leads to solutions. Creating tension and going down the wrong path will not solve anything. Dialogue is the most crucial thing. I have conducted 22 hunger strikes, but I never resorted to violence. Things should be resolved through dialogue. The welfare of society, whatever is right, should be done," he said after the CJP stir was called off.
"I did 22 fasts, never used violence, and because of that, 10 laws were enacted. This is essential; creating violence is not right. Whoever the person may be, one should never indulge in violence," he added.
Emphasising that governments must listen to the voice of the citizens, Hazare noted that democratic avenues are designed to ensure public welfare:
"One has to see what the public is saying. For the public's welfare, even if we have to step forward, there's no harm in it. But public interest must happen. Issues are never resolved by violence but by dialogue among people."
"Whatever happens through democracy happens. One should always follow the path of democracy," he added.

headline: Vijay backs Rahul Gandhi as PM face: Congress leader rejects rift with TVK
full_text:
Vijay backs Rahul Gandhi as PM face: Congress leader rejects rift with TVK
Tamil Nadu Congress Legislature Party leader Tharahai Cuthbert said that Chief Minister Vijay had backed Rahul Gandhi as the INDIA bloc's Prime Ministerial candidate, dismissing speculation of a rift with ally TVK.
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay has chosen Rahul Gandhi as the INDIA bloc’s Prime Ministerial candidate, Congress Legislature Party leader Tharahai Cuthbert said on Monday, while rejecting speculation of a rift between her party and ally TVK.
Speaking to reporters, Cuthbert referred to India Today’s Mood of the Nation survey, which ranked Vijay third as the preferred choice for Prime Minister. The TVK subsequently pitched Vijay for the top post, prompting the Congress to threaten to quit the alliance unless he backed Rahul Gandhi as the INDIA bloc’s PM face.
She said projections of Vijay becoming Prime Minister in some quarters were driven by the enthusiasm of TVK workers and did not reflect the leadership’s official position. “The CM has chosen Rahul Gandhi as the PM candidate. That is how he is proceeding,” she said.
Both Vijay and Rahul Gandhi share a close rapport. Vijay, whose TVK made a stunning debut in this year’s Tamil Nadu Assembly polls, ended the decades-long dominance of the DMK and AIADMK. He invited Rahul Gandhi to his swearing-in ceremony in Chennai, where he publicly referred to him as his “brother”. Rahul Gandhi has also expressed his support for the TVK government.
Meanwhile, Cuthbert said the Congress was expanding independently in Tamil Nadu and did not function in a subservient role to the TVK. She added that the Congress was a democratic and autonomous party.
She described the recent FIR against Rahul Gandhi in Uttarakhand's Haldwani over the 'shuddhikaran' row as a sign of the BJP’s political anxiety. She claimed the BJP was intimidated by Rahul Gandhi’s wide public acceptance and that he would become Prime Minister in 2029.
Cuthbert also said the change in her seating arrangement in the Tamil Nadu Assembly was routine and linked to her new role as Congress floor leader, not to any political move.
Cuthbert was appointed leader of the CLP in the Tamil Nadu Assembly on August 13, and after taking charge, she was given a front-row seat on August 31, a place usually allotted to leaders of opposition parties.

headline: Congress threatens to quit alliance if TVK backs Vijay for PM instead of Rahul Gandhi
full_text:
Congress threatens to quit alliance if TVK backs Vijay for PM instead of Rahul Gandhi
Following the assembly elections, the Congress joined hands with the TVK to form the ruling government in Tamil Nadu.
Congress leaders from Tamil Nadu have threatened to resign from the state cabinet if chief minister Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam does not accept Rahul Gandhi as the next candidate for prime minister.
Speaking at an event on Saturday, Tamil Nadu Tourism Minister S Rajesh Kumar stated that both Congress ministers will resign if TVK fails to back Gandhi in the 2029 general elections.
Kumar added that the party would not compromise on its stand, asserting that Rahul Gandhi is the only candidate the Congress party would support in the Lok Sabha elections.
These remarks from the Congress come as the TVK continues to push Vijay as the next prime ministerial candidate.
Following the assembly elections, the Congress joined hands with the TVK to form the ruling government in Tamil Nadu.
The newly formed Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), led by Vijay, won 108 seats in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections. TVK then formed the state government with support from the VCK, IUML, Congress, CPI, and CPI(M).
TVK's 'Vijay for PM' push
Over the past few weeks, the TVK has pushed the idea of chief minister C Joseph Vijay as the prime ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.
“People from north Indian states are also looking forward to our leader Vijay; he is the one who has the power to rule the entire India," said senior TVK leader KA Sengottaiyan.
I have travelled with MGR and Jayalalithaa. After these two leaders, Vijay is the force who will not only rule Tamil Nadu but also the future India, following their path,” the leader was quoted as saying by The Print.
However, this push received a sharp rebuke from Tamil Nadu Congress leaders, who said the TVK were still operating in "fan-mode."
“The TVK leaders are still operating in a fan-club mode. So, you cannot silence people who are in the fan-club mode," said State Congress president and MP B Manickam Tagore.

headline: TN CM Vijay announces further hike in milk procurement prices, unveils multi-crore infrastructure push
full_text:
TN CM Vijay announces further hike in milk procurement prices, unveils multi-crore infrastructure push
TN CM Vijay announces further hike in milk procurement prices, unveils multi-cr infra push
Chennai, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday announced major policy decisions regarding a further hike in Aavin milk procurement price for dairy farmers, and also unveiled a multi-crore infrastructure push spanning power, semiconductors, and logistics.
Announcing further increase in the Aavin-milk procurement prices, aimed at providing a crucial relief for the dairy farmers across the state, he said the state government has approved a ₹3 per litre increase in the milk procurement price, raising it from ₹41 to ₹44 per litre.
The announcement on enhancing the procurement prices comes closely on the heels of an earlier hike announced on August 19 in the Assembly, that had raised the price from ₹38 to ₹41.
Also Read: ‘Back Rahul Gandhi or…’: Congress minister’s big warning after TVK’s PM push for Vijay
He said the decision to address dairy farmers' growing concerns over rising cattle feed costs and maintenance expenses would entail the state government an additional financial outlay of ₹60 crore monthly, translating to an annual expenditure of ₹720 crore.
Apart from the relief to boost rural economy, Vijay unveiled major multi-crore infrastructure push spanning power, semiconductors, and logistics across the state.
Unveiling major investments to boost the state's power grid, manufacturing base, and tech ecosystem, he said ₹33,066 crore has been earmarked for the Tamil Nadu Transmission Improvement Scheme to set up 196 new substations and lay 15,000 km of power lines.
A 1,600 MW Super Critical Thermal Power Station will be set up in Tuticorin through Public-Private Partnership model, involving an investment of ₹20,800 crore, he said.
On combating urban flood resilience and high load demands, the CM said Chennai's distribution network will receive upgrades worth ₹1,762 crore.
A Semiconductor and Electronics Manufacturing Park will be set up at Maduramangalam in Kanchipuram district at a cost of ₹175 crore. Further, Coimbatore is slated to get a ₹400-crore FinTech Hub to accelerate digital financial services.
CM Vijay also announced plans to establish a multi-modal logistics hub in Tiruchirapalli region to strengthen industrial supply chains.

A Dammam-Delhi Air India Express flight made an emergency landing at Ahmedabad Airport on Monday after a crew member found a tissue paper bearing the word "bomb" inside the aircraft's lavatory, Ahmedabad Police said.
According to the Ahmedabad Police, all 32 passengers onboard were safely deboarded at Terminal 2, while security personnel are conducting a thorough check of the aircraft.
The aircraft is currently being checked by security agencies as part of precautionary measures, police said.
Air India Express spokesperson said the government-appointed Bomb Threat Assessment Committee (BTAC) was alerted immediately and all security procedures were initiated. The flight landed safely in Ahmedabad, and all passengers were deboarded.
"One of our flights from Dammam to Delhi was diverted to Ahmedabad as a precaution and in keeping with security protocols after being notified of a specific bomb threat. The government-appointed Bomb Threat Assessment Committee (BTAC) was alerted immediately, and all security procedures were promptly initiated. The flight landed, and all guests have been disembarked safely. The aircraft will be released for operations after necessary security checks are completed," an Air India Express spokesperson said.

headline: A computer-based examination centre in Jaipur’s Sitapura area came under scrutiny on Monday (August 31, 2026) after technical problems disrupted an All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) recruitment exam, a day after an internal power failur...
full_text:
A computer-based examination centre in Jaipur’s Sitapura area came under scrutiny on Monday (August 31, 2026) after technical problems disrupted an All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) recruitment exam, a day after an internal power failure at the same facility forced the cancellation of the NEET-PG 2026 exam for 2,445 candidates.
The developments have raised fresh questions on the reliability of power and technology infrastructure at centres conducting high-stakes national exams.
The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) had earlier said that the NEET-PG 2026 exam had been successfully conducted for the overwhelming majority of candidates on Sunday (August 29, 2026). More than 2.65 lakh candidates appeared at 1,111 centres across the country.
However, the exam could not be completed at two iON Digital Zone centres in Sitapura, Jaipur — test centre numbers 41682 and 41683 — because of an internal power supply failure.
NBEMS has scheduled a fresh examination for the 2,445 affected candidates on September 5 at 3 p.m. in Jaipur.
But the issue resurfaced on Monday (August 31). The same iON Digital Zone facility was being used for the AIIMS Common Recruitment Examination-5 (CRE-5). The institute cancelled the CRE-5 at two exam centres in Jaipur following a disruption caused by internal power supply issues, a source at AIIMS Delhi said.
The exam was conducted across the country on Monday (August 31), the source said. At the two affected centres — RJ0101 and RJ0102 at iON Digital Zone in Sitapura, Jaipur, operated by Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) — the test had commenced at 9 a.m. as scheduled.
However, the disruption subsequently affected the conduct of the examination, prompting AIIMS to cancel the test at the two centres. The decision, the institute said, was taken in the interest of the affected candidates and to ensure a fair, transparent and equitable recruitment process.
Around 2,000 candidates were registered at the two centres. Of these, 1,342 candidates appeared at the RJ0101 centre, and 436 at RJ0102.
AIIMS has scheduled a re-examination for the affected candidates on September 7, 2026.
The institute has also directed TCS, which operates the exam centres, to submit a detailed report on the incident. TCS has been instructed to preserve system logs, CCTV footage, and control room communications to facilitate a comprehensive assessment of the disruption.
The NEET-PG 2026 exam was successfully conducted for more than 2.63 lakh candidates across 1,111 centres in the country on Sunday (August 29), Venguswamy Ramaswamy, head of the iON Business Unit, TCS, said in a statement.
On Monday (August 31), the AIIMS CRE-5 was conducted for more than 21,000 candidates across 58 centres. The expert team from the vendors responsible for electrical maintenance was working on fixing the issue urgently. Further, all possible measures were being put in place to avoid recurrence of such issues in future, the TCS statement added.
“We deeply regret the inconvenience this has caused to the candidates undertaking the NEET-PG 2026 exam and AIIMS CRE at the centre and are working with the respective authorities to ensure that the candidates are able to complete these exams at the earliest,” the statement said.
Published - August 31, 2026 11:13 pm IST

headline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday arrived in Bishkek for the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit, being held at the Yrys Ordo Congress Hall. The summit has brought together leaders of the SCO’s 10 member states, along with partn...
full_text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday arrived in Bishkek for the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit, being held at the Yrys Ordo Congress Hall. The summit has brought together leaders of the SCO’s 10 member states, along with partner and observer countries.
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are also attending, alongside Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other regional leaders. Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov is hosting the summit as its current chair.
The meeting is being held in an expanded ‘SCO Plus’ format, with leaders from countries including Türkiye, Azerbaijan, Armenia, Mongolia, Laos and Togo, as well as UN Secretary-General António Guterres.
India, a full SCO member since 2017, is expected to highlight its priorities of security, connectivity and opportunity.
Earlier, PM Modi and other SCO leaders attended the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games in Bishkek. The 87-member Indian contingent includes 73 athletes competing across 43 sporting disciplines.

headline: Haryana private hospitals to halt Ayushman Bharat services for 24 hours over dues
full_text:
Haryana private hospitals to halt Ayushman Bharat services for 24 hours over dues
The Indian Medical Association has flagged nearly Rs 1,200 crore in unpaid claims and is also demanding a fair and transparent reimbursement system.
Private hospitals in Haryana will suspend Ayushman Bharat services for 24 hours on September 1 over pending claims, the Indian Medical Association (IMA) Haryana has announced, marking a fresh standoff with the state government.
The association has flagged nearly Rs 1,200 crore in unpaid claims and is also demanding a fair and transparent reimbursement system.
In Karnal, IMA spokesperson Dr Kamal Charaya said private hospitals empanelled under Ayushman Bharat would stop services for a day. He said the government had been given time to clear the dues and that the association would decide its next course of action on September 15.
“The pending amount runs into hundreds of crores and has not been released so far. We have given the government time to clear the dues. Further strategy will be decided on September 15,” Charaya said.
He warned that prolonged delays could force smaller hospitals to shut down.
In Panipat alone, private hospitals have reported around Rs 80 crore in pending claims. IMA district president Dr Hemendra Mangal said the delays had put hospitals under severe financial pressure, with some already shutting down and others struggling to survive.
“If the government wants private hospitals to continue providing Ayushman services, it must clear the pending amount. Neighbouring Uttar Pradesh settles claims on time, while Haryana faces repeated delays,” he said.
The IMA has warned of a longer suspension from September 16 if the dues are not cleared. Emergency cases will continue to be admitted, but hospitals will not take new routine patients under the scheme during the protest.
REPEATED STANDOFFS OVER AYUSHMAN DUES
This is not the first confrontation between private hospitals and the Haryana government this year.
Between January and April, the IMA repeatedly threatened to withdraw services over dues dating back to September 2025.
In June, nearly 600 private hospitals went on strike for several days over more than Rs 400 crore in unpaid claims and low package rates under Ayushman Bharat and the state's Chirayu Haryana scheme.
Around 650 empanelled hospitals again suspended services for 19 days from August 7 to 26 over pending payments and alleged arbitrary deductions.
The protest ended after the government agreed to expedite reviews of cases flagged for suspected fraud and withdraw show-cause notices. A review meeting was also scheduled for October 15.
However, tensions have resurfaced within days of services resuming.
OPPOSITION TARGETS HARYANA GOVERNMENT
Opposition leaders have criticised the state government over the dispute.
Leader of Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda accused the government of failing to address the problems faced by Ayushman patients.
Congress leaders Geeta Bhukkal and Aditya Surjewala also raised the issue after meeting the Governor in Chandigarh, while Vinesh Phogat accused the Saini government of repeatedly failing patients under the scheme.
Responding to the allegations, Chief Minister's media adviser Rajeev Jaitley said discrepancies had been found in some hospital bills and that doctors had also acknowledged the issue.
“We are following the Centre’s standard operating procedures for disbursal, which is being done regularly. Wherever there is any lacuna, the Chief Minister is personally looking into the matter and steps will be taken,” he said.
The immediate focus is now on the September 1 suspension and whether the government clears enough pending claims to prevent a longer disruption from September 16.

headline: Lucknow: In the run-up to the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the BJP and Samajwadi Party are turning to a new political weapon: AI-generated songs and videos. After BJP-backed handles nicknaming Akhilesh Yadav ‘Teepu’, the SP chief hit back w...
full_text:
Lucknow: In the run-up to the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, the BJP and Samajwadi Party are turning to a new political weapon: AI-generated songs and videos. After BJP-backed handles nicknaming Akhilesh Yadav ‘Teepu’, the SP chief hit back with a song referring to Adityanath as ‘Baba’—in a sign of how campaign battles are increasingly spilling from speeches and rallies into digitally manufactured political entertainment.
Recently, BJP-backed social media handles shared a song targeting Akhilesh Yadav, with these lyrics: “UP badnaam hua, Teepu tere maare… (UP has become infamous because of Teepu).” The video featured an AI-generated depiction of the SP chief. The song talks of lawlessness in Akhilesh’s regime.
On Monday, Akhilesh responded with another song targeting Chief Minister Adityanath during a press conference at the Samajwadi Party headquarters. The song said: “UP badnaam hua, Baba tere maare… (UP has become infamous because of Baba)”. The video showed AI-generated visuals of the CM.
Akhilesh has often referred to Adityanath as ‘Baba’ while taking jibes at the chief minister. The AI-generated video shows Yogi Adityanath smoking a ‘chillum’ (smoking pipe), while the song took aim at the state government over several issues, including unemployment and paper leaks.
“If the BJP uses AI to make songs targeting me, we will also respond to those songs with songs,” Akhilesh said.
The SP chief alleged that AI-generated videos were being prepared and circulated to defame opposition leaders. He warned the government against using AI for such purposes, saying that if the government chose to use AI against the Opposition, his party would leave it behind in the use of the technology.
According to sources in the Samajwadi Party, the party is planning a series of similar songs targeting the Yogi Adityanath government as part of its political campaign ahead of the 2027 UP Assembly elections. The songs are expected to use AI-generated visuals and focus on issues the SP plans to highlight against the state government.
Earlier targeted CM with ‘Rasputin’
At a press conference earlier this month, Akhilesh played a video showing a group of Japanese students taking selfies with Yogi Adityanath. The students were also seen placing their hands on the chief minister’s shoulder. The 1978 hit ‘Rasputin’ played in the background in the video.
Akhilesh then decided to play the song separately. After the song played for three minutes, he pointed to the phrase “hunger for power” in the lyrics. Drawing an indirect parallel with Uttar Pradesh politics, Akhilesh suggested that someone in UP had a similar “hunger for power”, hinting at the CM though not naming him.
Released in 1978 by the popular band Boney M., ‘Rasputin’ is based on the life of Grigori Rasputin, the Russian mystic who became a close confidant of Tsar Nicholas II (Russian emperor) and his family in the early 20th century. The song portrays Rasputin as a charismatic mystic, womaniser and influential political figure who wielded considerable influence at the Russian imperial court. In 1916, a group of Russian nobles plotted to kill Rasputin because they believed he was harming the monarchy.
During Monday’s press conference, Akhilesh also accused the state government of large-scale corruption and alleged that the current government was the “most corrupt” in the state’s history.
He also raised the issue of schools being shut down, saying the Samajwadi Party would organise programmes at schools that had been closed and inform people about the government’s performance.
Akhilesh also commented on Union minister and Rashtriya Lok Dal chief Jayant Chaudhary’s seat-sharing prospects with the BJP ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. He said Jayant’s respect within the alliance would increase only if the BJP gave his party 61 seats.
“If they get fewer than 61 seats, it will be considered an insult to Jayant Chaudhary,” Akhilesh said.
(Edited by Viny Mishra)

headline: PM Modi meets Iran's Pezeshkian at SCO; discusses West Asia war, trade expansion
full_text:
PM Modi meets Iran's Pezeshkian at SCO; discusses West Asia war, trade expansion
PM Modi’s post on diversifying and expanding trade with Iran comes a week after the US Treasury Department announced new sanctions targeting Iran’s economy.
India is concerned about the escalation of tensions in West Asia and supports all efforts aimed at lasting peace in the region, Prime Minister Narendra Modi told Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Monday, while also calling for freedom of navigation and the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure.
Modi and Pezeshkian met for the first time since the start of the Iran-US conflict in February on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in the Kyrgyz capital, Bishkek. The two leaders also reviewed bilateral relations against the backdrop of trade ties and cooperation for the development of Iran’s Chabahar port, which is being impacted by US sanctions.
“We had a discussion on the prevailing situation in the region. India will continue to support all efforts aimed at ensuring lasting peace,” Modi said on social media after the meeting.
Track live updates of PM Modi at SCO here
According to a readout from the external affairs ministry, Modi expressed concern at the escalation of tensions in the region and reiterated India’s “consistent position that all issues must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy”.
Modi reiterated the need for continued efforts to ensure lasting peace and stability in West Asia, which India describes as part of its extended neighbourhood and is home to more than 10 million Indian nationals.
“Calling for safeguarding the freedom of navigation and commerce, he [Modi] emphasised that civilians and civilian infrastructure, including commercial shipping and seafarers, must not be harmed under any circumstances,” the readout stated.
India has had to strike a delicate balance between maintaining its historic ties with Iran and its expressions of solidarity with Gulf Arab states, which have repeatedly been targeted by the Iranian military for housing US military bases. However, the Indian side has also been angered by Iranian attacks on merchant vessels near the Strait of Hormuz that have killed and injured Indian seafarers.
The Indian side has also had to work with Iran and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), which are on opposite sides of the West Asia conflict, to forge consensus ahead of the Brics Summit in September. Support from both the Brics member states is needed to adopt a summit declaration by consensus.
Modi says India, Iran want to ‘diversify’ trade basket
India-Iran relations also figured in the meeting and Modi said he reiterated New Delhi’s commitment to strengthen the long-standing friendship with Tehran across diverse sectors. “We want to expand and diversify our trade basket in the times to come,” he said.
Modi also pointed to India’s readiness to cooperate closely with Iran in multilateral organisations such as Brics and SCO, and said he looked forward to welcoming Pezeshkian to India for the Brics Summit in September.
Pezeshkian expressed appreciation for India’s “support and cooperation” with Iran during the war and emphasised the need to intensify diplomatic efforts to establish peace and security in West Asia, the Iranian embassy said in a statement.
He referred to India’s “important position and capacities in the region” and asked Modi to use “India’s extensive contacts with various parties to help them move away from the path of war and bloodshed and return to the path of dialogue and agreement”.
Iran’s efforts have focused on peace and security and resolving issues through dialogue, while the “Americans have chosen the path of war, insecurity and imposing their will through force”, Pezeshkian said. Iran has never “welcomed war” and is protecting its people and working for conditions necessary for peace, tranquillity and security, he said.
Referring to understandings between the parties to the conflict, Pezeshkian said Iran remains committed to “obligations it has undertaken within the framework of the agreements”, but the US has “failed to fulfill its commitments”. Iran believes the “continuation of war is in the interest neither of us, nor of the region, nor of humanity”, he added.
In the realm of bilateral ties, Pezeshkian emphasised Iran’s readiness to deepen relations with India in political, economic, scientific, cultural and other areas of mutual interest. “By strengthening bilateral cooperation and neutralising the effects of sanctions, we can further elevate the level of relations between the two countries,” he said.
The discussions covered collaboration in transportation and maritime affairs, and progress in cooperation at Chabahar port, the Iranian embassy said.
Pezeshkian referred to efforts by the US and Israel to “create restrictions and obstacles” to Iran’s cooperation with other countries, and said: “Despite the pressures and restrictions being imposed in an attempt to obstruct Iran’s relations with other countries, Tehran is ready to expand its cooperation with India across various fields.”
Iran was once among India’s top three energy suppliers, but New Delhi stopped purchasing Iranian oil in 2019 because of the threat of US sanctions. New trade-related sanctions drawn up by the US administration could hit India’s limited trade with Iran, including the sale of commodities such as rice and tea through third countries.

headline: Congress to hold massive protests over FIR against Rahul Gandhi: KC Venugopal
full_text:
Congress to hold massive protests over FIR against Rahul Gandhi: KC Venugopal
The FIR was registered by the Haldwani police on Sunday, a day after Rahul Gandhi addressed a press conference to seek a FIR over the ”purification ritual”
The Congress announced “massive protest marches” on Monday evening over a first information report (FIR) registered against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi in Uttarakhand, intensifying the political battle over some people “purifying” the Ramlila ground at Haldwani after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge addressed a public meeting there.
The FIR was registered by the Haldwani police on Sunday, a day after Gandhi addressed a press conference in New Delhi to demand that Prime Minister Narendra Modi order an FIR against those involved in the “purification” of the Ramlila ground at Haldwani.
Congress general secretary KC Venugopal said the FIR against Rahul Gandhi was a “shameless weaponisation of the state machinery” to target the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
Venugopal told the party’s state and district units to hold protest marches at the state and district headquarters on Monday evening to register their “vehement condemnation of this vendetta politics and to demand immediate legal action against the guilty BJP workers in Uttarakhand”.
The FIR, registered on a complaint by Amit Kumar, a member of Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas, accused Gandhi of offences under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and sections 196 (promoting enmity between classes) and 299 (malicious acts to outrage religious feelings) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The FIR said Gandhi wrongly described the cleaning and havan ritual as an act of “untouchability” and an atrocity against the Scheduled Caste community without verifying the facts.
Venugopal said the party’s fight against those who attack the values of social justice enshrined in the Constitution should continue and asked all party leaders at the state and district levels to participate in the protests.
He said party units should ensure the maximum mobilisation and media dissemination “to send an unyielding message: the Indian National Congress will not be intimidated by state-sponsored witch-hunts and will fight relentlessly for social justice, constitutional equality, and the dignity of every citizen.”
“The BJP’s blatant defence of this casteist behaviour and its shameless weaponisation of the state machinery to target the Leader of the Opposition unequivocally proves that they are the biggest perpetrators or protectors of social injustice today. They have demonstrated that they will deploy the entire might of the state to suppress anyone who dares to speak out against caste-based discrimination and Dalit atrocities,” he said.
Congress leaders Randeep Surjewala and Jairam Ramesh also attacked the BJP over the FIR.
In a post on X, Surjewala said, ”By registering an FIR against Shri Rahul Gandhi, the cowardly BJP government has revealed its true face. The Leader of the Opposition in the country and Congress President, Shri Mallikarjun Kharge ji, has publicly stated both inside and outside Parliament how the incident of purifying the stage after his speech deeply hurt his sentiments. Meanwhile, from CM Dhami to the BJP National General Secretary, they are all dispensing wisdom on the justification of this incident.”
Ramesh said Rahul Gandhi had raised the issue of injustice, humiliation, and discrimination faced by Dalits in his press conference, and the BJP-RSS took less than 24 hours to prove him right.
“He highlighted the issue of untouchability and humiliation carried out in the name of “purification” after the rally of Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge Ji in Uttarakhand, and demanded action against the BJP workers involved in it.
But this did not sit well with the BJP-RSS’s double-engine government in Uttarakhand. That’s why, even today, no action has been taken against the accused, but an FIR was filed against Rahul Gandhi Ji, who is demanding justice, the very next day,” said Jairam Ramesh.

headline: New Delhi: One out of two national office-bearers of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) under president Nitin Nabin—46 percent to be precise—have had no links with the party’s ideological fountainhead, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). Around 54 p...
full_text:
New Delhi: One out of two national office-bearers of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) under president Nitin Nabin—46 percent to be precise—have had no links with the party’s ideological fountainhead, the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). Around 54 percent of Nabin’s new team, announced earlier this month, have been previously associated with the RSS—slightly more than the 49 percent Sangh imprint on his predecessor J.P. Nadda’s team.
The trend is in sync with Nadda’s famous remarks ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha election that the BJP needed RSS in the past, but was “saksham” or competent now to run its own affairs.
ThePrint’s analysis of BJP’s national office-bearer teams over the last 20 years shows that the RSS imprint had peaked during Amit Shah’s term as the party president (2014-2019), when 78.7 percent of the members in top posts were associated with RSS, or its student wing, the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP).
The number stood at 77.41 percent during Rajnath Singh’s tenure as BJP president (2005-09), and at 60 percent under Nitin Gadkari (2010-13). Nadda had succeeded Shah as president on 20 January, 2020. Nabin succeeded him in January this year.
For the purpose of this analysis, ThePrint looked at Vice Presidents, General Secretaries, Joint General Secretaries (Org), Secretaries, Spokespersons and Media teams picked by the various BJP presidents. It doesn’t include the social media teams.
Nabin’s profile on BJP website does not mention his association with RSS, although his father, Nabin Kishore Prasad Sinha, was said to be a regular visitor to an RSS shakha in Patna. Sinha was a senior BJP leader and a four-time Member of Bihar Legislative Assembly from Patna West.
Among the 13 new V-Ps, at least five—Tirath Singh Rawat, Ram Madhav, Lal Singh Arya, M. Nagaraja and Dr Madhuchanda Kar—have RSS (including ABVP) background.
Rawat worked as an RSS pracharak, and held positions in the ABVP in the 1980s. Madhav’s association with the Sangh began in his teenage years, while Arya has been going to shakhas since he was seven years old. Both Nagaraja and Kar have been ABVP members.
Nabin retained B.L. Santhosh as National General Secretary (Org), and Shivprakash and Saudan Singh as National Joint General Secretaries (Org). A general secretary (organisation) is an RSS swayamsevak, who is virtually on deputation in BJP to serve as a link between the two organisations.
Among the eight general secretaries, at least seven have RSS or ABVP connections.
Vinod Tawde has been an RSS member, having held various posts in ABVP as well. Sunil Bansal, Harish Dwivedi, Sanjay Bhatia and Dr Satish Poonia have all been associated with ABVP. Biplab Kumar Deb was an RSS volunteer for 16 years, having trained under leaders like Gobinda Acharya and Krishnagopal Sharma. Gajendra Patel completed a three-year training programme offered by RSS, and went on to hold several posts in the organisation.
Among the 16 secretaries appointed by Nabin, at least six are associated with RSS or ABVP. These are K. Surendran, Dr Pradip Varma, Dr M. Venkateshan, Dr Swadesh Singh, Manoj Tigga and Jai Prakash. Venkateshan has also written a book titled Naan RSS SwayamSevakan, which translates to ‘I am an RSS Swayamsevak’.
Union Minister Piyush Goyal, who has spoken about how his association with RSS has been the best thing to happen to him, is the new Treasurer in Nabin’s team.
Additionally, among the four media convenors and co-convenors, three have been associated with the Sangh.
Also Read: Nitin Nabin’s team is not as ‘young’ as Nadda’s but why RSS and BJP leaders are happy about it
‘Changing’ composition of BJP
Dr Ratan Sharda, who has authored several books on RSS, put the numbers in context of BJP’s expansion from a “big party to a mammoth party”, and its changing composition.
“There are many highly qualified people who have joined the BJP during Modi ji’s time, who don’t have an RSS background. There are many important imports from other parties, which wasn’t very high earlier,” he told ThePrint.
“Before Modiji’s time, or let’s say when Atal ji was in power, BJP had very limited pull among non-BJP parties. It was still a politically avoidable party, virtually a pariah. But now that acceptability has increased and power also begets power, more people wish to be near the power as BJP becomes very dominant. The overall bench strength of BJP, in terms of leaders who are mid-level and new, and who are not from RSS, has naturally increased,” he explained. “And they have to be accommodated.”
Therefore, Sharda said, inclusion of fewer RSS-linked leaders in the national office-bearer team does not surprise him, but asserts that the party’s dependence on RSS remains.
“BJP is running on its own steam, like any other organisation that came with the support of RSS. Every organisation, like the BMS (Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh), ABVP and VHP (Vishva Hindu Parishad), have their own cadre and leaders. So, it is obvious that something similar will happen with the BJP also,” he said.
On whether the reduction in RSS imprint in BJP’s national team reflects Nadda’s 2024 remark, Sharda asserted, “Even now, the spine of the RSS organisational people has to remain if BJP has to remain strong.”
He added, “BJP cannot become the Congress. Every time they have tried to become Congress, they’ve suffered… so they have to have that spine, or that inner nervous system, where RSS people and cadres are there, but overall the composition and the character of the party will change as it grows.”
However, political analyst Badri Narayan does not think that any conclusion can be drawn from the changing RSS imprint in BJP’s organisational leadership structure.
“There are leaders within BJP who are associated with the Sangh, and some of them are selected. Sometimes more are chosen, and at other times, fewer. It is likely not a highly calculated process, where a specific percentage must be drawn from the Sangh,” he told ThePrint.
Narayan asserted that this isn’t a part of the political strategy, adding that it is only the post of the General Secretary (Org) which assumes significance in terms of the coordination between RSS and BJP.
“There is a flow of ideas, there are many flows of ideas in it, and many BJP leaders are influenced by it. Those who are doing good work get a place in the organisation or in the ministry,” he said.
(Edited by Mannat Chugh)

headline: India is bracing for below-average rainfall this September, signaling an early end to the monsoon season with overall inadequate precipitation.
full_text:
India is bracing for below-average rainfall this September, signaling an early end to the monsoon season with overall inadequate precipitation.
NEW DELHI: Monthly rainfall over the country as a whole is most likely to be âbelow normalâ in Sept, the last month of the monsoon season, said IMD on Monday â an indication that the four-month rainy season is likely to end with overall deficient cumulative (June-Sept) rainfall as predicted earlier with high probability due to the impact of El Nino.The Met department said August, which reported a deficit of more than 16 percent in monthly rainfall in the country despite good rains in certain parts, was the warmest August in India since 1901, recording a mean temperature of 28.01 degrees Celsius.Region-wise, August in south Peninsular India was the second-warmest August since 1901, whereas it was the third warmest for east and northeast India, and fifth warmest for northwest India in the past 126 years.So far, the country as a whole reported a deficit of 14 percent in cumulative (June 1-Aug 31) rainfall, despite ânormalâ rainfall in July. In June, the deficit was as high as 35 percent. Out of a total of 741 districts assessed for monsoon rainfall distribution, 312 districts (42 percent) received âbelow normalâ rainfall and 38 districts (5 percent) reported large deficient rainfall till Aug 31.A forecast of âbelow normalâ rainfall in Sept may lead to a deficit in overall kharif crop acreage.
Though sowing of most of the seasonal crops is almost complete with a decline in acreage by nearly 2 percent compared to the corresponding period last year, low rainfall in Sept means an increase in the input cost due to farmersâ spending on irrigation of standing crops.âSpatially, many parts of the country are likely to receive below-normal rainfall, but some areas of northwest, northeast, east, east-central and south-east Peninsular India are likely to receive ânormal to above-normalâ rainfall,â said IMD chief Mrutyunjay Mohapatra.He said currently âstrong El NiÃ±o conditionsâ are prevailing over the equatorial Pacific Ocean, with sea surface temperature (SST) remaining above normal across the central and eastern equatorial Pacific. âThese conditions are expected to strengthen further in the coming months,â said Mohapatra, hinting at its negative impact on Sept rainfall.
El NiÃ±o, characterised by the warming of ocean surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is invariably associated with a weak monsoon and a harsh summer in India.At present, neutral Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) conditions prevail over the Indian Ocean and the forecasts from the Monsoon Mission Coupled Forecast System (MMCFS) indicate that neutral IOD conditions are likely to persist through Sept. It means the monsoon may not benefit from this climatic phenomenon as only positive IOD helps increase rainfall activities.IMD noted that the extreme weather events (lightning, thunderstorm and heavy rains) took 113 human lives in Aug. Mohapatra, however, said this figure can be cross-checked with the data compiled by the states.

headline: Congress vs TVK in Tamil Nadu Assembly? ‘Vijay as PM’ pitch sparks rift buzz, seat-change adds fuel

Congress vs TVK in Tamil Nadu Assembly? ‘Vijay as PM’ pitch sparks rift buzz, seat-change adds fuel
The buzz of rift between Congress and TVK comes in the backdrop of statements by leaders of Vijay's party, projecting him as a potential contender for PM post.
Tensions between the Congress and the chief minister C Joseph Vijay-led TVK have been dominating the Tamil Nadu Assembly, with a seat change in the House adding fuel to the speculation of rift that reportedly stemmed from the pitch for Vijay as prime minister.
The buzz of rift between the Congress and TVK comes in the backdrop of statements by leaders of Vijay's party, projecting him as a potential contender for the prime minister's post.
Congress is part of the TVK-led Tamil Nadu government with five MLAs, along with 107 of Vijay's party, two of Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), and two of VCK / Left Factions (External Support).
Congress vs TVK?
Congress Legislature Party leader and MLA Tharahai Cuthbert was shifted to the front row of the Opposition benches in the Tamil Nadu Assembly on Monday, amid speculation over differences between the Congress and ruling TVK.
Cuthbert was earlier seated in the section allocated to TVK MLAs. However, her seat was changed on Monday, with the Congress leader now occupying a place in the front row of the Opposition benches, according to an ANI news agency report.
The development comes a day after Tamil Nadu tourism minister S Rajesh Kumar said that Congress ministers in the state Cabinet would resign if TVK did not support Rahul Gandhi as the Prime Ministerial candidate for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.
Kumar made the remarks on Saturday while speaking at the assumption-of-office ceremony of George Robinson, who took charge as president of the Kanyakumari West District Congress Committee.
He said Rahul Gandhi would become the Prime Minister of India in 2029.
TVK leaders have lately been projecting party chief minister Vijay as a potential contender for the PM post. TVK PWD Minister Aadhav Arjuna had earlier said that the country's top constitutional office should be held by a leader from Tamil Nadu.
The issue gained further attention after a private media survey's result also featured Vijay among the preferred candidates for the post of prime minister in 2029, ranked third. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi took the first and second spot, respectively, on the list.
Reacting to the developments, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national spokesperson CR Kesavan questioned why Congress continued to remain part of the TVK government if its leaders were opposed to the ruling party's position.
"Repeated assertions by multiple TVK Ministers even inside on the floor of the Tamil Nadu Assembly touting their leader as a probable Prime Minister is an outright rejection of the failed and dismal leadership of Rahul Gandhi by the TVK. Now, what is preventing the opportunistic Congress party from coming out of the Cabinet of the TVK government? Because the TVK minister's statements are a scathing vote of no confidence, and TVK is an alliance partner, but the Congress party still continues to be in the TVK government. Why is the Congress party not withdrawing support to the TVK government after their leader Rahul Gandhi has been insulted?" ANI quoted Kesavan as saying.
Vijay's TVK secured a landmark win in the Tamil Nadu assembly elections this year, winning 108 seats in its debut poll. The TVK-led government was formed days after the results were declared, as Vijay needed the support at least 10 MLAs to take oath.
The Congress had ended its long-standing alliance with the DMK following the election results and submitted a letter of support to the TVK, with the condition that communal forces be kept out of the government.

2 suspects in Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan's murder killed in UP Police encounter
Haryanvi singer and actor Ankit Baliyan was fatally shot in Shamli district on Wednesday evening as he stepped out of a gym.
Two alleged sharpshooters, carrying a reward of ₹50,000 each in connection with Haryanvi singer and YouTuber Ankit Baliyan's murder, died during treatment after being injured in what police said was an exchange of fire in Uttar Pradesh's Shamli on Monday.
Additional director general (law and order) Amitabh Yash said the exchange took place on Kairana Road when a police team intercepted the two suspects, Mohit, 22, and Sumit, 24, who were from Haryana's Sonipat.
In a statement, police said the suspects fired at their team, prompting retaliation in self-defence, which left Mohit and Sumit injured. The two were rushed to Shamli's District Joint Hospital, where doctors declared them dead during treatment. The statement said head constables Harvinder and Pradeep also sustained bullet injuries during the exchange of fire.
Police said they recovered three pistols, 10 live and nine spent cartridges of .30 bore ammunition, a motorcycle, a bag, a mobile phone, and ₹5,000 in cash from the two suspects.
ALSO READ: 18 rounds fired, one hit his head: How Haryanvi singer, YouTuber Ankit Baliyan was killed
Deep Dive
Mohit faced 14 criminal cases in Haryana and Sumit one. Police said they were verifying their criminal records and that further legal proceedings were underway.
The two men were identified as alleged killers of Baliyan, who was shot dead outside a gym in Shamli on August 26.
Their killings are the latest in a series of such "encounter killings" in Uttar Pradesh. Authorities maintain that such "encounters" are mostly in self-defence and are part of the government’s zero-tolerance policy against crime. Questions have been raised about the efficacy of such measures. Some argue that such measures are necessary. Others have flagged potential human rights abuses and the need for transparency in investigations.
