headline: 2 accused in Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan's killing shot dead in UP encounter
full_text:
2 accused in Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan's killing shot dead in UP encounter
Two shooters involved in Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan's murder were killed in an encounter with the UP STF. Police said four shooters and two recce suspects have so far emerged in the investigation.
Two shooters involved in the murder of Haryanvi singer Ankit Baliyan were killed in an encounter with Shamli Police and the SWAT team, officials said. The two men, identified as 24-year-old Sumit and 22-year-old Mohit, carried a reward of Rs 50,000 each.
According to police, Sumit and Mohit were among four shooters involved in Baliyan's killing, while two other suspects had conducted reconnaissance and identified the singer's location before the attack. Police said a total of six people have so far emerged as being involved in the case.
CCTV footage captured four armed assailants opening fire at Baliyan outside the gym, with the attackers reportedly firing around 12 rounds before fleeing the scene, triggering panic in the area.
Baliyan, a popular 35-year-old Haryanvi singer, was shot dead by four assailants outside a gym in Shamli, Uttar Pradesh. He was known for songs including Bhari Court Mein Goli Maarenge Meri Jaan, which had gained popularity in the region.
TWO RS 50,000-WANTED SHOOTERS KILLED IN ENCOUNTER
The encounter took place near an Indian Gas godown on Kairana Road in Shamli, where teams from Shamli Kotwali Police, Jhinjhana Police and the SWAT team were involved in the operation.
Police said both suspects were shot during retaliatory firing after they opened fire at police personnel. The two men were taken to the District Joint Hospital in Shamli, where doctors declared them dead during treatment.
Two SWAT team head constables, Harvinder and Pradeep, were also injured in the encounter, police said.
Police recovered two pistols, 10 live cartridges and nine spent cartridges of 30-bore ammunition from the encounter site. Another pistol, along with 16 live and six spent cartridges, was also recovered.
A Splendor motorcycle, a bag, a mobile phone and Rs 5,000 in cash were also seized from the spot.
TWO MEN RIDING BIKE OPENED FIRE: POLICE
Shamli SP Narendra Pratap Singh said police teams had been conducting intensive checks following Baliyan's murder, with the SWAT team, surveillance unit, SHOs, ASP and COs assigned to the case.
He said a blockade plan was implemented from midnight to 6 am to ensure that vehicles entering the district were checked.
According to Singh, at around 4 am, Hijana SHO Virendra Kasana spotted a motorcycle approaching from the Karnal side while conducting checks near his police station. When he tried to stop the motorcycle, the two men riding it opened fire.
Singh said Kasana narrowly escaped, although a bullet struck his vehicle. He immediately alerted other police teams over the wireless, following which the suspects fled towards Kairana.
When the motorcycle reached the area beneath the Manna Madra bridge, Kotwali SHO Dharmendra Gautam, who was conducting checks there, attempted to stop the suspects. They opened fire again, shattering the windshield of his vehicle.
The SHO then challenged the suspects, who turned left towards the city. However, by then, an alert had been circulated over the wireless network, prompting the SWAT team, surveillance unit, SHOs, CO City, ASP and CO Kairana to move towards the location.
Singh said the suspects subsequently swerved their motorcycle towards the area where the police teams had assembled, leading to the encounter.
Ankit Baliyan’s father, Satveer Singh Balyan, said the police encounter had brought his family “half justice”, but the remaining accused must also be brought to justice. He thanked Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and the police for the action.
MOHIT HAD 14 CASES IN HARYANA: POLICE
Police said preliminary checks showed that Mohit had around 14 criminal cases registered against him in Haryana. One case was reportedly registered against Sumit in Haryana.
Authorities are checking their complete criminal histories and investigating their roles in Baliyan's killing.
GOGI GANG CLAIMED RESPONSIBILITY
Baliyan was fatally shot outside a gym in Shamli, where the attackers opened fire before fleeing the scene. The murder triggered protests and demands for swift action against those responsible.
The Gogi gang later claimed responsibility for the killing. The gang cited Baliyan's purported links with its rivals and referred to a song associated with the singer as among the reasons for the attack.
A post from the Instagram account of Bholu Shahpuria, reportedly linked to the gang, read, “This is just the beginning, everyone’s turn will come.” The gang also issued a threat to the Uttar Pradesh Police, warning of more attacks similar to Baliyan’s killing.
Police, however, are continuing to investigate the motive and are examining several possible angles, including old rivalries and political or election-related connections.
TWO SHOOTERS CONDUCTED RECCE BEFORE KILLING: POLICE
Amitabh Yash, Additional Director General (ADG) of Law & Order and the Special Task Force (STF), Uttar Pradesh. said two shooters linked to the Gogi gang had conducted reconnaissance of Ankit Baliyan’s movements in Shamli on August 20, days before the singer was killed.
The two shooters allegedly travelled to Shamli and stayed at the Surya Hotel, where they provided documents including their Aadhaar cards during check-in.
Police subsequently examined CCTV footage from the hotel, which reportedly provided crucial leads in the investigation.
Yash also reiterated the Uttar Pradesh government's stated policy of zero tolerance towards crime and warned against testing the administration's resolve.
EIGHT POLICE TEAMS FORMED
Following the murder, Meerut Zone ADG Bhanu Bhaskar directed an intensified investigation into the case. The Uttar Pradesh Police had formed eight teams to conduct raids in Haryana and other locations, trace the suspects and recover weapons believed to have been used in the crime.
Investigators are also examining CCTV footage, call records and other evidence to establish the sequence of events leading up to the shooting.

headline: FIR against Rahul Gandhi for giving 'casteist spin' to Kharge 'purification' row
full_text:
FIR against Rahul Gandhi for giving 'casteist spin' to Kharge 'purification' row
An FIR has been registered against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi after a complaint alleged he gave a casteist spin to the 'purification' ritual held at the venue of Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge's rally in Uttarakhand's Haldwani.
An FIR has been registered against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi after a complaint alleged that he gave a casteist spin to a religious ritual held at the venue of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's programme in Uttarakhand's Haldwani, police said on Sunday.
Police said the case has been filed under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita related to promoting enmity between groups and deliberate acts intended to outrage religious feelings. Provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, have also been invoked.
The complaint was filed by Amit Kumar, a resident of Jawahar Nagar and a member of Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas. He said he was present during the "ritual and cleanliness drive" and that remarks made by Gandhi at a press conference in Delhi on August 29 hurt the sentiments of the Valmiki community. Kumar accused Gandhi of portraying those associated with the ritual as practising "untouchability" and being "anti-Dalit".
In his complaint, Kumar said he belongs to the Scheduled Caste community and that people from different sections of society, including Scheduled Castes, took part in the ritual. He said the event had "no connection" with Kharge's caste.
A political row had broken out after some people allegedly performed a "purification yajna" at the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani on August 11, days after a public meeting addressed there by Kharge on August 8.
The Congress called the incident a reflection of the BJP's anti-Dalit mindset. The BJP defended the action, saying the venue had been left littered after Kharge's rally and that slogans raised there were inappropriate for a religious site.
At a press conference in Delhi on August 29, Gandhi criticised the incident and demanded that an FIR be registered under the SC/ST Act against those responsible for the "purification". Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra later backed the demand, calling the incident a "reprehensible and shameful mindset" and alleging that it amounted to a violation of the SC/ST Act.

headline: 25-year Sone river rift to end as Bihar, Jharkhand set to sign water pact today
full_text:
25-year Sone river rift to end as Bihar, Jharkhand set to sign water pact today
The agreement settles the division of the erstwhile undivided Bihar’s allocation under the 1973 Bansagar Agreement.
Bihar and Jharkhand on Monday will sign an agreement formalising the sharing of Sone river waters, resolving the dispute that has persisted since Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar in 2000.
“All details had already been finalised. Chief ministers of both states are coming to sign the pact Monday,” a senior Union Jal Shakti ministry official told HT, on condition of anonymity.
HT had on July 24 reported that the agreement was very close to be signed after both states completed their internal approvals. The development comes after Jharkhand in July passed the matter in its cabinet earlier this month.
Also Read | Bihar’s Indrapuri reservoir project awaits Jharkhand nod on Sone water-sharing
The agreement settles the division of the erstwhile undivided Bihar’s allocation under the 1973 Bansagar Agreement.
Of the total 7.75 million acre-feet (MAF) of Sone river water originally allocated to Bihar, 5.75 MAF will now go to Bihar and the remaining 2.0 MAF of water to Jharkhand. The allocation follows the unanimous recommendation of a committee constituted by the Centre under the chairmanship of the Central Water Commission to resolve the long-pending issue.
The Bansagar Agreement, signed in 1973 between Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and the then undivided Bihar, governs the sharing of Sone river waters.

While the agreement continued after Jharkhand was carved out in November 2000, the division of Bihar’s share between the two successor states had remained unresolved for nearly 25 years.

headline: ED steps into NEET-UG paper leak case, seeks CBI's records
full_text:
ED steps into NEET-UG paper leak case, seeks CBI's records
The CBI filed its charge sheet earlier this month against 13 accused in the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has formally sought the Central Bureau of Investigation’s (CBI) complete case records in the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak, as the financial crimes agency examines the alleged financial trail behind the examination scandal, people familiar with the development said on Sunday.
The ED has sought the CBI’s charge sheet, witness statements, relied-upon documents and other case material through official channels. The request marks the first time the financial crimes investigation agency has formally sought information from the CBI in connection with the case.
Also read: ‘NEET exam system foolproof, difficult to breach’: Centre to SC after paper leak
ED seeks financial angle in alleged examination scam
The move could add a new dimension to the investigation. While the CBI has investigated the alleged conspiracy behind the leak -- from the setting of the question papers to the beneficiary candidates - the ED is examining the alleged financial aspects of the case and transactions connected with the alleged irregularities.
The ED has not yet registered a case under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002. People familiar with the matter said the agency is seeking to study the CBI material while it waits for the ongoing court proceedings in the CBI case to conclude.
“We definitely want to investigate a financial angle in the NEET-UG paper leak, but we will wait for CBI’s court proceedings to get over, which are currently ongoing in a fast-track court in Delhi,” an officer said, requesting anonymity. “For now, we have approached the CBI through proper official channels for its charge sheet, relied-upon documents and other case files so that we can study the alleged irregularities,” the officer added.
Also read: From AIPMT to NEET: A decade of paper leak scandals that shook India's education system
CBI charge sheet names 13 accused in leak case
The CBI filed its charge sheet earlier this month against all 13 people arrested in the case, saying its investigation had traced the alleged leak from the paper setters to beneficiary candidates and uncovered the alleged conspiracy.
The three paper setters appointed by the National Testing Agency (NTA)-- Manisha Gurunath Mandhare for Botany and Zoology, Prahlad Vithalrao Kulkarni for Chemistry, and Manisha Sanjay Havaldar for Physics -- have been named as accused in the case.
According to the CBI charge sheet, Kulkarni allegedly transcribed 135 Chemistry questions, along with their answer options, onto small pieces of paper and took them out of the confidential area. Mandhare and Havaldar allegedly memorised questions and their parameters and later reconstructed them with the help of textbooks, according to the agency’s case.
Also read: Delhi court flags ‘criminal breach of trust’ by 3 experts in NEET-UG paper leak
Agency relies on 360 witnesses, 422 documents
The CBI has invoked provisions relating to criminal conspiracy, cheating, criminal breach of trust and destruction of evidence, besides provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024. The agency has relied on 360 witnesses, 422 documents and 43 material objects to support its case. All 13 people named in the charge sheet are in judicial custody, while the CBI is continuing its further investigation.
The CBI has so far said that no NTA official has been found involved in the alleged leak.
The government has subsequently announced changes to the NTA’s examination system. The education ministry said on August 17 that more than 50 NTA staff had been removed and 10 professional leadership positions were being filled. The NTA subsequently said its examination team had been revamped, with 600 subject experts removed and new experts brought in, besides the introduction of a four-tier question-paper scrutiny system.

headline: Women appearing at public events will cause great destruction: Cleric sparks row
full_text:
Women appearing at public events will cause great destruction: Cleric sparks row
Kanthapuram AP Aboobacker Musliyar, a 95-year-old cleric from Kerala, has sparked a row, claiming that women should remain confined to their homes. He said that their appearance at public events would cause "great destruction".
A cleric from Kerala has made controversial remarks about women, claiming they should remain confined to their homes as their appearance at public events would cause “great destruction”, news agency PTI reported. The comments triggered a huge outcry from opposition parties like CPI (M) and BJP, calling them “derogatory” and "medieval seclusion”.
Kanthapuram AP Aboobacker Musliyar, 95, general secretary of the Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama, made the remarks days after the state's prominent council of Sunni-Shafi scholars directed that women should not share stages with men or appear in public spaces alongside them.
At an Islamic conference in Kochi on Sunday, Musliyar defended the directive and said Islam prescribed purdah for women to prevent such consequences. Musliyar, also known as Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad, serves as the tenth Grand Mufti of India.
“It is precisely recognising that bringing women onto public platforms in this manner causes great destruction that Islam mandated purdah for women. The Holy Quran states that women should live confined within their homes and must not make public appearances,” he said.
Musliyar said such views had been taught by religious scholars, particularly Samastha leaders, for the past 100 years, according to PTI.
“Therefore, you must understand that it is because all knowledgeable people, especially the leaders of Samastha, taught this here for 100 years that the women in this country have maintained their honour and dignity,” he said.
He said religious scholars had an obligation to speak on the issue despite criticism and would continue to do so.
“When this is said, if leaders of any other organisation or Samastha leaders object to or question it, we have studied the religion and therefore have an obligation to say it. We will say it and continue to say it. No one can make us stop,” he said.
This is not the first time Musliyar has faced criticism for his remarks on women. In 2015, he said gender equality was against Islam, though he later clarified his remarks had been distorted.
The cleric was also criticised in 2019 for saying women should not take to the streets against the Citizenship Amendment Act. In 2025, he objected to a fitness programme involving men and women exercising together, calling it against Islamic norms.
Notably, Musliyar played a key role in saving Kerala nurse Nimisha Priya, who is on death row in Yemen for the murder of Yemeni national Talal Abdo Mahdi. He intervened with Yemeni religious authorities ahead of Priya's scheduled execution in July 2025, which was later postponed.
CPI(M), BJP SLAM CLERIC'S REMARKS, DIKTAT ON WOMEN
Musliyar's recent remarks on women drew criticism from the CPI(M), with its leader PK Sreemathi saying that Islam teaches that Prophet Mohammed urged that women be treated with respect and consideration.
“No matter who makes such a statement, even if the person holds a very high position, I cannot agree with the expression that women should not be displayed,” she said.
Sreemathi called the remarks “insulting and derogatory” and demanded its immediate withdrawal.
CPI(M) leader KK Shailaja criticised the suggestion that women should remain confined to their homes, describing it as a “feudal custom”. She also questioned the directive from an organisation with a long history of work in education and social reform.
Kerala BJP chief and former Union Minister Rajeev Chandrasekhar said women have a constitutional right to “learn, celebrate, lead, dream, and live with total freedom and dignity”.
He opposed what he described as attempts to impose “clerics’ diktats” and said the BJP and NDA would resist any move to push women into “medieval seclusion”.

headline: Political graffiti is back on Jadavpur University’s whitewashed walls
full_text:
Political graffiti is back on Jadavpur University’s whitewashed walls
The Students Federation of India (SFI) Jadavpur unit announced its “Reclaim Your Wall” programme in a social media post on Sunday evening
Jadavpur University (JU) students belonging to Left unions repainted political graffiti across the campus on Monday, claiming the same walls that the authorities covered with white paint a day earlier following chief minister Suvendu Adhikari’s announcement that his government will not allow JU to remain a free ground for Maoist sympathisers.
The Students Federation of India (SFI) Jadavpur unit announced its “Reclaim Your Wall” programme in a social media post on Sunday evening, hours after a contractor deployed by the university’s maintenance department painted over the old graffiti.
“Members of the CPI(M)’s student front did not hold any demonstration on Monday. Instead, its members picked up cans of aerosol paint and brushes. Members of the other Left student unions also took part,” a JU professor said, requesting anonymity.
The incident happened after a JU emblem installed on one of the gates was damaged on August 20 when members of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), the students’ wing of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), allegedly tried to enter the campus following a clash between its members and supporters of Left student unions the earlier night. The university lodged a police complaint but no arrests have been made yet.
Also Read:Theatre artists repaint Kolkata’s Academy of Fine Arts white from saffron
The damage to the logo, which was designed by iconic painter Nandalal Bose, who drew the sketches for the first copy of the Indian Constitution, drew flak from the civil society. State finance minister Swapan Dasgupta said in a video statement that the incident was uncalled for.
On Friday, CM Adhikari addressed a large crowd outside the JU campus while attending a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-held mass singing of the national song, Vande Mataram on the occasion of Raksha Bandhan.
Also Read:Nabanna building signage changes to saffron; part of maintenance, says official
“You don’t express grief or hold rallies when 45 CRPF jawans are killed by terrorists in Awantipora and tourists belonging to a specific religion are gunned down at Pahalgam. But anti-war rallies are held when Operation Sindoor is carried out against Pakistan,” Adhikari said at the rally.
“I know the disease. I also know the medicine,” he said.
No political party made a statement after the graffiti returned to the JU campus.

headline: After unity pitch in US, RSS chief praises India's asylum policy in Canada: 'Came as aggressors, but still thrive'
full_text:
After unity pitch in US, RSS chief praises India's asylum policy in Canada: 'Came as aggressors, but still thrive'
The RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat said if someone was persecuted anywhere in the world, the person was given asylum by India.
Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat, who was in Toronto for an event of the Hindu community, said India has always offered asylum to outsiders, even after they came as "aggressors". The RSS ideologue said Hindus respect and accept all religions and that's why even those who came as aggressors "thrive" today. He went on to say that India is home to Muslims, Christians, Jews and Parsis.
"Many came to Bharat from outside as aggressors, but they still thrive there, with all their specialties intact. They are now Bharatiya citizens. Muslims are there, Christians are there. Jews are there in small numbers because many migrated from Israel. Parsis are there. Many people come to Bharat for asylum," said Bhagwat.
Deep Dive
The RSS leader said if someone was persecuted anywhere in the world, the person was given asylum by India.
Addressing the 'Hindu Vishwa Bandhu - Embrace the World in Friendship' event, the RSS chief also hailed India's rise over the years as "Vishwaguru", a title often used by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to describe the country.
"One may call Bharat a superpower, but it was not one. It served the world and by its own character, it became 'Vishwaguru', not Mahashakti," he said.
RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat highlighted the idea of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, or the belief that the entire world is one family. "While individuals in the material world may differ in body, shape, and complexion, in essence, we are all one. Therefore, serving others is our duty. We have gained this wisdom, which brings us enduring happiness and lasting contentment," he said.
ALSO READ: 'They should listen to Mohan Bhagwat’: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke says BJP in power because of RSS
Bhagwat also emphasised what he described as Bharat’s tradition of extending help to those in need, saying the country has historically offered assistance whenever called upon, and even without being asked.
He linked this outlook to the broader Hindu philosophy of recognising unity amid diversity and considering both living and non-living beings as part of a shared existence. He argued that diversity does not undermine unity in India; rather, the country’s traditions view diversity itself as an expression of underlying unity.
"This is our tradition, the DNA of Bharat. That is why you may have heard the saying—'If Hindus awaken, the world awakens'. They regard both the animate and the inanimate as their own. They have been taught to see unity in diversity. That is why diversity never poses a problem for unity in India; our tradition teaches us that not only is there unity in diversity, but diversity itself is a form of unity," said Bhagwat.
Prime Minister Modi is also expected to visit Canada this year. The event erupted with chants of "Modi, Modi" after former Canadian defence minister and former premier of Alberta, Jason Kenney hailed “renewed momentum” in the Canada-India relationship and said it will further be represented by the second visit of Prime Minister Modi to Canada later this year.

headline: Very country Babur came from: Owaisi jabs BJP over PM Modi's Uzbekistan honour
full_text:
Very country Babur came from: Owaisi jabs BJP over PM Modi's Uzbekistan honour
Owaisi questioned the Sangh Parivar's repeated references to Babur, urging its supporters to reconsider invoking the Mughal emperor after Uzbekistan, his place of origin, honoured PM Modi.
Owaisi invoked Babur to take swipe at BJP after PM Modi gets top Uzbekistan honour.
AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi on Sunday turned Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s latest foreign honour in Uzbekistan into a political taunt against the BJP, saying the honour came from the country from which Mughal emperor Babur originated. He asked how the BJP and the Sangh Parivar could now invoke Babur’s name to target the Opposition after the country of his birth honoured the Prime Minister.
Reacting to PM Modi being conferred the Order of 'Oliy Darajali Dustlik', Uzbekistan’s highest state award, the Hyderabad MP said, "I congratulate the BJP; the very country from which Babur came to India has conferred an award upon the Prime Minister."
Owaisi noted that Babur belonged to the Fergana Valley in present-day Uzbekistan and said it has become routine for Prime Minister Modi to receive honours during his foreign visits.
"Wherever the Prime Minister goes these days, he returns with an award. Congratulations," Owaisi said.
The AIMIM chief also took aim at the BJP and the broader Sangh Parivar over references to Babur in political discourse. "You used to shower so many insults in Babur's name, yet the people of that very country are now honouring you with an award," the MP added.
Owaisi said the development should prompt introspection within the RSS and its supporters.
"The Sangh needs to reflect on this. You used to abuse us, invoking Babur. And now you have been given a civilian award from the very place where Babur came from. We hope that people of the Sangh Parivar and those who support the RSS will no longer take Babur's name in this manner, because the Fergana Valley is there, in Uzbekistan. Now what will they say? he asked.
PM Modi was conferred with Uzbekistan's highest honour for foreign leaders on Sunday, the 'Oliy Darajali Do'stlik' Order, during his visit to the Central Asian country. The honour recognises his contribution to strengthening the strategic partnership and friendship between India and Uzbekistan.
"Honoured to receive the Oliy Darajali Do'stlik Order. I dedicate this to the enduring bond between India and Uzbekistan," Modi said in a social media post.
The Uzbek honour adds to a long list of top state and civilian awards conferred on Prime Minister Modi by nearly three dozen countries, recognising his leadership and contribution to strengthening bilateral ties.
In July, Indonesia conferred its highest civilian award, the 'Bintang Adipurna' of the Republic of Indonesia, on pm Modi for his contribution to strengthening ties between the two countries.
In June, Seychelles awarded the PM its highest national honour, the 'Guardian of the Blue Horizon', in recognition of his leadership in environmental conservation and sustainable development.
Earlier this year, Israel conferred the 'Medal of the Knesset' on PM Modi, making him the first recipient of the honour.
In 2024, Russia awarded him the 'Order of St Andrew the Apostle', the country’s highest state decoration, for his contribution to deepening the strategic partnership between India and Russia.
The United States also conferred one of its top honours, the 'Legion of Merit', on PM Modi in 2020, recognising his leadership in strengthening the India-US strategic partnership.

headline: 7 die, 5 injured as bus collides head-on with truck in Assam: Police
full_text:
7 die, 5 injured as bus collides head-on with truck in Assam: Police
According to the investigating officer Dhiren Saika Sonowal, the bus carried 14 passengers including a driver and a helper
At least seven persons died and five others were injured on Sunday after a bus carrying them collided head-on with a goods truck on National Highway-27 in Assam’s Kamrup Metro district, police said.
According to the police, the incident happened in the Sonapur-Khetri area on the outskirts of Guwahati city on Sunday evening. Police said that three persons died on the spot while around nine injured people were shifted to Guwahati Medical College and Hospital (GMCH), four of them later succumbed during treatment.
The deceased have been identified as Prashanta Talukdar (34), Anima Deka Bordoli (32) and Gopal Das (46) of Morigaon, and Insan Ali Sheikh (54), Tafajul Ali (53), Jutika Ronghang (46) and Idris Ali (42) of Kamrup district, police said.
“The accident took place at Nalagedera-Tetelia under Khetri police station in Kamrup Metropolitan district and as per the preliminary investigation, the passenger-carrying bus was heading towards Guwahati from Nagaon when it hit a goods truck after losing control,” police said.
According to the investigating officer Dhiren Saika Sonowal, the bus carried 14 passengers including a driver and a helper, both of whom died on the spot. However, the police found 12 persons during the rescue operations. “We found 12 persons, seven of whom died and five are now undergoing treatment. We believe some people who were sitting at the back of the vehicle managed to leave the spot on their own,” the officer said.
As per the locals, the bus hit a large pothole on the highway before it crashed into the truck coming from the opposite side.
“It was so massive that the front part of the vehicle was completely mangled, and the rescue team had to cut open portions of the damaged vehicle to pull out the passengers,” a local resident said.
The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Traffic), Guwahati, Safiqul Hussain said the bus lost control and crossed the divider before hitting the truck. The truck driver also managed to flee the accident site, police are looking for him. Police are examining the reason behind this, including the claim that it happened because of a pothole.
Police said no occupant of the goods truck was injured in the collision.
Officers said that the bodies have been sent for postmortem and the family members of the identified persons have been contacted.
The incident triggered anger among locals and a group of protesters blocked NH-27 on Monday morning, alleging that accidents caused by potholes on the highway have become a regular occurrence and the local administration has been ignoring the matter.
Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Monday visited the spot and said the state government would provide compensation of ₹5 lakh to the family of each deceased person.
He wrote on X, “The tragic accident at Khetri has left us anguished. My heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families.”
He said the issue concerning the condition of the road was being examined and the Chief Secretary of Assam will consult the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) on the matter.
“We have conveyed our concerns to NHAI and sought corrective action. If anyone is responsible, appropriate actions will be taken,” he said.
Kamrup Metropolitan deputy commissioner Swapneel Paul on Monday held a meeting at the Guwahati police commissioner’s office in Khanapara with representatives of the NHAI, police, district administration, elected representatives and local residents.
Following the meeting, NHAI agreed to repair all potholes along the Khanapara-Sonapur stretch within seven days. Paul said the administration had heard concerns from all sides before fixing the deadline.
“We have given NHAI a seven-day timeline to repair all potholes along the stretch from Khanapara through Sonapur to NH-37 in Kamrup (Metro) and they have agreed to comply,” Paul said.
NHAI official Abhishek Kumar said repair work will be completed within the stipulated period and that an investigation and legal action would be initiated against contractors connected with the stretch.
“We have also terminated our site engineer and have requested the administration to take legal action against the contractors and the respective agencies,” Kumar said.
A committee has been constituted to monitor the repair work and submit its report to the Deputy Commissioner by September 8.
Paul said that a special meeting of the District Road Safety Committee has also been scheduled at the Dimoria Co-District Commissioner’s office on September 3 to exclusively discuss safety concerns along the Sonapur highway stretch.

NEW DELHI: The political row over an alleged âfish feastâ at a Congress event in Ayodhya escalated on Tuesday, with Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai filing a defamation case against Yogi Adityanath, alleging that the chief minister's remarks had âhurt his faith.âRai approached the MP-MLA court in Lucknow, the UP Cong chief also denied eating fish at the event, saying he is a vegetarian. âWe do not eat non-vegetarian food. The allegation of a fish feast against me is wrong. The chief minister's statement has hurt my faith,â Rai told ANI.Rai said he had filed the defamation case to seek legal action and challenged the chief minister to produce evidence in court.âYogi cast aspersions on my character and my dietary habits; he claimed that I visit Hanuman Garhi, apply the tilak and sandalwood paste, and pay obeisance to Lord Ram, only to subsequently feast on fish. The fact is, we are not non-vegetarians; we hail from Kashi, the city of Baba Vishwanath. The chief minister levelled a false allegation. I have filed a defamation suit here today. If the CM possesses evidence, he should present it in court and prove whether I am in the wrong or he is,â Rai said.Explaining his presence at the event, Rai said he had been invited to a fish feast organised by the Nishad community and attended it out of respect for the organisers.
âI was invited to a fish feast organised by the Nishad community, a community whose livelihood involves rearing, selling, and consuming fish. I would not disrespect or insult anyone's event, so I attended and participated. He alleged that I consumed fish during the month of Sawan. I believe such tactics are characteristic of the BJP, not us,â Rai added.
The remarks came days after Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath launched a sharp attack on Rai over the alleged incident at an Ayodhya programme organised by members of the Nishad community.The controversy erupted after a video showing fish being prepared at the Congress event surfaced on social media during the month of Shravan, when many Hindus observe dietary restrictions.The event was held to welcome Rai, who had attended a programme organised by the Nishad community. The issue quickly became political, with the BJP targeting Rai over the alleged feast and the Congress rejecting the allegations.Addressing a gathering in Raebareli on August 24, Adityanath accused Rai of âduplicityâ for visiting Hanumangarhi to offer prayers and later attending a programme where fish was allegedly served.âYou saw the behaviour of the Congress state president: he goes to offer prayers at Hanumangarhi, but later outside he enjoys a feast of fish. He could have eaten whatever he wanted outside-anywhere other than Ayodhya. Yet, this is the duplicity they display,â Adityanath said.âEven a chameleon would be put to shame by these people; it would wonder what kind of human species this is-chanting 'Ram-Ram' inside the temple and feasting on fish the moment they step out,â he added.The chief minister also accused Rai of not standing up to mafia elements in the past and referred to the killing of his brother, former MLA Awadhesh Rai.âWhen a mafia don murdered his brother, this man did not testify against the criminal; instead, he knelt and bowed in submission before him,â he added.Rai had earlier challenged Adityanath to produce evidence of him eating fish. In an open letter to the chief minister on August 28, he said he was a vegetarian and would quit politics if proof was produced.âIt is an immutable truth that I am a vegetarian. If you have any authenticated photograph or video of me eating fish, make it public. I will retire from politics,â Rai said.
He said five days had passed since he issued the challenge but there had been no response. Rai also rejected Adityanathâs allegations about his alleged links with mafia elements, citing his nearly 32-year legal battle following the killing of his brother.He accused the state government of focusing on personal and provocative remarks instead of issues such as law and order, crimes against women and weaker sections, unemployment, inflation, farmersâ concerns, electricity supply, roads and alleged corruption.âMy humble but clear advice is to stop making false and unsubstantiated statements and focus on the real problems of Uttar Pradesh,â Rai added.

headline: 3-year-old kidnapped from Delhi found 1,000 km away in Bihar; accused woman had 6 daughters, wanted a son
full_text:
3-year-old kidnapped from Delhi found 1,000 km away in Bihar; accused woman had 6 daughters, wanted a son
The child went missing while he was playing near his mother, who had gone to the hospital to collect medicines, police said.
A three-year-old boy who was allegedly kidnapped from a government hospital in west Delhi was safely recovered from Bihar’s Munger district after police tracked the accused woman across more than 1,000 km, officials said on Monday.
The woman was identified as 31-year-old Chunari Devi, a temporary resident of Madipur and a native of Bihar’s Banka district.
The toddler went missing on August 27 while he was playing near his mother, who had gone to the hospital to collect medicines, police said. A case was registered at Khyala police station after a PCR call was received around noon, news agency PTI reported.
ALSO READ | 15-year-old girl gang-raped inside moving car in Bihar, 2 arrested
CCTV trail helps police trace woman
During the investigation, police examined CCTV footage from the hospital and nearby areas and spotted Chunari Devi carrying the child away.
Police then tracked her movements through multiple CCTV cameras. The footage showed her travelling towards Madipur village in an e-rickshaw, officials said.
Local inquiries revealed that she had left Delhi and travelled to her native state.
Acting on technical surveillance and local intelligence, a police team travelled to Asnaha village in Munger district in Bihar, where the child was safely recovered, officials said.
ALSO READ | 6-year-old boy kidnapped, thrown into canal alive in Meerut; accused was in relationship with his mother
Woman allegedly wanted to raise the boy
Devi was also traced and joined the investigation. During questioning, she allegedly told police that she was a mother of six daughters and, due to medical complications, was unable to have another child.
Police said she allegedly kidnapped the boy with the intention of raising him as her own son.
The child was subsequently brought back to Delhi and reunited with his family.
Infant kidnapped from Ghaziabad
Last month, a three-month-old boy was allegedly kidnapped from his home in Ghaziabad’s Sahibabad and was later rescued after police arrested seven people linked to a suspected child-selling racket.
The infant was taken on August 9 while his parents were at home, police said. An FIR was registered the next day under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita’s kidnapping provision.
Police found that the child had allegedly been passed through several people and was to be sold to a couple in Haryana for ₹5-6 lakh. The suspects were traced using CCTV footage and surveillance and arrested from Farrukhnagar near Tila Morh. The child was safely rescued.
Police also said some of the suspects had allegedly facilitated the sale of a minor girl about 18 months earlier and were investigating the case further.

headline: Goa-Delhi IndiGo flight makes emergency landing, engine failure suspected
full_text:
Goa-Delhi IndiGo flight makes emergency landing, engine failure suspected
The Delhi-bound flight had a total of 229 passengers on board. According to the airline, the flight landed after a technical issue was detected.
A Goa to Delhi IndiGo flight with 229 people on board made an emergency landing on Tuesday after the pilot reported a suspected engine failure minutes after take-off, prompting the declaration of a full emergency at Manohar International Airport. The flight 6E 2102 departed at 9.16am and landed safely at 9.50am.
Officials said no passengers or crew members reported injuries, and emergency response teams were on standby to handle the aircraft's return. “A full emergency was declared at the airport at 9.25am after the pilot alerted air traffic control (ATC) about the suspected engine failure and requested an emergency landing,” an official said.
Officials said a team from the regulator, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), will inspect the aircraft in Goa.
In a statement, IndiGo said the aircraft was undergoing maintenance checks. It added that the standard operating procedure was followed after a technical issue was detected shortly after takeoff. “...the relevant authorities were informed, and the pilots turned back and landed the aircraft safely at Manohar International Airport.”
The statement said the aircraft will resume operations after securing the necessary clearances. "We regret the inconvenience caused to our customers and made every effort to minimise it, including offering refreshments and timely updates."
The statement said alternative arrangements were made for customers to reach their destination. "The safety of our customers, crew, and aircraft remains our top priority at IndiGo."
A second official said the passengers remain at the Goa airport terminal and were expected to be flown to Delhi during the day.

full_text:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party on Tuesday withdrew its call for a march on September 5 after Supreme Court, on the Centre's request, quashed all FIRs registered across the country against students who participated in the NEET protests."I want to state that in view of the positive assurances of the government of India and the judicial sanctity bestowed upon them today, and in view of the order being passed by this court, the CJP deems it appropriate to withdraw the call for the march on September 5 and looks forward to compliance with today's order," CJP co-convener Sourav Das said during a hearing in the Supreme Court.Chief Justice of India Surya Kant appreciated the CJP's decision, observing that disputes could be resolved if both sides acted in good faith."If both sides show good faith, then all issues can be resolved one by one. There is nothing in the world which is too complicated that it cannot be discussed with an open mind," the CJI said.This comes after Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre and Delhi Police, informed the apex court that the Centre remains committed to fulfilling all three assurances given to the leadership of CJP during the meeting between the Centre and the party.
What were the three assurances
The first assurance was that the Centre would not pursue FIRs registered between July 20 and July 25.The second assurance was that no fresh FIRs would be registered in connection with the matter.The third assurance was that the government would pay compensation to students who died by suicide allegedly in connection with the NEET paper leak."Centre is committed to honour the assurance given to the CJP leaders to provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide after NEET exam cancellation; however, 3 months needed to work out the modalities," Mehta told SC."As of now, we are committed to fulfilling all three assurances," he added.Earlier on Monday, Centre moved the apex court seeking to quash FIR's registered against the student protesters with alleged violence during protests over the NEET paper leak in Delhi and other states.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta mentioned the plea before a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Monday, seeking the courtâs intervention in the matter.The Centre has urged the Supreme Court to exercise its extraordinary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to quash the FIRs registered against the protesting students.Also read: 'Keeping future of students in mind': Nadda after quashing of FIRs against NEET protesters.
Why CJP had called for Sept 5 march
CJP had called for a protest march in Delhi on September 5, Teachers' Day. It had accused the Centre of failing to honour the promises made on July 25 to persuade the group to withdraw its 36-day agitation against irregularities in exams and the NEET paper leak.
According to the CJP, the march was to be led by families of students who committed suicide following the cancellation of the NEET exam and the subsequent re-test, as well as those who were allegedly subjected to police excesses during the July agitation.

headline: PM Modi called for dismantling the entire ecosystem that enables terrorism at SCO
full_text:
PM Modi called for dismantling the entire ecosystem that enables terrorism at SCO
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said there can be no âdouble standardsâ in the fight against terrorism and called for dismantling its entire ecosystem, including financing, recruitment, radicalisation and safe havens.Addressing the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek, PM Modi described terrorism as a âgrave challenge to all of humanityâ and said the fight against it cannot be limited to a mindset of âaction-reactionâ.
âWe must dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorism--its financing, recruitment, radicalization, and safe havens. We must speak in one voice that there can be no place for double standards on this serious issue,â he said.âThose countries that use terrorism as an instrument of their policy, and provide shelter and support to terrorists, must be sent a strong message that terrorism cannot be a âstrategic assetâ for anyone,â the Prime Minister added.
He also outlined "Security, Connectivity and Opportunity" as the three pillars of Indiaâs vision for the SCO, with peace and security forming the first pillar.âOur shared aspiration for a peaceful and secure Eurasia is also linked to peace and stability in Afghanistan,â he said, adding that India would continue its development and humanitarian assistance to the Afghan people.
On the West Asia crisis, Modi said conflicts in one region can have repercussions across the world, affecting âenergy security, maritime trade, and supply chains of the entire worldâ.âThe countries of the Global South have to bear the maximum brunt of this. Therefore, India's call has been that the solution to all tensions and wars is not possible on the battlefield, but only through Dialogue and Diplomacy,â he said.
The Prime Minister also flagged drug trafficking as a serious threat to the younger generation and regional security, calling for stronger cooperation through SCO mechanisms dealing with security threats, organised crime, information security and narcotics. âWe must make them effective mediums for practical coordination and timely action,â PM Modi said.
He further stressed that SCO cooperation should translate into tangible benefits for people, with people-to-people ties placed at the centre of the groupingâs future agenda.âThe true measure of our success should be how many new opportunities our efforts have created for young people, how many new markets have opened up for our entrepreneurs, how much our farmers have benefited from technology, and how much better the lives of our citizens have become,â he said.
Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov is hosting the summit and serving as its chairman. PM Modi is attending alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other leaders of SCO member states.

headline: The search committee constituted to select the first Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust (SRJTKT) has shortlisted three candidates and submitted their names to the Trust, the committee said on Tuesday (Septe...
full_text:
New Delhi
The search committee constituted to select the first Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust (SRJTKT) has shortlisted three candidates and submitted their names to the Trust, the committee said on Tuesday (September 1, 2026).
The Trust, which oversees the Ram temple in Ayodhya, is expected to choose one of the three candidates at a meeting on Wednesday (September 2, 2026).
The decision to appoint a CEO came amid the controversy over alleged theft and irregularities in the handling of donations at the temple. Following the embezzlement allegations, SRJTKT general secretary Champat Rai and trustee Anil Mishra resigned.
On July 6, the trust announced a major administrative overhaul, including the creation of the CEO post. The move was aimed at strengthening administrative oversight and restoring confidence in the trust’s functioning.
“The trust was also considering changes to its bylaws to formally provide for a CEO and clearly define supervisory responsibilities, particularly in relation to fund management,” a source close to the selection committee informed.
Selection process
To select the CEO, a three-member committee was formed comprising retired Justice Pramod Kohli, retired Lieutenant General V.K. Chaturvedi and scientist Dr. Suresh Haware.
The selection process began in July after the committee finalised the eligibility criteria, which included experience in temple administration and being a “staunch Hindu”. Applications were closed on July 18, following which online interviews were held in early August. Sixteen candidates were subsequently called to Ayodhya for in-person interactions on August 11 and 12.
“A total of 5,585 applications were screened using AI-assisted tools as well as manual review,” said search committee secretary Sameer Panda. The evaluation was conducted by teams based in Delhi-NCR, Pune and Sambalpur in Odisha, Mr. Panda said.
The names of the shortlisted candidates have not been disclosed, but sources said the panel includes candidates from government and private sectors. The three names have not been placed in any order of preference.
The committee’s final report was presented at a meeting attended by trust treasurer Swami Govind Dev Giri, Mahant Dinendra Das, acting general secretary Krishna Mohan and Ayodhya District Magistrate Shashank Tripathi.

headline: PM Modi, Putin and Xi make a statement with handshake moment at SCO Summit
full_text:
PM Modi, Putin and Xi make a statement with handshake moment at SCO Summit
The moment between PM Modi, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping was captured as the SCO leaders gathered for the official family photograph, a traditional feature of the annual summit.
PM Narendra Modi, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping shared a striking moment of camaraderie at the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek on Tuesday, with the three leaders smiling and forming a chain as they shook hands.
The moment was captured as SCO leaders gathered for the official family photograph, a traditional feature of the annual summit.
A video posted by the Kremlin pool captured the Prime Minister and the two Presidents smiling as they held hands in a brief but striking display of bonhomie.
The Kremlin pool shared the video with the caption: “Strategic alignment: Russia-India-China.”
While PM Modi and Putin held a bilateral meeting on Monday, no one-on-one meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping was scheduled.
As PM Modi briefly exchanged words with Xi and Putin before posing for the group photograph earlier in the day, Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif was seen approaching the Russian President moments later.
As Putin walked away from the podium, Sharif appeared to stop him by holding his hand before engaging him in a conversation.
The latest visuals bring back memories of another much-noticed PM Modi-Putin-Xi moment at the 25th SCO Summit in China last year.
At the time, the Prime Minister and Putin were welcomed by Xi as they entered the summit venue, following which the three leaders engaged in a lengthy conversation marked by handshakes and laughter.
Their interaction soon turned into a huddle as their aides gathered around them, with the conversation lasting nearly a minute and a half.

headline: NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress leader Abhishek Banerjee on Tuesday claimed that Bharatiya Janata Party-led West Bengal government was pursuing "political vendetta" against his party after he was questioned for nearly six hours by Kolkata Police over t...

NEW DELHI: Trinamool Congress leader Abhishek Banerjee on Tuesday claimed that Bharatiya Janata Party-led West Bengal government was pursuing "political vendetta" against his party after he was questioned for nearly six hours by Kolkata Police over the removal of an unauthorised billboard.The Trinamool Congress MP from Diamond Harbour said that the Suvendu Adhikari-led government was selectively targeting TMC by removing its signboards, freezing party accounts and initiating cases against its leaders and workers."If they think they can silence us through false cases and arrests, they are mistaken," Abhishek Banerjee told reporters as he walked out of Shakespeare Sarani police station after questioning."They can question me but I am not scared, they are," he said, adding that the police action was a bid to weaken TMC.The TMC leader also alleged that several party workers arrested in connection with the incident were subjected to "custodial torture".

He secured bail yesterday, but 12 or 13 others remain in judicial custody," he alleged.This comes days after a confrontation broke out when Kolkata Municipal Corporation officials, accompanied by police, entered the office premises to dismantle the billboard mounted on an iron structure facing the road.

headline: A Delhi-bound IndiGo flight with 229 passengers on board returned to Goa about 30 minutes after takeoff on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) and made an emergency landing at Manohar International Airport after one engine failed mid-air, sources said.

A Delhi-bound IndiGo flight with 229 passengers on board returned to Goa about 30 minutes after takeoff on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) and made an emergency landing at Manohar International Airport after one engine failed mid-air, sources said.
The aircraft landed safely at the airport in Mopa, North Goa.
“IndiGo flight 6E 2102, which departed for Delhi at 9.16 a.m., returned to Goa after reporting a failure in one of its engines. The Air Traffic Control declared a full emergency around 9.30 a.m., and the aircraft landed safely on runway 28 at 9.51 a.m.,” a source said.

The SCO gathering was attended by PM Modi and Sharif, along with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russia's Vladimir Putin, Iran's Masoud Pezeshkian and others.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Tuesday that the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) needs to work together to dismantle the entire “ecosystem of terrorism” and its financing, in the presence of several world leaders at the summit, of which Pakistan is a part.
He said, "We must dismantle the entire ecosystem of terrorist financing, recruitment, radicalisation and safe havens.
Countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy and provide shelter and support to terrorists must receive a strong message that terrorism can never be a strategic asset."
Deep Dive
Conflicts should be resolved through dialogue: PM
The prime minister said all wars and conflicts around the world should be settled through dialogue and diplomacy, adding that battlefields cannot provide a solution.
Modi also said connectivity projects should uphold the sovereignty and territorial integrity of every country.
His remarks on tackling terrorism came at a time when India is continuing its efforts to put pressure on Pakistan over cross-border terrorist activities.
Modi on India's vision for SCO
On India's core vision for the SCO, Modi said it is based on three key pillars: Security, Connectivity and Opportunity.
He said, "Now is the time to take these three pillars beyond a 'vision' and toward 'concrete outcomes'".
He also urged the 10-member bloc to build on its 25 years of dialogue and cooperation and deliver "tangible outcomes". Modi called on member states to turn their "shared geography into shared opportunities" as the world faces growing uncertainty and instability.
"Today, when the world is passing through uncertainty and instability, we must turn our shared geography into shared opportunities. Through our efforts, we must bring positive changes to the lives of our people, " he said.

The summit has brought together representatives from 10 member states, 15 partner countries and two observer countries, with the gathering focused on strengthening dialogue and cooperation on regional and global issues.

headline: Photos, DNA matching: Indian embassy explains process to bring Nepal flood victims home
full_text:
Photos, DNA matching: Indian embassy explains process to bring Nepal flood victims home
For foreign nationals, the process involves nine steps before the remains can be handed over to their respective countries.
The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu has issued details of the process for identifying and repatriating the mortal remains of victims of the recent flash floods in Nepal, which have claimed more than 1,000 lives.
In a statement issued on September 1, the embassy said the details were provided by Nepali authorities as a follow-up to its August 29 press release on the identification of mortal remains of victims. For foreign nationals, the process involves nine steps before the remains can be handed over to their respective countries.
Also Read: Blasting hillsides, pumping oxygen: Inside the race to reach 600 trapped in Nepal's flooded tunnels
Deep Dive
What are the steps
As per the Government of Nepal, the following steps will be required for handing over the mortal remains of foreign nationals:
1.Documentation of mortal remains
2. Recording photographs and details of the mortal remains
3. Post-mortem examination
4. Verification of cause of death
5. Formal establishment of identification
6. Collection of fingerprints, DNA or forensic samples
7. Verification of the deceased's passport or ID
8. Completion of embassy/consular coordination
9. Completion of handover/release memo and receipt
The first four steps, documentation, recording photographs and details, post-mortem examination, and verification of the cause of death, will be carried out by Nepali authorities.
Check official advisory here:
What if families can identify the remains?
If relatives are able to identify the mortal remains through photographs and descriptions published on the Nepal Police website, the Embassy of India in Kathmandu will help coordinate with local authorities for the handover and repatriation process.
The Nepal government has temporarily interred a large number of mortal remains to prevent health risks. Identification of these remains will require DNA matching with first-degree relatives.
Also Read: Nepal rescue operation: Flash flood toll surpasses 950 as rescuers struggle through mud and debris
What about unidentified remains
Where identification is not possible, or where the mortal remains have been temporarily interred, the Nepal government will facilitate DNA matching.
Nepali authorities are collecting DNA samples from the mortal remains to create their DNA profiles. First-degree relatives of those reported missing can either send their DNA profiles by email to Nepal Police or provide blood samples along with preliminary information required by the authorities.
For assistance from the Indian Embassy, relatives can also copy their DNA profiles to the embassy's flood-support email address.
Further details on DNA profiling are available through the Nepal Police website and its helpline.
The Embassy of India has also provided three helpline numbers, with WhatsApp facility, for further assistance and enquiries: +977 985 131 6807, +977 970 910 7500 and +977 981 032 6117.

headline: SC Collegium recommends new chief justices for Rajasthan, MP, J&K-Ladakh HCs
full_text:
SC Collegium recommends new chief justices for Rajasthan, MP, J&K-Ladakh HCs
The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended new chief justices for Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Courts. The move awaits the Centre's formal appointments.
The Supreme Court Collegium, headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, has recommended new chief justices for the Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh high courts. The recommendations were made at its meeting on Monday.
The collegium, comprising the CJI and Justices Vikram Nath, BV Nagarathna, MM Sundresh and PS Narasimha, recommended Justice Sanjay K Agrawal for the Rajasthan High Court, Justice Alpesh Yeshwant Kogje for the Madhya Pradesh High Court, and Justice Dr Pushpendra Singh Bhati for the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court.
Justice Agrawal, whose parent high court is the Chhattisgarh High Court, has been recommended as the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court. The recommendation comes against the backdrop of allegations made by Supreme Court judge Justice Sandeep Mehta against the Rajasthan High Court's Acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma.
Justice Mehta, whose parent high court is also the Rajasthan High Court, had written three letters to the CJI on August 2, 10 and 17, urging the appointment of a permanent chief justice from outside the state.
Justice Kogje, a judge of the Gujarat High Court, has been recommended as the Chief Justice of the Madhya Pradesh High Court. Justice Bhati, whose parent high court is Rajasthan, has been recommended as the Chief Justice of the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court.
Separately, at its meeting held on August 6, the collegium recommended the appointment of Justice Krushna Ram Mohapatra, a judge of the Orissa High Court, as the Chief Justice of the Chhattisgarh High Court. The recommendation was made in view of the retirement of the incumbent Chief Justice on September 4.
These recommendations will take effect after the government makes the necessary appointments under the constitutional process.

headline: Manipur Deputy Chief Minister Losii Dikho has urged the Centre to take punitive measures against fellow Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen for “colluding” with a Kuki insurgent group allegedly involved in the killing of Naga civilians.
full_text:
Manipur Deputy Chief Minister Losii Dikho has urged the Centre to take punitive measures against fellow Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen for “colluding” with a Kuki insurgent group allegedly involved in the killing of Naga civilians.
Mr. Dikho and eight other Naga MLAs also threatened to pull out of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led government in Manipur if no action is taken against Ms. Kipgen and the leaders of Kuki-Zo extremist groups.
Five of these MLAs, including Mr. Dikho, are from the Naga People’s Front (NPF), two are from the BJP, one from the National People’s Party, and one is an Independent.
They listed their demand in a letter to Union Home Minister Amit Shah on August 29. “The letter was hand-delivered today (Monday),” Mr. Dikho said.
In the letter, the MLAs demanded the arrest of Kuki-Zo leaders, who publicly claimed responsibility for the killing and dismemberment of six Naga civilians, whose mutilated bodies were recovered on June 10, almost a month after they were abducted.
They also demanded the arrest of Thangboi Kipgen, the head of the extremist Kuki National Front (Presidential) faction and Ms. Kipgen’s husband.
“Initiate action against Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen as her office is colluding with the Kuki militant group led by her husband Thangboi Kipgen…” the letter read.
The Naga MLAs further demanded the immediate abrogation of the Suspension of Operation agreement that the Centre had signed with 25 Kuki-Zo rebel groups in 2008, citing alleged repeated violations and acts of terror against civilians.
“When the mutilated bodies of the six Naga men are still unclaimed in protest against the non-arrest of the perpetrators, another four Naga men were mercilessly killed in the IT road ambush on August 27, carried out by the Kuki militants,” the MLAs wrote, citing some other incidents of violence.
They warned that if action were not initiated, they would be “unable to defend or adequately respond to the challenges raised by the public concerning our continued support to the Government of Manipur.”
“This step is being taken solely in the larger interest of the people of Manipur, and out of absolute necessity,” they further wrote.
Manipur had 10 Naga MLAs. One of them, N. Kayisii of the NPP, died in January 2025.

SC questions CBI, ED's tardiness in Leaps and Bounds probe linked to Abhishek Banerjee, seeks interrogation details by Sept 7.
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday lashed out at CBI and ED for getting active in the probe against âLeaps and Boundsâ â a company allegedly linked to former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjeeâs nephew and Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee and tainted in the SSC recruitment scam â for getting huge sums from the previous TMC govt, and questioned the state policeâs sudden alacrity to probe it for the same illegalities.While seeking custodial interrogation of Sumit Roy, PA to TMC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee, in the illegal sale of govt land as private property, solicitor general Tushar Mehta mentioned Royâs involvement in the transfer of Rs 30 crore from a party account to Leaps and Bounds.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, âThe less said about Leaps and Bounds investigation, the better it is.â It noted Calcutta HC judgesâ frustration over the dragging of feet by CBI and ED in investigating the firm.Mehta justified the probe, asking whether the state police should not investigate the land scam just because one agency erred. He said custodial interrogation was required as Roy was feigning lack of knowledge about the transfer of lakhs of rupees in cash.
Royâs counsel Gopal Sankaranarayanan said he had mistakenly submitted during the last hearing that accused had the right to silence.
He said Roy had answered questions put to him during 11 days of interrogation.Bench asked Bengal police to submit by Sept 7 details of the interrogation relating to financial transactions. It said, âWhen we see a case like this, the courtâs job is to enable a fair investigation.â It said it wanted to examine agenciesâ âeagernessâ to arrest.

headline: Bihar and Jharkhand sign pact to end 25-year Sone river water dispute
full_text:
Bihar and Jharkhand sign pact to end 25-year Sone river water dispute
Bihar and Jharkhand signed an MoU in Delhi to share Sone river water. The agreement ends a nearly 25-year dispute and is expected to aid farmers and drinking water supply.
Bihar and Jharkhand on Monday signed a memorandum of understanding to share 7.75 million acre-feet of water from the Sone river, a move the Centre said had "permanently resolved" a nearly 25-year-old dispute between the two states. The agreement was signed in New Delhi in the presence of Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
Shah said the pact would help ensure irrigation and drinking water for large populations in both states and would directly benefit lakhs of farmers. He said the agreement showed that long-pending issues could be settled through dialogue and in the spirit of cooperative federalism.
Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Union Jal Shakti Minister CR Patil, Bihar's Deputy Chief Minister, the Union Home Secretary, and senior officials from the Centre and the two states were present at the signing ceremony.
In a post on X, Shah said, "It will directly benefit lakhs of farmers in both states and give new momentum to the development of rural areas. If all states move forward as one team, there is no problem that cannot be resolved."
Speaking at the event, he said the agreement to settle the nearly 25-year-old water dispute showed how any problem could be solved through dialogue in the spirit of cooperative federalism. He added that issues linked to vast geographical areas, farmers, rural regions and drinking water supplies in the two states had been "permanently resolved" through the agreement.
Officials said that in 1973, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and undivided Bihar had entered into an agreement on sharing the waters of the Sone river and the cost of the Bansagar dam in Madhya Pradesh.
The dispute began in 2000 after Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar. Jharkhand sought a larger share of water from the Bansagar project because a large part of its catchment area fell within the state, while Bihar relied on the 1973 agreement to press its claim.
Shah said this was the fourth water-related pact between states this year. He called it an "excellent" example of "Team Bharat" and cooperative federalism championed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said states had their own distinct identities, and if they moved forward as "Team Bharat" within the national context, no problem was beyond resolution.
According to Shah, the agreement will ensure adequate water for drinking and irrigation for a large population in Bihar's Bhojpur, Buxar, Rohtas, Kaimur, Aurangabad, Arwal, Gaya and Patna districts. He added, "Moreover, water would become available for irrigation and drinking purposes in the Palamu, Garhwa, and other regions of Jharkhand."
An official statement said Soren and Choudhary thanked Modi and Shah for resolving the issue. It added, "On the initiative of Home Minister Amit Shah, long-pending water disputes between various states that had been unresolved for several decades are being resolved through the Inter-State Council; so far this year, four historic agreements have been reached."
The statement said that on July 7, an agreement on settlement of outstanding payments was signed among the Narmada Award beneficiary states, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, in Shah's presence. It said the pact resolved long-pending disputes over cost-sharing for the construction of the Sardar Sarovar Project through a one-time settlement of dues.
It added that on June 29, Rajasthan and Haryana signed an agreement on the construction and implementation of the Yamuna Water Project, enabling Rajasthan to use the water allocated to it under the 1994 agreement on sharing usable surface water in the Upper Yamuna Basin.
It also said that during a meeting chaired by Shah on June 16, a consensus was reached on the long-pending Kishau Multipurpose Dam Project, with Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan agreeing to a memorandum of understanding for its implementation.
With Monday's agreement, Bihar and Jharkhand have settled a dispute that began after Jharkhand's creation in 2000, while the Centre has presented it as the latest in a series of inter-state water agreements reached this year.

headline: ‘Women entering public sphere will cause destruction’: Keralam Muslim cleric’s remarks spark row
full_text:
‘Women entering public sphere will cause destruction’: Keralam Muslim cleric’s remarks spark row
A prominent Muslim cleric in Keralam has drawn criticism after exhorting women to remain confined to their homes and claiming that their entry into the public sphere would “lead to destruction”
A prominent Muslim cleric in Keralam has drawn criticism after exhorting women to remain confined to their homes and claiming that their entry into the public sphere would “lead to destruction”.
The controversial remarks were made on Sunday by 95-year-old Kanthapuram AP Aboobacker Musaliyar, general secretary of the AP faction of the Samastha Kerala Jem-iyyathul Ulama, a prominent body of Sunni Muslim clerics in the state, at an Islamic conference in Kochi.
“If women enter the public sphere, it will lead to destruction. To avoid this, Islam instituted the concept of ‘purdah’. The holy Quran states that women must remain confined inside their homes and avoid coming out in public. It was the right decision,” Musaliyar was quoted as saying at the conference.
Deep Dive
He also hit out at those questioning his authority to speak on matters concerning the Muslim community.
“Samastha has been studying Islam for over 100 years, and that’s why we have the right to say this to the Muslim community. We will continue to say it. We are not the kind of people who get afraid and run away,” he claimed.
The remarks came days after the AP faction of Samastha issued a circular seeking to restrict Muslim women’s participation in public events. The circular stated that “displaying young women among unrelated men on roads and public stages is not appropriate for believers and is not permissible.”
It asked mosques, madrasas and mahal committees to ensure Islamic celebrations do not cross the limits of religion. The circular followed several Milad-e-Sharif events organised by youth clubs outside the purview of mosques and mahal committees, where women actively participated alongside men.
Keralam Women and Child Welfare Minister Bindhu Krishna condemned Musaliyar’s comments on Monday.
“While the Constitution allows everyone to express their opinions freely, such a stand (of Musaliyar) is not fit to propagate in Kerala, India or the rest of the world. Women in our society have equal rights under the Constitution. We are a country that upholds gender equality. Women faced a dark age, but with the help of social reformers and others, we have fought our way in and become part of the mainstream,” Krishna said.
Congress leader and home minister Ramesh Chennithala said he did not support restricting women in public spaces.
“He (Kanthapuram) can say what he wants. But I do not conform to the idea of restricting women in the public sphere,” he said.
Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) leader and Keralam Local Self-Government Minister KM Shaji, however, declined to comment on the remarks.
“I don’t want to say anything,” he told reporters.
