The Union minister’s party filed a complaint at Parliament Police Station against Bhardwaj, alleging that he had falsely used Paswan’s name and publicly claimed an association with the LJP(RV) president, reported news agency ANI.
The party has urged the police to register an FIR against Bhardwaj and formally record that he has no association with the party or the matter in question.
It has also called for strict action against the accused.
Will ensure justice for Aazad's father: Paswan
The complaint comes after Paswan earlier said he was "taking full responsibility" for ensuring justice for CJP activist Nishu Aazad's father, who was attacked and seriously injured during protests at Jantar Mantar.
"In public life, many people come to meet us. But if somebody claims, on this very basis to be a personal acquaintance of ours, then that is a misuse of our name. The attacker has sought to give the impression that action has not been taken against him because of me and my party. I have lodged a formal complaint against this misuse of my name," Paswan was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.
He added, "It is indeed a serious matter that the student activist's father was beaten so severely that he could have died. The attacker has the temerity to brag about the incident on TV, and he roams scot-free. I take full responsibility to ensure justice to the aggrieved family by pursuing the matter with Delhi police."
Swatantra Bhardwaj detained
Bhardwaj was taken into custody in Uttar Pradesh’s Bulandshahr on Friday, just hours after Delhi Police allegedly assured CJP protesters that he would be arrested within 72 hours.
Police said Bhardwaj had tried to flee but was caught, HT has learnt.

headline: The Lokayukta has registered a suo motu case over the collapse of a concrete ceiling at a government primary school in Mugalolli Tanda, Bagalkot district, during class hours, in which six students were injured.
full_text:
The Lokayukta has registered a suo motu case over the collapse of a concrete ceiling at a government primary school in Mugalolli Tanda, Bagalkot district, during class hours, in which six students were injured.
According to the Lokayukta, the school building was reportedly already in a dilapidated condition, and parents had earlier expressed concerns over the safety of the structure. The ceiling collapsed while classes were in progress, injuring six students. The children were shifted to a hospital for treatment, and their injuries were reported to be minor. All six students are said to be safe.
Taking serious note of the incident, the Lokayukta has directed its police wing to conduct random inspections of government primary schools across Bagalkot district and submit a comprehensive report on the condition of school buildings.
The Education Department has also been directed to conduct a safety audit of every school in the district. The audit will cover the structural condition of buildings, student safety, basic infrastructure, cleanliness and hygiene, playgrounds, compound walls, toilets and the availability of safe drinking water, among other facilities.
The Lokayukta has directed that classes must not be conducted in any portion of a school building identified as unsafe. Until the structure is certified safe for use, arrangements must be made to conduct classes at an alternative location. A qualified engineer has also been directed to carry out a structural safety assessment of the entire school building and submit a report.
As part of the suo motu proceedings, officials have been asked to submit details regarding the exact date and circumstances of the ceiling collapse, the number of students present in the classroom, particulars of the six injured students, the nature of their injuries, and the treatment provided.
Officials from the State Education Department, Dharwad Division, Bagalkot District Administration, Zilla Panchayat, Education Department and the Panchayat Raj Engineering Department, along with the headmaster of Mugalolli Tanda Government Primary School, have been issued notices in connection with the case.

headline: Jaishankar's terse reaffirmation of India's position that its energy sourcing is driven by national interests
full_text:
Jaishankar's terse reaffirmation of India's position that its energy sourcing is driven by national interests
The Russia-Ukraine conflict will be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy and not by dwelling over who is buying oil from where, said external affairs minister S Jaishankar rejecting the Western narrative that countries buying energy from Russia are bankrolling President Vladimir Putin's war.Reiterating India's stance, the minister stressed that while the responsibility of ending the conflict rested with the parties involved, New Delhi stood ready to extend any necessary assistance to facilitate peace. Jaishankar was speaking alongside his Ukraine counterpart Andrii Sybiha in Kyiv after a meeting in which he recalled PM Narendra Modi's message to Putin last week that the endless war must now give way to end of war. The minister also called on President Volodymyr Zelensky later to discuss "approaches to end the ongoing conflict".Jaishankar's terse reaffirmation of India's position that its energy sourcing is driven by national interests and the need to ensure adequate, affordable and reliable supplies came in response to a question if India would consider cutting down purchase of Russian oil because of US sanctions."It's important that you get the challenges of providing energy for 1.4 billion people at a time when the world energy situation is very difficult.
Ukraine has its perspective, which we respect. And we have ours, which I would expect others to also respect," said the minister. "This conflict, which is today in its fifth year, will not be solved because somebody is buying or not buying oil or minerals or fertilisers. This conflict will be solved by dialogue, by diplomacy, by negotiations ... and that's why it is something we would encourage."Zelensky later said that even while Jaishankar was in Ukraine, Russia launched jet-powered Shahed drones that were developed not without Iran's help. Zelensky also thanked India for its commitment to ending "this unjust war - Russia's war against Ukraine". He added, "This certainly must not be a time of war. Peace is needed. This is India's clear position."This was Jaishankar's first visit to Ukraine since he accompanied Modi for his landmark trip to Kyiv, months after his visit to Moscow. Asked if India was looking forward to hosting Zelensky, the EAM did not confirm if he was going to extend an invitation to him.
He invited Sybiha to visit India, though. Jaishankar reiterated Modi's message that each passing day of conflict only means more deaths and more destruction. "Understandably, it is for the parties involved to find a way. But, if India can be of any help in any manner, we are ready, and this was the core of my discussion so far with Sybiha," he said.Among other related issues raised were attacks on commercial shipping, with Jaishankar underlining that Indian seafarers man ships of many flags and have been among the casualties. "The impact on shipping is also significantly affecting many nations of the Global South," he said.In his remarks, Sybiha briefed Jaishankar about the "escalation from Russia and systemic Russian attacks on civilian ships, ports and infrastructure" and expressed condolences for the loss of Indian lives.

headline: Worm found in Blinkit egg, Mangaluru officials raid outlet after consumer complaint

Worm found in Blinkit egg, Mangaluru officials raid outlet after consumer complaint
Food safety officials inspected a Blinkit facility in Mangaluru after a consumer alleged a worm was found in an egg order. The storage room was sealed for cleaning as authorities prepare to seek an explanation and review further action.
Food safety officials inspected a Blinkit online retail facility in Mangaluru after a consumer allegedly found a worm inside an egg purchased through the quick-commerce platform, officials said on Thursday.
The complaint was made to Karnataka Health Minister U T Khader after the consumer claimed that some of the eggs delivered through Blinkit were damaged and that a worm was found inside one of them.
Acting on the complaint, food safety officials inspected the Blinkit facility operating from the Falnir Square building in the city's Falnir area.
During the inspection, officials found packets containing broken eggs at the facility. The staff were directed to immediately remove the affected packets from sale and dispose of them.
STORAGE ROOM SEALED FOR CLEANING
As a precautionary measure, officials temporarily sealed the food storage room to facilitate thorough cleaning and sanitisation of the premises. The department said a notice would be issued to the establishment, seeking an explanation over the incident.
Further action will be decided after the inspection findings are assessed, and the facility management submits its response, officials said.
The complaint comes amid increasing scrutiny of food safety practices at quick-commerce and online grocery facilities, particularly over the storage and handling of perishable products.

headline: Mumbai: India's weather office has forecast rains in September that are below average, with temperatures above average, after accruing a rainfall deficit in August, amid a strengthening El Niño weather phenomenon.The monsoon has been erratic until no...
full_text: Mumbai: India's weather office has forecast rains in September that are below average, with temperatures above average, after accruing a rainfall deficit in August, amid a strengthening El Niño weather phenomenon.The monsoon has been erratic until now, with many subdivisions receiving rainfall substantially below average, while only a handful got average rainfall.Even in areas where seasonal rainfall was normal, prolonged dry spells followed by intense downpours left totals looking healthy but stressed farming.Below-average rains in September could widen the seasonal monsoon deficit to make this India's weakest monsoon in nearly two decades..Monthly rainfall over India most likely to be below normal in September: IMD. Why is September rainfall more crucial for crops this year?The monsoon rains arrived late in June, with rainfall 35 per cent below normal in the first month of the season. The weak start delayed planting of summer crops, such as cotton, soybean, corn and rice, because of inadequate soil moisture.These crops were already facing moisture stress after below-average rainfall in August and are entering critical stages such as pod formation and grain filling, when adequate moisture is essential.If below-average rainfall persists through September, yields could fall.What roles does September rainfall play for winter crops? The monsoon typically begins to retreat from India's northwest around September 17, to withdraw completely by mid-October, the month when farmers usually start planting winter crops such as wheat, rapeseed, corn and chickpeas.September rainfall determines soil moisture and low moisture can hamper seed germination and crop growth. In some states, farmers could suffer yield losses and lower incomes if soil moisture stays below normal.Will a below-average monsoon bring changes in India's agricultural trade policy?India's agricultural production and trade policy is heavily influenced by the monsoon, with this year unlikely to be an exception.Below-normal rainfall is affecting the growth of water-intensive sugar cane, which sugar mills will start crushing from next month, and is likely to reduce new cane planting for the next season.Lower sugar output could force India to boost imports beyond the 1 million tons of raw sugar it has already allowed free of duty this year.The rainfall deficit is also likely to reduce yields of summer-sown soybeans and peanuts and curb the area planted with winter-sown rapeseed. This could force India to increase imports of vegetable oils from Indonesia, Malaysia, Argentina, Russia and Ukraine.Pulses such as chickpeas, pigeon peas and green gram are largely grown in rain-fed areas. A decline in production could lead to an increase in India's imports from Myanmar, Australia, Canada and African countries.Cotton production could also suffer, potentially prompting New Delhi to allow limited duty-free imports to bridge any domestic supply shortfall.India is the world's second-largest producer of wheat, cotton and sugar and the world's largest producer and exporter of rice. Large rice stocks, however, give New Delhi greater room to allow exports to continue without interruption..IMD forecasts 94% of average rainfall as India braces for below-normal monsoon. How does the monsoon affect inflation and central bank policy?The monsoon is emerging as a fresh risk to India's inflation outlook. Food makes up more than a third of the consumer-price basket, making rainfall crucial for household costs and Reserve Bank of India policy.Above-average rainfall over the past two years helped boost food supplies and contain inflation, giving the central bank room to cut borrowing costs. A weaker monsoon could reverse that trend if crop losses push up food prices.Higher commodity costs linked to the Iran conflict add to the risk. Retail inflation rose to 4.45 per cent in July, while food inflation climbed to 5.52 per cent.A mix of weaker growth and higher inflation would complicate the RBI's policy choices, while potentially deterring foreign investment and putting further pressure on the rupee.

headline: India opens forensic labs to identify Nepal flood victims through DNA profiling
full_text:
India opens forensic labs to identify Nepal flood victims through DNA profiling
India has opened its forensic laboratories to collect DNA samples from relatives of people missing in Nepal's flash floods. The step could speed up identification of mortal remains and support grieving families across the border.
India will make the services of central and state-level forensic laboratories available to help identify the mortal remains of people missing after the flash floods in Nepal, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Thursday. The move is aimed at helping first-degree biological relatives living in India provide samples for DNA profiling.
The decision comes as Nepal continues rescue and recovery work after the August 26 floods. According to Nepalese authorities, the death toll has risen to at least 1,259, more than 12,000 people have been rescued, and around 5,000 remain missing.
The MEA said first-degree biological relatives in India, including father, mother, son, daughter or sibling, may have their biological samples collected and DNA profiles prepared at Central Forensic Science Laboratories, State Forensic Science Laboratories, laboratories of the National Forensic Sciences University, and NABL-accredited laboratories with DNA profiling capability.
In a press statement on Tuesday, the Embassy of India in Kathmandu had outlined the available information on procedures for identifying the mortal remains of the flash flood victims. Against this backdrop, and as an additional step to support the ongoing identification process, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs has decided to make available the services of CFSLs, SFSLs and NFSU laboratories in India for "DNA profiling of first-degree biological relatives of persons who remain missing following the flash flood in Nepal", the MEA said.
The ministry also shared a list of government forensic science laboratories with DNA profiling facilities. "As advised by the Nepal Police, Autosomal STR DNA profiling may be undertaken for the purpose of identification, subject to the technical requirements communicated by the Nepali authorities. The helpline number in this regard is: +977 9841 6160 95," it said.
Once prepared, the DNA profiles, along with the preliminary information required by the Nepali authorities, may be sent by email to dnacodis@nepalpolice.gov.np for comparison with DNA profiles obtained from unidentified mortal remains, the statement said. For facilitation and coordination by the Embassy of India in Kathmandu, a copy of the DNA profile may also be sent to eoikathmandufloodsupport@gmail.com, it added.
The flash floods were triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border and devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal. India has now opened its forensic laboratory network to help families in India support the identification process as search and rescue operations continue in Nepal.

headline: The Karnataka State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) has designated Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital in Bengaluru as the nodal centre for collecting DNA samples from first-degree relatives of victims from Karnataka reported missing in Nepal.

The Karnataka State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) has designated Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital in Bengaluru as the nodal centre for collecting DNA samples from first-degree relatives of victims from Karnataka reported missing in Nepal.
The decision has been taken to facilitate the identification and repatriation of mortal remains of foreign nationals in Nepal, following a September 1 press note issued by the Embassy of India in Kathmandu.
According to an order issued by KSDMA, the hospital will coordinate the verification of first-degree relationships between relatives and missing victims and collect DNA samples for profiling and further processing.
Dr. Nagesh Kuppast, Professor and Head of the Department of Forensic Medicine at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, has been designated as the nodal officer. He will be responsible for verifying the relationship of those providing samples with the victims and overseeing the collection of samples. Dr. Vadiraj B. Pokkan, Resident Medical Officer, has also been designated as a coordinating doctor.
KSDMA has advised relatives to carry a recent passport-size photograph, government-issued identity proof such as Aadhaar, and other relevant documents establishing their identity and relationship with the missing person.
The collected samples will be forwarded to the Forensic Science Laboratory for DNA profiling and comparison with DNA profiles from unidentified mortal remains in Nepal, as per the prescribed procedure.

headline: India and Belgium signed deals to deepen defence and clean-energy ties and agreed to double bilateral trade

India and Belgium signed deals to deepen defence and clean-energy ties and agreed to double bilateral trade
New Delhi: India and Belgium signed deals to deepen defence and clean-energy ties and agreed to double bilateral trade within five years as PM Modi held talks with Belgian counterpart Bart De Wever, the first Belgian PM to visit India in nearly two decades, reports Sachin Parashar.Following the talks, Modi pitched India's 7.8% growth in the last quarter as an opportunity for the world. In a joint statement with De Wever, Modi said global conflicts were causing major upheaval, disrupting food, fuel and supply chains, and creating uncertainty across sectors."Today, India's growth story is becoming a source of confidence and new opportunities for the world," said Modi.PM Narendra Modi announced a mechanism to fast-track investment between the two countries.Belgium accounted for $4.2bn of FDI inflows from April 2000 to Dec 2025, making it the 18th-largest source of FDI into India. De Weverâs visit resulted in 10 major outcomes â five MoUs, including two to boost indigenous defence manufacturing, co-design and co-development, and another five announcements, including appointment of a defence attache in Indian embassy in Brussels.Asked whether there was any discussion on pending extradition of fugitive Mehul Choksi, who remains in a Belgium jail, MEA secretary Sibi George said law enforcement cooperation was an âimportant topic of discussion and an important aspect of the relationship with Belgiumâ.
âAll issues of concern and interest are discussed at all levels of our engagement ... India remains committed to ensuring that fugitives are brought back to the country to face the law,â he added.Modi said ties with Belgium had expanded beyond traditional sectors. âDefence and security cooperation is a key pillar of our relationship. Today, we agreed to enhance military exchanges and training cooperation between the two countries,â said the PM. âThe agreements between our govts and defence industries will open up opportunities for defence co-development and co-production. We will also further strengthen intelligence sharing and cooperation between our agencies to combat crime,â he added.PM said unprecedented cooperation, including the recently concluded FTA between India and EU â two of the worldâs largest democratic blocs â would give a boost to global stability, development and shared prosperity.The leaders also discussed Ukraine and West Asia, underlining their support for the rule of law, dialogue and diplomacy. In a joint statement, they stressed the importance of ensuring the safety and security of maritime routes and maintaining safe and unimpeded maritime shipping.âWhether it is Ukraine or West Asia, we support all efforts aimed at an early end to conflicts and the restoration of peace,â the PM added.The leaders called for closer partnerships in semiconductor technologies to create resilient and advanced technology ecosystems in both countries, with Modi saying that Belgiumâs expertise in semiconductors and Indiaâs scale complement each other.
The two leaders agreed to soon conclude a migration and mobility agreement to facilitate talent mobility.Belgium also expressed solidarity with India in the fight against terrorism. De Wever condemned the attack on civilians at Pahalgam in April 2025. âBoth leaders underscored their commitment to a comprehensive/global approach to counterterrorism and affirmed that terrorism, in any form and manifestation and anywhere, could never be justified and called for its perpetrators to be held accountable in accordance with the law,â said the statement.The leaders also focused on clean energy, critical minerals and reliable supply chains. âThe MoU on Renewable Energy signed today will give momentum to our sustainability cooperation. In critical minerals, we have decided to enhance ties in processing & recycling,â PM said.

headline: The Union government informed the Supreme Court on Thursday of its willingness to revert all the vacant National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test-Super Speciality seats (NEET-SS) for in-service government doctors to the State of Tamil Nadu.
full_text:
The Union government informed the Supreme Court on Thursday of its willingness to revert all the vacant National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test-Super Speciality seats (NEET-SS) for in-service government doctors to the State of Tamil Nadu.
Appearing before a Bench headed by Justice P.S. Narasimha, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, for the Centre, submitted that the qualifying percentile for super speciality admissions would be reduced. However, the extent or quantum of such reduction has not yet been decided.
Senior Advocate P. Wilson, appearing for petitioner Tamil Nadu Medical Officers Association, stressed that the State needed to return the vacant seats, as many eligible candidates, mostly doctors serving in rural areas, were awaiting a reduction in the qualifying percentile.
In a previous hearing, the Union government had submitted that out of the 152 seats transferred by the State of Tamil Nadu, approximately 40 seats continued to remain vacant. Mr. Wilson had submitted that all 40 in-service seats must be returned to Tamil Nadu as 111 candidates were awaiting a reduction in the qualifying percentile.
The association had challenged the “premature diversion” of 152 vacant Super Speciality seats earmarked for in-service government doctors in Tamil Nadu to the All India Quota. It had also sought protection of the State’s in-service reservation policy, pending a final decision on reduction of the NEET-SS qualifying percentile.
The petition has submitted that Tamil Nadu had earmarked 219 super speciality seats for in-service candidates for the academic year 2025-2026. Upon completion of two rounds of counselling, only 68 candidates had joined, leaving as many as 152 seats vacant.
“Over 111 in-service candidates remain on the waiting list and are legitimately anticipating a reduction of the qualifying percentile in accordance with the consistent practice followed during previous academic sessions.
A substantial number of these candidates narrowly missed the existing qualifying percentile and would become eligible if the qualifying percentile is reduced/relaxed,” the association said.
The court listed the case next on September 8 to hear from the Centre the extent of reduction in the qualifying percentile.

headline: NEW DELHI: The West Bengal fire department has ordered the evacuation of the basement, sixth and seventh floors of a high-rise building in central Kolkata that houses TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee's office, citing a "lack of fire safety measures", an ...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: The West Bengal fire department has ordered the evacuation of the basement, sixth and seventh floors of a high-rise building in central Kolkata that houses TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee's office, citing a "lack of fire safety measures", an official said on Friday.The order came a day after Banerjee's Camac Street office was ransacked, with the TMC blaming BJP-linked men for the attack. The BJP has denied the allegation.
The fire department said the building's fire safety certificate expired on August 10 and had not been renewed. A joint team of police and fire officials had conducted a floor-by-floor inspection of the premises on Monday."No fire safety measures were traced in the basement of the high-rise. Following that, we served a show-cause notice to the owner of the building and gave them a 48-hour deadline."Since we did not get any response and the deadline passed, we sent them a notice to evacuate the basement, sixth and seventh floors of the building. If the basement of any building has no fire safety measures, it could lead to a big disaster in case of a fire," the official told PTI.
According to the notice issued to the building owner on Friday, the basement, sixth and seventh floors cannot be used until the identified deficiencies are rectified and a valid fire safety certificate is obtained.
The inspection found inadequate firefighting measures on the seventh floor, no designated fire exit and problems with the fire alarm system, the notice said.The development follows a series of incidents involving the same building. A week earlier, authorities removed an "illegal" TMC billboard from the premises, during which private security guards at Banerjee's office, his supporters and some party leaders allegedly scuffled with police and Kolkata Municipal Corporation officials.

headline: Chennai: In a major embarrassment to the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in the Tamil Nadu Assembly Thursday, the party’s Ranipet MLA I. Thahira demanded the immediate closure of a JK Tyre factory in her constituency during the Question Hour. S...
full_text:
Chennai: In a major embarrassment to the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in the Tamil Nadu Assembly Thursday, the party’s Ranipet MLA I. Thahira demanded the immediate closure of a JK Tyre factory in her constituency during the Question Hour. She claimed it was causing severe pollution and operating through the night in the area. However, there is no such JK Tyre manufacturing unit in Ranipet.
Thahira, a first-time MLA, alleged that the unit was damaging the environment and local residents had been protesting without any action from the previous government. “That company must be shut down under our government, we do not need it in our place,” she said.
Environment and Climate Change Minister V. K. Rajeev responded in the House that an official inspection would be ordered and action taken based on the findings. Industries Minister S. Keerthana also responded and said that there is a need to ensure that there are adequate jobs for the youth and it needs to be balanced with proper environmental protection. She also suggested that rules could be framed so that industries continue to operate in the state, while environmental protection is kept in mind.
However, DMK was quick to cross check the issue raised and former Industries Minister and DMK leader T. R. B. Raajaa was among the first to point out the factual error.
In a post on X, he noted that while JK Tyre has a plant in Kancheepuram district near Sriperumbudur, there is no manufacturing facility in Ranipet. He questioned why ministers were responding to a demand about a non-existent factory and called the entire exchange an example of poor governance.
Taking a dig at TVK, he wrote, “…the TVK MLA is said to have called a tyre retreading outlet as ‘JK Tyre Company. Now, one thing is clear. One should not take anything said by the TVK MLAs as hard facts just like their reels. But, wonder why their own govt acknowledged it and even defended it. For them a retail retreading shop seems to be a polluting industry worthy of a question in the Assembly, instead of asking the local authorities to take action. Is this the kind of ‘industry’ they are going after? Hope not!”
The whole incident went viral on social media with netizens suggesting that Thahira may have been referring to smaller tyre vulcanising units in and around Ranipet rather than a full-fledged JK Tyre plant.
JK Tyre’s official list of manufacturing locations confirms its only Tamil Nadu facility is the Chennai Tyre Plant at Kolathur village on the Sriperumbudur-Tambaram Road, roughly 70 km from Ranipet.
Hours later, Industries Minister Keerthana issued a clarification on X. She stated that a reference had been made in the Assembly to a JK Tyre unit in Ranipet, but “on verification, JK Tyre does not have a manufacturing facility in Ranipet”. She added that the environmental concerns raised by the MLA would still be examined to identify the actual unit responsible.
Keerthana also noted that JK Tyre, which recently signed an MoU for expansion at the TN Vettri Conclave, has reiterated that its existing plant strictly follows pollution norms.
DMK leaders and supporters used the episode to take a dig at the ruling party, portraying it as evidence of hasty statements and inadequate homework by first-time legislators.
The episode has also triggered discussion on social media about the need for MLAs to verify basic facts before demanding the closure of industrial units on the floor of the House.
Upon verification, it was found that a small scale tyre melting plant in the name of AK Tyres operates in Ranipet and the tyre manufacturing major was wrongly named for causing pollution by the TVK MLA. Locals confirmed that the unit belonged to a local DMK panchayat president. JK Tyre’s Tamil Nadu plant remains operational in Sriperumbudur, and the company has not commented on the Assembly issue.
(Edited by Viny Mishra)

Because...the TVK MLA is said to have called a tyre retreading outlet as “JKTyre Company” Now, one thing is clear one should not take anything said by the TVK MLAs as hard facts just like their reels. But, Wonder why their own govt acknowledged it and even defended it.” “For them a retail retreading shop seems to be a polluting industry worthy of a question raised in the assembly, instead of asking the local authorities to take action. Is this the kind of “industry” they are going after!” he added.
Later in the evening, Tamil Nadu’s Industries Minister S. Keerthana took to X and posted: A reference was made in the Assembly today to a JK Tyre unit in Ranipet. On verification, JK Tyre does not have a manufacturing facility in Ranipet. The environmental issue raised by the Hon’ble Member will, however, be looked into to identify the concerned non-JK tyre unit and appropriate action will be taken wherever required.” “My response in the House was on a larger and important principle, Tamil Nadu needs industries and jobs, but growth cannot come at the cost of environmental compliance. Both have to go together. JK Tyre has also clarified that its operations are in compliance with all applicable statutory environmental clearances and regulatory requirements. It is also important to place on record that JK Tyre recently reaffirmed its confidence in Tamil Nadu by signing an MoU with Guidance Tamil Nadu at the VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment Conclave for an investment of ₹5,143 crore, with the potential to create 3,510 employment opportunities,” she had mentioned in her post.
JK Tyre issued an official statement in which it said: “With reference to recent comments on our operations in the State, we categorically state that our plant is fully compliant with respect to statutory approvals as on date and will remain so in the future as well. We have not committed any violation of any kind as the health and safety of the communities around our Tamil Nadu facility are central to how we run it. JK Tyre & Industries will continue to meet the highest environmental and manufacturing standards at the plant.”

headline: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court has imposed costs of Rs 1 lakh on the Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) for pursuing a 32-year-old dispute with a bus conductor over payment of 17 months' back wages, terming the prolonged litigation an abuse of the pr...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court has imposed costs of Rs 1 lakh on the Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) for pursuing a 32-year-old dispute with a bus conductor over payment of 17 months' back wages, terming the prolonged litigation an abuse of the process of law.According to PTI report, Justice Amit Mahajan dismissed the DTC's challenge to a 2004 Industrial Tribunal order in favour of the conductor, observing that the department's continued litigation over the limited claim had resulted in avoidable expenditure of public money.The court, in its September 2 order, said the DTC could recover the costs from the officer responsible for pursuing what it described as an "insignificant dispute". Of the Rs 1 lakh imposed, Rs 25,000 will be paid to the Delhi High Legal Services Committee, Rs 50,000 to the PM Relief Fund and Rs 25,000 to the conductor.
What's the dispute
The dispute dates back to November 1994, when the conductor was accused of failing to issue tickets to three passengers despite collecting a total fare of Rs 67. He was suspended following the incident.Although the enquiry officer had ruled in the conductor's favour, the disciplinary authority disagreed and issued a show-cause notice proposing his removal from service.
He was subsequently removed with effect from August 1996.The conductor challenged the action, following which the DTC chairman-cum-managing director set aside his removal. In 1998, the DTC chairman ordered his reinstatement but denied him back wages and reduced his pay scale.The dispute then reached the Industrial Tribunal, which in 2004 held that the punishment was illegal and without basis. It ruled that the conductor was entitled to wages on his regular pay scale, along with arrears arising from the reduced wages and regular wages for the relevant period.The high court stayed the tribunal's order in July 2005, but Justice Mahajan found no legal ground to interfere with the tribunal's findings. The court noted that the DTC had failed to produce the enquiry report or establish a lawful basis for disagreeing with the enquiry officer.
Justice Mahajan said the tribunal had taken a "reasonable and plausible view" based on the material before it and that its findings were neither perverse nor legally unsustainable.The court also criticised the DTC for litigating the issue of 17 months' back wages for 32 years, saying the prolonged proceedings over such a limited claim amounted to an abuse of the process of law and caused unnecessary expenditure of public money.

The first meeting of the Karnataka Artificial Intelligence University (KAIU) consultation committee was held in Bengaluru on Saturday (September 5), bringing together senior leaders from the technology industry, academia and the Karnataka government to discuss the roadmap.

Manjula, secretary, Department of Electronics, IT, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, has been constituted to prepare a roadmap for the phased establishment and operationalisation of the proposed university, said a release.

Among the key points discussed was the launching of certificate, diploma, finishing-school, executive education and reskilling programmes through industry and academic partnerships, ahead of the establishment of the full-fledged university.

headline: The Central Drugs Laboratory (CDL) in Kasauli, Himachal Pradesh, has flagged a batch of Abhayrab vaccine, used against rabies, “not of standard quality (NSG)” and “misbranded” after it failed a potency test, raising concerns about the circulation of ...
full_text:
The Central Drugs Laboratory (CDL) in Kasauli, Himachal Pradesh, has flagged a batch of Abhayrab vaccine, used against rabies, “not of standard quality (NSG)” and “misbranded” after it failed a potency test, raising concerns about the circulation of counterfeits and prompting a probe.
The vaccine samples, bearing batch number KE25012, were seized on April 22 during an enforcement action by the Delhi Police and officials of Delhi’s Drugs Control Department from an “unlicensed residential premises”. They were found to differ from genuine reference samples in packaging, labelling, artwork, QR-code verification, cap colour, and licence details.
Four persons have been arrested by the Delhi Police in connection with the incident so far, and further investigation and appropriate legal action are being undertaken by the competent authorities, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) said in a statement on Saturday (September 5, 2026).
The investigation will now have to establish who manufactured the suspect KE25012 vials and whether any patients received them.
While it is yet to be confirmed whether the misbranded vaccines entered circulation in the country, the CDCSO said that no part of the batch concerned was exported to any other country. The Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI), in a communication dated August 27, has requested all State Drugs Controllers to maintain strict vigilance over the movement, distribution, and availability batch KE25012 of Abhayrab, the CDCSO said.
Drug regulatory and law enforcement agencies are maintaining strict and continuous surveillance against illegal manufacture, distribution and supply of misbranded and spurious drugs, with coordinated action being undertaken to identify and disrupt unauthorised drug supply networks and safeguard the quality and safety of medicines available to the public, the regulator said.
Indian Immunologicals Ltd. (IIL), which manufactures Abhayrab through its Human Biologicals Institute (HBI), has said that the concerned vaccines bearing batch number KE25012 were not produced by the company.
In a statement issued on Friday (September 4, 2026), IIL said the genuine KE25012 batch had undergone the required testing and was released on November 7, 2025. The company said the batch comprised 83,370 vials and was distributed through its authorised network.
“Importantly, the laboratory [CDL] identified 17 differences between the questioned vials and the genuine retention samples of the same batch that HBI had submitted for batch release,” the IIL statement said.
IIL said the seized vials did not match the genuine product and indicated that the legitimate batch number may have been used on counterfeit material. Authorities are investigating the source and distribution of the suspect product and whether it is spurious.
The development follows an earlier counterfeit Abhayrab episode involving batch KA24014 in 2025. IIL had reported suspected counterfeit vials to authorities, following which health warnings were issued in some countries over the possibility that travellers to India could have received counterfeit rabies vaccine.
The latest case is particularly important because rabies is almost invariably fatal once symptoms develop, making effective post-exposure vaccination critical.
For IIL, the findings will be important in determining whether the episode represents a manufacturing-quality failure or a counterfeit and supply-chain problem.
IIL has submitted its manufacturing, quality-control, reconciliation and distribution records to CDSCO on 14 August 2026.
Following a specific representation on Friday (September 4, 2026) IIL noted it has requested authorities to trace the source of the questioned vials and take action against those responsible, while confirming its full cooperation with the investigation.

headline: A government laboratory has flagged rabies vaccine vials discovered at an unauthorized site as substandard and misbranded (Reuters)
full_text:
A government laboratory has flagged rabies vaccine vials discovered at an unauthorized site as substandard and misbranded (Reuters)
NEW DELHI: Vials labelled as Abhayrab, a rabies vaccine, found at an unlicensed residential premises in Mukherjee Nagar have been declared âNot of Standard Qualityâ and misbranded by the Central Drugs Laboratory, Kasauli, with the manufacturer saying the tested vials were not its product.The vials carried batch number KE25012 and were sampled by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) during an enforcement action and sent to the laboratory for testing. The laboratory report recorded 17 differences between the tested vial and the retention samples of the same batch submitted by Human Biologicals Institute, a division of Indian Immunologicals Ltd, for batch-release testing.
The sample failed the potency requirement, though it passed sterility, moisture and identity tests. Differences were also found in labelling, artwork, QR-code verification, cap colour, licence details and packaging text. Indian Immunologicals said the vials examined were not manufactured by Human Biologicals Institute.The company said the genuine KE25012 batch had been tested and released by the Central Drugs Laboratory under a batch-release certificate dated November 7, 2025. The 83,370 vials released from the batch were supplied only through its authorised distribution channel, it said, adding that no market complaint had been received for the batch.
The development is significant because a spurious or substandard rabies vaccine may fail to provide the protection expected after an animal bite. Rabies is almost invariably fatal once clinical symptoms develop, making effective post-exposure vaccination critical.The Delhi location is significant against the backdrop of a Crime Branch raid in Mukherjee Nagar earlier this year, in which 953 rabies vaccine vials were among medicines recovered in an alleged spurious-drug racket. Four people were arrested. However, there is currently no evidence establishing that those seized vials were from batch KE25012.The latest finding also comes less than two years after Indian Immunologicals informed the drug regulator in January 2025 about counterfeit Abhayrab doses carrying batch number KA24014. Health authorities in the US, UK and Australia subsequently issued alerts for people who may have received the vaccine in India.
Indian Immunologicals said it submitted its manufacturing, quality-control, reconciliation and distribution records to CDSCO on August 14. In its September 4 representation to the Drugs Controller General of India, it asked authorities to trace the source of the vials and act against those responsible.The company said every Abhayrab batch is independently tested and released by the Central Drugs Laboratory before sale. Vaccines supplied through hospitals, clinics, government facilities and licensed pharmacies via its authorised distribution chain, it said, are not affected by the matter.

She specializes in health and heritage reporting, expertly simplifying complex health information to make it engaging and understandable for readers. Her deep dives into heritage topics are well-researched, resulting in captivating narratives that resonate with her audience. headline: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday took a jibe at leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, describing the Congress party's student outreach campaign "Chhatron Ki Goonj" as "jhooth ki goonj".'Chhatron Ki Goonj' is a student-dialogue campaig...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday took a jibe at leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, describing the Congress party's student outreach campaign "Chhatron Ki Goonj" as "jhooth ki goonj".'Chhatron Ki Goonj' is a student-dialogue campaign launched by the Congress to raise issues including examination paper leaks, rising education costs, irregularities in government recruitment and unemployment.Over the past three months, the campaign has been held in Kota in Rajasthan, Dehradun in Uttarakhand, Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh and Pune in Maharashtra.
Addressing the centenary celebrations of Delhi University's Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC), PM Modi said, "...Main jaanta hoon, sach ki Hunkkaar ke aage jhooth ki goonj tik nahi sakegi (I know that the echo of lies cannot stand before the roar of truth)."
'Modi stands like a rock'PM Modi said he had the courage to remind students of his 2013 speech and compare his claims with India's current position."This is Modi. He stands like a rock in front of those who favour the 'mai-baap' culture. I have the courage, which is why I am reminding you of what I said that day.
I have come before you with my report card. At the same programme in 2013, when I said that we needed to work towards "Made in India," people from the ecosystem of that time simply could not understand it. They believed that Made in India was impossible during that period of despair. And those who were brought up with that mindset still make fun of Made in India today. But today you can see the brand value of Make in India,â the PM said.PM Modi takes 'Naraz Fufa' jibeThe Primr Minister also described those who oppose government initiatives as "Naraz Fufa", saying, "But outside this campus, you will encounter a new world. You will meet two kinds of people. One kind consists of people who positively transform the strength of society into the strength of the nation. The second kind is made up of people who become the "Naraz Fufa" whenever any work is started."Their favourite thing is to oppose everything. They have only one dialogue: What is the need for this? When we were building the world's tallest statue, the "Fufa" said, "What is the need for this?" When we started working on the high-speed train, the "Fufa" again said, What is the need for this? When we introduced UPI, these same "Fufas" asked, Why UPI? When we built the new Parliament building, they again said, "What is the need for this?" We built a memorial for our brave military heroes who dedicated their lives and made the supreme sacrifice for the country. The "Fufa" came onto the field again and asked, "What was the need for this?" But India gave an answer to all these "Fufas." No one can stop India from doing what is necessary for the country," he added.PM recalls 2013, attacks UPA-era recordRecalling the situation in 2013, PM Modi listed what he described as the major challenges facing the country at the time."There is a gang that will take what I am saying, break it into small pieces and put it in my account. So, let me warn you in advance about this. Let me tell you what used to dominate the media during that period in 2013. For example, Indian soldiers were being killed along the LoC. The current generation may find it surprising; perhaps they may wonder, "Did this really happen?" Yes, it did. The World Bank had lowered its GDP growth forecast. The current account deficit was at an all-time high. Inflation was around 10 per cent. The industrial sector was in the grip of a slowdown. Corruption in the helicopter deal had been exposed. There were bomb blasts in Hyderabad. These were all headlines at that time. I firmly believe that our students today may not know about all these things," PM Modi said."These developments show what the condition of the country was at that time. Growth was at the bottom, while inflation was at the peak. Scams were at their height, and the corrupt were moving around fearlessly. The economy was in distress. There was discussion everywhere about policy paralysis. The world was counting India among the "Fragile Five." Terrorists were operating unchecked, and Pakistan was out of control. In other words, there was nothing but disappointment and despair. There was a time when the country was struggling on every front..." he added.PM Modi said that despite being in the opposition during his 2013 visit, he had not used the SRCC platform to attack the then government."Your seniors were sitting here in 2013, and at that time I was the Chief Minister, but I was also a member of the country's main opposition party. Perhaps people were expecting me to launch a long, strong attack on the then Central Government and level a barrage of allegations. But, even though I was in the Opposition and a critic of the government of the time, I did not use this platform for that purpose. I presented a vision. I spoke positively. Whatever I said then was my conviction. I have always lived those thoughts and dreams. I continued to follow that path, to dedicate myself wholeheartedly to the country and to have the passion to live for the nation...At that time, all of you may have been in school. But today, if you go on the internet and read the news from 2013 and around that period, you will get an idea of what the situation was like then.""My 2013 speech at SRCC had become a wave, and even today, 13-14 years later, the impact of that address remains intact," he said.'Dimagi Naxal' remarkPM also referred to his recent "Dimagi Naxal" remark, comparing it to a homeopathic treatment. "You may have heard my speech from Red Fort. I gave a homeopathic pill from the Red Fortâ"Dimagi Naxal". According to the principles of homeopathy, when you begin homeopathic treatment, the disease initially gets worse. That is the nature of homeopathy. Similarly, as soon as I gave the "Dimagi Naxal" homeopathic pill, all the "Dimagi Naxals" started coming out one after another. And now the public is also seeing the true colours of those who are promoting this illness," PM Modi said.PM highlights handling of crisesThe prime minister listed the challenges India had faced in recent years, including the Covid-19 pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war and the West Asia crisis."I have told you so many things. Some people may think, "What is this? This is a country of 140 crore people. It was very easy. What new thing did Modi do?" But was it really that easy? I want to take you back to the old days once again. Remember, when you were in school, there was a disaster in Kedarnath in 2013. The entire government was shaken. They simply did not know what to do or how to respond. When the banking crisis came in 2008, the government at the time tried to hide behind the crisis for years. It did not even have the courage to tackle it," PM Modi said."The entire banking system of India was pushed to the brink of collapse. In 2008 itself, there was a horrific terror attack in Mumbai. The government of the time came under pressure from outside but did not even have the courage to teach Pakistan a lesson...Over the past six years, we have faced major crises. First came the COVID-19 pandemic, which brought the entire world to a standstill. Then the war between Russia and Ukraine broke out. After that, there was a period when trade and supply chains began to be weaponised," he added.Every time, people said, "Now India will not survive." And those who are my biggest admirers were happy, thinking, "Now Modi is trapped. Now Modi has fallen. Now they will crush him." But the blessings of the people of my country have so much strength, so much strength, that every wish of those who want India to fail is being left unfulfilled."'India is not only growing'PM Modi also highlighted India's latest economic figures, including 7.8 per cent quarterly growth, and said the country's performance showed its resilience despite global challenges."The world was calling India one of the 'Fragile Five.' Today, the world is watching India become the fastest-growing major economy. In just the past week, there have been several positive developments regarding India's economy. The 7.8 per cent quarterly growth has boosted the country's confidence. Meanwhile, a Japanese credit rating agency has upgraded India's rating. And this 7.8 per cent growth has come at a time when the war in West Asia is ongoing and there have been several trade-related challenges. Achieving such growth under these circumstances shows India's strength and potential. I know, and you also know, that those who became infamous for pushing India into the 'Fragile Five' are finding these figures difficult to digest. But all of you understand the data seriously...In other words, India is not only growing but also creating new employment opportunities. Despite this, those for whom the glass was half empty in 2013 continue to think the same way even today. For them, the glass will always be half empty. I talk about the glass; I am not talking about anything remaining empty," the PM said.India's armed forces enter their territory & strikePM Modi also said India's security situation had improved, citing developments in Jammu and Kashmir, the Northeast and the fight against Maoist insurgency."Today, those spreading terrorism are on the back foot. If Pakistan indulges in any misadventure, India's armed forces enter their territory and strike. Peace has increased from Jammu and Kashmir to the Northeast.""The back of Maoist terrorism and Naxalism has been broken. The world that was once concerned about India's policy paralysis is today talking about India's policy dynamism," he added.
PM praises SRCC alumniPraising SRCC and its alumni, PM Modi said the institution had produced prominent figures across fields, including economics, politics, law and the arts.
"The alumni of SRCC have also been very special. In your language, I would say the alumni here are the OGs. They have taken the name of SRCC across the world and made a mark for themselves in different fields. Our Arun Jaitley ji studied here. And I can say that perhaps there was hardly a meeting with him where he did not share an incident from his SRCC days. Sometimes I would get tired because he would tell me the same incident again and again. Even today, Sanjeev Sanyal, who is part of my team, is an alumnus of SRCC. We have many other colleagues who studied here as well. And it is not that SRCC has produced people only from the world of economics. From artists to politicians, lawyers and judges, people from every field have emerged from here."He also described the institution's 100-year journey as one marked by achievements and inspiration. "When a person lives for 100 years, they are considered an ocean of experience. And when an institution completes 100 years, it becomes an ocean of achievements and inspiration. In its 100-year journey, SRCC has shaped generations and connected them with a brighter future. Those who came here studied, and those who left emerged as well-shaped individuals," he added.
PM Modi took a metro ride to the college and interacted with students and fellow passengers during the journey. He also released a commemorative Rs 100 coin to mark the centenary.The prime minister's visit comes amid the BJP's ongoing outreach to young voters. He had last visited SRCC in 2013, when he was Gujarat chief minister.In April this year, PM Modi met the SRCC governing body and a delegation from the college at his residence to mark the institution's centenary. He also released a special commemorative postage stamp on the occasion.Established in 1926, SRCC has completed 100 years and has produced scholars, professionals, entrepreneurs, policymakers and leaders across different fields.
Kanchan Yadav is a writer at The Times of India, where she covers business, politics, international affairs and social issues. Her reporting also focuses on policy, governance and economic developments, with a close lens on how decisions in corridors of power affect everyday lives and community well-being.

headline: Bengal may ban mobile phones in schools, says CM Suvendu Adhikari
full_text:
Bengal may ban mobile phones in schools, says CM Suvendu Adhikari
He also said that the state has plans to reintroduce the traditional games and sports in schools such as Kho-kho, kabaddi
West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday hinted at banning mobile phones in schools while citing the example of Gujarat where students up to Class 12 are banned from bringing mobile phones to schools.
“Mobile phones have a huge negative impact on school children. It will be a tough decision and I may lose votes. In Gujarat mobile phone are banned for students up to Class 12. Even after their parents go off to sleep, the students remain awake till around 2am, watching mobile phones,” Adhikari said.
The CM was speaking at a government program on Teachers’ Day in Kolkata where he launched the Swami Vivekananda Merit Scholarship Scheme and the Transfer Management Module of College Teachers.
“We will be doing wrong if we restrict the students within the libraries and laboratories. We have done many things wrong in the state’s education sector. We have to bring back physical activities in our schools. NCC was withdrawn. It was a huge damage. NCC needs to be reintroduced in schools and colleges. We neglected sports activities. We have to bring back physical activities in schools and colleges,” he added.
He also said that the state has plans to reintroduce the traditional games and sports in schools such as Kho-kho, kabaddi.
The CM said that every district in the state would have two “CM Shri” model schools to train the best students who would be selected through exams in Class 6.
The schools, in the line of central schools, will have the best teachers, advanced laboratories and smart class rooms. He said that the government would set up two sports facilities in the state where the best talents would receive training.
Adhikari said that the School Service Commission has been reconstituted and teacher would be recruited in a transparent manner following the orders of the Supreme Court and Calcutta high court without any allowing any illegality to creep in.
“If reforms are not introduced then the whole education system and the concept of Teachers’ Day will be rendered meaningless,” he said.
“Felicitation of teachers should be based on certain parameters such as his attendance in schools, whether he has authored books, whether 100% students under him have passed the board exams and whether his students have become scientists and doctors,” he said.
“But one aspect shouldn’t be compromised. Those who harm the Nation, raise questions against patriotism, raise objections against singing the entire National Song, those who don’t protest after Pahalgam-like massacre while raising objections when India attacks Pakistan and seek peace. Nation comes first,” the CM said.

headline: India moves to buy 5 more S-400s after Op Sindoor success; Russia sends cost proposal
full_text:
India moves to buy 5 more S-400s after Op Sindoor success; Russia sends cost proposal
The decision for approval will be taken by the Cabinet Committee on Security after the cost is finalised and a green signal obtained from the finance ministry.
India’s decision to acquire five more S-400 Triumf air defence systems from Russia has gained further momentum with Moscow sending in Bill of Quantities (BOQ) proposal, which details the cost of construction and materials, to Delhi for the cost negotiations to begin.
The last of the five S-400 system contracted by the Narendra Modi government in 2018 at a cost of USD 5.43 billion will be reaching India in November this year.
Contrary to what a section of the media is reporting, India has taken no decision on the acquisition of two squadrons of fifth generation SU-57 fighter aircraft from Russia, but the Indian Air Force has shown interest in Moscow’s proposal as Chinese fifth generation fighter J-20 has been deployed by the Xi Jinping regime in Hotan, Lhasa and Nyinchi airbases in Tibet under the PLA’s western theatre command.
According to authoritative sources, the decision to approve five more squadrons of S-400 air defence system will be taken by the Cabinet Committee on Security after the cost is finalised with Moscow and a green signal obtained from the Indian finance ministry. The fifth S-400 system will be deployed in India’s eastern sector facing China.
During Operation Sindoor in May 2025, the S-400 system came out in flying colours with one of its long range missile targeting a Pakistan early airborne warning aircraft at a distance of 314 kilometers across the Indus in Pakistani heartland. While the Pakistanis used kamikaze drones to target the S-400 systems deployed in Adampur and Bhuj air bases, the Russian surface to air missile system ensured that none of the Pakistani fighters could come anywhere near the Indian border for the fear of being knocked down from the skies.
In fact, on May 10, the Pakistani air force moved all its air assets to bases near Durand Line with Afghanistan as 11 of their air bases were hit by Indian BrahMos missiles and as many as seven fighters were knocked down by Indian S-400 and Akash Tir air defence systems.
With Russian President Vladimir Putin expected to be in Delhi for BRICS summit on September 11-13, the Indian defence cooperation with Russia will be further cemented in the hypersonic missile sector.

headline: Tamil Nadu DVAC searchs former minister KN Nehru's residence in Tiruchirappalli
full_text:
Tamil Nadu DVAC searchs former minister KN Nehru's residence in Tiruchirappalli
NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu's Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) on Saturday conducted searches at the residence and premises linked to DMK leader and former minister KN Nehru in connection with alleged irregularities in the Municipal Administration and Water Supply (MAWS) Department.
The searches were conducted in Thillai Nagar, Tiruchirappalli.
DMK cadres gathered outside Nehru's residence during the searches. Former minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi also visited Nehru's home.The case relates to allegations of corruption in recruitment, contract allocation and transfers during Nehru's tenure as the minister in charge of the department.
The DVAC registered an FIR after the Madras high court directed it to initiate a probe into allegations related to the department. The agency named Nehru, his relatives and several officials as accused.The allegations include a Rs 888-crore cash-for-jobs scam, in which money was allegedly collected from candidates in exchange for government jobs, as well as irregularities in contracts worth around Rs 1,020 crore and illegal transfers and postings linked to the department.The Enforcement Directorate (ED) had earlier shared details of the alleged irregularities with Tamil Nadu authorities, following which the matter came under scrutiny.However, the Madras high court later granted an interim stay on further action by the vigilance agency and proceedings against the accused. Legal proceedings in the matter are continuing.(With ANI inputs)

headline: NEW DELHI: The West Bengal government's state tourism ad was trolled by netizens after it failed to include anything that represents Bengal apart from the Howrah bridge.The ad was released on Friday by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari during a public ...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: The West Bengal government's state tourism ad was trolled by netizens after it failed to include anything that represents Bengal apart from the Howrah bridge.The ad was released on Friday by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari during a public event. "Hon'ble Chief Minister Shri Suvendu Adhikari attends the grand unveiling of West Bengal Tourismâs new brand identity, organized by the Department of Tourism, Government of West Bengal," the BJP state unit said posting video of the event.Though the ad begins with Howrah bridge, it progresses into showing Eiffel Tower, the Pyramids and several other world tourist attractions.
TMC MP Derek O'Brien reacted to it calling it "Tacky. Trashy. Thooo."
"Where is West Bengal in this?What kind of tourism logo reveal is this?? It is more like promoting international tourism rather than promoting Bengal! Everywhere but Bengal. Ridiculous," said a social media user Barnali Bairagi.
Another user Joy said: "Letâs start with the bare minimum - The Background Music. With plethora of instruments available and tools to create OG music, they come with this trash that can put anyone to sleep (Play it on loop if u canât sleep).
The visuals and the shoddy video. It shows Howrah Bridge and moves on to deserts, pyramids, places that are not in West Bengal. Ya, the brilliant idea would have been to convey the experience of all the best things in the world u will find in West Bengal or something like that.""All they had to do is just study the communication and visual story telling of Kerala Tourism. Or even Odisha Tourism. Rajasthan Tourism also at one point of time had done great communications. The tagline: Where India feels different is so generic, it can be placed anywhere. It can even be the Tagline of an amusement park. Or a residential project. It doesnât evoke any emotion. Compare it with Kerala tourismâs - Godâs own Country.
Or Rajasthanâs - Padharo Mhare Desh. Which is such a welcoming and warm tagline," the user added.
Another user requested the CM to "ask the tourism department to create a fresh, professionally conceived, Bengal-centric campaign showcasing our mountains, forests, rivers, Sundarbans, coastline, heritage, literature, music, cuisine, festivals and extraordinary cultural diversity.""There was a time when Bengal Tourism meant Darjeeling, the Toy Train, Sundarbans, Howrah Bridge, trams, Jhau dance, heritage, culture and the unmistakable soul of Bengal. The âSweetest Part of Indiaâ campaign showcased Bengal as Bengal," Diptangshu Chaudhury said."Bengal doesnât need borrowed landmarks to attract the world. It needs the imagination and competence to showcase what it already has. From Darjeeling to the Sundarbans, from the Himalayas to the Bay of BengalâBengal itself is the advertisement. Please donât make Bengal invisible while trying to sell it," the person added.

headline: Officials of Tamil Nadu’s Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) conducted simultaneous searches at 30 places linked to former Minister and DMK leader K.N. Nehru in Chennai, Tiruchi, Coimbatore, Erode, and Tiruppur on Saturday.
full_text:
Officials of Tamil Nadu’s Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) conducted simultaneous searches at 30 places linked to former Minister and DMK leader K.N. Nehru in Chennai, Tiruchi, Coimbatore, Erode, and Tiruppur on Saturday.
According to sources, the searches were held as part of an investigation into the alleged irregularities in contracts awarded by the Municipal Administration and Water Supply (MAWS) Department between 2021 and 2025, when Mr. Nehru held the portfolio. In Chennai, Mr. Nehru’s residence in Mylapore and premises linked to him and his brother, Ravichandran, in Thiruvanmiyur, Adyar, Anna Nagar, and Raja Annamalaipuram were searched.
The DVAC officials seized 241 incriminating documents, besides electronic evidence, allegedly linked to irregularities in the tender process.
The investigation is continuing, the DVAC said.
Officials of the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) conducted a search at the residence of former Municipal Administration Minister and DMK principal secretary K.N. Nehru at Tiruchi on Saturday.
In Tiruchi, searches were conducted at the residences of the Corporation’s former Chief Engineer Sivapatham at Shanmuga Nagar and Mr. Nehru’s former Personal Assistant Manikandan in Srirangam. The searches were conducted based on a First Information Report (FIR) registered by the DVAC Headquarters in Chennai against Mr. Nehru and 12 others regarding allegations of party fund collection from the tender awardees, sources from the investigating agency said.
A DVAC team led by a woman Deputy Superintendent of Police began the search at Former Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, Tiruchi Mayor M. Anbazhagan and several DMK members were present during the search at Mr. Nehru’s residence at Thillai Nagar in Tiruchi around 8 a.m..The investigating agency has collected a few documents from the residence of Mr. Nehru and enquired him. The seven-hour-long search concluded at 3 p.m, the sources said.
After the seven-hour-long search concluded at 3 p.m., Mr. Nehru told reporters outside his residence that that the DVAC team had told him in the morning that there was some flaw in the tender based on which an FIR had been registered. Searches were also conducted at his residence in Chennai besides in the office of his brother, Mr. Nehru said and claimed that the team could not get anything. However, the team took a copy of a office file which he termed it as a “routine file”.
‘Extended full cooperation’
Mr. Nehru said he had extended full cooperation to the DVAC team during the search, which, he said, He alleged that he had not spoken to anyone regarding the tender issue and was innocent. This was a new case by the DVAC against him, he added.
Asked whether the searches were conducted by the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government to intimidate him and also because of political vendetta, Mr. Nehru said it , he was surely an act of political vendetta by the TVK government. Replying to a question, Mr. Nehru He further said DMK president M.K. Stalin had spoken to him and asked him to extend cooperation for the search.
‘No political vendetta’
Dismissing the allegations of political retaliation, Minister for Energy Resources and Law C.T.R. Nirmalkumar said the DVAC searches at the residences of senior political figures were entirely procedure-driven, and that no individual possessed the authority to interfere in anti-corruption investigations. Firmly dismissing allegations of political retaliation, he said: “There is absolutely no political vendetta behind this. No one has the right to interfere in the functioning of the DVAC.”
In Coimbatore, the DVAC conducted searches at the residences of Mr. Nehru’s brothers Manivannan at Kallimadai and Ravichandran at Masakalipalayam. The residence of the Corporation’s retired Town Planning Officer, Sasi Priya, at Sivaram Nagar in Ramanathapuram was also searched.
A team led by DVAC Additional Superintendent of Police (ADSP) Rajesh, along with Inspector Arumugam and other personnel, commenced the searches around 7 a.m. The teams searched the premises and examined documents and other material that could be relevant to the allegations against the individuals, police sources said.

headline: Three more Indian nationals, among them a five-year-old child, have been rescued from the flood-hit Trishuli Bazaar area of Nepal, bringing the total count of Indian evacuees to 169, while 275 nationals remain missing, the Ministry of External Affair...
full_text:
Three more Indian nationals, among them a five-year-old child, have been rescued from the flood-hit Trishuli Bazaar area of Nepal, bringing the total count of Indian evacuees to 169, while 275 nationals remain missing, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Friday (September 4, 2026).
Sharing broader updates on the safety of Indian nationals, MEA Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal noted that 1,907 Indians have safely crossed over to Nepal from China.
Also read | Nepal floods: Indian volunteers take relief to isolated communities
The three Indian nationals rescued from the Trishuli Bazaar area have been identified as Abhijit Suresh Pawar, Dipika Abhijit Pawar, and five-year-old Samarth Abhijit Pawar, Mr. Jaiswal said, adding that the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu is facilitating their return flight home.
The spokesperson said India has supplied around 95 tonnes of relief material to Nepal since the flash floods hit the country on August 26.
The death toll from the floods has risen to at least 1,295 after rescue workers recovered more bodies from affected areas, according to Nepalese authorities.
While emergency teams have rescued more than 12,000 people, roughly 5,000 remain missing as search and rescue operations continue.
"As per our information, 275 Indian nationals remain missing. We continue to be in close touch with the Nepali government," Mr. Jaiswal said at his regular media briefing.
"We deeply appreciate the efforts of the Nepalese authorities in this regard." Mr. Jaiswal said 169 Indian nationals have been rescued and 1,907 Indians have safely crossed into Nepal from China.
"As per official sources in China, there are no Indian travellers who are stranded in the Tibetan Autonomous Region in China," Mr. Jaiswal noted.
The MEA spokesperson said India will continue to provide assistance to Nepal as per the requirements of the government in that country.
"We do plan to send more forensic kits, Bailey bridges and other materials that are requested by the government of Nepal," he said.
Mr. Jaiswal said India has supplied around 95 tonnes of relief material on seven aircraft to Nepal till now.
"In addition to the relief material, we have also sent 54 personnel to support relief and rescue efforts in Nepal. This comprises 30 tunnel rescue experts, 19 forensic experts, and a five-member medical team. Our rescue and forensic teams are deployed on the ground, and they are working closely with the Nepalese authorities," he said.
ALSO WATCH More than a week after Nepal’s deadliest flood disaster in years, here’s what we know so far
The first tranche of relief materials was sent by India hours after Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah on August 26, the day the flash floods struck the Himalayan nation.
Mr. Modi had assured Mr. Shah of all possible humanitarian assistance to deal with the situation.
The floods have damaged 35 motorable bridges, 45 suspension bridges, and 40 km of black-topped roads, mainly in central Nepal, according to local authorities.
Mr. Jaiswal said India responded promptly to the flash floods in Nepal and will continue to support the reconstruction and recovery efforts in the country.
