headline: Chirag Paswan's party files complaint against influencer over assault claims
full_text:
Chirag Paswan's party files complaint against influencer over assault claims
Chirag Paswan's party has complained to Delhi Police against Swatantra Bhardwaj for falsely invoking his name in an assault case. The move coincided with Bhardwaj's detention after protests over his claimed attack on a student activist's father.
The Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) on Friday filed a complaint against Hindutva influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj, accusing him of falsely and publicly using party chief Chirag Paswan's name in connection with an assault on the father of a student activist during a CJP protest in July.
The complaint is being examined for further action and no case had been registered till Friday, a senior police officer said. Later in the day, Delhi Police detained Bhardwaj in Uttar Pradesh, hours after the Cockroach Janta Party staged a protest outside Parliament Street police station demanding his arrest over the assault that he had spoken about in an interview.
The complaint was lodged by the party's legal cell at Parliament Street police station in Delhi. Seeking protection from what it called Bhardwaj's false public claims, it said neither Paswan nor the party had anything to do with him. It also said the party stood with the activist and her injured father.
Bhardwaj was seen in a video clip from an interview in which he claimed that he had "cracked the skull" of the activist's father during a CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in July, leaving him with an injury that required 60 stitches, and still avoided being jailed.
There are also photographs of Bhardwaj with political leaders, including Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Delhi minister Kapil Mishra and Union Food Processing Industries Minister Chirag Paswan.
Speaking to reporters on Friday, Paswan said Bhardwaj had misused his name and the names of other leaders, and that he had lodged a complaint against him and demanded action. "No action despite the accused admitting to an attack that could have been fatal sets a bad example; I take responsibility for ensuring justice for the family," Paswan said.
In the clip that drew attention to him, Bhardwaj also referred to several political leaders. "I have the blessings of Hanuman upon me. And secondly, Kapil Mishra is my elder brother. They say Kapil Mishra called and I was released. Chirag Paswan is my elder brother. How many leaders do you know?" he claimed.
However, there is no evidence to establish that the political leaders named by Bhardwaj intervened on his behalf in the case.
The detention came after CJP representatives, accompanied by Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) chief and Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad and MP Pappu Yadav, met police officials and were assured that action would be taken against Bhardwaj within 72 hours. Overall, the day saw the LJP (Ram Vilas) move against Bhardwaj over his claims involving Paswan, while Delhi Police took him into detention after protests over the assault case.

headline: S Jaishankar said Friday India is exploring ideas with both Russia and Ukraine to bring the conflict to an end
full_text:
S Jaishankar said Friday India is exploring ideas with both Russia and Ukraine to bring the conflict to an end
NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar said Friday India is exploring ideas with both Russia and Ukraine to bring the conflict to an end, while again defending India's energy sourcing and underlining that it's important to "diagnose" the problem right. The minister had said in Ukraine a day ago that the conflict will end through dialogue and diplomacy and not oil trade.Without revealing if there was any specific peace proposal under consideration, Jaishankar said India was having "detailed discussions" with both sides about possible ways to facilitate peace. He was speaking in Warsaw after a meeting with his Polish counterpart Radoslaw Sikorski."PM Modi and President Putin met in Bishkek three days ago, and then I went to Kyiv. So, what we had were discussions with the Russian side, yesterday with the Ukrainian side, and what we are trying to do is to see if there are ideas and suggestions which can be developed in some way in which they would contribute to the mitigation, ideally the cessation of the conflict," he said.
India has so far not come up with a plan of its own to ensure a ceasefire as it believes the primary responsibility to end the war lies with Russia and Ukraine.
However, as Jaishankar reiterated, it's ready to offer any assistance, if required, to ensure peace.After Modi's renewed peace message to Putin, there seems to be more urgency in India's efforts, with Jaishankar calling on Zelensky and discussing "approaches to end the ongoing conflict"." ...We must each do what we can, in whichever way we believe would be most effective. And support the efforts of others to bring this conflict to an end. This is India's strong conviction, and we are acting on it," Jaishankar said in Poland. "I think let's diagnose the problem right. The issue is a conflict, and the solution to that is not in trade. The solution... is in negotiations."

headline: 8 Tamil Nadu students killed after speeding car rams parked lorry on highway in Kerala
full_text:
8 Tamil Nadu students killed after speeding car rams parked lorry on highway in Kerala
Eight students from Tamil Nadu died after their car hit a parked lorry on a highway in Kerala's Thrissur district, police said. CCTV footage captured the incident, and the bodies were sent to the mortuary at Thrissur Medical College.
Eight students from Tamil Nadu were killed after the car they were travelling in crashed into a lorry parked on a highway in Kerala’s Thrissur district, police said on Saturday.
The accident occurred around 11:40 pm on Friday in Kaipamangalam. CCTV footage shows the car speeding along an almost empty National Highway-66 before crashing into the lorry, which is not visible in the footage. A puff of dust can be seen rising immediately after the impact.
Preliminary information suggested that the victims were students of PSM Engineering College in Tamil Nadu's Dindigul.
The car, which had a Tamil Nadu registration, was travelling from the Guruvayur side towards Kodungallur when it crashed into the lorry, which was parked at a diversion on an under-construction stretch of the highway.
All eight occupants died on the spot, police said.
The occupants had to be pulled out of the mangled car by cutting it open. Locals, fire and rescue personnel and police took part in the rescue operation.
The bodies were taken to the mortuary at Thrissur Medical College, police said.

headline: 8 Tamil Nadu engineering students killed in Kerala, their car rammed into parked lorry
full_text:
8 Tamil Nadu engineering students killed in Kerala, their car rammed into parked lorry
The car in which the youths were travelling collided with a lorry parked on the highway at Panambikkunnu in Kaipamangalam.
At least eight engineering students from Tamil Nadu were killed in a road accident as a car rammed into a parked lorry in Keralam’s Thrissur, police said on Saturday.
According to police, the deceased were students of an engineering college in Dindigul, Tamil Nadu, and were travelling from Guruvayur towards Kodungallur along NH-66.
Six of the eight deceased have been identified. Four of them-Surya, Yuvasanjith, Vishva and Johua-were from Dindigul, while Santhosh and Prasanna were from Madurai, news agency PTI reported. Police said the identities of two others are yet to be confirmed.
The accident occurred around 11.40 pm on Friday, according to the police.
The car, carrying a Tamil Nadu registration, in which the youths were travelling collided with a Maharashtra-registered lorry parked on the highway at Panambikkunnu in Kaipamangalam and died on the spot, news agency PTI reported.
According to the FIR, the lorry was illegally parked on the right side of the highway near a barricaded section where traffic had been diverted as part of ongoing construction work. The car rammed into its rear.
Kaipamangalam police have registered a case against the lorry driver, who fled from the spot, under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for culpable homicide.
The car was travelling at high speed and the driver apparently failed to notice the diversion barricade before hitting the rear of the lorry, police said.
Police used student identity cards recovered from the bodies to contact the families of the deceased. Some of the families were unaware their children had travelled to Kerala, police said.
The victims were pulled from the car in a rescue operation involving locals, fire and rescue personnel, and police, before their bodies were taken to the mortuary of Thrissur Medical College.
Postmortem examinations will begin after the families of the deceased reach Thrissur Medical College, police said.

headline: In a major reshuffle of organisational responsibilities, the Congress on Saturday (September 5, 2026) appointed Sachin Pilot as the new All India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary in-charge of poll-bound Punjab, while Randeep Singh Surjewal...
full_text:
In a major reshuffle of organisational responsibilities, the Congress on Saturday (September 5, 2026) appointed Sachin Pilot as the new All India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary in-charge of poll-bound Punjab, while Randeep Singh Surjewala will handle Gujarat in addition to Karnataka.
The changes, made by party president Mallikarjun Kharge and announced by general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal, come ahead of crucial State elections. While Assembly elections in Punjab are scheduled for early 2027, Gujarat will go to the polls later next year.
Former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel has been moved from Punjab to Assam as the new Congress general secretary for the State.
The change in Punjab is most significant as it comes amid intense factionalism between the camps of former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi and Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring.
If not a snub to Mr. Baghel, the Punjab move can be seen as an attempt by the high command to press the reset button to contain factionalism.
In a party rejig in July, the high command’s decision to make Mr. Channi the chairman of the campaign committee while continuing with Mr. Warring as the PCC chief triggered triggered open factionalism.
By appointing Mr. Pilot, who served as a senior poll observer in Kerala, where the Congress-led United Democratic Front scored an impressive victory, the Congress high command has tried to convey its intent.
The factionalism has not only created bad optics but has also held up a proposed political yatra of the State by the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi.
Mr. Surjewala, too, seems to have been rewarded for ensuring a smooth transition of leadership in Karnataka, from Siddaramaiah to D.K. Shivakumar as the Chief Minister.
Mr. Surjewala has been made general secretary in charge of Gujarat and Karnataka, where the Congress is in power. Mukul Wasnik, who was handling Gujarat, will continue as an All India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary.
The party has also appointed Lok Sabha member from Jharkhand, Sukhdeo Bhagat, as AICC in-charge of Chhattisgarh; Sirivella Prasad as in-charge of Maharashtra; and P.V. Mohan as in-charge of Andhra Pradesh.
The Congress leadership thanked the outgoing general secretaries and in-charges.
While Jitendra Singh had resigned following the party’s debacle in the Assembly elections earlier this year, Ramesh Chennithala, who was handling Maharashtra, became Kerala’s Home Minister. Similarly, AICC in-charge for Maharashtra Manickam Tagore was made the new PCC president of Tamil Nadu.

headline: Congress makes Sachin Pilot Punjab in-charge, shifts Bhupesh Baghel to Assam
full_text:
Congress makes Sachin Pilot Punjab in-charge, shifts Bhupesh Baghel to Assam
Pilot's appointment places the former Rajasthan deputy chief minister at the centre of the Congress's preparations for the 2027 Punjab Assembly election.
The Congress on Saturday appointed Sachin Pilot as its general secretary in charge of poll-bound Punjab, replacing Bhupesh Baghel amid continuing factional tensions in the state unit.
The Punjab Congress has been divided over the leadership structure announced in July, under which Amrinder Singh Raja Warring was retained as state president and former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi was appointed campaign committee chairman.
Leaders from the Channi camp subsequently pressed for Warring’s removal during a meeting with Baghel. The dispute later spilled into the open through rival sloganeering and clashes at party events.
Pilot’s appointment places the former Rajasthan deputy chief minister at the centre of the Congress’s preparations for the 2027 Punjab Assembly election. His immediate challenge will be to unite the competing camps, coordinate among the state’s power centres and prevent factional differences from disrupting the campaign.
He will also have to manage organisational responsibilities and the politically sensitive process of candidate selection as the Congress seeks to mount a united challenge to the ruling Aam Aadmi Party.
The task assumes added significance given the factional turmoil that preceded the Congress’s defeat in the 2022 Punjab election.
The changes take effect immediately, AICC general secretary (organisation) KC Venugopal said in a statement.
Baghel has been shifted to Assam, while Randeep Singh Surjewala has been appointed general secretary in charge of Gujarat. Surjewala will retain charge of Karnataka.
Sukhdeo Bhagat has been appointed in charge of Chhattisgarh, Dr Sirivella Prasad of Maharashtra and PV Mohan of Andhra Pradesh.

headline: Chennai: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government has been on a spree of cancelling several infrastructure projects approved or planned by the previous DMK regime, including the controversial Parandur airport, which was cancelled due to environm...
full_text:
Chennai: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government has been on a spree of cancelling several infrastructure projects approved or planned by the previous DMK regime, including the controversial Parandur airport, which was cancelled due to environmental concerns and to protect farmland. However, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on 30 August announced a thermal power plant in Thoothukudi.
The power plant will have two units of 800 MW each, a total of 1,600 MW, at an estimated cost of Rs 20,800 crore. It would be built under a public-private partnership at the existing Thoothukudi Thermal Power Station complex. The five old 210 MW units, operating since the late 1970s and adding up to 1,050 MW, will be progressively replaced. The net addition to capacity would be around 550 MW.
The announcement was not received well by conservationists since it further threatens the environment in Thoothukudi villages, which was the main reason the DMK did not go ahead with thermal power plants in the district.
G. Sundarrajan of Poovulagin Nanbargal, an NGO focused on environmental protection, pointed out that the ash pond of the five-decade-old Thoothukudi station was already full. He alleged that slurry was being dumped into the sea, which was an environmental violation that would only worsen with a new plant. “There will be no space for an ash pond if a new plant is built. This will affect the fishery and the fishing activity,” he said in a statement, post the announcement.
Tamil Nadu has committed to net-zero carbon emissions by 2050, which is ahead of India’s 2070 target, and aims for 50 percent of its energy from renewable sources of energy by 2030. A new thermal power plant directly contradicts the plan of the state on reducing carbon emissions.
In a video statement on X, Prabakaran Veera Arasu of the Poovulagin Nanbargal also noted that the pollution levels will increase in Thoothukudi and will be higher than that of Delhi if another power plant is installed.
He also stated that the previous DMK government had taken a policy decision not to start new thermal projects because of environmental concerns, choosing instead to complete only those already underway. He also said that people living in areas where thermal power plants are installed are severely affected.
Activists also emphasise that the TVK government should address issues in transmission of electricity produced out of solar panels, and focus on renewables.
Tamil Nadu, despite its strong potential for wind and solar power, lags behind major Indian states in renewable energy capacity addition. Its solar capacity stands at just 14,121 MW, far below Gujarat’s 33,763 MW and Rajasthan’s 44,135 MW.
While Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation Limited (TNGECL) has not invited fresh applications for new solar and wind projects since March, there is a need for new 400 kV or 765 kV substations in high-potential areas like Tirunelveli-Kanniyakumari.
The TVK government that cancelled previous-regime projects on environmental and livelihood grounds, ironically plans to expand the energy project that DMK avoided on the same grounds.
The government had stated that old units would be replaced with more efficient supercritical technology, and thermal power remained necessary for peak demand and grid stability. Meanwhile, the government is yet to respond to the issue on whether it would reconsider the decision on the new thermal power plant.
(Edited by Viny Mishra)

headline: Suvendu Adhikari unveils new West Bengal tourism logo, plans ₹500 crore sector boost
full_text:
Suvendu Adhikari unveils new West Bengal tourism logo, plans ₹500 crore sector boost
West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari unveils a new tourism brand, announces ₹500 crore investment, better connectivity and tiger release in Buxa.
West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Friday unveiled a new tourism logo and brand identity, announcing plans to invest around ₹500 crore in the sector and improve infrastructure, connectivity and tourist facilities across the state.
“We have destroyed the tourism infrastructure in our state even as other states have moved forward. Tourists pass through West Bengal to reach Sikkim. More than Darjeeling and Kalimpong they prefer Gangtok. We have to come out of this,” he said.
Addressing a programme after unveiling the new logo, he said, “We are strengthening the state tourism development corporation. Discussions have been held at the state secretariat. We have allocated around ₹500 crore for the tourism sector in the (2026-2027) budget. Steps are being taken to increase the manpower.”
He also said that plans were afoot to renovate the tourist lodges and guest houses in the state, adding that there was also a need to improve connectivity to tourist destinations.
“We are exploring on how to boost tourism in the state with funds from the centre. A decision was taken to introduce water metro in the River Hooghly. We are in the process of procuring at least 11 boats which would ferry tourists to Sunderbans and Ganga Sagar. These boats would also come handy during disasters,” he said.

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Sunday reacted to the collapse of a building in Delhi's Satya Niketan, where around 40-50 students are suspected to have been trapped under the rubble, questioning the state of educational infrastructure and asking, "Will the PM visit DU again and explain how did this happen?"
"Yesterday, the PM visited DU, gave a political speech and even invoked the term “Dimagi Naxal,” while speaking very little about the state of our educational infrastructure," Dipke said in a post.
Deep Dive
"Today, a hostel building in South Campus has collapsed, with students feared trapped under the debris. The number of casualties is still unknown," he said.
"For how long will students in this country have to pay the price for failing infrastructure and neglect?" Dipke asked, adding, "Adivasi students are dying in tribal belts due to a lack of care and support, and even students studying in the national capital are not safe."
"Students deserve safe classrooms, safe hostels and basic dignity. Is that really too much to ask?" he said.
Dipke concluded his reaction by asking, "Will the PM visit DU again and explain how did this happen?"
AAP leader Saurabh Bhardwaj also reacted to the incident. "Another building collapse in Satya Niketan, it was a PG accommodation of South Campus college students for DU. Around 30-40 students are feared to be under the debris," he wrote in a post on X.

He likened today's incident to the Saket building collapse. "It’s the same story like Saket building collapse. In the name of audits, crores will again be looted from businesses, gyms, hotels, hospitals. Nothing will change."

headline: India backs ‘Equal Earth’ map at UN, but warns against inaccurate depiction of Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh
full_text:
India backs ‘Equal Earth’ map at UN, but warns against inaccurate depiction of Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh
India voted in favour of the map, while explaining that the vote stressed on “the underlying principle of promoting equal - area cartographic representation.”
The ministry of external affairs issued a clarification on Sunday regarding the union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh after backing the African Union's resolution to “rebalance” the world map.
In a statement, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that India voted in favour of the map, explaining that the vote stressed“the underlying principle of promoting equal - area cartographic representation.”
“We also highlighted that the resolution does not constitute endorsement of any specific map, projection or depiction of national boundaries,” the MEA added further.
The United Nations General Assembly voted on Friday to back a resolution spearheaded by several African countries to adopt a map that makes their continent bigger while shrinking North America and Europe.
The resolution aimed at "a more accurate representation" of continental landmasses. The resolution was supported by 164 countries, while the United States voted against it, and six other states abstained.
Also Read | Africa gets bigger, North America smaller as UN adopts new world map; US says ‘focus on genuine problems’
India warns against ‘incorrect depiction'
India has time and again been an ally for the African Union states, from ensuring its inclusion in the group of twenty (G20) to now backing the "equal earth" map at the United Nations.
However, New Delhi insisted that the equal earth map will not change the depiction of current national boundaries.
"India’s sovereign territory, including the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, must be depicted in accordance with India’s official map. Any inaccurate or misleading depiction is unacceptable. Our position on India’s sovereignty and territorial integrity is clear, consistent and non-negotiable," Jaiswal added in the statement.
What led to the call for a new map?
The Mercator map, which has been in common use since the 16th Century, has been criticised for showing Africa as being of similar size to Greenland, even though its mass is actually 14 times larger.
This map, first designed in 1569, was made to help European explorers navigate across the world. The distortion of the map is based on the fact that the surface of a globe cannot be represented on a two-dimensional chart.
In the Mercator map, the curvature of the Earth is accommodated for by making countries near the equator seem smaller than they are and countries near the poles appear larger.
In order to address this, an "equal earth" map was created in 2018 and in February 2026, all 54 nations in the African Union adopted the map due to its "accurate representation of all continents, especially Africa."
The map was put before the United Nations by Togo, backed by African Union countries.
"Changing the map obviously doesn't change the world. But correcting a representation that distorts it is already an act of truth," Togolese Foreign Minister Robert Dussey told reporters before the vote on the map.

headline: The role of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was “by no means diminishing”, said IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Kumar Goenka on Sunday (September 6, 2026), responding to a joint letter from nine ISRO employee associations seeking written clarif...
full_text:
The role of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was “by no means diminishing”, said IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Kumar Goenka on Sunday (September 6, 2026), responding to a joint letter from nine ISRO employee associations seeking written clarification on whether the government intends to transfer the agency’s launch-vehicle and satellite manufacturing to private firms.
“ISRO will remain the bedrock of the Indian space sector,” Dr. Goenka said in a post on X, describing recent reporting as a “misleading narrative.”
The reforms begun in 2020, he said, were aimed at expanding India’s overall space ecosystem, with IN-SPACe authorising non-government participation and NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) commercialising mature capabilities.
Industry would increasingly manufacture and scale mature launch vehicles and satellites, he added, while ISRO would concentrate on advanced R&D, scientific and strategic missions, and infrastructure too complex for private developers — including the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and an Indian crewed lunar mission by 2040. “The direction is not a smaller ISRO,” he wrote.
His post was followed by a longer clarification from ISRO, calling suggestions of privatisation “completely baseless and incorrect” and stating that the agency would neither be privatised nor have its importance reduced. Transferring a mature technology, it said, did not amount to withdrawal from that domain; the shift was towards an “ISRO-led national space ecosystem”, institutionalised through the Indian Space Policy 2023.
The agency said India now has over 450 space startups against a handful in 2020, and aims to grow its roughly $8.4-billion space economy to $44 billion by 2033. Ownership of critical national space infrastructure, it said, would remain with the government.
The letter that prompted the responses was dated September 4 and addressed to Dr. V. Narayanan, Secretary, Department of Space and Chairman, ISRO. Its signatories cited Dr. Goenka’s public remarks on August 21 that ISRO would eventually not make or manufacture any launch vehicles. They asked whether that position represented an approved Space Commission decision, what would happen to sanctioned strength and recruitment over the next five to ten years, and whether the associations would be consulted before irreversible decisions.
Employees of the Department of Space are exempted from the statutory definition of “industry” and cannot form trade unions. They instead organise as service associations recognised under the Central Civil Services (Recognition of Service Associations) Rules, 1993. The letter was copied to the Confederation of Central Government Employees and Workers.
The letter was sent on the same day ISRO successfully launched its first Earth imaging satellite, the EOS-05, aboard the GSLV-F17 from Sriharikota. This was the first successful launch by ISRO this year after a series of setbacks.

headline: Delhi HC cancels FIR in fight between friends, orders community service in Manipur
full_text:
Delhi HC cancels FIR in fight between friends, orders community service in Manipur
Observing that the chances of the case ending in a conviction were remote, the court said continuing the criminal proceedings would serve no useful purpose.
The Delhi High Court has cancelled an FIR lodged after a fight between friends, saying the dispute had been amicably settled and ordering the two accused to perform community service at a hospital in Manipur. The court said the complainant and the accused remained friends and had no subsisting grievance against each other.
Observing that the chances of the case ending in a conviction were remote, the court said continuing the criminal proceedings would serve no useful purpose. It made the relief of cancelling the FIR conditional on community service and payment of costs.
In an order passed on August 21, Justice Prateek Jalan said, "... I am of the view that it would be appropriate to make the relief sought (quashing of FIR) subject to undertaking community service and paying appropriate costs. The petitioner and respondent no. 4 (both accused) shall undertake community service for a total of six sessions of two hours each at Regional Institute of Medical Science, Manipur."
The court said both men must report to the hospital's medical superintendent, who will assign suitable duties to them. The court directed that the community service be completed within two months from the date of commencement.
After that, the medical superintendent will issue a compliance certificate, which is to be placed on the court record. The two men were also directed to collectively pay Rs 10,000 to the Delhi High Court Bar Association within two weeks.
The order came while allowing a plea seeking cancellation of an FIR registered at Dabri Police Station in Delhi.
The FIR, registered in March last year, was based on a complaint by a man who alleged that he was living in a rented flat with his friend when both accused forcibly entered the premises and assaulted him and his friend.
According to the FIR, one of the residents was allegedly kicked and punched, causing him to fall headfirst onto the kitchen slab and suffer a head injury.
In its order, the court noted that the FIR did not allege the use of any firearm or sharp weapon, or any separate act directed towards causing the head injury.
The court was told that the parties had settled the matter without any coercion or undue pressure and had signed a settlement deed.
The injured person also told the court that he had recovered from the injury and was not suffering from any lasting consequences. The parties said they remained friends and had no subsisting grievances against each other.
While cancelling the FIR, the court noted that the dispute arose from a quarrel between friends and was resolved shortly after the FIR was registered.
"In these circumstances, continuation of the criminal proceedings would serve no meaningful purpose and would only perpetuate discord and animosity between parties. The ends of justice would, therefore, be better served by bringing the proceedings to a quietus," the court observed.

headline: Manipur final electoral roll records 1.96 million voters after revision
full_text:
Manipur final electoral roll records 1.96 million voters after revision
The final photo electoral rolls, 2026 has recorded a total of 19,60,620 voters with 9,53,350 male, 10,06,962 female and 308 third gender
The photo electoral roll of the 60 assembly constituencies of Manipur were published on Sunday, with the state recording 19,60,620 total voters amid the growing sensitive demand for updated National Register of Citizen (NRC) before Census exercise.
According to a press note issued by chief electoral officer, Manipur (CEO), the final photo electoral roll of the 60-assembly constituency of Manipur was published in compliance of the instruction of the Election Commission of India.
The final photo electoral rolls, 2026 has recorded a total of 19,60,620 voters with 9,53,350 male, 10,06,962 female and 308 third gender with elector population (EP) ratio of 51.99 and gender ratio of 1056.
The final roll shows a net increase of 26,221 electors over the draft roll published on July 5, 2026, which had 19,34,399 electors. During the revision process, 56,871 electors were added while 30,650 were deleted from the draft electoral roll.
The centre has deferred Census exercise of Manipur following several demands of civil bodies of different communities that the NRC updated before the Census. The deferment of Census exercise decision was followed a high-level meeting chaired by Union home minister Amit Shah.
Following the Centre’s decision Ministry of Home Affairs on September 5, 2026 has issued a gazette notification for deferment of Census exercise in Manipur in.
The notification signed by registrar general of India and Census commissioner Mritunjay Kumar Narayan said that “In exercise of the powers conferred by section 3 and section 17A of the Census Act, 1948 (37 of 1948) read with rules 6A and 6D of the Census Rules, 1990, the Central Government hereby defers the houselisting operations for Census 2027 for the State of Manipur and for that purpose, hereby makes the following amendment in the notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Home Affairs number S.O. 99(E), dated the 7th January, 2026 published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (ii), dated the 7th January, 2026.”
The notification further said that “after the words ‘in all States and Union territories in India’, the words and brackets ‘(except the State of Manipur till further declaration)’ shall be inserted.”
The ongoing 8th session of 12th Manipur legislative assembly on September 2 also unanimously reaffirmed its earlier resolution of August 5, 2022 and March 1, 2024, urging the Centre to update NRC in Manipur before conducting Census exercise.
The issue of NRC update in Manipur has brought all political parties irrespective of ruling and opposition, civil bodies of several communities under a same demand. However, Kuki-Zo civil bodies have refrain from NRC update with base year 1951 as the Kuki communities accept to conduct Census exercise periodically.
“Census is a periodic exercise conducted by the government, and there is nothing inherently objectionable about it. However, when it comes to the NRC in Manipur, the use of 1951 as the base year raises serious concerns and creates a cloud of uncertainty,” Kuki-Zo Council (KZC), a Kuki Zo apex body spokesperson Ginza Vualzong said.
The electoral roll revision itself involved an extensive verification exercise. Of the 20,93,076 electors recorded before the draft publication, enumeration forms were received for 19,34,399 electors, while 1,58,677 forms were not received back. These cases were categorised as absent, shifted, deceased, duplicate and others.
The Election Commission’s exercise also involved verification of 91,178 unmapped electors and 11,30,655 electors with logical discrepancies. A total of 12,21,833 notices were issued during the verification phase. Following hearings and examination of documents, 26,362 electors from the draft roll were marked ineligible.
Besides a total number of 20,819 service electors were also enrolled in the final electoral rolls.

DU colleges open doors to anguished students of nearby PGs after building collapse in Satya Niketan
The PG was located in South-West Delhi's Satya Niketan near the Delhi University's South campus. Many of those residing in the PG are DU students.
Following the deadly collapse of a PG hostel building in Delhi's Satya Niketan, several colleges of the Delhi University have opened doors to the students of the nearby PGs.
ARSD College opened its canteen and said that arrangements for students' accommodation was also being made. Gyantosh Jha, principal of ARSD college, said, "We have opened the college canteen for students to have food. We have made arrangements for stay of the students at the nearby community centre and gurdwara. We will assess the situation tomorrow." Track updates on Satya Niketan building collapse
Colleges open doors to anguished students
Surjit, a second year BA student of Aryabhatta College also said that Delhi University colleges like ARSD and Venkateshwara have welcomed the students. “College buildings have opened their doors for students. Many students from nearby PGs have shifted to nearby colleges. ARSD, Venkateshwara College, have welcomed students,” he said.
Deep Dive
Venkateshwara College also announced a holiday for tomorrow in view of the situation in Satya Niketan where three students died and many are still trapped after a PG building collapsed. Many of the students residing in the PG are students of DU colleges nearby.
The Hostel Administration of Maitreyi College also said that it would arrange accommodation for students who require it.
“In light of the unfortunate incident in Satya Niketan, we want to make sure that all Maitreyi students staying in or around the area are safe and have access to help if needed. The Hostel Administration of Maitreyi College will also arrange accommodation for students who require it, along with necessary arrangements,” the college said in a post on Instagram.
DU reacts after building collapse kills 3
Expressing grief over the building collapse incident, the Delhi University wrote on X, “We are deeply pained and saddened by the building collapse in Delhi’s Satya Niketan. Our thoughts are with the students and families affected. We pray for the safe rescue of all those trapped and stand ready to support our students in every possible way.”
MCD action on 50-year-old building
Following the collapse of the multi-storey building, locals blamed repair work and water accumulation in the basement, while the MCD said it could not verify whether work was underway until the debris was cleared.
According to officials, the MCD has evacuated tenants from the building housing a girls' PG adjoining the collapsed building and sealed it.

full_text:
3 critical after boys’ PG building collapses in Delhi’s Satya Niketan, several feared trapped
Eight fire tenders are present at the site, as rescue personnel are currently carrying out operations to evacuate people trapped under the debris.
A building collapsed near Satya Niketan in southwest Delhi on Sunday afternoon, with several people feared trapped under the debris, police said. The exact number of people trapped is yet to be ascertained, while two people have been rescued from the debris so far. According to locals, the building that collapsed was a boys' PG.
Three people were rescued from the rubble and are in critical condition. They are undergoing treatment at the AIIMS trauma centre, the hospital said.
A police official at the site said a preliminary inquiry suggested that around 40 to 50 people were suspected to have been inside the building.
What happened?
Deep Dive
The Delhi Fire Services received an alert about the collapse at around 1.30 pm, following which a rescue operation was launched. A PCR call regarding the incident was received at South Campus police station at around 1.34 pm, reporting the collapse of a building near Nanakpura Gurdwara.
Eight fire tenders have been deployed at the site, while local police personnel, the fire brigade, CAT ambulance, and other emergency services are carrying out rescue and relief operations.
A team of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) has also reached the spot.
Also Read | Builder held for Bhiwandi crash, partner still at large
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta expresses concern
Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta expressed concern over the building collapse at Satya Niketan and noted that the adjacent building was vacated as a precautionary measure.
"Deeply concerned by the building collapse incident at Satya Niketan, RK Puram. Teams from DDMA, NDRF, Delhi Fire Services, Delhi Police, MCD, CATS and Civil Defence are carrying out rescue operations on a war footing. The adjacent building has been vacated as a precautionary measure. Every possible effort is being made to safely rescue those trapped and provide immediate assistance to the affected families," the CM said in a post on X.
"The situation is being closely monitored, and all concerned agencies are working in coordination. The safety and well-being of every citizen remain our highest priority," she added.
Also Read | Dilapidated building collapses mid-demolition in Capital, one dead
Two died in 2022 building collapse
The incident comes four years after a similar building collapse in Satya Niketan in April 2022, when two labourers were killed and four others injured after an under-construction four-storey building collapsed.
Six workers were rescued from the debris during a rescue operation involving the National Disaster Response Force, fire department and Delhi Police that lasted more than three hours.
The South Delhi Municipal Corporation had then said the building had been flagged for alleged illegal structural alterations a month before the collapse and that the police and district administration had been informed.
At that time, then South Delhi Municipal Corporation mayor Mukesh Suryan had said a notice was issued to the building owner on March 31, warning that the structural alterations being carried out were dangerous. He had also claimed that the police were informed about the matter.
A senior police officer, however, said the civic body should have followed up and checked whether the alleged illegal construction had continued after the notice was issued.

headline: A day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi branded critical Opposition leaders as “naraaz fufa (angry uncle)”, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president Nitin Nabin declared on Sunday (September 6, 2026) that the PM had hit the nail on the head in his cha...
full_text:
A day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi branded critical Opposition leaders as “naraaz fufa (angry uncle)”, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president Nitin Nabin declared on Sunday (September 6, 2026) that the PM had hit the nail on the head in his characterisation of politicians focussed on their “own personal interest”, who get angry whenever India makes progress.
The PM had used the phrase to attack Opposition leaders during a speech to youth at the Shri Ram College of Commerce in Delhi on Saturday (September 5, 2026). A day later, Mr. Nabin doubled down in a video message posted on Facebook.
“There are some people who remain dissatisfied within family and society and can never move forward or think in any positive direction. It was precisely such people whom Modi Ji referred to as “naraaz fufa”, Mr. Nabin said in his two-and-a-half minute video message.
Also Read | PM Modi used student interaction as political campaign: Kharge
Questions Opposition anger
“I want to ask the Opposition, when India is developing today, why are they angry? When India abrogates Article 370 and hoists the tricolor at Lal Chowk in Kashmir, why do they get angry? Today, when Naxalism is being completely eradicated from its roots, why do they get angry?” he asked. “With the slogan under which they remained in power for so many years, today when that slogan has been truly fulfilled and 25 crore poor families have been brought out of poverty by Modi Ji, they are angry even at this,” he added.
Without naming anyone, Mr. Nabin explained that Opposition leaders cannot bear to see India’s development, heritage, and culture moving forward.
Personal interest, prestige
“Because they remain completely hidden in personal interests and personal prestige. The situation of “naraaz fufa” within a family has today become the situation of the Opposition in India. I want to state clearly that Modi Ji’s vision is to fulfil the dream of a Viksit Bharat by 2047, and with that dream, today, 140 crore Indians have set out,” he said.
No matter how much anger or opposition comes from the political Opposition, India’s development will not be stopped, and together with 140 crore countrymen, the resolve of a developed India will be fulfilled, he added.
Earlier in the day, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi lashed out at Mr. Modi and Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary regarding the harsh police action taken against protesting students in Bihar.

headline: Amid concerns over conflicting territorial claims and military buildup along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the Indian and Chinese armies held their first Corps Commander-level meeting in the Eastern Sector on Sunday (September 6, 2026), marking a...
full_text:
Amid concerns over conflicting territorial claims and military buildup along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the Indian and Chinese armies held their first Corps Commander-level meeting in the Eastern Sector on Sunday (September 6, 2026), marking a significant expansion of the military dialogue mechanism beyond the Ladakh sector.
The meeting was held at the Vacha-Damai Border Personnel Meeting Point in Arunachal Pradesh amid reports of tension in the Taksing area of the Upper Subansiri district.
According to Defence Ministry sources, Lieutenant General Girish Kalia, Commander of the 3 Corps (Spear Corps), led a 12-member delegation that included an Inspector General of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police.
The talks are significant as Corps Commander-level meetings between the two armies have largely been held at the Chushul-Moldo Border Meeting Point in eastern Ladakh, particularly after the June 2020 Galwan Valley clashes. The meeting comes days before India hosts the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi from September 11 to 13, where Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to participate.
The 3 Corps, headquartered at Rangapahar in Nagaland, is responsible for operational areas along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh. The Indian Army has two Corps formations responsible for the frontier in the State — the Tezpur-based 4 Corps and the Rangapahar-based 3 Corps.
Until now, the Corps Commander-level mechanism had primarily been used to address military issues and tensions along the western sector of the India-China boundary in Ladakh. The mechanism became particularly important following the Galwan clashes, in which both sides suffered casualties.
Since then, India and China have continued to use military and diplomatic channels to manage differences and maintain stability along the LAC.
The latest meeting comes amid reports of continued Chinese activity and alleged incursions in the Taksing area, despite two high-level engagements since July.
On August 6, the two countries held the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs. This was followed by the 25th round of talks between the Special Representatives (SR) on the Boundary Question in Beijing on August 26. National Security Adviser Ajit Doval represented India, while the Chinese delegation was led by Wang Yi, Member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs.
The two sides signed an eight-point outcome document following the SR-level talks. The agreement included a decision to establish two additional Border Personnel Meeting Points and new hotlines to strengthen communication and confidence-building mechanisms along the frontier.
According to sources, one of the newly proposed meeting points will be in the Eastern Sector under the operational responsibility of the 3 Corps, while another will be in the Central Sector. The sources clarified that Joshimath is not among the newly identified meeting points.
Meanwhile, the Indian Army has been closely reviewing its operational preparedness along the frontier. Recently, Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth visited the headquarters of the 3 Corps, where formation commanders briefed him about operational readiness and measures being undertaken to strengthen combat capabilities.

About 6.3% of voters in Manipur and 11.2% of voters in Sikkim have been deleted from the electoral rolls after the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise. The final photo electoral rolls were published in both northeastern States on Sunday (September 6, 2026).
Before the SIR exercise began, Manipur had 20,93,076 voters, and Sikkim had 4,71,081 voters. After the SIR, the names of 1.85 lakh voters — 1,32,456 in Manipur and 52,614 in Sikkim — were deleted from the rolls of the two States. Manipur now has 19,60,620 eligible voters, while Sikkim has 4,18,467.
Before and during the SIR exercise, Manipur’s Kuki-Zo groups expressed fears that community members displaced after the ethnic conflict erupted on May 3, 2023, would be deleted from the electoral rolls, though the government sought to dispel such apprehensions.
More women voters in Manipur
In Manipur, female voters (10,06,962) outnumber their male counterparts (9,53,350), recording a gender ratio of 1,056 females for every 1,000 male electors. The State has 308 third-gender electors.
In a statement, the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) said the final photo electoral rolls were published in compliance with the instructions issued by the Election Commission of India. The draft electoral roll published on July 5 had 19,34,399 electors.
Altogether, 96,985 claims and objections filed during the claims and objections period were processed for the final roll. In addition, all forms received before July 5 were processed for final publication. “A total of 56,871 electors have been included, and a total of 30,650 electors have been deleted from the draft electoral roll,” the statement said.
The CEO’s office said it received 19,34,399 of the total enumeration forms generated for the electors. Altogether, 1,58,677 electors whose enumeration forms were not received were excluded from the draft electoral roll. Of them, 72,473 were identified as shifted, 43,000 as deceased, 34,740 as absent, 7,394 as duplicate entries, and 1,070 under other categories.
Logical discrepancies in Sikkim
The Sikkim CEO’s office in Gangtok said the State’s final electoral roll has 4,18,467 voters, after the deletion of 52,614 names.
The draft electoral roll released in July had 4,33,294 electors, of whom 3,61,159 or 83.35% were successfully mapped with their own or parents’ electoral details from the previous qualifying roll or the last SIR. The remaining 72,135 electors (16.65%) could not be mapped, an official statement said.
Among the mapped electors, the Election Commission’s digital system identified 52,384 as having “logical discrepancies”.
“A total of 1,24,519 electors, comprising those in the unmapped and logical discrepancy categories, were issued notices to appear for hearings and establish their eligibility. Following hearings and verification, 16,485 electors were found ineligible,” the statement said.
Another 324 electors were deleted through Form-7 on grounds including death or shifting from the address. The total number of electors deleted during the claims and objections process was 16,809.
A total of 1,982 electors were then added back to the final roll following claims and objections, bringing the total number of electors from the draft roll to 4,18,467.
The final roll includes 2,12,534 male voters, 2,05,931 females, and two belonging to the third gender.

headline: India, China to hold first Corps Commander-level talks today at Wacha along LAC in Arunachal Pradesh
full_text:
India, China to hold first Corps Commander-level talks today at Wacha along LAC in Arunachal Pradesh
The first meeting between the officers at the Corps Commander level in the eastern sector has reportedly been scheduled for September 6.
The Armies of India and China are scheduled to meet today at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point in Arunachal Pradesh for the first Corps Commander-level talks between them amid ongoing issues between the two sides along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in the area.
Sources said the first meeting between the officers at the Corps Commander level in the eastern sector has been scheduled to be held on September 6 and would help to address the ongoing issues in the area. The meeting is to be held at the Wacha border meeting point on the Indian side.
At the meeting, the Indian side would be represented by the 3 Corps Commander, Lt Gen Girish Kalia. Indian Army’s two Corps formations look after the Line of Actual Control with China in Arunachal Pradesh, including the Tezpur-based 4 Corps and the Rangapahar-based 3 Corps.
Also Read | SCO’s China test: Can India cooperate without trusting Beijing?
The Indian Army has taken a very firm stance in dealing with the position taken by the Chinese troops in the area where issues are going on, sources said.
India and China have different perceptions of the Line of Actual Control in their territories and at times, that leads to issues on the ground.
The Indian and Chinese sides have, till now, been holding Corps Commander-level meetings to address the issues between them at the LAC at the Chusul-Moldo border meeting point in the Ladakh sector after the Galwan clashes in 2020, in which both sides suffered major casualties.
Also Read | India at the SCO: Navigating China, Russia and a changing Eurasian order
The meetings are taking place after the visit of National Security Advisor Ajit Doval to China, after which the two sides announced a number of measures to maintain peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control.
Recently, Army Chief Gen Dhiraj Seth had also visited the 3 Corps headquarters and was briefed on the operational readiness and steps taken to further enhance the combat capability by the formation commanders.
Also Read | India, China must first settle smaller disputes
India had responded very strongly during the Galwan crisis in response to Chinese attempts to unilaterally alter the Line of Actual Control in the Eastern Ladakh sector by moving forward a large number of troops and rebalancing responsibilities of its Strike Corps for mountain warfare.

headline: MP: 10 dead, 25 hospitalised after alleged spurious liquor consumption in Sagar
full_text:
MP: 10 dead, 25 hospitalised after alleged spurious liquor consumption in Sagar
Ten people died and over 25 were hospitalised after alleged spurious liquor consumption in Sagar, Madhya Pradesh, with six in serious condition.
At least 10 people died and around 25 were hospitalised after allegedly consuming spurious liquor in Baraj village of Madhya Pradesh’s Sagar district on the intervening night of Saturday and Sunday, prompting the district administration to order a magisterial inquiry.
“A group of people from Baraj village consumed liquor on Saturday night. Their condition deteriorated soon after and they complained of nausea and vomiting. They were rushed to hospital where five were declared dead. Six others are in serious condition and are undergoing treatment,” Superintendent of Police Anurag Sujania said.
“Prima facie, the cause of death appears to be poisoning, but we are awaiting the autopsy report for confirmation. A case has been registered and investigation is underway,” the SP added.
A team from the excise department also reached the village and seized liquor bottles from a local vend for forensic examination.
Also read: Gujarat spurious liquor case death toll rises to 13; three remain hospitalised
Chief medical and health officer Devesh Pateriya said, “The first death was reported on Saturday evening and nine people died on Sunday morning. The patients are reaching from three-four villages of the district. As many as 25 people reached civil hospital and referred to medical college in Sagar.”
District collector Pratibha Pal said, “Following deaths caused by the consumption of spurious liquor in Nauraj and Googra Khurd villages of the Banda block in Sagar, Madhya Pradesh, officials met with the affected families and reviewed the medical care being provided to patients admitted to the hospital.
The administration has appealed to anyone who has consumed the liquor and is experiencing symptoms such as vomiting, headache, or fever to visit the nearest health center immediately for a check-up as a precaution.”
Chief Minister Mohan Yadav ordered an inquiry. “The news of deaths caused by alcohol consumption in the Banda-Shahgarh area of Sagar district is extremely tragic and unfortunate. I have directed the minister in-charge and the officials to conduct an immediate inquiry and take strict action against those responsible. No one found guilty in this matter will be spared,” he said.
The incident comes days after a licensed liquor contractor had lodged a complaint with the Excise Office alleging the sale of counterfeit liquor branded as ‘Bombay Whisky’ in the area. Four days ago, during an excise department meeting, licensed contractors had raised strong objections over the alleged supply of illicit and spurious liquor in the district.
The collector has ordered a magisterial inquiry into the incident.

headline: At least 11 people died after consuming spurious liquor in Madhya Pradesh’s Sagar district on Sunday (September 6, 2026).
full_text:
At least 11 people died after consuming spurious liquor in Madhya Pradesh’s Sagar district on Sunday (September 6, 2026).
Following directions from Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, the government launched a police investigation, suspended three excise officials and two police officers, and relieved one excise official from duty and transferred her. Speaking in New Delhi, Mr. Yadav termed the deaths “extremely distressing and unfortunate” and said “no guilty party will be spared”.
Deepak Saxena, the State Excise Commissioner, told The Hindu that action was taken against four officials for serious negligence and for failing to act on recent complaints about the sale of spurious liquor in some villages of the district.
Sagar Superintendent of Police, Anurag Sujania, said 12 suspects have been detained and are being questioned.
Officials said that early on Sunday, people fell ill in four villages – Nauraj, Gogra Khurd, Bamura, and Patan under the Banda tehsil limits.
Sagar Collector Pratibha Pal said post-mortem examinations were still ongoing and the administration is on the lookout for people who have fallen ill. “A doctors’ team is screening for such people, and officials like the SDM are on the spot. We are trying to identify anyone with such symptoms and send them to the Bundelkhand Medical College for observation,” she said.
Ms. Pal said a few postmortem examinations indicated that consumption of methyl alcohol may have caused the deaths. “Interactions with locals indicated that the deaths occurred after they (victims) consumed illegal, spurious liquor. Screening has already begun in the affected villages,” Ms. Pal added.
She said the initial investigation pointed to the involvement of a gang from Uttar Pradesh. “There is a gang from Lalitpur, U.P., which is involved in supplying methyl alcohol, and since we share a border with Lalitpur, we have received information that their chain in our area has also come to (our) notice. Further investigation is underway,” she added.
Additional SP of Sagar district, Narendra Solanki, told The Hindu that, besides the dead, those who fell ill were hospitalised. “But all are out of danger now,” he said.
Mr. Sujania, too, said the liquor could have come from Lalitpur. “Such activities have been found there even in the past. So, we are working in the same direction and will reach its main source soon. We have detained 10-12 people so far and are trying to establish a link through a systematic interrogation. We are also trying to curtail its movement, if it is anywhere else, to prevent anymore loss of life,” he said.
Ajay Lodhi, a resident of Nauraj who fell ill after drinking the spurious liquor, told reporters that fake alcohol is sold in the villages and that he bought it from a small grocery shop in his village.
Mr. Saxena suspended Kirti Dubey (Assistant Commissioner Excise, Sagar), Dilip Khandate (Assistant District Excise Officer), and Proshni Ureti (Excise Sub-Inspector, Banda Circle). Neerja Srivastava, Deputy Commissioner and in-charge of the Divisional Flying Squad, was attached to the Gwalior headquarters.
The Banda police station in-charge and the Ghughra police outpost in-charge have also been suspended.
“Prima facie, it has been found that there had been some complaints in the area in the past few weeks, and the officials were aware of this but failed to act properly. Had they run a seizure campaign or taken any action, the sale could have been controlled. It was their responsibility,” Mr. Saxena, who is among the senior officials deployed in Sagar to handle the situation by the Chief Minister, said about the suspensions.
He denied that there were complaints from other districts, but said there has been a pattern in the production and sale of illicit liquor in Sagar.
“This is why we have deployed the team of the state flying squad in Sagar for the next few days. But we cannot label this as a single unfortunate incident and need to take lessons from this. We have instructed officials in all districts to run campaigns against such liquor by inspecting shops and visiting villages,” he said, adding that a meeting of excise officials from all districts has been scheduled for Monday.
“We will have to take this issue up in campaign mode by breaking the supply chain of illicit liquor. We will also conduct random inspections to check methyl alcohol content in liquor sold at shops to determine if it is counterfeit,” he said.
Earlier, Chief Minister Yadav said, “The news of death due to alcohol consumption in the Banda-Shahgarh area of Sagar district is extremely distressing and unfortunate. The in-charge Minister and officials of Sagar district have been directed to immediately investigate the incident and take the strictest possible action against the culprits. No guilty party will be spared in this matter after the investigation.”
The Madhya Pradesh Congress hit out at the BJP government, demanded a judicial inquiry into the incident, the arrest of those responsible within 24 hours, and a compensation of ₹25 lakh for each victim.
State Congress Jitu Patwari wrote to the Chief Minister saying, “The second such tragedy surfacing in Sagar is proof that the BJP government has not learned from the first incident! Don’t wait for the third warning now! Take action so severe that no more news of deaths from poisonous liquor emerges from any village in Sagar!”

headline: Delhi HC quashes FIR arising out of fight between friends, directs community service at Manipur hospital
full_text:
Delhi HC quashes FIR arising out of fight between friends, directs community service at Manipur hospital
New Delhi, The Delhi High Court has quashed an FIR that was lodged following a fight between friends as the dispute has been amicably settled, and directed them to do community service at a hospital in Manipur.
Noting that the complainant and the two accused remain friends and harbour no subsisting grievance against each other, the high court said the likelihood of the proceedings culminating in a conviction is remote and continuation of the criminal proceedings would serve no useful purpose.
"… I am of the view that it would be appropriate to make the relief sought subject to undertaking community service and paying appropriate costs. The petitioner and respondent no. 4 shall undertake community service for a total of six sessions of two hours each at Regional Institute of Medical Science, Manipur," Justice Prateek Jalan said in an order passed on August 21.
The court said both the friends should report to the hospital's medical superintendent who would assign suitable duties to them. The community service should be completed within two months from the date of commencement after which the medical superintendent would issue a compliance certificate and it should be placed on court's record.
The court also directed the two men to collectively pay ₹10,000 to the Delhi High Court Bar Association within two weeks.
The court passed the order while allowing a plea seeking quashing of an FIR lodged at the Dabri Police Station here.
The FIR was registered in March last year on the complaint of a man alleging that he was residing in a rented flat with his friend and both the accused forcibly entered the premises and assaulted him and his friend.
The FIR stated that one of the victims was allegedly kicked and punched, causing him to fall headfirst onto the kitchen slab and sustain a head injury.
In its order, the court noted that the FIR did not allege use of any firearm or sharp weapon, or any separate act directed towards causing the head injury.
The court was informed that the parties have settled the issue without any coercion or undue pressure and signed a settlement deed.
The injured person also told the court that he had recovered from his injury and was not suffering from any lasting consequence. The parties stated that they remained friends and had no subsisting grievance against each other.
The court, while quashing the FIR, noted that the dispute between the parties arose out of a quarrel between friends and it was resolved shortly after registration of the FIR.
"In these circumstances, continuation of the criminal proceedings would serve no meaningful purpose and would only perpetuate discord and animosity between parties. The ends of justice would, therefore, be better served by bringing the proceedings to a quietus," the court observed.

NEW DELHI: Congress leaderRahul Gandhi on Sunday shared a video of his interaction with three students who were injured during police action amid recent student protests in Bihar.The three were part of a group of students from Bihar who met the Lok Sabha leader of opposition at his Delhi residence on September 3. âThink about it: what crime had these children committed that they were shot? They had asked the government for just three things â education, employment, and accountability,â the Raebareli MP wrote on X.

They were children from poor families who had gone out to study carrying the dreams of their families â some wanted a good job, while others wanted to change the circumstances of their homes,â he added.The Congress leader further remarked that while their physical wounds would heal, there is no answer to how the psychological trauma they had suffered could be treated.

headline: ‘Distressing’: PM Modi expresses condolences after Delhi building collapse
full_text:
‘Distressing’: PM Modi expresses condolences after Delhi building collapse
“The collapse of a building at Satya Niketan, Delhi is distressing. Condolences to those who lost their loved ones,” the Prime Minister's office said.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday condoled the loss of lives following the collapse of a building in Delhi's Satya Niketan area, terming the incident as “distressing.”
“The collapse of a building at Satya Niketan, Delhi is distressing. Condolences to those who lost their loved ones,” the Prime Minister's office said in a post on X.
PM Modi said authorities present at the site were working to assist those affected by the mishap. The Prime Minister further said he was “praying for the speedy recovery” of those injured in the incident.
At least five people were killed, and around 40 students feared trapped after a multi-storey building of a boys' PG hostel in Satya Niketan collapsed on Sunday afternoon. Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta said that 11 people had been rescued from the rubble.
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta, L-G Sandhu visit site
Rescue operations continued at the site, with Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta and L-G Taranjit Singh Sandhu visiting the spot to review the situation. Delhi minister Kapil Mishra had also visited the spot.
Teams from DDMA, NDRF, Delhi Fire Services, Delhi Police, MCD, CTS and Civil Defence were deployed, with CM Gupta saying the rescue and emergency operations were underway on “war footing.”
Students rescued from the rubble were taken to nearby hospitals, while two of them were admitted to the AIIMS trauma centre and are in a critical state, the hospital said. CM Gupta also visited the AIIMS trauma centre, along with minister Kapil Mishra.
Delhi Police says FIR being registered in the incident
Deputy commissioner of police (southwest) Amit Goel said an FIR has been registered against the building owner Hariram and others under sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder), 290 (negligent conduct with respect to pulling down, repairing or constructing buildings), and 125 (act endangering life or personal safety of others) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) at the South Campus police station. The DCP said renovation work was underway on the ground floor, which led to collapse of the building.
The Additional DCP had earlier said statements were being recorded from the eyewitnesses and those rescued as to what happened and how the incident occurred. “Whatever legal action is required will be taken, and further action is underway,” Poswal said.

headline: Jharkhand minister Sudivya Kumar dies of heart attack at 56
full_text:
Jharkhand minister Sudivya Kumar dies of heart attack at 56
Jharkhand minister and senior JMM leader Sudivya Kumar died after a heart attack on Sunday. His sudden death has jolted the party and government, which called it an irreparable loss.
Jharkhand minister and senior Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) leader Sudivya Kumar died on Sunday, the party said. He was 56 and died of a heart attack, according to a JMM leader.
Kumar, a legislator from Giridih, held the Higher and Technical Education and Urban Development portfolios. He also had charge of Tourism, Arts and Culture, and Sports and Youth Affairs. His death has left the JMM and the Jharkhand government mourning the loss of a senior leader and minister.
In a condolence message posted on X, Chief Minister Hemant Soren shared a heartfelt tribute for Kumar, whom he referred to as "Sonu Bhaiya."
"Sonu Bhaiya was not just a senior colleague or political associate to me. He was like an elder brother – affectionate, guiding, and steadfastly standing by my side in every difficult time. The moments spent with him and the lessons learnt from him will always remain with me," he wrote (in Hindi).
The Jharkhand CM added, "As a dedicated soldier of the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha, he devoted his entire life to the fight for Jharkhand's identity, rights, and pride. His dedication to Jharkhandiyat and his indomitable spirit will always be remembered."
The JMM also expressed shock and grief over Kumar's death, calling it an "irreparable loss" to the party, the government and Jharkhand. "The Jharkhand Mukti Morcha family is stunned and heart-broken by the untimely demise of Sudivya Kumar, a dedicated comrade of JMM and a Minister in Jharkhand government," the party said in a post on X.
The party also conveyed condolences to Kumar’s family and prayed for peace to the departed soul. He is survived by two daughters and a son.
Kumar was first elected to the Jharkhand Assembly from Giridih in 2019. A close aide of Chief Minister Hemant Soren, he played a key role in managing crises within the JMM, including during Soren’s arrest in 2024 in connection with an alleged land fraud and money laundering case.
He had returned this week from Karnataka, where he led a Jharkhand government delegation to explore ways to improve tourism infrastructure management in the state. During the visit, he met Karnataka Tourism Minister KJ George and discussed possibilities of cooperation between the two states in tourism and forest management.
The delegation also held detailed discussions on the possibility of associating Jungle Lodges & Resorts as a knowledge partner for better operation and management of tourism assets and resorts at major tourist destinations in Jharkhand.
Kumar’s death marks the loss of a senior JMM leader who handled several key ministries and played an important role in the party and the government.

headline: Jharkhand minister Sudivya Kumar dies at 56, state declares two-day mourning
full_text:
Jharkhand minister Sudivya Kumar dies at 56, state declares two-day mourning
The Jharkhand government declared a two-day state mourning in honour of Sudivya Kumar, besides cancelling all its scheduled programmes
Senior Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) leader and state higher and technical education and urban development minister Sudivya Kumar died to cardiac arrest early Sunday, following which the Jharkhand government declared two-day state mourning in honour of the Giridih MLA, considered the party’s ‘think tank’ and a close advisor to chief minister Hemant Soren.
The 56-year-old minister, who also held charge of the tourism, arts and culture and sports and youth affairs ministries, was admitted to a private hospital late Saturday night after complaining of chest pain at his residence in Giridih. Doctors declared him dead around 4am on Sunday.
Dr Shahzad Shaikh of Mercy Hospital said, “The patient, Sudivya Kumar Sonu, came to us at around 2.15am. He had been experiencing chest pain for approximately two hours. By the time he arrived, he had already aspirated. Basically, the vomit had gone into his lungs. He was immediately intubated to secure his airway. An ECG was performed, which showed signs of a heart attack...About 10–15 minutes later, the patient collapsed, and CPR was initiated. All necessary resuscitative procedures were carried out. However, despite all resuscitative measures, the patient could not be saved.”
Kumar, serving his second consecutive term as legislator from Giridih, was later cremated with full state honours in his hometown, attended by the chief minister, cabinet colleagues and a host of elected representatives cutting across party lines.
Chief minister Hemant Soren along with governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar expressed condolences. Both went to Giridih to pay floral tributes to Kumar, who had risen through the party ranks over the past three decades.
“Late at night, I received the heartbreaking news of the passing of my elder brother, our beloved Sudivya Kumar Ji. Accepting this news is extremely difficult for me. Sonu Bhaiya’s departure has left a void in my life that cannot be expressed in words,” Soren said.
“Kumar was not just a senior colleague or political associate but was like an elder brother...affectionate, guiding, and steadfastly standing by my side in every difficult time. The moments spent with him and the lessons learned from him will always remain with me,” Soren posted on X.
From the days of the Jharkhand movement, he stood with full devotion and strength alongside the late Baba Dishom Guruji (JMM founder Shibu Soren), the chief minister said.
As a dedicated soldier of the JMM, he devoted his entire life to fighting for Jharkhand’s identity, rights, and pride, Soren said, adding his dedication to ‘Jharkhandiyat’ and his indomitable spirit will always be remembered.
“Today, as I remember him, my heart keeps thinking how fragile life is. The voice that was among us until yesterday is now only in memories. Sonu Bhaiya, your passing is a personal loss for me. Your absence will always be felt. I will carry your affection, your struggles, and your commitment to Jharkhand with me for life,” Soren posted.
“The news of the untimely demise of the Honorable State Minister, Shri Sudivya Kumar, is deeply saddening and heart-wrenching. His passing is an irreparable loss to the state. May the Almighty grant the bereaved family and supporters the strength to bear this immense grief,” said governor Santosh Gangwar.
The JMM expressed grief over the minister’s death, describing his demise as an “irreparable loss” to the party, the government and Jharkhand.
“The Jharkhand Mukti Morcha family is stunned and heart-broken by the untimely demise of Sudivya Kumar, a dedicated comrade of JMM and a Minister in the Jharkhand government,” the party said in a statement.
Government declares two-day state mourning
