headline: Drug regulator cracks down after misbranded Abhayrab rabies vaccine seized in Delhi
full_text:
Drug regulator cracks down after misbranded Abhayrab rabies vaccine seized in Delhi
A seized batch of Abhayrab rabies vaccine from an unlicensed Delhi premises was found misbranded and substandard. The finding has triggered tighter nationwide surveillance and legal action against unauthorised drug networks.
Regulatory and law enforcement agencies have intensified action against the illegal manufacture and distribution of spurious drugs after a batch of Abhayrab rabies vaccine was seized and later found to be misbranded, according to a notice from the Drugs Controller General of India.
The notice said the agencies are maintaining "strict and continuous surveillance" to identify and disrupt unauthorised drug supply networks and safeguard the quality and safety of medicines available to the public.
The action follows the seizure of Abhayrab rabies vaccine bearing batch number KE25012 from an unlicensed premises in Delhi's Mukherjee Nagar on April 22. The notice said the vaccine was found to be "misbranded" and "not manufactured by Indian Immunologicals Ltd.", while the Central Drugs Laboratory in Kasauli later reported it as "misbranded and not of standard quality".
As part of the enforcement action, Delhi Police's Crime Branch, along with drugs inspectors from the Delhi government's Drugs Control Department, searched the premises and seized the vaccine. Officials from the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation were then called in for legal sampling, and the samples were sent to the Central Drugs Laboratory, Kasauli, for examination. The laboratory's findings, including details of the misbranding detected in the seized product, were later communicated by the DCGI to states and Union territories for regulatory vigilance and necessary action.
In a communication dated August 27, the DCGI asked all state drug controllers to alert their inspectorate staff and maintain strict vigilance over the movement, distribution and availability of the affected batch. States were also asked to take appropriate regulatory action under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and the rules framed under it.
As a precautionary measure, the manufacturer of Abhayrab issued a public communication on the misbranded product and reaffirmed its commitment to quality, saying every batch of Abhayrab is released for sale only after independent testing and batch-release certification by the Central Drugs Laboratory, Kasauli.
The notice said vaccines given at hospitals, clinics and government healthcare facilities, or dispensed through licensed pharmacies, reach patients through the authorised and regulated supply chain after the prescribed quality-control and batch-release procedures. It also said no part of the batch in question was exported to any other country.
The seizure and follow-up action are part of an ongoing surveillance and enforcement mechanism to detect unauthorised manufacturing and distribution activities and prevent the circulation of misbranded and spurious medicines.
The development comes amid intensified scrutiny of the authenticity and quality of medicines supplied through unauthorised channels. "Four persons have been arrested by Delhi Police" in connection with the case, the notice said, adding that further investigation and appropriate legal action are being taken by the competent authorities.

headline: Observing that the use of mobile phones is creating a negative impact among children, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday (September 5, 2026) said that mobile phones should be restricted in schools.
full_text:
Observing that the use of mobile phones is creating a negative impact among children, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday (September 5, 2026) said that mobile phones should be restricted in schools.
The Chief Minister who was addressing a gathering on the occasion of Teachers Day said that unless we address such issues there is no such significance of reforms in education or observing Teachers’ Day.
“My votes may perhaps decrease. But I will still say that the use of phones in schools needs to be regulated. In Gujarat, phones are not used in schools from Class I to Class XII,” Mr. Adhikari said. Earlier this year the Karnataka government had said that it was mulling over a law for restricting mobile phones for children under 16 years.
Speaking at the gathering in Kolkata the Chief Minister announced that two ‘CM Shri’ schools, modelled after PM Shri schools, will be opened in each district. “In these schools, admission will be given from Class VI based on merit. Like the Central Model School, the schools will have all modern facilities, including smart boards. Large sports-related institutions will be set up in the western and northern regions.” he said.
The Chief Minister also announced that his government would undertake teacher recruitment in a transparent manner in accordance with the directions of the Supreme Court and the Calcutta High Court.
“Merit will be the primary criterion for selection. We will recruit teachers in accordance with the directions of the Supreme Court and the Calcutta High Court. There is no need to worry. I have asked officials to ensure viva voce should not exceed five marks,” he said.
The Chief Minister said that his government has amended the OBC list and the fresh recruitment will be undertaken as per the amendment list. The West Bengal Legislative Assembly had recently passed two OBC amendment bills in June 2026, removing 77 communities (mostly added post-2010) and reverting the state’s OBC list back to the original 66 pre-2010 categories.
Allegations of corruption in the recruitment of teachers have surfaced in the previous Trinamool Congress government and several prominent leaders of the ruling party including former Education Minister Partha Chatterjee were arrested for the alleged involvement in the scam.

headline: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Sunday (September 6, 2026) accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of turning his interaction with students at Delhi University’s Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) into a “political campaign” instead of engagin...

headline: Dinesh Sharma, ex-UP Deputy CM, appointed Andaman and Nicobar Lt Governor
full_text:
Dinesh Sharma, ex-UP Deputy CM, appointed Andaman and Nicobar Lt Governor
BJP Rajya Sabha MP Dinesh Sharma has been appointed Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The former Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister said the post was a commitment to the Constitution, the nation and public service.
BJP Rajya Sabha MP and former Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Dinesh Sharma was appointed Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands on Saturday, the Rashtrapati Bhavan said in a late-night communique.
Sharma, 62, will succeed Admiral D K Joshi (retd), who has served as the Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory since October 8, 2017.
"The President of India is pleased to appoint Dr Dinesh Sharma as Lt Governor of Andaman and Nicobar Islands with effect from the date he assumes charge of his office," the Rashtrapati Bhavan said.
Following his appointment, Sharma expressed gratitude to President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and the BJP's central leadership in a post on X.
"Hon'ble President, Hon'ble Prime Minister, Hon'ble Home Minister, and the party's central leadership -- my heartfelt thanks," Sharma said.
He thanked senior leaders, well-wishers, friends and citizens for their continued support and blessings, saying the new responsibility was not merely a position but a commitment to the Constitution, the nation and public service.
"I pledge to fulfill this duty with complete devotion, honesty, and dedication," he said, adding that he hoped their affection, trust and blessings would continue.
Sharma, a former deputy chief minister of Uttar Pradesh, is currently a BJP member of the Rajya Sabha and serves as its vice chairperson. His term in the Upper House was scheduled to end on November 25.

headline: JMM senior leader and state Higher and Technical Education and Urban Development Minister Sudivya Kumar has died, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha said on Sunday (September 6, 2026).
full_text:
JMM senior leader and state Higher and Technical Education and Urban Development Minister Sudivya Kumar has died, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha said on Sunday (September 6, 2026).
He was 56.
Mr. Kumar, a legislator from Giridih, also held charge of crucial Ministries like Tourism, Arts & Culture and Sports and Youth Affairs.
Mr. Kumar died of cardiac arrest, a JMM leader said.

Mr. Kumar was first elected to the Jharkhand Assembly from Giridih in 2019.
He is survived by two daughters and a son.
A close aide of Chief Minister Hemant Soren, Mr. Kumar played a key role in managing crises within the JMM, including during Mr. Soren's arrest in 2024 in connection with an alleged land fraud and money laundering case.
Mr. Kumar returned this week from Karnataka, where he led a Jharkhand government delegation to explore ways to improve tourism infrastructure management in the state.

headline: Rescue operation underway after a five-storey building collapsed at Satya Niketan area, in New Delhi. (PTI Photo)
full_text:
Rescue operation underway after a five-storey building collapsed at Satya Niketan area, in New Delhi. (PTI Photo)
NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday expressed grief over the building collapse in Delhiâs Satya Niketan, urging the NDRF, Delhi Fire Service and other rescue teams to make every possible effort to reach those trapped under the debris. One person has died, two are in critical condition and several others are feared trapped following the collapse, officials said.Rahul Gandhi, in a post on X, said: " The news of the building collapse in Satya Niketan, Delhi, is extremely heartbreaking and alarming. Reports indicate that several people are trapped under the debris, including many students from Delhi University. My appeal is that NDRF, Delhi Fire Service, and all rescue teams reach every single student by making every possible effort, ensuring that the injured receive the best possible immediate treatment, so that no effort is spared in saving anyone."
"Congress and NSUI workers are present at the scene and are ready to provide every possible assistance. In this hour of difficulty, we all stand with the victims and their families. Students' lives were already filled with strugglesânow the situation has turned life-threatening. Due to the lack of good hostels in colleges or universities, students are forced to live in PG accommodations, 40-40 at a time under one roof, in inhumane conditions.
Every student's life is precious, and their protection must be ensured under all circumstances," Rahul added.
A five-storey building being used as a boys' paying guest accommodation collapsed in the Satya Niketan area of South-West Delhi at around 1.30 pm on Sunday, triggering a major search and rescue operation in the densely populated neighbourhood near Delhi University's South Campus.Officials said one person was killed in the collapse, while two others were critically injured. Several people were initially feared trapped beneath the rubble as rescue personnel searched through the debris.JCB machines were deployed at the site to clear the collapsed structure and assist emergency teams in reaching those who may have been trapped.Delhi Police said the exact number of people trapped or injured was not immediately known. Multiple people were rescued and shifted to hospitals as the search operation continued.The building, located in an area lined with student accommodations, paying guest facilities and eateries, collapsed along narrow and densely populated lanes, making rescue operations challenging.
Building was being used as PG
According to Delhi Police, a local enquiry found that the structure was around 40 to 50 years old and comprised a basement and five upper floors. It was being used as a PG accommodation."From the local enquiry, it came to knowledge that this was a 40â50-year-old building, comprising a basement and five upper floors, and it was used as a PG accommodation. Repair work was underway in the basement when the incident occurred," the Delhi Police stated.The Delhi Fire Department received an alert about the collapse at around 1.30 pm, following which emergency personnel and rescue teams were rushed to the site.The rescue operation remained underway as teams continued to remove debris and search for survivors.Congress demands immediate actionCongress leader Abhishek Dutt described the incident as deeply distressing and called for immediate assistance to the victims and their families.âThe issue far more significant than the election itself is the manner in which children are losing their lives here and how buildings in Delhi keep collapsing like this,â Dutt told ANI.He described the loss of lives as âdeeply tragicâ and called on the government to support the victims' families and take steps to prevent similar incidents.âRight now, the focus must be on helping the children and their families,â he said.
Kejriwal calls collapse alarming
AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal also described the incident as "extremely tragic and alarming" and urged the Delhi government to take large-scale measures to improve public safety."The incident of the building collapse in Satya Niketan, Delhi, is extremely tragic and alarming. I pray to God that the people trapped in the debris are rescued safely and quickly. Due to the government's negligence in Delhi, many such accidents have already occurred. The government must wake up from its slumber. There is a need to take large-scale action to ensure the safety of citizens."AAP MP Atishi demanded urgent relief operations and a high-level inquiry into the collapse."The news of the building collapse at Satya Niketan in Delhi's Moti Bagh is extremely heartbreaking and alarming. The apprehension that several people, including students, are trapped under the debris is deeply distressing. We appeal to the administration to carry out relief and rescue operations with utmost promptness and to safely extricate all those trapped under the rubble."She added, "The government must conduct a high-level investigation into this incident and ensure strict action against those responsible for negligence, so that such painful tragedies can be prevented in the future."AAP leader Saurabh Bharadwaj alleged that unchecked illegal construction and corruption had contributed to repeated building-related incidents in Delhi."Just a few days ago, you saw a four-story building collapse in Saket. It took the government and the MCD a whole week to admit it was a four-story building. Initially, they kept claiming it had only two floors... I am telling you about this case here as well. An illegal PG facility was operating in a four-story building... A basement was being illegally excavated there during the monsoon season," Bharadwaj told ANI.
He further alleged lapses involving multiple departments, saying, "Unless you go beyond the 'small fish' and target the 'big crocodiles'âthe DC, the Commissioner, the one who was walking his dog in the stadium- this will keep happening... Previously, only the MCD was taking bribes. But for the past year, the MCD, the Fire Department, and the SDM/DM departments have all been taking bribes."AAP leader and former Delhi mayor Shelly Oberoi also criticised the Delhi government and the BJP-ruled Municipal Corporation of Delhi over alleged safety violations."Sometimes buildings are collapsing, sometimes fire incidents are shaking Delhi. The tragic accident in Satya Niketan is yet another proof of the BJP's dilapidated governance system and the failure of the BJP-ruled MCD. No action against illegal constructions, no adherence to safety rules, and no accountability either. Why should the people of Delhi pay the price for these accidents with their lives?"

headline: CM orders magisterial probe, FIR against building owner over Satya Niketan PG collapse
full_text:
CM orders magisterial probe, FIR against building owner over Satya Niketan PG collapse
Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southwest) Amit Goel said an FIR has been registered against building owner Hariram and others.
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta ordered a magisterial inquiry into the Satya Niketan boys’ PG building collapse and directed that an FIR be filed against the building owner, following an on-site review and preliminary assessment.
"Those found responsible will be held fully accountable and dealt with under the strictest provisions of the law," said the CM.
DCP's statement
Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southwest) Amit Goel said an FIR has been registered against building owner Hariram and others at the South Campus police station.
The case has been registered under Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder), 290 (negligent conduct with respect to pulling down, repairing or constructing buildings) and 125 (act endangering life or personal safety of others) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
“The building was a PG. It is alleged that renovation work was being undertaken at the ground floor, which led to the collapse of the building. Multiple teams have been formed to trace the alleged persons. A total of 10 people have been rescued till now. Four were declared brought dead and one succumbed to injuries during treatment. The rescue operation is still undergoing,” said the DCP.
On being asked whether the renovation work was going on at the ground floor or the building’s basement, the DCP said that their preliminary investigation suggested it was on the ground floor.
“However, further probe will give the clear picture,” He added
Deep Dive
Delhi CM reviewed rescue and relief operations
According to the Delhi Chief Minister’s Office (CMO), Gupta reached the site soon after being informed about the incident and reviewed the rescue and relief operations with senior officials. She directed the agencies involved to make every possible effort to safely evacuate those trapped and ensure that the rescue operation was carried out without any lapse.
Multiple agencies, including the Delhi Disaster Management Authority (DDMA), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Delhi Fire Services, Delhi Police, Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), Centralised Accident and Trauma Services (CATS) and Civil Defence, have been deployed at the site and are working in coordination to carry out the rescue operation.
As a precautionary measure, the building adjacent to the collapsed structure has also been evacuated.
The Chief Minister has remained in touch with the Regional District Magistrate, Delhi Police, NDRF and other officials, seeking regular updates on the situation. She also spoke to local MP Bansuri Swaraj and RK Puram MLA Anil Sharma, who reached the spot and took stock of the ongoing rescue efforts.

CM Rekha Gupta visited AIIMS

The injured are undergoing treatment at AIIMS, where doctors are providing them with the necessary medical care. Gupta directed the medical team to ensure that all required treatment and assistance are made available to the victims.

headline: Lucknow: Nearly three years after Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati declared him as her political successor, nephew Akash Anand is once again an ordinary party worker. This marks the third instance in the past two years when aunt Mayawati took...
full_text:
Lucknow: Nearly three years after Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati declared him as her political successor, nephew Akash Anand is once again an ordinary party worker. This marks the third instance in the past two years when aunt Mayawati took away key organisational responsibilities from the 31-year-old.
At a meeting of the BSP’s national-level office-bearers here Thursday, Mayawati said Akash would continue to work in the party but would not be given any major responsibility for now. “I have allowed Akash Anand to work in the party, which is before all of you, but he still needs to become more mature,” the BSP chief said. While Akash was not present at this meeting, younger brother Ishan Anand sat in the chair usually occupied by Akash. There has been no indication as yet about Ishan replacing Akash in any formal capacity.
In a statement issued after the meeting, Mayawati invoked BSP founder Kanshi Ram, her political mentor, to say that he allowed his family members and relatives to assist with party work but was never in favour of giving them tickets to contest elections or positions in government if the party came to power.
Mayawati maintained that she followed the same principle. Akash, she said, was allowed to work in the BSP but still needs to attain political maturity. According to her, the latest move was necessary to ensure that the BSP does not suffer electoral losses.
BSP leaders confirmed to ThePrint that Akash will no longer be handling the responsibilities of national coordinator for now.
His demotion follows reports in some local newspapers suggesting Akash would play a role in selecting BSP’s candidates for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Sources in the BSP said Mayawati was unhappy with these reports and was told that they had been planted by Akash’s father-in-law and former Rajya Sabha MP, Ashok Siddharth.
Mayawati had expelled Siddharth from the party in August.
Sources close to Akash Anand said he is upset with Mayawati’s decision but has little choice other than accepting it as fait accompli. Several political parties have approached Akash with offers to join them, but he is in no hurry, said one source.
The latest shake-up within the BSP also comes against the backdrop of the party’s declining electoral fortunes in Uttar Pradesh. In 2017, it contested all 403 seats, won 19 and secured 22.23 percent of the vote. In 2022, it again contested all 403 seats but won only a single seat, with its vote share falling to 12.88 percent—its lowest in the state since 1993.
The decline continued in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, when the BSP failed to win a single seat and its vote share in Uttar Pradesh dropped further to 9.46 percent.
Also Read: Why Mayawati has revived demand for Western UP state ahead of 2027 polls
Why Akash Anand is under scrutiny
Last month, Akash Anand had written a post on X in support of Ankit Kumar, a Dalit cab driver who was reportedly banned by a cab aggregator after he objected to a group of passengers, supposedly “Railways employees”, making casteist remarks about a senior official from the Dalit community. In the same post, Akash wrote that millions of Dalit youngsters like Ankit were looking for answers from Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat, who has put forth his views on reservation on multiple occasions.
BSP insiders said Akash deleted the post after Mayawati told him to do so during a phone call.
When Akash was brought back into the party fold, Mayawati had advised him to reduce his media and social media presence, and focus instead on carrying out organisational assignments without drawing too much attention to himself, BSP insiders said.
Under the BSP’s current structure, only Mayawati dictates the party line or decides who can speak to the media and to what extent. Senior leaders such as Satish Mishra and state BSP chief Vishwanath Pal speak to the media, but their interactions are subject to restrictions.
Akash, on the other hand, is relatively more adept at media and social media management. He sought to modernise the BSP’s communication strategy and his team built a network of social media volunteers who regularly promote the party’s position online.
However, according to one BSP leader, this approach did not find favour with Mayawati.
“Behan ji is surrounded by senior leaders such as Satish Mishra and Ramji Gautam and takes advice from them. Akash was trying to bring young people into the party and wanted the BSP to become more visible in the media and on social media. He also wanted to break the party’s old organisational structure. This is why senior leadership keeps giving Mayawati negative feedback about him,” said the BSP leader, requesting anonymity.
The leader added that, owing to her limited engagement with the cadre, Mayawati now relies largely on senior leaders’ feedback. There is also some level of insecurity since she does not want any other power centre within the BSP, claimed the BSP leader. Adding, “Meanwhile, young leader Chandrashekhar is continuously reaching out to people and is also gaining acceptance. The space that he is occupying was left vacant by the BSP.”
Uttar Pradesh-based political analyst Shilp Shikha Singh said actions against Akash have weakened the BSP’s political narrative. “Perhaps no other party has treated its projected successor in this manner in such a short period. It has not only raised questions about Akash Anand’s credibility but has also weakened the party’s narrative,” she told ThePrint.
Singh said the latest developments could also strengthen the Opposition’s narrative that the BSP was not taking a strong enough position against the ruling BJP. “At a time when political parties are making efforts to attract young voters and leaders, the BSP is taking action against its own young leader.”
Seven years of political ups & downs
Akash Anand is the son of Mayawati’s younger brother Anand Kumar, who is also a vice president of the BSP.
Mayawati introduced Akash to BSP workers at a political rally in 2017 upon his return from London where he did his MBA. He was formally inducted into the party in April 2019 and emerged as one of its most prominent campaigners during the general election that year.
Mayawati named him as her political successor in December 2023 only to remove him from all party positions during the Lok Sabha campaign in May 2024 after one of his speeches led to the possibility of an FIR against him.
The BSP chief reinstated Akash to party posts in June 2024.
However, in March 2025, she again removed him from all party posts. In August that year, Akash apologised to Mayawati and was subsequently appointed national coordinator again.
A second BSP leader said the flip-flops have led to uncertainty not just over Akash’s political future but also the direction the BSP is taking. “Whenever Akash takes a position that could help revive the BSP or potentially hurt the BJP, a new crisis seems to emerge for him. Nothing is written down, but Mayawati’s decisions suggest that she remains caught between competing considerations.”
“The latest decision has put several more dots on Akash Anand’s political career. headline: Congress replaces Bhupesh Baghel with Sachin Pilot as Punjab in-charge amid internal discord
full_text:
Congress replaces Bhupesh Baghel with Sachin Pilot as Punjab in-charge amid internal discord
The reshuffle comes ahead of Punjab’s 2027 assembly polls, with the party also assigning Randeep Surjewala to Gujarat and moving other state in-charges.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Saturday removed Bhupesh Baghel as the general secretary in-charge of the poll-bound Punjab, replacing him with former Rajasthan deputy chief minister Sachin Pilot.
The party also appointed Randeep Surjewala as Gujarat in-charge, another state going to polls next year, shaking up the organisation ahead of the series of upcoming elections.
A total of three general secretaries have been allotted new states while another three leaders got dropped, according to a press release issued by party general secretary (organisation) KC Venugopal.
The Congress has also moved its three more in-charges (apart from the general secretaries) to other states. A senior Congress leader remarked that this is one of the biggest reshuffles at the higher level of the party organisation.
Baghel, the former chief minister of Chhattisgarh, has been assigned Assam, where assembly elections were held in April this year.
The Congress, according to two insiders, “rewarded” Surjewala by bringing him to Gujarat while he will continue to hold “additional responsibility as in-charge of Karnataka”.
Also read: Sachin Pilot is new Congress Punjab in-charge, Bhupesh Baghel moved to Assam in reshuffle
Karnataka gets fresh organisational focus
The reshuffle in Karnataka comes three months after DK Shivakumar was appointed the chief minister in June this year, replacing Siddaramaiah in a transition of power.
Appointed as Punjab in-charge in February 2025, Baghel’s removal comes amid his strained equation with former Punjab chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi, who has been demanding that party’s Punjab unit chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring be replaced.
Channi had boycotted nearly all meetings chaired by Baghel in the past few months leading to an impasse that is affecting the poll preparations.
Also read: Congress to launch 100-day OBC campaign over caste census format
Baghel had backed status quo in Punjab
Last month, Baghel had submitted his report on Punjab to the party high command. It favoured no leadership change in the state. According to officials, Baghel was scheduled to go to Chandigarh on Sunday for further meetings.
In his tweet, Channi thanked the party leadership for the “important decision”.
“A warm welcome to Shri Sachin Pilot Ji on his appointment as General Secretary In-charge of Punjab Congress. Heartfelt thanks to the Congress Party High Command for this important decision,” Channi posted on X.
“Shri @bhupeshbaghel Ji has been a guide and mentor for @INCPunjab and all Congress workers in the state. His guidance has been instrumental in strengthening the party at the grassroots level. Personally, I have learnt a lot from him and will always remain indebted to him. Thankful for everything sir,” Warring wrote on X.
He also congratulated Pilot for his appointment. “His energy and dynamism will for sure add to the vigour of the party ahead of crucial assembly elections just a few months away.”
Also read: BJP MP attacks Congress over low women representation in state cabinets
Punjab polls loom in 2027
Punjab faces assembly election in early 2027.
In September 2021, the Congress had forced then Punjab chief minister Captain Amrinder Singh to resign and elevated Channi to the post before the polls in 2022.
Baghel’s removal also comes ahead of the proposed Punjab yatra of Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi.
Baghel was deeply involved in the preparations for the yatra and held a meeting in Delhi last week.
Also read: Congress attacks BJP for ‘injustices’ against Dalit, Muslim women
“Gratitude to the top leadership for this new responsibility as the in-charge General Secretary of Assam Congress. Congratulations also to all newly appointed General Secretaries / State In-charges...We, all Congress workers of Chhattisgarh, are grateful for the able leadership of Congress General Secretary, the esteemed Shri Sachin Pilot Ji,” Baghel tweeted.
Pilot was handling party affairs in Chhattisgarh. A senior leader from Punjab told HT, “We now expect Channi to attend election-related meetings. The equation will also undergo a change as Pilot, 48, is younger to the 63-year-old Channi. The reshuffle was necessary as Channi is the head of the campaign committee.”
Pilot brings Rajasthan experience
Pilot brings considerable organisational experience to the assignment.
He served as Rajasthan Pradesh Congress Committee president from 2014 to 2020 and was deputy chief minister from 2018 to 2020. As PCC chief, he led the Congress campaign in Rajasthan after the party’s poor performance in the 2013 assembly elections and remained at the centre of the party’s organisational revival that culminated in its victory in the 2018 polls.
“His immediate task is likely to be less about organisational restructuring and more about ensuring that the competing factions work together on Rahul Gandhi’s proposed Punjab programme and the party’s election preparations,” said a Congress leader.
Pilot sets sights on Punjab polls
Meanwhile, Pilot said the upcoming election in Punjab would be an important opportunity for the party.
“I express my gratitude to the Congress President, the esteemed Shri@kharge ji, CPP Chairperson Smt. Sonia Gandhi ji, and the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Shri @RahulGandhi ji for assigning me the responsibility of Punjab in-charge. The elections to be held in the state in the coming days are an important opportunity for us. Our goal and resolve is to move forward with complete dedication and loyalty and to bring the party to power. I am confident that through collective efforts, a strong organization, and the hard work of the workers, we will strengthen the Congress in Punjab once again and pave the way for a return to power,” Pilot wrote on X.
Also read: Congress threatens to quit alliance if TVK backs Vijay for PM instead of Rahul Gandhi
More state in-charges reassigned
Congress MP Sukhdeo Bhagat has been given the charge of Chhattisgarh and Shrivel Prasad will handle Maharashtra affairs. PV Mohan, an AICC secretary, is made in charge of Andhra Pradesh.
Venugopal has announced that two general secretaries Jitendra Singh and party veteran Ramesh Chennithala have been dropped in the latest reshuffle. Tamil Nadu Congress president Manickam Tagore, who was in charge of Andhra Pradesh, has also been dropped.
Senior leader Mukul Wasnik will continue as General Secretary, AICC, Venugopal added.

headline: Right-wing ‘influencer’ Swatantra Bhardwaj sent to 1-day judicial custody in Jantar Mantar assault case
full_text:
Right-wing ‘influencer’ Swatantra Bhardwaj sent to 1-day judicial custody in Jantar Mantar assault case
Bhardwaj was produced before Duty Magistrate Anjali Singh of the Patiala House Court through video conference by the Delhi Police.
A Delhi court on Sunday sent right-wing ‘influencer’ Swatantra Bhardwaj to one-day judicial custody in connection with an assault case registered under the SC/ST Act.
Bhardwaj was produced before Duty Magistrate Anjali Singh of the Patiala House Court through video conference by the Delhi Police.
The case relates to allegations that Bhardwaj severely injured a 38-year-old man during a CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in June.
Deep Dive
Bhardwaj had been produced at the residence of Additional Sessions Judge Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler on Saturday. The judge had allowed the Delhi Police's plea seeking one-day custodial interrogation of the accused.
Delhi Police on Friday added provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and criminal intimidation to the FIR against Bhardwaj in connection with the alleged assault on Sanjay Kumar, the father of a teenage student activist, during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest at Jantar Mantar in June.
A separate case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act has also been registered against Bhardwaj.
What is the case about
Bhardwaj was detained in Bulandshahr on Friday, hours after the CJP held a protest outside the Parliament Street police station demanding his arrest over the alleged assault.
The detention came amid outrage over an interview in which Bhardwaj claimed he had "cracked the skull" of the student activist's father during the June 23 protest and escaped arrest because of his political connections.
"I cracked the skull... Do you know which section this crime attracts? Section 307. He needed 60 stitches," Bhardwaj had said in the interview.
Delhi Police had earlier said Sanjay Kumar's injuries were "simple" in nature and were caused by a steel bracelet. Bhardwaj later claimed in a podcast that he had acted in self-defence.
On Friday, police registered a separate FIR under the POCSO Act following a complaint by the minor activist, who alleged online threats and harassment.
Police also reportedly invoked BNS Sections 351(3), 78 (stalking) and 79 (insulting the modesty of a woman), along with Section 67 of the Information Technology Act.
The student had earlier alleged that she received rape threats, verbal abuse and morphed images after speaking out against the alleged assault on her father and filing a police complaint.
The developments followed a meeting between CJP representatives, accompanied by Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) chief and Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad, and police officials at the Parliament Street police station. The delegation sought action against Bhardwaj.

headline: The Union Petroleum Ministry on Monday (September 7, 2026) reduced the interval between bookings of domestic liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders for rural consumers to 25 days, months after it had been increased to 45 days during the peak of the ...
full_text:
The Union Petroleum Ministry on Monday (September 7, 2026) reduced the interval between bookings of domestic liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders for rural consumers to 25 days, months after it had been increased to 45 days during the peak of the West Asia conflict.
This brings the interval between bookings for rural consumers on par with urban consumers, for whom the period remains unchanged at 25 days.
In a letter to oil marketing companies, the Ministry cited “considerable reduction” in refill backlogs in the current supply situation among the reasons that prompted the relaxation.
Impact of West Asia crisis
At the peak of the conflict in West Asia in March 2026, the government had expanded the booking interval for domestic LPG cylinders from 21 days to 25 days for urban consumers and 45 days for rural consumers.
Prior to the conflict, India met 60% of its overall LPG requirements through imports. Of these imports, 90% were routed via the Strait of Hormuz, which faced a blockade as a result of the conflict.
Indian oil marketing companies then began increasingly importing LPG from the United States, which now forms nearly two-thirds of India’s LPG import basket.
The government’s subsequent push for piped natural gas (PNG), among other factors, led to India’s consumption of LPG declining by 17.4% in June compared to the same month last year, and 16.2% in August compared to the same period last year.
Distributors hail move
Speaking to The Hindu, LPG distributors’ associations welcomed the move.
Chandra Prakash, president of the All-India LPG Distributors Federation, said certain distributors categorised as rural were actually located in areas that had later developed into full-fledged urban centres, such as Noida in Uttar Pradesh and Navi Mumbai in Maharashtra. The Petroleum Ministry’s move will benefit such distributors, he said.
Mr. Prakash assured that distributors would be able to meet the demand arising from the revision in the booking interval. “There will not be a massive surge in demand with the move. India’s oil marketing companies have diversified their procurement, and we have augmented our domestic production as well. We do not foresee any shortage even in the upcoming festival season,” Mr. Prakash said.
Pawan Soni, general secretary of the Federation of LPG Distributors of India, also said the Ministry’s move would benefit distributors that come under the rural categorisation.
“LPG is an essential commodity. Consumers would have had to wait less if they had a distributor under the urban categorisation [rather than the rural categorisation]. We had spoken to the Ministry to address this and accord equality,” he said, thanking the Ministry and oil marketing companies’ leadership for the “practical decision in the larger interest of consumers”.

headline: The Gauhati High Court has directed the Assam government to pay ₹2 lakh as interim compensation to the husband of a Bengali-origin Muslim woman for expelling her to Bangladesh without an opportunity to challenge the order of a Foreigners’ Tribunal (F...
full_text:
The Gauhati High Court has directed the Assam government to pay ₹2 lakh as interim compensation to the husband of a Bengali-origin Muslim woman for expelling her to Bangladesh without an opportunity to challenge the order of a Foreigners’ Tribunal (FT).
The September 3 order was the first instance of any court imposing a cost on the State for pushing a person across the border to Bangladesh by violating deportation rules.
A Division Bench of Justices Kalyan Rai Surana and Susmita Phukan Khaund passed the order after hearing a habeas corpus petition filed by Mujammel Hoque, the husband of the “deported” Mumtaz Begum.
The court took serious exception to the way the FT in central Assam’s Nagaon handled Ms. Begum’s case, observing that “malice in law” on the part of the tribunal appeared evident from the record. An FT is a quasi-judicial body established to determine whether a person suspected of being an illegal immigrant is a legal citizen or a foreigner.
The FT declared Ms. Begum a foreigner on May 30, after she appeared before it following an earlier High Court direction to reconsider her case. The High Court had found that the tribunal did not consider all the evidence submitted by her.
The Bench noted that Ms. Begum was arrested soon after she was informed about the May 30 order, without getting an opportunity to challenge the decision. It also questioned the accounts of the tribunal member and the police regarding the timing and circumstances of her arrest.
‘Violation of procedure’
The court held that the procedure followed amounted to a “direct violation” of the standard operating procedure governing the expulsion of declared foreign nationals. Under the procedure, a person must be allowed to exhaust available legal remedies before expulsion.
Observing that the State machinery prevented Ms. Begum from exercising her right to approach the High Court against the tribunal’s order, the Bench ordered the Assam government to pay the petitioner (her husband). It, therefore, directed the Assam government to pay her ₹2 lakh as interim compensation.
“This palliative payment of compensation shall be in addition to and not in derogation of the right of the petitioner to seek compensation before the civil court,” the order read.
The court also directed Assam’s Home and Political Department to inquire into the date and time when the tribunal’s May 30 order was prepared. It added that the tribunal member’s computer could be seized, if necessary, to establish when the opinion was written.
The Bench further directed district Superintendents of Police to ensure that declared foreign nationals are informed about tribunal orders before being taken into custody. An adult family member must also be informed before the person is removed from the district, it said.
Moreover, the court impleaded the Ministry of External Affairs in the case and advised it to “make an endeavour to have the woman located in Bangladesh and to expatriate her to India”.

headline: Assam ordered to pay ₹2 lakh to family of woman pushed into Bangladesh: ‘Expelled without information to husband’
full_text:
Assam ordered to pay ₹2 lakh to family of woman pushed into Bangladesh: ‘Expelled without information to husband’
This is the first such instance where a court has imposed a cost on the state for pushing a person into Bangladesh, in violation of deportation rules.
The Gauhati high court has directed the Assam government to pay ₹2 lakh as interim compensation to the husband of Mumtaz Begum, a Bengali-speaking Muslim woman who was pushed into Bangladesh after a foreigners tribunal declared her a foreign national.
This is the first such instance where a court has imposed a cost on the state for pushing a person into Bangladesh, in violation of deportation rules. The order was passed by a bench of justices Kalyan Rai Surana and Susmita Phukan Khaund while hearing a habeas corpus petition filed by Begum’s husband Mujammel Hoque, a resident of Juria in Nagaon district.
“As the detenue (the woman) has been expelled out of India without providing any information to the petitioner (the woman’s husband) or any adult family member… as an interim palliative measure, the court is inclined to direct the Assam government to pay an interim compensation of ₹2 lakh to the petitioner,” the bench said in its order dated September 3.
Also Read I Vice President Radhakrishnan arrives in Assam on two-day trip
The bench directed the state government to pay the amount within 60 days and ruled that the petitioner could seek more relief from a civil court.
The division bench also impleaded the ministry of external affairs in the case and said it would direct it to “make an endeavour to have the woman located in Bangladesh and to expatriate her to India”.
Begum's brush with foreigner tribunals
Hoque moved the high court in June after failing to locate his wife at the detention camp meant for people declared foreign nationals by the foreigners tribunals, at Matia in Goalpara district.
Foreigners tribunals are quasi-judicial bodies unique to Assam that adjudicates on matters of citizenship of those marked as suspected foreigners by the border police or those listed as doubtful voters (D-voters) in electoral rolls.
The Nagaon tribunal had declared Begum, who claims to have been born in Rupahihat in Nagaon district in December 1982, a foreigner in 2019, despite producing documents showing that her grandfather’s name was in voter lists prior to 1971 — the cut-off year for citizenship in Assam.
Also Read I Two held for raping 15-year-old girl in Assam’s Sivasagar, found pregnant: Police
Begum challenged the tribunal’s order in the high court. In April this year, the high court set aside the tribunal’s order and sent the case back to the tribunal for a “fresh decision”.
But within minutes of appearing before the tribunal on May 30, Begum was taken into custody by police, kept overnight at the Juria police station and shited to the detention centre at Matia the next day.
It was only after the habeas corpus plea came up for hearing in late June that the authorities informed that Begum was handed over to Border Security Force and “sent back to Bangladesh” on the midnight of June 14 through an international border point at Sribhumi district.
Family not informed of Begum's expulsion
The bench noted that Begum and her family was not informed of the May 30 order, observing that not providing a copy of the tribunal’s order to Begum or her family members or failure to inform them about her expulsion, were procedural lapses on the part of the state machinery and police.
The high court also asked the Assam home department to order an inquiry into the entire episode.
“The state machinery, acting in tandem, had prevented the detenue to exhaust her right to move this court by way of a writ petition to challenge the impugned opinion dated May 30. Thus, only when this writ petition was filed, the petitioner could come to know that the detenue was expelled from the country,” the order said.

In light of the proceedings, the bench directed district superintendents of police to ensure that declared foreign nationals are informed of tribunal orders before being taken into custody. Also, an adult family member must be informed before the person is removed from the district.
The matter will be heard next on September 24.
In July this year, chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma informed the state assembly that 1,679 illegal Bangladeshis had been repatriated from Assam in the past two years. He also informed that there were 91,385 ‘D-voters’ (voters with doubtful citizenship) in the state in the electoral rolls.

headline: 'Orwellian dystopia': Allahabad HC reprimands Noida DM over DU student's NSA detention during Noida workers protest
full_text:
'Orwellian dystopia': Allahabad HC reprimands Noida DM over DU student's NSA detention during Noida workers protest
The bench ordered immediate release of Akriti Chaudhary and awarded her a compensation of ₹5 lakh last week.
Allahabad High Court came down heavily on Gautam Buddha Nagar District Magistrate Medha Roopam last week while quashing the detention of a Delhi University student and called her conduct “despotic”.
On Wednesday last week, the Allahabad high court quashed the detention order against a 25-year-old Delhi University graduate Akriti Chaudhary who has been in judicial custody for around five months in connection with the Noida workers’ protest of April 2026, saying her detention was based on a “concocted story”.
Chaudhary was detained under the stringent National Security Act (NSA) and the order of detention was passed by Roopam.
Also read: ‘Concocted story’: Allahabad HC quashes DU grad’s NSA detention over Noida workers’ protest
While quashing the move, the bench of justice Atul Sreedharan and justice Achal Sachdev made a reference to English writer George Orwell, who is well-known for his dystopian novel ‘1984’ and his allegorical novella ‘Animal Farm’.
The court said that “it shan't be long before the errant in the bureaucracy reduce the State of Uttar Pradesh to an Orwellian Dystopia”, reported Live Law.
It also said that when bureaucrats and cops go against their oath, they may be viewed as an “oppressive vestige of the British Empire”.
The bench also ordered immediate release of Chaudhary and awarded her a compensation of ₹5 lakh and directed that it must be recovered from the salaries of the district magistrate to every officer responsible “right down to the SHO”.
The court observed that the police report only contained allegations against Chaudhary and it was on the district magistrate to examine the record 'threadbare' and see if the case warranted stringent action such as the NSA.
“The conduct of the District Magistrate Gautam Buddha Nagar who passed the impugned order, is worthy of derision,” the court said, adding that Roopam "desired to set an example" out of Chaudhary to deter others from protesting or supporting the protesting workers.
The state counsel had told the judges that Chaudhary was arrested on the morning of April 12, 2026, on charges of instigating the mob to resort to arson and stone-pelting. The Uttar Pradesh Police subsequently invoked the National Security Act (NSA), 1980 against Chaudhary.
To this, the judges said that a proper notice under Section 126 of the BNSS had not been served on the petitioner before her arrest.
Earlier on Tuesday, September 1, the high court had directed the state government to produce footage showing whether Chaudhary had instigated protesters to engage in stone-pelting or set vehicles ablaze. The state sought additional time to submit the footage, but the bench refused, pointing out that Chaudhary had already spent five months in jail.

It also directed that the court's displeasure with the officials be entered in their service records.In a strongly worded September 2 order, the court criticised the manner in which the detention order was passed and warned that continued "despotic" conduct by "errant" bureaucrats could reduce Uttar Pradesh to an "Orwellian Dystopia", reported PTI.Chaudhary, a 24-year-old history graduate, was arrested in connection with cases arising from a workers' protest in Noida in April 2026.
The UP Police invoked the NSA against her and activist-journalist Satya Verma on May 13. They were among activists arrested in cases related to the protest seeking higher wages.The court said the police dossier against Chaudhary contained allegations but lacked credible supporting material. It said the DM was required to independently examine the record before deciding whether preventive detention was warranted."The conduct of the Gautam Buddha Nagar DM who passed the impugned order is worthy of derision," the court said.The bench noted that Chaudhary had no previous criminal record and that there was no material showing she had incited violence. It said the circumstances suggested that the detention was intended to make an example of her and discourage others from exercising their right to freedom of speech and expression in support of labourers.The court also questioned the state's version of when Chaudhary was arrested. It recorded that she was taken into custody around 5.30 pm on April 11 at Botanical Garden Metro Station, although the state claimed her arrest took place on April 12.A notice issued under Section 130 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was cited by the state. However, the notice carried General Diary Entry No. 37, which was generated only at 10.20 am on April 12."Mentioning the GD number in the notice under section 130 of the BNSS reveals that the petitioner was already arrested and the procedure of giving a notice under section 130 of the BNSS was ex post facto the arrest and nothing more than a sham," Justice Sreedharan said."I agree with the view of brother Justice Achal Sachdev that the notice u/s. 130 of the BNSS was prepared after the arrest of the Petitioner and that is the reason why the time of issuance is not mentioned in the notice and its omission is deliberate," he added.The court said preventive detention under the NSA is an exception and cannot be used in place of ordinary criminal law. It described the grounds of Chaudhary's detention as "repetitive, speculative and are only opinion-based", noting the absence of material supporting those conclusions.It also cautioned authorities against treating peaceful public protests as a threat merely because they could potentially lead to a breach of peace."Preventing people from gathering in public spaces or agitating for their rights on the grounds of assumed breach of peace would be throwing the baby out of the bath water," the court said.The bench said the constitutional protection of freedom of speech and expression extends to peaceful gatherings and collective action, and cannot be curtailed merely on the basis of the state's subjective assessment.
The court also reminded bureaucrats and police officers that their duty is to the Constitution rather than the political executive, saying that people are the masters in a democracy.It warned that officials who disregard their constitutional oath could come to be seen as an "oppressive vestige of the British Empire", creating an environment of civil unrest.The court said the judiciary could pass "harsh orders" to compensate citizens where official excesses or illegalities infringe upon civil liberties without adequate cause or due process.

headline: The Election Commission on Monday (September 7, 2026) announced that bypolls to five Assembly constituencies in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry and one Lok Sabha seat in Assam would be held on October 6.
full_text:
The Election Commission on Monday (September 7, 2026) announced that bypolls to five Assembly constituencies in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry and one Lok Sabha seat in Assam would be held on October 6.
The nomination process will remain open until September 16, and counting will be held on October 9. The election process would be completed by October 11.
The by-elections were necessitated following the resignations of elected legislators across the three States and the Union Territory for various reasons. In Tamil Nadu, vacancies arose in Madurantakam (SC) and Dharapuram (SC) following the resignations of Maragatham Kumaravel and P. Sathyabama, respectively.
Ms. Kumaravel and Ms. Sathyabama both had been elected on AIADMK tickets in the 2026 Assembly polls and resigned after joining Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).
Five other Assembly seats in Tamil Nadu are vacant following resignations, including Tiruchirappalli East, which was won by the Chief Minister. He had won two seats and retained Perambur as his constituency. The other vacant seats—Ambasamudram, Karur, Veeralimalai and Perumdurai—have election petitions pending, preventing the EC from announcing bypolls there.
In Puducherry, the Thattanchavady constituency opened up after the resignation of N. Rangasamy. He had won from both Thattanchavady and Mangalam seats and decided to give up the former.
In West Bengal, Rejinagar and the high-profile Nandigram are up for election following the resignations of Humayun Kabir and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, respectively. Mr. Adhikari decided to retain the Bhabanipur seat where he had defeated incumbent Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee.
Mr. Adhikari, who led the BJP to form its maiden government in West Bengal, had defeated Ms. Banerjee in her Bhabanipur stronghold by 15,105 votes. He had also defeated her in Nandigram in the 2021 Assembly polls.
Mr. Kabir, a former Trinamool Congress leader who floated the AJUP after his expulsion from the party, won from both Nowda and Rejinagar and decided to retain the former. He has offered the Rejinagar seat to Ms. Banerjee to contest.
It remains to be seen whether Ms. Banerjee will choose either Nandigram or Rejinagar to make a return to the Assembly.
In Assam, the bypoll will be held in the Nagaon Parliamentary Constituency following the resignation of Pradyut Bordoloi. He had won the constituency on a Congress ticket in 2024 and subsequently joined the BJP and won from Dispur in the recent Assembly polls.
Two other Lok Sabha seats—Shillong in Meghalaya and Basirhat in West Bengal—remain vacant, and polls have not been scheduled there yet.
Shillong fell vacant following the death of Voice of the People Party (VPP) MP Ricky Andrew J. Syngkon in February this year, while Basirhat has remained vacant since the death of Trinamool Congress MP Haji Sheikh Nurul Islam in September 2024.
The Model Code of Conduct will come into effect immediately in the respective districts encompassing the poll-bound constituencies, the ECI said in a statement.
While Electoral Photo Identity Cards (EPIC) remain the primary identification document, voters may present alternative approved documents, including passport, driving licence, PAN card, or official photo ID issued by government entities.

headline: Chennai: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay levelled a series of corruption allegations against the previous DMK government, citing an Enforcement Directorate (ED) document and the decades-old Sarkaria Commission report.
full_text:
Chennai: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay levelled a series of corruption allegations against the previous DMK government, citing an Enforcement Directorate (ED) document and the decades-old Sarkaria Commission report.
Speaking in the Assembly, Vijay vowed zero tolerance for crimes against women and children, and drug menace, stating that strict action would be taken. “Whoever the wrongdoer is, whichever party they belong to, action will be taken, we believe that everybody is equal before law,” Vijay said in the Assembly.
He also said personal attacks and comments with double meaning against women should stop, noting that people were observing such things. “Before speaking about women in a double entendre, think about the women in your own homes,” he said.
His comments come after DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin’s remark, allegedly against actor Trisha, and the online comments about Industries Minister Keerthana over a look alike. Vijay also referred to past attacks on former chief minister J. Jayalalithaa in the Assembly.
Vijay said the DMK had challenged him to open files from three departments he had earlier described as corrupt under the previous regime.
“Before I open the said files, I want to read the Sarkaria Commission report on the DMK government’s corruption in 1988. The Sarkaria Commission, in its report, has highlighted and accused former chief minister Karunanidhi of abusing his official position as chief minister. The Enforcement Directorate has also accused the DMK of corruption through party funds. The ED mentioned that during the last regime, former chief minister M. K. Stalin, former deputy chief minister Udhayanidhi Stalin, and former minister Senthil Balaji collected money in the name of party funds,” he said.
He referred said the Sarkaria Commission recorded demands for commissions, including a reported 2.5 percent “party fund” linked to a tender.
He read portions of an ED document sent to the previous DMK government which stated that 7.5 to 10 percent of contract values in departments such as Municipal Administration and Water Supply had been collected as “party funds,” which he characterised as bribes taken in instalments “like EMIs on a loan”.
Vijay added that ED had described Stalin senior, Stalin junior and Balaji as direct beneficiaries. He stressed that these were not his personal allegations but those contained in the ED papers.
He also questioned the involvement of Ratheesh, a close associate of DMK leader and Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin. He has been named in Enforcement Directorate (ED) investigations related to alleged irregularities in the Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (TASMAC) and other matters, including references in documents concerning “party funds” and municipal administration contracts during the previous DMK regime.
Vijay also questioned why Ratheesh was “hiding” in Dubai and what was his connection with the previous government.
After repeated allegations by DMK on poor law and order management in the state since the TVK government came to power, the Chief Minister stated that crimes reported in the past three months were largely driven by past enmities and revenge rather than a sudden breakdown under the current government.
Replying to the debate on the police department demands of grants, Vijay outlined plans to reform the police, describing them as protectors of people rather than a power centre. He said the police should be friends to those who abide by the law and foes to those who violate it.
He also informed the Assembly that 36 people had been arrested in connection with the murder of a college student in Coimbatore.
DMK members protested over Vijay’s allegations in the House by surrounding the Speaker’s podium and staging a sit-in protest. Speaker J. C. D. Prabhakar initially declined to allow an immediate response, stating that the Opposition had interrupted the chief minister.
Vijay indicated that the Speaker should permit the Opposition to speak, and later he requested that they be allowed. The Speaker, however, maintained that permission could not be granted under the circumstances, after which DMK members walked out.
Outside the Assembly, Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin held a press interaction. He accused Vijay of diverting attention from questions on law and order and the government’s performance in its first few months, saying the chief minister had spoken in “dialogues and reels-style” and focused on events from the 1960s and 1970s rather than current issues.
He questioned Vijay’s knowledge of the Sarkaria Commission and the Maintenance of Internal Security Act, describing the ED references as mere allegations that had not prevented the DMK from returning to power multiple times after the report.
“We are asking about things happening today, but he is going back to the 1960s and 70s, with baseless allegations. Someone has written these dialogues and given them to him, and he is delivering them here. There is nothing in the Sarkaria Commission report, and everyone knows it. Where are the answers for the recent murders and law and order incidents?” Udhayanidhi said.
Udhayanidhi also said the Speaker had not allowed the Opposition to respond and suggested external pressure may have influenced the decision. “CM Vijay seems to think there is still a DMK government in Tamil Nadu. He should be speaking about his government’s last three months and his plans for the future,” Udhayanidhi said.
DMK spokesperson Saravanan Annadurai also alleged that Vijay was attempting to deflect attention from internal coalition issues and other contemporary controversies.
“Vijay is scared of the DMK. He has only 107 seats, and there are already a lot of ripples inside the coalition. One MLA goes and says he was offered so many crores for becoming a minister to support the government. Please take action, find out the truth, what he meant, and whom he meant,” Saravanan told ANI.
(Edited by Viny Mishra)

headline: New Delhi: A political row erupted in West Bengal Monday after a state government advertisement depicted Hindu goddess Durga with 11 arms instead of 10. The Trinamool Congress (TMC) raised an uproar, asking why the BJP was “so alien to Bengali cultur...

New Delhi: A political row erupted in West Bengal Monday after a state government advertisement depicted Hindu goddess Durga with 11 arms instead of 10. The Trinamool Congress (TMC) raised an uproar, asking why the BJP was “so alien to Bengali culture”. Later in the day, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari issued an apology.
The newspaper advertisement—which also featured Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Adhikari—was published ahead of a coordination meeting the CM chaired with Durga Puja committees in Kolkata Monday. The meeting was organised jointly by the Kolkata Police and the Kolkata Municipal Corporation in association with West Bengal’s Information and Cultural Affairs department.
“A government that claims to speak for Bengal seems increasingly disconnected from Bengali culture, traditions and the festivals that define Bengal’s identity. Since when does Maa Durga have 11 hands?” the TMC posted on X.
It added: “Durga Puja is not just a festival, it is an emotion and the very heartbeat of Bengal. Maa’s homecoming is sacred to millions of Bengalis. Yet a government that claims to speak for Bengal seems increasingly disconnected from Bengali culture, traditions and the festivals that define Bengal’s identity.”
So now, according to the @BJP4Bengal government, Maa Durga has 11 hands?
From their leaders to the Chief Minister, this repeated mishandling of Maa Durga and Bengal’s cultural traditions is deeply insulting!
Durga Puja is not just a festival, it is an emotion and the very… pic.twitter.com/HnnKdeOq7h
— All India Trinamool Congress (@AITCofficial) September 7, 2026
TMC spokesperson Kunal Ghosh, in his own X post, tagged Adhikari, saying: “Mother Dashabhuja has become Ekadashbhuja. According to the scriptures, one hand needs to be reduced. I keep hearing about various conduct rules every day. Among them, if Mother’s hand count increases in 2026, the matter will become complicated. Immediately instruct the concerned department not to distort the original maternal idol.”
.@SuvenduWB 
মাননীয় মুখ্যমন্ত্রী, সরকারি বিজ্ঞাপনে মা দশভূজা তো একাদশভূজা হয়ে গিয়েছেন। শাস্ত্রমতে একটি হাত তো কমানো দরকার। নানা আচরণবিধি রোজ শুনছি। তার মধ্যে মায়ের হাত সংখ্যা 2026-এ এসে বেড়ে গেলে বিষয়টা জটিল হবে। অবিলম্বে সংশ্লিষ্ট দপ্তরকে বলুন মূল মাতৃপ্রতিমা বিকৃত না… pic.twitter.com/uQzRbmemF5
— Kunal Ghosh (@KunalGhoshAgain) September 7, 2026
West Bengal CPI(M) state secretary Mohammad Salim told ThePrint: “Since their (BJP’s) government in the state is new, they want to create fanaticism in the name of Sanatan and are bent upon administering new religious codes to Bengalis. They have outsourced all government work to agencies who do not have one iota of idea about Bengali rules, laws, customs and culture.”
He further claimed that at a time people are concerned about the education system, inflation, women’s safety, corruption and democracy, the BJP is trying to distract the masses in the name of religion. “Those who thought they would improve the socio-political-economic conditions of the state are the same people who are pushing Bengalis and their education, culture, economy and the rest towards doom.”
CPI(M) leader Shatarup Ghosh also sarcastically remarked on Facebook, “A wonderful government advertisement! Here, Ma Durga has eleven arms. The gods had bestowed weapons upon Durga in ten hands to slay the demon. Meanwhile, the BJP government has gifted the deity an extra arm.”
CM Suvendu, while addressing the coordination meeting with Durga Puja committees at the Milan Mela Prangan, said those responsible for the advertisement have been cautioned and assured people that the government would be more careful in the future. “First of all, as the chief minister of the state, I apologise. A defective advertisement was published this morning. I apologise for that. Those who issued the defective advertisement have been cautioned. The government will be more careful about such matters in future.”
Responding to the controversy, BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya said the 11-armed depiction had made “Maa Durga” even more powerful. He added that although he had not come across the advertisement, a mistake by an agency was not a political issue and the error would be rectified.
The controversy comes on the heels of another one surrounding Durga Puja, with the Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) asking organisers to prohibit non-vegetarian food inside pandals, arguing that meat and fish should be kept outside the sacred premises.

headline: A day after India’s UN map remarks, Pakistan provokes again over Jammu and Kashmir
full_text:
A day after India’s UN map remarks, Pakistan provokes again over Jammu and Kashmir
This follows India's vote supporting the ‘Correct the Map’ UN resolution aiming to promote equal-area representation of world maps.
Jolted by the statement of India's Ministry of External Affairs on the map of Jammu and Kashmir, Pakistan attempted to provoke again on Monday, calling New Delhi's assertion “baseless”.
The statement by Pakistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs comes a day after MEA's Randhir Jaiswal issued a clarification regarding the union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh after backing the African Union's resolution to “rebalance” the world map.
New Delhi's assertion came two days after it voted in favour of a UN General Assembly resolution aimed at correcting the world map to promote a more accurate representation of continental landmasses.
In a statement, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that India voted in favour of the map, explaining that the vote stressed “the underlying principle of promoting equal - area cartographic representation.”
“We also highlighted that the resolution does not constitute endorsement of any specific map, projection or depiction of national boundaries,” the MEA said on Sunday.
The statement by Pakistani foreign ministry spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan on Monday categorically rejected what it described as “India's baseless assertions regarding the status of Jammu and Kashmir which are contrary to internationally recognized facts.”
“India's unilateral actions and continued illegal occupation cannot alter the internationally recognized disputed status of Jammu and Kashmir. Jammu and Kashmir dispute remains one of the oldest unresolved, internationally recognized disputes on the agenda of the United Nations Security Council. The relevant UN resolutions stipulate that its final disposition must be made in accordance with the relevant Security Council resolutions and the will of the Kashmiri people, expressed through a free and impartial plebiscite under UN auspices,” the Pakistani statement read.
Appearing to be uneasy by New Delhi's firm stand, the Pakistani statement said, “India's so-called official maps and unilateral claims of sovereignty have no bearing on the status of the disputed territory.”
The UN resolution over map
The resolution titled "Correct the Map: Rebalancing Global Cartographic Representation and Promoting Equitable Representation of the World's Regions, Particularly Africa" was adopted on September 4.
MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal on Sunday said, “India voted in favour of the resolution and also made an explanation of vote stressing on the underlying principle of promoting equal - area cartographic representation.”
"Our position on India's sovereignty and territorial integrity is clear, consistent and non-negotiable," Jaiswal noted.
Jaiswal said the purpose of the UN resolution is "to encourage the use of equal-area map projections that preserve the relative sizes of continental landmasses."
"The resolution neither adopts nor authenticates any particular world map, nor does it address political cartography, including international boundaries, disputed territories or place names," he said.
The resolution, sponsored by Togo, received 164 votes in favour, with abstentions from Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia and Ukraine, and a lone vote against from the United States.

The UN described it as an important step towards correcting distortions in commonly used world maps, especially the Mercator projection, which are seen as “misrepresenting the relative size of continents and contribute to a diminished perception of Africa”.
However, the resolution favours the Equal Earth projection — created in 2018 by the cartographers Bojan Savric, Bernhard Jenny and Tom Patterson — which inaccurately depicts the northern frontiers of India by showing parts of Jammu and Kashmir within the borders of China and Pakistan.
MEA spokesperon clarifies India' stance
“India voted in favour of the resolution and also made an explanation of vote stressing on the underlying principle of promoting equal-area cartographic representation,” external affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.
“We also highlighted that the resolution does not constitute endorsement of any specific map, projection or depiction of national boundaries.”
Jaiswal made it clear that India’s sovereign territory, including the union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, “must be depicted in accordance with India’s official map”. He added, “Any inaccurate or misleading depiction is unacceptable. Our position on India’s sovereignty and territorial integrity is clear, consistent and non-negotiable.”
Also Read I Africa gets bigger, North America smaller as UN adopts new world map; US says ‘focus on genuine problems’
Jaiswal noted that the UN resolution’s purpose is encouraging the use of equal-area map projections that preserve the relative sizes of continental landmasses. “The resolution neither adopts nor authenticates any particular world map, nor does it address political cartography, including international boundaries, disputed territories or place names,” he said.

headline: A new world map that was endorsed at the UN during the India-backed “Correct the map” resolution of September 4 in the UN General Assembly has projected India’s Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin, which India has maintained as part of Ladakh, as distin...
full_text:
A new world map that was endorsed at the UN during the India-backed “Correct the map” resolution of September 4 in the UN General Assembly has projected India’s Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin, which India has maintained as part of Ladakh, as distinct regions caught between Indian and Chinese “claim lines”.
The map which came up on July 1 during the months-long discussion for the UNGA resolution shows Arunachal’s southern State border with Assam, indicating the “Chinese line” while eliminating the State’s border with Nagaland. It shows the State’s northern border, indicating the “Indian line”. Similarly, the map shows Aksai Chin’s eastern borders, indicating the “Indian Line” while presenting the western borders of Aksai Chin in what appears to be the “Chinese line”. These “claim lines” appear to be a continuation of previous similar maps of the UN. But unlike in the 2011 map of the UN, these lines are not specified as “claim lines” in the July 1 map.
Also read: Line of Actual Control | India-China: the line of actual contest
The map has also depicted Jammu and Kashmir with a dotted line indicating the Line of Control (LoC) between India and Pakistan. However, the issue of the LoC is clearly mentioned in a brief note on the left side of the map, explaining that the “dotted line represents approximately the Line of Control in Jammu and Kashmir agreed upon by India and Pakistan. The final status of Jammu and Kashmir has not yet been agreed upon by the parties.”
However, there is no note explaining why the “Map of the World” issued by the UN during the consultation process and endorsed by the “Correct the Map” resolution that was sponsored by Togo and supported by the African Union depicted Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin as territories caught between Indian and Chinese claim lines.
The map is non-binding, but understandably, it will be used by multilateral institutions worldwide.
Discussions on the map began in March 2026 when the African Union supported the “Equal Earth cartographic projection to more accurately represent Africa”. African Union called this approach “cognitive justice”. Subsequently, Togo prompted UNGA consultations on the map in April 2026, and the UN General Assembly started informal consultations in July, when the draft map authored by the UN Geospatial on July 1 was taken up.
The External Affairs Ministry (MEA) had reiterated India’s support for the “Correct the Map” resolution on Sunday but declared that “India voted in favour of the resolution” and explained its position as a vote on the “underlying principle of promoting equal–area cartographic representation”. “We also highlighted that the resolution does not constitute endorsement of any specific map, projection or depiction of national boundaries,” the MEA had said.
“India’s sovereign territory, including the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, must be depicted in accordance with India’s official map. Any inaccurate or misleading depiction is unacceptable,” said the Official Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal in response to media queries. MEA is yet to respond to The Hindu’s query on the separate demarcation of Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin with contesting claim lines from India and China.
The traditional map of India depicts both Arunachal Pradesh and the entire Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh (including Aksai Chin) as parts of the sovereign territory of India.
In relation to India’s ongoing Kalapani border controversy with Nepal, the map seems to have gone in favour of India, as it reflects India’s control over the Kalapani-Lipulekh-Limpiyadhura region, which is claimed by Nepal.
Earlier this year, Nepal’s new government had written to India, asserting Kathmandu’s claim over the Lipulekh region, which India uses for transportation of pilgrims and traders to Tibet and to the Kailash Manasarovar region. Nepal, recently hit by the disaster at the Bhote Koshi River, had in 2019 protested against India’s new political map issued after the abrogation of Article 370 that year. Kathmandu is yet to comment on the new UN map.
