headline: 6 killed in Satya Niketan building collapse; FIR against owner
full_text:
6 killed in Satya Niketan building collapse; FIR against owner
NEW DELHI: The death toll in the Satya Niketan building collapse in Delhi rose to six as search and rescue operations continued at the site, with teams clearing heavy debris and looking for any remaining trapped persons. Hours after the building collapse in a student-dominated area near Delhi Universityâs South Campus, the MCD has ordered action against illegal buildings with four or more storeys.One more body was recovered during late-night operations, taking the total number of fatalities to six.
Teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Delhi Fire Service, Delhi Police and other agencies continued rescue operations at the site as they worked to remove the debris.The collapse that took place on Sunday afternoon, has raised fresh questions over the safety of buildings being used as paying guest (PG) accommodations and the enforcement of construction and fire safety norms in densely populated parts of the national capital.The Rekha Gupta-led Delhi government has ordered a magisterial inquiry into the incident and directed that an FIR be registered against the building owner, the chief ministerâs office (CMO) said.
The decision was taken following an on-site review and a preliminary assessment of the incident, the CMO said.âFollowing an on-site review and based on the preliminary assessment, the chief minister has ordered a Magisterial Inquiry of the incident and an FIR against the building owner,â the CMO said.It added that those found responsible for the incident would be held fully accountable and face the strictest provisions of the law.Meanwhile, Congress leader and AICC Uttarakhand in-charge Kumari Selja questioned the BJP government over the safety of students living in such accommodations. She said students are sent to Delhi with hopes of building their future and questioned who would be held responsible for their safety.âWhat is the BJP government doing? They have forgotten what happened at the coaching centre. A mafia is operating in Delhi. These children are sent away with so many hopes. They are the only support for their parents. Who is responsible for their safety?â Selja said.Former Delhi chief secretary Omesh Saigal said the incident should not be viewed as an isolated case, claiming that similar incidents occur every few months. He also raised concerns over unauthorised construction in parts of Delhi.Saigal alleged that some buildings either have unapproved blueprints, additional floors added later or substandard construction, and questioned whether authorities responsible for approving building plans had adequately checked their safety."Look at the kind of buildings constructed in Delhi - I would say that in some areas, one in five buildings is unauthorised; either the blueprints weren't approved, extra floors were added, or the construction is substandard," he said.He also called for restrictions on new construction in areas that are already overcrowded and over-built, saying authorities should consider stopping the sanctioning of new building plans in such areas and examine the safety of existing structures."At the very least, we should ban new construction in these areas. We must halt new constructionâor stop sanctioning building plansâfor areas that are already over-congested and over-built. These are the things that need to be addressed," he added.NSUI President Vinod Jakhar described the situation as extremely grave and said rescue operations were continuing under difficult conditions."Rescue operations are ongoing, and conditions are dire. Almost all the students being pulled out are dead. We tried our best to get those students out; we actually succeeded in rescuing about three of them. Had the medical facilities, medical teams, police, and fire brigade arrived on timeâhad all necessary resources and responsible officials been present promptlyâperhaps more students could have been saved. But the BJP has no disaster management plan. Just look at how the country's Home Minister inaugurates a grand BJP office in Goa today, while here, a building collapses. BJP offices never collapse because they are built using money extorted from PG and coaching centre operators. Our only demand is justice for the students. Several of our colleagues have also sustained serious injuries. There is absolutely no accountability," Jakhar told news agency ANI.Meanwhile, Delhi Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha president Rajat Choudhary said the situation remained serious and appealed for speedy rescue efforts. He said ambulances and doctors were present in large numbers and urged both the Delhi and Central governments to ensure that those trapped were rescued quickly.Choudhary also appealed to political parties to avoid politicising the tragedy and instead extend support to the affected families and those involved in the rescue operation.
"This is not the time for politics; those affected were someone's children. Instead of playing politics, one should offer support. The opposition should not do this; they should stand in solidarity," he said.In a separate response, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) ordered the immediate sealing of all illegal constructions with more than four floors and warned of strict action against officials found responsible.âAll illegal constructions with more than four floors will be immediately sealed, and strict action will be taken against the guilty officials, leading to their immediate dismissal. These orders will be implemented with immediate effect,â the MCD said.

headline: UAE move may delay India’s bid to extradite Mahadev app kingpin
full_text:
UAE move may delay India’s bid to extradite Mahadev app kingpin
Chandrakar was detained in Muscat in June on an Interpol red notice after allegedly fleeing the UAE with a fake passport in April.
India’s attempt to extradite Sourabh Chandrakar, the mastermind of the ₹6,000-crore Mahadev online gambling racket, from Oman has hit a hurdle. Agencies in India have learned that the UAE has also sent an extradition request to Oman seeking his transfer, people familiar with the development said.
This, officials said, means that even if India wins the extradition case in Oman—which may take months or even years—the timeline to bring him back to India will be affected as New Delhi will have to wait for Oman’s decision on the UAE’s request.
Both the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED) are pursuing Chandrakar’s extradition since the Royal Oman Police detained him in Muscat last week of June based on an Interpol red notice. He had fled the UAE, where he was hiding since 2019, to Oman sometime in April this year using a fake passport, according to officials.
Also read: Mahadev app’s Chandrakar held in Oman; India to seek extradition
Suspicion over UAE's extradition request
“We have learnt that the UAE authorities have also sent an extradition request for Chandrakar to Oman on some unknown charges, which we don’t know about. We are in regular touch with Omani authorities through diplomatic channels but this latest development has the potential to delay our attempts to get him sooner,” said an officer, requesting anonymity.
Officials hinted that Chandrakar might have, through his aides, registered a false case against himself in the UAE, which is now cited in Abu Dhabi’s extradition request.
After he fled to Dubai, extradition requests sent by India twice to the UAE authorities did not fructify. He was, in fact, detained in Dubai in 2024 but was subsequently released.
Also read: ED makes new extradition bid to UAE for arrest of Mahadev app co-founder
Mahadev network ran thousands of betting panels
Chandrakar, who is believed to be in his early 30s, set-up the Mahadev betting empire along with co-founder Ravi Uppal. Uppal went missing from the UAE sometime in November 2025 and reportedly fled to Vanuatu.
Their illegal betting operations, still running across India despite the government banning multiple platforms and apps linked to Mahadev, allow people to place illegal bets on poker and other card games, cricket, badminton, tennis and football matches and even election outcomes.
ED has claimed, in one of its charge sheets in the case, that the “betting empire” was operating at least 3,200 (betting) panels in different cities, generating around ₹240 crore per day.
Also read: Mahadev case probe: Betting apps generated proceeds of around ₹43,000 crore in last 7 years, says ED
Bhupesh Baghel named accused, denies involvement
Former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel is also named as accused in the probe. He has consistently denied his involvement.
In March, ED attached 20 immovable properties worth ₹1,700 crore including high-value luxury villas in an estate and apartments in Burj Khalifa in Dubai linked to Chandrakar.
The financial crimes probe agency has claimed that “Mahadev Online Book operated as a large-scale international betting syndicate, which facilitated illegal betting through multiple online platforms and domain names such as Tiger Exchange, Gold365 and Laser247”.

headline: Influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj was remanded to 14-day judicial custody.
full_text:
Influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj was remanded to 14-day judicial custody.
Counsel for self-styled right-wing influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj told the Delhi high court on Monday that the Delhi Police had the "audacity" to travel to Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr and arrest him in connection with the Jantar Mantar protest case."The SC has already quashed all the FIRs and the Delhi Police had the audacity to go to Bulandshahr and arrest me," the counsel was quoted as saying by Bar and Bench.
Police, however, contested the claim and told the court that the FIR in the present case had not been quashed by the Supreme Court. The bench then sought a clear response from the Delhi Police, asking it to inform the court whether the FIR was "alive or not" and giving it the option of filing an affidavit or making a statement immediately, Bar and Bench report said.The police counsel also pointed out that Bhardwaj had been produced before a court following his arrest and was subsequently remanded to police and judicial custody.The HC rejected Bhardwaj's habeas corpus plea challenging his arrest in Jantar Mantar assault case.Meanwhile, a Delhi court extended his judicial custody by 14 days till September 21 in connection with the alleged assault on Sanjay Azad during the June 23.
Bhardwaj was produced before Special Judge Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler through video conferencing from Tihar Jail after his one-day police custody ended.He was detained in Bulandshahr on September 4 and brought to Delhi, following which a court had on September 5 granted the police one dayâs custodial interrogation. He was subsequently sent to one-day judicial custody on Sunday.
The arrest followed outrage over a video podcast in which Bhardwaj allegedly claimed that he had "cracked the skull" of Azad during the Jantar Mantar protest and said the alleged assault attracted Section 307. He later claimed he had acted in self-defence. Delhi Police had earlier said Azad's injuries were simple in nature and were caused by a steel bracelet.Police subsequently added provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and criminal intimidation to the FIR. A separate FIR under the POCSO Act was also registered following a complaint by the teenage activist alleging online threats and harassment after she spoke about the alleged assault on her father.

The adjectives for the opposition may keep changing, but Modi govt's "anti-people policies" do not change, Kharge added.

headline: Indian, Chinese armies hold talks focusing on maintaining peace along LAC
full_text:
Indian, Chinese armies hold talks focusing on maintaining peace along LAC
The Indian delegation was headed by Lt General Girish Kalia, the commander of the Army's Dimapur-based 3 Corps.
The Indian and Chinese armies reviewed the situation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in the Arunachal Pradesh sector, days after the two sides held Special Representative talks in Beijing on the festering boundary question.
The focus of the corps commander-level talks at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point in Arunachal Pradesh's Kibithoo region on Sunday was to maintain peace and tranquillity along the frontier, people familiar with the matter said.
The Indian delegation was headed by Lt General Girish Kalia, the commander of the Army's Dimapur-based 3 Corps.
There is no official word yet on the talks.
The meeting also came amid reports of aggressive military posturing by Chinese troops along the LAC in the Upper Subansiri region of Arunachal Pradesh.
Also Read | India, China armies hold LAC talks in Arunachal Pradesh
In the Special Representative (SR) talks on August 25, India conveyed to China the importance of maintaining peace and tranquillity along the frontier for overall bilateral ties.
National Security Advisor Ajit Doval held the SR talks with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi which focused on delimitation of the frontier and sustaining work on trans-boundary cooperation.
In his remarks at the meeting, Doval said that normalcy in the ties has been a direct result of both sides maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas.
The Indian side highlighted the importance of maintaining peace and tranquillity in the India-China border areas for the continued development and progress of the bilateral relationship, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) had said on the SR talks.
Both Doval and Wang are the designated SRs for the boundary talks mechanism, which was established in 2003 to comprehensively address the dispute over the India-China border spanning 3,488 km.
In the last few months, the two sides have taken a series of measures to rebuild their relationship after it came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020.

headline: NEW DELHI: Corps Commanders of the Army and Chinese PLA Commanding formations in the eastern part of Arunachal Pradesh Sunday geared up for talks to sort out ongoing tensions along the state's stretch of the 1,126-km Line of Actual Control. The meeti...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Corps Commanders of the Army and Chinese PLA Commanding formations in the eastern part of Arunachal Pradesh Sunday geared up for talks to sort out ongoing tensions along the state's stretch of the 1,126-km Line of Actual Control. The meeting is the first Corps Commander-level military talks in the eastern sector at the Vacha-Damai border meeting point.The latest talks are significant as India and China have so far held Corps Commander-level meetings primarily at the Chusul-Moldo border meeting point in the Ladakh sector. The latest engagement marks a new start from both sides to address issues in the eastern sector. A source told TOI, "The Indian side will be represented by Lieutenant General Girish Kalia, Commander of the Indian Army's 3 Corps, also known as Spear Corps."The 3 Corps is headquartered at Rangapahar in Nagaland and is responsible for operational areas along the LAC in Arunachal. The Army has two Corps formations looking after the LAC in the state, including Tezpur-based 4 Corps and Rangapahar-based 3 Corps.
India and China have different perceptions of the LAC, resulting, at times, in face-offs. The latest engagement is expected to provide them with an opportunity to address such issues directly through military channels.
The talks follow a meeting in Beijing in Aug between national security adviser Ajit Doval and China's foreign minister, Wang Yi. There, they agreed on an eight-point plan to improve how both countries manage the border, promising quicker action through diplomatic and military channels whenever issues pop up.

headline: India-France ties reach new heights, says PM Modi at Paris temple inauguration
full_text:
India-France ties reach new heights, says PM Modi at Paris temple inauguration
Speaking virtually at the inauguration of the Swaminarayan temple in Paris, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said India and France are building a special global strategic partnership. He said the BAPS temple would strengthen cultural ties, reflect shared craftsmanship and serve as a centre for service.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said India-France relations have reached new heights and this strategic partnership is particularly special because it rests on the solid foundation of long-standing cultural and political ties.
Addressing virtually the inauguration of the Swaminarayan temple in Paris, PM Modi hoped that the grand temple in Paris will stand for centuries as a symbol of cooperation and opportunity between both the nations.
"In recent years, relations between India and France have reached new heights. Together with my friend, President (Emmanuel) Macron, both nations are building a Special Global Strategic Partnership," he said.
The prime minister said that from technology, AI, and defence to space and climate action, India and France are moving forward together with new momentum and energy.
"We are also celebrating 2026 as the India-France Year of Innovation. This strategic partnership is particularly special because it rests on the solid foundation of our long-standing cultural and political ties," he said.
Modi said these days, there is much talk about joint venture possibilities between India and France.
He said history bears witness that the sacrifice of Indian soldiers in France remains alive in the hearts of people to this day.
"Language enthusiasts also know the pivotal role French scholars played in popularising Sanskrit. Romain Rolland's writings on Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and Swami Vivekananda brought our societies closer," he said.
Furthermore, the prime minister said, the spiritual journey of 'The Mother' from Paris to the Sri Aurobindo Ashram in Puducherry has inspired countless Indian and French seekers.
He said decades ago, Srila Prabhupada Swami also visited France, opening a new chapter in spiritual connections through ISKCON.
"Today, yoga has also become a bridge for people-to-people connections between our nations. Images from the Eiffel Tower on International Yoga Day reflect yoga's immense popularity in France," he said.
PM Modi said the Swaminarayan temple adds a new dimension to those possibilities - it is 'Made in India' and 'Built in France.'
"Many of its stones were carved in India, blending India's ancient craftsmanship with modern engineering here in France," he said.
PM Modi said he was confident that the resonant values of Indian culture originating from the newly built temple in Paris will benefit people across Europe.
He said that whenever time permits in the future, he will certainly try to visit the temple and pay respects.
"Now, through this magnificent BAPS temple (BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha), another milestone is being added to our cultural relations," he said.
The prime minister said Swaminarayan temples have always served as hubs of service alongside devotion.
"I am informed that this temple will likewise become a centre for service projects," he said.
Modi said that through BAPS, whenever temples are consecrated in different countries, India's ancient thoughts and human values travel right along with them.
"A magnificent temple stands ready today in France and it will not only enrich France's diversity but also energise the cultural relations between India and France," he said.

The Delhi police subsequently added provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and criminal intimidation to the FIR registered against Mr. Bhardwaj over the alleged assault of the minor activist’s father. A separate case under the POCSO Act has also been registered against him.
Mr. Bhardwaj came under scrutiny after a video podcast in which he claimed to have “cracked the skull” of the student’s father during the demonstration went viral. He also claimed during the interview that he had political connections that helped him avoid arrest.

headline: The Foundation for Science, Innovation and Development (FSID), a single-window interface to the deep science and deep-tech capabilities of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), said on Monday that it would undertake 1,000 industry projects and buil...

The Foundation for Science, Innovation and Development (FSID), a single-window interface to the deep science and deep-tech capabilities of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), said on Monday that it would undertake 1,000 industry projects and build a portfolio of 300 deep-tech start-ups by 2030.
Through an open, domain-agnostic approach to incubation and stronger industry partnerships, the FSID would position itself as a leading platform connecting science, industry and entrepreneurship, with an impact that extends well beyond India, it stated in an event held on the IISc campus here.
Speaking at the event, the newly appointed CEO of FSID, Omprakash Subbarao, said, “As the world of research, innovation and technology translation evolved rapidly, so were the expectations of industry, government and other external stakeholders.”
“To enable the FSID to respond to these changing requirements with greater agility, professionalism and scale, we are strengthening its governance and leadership structure. For the first time, we are having an industry leader as the CEO to drive this transformation,” Mr. Subbarao said.
With a vision of ‘Built on Science, Scaled for the World,’ the FSID was built on two strong pillars: Innovation and Incubation, he said. “Our ambition is to deepen engagement with multinational corporations, indian corporates and Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises, while creating stronger pathways for science and research to translate into real-world impact,” Mr. Subbarao added.
The FSID unveiled a new governance model and the move marked a new phase in the FSID’s journey to build a self-sustaining Section 8 company. To ensure a strong and effective linkage with the IISc, Suryasarthy Bose would function as professor in-charge and provide institutional oversight and serve as the principal interface between the FSID and the IISc.

headline: Justice Sanjay K Agrawal sworn in as Rajasthan High Court Chief Justice
full_text:
Justice Sanjay K Agrawal sworn in as Rajasthan High Court Chief Justice
The Centre notified Justice Mishra’s appointment on Saturday, about a month after the Supreme Court Collegium had recommended his elevation
Governor Haribhau Bagade administered the oath of office to Justice Sanjay K Agrawal as the 44th Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court on Monday at a ceremony held at Lok Bhavan.
After taking the oath, Justice Agrawal signed the warrant of appointment issued by the President.
Chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma, deputy chief ministers Diya Kumari and Prem Chand Bairwa, state ministers, chief secretary V Srinivas and Rajasthan High Court judges were in attendance.
Deep Dive
Justice Agrawal, who was serving as a judge of the Chhattisgarh High Court, assumes office amid a controversy involving then acting chief justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma.
Supreme Court Justice Sandeep Mehta had written to Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant seeking Justice Sharma’s transfer out of Rajasthan and appointment of a regular Chief Justice from another High Court. Justice Mehta had raised allegations concerning Justice Sharma’s exercise of administrative powers and the listing of cases.
Also Read: Mishra to take oath as high court CJ today despite Punjab govt objection
The CJI indicated that the allegations against a sitting judge would have to be examined through the established institutional mechanism and that Justice Sharma should be given an opportunity to respond.
Justice Sharma subsequently submitted a detailed response to the CJI, rejecting the allegations as baseless and saying his response was supported by evidence.
Justice Agrawal briefly served as acting chief justice of the Chhattisgarh High Court following the retirement of Chief Justice Ramesh Sinha on September 4, pending the completion of his appointment to the Rajasthan High Court.
The central government notified Justice Mishra’s appointment on Saturday, about a month after the Supreme Court Collegium had recommended his elevation

headline: The Punjab Cabinet on Sunday (September 6, 2026) evening passed a resolution against the Centre notifying the appointment of Ashwani Kumar Mishra as the Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court, claiming it was done without awaiting the State g...
full_text:
The Punjab Cabinet on Sunday (September 6, 2026) evening passed a resolution against the Centre notifying the appointment of Ashwani Kumar Mishra as the Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court, claiming it was done without awaiting the State government's views bypassing Constitutional norms and set procedures.
Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann also wrote separate letters to President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging the Centre not to move forward with the administration of oath to Justice Mishra, which is scheduled for Monday (September 7, 2026), "till the state government's concerns are adequately addressed".
However, Additional Solicitor General of India, Satya Pal Jain, said the controversy raised by the Punjab Government over the appointment is "most unfortunate and totally uncalled for", and asserted that the State had sufficient time to send its views.
He said the Supreme Court collegium on August 6 recommended the names for the appointment of Chief Justice of eight high courts.
"All the state governments except Punjab sent their views within a week... No one has the right to sit over the proposal for an indefinite period with a view to scuttle the judicial process and politicise a non- political issue," Mr. Jain said in a statement and added that states do not hold a "veto" power on these appointments.
The Centre notified Justice Mishra's appointment on Saturday (September 5, 2026), about a month after the Supreme Court Collegium had recommended his elevation. He has been functioning as the Acting Chief Justice of the High Court here since June and is scheduled to be administered the oath as the High Court Chief Justice by the Governor here on Monday (September 7, 2026).
Hours before the oath ceremony, the Mann government convened an emergency meeting of the cabinet through video conferencing against the Centre's decision.
State's constitutional rights
An official statement after the meeting of the State cabinet said it had resolved that the appointment and administration of oath should be put on hold until Punjab's views are obtained and duly considered.
The cabinet strongly condemned "another instance" of central government "bypassing" the state's constitutional rights and established procedure, the statement said.
Sources said Chief Minister Mann is unlikely to attend the oath ceremony on Monday (September 7, 2026) and is leaving for Delhi to meet Punjab Minister Sanjeev Arora, who is in jail on money laundering charges.
In a post on X in Punjabi after the meeting, Mr. Mann stated: "Today, the Punjab Cabinet unanimously passed an important resolution against the continued assault on Punjab's rights by the Central Government and the violation of constitutional norms.
"Appointing the new Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court without obtaining the consent of the State Government is a direct violation of the prescribed procedures (Memorandum of Procedure) and constitutional norms." Mr. Mann, in his letters, requested urgent intervention in the matter by the President and the Prime Minister.
According to the official statement issued after the cabinet meeting, Mr. Mann said earlier the Centre withheld the State's ₹9,000 crore Rural Development Fund (RDF) and flood relief package, changing the BBMB rules, "and now its direct interference in judicial appointments will not be tolerated".
"We demand that this appointment be immediately put on hold and that, in accordance with the constitutional process, the views of the State be accorded due respect," he said.
The statement said that "the 'Memorandum of Procedure for appointment and transfer of Chief Justices and Judges of High Court', in its Para 6, clearly indicates that after receipt of the recommendation of the Chief Justice of India, the Union Minister of Law, Justice and Company Affairs would obtain the views of the concerned State Government.
"After receipt of the views of the State Government, the Union Minister of Law, Justice and Company Affairs, will submit proposals to the Prime Minister, who will then advise the President as to the selection.
"...In the instant case, the Collegium of the Supreme Court of India vide minutes dated August 6, 2026, has recommended the appointment of Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra, Acting Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court as the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court.
"On August 12, the State of Punjab received the letter from Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Minister of State for Law & Justice, for the consent of the State of Punjab in terms of Para 6 of the 'Memorandum showing the procedure for appointment and transfer of Chief Justices and Judges of the High Court'," it added.
The statement said that no clear time limit is prescribed for the State and the Governor to send its recommendation in the case of appointment of the Chief Justice.
"In complete disregard to the Memorandum of Procedures and established Constitutional norms, the Centre has hurriedly notified the appointment of the Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court without awaiting response of the State Government." "This appointment has been made without obtaining the consent of the state government thereby bypassing all Constitutional norms and set procedures," the statement said.

headline: 'Isro’s role won’t diminish': Agency allays concerns over privatisation
full_text:
'Isro’s role won’t diminish': Agency allays concerns over privatisation
ISRO said private-sector participation would enable the agency to focus on the next generation of India’s space programme while industry matures technologies.
Two days after nine associations representing thousands of Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro) employees sought clarity on the privatisation of the space sector, IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka and Isro on Sunday said the space agency’s role would not diminish.
Goenka said there had been “some misleading narrative” in the media about Isro’s future role. “Let me say it unequivocally: ISRO’s role is by no means diminishing. It will remain the bedrock of Indian space sector. The reforms since 2020 are about expanding India’s overall space ecosystem,” he said in a post on X.
The employees’ associations had written to the Department of Space secretary and Isro chairman V Narayanan seeking clarity after Goenka said that “eventually, ISRO will not make any launch vehicles and will not manufacture any launch vehicles. That will all be done by the private sector or PSU.”
The associations sought clarity on whether Goenka’s statement represented government policy, besides asking about the transfer of Isro’s manufacturing and operational functions, the agency’s future role and the impact on serving employees and future generations.
Also Read I Thousands of ISRO employees question fate, write to chairman amid privatisation push
ISRO clarifies on its privatisation stance
Isro, in a separate post on X on Sunday, said neither it would be privatised nor its importance diminished.
The agency said private-sector participation would enable the agency to focus on the next generation of India’s space programme while industry scales mature technologies.
Isro said its “role will progressively strengthen in areas where its scientific expertise matters most: frontier R&D, advanced technologies, human spaceflight, next-generation launch systems, deep-space and planetary missions and strategic national capabilities.”
“Meanwhile, mature and routinely manufactured systems can increasingly be scaled through industry. Production of mature launch vehicles, routine satellites and other established systems can increasingly be undertaken by industry or PSUs through appropriate competitive processes,” said Isro.

We wish to categorically state that Isro will neither be privatised nor will its importance be diminished,â it said.Isro further said it would continue to remain âIndiaâs principal institution for advanced space research and technology development, national and strategic missions, space science and exploration, and critical and frontier space capabilitiesâ.Space promoter and regulator Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (INSPACe) chairperson Pawan Goenka also said Sunday that Isro would âremain the bedrock of the Indian space sectorâ and at the core of Indiaâs space programme leading frontier research and the next generation of national missions like the space station and Gaganyaan.The agency said, âParticipation of private sector in space is not about reducing its role.
It is about enabling Isro to focus even more strongly on the next generation of Indiaâs space programme, while industry scales mature technologies and capabilities. What is changing is not the importance of Isro, but the scale and structure of Indiaâs space ecosystem. The transition is therefore towards an Isro-led national space ecosystem.âThe agency also said its role would progressively strengthen in areas where âits scientific expertise matters most: frontier R&D, advanced technologies, human spaceflight, next-generation launch systems, deep-space and planetary missions and strategic national capabilities. It will continue developing cutting-edge technologies, including advanced payloads for communication, navigation and Earth observation, sensors, propulsion systems and other critical technologiesâ.After nine Isro staff associations representing thousands sought clarification from the agency chairperson on the private sector shift, Goenka said on X, âLet me say it unequivocally: Isroâs role is by no means diminishing.âOn scaling up the production of rockets and satellites in India, the INSPACe director declared that the country had set an âambitious targetâ of 50 launches a year by 2030. âA goal of this scale cannot be achieved by one organisation alone. Govt and private industry have to build this future together,â he said.The INSPACe chairperson said, âThe reforms since 2020 are about expanding Indiaâs overall space ecosystem. IN-SPACe will facilitate and authorise greater non-govt participation, while NSIL will help commercialise mature capabilities.âGoenka said the idea of space reforms is to âlet industry increasingly manufacture and scale mature launch vehicles, satellites and other systems, while Isro focuses on what it is uniquely placed to do: advanced R&D, scientific missions, strategic missions, new technologies, and infrastructure that is too complex for the private sector to develop on its ownâ.
Assuring staff that they were going to handle big projects, he said, âIsro will remain at the core of Indiaâs space programme, leading frontier research and the next generation of national missions, including Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035, an Indian crewed mission to the Moon by 2040, next-generation launch systems, and sustained lunar and planetary exploration.ââThe direction is not a smaller Isro. headline: Chandigarh: Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra was sworn in as Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court Monday amid an unprecedented standoff between the Punjab government and the Centre over his appointment.
full_text:
Chandigarh: Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra was sworn in as Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court Monday amid an unprecedented standoff between the Punjab government and the Centre over his appointment.
Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann was conspicuous by his absence from the brief swearing-in ceremony held at Raj Bhawan here.
Punjab governor Gulab Chand Kataria administered the oath to Justice Mishra in the presence of Haryana governor Prof Ashim Kumar Ghosh and Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini. An empty chair on which the Punjab Chief Minister was supposed to sit marked the ongoing sharp confrontation between the Punjab government and the Centre over Justice Mishra’s appointment. The oath ceremony, however, was conducted by Punjab chief secretary K. A. P. Sinha.
The Punjab cabinet held an emergent meeting Sunday to resolve the issue of Justice Mishra’s appointment and decided the administration of oath should be put on hold till the Punjab government had given its views on his appointment, a procedural requirement which, according to the Punjab cabinet, the Centre had not fulfilled in this case.
In a statement issued following the cabinet meeting, Mann sought to place the dispute within a wider narrative of the Centre allegedly ignoring Punjab’s interests. The chief minister linked Justice Mishra’s appointment with other contentious issues, including Punjab’s demand for release of the Rural Development Fund and its demands for greater central assistance following the floods.
However what appeared primarily to be a dispute over administrative procedure acquired a considerably more serious institutional dimension with the Opposition framing the controversy as an attempt by the government to encroach upon the independence of the judiciary and a “lowly bid” to preempt possible adverse orders from the high court.
BJP national office in-charge and Rajya Sabha MP Tarun Chugh told mediapersons Sunday that this was a planned conspiracy. “It’s all well thought out by them. The idea is to defame the judiciary so that the government can work on a narrative that the judiciary is biased against them when issues like corruption and giving dearness allowance to employees come up in the court,” he said.
“They already know what the procedure is. Arvind Kejriwal has remained an officer. It’s a deeper conspiracy to preempt what the judiciary might do in the multiple cases of corruption,” said Chugh.
— Tarun Chugh (@tarunchughbjp) September 7, 2026
Shiromani Akali Dal General Secretary Dr Daljit Cheema said any attempt by the executive to question or influence judicial appointments undermines the independence of the judiciary and the constitutional separation of powers.
“The High Court has delivered several strong judgments against the Punjab government, while matters concerning alleged corruption in the highest offices are reaching a crucial stage. At such a juncture, creating controversy around the judiciary raises serious questions about the government’s intentions,” he wrote on X.
Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann’s objections to the appointment of Justice Ashwani Misra as Chief Justice of the Punjab & Haryana High Court are deeply concerning and must be condemned in the strongest terms. Any attempt by the executive to question or influence judicial appointments… pic.twitter.com/UO63Z5pB0T
— Dr Daljit S Cheema (@drcheemasad) September 6, 2026
Senior Akali leader Bikram Singh Majithia said the AAP government had already tried to “eliminate the Opposition, crush the press, keep only puppet media, and use the police as servants.”
“Now only one institution remained: The judiciary. Is that beginning to trouble you too? Passing a resolution against the appointment of the Chief Justice is not a resolution. It is a direct threat to the judiciary! Do you want to intimidate judges and cover up your corruption and scams?” Majithia questioned on X.
👉 Listen, Guru Dokhi!
👉 Trying to eliminate the Opposition, crush the press, keep only puppet media, and use the police as your servants!
👉 Now only one institution remained: the judiciary. Is that beginning to trouble you too?
👉 Passing a resolution against the… pic.twitter.com/hsvEhJFj8s
— Bikram Singh Majithia (@bsmajithia) September 6, 2026
Amarinder Singh Raja Warring said what was happening was quite unprecedented. “A state government is objecting to and opposing the appointment of the Chief Justice of the state high court. AAP Punjab has achieved yet another dubious distinction of doing that… Does the AAP want a judiciary of its own choice?”
This is quite unprecedented that a state government is objecting to and opposing the appointment of the Chief Justice of the state High Court. @AAPPunjab has achieved yet another dubious distinction of doing that. 
What does the AAP government want to convey with this stand?…
— Amarinder Singh Raja Warring (@RajaBrar_INC) September 7, 2026
Punjab cabinet’s opposition to Justice Mishra as chief justice comes at a time when matters of vital political significance are before the high court. With barely six months to go before Punjab Assembly elections, the outcome of these cases could have a decisive impact on the elections.
Justice Mishra, who took over as acting chief justice in the high court in June headed the Bench that recently directed the Punjab government to clear thousands of crores in pending dearness allowance and dearness relief to employees and pensioners—an order that the state has challenged in the Supreme Court.
He also barred the government from indulging in “unnecessary” expenditure of issuing advertisements till the allowances to the employees were paid.
At the same time, other politically sensitive cases are pending before the high court, including matters concerning allegations of demands of illegal gratification by relatives of the Punjab chief minister’s wife and alleged corruption by Punjab government officials linked to the CMO.
One such case filed as a public interest litigation by advocate Nikhil Saraf has sought investigation by the CBI into alleged “large-scale and institutionalised corruption” by government officials in “cahoots” with private persons—information about which had already been gathered by the Enforcement Directorate.
Two separate cases related to allegations of rape and its cover-up filed by the victim and the accused are also before the high court. Both the victim and the accused have told the court that a close relative of the chief minister’s wife was interfering in the investigation of the case demanding crores of rupees to settle the matter.
Senior Congressman and Leader of the Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa, while congratulating the chief justice, said the “court has time and again shown the Punjab Government the mirror and stood firm for justice and the rights of Punjabis from the DA case to the PIL filed by Nikhil Saraf.”
“Attempts to intimidate or undermine the judiciary must stop. The judiciary must remain independent, fearless and committed to justice,” he posted on X.
Congratulations to Hon’ble Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra on taking oath today as the Chief Justice of the Punjab & Haryana High Court.
The Court has time and again shown the Punjab Government the mirror and stood firm for justice and the rights of Punjabis from the DA case to the…
— Partap Singh Bajwa (@Partap_Sbajwa) September 7, 2026
Congress MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa questioned the timing of the objection raised by the Punjab government.
“The timing is telling,” he wrote on X. “Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra’s Bench tells the Punjab Government: Pay the DA owed to your employees and stop wasting public money on large-scale advertising. Days later, the Aam Aadmi Party Government moves to oppose his elevation as Chief Justice. If a government starts treating an inconvenient judicial order as a reason to object to the judge, we have a very serious problem.”
The timing is telling.
Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra’s Bench tells the Punjab Government: pay the DA owed to your employees and stop wasting public money on large-scale advertising.
Days later, the @AamAadmiParty Government moves to oppose his elevation as Chief Justice.
If a…
— Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa (@Sukhjinder_INC) September 6, 2026
The political atmosphere surrounding the dispute was further charged by what Mann said at a public meeting Sunday evening after the cabinet meeting. During his public address in village Gudda in Bathinda, Mann talked about the appointment of the chief justice.
“When the chief justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court has to be appointed, permission has to be taken from the state government. Sandhawalia, our Punjabi judge, was made the chief justice of Madhya Pradesh (high court). But the Madhya Pradesh Government did not give permission and he was sent to Himachal Pradesh as the chief justice,” said Mann referring to Justice G. S. Sandhawalia.
The chief minister went on, “Now when the chief justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court was to be appointed, permission was sought from me. I had not even given the permission and today they have appointed him saying forget about Punjab. This means that Punjab is not important and they do not think that it is of any value.”
ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੇ ਸੰਵਿਧਾਨਕ ਹੱਕਾਂ ’ਤੇ ਡਾਕਾ ਕਿਸੇ ਕੀਮਤ ’ਤੇ ਬਰਦਾਸ਼ਤ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਵੇਗਾ। ਨਿਆਂਪਾਲਿਕਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੇਂਦਰ ਦੀ ਇਸ ਦਖ਼ਲਅੰਦਾਜ਼ੀ ਦਾ ਅਸੀਂ ਡਟ ਕੇ ਵਿਰੋਧ ਕੀਤਾ ਹੈ। ਪੰਜਾਬੀਓ, ਇਹ ਸਮਾਂ ਇੱਕਜੁੱਟ ਹੋਣ ਦਾ ਹੈ। ਸੂਬੇ ਦੇ ਹੱਕਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਹਿੱਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਰਾਖੀ ਲਈ ਅਸੀਂ ਹਮੇਸ਼ਾ ਮੋਹਰੀ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਖੜ੍ਹੇ ਹਾਂ। pic.twitter.com/dl5BZrg0OF
— Bhagwant Mann (@BhagwantMann) September 6, 2026
The chief minister speaking about the appointment of a chief justice at a public rally was severely criticised by opposition leaders, who alleged the CM appeared to be inebriated during the rally.
Congress MLA Sukhpal Singh Khaira and Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia were among those who seized on Mann’s alleged demeanour and questioned his condition.
“An intoxicated chief minister running an intoxicated government!” Majithia posted on X. “An attack on the judiciary? Will even the appointment of the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court now be decided under the influence of alcohol? Those entrusted with safeguarding democracy are being questioned by an intoxicated man. Shameful! Will the Constitution of the country now also be dictated by the whims of an intoxicated chief minister? This is not change. This is destruction, something Punjab is witnessing for the first time in 70 years!”
👉 An intoxicated Chief Minister running an intoxicated government!
👉 An attack on the judiciary?
Will even the appointment of the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court now be decided under the influence of alcohol?
👉 Those entrusted with safeguarding democracy… pic.twitter.com/K2BVWf2Rnw
— Bikram Singh Majithia (@bsmajithia) September 7, 2026
“Never seen such a duplicate shameless leader like Bhagwant Mann who in a drunken state is publicly condemning the elevation of Justice A. K. Mishra as Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court but in the same breath his government is inviting Punjab MLAs to his oath taking ceremony!”
Never seen such duplicate shameless leader like @BhagwantMann who in a drunken state is publicly condemning the elevation of Justice Ak Mishra as Chief Justice of Pb & Hry High Court but in the same breath his govt is inviting Punjab MLA’s to his oath taking ceremony !
It shows… pic.twitter.com/hdwiyhhexC
— Sukhpal Singh Khaira (@SukhpalKhaira) September 6, 2026
The allegations nevertheless carry political weight because they revive an issue that has surfaced around Mann before. Khaira had earlier alleged in the Punjab Assembly that Mann appeared to be under the influence of alcohol and had demanded an alcohol or dope test.
Khaira also posted what he claimed were instructions from the government to its cabinet ministers to attend the oath taking ceremony of the chief justice.
Majithia also questioned the presence of the Punjab chief secretary K. A. P. Sinha as the master of ceremonies at the oath taking. “Yesterday, the chief secretary is attending the cabinet meeting where the cabinet is resolving against the appointment of the honourable chief justice. And today the same chief secretary is conducting the oath ceremony?” asked Majithia in a video message Monday, claiming that the state was witnessing a “breakdown of the Constitution”.
👉 For the first time in Punjab's history, we are witnessing a breakdown of the Constitution!
👉 A High Court Chief Justice is not appointed by an inebriated Chief Minister. The appointment is made through the Supreme Court Collegium. Who will explain this to the Guru Dokhi, who… pic.twitter.com/5o9nzZFES0
— Bikram Singh Majithia (@bsmajithia) September 7, 2026
Justice Mishra, whose parent high court is the Allahabad High Court, was transferred to the Punjab and Haryana High Court in July 2025. He took over as acting chief justice on 1 June, following the elevation of his predecessor, Justice Sheel Nagu, to the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court collegium, headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, recommended Justice Mishra’s appointment as the full-time chief justice on 6 August. The Centre notified the appointment on 5 September, completing a process that had remained pending for nearly a month.
(Edited by Viny Mishra)

headline: NCPCR summons Meta India official over child sex abuse material on social media
full_text:
NCPCR summons Meta India official over child sex abuse material on social media
India's child rights body summons Meta's MD over Instagram showing ads linked to child sexual abuse, amid ongoing investigations and policy discussions.
India’s apex child rights body, the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR), has summoned Meta India managing director Arun Srinivas on September 9 as part of its enquiry into Instagram hosting advertisements related to child sexual abuse material (CSAM) on the platform, as per a BBC Eye investigation news report.
The hearing will be led by NCPCR chairperson Valeti Premchand at its New Delhi office on Wednesday afternoon, according to people aware of the matter.
NCPCR has the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure to summon and enforce the attendance of any person. A representative from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) is also expected to be at the hearing, people aware of the matter told HT, as discussions on algorithms and other technical aspects are expected to be central to the proceedings.
Also Read | Meta settles $18 billion with 29 US states over child safety case
According to the BBC report, Instagram displayed advertisements containing phrases such as “rape video” and “child video” that directed users to Telegram channels allegedly selling child sexual abuse material. The report said after it flagged one advertisement to Instagram, the platform initially responded that the ad did not violate its community standards. Following the BBC’s findings, Meta removed several advertisements, disabled multiple accounts and blocked URLs found to be in violation of its policies, the report said.
On July 3, MeitY summoned top Meta officials and issued a notice on July 4, directing the company to immediately disable all Instagram advertisements and content that promote or facilitate access to CSAM.
As reported by HT on July 27, NCPCR sought a report from Meta on why the company did not inform the police after allegedly becoming aware of CSAM being promoted on Instagram, as required under under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act. Section 19 of the Pocso Act requires any person who has knowledge of an offence under the Act to report it to the Special Juvenile Police Unit or the local police. Meta replied to NCPCR in a week’s time.
An NCPCR official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told HT, “When we initiate an inquiry, there is a procedure. The body first calls for the relevant documents, studies them and then questions the people concerned. We now want to hear Meta’s side, understand the arguments it has presented in its report, and give the Meta India MD an opportunity to explain himself. This is part of the principles of natural justice before we reach any conclusion. At the hearing, Meta can substantiate the arguments made in its reports with relevant evidence, and we may seek further clarifications or documents. The MD will also have to depose under oath when summoned, and that deposition can subsequently be produced before a court of law.”
NCPCR’s summons to Meta come weeks after the company ran into hot waters over the temporary takedown of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Facebook video. Meta’s chief global officer, upon being summoned by MeitY, apologised to IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw over the incident, attributing it to a technical error. In the two-day meeting on August 5 and 6, discussions between the government and Meta’s global team also covered proliferation of CSAM on its platforms.
MeitY has since then acknowledged that the platform has stepped up efforts to detect and remove CSAM from Instagram and Facebook, including by strengthening filters and hiring regional-language moderators.
Also Read | Delhi HC asks Meta to explain its access policy on copyright management tool
A senior MeitY official on August 18 said, “We are not seeing that kind of content (CSAM) coming up in the same way, and platforms are being more cautious. Meta is also putting in place its own filters and working to identify unlawful content, with its content moderators becoming more sensitive to the Indian context. But we have to keep watching this. We cannot say overnight that we are fully satisfied.”
Separately, NCPCR is also in the process of drafting a uniform voluntary code of conduct for social media platforms to strengthen online safeguards for children. The guidelines are expected to cover age-appropriate access, harmful content, recommendation algorithms and online safety, while focusing on safer use rather than restricting children’s access altogether. The commission is consulting MeitY, DoT, platforms and civil society, with age verification and privacy among the key issues, HT reported on August 21.

headline: Expelled Bihar Congress functionaries protest outside party office, seek Rahul Gandhi meeting over state unit issues.
full_text:
Expelled Bihar Congress functionaries protest outside party office, seek Rahul Gandhi meeting over state unit issues.
NEW DELHI: A group of expelled Bihar Congress functionaries Tuesday protested in front of the party office here, and demanded a meeting with Rahul Gandhi so that they could âappriseâ him of the realities of the state unit.The former Congress functionaries, led by Anand Madhab, were expelled for âanti-party activitiesâ after Bihar assembly elections. They had alleged irregularities in the selection of candidates and blamed AICC in-charge Krishna Allavaru and Bihar Congress chief Rajesh Kumar.
Madhab said their demands include an immediate appointment with Rahul, withdrawal of all disciplinary and expulsion proceedings and orders against them. He also demanded removal of Allavaru and Kumar from their posts. Madhab said the process of restoration of faith in the party would start with the fulfilment of their demands. He said the leaders charged with indiscipline should be restored to their earlier positions in the organisation.Madhab said he and colleagues had been demanding a meeting with Rahul for a while, and decided to come to the capital after their demands and concerns were not heard. He said the group protesting is not a dissident bloc but comprises dedicated Congress workers. âWe have come to our own house, to meet our guardians and apprise them of the goings on in Bihar Congress,â he said.The protesters included former MLAs Anil Singh, Chhatrapati Yadav, Poonam Devi, and former Bihar Pradesh Congress vice-president Jamal Ahmed, Nagendra paswan.

headline: NEW DELHI: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) chief and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Tuesday clarified that a gesture he made during his Assembly speech was inadvertent and "not in any way intentional" . This comes as DMK accused him of at...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) chief and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Tuesday clarified that a gesture he made during his Assembly speech was inadvertent and "not in any way intentional" . This comes as DMK accused him of attempting to body-shame former chief minister MK Stalin.The clarification came amid a major uproar in the Tamil Nadu assembly, where DMK MLAs demanded that Vijay's remarks, including references based on Enforcement Directorate documents and the Sarkaria Commission, be expunged from the records. The protesting legislators were later evicted from the House by marshals after Speaker JCD Prabhakar rejected their demand.In a post on X, Vijay said his body language during his response to the police department's grant request on September 7 should not be interpreted as a personal attack."I wish to clarify that, during my response speech on the police department's grant request in the Legislative Assembly on 7.9.2026, my body language, which inadvertently came across in between, was not in any way intentional. Therefore, I kindly request that it not be interpreted as an act intended to hurt anyone's feelings on a personal level," Vijay said.
The controversy centres on a gesture Vijay made while referring to the history of the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA), when he placed his right palm against his jaw. The gesture was widely interpreted as a reference to Stalin's broken jaw, which he suffered after being assaulted during his detention under MISA during the Emergency.CPI(M) leader P Shanmugam criticised Vijay, accusing him of making a personal attack on Stalin."It is a well-known historical fact that the Emergency period in India witnessed massive struggles to protect democracy, accompanied by repression and excesses. During that time, former chief minister MK Stalin was brutally assaulted by the police, resulting in a broken jaw," Shanmugam said in a post on X."Ridiculing someone's physical appearance is condemnable, regardless of who engages in it; for the Chief Minister himself to do so is an act of irresponsibility," he added.
DMK protests over Vijay's remarks
The assembly witnessed heated exchanges on Tuesday after DMK Whip EV Velu demanded that Vijay's references to ED allegations of graft and the Sarkaria Commission be removed from the records.Velu also objected to references to people who were not present in the House to defend themselves, as well as references to deceased individuals.He argued that the Sarkaria Commission had examined 28 charges and claimed that no legal action could follow as the charges were not proved."Bringing this up without evidence is misleading," he contended.Velu also objected to Vijay's references to the MISA period, saying that repeated discussion of the issue and personal attacks on individuals were inappropriate.State law minister R Nirmal Kumar defended Vijay's remarks, saying they were based on official ED documents and the Sarkaria Commission report. He also reiterated allegations of corruption against the then DMK regime.
Kumar disputed claims concerning Stalin's arrest under MISA, arguing that it was linked to derogatory comments made against former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi regarding her "21-point programme".Leader of the House K A Sengottaiyan said there was no reason to expunge Vijay's remarks, citing a precedent in which late Chief Minister J Jayalalithaa had also spoken about the issue.The DMK members continued to protest after Speaker Prabhakar ruled against expunging the remarks. Several MLAs gathered before the Speaker's podium and raised slogans despite repeated appeals to return to their seats.Prabhakar eventually ordered marshals to evict the protesting MLAs. The legislators continued raising slogans as they were taken out of the Assembly hall.

headline: Bihar Congress row deepens as expelled leaders protest in Delhi, seek total revamp
full_text:
Bihar Congress row deepens as expelled leaders protest in Delhi, seek total revamp
Anand Madhav, who led the protest outside Indira Bhavan on Tuesday, said the Bihar Congress unit was being run like a corporate, that too in NGO format
A larger group of Congress leaders from Bihar, most of them expelled from the party after the debacle in the 2025 assembly polls, on Tuesday staged a dharna outside Indira Bhavan, the Congress headquarters in the national capital, to demand removal of the state unit chief Rajesh Kumar and the party in-charge Krishna Allavaru. They have also sought an appointment to meet Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi to appraise him of the issues of the party workers.
Led by Anand Madhav, a former spokesperson of the Bihar unit of the Congress, the dharna was held from 11am to 4pm. HT reported on August 29 that a section of Bihar leaders would stage a dharna.
Madhav said they had to stage the protest because they were going unheard.
“A political party can be run on political vision and by political leaders, not by any agent. Current in charge and president does not have political vision, they are running party like a corporate that too in NGO format. Infact we feel that Krishna Allavaru and Rajesh Ram are working as they are above party constitution and party president. They are working on their whims and fancies. And making mockery of Bihar congress by coming out with weirded ideas,” he told HT.
“We had to take this step because our issues remain unheard. We also want that the expulsion notices against us should be withdrawn and we should be reinstated in respectable positions in the BPCC,” Madhav said, adding that they were seeking a meeting with senior party leader Rahul Gandhi also..
Another expelled leader Shaukat Ali, former district president of Gopalganj, told reporters: “We want to meet [Rahul] Gandhi to tell him the actual situation of the party. We have four key demands that includes our meeting with Rahul Gandhi. Bihar Congress needs a revamp.”
Senior Congress leader and AICC member Kishore Jha said a disgruntled faction of state Congress workers has been consistently demanding that the party high command remove the state leadership and the state in-charge after the last assembly election results.
“They have also been making persistent efforts to meet the high command to offer key suggestions for the party’s improvement in the state; however, as their concerns were ignored, they were compelled to take such steps to press for their demands. To stage a dharna is an unfortunate decision but I urge the high command to engage with these individuals and take the necessary steps.”

headline: Can't keep it lingering: SC pulls up Odisha over delay in Dara Singh remission plea
full_text:
Can't keep it lingering: SC pulls up Odisha over delay in Dara Singh remission plea
The Supreme Court has asked the Odisha government to decide Ravindra Pal alias Dara Singh's remission plea without further delay. The court said prolonged inaction is unacceptable and warned it could summon officials.
The Supreme Court on Tuesday asked the Odisha government to take a clear decision on the remission plea of Ravindra Pal alias Dara Singh, who is serving a life sentence for the 1999 murder of Australian missionary Graham Stuart Staines and his two minor sons. The court said the matter could not be kept pending any longer.
A bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Vijay Bishnoi expressed displeasure that the state had still not informed it whether any decision had been taken. “You want to reject it, you do it. You take a decision. We will deal with it. You can’t keep it lingering like this,” the bench said.
Counsel for the state told the court that a letter seeking adjournment had been circulated because the advocate-on-record was unwell. Referring to its August 19 order, the bench said it had already directed the State Sentence Review Board to take a decision and inform the court. “Last time also, time was granted to decide on the application. You convey to us the decision,” the bench said. It added, “You can’t avoid taking a decision. For two years, you are delaying the matter. Yes or no, you take a decision.”
When the state’s counsel asked for the matter to be listed on September 17, the bench said, “We are not going to adjourn it on the next date.” It further told the state, “You take a decision and inform us, or we will summon your officer.” The court then posted the matter for hearing on September 17 and directed the respondent to inform it about the decision taken pursuant to its August 19 order.
While hearing the case on August 19, the top court had also pulled up the Odisha government for not deciding Singh’s remission plea. It noted that the matter had been adjourned repeatedly to enable the authority to act on his plea. During a hearing in July, the court had given the state a month to decide on it. Singh, 63, has been in jail for more than 26 years.
Singh moved the Supreme Court in 2024 seeking premature release, saying he had spent over 24 years in prison and had “repented” for what he described as an act committed in a fit of “youthful rage”. In his plea, he said he believed in karmic philosophy and should be given a chance to reform his character and address the effects of the bad karma he had accumulated through his actions. Seeking the court’s mercy, he said he would give back to society through “service-oriented actions”. He also asked for directions to the state government to consider his case under the 2022 guidelines for premature release in the three cases in which he was convicted.
According to his plea, Singh, who is lodged in Keonjhar district jail, has completed more than the qualifying period of 14 years under the April 19, 2022 policy and has undergone more than 24 years of actual imprisonment without remission. He said the authorities were under a legal obligation to consider his case under the Odisha government’s “Guideline for Premature Release 2022”, and that their failure to do so had jeopardised his right to liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution.
The case relates to the attack on the intervening night of January 22 and 23, 1999, when a mob led by Singh attacked Staines and his sons, 11-year-old Philip and eight-year-old Timothy, while they were sleeping in their station wagon in Manoharpur village of Keonjhar district and set the vehicle on fire. Singh, the main accused in the triple murder, was convicted and sentenced to death by a CBI court in 2003. The Orissa High Court commuted the sentence to life imprisonment in 2005, and the Supreme Court upheld that decision in 2011.
Mehendra Hembram, an accomplice of Singh, is also serving a life sentence in the case, while 11 other accused were acquitted by the high court for lack of evidence. Staines and his wife Gladys worked with the Mayurbhanj Evangelical Missionary organisation and cared for leprosy patients. Gladys Staines, who received the Padma Shri in 2005, had said she had forgiven the killers of her husband and sons and held no bitterness against them. The Supreme Court has now asked the Odisha government to state its decision on Singh’s remission plea at the next hearing on September 17.

headline: 'To stop love jihad': Maharashtra minister Nitesh Rane backs VHP's call to bar Muslims from Navratri events
full_text:
'To stop love jihad': Maharashtra minister Nitesh Rane backs VHP's call to bar Muslims from Navratri events
TOI News Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Sep 08, 2026, 12:33 IST
Comments

Maharashtra inister Nitesh Rane (File photo)
NEW DELHI: Maharashtra minister Nitesh Rane expressed support for the Vishva Hindu Parishad's (VHP) call to bar Muslims from the Navratri events in the state, alleging that otherwise this would lead to an increase in "love jihad" cases.Attendees at such festivities should undergo identity checks and recite the Hanuman Chalisa before entry, the BJP leader told PTI Videos on Monday.
"Love jihad" is a term used by right-wing activists to allege a ploy by Muslim men to lure women (mostly from the Hindu community) into relationships for religious conversion."Those who do not follow idol worship should not participate in Hindu religious events. Those coming for garba should show their identity and chant the Hanuman Chalisa before being allowed entry," Rane said, extending support to the VHP's demand.
The VHP last week announced that Muslims "would not be allowed" entry to garba and dandiya venues across the state during the upcoming Navratri festival, and issued "guidelines" for organisers to verify participants' identities by checking their Aadhaar cards and applying tilak on their foreheads.
The Navratri festival will begin on October 11.On the demand to curb DJ sound systems during the upcoming Ganesh festival, Rane called for the rules to be applied uniformly to all religious processions.
âIf DJs are not permitted during Ganesh festival celebrations, similar restrictions should apply to Eid processions as well,â he said.Rane alleged that loud music was played late into the night during recent Eid processions, adding that Hindus follow court orders and noise regulations.He also slammed Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray over his reported remarks about alleged vulgar dances during Kanwar Yatra events in parts of Uttar Pradesh, questioning why criticism was directed only at Hindu practices while statements by Muslim clerics were not similarly discussed.

headline: Fifty-four-year-old Chongtham Vikram Singh was a peace-loving musician who lived a peaceful life, his wife, Joshna Chongtham, said on Tuesday, a day after he died from injuries sustained in an assault by a group of allegedly inebriated men outside hi...
full_text:
Fifty-four-year-old Chongtham Vikram Singh was a peace-loving musician who lived a peaceful life, his wife, Joshna Chongtham, said on Tuesday, a day after he died from injuries sustained in an assault by a group of allegedly inebriated men outside his home in Delhi’s Ashram area. “We hope such an incident never happens to another family, and we hope justice will be done,” she said.
Ms. Chongtham made the statement at a press conference at Manipur Bhawan in New Delhi, a day after her husband, a well-known musician, succumbed to his injuries while undergoing treatment at Holy Family Hospital.
“I am still struggling to come to terms with the loss of my husband, Vikram Chongtham Singh. He was my husband, my child’s father, a son and a brother, a musician, and a person deeply loved by my family, friends and relatives. His sudden death has left a loss that cannot be expressed in words,” Ms. Chongtham said.
At the State Bhawan, Manipuri rights activist Binalakshmi Nepram, who has been supporting the family since the assault, demanded life imprisonment for the accused. She said it was the government’s responsibility to educate people about those from the northeastern States so that “they learn to love and respect us, not kill us”.
The Delhi Police have registered an FIR under BNS sections relating to mob lynching and arrested seven men and apprehended a 15-year-old boy. All of them were delivery or packaging workers at nearby dhabas. In the moments after the assault, Mr. Singh told his son that the people who assaulted him had previously threatened him for asking them not to make noise late into the night, according to the FIR.
Ms. Nepram told presspersons, “We wish to convey the message on behalf of 3.3 million Manipuris. You touch another brother, you touch another sister and Manipur will wage war against the people who are trying to kill our brothers, our children, both at home and in Delhi. Manipur is in a state of conflict right now. People come to Delhi for safety and you are killing us? Is this the India you want to develop”
People close to the family said Ms. Chongtham and her son would return to Imphal with Mr. Singh’s body, where a funeral would be held. Since Mr. Singh’s death, condolences and condemnations have poured in, with several civil society organisations holding a candlelight vigil near the Sunlight Colony police station on Monday night.
According to the police complaint filed by Mr. Singh’s son, Mr. Singh had left the home after dinner on Sunday night and at around 11:30 pm, his screams could be heard from the stairwell of the building where they lived. His 20-year-old son said he opened the door to find his father being kicked and punched by a group of people, who soon ran away.
Ms. Chongtham said that soon after Mr. Singh left the house, “he came running back, chased by eight men who beat him and ran away”, adding that he was complaining of breathlessness after the assault and was then rushed to the hospital.
