headline: New Delhi: Electoral donations of over Rs 10,000 crore between 2022 and 2024, up from Rs 4.37 crore in 2015-16—the audit and contribution reports of several unknown political parties in India have increasingly exceeded donations even to national part...
full_text:
New Delhi: Electoral donations of over Rs 10,000 crore between 2022 and 2024, up from Rs 4.37 crore in 2015-16—the audit and contribution reports of several unknown political parties in India have increasingly exceeded donations even to national parties in the country.
In fact, just 5 unrecognised political parties in Gujarat, together reported an income of Rs 2,316 crore between 2019 and 2024.
These unknown parties are called Registered Unrecognised Political Parties or RUPPs. A RUPP is a party that is formally registered with the Election Commission of India (ECI) but does not qualify for the status of a recognised state party or national party.
These parties, like other political parties, enjoy income tax exemptions. And that’s where the gap lies. As per an October 2025 notification by the ECI, there are over 2,000 such parties registered with the ECI.
Over the years, the ECI has attempted to reign them in, by “delisting” parties that failed to fulfill the essential condition of contesting even a single election in the last six years, and whose offices could not be physically located.
After the delisting, ECI also refers these cases to the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) to investigate the tax exemption claims by such parties. However, despite continued media scrutiny as well as delisting, the opacity around the finances of RUPPs has persisted due to low compliance with the requirement to file audit and contribution statements, and the lack of power to actually “deregister” such parties.
Former Chief Election Commission S. Y. Quraishi says that the concept of RUPPs has existed for several years now.
“But we have no way to track what they are getting, how much money they are earning. They are supposed to submit their returns, but even if they don’t, we can’t do anything because we have no power to deregister them. This was an old 2002 decision of the Supreme Court saying the ECI cannot deregister parties,” he explains.
Quraishi asserts that the government should have brought in a law allowing the ECI to deregister parties.
The ECI has “delisted” several such RUPPs over the years, taking such parties off the register containing a list of such unrecognised parties. But Quraishi questions the impact such delisting may have.
“There is no such term called ‘delisting’ in the Rules. About 4-5 years ago, because of so much public hue and cry, they said they were delisting such parties, but that, according to me, means nothing. It does not amount to deregistering,” he says. “We should be able to deregister them but we cannot. We know they are collecting money but what can we do?” he asks.
Anjali Bhardwaj, co-convener of the National Campaign for People’s Right to Information, pointed out that another way in which corruption can happen is with registration as a political party.
“It can be a way for money laundering, including through the use of shell companies. There is massive potential for corruption of different kinds,” she explains.
The questions that arise, according to her, are: “What are the regulators doing? What are agencies like the Lokpal, ED and CBI doing?”
“These political parties are clearly filing their income tax returns. They are submitting their reports to the Election Commission. They are, after all, registered political parties. If journalists can see this, if citizens can see that there is a cause for concern, what are the regulators doing?” Bhardwaj, who is also the founding member of Satark Nagrik Sangathan, asked. “Why is there no scrutiny of the kind of money that they are amassing and their political footprint, which is apparently disproportionate?”
Unrecognised versus recognised parties
Quraishi points out that it is “easy” to register as a political party. Earlier it needed 30 persons, now it needs an association of at least 100 registered electors as members.
“It is very, very easy. Registered parties then contest elections and on the basis of their electoral performance, they are recognised as a national party or a regional party,” he explains.
A party becomes a recognised state party if it meets specific voting thresholds—securing at least 6 percent valid votes in an Assembly election, and winning at least two seats in the same Legislative Assembly, or winning 3 percent of the total seats in the Assembly.
For national party recognition, a party needs to secure 6 percent vote share in four or more states during Lok Sabha polls, and win at least four seats in the Lok Sabha or win 2 percent of total Lok Sabha seats from three different states.
Currently, there are six national parties and 60 regional or state parties.
Section 29C of the Representation of People Act 1951 requires all political parties to furnish their contribution reports as prescribed under the Conduct of Election Rules 1961. Such contributions received by the parties are also 100 percent exempt from Income Tax as an incentive to the parties.
Section 29A(9) mandates every political party to communicate any change in its name, head office, office bearers, address, PAN number to the ECI without delay.
Political parties are also mandated to furnish their annual audit statements to the ECI, and are under a statutory obligation to furnish a return of income for each assessment year to be eligible for exemption from income-tax.
According to the guidelines on ‘Transparency and Accountability in party funds and election expenditure’, as published by the ECI in August 2014, all unrecognised parties have to file audit reports, contribution reports and election expenditure statements with the Chief Election Officers of their respective states.
However, RUPPs often fail to file their returns. For instance, a report by the Association of Democratic Reforms (ADR), published in July last year, said that in 2019-20, 219 RUPPs claimed tax exemptions worth Rs 608 crore, but 66 of them did not submit mandatory contribution reports. It also claimed that as per ECI data, only 5 percent RUPPs submitted donation reports between 2013 and 2016.
As per guidelines for registration of political parties, if a party does not contest elections continuously for six years, the party shall be taken off the list of registered parties.
Thousands of crores without electoral support
It has been seen through consecutive ECI records that RUPPs have amassed considerable wealth over the years, while displaying little to no electoral support on the ground.
An ADR report, dated 18 July 2025, recognised the top 10 RUPPs that declared their income from FY 2019-20 to FY 2023-24, and found that Gujarat-based parties alone account for 73.22 percent (Rs 1158.1154 crore) of the top 10 parties’ declared income of Rs 1581.7517 crore between FY 19-20 and FY 23-24.
Bharatiya National Janata Dal, registered in Gujarat in February 2009, declared the highest total income of Rs 957.4454 crore (31.76 percent of total) between FY 2019-20 and 2023-24. Of the top 5 parties in this list, three—Bharatiya National Janata Dal, New India United Party, Satyawadi Rakshak Party—were registered in Gujarat.
Of the top ten, five were registered in Gujarat, two in Bihar, two in Haryana and one in Delhi.
The ADR report had noted that there was a dramatic increase in declared income of RUPPs starting from FY 2021-22 (Rs 490.2151 crore), which then rose by 223 percent in FY 2022-23 (Rs 1581.7517 crore), and remained high in FY 2023-24 (Rs 915.4172 crore).
As per a report in The Hindu Businessline in November 2025, the CBDT had even unearthed an organised network involving RUPPs, chartered accountants and intermediaries engaged in laundering money worth Rs 9,169 crore, by getting tax exemptions for political donations to these RUPPs.
In December 2025, a PIB release also said that fake donation claims to political parties were under the tax scanner, and said that “huge amounts of bogus claims have been made on account of donation” to RUPPs.
The crackdown
Back in December 2016, the Indian Express had conducted an investigation of political parties delisted by the ECI following a review, finding that many of these parties only existed on paper.
For instance, it had found that those behind the establishment of such parties included a homoeopathy practitioner based in a three-storey bungalow in Gurgaon, and another party was found to have the office of the J&K CID listed as its registered address. Another party had a lawyer’s chamber in Patiala House courts listed as its registered address, and the address of a fourth party was the residence of an employee of the Delhi Development Authority (DDA).
It was after this that the ECI decided to delist around 200 political parties and send their names to the CBDT. Officials suspected that these parties were money laundering operations, since they had not contested any election since 2005 and existed only on paper.
In 2022, the ECI initiated action for enforcing due compliances by RUPPs, under Sections 29A and 29C of the RP Act 1951. It had noted with concern that out of a total 2,796 RUPPs, over 92 percent RUPPs had not filed their Contribution Report in 2019. It had noted that 199 RUPPs had claimed Rs 445 crore IT exemption in 2018-19, and 219 RUPPs claimed Rs 608 crore IT exemption in 2019-20.
However, out of these 219, 66 RUPPs had claimed income tax exemption without submitting contribution reports in Form 24A as mandated under section 29C of the Act. And in 2019, out of 2,354 RUPPs only 623 contested elections
The ECI found 87 RUPPs were not even in existence. When physical inspection by the respective Chief Electoral Officers did not find these parties at their registered addresses, their names were deleted from the register of unrecognised registered political parties.
Since then, the ECI has done this delisting exercise several times. For instance, in June 2025, the ECI had started proceedings to delist 345 RUPPs, asserting that they had failed to fulfill the essential conditions required to continue as a registered state party.
The CEOs of respective states and UTs were asked to issue show-cause notices to these parties, giving them an opportunity for hearing, post which, it said, a decision would be taken by the ECI.
In August last year, 334 RUPPs were delisted, and in September 2025, another 474 RUPPS were delisted. In October, the commission once again notified a list of RUPPs, containing details of 2,049 such parties, and since then, it has continued to notify and add to this list.
‘The fountainhead of corruption’
Experts view political party funding as the source of opacity and corruption.
“It has been recognised very widely that political party funding has been the fountainhead of corruption in our country. The kind of data that came for electoral bonds made it very clear that there was a very large scale potential quid pro quo and extortion that was happening. It showed how political party funding can lead to corruption,” Anjali Bhardwaj told ThePrint.
Bhardwaj points out that there has been a longstanding demand to bring political parties under the purview of the Right to Information Act.
In June 2013, the Central Information Commission (CIC) declared six national political parties—the INC, BJP, CPI(M), CPI, NCP and BSP—to be “public authorities” under the RTI Act. What this meant is that political parties were, therefore, required to make disclosures and provide information under the law.
However, in March 2015, the CIC admitted that it was powerless to enforce its own ruling, calling it a case of “wilful non-compliance” by political parties. The ADR and RTI activist Subhash Chandra Agrawal then approached the Supreme Court in 2015, demanding that all the national and regional political parties be brought under the ambit of the RTI Act. This case is pending before the court.
Bhardwaj points out that political parties have neither got a stay from the courts, nor have they challenged the CIC order, so the order stands. But the parties, she says, are in “uncivil disobedience” of the order.
“There is a lot of public interest in people knowing about these political parties that claim to work for the public, that are collecting money from the public, and are, therefore, also in many ways, substantially financed by taxpayers’ money because they are getting income tax benefits and exemptions and other kinds of benefits. All of them should be under the RTI law so that people, citizens, can also monitor them,” she asserts.
(Edited by Viny Mishra)

headline: The government on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) faced questions over its links to a religious group whose allegedly “anti-women” demands caused the iconic Eiffel Tower in Paris to shut down for a day, leading to a major political row in France. Paris c...
full_text:
The government on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) faced questions over its links to a religious group whose allegedly “anti-women” demands caused the iconic Eiffel Tower in Paris to shut down for a day, leading to a major political row in France. Paris city officials have begun a formal inquiry into the incident, and the Hindu group, known as BAPS, denied making any demands to “limit interactions” with women employees at the tower.
The shutdown came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated a temple built by BAPS in a Paris suburb. In a 10-minute virtual address, Mr. Modi had called the construction a “new chapter” in India-France cultural relations. The External Affairs Ministry said the Prime Minister often addressed such events and India was not involved in the controversy at the Eiffel Tower.
According to officials managing the Eiffel Tower, BAPS leaders, who were in Paris for the temple’s inauguration and planned a weekend visit to the landmark, specifically asked for women employees to be moved out of sight of the delegation of monks, particularly their 93-year-old leader. The union of the Eiffel Tower employees, which called the one-day strike in solidarity with female colleagues, said the women, who had been replaced by men at certain posts, were instructed not to cross certain areas while the delegation was present.
“We are aware of the opening of a temple by the BAPS Sanstha in the Paris area. As to the issue pertaining to the Tower, this is a matter purely between the entities [BAPS and the Eiffel Tower authorities] concerned,” Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in his first response to the controversy.
To a follow-up question from The Hindu on whether the government has asked BAPS for an explanation of its alleged demand to deny women employees access to parts of the Eiffel Tower or whether it would now distance itself from the group, Mr. Jaiswal said that it was a “common practice” for the Prime Minister to “convey his good wishes” on such occasions, and there would be no comment.
Earlier this year, India’s Ambassador to France, Sanjeev Singla, had spoken at a ceremony for the temple. India’s Ambassador to UNESCO, Vishal Verma, praised the BAPS group in a social media post on Tuesday and said his wife had participated in the “shilanyas” or stone-laying ceremony of the temple in 2022.
The group, called the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha or BAPS, is known for the Akshardham temple in Delhi. It runs temples across the world and is headquartered in Ahmedabad. While women are part of the organisation, it is known for strict rules for its celibate monks and segregation between men and women.
In written responses to The Hindu, BAPS denied having made the requests. “We want to be unequivocally clear: this coordination was undertaken purely as a matter of operational courtesy and logistics to ensure a smooth visit for a large group without inconveniencing the Tower’s employees or the public,” BAPS, France, said, pointing out that the delegation had more than 100 members. “It was never, at any point, intended as a request rooted in gender, and any suggestion to the contrary does not reflect the spirit or values of our fellowship or the delegation,” it added, insisting that BAPS did not know about the denial of access to anyone.
However, the women employees had said earlier that they were made to feel “invisible”. French right-wing and centrist opposition leaders criticised the Macron government for the incident and demanded an explanation.
“In France, we do not ask women to erase themselves. No dogma, no religion is above the laws of the Republic,” France’s Equality Minister Aurore Berge said in response. Several French commentators questioned the reasons behind the group’s influence, pointing to the BAPS temple in the U.S. that faced legal cases after the Federal Bureau of investigation accused the group of labour code violations.
On Monday, the Mayor of Paris, Emmanuel Gregoire, ordered an inquiry into the incident, while the President of the operator SETE (Société d’Exploitation de la tour Eiffel) Ariel Weil issued an apology.
“I understand the emotion of the Eiffel Tower staff: no motive of a religious order could justify a distinction based on gender or any other discriminatory consideration in welcoming the public,” Mr. Weil said in a social media post.
(With inputs from Sriram Lakshman in London)

headline: The Foundation for Science, Innovation and Development (FSID) at IISc has adopted a new governance and leadership model.
full_text:
The Foundation for Science, Innovation and Development (FSID) at IISc Â has adopted a new governance and leadership model.
Bengaluru: The Foundation for Science, Innovation and Development (FSID) at IISc has adopted a new governance and leadership model, appointing Omprakash Subbarao as its CEO and bringing an industry professional to the helm for the first time.The change marks a new phase for FSID, which said it is seeking to build a self-sustaining Section 8 company anchored around two pillars: innovation and incubation. Historically, the organisation has been led by faculty members of IISc.Under the new structure, Subbarao will be a full-time CEO reporting to the FSID Board, with full operational autonomy and responsibility for the organisationâs day-to-day management, external engagement and execution of activities. Prof Suryasarthy Bose will serve as Professor-in-Charge, providing institutional oversight and acting as the principal interface between FSID and IISc.Subbarao, an IISc alumnus, brings experience across technology, industry, public digital infrastructure and innovation. Before his appointment, he was CEO of CORE Labs at FSID, where he led research and innovation collaborations with large corporations.
âAs the world of research, innovation and technology translation evolves rapidly, so too are the expectations of industry, govt and other external stakeholders,â Subbarao said. To respond to these changing requirements âwith greater agility, professionalism and scaleâ, he said, FSID was strengthening its governance and leadership structure.âFor the first time, weâre having an industry leader as the CEO to drive this transformation,â he added. FSID has set a target of undertaking 1,000 industry projects and building a portfolio of 300 deep-tech startups by 2030.âWith a vision of âBuilt on Science, Scaled for the Worldâ, we are building FSID around two strong pillars: Innovation and Incubation,â Subbarao said. The organisation wants to deepen engagement with multinational corporations, Indian corporates and MSMEs while creating stronger pathways for science and research to translate into real-world impact, he said.
Over the past year, FSID has expanded industry engagement through Innovation Hub, or iHUB, its innovation and research facility that brings corporates and startups closer to IIScâs scientific ecosystem.The facility provides R&D laboratories for corporate partners and infrastructure for incubated startups. BEML, Toyo Ink and Schaeffler are among companies that have established research labs and workspaces there. FSID serves as IIScâs single-window interface for its deep science and deep-tech capabilities, supporting collaborative research, incubation, product development, consulting and industry-funded research.
Chethan Kumar is a Senior Assistant Editor with the Times of India. Aside from specialising in Space & Science, he has reported extensively on varied topics, with special focus on defence, policy and data stories. He has covered multiple elections, too. As a young democracy grows out of adolescence, Chethan feels, there are reels of tales emerging which need to be captured. To do this, he alternates between the mundane goings-on of the Common Man and the wonder-filled worlds of scientists and scamsters, politicians and soldiers. In a career spanning nearly 18 years, he has reported from multiple datelines â Houston, Florida, Kochi, Hyderabad, Chennai, Sriharikota (AP), NH-1 (J&K Highway), New Delhi, Ahmedabad, Raichur, Bhatkal, Mysuru, Chamarajanagar, to name a few â but is based out of Bengaluru, Indiaâs science capital that also hosts the ISRO HQ.

headline: NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Tuesday slammed Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi for "politicising" the killing of Manipuri musician C Vikram Singh in Delhi, saying that the focus should be on immediate action.While talking to re...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Tuesday slammed Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi for "politicising" the killing of Manipuri musician C Vikram Singh in Delhi, saying that the focus should be on immediate action.While talking to reporters, Rijiju said that Rahul should not bring BJP into the issue and said that Delhi Police takes immediate action whenever an incident involving people from the North East occurs."This is not the time for politics. I keep asking why Rahul Gandhi brings the BJP into this? When an incident occursâa tragedy resulting in someone's deathâthe focus should be on immediate action. This is not a matter for politics," Rijiju said."The North East Special Police Cell established within the Delhi Police remains in constant contact, ensuring immediate action in the event of any incident. Things are no longer as they used to be; we have put a system in place to take swift measures. Consequently, whenever an incident involving people from the North East occurs in Delhi, immediate action is taken," he added.This comes after Rahul condemned the death of Manipuri musician Chongtham Vikram Singh, who was allegedly assaulted by a group of men and questioned Union home minister Amit Shah and Delhi Police over what they were doing to stop the "growing lawlessness" against people from the Northeast in Delhi.
"Chongtham Vikram Singh ji, a renowned musician from Manipur, went downstairs to ask some men to lower the noise outside his home. He was beaten to death for it. A father, killed outside his own home, in his own country's capital. After many such incidents, every Northeast family in Delhi is asking the same question today - are we safe here?" the Congress leader said."What are Shah's MHA and Delhi Police doing to stop this growing lawlessness, especially against people from the Northeast? There must be a swift investigation, and the culprits must be brought to justice. My condolences to Vikram ji's family," he added.The 54-year-old Manipuri music teacher allegedly died after being assaulted by a group of men in Kilokari Village, in Delhiâs Ashram area, following a dispute over noise and nuisance outside his residence.
According to police, Vikram Singh had objected to alleged shouting and nuisance by delivery boys and dhaba staff opposite his house. When he came downstairs to object, he was allegedly attacked with fists and blows.Vikram was taken to Holy Family Hospital by his son Yaiphaba for treatment, where he later succumbed to his injuries.According to the Police, a PCR call regarding the alleged beating of C Vikram Singh was received at Delhi's Sunlight Colony police station on September 7. Police said the preliminary enquiry indicated that Singh had objected to alleged shouting and nuisance by delivery boys and dhaba staff in front of his residence in Kilokari Village. When he came downstairs and objected, he was allegedly assaulted with fists and blows.
The official further informed that they have registered an FIR under murder provisions and said all the accused, including minors, have been apprehended.Further investigation is still under way.
Rohitashwa Ranjan is a digital journalist with The Times of India, where he decodes Indian politics as a carefully staged production with scripts, subtext and everything behind. His stories track elections, party dynamics and the things that often are buried beneath the headlines. When not parsing vote shares or alliances, he is usually reading between the lines, where the real story tends to reside.

headline: PM Modi, Russia's Putin to hold bilateral talks on Friday, Su-57 aircraft sale to India on agenda
full_text:
PM Modi, Russia's Putin to hold bilateral talks on Friday, Su-57 aircraft sale to India on agenda
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said that Putin and Modi are set to hold bilateral talks on Friday, with the sale of Su-57 aircraft to India on the agenda.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin are set to hold a bilateral meeting on Friday (September 11) on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit 2026 in New Delhi, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on Tuesday.
Speaking to reporters via a virtual briefing from Moscow, Peskov said, “We're looking forward to the President and Prime Minister having another bilateral meeting during the visit. It is scheduled. It is scheduled for Friday, so, as always, they will first touch on the bilateral agenda."
The 18th BRICS Summit will take place at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. India took over the BRICS presidency on January 1 this year, becoming the grouping's chair for the fourth time.
Su-57 aircraft sale, trade on agenda
Peskov said that the sale of Su-57 aircraft to India is on the agenda, alongside other talks on trade and economy. India has not yet officially commented on Peskov's remarks.
On the United States' proposed move to levy 100% tariffs on countries buying Russian crude oil, he said the action is “illegal and unacceptable”.
BRICS Summit in India
The two-day event will bring together leaders of member countries, invited participants, and senior officials at Bharat Mandapam in Pragati Maidan.
The 11-member core group consists of Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates. Indonesia became a full member in 2025.
The bigger BRICS framework also includes 10 partner countries: Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam. These countries are partner nations and are separate from the full members.
Who is attending?
PM Modi will host the summit. Putin has confirmed his attendance, while Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to participate. If Xi visits India, it will be his first trip to the country since his informal meeting with PM Modi in Mamallapuram in 2019.
Other leaders expected at the summit include South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul. United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres is also expected to attend.
Modi, Putin last met at SCO Summit
PM Modi and Putin most recently met on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. It was their first face-to-face meeting since the annual India-Russia Summit in New Delhi last December.
“Every day spent perpetuating war pushes humanity backwards, and every step taken towards peace fills the whole of humanity with new hope and enthusiasm. We must move from endless war towards the end of war, which is very necessary for the well-being of humanity,” Modi said in televised opening remarks at the meeting with Putin.
“A peaceful resolution of all issues as soon as possible is the call of humanity, and this is also India’s message. The land of Gandhi and Buddha has one message — the path of peace,” he said, speaking in Hindi.
Modi said the Ukraine issue had featured in his discussions with Putin at every meeting and stressed that India “supports all efforts for peace and will continue to do so in future”.

headline: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian president Vladimir Putin are scheduled to hold a bilateral meeting on Friday, with trade and economic cooperation expected to feature prominently on the agenda, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov sa...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian president Vladimir Putin are scheduled to hold a bilateral meeting on Friday, with trade and economic cooperation expected to feature prominently on the agenda, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said.Moscow also welcomed Indiaâs willingness to contribute to efforts aimed at finding a peaceful resolution to the Ukraine conflict.Putin is scheduled to visit India for the BRICS Summit, which will begin in New Delhi on September 12. Ahead of the visit, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said the trip will provide an opportunity for the two countries to discuss issues concerning bilateral relations. He also wished India success in hosting the summit.
"In a couple of days, President Putin will begin his India visit. You know that our two leaders, Indian and Russian leaders, are in a very close personal contact. They are very pragmatic in their relationship, and they are as sincere as to be able to discuss in a very open and constructive way the most sensitive issues of our agenda and our bilateral relations. Of course, it opens additional horizons for our cooperation," Peskov said.
"We have no doubt that the summit will be successful. Russia, we are doing our best to contribute to further development of BRICS cooperation in the three main pillars of our interaction. So, those are policy and security. economy and finance, and cultural and humanitarian contexts. So, we are supporting idea of inviting new countries to join different formats within BRICS," he added.Peskov said Russia is awaiting negotiations with India on setting up new nuclear power plants, adding that the sale of Su-57 fighter aircraft to India is also on the agenda.The Kremlin spokesperson stressed the need for cooperation in the financial sector, alleging that some countries were using their currencies as a tool of political oppression."The cooperation space within Brics financial sphere is of great importance. Russia recently reached a level of 90 percent of all the payments, all the transactions with Brics countries being made in national currencies, it's very important. It's not because we are aiming for de-dollarization, for getting rid of US dollars. To the contrary, we are open to to every acceptable methods of payments, but you know that certain countries are using some national currencies as a tool for political oppression.
They are introducing sanctions based on their national currencies. So, if they don't let us use their money, we use our own money," Peskov said.India is set to host the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13, 2026, as the grouping of major emerging market economies and developing nations continues to expand its role in global affairs.The grouping began as Bric, comprising Brazil, Russia, India and China. It held its first Foreign Ministersâ meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York in 2006, followed by its inaugural summit in Yekaterinburg, Russia, in 2009. South Africa joined the grouping in 2011, leading to the formation of BRICS.
Under Indiaâs 2026 chairship theme, âBuilding for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability,â New Delhi is seeking to move the groupingâs agenda beyond political coordination towards practical cooperation in areas including trade, agriculture, healthcare, energy, digital technology, urban development, small enterprises, startups, climate action and cultural exchanges.

headline: NEW DELHI: As India prepares to host the 18th BRICS Leadersâ Summit, luxury hotels in the national capital are facing a sharp squeeze in room availability, with tariffs at some marquee properties climbing beyond Rs 2 lakh a night ahead of the Septemb...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: As India prepares to host the 18th BRICS Leadersâ Summit, luxury hotels in the national capital are facing a sharp squeeze in room availability, with tariffs at some marquee properties climbing beyond Rs 2 lakh a night ahead of the September 12-13 gathering.The summit, which brings leaders of the expanded BRICS grouping to Delhi and marks two decades since the blocâs founding, is driving concentrated demand for high-end accommodation, with several premium hotels showing limited or no availability and others quoting rates of more than Rs 2 lakh per night, according to news agency PTI.Booking checks showed no room availability at Taj Mahal and The Oberoi in New Delhi for September 11-12, while Taj Palace had no rooms available for September 10-12. The Leela Palace, New Delhi, was also not accepting bookings for stays between September 10 and 12.At ITC Maurya, New Delhi, rooms available for September 10-13 were commanding tariffs starting at more than Rs 2.3 lakh a night.The surge comes as delegates and other visitors are expected to arrive in the capital ahead of the two-day summit and extend their stays, putting pressure on room inventory, particularly in central Delhi.
K B Kachru, president, Hotel Association of India (HAI) and Chairman - South Asia, Radisson Hotel Group, said the summit was highlighting the pressure on India's hospitality infrastructure."India is commanding global attention at a defining moment -- as the nation prepares to host marquee international events and cements its position as a premier MICE destination, the world is watching how we scale to meet our tourism targets."The BRICS Summit alone will put considerable focus on room inventory and that spotlight is exposing a hard truth: our hospitality infrastructure has not kept pace with our tourism ambition," he said, according to PTI.Kachru said India currently has only about 200,000-220,000 branded hotel rooms, which he described as inadequate for the country's tourism ambitions.The demand is also being felt beyond central Delhi. Rahool Macarius, Market Managing Director, Eurasia, Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, said the summit was creating a distinct demand pattern across Delhi-NCR."At Ramada Encore by Wyndham, Dwarka Expressway, this event-led demand is reflected in occupancy for September 12-15, currently tracking at 65 per cent, significantly ahead of the broader market demand," he said.For tourists, business travellers and families visiting Delhi during the period, the squeeze could mean higher accommodation costs or a shift towards hotels outside central areas and lower-priced properties.
However, hotel tariffs and availability remain dynamic and can change with bookings, cancellations and fresh inventory releases. Emails seeking comments from the hotels cited for availability and tariffs remained unanswered till the time of publication, PTI reported.
Subhadra Srivastava is a journalist with The Times of India, covering geopolitics, international and national affairs. With over three years of experience, she focuses on national and global developments, conflict, diplomacy and their impact on India. Her work combines breaking news with in-depth analysis, offering readers context and clarity on the stories shaping the world.

headline: NEW DELHI: Deaths linked to second-hand smoke in India have soared, surging almost 50% since 1990 and claiming 325,600 lives in 2023 alone. According to a study published in The Lancet Public Health Monday, India had the world's second-highest number...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Deaths linked to second-hand smoke in India have soared, surging almost 50% since 1990 and claiming 325,600 lives in 2023 alone. According to a study published in The Lancet Public Health Monday, India had the world's second-highest number of people exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, after China, with 444 million Indians affected.While India's age-standardised exposure prevalence declined from 43.2% to 30.6% over the last three decades, the absolute number of people exposed rose from 375 million in 1990 to 444 million in 2023, an increase of 18.4%. The health toll also rose sharply, with deaths attributable to second-hand smoke climbing from 217,700 to 325,600 during the same period.Fatalities among women rose from 113,400 to 156,900, while deaths among men from 104,300 to 168,700 over the same period. Second-hand smoke also accounted for 9.28 million disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) in India in 2023, representing healthy years lost to premature death, illness or disability.Dr G C Khilnani, chairperson of pulmonary, critical care at PSRI Hospital, said, "Second-hand smoke contributes not only to illness and disability but also to premature deaths and loss of healthy years. Kids and women are particularly vulnerable, with children's developing lungs making them more susceptible to respiratory issues.
Smoking should be done outdoors, and greater public awareness is needed."The study links second-hand smoke to ischaemic heart disease, stroke, lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, breast cancer, type 2 diabetes, asthma and lower respiratory infections. Among children, lower respiratory infections were the leading contributor to the disease burden.Globally, 2.71 billion people were exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, contributing to 1.66 million deaths and 44.8 million DALYs. China, India and Indonesia accounted for nearly half of world's exposed population, with China recording 664 million exposed people.
Anuja Jaiswal is a Senior Assistant Editor at The Times of India, with an impressive 18-year career in narrative journalism. She specializes in health and heritage reporting, expertly simplifying complex health information to make it engaging and understandable for readers. Her deep dives into heritage topics are well-researched, resulting in captivating narratives that resonate with her audience. Over the years, she has worked in Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh and West UP, gaining diverse on-ground experience that shapes her storytelling.

headline: Despotic officers will turn UP Orwellian: HC raps Noida DM over student's detention
full_text:
Despotic officers will turn UP Orwellian: HC raps Noida DM over student's detention
The Allahabad High Court rapped Gautam Buddha Nagar DM Medha Roopam over the NSA detention of a Delhi University student. While cancelling the DM's NSA detention order, the court warned that "despotic" conduct by errant officials could turn Uttar Pradesh into an "Orwellian Dystopia".
The Allahabad High Court has cancelled the NSA detention of a Delhi University student arrested during April's Noida workers' protest. The court came down heavily on Gautam Buddha Nagar DM Medha Roopam, warning that "despotic" conduct by errant officials could turn Uttar Pradesh into an "Orwellian Dystopia".
A bench of Justices Atul Sreedharan and Achal Sachdev held on Monday that the continued incarceration of 25-year-old Akriti Chaudhary violated her fundamental rights, finding that the DM's NSA detention order and its grounds were devoid of material and showed "non-application of mind".
The court also awarded Chaudhary Rs 5 lakh compensation and directed that the amount be recovered from the salary of the Gautam Buddha Nagar DM and other officers responsible, "right down to the SHO", LiveLaw reported.
The court's reference to Orwellian Dystopia draws on George Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four, which depicts a society marked by unchecked state power, pervasive surveillance and suppression of dissent. The High Court used the phrase to warn against arbitrary exercise of governmental power and erosion of civil liberties.
'NO EVIDENCE OF VIOLENCE'
Chaudhary, a Delhi University history graduate and activist, was arrested in cases arising from a workers' protest in Noida in April this year. The protest sought higher wages and humane working hours. The Uttar Pradesh Police later invoked the NSA against her and activist-journalist Satyam Verma, alleging a conspiracy to foment violence during the agitation, LiveLaw reported.
The High Court, however, found no material showing that Chaudhary had incited violence.
While examining WhatsApp conversations and videos cited by the state government, the bench asked it to identify evidence showing that she had called for rioting, arson or destruction of property. The state could not point to "a single message" or video clip showing such incitement, the order said.
The court noted that the videos showed people gathering to demand higher wages and humane working hours, without showing them to be armed or engaged in violence.
The bench said NSA detention is an exception and cannot be used as a substitute for ordinary criminal law. It found the grounds of detention "repetitive, speculative and are only opinion-based", stressing that extraordinary powers resulting in incarceration cannot be exercised on the basis of "surmises, biases, conjectures and opinions".
COURT FLAGS ARREST DISCREPANCIES
The court also found discrepancies in the account of Chaudhary's arrest. She was taken into custody around 5:30 pm on April 11 at Botanical Garden Metro Station, while the state government claimed she was arrested on April 12, LiveLaw reported.
The state government relied on a notice relating to a bond for good behaviour. However, the notice carried a General Diary entry number generated at 10:20 am on April 12.
The bench observed that if the notice had been prepared before the arrest, it could not have contained a subsequently generated GD number. It concluded that the notice appeared to have been prepared after the arrest and described the procedure as "ex post facto" and "nothing more than a sham".
'LOYALTY IS TOWARDS CONSTITUTION'
The court was particularly critical of Gautam Buddha Nagar DM Roopam's decision to invoke the NSA, saying Chaudhary had no previous criminal record and that the material did not show she had incited violence. "The conduct of the District Magistrate of Gautam Buddha Nagar who passed the impugned order, is worthy of derision," the court said.
It further observed that the District Magistrate "desired to set an example" out of Chaudhary and deter others from exercising their right to freedom of speech and expression in public spaces in support of labourers.
The bench stressed that officials' "loyalty is towards the Constitution and not the political executive" and said government officers are servants of the people, who are "the masters in a democracy".
It warned that officials acting contrary to their oath could be viewed as an "oppressive vestige of the British Empire", creating an environment of civil unrest. "It shan't be long before the errant in the bureaucracy reduce the State of Uttar Pradesh to an Orwellian Dystopia," the court observed.
The High Court also upheld the right to peaceful protest, saying freedom of speech and expression extends to people gathering in public spaces and agitating for their rights.
"Preventing people from gathering in public spaces or agitating for their rights on the grounds of assumed breach of peace, would be throwing the baby out of the bath water," it said.
The court directed that its displeasure against the District Magistrate and police officers involved in preparing the NSA dossier be recorded in their service records.
Chaudhary, however, continues to remain in judicial custody in the underlying criminal cases, as her bail applications have been rejected, LiveLaw reported.

headline: New Delhi: The number of voters have shrunk by 6.51 per cent or 2.24 lakh in Manipur, Sikkim and Mizoram where final electoral rolls have been published after the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Interestingly, Sikkim is the only state ...
full_text: New Delhi: The number of voters have shrunk by 6.51 per cent or 2.24 lakh in Manipur, Sikkim and Mizoram where final electoral rolls have been published after the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Interestingly, Sikkim is the only state where the number of voters have shrunk below the draft list prepared during the cleaning up of voter lists.According to the electoral rolls, Manipur saw the highest deletions of 1,32,456 voters from the pre-SIR list while Sikkim saw 52,551 and Mizoram 39,199. The voter lists of Manipur and Sikkim were published on Sunday while the Mizoram list came out on Monday..Telangana SIR | Hyderabad voters face long waits, uncertainty at hearings.The Manipur list has declined by 6.32 per cent -- from 20,93,076 as in May this year before kickstarting SIR to 19,60,620 now. A draft list prepared during the exercise had initially brought the number of voters down to 19,34,399. During the claims and objections period, 30,650 more names were deleted but another 56,871 were added, leading to a net deletion of 1,32,456 in the final count.The voter list now has 9,53,350 men and 10,06,962 women besides 308 third-gender electors. The gender ratio is pegged at 1,056.The Mizoram list shows a decrease of 4.47 per cent or 39,199 from 8,75,068 to 8,35,869. The final voter count is also an increase from the draft list's figure of 8,28,906. Apart from those deleted during the enumeration phase, another 32,280 were removed during claims and objections period while adding another 39,243. Mizoram also had more women voters at 4,32,689 as against 4,03,179 men and one transgender voter.While the state's gender ratio of voters was 1073, Aizawl North-III seat recorded a high of 1,221 women for every 1,000 voters while it was lowest in West Tuipi seat where there were only 848 women voters for every 1,000 male voters.Sikkim has seen the highest contraction among the three north-eastern states -- 11.15 per cent or 52,551 down from 4,71,018 to 4,18,467. The final voter count is also less than what was in the draft list (4,33,294), as against the increase witnessed in the other two states.It also differed from the other two states in gender ratio -- 969 female voters for 1,000 male -- with men outnumbering women. The number of male voters was 2,12,534 while women were 2,05,931. There are two third gender voters also. headline: India, China hold first high-level military flag meeting in Arunachal sector
full_text:
India, China hold first high-level military flag meeting in Arunachal sector
NEW DELHI: India and China have held their first Senior Highest Military Commander-Level Flag Meeting in the Arunachal Pradesh sector, with talks taking place on both sides of the frontier earlier this week.The meeting followed understandings reached during the Special Representatives dialogue between National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval and Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi. The talks are part of efforts by the two countries to maintain peace along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and gradually improve bilateral ties.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the meeting was held at Wacha on the Indian side on September 6 and at Damai on the Chinese side on September 7.
New military mechanism along eastern frontier
Jaiswal said the meeting followed agreements reached during the Special Representatives talks in August 2025 and August 2026, along with subsequent discussions under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination."Pursuant to the understandings reached between the Special Representatives of India and China in August 2025 and August 2026, and subsequent discussions at the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination meetings held in Beijing and New Delhi in May and August 2026 respectively, the first Senior Highest Military Commander-Level Flag Meeting was held at Wacha on the Indian side in Arunachal Pradesh on September 6 and Damai on the Chinese side on September 7," Jaiswal said at his weekly media briefing.
"A similar mechanism also exists in the Western Sector," he said.The talks took place amid reports of aggressive military posturing by Chinese troops along the LAC in the Upper Subansiri region of Arunachal Pradesh.Jaiswal also said that India-China relations are gradually moving in a "positive direction".
Border peace remains key to improving ties
Doval and Wang, who are the designated Special Representatives for the India-China boundary talks, held their latest dialogue in Beijing last month.During the meeting, the two sides discussed the delimitation of the boundary, trans-boundary cooperation and the need to maintain peace along the LAC.The Indian side stressed that peace and tranquillity along the border are important for the continued development of bilateral relations.
The Special Representatives mechanism was established in 2003 to address the India-China boundary dispute, which covers a 3,488-km frontier.
Military engagement ahead of Xi visit
India and China have taken several steps in recent months to rebuild relations that deteriorated sharply after the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020. The latest military engagement comes days before Chinese president Xi Jinping is expected to visit India for the BRICS summit. Xi is likely to arrive in New Delhi on Saturday.

headline: The Allahabad High Court has come down heavily on Gautam Buddha Nagar District Magistrate Medha Roopam, who had issued the order to detain a 25-year-old Delhi University law student under the National Security Act (NSA) over a workers’ protest in Noi...
full_text:
The Allahabad High Court has come down heavily on Gautam Buddha Nagar District Magistrate Medha Roopam, who had issued the order to detain a 25-year-old Delhi University law student under the National Security Act (NSA) over a workers’ protest in Noida in April this year. In a detailed order released on Monday (September 7, 2026), the court observed that Ms. Roopam “desired to make an example” out of the petitioner.
A Bench of Justices Atul Sreedharan and Achal Sachdev had on September 2 quashed the NSA detention of Akriti Chaudhary, who had spent nearly five months in custody.
The Bench had allowed Ms. Chaudhary’s habeas corpus petition and ordered her immediate release, unless she was required in another case. The court flagged discrepancies in the arrest notice and termed the State’s version a “concocted story”.
Ms. Chaudhary was among several activists arrested in connection with the protest held between April 10 and 18, during which industrial and contractual workers demanded a hike in salary and parity with wages paid in neighbouring Haryana. The protest had turned violent on April 13 and roads were blocked.
The Uttar Pradesh police invoked the NSA against Ms. Chaudhary a month later, alleging that she had instigated protesters to indulge in stone-pelting and arson. During a press conference, the police claimed to have “strong electronic and videographic evidence” against her.
In her petition, Ms. Chaudhary argued that she was already in custody before the violence broke out on April 13. She contended that there was no factual basis for her detention and that the process leading to her preventive detention was procedurally flawed.
‘Guilty of violating oath’
Pulling up the District Magistrate, the Bench noted, “In this case, the conduct of the District Magistrate, Gautam Buddha Nagar, who passed the impugned order, is worthy of derision”
“In a case where the police report against the petitioner had only allegations without any credible material against her, the District Magistrate was expected to be vigilant and examine the record threadbare to determine if there was any material in support of the allegations and, even thereafter, assess whether the oppressive provisions of the NSA were warranted against the petitioner and how the general law of the land was inadequate against a female student activist without any previous criminal record,” order read.
The court observed that the District Magistrate “desired to set an example” out of the petitioner and deter others from exercising their right to freedom of speech and expression in public spaces in support of workers.
It added that Ms. Roopam is “guilty of violating her oath of allegiance, making this a fit case for the imposition of compensation to the petitioner”.
The court directed that Ms. Chaudhary be paid compensation of ₹5 lakh and that the amount be recovered from the salary of the District Magistrate, who passed the order of detention “without application of mind”, and “all such other officers who may have been responsible, right down to the Station House Officer” of the police station, who had prepared the initial report warranting the detention of the petitioner under the provisions of the NSA.
‘No show-cause notice’
The State had submitted in the court that Ms. Chaudhary was arrested at 10.56 a.m. on April 12 and was issued a warning notice under Section 130 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita. Justice Sreedharan questioned why no show-cause notice was issued before the warning.
The State accepted that no notice was served under Section 126. The court then called for the police’s general diary, which showed that Ms. Chaudhary was arrested before the notice was prepared. The court asked whether she had been produced before a magistrate before the arrest and asked for evidence of incitement.
The State told the court that protesters gathered at the site on April 11, but the court pointed out that, according to police records, no violence took place that day. The State also failed to submit the video footage showing Ms. Chaudhary provoking protesters to throw stones or set vehicles on fire.

headline: Congress has handed Sachin Pilot a familiar problem and a bigger opportunity.
full_text:
Congress has handed Sachin Pilot a familiar problem and a bigger opportunity.
NEW DELHI: The Congress leadership last week finally responded to 'Mayday' calls from Punjab rebels and brought in Sachin Pilot, replacing Bhupesh Baghel, to prevent a crash landing of the deeply fractured state unit ahead of the assembly elections early next year.Months of open infighting between Charanjit Singh Channi, the former chief minister leading the rebel camp, and Raja Warring, the state unit chief, not just embarrassed the Congress but also threatened to derail its 2027 campaign.Before being put in the driver's seat in Punjab, Pilot was in charge of Chhattisgarh, where Baghel remains a key Congress leader and former chief minister.
Why Congress was forced to budge
The Congress had sent former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhagel to Punjab in February this year to defuse the brewing Channi vs Warring crisis in the state unit. Ironically, as things turned out, Baghel faced resistance and became part of the crisis, with the Channi camp openly accusing him of siding with Warring. More so, since July, after the partyâs central leadership decided to ignore Channiâs claim for the top post in the state and announced that it would continue with Warring as state Congress president.
Bhupesh Baghel had asserted that it is not a 'child's play' and the decision of the high command will not change.
With several senior state leaders backing Channi, the fight turned ugly and Baghel became ineffective.
Congress meetings in the districts saw open âGo back Baghelâ chants from Channi supporters, taking the infighting to the streets and embarrassing the top leadership.So, while the ruling Aam Aadmi Party was already in full election mode with chief minister Bhagwant Mann at the centre of its campaign, the Congress was still struggling to get its senior leadership to sit across the table.Not just the AAP, even the BJP and the Akalis had their house in order and were planning their electoral moves on the ground. With the party's 2027 campaign failing to take off under Baghel, the Congress was forced to budge and turn to Pilot.
Why Sachin Pilot
The Congress decision to send Pilot to Punjab, while ironic, may still be the best bet for the leadership. Sachin Pilot, during his years in the Congress, has seen enough internal wars to know how quickly a fight over one post can turn into a larger battle over leadership, political space and, of course, eventually the chief minister's chair.Throwback to Rajasthan, where he spent years at the centre of a similar leadership tussle with senior leader Ashok Gehlot. Pilot brings something the Congress needs badly right now: the experience of being at the centre of a difficult internal power struggle.
Punjab Congress working president welcomed Sachin Pilotâs appointment, saying it will help iron out differences within the state unit.
Pilot has led the Rajasthan unit, worked closely with the high command, weathered the bitter internal battle, survived the fallout and then rebuilt his position within the Congress.He was appointed Rajasthan Congress chief in 2014, after the party's abysmal performance in the 2013 assembly election. Over the next four years, he emerged as one of the key faces of the party's rebuilding effort before Congress returned to power in 2018. That victory, however, did not give him the chief minister's chair.Ashok Gehlot became chief minister, while Pilot was made deputy chief minister and continued as PCC president. While both sides got something, the arrangement never really settled the rivalry between Gehlot and Pilot.By 2020, those differences exploded into an open rebellion.Pilot left Jaipur with a group of MLAs and challenged the Gehlot government. Congress responded by removing him as deputy chief minister and state president. The Gehlot camp even accused him of working with the BJP. A truce was eventually worked out, and Pilot stayed with Congress.But he never quite returned to the position he had occupied before and has been on the sidelines ever since. He remained a prominent face in the party and was later given charge of Chhattisgarh, but his role in Rajasthan remained limited.It is interesting how, in Rajasthan, Pilot was the leader asking the Congress high command to listen to a dissatisfied camp. In Punjab, he now has to convince dissatisfied leaders to accept the high command's decisions and work together.That may be why Congress believes he is best suited for the job.
Baghel gone. Will Warring be next?
But will Pilotâs appointment end the crisis in the Punjab unit?Channi's supporters had demanded Warring be removed as Punjab Congress chief, and the Jalandhar MP be declared Congressâs chief ministerial face for the 2027 assembly polls. The Congress has not accepted either of the two demands. So, while Channi has not made any significant gains, Warring has been left wondering if he will be the next to be axed.Warring was picked up to lead and rebuild the Punjab unit after the Congress was decimated in the 2022 assembly polls. Channi, who was the chief minister then, led the Congress to its worst-ever performance in the state. The Congress not just lost its government to AAP but was also reduced to 18 seats in the 117-member assembly.The leadership tussle between the two had been brewing for quite some time. But as is the Congressâs wont, the party kept dilly-dallying on the issue for nearly 4 years. Finally, when the Congress did take a decision, it ended up opening deep faultlines.For now, both camps have welcomed his appointment. Warring said Pilot's energy and dynamism would "for sure" add to the vigour of the party ahead of the crucial polls, while Gurdaspur MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa, a close associate of Channi, said Pilot's experience, leadership and connect with the people would give new strength and momentum to the Congress in Punjab.Punjab Congress working president Raj Kumar Verka hopes that under Pilotâs leadership all state leaders would come together. "Pilot knows all leaders of Punjab, and they also have confidence in him," said Verka.For Pilot, this may be his first real test. If party leadership decides to keep Warring, he has to get Channi, Randhawa and other leaders to fall in line. If Warring goes, he has to make sure one problem is not replaced by the other.
Congress has a lot at stake
The Congress, which remains the main challenger for now, cannot afford this infighting because Punjab is one of the states where it still has a real chance. There is anti-incumbency against the Bhagwant Mann-led AAP government.In 2022, AAP swept 92 of the 117 assembly seats, while Congress was reduced to 18. But the 2024 Lok Sabha election brought some relief for the grand old party. The Congress won seven of Punjab's 13 seats, compared with AAP's three, showing that the party still has enough ground to be a serious challenger.AAP is perhaps no longer riding the wave that brought it to power in 2022 and is now defending its record under Bhagwant Mann. Raghav Chadha's exit has also added to the churn in the party.The BJP and the Akalis are still on the margins of the stateâs politics. But the scenario could change very fast. The BJP is going all out to broaden its organisational base and rope in leaders from other parties. There are also reports of talks between the BJP and the Akalis to revive their old alliance. The Congress needs to remember that the BJP is coming off a massive victory in West Bengal and is looking to expand its footprint in Punjab as well.
Punjab could shape Pilot's Rajasthan future
Pilot has already made it clear that he sees Punjab as a comeback opportunity for the Congress. On Monday, he said he was confident that with a strong organisation, collective effort and the energy of party workers, Congress could return to power in the state.
Pilot has the experience of being a part of successful strategising in Himachal Pradesh in the previous assembly polls and has also been a senior observer for the Kerala polls, where Congress returned to power after a decade.If Pilot can manage to bring the rival Punjab camps together and help the Congress put up a strong show in 2027, it will add to his standing within the party at a time when Rajasthan is already looking ahead to the 2028 assembly election.There has long been speculation over a bigger role for Pilot in Rajasthan. He may not have got it yet, but a successful Punjab stint could considerably strengthen his case.For a leader who has had to rebuild his own position in the party before, Punjab could well become the next big step in that comeback.

headline: NCPCR summons Meta India chief (representative image)
full_text:
NCPCR summons Meta India chief (representative image)
NEW DELHI: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has summoned Meta Indiaâs managing director and country head to appear before it on Wednesday over advertisements allegedly linked to child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) on Instagram.The commission took suo motu cognisance of a BBC Eye report and issued a notice to Meta Platforms Inc on July 3, seeking an explanation and documents. Meta replied a week later, following which the NCPCR instituted a formal inquiry to establish the facts.Commission officials remained tight-lipped about Metaâs response. However, officials said the inquiry would examine Meta Indiaâs role in the appearance of the advertisements, how they cleared Instagramâs systems and why the situation arose.The scrutiny would consider the stringent provisions relating to such material under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, they added.Last week, the National Human Rights Commission issued notices to the ministry of electronics and information technology and ministry of information and broadcasting as part of its scrutiny of the alleged circulation of CSAM on Instagram. The Commission has given the ministries two weeks to give their response.
NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo, whose bench issued the notices on September 2, said the inquiry was no longer limited to identifying who uploaded the objectionable content. âIt also examines the extent to which the platformâs own editorial and publishing systems participate in the generation, selection, circulation, amplification or monetisation of content,â he said.Meta had earlier said it had zero tolerance for child exploitation and had removed violating advertisements and accounts. It also said its detection systems had led to the removal of more than 1.6 lakh suspicious accounts in India during the preceding six months. The company denied knowingly targeting such advertisements at people displaying an inappropriate interest in children.Queries sent to Meta on NCPCR summoning its top brass did not elicit a response.

headline: NEW DELHI: With improvement in LPG supplies and a fall in refill backlogs, govt Monday reduced the minimum time gap for booking LPG refills in rural areas to 25 days from 45 days, bringing it on a par with the interval for urban consumers, reports At...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: With improvement in LPG supplies and a fall in refill backlogs, govt Monday reduced the minimum time gap for booking LPG refills in rural areas to 25 days from 45 days, bringing it on a par with the interval for urban consumers, reports Atul Mathur.
Union minister of state for petroleum and natural gas Suresh Gopi said the restriction had been imposed amid pressure on LPG supplies following the outbreak of the conflict in West Asia, with the booking interval set at 25 days in urban areas and 45 days in rural areas.
"However, in view of the current LPG supply situation improving and the significant reduction in refill backlog, Centre has relaxed this restriction. Now, all domestic LPG consumers, regardless of urban or rural, can book refills at an interval of 25 days," Gopi said. Petroleum ministry has issued an order to oil marketing companies IOC, BPCL and HPCL, asking them to implement this with immediate effect.

headline: Justice Sanjay Kumar Agrawal, transferred from Chhattisgarh, was sworn in as the 44th Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court at a ceremony held at Lok Bhavan here on Monday (September 7, 2026). Governor Haribhau Bagade administered the oath of off...
full_text:
Justice Sanjay Kumar Agrawal, transferred from Chhattisgarh, was sworn in as the 44th Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court at a ceremony held at Lok Bhavan here on Monday (September 7, 2026). Governor Haribhau Bagade administered the oath of office in the presence of Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma, his Cabinet colleagues, judges and administrative officials.
The Union government notified Justice Agrawal’s elevation as the Chief Justice and appointment in Rajasthan following a recommendation by the Supreme Court Collegium. He was first appointed as an additional judge of the Chhattisgarh High Court in September 2013 and became a permanent judge in March 2016.
Justice Agrawal left for Jodhpur immediately after the swearing-in ceremony for joining the judicial work at the High Court’s principal seat. His appointment is considered significant for streamlining the judicial system in the State and ensuring speedy disposal of the pending cases.
Justice Agrawal’s appointment in Rajasthan comes amid a controversy surrounding Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma, who had been serving as the High Court’s Acting Chief Justice since September 2025. A Supreme Court judge, Justice Sandeep Mehta, recently wrote a series of letters to the Chief Justice of India making complaints about Justice Sharma’s conduct and seeking his transfer.
Justice Mehta alleged “misuse of powers, favouritism, nepotism, and administrative lapses” by Justice Sharma in his letters. The issue also triggered protests by lawyers in Jodhpur as well as at the High Court’s Bench in Jaipur. The protesting lawyers demanded that Justice Sharma be divested of his charge and a permanent Chief Justice be appointed in the State.
Justice Sharma, who is due to retire on September 26, has rejected the allegations levelled against him as baseless and called upon all concerned to “remain patient” until the CJI takes a decision. In a statement released last week, Justice Sharma said he had placed his version with the supporting evidence before the CJI.

headline: YouTuber Ajit Bharti moves Delhi HC against trial court order denying anticipatory bail
full_text:
YouTuber Ajit Bharti moves Delhi HC against trial court order denying anticipatory bail
Ajit Bharti has challenged the September 7 order of a Delhi trial court which dismissed his anticipatory bail application.
Social media influencer and YouTuber Ajit Bharti has approached the Delhi High Court seeking anticipatory bail in the SC/ST Act case registered against him over his comments concerning Chandrashekhar Azad Ravan, after a trial court denied him relief earlier this month.
Bharti has challenged the September 7 order of a Delhi trial court which dismissed his anticipatory bail application.
The trial court had declined Bharti’s plea after holding that the material placed on record prima facie disclosed the ingredients of an offence under Section 3(1)(r) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
Also Read | Delhi Court dismisses YouTuber Ajeet Bharti’s anticipatory bail plea in caste remarks case
It had further held that the bar under Section 18 of the SC/ST Act applied and, consequently, precluded the grant of anticipatory bail.
“For the foregoing reasons, this Court finds that the ingredients of an offence under Section 3(1)(r) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 are prima facie disclosed on the material on record,” the trial court had observed while dismissing the plea.
Additional Sessions Judge Saurabh Partap Singh Laler of Patiala House Courts had passed the order on September 7 in connection with an FIR registered at North Avenue police station.
Also Read | Quota within quota, more EWS benefits: YouTuber Ajeet Bharti's key demands at 'Reservation Hatao' protest
The case concerns statements allegedly made by Bharti during a programme aired on social media. The complainant had alleged that certain remarks made during the programme were casteist and derogatory towards members of the Scheduled Caste community.
Bharti had sought protection from arrest, contending that the allegations did not make out an offence under the SC/ST Act. It was argued on his behalf that the remarks had to be considered in their overall context and that custodial interrogation was not required as the material forming the basis of the case was already available in the public domain.
The State and the complainant had opposed his anticipatory bail application.
After examining the FIR, transcript and other material placed before it, the trial court concluded that a prima facie case under Section 3(1)(r) of the SC/ST Act was made out and dismissed the application.
The court had, however, clarified that its observations were confined to the disposal of the anticipatory bail plea and should not be construed as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case.
Also Read | Court denies anticipatory bail to duo in ₹18.35-cr fraud
It had also made clear that the trial court dealing with the matter would not be influenced by any observations made in the bail order and that Bharti would remain free to seek appropriate remedies available under law if circumstances changed.

headline: Nitin Gadkari ‘ashamed’ of Mumbai-Goa Highway expansion delays, says won't join inauguration
full_text:
Nitin Gadkari ‘ashamed’ of Mumbai-Goa Highway expansion delays, says won't join inauguration
The minister said the highway is 93-94% complete and plans to travel from Mumbai to Goa by road in October to assess the remaining work.
At a function to open a 5.15km long elevated road that would bypass a congested stretch north of Panaji, Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari said he was “ashamed” of the delays around the expansion of the Mumbai-Goa Highway and had declared that he did not want to attend its inauguration when the project is finally completed.
“The Mumbai-Goa Highway has been hopelessly delayed, and the contractors have failed. From my point of view, what has happened is very unfortunate. My department has as many as seven world records, but now I wish my department will have the record for blacklisting and debarring the single largest number of contractors and suspension of officials in a single year,” Gadkari said at an event to inaugurate the 6-lane Porvorim flyover.
“Now I’ve given up waiting for an auspicious time (to have it inaugurated). I’ve decided that I will not go for the inauguration of the Mumbai-Goa highway because I’m ashamed at the delays,” he said.
Also read: NHAI failed to address highway safety concerns, alleges Keralam minister after 8 students killed
Minister says highway completion is near
Gadkari, however, held out hope that the project completion was round the corner.
“Yesterday I had a meeting and was told the highway was 93-94% complete… and in October, I’ll get off at the Mumbai airport and come to Goa by car to see the status of the completion,” he said.
The project to convert the old two-lane Mumbai-Goa highway into a four-lane road was launched in 2011, with the objective of reducing the travel time from nearly 12 hours to six hours.
But work on several crucial stretches of the highway has stalled for a prolonged duration. Also, there have been concerns about construction quality on social media after images of damage on some stretches.
The elevated corridor that Gadkari opened on Wednesday runs through the Porvorim suburb north of the state capital and had been on the drawing board for more than seven years. Work on the ground started in January 2024.
Also read: Rain washes away soil beneath Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway’s retaining wall in Unnao
New corridor aims to ease north Goa traffic
The flyover, built at an estimated cost of ₹364.68 crore by RRSM Infra Private Limited, is expected to ease traffic flow and reduce bottlenecks along routes connecting the state capital with popular beaches such as Calangute and Anjuna, as well as towards the newly constructed Mopa Airport.
The new flyover will serve as a crucial link from Panjim to the newly constructed Mopa airport, and will be part of the Mumbai-Goa highway and the larger Mumbai to Kanyakumari Highway,

headline: Mayawati sets 'sanyas' condition to restore nephew Akash Anand's role in BSP
full_text:
Mayawati sets 'sanyas' condition to restore nephew Akash Anand's role in BSP
Mayawati issued an ultimatum to former Rajya Sabha MP Ashok Siddharth, linking the political future of Akash Anand to Siddharth's exit from politics.
Ahead of the crucial 2027 state assembly elections, Uttar Pradesh's political battleground is growing tense as Bahujan Samaj Party's internal friction is playing out before the public's eyes. Days after removing her nephew Akash Anand from his organisational post, party supremo Mayawati on Wednesday set a 'sanyas' condition for his responsibilities to be restored.
In a post on X, Mayawati issued an ultimatum to former Rajya Sabha MP Ashok Siddharth, directly linking the political future of Akash Anand to Siddharth's exit from politics.
The former UP chief minister said that Akash Anand could return to an active role in BSP only if his father-in-law, Ashok Siddharth, gives up his political ambitions and retires.
Also Read | After removing nephew Akash Anand, Mayawati appoints his brother Ishan to key BSP post
‘Prioritised his personal and familial interests…’
Mayawati accused Siddharth of prioritising his personal and family ambitions over the party's mission.
"And against those who try even slightly to create obstacles in this path, disciplinary actions, etc., are also being taken, a prominent example of which is Shri Ashok Siddharth, who was once a Rajya Sabha MP of the BSP," she wrote in the post.
"The party gave him not just one but several opportunities to mend his ways, but he prioritised his personal and familial interests and ambitions over the BSP's mission, the consequences of which he himself, along with his son-in-law Shri Akash Anand, has had to bear," the BSP chief added.
Also Read | Akash Anand’s roller-coaster ride continues, Mayawati removes him from key BSP post again
Mayawati stated that Siddharth had "never truly cared" about Anand or the BSP movement because of his personal interests.
Furthermore, she added that Siddharth has an opportunity to put aside his political ambitions and retire completely from politics in the interest of the BSP, the movement, his family, and his son-in-law.
“Aise mein BSP party wa movement ke hit ke saath-saath khud unke parivaar evam apne daamaad Shri Akash Anand ke bhavishya ko dhyan mein rakhkar Shri Ashok Siddharth ke paas abhi bhi mauka hai ki ve apni raajneetik mahatvaakaanksha ko tyaag kar wa niji swarth aadi se upar uthkar raajneeti se poori tarah se sanyaas le lein. (In such a situation, keeping in mind the interests of the BSP Party and Movement, as well as his own family and the future of his son-in-law Shri Akash Anand, Shri Ashok Siddharth still has the opportunity to renounce his political ambitions, rise above personal interests, etc., and completely retire from politics.),” she stated in the post.
"Only then will Shri Akash Anand be able to work freely in the party, and only then will the party sympathetically consider restoring his responsibilities so that he can play an active role in the party—this is the general consensus in the party," she said.
Also Read | BSP to go solo in Punjab, U’khand, UP, says Mayawati
UP, Punjab, Uttarakhand elections
In the post, she noted that the assembly elections in the three states are approaching and described them as particularly important for the BSP and the Bahujan movement.
She also called on party workers, office-bearers, supporters and well-wishers to work with full dedication.
Seeking support from people across communities, she said that the BSP was facing challenges from opposition parties and "casteist elements".
Also Read | Mayawati removes nephew from key BSP post, believes he ‘requires further maturity’
Akash Anand and the BSP
Mayawati's latest condition for Anand's return comes just days after she removed him from the post of BSP national coordinator during a meeting of party office-bearers.
The organisational structure of the BSP is divided into three sectors: two sectors comprise other states, while the third consists of UP and Uttarakhand, as HT reported earlier.
