headline: Kuki police constable suspended in Manipur over abduction of 6 Nagas who were later murdered
full_text:
Kuki police constable suspended in Manipur over abduction of 6 Nagas who were later murdered
The decision follows rising tensions between Naga and Kuki communities, with Naga politicians demanding accountability for the violence.
Manipur police have ordered a departmental enquiry and suspended a serving Kuki police constable for his alleged role in abduction of the six Naga men who were later murdered, people aware of the matter confirmed to HT.
HT has seen the copy of the constable’s suspension order dated September 8 issued by the SP of the Bishnupur district police.
“He was with Bishnupur police in the valley but was transferred (transferred) to Kangpokpi hill district in the hills due to the conflict. He has been suspended and a DE has been ordered,”an officer who asked not to be named confirmed.
HT had on July 6 reported about police probing the role of a serving Kuki constable in the case.
Also Read: Manipur: Kuki-Zo launch counter-economic blockade, ask govt to ensure essentials
Police have taken action against the constable amid escalating differences between Naga and Kuki politicians in the state. The Naga MLAs, including deputy chief minister Losii Dikho who is a Naga, have demanded action in the case and accused another deputy CM Nemcha Kipgen(she is a Kuki) of being involved in the violence. The Naga MLAs have also refused to share the assembly room with Kipgen and abstained from assembly proceedings.
The Naga families have also refused to bury the mutilated bodies of the six men till date.
The bodies of the six Naga men were recovered about a month after they were abducted along with their families by Kuki militant groups during the height of the Naga-Kuki clashes in Manipur on May 13.
The abductions took place on the afternoon of May 13, 2026, after three Kuki church leaders were killed in an ambush in Kangpokpi, allegedly by Naga groups, triggering a fresh escalation in tensions. Armed groups from both communities subsequently abducted members of the rival community in retaliatory incidents.
Also Read | Kuki group ends counter-inter-district economic blockade, highway shutdown
Women and children from both sides were released on May 15 following a hostage exchange facilitated by church leaders and government authorities. However, 14 Kuki-Zo men and six Naga men remained in captivity.
The 14 Kuki-Zo men were later released by Naga groups following the intervention of church leaders, security forces, the army and the Intelligence Bureau (IB). The six Naga men did not return. Although Kuki-Zo groups denied holding them hostage, their mutilated bodies were recovered from forests in Kangpokpi district on June 10. The National Investigation Agency (NIA) is investigating the case.

headline: Delhi decorated with posters and lighting ahead of the BRICS Summit 2026
full_text:
Delhi decorated with posters and lighting ahead of the BRICS Summit 2026
NEW DELHI: Delhi has tightened security across the national capital ahead of the 18th Brics Summit, with nearly 4,800 traffic police personnel set to manage VVIP movement and more than 35 major roads identified for traffic restrictions and diversions.The summit will be held at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi from September 11 to 13, with foreign leaders and other dignitaries expected to attend.According to ANI, Delhi Police and other security agencies have entered the final phase of preparations, with thousands of personnel deployed and heightened surveillance along routes designated for VVIP movement.
Around 22 diversion points will be used to regulate traffic during the movement of foreign delegations and VVIP convoys. Nearly 4,800 traffic police personnel will be deployed to ensure the safe and uninterrupted movement of the dignitaries.Security has also been stepped up at around 10 major hotels where foreign delegates are expected to stay, along with 12 other important locations across the capital.
India is hosting the 18th BRICS Summit as the grouping's chair for 2026. The main leaders' summit will be held at Bharat Mandapam on September 12 and 13, while the BRICS Business Forum is scheduled for September 11.
India's Brics chairship is being guided by the theme âBuilding for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainabilityâ. The summit is expected to focus on strengthening cooperation among member and partner countries, as well as global and regional issues.India has held more than 350 BRICS meetings and high-level engagements across over 25 cities during its 2026 chairship.The 2026 summit also marks 20 years of BRICS. The grouping has expanded beyond its original five members and now has 11 members.India assumed the Brics chairship on January 1, 2026, marking its fourth time leading the bloc after 2012, 2016 and 2021.

headline: CM Vijay's TVK alliance named ‘Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance’
full_text:
CM Vijay's TVK alliance named ‘Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance’
The name was announced at an alliance meeting chaired by CM Vijay at TVK's headquarters in Tamil Nadu.
Tamil Nadu’s new ruling party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam, and its political partners on Wednesday named their coalition the "Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance" (SSJVA), solidifying a post-election bloc following a high-level coordination meeting near Chennai.
The new alliance was formed under the leadership of TVK president and chief minister C Joseph Vijay, Tamil Nadu Congress committee president B Manickam Tagore announced after the meeting. Tagore added that the alliance’s name spoke volumes about the coalition's ideals and agenda, and that it would jointly fight the bypolls to three assembly seats in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry.
Also read: ‘Tax money wasted for Vijay's luxury’: BJP questions ₹6.17 crore allocation for shifting CM's office
"We will henceforth work together. We are on a strong foundation,” he said, adding that the combine would announce its candidates for the October 6 bypolls to three seats in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry in a day or two.
State health minister KG Arunraj echoed the sentiment, saying that the name was chosen unanimously.
"This is not just a name; it is a statement we are making today…. A new alliance is born," he said after the meeting attended by leaders of key alliance partners, including Congress, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK), Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (MDMK) and Indian Union Muslim League (IUML).
Also read: CM Vijay clarifies row over his ‘body language’ in Tamil Nadu Assembly: ‘Not in any way intentional’
The Communist Party of India (CPI) and Communist Party of India (Marxist), which offer 'outside' support to the TVK government, have clarified that they will not be part of the TVK-led alliance.
Members of the alliance
The alliance was formed after the TVK secured 108 seats in the April 23 Tamil Nadu elections and formed a post-poll alliance with the Congress, Indian Union Muslim League, and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK).
The Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (MDMK), which was also a member of the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam-led Secular Progressive Alliance, also became part of the state’s ruling coalition on Wednesday. The VCK and IUML have one minister each in the council of ministers, while the Congress has two ministers.
Also read: An extra 'F', a big row: EC now says will visit Bharat Ratna CNR Rao's house over SIR notice
Among those present at Wednesday’s meetings were senior TVK leaders N Anand, KG Arunraj, Aadhav Arjuna, C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar. Tamil Nadu Congress legislative party leader Tharahai Cuthbert, party MP Praveen Chakravarthy, Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) president Khader Mohideen, MDMK chief and MP Vaiko were also in the meeting.
Alliance meeting amid rift buzz
The key alliance meeting comes days after Congress leaders from Tamil Nadu threatened to resign from the state cabinet if Vijay's TVK did not accept Rahul Gandhi as the next prime ministerial candidate.
Tamil Nadu tourism minister S Rajesh Kumar had stated that both Congress ministers will resign if TVK fails to back Gandhi in the 2029 general elections.
Kumar added that the party would not compromise on its stand, asserting that Rahul Gandhi is the only candidate the Congress party would support in the Lok Sabha elections.
These remarks from the Congress come as the TVK continues to push Vijay as the next prime ministerial candidate.

headline: Vijay named his alliance with the Congress, VCK, MDMK and IUML the 'Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance'
full_text:
Vijay named his alliance with the Congress, VCK, MDMK and IUML the 'Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance'
NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister and TVK chief C Joseph Vijay on Wednesday named his alliance with the Congress, VCK, MDMK and IUML the âSecular Social Justice Victory Allianceâ as leaders of the parties met for the second time at the TVK headquarters in Chennai.TVK sources cited by news agency PTI had earlier confirmed that key alliance partners, including the Congress, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK), Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), and Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (MDMK), would participate in the meeting.
However, the CPM and CPI have decided to skip the meeting, marking their second consecutive boycott of formal alliance talks since July 1.Explaining the decision, CPM state secretary P Shanmugam said on Tuesday that the Left partiesâ outside support would remain strictly issue-based, with the aim of maintaining stability in the Assembly.Adding to the tensions is a growing public rift between the TVK and the Congress over the question of national leadership.Statements from TVK legislators and ministers projecting chief minister Vijay as a potential Prime Ministerial candidate for the 2029 general elections have drawn strong opposition from Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) leaders.Congress minister S Rajesh Kumar has firmly asserted that Rahul Gandhi remains the undisputed leader of the national opposition bloc. He warned that any attempt to undermine this consensus could prompt the party to reconsider its participation in the state cabinet.The TVK leadership subsequently sought to play down the controversy, maintaining that the âVijay for PMâ remarks reflected the personal views of individual lawmakers.

headline: The Ruling National Conference (NC) and its ally the Congress traded barbs on Wednesday over the NC leadership’s decision to stand for all stanzas of the national song, Vande Mataram, after it was played at the inauguration of the International Film ...
full_text:
The Ruling National Conference (NC) and its ally the Congress traded barbs on Wednesday over the NC leadership’s decision to stand for all stanzas of the national song, Vande Mataram, after it was played at the inauguration of the International Film Festival Jammu & Kashmir (IFFJK) in Srinagar on September 7.
J&K Congress chief Tariq Hameed Karra, in a post on X, questioned Chief Minister Omar Abdullah and NC president Dr. Farooq Abdullah’s decision to stand for all stanzas of the song.
“National symbols, songs and traditions occupy a special place in the heart of every Indian. Their true strength lies in their ability to bind together a nation as diverse as ours. It is therefore a matter of concern that our alliance partners chose to sing the full version of Vande Mataram, disregarding the considered evolution of the song’s place in India’s national life, not merely during the freedom movement, but through the constitutional journey of the Republic thereafter. The adopted version represented a conscious balance preserving the historic ... ,” said Mr. Karra.
Mr. Karra’s post followed a social media statement by Congress General Secretary K. C. Venugopal, who posted the video of the Srinagar ceremony in which NC leaders stood for all the stanzas.
“The full version of Vande Mataram sits uneasily with the syncretic and pluralist ethos that our freedom fighters envisioned and nurtured for India. For us, the considered judgment of Mahatma Gandhi, Pandit Nehru, Sardar Patel, Subhash Chandra Bose, Rajendra Prasad, Acharya Narendra Dev, Maulana Azad, Sarojini Naidu and J.B. Kripalani — shaped in no small part by the counsel of Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore — remains paramount,” said Mr. Venugopal.
Honour freedom fighters
In the post, the Congress leader said, “With respect and humility, we would like our allies to honour the wisdom and judgment of our freedom fighters and stand with us in singing only the version of this beautiful and historic song that they adopted. That version was chosen deliberately, to keep the song from being communalised — a threat as real today as it was then. Upholding it is how we uphold the secular, inclusive character of our Republic.”
The Congress posts on social media platforms drew a sharp reaction from NC leaders. NC legislator Tanvir Sadiq shared videos of swearing-in ceremonies involving a Congress chief minister and asked Mr. Karra to comment.
NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar said, “The NC’s official position is that it is not a votary of either the first two stanzas or six stanzas of the national song. However, it is a Constitutional obligation, and every holder of a Constitutional office has to accept it, whether it is the CM, a MP or anyone else.”
Referring to videos from the Congress-ruled states of Karnataka and Telangana, Mr. Dar said, “The chief ministers stand for all the six stanzas. However, we do not want to make this a controversy. We are not here to fight the Congress.”
Meanwhile, the Opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) also criticised the NC. “On every key issue, Rahul Gandhi took a stand, his J&K ally NC caved and rolled out the red carpet for the BJP. No condemnation on the Waqf amendment Bill. No condemnation of SIR fraud. Justifying EVM rigging concerns. Accepted Vande Mataram’s addition. INDIA bloc in elections, BJP’s silent enabler in practice,” said PDP leader and legislator Waheed-ur-Rehman Parra.

headline: A portion of an under-construction building collapsed in the Kudasan area of Gandhinagar, Gujarat, prompting an immediate rescue operation. The incident occurred around 9:30 PM when a concrete slab gave way, trapping several labourers beneath the deb...
full_text:
A portion of an under-construction building collapsed in the Kudasan area of Gandhinagar, Gujarat, prompting an immediate rescue operation. The incident occurred around 9:30 PM when a concrete slab gave way, trapping several labourers beneath the debris. Fire department personnel and emergency response teams reached the site to clear the rubble and rescue survivors. At least 12 labourers have been safely pulled out and shifted to a local hospital for medical care, while search and rescue operations continue for others feared trapped.
In an interview with India Today, former Labour Secretary Sumita Dawra shared insights on bureaucratic accountability following the Satya Niketan building collapse in Delhi. Commenting on the suspension of civic officials, Dawra stated, "Suspension may not be a punishment, but it, reflects, it indicates visible action." She stressed that suspensions must be followed by swift investigations, proper inquiries, and the fixing of culpability. Dawra noted that addressing systemic issues requires examining violations across the entire chain of command, from junior engineers to senior supervisory authorities. Emphasizing the need for institutional deterrence, she said, "There should be exemplary punishment so that it's a warning for the system." She also highlighted the importance of leveraging modern technology, such as GIS mapping and municipal tax data, to monitor structural deviations and flag unauthorized constructions early.
In an interview with Maria Shakil on India Today, former Intelligence Bureau Special Director Yashovardhan Azad addressed systemic administrative failures and accountability lapses in Delhi's municipal governance following urban tragedies. Azad asserted that municipal commissioners and senior bureaucrats must be directly held accountable for rampant illegal constructions and safety oversights. Emphasizing top-level responsibility, he stated that "the buck should stop right at the top" and suggested issuing charge sheets to the municipal commissioner and housing development secretaries rather than only suspending junior personnel. He highlighted how councillors and local politicians exert pressure on junior engineers, protecting illegal establishments and avoiding structural oversight. Azad argued that IAS officers frequently escape disciplinary measures due to undefined culpability and close alignments with ministers. Calling the situation an absolute collusion between the political class and bureaucracy, he demanded systemic reforms to restore civic safety and administrative accountability across the capital.
In an interview, Dr. Kiran Bedi discussed institutional accountability and administrative responsibility following observations by the Delhi High Court regarding the Municipal Corporation of Delhi. Addressing questions on official negligence, postings, and transfers, Bedi emphasized that accountability rests with the leadership, stating, 'The buck stops with him, at him.' She noted that the municipal commissioner serves as the administrative head responsible for personnel decisions, alongside ministers handling urban development. Bedi also stated that bureaucratic guidelines are established, remarking, 'The rulebook is very clear,' and explained that disciplinary action for administrative lapses depends on how senior supervisory authorities evaluate delinquency.
Three separate incidents within two months have sparked concern among the Christian community in West Bengal. On 5 July, an under-construction church was vandalised in Subashgram, leading to the arrest of six suspects who were later granted bail. On 14 August, tension erupted in Raibati village in East Burdwan over the removal of a body from an allegedly disputed cemetery. On 26 August, a prayer gathering at a residence in Mahishadal was disrupted over allegations of religious conversion. While church bodies have condemned the incidents and rejected forced conversions, Hindu outfits have called for strict vigilance against missionary activities. The Christian community has urged the state government to safeguard their rights.

headline: Congress sees caste census fire at home as Siddaramaiah demands 75% quota in Karnataka
full_text:
Congress sees caste census fire at home as Siddaramaiah demands 75% quota in Karnataka
Former Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah has demanded 75% reservation for socially disadvantaged communities and urged the DK Shivakumar-led government to implement the findings of the state's caste survey. His push comes even as the Congress seeks to corner the BJP-led Centre over the caste enumeration in Census 2027.
The Congress is trying its best to use the issue of caste enumeration in Census 2027 to corner the BJP-led Centre. However, it might face a Catch 22 situation with its senior leader and former chief minister Siddaramaiah piling pressure on the Congress government in Karnataka to implement the findings of the caste survey in the state. Talking about caste survey is one thing, but confronting the political consequences of the caste arithmetic is entirely different. It could create dissonance, threatening the state government itself.
At the national level, the Congress has made caste enumeration one of its biggest political weapons against the BJP, arguing that India needs to know the numerical strength of its communities before questions of representation, reservation and distribution of resources can be settled. The party is taking that argument into the 2027 Census, which will enumerate castes beyond Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes nationally for the first time since Independence.
But in Karnataka, where the Congress has been in power since 2023, the party is facing an awkward question — why did it not provide the details of a caste survey that it already has in the state?
Former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has now turned that question into a political challenge to his own party's government. The 79-year-old leader is demanding that the Karnataka caste survey be implemented and has called for reservations to be raised to 75% for Dalits, backward communities and minorities.
Siddaramaiah had reluctantly handed over the CM's chair to DK Shivakumar in May.
The intervention of Siddaramaiah, who is hailed as the face of AHINDA, a social coalition of backward classes, minorities, and Dalits, puts the Congress in an awkward position. Siddaramaiah is a Kuruba, which is part of his AHINDA social coalition.
Shivakumar is a Vokkaliga, which is among the dominant castes.
The Congress can demand caste numbers from the BJP at the national level, but acting on those numbers in Karnataka could disturb the very social and political equations that keep its state government together.
The issue, therefore, is no longer simply about a caste census. It is about whether the Congress is prepared to confront the political consequences of the caste arithmetic it has spent years trying to corner BJP at the national level.
NATIONAL CASTE PUSH OF CONGRESS MEETS A PROBLEM IN KARNATAKA
The timing of Siddaramaiah's push could hardly have been more politically significant. The Congress has accused the Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led central government of failing to adequately capture OBC representation in the Census 2027 exercise and has described the alleged omission of the OBC category from the Census questionnaire as a "deep conspiracy" to prevent the actual population of OBCs from entering official records.
Its broader argument is that without reliable caste numbers, claims of social justice and proportional representation remain built on estimates rather than evidence.
Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, and the Congress have increasingly placed this argument at the centre of their politics, linking caste enumeration with representation in institutions, access to resources and the distribution of political power.
But Karnataka holds an inconvenient mirror to the Congress high command. The state does not have to wait for Census 2027 to begin implementation in Karnataka. It has already conducted a caste survey, and a fresh report has been ready since November 2025.
Yet the report remains politically difficult to operationalise. That is where Siddaramaiah's intervention becomes important.
If caste data is necessary for social justice, as the Congress argues nationally, then Karnataka provides the party with an opportunity to demonstrate what that principle means in practice.
But if the numbers lead to demands for a redistribution of reservation and representation, the political consequences could be far more complicated. And Siddaramaiah's fresh demand of 75% reservation is now confronting this very point.
SIDDARAMAIAH'S 75% RESERVATION FORMULA FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE
Speaking at the Karnataka State Backward Castes Federation's Silver Jubilee celebration on Sunday (September 6) in Bengaluru, Siddaramaiah called for implementation of the caste survey and demanded that reservations for Dalits, backward communities and minorities be increased to 75%.
"If all of you are to get social justice, there must be at least 75% reservation," he said, arguing that reservations should correspond to the population of different communities.
His argument goes beyond government employment and educational institutions. Siddaramaiah has also argued that representation in the Lok Sabha and state Legislative Assemblies should reflect caste and population if political equality is to be achieved.
The former Karnataka CM's proposition is one that the Congress itself has increasingly embraced nationally. The Congress has been demanding that representation should not be determined in the absence of data about who actually makes up India's population. But the moment that principle moves from political rhetoric to government policy, the complications begin for the Grand Old Party.
THE CASTE CENSUS DILEMMA FOR CONGRESS IN KARNATAKA
Karnataka's caste survey has already had a long and politically complicated journey. The first survey was ordered during Siddaramaiah's earlier tenure as chief minister. Conducted in 2015 under the leadership of H Kantharaj, it was completed by 2017 but never became politically actionable.
The report was never tabled due to objections from influential communities of the state — Lingayats and Vokkaligas.
Successive governments, including JD(S)-Congress and BJP administrations, largely avoided turning it into a major policy instrument. That reluctance by these parties was clear. Caste data does not merely describe society. Once published, it can become the basis for demands over reservation, representation, welfare benefits and political power.
When Siddaramaiah returned as CM in 2023, the caste census issue returned to the spotlight. His government moved towards accepting the Backward Classes Commission's report in 2025. But rather than settling the row, it reopened the larger question over the reliability and age of the data.
Siddaramaiah subsequently ordered a fresh caste survey. The new exercise was also projected as a way of generating a more current database and building wider political consensus.
The new report has been ready since November 2025 that the Congress government has not turned the survey into the political breakthrough that its national caste-justice campaign might suggest. And that gap is precisely what Siddaramaiah is now exploiting.
HOW SIDDARAMAIAH IS MAKING DK SHIVAKUMAR GOVT UNCOMFORTABLE
Siddaramaiah might no longer occupy the CM's chair, he has also announced his retirement from electoral politics. But his intervention demonstrates that leaving office does not necessarily mean leaving the political agenda behind.
By returning to caste enumeration and proportional reservation, he has effectively put the Congress government led by incumbent CM DK Shivakumar under pressure to act on an issue closely associated with his own political identity.
For DKS, this is an uncomfortable inheritance. The Congress cannot easily dismiss the demand. Doing so could make the party vulnerable to the charge that its commitment to caste justice is stronger when it is directed at the BJP than when it requires difficult decisions in a state it governs.
But implementing the survey is not politically cost-free either. Karnataka's social structure includes several politically powerful communities with competing claims over reservation, representation and state resources. Any data-driven redistribution could therefore create winners and losers.
Siddaramaiah has trapped the Congress and DKS government in Karnataka. The demand for a 75% reservation adds another layer of difficulty.
Siddaramaiah's 75% formula has an obvious political appeal but a complicated legal path. It is politically significant because a caste survey without a policy response risks being reduced to a statistical exercise, while a policy response based on caste data could fundamentally alter the state's political equilibrium.
For the Congress, the Karnataka caste survey is more than Siddaramaiah's legacy. It is a test of the party's national rhetoric on caste.
The BJP might be the intended target of the caste-census politics of Congress. But Siddaramaiah has ensured that the first serious political battle over what caste data actually means could take place inside Congress-ruled Karnataka. The party wanted caste arithmetic to become a national question. Now, its own AHINDA leader is asking it to do the arithmetic at home.

headline: PATNA: Water levels across several districts in Bihar have started receding or stabilising, bringing relief to millions of affected people. However, multiple rivers remain above the danger mark in other areas and the flood threat persists, according ...
full_text:
PATNA: Water levels across several districts in Bihar have started receding or stabilising, bringing relief to millions of affected people. However, multiple rivers remain above the danger mark in other areas and the flood threat persists, according to Disaster Management Department officials.
As per latest figures, approximately 34.31 lakh people have been affected by floods across 480 gram panchayats in 79 blocks of 13 districts.
On Tuesday, the discharge at Kosi Barrage and the Son river’s discharge at the Indrapuri Barrage was recorded at 1,69,985 cusecs and 1,04,758 cusecs respectively -- both registering a declining trend. The water level of the Gandak river at Valmiki Barrage remains stable, while that of Ganga at Sultanganj has stopped rising after slightly surpassing its 2021 record high. However, the Gandak, Kosi, Burhi Gandak, Ganga, Punpun and Ghaghara are flowing above the danger mark at multiple locations.
“A total of 432 community kitchens are currently being operated in various districts for flood-affected people, and more than 10 lakh people have so far been provided meals twice a day,” a DMD official said, adding that accommodation, food and medical facilities have been arranged for 12,294 flood victims at 14 relief camps.
A total of 1,832 boats are being operated to facilitate the evacuation of residents. Besides, 27 State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams and 10 National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams have been deployed across various districts.
Former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar visited the flood-affected villages in Patna district and instructed Deputy Chief Minister and Water Resources Minister Vijay Kumar Choudhary to ensure proper arrangements be made to monitor relief and rescue operations.

headline: Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday said the party’s student wing has adopted a blue T-shirt and jeans as its new dress code, adding that the wing will launch a two-week student awareness campaign to connect with young people in ...
full_text:
Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday said the party’s student wing has adopted a blue T-shirt and jeans as its new dress code, adding that the wing will launch a two-week student awareness campaign to connect with young people in educational institutions.
Addressing a press conference here, Mr. Yadav said, “When the new generation has a new way of thinking, then their uniform should also be new.” He said the new dress code not only provides a unique identity, but also speaks of socialist values of the party and the ‘Bahujan Samaj’.
Earlier, Chhatra Sabha workers used to wear red shirts or kurtas. Blue is generally associated with the Mayawati-led Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP).
Mr. Yadav said that a two-week student awareness week would be organised during which members of the student wing would visit campuses, universities, colleges and hostels, and connect the youth with the PDA movement.
In 2023, Mr. Yadav coined the acronym PDA which stands for ‘Pichhde’ (backward classes), Dalits and ‘Alpsankhyak’ (minorities). On Monday, he had said that the PDA is an alliance of progressive and positive people -- the ‘pidhit’ (harassed), ‘dukhi’ (sad) and ‘apmaanit’ (humiliated) people -- who will form a PDA government and will establish social justice.
The Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly elections are scheduled to be held in 2027.
“PDA is progressive, positive, democratic and affirmative action. It is about bringing people together, increasing brotherhood, strengthening social harmony, democratic values and following the Constitution... We will work to establish a rule of social justice by bringing together the people of PDA,” Mr. Yadav said on Tuesday.
Sunil Singh Yadav ‘Sajan’, the SP spokesperson, said the blue colour signifies socialist values and idea of equality. “The blue colour is a progressive step signifying a broader outreach. It shows our commitment to the socialist values and equality,” he said. He also said that the blue colour is also to bring various sections of the society under the SP’s PDA umbrella who are facing oppression and marginalisation at the hands of the feudal forces supported by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

headline: New Delhi: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi has begun interviewing candidates as the party high command steps up the process of appointing new All India Congress Committee (AICC) secretaries, sources told ThePrint. The interviews are expected to continue ove...
full_text:
New Delhi: Congress MP Rahul Gandhi has begun interviewing candidates as the party high command steps up the process of appointing new All India Congress Committee (AICC) secretaries, sources told ThePrint. The interviews are expected to continue over the next couple days till 11 September, with around 25-30 names likely to be finalised out of nearly 150 prospects.
The new team is expected to include multiple new faces as Rahul looks to reshape Congress’s organisational structure.
The vetting process has been underway behind the scenes for some time, with the party carrying out a detailed exercise to screen potential candidates before calling them in for interviews.
Party General Secretary K.C. Venugopal had sought details of the work done by the candidates and their previous organisational responsibilities. Feedback was also sought from leaders in the states, following which a report was prepared.
Venugopal’s office playing key role
Venugopal’s office has been playing a significant role in shortlisting candidates for interviews. State in-charges and senior party leaders have been recommending names, but according to sources, not all candidates backed by senior leaders have been called in. Some who secured recommendation letters from several leaders have still not received an interview call.
“Having Venugopal’s backing is important in the process. No matter who recommends a candidate, the call is taken by someone else,” said a Congress leader familiar with the ongoing exercise.
One such candidate told ThePrint, on the condition of anonymity, “I have been with the party since I was 18. I have extensively organised the Bharat Jodo Yatra in my state. I have had three senior leaders write letters for me, but due to someone close to the high command (Venugopal) being upset with me, I am not getting a chance. I have worked really hard and given my soul to the party. If I am not even given a chance to interview, I will have doubts.”
The interview
Those who have made it through the vetting stage are now being interviewed by Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra at 10 Janpath, Delhi.
The interviews are being conducted in groups of around 10, rather than one-on-one meetings. Each session lasts around 30-45 minutes, according to candidates who have appeared for the interviews.
Rahul began a two-day visit to Rae Bareli Tuesday and the process will continue as soon as he is back.
Candidates are being asked about their biodata and the organisational responsibilities they have handled so far in the party. The Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition is also seeking their views on the political situation in their respective states, the current national political environment and international affairs.
“I got a call from KC’s (Venugopal) office. I did not apply for this. The interview was in a group setting, and the questions were based on biodata. Mr Gandhi was also keen on knowing our political and international views. The grouping was random,” one of the candidates interviewed by Rahul said.
Another candidate told ThePrint that the exercise felt like a “proper interview process”, with no fixed set of questions. “There was no set pattern of questions, and Gandhi asked whoever whatever he wanted.”
According to some who have appeared for the interviews, the questions vary candidate to candidate, with Rahul moving from organisational record, to state politics, and understanding of national and international developments.
‘Young leaders unhappy over exclusion’
The process has also caused some discontent within the party, it is learnt. Some younger Congress leaders who have worked in the organisation for years, but were not called for interviews have been unhappy with the way the shortlist was prepared.
For some of them, the issue is not just about getting the secretary post, but also about not being given the opportunity to appear for the interview despite years of organisational work and recommendations from senior leaders. Leaders involved in the process said that this could have a demoralising effect on those who were expecting organisational responsibilities after years of work.
There is also some friction over the decision to interview leaders who already hold such responsibilities. Sources told ThePrint that Rahul is looking to bring in new faces and considering leaders who do not currently hold major organisational ranks, although some existing office-bearers have also been called in for the exercise.
A senior Congress leader, speaking on condition of anonymity, questioned the manner in which the process was being conducted.
“Good for those who get selected, but those who are left out will have a bitter taste in their mouth as they have been rejected by the head of the party. The exercise should have been planned better and more democratically,” the leader said.
(Edited by Mannat Chugh)

headline: NEW DELHI: Centre on Wednesday told Supreme Court that it will challenge the Allahabad high court's decision to quash the detention of Delhi University student activist Akriti Chaudhary under the National Security Act (NSA).Solicitor General Tushar M...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Centre on Wednesday told Supreme Court that it will challenge the Allahabad high court's decision to quash the detention of Delhi University student activist Akriti Chaudhary under the National Security Act (NSA).Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, also clarified that a notice issued to a Greater Noida student over participation in the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest at Jantar Mantar was issued by an executive magistrate and not the district magistrate.
"I am not on the matter, but the Noida DM is flooded with queries from media, etc. what order have you passed, etc," Mehta told a bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.Referring to the Allahabad high court's recent order quashing Chaudhary's detention, Mehta said, "That we are challenging."Earlier in the day, the CJI reprimanded Greater Noida executive magistrate for issuing a notice to a student over participation in the CJP-led protest, questioning how the magistrate "dared" to issue the notice despite the Supreme Court's earlier order.The apex court said it would seek an explanation from the executive magistrate over the issue.
Earlier on September 2, Allahabad high court quashed Chaudhary's detention under the NSA in connection with the April workers' protest in Noida.A division bench of Justices Atul Sreedharan and Achal Sachdev strongly criticised the manner in which the detention order was passed by the Noida district magistrate and warned that continued "despotic" conduct by "errant" bureaucracy could reduce Uttar Pradesh to an Orwellian dystopia.The court also awarded Rs 5 lakh compensation to Chaudhary and directed that the amount be recovered from the salary of Gautam Buddha Nagar DM Medha Roopam, who passed the detention order, and other officers responsible, including the SHO.
Chaudhary, a history graduate from Delhi University, was arrested in connection with cases arising from the Noida workers' protest in April 2026.The UP Police subsequently invoked the NSA against Chaudhary and activist-journalist Satya Verma on May 13. They were among several activists arrested in cases related to the peaceful protest seeking higher wages.In its order, the high court also made significant observations on the role of the bureaucracy and police, noting that officers are entrusted with immense powers because they bear responsibility for upholding the constitutional and legal rights, dignity, honour and welfare of citizens.It directed that the court's displeasure against the DM and police officers involved in preparing the dossier be recorded in their service records.
Rohitashwa Ranjan is a digital journalist with The Times of India, where he decodes Indian politics as a carefully staged production with scripts, subtext and everything behind. His stories track elections, party dynamics and the things that often are buried beneath the headlines. When not parsing vote shares or alliances, he is usually reading between the lines, where the real story tends to reside.

headline: Meta India officials summoned over child abuse ads
full_text:
Meta India officials summoned over child abuse ads
NEW DELHI: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has summoned Meta India's managing director and country head to appear before it on Wednesday over advertisements allegedly linked to child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) on Instagram.NCPCR commission took suo motu cognisance of a BBC Eye report and issued a notice to Meta Platforms Inc on July 3, seeking an explanation and documents. Meta replied a week later, following which the NCPCR instituted a formal inquiry to establish the facts.
Commission officials remained tight-lipped about Meta's response. However, they said the inquiry would examine Meta India's role in the appearance of the advertisements, how they cleared Instagram's systems and why the situation arose.The scrutiny would consider the stringent provisions relating to such material under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, they added.Last week, NHRC issued notices to the ministry of electronics and information technology and ministry of information and broadcasting as part of its scrutiny of alleged CSAM on Instagram. An NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo, whose bench issued the notices Sept 2, said the inquiry was no longer only identifying who uploaded the content. "It also examines the extent to which the platform's own editorial and publishing systems participate in the generation, selection, circulation, amplification or monetisation of content," he said. The company denied knowingly targeting such advertisements at people.Queries to Meta did not elicit a response.

headline: VHP's call to bar Muslims from Navratri events ‘against the Constitution’, says Union minister Athawale
full_text:
VHP's call to bar Muslims from Navratri events ‘against the Constitution’, says Union minister Athawale
The MoS for Social Justice & Empowerment said such stand is inappropriate as people of different faith have the right to participate in each other's festivals.
Union minister Ramdas Athawale on Wednesday opposed calls to bar Muslims from attending 'garba' events during the Navratri festival, and said India is governed by the Constitution, which guarantees equal rights to people of all religions.
Asked about Vishva Hindu Parishad's call to bar Muslims from Navratri events in Maharashtra, Athawale said such a stand is not appropriate as people of different faiths have the right to participate in each other's festivals.
The Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment was talking to reporters at Swami Vivekananda Airport here after arriving on a day-long visit to Chhattisgarh.
"I feel this stand is not right because India runs on the Constitution. The Constitution given by Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar ensures justice to all religions. Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs, Christians, Jains, Buddhists, Lingayats, Parsis and people of several other faiths live in India, and the Constitution seeks to protect all religions," he said.
"It is not good to say that Muslims should not attend garba. Hindu and Muslim communities need to come together and work for the country," said Athawale, who heads the Republican Party of India (A).
He cited the example of Ajmer Sharif Dargah in Rajasthan, saying a large number of Hindus visit the shrine.
"Our country is such that people of all religions should participate in each other's festivals. We oppose those taking such a stand. Such a stand is against the Constitution," he asserted.
The VHP last week announced that Muslims would not be allowed entry to 'garba' and 'dandiya' venues across Maharashtra during the Navratri festival, which begins on October 11.
It has issued "guidelines" for organisers to verify participants' identities during Navratri 'garba' and 'dandiya' events by checking their Aadhaar cards and applying 'tilak' on their foreheads.
Maharashtra minister and BJP leader Nitesh Rane on Monday backed the VHP, alleging that cases of "love jihad" tend to increase during such festivals. He said attendees at such festivals should undergo identity checks and recite the Hanuman Chalisa before entry.
Love jihad' is a term used by right-wing activists to allege a ploy by Muslim men to lure women (mostly from the Hindu community) into relationships for religious conversion.

You cannot avoid taking decision," the bench said.
Noting that hearing in the case had been adjourned multiple times to allow the state to take a call on the remission plea, the court at the previous hearing also expressed displeasure over State Sentence Review Board not having made a decision yet. headline: Chennai: Facing a storm of criticism for allegedly mocking Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) president M.K. Stalin’s facial injury linked to a broken jaw he suffered during the 1975-77 Emergency, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay Tuesday clarif...
full_text:
Chennai: Facing a storm of criticism for allegedly mocking Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) president M.K. Stalin’s facial injury linked to a broken jaw he suffered during the 1975-77 Emergency, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay Tuesday clarified that the gesture he made in the Assembly was inadvertent and not intended to hurt anyone.
The controversy arose during Vijay’s reply to the debate on demands for grants for the police department in the Assembly Monday. Criticising the DMK and referring to its frequent mentions of the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA) from the Emergency era, Vijay placed the palm of his right hand near his jaw. Opposition leaders, including from the DMK, interpreted this as bodyshaming, or mimicking the lasting effect of Stalin’s jaw injury during his imprisonment because of the MISA protests.
Vijay responded on X Tuesday, “My body language, which inadvertently came across in between, was not in any way intentional. It was purely spontaneous and carried no ulterior motive. I requested that it should not be interpreted as an act intended to hurt anyone’s feelings on a personal level.”
Earlier Monday, DMK chief whip E.V. Velu and others accused Vijay of demeaning Stalin instead of addressing issues raised in the debate. This also led to a protest by DMK legislators. M.K. Stalin, then the young wing leader in his early 20s, was arrested in early 1976 after the Karunanidhi-led DMK government was dismissed under MISA during the Emergency (1975–77) and lodged in Madras Central Prison for several months until the Emergency ended. DMK leaders describe the mark as a “brave scar” from resisting repression when democracy was under strain.
Communist Party of India (Marxist) state secretary P. Shanmugam, whose party provides external support to the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government, also strongly objected to Vijay’s actions, accusing him of body-shaming Stalin and launching a personal attack by appearing to mimic the broken jaw.
On Tuesday, Shanmugam posted that the Emergency saw struggles to protect democracy along with repression and excesses, when many left leaders were arrested and attacked. He said that former CM Stalin was brutally assaulted by the police, resulting in a broken jaw. He called ridiculing someone’s physical appearance condemnable regardless of who does it, and “an act of irresponsibility” when done by the chief minister.
He also criticised using the taxpayer-funded Assembly for personal attacks or self-praise instead of public issues, and said harsh personal attacks belong outside it.
(Edited by Nardeep Singh Dahiya)

headline: BJP launches month-long Seva Sankalp Abhiyan to mark PM Modi’s 25 years in public service
full_text:
BJP launches month-long Seva Sankalp Abhiyan to mark PM Modi’s 25 years in public service
Nabin said PM Modi’s journey from an ordinary party worker to becoming the head of government had been marked by his “vision and resolve”
The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will organise a month-long Seva Sankalp Abhiyan (a campaign) beginning September 17 to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 25 years in public service.
Party president Nitin Nabin on Wednesday said the PM will complete 25 years of public service on October 7. He was sworn in as chief minister of Gujarat on the day in 2001.
“Over the last 25 years, he has continued his journey of serving the people,” Nabin said addressing the media.
Reflecting on Modi’s tenure in public service, Nabin said his journey from an ordinary party worker to becoming the head of government had been marked by his “vision and resolve” to improve the lives of people, adding that he had been able to deliver on his promises.
“During this time he’s been able to fulfil the promises he made, whether it was pulling 25 crore people out of poverty, giving 80 crore free ration…or giving 200 crore people free vaccines during the Covid-19 pandemic…These are not ordinary changes. These are his efforts to improve the lot of the people,” Nabin said.
The party president went on to say that when the PM took charge (in 2014), there was disillusionment and darkness. “There was policy paralysis and we were among the fragile five (economies). Now we are among the top 5, and India is making progress. The awards that have been given to him are an acknowledgment of his hard work,” he said.
Also Read:PM Modi, Russia’s Putin to hold bilateral talks on Friday, Su-57 aircraft sale to India on agenda
Nabin, who is also a Rajya Sabha member said India is now progressing with dignity.
“We have made significant progress in ending Naxalism. Under the leadership of PM Modi, India’s progress has not been limited to development. Our cultural identity and heritage have also been strengthened. From the Ram Mandir to Kashi Vishwanath, he has worked to preserve, restore and develop the country’s rich cultural heritage.”
“Terrorism was a real fear for the common man. But he’s not only secured the country but also given people encouragement,” Nabin added.

headline: BrahMos belt in China's backyard: How India is expanding missile's footprint
full_text:
BrahMos belt in China's backyard: How India is expanding missile's footprint
Several countries encircling the disputed South China Sea have started acquiring BrahMos missiles from India. Experts have called it the BrahMos belt strategy, which helps strengthen regional deterrence against aggressive Chinese maritime moves. What is it?
Is India trying to create a security presence in China's backyard via a BrahMos belt? Experts believe so, as India expands the footprint of its BrahMos supersonic cruise missile across the South China Sea. In an interview with Taiwan Talks, Lieutenant General PR Shankar (retd) said the BrahMos Belt strategy seemed aimed at strengthening regional deterrence, rather than targeting China alone. Three ASEAN nations have already signed deals for the BrahMos - the star of Operation Sindoor - with a fourth, Thailand, evaluating the missile.
BrahMos, the fastest cruise missile of its class, has generated renewed interest after its heroics during last year's Operation Sindoor. Its precision and long-range capabilities were on show as India struck Pakistani air bases during the hostilities, forcing Islamabad to seek a ceasefire.
Over the past year, Vietnam and Indonesia have signed deals with India for the BrahMos. Malaysia and Thailand could be next. In 2022, the Philippines was the first country to buy the BrahMos for coastal defence in a massive $375 million deal. All these countries encircle the disputed South China Sea, where they face a hostile and increasingly aggressive Beijing.
Lt General PR Shankar, who was closely involved in the missile's induction and development, underlined that the BrahMos belt strategy would not affect India-China ties. However, it would definitely make China aware of the fact that it is "dealing with a stronger India", he said.
"A whole regional signalling is going on. China needs to read the writing on the wall," Lt General PR Shankar said in the interview, titled 'BrahMos spreads across South China Sea'.
"China has seen how the BrahMos works. In the South China Sea, China is operating at maximum extended range. And as it keeps extending the range, it comes into the arc of the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia. Thus, China becomes vulnerable," he further said.
Tristan Tang, co-founder of Taiwan Defence Studies Initiative, underlined that the BrahMos would act as a deterrent to possible Chinese amphibious operations.
"ASEAN is not an Asian NATO, but with exports from India and better coordination, it can have a BrahMos belt," Tang said.
WHAT IS THE 'BRAHMOS BELT'?
The development has shifted focus to what India may be quietly building: a BrahMos belt.
It does not, however, refer to any formal military alliance. The term has been used by experts to loosely refer to India's growing network of BrahMos partnerships with countries that have maritime disputes or strategic concerns involving China.
At the heart of the dispute lies the South China Sea, a major shipping route that accounts for 21% of global trade.
Now, China claims about 90% of the South China Sea through its "nine-dash line", creating overlapping territorial disputes with Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei, and Taiwan. Over the years, China has sought to assert its claim by building islands and conducting naval patrols. This has led to standoffs with the Philippines (2012) and Vietnam (1974, 1988).
However, confronting a large power like China brought its own set of challenges for these smaller Southeast Asian nations. The key challenge has been their inability to threaten Chinese vessels operating in disputed areas.
With more Southeast Asian nations now acquiring the BrahMos anti-ship missiles, the scenario has started to change. The deal with Vietnam is around Rs 5,900 crore, while Indonesia has decided to acquire two BrahMos batteries worth Rs 1,900 crore.
If more nations like Thailand go on to acquire the missile, the result will be a chain of BrahMos batteries positioned around some of Asia's most strategically sensitive waters.
Experts have viewed it as a shrewd move by India, raising China's hackles without sending a soldier or ship to the South China Sea.
WHAT MAKES THE BRAHMOS SIGNIFICANT?
Notably, the BrahMos missile is particularly suited for this role. With a flight range of up to 290 km, the 'fire-and-forget' missile can be launched from land, ship or fighter aircraft.
"BrahMos is very fast and accurate, and you virtually cannot intercept it. It was the one that caused maximum damage at Pakistani air bases like Nur Khan, Sargodha and Murid. BrahMos was a game changer for us. No air defence system in China can intercept the BrahMos," Lt General PR Shankar said.
This will make China cautious. Much of China's maritime strategy depends on deploying large naval platforms across disputed waters. BrahMos's speed and precision pose a significant threat to such vessels, which can force China to remain far from contested areas.
An article in China's mouthpiece, Global Times, in 2024 laid bare Beijing's concerns. It mentioned how the acquisition of the BrahMos by the Philippines could give it striking capability towards reefs and regions in the disputed Spratly Islands.
WHY CHINA COULD BE CONCERNED
Against this backdrop, two waterways are particularly significant for China - the Malacca Strait and the Luzon Strait.
For China, the Strait of Malacca is nothing short of a lifeline - a dependence Beijing calls the "Malacca dilemma". Around 80% of China's oil imports and a significant share of its trade flow through this waterway, which is surrounded by Malaysia, Indonesia, and Singapore.
Adding to China's concerns is a recent deal between India and Indonesia to jointly develop the Sabang Port, which overlooks the strait. This is roughly 100 miles from India's upcoming Great Nicobar transhipment port.
On the other hand, the Luzon Strait, between Taiwan and the Philippines, connects the South China Sea with the wider Pacific Ocean.
Thus, any significant disruption to either route is likely to have major consequences for China's trade and energy security.
With the BrahMos in their arsenal, countries along China's maritime periphery can not only bolster their military capabilities, but also strengthen regional deterrence. It also helps India strategically without getting into a direct confrontation with China.

headline: SRINAGAR: Ladakh has recorded a sharp rise in tourist arrivals this year, with 4,05,085 visiting the Union Territory in the first eight months of 2026, exceeding the 3,35,872 tourists recorded for all of 2025. âIn just eight months of 2026, the total...
full_text:
SRINAGAR: Ladakh has recorded a sharp rise in tourist arrivals this year, with 4,05,085 visiting the Union Territory in the first eight months of 2026, exceeding the 3,35,872 tourists recorded for all of 2025. âIn just eight months of 2026, the total tourist footfall has exceeded by 20.6% from the total tourist arrivals recorded in 2025,â a govt spokesperson said.Aug 2026 saw the highest foreign tourist footfall recorded in any month so far this year, with 10,075 foreigners travelling to Ladakh. âThis is also considerably higher than the 8,148 foreign tourists recorded in Aug 2025,â the spokesperson said.The growth was recorded across both domestic and foreign tourist segments. âDuring the first eight months of 2026, Ladakh received 3,71,739 domestic tourists and 33,346 foreign tourists, compared to 2,44,308 domestic and 25,082 foreign tourists during the corresponding period in 2025,â the spokesperson said.In Aug, major festivals like Changthang Nomadic Festival, the first-ever Black-necked Crane Festival, Suru Summer Festival, and Ladakh Book Festival added new attractions to Ladakhâs tourism calendar and attracted a huge number of tourists, the spokesperson said.
âThe first edition of Black-Necked Crane Festival alone saw the participation of more than 10,000 people from India and abroad. These festivals showcase Ladakh regionâs unique culture, nomadic traditions, wildlife and natural heritage,â he added.Ladakhâs tourism calendar remains active in Sept as well, with a series of major events lined up, including Ladakh Bike Week, Ladakh Festival, Zanskar festival, and the Ladakh Marathon, the spokesperson said. âThe marathon, in particular, attracts runners from across the country and beyond, with many participants travelling to Ladakh with their families, thereby generating wider benefits for hotels, homestays, restaurants, transport operators, guides, local businesses and other tourism-related services,â he added.
Ladakh Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena attributed the growth to central govtâs sustained push for infrastructure development in Ladakh, as well as PM Narendra Modiâs appeal to citizens to visit locations in India and promote domestic tourism.âThe fact that Ladakh has already crossed its entire 2025 tourist footfall in just eight months of this year is a very encouraging sign. Our focus, however, is not merely on increasing tourist numbers but on building a sustainable, responsible and year-round tourism economy that benefits our people,â Saxena said. Festivals, sporting events and cultural programmes are helping the region expand the tourism calendar beyond the traditional summer season and bring visitors to Ladakh during the shoulder and off seasons, he said.

headline: In the wake of the defeat of the DMK-led front in this year’s Assembly elections in Tamil Nadu, the party’s president and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin has now announced a massive revamp exercise in the organisation's structure. An age limit and ...
full_text:
In the wake of the defeat of the DMK-led front in this year’s Assembly elections in Tamil Nadu, the party’s president and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin has now announced a massive revamp exercise in the organisation's structure. An age limit and cap on tenures have been established. This internal restructuring reform is expected to see the exit of several regional satraps from the posts of party district secretaries and give opportunities for many next-generation leaders.
How deftly Mr. Stalin manages to pull off this exercise and what compromises he would be forced to make — such as rewarding family members of incumbents — remains to be seen. A massive shake-up in ranks is not easy in a legacy organisation. For that matter, even minor shifts are resisted by the seniors. This was evident during the last Assembly elections when former Minister R. Gandhi, aged 81, could not come to terms with and accept the leadership’s decision to give the ticket to his son in Ranipet. Eventually, on the last day of filing nominations, his son Vinod Gandhi withdrew from the race, and Mr. Gandhi ended up entering the race only to be defeated.

headline: India’s education spending rises, still lags some BRICS nations
full_text:
India’s education spending rises, still lags some BRICS nations
In urban India, education accounted for 6% of household expenditure in 2025, while in rural areas the expenditure stood at 3.2%
India’s public spending on education has increased over the years, but remains below those of some other Brics countries, according to the Brics Joint Statistical Publication 2026, released last month.
India also continues to face the challenge of converting educational investment into a workforce employed in higher-productivity sectors, amid the need for greater “alignment of training programmes with evolving market demands” and stronger “linkage of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions with industries” according to Brics Education Ministers’ Declaration adopted at the 13th Brics Education Ministers’ Meeting in Bhubaneswar on August 7, 2026.
India’s public expenditure on education increased from 1.2% of GDP in 2016 to 4.1% of GDP in 2023. This compared with 4.9% in Brazil and 10.5% in South Africa, while it was marginally higher than China’s 4.02%, Russia’s (3.5%), the UAE’s (3.8%) and Indonesia’s (1.3%), according to the report. To be sure, China’s GDP is much higher than India’s, and its population older (a median age of 41 compared with India’s 29 years, according to the UN’s World Population data).
Also Read | Beyond Enrolment: Are India's universities preparing youth for the economy of 2047?
According to the report, India’s household spending on education also increased. In urban India, education accounted for 4.3% of household expenditure in 2000, rising to 6% in 2025 — an increase of 1.7 percentage points. In rural areas, the share rose from 1.9% to 3.2%, an increase of 1.3 percentage points. By comparison, Indonesia’s education spending accounted for 3.7% of urban household expenditure and 2.1% of rural expenditure in 2025. In China, the broader category of ‘Education, cultural and recreation’ accounted for 12.0% of urban household consumption and 11.5% of rural household consumption in 2025.
Yet India’s employment structure remains heavily dependent on agriculture and allied activities. In 2025, 43% of India’s employed population was in the primary industry, compared with 29.3% in Indonesia, 22.2% in China, 8% in South Africa and 5.3% in Russia. India’s primary-sector share has fallen only 1.6 percentage points from 44.6% in 2018. Industry accounted for 25.1% and services 31.9% of employment in India, the report said.
- ABOUT THE AUTHORSanjay MauryaSanjay Maurya is a Principal Correspondent with Hindustan Times, where he covers education, with a focus on school and higher education, competitive examinations, education policy and governance. Working as part of the National Bureau, he is based in New Delhi and reports on the Ministry of Education and covers various statutory bodies like UGC, AICTE and NCTE and autonomous bodies like CBSE and NCERT. His reporting also tracks the implementation of key government reforms and policies from school education to higher education including in IITs, NITs, IIMs, central and state universities, and their impact on students and educational institutions. His reporting on the irregularities and rushed implementation of CBSE's On-Screen Marking (OSM) system for evaluation of Class 12 board exams 2026, triggered administrative action, leading to the transfer of the board's two senior-most officials and the constitution of a committee to probe alleged irregularities in procurement process of the system. He joined Hindustan Times in December 2024. Prior to that, he had a three-year stint at Careers360, where he reported on school and higher education, entrance examinations, admissions, rankings and various education policies involving universities and professional education bodies. Over the years, Maurya has reported extensively on major developments in India's education sector, including the implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, reforms in the National Testing Agency (NTA) following the NEET-UG 2024 controversy, changes in school education, higher education regulation, and the evolution of entrance examinations such as NEET, JEE and CUET. He regularly produces data-driven and explanatory stories based on government documents, parliamentary proceedings, court records and official data. His focus remains on helping readers understand how education policies and institutional decisions affect millions of students, teachers and educational institutions across the country.Read More

headline: Lucknow: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati has expelled nephew Akash Anand from the party. In a post on X, she cited Akash favouring his father-in-law Ashok Siddharth over the party and Akash’s failure to repost one of her posts on X concernin...
full_text:
Lucknow: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati has expelled nephew Akash Anand from the party. In a post on X, she cited Akash favouring his father-in-law Ashok Siddharth over the party and Akash’s failure to repost one of her posts on X concerning Siddharth.
Mayawati had in August expelled Siddharth, a former Rajya Sabha MP, from the BSP.
A senior BSP functionary told ThePrint, “For the past two years, the party has been caught up in family drama. Behanji (Mayawati) inducts Akash (into the party), and then she removes or punishes him. There is no guarantee that she will not bring him back again.
“With elections just a few months away, we are still stuck in this family politics. How will we be able to take on the BJP and SP like this?”
The action against Akash came a week after Mayawati, on 3 September, removed him as the BSP’s national coordinator. She has now cancelled his primary membership of the BSP, severing his association with the party altogether.
This is the third major action by Mayawati against Akash in the past two years. She had earlier relieved him of key party responsibilities in May 2024 and March 2025. However, Akash was later re-inducted into the party and made national coordinator.
Explaining her decision, Mayawati said Thursday that Siddharth’s retirement from politics came too late. Had he retired earlier, Akash, the BSP and the broader Bahujan movement would not have had to repeatedly face difficult and adverse circumstances, she argued.
Mayawati also expressed displeasure over Akash’s response to her posts on X. She said he used to repost her regularly but did not do so this week when she posted about Siddharth.
1. आज श्री अशोक सिद्धार्थ द्वारा राजनीति से संन्यास लेने की घोषणा अति-देर से उठाया गया यह सही क़दम है। 
2. वैसे लोगों का यही कहना है कि अगर यह फैसला वे काफी पहले ही ले लेते तो बी.एस.पी., बहुजन समाज व बहुजन मूवमेन्ट तथा उनके दामाद श्री आकाश आनन्द को भी लगातार विपरीत परिस्थितियों…
— Mayawati (@Mayawati) September 10, 2026
According to Mayawati, this was a clear indication that Akash was favouring family ties over the party. She asked how someone working with a ‘double mind’ could serve the interests of the BSP.
She also questioned Siddharth’s intentions, saying if he was genuinely concerned about Akash’s political future and the Bahujan movement, he should have retired from politics much earlier.
The BSP chief has now asked party workers to prepare for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections and counter the tactics of political opponents. She called on BSP workers to work towards forming a government with a full majority while following the principle of ‘Sarvajan Hitay, Sarvajan Sukhay’ (welfare, happiness for all).
On Wednesday, Mayawati had hinted on X that, if Ashok Siddharth were to retire from politics, it could help save son-in-law Akash’s political career. Later that evening, Siddharth announced his retirement from politics. But that did not help Akash’s case.
A source in BSP told ThePrint that Mayawati remains deeply hurt by what she sees as Siddharth’s ‘family politics’.
The BSP chief believes Siddharth and those close to Akash are driven more by family interests than by larger interests of the party and the Bahujan movement, said the source.
Also Read: The other nephew rises: Mayawati hands key BSP position to Ishan Anand days after removing Akash
Ishan Anand new ‘political heir’?
The latest move comes amid a significant reshuffle within the BSP’s top leadership.
Four days after removing Akash as national coordinator, Mayawati Monday appointed his younger brother Ishan Anand as the party’s chief sector in-charge. Ishan, 27, will review the party’s organisational work across states other than Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
According to BSP functionaries, he will submit organisational reports from these states to his father, Anand Kumar, who is the BSP’s national vice-president. These responsibilities were earlier handled by Akash as chief national coordinator.
BSP functionaries said speculation about Ishan’s growing role intensified after the BSP’s national executive meeting in Lucknow, where Ishan was also present. Ishan, they said, could emerge as Mayawati’s new successor.
(Edited by Amrtansh Arora)

headline: Xi to visit India after 7 years, hold meet with Modi on Day 1 of BRICS Summit
full_text:
Xi to visit India after 7 years, hold meet with Modi on Day 1 of BRICS Summit
PM Modi is expected to hold bilateral meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Friday.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to hold bilateral meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Friday and China’s President Xi Jinping on Saturday on the margins of the BRICS Summit, people familiar with the matter said.
Modi met both Putin and Pezeshkian on the margins of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Kyrgyzstan on August 31, while Xi is set to visit India for the first time in seven years. Xi last travelled to India in 2019, months before the start of a military face-off in Ladakh that lasted more than four years and took bilateral ties to a six-decade low.
These bilateral meetings will be opportunities for the leaders to take stock of bilateral relations and discuss a range of global issues, especially the war in Ukraine and the West Asia conflict, the people said.
Also Read | BRICS Summit 2026: Full list of leaders attending PM Modi’s mega meet in New Delhi
Deep Dive
The bilateral meeting between Modi and Xi, to be held on the main day of the Brics Summit, is the one that will be most closely watched as it will provide a chance for the two leaders to assess the ongoing process to normalise India-China relations and to address the dragging border dispute.
Modi and Xi had unveiled a range of measures to normalise ties and build confidence when they met in October 2024, soon after India and China reached an understanding on ending the standoff in Ladakh. Since then, the two sides have resumed direct flights, revived the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra and started border trade through three designated routes.
Also Read | Russia optimistic BRICS will bridge Iran-UAE gap at India-hosted summit
The Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) on border affairs and the Special Representatives on the border issue have met several times and discussed matters such as a possible “early harvest” in boundary demarcation. The first meeting of senior military commanders of both sides in the Arunachal Pradesh sector will be held this week to discuss the maintenance of peace and tranquillity on the border.
However, differences continue to persist on a range of issues, including China’s restrictions on visas for Indian businessmen, Beijing’s curbs on exports of key technologies and equipment and an insistence that the border issue should be separated from the development of the overall relationship. The Indian side has repeatedly said the state of the border will determine the course of bilateral ties.
Also Read | BRICS and India's policy of strategic autonomy
Xi is also expected to travel to India weeks after reports of fresh tensions between Indian and Chinese troops at Taksing in Arunachal Pradesh. The upcoming meeting, the people said, will be an opportunity to take up such issues.

headline: Russian President Vladimir Putin is expected to arrive here on Friday (September 11, 2026) morning to attend the 18th BRICS summit that will be held here this weekend, Russian sources said.
full_text:
Russian President Vladimir Putin is expected to arrive here on Friday (September 11, 2026) morning to attend the 18th BRICS summit that will be held here this weekend, Russian sources said.
Mr. Putin is likely to hold a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi hours after his arrival, where the two sides are expected to discuss defence and other related matters. President Putin is among the top leaders of BRICS members and partner countries who are scheduled to arrive for the two-day summit.
Several heads of multilateral organisations, including the United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, are also scheduled to attend the BRICS summit.
The External Affairs Ministry has confirmed that, apart from President Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, Ethiopia’s Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali, and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto are among the top leaders who are expected to reach Delhi for the summit that is being held against the backdrop of a global crisis in the supply chains of energy and agriculture because of wars in West Asia and Ukraine.
The conflict in West Asia that started in February, when Israel and the U.S. launched a joint attack on Iran, is likely to be among the top topics of the summit, especially as Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian is scheduled to be here. This will be the first visit to India by President Pezeshkian since he took charge after the death of President Ebrahim Raisi in a helicopter crash in 2024.
Mr. Pezeshkian met Prime Minister Modi on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic, on August 31. That was the first meeting between the two leaders since the war began. The differences between Iran and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) will be keenly watched as the two sides have been exchanging tough messages because of the ongoing hostilities in the region. UAE will be represented by Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the Ministry informed. The Gulf Cooperation Council, which is also in focus because of the hostilities in the Persian Gulf region, will be represented by Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani, Foreign Minister of Bahrain.
Among the founding members of BRICS — launched in 2009 with the first summit hosted by Russia — South Africa will be represented by Cyril Ramaphosa and Brazil will be represented by Mauro Vieira. Among the founding members of BRICS, President Putin is the longest-serving leader.
Indonesia’s President Subianto, who was the Guest of Honour at the Republic Day parade here on January 26, 2025, is also scheduled to attend the BRICS summit. Among the ten partner countries of BRICS, the notable leaders will be Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Vietnam’s Prime Minister Le Minh Hung. President of the Philippines Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr, will attend the summit in his capacity as Chair of ASEAN and President of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev will participate in the event in his capacity as President of the Eurasian Economic Union.
Apart from Mr. Guterres, World Health Organization head Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, World Trade Organization Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, and Dilma Rousseff, former President of Brazil, who will participate as the representative of the New Development Bank, will attend the summit. Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was invited to participate in the summit, but Bangladesh will not be represented at the event, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kobir has confirmed.

headline: An IndiGo Lucknow-Dammam flight made an emergency landing in Ahmedabad after a bomb threat, but security checks found nothing suspicious.
full_text:
An IndiGo Lucknow-Dammam flight made an emergency landing in Ahmedabad after a bomb threat, but security checks found nothing suspicious.
NEW DELHI: An IndiGo flight from Lucknow to Dammam made an emergency landing at Ahmedabad airport on Thursday after a bomb threat was reported onboard, news agency ANI reported quoting Ahmedabad Police .The threat was discovered after a crew member found the word 'Bomb' written on a piece of paper inside the aircraft.There were 107 passengers and six crew members onboard the Lucknow-Dammam 6E 97 flight. All passengers and crew members were safe at Terminal 2 of the airport, police said.
Ahmedabad Police said, "Lucknow-Dammam 6E 97 IndiGo flight made an emergency landing in Ahmedabad after a bomb threat onboard. A member of the crew had found 'Bomb' written on a piece of paper. There are 107 passengers and 6 crew membes onboard, all of them are safe at Terminal 2 of the airport. SOG, local Police and CISF conducted an inspection of the aircraft. Nothing suspicious was found onboard the aircraft."The Special Operations Group (SOG), local police and Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) conducted a thorough inspection of the aircraft after it landed.No suspicious object or material was found onboard during the inspection, according to the police.

A ‘bomb’ note on IndiGo's Lucknow-Dammam flight forced it to make emergency landing in Ahmedabad on Thursday. A crew member found ‘bomb’ written on a piece of paper following which the flight, with 107 passengers and six crew members onboard, made the emergency landing, officials said.
IndiGo's flight 6E 97 landed safely at the Ahmedabad airport at 5:40 pm and security checks as per the protocol are underway. Recovery flight from Ahmedabad is likely to take off at around 8:30 pm.
