headline: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has proposed an elected body for the Union Territory (UT) of Ladakh by introducing a new constitutional provision under Article 371 of the Constitution in a proposed Chapter K, civil society members who attend...
full_text:
The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has proposed an elected body for the Union Territory (UT) of Ladakh by introducing a new constitutional provision under Article 371 of the Constitution in a proposed Chapter K, civil society members who attended a meeting with MHA officials in Delhi on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) said.
Cherring Dorjay Lakruk of the Leh Apex Body (LAB), who attended the meeting, told The Hindu, however,that he was “disappointed” as this was a reiteration of the May 22 meeting and that even though they were shown a PowerPoint presentation mentioning Chapter K, they were not yet provided a detailed “draft proposal” by the MHA.
“The MHA stated that the intended UT-level body would be elected by direct election, and would have legislative powers with respect to land, culture and language, forest, environment, natural resources, and any other subject matter reserved for the UT under Article 240,” a statement by the civil society members said.
Article 371, which currently has chapters that run from A to J, deals with “Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions” and exists under Part XXI of the Constitution. It is currently applicable in 12 States: Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Mizoram, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Sikkim, and Karnataka.
Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra, who attended the meeting, said in a post on X, “Attended the sub-committee meeting with leaders of Ladakh at MHA in Delhi today. A general air of positivity prevailed as the broad contours of a sui generis model of governance under Article 371 of the Constitution were discussed. Deepening democracy is the goal.”
Ladakh leaders’ demands
Representatives of the Leh Apex Body and the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) asked the MHA to ensure that the Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh does not take any major decisions concerning the administration, bureaucracy or land until the proposed constitutional safeguards are put in place, while pressing for the legislation to be passed in the upcoming Winter Session of Parliament.
The members also sought compensation for the families of the victims of the violence that broke out on September 24, 2025, in Leh city, where four people were killed in police firing. They also sought the withdrawal of criminal cases against 80 people, along the lines of the protection afforded to those who took part in the “Gen Z protest” at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar in July this year. The violence in Ladakh erupted amid a protest that was called to demand constitutional safeguards for the region.
After Ladakh lost its special status under Article 370 of the Constitution as part of the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir, it was turned into a Union Territory without a legislative assembly in 2019. Since then, the LAB and the KDA, representing the Leh and Kargil regions respectively, have been demanding Statehood and tribal status for Ladakh and seeking a larger role for local residents in decisions relating to land and infrastructure projects.
Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk, who was also part of the delegation that met MHA officials, said, “We cannot say that the meeting was a complete success. We hoped to get a draft proposal assuring us protection under Article 371. However, that was not provided. We have asked the government to take back the cases registered against protesters after last year’s incident in Leh city. We hope that the way cases were withdrawn against Gen Z protestors in Delhi, it will be done in Ladakh, too.”
The civil society groups had earlier called a protest march from Leh to Kargil on September 10, following which the MHA called for a meeting in Delhi on September 9.
“We had proposed that the assembly should have control over the police and bureaucracy. The MHA only said that they will look into these demands. No assurance was given. The government assured us that compensation will be announced soon for the injured people and the families of those who were killed in the September 24, 2025, violence,” Mr. Wangchuk said, adding that they would be observing a condolence meeting on September 24.
Sajjad Kargili of the KDA said civil society members asserted that no major administrative decisions should be taken by the Ladakh L-G until a decision on the elected body for Ladakh is finalised. “We stressed that legislation to this effect be passed by a two-thirds majority in Parliament in the coming Winter Session,” he said.
Published - September 10, 2026 12:04 am IST

headline: TVK names former AIADMK MLAs for Tamil Nadu bypolls, setting up 3-way fight with DMK
full_text:
TVK names former AIADMK MLAs for Tamil Nadu bypolls, setting up 3-way fight with DMK
The bypolls will be the first electoral battle in the state since the C Joseph Vijay-led TVK formed its first government with the support of allies after winning the April 23 Assembly polls.
The ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) on Thursday named its candidates for the October 6 bypolls to two Assembly seats in Tamil Nadu, setting up a direct contest with the DMK, while the AIADMK has also entered the fray.
The bypolls will be the first electoral battle in the state since the C Joseph Vijay-led TVK formed its first government with the support of allies after winning the April 23 Assembly polls.
The two seats, Madurantakam and Dharapuram, are considered AIADMK strongholds in northern and western Tamil Nadu.
In a party statement, TVK founder and Chief Minister Vijay nominated former AIADMK MLAs K Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama from Madurantakam and Dharapuram, respectively. Both had represented the constituencies as AIADMK legislators before joining the ruling party.
Kumaravel and Sathyabama had won the two seats in the April 23 Assembly polls as AIADMK candidates. They later resigned as MLAs and joined the TVK, resulting in the two constituencies falling vacant.
Kumaravel is currently serving as TVK deputy general secretary, while Sathyabama is the party's Tiruppur south-east district secretary.
TVK sources said the decision to field the two former MLAs again was aimed at leveraging their existing support bases in the constituencies and strengthening the ruling party's position following its government formation.
Vijay said the bypolls in both reserved constituencies would be contested under the banner of the "Secular Social Justice Victory Front", the name given to the alliance after a meeting of its leaders on Wednesday. The bloc includes the Congress and MDMK.
The DMK has fielded advocates I Parandaman, a former MLA from Madurantakam, and S Suganya from Dharapuram.
The AIADMK has also announced its candidates, with former MLA Kanitha Sampath contesting from Madurantakam and K Banumathi from Dharapuram.
The Election Commission has scheduled polling for October 6, with counting of votes set for October 9. With nominations now open, campaigning in the two constituencies is expected to intensify in the coming days.
Kumaravel had won the Madurantakam seat in Chengalpattu district in the April 23 polls, defeating her nearest rival from the TVK. Sathyabama, meanwhile, defeated DMK's Indirani T in the Dharapuram constituency in Tiruppur district.
Kumaravel has expressed confidence of retaining the Madurantakam seat, citing the performance of the TVK government.
Asked by reporters whether she could repeat her victory in the constituency considered an "AIADMK fortress", she said the government's "100-day achievements" would be taken to the people and that the party would ensure victory.

headline: Xi Jinping to attend BRICS summit in New Delhi, China confirms
full_text:
Xi Jinping to attend BRICS summit in New Delhi, China confirms
The summit is being hosted by India and will bring together leaders of the BRICS grouping for discussions on key global and economic issues.
Chinese President Xi Jinping will visit India for the first time in nearly seven years to attend the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13, China’s foreign ministry said on Thursday. Xi’s visit, at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, will also provide an opportunity for the two leaders to review the gradual improvement in India-China ties and the efforts to resolve outstanding border issues.
Xi last visited India in October 2019, when he met Modi in Mamallapuram. Relations between the two countries deteriorated sharply months later after a military standoff erupted along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in eastern Ladakh in 2020. The Galwan Valley clash in June that year, in which 20 Indian soldiers and at least four Chinese troops were killed, pushed bilateral ties to their lowest point in decades.
The four-year military face-off began to ease after India and China reached an understanding in October 2024 on disengagement at the remaining friction points of Depsang and Demchok. Modi and Xi met days later on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in Kazan and agreed to revive mechanisms for addressing the border dispute and normalising relations.
Since then, the two sides have taken several steps to rebuild ties, including resuming direct flights and reviving the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra. India and China have also continued discussions through diplomatic and military channels on maintaining peace and tranquillity along the LAC. In May this year, the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs reviewed the situation and noted progress in maintaining peace along the frontier.
The effort to improve relations has continued in recent months. At talks in August, National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, who are the two countries’ Special Representatives on the boundary question, reached an eight-point consensus that included additional military meeting points, new hotline channels and the reopening of three designated border trading points. India and China also held their first corps commander-level meeting in the eastern sector in Arunachal Pradesh on September 6.
New Delhi, however, continues to maintain that peace and tranquillity along the border are essential for normal ties. External affairs minister S Jaishankar reiterated this position during a meeting with Wang in July, saying that progress on the border remains a prerequisite for fully normalising India-China relations.
Xi’s visit and his meeting with Modi are therefore expected to be closely watched for indications of how far the two countries are prepared to take the ongoing process of stabilising relations while addressing the unresolved boundary dispute.
Deep Dive
BRICS summit in New Delhi
India is hosting the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, with the grouping’s leaders expected to discuss a range of global political and economic issues. Xi’s presence will make his bilateral meeting with Modi one of the most closely watched engagements on the margins of the summit, particularly against the backdrop of the efforts by India and China to stabilise relations.
The summit will also provide an opportunity for India to engage with other major BRICS members on issues including global conflicts, economic cooperation and reforms of multilateral institutions.

headline: Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi
full_text:
Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend the 18th Brics summit in New Delhi
NEW DELHI: Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi from September 12 to 13 at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
This is his first trip to India in seven years and comes as the two countries work to stabilise ties after years of tensions over their disputed border.Xi will be attending Brics summit with a large delegation, more than double the Chinese contingent that accompanied him on his last India visit in 2019, according to Reuters.Earlier, two Indian sources said Xi was likely to be accompanied by around 400 officials, compared with fewer than 200 during his 2019 visit.
The Chinese foreign ministry said, âChina attaches great importance to and actively participates in Brics cooperation, and supports India, the current chair, in successfully hosting this year's Brics summit.âThe visit comes amid India and China's continued high-level efforts to improve ties.Last month, national security advisor Ajit Doval met Chinese vice president Han Zheng in Beijing, with the two sides discussing ways to maintain peace and tranquillity along the border and strengthen relations across economic, political and multilateral platforms.

headline: Mayawati ‘frees’ nephew from BSP after exit of his father-in-law
full_text:
Mayawati ‘frees’ nephew from BSP after exit of his father-in-law
The father-in-law announced his retirement from politics after Mayawati indicated Anand could regain a role if the former did so
Former Uttar Pradesh chief minister Mayawati on Thursday expelled her nephew Akash Anand, 31, from the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) for the second time, a week after removing him as its chief national coordinator for the third time since 2024, following his reinstatement in March.
The expulsion came despite Anand’s father-in-law, Ashok Siddharth, announcing his retirement from active politics after Mayawati indicated on Wednesday that her nephew could regain an organisational role if Siddharth did so. In a post on X, Mayawati on Thursday said Anand is now completely free from the party. She added that he has been fully relieved.
Siddharth said that instead of harming the party’s mission, he was renouncing political and social life. He blamed opponents in the BSP for engaging in anti-party activities and conspiring against him. Siddharth clarified that he was not misleading Anand or trying to take over the BSP.
ALSO READ: Mayawati sets 'sanyas' condition to restore nephew Akash Anand's role in BSP
Two hours after Siddharth’s post on X announcing his retirement, Mayawati said if he had even a little concern for Anand’s future, BSP’s interests, and its Ambedkarite Movement, he would have announced his retirement on Wednesday. “This would have ensured Akash Anand’s active involvement in the party and the movement. But the fact that this did not happen proves that the flaw and ambition in Ashok Siddharth’s intentions have not diminished and remain fully intact.”
Mayawati said Anand is attached to Siddharth more than to his own career. She added he did not even deem it appropriate to repost her post on X even though it was for his own benefit and well-being. Mayawati said he used to try to prove his loyalty by reposting her posts. “This too suggests that Ashok Siddharth and Akash Anand have less attachment to the success of the party and the movement and more to their personal and familial interests.”
Mayawati said the BSP elevated both of them to heights. “For this, no matter how much gratitude and indebtedness all these people feel toward the BSP and its leadership, it would still be too little...”
Mayawati said if Anand cares less about the party, the movement, his own career, and more about attachment to relationships and kin, then how can he possibly do good?
In March 2025, Mayawati expelled Anand after removing him from the national coordinator post.
Last week, Mayawati said Anand requires more maturity and entrusting him with major party responsibilities at this stage would be inappropriate. She had also introduced her younger nephew, Ishan Anand, to the party leaders.
In May 2024, Mayawati removed Akash Anand from the national coordinator post during the Lok Sabha election campaign and said he is no longer her successor. The move came after a hate speech case was lodged against him for the alleged “use of unparliamentary language” in criticising the Bharatiya Janata Party government.
ALSO READ: Mayawati alleges CJP Gen-Z movement has been hijacked by political parties
Mayawati reinstated Akash Anand after eight months in August 2024 and entrusted him with leading the campaign in the assembly elections in Haryana, Maharashtra, Jharkhand and Delhi.
Mayawati named Ramji Gautam, Randhir Singh Beniwal and Raja Ram as national coordinators after sacking Akash Anand in March and expelling him from the party.
She reinstated Akash Anand and reappointed him chief national coordinator in May 2025. The BSP planned to woo the younger Gen Z voters by promoting him to the top organisational post. Akash Anand was asked to counter the increasing influence of the Azad Samaj Party chief Chandrashekar Azad over the Dalit community.
Akash Anand’s fresh expulsion came days after the BSP launched the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election campaign with his two rallies in Hathras and Gautam Buddha Nagar on August 10 and 25. Mayawati had groomed him as her political successor since 2017. She first appointed him as the national coordinator in June 2019. In December 2023, she named Akash Anand as her political heir.
On August 2, Mayawati expelled Siddharth, a former lawmaker, from the party for anti-party activities. Mayawati, who won a clear five-year mandate to rule Uttar Pradesh in 2007, has maintained an iron grip over the party despite growing erosion in the BSP’s support base. BSP’s lone lawmaker in the 403-member Uttar Pradesh died in August. The party has no seats in Parliament.
Mayawati, 70, has made it clear that she will continue to lead the party despite demands from the party cadre to promote younger leadership. She told party leaders that she will finalise the candidates for the 2027 assembly election, devise the election campaign, and monitor the fundraising.

headline: August 2026 becomes joint warmest month recorded globally, ties with July 2023: Report
full_text:
August 2026 becomes joint warmest month recorded globally, ties with July 2023: Report
August was the joint hottest month on record globally, with average surface air temperature 1.65°C above pre-industrial baseline, C3S said.
Amidst a strengthening El Nino, August was the joint warmest month ever recorded globally, tied with July 2023, the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) said on Thursday. The global average surface air temperature was 1.65°C higher than the estimated pre-industrial baseline this August, also making it the first month to exceed 1.5°C since November 2025, it said.
At the same time, August also saw the joint highest monthly average sea surface temperatures (SSTs) ever recorded across the extra-polar ocean, tied with March 2024, and the highest daily global SST over the extra-polar ocean ever recorded, at 21.11ºC, it said, linking it to strong El Nino conditions.
This comes a week after the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) on August 3 said El Niño has firmly established and will intensify into a ‘very strong’ event in the coming months. It had attached a near 100% likelihood that it will persist through February 2027, warning of impacts on rainfall and temperature patterns globally. A day prior to that, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) had said global temperature rise is likely to cross the 1.5°C threshold by the end of this decade, pushing climate risks and impacts such as intensified extreme weather to increasingly dangerous heights.
Also Read: A strong El Nino is inevitable — history shows its effects will hit hardest in 2027
“With a global average surface air temperature 1.65°C higher than the estimated pre-industrial baseline, this August was the first month to exceed 1.5°C since November 2025. Meanwhile, record high SSTs were seen across the tropical Pacific, an area where a potentially extreme El Niño event continues to intensify. The impacts of this event are already being felt over land, with conditions favouring the intensification of seasonal wildfires across Indonesia..” C3S said in a statement on Thursday.
Copernicus is the Earth observation component of the European Union’s Space programme. It includes assistance from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) -- both as a research institute and operational service which gives global numerical weather predictions.
The month also marked the end of western Europe’s warmest summer on record --surpassing the previous record set in 2003. The region saw further heatwaves in August, continuing an exceptional run of extreme heat that began in May. Much of the region and large parts of central and eastern Europe also saw widespread dryness in August, in some cases persisting since May, with severe drought conditions reported in France, United Kingdom Hungary, Romania and Serbia. Across the dry regions, major European river flows were exceptionally low, including – from west to east – the Rhine, Danube, Southern Bug and Dnieper experiencing exceptionally low flows.
Also Read; Biggest El Nino in ‘over a century’ to dial up global heat, India braces for double crop hit
Samantha Burgess, Strategic Lead for Climate at ECMWF said August 2026 was a remarkable month in the global climate record. “These observations show how climate change is driving extremes across both the atmosphere and the oceans. The impacts of these conditions are increasingly being felt by communities, economies and ecosystems across the world.”
Speaking at the European Parliament Committee on the Environment, Climate and Food Safety in Brussels on the same day, UN Climate Change executive secretary Simon Stiell said the impacts of climate were already visible, with this summer’s climate-driven extreme heat killing tens of thousands of people.
“It has hammered Europe’s infrastructure, businesses, and economies. We’ve seen mass evacuations. Power stations closed and trade routes choked. Crops lost, yields went down and food prices up – and are set to rise further,” Stiell said, calling for countries to work in partnership and forge International alliances that secure supply chains for clean energy and new industries.
“The Turkish COP31 Presidency, working closely with Australia, has set key Action Agenda targets, including 35% of final global energy demand met by electricity by 2035,” he added.

Gandhiok has over a decade of experience in journalism and is based in Delhi. He has reported extensively on Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR). This includes the region's air pollution woes, a polluted Yamuna and on urban wildlife still thriving in the region. He joined HT in October 2021. Prior to that, he had five-year stint at The Times of India in Delhi, where he also covered Delhi, with a focus on environment and wildlife. Gandhiok has covered some recent events around the Capital too, ranging from the farmers' protests, the northeast Delhi riots and the CAA-NRC protests, reporting from the ground on all of these. He also travels across the country to report on how environment and climate change impact everyday life, while also writing on endangered species. headline: Bengaluru: After a gap of 37 years, Karnataka’s D.K. Shivakumar-led Congress government has approved student body elections in the state’s educational institutions from the 2026-27 academic year.
full_text:
Bengaluru: After a gap of 37 years, Karnataka’s D.K. Shivakumar-led Congress government has approved student body elections in the state’s educational institutions from the 2026-27 academic year.
Student elections were last held in the state in 1989-90, after which the Veerendra Patil-led Congress government banned them. The move to restart is seen as an extension of efforts by all political parties, including the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Congress, to woo the Gen Z.
“We (the government) had banned this, but now we have decided to restart it,” said Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara.
Why were the elections banned in the first place? The answer depends on whom you ask.
Restricting new political faces from emerging, promoting family members or loyalists, containing BJP’s rise and uncontrollable campus violence were among the key reasons why student polls were banned in Karnataka nearly four decades ago. “Student elections were banned because some senior leaders with feudal mindsets and dominating groups did not want new faces to emerge,” said a senior Congress leader, requesting anonymity.
The BJP welcomed the move to resume college elections, but offered a different reason for why the practice was stopped.
“At the time (1980s), the Congress was strong and in power. But it was also the time that the ABVP (Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad) was winning college elections and Congress did not want the BJP to gain out of this,” N. Ravi Kumar, BJP MLC and Opposition chief whip in the Karnataka legislative council, told ThePrint.
“This is why they banned student elections,” added Kumar, who served as president of Government B.Ed College in Chitradurga in 1989.
There is also a perception that the decision by the government will help revive the sagging fortunes of the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI), Congress’s student wing, in Karnataka, which has ceded space to the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh-backed ABVP and other left-leaning groups in recent years, political leaders say.
Under the new system, student bodies will have one student president, two vice presidents, one general secretary, two joint secretaries and six executive committee members.
Parameshwara said that of the two vice president posts and two joint secretary posts, one each would be reserved for women, as would two positions on the executive committee.
The latest version of these elections will have gender-based reservations, not caste-based ones. “We consciously wanted to keep caste and religion away from students,” the deputy CM said.
However, people aware of the developments say more changes or tweaks are expected, as colleges and universities are yet to embrace this idea.
Parameshwara said that it is up to the students to decide if they want elections or not and the management must act accordingly.
Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi had approved the restart of these elections in July last year, ThePrint had reported.
Also Read: From footpaths to garbage: Minister Gowda faces Bengaluru’s tangled web of civic crises and politics
‘Colleges became hotbed of violence’
For decades, elections in colleges and universities were one of the few avenues for youngsters to enter politics.
Nationally, leaders like Arun Jaitley, Sitaram Yechury, Lalu Prasad Yadav, Ananth Kumar, Ajay Maken and Ashok Gehlot, among others, all came up through student movements.
In Karnataka, Shivakumar, incumbent state Congress president B.K. Hariprasad, legislative council chairperson Saleem Ahmed, Ramalinga Reddy, N. Ravi Kumar of the BJP and several others from the state have risen through student politics.
In the 1970s and 1980s, student elections in several parts of Karnataka, especially Bengaluru, frequently turned violent.
“Threats, intimidation, ragging, and even murders have taken place between rival gangs in colleges at the time. Noted rowdies like Kotwal Ramachandra and Jairaj, among others, were all linked to college elections where students used to identify with these rowdies to seek votes and inflict fear and violence on campuses,” B.B. Ashok Kumar, a retired Assistant Commissioner of Police, told ThePrint.
He said that the popular Kannada movie Om, starring Shivarajkumar, which gained cult status over time, was based on the life of a student who was chased and murdered near Bengaluru’s Kurubara Hostel locality in the early 1980s.
This storyline has become a genre of sorts in the Kannada movie industry, with several former and reformed criminal elements now recounting their roles during such elections as well as the larger underworld-student nexus in Bengaluru.
Several people familiar with that period said that these college campuses became recruiting grounds for the underworld, which would often get involved in student-related issues, including backing candidates during elections.
Shivakumar himself has mentioned the influence of rowdy elements during college elections during his time in Bengaluru’s Sri Jagadguru Renukacharya College of Science, Arts and Commerce, or RC College.
He has denied having any links with these anti-social elements, reiterating that he has come up through the ranks of the Congress-affiliated National Students Union of India or NSUI.
Hariprasad, who served as president of Bengaluru’s MES College in 1973-74, said that restarting college elections is a good way to bring youngsters into mainstream politics.
He, however, delinked the party’s outreach to Gen Z with the latest announcement.
“Gen Z engagement is just about three months old. I have been trying to restart college elections for the past two years. College elections will not be fought under any party banner. They will be independent,” he said.
(Edited by Sugita Katyal)

headline: 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi focused on cooperation and sustainability.
full_text:
18th Brics Summit in New Delhi focused on cooperation and sustainability.
Brics has evolved from an economic concept to a global governance platform.
Recent expansion includes six new members, strengthening its influence.
New Delhi will play host to the 18th Brics Summit
The 18th Brics Summit is set to take place in New Delhi on September 12-13, bringing together leaders of the expanded grouping at a time when wars, trade tensions and a shifting global order are testing its ability to act as a united bloc.India is hosting the summit as the current Brics chair, with the grouping now comprising 11 members and 10 partner countries.Under the theme âBuilding for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability,â New Delhi has placed greater focus on cooperation across economic and financial issues, technology, energy, development and global governance.The scale of that transformation becomes clearer when traced back to the origins of Brics, a term coined 25 years ago by a Goldman Sachs economist to describe four emerging economies that he believed would become major drivers of global growth.From a Wall Street acronym to a global groupingTwenty-five years ago, Brics did not exist as a political grouping. It was a term coined by Goldman Sachs economist Jim OâNeill in 2001 to describe Brazil, Russia, India and China as emerging economies that could become major drivers of global growth.His paper, Building Better Global Economic BRICs, argued that the weight of these economies in the world economy would rise significantly and called for their greater representation in global policymaking forums.
The transition from an economic concept to a government-led grouping began in 2006, when the foreign ministers of Brazil, Russia, India and China met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York. The first summit of their leaders followed in 2009 in Yekaterinburg, Russia, giving the grouping a formal leaders-level platform.The following year, South Africa joined, turning BRIC into Brics and giving the grouping its first member from Africa.The next major transformation came at the 2023 Johannesburg Summit, when Brics agreed to its first large-scale expansion. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE were invited to join from January 1, 2024. Indonesia subsequently became the bloc's 11th full member in January 2025.The expansion also created a partner-country category, allowing a wider group of developing economies to engage with Brics without becoming full members.Why Brics matters in the changing global orderBrics has evolved from a forum focused largely on economic cooperation into a broader platform for emerging and developing economies seeking a greater role in global governance.Its members have repeatedly called for reforms in institutions such as the United Nations and international financial institutions, arguing that the architecture of global governance should better reflect the changing balance of economic power.
Its growing importance is also backed by institutions created by the grouping itself. The New Development Bank, established in 2015, was designed to mobilise resources for infrastructure and sustainable-development projects in Brics and other emerging and developing economies.The bloc's significance has increased further with its expansion. The addition of countries such as Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Indonesia has widened Brics' economic and geographic reach and strengthened its claim to be a platform for the Global South.

headline: TVK announces candidates for Dharapuram, Madurantakam by-polls
full_text:
TVK announces candidates for Dharapuram, Madurantakam by-polls
TVK chief Vijay appealed to his party cadres to work towards securing a historically significant victory for the two party candidates in the by-polls
The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) on Thursday formally announced K Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama as its candidates for the forthcoming by-poll in Tamil Nadu.
In a first communication under the title “Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance’ headed by TVK chief C Joseph Vijay, the party said its deputy general secretary and former MLA K Maragatham Kumaravel would be the candidate for the Madurantakam SC assembly constituency.
Similarly, the party has fielded P Sathyabama who is TVK’s Tiruppur south-east district secretary, as its nominee for the Dharapuram (SC) assembly seat.
Vijay appealed to his party cadres to work towards securing a historically significant victory for the two party candidates in the by-polls.
On Wednesday, TVK and its partners formally adopted the Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance name for the ruling grouping, party leaders said following a coordination committee meeting held at TVK headquarters near Chennai.
The TVK which won the April 23 Assembly polls with 108 of the 234 Assembly polls in Tamil Nadu, formed a post-poll coalition with the Congress, Indian Union Muslim League, and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK).
Tamil Nadu Congress Committee President B Manickam Tagore had said that the candidates under the newly Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance would be formally announced by TVK in a day or two.
The Election Commission of India (ECI) has announced the by-polls for the two assembly segments on October 6 and the results would be declared on October 9, 2026.
By-elections has been necessitated following the resignation of the two MLAs (K Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama) who won under the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) ticket in the April 23 assembly polls in Tamil Nadu.
With TVK emerging victorious in the assembly elections, the two MLAs Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama along with four other AIADMK lawmakers tendered resignation and joined the TVK in May 2026.
The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) has already announced its party candidates for the by-elections, while the AIADMK is expected to announce its nominees in a day or two making it a triangular poll contest in the southern state.

headline: Delhi HC orders mandatory biometric Aadhaar for GST registration
full_text:
Delhi HC orders mandatory biometric Aadhaar for GST registration
Delhi HC directed authorities not to allow GST registrations without biometric Aadhaar authentication, citing fraudulent registrations and tax evasion.
The Delhi high court has directed authorities to make biometric-based Aadhaar authentication mandatory before granting any Goods and Services Tax (GST) registration, citing the continued use of stolen or forged PAN and Aadhaar details to obtain fraudulent registrations.
A bench of Justices Anil Kshetarpal and Shail Jain issued the direction in its September 8 order, noting that the finance minister had informed the Rajya Sabha that 2,800 fraudulent GST registrations were obtained using stolen or forged PAN/Aadhaar details in 2023-24, involving detection of ₹15,085 crore in tax evasion. In 2024-25, 1,654 such fraudulent registrations were detected, involving tax evasion of ₹13,109 crore.
The bench further noted that, although biometric Aadhaar-based authentication had been made mandatory for GST registration, more than a year had passed since the minister’s statement in Parliament and the measure had not been fully implemented. Fake GST registrations using stolen or forged PAN and Aadhaar details continued to be obtained.
“Minister of State in the Ministry Of Finance, while answering the question on fraudulent GST Registration has disclosed in the Rajya Sabha that in the year 2023-2024, there were 2800 fraudulent GST Registrations obtained by using stolen or frozen PAN/ AADHAR details involving detection of Rs.15,085 Crores of tax evasion. In the year 2024-2025, the number of fraudulent GST Registrations were 1654 and tax evasion of Rs.13109 Crores was detected. It was disclosed that biometric AADHAR based authentication has been made mandatory for the GST Registration. It appears that despite passage of more than one year, the statement given by the minister on the floor of the house has not been fully implemented, resulting in continuous fake GST Registration obtained using stolen or frozen PAN/ AADHAR details,” the court said.
It added, “Hence, for the time being, directions are issued to all the authorities across the country not to allow any GST Registration without biometric based AADHAR authentication henceforth.”
The court passed the order in a petition filed by a woman who alleged that fraudulent GST registrations had been created by third parties using her PAN and Aadhaar details, resulting in the siphoning off of over ₹4.46 crore from her savings account with Punjab National Bank.
It was her case that, upon inquiry, the bank informed her that it had received a purported GST notice seeking payment of the said amount to a GST authority. She lodged complaints with the concerned GST authorities in March 2026. However, after no action was taken, she approached the high court seeking directions for an effective investigation.
The Centre and GST authorities had maintained that biometric-based Aadhaar authentication is carried out only if the system identifies the case as ‘risky’ on the basis of various parameters and data analytics.
The matter will be next heard on September 22.

headline: Abhishek Banerjee's PA Sumit Roy arrested by CID in Salboni land grab case
full_text:
Abhishek Banerjee's PA Sumit Roy arrested by CID in Salboni land grab case
Sumit Roy's arrest came after the the Supreme Court on Thursday refused to grant him an anticipatory bail in the land grab case.
The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) on Thursday arrested Sumit Roy, the personal assistant of Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee, in connection with an alleged land-grabbing case.
The arrest came hours after a Supreme Court bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana dismissed Roy’s anticipatory bail plea and lifted its interim order protecting him from arrest.
“We have arrested Sumit Roy from 121 Kalighat Road. Investigation is going on,” said a senior CID officer.
Also read: Sonam Wangchuk threatens fresh agitation from Sept 19 to 24 over Ladakh issues
Roy was taken into custody from the Kalighat residence of Banerjee, who is on a visit to the United States of America for eye treatment. Last month, Banerjee was granted permission to travel abroad for three weeks for the treatment.
Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, who also holds the home portfolio, announced Roy’s arrest in the state assembly, describing him as a "well-known extortionist".
Investigation in land grab case
The West Bengal police started investigating Roy in June after former TMC legislator Sujoy Hazra, who had been arrested days earlier, accused the TMC leader’s aide of involvement in the sale of large tracts of government land in West Midnapore’s Salboni based on fabricated documents.
On June 13, the state police also carried out a mid-night.

At 2 am on June 13, a large police contingent turned up at Banerjee’s Kalighat Road residence to look for Roy after his phone number was allegedly found to be active in the area. They were able to enter the house only four hours later when the Kolkata Police’s disaster management group was called in to break open the locks.
Roy later moved the Calcutta high court to seek protection from arrest. When the plea was rejected on August 3, he moved the Supreme Court.
The top court stayed Roy's arrest and directed him to appear for interrogation and cooperate with the investigation.
Police had questioned Roy for more than 80 hours in the past ten days but insisted that he was not cooperating.

In a video message, TMC spokesperson Anirban Banerjee said the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party had stopped to the lowest possible level of revenge politics.
“The arrest comes at a time when Banerjee is out of his residence and the country and is undergoing eye treatment. He has gone there with the Supreme Court’s permission. His family is residing at the residence. The BJP has stooped to the lowest possible filthy level of revenge politics. They are targeting the family of the MP. We strongly condemn this,” the TMC spokesperson said.

headline: Mayawati said Akash Anand, the BSP's national coordinator, would continue to work in the party. (File Photo)
full_text:
Mayawati said Akash Anand, the BSP's national coordinator, would continue to work in the party. (File Photo)
NEW DELHI: Three promotions. Three demotions. And now staring at a possible exit!Well, thatâs how the political scorecard reads for Akash Anand, whose âmaturity meterâ has not just failed him again, but has also put him on the brink of exit from the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP).7 days after his third demotion, Akash Anand finds himself in a difficult spot, with BSP chief Mayawati opening the doors for his exit from the party. "The people in the party feel that just as he was relieved of all the important responsibilities of the post of national coordinator on September 3, 2026, he should now also be completely freed from the party from today. Therefore, if Akash Anand wants to remain independent in the party, he is free to do so; that is, he has now been completely freed from the party," Mayawati posted on X.This despite the fact that Akash Anand's father-in-law, former Rajya Sabha MP Ashok Siddharth on Thursday bowed before Mayawati's ultimatum and announced his retirement from politics and social life, after the BSP chief linked his "sanyas" to any future reinstatement of responsibilities to her nephew Akash Anand.In an emotional post on X, Siddharth said he was retiring from political and social life "right now", adding that if he ever had to give his life for Mayawati, it would be a matter of pride for him.
FIL bends but Mayawati refuses to budge
But neither Siddharth's actions nor his words made any impact on Mayawati.She questioned Siddharth's intentions, saying his "announcement should have come immediately after her call for him to retire." Mayawati alleged that the delay showed that Siddharth's ambitions and intentions had not changed completely.
Akash Anand's on-off jouney with BSP.
"If Ashok Siddharth had even a little genuine concern for the bright future of his son-in-law Akash Anand and the larger interests of the BSP and its Ambedkarite Bahujan movement, he would have announced his retirement without delay," she said.Mayawati also slammed Anand for not reposting her earlier X post linking his future responsibilities in the party to his father-in-law's retirement. She said Anand had earlier reposted posts from her social media account "to demonstrate his loyalty," but had not done so in this case despite the post being in his own interest.Mayawati said this indicated that both Siddharth and Anand were more attached to personal and family interests than to the success of the party and its movement.She questioned whether Anand could effectively serve the BSP while remaining caught between his family ties and the interests of the party."If Akash Anand is less concerned about the real interests of the party and the movement and his own political career, and more attached to family relationships, then it is natural to ask how he can work for the good of the BSP and the movement while remaining double-minded," she said.
Third time unlucky?
Akash Anandâs latest demotion was on September 3, when aunt Mayawati announced that her nephew had again lost his political maturity."I have allowed Akash Anand to work in the party, which is before all of you, but Akash Anand still needs to become more mature. Till then, it would not be appropriate to give him a major responsibility in the party," Mayawati said at a national-level meeting of BSP office-bearers.And that ensured Akash Anand, the chief national coordinator of BSP, was back to square one. His Twitter bio reflected the sudden change in his status within the party. From BSP "National Convenor", he became "Party Worker, BSP." Just a few days later, he made yet another edit to his bio, which read: "Party Supporter, BSP." This is how his X bio reads now.It was less than a month back, August 10 to be exact, that Akash Anand had formally launched the BSPâs election campaign for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections from Sadabad assembly constituency in Hathras. He addressed a well-attended rally and launched a broadside against the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh over jobs, education and law and order, while taking digs at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, calling them both âuncle.âFrom being anointed Mayawatiâs successor to being a party worker and now a party supporter - it has been a tumultuous and bumpy ride for the young Akash Anand. And this time around there is a twist in the tale: Akashâs younger brother Ishan Anand has been brought to the centre stage.On September 3, when Mayawati entered the venue of the meeting of office-bearers, walking behind her was not Akash but his younger brother Ishan. Wearing the BSP's blue sash around his neck, he stood behind his aunt till she settled down.Akash Anand entered politics in 2017 at the young age of 22. Anand, who did his MBA from London, made his political debut with Mayawati at a rally in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur, where he shared the dais with Akhilesh Yadav and Ajit Singh.In April 2019, Akash Anand addressed his first rally in Uttar Pradesh's Agra. The BSP was then part of the opposition Mahagathbandhan, an anti-Congress and anti-BJP bloc formed in the run-up to the 2019 general election under the leadership of Akhilesh Yadav and Mayawati with Ajit Singh's Rashtriya Lok Dal.Mayawati appointed him BSPâs national coordinator in June 2019. Since then, it has been a bumpy ride for him. Every promotion since then has been followed by a demotion.
Anand's FIL connection and maturity question
After 6 days of suspense, Mayawati finally revealed what triggered her against Akash Anand yet again. In a long post on X, Mayawati explained how Akash Anand had once again, after two years, lost his âpolitical maturity.â And also, what he could do to get it back.The trigger this time around was Ashok Siddharth, the father in law of Akash Anand. Ashok Siddharth was expelled by Maywati from BSP last month for the second time over indiscipline and anti-party stance.Taking to X, the BSP supremo wrote: âIt is well known that Ashok Siddharth had previously been expelled for indiscipline and violating guidelines, specifically regarding the distribution of party tickets and a failure to coordinate properly with BSP Maharashtra state president during state elections. He had been reinstated on the condition that he would not repeat such mistakes and would be assigned responsibility of expanding the party's support base only in other states, not in Uttar Pradesh.âShe also informed that Ashok Siddharth will not be taken back into the party âunder any circumstances in the futureâ.Hardening her stand further against Ashok Siddharth, Mayawati stated that a clear path remains for Akash Anand to resume an active leadership role within the movement, provided Siddharth steps aside completely."In such a situation, keeping in mind the interests of the BSP Party and Movement, as well as his own family and the future of his son-in-law Shri Akash Anand, Shri Ashok Siddharth still has the opportunity to renounce his political ambitions, rise above personal interests, etc., and completely retire from politics. Only then will Shri Akash Anand be able to work freely in the party, and only then will the party sympathetically consider restoring his responsibilities so that he can play an active role in the partyâthis is the general consensus in the party," Mayawati said in her post.Urging people from the Dalit community, to not engage in any action driven by personal or familial interests that creates obstacles in their path, for which âhistory may not forgive them," Mayawati cited Ashok Siddharth as a prime example of an official prioritising "personal and familial interests and ambitions over the BSP's mission, despite receiving multiple opportunities to reform."The party gave him not just one but several opportunities to mend his ways, but he prioritised his personal and familial interests and ambitions over the BSP's mission, the consequences of which he himself, along with his son-in-law Shri Akash Anand, has had to bear," Mayawati said in her statement.
Can BSP afford this 'family drama'?
With the UP assembly elections just months away, a family drama is the last thing that the BSP cadres in the state would have hoped for. The partyâs trajectory in the state has been downhill. In the 2022 assembly elections, the BSP could win just 1 seat with a vote share of 12.88%. This was a sharp decline from the 19 seats and a 22.23% vote share that Mayawati had got in 2017.The 2024 Lok Sabha elections went on to showcase that Mayawatiâs dismal 2022 performance was not an aberration. The BSP supremo failed to win even one Lok Sabha seat, while her partyâs vote share dipped to 9.4% from 19.43% in 2019. Clearly, the results reinforced the gradual decline in BSPâs influence among Dalits.From a sweeping majority in 2007 to allegations of being the B-team of BJP, the BSPâs political fortunes have nosedived in the state. The BSP supporters have dwindled and some have even changed loyalties, but what remains still strong is Mayawatiâs appeal and popularity among the partyâs cadres.
However, the 2027 challenge is going to be tough for Maywati and her BSP. The SP-Congress alliance managed to garner a lot of Dalit support in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, upsetting BJPâs applecart in the state and eventually at the Centre. Cleary this was not the time when the BSP chief should have precipitated action against Akash Anand and pitched one nephew against the other.Mayawati needs a strong comeback and to ensure that she has to first set her house in order. All the more, as she has announced that BSP will not enter into any alliance in future elections. The BSP needs to perform if Mayawati wants to remain relevant in the stateâs politics. Another poor show where she wins votes but not seats will reinforce allegations that BSP is the B-team of the BJP.

headline: After Mayawati's diktat, nephew Akash Anand's father-in-law announces retirement from politics
full_text:
After Mayawati's diktat, nephew Akash Anand's father-in-law announces retirement from politics
Lucknow, Former Rajya Sabha member Ashok Siddharth on Thursday announced his retirement from politics and social life, a day after BSP chief Mayawati linked his retirement to any future reinstatement of responsibilities to her nephew and his son-in-law Akash Anand.
In an emotional post on X, Siddharth said he was retiring from political and social life "right now", adding that if he ever had to give his life for Mayawati, it would be a matter of pride for him.
"Mayawati's order is greater than anything else in the world for me," Siddharth said, adding that he had been dedicated to the BSP's mission for the past 35 years and had tried to discharge every responsibility assigned to him to the best of his ability.
Siddharth said all relationships were insignificant before Mayawati's order.
"You made a small worker like me a member of your family. This is a debt I cannot repay in this lifetime," he said.
Siddharth also swore by Gautam Buddha and his political mentor Kanshi Ram that he had never worked against the interests of the BSP.
Referring to Mayawati's allegation that he had tried to influence Anand, Siddharth said he had not even met his son-in-law for several months, let alone advised him.
He alleged that some party colleagues accused him of wanting to take control of the BSP and trying to mislead Anand because of the respect Mayawati had shown him, but asserted there was "not the slightest truth" in the allegations.

headline: Stalin snipes at Vijay over body-shaming row: You're right, my jaw was fractured
full_text:
Stalin snipes at Vijay over body-shaming row: You're right, my jaw was fractured
MK Stalin told Vijay that the scars from his Emergency-era torture still remain and urged him to respect the dignity of the Chief Minister's office.
DMK president MK Stalin on Thursday launched a sharp counterattack on Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay over his reference to Stalin’s Emergency-era imprisonment and the alleged torture he suffered under MISA Act, recounting his arrest and saying the scars of the brutal treatment he endured in prison remain with him even today.
The controversy began during a debate on police department grants in the Assembly, where Vijay accused the DMK of repeatedly invoking its MISA-era struggles to deflect allegations of present-day corruption. While referring to Stalin’s detention under the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA) during the Emergency, Vijay made a gesture involving his jaw, which Opposition members saw as a mockery of Stalin’s prison injury.
Responding to the controversy in a video message, Stalin urged Vijay to maintain the dignity expected of the occupant of the state’s highest constitutional office.
"Brother Vijay, what you said is true. There is no lie in it," Stalin said, referring to his imprisonment under MISA.
The former Chief Minister then gave a graphic account of what he described as the brutality he suffered in prison.
"I suffered many forms of torture in prison," he said, alleging that political prisoners were taken to a facility where leprosy patients had previously been housed.
"Ten people were confined in a small room. Inside that room, all of us had to urinate in a single vessel. The place was extremely filthy. That was where we slept," Stalin said.
He alleged that prisoners were beaten at night with lathis and kicked with boots, while life convicts were allegedly brought in to assault them.
Stalin said DMK leader and former parliamentarian Chitti Babu died in prison following the alleged assaults.
He also directly addressed Vijay’s gesture in the Assembly, where the Chief Minister had held his jaw while referring to Stalin’s MISA imprisonment.
"My jawbone was fractured because of the beatings. You too showed your jaw by placing your hand there, didn't you? That was correct," Stalin said.
"Even today, I have scars from the beatings. I am not denying that," he added.
Stalin also recalled how he was arrested during the Emergency.
He said the DMK government headed by his father and former Chief Minister M Karunanidhi was dismissed by the Union government on January 31, 1976, during the Emergency, after Karunanidhi had opposed the Emergency and strongly criticised MISA.
Stalin said that immediately after the government was dismissed, police went to the Karunanidhi residence in Gopalapuram to arrest him under MISA.
"I was not at home that day. Kalaignar told them, 'The boy has gone for campaigning. He will return tomorrow. Once he comes, I myself will call you. You can come and arrest him,'"Stalin recalled.
He said that when he returned the next day, Karunanidhi himself asked the police to come and arrest him.
Stalin said the repression faced by political activists during the Emergency was part of the broader history of the DMK and those who had fought for Tamil Nadu.
"Opposing something and facing the consequences of that opposition is nothing new to us," he said.
He challenged Vijay to verify his account through official records.
"You said there is a library in the Legislative Assembly, didn’t you? All the documents are available there. Go there and read about my history of struggle. You will understand what the truth is," Stalin said.
STALIN QUESTIONS VIJAY'S SARKARIA COMMISSION CLAIMS
Stalin also accused Vijay of providing incorrect information about the Sarkaria Commission and corruption allegations involving the Karunanidhi government.
He questioned why no action had been taken against those accused if the allegations had substance.
"After the Sarkaria Commission was constituted, governments changed several times at both the Union and state levels. If any of these allegations had been true, action would certainly have been taken," Stalin said.
He accused Vijay of repeating what he described as politically motivated allegations against Karunanidhi and also criticised the Chief Minister for citing an Enforcement Directorate letter in the Assembly.
Stalin claimed that "95 per cent" of cases in which the ED had made allegations had not resulted in convictions and alleged that the agency was frequently used for political vendetta.
"Everyone here knows very well that the Enforcement Directorate is largely used for political vendetta," he said.
Pointing to cases involving Congress leaders, Stalin asked how Vijay could remain unaware of the issue while portraying the Union government as an ideological adversary.
'ASSEMBLY HAS DIGNITY AND HONOUR'
Stalin then urged Vijay to focus Assembly debates on issues concerning Tamil Nadu rather than personal and political controversies.
"The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly has its own dignity and honour," he said and urged the Chief Minister to discuss law and order, welfare schemes, development and the protection of Tamil Nadu's rights.
"That is what is good for Tamil Nadu and the Tamil people," Stalin said, adding that unnecessary controversies should not be raised in the House.
Stalin also recalled Vijay's visit to his residence after becoming Chief Minister, claiming that Vijay had apologised for criticising him during the election campaign.
"I told you, 'It is okay, brother. I have not taken any of that to heart.' I also told you, Now that you are the Chief Minister of a state, whenever you speak about anyone, speak with that dignity," Stalin said.
He reiterated the message, telling Vijay, "Your words and your body language must reflect the dignity expected of a Chief Minister. We are the examples before the people. Do not forget that."
However, following the backlash over his gesture in the Assembly, Vijay clarified that his body language was not intentional.
The Chief Minister said his body language, which inadvertently came across in between, was not in any way intentional.

headline: India Today's 2018 crypto scam exposé leads to arrest of Amit Lakhanpal in UAE
full_text:
India Today's 2018 crypto scam exposé leads to arrest of Amit Lakhanpal in UAE
Amit Lakhanpal, accused of masterminding the Money Trade Coin scam, has been arrested in the UAE after Indian agencies traced him. The arrest advances extradition efforts in a case exposed by India Today's 2018 undercover investigation.
Eight years after India Today TV's undercover investigation exposed the multi-crore Money Trade Coin (MTC) cryptocurrency scam, the mastermind, Amit Lakhanpal, has been arrested in the UAE, marking a major breakthrough in a case that defrauded investors of more than Rs 113 crore.
Lakhanpal, who fled India in 2018 after the scam came under scrutiny, was arrested on September 1 following efforts by Indian agencies. A Red Notice had been issued against him at the request of the Thane Police. The Enforcement Directorate (ED), which intensified its probe, shared details of Lakhanpal's whereabouts with authorities, leading to his arrest. The Indian government has since initiated the process for his extradition from the UAE and sought case-related details from investigating agencies.
The arrest comes years after India Today's February 2018 special investigation, "Operation Bitcoin", revealed how investors across the country were being lured into a cryptocurrency scheme promising extraordinary returns.
HOW INDIA TODAY EXPOSED THE MTC SCAM
As part of the undercover operation, India Today reporters posed as wealthy investors and visited the Thane office of the Flintstone Group, the company behind Money Trade Coin.
During the sting, company officials and Digamber Jangle, introduced as a senior MTC functionary, claimed investors could earn returns of 10 to 20 times their investment within four to six months. They also promised benefits such as access to escrow accounts and even citizenship of a Caribbean nation for large investors.
Jangle further claimed that MTC was in discussions with the governments of Antigua and Barbuda and could soon be recognised as legal tender in countries in the region.
The investigation uncovered how such claims were being used to entice investors with promises of quick riches and a lavish lifestyle.
FIR REGISTERED AFTER EXPOSE
Following the India Today investigation, the Thane Police registered an FIR in June 2018 against Flintstone Group owner Amit Lakhanpal and his associates. By then, however, Lakhanpal had already left the country.
Then Thane Crime Branch officer Nitin Thakre had confirmed that cases were registered against Jangle and others linked to the operation. Investigators had also examined allegations that certain police personnel may have had connections to the racket.
At the time, then Thane Police Commissioner Param Bir Singh publicly acknowledged India Today's role in bringing the alleged fraud to light.
ED PROBE REVEALS WIDER FRAUD NETWORK
The ED, in a statement issued on August 20, 2026, said its investigation stemmed from the FIR filed by Thane City Police against Amit Madanlal Lakhanpal, Taha Hafiz Qazi, Sachin Vasant Shelar, Komal Bhimrao Shirsath and others.
According to the agency, investors were induced to invest in the unregulated cryptocurrency between August 2017 and April 2018, resulting in losses of around Rs 113.10 crore.
The ED alleged that Lakhanpal organised seminars in Delhi, Pune and Nashik, falsely portraying himself as a Finance Ministry official and assuring investors that MTC would receive government recognition. He promised substantial returns on investments and projected the scheme as a legitimate financial opportunity.
Investigators also found that several related platforms and exchanges, including Coin Deposit Ratio, MTC Banque, MTCX India and Cryptozaniya, were launched as part of the operation. The agency alleged that MTC coin prices were manipulated and that trading and withdrawal facilities were later suspended, leaving investors unable to access their funds.
ACCUSED ESCAPED USING CARIBBEAN PASSPORTS
The ED claimed that Lakhanpal and his associates fled India after obtaining passports from Antigua and Barbuda and were living in Dubai under assumed identities.
Searches conducted by the agency last month resulted in the seizure of nearly Rs 1 crore in cash, along with digital devices and documents that investigators believe are linked to the alleged money laundering network.
With Lakhanpal now in custody in the UAE, Indian authorities are pushing ahead with extradition proceedings in a case that first came to light through India Today's 2018 undercover investigation.

headline: Stalin hits back at Vijay amid Assembly gesture row: ‘Posting reels, running admin like cinema’
full_text:
Stalin hits back at Vijay amid Assembly gesture row: ‘Posting reels, running admin like cinema’
MK Stalin's response came two days after CM Vijay clarified that a gesture he made while referring to MISA in the Assembly was “not in any way intentional”.
Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay “must not talk about unnecessary controversies in the Assembly,” DMK president MK Stalin said on Thursday.
The former chief minister fired back after Vijay brought up the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA) during recent Assembly proceedings. He also accused the actor-turned-politician of using social media reels and publicity to cover-up his administrative failures.
Addressing the CM as “Thambi [brother] Vijay”, Stalin said his Emergency-era struggle was part of the DMK’s history. “History can never be changed,” the DMK leader said.
“You [CM Vijay] turned the Assembly itself into a place where reels happen, standing on the bridge we built and doing photoshoots," Stalin said in a video posted to X. "You are running the administration also, just like a cinema shooting. To hide your inefficient administration, you are posting various reels like this and cheating a whole generation,” he added.
Stalin's remarks came two days after Vijay clarified that a hand gesture he made while referring to MISA in the Assembly was “not in any way intentional”. The gesture, in which Vijay placed his hand near his jaw, was widely interpreted as a reference to Stalin's jaw injury during his detention in 1976.
‘Police came to arrest me’
Stalin said the DMK held a major gathering at Marina Beach in 1976 to oppose the Emergency and criticise MISA. He recalled that police then went to the Karunanidhi residence in Gopalapuram to arrest him under MISA. Stalin said he was away campaigning at the time.
“The Union Government that was in power at that time, on 31st January 1976, dismissed the DMK government. The very next second after dismissing the government, police came to the Gopalapuram house to arrest me under the MISA Act,” he said in his video.
Veteran leader M Karunanidhi told the police that his son had gone campaigning and would return the next day, according to Stalin. He then asked them to come back and arrest Stalin after he returned.
“When I came, he himself called the police and asked them to arrest me,” Stalin said, recounting the incident.
Stalin was later detained under MISA. His imprisonment during the Emergency has long been cited as a major episode in his political career. Several senior DMK leaders, including Stalin, Murasoli Maran and Chitti Babu, were reportedly detained and allegedly subjected to custodial violence.
‘My jaw was broken, you showed this’
Stalin also described the conditions he said he faced in prison. Detainees were kept in an extremely unhygienic room and subjected to repeated beatings by police and other prisoners, he said.
He said he suffered injuries to his jaw and still carried scars from the alleged assaults.

The ex-CM also recalled the death of former Madras mayor and DMK leader Chitti Babu, who died after being beaten in prison. He previously said Chitti Babu took blows meant for him during his incarceration.
“Due to their beating, my dear brother, Member of Parliament Chitti Babu, died inside the jail itself. Due to their beating, my jawbone was broken. You also showed it like this, keeping your hand near the jaw, right? That is correct. Even today, I have the scars of the beatings I received. I am not saying no,” Stalin said.
‘Proud to be part of DMK history’
Stalin said his imprisonment was part of the DMK’s ideological history dating back to party founder CN Annadurai (also known as Perarignar Anna).
“You say you are an ideological leader. From the time of Perarignar Anna, this is the history of the DMK. That I am also part of that history is a matter of pride for me,” he said.

He asked Vijay to verify this through official records. “If you have any doubts…Go and read my history of struggle. You will understand what the truth is,” Stalin said.
Stalin on Sarkaria Commission allegations
Stalin also hit back at Vijay’s references to the Sarkaria Commission and allegations against Karunanidhi. Vijay earlier cited the commission while making corruption allegations against the DMK government and referred to alleged irregularities in tenders and commissions.
Stalin said several governments had changed at the Centre and in Tamil Nadu since the commission was set up. If the allegations had merit, he said, action would have been taken.

Stalin accused Vijay of repeating allegations made against Karunanidhi out of “political vendetta”. He also criticised the chief minister for citing an Enforcement Directorate letter to level corruption allegations against DMK leaders. Stalin claimed that a large majority of cases filed by the ED had not led to convictions and alleged that the agency was being used for political vendetta.
‘Assembly no place for unnecessary controversies’
Stalin said the Assembly, shaped by several senior leaders, should focus on law and order, welfare, Tamil Nadu’s rights and the state’s development.
“My request is that you should not talk about unnecessary controversies in the Assembly,” Stalin said. He also recalled Vijay’s visit to his home after becoming chief minister.
The ex-CM said Vijay, at the time, told him that he spoke critically about Stalin during the election campaign and apologised.
“I said, it’s okay, brother. I don’t keep all that in my heart,” he said.

Stalin asked that Vijay remember he was now the chief minister and should speak with the dignity expected of the office. “A chief minister’s words and body language should have the dignity of a chief minister. We are the role models for the people. Don’t forget that,” he added.
