headline: NEW DELHI: Taking exception to Centre declaring an "outstanding" Indian Trade Service officer "dead wood" and punishing him with compulsory retirement, Supreme Court Wednesday directed all pecuniary benefits and notional promotions to him be restored...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Taking exception to Centre declaring an "outstanding" Indian Trade Service officer "dead wood" and punishing him with compulsory retirement, Supreme Court Wednesday directed all pecuniary benefits and notional promotions to him be restored and ordered govt to pay him Rs 15 lakh as compensation. S S Das was forced to retire in 2018, five years before his superannuation.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu, which had directed Centre to place dossiers and the annual confidential record of the officer before it, found he was consistently graded as outstanding/very good from 1994 and promoted just months before the punishment. It directed govt to grant Das the honourable farewell he would have been entitled to had he not been forced to retire."The manner of decision-making in course whereof 'OUTSTANDING' gradings are completely ignored, grant of promotion is looked upon as if it were a ministerial exercise, followed by a vague and omnibus finding that it is not desirable in public interest to retain the appellant in service, discloses that the officers entrusted to take a decision were determined to ensure the appellant's ouster at any cost and invented reasons to sustain a pre-decided conclusion," the bench said, calling the exercise "sheer abuse of high offices".
"Having promoted the appellant, barely a couple of months later, the superior officers in the department could not have branded him... 'dead wood' to justify weeding him out. The two actions are mutually destructive and cannot co-exist," it said.
SC said the action demolished the reputation of an officer which was uncalled for. It directed that Das be called to the office by the director general of foreign trade for a farewell with full honours."It must be remembered by all and sundry that reputation is not built overnight. It is built by years of dedicated and selfless service. It comes at a great cost, often at the cost of family life and personal comfort. Such a reputation earned by sweat and toil over decades can, however, be marred by a single stroke of a pen," the bench said.SC said FR 56(j) - which gives Centre the right to prematurely retire a govt servant - should not be exercised lightly or in a casual manner. "It must be founded on material which is credible, cogent and worthy of being acted up-on, and not on mere suspicion and conjecture," it added.

headline: Lucknow: As the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections draw closer, the Samajwadi Party (SP) is tweaking its political strategy with a new visual identity. The party has decided on a new dress code for its student wing, the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha, wi...
full_text:
Lucknow: As the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections draw closer, the Samajwadi Party (SP) is tweaking its political strategy with a new visual identity. The party has decided on a new dress code for its student wing, the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha, with blue set to become a prominent colour.
Under the new dress code, members of the student wing will wear blue T-shirts with red caps. Until now, the organisation had no formal dress code, although its members were often seen wearing red Gandhi-style caps.
SP president Akhilesh Yadav was recently seen wearing a blue scarf instead of the party’s traditional red and green at a meeting of district and city presidents.
Party functionaries see the move as part of a broader attempt to expand the party’s appeal among Dalit youth. Dalits are an important component of the party’s PDA—Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak (backward classes, Dalits and minorities)—strategy.
The choice of T-shirts and red caps, instead of the traditional kurta-pyjama and Gandhi caps, is also being seen as an attempt to connect with Gen Z. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has attracted considerable attention in recent years for wearing T-shirts in public appearances.
The change in Akhilesh’s colour choices is, therefore, being viewed as more than an organisational decision. It is being interpreted as an effort to improve the SP’s acceptability among Dalit youth and expand its presence among students in colleges and universities.
Blue carries particular political significance in Uttar Pradesh. It has long been associated with Dalit politics and the ideology of Dr B.R. Ambedkar. The Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), which has historically represented Dalit politics in the state, has prominently used blue in its flags and political imagery. The SP, by contrast, has traditionally been identified with red and green.
Akhilesh said the colour blue represents the Constitution.
“Blue is the colour of the Constitution, freedom and democracy. It has been associated with the Bahujan community and Babasaheb. It is the colour of an ideology. The new generation has a new way of thinking. So we have chosen a new colour,” he told media persons.
However, the change will be limited to the student wing. The uniforms and visual identity of the SP’s other organisational wings will remain unchanged.
Akhilesh also spoke about student union elections and said that if the SP came to power, it would constitute a committee to examine the future of student politics. He said universities in Cambridge, Oxford and the European Union would be approached for possible tie-ups and exchanges.
The SP’s PDA formula, he said, stood for “Positive, Democratic and Affirmative action”.
Taking a swipe at the BJP, Akhilesh alleged that BJP people are afraid of colours but not of God. “They have stolen donations from Prabhu Ram’s temple and have now looted the Ram Van Gaman Path. The BJP is running a negative campaign,” he said.
Also Read: The other nephew rises: Mayawati hands key BSP position to Ishan Anand days after removing Akash
From red and green, to blue and red
A senior SP leader said red and green had been the party’s official colours since its formation on 4 October, 1992. However, the party was now looking to expand its visual symbolism.
“Blue is a powerful symbol of Dalit assertion. The SP has formulated a strategy to increase its reach among young people and Dalits ahead of next year’s Assembly elections,” the leader said.
The change has been particularly evident within the party’s student wing.
The Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha is preparing to adopt a more contemporary look, with members expected to wear blue T-shirts and jeans, or shirts and trousers in similar shades.
The move is being positioned within the party as an attempt to create a distinct identity for its student activists and connect with Gen Z.
Party strategists believe the decision to introduce blue is also aimed at making the student wing more appealing to Gen Z, which forms a large part of its membership.
This is not the first time the SP has experimented with blue. On 31 August, during a meeting of district and city presidents from across Uttar Pradesh, Akhilesh Yadav, national general secretary Shivpal Yadav and other senior leaders were seen wearing blue scarves featuring the party’s bicycle symbol in red.
The blue scarves were markedly different from the red and green scarves traditionally associated with the party and the red checkered gamchas used during the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign.
When asked about the significance of the blue scarves at the time, party functionaries had avoided giving a clear explanation.
Party leaders now say blue symbolises the vast open sky, under which everyone is equal and free from caste-based discrimination.
But the colour also has a strong association with Ambedkarite and Dalit politics, making its adoption politically significant for a party seeking to strengthen its PDA outreach.
A formal announcement of the new dress code for the Chhatra Sabha is expected to be made at a special programme at the SP headquarters in Lucknow in the coming days.
Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha general secretary Avnish Yadav said the combination of blue and red reflected both the party’s traditional political identity and its outreach to a new generation.
“Red is the colour of revolution, while blue brings new energy. It will help spread the ideas of Babasaheb B.R. Ambedkar among students. Both blue and red fit our PDA formula. We will take these T-shirts to students across the state,” he told ThePrint.
Political observers say colours have long carried ideological and electoral significance in Indian politics. Saffron is closely associated with the BJP, red with the Left, while blue has become strongly identified with Ambedkarite politics.
Professor Kaviraj, a political science faculty at Lucknow University, said the SP’s decision appeared to be a deliberate political strategy.
“Every colour has its own significance in politics. Saffron is associated with the BJP, red with the Left and blue with Ambedkarites. SP leaders have traditionally been seen wearing red caps. The combination of blue and red that the party is now introducing also appears to be part of a political strategy,” he said.
He added that there was nothing unusual about a political party trying to expand its outreach.
“The question is how far the SP will be able to bring Dalit youth into its fold. It has to compete with the BSP, which remains the traditional political home for many Dalits, as well as an emerging Dalit political option in Chandrashekhar Azad. Winning over the entire community will not be easy, but political parties have to keep making such efforts,’” he told ThePrint.
(Edited by Sugita Katyal)

headline: Ashamed of delays, won't join inauguration: Gadkari on Mumbai-Goa Highway expansion
full_text:
Ashamed of delays, won't join inauguration: Gadkari on Mumbai-Goa Highway expansion
Union Minister Nitin Gadkari said he would not attend the inauguration of the widened Mumbai-Goa Highway after repeated delays. He said he will inspect the route in October and act against contractors and officials over poor execution.
Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari said he felt “ashamed” over the prolonged delays in widening the Mumbai-Goa Highway and announced that he would not attend the inauguration of the project when it is finally completed.
Speaking after inaugurating a six-lane elevated road corridor at Porvorim near Panaji on Wednesday, Gadkari said he had earlier decided against attending the inauguration because of the delay in completing the highway.
“I had announced (earlier) that I would not come for the inauguration of the (widened) Mumbai-Goa highway because I felt ashamed that it had been delayed so much,” he said.
The Union Minister said a meeting on the issue was held with officials on Tuesday and that he would personally inspect the highway in October.
“I would land at the Mumbai airport in October, and travel by road to Goa to personally inspect the highway and assess whether the journey has been made convenient for travellers,” he said.
Gadkari also said he wanted to “set a record” for blacklisting contractors and taking action against officials responsible for delays and poor execution of infrastructure projects.
“Now I want to set a record of blacklisting the maximum number of contractors and taking action against them, as well as suspending officials, within a year. I am not going to stop doing this now,” he said.
The widening of the 440-km Mumbai-Goa Highway has faced repeated delays despite years of work and substantial expenditure, with parts of the recently upgraded stretch developing potholes and surface damage after the first monsoon rains.
The highway continues to see diversions, waterlogging, repairs and traffic jams, even as toll collection began at the Kharpada toll plaza in May.
A monkey overpass built near Kannala Animal Sanctuary in 2021 has also collapsed, raising another safety concern along the route.

headline: New Delhi: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha, attended a memorial gathering organised Thursday for Manipuri musician Chongtham Vikram Singh. Condemning Singh’s killing, Gandhi said the incident reflected “violence, hatred and arroga...
full_text:
New Delhi: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha, attended a memorial gathering organised Thursday for Manipuri musician Chongtham Vikram Singh. Condemning Singh’s killing, Gandhi said the incident reflected “violence, hatred and arrogance,” adding that such behaviour had “become a fashion” these days.
Singh died after he was assaulted outside his residence in Kilokari in southeast Delhi by a group of men for objecting to their loud noise on 7 September.
The memorial, organised at the Dr Ambedkar International Centre here, was attended by senior Congress leaders, including Jairam Ramesh and Supriya Shrinate, as well as members of the Manipuri community. Musical performances were also held in Singh’s memory.
Addressing the gathering, Gandhi said, “It’s a tragedy that a young man has been murdered. It’s also a tragedy that he was attacked because of where he was from. It’s a tragedy for the people of Manipur. Of course, it’s not the only tragedy that the people of Manipur have been facing.”
He added, “Whether he (Singh) was killed or was not killed, there was violence in this act. There was violence, there was hatred, and there was arrogance. And it is something that has become a fashion these days, that if you are powerful, you can be violent.”
Watch: A Tribute to Chongtham Vikram Singh | Dr. Ambedkar International Center, Janpath, New Delhi https://t.co/g4XmfmTG0u
— Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) September 10, 2026
Gandhi also said the response to such an incident should not be anger or hatred.
He told the gathering, “So then the question arises: how do you respond to something like this? What I will say is, you don’t respond with anger, you don’t respond with hatred, because then you are doing exactly what was done to Vicky.
“But you respond just the way that you have responded: by expressing yourself, by defending the idea that you stand for, by showing the talent that you have, and by saying that we are not going to accept this nonsense.”
Gandhi also described Singh as a symbol of love and affection. “In politics and in life, symbols matter a lot. He is a symbol of love and affection,” he said.
The Congress leader went on to say that the assault on Singh should also be viewed against the backdrop of incidents involving other communities. “This is not a single incident. It happened every time. Not always does it end up in murder, sometimes there is insult or violence. This is happening with so many communities,” he said.
Singh was a prominent musician from Manipur and had been associated with multiple bands including Ultra Vires, Phoenix and Eastern Dark. He later moved to Delhi, where he had been working as a music teacher.
According to police, he stepped out of his house in Kilokari in southeast Delhi around 11.30 PM Monday to ask a group of men standing on the street to not make loud noises. An argument followed, after which he was allegedly chased into the building and assaulted. Singh’s son took him to the hospital where the musician died the following morning.
Delhi Police have arrested eight men in connection with the incident, and are investigating whether there was a racial angle to the assault.

headline: New Delhi: Former MP Madhu Goud Yaskhi has been appointed the new chairperson of the All India Professionals’ Congress (AIPC), replacing Rajya Sabha MP Praveen Chakravarty who held the post since November 2023.
full_text:
New Delhi: Former MP Madhu Goud Yaskhi has been appointed the new chairperson of the All India Professionals’ Congress (AIPC), replacing Rajya Sabha MP Praveen Chakravarty who held the post since November 2023.
In a brief press release signed by Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal, the party thanked Chakravarty for his contributions. The Congress’s decision to replace Chakravarty as the AIPC chairperson comes three months after his elevation to the Rajya Sabha in June.
Yaskhi’s appointment marks a shift from a data and analytics-focused leader to a politician with electoral and organisational experience, giving the AIPC a more visible political face.
Chakravarty was among the Congress leaders who had explored a possible alliance with actor-turned-politician Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) ahead of the Tamil Nadu elections.
Congress President Shri @kharge has appointed Shri Madhu Goud Yaskhi as the Chairperson of the All India Professionals' Congress, with immediate effect. pic.twitter.com/9udpOrWoYu
— Congress (@INCIndia) September 9, 2026
He met Vijay before the polls to explore the possibility of a tie-up, though the Congress remained with its long-standing ally Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), only to finally dump them and join hands with the TVK.
The Rajya Sabha MP’s background, according to a Congress insider, was not the best fit for the role. A data and analytics specialist who has largely worked behind the scenes, he was seen as less suited to a position that requires extensive public engagement and interaction with professionals outside politics.
The source added that Chakravarty failed to make the kind of impact expected from the organisation, particularly when compared with the visibility AIPC had under its first chairperson Shashi Tharoor.
The new AIPC chairperson is a two-time former Lok Sabha MP, has served as a Congress spokesperson and chaired the Telangana Congress Campaign Committee. He is also considered close to Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi.
“With the love, support, and cooperation of all of you, I sincerely wish to work together to strengthen the Congress Party from the state level to the national level and to make Shri Rahul Gandhi Garu the Prime Minister of India.” Yakshi posted on X, responding to a congratulatory message.
Telangana CM Revanth Reddy also took to X to congratulate Yaskhi, saying his experience will help the party deepen its engagement with India’s professional community and bring their expertise into nation-building,” he posted.
Political analyst Chandrachur Singh explained the move was largely an organisational reshuffle following Chakravarty’s elevation to the Rajya Sabha, but added that Yaskhi’s political experience could help the Congress build a stronger connect with professionals.
“Professionally, people don’t take part directly in politics, but they do have their political viewpoints. So I think that might be a reason when you have a political heavyweight heading your organisations and the different branches of it, definitely that gives it a bit of gravitas and it gives them a bit of weight by which they can also bring in these sets of people,” the political science professor of Hindu College explained.
“I think India becoming more urbanised and becoming more market-oriented would mean that these professional sets of people would be brought in, whether they are really able to do that or not is something that only we can see later. But all political parties do that.”
The All India Professionals’ Congress was formally launched in August 2017, with Shashi Tharoor as its first national chairperson. It was created as an AICC organisation to reach out to educated, tax-paying professionals, entrepreneurs and the urban middle class—people who may be interested in politics and policy but are not necessarily drawn to conventional political activity.
(Edited by Tony Rai)

headline: NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi will host a gala dinner for the leaders participating in the Brics summit on Saturday evening, said govt in an announcement Wednesday. The summit will formally begin earlier in the day with Modi welcoming the leaders of Br...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi will host a gala dinner for the leaders participating in the Brics summit on Saturday evening, said govt in an announcement Wednesday. The summit will formally begin earlier in the day with Modi welcoming the leaders of Brics member states at the venue, Bharat Mandapam, and later joining them for a closed session titled Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism.India is hosting the 18th Brics summit on Sept 12-13, exactly 20 years after the grouping that counts 11 major emerging economies as members was formalised. After the session, the leaders will witness the Bharat Innovates exhibition at the summit venue, before congregating on the outside lawns for a Brics family photo. This event will be followed by leaders participating in a joint tree plantation.Modi is also expected to have a formal bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping Saturday in which both leaders will look to consolidate gains from the recent uptick in bilateral ties. Xi had last visited India in 2019 for the Mammalapuram informal summit. A formal announcement by Beijing about Xi's visit was still awaited on Wednesday.Modi's bilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin is scheduled for Friday. The PM is also expected to have a meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. UAE will likely be represented by Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
Bridging bilateral divides over the West Asia situation to secure a unified Brics declaration remains the primary hurdle for India, ahead of the meetings.On Sunday - second day of summit - Modi will welcome leaders of the 10 Brics partner countries, along with other outreach invitees. The leaders will join the final session titled Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth.
The summit will see a renewed call by Modi for a reinvigorated, inclusive and effective multilateral order at a time when the world is faced with complex challenges. As EAM S Jaishankar had said, Brics needs to commit to a reformed multilateralism that reflects contemporary realities - one where institutions like United Nations, WTO, IMF and World Bank are representative and inclusive.

headline: SRINAGAR: National Conference fired a political broadside at ally Congress Wednesday, defending full renditions of Vande Mataram at govt functions in J&K as a âconstitutionalâ duty.Congress objected after all six stanzas of the national song was play...
full_text:
SRINAGAR: National Conference fired a political broadside at ally Congress Wednesday, defending full renditions of Vande Mataram at govt functions in J&K as a âconstitutionalâ duty.Congress objected after all six stanzas of the national song was played at the inauguration of J&Kâs first international film festival in Srinagar attended by CM Omar Abdullah and NC president Farooq Abdullah on Sept 7. As at other official functions, Omar stood at attention throughout.J&K Congress president Tariq Hamid Karra said NC and Congress should respect how the songâs place in Indiaâs national life evolved through both the freedom movement and constitutional journey. âNational symbols, songs and traditions occupy a special place in the heart of every Indian. Their true strength lies in their ability to bind together a nation as diverse as ours,â he said, calling it a concern that alliance partners had chosen to sing the full version.NC countered, asking Congress to look at CMs of states governed by the party, including Telangana and Karnataka, who have participated in full renditions.NC chief spokesperson Tanvir Sadiq shared on X a video featuring Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar at an event where the unabridged song was sung. He said govt protocol must be separated from party ideology. âNC has a clear stand. When Parliament has adopted it, playing Vande Mataram becomes a statutory obligation and that is what govt did,â Sadiq said.
CM Omar later shared Sadiqâs statements on X.A Union home ministry protocol directive in Feb mandated the six-stanza version of the song at all state functions, official events and legislature sessions. In Aug, the President cleared Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, which puts Vande Mataram on a par with the national anthem, making disrespect/disruption a punishable offence. The amended law did not change the stanzas, but people are now obligated to respect Vande Mataram as a constitutional duty.NC spokesperson Imran Nabi Dar said: âThis is a constitutional obligation, and every one holding a constitutional office has to accept it, whether it is the CM, an MP or anyone else,â he said, adding the full version is now regularly played at govt functions across J&K.
Dar acknowledged the objection among Muslims. âThough religiously it is not acceptable to Muslims, it is a constitutional obligation that has to be fulfilled,â he said.The freedom movement broadly adopted first two stanzas of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyayâs 1875 poem, while the full song has six containing religious imagery that has drawn objections from Muslims. Congress general secretary GA Mir said freedom fighters had shaped the version used by the movement with inclusivity in mind.(inputs from PTI)

headline: Mumbai: Days after the the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) called for ban on Muslims attending garba and dandiya events in Maharashtra, Amruta Fadnavis, wife of Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, has said she believes that Navratri celebrations should be ...
full_text:
Mumbai: Days after the the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) called for ban on Muslims attending garba and dandiya events in Maharashtra, Amruta Fadnavis, wife of Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, has said she believes that Navratri celebrations should be inclusive and anyone including Muslims can attend and enjoy it.
On Wednesday, BJP minister Nitesh Rane also supported the ban, but Amruta countered it.
“I feel our festival is inclusive and if a Muslim wants to come and enjoy Garba and Dandiya, I don’t object to it,” she said Wednesday night at Chandrapur.
She further said that those who are opposing it must have their reasons. “I haven’t studied in-depth about it but garba and dandiya are national events and celebrated even internationally, so if anyone from any community or faith wants to come and enjoy and peacefully celebrate it, I think it is alright.”
The VHP’s call for issuing guidelines for garba and dandiya events in Maharashtra and bid to restrict the entry of Muslims have sparked a political row. The RSS affiliate has proposed checking of Aadhar cards at entry and applying of tilaks to prove Hindu identity.
The VHP has argued that these Navratri festival events are more than food and dance, they are about worshipping a deity and since Muslims don’t believe in idol worship, they should not be allowed to attend.
Cabinet minister Nitesh Rane has backed the VHP’s call, saying such events have become breeding grounds for “love jihad” cases.
“If garba and dandiya become the headquarters of love jihad then how can we remain silent? It is the responsibility of VHP and Hindutva activists like us to stop love jihad,” he told the media persons.
Navratri begins on 11 October. The Maharashtra government has not officially commented on the matter so far.
(Edited by Gitanjali Das)

headline: Fifteen workers were rescued after a metal slab collapsed at site under construction in the Kudasan area of Gandhinagar on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) night, Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi said, adding that the debris-clearing operati...
full_text:
Fifteen workers were rescued after a metal slab collapsed at site under construction in the Kudasan area of Gandhinagar on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) night, Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi said, adding that the debris-clearing operation would continue through the night to ensure that no one remained trapped.
Mr. Sanghavi said 12 of the rescued workers were admitted to Gandhinagar Civil Hospital, while three others who did not suffer major injuries were discharged.
“According to the report received just five minutes ago from the Gandhinagar Civil Hospital Superintendent, all 12 individuals currently hospitalised are safe, and none are in critical condition,” he said at the accident site.
The accident occurred around 9 p.m. at the an construction site in the Kudasan area of Gandhinagar when a large metal slab collapsed during ongoing construction work.
According to the Gandhinagar police control room, firefighters, police and the local administration were carrying out rescue operations at the site as labourers claimed that several persons were working on the metal structure and might have been trapped in the debris.
More than four fire brigades rushed to the spot after being alerted about the incident and launched a rescue operation. Ambulances were also deployed to provide immediate medical assistance to those rescued.
"Five persons have been shifted at the hospital for treatment so far. A team of doctors is taking care of them. Some of them have received fractures on their back and on leg. Doctors will take a call if there is need to operate them," Health Minister Praful Pansheriya told reporters at the Gandhinagar Civil hospital.
A firefighter said that a large crane and electric cutters were being used to remove the metal debris and check whether other workers were still trapped underneath.
The exact number of workers trapped under the collapsed metal structure was not immediately clear, officials said.

Gandhinagar Fire Brigade rushed multiple engines and specialised rescue units as ambulances were deployed. By late night, 12 workers had been pulled out and sent for treatment. Teams were still trying to rescue the remaining 10 under the debris.

headline: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) assured that “all parties are treated equally” in the Supreme Court after senior advocate and BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia, appearing for a complainant in a defamation case against ...
full_text:
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) assured that “all parties are treated equally” in the Supreme Court after senior advocate and BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia, appearing for a complainant in a defamation case against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, alleged that the Opposition leader’s matter is being repeatedly adjourned.
The exchange happened during an oral mentioning by Mr. Bhatia to de-tag Mr. Gandhi’s plea against criminal proceedings arising from his alleged remarks concerning the Army and the Chinese attack in the context of the 2020 Galwan clash.
He said the last time the case was listed was in December last year. At the time, the top court had scheduled the next hearing on April 22, 2026. However, the case had not been listed until September 9.
Mr. Bhatia alleged the case was not being listed due to the “person mentioned”, and he should not be treated like a “VVIP”. He said Mr. Gandhi’s side was indulging in “dilatory tactics” to avoid a hearing.
Advocate Prasanna S., for Mr. Gandhi, vehemently objected to the submissions made by Mr. Bhatia, saying that such statements should not be permitted to be made in court.
“All parties are treated equally here,” Chief Justice Kant addressed Mr. Bhatia.
The Bench advised Mr. Bhatia to submit an application for de-tagging of the case.
The court had earlier stayed proceedings against Mr. Gandhi in the case based on a complaint filed by a retired Border Roads Organisation (BRO) officer, Uday Shankar Shrivastava, before a Lucknow Magistrate court in August 2023. The Lucknow court had issued summons to the Congress leader in February 2025.
Mr. Gandhi’s appeal to quash the summons had been declined by the Allahabad High Court in May 2025, compelling Mr. Gandhi to approach the Supreme Court in a special leave petition.

headline: ‘Secure sea lanes, seafarers’: PM Modi’s navigation safety message to BRICS leaders
full_text:
‘Secure sea lanes, seafarers’: PM Modi’s navigation safety message to BRICS leaders
Modi also raised the safety of Indian seafarers in the Black Sea with Russian President Vladimir Putin during the bilateral talks.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi took up the issue of seafarers' safety during the Leaders' Session of BRICS Business Forum on Friday and emphasised on the need to have secure sea lanes. Modi noted that India is a staunch supporter of freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers.
“Global trade progress is possible only when sea lanes are secure, supply routes remain open, and seafarers are safe. That is why India is a staunch supporter of freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers.” Modi said. The remarks come in the backdrop of the West Asia conflict that hit fuel supplies through the Strait of Hormuz route as US and Iran continue to be at loggerheads. Track live updates on BRICS summit
Modi also raised the safety of Indian seafarers in the Black Sea with Russian President Vladimir Putin as the two leaders held bilateral talks. He reiterated India's readiness to support any peace initiative to end the Ukraine conflict even as both leaders agreed to shore up bilateral trade ties amid growing uncertainties and geopolitical upheaval.
Deep Dive
Indians impacted in West Asia war
Two Indian nationals, 31-year-old Rohan Kumar from Bihar's Gopalganj district and 30-year-old Herambh Karmarkar from Pune, were reportedly killed in separate incidents on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz over the past few months amid US-Iran war.
India is the world's third-largest supplier of seafarers, with more than 300,000 sailors working on ships worldwide, according to government data.
Following the killings, India directed shipowners, ship managers and recruitment companies not to deploy Indian seafarers on vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz.
Between March and July, Since March 1, 57 vessels carrying India-bound cargo transited the strait. About 21 of these were India-flagged and 36 foreign-flagged, HT reported earlier.
What Modi said at Leaders' Session
Modi also urged the BRICS Business Council to prepare to identify the top 10 trade barriers among BRICS nations and called for supporting 100 BRICS startups annually to expand into other member markets. He also called for forging 1,000 new partnerships among businesses across BRICS nations and suggested that progress on these three parameters should be reviewed every year.
"As BRICS enters its third decade, I would like to urge the BRICS Business Council: Can you prepare a report on removing the top ten trade barriers among BRICS nations? Can we support 100 BRICS startups annually to scale up in other BRICS markets? Can we forge a thousand new partnerships among our businesses?" PM Modi said.
"We should review our progress on these three parameters every year. Let us transform BRICS' ambitions into action and our collective strength into global solutions. Let BRICS move forward and propel the world forward as well," he added.
The Prime Minister also stressed the importance of secure sea lanes and supply routes for the growth of global trade.
"Global trade progress is possible only when sea lanes are secure, supply routes remain open, and seafarers are safe. That is why India is a staunch supporter of freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers," PM Modi said.
BRICS currently comprises 11 countries including Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the UAE.
According to background information on India's 2026 chairship, BRICS members collectively account for around 49.5 per cent of the global population, 40 per cent of global GDP and 26 per cent of global trade.

Alliance Air's Prayagraj-Delhi flight faces engine snag, lands safely with 44 onboard
One of the engines became inoperative, officials said.
An Alliance Air flight from Prayagraj to Delhi on Friday faced technical snag ahead of landing as one of its engines became inoperative, airport officials said. Following the technical snag, the flight landed safely at the Delhi airport.
Flight 9I 698, operated by Alliance Air and flying an ATR 72 aircraft, had around 40 passengers on board. “The flight declared a full emergency due to one engine being inoperative. All necessary emergency response measures were activated,” an airport official said.
The aircraft landed at the Delhi airport around 2.15 pm, as per information available on flight tracking website Flightradar24.com. However, the airlines said that no emergency was declared.
“On 11 Sept 2026, Alliance Air flight 9I-698 operated by aircraft VT-AIU, was operating on the Bilaspur–Prayagraj–Delhi routing. During the inbound approach to Delhi, the Pilot-in-Command requested a priority landing due to low oil pressure on LH Side engine,” the airlines said in a statement.
On August 28, a Delhi-Bilaspur Alliance Air flight suffered a tyre burst during landing at Bilasa Devi Kevat Airport in Bilaspur, with all 37 passengers and four crew members on board safely evacuated from the aircraft.
Bilasa Devi Kevat Airport Director B Singh said the left tyre of the aircraft burst during landing, following which the aircraft suffered a glitch on the runway. He said the passengers and crew members were deboarded on the runway and subsequently taken safely to the terminal building.
"During landing, the left tyre burst. So, it suffered a glitch on the runway itself. There were 37 passengers and 4 crew members on board. None of them suffered any injuries. Later, they were deboarded on the runway and safely brought to the terminal building. All passengers belonged to Bilaspur," the Airport Director was quoted as saying by news agency ANI.
On Monday, Air India's Dammam-Delhi flight made an emergency landing at Ahmedabad Airport after a crew member found a tissue paper bearing the word "bomb" inside the aircraft's lavatory, PTI reported.
All 32 passengers onboard were safely deboarded at Terminal 2, while security personnel are conducting a thorough check of the aircraft, Ahmedabad Police said.
The aircraft is currently being checked by security agencies as part of precautionary measures, police said.

headline: Congress shifts Rahul Gandhi's Indore event to leased ground after stadium denial
full_text:
Congress shifts Rahul Gandhi's Indore event to leased ground after stadium denial
Congress has secured a leased ground in Indore for Rahul Gandhi's 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' after being denied the stadium. The venue row has triggered a fresh Congress-BJP clash over permissions and political intent.
The Congress has leased an alternative venue in Indore for Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's upcoming 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' programme after it was denied permission to use the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium. An official of the Indore Development Authority said the party paid Rs 10.08 lakh for a temporary lease of 12,000 square metres of land in front of the Regional Park from September 17 to 19.
Congress leaders accused the BJP of delaying permissions because it was nervous about Gandhi's visit, while the BJP dismissed the charge and accused the opposition party of propaganda. The programme, which the Congress says has drawn registrations from around 1.5 lakh students, is now scheduled for September 19.
An Indore Development Authority letter to Indore City Congress Committee president Chintu Chouksey said permission for the event would be issued after the funds were deposited and subject to prescribed conditions. The letter also said the organisers would be responsible for security arrangements at the venue and for obtaining no-objection certificates from the relevant departments.
Talking to PTI, Chouksey said, "We have deposited the agreed amount into the IDA's bank account." He alleged that the BJP government was nervous about Gandhi's upcoming event in Indore and, in that panic, had been harassing the Congress over the venue.
"We initially wanted to hold the event at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on September 12, but after not receiving permission, we had to change the date to September 19. We were made to run around for 10 days for the land located in front of the Regional Park," Chouksey said.
The Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, where the Congress had first sought permission for the event, falls under the municipal corporation. Indore Mayor Pushyamitra Bhargava said that under an old order of the Madhya Pradesh High Court, the stadium can only be used for sports or state-level government events.
BJP state co-media in-charge Alok Dubey said the Congress was indulging in propaganda politics and that the public knows the truth about the party. Taking a jibe at the Congress, he said the name of Gandhi's event should be changed from "Chhatron Ki Goonj" to "Jhooth Ki Goonj." The Congress has named the new venue "Bharat Jodo Maidan".
'Chhatron Ki Goonj' is a student dialogue campaign launched by Gandhi to target the BJP on issues such as question paper leaks, expensive education, irregularities in government recruitment and unemployment. Four editions of the programme have so far been held in Kota, Dehradun, Prayagraj and Pune, with the previous one in Pune on August 22 held for female students. With the Indore venue now secured, the Congress has shifted the event from the stadium to the leased ground in front of the Regional Park.

headline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday (September 11, 2026) met with Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian ahead of the BRICS Summit and called for resolving the ongoing conflict with the United States “through dialogue and diplomacy”. Speaking at a pub...
full_text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday (September 11, 2026) met with Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian ahead of the BRICS Summit and called for resolving the ongoing conflict with the United States “through dialogue and diplomacy”. Speaking at a public event later in the evening, President Pezeshkian said his talks with Mr. Modi will help Iran’s energy and commercial ties with India and referred to Israel and the U.S. as “bullies” and said, “Iran will not be bullied.”
Mr. Modi drew attention to the disruption in the energy supply chain because of the conflict and emphasised the need to ensure freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been caught in a chokehold ever since the U.S.-Israel coalition attacked Iran on February 28. President Pezeshkian, who arrived here earlier in the day for his first visit to India since he took charge in 2024, emphasised “commonalities” between the two sides and called for deeper cooperation.
BRICS Summit 2026 LIVE updates
“Happy to have met Dr. Masoud Pezeshkian, the President of Iran. This visit is more special because it is his first visit to India. We talked about the India-Iran friendship. We believe that we should move forward with a long-term win-win strategy. The prevailing situation in the region was also discussed. India remains steadfast in its commitment to the pursuit of enduring peace,” said Prime Minister Modi in remarks after the meeting.
Referring to the U.S.-Israel attack on Iran, President Pezeshkian said, “Iran will not accept bullying. History of the humanity tells us that bullies and oppressors are ultimately destroyed.” Citing the hostilities between Iran and the U.S., he added, “Since the day of the Islamic Revolution, they have been trying to impose sanctions and have been sowing seeds of divisiveness in our society. We are seeking truth and justice. We will not surrender to bullying.”
“The two leaders exchanged views on recent developments in West Asia. Prime Minister reiterated India’s consistent position that all issues must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy,” said the Ministry of External Affairs in a statement after the two leaders met.
ALSO WATCH India hosts BRICS | What’s on the agenda?
“He also underscored the need for continued efforts to ensure lasting peace and stability in the region, safeguarding freedom of navigation and commerce, and the safety and well-being of seafarers,” said the Ministry on Prime Minister Modi’s remarks, highlighting the challenges that India has been facing on energy security and maritime freedom because of the chokehold in the Strait of Hormuz.
Mr. Modi appreciated Iran’s regular participation in the multilateral consultations under BRICS and welcomed President Pezeshkian to the Leaders’ Session of the BRICS Business Forum.
Mr. Pezeshkian previously met Prime Minister Modi on August 31 in Bishkek on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. The Iranian leader is accompanied by a large delegation that includes Foreign Minister Syed Abbas Araghchi and Minister of Finance Seyed Ali Madanizadeh. Mr. Araghchi visited India earlier to attend the BRICS Foreign Ministers-level meeting in May. The top-level Iranian delegation’s presence at the BRICS summit is being keenly watched as Iran is caught in a war of words with fellow BRICS member United Arab Emirates.
At the BRICS Business Forum, President Pezeshkian called for greater use of national currencies to deal with “currency risk and mutual settlement”. He called for the creation of a Joint BRICS insurance company with an initial capital of $10 billion to cover major infrastructure and energy projects.
Citing Mr. Pezeshkian’s speech, the Iranian News Agency (IRNA) said, “Iran, with its huge energy reserves and unique geographical position, is ready to play the role of a strategic partner in BRICS energy, food, and transportation supply chains.”
In a pre-departure statement, Mr. Pezeshkian described BRICS as an “important platform” for dialogue with major economies. “The President said one of BRICS’ main objectives is to counter unilateralism and enable countries to preserve their independence while expanding commercial relations,” IRNA reported.
The public meeting, in which the Iranian President was present, was attended by representatives and leaders of various religions, including Mirwaiz Umar Farooq of Kashmir, heads of think tanks, and businesspeople.
Speaking on the occasion, Iran’s ambassador Mohammad Fathali appreciated the support from the Indian people during the ongoing conflict. He said Iran has lost many of its top commanders and the Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed on February 28, but the country has managed to emerge stronger from the conflict. “The people are standing with the government and the government is standing with the people,” said Ambassador Fathali.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday urged Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian to resolve the West Asia conflict through dialogue, even as he sought continued efforts to ensure freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers.
Modi and Pezeshkian met on the margins of the Brics Summit in New Delhi for the second time since August 31, when they held talks on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in Bishkek. Pezeshkian is on his first visit to India since he became President in 2024.

headline: Trade barriers rising globally, India building economic bridges: PM Modi at BRICS Business Forum
full_text:
Trade barriers rising globally, India building economic bridges: PM Modi at BRICS Business Forum
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday positioned India as a bridge-builder in an increasingly fragmented global economy, saying the country is responding to rising trade barriers by expanding free-trade partnerships, strengthening supply chains and creating new avenues for businesses across the BRICS grouping.Addressing the Leaders' Session of the BRICS Business Forum in New Delhi, PM Modi said the global trading environment is becoming more difficult as countries increasingly turn to tariffs, restrictions and other barriers to protect domestic industries. Against this backdrop, he said, India is pursuing greater economic integration by negotiating and signing trade agreements with a growing number of countries.
âToday, while trade barriers are rising globally, India is building economic bridges. Since 2014, we have entered into free trade agreements with nearly 40 countries,â PM Modi said.The Prime Minister's message was aimed not only at highlighting India's expanding trade network but also at presenting the country as a stable and increasingly attractive destination for investment at a time when global businesses are trying to reduce their dependence on concentrated supply chains.âOur approach remains focused on reducing barriers and expanding opportunities for businesses,â PM Modi said.
India seeks deeper economic role within Brics
PM Modi also used India's Brics presidency to push for greater economic cooperation among the 11-member grouping.Rather than limiting Brics cooperation to government-to-government engagement, India is seeking to create networks that allow companies, startups and smaller businesses to access new markets, investment and technology.Under India's chairship, new cooperation networks have been established in areas including agriculture, healthcare, skills development and smart grids. These initiatives are intended to translate the political and economic weight of BRICS into practical opportunities for businesses.India has also launched the Brics Incubator Network, Brics MSME Portal and Brics Startup Innovation Fund.These initiatives are particularly significant for startups and micro, small and medium enterprises, which often face greater difficulties than large corporations in entering overseas markets, finding investors and establishing business partnerships.âTo connect startups and MSMEs with markets and finance, we have launched initiatives like the Brics Incubator Network, the Brics MSME Portal, and the Brics Startup Innovation Fund,â PM Modi said.He urged businesses from Brics countries to use these platforms to increase the movement of investment, technology and talent across member economies.
Supply-chain resilience becomes a key priority
A major theme of PM Modi's address was economic resilience. The disruption of global supply chains in recent years, from the Covid-19 pandemic to geopolitical conflicts and trade tensions, has pushed countries to diversify sources of energy, technology, raw materials and manufactured goods.India, PM Modi said, has been working to make its supply chains more diversified and reliable.âThe theme of India's Brics chairmanship is 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability.' Over the past 12 years, India has made this mantra the foundation of its economic and trade policies,â he said.He pointed to India's efforts across sectors ranging from energy to technology, arguing that stronger and more diversified supply chains would help the economy withstand external shocks.âIt is a result of this resilience that, even amidst global uncertainties, India today offers the assurance of growth and stability,â the PM said.The emphasis on resilience also reflects India's broader push to reduce vulnerabilities in strategically important sectors. The government has increasingly sought to build domestic manufacturing capacity while simultaneously attracting global companies looking to diversify production beyond existing manufacturing hubs.
Infrastructure and strategic technologies
PM Modi highlighted infrastructure expansion as another pillar of India's economic strategy.India is rapidly expanding its network of roads, railways, ports and airports, he said, arguing that better physical connectivity is essential for lowering logistics costs and improving the movement of goods and people.At the same time, the government is trying to build domestic capabilities in technologies and industries that could have long-term economic and strategic importance.âWe are rapidly expanding our roads, railways, ports, and airports. Simultaneously, we are building new capabilities in strategic sectors such as shipbuilding, semiconductors, quantum technology, critical minerals, and biotechnology,â PM Modi said.These sectors are increasingly important because they sit at the intersection of economic security and national security.Semiconductors, for example, are essential for everything from smartphones and automobiles to advanced weapons and artificial intelligence systems. Critical minerals are required for batteries, electronics and clean-energy technologies, while shipbuilding is important both for trade and maritime security.By expanding domestic capabilities in such areas, India is seeking to become not merely a large consumer market but a producer and supplier within global value chains.
UPI as India's digital infrastructure model
PM Modi also highlighted India's digital public infrastructure, particularly the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), as an example of how technology can expand economic participation.UPI has transformed the way payments are made in India by enabling fast digital transactions between bank accounts and mobile applications. PM Modi said the system has given fresh momentum to financial inclusion and digital payments on a massive scale.âToday, 50% of the world's real-time payments take place using this technology,â he said.India has increasingly sought to promote its digital infrastructure model internationally, particularly among developing economies. The broader objective is to demonstrate how digital systems can bring more people and businesses into the formal economy while making transactions faster and cheaper.
The Brics Business Forum is the grouping's main private-sector platform, bringing together business leaders, government ministers and heads of state to discuss trade, investment, finance, technology and development.Its importance extends beyond discussions at individual meetings. Recommendations from the Brics Business Council and the Business Forum can feed into summit declarations and subsequent work programmes, giving the business community a role in shaping the bloc's economic agenda.
Brics members and partner countries now account for over 40% of the global GDP.
The Leaders' Session in New Delhi was attended by Brics leaders, the Chairs of the Brics Business Council and the Brics Women's Business Alliance. Modi also joined the participating dignitaries for a group photograph.The forum is being held as India hosts the 18th Brics Summit under its 2026 chairship. India's presidency is centred on the theme âBuilding for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainabilityâ, with development, sustainability and innovation among its principal priorities.
Why Brics matters to India
Brics has expanded considerably from its original five-member format and now comprises 11 countries: Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the UAE.Collectively, the grouping represents around 49.5% of the world's population, 40% of global GDP and 26% of global trade, according to background information on India's 2026 chairship.For India, the economic significance of Brics therefore goes beyond the traditional diplomatic role of the grouping. Its large consumer markets, energy producers, manufacturing economies and emerging technology sectors create opportunities for greater trade and investment.
PM Modi's address sought to underline India's position within that changing economic landscape: as a country attempting to keep markets open, diversify supply chains, build strategic industrial capacity and use its digital infrastructure to expand economic participation.His broader pitch was that as geopolitical tensions and protectionism reshape global commerce, India wants to position itself as a reliable economic partner, one that can connect businesses, markets, investment and technology across an increasingly fragmented world.
Aashish Saxena is an Assistant News Editor at the Times of India. He has 14 years of editing and reporting experience in both print and digital media. He writes extensively on geopolitics, Indian politics, defence tech, and current affairs in South Asia and Middle East.

Kharge said the government’s foreign policy appeared to be off track and questioned its handling of India’s economic and strategic interests.
“It’s been over a decade, the foreign policy has been in shambles. If you see, whether it is procurement of cheap Russian oil, America arm-twists you, you backtrack. At the same time, you hobnob with the Chinese Premier and he annexes Arunachal Pradesh. On one hand, you ban Chinese apps and Chinese goods, and then you backtrack. So, I’m not sure if the foreign policy is on track. Earlier, when the BRICS meeting was held, you promised that you will strengthen the rupee. It will become a currency that will travel across the globe. Instead, the dollar price has increased. The rupee has plummeted to new depths. And as usual, the MEA and the Prime Minister is clueless on what to do with India’s foreign policy,” Kharge said.
He also targeted the Centre over its approach towards China, alleging that Beijing was expanding its presence along areas claimed by India.
“If you recollect, the Prime Minister of India and the Chinese Premier sat on a swing in Gujarat, had discussions in Mahabalipuram, and what happened after that? They annexed Arunachal Pradesh. They’re annexing other parts of India. They’re building villages within our borders. And the Prime Minister does not even have it in him to rise to the occasion and say that what the Chinese government is doing is wrong. You have lost key patrolling sites. You have lost key areas for the Indian Army. And you don’t even have the courage to stand up to them,” he said.

“Does BJP think they’re bigger than Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel? Are they bigger than Nehru, Gandhi or Subhash Chandra Bose? These are the people who decided what has to be sung. Is BJP above these people?” he said.

As New Delhi prepared to host the BRICS Summit of 11 emerging economies, negotiators were working late into the evening on Friday (September 11, 2026) to forge a consensus for the “Delhi Declaration”.
Diplomatic sources and officials said that all member countries had agreed to “almost all the text, with the exception of one paragraph”, indicating that the references to the war in Iran started by the U.S. and Israel, and Iran’s attacks on installations in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and other West Asian countries, had still not been resolved.
BRICS Summit 2026 updates on September 11
Both Iran and the UAE are members of the BRICS grouping and were inducted in 2024. Their tensions have held up a joint statement at all BRICS ministerial meetings this year, and at the crucial meeting of Foreign Ministers in mid-May, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar issued a “Chair’s Summary” instead.
“We continue to engage on [the] Outcome Document”, an official privy to the negotiations told The Hindu on Friday, while others said they remained hopeful of a breakthrough, as India was able to do in 2023 by forging a joint statement at the G-20 Summit after the Russian war in Ukraine had divided members.
‘Equal condemnation’ demand
In the current series of negotiations, Iran has been pitching for a clear condemnation of the U.S. and Israel’s actions, and the UAE wants “equal condemnation” of Iran’s actions, a diplomat told The Hindu. However, Iran has contested this in Sherpa meetings, insisting that it would be akin to Iran criticising itself. Tehran has contended that its attacks on the Gulf region were in “self-defence”, limited to U.S. military and ancillary installations, the sources said.
The top leaders of eight BRICS countries, including Russia, India, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, South Africa, Indonesia and Iran, will meet around the table at the Bharat Mandapam complex in New Delhi on Saturday afternoon for the first time since the Iran war began. Brazil heads to elections shortly, and President Lula da Silva will be represented by Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira, while UAE President and Ruler of Abu Dhabi Mohamed Bin Zayed Al Nahyan (MbZ), who is visiting Germany at present, will be represented by his son, the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. Saudi Arabia, which was granted BRICS membership in 2024 but has yet to join formally, has sent Foreign Minister Farhan bin Saud.
On Friday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi is understood to have stressed the importance of a joint statement from the BRICS coalition in each of his bilateral talks, including with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian as well as Russian President Vladimir Putin, who, as a strong ally of the Iranian government, has considerable sway with Tehran.
All eyes will also be on Mr. Modi’s meeting with the UAE Crown Prince on Saturday morning, before the joint session. Diplomatic insiders say the decision by the UAE President to send his son, not a minister, is an indication of the importance of the Summit being hosted by India.
Outreach to Iran President
The government’s outreach to President Pezeshkian was apparent from the moment he landed, with a red-carpet welcome accorded to him. Mr. Modi was seen personally leading Mr. Pezeshkian at the BRICS Business event, while holding his hand firmly. On Saturday, according to an advisory by the External Affairs Ministry, Mr. Pezeshkian will be the only BRICS leader to meet President Draupadi Murmu as well.
The BRICS grouping has been particularly affected by the war in Iran that was started by the U.S. and Israel’s attacks and the assassination of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei on February 28, 2026. Apart from Iran and the UAE, which has been targeted repeatedly by Iranian drone and missile strikes, other members of BRICS have been severely hit by the economic disruptions caused by the war, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz for cargo trade traffic, as well as rising energy prices and availability issues.

headline: Putin arrives in Delhi for BRICS Summit, set for bilateral talks with PM Modi today
full_text:
Putin arrives in Delhi for BRICS Summit, set for bilateral talks with PM Modi today
The PM Modi-Putin talks come at a critical juncture, with India and Russia seeking to deepen their strategic partnership while navigating the Ukraine war, global energy disruptions and shifting geopolitical alignments.
Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in New Delhi on Friday for a three-day visit to India, where he will participate in the 18th BRICS Summit and hold wide-ranging bilateral talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi aimed at expanding cooperation in trade, investment and energy.
Putin, who was accompanied by a high-level delegation, arrived at Palam Air Force Station and was received by Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh.
It will be Putin's first in-person participation at a BRICS summit outside Russia since the war in Ukraine began in February 2022.
PM MODI PUTIN MEETING
The Russian President and PM Modi are scheduled to hold bilateral talks at 3.30 pm on Friday. The meeting is expected to focus on strengthening cooperation in defence, energy, technology, pharmaceuticals and people-to-people exchanges, besides expanding bilateral trade and investment.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on Tuesday that Russia and India were also exploring upgrades to BrahMos missiles. Moscow remains committed to completing the remaining deliveries of the S-400 air defence systems and is discussing a proposed supply of Su-57 fighter jets, he said.
Peskov also said energy cooperation between the two countries remained robust and that Moscow and New Delhi were looking at negotiations over India’s plans to establish new civil nuclear reactors.
The Ukraine conflict and efforts towards a peace settlement are expected to feature prominently in their talks on Friday, amid renewed efforts, including by the Trump administration in the US, to find a way to resolve the war.
PM Modi and Putin had previously met on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Bishkek last week. During that meeting, PM Modi called for an immediate end to the Ukraine conflict and urged Putin to move from an “endless war towards the end of war”.
BRICS SUMMIT AMID GLOBAL CRISES
The two-day BRICS summit, hosted by India from Saturday, is expected to focus on strengthening collective resilience in areas including food, energy, health, disaster reduction and critical supply chains.
New Delhi is positioning BRICS as an effective anchor for navigating an increasingly fragmented geopolitical and economic environment.
The summit is taking place against the backdrop of pressures on the global economy arising from the Russia-Ukraine war, the West Asia crisis, particularly the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the Trump administration’s trade and tariff policies.
Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali and Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung are among the leaders attending the summit.
For Xi, the visit will be his first to India since 2019 and comes as New Delhi and Beijing have cautiously worked to improve ties after a deadly military clash along their disputed Himalayan border.
Flights, visas and high-level contacts have gradually been restored between the two countries, although their contested frontier, widening trade deficit and strategic rivalry continue to complicate relations.
WEST ASIA, UKRAINE IN FOCUS
The expanded BRICS grouping is expected to face a test of its cohesion over the West Asia conflict. The bloc, created in 2009 as a forum for major emerging economies seeking greater influence in institutions dominated by Western powers, has since expanded to include countries such as Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
India maintains relations with both Iran and Israel while also seeking to balance its ties with Washington. The West Asia crisis is therefore expected to feature prominently in PM Modi’s discussions with Putin, China's Xi and with Iran's Pezeshkian as well as in the broader BRICS deliberations.
India has also turned to Russia amid the energy crisis linked to the Iran conflict. Russia remains one of India’s key strategic partners and an important source of fuel as the Ukraine war continues.
Putin last visited India in December 2025 and briefly met PM Modi again at the Bishkek Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit earlier this month.

NEW DELHI: Aug 2026 was the joint-warmest month ever recorded globally across all calendar months, on a par with July 2023, said Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) of the European Union's space programme on Thursday.It noted that this Aug was 1.65Â° Celsius above the estimated pre-industrial (1850-1900) baseline, marking the first month above 1.5Â° Celsius since Nov 2025, and the period from June to Aug 2026 was the joint-warmest three-month period on record globally, on a par with 2024."Aug 2026 was a remarkable month in the global climate record. It was both the warmest Aug and the warmest month ever recorded," said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts. Though the global average temperature rise in the month breached the limit of 1.5Â°C, it technically did not cross the Paris Agreement threshold, which actually refers to long-term temperature increase over decades, not over one to five years.
Under the Paris Agreement, countries agreed to keep long-term global average surface temperature well below 2Â°C above pre-industrial levels and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5Â°C by end of century.
Nevertheless, the rise in temperatures to this level in Aug is a stark warning that the world is getting warmer, with its consequences of extreme weather events, glacier melt, sea-level rise and uneven distribution of rainfall over a short period of time being visible across the globe."Until humanity stops burning colossal amount of coal, oil and gas, the pollution this causes will keep baking our planet, and extreme heat will keep smashing all-time records, killing millions and costing trillions, hitting transport and health systems, and pushing up prices for household basics like food," said UN Climate Change executive secretary Simon Stiell in his response to the report.Aug in India was the warmest Aug in the country since 1901, with a mean monthly temperature of 28.01Â°C.

The Supreme Court on Thursday (September 10, 2026) refused anticipatory bail to Sumit Roy, personal assistant to TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee, in connection with the Salboni land grab case.
A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant decided to not interfere with a Calcutta High Court order of August denying him pre-arrest bail.
The West Bengal government, represented by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, argued that Mr. Roy’s answers were proving evasive and his custodial interrogation was necessary to the investigation.
The case was registered under penal provisions relating to cheating, criminal breach of trust, forgery, use of forged documents and criminal conspiracy.
Mr. Mehta alleged that about ₹15 crore was deposited by Mr. Roy in multiple transactions.
Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for Mr. Roy, countered that there was not a single shred of proof of his client’s involvement in the case. He submitted that Mr. Roy had already undergone approximately 88 hours of questioning but had not been confronted with documents or witnesses directly linking him to the alleged transactions.
He argued that the investigating agency was trying to link the banking transactions of the TMC with the personal account of his client. Even the other accused had denied Mr. Roy’s involvement before the investigating agency. However, the court was not convinced.
