headline: Ethiopia, Malaysia eye strong defence, business ties with India after Modi meet at BRICS
full_text:
Ethiopia, Malaysia eye strong defence, business ties with India after Modi meet at BRICS
Ethiopia and Malaysia expressed keenness to deepen defence ties with India.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s bilateral meetings with the leaders of Ethiopia and Malaysia on Saturday put India’s relations with the two countries on a new trajectory, with defence cooperation, investment and emerging technologies emerging as key areas of discussion, government sources said.
Both Ethiopia and Malaysia expressed keenness to deepen defence cooperation with India, including through joint personnel training and procurement of defence equipment from Indian companies, the sources said.
The discussions come as India seeks to expand its defence partnerships and exports, particularly among countries in the Global South. A growing number of nations have shown interest in Indian-made military platforms, missiles, artillery systems, radars and aircraft in recent years.
Deep Dive
Several smaller countries seek deeper defence ties with India after Operation Sindoor: Here’s the list
India’s growing defence engagement with smaller and middle-sized countries has gained momentum, with countries in Asia, Africa and elsewhere looking at Indian platforms for their security requirements.
Indonesia is among the more notable recent examples. In July 2026, Jakarta finalised a BrahMos arrangement with India and also signed an air-to-air missile cooperation agreement involving India’s Astra missile.
Vietnam has also emerged as an important potential defence partner, with India officially confirming a BrahMos deal, although details of the agreement have not been made public.
The Philippines is already a BrahMos customer. It signed a $375-million deal for three shore-based anti-ship missile batteries, with deliveries completed in 2026.
Armenia is another significant Indian defence customer. It has acquired a basket of Indian systems, including Pinaka multi-barrel rocket launchers, Akash-1S air defence systems, ATAGS artillery guns and Swathi weapon-locating radars. India accounted for about 43% of Armenia’s arms imports during 2022-24.
Other countries are also exploring Indian systems. Thailand has reportedly been evaluating the BrahMos shore-based anti-ship system, although discussions remain exploratory rather than representing a signed deal.
Also Read: 'Mother of all deals': EU Commission's crucial step advances India-EU free trade agreement
Malaysia, meanwhile, has shown interest in BrahMos, including the possibility of an air-launched version for its Su-30 fighter aircraft. Nigeria has expressed interest in the Tejas fighter aircraft, with Hindustan Aeronautics Limited having confirmed discussions.
Egypt has also shown interest in Tejas, while Argentina had previously expressed interest in the fighter, although the prospect is complicated by the presence of British-origin components.
The UAE has reportedly looked at BrahMos as well as India’s Akashteer air-defence command-and-control system. Interest or enquiries around BrahMos have also emerged from countries including Chile, Brazil and Saudi Arabia, though these are at a much earlier stage than the arrangements with Indonesia, the Philippines or Vietnam.
India’s defence engagement also has a wider Indian Ocean footprint, with countries such as Maldives, Mauritius, Mozambique, Myanmar, Seychelles and Sri Lanka receiving various Indian maritime and aviation systems, including patrol aircraft, patrol vessels, helicopters and radars.
The trend reflects New Delhi’s broader push to position India as a reliable defence partner, particularly for countries seeking cost-effective military equipment, training and technology partnerships.

Ethiopia keen on Indian mining companies
During Modi’s meeting with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, the two sides discussed expanding economic engagement and investment opportunities. Ethiopia specifically welcomed greater participation by Indian mining companies, according to government sources.
The discussions also covered stronger defence cooperation, including joint personnel training and defence procurement from India.
The focus on mining could open new opportunities for Indian companies in Ethiopia, which is seeking greater foreign investment and partnerships across its natural-resource sector.
For India, deeper commercial engagement with Ethiopia also fits into its broader effort to expand economic ties with Africa and encourage Indian industry to participate in projects across the continent.
Semiconductors, defence on India-Malaysia agenda
In his meeting with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Modi discussed opportunities for expanding cooperation in the semiconductor sector, besides defence and investment, the sources said.
Malaysia has emerged as an important partner for India in the semiconductor ecosystem, with the two countries exploring opportunities across the value chain, including technology, workforce development and supply-chain resilience.
Defence is another area with considerable potential. Malaysia’s interest in BrahMos, including the possibility of an air-launched variant for its Su-30s, could provide an avenue for deeper defence-industrial cooperation between the two countries.
Both sides also discussed encouraging greater investment and participation by industry, with India seeking to attract Malaysian companies while encouraging Indian businesses to expand their presence in Malaysia.

headline: India, China differ in wording on border issue after PM Modi-Xi Jinping meeting
full_text:
India, China differ in wording on border issue after PM Modi-Xi Jinping meeting
Since 2020, India has maintained that the state of the border cannot be separated from the state of the broader relationship. China, by contrast, has left room for bilateral ties to make headway while the boundary question remains unresolved.
The Indian and Chinese statements issued after Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s meeting with President Xi Jinping on Saturday reveal a difference in how the two countries see the relationship between the boundary question and broader bilateral ties.
The Asian giants' statements assume significance as Xi visited India after seven years following border tensions in the wake of the 2020 Galwan Valley clash, which left 20 Indian soldiers and four Chinese Army personnel dead.
In its statement, China called on both sides to advance bilateral relations and address the boundary question at the same time. It said they should seek “parallel, mutually reinforcing progress” on the two fronts while maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas.
“Third, remove irritants with the political wisdom of mutual respect and mutual understanding. The two sides should stay committed to advancing bilateral relations and resolving the boundary question, seek parallel, mutually reinforcing progress, and maintain peace and tranquility in the border areas,” the Chinese statement said.
India’s readout framed the border situation differently.
It said PM Modi emphasised that peace and tranquillity in the border areas remained “an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations”. He also underlined the need for both countries to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues.
According to the Indian statement, the two leaders expressed a commitment to a “fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable” resolution of the boundary question, taking into account the overall bilateral relationship and the long-term interests of the people of both countries.
The point of divergence lies in the order of progress.
China’s wording envisages movement on the wider relationship and the boundary question in parallel. India’s wording makes peace and tranquillity along the border the basis on which the wider relationship can continue to develop.
India's stated condition concerns the situation on the ground: the border must remain peaceful, and existing agreements must be observed.
The difference carries weight after the 2020 Galwan clash, which sharply damaged ties. India has since maintained that the state of the border cannot be separated from the state of the broader relationship.
China’s latest formulation, by contrast, leaves room for bilateral ties to make headway while the boundary question remains unresolved.

headline: PM Modi, Xi welcome 'steady progress' in India-China ties at BRICS meet, bat for mutual resolution of border dispute
full_text:
PM Modi, Xi welcome 'steady progress' in India-China ties at BRICS meet, bat for mutual resolution of border dispute
Xi travelled to India for the first time in seven years to attend the BRICS Summit.
India on Saturday emphasised that peace and tranquillity in the border areas remain the “essential basis” for developing ties with China, as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Xi Jinping welcomed “steady progress” in bilateral relations during a meeting on the margins of the Brics Summit in New Delhi.
Track live updates on BRICS Summit
Xi travelled to India for the first time in seven years to attend the Brics Summit, setting up the meeting with Modi to take forward the normalisation of bilateral ties amid lingering tensions on the border. The two leaders last met on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit in the Chinese city of Tianjin a year ago.
Deep Dive
‘Peace and tranquillity essential for ties’
Modi emphasised that peace and tranquillity in the border areas “remains an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations”, the external affairs ministry said in a readout. He also underlined that both sides should “observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues”.
The two leaders “expressed commitment to a fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary question proceeding from the political perspective of their overall bilateral relations and the long-term interests of the two peoples”, the ministry said.
Modi’s comments reiterated India’s stated position that the state of the border will determine the overall course of bilateral ties. The Chinese side, however, has argued that the two sides should place the border dispute in an “appropriate place” while taking forward relations in other spheres such as trade and investment.
Meeting amid border tensions
The two leaders met against the backdrop of fresh tensions between Indian and Chinese troops in the remote Taksing region of Arunachal Pradesh, with reports of face-offs during July and August. The two sides reached an understanding in October 2024 on disengaging troops at “friction points” in the Ladakh sector of the Line of Actual Control (LAC), ending a standoff that lasted more than four years and took ties to a six-decade low.
Modi and Xi welcomed the “steady progress” in India-China relations since their last meeting at Tianjin in August 2025, and reaffirmed that both countries should “take a strategic and long-term perspective of their ties”, the readout said.
“Differences should not become disputes. Prime Minister [Modi] highlighted that both sides must be guided by three mutuals – mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest,” the readout said.
Modi and Xi also noted progress in people-to-people ties and underscored the need to promote cultural exchanges, business linkages, and greater mobility between the two countries, the statement added.
In the context of economic and trade relations, they underlined the need to “address each other’s concerns, including structural trade imbalance and supply chain issues, and facilitation of meaningful and predictable market access”, it said.
India continues to have a range of concerns in the economic sphere, including China’s visa curbs for Indian businesspeople, export restrictions on critical machinery and commodities such as fertilisers, and the yawning imbalance in two-way trade. Since Xi’s last visit, India-China trade has grown from about $93 billion in 2019 to $127 billion in 2025, while the trade deficit has risen from $57 billion to almost $100 billion in the same period.
The two leaders further agreed that both sides “must continue to expand common ground on regional and global issues, and in addressing challenges”, the readout said without going into details.
Modi appreciated China's support for India's Brics presidency and its contributions towards the success of the Brics Summit.
Xi, who last visited the Indian capital in 2014, was received at the airport by minister of state for commerce Jitin Prasada. The leaders of India and China have not made any bilateral visits since 2020, when relations plummeted to their lowest point since the 1962 border war because of the face-off in Ladakh. Xi last travelled to India in 2019 for an informal summit with Modi, months before the standoff began.
The talks between Xi and Modi also offered an opportunity to take stock of several rounds of dialogue between the Special Representatives on the border issue, the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC), and senior military commanders. India and China held the first round of talks between military commanders in the eastern sector in Arunachal Pradesh on September 6 and 7.
The issue of a possible “early and substantial harvest” of boundary delimitation and border management has figured in recent discussions through diplomatic channels, though the two sides have not released any details so far.

headline: BRICS nations condemn Pahalgam attack, seek action against terror safe havens
full_text:
BRICS nations condemn Pahalgam attack, seek action against terror safe havens
Backed by the Pakistani state, UN-designated terrorist Hafiz Saeed-led LeT and its proxy TRF carried out the Pahalgam terror attack on April 22 last year
BRICS nations on Saturday strongly condemned the April 2025 terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir’s Pahalgam that killed 26 people, and called for concerted action against all UN-designated terrorists and strict accountability for those supporting terror.
Backed by the Pakistani state, UN-designated terrorist Hafiz Saeed-led Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and its proxy The Resistance Front (TRF) carried out the Pahalgam terror attack on the morning of April 22 last year, killing 25 Hindu tourists and one local pony operator from the Kashmir Valley. The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has already filed two charge sheets in the terror attack, including one against Saeed. The three Pakistani terrorists who carried out the killings were killed in an encounter with security forces in July last year and now India is preparing to conduct a trial in absentia for Hafiz Saeed.
In a joint statement issued in New Delhi, the 11-nation grouping said, “We condemn in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir on 22 April 2025, during which 26 people were killed and many more injured. We reaffirm our commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including the cross-border movement of terrorists, terrorism financing and safe havens”.
Deep Dive
While reiterating that terrorism should not be associated with any religion, nationality, civilisation, or ethnic group, the BRICS declaration stated that “all those involved in terrorist activities and their support must be held accountable and brought to justice in accordance with relevant national and international law.”
“We urge to ensure zero tolerance for terrorism and reject double standards in countering terrorism”.
Also Read: BRICS Summit 2026 LIVE: China, India can learn from each other’s strengths, Xi Jinping tells PM Modi
The BRICS leaders further emphasized that the primary responsibility is that of States of combating terrorism. “Global efforts to prevent and counter terrorist threats must fully comply with their obligations under international law, including the Charter of the UN, in particular the purposes and principles thereof, and relevant international conventions and protocols, in particular international human rights law, international refugee law and international humanitarian law, as applicable”, the statement added.
The member states on Saturday welcomed the activities of BRICS Counter-Terrorism Working Group (CTWG) and its five subgroups based upon the BRICS counter-terrorism strategy, the Brics counter-terrorism action plan and the CTWG Position Paper.
“We look forward to further deepening counter-terrorism cooperation. We call for an expeditious finalization and adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism in the UN framework. We call for concerted actions against all UN designated terrorists and terrorist entities,” the statement added.
The BRICS nations further emphasized the importance of “countering extremism and radicalization” specially among the younger generations.
In response to the terror attack, India had launched Operation Sindoor bombing nine terror camps in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) in pre-dawn strikes --- in which at least 100 terrorists were killed --- and sparked a series of attacks and counter-attacks across the western border, involving fighter jets, missiles, armed drones, and fierce artillery and rocket duels. In one such attack on the night of May 9-10, the Indian Air Force struck targets at 13 Pakistani airbases and military installations. After four days of fighting, military hostilities were stopped on May 10 evening as the two nations reached an understanding.

headline: India calls for local currency trade among BRICS to enhance economic resilience
full_text:
India calls for local currency trade among BRICS to enhance economic resilience
External Affairs Minister Jaishankar emphasized self-reliance amid global economic challenges.
India on Friday urged Brics nations to create a predictable business environment, build resilient supply chains and link their payment systems to allow trade in local currencies, as Russia proposed a Brics grain exchange to strengthen food security across the bloc.
Delivering the keynote address at the Brics Business Forum, external affairs minister S Jaishankar said India’s chairship was focused on resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability. “We meet at a time when [the] global political and economic order is under churn. Volatility, uncertainty, and complexity have become defining features of the world around us. We are witnessing the economic consequences of geopolitical conflicts, of pandemics, and of climate-related disruptions,” he said.
Jaishankar called for “greater self-reliance” within Brics to strengthen economic security. “The objective is to strengthen our ability to absorb shocks while remaining connected and competitive,” he said, listing genuine market practices, dependable logistics, a predictable business environment, diversified commercial relationships and transparent trade and investment as priorities. Energy systems capable of coping with disruption, and transition pathways suited to different national circumstances, were also needed, he added, citing digital public infrastructure (DPI), artificial intelligence, fintech and advanced manufacturing as areas of major opportunity.
Deep Dive
Addressing roughly 2,000 delegates, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said Brics accounted for almost a quarter of global trade and India was a key pillar of intra-bloc commerce. “We believe trade amongst partners should be deep, resilient with diversified supply chains and ensuring that at no point of time trade becomes an impediment to growth and the well-being of the people of each member state. We should open our markets for each other’s products including for raw materials and critical minerals,” he said.
“Our supply chains will be resilient when they run both ways,” Goyal said, urging members and partner countries to open markets, simplify regulations and speed up clearances. He also called on Brics to open services markets, ease professional mobility and recognise each other’s qualifications, and to back agri-tech startups working on food security.
On payments, Goyal said India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) now handled over 250 billion transactions a year — more than half the world’s total by volume — and was accepted in 11 countries. “I would urge the Brics member countries and partner countries to link our payment systems, trade, in each other’s local currencies,” he said.
Also Read | ‘India building economic bridges’: PM Modi hails country's business push at BRICS forum
Russian minister of economic development Maxim Reshetnikov said Russia was increasingly settling trade in local currencies. “Three years ago, dollar and euro totaled 85% of settlements for Russian exports. The figure now stands at about 11%,” he said.
He proposed a Brics grain exchange, arguing that member countries were among the world’s leading producers and consumers of grain but still relied on price benchmarks set in other markets.

headline: Brics slams US, backs Iran, calls out Israel. Has India shifted stance?
full_text:
Brics slams US, backs Iran, calls out Israel. Has India shifted stance?
The joint declaration of the Brics Delhi Summit has criticised the US over unilateral sanctions without naming it. It has backed Iran's WTO entry, and slammed Israel while dedicating five paras to Gaza. Is this a signal of India leaning away from the US, or is New Delhi keeping another diplomatic option open?
The joint declaration of the 18th Brics Summit held in New Delhi is out, and the bloc has issued some strong remarks. While it has named Israel, criticising it over Lebanon, it didn't name the United States (US) while slamming DC's unilateral sanctions. Getting the members to agree on a joint statement was a big diplomatic challenge for India, the president and host. Now, it is to be seen how the words are interpreted and the signals from New Delhi received.
There is, however, careful diplomacy in the wording. The document does not name the US while criticising non-UN sanctions, nor does it identify Iran while condemning attacks on nuclear facilities. Israel is the exception. It is named in several passages concerning Gaza and Lebanon.
Producing the declaration was a major challenge because Iran and the UAE had pushed competing formulations on the war in the Middle East. Its adoption is a diplomatic victory for India, particularly after speculation that Russia and Iran would seek sharply anti-US language that New Delhi and other members of the grouping might resist. In a way, India has succeeded in keeping Brics within its preferred formulation of being "non-Western but not anti-Western".
Speaking to India Today TV, India practice head at Eurasia Group and journalist Pramit Pal Chaudhuri said, "The accomplishment of the summit is to actually have a joint statement in the first place”, given the earlier Iran-UAE deadlock.
Chaudhari said Brics had long been divided between a China-led camp seeking to challenge Western structures and an India-Brazil camp seeking to "modify" rather than overthrow them.
"Whenever you and the Chinese get in the same room, it’s all daggers drawn, and we can't get anything done," Chaudhari recalled Russian diplomats telling him. Chaudhuri said the US had "massively undermined its own standing", giving Chinese President Xi Jinping an opportunity to seek convergence with India and Brazil on local-currency trade, digital payments, logistics and connectivity.
On Israel, the Brics declaration highlighted its legal obligation to allow humanitarian aid into Gaza and opposed forced Palestinian displacement. On Lebanon, it went further, asking Israel to "withdraw its occupying forces from all of the Lebanese territories" where they remain.
'UNILATERAL SANCTIONS' TARGET THE US WITHOUT NAMING IT
The US is present in the New Delhi Declaration without being named, as the Brics members condemned "unilateral economic sanctions" and attacks on "peaceful nuclear facilities".
"We condemn the imposition of unilateral coercive measures that are contrary to international law, and reiterate that such measures, inter alia in the form of unilateral economic sanctions and secondary sanctions, have far-reaching negative implications," the Delhi Summit declaration said, adding that such economic sanctions end up "disproportionally affecting the poor".
Though the joint declaration didn't name the US, it is common knowledge that Washington DC is the non-UN entity that imposes the most sanctions. In fact, it has imposed crippling sanctions against two Brics members, Russia and Iran.
"We reaffirm our opposition to unilateral coercive measures that are contrary to international law and the Charter of the United Nations, including non-UN Security Council authorized sanctions," the declaration read.
The formulation clearly reflects the longstanding criticism of America by Russia and Iran of Washington's sanctions architecture and policies.
The language is therefore critical of the US in substance, but stops short of turning the declaration into a direct attack on Washington. That's a careful diplomatic position. That compromise would have helped India, the UAE and other members retain important relationships with the US while allowing Iran and Russia to secure language opposing unilateral sanctions.
Brics also voiced "serious concerns" about unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures inconsistent with World Trade Organisation rules (WTO). The New Delhi Declaration of the Brics could be read as a broader warning against Washington's use of tariffs and economic pressure, though the declaration again avoids identifying any country.
Since US President Donald Trump's return to the White House, US tariffs have hit imports from every Brics member except heavily sanctioned Russia, while Iran has faced both the baseline tariff and extensive sanctions. Trump has repeatedly branded Brics "anti-American", threatened an extra 10% tariff on countries aligning with it and warned of 100% duties over attempts to weaken the dollar.
India called Washington's additional tariff over its Russian oil purchases "unfair, unjustified and unreasonable" and vowed to take all necessary steps to protect its national interests.
BRICS BACKS IRAN'S CASE WITHOUT NAMING IRAN
Iran had been critical that the Brics didn't issue any statement against the US and Israel over their airstrikes. While Iran is a Brics member, the US and Israel aren't. Tehran was seeking backing from the grouping, and the New Delhi Declaration does that to the best extent possible.
The passage does not name Iran, the US or Israel. In the context of the war in the Middle East, however, it appears to support Tehran's argument that US-Israeli attacks on its safeguarded nuclear facilities violated international law.
Brics also urged respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of states and calls for "maximum restraint" in West Asia.
Notably, the declaration expressed "serious concern over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities under full safeguards" of the International Atomic Energy Agency.
Crucially, it prefaced the section by recalling the members' "respective national positions", allowing countries such as Iran and the UAE to sign the same document without abandoning their conflicting accounts of the war.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi was seen holding Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's hand as the two leaders held talks, underscoring New Delhi's careful outreach to Iran during the Brics Summit.
In a striking display of Indian diplomacy's heft, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met UAE Crown Prince Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on the sidelines of the Brics Summit in New Delhi. The meeting was striking because Iran had fired over 500 missiles and 2,000 drones at the UAE since the war started in February, killing more than a dozen civilians and injuring more than 220.
Iran is not explicitly named elsewhere, with Brics strongly supporting its bid to join the WTO. Therefore, the declaration backs important Iranian positions, but its war-related language remains general.
ISRAEL CALLED OUT OVER WAR IN GAZA AND LEBANON
Israel received more direct treatment than the US in the New Delhi Declaration. The Brics leaders expressed concern over continued violence in Gaza, opposed the forced displacement of Palestinians and supported a sovereign Palestinian state within the 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.
The declaration also referred to proceedings brought by South Africa against Israel at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and noted Israel's "legal obligation to ensure the provision of humanitarian aid in Gaza."
On Lebanon, the declaration stated, "We welcome the ceasefire in Lebanon and call on all parties to strictly adhere to its terms and to fully implement UNSC Resolution 1701. We condemn the continued violations of the ceasefire and of the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Lebanon."
In the same paragraph, it said,"We call on Israel to respect the terms agreed with the Lebanese government and to withdraw its occupying forces from all of the Lebanese territories, in which they remain."
This is the only place in the entire document where Israel is named in a direct call for the withdrawal of occupying forces from a neighbouring country's territory.
The UN Security Council Resolution 1701 ended the 2006 Israel-Hezbollah war and called for an Israeli withdrawal and the deployment of Lebanese troops and UN peacekeepers in southern Lebanon.
DOES BRICS JOINT DECLARATION SIGNAL A SHIFT ON INDIA'S POSITION?
So has India's position changed? While the declaration's language on a few issues is sharper than India's calibrated bilateral statements, it does not establish a fundamental policy shift.
India has charted a non-aligned foreign policy, but it has, at times, been perceived to be closer to Moscow or to Washington DC depending on the political situation.
India's ties with the US had been on the upswing since the turn of the century, and experts saw a definitive leaning towards DC. But Donald Trump's second stint in the White House changed everything. The US President's imposition of tariffs, claims to have brokered a ceasefire between India and Pakistan in May 2025, and action against Indian professionals have dampened ties.
With a White House that doesn't really seem to care for friends and allies, most countries are repositioning.
India has been doing an excellent tightrope walk all this while. It has been talking to and trading with all the warring sides; Russia and Ukraine, the US, Israel and Iran. Even as it backed the two-state solution on Palestine, India has deepened its ties with Israel, the country that backed it during Operation Sindoor.
The Brics is, however, a different club altogether. Russia and China, the main counterweight to a US-dominated West, are at its core. As seen during the declaration of the SCO Summit on September 1, India had to make a choice even during the Brics summit.
The Brics joint declaration might be a signal of correcting perceptions on New Delhi's alignment. However, one needs to be careful in reading it because, in diplomacy, what is left unsaid conveys more than what has been forced into words.
Experts have warned against India's very strong Brics association, saying it could be counterproductive.
Rajesh Rajagopalan, Professor of international politics at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) cautioned of China's "great ambitions".
"India's objective in the BRICS should be to make it ineffective so that it doesn't become a vehicle for China's great power ambitions," Rajagopalan posted on X, sharing his Opinion in The Print.
'Forget Brics, look West' was how economist Surjit Bhalla's piece in The Indian Express was headlined on September 11.
"What should India do to enhance our future? Forget BRICS. Our future is as a global partner of the West — Europe and the US. And note, and remember, who gains if India does not sign a trade deal with America," wrote Bhalla.
India's multilateralism is reflected in the New Delhi Declaration.
India has continued to advocate dialogue and diplomacy in the Middle East while supporting Palestinian statehood and maintaining close strategic relations with Israel. Prime Minister Narendra Modi reiterated during his meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian that disputes should be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy, alongside protecting navigation, commerce and seafarers.
A Brics declaration is also a consensus document, not an exclusively Indian statement. As chair, New Delhi's task was to find language acceptable to all 11 members of the expanded Brics.
India has therefore accepted criticism of non-UN sanctions, implicit support for Iran's case and explicit demands directed at Israel. But by keeping the US and Iran unnamed in the war-related passages, it has preserved room for its multi-aligned foreign policy. For India, Brics is a vehicle for non-aligned diplomacy. It has succeeded in getting a joint declaration agreed to despite 11 varying interests. And through the declaration, it sent out a signal of its diplomatic flexibility.

headline: Don't want to weaken party: Harish Rawat quits Congress posts amid cash row
full_text:
Don't want to weaken party: Harish Rawat quits Congress posts amid cash row
Harish Rawat resigned from his Congress posts after reports linked his former aide to a cash and recruitment controversy. He said he did not want any action associated with him to weaken the party's anti-corruption fight before the Uttarakhand polls.
Former Uttarakhand Chief Minister Harish Rawat has resigned from his posts in the Congress, saying he does not want anything associated with him to weaken the party's fight against corruption ahead of the state Assembly elections.
In a Facebook post, Rawat referred to reports that a large amount of cash and jewellery had been seized from his former OSD and aide, Jina, in Dehradun. Rawat said the facts surrounding the seizure would become clear in due course, while defending Jina as a "gentle" and hardworking person.
Rawat said Jina had served as his OSD and had handled important responsibilities during his tenure in government as well as in the party.
He added that if Jina was found to have tampered with OMR sheets in the recruitment of village development officers, and there was evidence to establish his involvement, he would be "ashamed" of such an act. However, Rawat said he did not believe the allegations against his former aide.
'DON'T WANT TO WEAKEN PARTY'S FIGHT'
Rawat said the Uttarakhand elections carried high stakes and recalled that he had often joked that elections would be held when the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) knocked on his door.
"This time, instead of my house, an attempt has been made to create a narrative by knocking on the house of one of my associates," he said.
He said the Congress and its workers were fighting against corruption and referred to party leader Rahul Gandhi's campaign against corruption in the education system.
"At such a time, if any action of Harish Rawat weakens the party's struggle, I would not want that," he said.
Rawat said he was not holding any government post but was a member of the Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee executive and a permanent invitee to the Congress Working Committee. He said he would "very humbly" step down from both positions.
RAWAT SEEKS PROBE INTO RECRUITMENT IRREGULARITIES
Addressing questions surrounding the Uttarakhand Subordinate Service Selection Commission, Rawat defended the steps taken by his government to strengthen recruitment mechanisms and said more than 42,000 government posts were filled during its three-year tenure.
He said his government had created recruitment boards for areas including medical and education services and had pushed the Public Service Commission to conduct examinations on time.
Rawat acknowledged that there could have been "errors of judgement" during the process and apologised to the people of Uttarakhand if any such mistakes had affected the future of the state's youth.
He also spoke about the appointment of a former chairman of the Subordinate Service Selection Commission, saying the appointment had been based on the person's service record. Rawat said he had removed the chairman or sought his resignation after receiving complaints.
He said former Chief Minister Major General BC Khanduri had advised him on the appointment and had met him twice regarding it.
'IF I AM INVOLVED, LAW SHOULD PUNISH ME'
Rawat said irregularities in government recruitment and examinations amounted to "playing with the future" of the next generation. He said he should be held accountable if he had knowingly or unknowingly contributed to any such wrongdoing.
He appealed to anyone possessing evidence of his involvement in interference in recruitment matters to submit it to the CBI, Enforcement Directorate or state police.
Rawat said people entrusted with public responsibilities must avoid such temptations and reiterated that if he had made any such mistake, he considered himself deserving of punishment and said the law should take its course.

headline: Ganga water recedes in Bihar; severe flood conditions persist in UP
full_text:
Ganga water recedes in Bihar; severe flood conditions persist in UP
Flood-like conditions also affected several areas in UP due to a rise in the Ganga's water level. Moradabad is one of the worst-hit areas in the state.
Amid a flood-like situation triggered by rising water levels of the Ganga across Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, ground conditions remained grim on Saturday, even as official data showed a receding trend at most monitoring stations in Bihar.
According to data released by the Bihar Water Resources Department, Ganga levels fell at Allahabad (-0.43), Varanasi (-0.22), Buxar (-0.02), Dighaghat (-0.15), Gandhighat (-0.06), Hathidah (-0.09), Sultanganj (-0.14) and Bhagalpur (-0.12). The Punpun also fell at Fatehpur (-0.19) and Sripalpur (-0.27), as did the Sone at Maner (-0.03). Only Sone in Koelwar showed a marginal rise of 0.01, as per the latest update at 6 AM.
Despite the receding trend, ground conditions in Bihar remain severe for citizens.
On NH-80, the swollen Ganga has submerged the NH-80 and a four-lane stretch in Bhagalpur, forcing police and administration to seal it from both ends with barricades.
A resident travelling on the Sultanganj-Bhagalpur stretch, Vinod Thakur, said that he had never seen such high water levels in his lifetime.
"The water level of the Ganga has risen so much that we have seen this much water for the first time in our lives," he told ANI.
The floods have already claimed lives in the state. Five people, including four children, drowned after falling into water-filled ditches in Koyli Khutaha village of Bhagalpur district, officials and residents said on Friday.
Flood-like conditions also affected several areas in Uttar Pradesh due to a rise in the Ganga's water level. Moradabad is one of the worst-hit areas in the state.
The cremation ground at Gegaso Ghat has also been submerged, disrupting the last rites ritual for families.
"As for the body, we cremate it right here outside, and afterwards, we take it into that same area. There, we immerse it. We are enduring it," a local Shiv Bahadur told ANI, underscoring the grim situation for the residents.
The water level has slowed down commuters in several areas.
A resident described the situation as gravely severe. "The waterlogging situation is such that in just a short while, water will enter all the houses... There is a problem with movement, there is a problem with everything," he said.
Meanwhile, in Varanasi, municipal authorities maintained that the city's drainage network is managing the rainfall load.
PRO of Varanasi Municipal Corporation Sandeep Srivastava said, "Currently, the drainage lines in the Varanasi area extend to about 1300 kilometres, along with around 400 small and large drains. These drainage systems are regularly cleaned every year to prevent waterlogging. At present, drainage arrangements are being made in all other areas as needed."
Emphasising continuous efforts for smooth travel for citizens, he said, "With the current rainfall, as you can see, even after heavy rain, the water completely drains from the roads within half an hour... All our engineers wade into the water to facilitate drainage... We will continue to work in this manner going forward so that no one has to face any waterlogging issues."

headline: Harish Rawat resignation row: Why is Congress leader’s PA facing ED raids?
full_text:
Harish Rawat resignation row: Why is Congress leader’s PA facing ED raids?
The decision came after ED conducted raids on the premises of Chandan Singh Jeena and seized around a dozen luxury wristwatches and ₹32 lakh in cash.
Senior Congress leader and former Uttarakhand chief minister Harish Rawat on Saturday refuted reports of his resignation from party posts, saying he had not stepped down, as inferred from his social media post. Rawat clarified that he would be willing to resign if Enforcement Directorate (ED) action against his personal assistant Chandan Singh Jeena would lead to the weakening of Congress' stand against corruption.
In a social media post, Rawat said Congress membership runs through his “blood and bones”, while calling the recent ED searches in Dehradun as a “hypocritical spectacle”.
Row over ED raids against Rawat's PA
Harish Rawat's offered to resign after the Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Thursday conducted raids on the premises of Chandan Singh Jeena and seized around a dozen luxury wristwatches and ₹32 lakh in cash, news agency PTI reported.
Jeena is currently Rawat’s personal assistant and had earlier worked as an officer on special duty (OSD) when Rawat was Uttarakhand chief minister from 2014 to 2017.
The ED said that the raids were conducted as part of a money laundering investigation linked to alleged irregularities in a 2016 exam conducted by the state service selection commission.
The agenc conducted searches at the residential premises of the then Chairman and Secretary of UKSSSC, the then Exam Controller, the owner of the private computer agency engaged for OMR processing, and associated middlemen allegedly linked to the conspiracy.
Why Harish Rawat offered to resign
In a post on X, Rawat said that while he did not believe the allegations of irregularities in recruitment exams levelled against Jeena, who has long been his associate, he absolutely did not want the issue to weaken the party's campaign.
“Shri Jeena is an extremely decent, humble, and hardworking person. If there is evidence that he tampered with OMR sheets during the recruitment of village development officers or committed any such error, then I am ashamed of this alleged audacious act. However, I do not believe these allegations at all,” Rawat said.
“At such a time, if any action of Harish Rawat introduces any weakness in the party's struggle, I would absolutely not want that. Therefore, having just remembered my beloved deity, I have taken a major decision: I am not on any government position, so what resignation would I tender from that!”
“Yes, I am a member of the executive of the Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee and a permanent invitee member of the Congress Working Committee at the national level, and with utmost humility, I wish to step down from both these positions, because no weakness should come into the party's struggle on my account,” he added.
‘Not resigned from Congress’
In a separate post, Rawat clarified that he has only stepped down from a position and not resigned from the Congress party. He was responding to media reports that suggested the latter.
“Some sections of the media are reporting the news that Harish Rawat has resigned from the Congress Party. Brother, Congress Party membership is in my blood and bones; it shapes everything that Harish Rawat is. It will go to heaven with me,” he wrote on X.
“Yes, if the ED's hypocritical circus that happened in Dehradun yesterday or the day before has any impact on the narrative of fighting against corruption in the Congress Party, then the positions I hold in the party—member of the state executive and member of the AICC working committee—I would want to resign from those positions,” he added.
He urged his “friends” in the media to read his post and correct the news.
“Therefore, I urge my friends in the media to read my post/tweet in its entirety and correct their news.”

headline: After being denied permission to use the Indore stadium, the Congress on Friday (September 11, 2026) paid over ₹10 lakh to lease an alternative venue in the city for party leader Rahul Gandhi’s upcoming ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ programme.
full_text:
After being denied permission to use the Indore stadium, the Congress on Friday (September 11, 2026) paid over ₹10 lakh to lease an alternative venue in the city for party leader Rahul Gandhi’s upcoming ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ programme.
Accusing the ruling BJP of deliberately delaying permissions out of panic, Congress leaders confirmed that the party secured a three-day lease of 12,000 sq metres of land in front of the Regional Park from the Indore Development Authority for the student outreach event.
An Indore Development Authority (IDA) official said that the land in front of the Regional Park has been temporarily leased to the Congress from September 17 to September 19, and the fee was fixed at ₹10.08 lakh as per the prevailing rates.
A letter from the IDA to Indore City Congress Committee President Chintu Chouksey stated that permission to hold the event would be issued after the deposit of the funds, subject to the prescribed conditions.
The letter also stated that the organisers would be responsible for ensuring necessary security arrangements at the venue and obtaining no-objection certificates from the relevant departments.
Talking to PTI, City Congress Committee President Chouksey said, “We have deposited the agreed amount into the IDA’s bank account.” He alleged that the BJP government was nervous about Gandhi’s upcoming event in Indore, and in this panic, it has been harassing the Congress over the venue.
“We initially wanted to hold the event at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on September 12, but after not receiving permission, we had to change the date to September 19. We were made to run around for 10 days for the land located in front of the Regional Park,” Chouksey said.
The Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, where the Opposition party initially sought permission for the programme, falls under the municipal corporation.
Indore Mayor Pushyamitra Bhargava said that under an old order of the Madhya Pradesh High Court, the stadium can only be used for sports or state-level government events.
The BJP’s state co-media in-charge Alok Dubey said that the Congress is indulging in propaganda politics and the public knows the truth about this party.
Taking a jibe at the Congress, he said the name of Gandhi’s event should be changed from “Chhatron Ki Goonj” to “Jhooth Ki Goonj”. Congress, meanwhile, has named its event venue as “Bharat Jodo Maidan” and claims that approximately 1.5 lakh students have registered for the programme.
“Chhatraon Ki Goonj” is a student-dialogue campaign launched by Mr. Gandhi to corner the BJP on issues such as question paper leaks, expensive education, irregularities in government recruitment, and unemployment.
Under Mr. Gandhi’s leadership, four editions of the “Chhatron Ki Goonj” programme have been organised so far in Kota, Dehradun, Prayagraj, and Pune.
The previous one held in Pune on August 22 was for female students.

headline: PM Modi proposes seafarers' safety network on the opening day of Brics summit

PM Modi proposes seafarers' safety network on the opening day of Brics summit
The safety of Indian seafarers has emerged as a recurring focus of Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs Brics engagements. On Saturday, he proposed a seafarers emergency support network among BRICS members to provide distress alerts, medical aid, family communication and evacuation support.The proposal came on the opening day of the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi, where the safety and wellbeing of seafarers emerged as a recurring theme in PM Modiâs remarks amid heightened tensions in West Asia and disruptions to key shipping routes.
âSeafarers make a significant contribution to global trade, but they often find themselves without adequate support during difficult times. My proposal is: Can we create a Seafarers Emergency Support Network?â, PM Modi said during his opening remarks while addressing the summit.âThrough this, the Maritime Authorities and Missions of the concerned countries can be connected. It can provide support for distress alerts, medical assistance, informing families and evacuation,â he added.
Modiâs proposal follows his remarks at the Brics Business Forum on Friday, when he highlighted the importance of safe sea lanes and the protection of seafarers, particularly amid the conflict in West Asia.
âGlobal trade can move forward only when sea lanes are secure, supply routes remain open, and seafarers are safe. That is why India is a staunch advocate of freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers,â PM Modi said at the forum.The issue also featured in PM Modiâs meeting with Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian on Friday. According to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), PM underscored the need to ensure âfreedom of navigation and commerce, and the safety and well-being of seafarersâ during discussions on the conflict in West Asia.The concern has a direct bearing on India, which has a large seafaring workforce and has faced casualties amid the wider regional conflict. In July, the government had said in Parliament that 16 Indian nationals, including 10 seafarers, have lost their lives in the region since the outbreak of the of the conflict, while 75 have been injured.The summit is taking place against the backdrop of continuing geopolitical and economic uncertainty, including the West Asia crisis, disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, the Russia-Ukraine war and US trade and tariff policies. India has repeatedly stressed the importance of keeping shipping and commercial routes open.On Saturday, PM Modi also linked the maritime proposal to a wider call for Brics to translate its consensus into practical outcomes as the grouping marked two decades since its formation.âI am delighted to welcome you all to India. Indiaâs chairship is based on a people-centric and humanity-first approach. Resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability have been our priority,â PM Modi said.
He said India had organised more than 350 meetings across nearly 30 cities during its chairship and thanked member countries for their participation.âThis year's Brics summit marks a historic milestone. We are celebrating the 20th anniversary of Brics. In human life, the age of twenty heralds the beginning of a new phase of maturity and responsibility,â PM said.
âThis is the stage where responsibility aligns with aspirations, and potential finds a new direction. Today, Brics, too, is at a moment of coming of age,â he added.âNow is the time for us to translate the unity and consensus within Brics into tangible outcomes on the global stage.âThe summit was attended by Chinese president Xi Jinping, Russian president Vladimir Putin, Saudi Arabiaâs Crown Prince, South African president Cyril Ramaphosa, Egyptian president Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Ethiopian prime minister Abiy Ahmed Ali, Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian, Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan and Indonesian president Prabowo Subianto, among other leaders and representatives.

headline: U.S. envoy Sergio Gor visits Manipur, meets CM and governor
full_text:
U.S. envoy Sergio Gor visits Manipur, meets CM and governor
US Ambassador Sergio Gor visited Manipur, meeting local leaders and exploring historic sites, emphasizing US-Manipur relations and tourism development.
IMPHAL: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor reached Imphal on Friday for a two-day visit to Manipur, during which he called on chief minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh and governor Ajay Kumar Bhalla and visited two historic places in the state capital.
Gor, accompanied by US Consul General in Kolkata Kathy Giles-Diaz, visited Kangla Fort, the ancient capital of the erstwhile Manipur kingdom, and Khwairamband Keithel, the all-women-run market in the heart of Imphal.
On Friday evening, Gor met Khemchand at the chief minister’s secretariat in Mantripukhri. In a social media post, the chief minister said, “It was a pleasure to meet the Ambassador of the United States to India, Sergio Gor, today. We had the opportunity to discuss relations between the US and Manipur. I am confident that the engagement between the US and Manipur will strengthen in the years to come.”
According to a statement issued by the chief minister’s secretariat, Gor hailed Manipur’s natural beauty, saying, “Manipur is a stunning place and it has a stunning beauty.”
The US ambassador also enquired about the number of tourists visiting the state and expressed happiness that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was focusing on the development of the Northeast.
Gor also met governor Ajay Kumar Bhalla at Lok Bhavan in Imphal on Friday evening. He said there was a “special bond between PM Modi and US President Donald Trump, beyond the normal Prime minister-President relationship,” adding that “Trump personally cherished the relationship,” the statement said.
Khemchand invited Gor to the upcoming Manipur Sangai Festival 2026, scheduled for late November. He said India was a “mini world” and Manipur a “mini India”, and that the state was home to 36 communities, it added.

headline: Against the backdrop of continued hostilities in West Asia, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, held talks in New Delhi on Saturday (September 12, 2026) on the sidelines of th...
full_text:
Against the backdrop of continued hostilities in West Asia, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, held talks in New Delhi on Saturday (September 12, 2026) on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit. The two sides discussed the regional hostilities and expressed support for "de-escalation".
The conversation came ten days after Iran targeted military installations in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The ‘New Delhi Declaration’, adopted at the BRICS Summit and announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has expressed “deep concern” about the multiple conflicts in West Asia, but stopped short of naming any of the major stakeholders, including the United States, in the text.
‘Efforts to ease tensions’
The Abu Dhabi Media Office said in a statement, “During the meeting, His Highness and the Iranian President discussed several regional and international issues of mutual interest. They also underscored the importance of supporting efforts to ease tensions, promote de-escalation and strengthen regional stability, while advancing opportunities for peace and development for the peoples of the region.” Iranian state-owned news outlet IRNA said the meeting was held following “Iran’s consistent calls for and emphasis on strengthening relations with its southern neighbours”.
Mr. Pezeshkian said on Saturday (September 12, 2026) that West Asia does not need the United States, which is at war with Iran, to be a “regional policeman”. After a meeting with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, the Iranian President said, “The territorial integrity and security of the region [West Asia] can only be guaranteed by its main players and the countries that comprise it.”
The conflicts in West Asia acquired prominence on the first day of the BRICS Summit here on Saturday, with the joint declaration announced at the end of the first day’s leaders’ dialogue dropping any references to the contesting parties in order to reach a consensus. The joint statement — the New Delhi Declaration — announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed “deep concern” over the tension in West Asia while also supporting the “inalienable rights” of the Palestinian people in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank.
“We express deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in West Asia and, recalling our respective national position, call for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation,” said the New Delhi Declaration, highlighting the need to maintain “smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy, in accordance with applicable international law".
‘Deep concern’ over Palestine
The declaration further expressed “deep concern” regarding the continued fighting in the Gaza Strip and called for “halting any policies aimed at forced displacement of Palestinians”. It also highlighted the need for a “just and lasting solution” to the Israel-Palestine conflict.
The document extended support to the “establishment of a sovereign, independent and viable State of Palestine” within the “internationally recognised 1967 borders that include the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, with East Jerusalem as its capital”. The declaration said that Israel has the “legal obligation” to ensure the supply of “humanitarian aid in Gaza” and called on Israel to respect the terms agreed with the Lebanese government and to withdraw its occupying forces from all Lebanese territories.
The declaration took a strong position on the attacks on the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) that have been continuing since the Israel-Palestinian conflict flared up in October 2023.
Iran had gained diplomatically at the SCO Summit in Bishkek earlier this month, when a joint statement clearly condemned the attacks on Iran and supported Iran’s territorial integrity and sovereignty.
The conversation around West Asia in New Delhi gained further prominence with the arrival of Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud on Saturday (September 12, 2026) evening. The External Affairs Ministry had earlier condemned attacks by the Houthi militia on Saudi sovereign territory and civilian and economic facilities, saying that “such attacks that undermined regional security and stability and threatened freedom of navigation in the Bab-el-Mandeb were unacceptable”.

headline: ‘India building economic bridges’: PM Modi hails country's business push at BRICS forum
full_text:
‘India building economic bridges’: PM Modi hails country's business push at BRICS forum
PM Modi's statement acquires significance in the context of disruptions to global trade over the past 18 months.
India’s focus is on reducing barriers to trade and increasing opportunities for business, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said at the BRICS Business Forum on Friday, a statement that acquires significance in the context of disruptions to global trade over the past 18 months, first on account of US action on tariffs, and then because of the war in West Asia that choked a key shipping route for energy supplies.
Modi added that India strongly supports freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers. India is disproportionately represented in global merchant navies, and according to earlier statements by the ministry of external affairs, at least 10 Indian seafarers have died in the West Asia conflict and five in attacks on ships in the Black Sea.
“Global trade can move forward only when sea lanes are secure, supply routes are open, and seafarers are safe. And therefore, India is a strong supporter of freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers,” he said.
“Today, when trade barriers are increasing in the world, India is building economic bridges,” he said, citing examples of FTAs with about 40 countries since 2014 to boost trade amid global headwinds.
Deep Dive
“Our approach in BRICS is also the same -- to reduce barriers and increase opportunities for businesses,” Modi said. Therefore, under our chairship, we have formed new cooperation networks in areas such as agriculture, health, skills, and smart grids, he added.
He named some of the initiatives, such as the BRICS Incubator Network, BRICS MSME Portal, and BRICS Startup Innovation Fund, as examples to connect businesses, startups and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) of member countries with markets and finance.
Addressing a large number of delegates from India and other member countries at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, Modi said: “All of you can take advantage of these cooperation frameworks and increase the exchange of investment and talent among our countries.”
Emphasising the theme of India’s BRICS chairship -- “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability” – the Prime Minister said this mantra has also been the foundation of India’s economic and trade policy for the last 12 years. “If we talk about resilience, India has made supply chains more diversified and reliable, from energy to technology. The result of this resilience is that, even amid global uncertainties, India today is providing confidence of growth and stability.” India’s economy grew at 7.8% in the first quarter of this year.
India has done this by building infrastructure, promoting start-ups, and focusing on innovation, Modi explained.
He gave the example of India’s investments in creating public infrastructure such as roads, railways, ports, and airports, and in creating new capacities in strategic sectors such as shipbuilding, semiconductors, quantum, critical minerals, and biotechnology.
“Today, a startup revolution is taking place in India,” Modi said; India boasts over 2 lakh startups and more than 120 unicorns. “Our startups are transforming education and healthcare through AI, working on green hydrogen and batteries, and also crossing new frontiers in defence and space. Now, through BRICS as well, we have to take these world-class innovations to global markets.”
The PM highlighted India’s innovation story in digital payments, which has been scaled up to almost the entire population of 1.4 billion people. “India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has given new momentum to financial inclusion and digital transactions at population scale. Today, 50% of the world’s real-time payments take place through this technology… We are proud that many countries are adopting this world-class ecosystem of India. Innovators from BRICS countries can also, based on this experience, develop new solutions for their own countries,” he said.
Underscoring the growing importance of BRICS since 2006, Modi said the grouping initially had only four member countries, which have now risen to 21, representing 50% of the world’s population, 40% of GDP and over 25% of trade. BRICS has 11 members— Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates, and 10 partners—Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam.
“Not only that, while global GDP has grown by 2.5 times during these years, the combined GDP of BRICS nations increased by approximately 4.5 times,” Modi said, referring to the growing economic strength of BRICS that increased about twice the speed of global growth.

headline: Putin's Aurus, Xi's Hongqi: Inside the super-secure armoured cars at BRICS Summit
full_text:
Putin's Aurus, Xi's Hongqi: Inside the super-secure armoured cars at BRICS Summit
Both limousines combine heavy armour with secure communication systems, allowing the leaders to remain protected and connected while on the move.
Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping are bringing more than their delegations to the BRICS Summit in New Delhi. Their presidential motorcades feature two heavily armoured, specially built state cars.
Putin, who arrived on September 11, is travelling in his Russian-made Aurus Senat. Xi, who arrives on September 12, is expected to use China's Hongqi N701.
Both limousines combine heavy armour with secure communication systems, allowing the leaders to remain protected and connected while on the move.
Here is a closer look at the two cars set to be part of the high-security BRICS Summit in New Delhi.
PUTIN'S AURUS SENAT
Putin switched to the Aurus Senat in 2018, replacing the Mercedes-Benz S 600 Guard Pullman previously used by the Russian presidency.
The car was developed under Russia's Kortezh project to build domestically manufactured vehicles for the country's top officials. The presidential L700 is around seven metres long and weighs several tonnes, much of it due to its armour and security equipment.
It is powered by a 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8 hybrid engine producing around 598 horsepower and 880 Nm of torque, paired with a nine-speed automatic transmission and all-wheel drive.
The exact level of protection remains classified, but the Senat is reported to be capable of withstanding high-calibre and armour-piercing bullets. Its windows use multi-layer bullet-resistant glass several centimetres thick.
It also has run-flat tyres, a reinforced fuel tank and underbody protection against explosions. The passenger compartment reportedly has an independent oxygen and filtration system for use in the event of a chemical attack, along with fire-suppression systems.
Secure communications allow Putin to remain in contact with officials while travelling.
The rear cabin has heated and ventilated massage seats, digital screens, work tables, a refrigerator and a privacy partition.
A civilian Senat costs around 18 million roubles, or roughly Rs 2.5 crore. Putin's presidential version has additional security systems and is not commercially available.
The car also has an India connection. Prime Minister Narendra Modi travelled with Putin in the Aurus during the SCO Summit in China last year.
XI'S HONGQI N701
Xi's presidential car comes from Hongqi, or "Red Flag", a marque established in 1958 by First Automotive Works to build cars for China's political leadership.
Its early models were used by senior Communist Party officials and visiting foreign leaders. The marque later lost prominence as foreign luxury manufacturers expanded in China before being revived as a premium domestic brand.
Xi's high-security movements are now associated with the Hongqi N701, although China has released few official details about the limousine.
The N701 is estimated to be more than 18 feet long and weigh over three tonnes. It is believed to have heavy armour, bullet-resistant glass and reinforced bodywork, along with independent life-support and secure communication systems.
Unlike the Aurus, even the N701's basic mechanical specifications remain largely undisclosed. China has not officially revealed its engine, power output or precise level of ballistic protection.
The limousine is produced in very limited numbers and is not available to private buyers.
Hongqi also has a direct India connection through another of its flagship cars, the L5.
PM Modi travelled in a Hongqi L5 during his visit to Tianjin for the SCO Summit in 2025. Xi had earlier used an L5 during his 2019 visit to India for informal talks with the PM in Mahabalipuram.
The L5 is more than 5.5 metres long and weighs over three tonnes. It has been offered with a 6.0-litre V12 producing more than 400 horsepower and can reportedly reach nearly 210 kmph.
Its cabin has leather seats, wood and jade detailing, heated and ventilated massage seats and individual entertainment screens. The L5 costs nearly 5 million yuan, or around Rs 7 crore.

headline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping held bilateral talks on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi, marking Xi Jinping's first visit to India in seven years. The summit resulted in the adoption of the New Delhi Decla...
full_text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping held bilateral talks on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi, marking Xi Jinping's first visit to India in seven years. The summit resulted in the adoption of the New Delhi Declaration, which condemned terrorism, specifically referencing the 22 April 2025 Jammu and Kashmir terror attack, and called for action against cross-border terrorism, terror financing, and safe havens. Discussions between the leaders and diplomatic panels focused on maintaining peace along the Line of Actual Control, expanding economic cooperation, and addressing trade imbalances, including market access barriers for Indian pharmaceutical and software sectors in China alongside potential amendments to Press Note 3. The forum also examined the Russia-India-China troika dynamics, multipolar diplomacy, US trade policies, de-dollarisation, and the expansion of India-Russia bilateral trade in energy, fertilizers, and technology under Western geopolitical pressure. The meeting follows prior summits in Wuhan and Mahabalipuram and ongoing high-level talks focused on border stability.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed regional diplomacy and the BRICS framework, stating, 'We have no problems with the UAE' and describing regional nations as brothers with long-standing trade ties. He identified US military bases across the region as the source of aggression against Iran's people and infrastructure. Pezeshkian noted that Washington seeks to exploit regional energy resources and create division. On BRICS, he highlighted ongoing efforts toward a joint communique, collaborative investments via the New Development Bank, and reducing reliance on the US dollar to challenge unilateralism.
In an interview at the BRICS Summit, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed regional conflicts, bilateral cooperation with India, and resistance to unilateral economic measures. Defending his country against accusations, Pezeshkian stated, "You see, we did not start the war. They started the war." He highlighted Iran's strategic geopolitical role as a connectivity crossroads and underscored readiness to revive historic trade routes like the Silk Road with India through investments in Chabahar Port. Pezeshkian noted that ongoing discussions with the Indian Prime Minister cover broader investment partnerships, trade, and economic networks. Discussing US sanctions, he affirmed that BRICS aims to break unilateralism and totalitarianism in global commerce alongside major economies like China, India, and Russia.
Union ministers and chief ministers arrived at Bharat Mandapam in a special bus from Parliament to attend a gala dinner hosted on the opening day of the 18th BRICS Summit in the national capital. The venue is hosting leaders and delegates from twenty-one nations. The official gathering comes amid diplomatic engagements and the anticipation of a possible joint statement following bilateral discussions, highlighting both formal proceedings and broader diplomatic outreach during the summit.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit 2026. The two leaders welcomed the progress in India-China relations and affirmed taking a strategic, long-term perspective, noting differences should not become disputes. Prime Minister Modi highlighted that ties must be guided by mutual respect, mutual sensitivity, and mutual interest, emphasizing that peace and tranquillity in border areas remain essential for developing bilateral relations. Both sides agreed on resolving the boundary issue fairly and observing existing agreements. Discussions also addressed structural trade imbalances, supply chain issues, market access, and expanding people-to-people exchanges.

New Delhi, The Delhi High Court will pass on Monday its order on the point of jurisdiction to entertain a plea by makers of Vimal Elaichi seeking to quash show-cause notices issued to their brand ambassadors, Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff, by the Maharashtra FDA for alleged misrepresentation of the product in their advertisement.

It said regulatory notices were issued by the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration alleging that advertisements for Vimal Elaichi amount to surrogate promotion of Vimal Pan Masala, a chewable product banned within Maharashtra.
The plea said the Maharashtra FDA had directed the actors featured in Vimal Elaichi advertisements to provide documentation demonstrating that Vimal Elaichi is a product different from banned pan masala products. headline: Uniform Civil Code will be implemented by 2029 in the 21 States where the Bharatiya Janata Party and the NDA are in power, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said in Mumbai on Sunday (September 13, 2026). He said the government was committed to deporting ...
full_text:
Uniform Civil Code will be implemented by 2029 in the 21 States where the Bharatiya Janata Party and the NDA are in power, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said in Mumbai on Sunday (September 13, 2026). He said the government was committed to deporting every illegal immigrant from the country.
Mr. Shah, who spoke to the press, refused to give a timeline for the implementation of the National Register of Citizens (NRC) in Manipur. However, he said the government was discussing with allies and political parties the use of the 1951 baseline for the exercise.
Speaking about the Gen Z protests in July, he said everyone must express opinions in a democracy. “We want to communicate with everyone. We don’t want to run the country in an Emergency-like situation. Congress culture was different. Our culture is different,” he said.
Mr. Shah, who is on a two-day visit to Maharashtra, was speaking on the occasion of the ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyaan’, a month-long national drive from September 17 to October 17 to celebrate Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday and the completion of his 25 years of service as a Chief Minister and as the Prime Minister.
The Congress slammed the Home Minister for evading questions on the allegations of corruption surrounding the Maharashtra State Co-operative Bank Limited ‘scam’ involving alleged financial irregularities of ₹25,000 crore through improper loan disbursals and distress sale of cooperative sugar factories.
Mr. Shah is also the Union Minister of Co-operation, and when asked whether his Ministry planned to present a white paper in the case, owing to the differences in the probe findings by the Central and the State agencies, he said, “Why should we? The agencies are doing their work. They will file a charge sheet in the court. I now request you all to limit yourselves to the topic of the 25 years of service.”
Maharashtra Congress president Harshawardhan Sapkal said the Union Minister “ran away” from the press conference as he did not have the “courage” to answer questions on the multi-crore ‘scam’.
Mr. Shah’s visit to the State comes amid differences over making functional Marathi compulsory for cab and auto drivers. He will attend the Hindi Divas celebration in Mumbai on Monday (September 14, 2026). Asked about the conflicts over language and regional identity arising from migration, he said, “It is our government’s policy to prioritise the mother tongue, and the Constitution has issued specific directives to the States in this regard. I do not believe this will become a major issue. While isolated incidents may occur if certain individuals attempt to stoke tensions, the States have experienced leadership and will certainly find a way to resolve such issues.”
The BJP enjoys the electoral support of the migrant population, particularly in financial centres like Mumbai and Pune.
Mr. Shah, who presented the 52nd India Gem and Jewellery Awards at another event, urged the diamond industry to take a lead in controlling the lab-grown diamond ecosystem.
“In terms of volume, the market for lab-grown diamonds is poised to expand to nearly 50 times the size of the current diamond market. This represents a huge opportunity. It is my appeal to you that the lab-grown diamond ecosystem should be in the control of people of Bharat.”

headline: Air India's Bhopal-Delhi flight diverted to Jaipur due to technical issue, safety checks underway
full_text:
Air India's Bhopal-Delhi flight diverted to Jaipur due to technical issue, safety checks underway
Flight AI1886 operating from Bhopal to Delhi on 13 September was diverted to Jaipur where it landed safely.
Air India flight AI1886 operating from Bhopal to Delhi on Sunday was diverted to Jaipur due to a technical issue, the airline said.
“Flight AI1886 operating from Bhopal to Delhi on 13 September was diverted to Jaipur due to a technical issue as per laid-down procedures. The aircraft landed safely at Jaipur and is undergoing checks in line with Air India’s safety standards,” Air India said.
The airline regretted the inconvenience caused to passengers due to the situation and said efforts were being made to fly them to their destination at the earliest.

“Air India regrets the inconvenience caused to passengers by this unforeseen situation, and every effort is being made to fly the passengers to their destination at the earliest. Our ground team at Jaipur has been providing immediate assistance and support to the passengers. Our ground team at Jaipur has been providing immediate assistance and support to the passengers,” the airline said.
Earlier on Wednesday, Air India flight AI 131 from Mumbai to London was diverted and landed in Zurich amid an air traffic control-related disruption at London Heathrow Airport.

The flight, carrying over 290 passengers, landed at Zurich Airport after the disruption affected operations at Heathrow.
Initially, passengers remained onboard the aircraft at Zurich and were instructed to wait as the situation at London Heathrow was expected to be resolved.
However, the flight was subsequently cancelled, and all passengers disembarked at Zurich Airport.
The development came amid a technical issue in the UK's air traffic control system that disrupted flight operations at major airports, including Heathrow, leading to widespread delays and cancellations.
Monitoring service FlightRadar has reported that "more than 1,000 flights have been cancelled" across UK airports.
In a post on X earlier on Tuesday evening, the service said, "Inbound flights to London airports Manchester Birmingham are looking very different tonight compared to last Tuesday.
