headline: Did Swatantra Bhardwaj use casteist slur during CJP protest? Court asks police
full_text:
Did Swatantra Bhardwaj use casteist slur during CJP protest? Court asks police
A Delhi court reserved its order on Swatantra Bhardwaj's bail plea after asking police whether he used a casteist slur during a June 23 protest. Police said the original complaint did not mention one, but the allegation was added later, leading to invocation of SC/ST Act provisions. The order is due Tuesday.
A Delhi court on Monday asked Delhi Police whether Hindutva influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj had used a casteist slur during an alleged assault on the father of a student activist at a June 23 protest at Jantar Mantar. The police told the court that the original complaint did not mention any casteist slur, but when the statement was recorded again, such an allegation was made, after which provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act were invoked.
The court also reserved for September 15 its order on the bail plea of Bhardwaj, who is facing charges linked to the alleged assault. The court said it would pass the order on Tuesday after hearing both sides.
During the hearing, Bhardwaj's lawyer said his client was arrested only after "some political developments" and claimed that the complainant had in fact attacked Bhardwaj during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest. The complainant's lawyer opposed the bail plea, saying there was no illegality in the arrest and that FIRs, including under the SC/ST Act and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, had been registered against the accused.
Bhardwaj had been remanded to 14 days' judicial custody on September 7, and Additional Sessions Judge Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler last week extended it till September 21.
Appearing for Bhardwaj, his counsel said an FIR was registered against him on June 23 and a notice was issued on June 27 asking him to appear for questioning. "I appeared for questioning on June 29. After that, I was allowed to go. Then, after some political developments, I was arrested on September 4. After my arrest, a new FIR (under POCSO Act) was registered," the lawyer said.
He also told the court that "the complainant himself attacked me" during the CJP protest and said a video on social media showed Bhardwaj falling before being rescued by police. The court then played the video clip.
After this, the complainant's lawyer reiterated that the arrest was lawful. Judge Laler then said the proceedings would be held in-camera, following which court staff asked media personnel to step outside. Later, the staff said the order had been reserved and would be delivered on Tuesday.
Bhardwaj was detained in Bulandshahr on September 4, hours after the CJP staged a protest outside Parliament Street police station demanding his arrest over the alleged assault. The action followed outrage over an interview in which Bhardwaj claimed he had "cracked the skull" of the student activist's father during the June 23 protest and escaped arrest because of his political connections.
He was produced at Judge Laler's residence the next day, when the court allowed Delhi Police's plea for one-day custodial interrogation, and a magisterial court sent him to one-day judicial custody the following day. The bail order is now awaited.

headline: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday (September 14, 2026) said cultural nationalism meant creating awareness about India's culture and history, asserting the country's diverse languages could have different voices but the national sentiment should...
full_text:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday (September 14, 2026) said cultural nationalism meant creating awareness about India's culture and history, asserting the country's diverse languages could have different voices but the national sentiment should remain one.
“All political differences must be set aside to promote Indian languages,” Mr. Shah said while asserting that a child can understand the country only through his or her mother tongue.
Mr. Shah linked the promotion of Indian languages to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's pledge of freeing the country from a "mindset of slavery".
Addressing the 6th All India Rajbhasha Sammelan, Mr. Shah said Bal Gangadhar Tilak had understood that awareness about the country's culture and history could be created through cultural nationalism.
“Tilak started public Ganesh festivities and celebrations of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's birth anniversary, both festivals eventually spreading beyond Maharashtra, helping create a wave of patriotism during the freedom struggle,” Mr. Shah said.
The Minister said 'Hindi Shabd Sindhu', which began with 51,000 words, had now grown to eight lakh words and expressed confidence that it would become the world's largest dictionary by 2029.
Mr. Shah said more than 50,000 words from Indian regional languages had been incorporated into 'Hindi Shabd Sindhu' to fill gaps where Hindi lacked words. He said the dictionary had accepted words from Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Bengali and Odia etc, thereby making Hindi more flexible.
Mr. Shah said Maharashtra had the country's most multilingual culture, with Marathi, Konkani, Gujarati, Sindhi, Hindi, Kannada and Warli among the languages spoken and developed here.
He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had accorded Marathi the status of a classical language.
Mr. Shah said Hindi should act as a means of communication and connection among India's languages rather than competition.
“Vinoba Bhave had said the use of Hindi had enabled him to take the message of the Bhoodan-Gramdan movement nationwide,” Mr. Shah added.
The Home Minister said his knowledge of Hindi had helped him work across the country when his party assigned him a national-level responsibility.
He also said the Rajbhasha department had developed the multilingual translation tool 'Bharati', while the government had set up 'Bharatiya Bhasha Anubhag'. He invited elected representatives to communicate with the Centre in Marathi, assuring them arrangements were in place for translation.
“The Union government wants to make Indian languages the language of governance and science,” he said, adding that the aim is to enrich them through literature.
“Candidates can appear for examinations such as IAS and IPS in their mother tongue, while JEE, NEET and undergraduate exam were being conducted in 13 languages,” he pointed out.
"Political differences must be set aside to promote Indian languages. A child can understand India only through the mother tongue," Mr. Shah asserted.
“Prime Minister Narendra Modi made imparting of primary education in one's mother tongue mandatory under National Education Policy (NEP),” Shah added.
"The biggest work PM Modi has done is that, under NEP, he has made learning in mother tongue compulsory and also made learning another Indian language mandatory. Those opposing NEP provision of learning one more Indian language apart from mother tongue do not know what sin they are committing," he said.
Mr. Shah said more than five lakh Central government employees had undergone language training, while AI-based 'Kanthasth 2.0' had been made available to foreigners with more than five crore sentences. 'Leela Rajbhasha' and 'Leela Pravah' had been developed as language-learning resources.
He said nine volumes had so far been prepared by Rajbhasha Committee. Five of them would be dedicated during the Modi government's tenure.
Mr. Shah said the government had been taking the Rajbhasha conference to different states since 2019 instead of restricting it to Delhi.
He said several publications were released during the day, including 'Rajbhasha Bharati' (Vande Mataram special issue) and 'Vande Mataram Ke 150 Adhyay'. The 'Hindi Shabd Sindhu' digital resource and training in Hindi typing and shorthand were also launched, while 'Rajbhasha Kirti' and 'Rajbhasha Gaurav' awards were presented.
Speaking on Vande Mataram, Mr. Shah said it took 80 years to restore full glory of the national song.
"Vande Mataram is not merely a song but an effort to awaken Indian consciousness to get freedom. It laid the foundation of India's cultural nationalism," he said.
“The song was later split and it took decades to restore it to glory,” Mr. Shah said referring to an old decision to just sing the first two stanzas at official events.
“Vande Mataram regained its glory and began to be sung in full at all government functions because India got a prime minister like Narendra Modi,” he said.
Mr. Shah said Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj had treated 'Swaraj', 'Swadharma' and 'Swabhasha' as integral parts of self-rule and had accorded importance to Marathi in governance.
“Mr. Modi had consistently delivered speeches in Hindi or other Indian languages at major international forums,” Shah said.
Citing Rabindranath Tagore, Mr. Shah compared Indian culture and literature to a many-petalled lotus, with each regional language forming a petal.
"Languages could remain many, but the sentiment should remain Indian and India's voice should remain one," the Union Minister asserted.

headline: DMK joins issue TVK govt over investments secured, mocks Vijay’s London visit
full_text:
DMK joins issue TVK govt over investments secured, mocks Vijay’s London visit
Chennai, Tamil Nadu's main opposition DMK on Monday took on the TVK regime over its claim of attracting investments worth more than ₹1 lakh crore within about 100 days of assuming power.
The Dravidian party mocked Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay's ongoing London visit to attract investments to the state, alleging that he had travelled there to watch a car race.
The DMK's Tamil mouthpiece Murasoli claimed that reports showed new investment proposals in Tamil Nadu had declined by about 74.5 per cent in the first quarter of 2026.
Reports had emerged that Tamil Nadu's national ranking in attracting investments had slipped from sixth to 17th, the daily alleged in an editorial published on September 14, 2026.
It was noted in such reports that following the swearing-in of new chief ministers in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Keralam and West Bengal, Tamil Nadu suffered a setback in industrial investments in the first quarter, while proposed investments in the other three states increased significantly.
"All industrial companies are marching towards Andhra Pradesh," the DMK alleged.
Against this backdrop, the TVK government, "without any visionary thought", cancelled the Parandur greenfield airport project, which had turned out to be a massive advantage for the governments of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Telangana, Murasoli claimed.
It further said social media was mocking that "Vijay is also acting as the CM of Karnataka, Andhra and Telangana".
The DMK's official organ further alleged that "various lies are being fabricated to conceal this", with the recent investors' meet being one such instance.
The Industries Department has stated that at the 'Vetri Tamil Nadu Investors Meet' held in Chennai in the presence of Vijay on August 13, as many as 97 MoUs were signed, involving investments worth ₹67,452 crore and promising to create 1,06,998 jobs.
Pointing out that the Vijay-led regime had claimed that industrial investments worth more than ₹1 lakh crore had been attracted in the 100 days since it assumed office, assuring employment opportunities for 1,21,788 people, the DMK alleged: "None of these is true."
The DMK alleged that no media outlet was permitted to cover the investors' meet.
"If investments worth ₹67,000 crore had been attracted, all media outlets could have been flown in from Delhi to showcase it, as there could be no greater source of pride for Tamil Nadu," it said.
"But what did Vijay do? He attracted investments as if he were inside a caravan, keeping it all behind closed doors. He attracted and piled them up," the DMK said sarcastically.
As soon as Vijay became chief minister, the first thing to collapse was Tamil Nadu's industrial growth, it alleged.
"It was industrialists who were the first to realise that if they invested now, neither their companies nor Tamil Nadu would grow, as Vijay knew nothing, had no visionary thinking and operated solely within the web of a few brokers," the DMK daily alleged.
More importantly, Industries Minister S Keerthana, appointed by Vijay, "cannot bring in any investments, and no one is going to invest by trusting her", it alleged.
"Even existing companies will only look to escape," the daily said.
In such an environment, the CM has undertaken a foreign trip "reportedly to attract investments", the DMK alleged.
"Believing that the country and its people will believe whatever an actor says, Vijay has left the country after pulling the wool over the eyes of crores of people," it said.
If investments are to be attracted from abroad, the chief minister's trip is usually planned only after multiple rounds of discussions involving ministers and officials, the DMK said.
"But here, the chief minister suddenly took off on his own," it alleged.
"It is unclear if someone had suggested that investments would pour in the moment Vijay stood at the London airport. The CM has gone to London not to attract investments but to witness a car race. Why should a lie be peddled that it was to get investments?" the DMK daily alleged.
Vijay assumed office as the CM of Tamil Nadu on May 10, 2026.

headline: Home Ministry calls urgent meet after 3 Italians skip immigration at Delhi airport, fly to Munich
full_text:
Home Ministry calls urgent meet after 3 Italians skip immigration at Delhi airport, fly to Munich
The three passengers had travelled from Amritsar to Delhi to board a Lufthansa flight to Munich.
The Union ministry of home affairs (MHA) has called an urgent meeting of senior officials from the home and civil aviation ministries and other stakeholders on Tuesday evening after three Italian passengers travelled from Amritsar to Delhi and boarded a Lufthansa flight to Munich without completing the mandatory immigration process, officials aware of the matter said on Monday.
According to the notice seen by HT, the meeting, to be chaired by home secretary Govind Mohan, will include the secretary and additional secretary of the civil aviation ministry, Intelligence Bureau director, secretary and additional secretary of the home ministry, Bureau of Immigration (BoI) commissioner, Air India Group head and Delhi airport CEO.
The meeting comes after the Union ministry of civil aviation (MoCA) issued a show-cause notice to Air India on September 12, following concerns raised by the MHA over the airline’s handling of the passengers.
The incident took place on September 4.
“The home ministry has called for a meeting of the stakeholders at 7pm in Kartavya Bhawan (MHA office) to discuss the incident on Tuesday,” an official said.
An Air India spokesperson did not comment on the matter. MoCA also did not offer a comment.
However, HT learnt that the airline had not responded to the show-cause notice as of Tuesday evening.
The three passengers had travelled from Amritsar to Delhi to board a Lufthansa flight to Munich. They did not complete immigration formalities at Delhi airport before boarding the international flight, people aware of the matter said. The lapse appears to have occurred at Amritsar airport, they said.
“They were issued two boarding passes at the Amritsar airport for Delhi as well as for the Munich flight operated by Lufthansa. The passengers were supposed to complete their immigration at the Delhi airport but they were directed to the I-to-I (international-to-international) transfer, due to which they were able to board their international flight without completing the mandatory process,” one of the people said.
Amritsar is among the airports where the government has introduced a “hub-and-spoke model”.
Under the model, passengers travelling to international destinations complete immigration formalities at the origin airport before transferring to an international flight at the designated hub. At the hub, passengers are required only to undergo security checks before boarding their onward international flight.
In the present case, however, the passengers were travelling from Amritsar, the spoke, to Delhi, the hub, before taking their international flight to Munich.
Since the two flights were not operating under the applicable hub-and-spoke arrangement, the passengers were required to complete immigration formalities in Delhi before boarding the Lufthansa flight, according to people aware of the matter.

headline: Why Delhi HC rejected Vimal Elaichi makers' plea over FDA notice to SRK, Ajay Devgn, Tiger Shroff
full_text:
Why Delhi HC rejected Vimal Elaichi makers' plea over FDA notice to SRK, Ajay Devgn, Tiger Shroff
The court said the petitioner should approach courts in Maharashtra, which would be the more suitable forum to address its concerns about the notices.
The Delhi high court on Monday rejected a petition by the makers of Vimal Elaichi seeking to quash show-cause notices issued by the Maharashtra food and drugs administration (FDA) to brand ambassadors Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff.
Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said the court lacked territorial jurisdiction to hear the matter. The judge said the petitioner should approach courts in Maharashtra, which would be the more suitable and convenient forum to address its concerns about the notices, under the doctrine of forum conveniens.
What did the petition say?
PB Agro LLP, in its petition, said it hires established film actors to advertise its cardamom product sold under the 'Vimal' brand. The company said it has entered into endorsement deals with the actors and is taking steps to ensure its advertising campaigns comply with applicable laws.
The company said the Maharashtra FDA had issued notices alleging that advertisements for Vimal Elaichi were a form of surrogate promotion for Vimal Pan Masala. Its counsel argued that the August 11 FDA notice was issued only to the actors, not to the company, even though the company would be the one to face serious consequences from any action by the state regulator.
Inside the FDA notice over Vimal ad
The notice, dated August 11, 2026, was issued under the Food Safety and Standards Act (FSS Act), 2006, and related regulations to Bollywood actors Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff over their role as brand endorsers in an advertisement for Vimal Elaichi, HT reported earlier.
The FDA said in the notice that the Vimal brand is “prominently associated with Pan Masala in the market” and noted that pan masala products are prohibited in Maharashtra.
The FDA told the actors to end their involvement in the advertisement with immediate effect. It also instructed them to take down promotional material from their official social media accounts and other platforms, while seeking information about the due diligence they had conducted before agreeing to endorse the product.
The actors were further asked to hand over their endorsement agreements, campaign briefs and other relevant records.
The FDA also sought an explanation on whether Vimal Elaichi is a standalone product or is being used as a surrogate communication for Vimal Pan Masala or tobacco-related products.

headline: Court rejects Vimal Elaichi plea over FDA notices to Shah Rukh, Ajay Devgn, Tiger
full_text:
Court rejects Vimal Elaichi plea over FDA notices to Shah Rukh, Ajay Devgn, Tiger
The Delhi High Court dismissed PB Agro LLP's plea against Maharashtra FDA notices to Vimal Elaichi brand ambassadors. The order pushes the company to Maharashtra courts without ruling on the surrogate advertising allegations.
The Delhi High Court on Monday dismissed a plea by PB Agro LLP, the maker of Vimal Elaichi, which had sought to quash show-cause notices issued by the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration to its brand ambassadors Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff. The notices alleged that advertisements for Vimal Elaichi amounted to surrogate promotion of Vimal Pan Masala, a chewable product banned in Maharashtra.
Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma held that the petition was not maintainable before the Delhi High Court because of lack of territorial jurisdiction. The court said courts in Maharashtra were the more appropriate and convenient forum for the petitioner to raise its grievances concerning the impugned notice, in line with the doctrine of forum conveniens.
In its order, the court said, "The petition is therefore dismissed on this ground, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the petitioner's challenge. Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of."
PB Agro LLP had said in its petition that it engaged reputed actors to promote its cardamom product under the brand Vimal and that its endorsement agreements and advertisement campaign were in full compliance with applicable laws.
The company said the Maharashtra FDA had issued regulatory notices alleging that Vimal Elaichi advertisements were surrogate advertisements for Vimal Pan Masala. According to the plea, the FDA had directed the actors appearing in the advertisements to submit documents showing that Vimal Elaichi was different from the banned pan masala products. It had also called for the promotional campaign to be stopped and related material to be removed from digital platforms.
Counsel for the petitioner argued that the August 11 FDA notice had been sent only to the actors and not to the company, even though the company alone would suffer irreparable loss because of any action by the state regulator. The counsel also said the petitioner had not been given an opportunity to be heard. The company further claimed that the Maharashtra FDA lacked jurisdiction to direct that the advertisements be halted. In its petition, it also said the allegation of surrogate advertising was baseless because Vimal Pan Masala had neither been manufactured nor sold in Maharashtra since 2001, and pan masala containing tobacco had been barred nationwide by the Supreme Court since 2013.
The high court, however, said the petitioner had failed to show that any substantial or material part of the cause of action had arisen within the territorial jurisdiction of the Delhi High Court. It noted, "The impugned show-cause notice was issued by the FDA, Mumbai, state of Maharashtra – to the brand ambassadors engaged by the petitioner, who are residents of Mumbai – in relation to alleged activities and alleged statutory violations in Maharashtra." The court also said that although the petitioner had made the ministry and the FSSAI, both based in Delhi, parties to the case, "neither any specific relief is claimed against either of them, nor any direction or order passed by these authorities has been challenged before the court or even placed on record with the writ petition".
The court said the fact that the petitioner operated from Delhi or engaged brand ambassadors from Delhi could not by itself give the Delhi High Court territorial jurisdiction, especially when the impugned notice had not been issued to the petitioner. Justice Sharma said jurisdiction could not be created by selectively relying on facts such as the petitioner's registered office, the place from which payments were made, or where the advertising campaign may have been conceived or managed, when those facts had no direct bearing on the validity of the notice. The court added that it must guard against pleadings being shaped to present incidental facts as the cause of action when the material facts of the dispute lay elsewhere, and that background facts did not confer territorial jurisdiction merely because they were mentioned in the petition. Counsel for the Centre and the Central Consumer Protection Authority had also argued that the petition should have been filed before the Bombay High Court because the show-cause notice had been issued by the Maharashtra government.
With this, the Delhi High Court dismissed PB Agro LLP's plea on the ground of territorial jurisdiction, leaving it free to pursue its challenge in Maharashtra, while making no observation on the merits of the dispute over the Vimal Elaichi advertisements.

headline: Why Brics Delhi Summit was a diplomatic victory for India | 5 big points
full_text:
Why Brics Delhi Summit was a diplomatic victory for India | 5 big points
India steered Brics nations to adopt the New Delhi Declaration despite deep splits. India got the backing on the Pahalgam terror attack and kept the bloc from turning overtly anti-West. It also turned New Delhi into a stage for the Iran-UAE meeting. Here's India's Brics success explained in five points.
For India, the real test at the Brics Summit was whether a bloc pulled in different directions by wars and sharply different positions on West Asia could still find common ground. Another big test was if New Delhi could prevent the Brics from becoming an anti-US bloc given the joining of forces by China and Russia.
The 18th Brics Summit was held against the backdrop of two active wars involving members of the grouping. Just four months earlier, Brics foreign ministers had failed to produce a joint statement in New Delhi because of differences over the Middle East.
The failure to produce a joint statement at the foreign ministers' meeting in Rio de Janeiro in April 2025 had already exposed the challenge of finding consensus in an expanded Brics, which had grown from five members until 2023 to 11 by 2025. The expanded grouping brought more divergent geopolitical interests to the table.
Yet, on September 12 (Saturday), the leaders adopted the New Delhi Declaration by consensus. India was also able to get the bloc to put its collective weight behind the condemnation of the Pahalgam terror attack, while keeping the larger Brics agenda focussed on the concerns of the Global South rather than turning it into an explicitly anti-West platform.
Economist and Columbia University professor Jeffrey Sachs described the summit as a success, saying the declaration showed that "the Brics nations are taking their place in the world scene". Comparing it with India's G20 presidency, Sachs said New Delhi had again managed to build consensus "even at a very difficult time".
Notably, in three days — the eve and the two days of Brics Summit — Prime Minister Narendra Modi held 15 formal bilateral meetings with foreign leaders.
The diplomatic test for New Delhi was to steer a diverse grouping amid two active wars, trade tensions between nations, and geopolitical divisions, without allowing those differences to derail the bloc. On that measure, the Delhi summit gave India five significant wins. Let's have a look at them.
1. NEW DELHI BECAME A PLATFORM FOR IRAN-UAE MEETING
The most immediate challenge facing the summit was the war in the Middle East.
Iran and the UAE arrived at the Brics table with sharply divergent positions over the conflict in the Middle East. Since the US-Israel-Iran war began in late February, Iranian missile and drone attacks have targeted US military assets in the UAE. The two countries had already emerged as a major fault line inside the grouping.
In May, the Brics foreign ministers' meeting in New Delhi ended without a joint statement, with differences over the Middle East preventing consensus. Iran had wanted stronger language on the US-Israeli war, while the UAE had objected to positions it regarded as unacceptable.
That made a leaders' declaration in September far from certain.
Harsh V Pant, Vice President of Studies and Foreign Policy at the Observer Research Foundation, had warned before the summit that the Iran-UAE tensions could again prevent a joint declaration.
The breakthrough was visible not only in the declaration but also in the diplomatic optics.
Iran and the UAE both signed on to the Brics statement calling for restraint in the Middle East. Then, on the sidelines of the Brics Summit, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met Abu Dhabi's Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, in what Reuters described as the highest-level meeting between the two countries since the conflict began.
India's diplomatic win, therefore, was finding a way to prevent the divide between Iran and the UAE from becoming a wider Brics divide and making New Delhi a stage for an Iran-UAE meeting.
2. INDIA RESTORED CONSENSUS, MAKING IT AN INSTITUTIONAL WIN FOR BRICS
The second and perhaps more consequential achievement was institutional.
Brics had already demonstrated that its expansion had made consensus harder. The April 2025 foreign ministers' meeting in Rio de Janeiro failed to produce a joint communique. Brazil, then the Brics president, issued a chair's statement instead.
The Delhi summit therefore came with a credibility question hanging over it. Can, what couldn't be done in 2025 and earlier in 2026 be done at the Delhi Summit? Yes, it was done.
The New Delhi Declaration not only recorded consensus on geopolitical questions but also contained a wide range of institutional and economic commitments.
It endorsed continued work on global governance reform, development finance, trade, digital public infrastructure, artificial intelligence (AI), supply chains and other areas of cooperation. The declaration also explicitly commended India's Brics presidency and thanked New Delhi for hosting the summit.
That matters because a summit declaration is more than a ceremonial document for a grouping that operates largely through consensus. Its adoption demonstrates that disagreements can be contained without making the institution itself irrelevant.
Foreign policy expert Harsh V Pant had identified this as a critical test before the summit, saying that Brics' credibility was at stake because "many countries are looking at Brics with a degree of optimism". Failure to produce a joint statement, he had warned, could make that optimism fade.
India's achievement, therefore, demonstrated that an increasingly fractious grouping could still produce a common document.
3. PAHALGAM ATTACK CONDEMNATION GAVE INDIA A SIGNIFICANT DIPLOMATIC WIN
Another important outcome for India was the explicit reference to the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack.
The New Delhi Declaration says Brics members "condemn in the strongest terms" the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir, in which 26 people were killed and many more injured. It reiterates the grouping's commitment to combating terrorism, including cross-border movement of terrorists, terror financing and safe havens. It also calls for "zero tolerance" towards terrorism and rejects double standards in counter-terrorism.
Sana Hashmi, an expert on China, the Indo-Pacific and Taiwan, highlighted this in a post on X.
The declaration does not name Pakistan. But it does specifically identify the Pahalgam attack and collectively condemn it as a terrorist attack. The language also says that "all those involved in terrorist activities and their supporters must be held accountable and brought to justice in accordance with relevant national and international law".
That distinction is very important.
The outcome was particularly significant given China's presence in Brics and its close relationship with Pakistan. The declaration allowed New Delhi to isolate the issue of terrorism from the wider geopolitical disagreements within the grouping.
It also fit India's broader attempt to make counter-terrorism a central part of its diplomatic agenda. Rather than presenting Pahalgam solely as an India-Pakistan issue, New Delhi placed it within Brics' existing language on terrorism, financing, safe havens and international accountability.
4. INDIA PREVENTED BRICS FROM BECOMING ANTI-US BLOC
The fourth achievement was more subtle.
India used its Brics presidency to amplify the concerns of developing countries, but did not turn the grouping into an explicitly anti-US or anti-Western alliance.
The declaration calls for reform of global governance and greater representation for emerging markets and developing economies. It backs reform of the UN Security Council (UNSC) and says China and Russia support the aspirations of India and Brazil to play a greater role in the United Nations, including the Security Council. It also calls for greater representation of developing countries in institutions such as the IMF and World Bank.
At the same time, the document does criticise unilateral sanctions and protectionist measures. It condemns unilateral coercive measures that are contrary to international law and highlights their impact on development, health and food security. It also supports a more open, equitable and rules-based multilateral trading system.
Russia has faced some of the most crippling sanctions from the US and is fighting a war with Ukraine to prevent Nato from reaching its doorsteps. China has been competing against the US for global supremacy in trade and influence. Both Moscow and Beijing would have exerted unidirectional pressure to turn Brics into an anti-West bloc.
Former diplomat Veena Sikri on Saturday described India's position as "non-West" rather than "anti-West". She said, "We are not anti-West; we want to live as one world."
The Delhi declaration reflects that balance.
5. INDIA STEERED A DIVERSE BLOC THROUGH A CATACLYSMIC YEAR
The final achievement is perhaps the broadest one.
Brics in 2026 is not the Brics of its original five members. Its expansion has brought together countries with very different political systems, economic interests and strategic partnerships. The challenge became sharper this year because two members were directly caught up in major wars.
Russia remains at war with Ukraine, while Iran has been at the centre of the escalating conflict with the United States and Israel. The wars have had consequences far beyond the battlefield, affecting energy markets, shipping, supply chains, food security and inflation.
Yet the declaration managed to accommodate these competing interests.
On West Asia, it called for maximum restraint and diplomacy while explicitly recognising "our respective national positions". On broader international disputes, it endorsed dialogue, consultation and diplomacy.
On economic issues, it focussed heavily on resilience, development, supply chains, technology and finance.
In a year when war, economic fragmentation and great-power rivalry threatened to pull Brics apart, New Delhi managed to help reach consensus and secure outcomes important to the Global South. India has shown that Brics can remain functional despite profound differences.
The next test will be whether China can sustain the consensus India built, as Beijing takes over the presidency for 2027.

headline: Bangladesh on Sunday (September 13, 2026) said it wants to “reset” its relationship with India and build a new bilateral engagement based on mutual interests, while describing ties during the tenure of deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina as “uncomfo...
full_text:
Bangladesh on Sunday (September 13, 2026) said it wants to “reset” its relationship with India and build a new bilateral engagement based on mutual interests, while describing ties during the tenure of deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina as “uncomfortable”.
The remarks by State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir came two days after Bangladesh said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman would not participate in the BRICS Summit hosted by India as he was not invited to the event, with the invitation instead extended to the BIMSTEC chair.
The two-day BRICS Summit concluded on Sunday (September 13, 2026). India had invited Mr. Rahman to attend the summit as chairperson of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC), while a separate bilateral invitation had been in place since February.
Bangladesh wants to “reset” its bilateral relationship with India, Mr. Kobir told reporters. “We want to move towards a new relationship, which should be done through bilateral discussions, not through a multilateral forum,” he said.
India-Bangladesh ties have been strained over New Delhi providing refuge to Hasina, who fled to India following her ouster in a youth-led agitation in August 2024.
Mr. Kobir said Bangladesh needs to move beyond what he described as an “excessive preoccupation” with India and approach its relationship with New Delhi in a balanced manner, focusing on mutual interests and treating it as part of its broader engagement with other countries.
“We have to get out of the India fascination. India is just another country, and Bangladesh wants good bilateral relations with it,” he said.
Responding to a question, the Minister said, “Breakfast in India, lunch in India, dinner in India — then when will you eat your own food?” Mr. Kobir also said Prime Minister Rahman is scheduled to leave for New York on September 21 to attend the 81st session of the UN General Assembly and stay there until September 26.
Asked about the possibility of a meeting between Mr. Rahman and U.S. President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the UNGA, he said such meetings are often decided at the last moment during major international conferences.
“The primary focus of the Prime Minister’s visit is to address the UN General Assembly,” Mr. Kobir said, adding that details of the sideline meetings would be known in due course.

The Congress secured majority in Bikaner Municipal Corporation and scored a major victory in Municipal Council in Jhalawar, considered a stronghold of former chief minister Vasundhara Raje.
Independents emerged as a major force by winning 2,273 wards and dominating the verdict in Municipal Corporation in Bharatpur, the hometown of Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma, where they bagged 36 of the 65 wards.
Bharatpur gave one of the most striking verdicts of the elections as Independents won 36 of the 65 wards, while BJP managed 20 and Congress seven. BSP and RLP won one ward each.
The result assumed political significance as Bharatpur is the hometown of Chief Minister Sharma. As the numbers streamed in, Sharma termed the victory to people’s faith in the BJP, and central leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Mr. Sharma said, “On the auspicious occasion of Ganesh Chaturthi, the people of Rajasthan have delivered a historic verdict, resoundingly endorsing Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of a ‘Viksit Bharat–Viksit Rajasthan’. This magnificent victory reflects the tireless dedication of our karyakartas and the unwavering faith of our citizens. By wholeheartedly embracing ‘One State, One Election’, voters have decisively chosen resource conservation and uninterrupted development. This decisive mandate will pave the way for an even greater victory in the upcoming Panchayat polls.”
Congress on BJP’s winning margins
Congress Rajasthan chief Govind Singh Dotasra, however, claimed that the BJP’s winning margins had thinned against the pattern, even as he blamed an “unfair” delimitation to his party’s narrow losses.
Earlier, even as the vote count was on, Mr. Dotasra accused the BJP of misusing government machinery and police to influence the outcome.
According to figures available on the State Election Commission website, results for 10,235 of the 10,244 wards where counting was being held were declared till 8.30 p.m.
Apart from BJP’s 4,179 and Congress’s 3,613 wards, the Rashtriya Loktantrik Party won 63, AAP 42, CPI(M) 38, BSP 19 and Bharat Adivasi Party eight.
The BJP crossed the majority mark in Jaipur, Udaipur, Kota, and Bhilwara municipal corporations, while the Congress secured a majority in Bikaner.
In Jaipur Municipal Corporation, the BJP won 78 of the 150 wards, Congress won 53, and Independents won 15 wards. Results for four wards were yet to be declared on the SEC website.
The BJP won 53 of the 80 wards in Udaipur, while the Congress secured 23, Independents three and CPI(M) one.
In Bhilwara, the BJP won 45 of the 70 wards against the Congress’s 10, while Independents won 15.
The BJP also crossed the majority mark in Kota, winning 55 wards in the 100-member corporation.
Congress, in Bikaner Municipal Corporation, won 42 of the 80 wards against the BJP’s 27. Independents won 10 and RLP one.
Jodhpur remained on the fence as the BJP and Congress won 44 wards each in the 100-member corporation. Independents won 10 and RLP one, while one result was yet to be declared.
In Ajmer, Congress emerged as the largest party with 37 of the 80 wards against BJP’s 32 and Independents’ 11, leaving no party with a clear majority.
Congress also emerged as the largest party in the municipal corporation of Pali, the hometown of BJP state president Madan Rathore, winning 29 of the 65 wards. The BJP won 21 and Independents 15.
In Alwar, BJP was the largest party with 28 of the 65 wards, followed by Congress with 23, Independents 13 and BSP one.
Congress also scored a notable victory in Jhalawar, a region considered a political stronghold of senior BJP leader Vasundhara Raje.
It won 29 of the 45 wards in Jhalawar Municipal Council, while BJP secured 13, Independents two and AAP one.
The BJP, however, retained its dominance in Jhalrapatan municipality, winning 22 of its 35 wards against Congress’ eight and AAP’s five. Raje, a two-time chief minister, is the sitting BJP MLA from Jhalrapatan.
BJP state president Madan Rathore thanked voters and party workers and described the results as a historic victory for the party. Addressing a press conference here, Dotasra said the BJP has traditionally had an advantage in urban local body polls, particularly when in power, but Monday’s results showed that it failed to retain that edge.
He claimed that the BJP had a vote-share lead of 8.12% points over the Congress during the 2014-16 urban polls under the Vasundhara Raje government, while the Congress had a 2.2% point lead over the BJP during the 2019-21 polls under the Ashok Gehlot government.
“In this election, the BJP’s lead over the Congress is less than one per cent,” he said.
Delimitation of wards
Mr. Dotasra also alleged that the Congress would have won around 1,500 more wards but for irregular and “unfair” delimitation of wards.
The elections were held for 309 urban local bodies comprising 10 municipal corporations, 51 municipal councils and 248 municipalities.
More than 1.44 crore voters were eligible to exercise their franchise in the two-phase polling held on September 9 and 11.
In the previous municipal election cycle held between November 2019 and February 2021, Rajasthan had 196 urban local bodies comprising 7,500 wards.
After the elections for mayors and chairpersons, Congress controlled 123 of the 196 bodies and BJP 64, while Independents and other parties headed nine.
Mayors and chairpersons of the newly elected urban bodies will be elected on September 21, followed by deputy mayors, deputy chairpersons and municipal vice-presidents on September 22.

headline: New Delhi: The Aam Aadmi Party and the Goa Forward Party have joined hands ahead of the 2027 elections in the state, announcing a new alliance called ‘Goa First’, and pitching it as an alternative to the BJP and Congress.
full_text:
New Delhi: The Aam Aadmi Party and the Goa Forward Party have joined hands ahead of the 2027 elections in the state, announcing a new alliance called ‘Goa First’, and pitching it as an alternative to the BJP and Congress.
The alliance brings together AAP’s two MLAs and GFP chief Vijai Sardesai, the party’s lone MLA and a three-term legislator from Fatorda.
Sardesai has extended support to the BJP, Congress and AAP at different points in his political career and has remained a prominent figure in Goa politics.
Sardesai’s political relevance in Goa goes beyond Fatorda. He began his political career in student politics and later became the president of the Goa Pradesh Youth Congress. He was also co-opted as a councillor of the Margao Municipal Council.
Also read: Half of CJP core cockroaches have AAP in their past
Why Sardesai matters
After being denied a Congress ticket from Fatorda, he contested the 2012 Assembly election as an Independent, and won.
He founded the Goa Forward Party in 2016. In the 2017 Assembly election, the GFP contested four seats and won three, polling 3.48 per cent of the statewide vote. The election threw up a hung Assembly, with the BJP winning 13 seats and Congress 17, against the majority mark of 21.
Sardesai emerged as a kingmaker, with GFP’s three MLAs backing Manohar Parrikar to form the BJP-led government. All three GFP MLAs were made ministers, with Sardesai holding portfolios including Town and Country Planning and Agriculture. He later became deputy chief minister after Parrikar’s death.
The people of Goa didn’t have a non-BJP, non-Congress option. Our alliance, ‘Goa First’, is the formidable alternative that people have been seeking.
The Goa First alliance is loyal to the people of Goa. We will fight this election and we will win it on our own strength. pic.twitter.com/khfURgSipr
— Arvind Kejriwal (@ArvindKejriwal) September 13, 2026
The GFP withdrew support from the BJP-led government in 2019 and returned to the Opposition. He retained Fatorda in the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections.
Sardesai has remained an important regional player despite the GFP’s declining electoral strength. The party contested three seats in 2022 and won only Fatorda, polling 1.84 percent of the statewide vote. His political network and experience in both government and Opposition have kept him relevant to Goa’s political equations. His role in the 2017 hung Assembly also showed how the GFP could have an influence beyond the seats it won.
“The GFP may not have the numbers, but it carries considerable political weight because of its strong regional connect and Sardesai’s ability to raise issues that resonate with Goans. His interventions in the Assembly, particularly on issues such as jobs and local interests, have often put the government under pressure,” Professor Rahul Tripathi of Goa University told ThePrint.
He said the AAP knows that it may not be able to build that kind of reach across Goa on its own, so this alliance gives it access to pockets where the GFP and Sardesai already have an influence.
“Sardesai has shown that even with limited numbers, he can become a kingmaker when the Assembly is fractured. The alliance gives the AAP a regional face and a political network that it may not be able to replicate on its own. At the same time, it effectively ends the possibility of opposition unity, particularly with the Congress and GFP having been in talks until recently,” Tripathi added.
What does AAP get
The AAP had a larger statewide vote share than the GFP in the last Assembly election. It contested 39 of the 40 seats in 2022, winning Benaulim and Velim and securing 6.77 per cent of the vote. In 2017, the party had polled 6.27 percent but failed to win a single seat.
The BJP won 20 of the 40 seats in the 2022 election, while the Congress won 11. The AAP and GFP won two and one seat respectively.
The two parties are now seeking to combine their respective strengths — the AAP’s wider electoral footprint and two sitting MLAs with GFP’s regional base and Sardesai’s political experience.
The alliance was announced at a press conference on Sunday, with the two parties positioning “Goa First” as an alternative to the BJP-Congress politics in the state.
“On the eve of Ganesh Chaturthi, we make a new beginning in Goa’s politics. ‘Goa First’ — an alliance between Aam Aadmi Party and Goa Forward Party — to be an alternative to the BJP-Congress collusion that has destroyed the state of Goa,” AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal wrote on X.
Kejriwal further alleged that the BJP and Congress collude to help each other form governments. “The people of Goa have been cheated twice. They won’t be cheated a third time. BJP and Congress may fight during elections, but behind closed doors, they come together, make deals and help each other form governments,” he said.
The alliance also marks a break between the GFP and Congress, which fought the 2022 Goa Assembly election together. The announcement comes just days after Goa Congress president Girish Chodankar said on Saturday that talks with GFP were still underway.
The Congress has also hit out at the alliance, with party leader Pawan Khera calling the AAP the “English-medium BJP”.
“I have already said that AAP is the English-medium BJP. Here is Arvind Kejriwal himself admitting that there isn’t much difference between the BJP and AAP. Appreciate this rare display of honesty,” he said on X.
Goa’s next Assembly election is due in early 2027.
(Edited by Ajeet Tiwari)

headline: Man killed by falling boulders as Kedarnath route blocked by debris
full_text:
Man killed by falling boulders as Kedarnath route blocked by debris
A 65-year-old man died after falling boulders struck him near the Cheerbasa Helipad on the Kedarnath route. Heavy rain and landslides have blocked the path, halting pilgrim movement until conditions improve.
A 65-year-old man was killed after being struck by falling boulders near the Cheerbasa Helipad on the Kedarnath pilgrimage route in Uttarakhand on Sunday, as heavy rain and landslides forced authorities to temporarily suspend pilgrim movement.
According to the State Emergency Operation Centre, boulders rolling down a hillside near the helipad struck the man, identified as Madan Mohan Tiwari, a resident of Ukhimath. He died on the spot.
The Kedarnath pilgrimage route has also been blocked by debris amid the ongoing rain, police said.
Authorities have advised pilgrims travelling towards Kedarnath to halt at Sonprayag and Gaurikund, while those returning have been asked to stop at Jangalchatti.
Officials urged pilgrims not to proceed further along the route until the debris is cleared and permission is given to resume movement. The pilgrimage will restart only after weather conditions improve and the route is declared safe, authorities said.

headline: NEW DELHI: Ten years after the current disability law was passed, govt is yet to frame a revised National Policy for Persons with Disabilities. The existing National Policy for Persons with Disabilities was adopted 20 years ago."This prolonged delay ...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Ten years after the current disability law was passed, govt is yet to frame a revised National Policy for Persons with Disabilities. The existing National Policy for Persons with Disabilities was adopted 20 years ago."This prolonged delay is particularly concerning because a contemporary national policy is essential to translate the rights guaranteed under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPDA) Act, 2016 and India's commitments under UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities into a coordinated, measurable and adequately resourced whole-of-govt framework," stated the organisation, Doctors with Disabilities: Agents of Change (DwDAoC), in its letter to the minister for social justice and empowerment and secretary of Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD).Govt had acknowledged the need for a new national policy in its 2022 public notice inviting comments on the draft policy. The task force constituted to draft the policy had submitted the draft on Oct 12, 2021, and the deadline for stakeholder comments was Sept 30, 2022. Four years after the consultation process, India continues to operate under the national policy formulated in 2006, pointed out the letter.When drafting the new policy, the department explicitly acknowledged the significant developments since 2006, including India's ratification of the UN convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, enactment of RPDA, 2016, and adoption of National Education Policy, 2020.
In 2016, RPDA replaced Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995. "As an organisation led by and representing health professionals with disabilities, we are particularly concerned about the gaps that arise when disability policy is not effectively integrated across health, social protection and other sectors. The medicalisation of disability in professional assessment and eligibility has also been challenged ... These judgments underscore the need to move decisively towards a rights-based, functional and accommodation-oriented approach rather than one that treats disability itself as a proxy for incapacity," stated DwDAoC founder Dr Satendra Singh in his letter.
The letter pointed out several shortcomings in the draft national policy including the lack of adequate convergence with health ministry's proposed accessibility standards for healthcare and how accessibility requirements for goods and services remained inadequately reflected in public procurement frameworks.The organisation sought the current status of the revised national policy, reasons for its delay, whether a revised draft had been prepared following consultations, the proposed mechanism and timeline for further consultation, if any, and the expected date by which the revised national policy would be notified.

headline: India on Sunday (September 13, 2026) condemned an attack on a Panama-flagged oil tanker off the coast of Oman that resulted in one Indian seafarer being reported missing.

New Delhi has been concerned over attacks on commercial shipping as most of the vessels usually have Indian seafarers.

headline: Brics Summit: PM Modi’s bilateral talks put security, trade in focus
full_text:
Brics Summit: PM Modi’s bilateral talks put security, trade in focus
Modi and Marcos agreed to enhance India-Philippines cooperation in defense, trade, and security at the Brics Summit, addressing regional issues together.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Philippines President Ferdinand R Marcos Jr agreed to expand cooperation in defence, security, trade and investment during a meeting on the margins of the Brics Summit on Sunday.
The Philippines participated in the summit as the current chair of Asean, providing an opportunity for the two leaders to review bilateral ties. The Philippines is a key partner for India in the Asean grouping and shared concerns over China’s actions across the region have fostered closer strategic and security cooperation between the two countries.
The leaders expressed satisfaction at progress in bilateral cooperation across all areas and agreed to deepen and expand collaboration in defence, security, trade, investment, space, railway infrastructure, fintech, education, tourism, technology, and people-to-people ties, the external affairs ministry said in a readout.
Deep Dive
Modi and Marcos also discussed regional and global issues and reiterated their commitment to strengthen cooperation across all areas of the bilateral strategic partnership.
“We reviewed the growing momentum in the India-Philippines strategic partnership,” Modi said on social media, adding that focus areas in the discussions included economic linkages, technology, trade and space.
Modi held a separate meeting with South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and reviewed cooperation in diverse areas. They also exchanged views on global issues and agreed to maintain close coordination at multilateral forums, the ministry said.
Modi said on social media that he and Ramaphosa reviewed the India-South Africa strategic partnership, including the India-SACU trade agreement, mining and critical minerals, infrastructure, food security, digital public infrastructure and emerging technologies.
“We will work closely for Africa’s progress, the priorities of the Global South and a more balanced global order,” Modi said.
Modi also held meetings with Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, Ugandan vice president Jessica Rose Epel Alupo, Nigerian vice president Kashim Shettima Mustapha, Burundi President Évariste Ndayishimiye, who is also chairperson of the African Union, and reviewed bilateral ties.
Modi and Tokayev reviewed bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, security, connectivity, energy, critical minerals and emerging technologies, and exchanged perspectives on regional and international developments.
They agreed to strengthen the bilateral strategic partnership for peace, stability and development in the region.
Modi and Alupo reviewed ties between India and Uganda and emphasised the need to enhance cooperation in priority areas through technology partnerships, investment facilitation, and private sector collaboration. They also called for closer bilateral engagement to champion the voice of the Global South.
Modi and Mustapha reviewed the India-Nigeria relationship and discussions focussed on key areas such as trade, investment, defence, energy partnership, agriculture, health and digital technologies. Modi and Mustapha also discussed regional and global matters, including priorities and concerns of the Global South.
They emphasised the importance of strengthening cooperation in multilateral forums and working together for a more representative, inclusive and multipolar global order. Modi highlighted India’s commitment to deepen engagement with Africa, and Mustapha appreciated India’s contribution to capacity building and economic development in Nigeria.
Modi and Ndayishimiye stressed that the India-African Union partnership is a key pillar of cooperation within the Global South. They discussed the early convening of the India-Africa Forum Summit.
Modi commended the African Union leadership for combating the Ebola outbreak, and Ndayishimiye appreciated New Delhi’s medical support to Africa CDC to help in mitigating the outbreak.

NEW DELHI: Russian President Vladimir Putin Sunday proposed a new insurance mechanism and a collaborative initiative for the grain market among Brics nations and called on the grouping to adopt a comprehensive approach to global challenges.He sought to assure members of the grouping that they have it in them to operate independently of the West-dominated trade systems. "We have independent routes for moving capital, labour and technologies. In fact, we can operate regardless of outside pressure. We have some promising initiatives going forward, such as creating an insurance mechanism and a grain market. These are Russian proposals, and we invite all other member states to make use of them."His emphasis on Brics countries having their own insurance mechanism has come amid sanctions on ships exporting crude and grains from Russia. Insurance costs have risen, and the "shadow fleet "engaged by Russia to sell its products abroad is finding it difficult to operate.
Read alongside the speeches of Chinese President Xi Jinping and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the second day of the summit, Putin's pitch reflected the strong push from powerful Brics members to break away from the West-dominated system and build an alternative.
They attested to efforts India made by seeking to prevent the grouping from turning into an anti-West bloc under its presidency.Grain exports from Russia, the world's largest wheat producer, have taken a big hit from Ukraine's drones. "Global South nations must jointly advance a better (global) governance structure and tackle both traditional and non-traditional security threats," Putin said. The Russian president also said Brics' global stature is rising as it focuses on charting an independent course to combat pressing global challenges.

headline: Taking strong exception to Union Home Minister Amit Shah's remarks that BJP-led NDA governments in 21 States would introduce the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) before 2029, AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi on Monday (September 14, 2026) questioned whether ...
full_text:
Taking strong exception to Union Home Minister Amit Shah's remarks that BJP-led NDA governments in 21 States would introduce the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) before 2029, AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi on Monday (September 14, 2026) questioned whether the BJP's allies had an independent political voice.
He said they should demonstrate that they were not merely "choti BJP".
In a post on X, Mr. Owaisi said the Law Commission appointed by the NDA government had concluded that a UCC was neither necessary nor desirable.
Observing that the "soul" of the country was its pluralism, he claimed that a Uniform Civil Code would amount to imposing Hindu law on non-Hindus.
"It’s ironic that the BJP wants a UCC while its own states pass laws like the Disturbed Areas Act, which prohibit the sale of property between Muslims and Hindus. The so-called 'love jihad' laws have been applied exclusively against Christians and Muslims. A UCC isn’t about equality; it’s about targeting Muslims," he said.
Love jihad is a term used by right-wing Hindu groups to allege that Muslim men deceive Hindu women into marriage as part of an attempt to convert them to Islam.
Mr. Owaisi further alleged that Mr. Shah's "misplaced arrogance" and "chronology" had led to the anti-CAA/NRC protests in 2019. Prime Minister Narendra Modi himself had to clarify that no NRC was going to be implemented, he said.
He alleged that a similar situation was now unfolding with the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, with ordinary people being forced to attend hearings with documents.
The SIR process had caused immense hardship, particularly to minorities, SC/STs and migrants, Mr. Owaisi said, adding that an NRC would be "100 times worse". He said the consequences of the NRC had already been seen in Assam.
"The National Register of Citizens will force everyone to stand in line and prove their citizenship. In a country where 80 crore people depend on ration for food, you want them to find documents and prove their citizenship? To what end? This government wants us to be at the mercy of one babu or another," he said.
Amit Shah champions UCC implementation
Mr. Shah on Sunday (September 13, 2026) said BJP-led NDA governments in 21 states would introduce the UCC before 2029.
"Triple talaq has been abolished, giving Muslim women equal rights. We have introduced the Uniform Civil Code in several states, and I am confident that in the 21 BJP-NDA-ruled states, we will introduce the UCC before 2029," Mr. Shah said in Mumbai.
Asked whether the 1951 baseline would be used for implementing the NRC in Manipur, Mr. Shah said the Centre was holding discussions with its allies and political parties in the state.
"We are discussing these issues with our allies and also with the political parties of Manipur. Whatever decision is taken, we will inform you," he said.

Leader of the Opposition in Bihar Tejashwi Yadav on Sunday (September 13, 2026) slammed both the State and central government over the lack of seriousness in dealing with the recent Bihar floods, claiming that the State is being treated like a “stepchild”.
Mr. Yadav, who is the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) National Working President, said he had written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi demanding that the Bihar floods be declared a national disaster, and also sought compensation and a special economic package for affected families. The Central government has not shown any seriousness in this regard so far, he said.
Over 48 lakh people are affected by the floods, Mr. Yadav said, adding that he had also written to Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, but to no avail. Mr. Yadav alleged that the ‘double-engine’ government in Bihar is not serious about this issue and that both engines have caught fire, preventing people from receiving aid. There has been no hearing or action taken yet, he added.
The RJD leader asserted that although there are eight NDA Ministers and 30 Lok Sabha MPs from Bihar, the people of the State have been left to deal with the situation by themselves.
“The state government withdrew ₹4,000 crore from the Contingency Fund in July and utilised the money for salaries and other administrative expenses. Bihar’s treasury is empty, and the Central Government ministers from the state lack the clout to secure central assistance,” Mr. Yadav said.
He added that during the Kosi floods (2008), his father and then Union Minister for Railways Lalu Prasad had secured a special package for Bihar. “At that time, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh ji and Congress National President Sonia Gandhi ji visited Bihar to provide relief funds and ensure justice for the Kosi flood victims. In contrast, the attitude of the Narendra Modi government towards Bihar reveals their mindset,”Mr. Yadav said.
He further claimed that in Gujarat, even if there is rainfall, the government immediately sets up relief camps and provides all possible assistance, including a package to the State.
Mr. Yadav also alleged that leaders of the BJP and the central government always ignore the people of Bihar during times of disaster, and when election season comes, everyone from the Prime Minister to the Home Minister starts visiting to seek votes.
“Bihar is being treated like a stepchild, as no assistance is received from BJP-ruled states. During elections, Amit Shah speaks of making Bihar flood-free; however, when more than 47 lakh people are trapped in the devastation of the floods—he is nowhere to be found, not even issuing a single statement. This attitude reveals the nature of the Centre and State’s conduct towards Bihar; those in power are simply not serious about this issue,” Mr. Yadav said.
He claimed that when he visited the flood-affected areas to meet the victims, the boat he was given by State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) began to deflate in the middle of the river, and villagers had to rescue him.
Mr. Yadav said that in his capacity as the Leader of the Opposition, he assessed the situation and demanded that the government should provide aid and financial assistance to the flood victims.
According to the Bihar Disaster Management Department (DMD), over 48.35 lakh people were affected by floods in 87 blocks of 15 districts.

headline: Congress, BJP trade barbs over all-vegetarian fare for dignitaries at Brics Summit
full_text:
Congress, BJP trade barbs over all-vegetarian fare for dignitaries at Brics Summit
This is not the first time the government arranged a full vegetarian spread for heads of states and other important leaders.
As the two-day Brics Summit came to an end on Sunday, a political tussle began between the Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) with the Opposition party accusing the BJP of imposing its dietary preference and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi pointed out that 80% of Indians are non-vegetarians, after an all-vegetarian fare was served for international leaders at New Delhi’s Bharat Mandapam.
“The BJP’s habit of imposing its dietary preferences on fellow Indians is deeply problematic. Now, they have taken it a step further by imposing their own choices on dignitaries from across the world,” Congress leader Pawan Khera said in a post on X.
“India is a rich, diverse, multi-cuisine country, home to some of the finest non-vegetarian delicacies that people across the world relish and enjoy. So why did the Modi government choose to hide this part of India’s culture? Is it ashamed of the diversity that makes India what it is?” Khera added.
Deep Dive
Rahul Gandhi posted a picture of Chhole Bhature—one of Delhi’s popular snacks—and said, “For the record: 80% of Indians are non-vegetarian. Indian non-vegetarian food is delicious. As are my sister’s chole bhature.”
Trinamool Congress (TMC) leader Mahua Moitra suggested the international dignitaries to go to Karim’s. “Would I be a bad MP if I advised the visiting Brics leaders to give this menu a miss & get security to nip down to the nearest Karims & bring back some Burrab Kababs,” she said in a post on X.
To be sure, this is not the first time the government arranged a full vegetarian spread for heads of states and other important leaders. During the G20 meeting in Delhi, the food at both Bharat Mandapam and the President’s banquet was fully vegetarian, showcasing India’s culinary diversity.
BJP MP Sambit Patra hit back at the Congress and quipped that some Opposition members and the Congress are suffering from indigestion. “Today, some people—certain opposition members and the Congress Party—are suffering from indigestion because India is surging ahead. Remember, the ‘I’ in Brics stands for India, and that ‘I’ represents 1.4 billion people. I am India. I am one of the strongest partners of Brics, and I am proud of it.”

17 NCPI MPs to join BJP before Durga Puja: Rebel TMC MP's big claim
Jagadish Basunia said the initial plan was to join the BJP directly, but it could not happen owing to objections from Abu Taher and two other parliamentarians.
A rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) Lok Sabha MP said on Monday that all but three Muslim lawmakers from the dissident group are set to join the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) before Durga Puja in October, ratcheting up political speculation in Delhi and Kolkata.
Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia, the MP from Cooch Behar in West Bengal, was among the 20 rebel TMC parliamentarians who joined the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) in June, after the TMC lost power in West Bengal. But their application to merge their grouping with the unrecognised party, headquartered in Howrah, has been pending before Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla since June.
Rebel MPs wary of anti-defection law
All 20 rebel MPs are also facing disqualification proceedings after TMC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee approached the Supreme Court last month.
Basunia said 17 MPs had finalised plans to join the BJP together and the number would be sufficient to keep them outside the purview of the anti-defection law.
“Seventeen of our MPs are going to the BJP together. Since more than two-thirds of the 20 members will be switching, the anti-defection law will not apply to us,” he told reporters.
Also Read I Mamata Banerjee vs Ritabrata faction before ECI over TMC name, symbol and control
He said that Murshidabad MP Abu Taher Khan, Jangipur MP Khalilur Rahman, and Berhampore MP Yusuf Pathan –– all representing constituencies in Muslim-majority Murshidabad –– will not join the BJP. “They objected to the idea of joining the BJP,” Basunia said.
He said the initial plan was to join the BJP directly, but it could not happen because of objections from Abu Taher Khan and the two others. “So, an arrangement was made for us to join the NCPI,” he said.
NCPI's plans for merging with NDA
NCPI is an unrecognised party that contested two assembly seats in Tripura and polled a few hundred votes. Basunia acknowledged they knew nothing about the NCPI until they joined on June 14. “Now, 17 NCPI MPs will join the BJP,” said Basunia. “I have to follow what the others do.”
If the 17 MPs finally join the BJP, it will push the party’s tally to 29 out of Bengal’s 42 Lok Sabha seats –– its highest ever. It’ll also leave the BJP with 257 lawmakers in the Lok Sabha.
West Bengal BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya did not rule out the possibility of the NCPI MPs joining the party. “Anybody may want to join the BJP. But whether they will be accepted or not is a decision made at our highest level,” Bhattacharya said.
A senior BJP functionary and national officebearer said the rebel TMC lawmakers had already indicated that they want to join the NDA. “One thing is certain that they do not want to return to the TMC… They do not want to associate with Mamata Banerjee,” the functionary said.
Khan, Rahman, and Pathan have so far stayed away from National Democratic Alliance (NDA) meetings even though they joined the NCPI, a constituent of the ruling coalition.
NCPI members were also allotted separate seats in the previous monsoon session of Parliament.
Rebel MPs steer clear of jining BJP
Khan said nobody authorised Basnia to speak on their behalf. “We follow our own strategy. We have said repeatedly that we will never join the BJP.”
The other NCPI lawmakers neither dismissed nor confirmed Basunia’s claim. Birbhum MP Shatabdi Roy, one of the 17 lawmakers, said she did not know if Basunia made the statement after discussing the issue with their leaders. “I am not aware of any such decision being made.”
Arup Chakraborty, the Bankura MP, said, “I am not aware of any decision to join the BJP. I have to follow the others.”
Mitali Bag and Kalipada Soren, two other NCPI MPs, made similar remarks.
“If our leaders join the BJP then I will have to do the same,” Soren said.
“This decision can be taken only by our leaders,” said Bag.
Also Read I Mamata Banerjee-led TMC announces candidates for Bengal, Assam bypolls
TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh slammed the lawmakers, saying they “could become MPs only because Mamata Banerjee fielded them” in the elections. “Ever since they left, they have been moving from door to door just to hang on to their chairs. First it was NCPI and now it is BJP,” he said.
The TMC swept the 2024 Lok Sabha polls in West Bengal, winning 29 of 42 Lok Sabha seats. One of them died after the election, and 20 of the remaining 28 joined the NCPI on June 14, questioning Abhishek Banerjee’s leadership. Around the same time, 58 of the 80 TMC assembly members rebelled and claimed the right to the party’s election symbol.

headline: 17 NCPI MPs to join BJP together, 3 to back NDA from outside: Rebel TMC MP Basunia
full_text:
17 NCPI MPs to join BJP together, 3 to back NDA from outside: Rebel TMC MP Basunia
NEW DELHI: Seventeen of the 20 MPs are likely to join the ruling Bhartiya Janata Party either before or after Durga Puja in October, rebel TMC leader and Cooch Behar MP Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia claimed Monday.According to Basunia, the MPs have decided to make the switch together, which he said would ensure that they are not disqualified under the anti-defection law."We are 17 MPs going to the BJP together. Since more than two-thirds of the 20 members will be moving, the anti-defection law will not apply to us," Basunia said.The development comes nearly three months after 20 dissident TMC MPs announced their merger with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) on June 14 and extended support to the ruling NDA.The anti-defection law requires at least two-thirds of members of a legislature party to agree to a merger to avoid disqualification. In the case of the 20-member NCPI group, the threshold is 14 MPs.Basunia said, however, that three of the 20 MPs from the minority community would not formally join the BJP, citing the political and administrative dynamics in their constituencies.He named Abu Taher Khan, Khalilur Rahaman and Yusuf Pathan, saying they would extend support to the NDA from outside.
"They will support the NDA, and may be given important responsibilities or portfolios," Basunia said.Basunia's claim comes days after he and his wife, TMC MLA Sangeeta Roy, faced protests on returning to their ancestral home in Sitai, Cooch Behar.
Locals and BJP workers staged demonstrations against the couple amid criticism of Basunia's political shift. A TMC office near his residence was also allegedly set on fire during the unrest.Basunia has maintained that he has severed ties with the TMC and is now aligned with the NDA.The Mamata Banerjee-led party suffered a massive breakaway of Parliament and assembly strength after its stinging defeat in Bengal polls at the hands of the BJP.
