headline: Manipur: 4 Naga homes set afire in retaliatory attack hours after Kuki killings
full_text:
Manipur: 4 Naga homes set afire in retaliatory attack hours after Kuki killings
A couple was among the four Kukis killed in the Tamenglong district on Sunday while a six-year-old sustained a bullet injury
Four abandoned Naga homes were set on fire at Khedaghar in ethnic violence-hit Manipur’s Tamenglong district on Sunday evening in a retaliatory attack hours after four Kukis were killed in separate attacks earlier that day, officials said on Monday. Officials said unidentified arsonists set the houses around 27 km from the district headquarters on fire, and no casualties were reported, as the Nagas had left their homes weeks ago fearing Kuki retaliation amid heightened tensions between the two communities.
An officer requesting anonymity said security forces, including the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), dominated the area and residents had fled. “The district has only one remote Naga village, Baiboni, around 30 km from headquarters. There are around 20 houses, and a permanent platoon of CRPF is stationed there. A column of 38 AR [Assam Rifles] is also stationed at Muolzol Kuki village, almost three km from Baiboni.”
A couple was among the four Kukis killed in Manipur’s Tamenglong district on Sunday while a six-year-old sustained a bullet injury. Police said 46-year-old Lhingzangai Singsit was shot dead on the spot in the first attack around 5.30am at Tollen village. Her husband Seineh Singsit succumbed to bullet injuries. In the second attack, a man and a woman were killed in Longpi village. No groups have claimed responsibility for the attacks.
Western Village Volunteer, a Kuki group, blamed the National Socialist Council of Nagaland-Isaac Muivah (NSCN-IM) and Zeliangrong United Front-Kamson (ZUF-K) for the attacks, coinciding with the “Black Day”, which Kukis observe annually on September 13 in memory of the victims of ethnic violence during the Kuki-Naga conflict in the 1990s.
On Monday, the Kuki-Zo Council (KZC), a Kuki-Zo apex civil body, condemned the attacks in Tollen and Longpi. It said a Tollen couple was killed and their six-year-old son sustained a gunshot injury to his hand, reportedly leaving it nearly severed. It added that in Longpi, Julie Gangte, a pregnant woman, and Thangvel Roel Gangte, the only son of his family, were killed, while Nei Esther sustained critical injuries.
The council alleged NSCN-IM cadres operating through or alongside ZUF-K and Naga Village Guards carried out the attacks. It hit out at the double standards of Naga leaders in Manipur. “...the brutality of Naga armed groups can no longer be ignored.”
The council said Naga leaders demand justice for six Nagas killed in May but remain silent over the 22 Kuki-Zos, including women and children, whom Naga armed groups have reportedly killed since the beginning of 2026.
Kuki militants abducted and killed the six Nagas after holding them captive for nearly a month in Kangpokpi on May 13. The killings followed a twin ambush on the same day, which killed four people, including three church leaders and one Naga. The Naga groups have been demanding the arrest of all accused involved in the killing of the six Nagas and the abrogation of the ceasefire pact with Kuki militants.
On August 31, the nine Naga legislators submitted a memorandum to Union Home Minister Amit Shah demanding immediate arrest of Kuki-Zo leaders, who have claimed responsibility for the killing and dismemberment of the six Nagas, including Thangboi Kipgen, the husband of deputy chief minister Nemcha Kipgen, a Kuki.
Self-styled Gen ‘Tiger’ Kipgen cadres are alleged to have killed and mutilated the bodies of the six Nagas.
Naga and Kuki-Zo tensions escalated after the May 13 twin ambushes. On the same day, Kuki-Zo and Naga groups captured 48 people. On May 15, 14 captives each from the two communities were released. The remaining 14 Kuki-Zo hostages were freed unharmed on June 9. Mutilated bodies of the six Nagas were found the next day.
The ethnic violence in Manipur first began in 2023 between the Meitei and Kuki communities before involving almost every community. The state’s Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities have shut each other out of the areas they dominate.
A new government was formed in February, nearly a year after the imposition of President’s Rule. It includes representatives from all three major communities as part of an attempt to maintain balance. But sporadic violence has continued and left 306 people dead and 49 missing since May 2023.

headline: NEW DELHI: Swatantra Bhardwaj told a Delhi court on Monday that his arrest was politically motivated and claimed that it was the complainant who attacked him during the incident at Jantar Mantar in July, Bar and Bench reported.Bhardwaj's counsel Umes...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Swatantra Bhardwaj told a Delhi court on Monday that his arrest was politically motivated and claimed that it was the complainant who attacked him during the incident at Jantar Mantar in July, Bar and Bench reported.Bhardwaj's counsel Umesh Sharma made the submission while seeking bail for Bhardwaj, who is accused of assaulting the father of a Dalit student-activist during the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) protests at Jantar Mantar.The court was hearing Bhardwaj's bail application in-camera before Additional Sessions Judge Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler.
Sharma told the court that a video purportedly showed the complainant attacking Bhardwaj and claimed that the Delhi Police had taken no action against the complainant."Police ko wo video nazar nahi aa raha... Is video m clearly dikhai de raha hai ki complainant is mujhpe attack kiya hai aur main gir gaya hu (The police are not able to see that video. It is clearly visible in this video that the complainant attacked me and I fell down),â Sharma told the court.Sharma also alleged that Bhardwaj was arrested under the SC/ST Act for political reasons. He said Bhardwaj had initially received a police notice to appear for questioning on June 27 and appeared on June 29, after which he was allowed to leave.
"The police issued me a notice on June 27 to appear for questioning, and I appeared for questioning on June 29. After that, I was allowed to go. Then, after some political developments, I was arrested on September 4. After my arrest, a new FIR [under POCSO] was registered," Sharma said.Advocate Swati Khanna, appearing for the complainant, opposed the bail plea and alleged that Bhardwaj had used casteist slurs against the complainant. She also claimed that Bhardwaj had admitted in a video that he was the one who attacked the complainant.Delhi Police told the court that the original complaint did not mention any casteist slur. However, a casteist slur was mentioned in a subsequent statement, following which provisions of the SC/ST Act were invoked.Khanna also informed the court that Bhardwaj had approached the Delhi High Court with a habeas corpus plea challenging his arrest, but the plea was rejected.After hearing the arguments from both sides, the court reserved its verdict on the bail application.Bhardwaj was arrested from Uttar Pradesh on September 5 in connection with the alleged assault on the father of a Dalit student-activist during the CJP protests at Jantar Mantar in July.
He was initially booked under Sections 115(2) and 126(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to causing simple hurt and wrongful restraint. The case later invoked provisions of the SC/ST Act and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO).Bhardwaj had subsequently claimed on social media that he had cracked the skull of the girl's father and had been detained by police only for a few hours. He had also claimed proximity to NDA leaders Kapil Mishra and Chirag Paswan.Paswan denied the claim and filed a separate complaint against Bhardwaj for allegedly misusing his name.The charges against Bhardwaj were intensified after CJP leaders, along with the student and her father, protested at the Parliament Street police station.Bhardwaj is currently in judicial custody.

headline: India approves up to 654 MW of power export to flood-hit Nepal for 18 hours every day till December 31
full_text:
India approves up to 654 MW of power export to flood-hit Nepal for 18 hours every day till December 31
The decision comes amid the large-scale devastation caused by the recent floods and landslides in Nepal
The Ministry of Power has approved the export of up to 654 MW of electricity to Nepal from September 13 to December 31, as the neighbouring country grapples with power shortages following extensive damage to its hydropower infrastructure caused by recent devastating flash floods.
Under the approval, electricity will be supplied to the Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA) for 18 hours a day, from 0000 hours to 1800 hours, the Ministry of Power said.
Also Read | Nepal govt report says floods led to estimated $4.7 billion recovery, reconstruction needs
How will electricity be exported?
Of the total approved capacity, up to 600 MW of electricity can be exported through the Muzaffarpur-Dhalkebar 400 kV D/c transmission line. Another 54 MW can be supplied through the Tanakpur-Mahendranagar 132 kV S/c transmission line, according to the Ministry.
The Ministry said the arrangement has been approved as an immediate measure to help Nepal address the shortfall in domestic electricity generation after the floods severely affected several hydropower facilities.
"The quantum of power to be exported from January 2027 will be reviewed in December 2026," the Ministry of Power said in a release.
The decision comes amid the large-scale devastation caused by the recent floods and landslides in Nepal, which have damaged critical infrastructure and disrupted essential services across several parts of the country.
Also Read | Nepal’s flash floods death toll rises to 1,385
Why need of additional electricity?
Explaining the need for additional electricity supplies, the Ministry said the recent floods have caused significant damage to hydropower infrastructure, reducing Nepal's domestic power generation capacity and creating an additional requirement for electricity.
"The approval will help Nepal meet its power requirements during this difficult period and further strengthen the close and longstanding energy cooperation between India and Nepal," the Ministry said.
The additional power supply is expected to provide support to Nepal's electricity system as the country works to restore damaged hydropower infrastructure and cope with the wider impact of the floods.
The Ministry further said that India remains committed to supporting Nepal and strengthening bilateral cooperation in the energy sector.
The electricity export is part of India's broader assistance to Nepal following the devastating floods. India has continued to provide support for rescue, relief and forensic operations as Nepal deals with the mounting human and infrastructure losses.
According to the latest Search, Rescue and Relief update issued by Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) on September 11, the death toll from the floods had reached 1,385, while 5,130 people remained missing.
Against the backdrop of the rising death toll and the continuing relief operations, India has stepped up its humanitarian assistance to Nepal. An eighth Indian Air Force flight carrying relief material and humanitarian assistance recently reached Kathmandu.
Earlier, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said India had expedited the delivery of relief supplies, specialised equipment and expert personnel to Nepal through eight special flights since August 26.
More than 130 tonnes of relief material have been sent to Nepal as part of the assistance, the MEA said in a statement issued on September 9.

headline: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday thanked the people of Rajasthan after the BJP emerged as the largest party in the stateâs municipal elections, winning more wards than the Congress and securing majorities in four of the 10 municipal ...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday thanked the people of Rajasthan after the BJP emerged as the largest party in the stateâs municipal elections, winning more wards than the Congress and securing majorities in four of the 10 municipal corporations.In a post on X, PM Modi said the results reflected support for the BJPâs policies of development and good governance under the âdouble-engine governmentâ.âHeartfelt thanks to the people of Rajasthan for delivering a resounding victory to the BJP in the municipal elections,â PM Modi wrote.âThis is a testament to the triumph of truth over the jhooth ki goonj (echo of lies),â he added.
PM Modi also congratulated the winning candidates and BJP workers, saying the mandate would strengthen the partyâs resolve to work towards development and prosperity in the state.
BJP ahead of Congress in urban polls
According to figures from the Rajasthan State Election Commission, results for 10,235 of the stateâs 10,244 wards had been declared by 8.30 pm on Monday.The BJP had won 4,179 wards compared with 3,613 for the Congress. The BJP crossed the majority mark in Jaipur, Udaipur, Kota and Bhilwara municipal corporations, while the Congress secured a majority in Bikaner.The Congress also recorded a major victory in the Jhalawar municipal council, considered a stronghold of former chief minister Vasundhara Raje.
The elections covered 309 urban local bodies â 10 municipal corporations, 47 municipal councils and 252 municipal boards.
BJP crosses majority in Kota
In Kota Municipal Corporation, the BJP secured 55 of the 100 wards, while Congress won 40 and Independents three. The result for Ward 87 was put on hold after an EVM malfunction.Congress candidate Laxmi Sharma and other party workers staged a protest outside the counting centre, seeking the result and alleging irregularities.Officials later sealed the machine in the presence of the district collector and additional district magistrate and forwarded a report to the Election Commission through the returning officer.The BJP also retained several individual seats. Vivek Rajvanshi won his fourth consecutive term from Ward 54, defeating Congress candidate Manish by 2,226 votes.Gopal Ram Manda secured his fifth consecutive election victory, defeating Congress candidate Sanjay Yadav by 899 votes.Congress and Independent candidates, however, registered victories in some key wards. Youth Congress candidate Arpit Jain defeated BJP veteran and former deputy mayor Yogendra Khinchi by 250 votes in Ward 86.Independent candidate Vandana Faujdar won Ward 71 with 1,264 votes, defeating BJP candidate Meenakshi Sen by 160 votes.
Independents give BJP majority in Bundi
In Bundi, the BJP initially emerged as the largest party with 29 wards, two short of a majority. Congress won 20 wards, while Independents secured 11.Later in the day, three Independent candidates, Prabhat Devi, Aatmaram Chopdar and Vishal Sharma, joined the BJP, taking the party to a majority and enabling it to form the board.The BJP had also captured the previous mid-term board after Congress council chairperson Madu Nuwal was suspended.Congress leaders had expected to retain control but faced criticism over ticket distribution. Former councillors Devraj Gochar, Ankit Buliwal and Jeeshan Ali, who were denied Congress tickets, won as Independents.
BJP calls results a mandate for governance
BJP president Nitin Nabin thanked Rajasthan voters for what he described as a âhistoric victoryâ, saying the results showed continued faith in Modiâs leadership.
BJP national spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi also cited the partyâs performance in Kota, where Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had conducted the student-centric programme âChhatron Ki Goonjâ.âIn Kota, where Rahul Gandhi had gone and attempted to create âjhooth ki goonjâ, the BJP appears to be winning spectacularly,â Trivedi said.He claimed the results demonstrated that the Congress had âmore propaganda and less realityâ in its claims.

headline: The Congress on Monday (September 14, 2026) took a swipe at the government over the recent Wholesale Price Index (WPI) data, saying Prime Minister Narendra Modi keeps saying "sab changa si", but actually "sab mehenga si".
full_text:
The Congress on Monday (September 14, 2026) took a swipe at the government over the recent Wholesale Price Index (WPI) data, saying Prime Minister Narendra Modi keeps saying "sab changa si", but actually "sab mehenga si".
Wholesale price-based inflation rose to 9.92% in August, compared to 9.78%in July, on rising prices of food, manufactured items, and fuel and power, government data showed on Monday (September 14). Inflation in the food index rose to 7.05% in August, from 6.65% in July.
In manufactured items, WPI inflation was at a series high of 8.37%, higher than 8.29%in July.
In a post on X, Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said, "Official data just released shows that for four consecutive months now the WPI (Wholesale Price Index) inflation has been hovering around 10%. Prices of all essential commodities have continued their upward rise causing huge hardships to crores of families.”
“To compound the misery, according to CMIE data, inflation-adjusted wages have also been consistently falling with a 5.7% drop since April. Rural India has seen a massive 9% decline - even in nominal terms rural wages have fallen," Mr. Ramesh said.
"The PM keeps saying 'sab changa si (all is well), but actually 'sab mehenga si (everything is expensive)," Mr. Ramesh added.
The WPI has been on an upward trajectory since the beginning of this fiscal year as the West Asia war and the resultant blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, through which the majority of crude oil is imported into India, pushed up global crude and fertiliser costs with a spillover effect on food prices.

headline: NEW DELHI: India and France have stepped up their space cooperation as companies from the two countries signed three key agreements at the recent International Space Summit in Paris relating to satellite launches, space surveillance and microsatellit...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: India and France have stepped up their space cooperation as companies from the two countries signed three key agreements at the recent International Space Summit in Paris relating to satellite launches, space surveillance and microsatellite technology.In the first agreement, Franceâs Safran Space signed contracts worth more than 5 million euros with Indian space company Dhruva Space to supply communication systems, inertial navigation units, optical payloads and ground stations for Indiaâs planned SBS-III space-surveillance constellation. The constellation is envisaged to deploy 52 satellites between 2027 and 2030, according to the announcement.In another deal, French launch-services provider RIDE! signed an agreement to launch two satellites for TakeMeToSpace, which is the countryâs first designer of orbital data centres. The pact builds on several years of cooperation between RIDE! and Indian space companies, including the recent integration, launch and return of a European atmospheric re-entry capsule aboard Indiaâs PSLV rocket.In the third deal, French space company U-Space and Indian company AXISCADES signed a commercial cooperation agreement to explore Indiaâs microsatellite market and address growing commercial and institutional demand.
The new agreements come against the backdrop of over five decades of space cooperation between India and France.The partnerships will follow a phased roadmap under Indiaâs âMake in Indiaâ policy, combining French space technology with Indiaâs industrial integration capabilities.

headline: Sachin Pilot, Raja Warring detained amid protest against Punjab minister over Dalit man's 'suicide'
full_text:
Sachin Pilot, Raja Warring detained amid protest against Punjab minister over Dalit man's 'suicide'
Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring called upon Congress workers to join the stir seeking “justice” for the victim’s family.
Police on Tuesday detained Punjab Congress in-charge Sachin Pilot, state chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, and leader of the opposition in the Punjab assembly Partap Singh Bajwa amid the party's protest against finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema.
Along with Pilot, Warring and Bajwa, several other Congress leaders were also detained during the protest over a Dalit man's alleged suicide as they were moving towards Cheema's residence in the state capital, Chandigarh. The opposition party is demanding the minister’s dismissal and a time-bound, independent investigation into the death of the Sangrur resident.
Before the protest began, Punjab Congress president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring called upon Congress workers to join the stir seeking “justice” for the victim’s family and accountability from the AAP government.
The September 15 protest was being seen as an early test for Pilot’s political strategy in Punjab following his appointment as state in-charge by the Congress high command, replacing Bhupesh Baghel. As the Punjab Congress grapples with internal factionalism, observers note that the Charanjit Singh Channi faction has so far remained absent from events organised by the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC).
The case
The protest comes days after a Dalit man died allegedly by consuming poison. He had publicly questioned minister Harpal Cheema during a village programme on September 6 over the availability of drugs, particularly “chitta”, and had spoken about his son’s addiction.
Police subsequently registered a case against the village sarpanch, her husband and other persons on charges, including abetment to suicide and provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. However, opposition parties are demanding that Cheema’s name be included in the FIR.
What Sachin Pilot said
Sachin Pilot had said that he would take out a protest against AAP minister Harpal Singh Cheema, demanding justice for the family of the Dalit man who died because “he dared to question the minister about the uncontrollable drug menace in Punjab”.
“I, along with the Punjab Congress leaders will be taking out a march to the residence of AAP minister Harpal Singh Cheema on September 15 in Chandigarh, demanding justice for the family of the Dalit man, who allegedly died by suicide by consuming poison after facing pressure and mental harassment because he dared to question the minister about the uncontrollable drug menace in Punjab,” Pilot wrote on X.

“His last video recording before his death clearly names the minister. The victim’s family also alleged that they were denied dignity and respect while conducting his final rites. This is a serious matter that demands an independent investigation. The Congress demands nothing less than the termination of the minister and an immediate, time-bound, independent inquiry into the matter,” he wrote.

headline: Meta Platforms Inc., the parent firm of Instagram and Facebook, will share child sexual abuse material (CSAM) reports with Indian law enforcement in addition to the U.S.-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC), the company said...
full_text:
Meta Platforms Inc., the parent firm of Instagram and Facebook, will share child sexual abuse material (CSAM) reports with Indian law enforcement in addition to the U.S.-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC), the company said on Tuesday. Indian agencies have for years already had access to CSAM reports from Meta and other U.S.-based technology companies, following an MoU in 2019 between the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) and NCMEC.
Also read | Why is NCPCR investigating Meta, Instagram?
Now, the information will be shared directly by Meta with Indian agencies. “As on 31.03.2024, more than 69.05 lakh Cyber Tip-line reports have been shared with States/UTs concerned,” Union Minister of Women and Child Development Annpurna Devi had informed the Rajya Sabha in 2024. “Protecting children on our platforms is a priority for us and we are committed to working with the government to ensure that the perpetrators of these crimes are held responsible,” a Meta spokesperson said in a statement.
Cybercrime portal
“To collectively strengthen our efforts to combat this harm, Meta will now report child safety matters directly to the Cyber crime portal managed by I4C,” the spokesperson added, referring to the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre, under the Union Home Ministry.
Meta has been scrutinised in recent weeks by the Union government and the National Commission For Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) over news reports describing CSAM being served in ads on Instagram and Facebook. The firm had then said that while it screens all ads being posted by third parties on its platform, some bad actors are able to get such content posted anyway.

The 22nd edition of the India-U.S. joint military exercise, ‘Yudh Abhyas’ (war practice), commenced on Tuesday (September 15, 2026), with a focus on enhancing interoperability between the two armies, and integrating emerging technologies into operations in mountainous and semi-mountainous terrain.
The opening ceremony of ‘Yudh Abhyas’ was held at the Auli Foreign Training Node in Uttarakhand, where Major General Amaresh Gunjan, General Officer Commanding, 14 Infantry Division, and Colonel Benjamin Jackman, Commander, 1st Infantry Brigade Combat Team, 11th Airborne Division, U.S. Army, addressed the participating contingents, according to a Union Ministry of Defence statement.
Around 600 personnel from each side are taking part in the exercise, which is being conducted simultaneously at Auli and the Mahajan Field Firing Range in Rajasthan.
The exercise is aimed at enhancing the joint military capability of the two armies for the employment of integrated battle groups in mountainous and semi-mountainous terrain, with a focus on infantry-dominated operations.
A key focus of the exercise is the use of technology in battlefield operations. Participating troops will train in the employment of drones and autonomous systems for surveillance and reconnaissance, while contemporary weapon systems will be demonstrated at the Mahajan Field Firing Range.
Subject matter experts from the two armies will also exchange views on emerging technologies, and developments in multi-domain warfare, the Defence Ministry said.
The exercise will provide an opportunity for both sides to share tactics, techniques and procedures, and strengthen their ability to plan and execute coordinated military operations across varied terrain and operational environments. It is also expected to strengthen interoperability between the two forces through joint training and exchange of best operational practices.

headline: Five states and Union Territory of Delhi signed an agreement on the long-pending Kishau Project
full_text:
Five states and Union Territory of Delhi signed an agreement on the long-pending Kishau Project
NEW DELHI: Five states and Union Territory of Delhi on Tuesday signed an agreement on the long-pending Kishau Project, which is expected to regulate water availability in the wider Yamuna basin and increase flows downstream, benefitting the national capital and Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan in one way or another. The water stored in the Kishau reservoir will augment drinking water supply for Delhi.The Kishau multi-purpose project is a proposed dam and hydropower project on the Tons river, a major tributary of the river Yamuna, flowing along the border of Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Besides supplying drinking water, the multi-purpose project will also provide irrigation water for 97,000 hectares of land in riparian states and generate 1,476 million units of hydroelectric power.The agreement was signed here by all six chief ministers in the presence of Union home and cooperation minister Amit Shah, who said the Centre and the chief ministers of these six states/UTs of Yamuna basin are committed to complete the project at the earliest.Calling it a âhistoric agreementâ, Shah said Delhi will be the biggest beneficiary of the project and it will also contribute to environmental conservation by ensuring environmental flow of river Yamuna.
Under the Kishau Multipurpose Project agreement, an around 232-metre-high concrete gravity dam will be constructed on Tons. It will have a water storage capacity of 1,562 million cubic metres.Shah said the Centre that declared the Kishau Multipurpose Project a ânational projectâ will bear approximately 90% of its financial burden, while the remaining 10% will be borne by the participating states in accordance with the 1994 agreement.Shah, on the occasion, recalled the signing of several other agreements on water issues and said that the period from 2018 to 2026 will be remembered as a period in which almost all water disputes, from Kashmir to Uttar Pradesh, were resolved. The foundation for these resolutions was laid in meetings of the Zonal Councils and the Ministry of Jal Shakti efficiently took these agreements forward, he added.
Citing examples, Shah recalled that first, in August 2018, the dispute over the Lakhwar Multipurpose Project was resolved. In the same month, the dispute over Shahpur Kandi Dam Project was settled. In 2019, the dispute over Renukaji Multipurpose Dam Project in Upper Yamuna Basin was resolved. In 2021, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh reached an agreement on the Ken-Betwa Link Project, benefiting the water-stressed region of Bundelkhand, he added.The other projects in this league are the revised Parbati-Kalisindh-Chambal River Link project in 2024; the scheme for transferring water from Hathnikund to the Yamuna through an underground pipeline in Feb 2024; resolving dispute over the rehabilitation of families displaced by the Narmada Project in July 2026; and settling the dispute over water sharing between Bihar and Jharkhand in the river Son Basin in Aug 2026.

Before switching over to explore sustainable development issues, Vishwa had covered internal security and investigative agencies for more than a decade.

headline: UPI charges of 0.4% to be levied on merchant transactions above ₹2,000
full_text:
UPI charges of 0.4% to be levied on merchant transactions above ₹2,000
The update comes after the Centre had on September 14 notified that UPI transactions up to ₹2,000 will attract zero MDR.
UPI payments above ₹2,000 made to merchants will attract a 0.4% Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), according to detailed guidelines issued by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) on Tuesday.
This comes after the Centre had on September 14 notified that UPI transactions up to ₹2,000 will attract zero MDR.
The new rules apply only to person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions above ₹2,000. There will be no charges on person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions, irrespective of the transaction amount.
Deep Dive
For transactions of ₹75,000 and above, the MDR will be capped at ₹300 per transaction, according to the notification.
Also read: Consumer body slaps ₹10 lakh fine on Rapido over misleading fare prompts, dark patterns
The 0.4% charge will be shared among banks, payment apps and other partners in the payment ecosystem.
What is MDR?
MDR is a small fee that merchants pay to banks and payment companies each time a customer makes a digital payment. A customer pays a shopkeeper through a digital payment system, and the shopkeeper pays a small processing fee to the payment provider.
While that is the norm, in reality, many pass on MDR to customers, especially in high value card transactions where it does not have the same waiver as it does in UPI.
Also read: Govt says no UPI charges up to ₹2,000, Congress scoffs: Inside the digital wallet row
UPI had been exempt from MDR since 2020, a policy choice meant to push India away from cash and towards digital payments. However, now, a “nominal MDR of 0.4% will be levied on P2M transactions above ₹2,000”, says the government notification.
Flat MDR, rules for P2PM transactions
Certain essential sectors such as railways, telecom, insurance and fuel, will have a flat MDR of ₹5 per transaction for payments above ₹2,000.
Payments involving mutual funds, securities, stock brokers and dealers will attract a lower MDR of 0.02%, capped at ₹300.
In huge relief for small vendors, transactions of up to ₹1 lakh a month through UPI QR codes under the Person-to-Person-Merchant (P2PM) category will continue to have zero MDR on all transactions.
“This bridges informal street vendor setups with formal merchant acquiring accounts, promoting digital adoption in the unorganized sector,” said the notification.
Consumer Safeguards
The new framework also includes measures aimed at ensuring that customers do not have to pay extra for using UPI.
No platform fees: UPI apps will not be allowed to charge users any platform fee or hidden charges for transactions.
Merchants cannot pass on MDR: Banks have been advised to ensure that merchants do not recover the MDR from customers by adding it to the bill.
Unlimited free UPI transactions: Individuals will continue to have access to free UPI transactions without any monthly or transaction-volume limits.
Daily limits are not charges: Transaction limits of ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh, depending on the category, are meant only for security and risk management. They do not mean customers will be charged after reaching a certain number or value of transactions.
How will merchants be impacted?
Centre said that according to data analysis, the new MDR rate will only impact 4 percentage of merchant transactions because most of such transactions fall below the threshold of ₹2,000.
This would ensure that micro and small businesses remain shielded from cost burdens.

‘Modi tax’: Opposition slams Centre over UPI charges on merchant transactions; Rahul, Kharge target PM
The government announced a 0.4 per cent Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI payments above ₹2,000 made to merchants.
The Opposition on Tuesday slammed the BJP government over its decision to introduce a 0.4 per cent Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI payments above ₹2,000 made to merchants. The Congress called it the "Modi tax" and alleged that a "compromised" prime minister had "surrendered" to US pressure.
After nearly six years of allowing merchants to use UPI without a transaction fee, the government announced a 0.4 per cent MDR charge on payments above ₹2,000, effective October 15.
MDR is a fee that merchants pay to banks and payment companies when a customer makes a digital payment. The new rules apply only to person-to-merchant (P2M) transactions above ₹2,000. Person-to-person (P2P) payments will continue to remain free, regardless of the amount.
Opposition targets BJP over UPI move
Pawan Khera, Congress' media and publicity department head and Rajya Sabha MP, said the 0.4 per cent MDR on UPI payments above ₹2,000 should be termed the "Modi Tax".
"He popularised UPI, wanted all the credit for building a 'cashless economy' -- and now he is taxing people for using it," Khera said on X.
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)'s official X account posted, “Loot the people, fill up the pockets of your own, this is the BJP’s way.”
Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) Rajya Sabha MP Haris Beeran told news agency PTI that the government has “betrayed the general public”.
“...It means that merchants will definitely have to pay. They will then try to recover the cost from customers. Secondly, this will discourage merchants from going digital,” he said.
Rahul Gandhi, Kharge on UPI charges
Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi alleged that the Modi government has quietly cleared the way for UPI charges, while Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge said the Modi government's "loot" has now reached UPI.
"The government says no fees will be charged to customers. But where will the fees imposed on shopkeepers ultimately come from? Added to the prices, straight out of the customer's pocket," Gandhi wrote.
Gandhi alleged that US payment companies have long opposed India's zero-MDR policy, adding, "Just like with the US Trade Deal, Compromised PM Modi is once again surrendering to American pressure,"
In a post, Kharge alleged that high inflation has already put a strain on the common person's finances.
"Wholesale inflation is near 10%, and the BJP government has planned to impose a 'Digital Payments Tax' on the public, aiming to destroy whatever little savings they have left," he said in a post in Hindi on X.
Govt clarifies new UPI rules
From October 15, a 0.4 per cent MDR will apply to person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above ₹2,000. The charge will be capped at ₹300 for payments of ₹75,000 and above.
Essential and thin-margin sectors, including railways, telecom, insurance, fuel and agricultural inputs, will face a flat MDR of ₹5 on each transaction above ₹2,000. These sectors account for nearly 17 per cent of P2M transaction volume, while making up around 46 per cent of P2M transaction value.
Person-to-person (P2P) transfers, which account for 37 per cent of UPI's transaction volume and 70 per cent of its transaction value, will remain free regardless of the transaction amount.
The government said small-value transactions of up to ₹2,000 make up more than 95 per cent of total P2M volume. These transactions will not be affected by the new charge.

headline: 1999 Staines murder case: Odisha rejects Dara Singh’s premature release plea
full_text:
1999 Staines murder case: Odisha rejects Dara Singh’s premature release plea
The board cited possible social and communal repercussions, after a recent gathering outside Keonjhar jail raised concerns over provocative slogans.
Odisha’s State Sentence Review Board has rejected a plea for premature release by Dara Singh, who is serving life imprisonment for the 1999 murder of Australian missionary Graham Staines and his two minor sons, ending months of uncertainty over his remission plea.
The board’s decision comes ahead of the next hearing in Supreme Court on September 17, and after multiple prompts from the apex court.
Board cites possible social and communal disturbances
The board, which considered the case at its special meeting on August 31 said Singh’s release could have “societal ramifications” and potentially lead to communal disturbances in the area. District authorities in Keonjhar, where Singh is lodged in a jail, had in March 2025 conditionally recommended that he could be allowed premature release, but made this contingent on imposing conditions to ensure social harmony. In its latest report, the district administration reported that a crowd of about 200 to 250 people associated with the Dara Sena assembled outside the Keonjhar District Jail on August 15 and raised provocative slogans.
HT has reviewed a copy of the minutes of the board meeting.
The board noted that the latest report from the Keonjhar administration did not contain a specific recommendation and was inconclusive.
Singh became eligible under 2022 remission guidelines
Singh, 67, has spent more than 26 years and six months in prison and became eligible for consideration for premature release under Odisha’s 2022 remission guidelines. He approached the Supreme Court in 2024 seeking directions to the Odisha government to consider his premature release under those guidelines.
The board had earlier rejected his plea of premature release in November 2016, June 2019, December 2020, January 2022 and February 2023 citing various grounds, including concerns over communal harmony.
The latest decision came after the top court last week directed the state government to take a clear position on Singh’s plea.
“You want to reject it, you do it. You take a decision. We will deal with it. You can’t keep it lingering like this,” the SC bench of justices Manoj Misra and Vijay Bishnoi said while warning that state officials could be summoned if the Sentence Review Board continued to delay its decision. The court, on August 19, directed the board to take a decision by September 2 and inform it of the outcome.
Also read: SC asks Odisha to decide remission plea of Dara Singh in Staines murder case
Singh convicted over 1999 killing of Staines, sons
Singh was convicted for the killing of Staines and his sons, Philip, 10, and Timothy, 6, who were burnt alive while sleeping in a station wagon at Manoharpur in Odisha’s Kendujhar district on January 22, 1999. A CBI court sentenced Singh to death in 2003 and convicted him under several provisions of IPC including murder, criminal conspiracy and rioting. Following an appeal, the Orissa High Court in 2005 acquitted 11 other accused and commuted Singh’s death sentence to life imprisonment. His appeal against the conviction was subsequently dismissed by the Supreme Court.
Singh was also convicted in two other murder cases in Mayurbhanj district — the killing of Catholic priest Father Arul Doss at Jambani Church and the murder of garment shop owner SK Rahman. He received life sentences in both cases in 2007. His appeals were later dismissed by the Orissa High Court.
Co-accused released prematurely in April 2025
One of his co-accused, Mahendra Hembram, was released prematurely from Kendujhar district jail in April 2025.
Singh first sought premature release through the state review process several years ago, but successive boards rejected or deferred his plea. After a 2023 direction from the Orissa High Court, the Sentence Review Board held a special meeting on February 20 that year and again rejected his request.
His case was placed before the board in November 2024, when it sought a fresh opinion from the district authorities. Kendujhar officials subsequently recommended his release in March 2025, subject to conditions.
Also read: Odisha defers decision to release Staines murder convict Dara Singh from jail
Three murder convictions cited as reason for deferral
The board nevertheless deferred the matter in May 2025, citing his convictions in three murder cases and seeking further reports.
It again deferred the case in September 2025, seeking a fresh opinion from authorities in Auraiya district of Uttar Pradesh, where Singh originally lived. The Auraiya authorities subsequently supported his premature release in February 2026.
In July 2024, the Supreme Court said his premature release should have been considered by the competent state committee.
The matter was subsequently adjourned several times as the state sought time for the review process.

headline: Compelling rape survivor to continue pregnancy impairs right to live with dignity: Delhi HC
full_text:
Compelling rape survivor to continue pregnancy impairs right to live with dignity: Delhi HC
New Delhi, Compelling a rape survivor to continue with a pregnancy resulting from the crime and fastening the responsibility of motherhood on her against her will would amount to a serious impairment of her right to live with dignity, the Delhi High Court has held.
The court made the observations while allowing a plea on behalf of a 15-year-old rape survivor seeking the termination of her pregnancy, which had exceeded 30 weeks of gestation.
Under Section 3 of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, termination of pregnancy beyond 20 weeks and up to 24 weeks is permissible in respect of specified categories of women, subject to the statutory requirements.
Terming it an unfortunate and distressing case, Justice Madhu Jain said the fact that the pregnancy had crossed the statutory limit, by itself, could not be viewed in isolation.
"In cases arising out of sexual assault, compelling a survivor to continue with a pregnancy resulting from the assault and thereby fastening upon her the responsibility of motherhood against her will would amount to a serious impairment of her right to live with dignity," the court said in its September 8 order.
It said that a woman's right in relation to her body necessarily included the right to decide whether or not she wished to become a mother.
To compel a survivor of sexual assault to carry and deliver a child conceived as a consequence of the alleged assault might subject her to further and enduring physical and psychological trauma, the court added.
The judge observed that while the advanced gestational age of the pregnancy required heightened medical caution, it could not by itself deprive the minor of consideration of her rights to bodily autonomy, dignity and reproductive choice.
At the same time, any medical procedure must necessarily remain subject to an assessment of her physical fitness and medical feasibility and to all requisite safeguards, it added.
Justice Jain said while exercising jurisdiction under Articles 226 or 32 of the Constitution, the court must give due primacy to the best interests and welfare of the minor mother-to-be, while simultaneously considering the statutory framework under the MTP Act.
"Where the welfare and well-being of the pregnant woman or minor are under consideration, her reproductive autonomy, dignity and bodily integrity assume significant importance, particularly having regard to the peculiar facts and circumstances of each case," it said.
The court said it was constrained to observe that cases like this one leave an "indelible sense of anguish" and noted that the petitioner was a child of aged merely 15 who had already been subjected to the trauma of a heinous sexual assault and, to add to her vulnerability, had lost both her parents.
At an age when a child ought to be protected, nurtured and allowed to grow in safety and dignity, she had instead been compelled to confront circumstances which no child should ever have to face, it said.
"A child of 15 years cannot, in the eyes of this court, be reduced to the description of a 'mother' merely because she has been forced into pregnancy as a consequence of sexual violence," the court said.
It said the court was mindful that the loss of both parents made the circumstances of the girl more difficult.
The law might provide remedies and procedures, but no order of a court could undo the trauma that the child had endured, it said.
"What the court can, however, do is ensure that, at a moment of such profound vulnerability, the child is met not with further hardship, but with care, dignity, compassion and the protection of the law," the court said.
The judge said she hoped that the petitioner would be provided every possible support, care and protection so that she could have an opportunity to reclaim the childhood and dignity which no child should ever be deprived of.
While allowing the plea, the court directed medical superintendent of Lady Hardinge Medical College and S K Hospital to make arrangements for the termination of the girl's pregnancy at the earliest and maintain a record of the procedure undertaken.
It asked the doctors to preserve the tissue or foetal material for DNA identification and other purposes in connection with the criminal case lodged in relation to the rape.
The State was directed to bear all expenses relating to the termination, including the procedure, medicines, investigations, hospitalisation, food and incidental medical requirements.
The court directed that if the child was born alive despite the medical procedure, all feasible measures be taken for its medical care, with the Child Welfare Committee to take further steps in accordance with law.

UPI transactions have so far remained free of charges, irrespective of the amount.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also accused the PM Modi government of laying the groundwork for a âDigital Payments Taxâ by allowing the possibility of charges on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000.âThe Modi government's loot has now reached UPI. "No fees on UPI" has been changed to "no fees on UPI transactions up to Rs 2,000." Sky-high inflation has already emptied the common man's pocket. Wholesale inflation is near 10%, and the BJP government has planned to impose a "Digital Payments Tax" on the public, aiming to destroy whatever little savings they have left,â Kharge said in an X post.âTen years ago, demonetization delivered a shock to the country's economy. When questions were raised about the disastrous outcomes of demonetization, the government argued that it was imposed to promote Digital Payments and a Cashless Economy. The Finance Minister had recently stated in Parliament that no Tax or Charges would be levied on UPI, but according to several reports: A potential collection of Rs 25 on a Rs 5,000 transaction and up to Rs 50 on Rs 10,000. Is this true?â he added.He also warned that any Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) imposed on merchants could eventually be passed on to consumers through higher prices.Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh also questioned whether the transaction limit could be changed through a future notification to cover person-to-person transfers.âIt is evident that the groundwork is being laid to collect fees on UPI transactions from all of us. Tomorrow, through another similar notification, this limit could also be alteredâthere is now no guarantee of this in the law. As far as we know, the government could impose charges even on everyday person-to-person UPI transactions,â he wrote on X. âIs all this being done with the intent of opening up digital payments for American companies to please President Trump?â he asked.
What does the notification say?
According to a gazette notification dated September 14, no bank or system provider can impose a direct or indirect charge on a person making or receiving a payment through a RuPay debit card or a UPI transaction of up to Rs 2,000.The notification follows an amendment to Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. The amendment provides an enabling framework for imposing MDR on UPI and other notified electronic payment modes.The amendment Bill was passed by Parliament during the Monsoon Session, which concluded on August 13, 2026. The government had said that the UPI and Services Steering Committee, headed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), would decide the MDR rates.The government has argued that rising transaction volumes require continuous investment in cybersecurity, fraud prevention and payment infrastructure. It has also said that charges would support market expansion, encourage competition and help create a self-sustaining revenue model for the payments ecosystem.UPI is operated by NPCI, an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India and the Indian Banksâ Association. It enables real-time payments between individuals and allows customers to pay merchants directly.Launched on August 25, 2016, UPI has transformed Indiaâs digital payments landscape. Its transaction value rose from Rs 0.07 lakh crore in FY17 to around Rs 314 lakh crore in FY26, an increase of more than 4,000 times in a decade.
UPI is now accepted in 11 countries, including Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia, Greece and Uzbekistan.According to Reuters, the introduction of UPI charges could benefit Paytm and Pine Labs, create an additional revenue stream for banks and improve prospects for IPO-bound PhonePe and Razorpay. Analysts at Jefferies estimate that the fees could generate Rs 5,000 crore to Rs 10,000 crore annually for the payments industry.
Kanchan Yadav is a writer at The Times of India, where she covers business, politics, international affairs and social issues. Her reporting also focuses on policy, governance and economic developments, with a close lens on how decisions in corridors of power affect everyday lives and community well-being.

headline: NEW DELHI: India on Tuesday criticised Pakistan over its announcement of a PKR 70 lakh reward for information leading to the arrest or conviction of Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) chief Masood Azhar, calling it a âphoneyâ move and asking Islamabad to take co...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: India on Tuesday criticised Pakistan over its announcement of a PKR 70 lakh reward for information leading to the arrest or conviction of Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) chief Masood Azhar, calling it a âphoneyâ move and asking Islamabad to take concrete action against the terror group chief.Responding to Pakistan maintaining the bounty on Azhar, ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Islamabad's announcement was unlikely to have any consequence.
"Such gimmicks and attempts at hoodwinking people by Pakistan are nothing new. We have seen similar gimmicks in the past as well. For a state sponsor of terrorism to make such phoney announcementsâwe all know how hollow they are. Pakistan must take concrete action rather than make announcements that are ultimately of no consequence..."Pakistan has continued to list Azhar in the Federal Investigation Agency's (FIA) âRed Bookâ of most-wanted terrorists and has retained a reward of PKR 70 Lakh for information leading to his apprehension or conviction.Also read | Pakistan lists Jaish-e-Mohammed chief Masood Azhar as fugitive, hikes bounty ahead of FATF reviewAzhar, the founder and chief of JeM, is wanted in India in connection with several terror cases, including the 2001 Parliament attack. India has also linked JeM to the 2016 Pathankot airbase attack and the 2019 Pulwama bombing.
His name was first included in the FIA's Red Book in 2021 and has been retained in its 2026 edition. He is listed at serial number 1480 among 1,804 most-wanted terrorists.The FIA entry identifies Azhar as the head of Jaish-e-Mohammad and says the reward of up to PKR 70 lakh is for information leading directly to his âapprehension or convictionâ.
The cases cited against him in the FIA list were registered in Gujranwala, Multan and Lahore under provisions of Pakistan's Anti-Terrorism Act.India has for years accused Pakistan of sheltering Azhar. Islamabad has maintained that he fled to Afghanistan, a claim rejected by Afghanistan's Taliban government.Azhar was among the fugitives India sought from Pakistan following the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, in which 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists killed 166 people.The latest development comes ahead of the Financial Action Task Force's next plenary in Paris from October 26 to 30. Pakistan was placed on the FATF's increased monitoring list, commonly known as the grey list, in 2018 and remained there until 2022.It was removed after completing commitments under two FATF action plans focused on strengthening its anti-money laundering and counter-terror financing framework and implementing targeted financial sanctions.

headline: NEW DELHI: Govt has agreed to export 654MW of electricity daily to flood-ravaged Nepal for 18 hours a day till Dec 31. The ministry of power Monday said the recent floods caused significant damage to hydropower infrastructure in Nepal, reducing its d...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Govt has agreed to export 654MW of electricity daily to flood-ravaged Nepal for 18 hours a day till Dec 31. The ministry of power Monday said the recent floods caused significant damage to hydropower infrastructure in Nepal, reducing its domestic power generation capacity and creating an additional requirement for electricity, reports Atul Mathur.Beginning Sunday, India started exporting up to 600MW electricity between midnight and 6pm to Nepal Electricity Authority through the Muzaffarpur-Dhalkebar 400 kV DC line and up to 54MW through the Tanakpur-Mahendranagar 132 kV SC line.
"The quantum of power to be exported from Jan 2027 will be reviewed in Dec," the ministry said in a statement, adding, "India remains committed to supporting Nepal and strengthening bilateral cooperation in the energy sector," the ministry added.Officials said floods in the Trishuli/Lhende Khola river basin on Aug 26 caused severe damage to infrastructure and disrupted some generating stations, following which Kathmandu requested India to advance the export mechanism, which otherwise begins in Oct and remains in place during the winter months.Nepal's generation capacity was reduced by nearly 550MW due to the damage."The approval will help Nepal meet its power requirements during this difficult period and further strengthen the close and long-standing energy cooperation between the two countries," an official said. India imports hydropower from Nepal during summer and exports electricity in the dry winter, when river flows fall and generation is impacted.

headline: Gurugram petrol pumps to get 249 cameras to detect old, end-of-life vehicles
full_text:
Gurugram petrol pumps to get 249 cameras to detect old, end-of-life vehicles
The cameras are part of the first phase of a project to install 775 ANPR cameras in four National Capital Region districts
The Haryana Transport Department will install 249 Automated Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras at petrol pumps across Gurugram to identify end-of-life vehicles and enforce environmental norms, Transport Minister Anil Vij said on Monday.
The cameras are part of the first phase of a project to install 775 ANPR cameras in four National Capital Region districts, including Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat and Jhajjar, at an estimated cost of ₹41.74 crore. The proposal has been approved by chief minister Nayab Singh Saini.
Gurugram will receive the highest number of cameras under the first phase, followed by Sonipat with 215, Jhajjar with 195 and Faridabad with 116. The cameras will be installed at petrol pumps to facilitate the identification of old and end-of-life vehicles and ensure compliance with directions issued by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM).
Also Read:Deliberate act, car driver would have stopped otherwise: Gurugram biker’s brother
Vij said the installation process was being expedited and would be completed by September 30, 2026. From October 1, fuel will not be supplied to end-of-life vehicles registered in Haryana, in accordance with CAQM directions.
The minister said the government’s objective was not merely to install cameras but to use technology to make vehicle identification more effective and systematic. He added that the initiative would strengthen pollution-control measures in the NCR and ensure compliance with environmental regulations.
Also Read:NHAI starts sinkhole repairs at Gurugram’s Iffco Chwk, opening date unclear
The state is expected to require around 2,780 ANPR cameras in total. The first phase will focus on the four major NCR districts, where vehicle emissions contribute to the region’s air pollution concerns.
Vij said the Haryana government directed the concerned departments to complete the necessary work within the stipulated timeline. He added that improving air quality in the NCR remained a priority and that the ANPR system would help authorities enforce restrictions on end-of-life vehicles more efficiently.

headline: CBI books Arunachal anti-dam activist Bhanu Tatak over FCRA violations
full_text:
CBI books Arunachal anti-dam activist Bhanu Tatak over FCRA violations
According to the first information report (FIR), the CBI alleged that Tatak received more than ₹17.6 lakh from various foreign organisations
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) registered a case against Arunachal Pradesh-based lawyer and environmental activist Bhanu Tatak for allegedly receiving over ₹17.6 lakh from foreign organisations and individuals in violation of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA), officials said.
Tatak, legal adviser to the Siang Indigenous Farmers’ Forum (SIFF) and coordinator of civil society organisation Dibang Resistance, was associated with protests against major hydropower projects proposed in the northeastern state.
According to the first information report (FIR), the CBI alleged that Tatak received more than ₹17.6 lakh from various foreign organisations and individuals directly into her personal savings bank account without obtaining the registration or prior permission required under the FCRA.
The agency named several overseas entities as alleged sources of the funds, including Philippines-based Asia Indigenous Peoples Network on Extractive Industries and Energy and Indigenous Peoples Rights International, Ireland-based Front Line and UK-based Human Rights Resource Centre.
CBI launched a probe in the matter on the direction of ministry of home affairs (MHA).
According to the first FIR, filed on August 20 naming Tatak and unknown persons as accused, CBI has alleged that between 2022 and 2025, she received ₹20.94 lakh in her bank account maintained in the State Bank of India, Roing branch, through forex transactions.
“Such foreign funds are being utilized to organize and sustain anti-dam protests in Arunachal Pradesh against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) and Dibang Multipurpose Hydropower Project, thereby adversely affecting economic and strategic interests of the country,” the FIR, seen by HT, alleges.
The agency alleged that Tatak has not filed any ITR between 2017-18 and 2025-26 and “therefore has not made any declaration with respect to the receipt of the funds from the foreign entities.”
Before registering the FIR, CBI had conducted a preliminary enquiry (PE) - a precursor to the formal case, to ascertain the charges.
In September 2025, Tatak was stopped by immigration authorities at Delhi airport from boarding a flight to Ireland following a lookout circular issued against her by the Arunachal Pradesh police.
She was scheduled to attend a three-month academic programme at Dublin City University.
The CBI further alleged that Tatak did not file income tax returns and that the foreign contributions received by her were not reflected in official records.
The agency claimed that the funds were allegedly used to “organise and sustain anti-dam protests” in Arunachal Pradesh, which, according to it, were adversely affecting the country’s economic and strategic interests.
Responding to the allegations, Tatak said the matter was under investigation and that she was fully cooperating with the investigating authorities.
“I am a law-abiding citizen and have committed no violation of the law,” she told HT.
Tatak said she was a recipient of the Bhagirath Prayas Samman Award, India 2023, for her work in river conservation, besides educational and research scholarships. The award was presented to Tatak and Dibang Resistance at the 10th India Rivers Week function held at BAIF in Maharashtra in November 2023.
Tatak and the organisations she is associated with have been opposing the proposed 12,500-MW Siang Multipurpose Project on the Siang River. Dibang Resistance has also opposed the 2,880-MW hydropower project on the Dibang River.
Tatak joined the Indian National Congress (INC) in Itanagar on December 2, 2025.

headline: Every June, before the monsoon fully sets in, a familiar sequence plays out across Indian cities. Mumbai's suburban trains stall in ankle-deep water. Bengaluru's tech corridors flood after a single evening's rain. Delhi's underpasses fill up fast eno...
full_text:
Every June, before the monsoon fully sets in, a familiar sequence plays out across Indian cities. Mumbai's suburban trains stall in ankle-deep water. Bengaluru's tech corridors flood after a single evening's rain. Delhi's underpasses fill up fast enough to trap cars. None of this is new, and none of it, by now, is unpredictable. What is harder to explain is why a country that trains more engineers than almost anywhere else on earth keeps failing at the most basic engineering problem a city faces: keeping water out and heat down.
Waterlogging in Delhi
India's technical education system is producing at record scale. AICTE data shows 12.53 lakh BTech seats were filled in the 2024-25 academic session, an eight-year high and a 67 percent increase over 2017-18. But that surge is concentrated in one discipline. Computer science and engineering leads enrolment at 3,90,245 students, followed by mechanical engineering, civil engineering at 1,72,936, electronics and communication, and electrical engineering. Civil engineering, the discipline that actually builds and maintains drains, embankments and disaster-resilient housing, trails computer science by more than two to one at the point of enrolment itself, before a single graduate has even entered the job market.
Where the engineers actually goThe surplus is real, but it isn't evenly distributed across the problems India needs solved. Computer science and IT graduates are pulled toward software, finance and consulting at a pace and pay scale that civic engineering roles, largely government postings with slower promotion cycles and lower starting salaries, cannot match. The result is a lopsided allocation: a country producing engineering talent at record volume, with that volume skewed away from the disciplines that keep cities functioning, and further skewed again once graduates choose where to build a career.
India's engineer surplus ends before it reaches the drains
This isn't a story about a shortage of trained people. It's a story about where trained people end up, and about how thin institutional capacity is on the other side of that choice, inside the departments actually responsible for stormwater drains, building safety audits and urban planning.The departments meant to absorb them are understaffed by designThe gap shows up starkly inside Urban Local Bodies, the municipal corporations and councils responsible for drainage, building approvals and disaster preparedness. A compendium of CAG performance audits covering 393 urban local bodies across 18 states, released in 2025, found a 42 percent gap between the revenue resources and actual expenditure of ULBs, with just 32 percent of ULB revenue self-generated and the rest arriving as grants from state and central governments. In Karnataka, government data reviewed this year showed close to 60 percent of sanctioned ULB posts vacant across ten city corporations, prompting the state to permit hiring retired engineers just to keep basic project planning functioning.Building codes compound the problem. The National Building Code, published by the Bureau of Indian Standards, is only a recommendatory document, not a binding law, so states can adopt, adapt or largely ignore its provisions. Maharashtra's own regulations don't even apply uniformly within the state: the Unified Development Control and Promotion Regulations explicitly exclude the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai and other planning authorities within its limits, leaving the city to run on a separate rulebook altogether.Drainage systems in most major cities were designed decades ago and were never built for the rainfall intensities cities now regularly see. On June 28, 2024, Delhi's Safdarjung Observatory recorded 228.1 mm of rainfall in 24 hours â more than three times the June average and the highest for the month in 88 years, since 1936, according to the India Meteorological Department. The waterlogging and traffic disruption that followed looked no different from floods a decade earlier.What a new industrial corridor risks repeatingThis matters beyond the annual monsoon cycle because India is now committing serious capital to exactly the kind of large-scale infrastructure build-out that depends on this workforce functioning well. The East Coast Industrial Corridor, pegged to the Union Budget 2026-27's announcement of a Durgapur-anchored industrial belt spanning ports, manufacturing zones and logistics networks across Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal, is one of several major infrastructure pushes riding on the assumption that India's technical capacity can execute at scale. But the same staffing vacancies, advisory-only codes and enforcement gaps that produce annual urban flooding sit underneath these new projects too. A corridor is, in the end, drainage, ports, road networks and disaster-resilient construction multiplied across four states; the same civic engineering functions currently understaffed in every city that already exists.
India's next industrial boom to happen on the East Coast
The heat side of the problem makes the stakes clearer still. India's peak power demand climbed from 214.9 GW on April 1 to a record 270.8 GW on May 21, 2026, according to the Union Ministry of Power, a 26 percent jump in fifty days, driven by sustained heat. That's a building-design and urban-planning failure as much as a climate one: cool roofs, passive ventilation and heat-resilient construction are still treated as add-ons rather than baseline requirements in most bye-laws.A multi-city study analysing roughly 3.6 million deaths across ten Indian cities between 2008 and 2019 found that heatwave days were associated with a 14.7 percent increase in daily mortality, and estimated around 1,116 deaths a year attributable to heatwaves. The 2025 Report of the Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change estimated that India lost about 247 billion labour hours to heat exposure in 2024, translating to roughly $194 billion in economic losses, concentrated in agriculture and construction.None of this points to a talent problem. India has the engineers, more of them, and more concentrated in one discipline, than ever before. What it doesn't have, consistently, is a civic system built to employ the rest where the predictable failures actually happen, inside municipal drainage departments, building-approval desks and disaster-management cells that are short-staffed and underfunded by a documented, audited margin.
Every large infrastructure announcement adds new physical assets to maintain. Unless the capacity gap inside the institutions responsible for maintaining them closes at the same pace, each new corridor, each new industrial belt, inherits the same vulnerability the rest of urban India already lives with every monsoon and every summer.

headline: NEW DELHI: An eighth-pass jewellery trainee, a Class XI florist, a farmerâs son trained in refrigeration and young specialists in robotics, cyber security and Industry 4.0 will form Indiaâs unusually diverse challenge at the âOlympics of Skillsâ in S...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: An eighth-pass jewellery trainee, a Class XI florist, a farmerâs son trained in refrigeration and young specialists in robotics, cyber security and Industry 4.0 will form Indiaâs unusually diverse challenge at the âOlympics of Skillsâ in Shanghai this month.India will field 70 competitors across 63 skill categories at WorldSkills 2026, scheduled from September 22 to 27. The contingent spans 16 states and brings together students, apprentices and young professionals trained in traditional trades as well as emerging technologies. The line-up, however, remains heavily male-dominated: only 14 of the 70 competitors are women.Karnataka has the largest representation with 16 contestants, followed by Odisha with 13 and Tamil Nadu with 12. Maharashtra has five competitors, while Bihar, Haryana, Telangana and Gujarat have three each.Among those heading to Shanghai is Md Dilkhush of Bihar, whose father is a farmer. Trained in refrigeration and air conditioning, Dilkhush emerged as the IndiaSkills national champion and will be tested on installation, maintenance, fault diagnosis and energy-efficient cooling systems.Tamil Naduâs Joy Das, son of a fisherman, studied till Class VIII and trained in jewellery-making before winning gold at the state and national levels.
Mizoramâs Lawmnakima, a Class XI student, will compete in floristry, while Gujaratâs Prakash Suthar has followed his carpenter father into joinery.The contingent also reflects how vocational pathways are increasingly cutting across family and educational backgrounds. Anuja Vare of Karnataka, whose parents are doctors, will compete in visual merchandising. She has previously designed an exhibition space at Bharat Tex that was visited by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and won gold at the regional and national skill competitions.Telanganaâs Mehrunissa Begum moved from an apprenticeship in logistics and freight forwarding to successive gold medals at the state, regional and national levels. The daughter of a bakery owner and a homemaker, she has spoken of overcoming anxiety and the feeling of being overwhelmed during her competition journey.Smriti Nambiar of Karnataka, a bakery competitor trained at IHM Pusa, was named the instituteâs All-Rounder Student and Rising Culinarian for two consecutive years. Odishaâs Krishnanjali Sahoo will represent the country in patisserie and confectionery, while Jhansirani Rout will compete in restaurant service.The team also carries a strong green-skills component. Rajasthanâs Vishnu Prajapat, whose father is an electrician, will compete in renewable energy after gaining hands-on experience in solar installations and exposure to wind turbines. Rushikesh Pithambaram will represent India in water technology.At the technology end of the spectrum, the Indian contingent will compete in autonomous mobile robotics, cloud computing, cyber security, software testing, unmanned aerial systems, optoelectronics and robot systems integration. Mobile-app developer Arjun Vijayabashkar began coding at 12, while Industry 4.0 contestant Suhan Mascarenhas is the son of two employees of Isroâs Master Control Facility in Hassan.
Maharashtraâs Harsh Pawar, whose father works as a quality supervisor at a cylinder-manufacturing company, will compete in 3D digital game art. Pawar has already won silver at the Global Skills Challenge in Australia. Two-member teams will represent India in areas such as autonomous mobile robotics, mechatronics, landscape gardening, concrete construction and robot systems integration.The 48th edition will open on September 22, with competitions running from September 23 to 26 and the closing ceremony on September 27. Participants will perform industry-standard assignments under the scrutiny of international experts. The event will also host a conference and industry exhibitions on technical education, workforce development and sustainable technologies.India will seek to improve on its WorldSkills Lyon 2024 performance, where it secured four bronze medals and 12 Medallions of Excellence.
Manash Pratim Gohain is a seasoned journalist with over two decades at The Times of India, where he has built a rich body of work spanning education policy, politics, and governance. Renowned for his incisive coverage of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, accreditation reforms, and skilling initiatives, he has also reported on student politics, urban policy, and social movements. His political reportageâboth reflective and news-drivenâadds depth to his writing, bridging policy with public impact. Through his 2,500 articles and related outlets, he has emerged as a trusted voice in national discourse, particularly in linking education reform to broader societal change.

headline: 'Compromised PM Modi again surrendering to US': Rahul Gandhi says govt 'opening doors' for UPI transaction fee
full_text:
'Compromised PM Modi again surrendering to US': Rahul Gandhi says govt 'opening doors' for UPI transaction fee
After the Centre notified changes barring charges on transactions up to ₹2,000, Rahul Gandhi said merchants could pass UPI costs on to consumers.
The Centre has “quietly opened the door” to imposing fees on UPI transactions above ₹2,000, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alleged on Tuesday. Merchants could eventually pass the cost on to consumers, the Lok Sabha Opposition leader said.
His remarks came a day after the Centre notified changes under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act and clarified that no charges can be imposed on UPI transactions of up to ₹2,000.
On X, Rahul Gandhi said transactions above ₹2,000 may account for only about 5% of UPI transactions by volume but represent nearly 65% of their total value. He said that even if customers were not directly charged, merchants could recover the fee by increasing prices.
“The government says no fees will be charged to customers. But where will the fees imposed on shopkeepers ultimately come from?” Gandhi said, alleging that this was aimed at changing India’s zero-MDR policy.
He also accused the Prime Minister Narendra Modi government of responding to pressure from American payment companies.
"American payment companies have long opposed India's zero-MDR policy. Now, the Modi government has opened the path to changing the policy in exactly that direction. Just like with the US Trade Deal, Compromised PM Modi is once again surrendering to American pressure," Rahul Gandhi wrote on X.
Kharge, Khera react
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged that the government changed its “no fees on UPI” policy to allow charges on transactions above ₹2,000.
He questioned reports that a ₹5,000 transaction could attract a fee of ₹25 and a ₹10,000 transaction up to ₹50. Any additional burden on merchants would eventually be passed on to consumers through higher prices, he added.
“Instead of providing relief to the inflation-weary public, the Modi government is searching for a new way every day to rob their pockets!!” Kharge said on X.
Congress leader Pawan Khera also accused the government of bowing to US pressure over India’s zero-MDR regime.
“There was pressure coming from the Americans on the MDR regime of India. And again, we have surrendered before Americans, again we are destroying our home-grown digital payment ecosystem under pressure from the US. Why?” he told PTI.
What the government has changed
The Centre's Monday notification covers UPI payments up to the ₹2,000 threshold as well as payments made through RuPay debit cards. It says banks and payment system providers cannot impose charges, directly or indirectly, on people making or receiving payments through these modes.
The change follows Parliament’s passage of the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman earlier said in the Rajya Sabha that the amendment was only an “enabling provision” and did not impose any tax or transaction charge on UPI users.
She also said street vendors, cab drivers, kirana stores and small merchants would not face such charges. Any fee that may eventually be introduced for eligible transactions, she said, would be paid by merchants rather than customers.
ALSO READ | Government says no charges on UPI payments up to ₹2,000. What happens beyond that?
What happens to UPI payments above ₹2,000?
The amendment does not itself introduce a fee on UPI payments above ₹2,000. Instead, it removes the earlier legal provision that prevented banks and payment service providers from charging Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions.
This means the government has created the legal framework under which MDR could be introduced for certain merchant transactions in the future. The final decision on whether MDR should be imposed, and on which transactions, is yet to be taken.
What is MDR?
MDR is a fee paid by a merchant to banks or payment companies for processing a digital payment. Under the existing UPI system, merchants have generally not paid MDR since the zero-MDR policy was introduced in 2020.
ALSO READ | PM Modi says UPI now live in 11 countries, pushes for further global reach
The government has instead provided financial incentives to banks and other participants to help cover the cost of running the UPI ecosystem.
Sitharaman said the UPI & Services Steering Committee, headed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) and including major banks and leading UPI apps, would consider whether MDR should be introduced and determine its scope and structure.
