headline: Rapido fined Rs 10 lakh for pressure tactics to increase ride fares, pre-ride tips
full_text:
Rapido fined Rs 10 lakh for pressure tactics to increase ride fares, pre-ride tips
The consumer authority found Rapido's pre-ride payment prompts used dark patterns, pressured riders to pay more and made unsupported claims that higher payments improved their chances of getting a ride.
The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a Rs 10 lakh penalty on Rapido, for misleading advertisements, unfair trade practices, an unfair contract and the use of dark patterns to prompt riders to pay more before their rides were confirmed.
The action against Roppen Transportation Services Private Limited, the company operating the ride-hailing platform, follows a sector-wide examination by the consumer watchdog of cab and bike-taxi aggregators operating in India, focusing on practices related to pre-ride tipping and dynamic pricing.
During its examination, the CCPA found that the Rapido app displayed prompts encouraging riders to increase the amount they were willing to pay while their booking was being processed.
Among the messages displayed on the app were:
"Higher the price, higher the chance of getting a ride."
Another prompt said, "Captains aren't accepting at Rs 60. Try adding +10, +20, +30."
According to the CCPA, Rapido's algorithm first quoted a fare to the rider. After the rider booked at that fare, the app prompted them to pay more, stating that drivers were not accepting the original price.
The authority said this created a false impression that a rider's chances of getting a ride quickly depended on paying an additional amount.
The CCPA said that, once a rider had committed to a booking, there was limited scope for negotiation. The prompts could create a sense of urgency and fear of losing the ride if the consumer declined to pay more, it added.
The authority classified the practice as "Confirm Shaming", a dark pattern identified under the Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023.
According to the CCPA, prompting consumers to make an additional payment after they had accepted the initially displayed fare could place them under psychological pressure.
This was particularly significant because the rider had already reached the booking stage and was relying on the platform to secure a ride, the authority said. A message suggesting that the chances of getting a ride were lower without an additional payment could therefore push the consumer towards paying more.
‘SET YOUR PRICE’ SLIDER UNDER SCRUTINY
The Consumer Protection Authority also examined Rapido's 'Set your price' feature and raised concerns over how its pricing options were presented.
According to the authority, the slider used different colours to display options to increase or decrease the fare. When riders increased the price, the message 'Higher chance of getting a ride' appeared in green. When they tried to lower it, a warning appeared in red or orange.
The CCPA also noted that the slider offered more space to increase the price, while providing comparatively less scope to reduce it.
The authority classified this design as 'Interface Interference', another dark pattern, saying the interface influenced consumers towards choosing a higher amount.
CCPA QUESTIONS TIPPING BEFORE RIDE BEGINS
The CCPA also objected to the practice of suggesting a tip before a ride had started.
According to the authority, the fare displayed at booking already takes into account factors such as distance, time, traffic, tolls and the amount payable to the driver.
Against this backdrop, the CCPA said it found no justification for subsequently suggesting that the rider pay an additional amount for the same ride before the service had begun.
The authority said a tip is ordinarily a voluntary payment made after a service has been completed. It therefore should not be presented as a condition for providing the service or as a payment necessary to obtain a ride.
The CCPA also cited the Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025, which provide that a tipping facility should be made available after completion of the ride, rather than at the time of booking or during the ride.
RAPIDO SAYS TIPPING VOLUNTARY
Before the central authority, Rapido said tipping was completely voluntary. The company also claimed that its matching algorithm continued to operate regardless of whether a passenger paid an additional amount.
Rapido further argued that the prompts on its app were similar to real-time conversations between passengers and drivers, including fare negotiations that could take place offline.
The CCPA, however, rejected Rapido's submissions on tipping.
The authority said the timing of the prompts and the interface design could put pressure on passengers at a point when they were relying on the platform to secure a ride.
NO SUFFICIENT DATA TO SUPPORT HIGHER-PAYMENT CLAIM
The Consumer Protection Authority also examined Rapido's claim that paying a higher amount increased the chances of getting a ride.
According to the authority, Rapido did not provide sufficient data or evidence to substantiate the claim that an additional payment actually increased the likelihood of getting a ride.
The company could not produce evidence establishing the claim, the CCPA said.
The authority therefore considered the claim that a higher payment increased the chances of getting a ride to be unsupported and misleading.
The action against Rapido is part of the CCPA's wider examination of practices followed by ride-hailing platforms in India.
The authority has issued notices to several platforms, including Uber, Ola, Rapido and Namma Yatri, directing them to comply with the Dark Patterns Guidelines, 2023, and submit self-declarations on compliance.
The CCPA, headed by Chief Commissioner Nidhi Khare and Commissioner Anupam Mishra, said its examination of Uber and Ola in relation to these practices is ongoing.

headline: Modi government’s loot has reached UPI, says Congress; BJP hits back
full_text:
Modi government’s loot has reached UPI, says Congress; BJP hits back
The new framework, effective October 15, will leave person-to-person transfers and payments up to ₹2,000 free, while merchants bear the charge.
The Congress on Tuesday accused the government of breaking its own promise of keeping the United Payment Interface free of fees after a notification issued the day before paved the way for a Merchant Discount Rate charge on UPI transactions above ₹2,000.
Rahul Gandhi, Kharge attack move as UPI policy shift
Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said the move breaks the government’s promise of a free UPI system and accused it of “surrendering to American pressure” on digital payments. “The Modi government’s loot has now reached UPI,” Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge said in a statement. “‘No fees on UPI’ has been changed to ‘no fees on UPI transactions up to ₹2,000.’”
On Tuesday evening, the government introduced a 0.4% transaction fee on payments above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 for payments of ₹75,000 and above, from October 15, while explicitly ring-fencing everyday person-to-person transfers from any charge.
Deep Dive
Also read: UPI charges of 0.4% to be levied on merchant transactions above ₹2,000
BJP rejects Congress claims over impact on users
Reacting to the Congress statements, the BJP accused the party of spreading “fake news” to create panic about UPI transaction charges and derail Digital India. BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari called the opposition party a “jhooth ki dukaan (shop of lies)” and said the government has made it absolutely clear that MDR charges will not be levied on transactions between individuals. He said 96 per cent of UPI merchant (P2M) transactions are ₹2,000 or below, and they are 100 per cent charge-free. “Even if these transactions account for just 5% of the volume, they make up nearly 65% of UPI’s total transaction value,” Gandhi said in a post in Hindi on X. He argued that even if customers are not billed directly, the cost will still reach them. “The government says no fees will be charged to customers. But where will the fees imposed on shopkeepers ultimately come from? Added to prices, straight out of the customer’s pocket.” Gandhi also linked the decision to trade negotiations with Washington, arguing that the US has pushed against India’s zero-MDR policy for years.
Kharge calls proposed charge a burden on consumers
Kharge, in a post, alleged that sky-high inflation has already emptied the common person’s pocket. “Wholesale inflation is near 10%, and the BJP government has planned to impose a ‘Digital Payments Tax’ on the public, aiming to destroy whatever little savings they have left,” he said on X.
Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said the sequence of events that led to announcement of the MDR was “another example of Modi Govt’s FAST moves (First Announce, Subsequently Think).”
Congress’s media and publicity department head Pawan Khera said the 0.4 per cent MDR on UPI transactions above ₹2,000 should be called the “Modi Tax”.

NEW DELHI: Nepal finance minister Swarnim Wagle will be in New Delhi for a two-day visit from Thursday for talks on post-flood reconstruction and wider economic cooperation as Kathmandu looks to India for support after the Aug 26 disaster devastated hydropower projects, roads, bridges and settlements. The visit will be the first high-level trip from Nepal to India since the floods.
Wagle is expected to meet finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, external affairs minister S Jaishankar and commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal. He will also address an industry gathering and deliver a lecture at Delhi School of Economics. The disaster's confirmed toll has reached 1,429 dead and more than 5,649 missing across Nepal and Tibet. Wagle has estimated that Nepal may need as much as $5 billion for rebuilding. "We will require much less than what we needed for the 2015 earthquake," he said.
India has sent nearly 50 tonnes of relief material to Nepal following the flood, including medicines, temporary shelters and solar lamps.

headline: âChennai shouldnât alienate Delhiâ: SC tells Tamil Nadu to reconsider opposition to Navodaya schools
full_text:
âChennai shouldnât alienate Delhiâ: SC tells Tamil Nadu to reconsider opposition to Navodaya schools
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Tamil Nadu government to comply with its December 15, 2025 order to identify land in every district for establishing Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas, while urging the state and Centre to resolve their differences over the schools through dialogue.A bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and Augustine George Masih also questioned Tamil Nadu's opposition to the three-language policy followed by Navodaya schools and said the state should not view the establishment of the centrally funded institutions as a threat to its existing education system.
"You have to change your mindset, it canât be that Hindi will not be taught in the soil of Tamil Nadu," Justice Nagarathna observed during the hearing.The bench also said the people in Chennai should not alienate those in Delhi while stressing the need for cooperative federalism."We are saying in addition to all the good things youâre doing in your State, having something in addition will not bring down your standards. Coming from Delhi, will not lower the standards of Chennai. People in Chennai should not alienate Delhi and vice versa," the Court said.The court granted Tamil Nadu three more months to identify suitable land in each district and directed representatives of the state and Central governments to hold further discussions on the policy for establishing the schools.
The matter has been posted for December 14.
Tamil Nadu raises language concerns
The case relates to Tamil Nadu's challenge to a Madras High Court direction to establish Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district.Navodaya schools are centrally funded, co-educational residential schools run by the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti under the Union Ministry of Education. Tamil Nadu has opposed their establishment, among other reasons, because the schools follow a three-language policy that includes Hindi, while the state follows a two-language policy.Senior Advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for Tamil Nadu, told the court that the state's objection was not to schools or the teaching of Hindi as such, but to the language policy associated with the Navodaya scheme."It is against the State policy. It supersedes Tamil. This kind of unification is not the purport of the Constitution. It is not a Central government school. It is a school run by a society. There is an adamancy that Hindi must predominate."Justice Nagarathna said the language issue could be discussed between the Centre and the state."If you want Tamil as a second language, it is a matter which can be considered," the Judge said, asking the state Secretary to speak to the corresponding Central government Secretary.Gupta said discussions had already taken place but the Centre had remained adamant about Hindi. He nevertheless agreed to another round of consultations.
Court stresses cooperative federalism
Tamil Nadu also argued that the judiciary could not compel a state to adopt an optional Central government policy through a mandamus.Gupta submitted that education is in the Concurrent List and that Tamil Nadu has constitutional authority to frame its own education policy. He also argued that the Navodaya scheme was not compulsory.Justice Nagarathna questioned the consequences of individual states refusing to accept Central policies."Education is in the Concurrent List. There has to be cooperative federalism. If each State says that I don't accept your policy, what will happen?" the Judge asked.The bench said Tamil Nadu could continue running its own institutions and following its own syllabus, while Navodaya schools would provide an additional educational option.The court also rejected the argument that the establishment of Navodaya schools would lower Tamil Nadu's educational standards."We are not alienating you and we are not alienating them. Some more type of schools come in your state also which will only enhance the high standard which we are aware of. This is not going to lower your standards. If Navodaya schools were going to lower the standard of education in Tamil Nadu we would have said that irrespective of what you would have said. That is not the case here. It will provide more opportunity," Justice Nagarathna told Gupta."Ultimately everybody must work together," Justice Nagarathna said.
State raises financial concerns
Tamil Nadu also raised financial concerns, submitting that the Centre had promised to release Rs 5,000 crore for education but had not done so.Gupta argued that the state could not take on additional financial liabilities when funds under existing schemes had allegedly not been released.Additional Solicitor General KM Nataraj, appearing for the Centre, submitted that the state's primary requirement under the scheme was to provide land, while construction and other expenses would be borne by the Central government.Nataraj said the scheme was at an early stage and construction would take several years, during which the language-related differences could be addressed through discussions.Gupta, however, said around 30 acres of land would be required in each district and that identifying land before deciding whether to accept the policy would create difficulties.The bench clarified that it was not directing the state to acquire land immediately, but only to identify suitable land in its government plan.
Supreme Court refuses to recall land direction
The Supreme Court had in December 2025 directed Tamil Nadu to identify land required for establishing Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district within six weeks. The state subsequently sought recall of the order.On Thursday, the bench declined to recall the direction and instead granted the state three months to comply.
In its order, the bench recorded that Tamil Nadu had cited the change in government and lack of material progress in discussions with the Centre as reasons for non-compliance."Be that as it may, we direct the petitioner to comply with our order of 15.12.2025 in so far as identification of the land necessary to establish the school in each district," the order stated.The bench also directed the Centre and Tamil Nadu to continue discussions on the policy while the state works on identifying the land.Advocates G Priyadarshini and Rahul Shyam Bhandari, appearing for Kumari Maha Sabha, the petitioner before the High Court, argued that Tamil Nadu could not deny students access to free education through Navodaya schools."The Court should not get into this debate," Gupta said during the hearing.Justice Nagarathna responded: "That perception that you are surrendering to the central govt should not be there."

Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday extended birthday greetings to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, describing the India-Israel relationship as an âunprecedented partnershipâ and saying the friendship between the two countries had ânever been strongerâ.Birthday greetings poured in from across the world, with foreign leaders, envoys and diplomatic missions highlighting Indiaâs bilateral partnerships and Modiâs role in strengthening ties. Russian president Vladimir Putin praised his contribution to the âspecial and privileged strategic partnershipâ between India and Russia, while Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni wished Modi âhealth, energy, and successâ.âHappy birthday, Narendra!â Netanyahu wrote in a post on X, alongside an image of the two leaders. âYour leadership has transformed India into a world power. Together, we have built an unprecedented partnership between our two great democracies.âThe Modi-Netanyahu bonhomie has become a prominent feature of India-Israel ties, with both leaders repeatedly highlighting their personal friendship and political trust.
Their meetings and public exchanges have highlighted a relationship that extends beyond formal diplomacy into close strategic cooperation.âThe friendship between Israel and India has never been stronger, and together we will take it to even greater heights,â he added, wishing Modi âmany more years of leadership, health and fulfillmentâ.India and Israel established full diplomatic relations in 1992, while PM Modiâs July 2017 visit to Israel elevated the relationship to a strategic partnership. Netanyahu followed with a visit to India in January 2018.The relationship now covers defence, security, technology, agriculture, water, innovation, trade and other areas. During PM Modiâs visit to Israel in February 2026, Netanyahu described him as âmy dear friendâ and said, âYou are more than a friend; you are a brother in many respects.â He also said, âIsrael is stronger than ever and India is stronger than ever.âNetanyahu's birthday message came days after India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, where the grouping adopted a New Delhi Declaration that included strong references to the Israel-Lebanon conflict and the Gaza war.On Lebanon, BRICS leaders said, âWe welcome the ceasefire in Lebanonâ and called for full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701. The declaration also called on Israel to âwithdraw its occupying forces from all of the Lebanese territories, in which they remainâ.
That diplomatic contrast has not, so far, translated into a visible rupture in India-Israel ties. Netanyahuâs latest message instead points to continued political engagement, while New Delhi maintains separate tracks with Israel, Arab countries and the wider BRICS grouping.

headline: Pakistan's PNS Hunain sustained significant damage after colliding with India's INS Kolkata.
full_text:
Pakistan's PNS Hunain sustained significant damage after colliding with India's INS Kolkata.
NEW DELHI: When 2600-tonne Pakistan warship PNS Hunain collided with Indian Navyâs 7400-tonne destroyer INS Kolkata, three times its weight, on Tuesday evening, the outcome was known as the Pakistani vessel was no match to Indiaâs big warship. The Pakistan offshore vessel was severely damaged and had to return to the harbour whereas, Indian sources said, the Indian destroyer suffered no damage in the collision.In a statement on Thursday, Pak govt said its âNavy was undertaking its biennial exercise SEASPARK-26 when the Indian vessel carried out aggressive manoeuvres in dangerously close proximity to a Pakistani naval ship, resulting in contact between the two vesselsâ. Its foreign ministry, in a tit-for-tat reaction on Thursday, summoned the Charge d'Affaires of the Indian High Commission in Islamabad and lodged a strong protest.However, Indian defence sources told TOI that it was the âPakistani ship that closed the Indian warship on a routine surveillance mission in the North Arabian Sea at high speed, manoeuvring in an unprofessional and unsafe manner that led to the collisionâ.
Visuals emerging showed PNS Hunain a huge dent on it and the warship had to be sent for repairs. PNS Hunain is aYarmook-class patrol vessel designed for maritime security, surveillance and limited combat capabilities. Commissioned in 2014, PNS Hunain is about 98 metres long.
On the other hand, INS Kolkata is 164 metres long and has a maximum speed of 30 knots and is the lead ship of the indigenously designed and constructed Kolkata-class guided missile destroyers. It carries a heavy mix of surface-to-air missiles, anti-ship cruise missiles, rapid-fire guns, and anti-submarine weapons like BrahMos missiles, Barak 8 missiles and close-in weapon system. For anti-submarine warfare, the Indian warship has torpedo launchers, rocket launchers and a bow-mounted sonar system.PNS Hunain would have sunk if INS Kolkata had taken offensive action. âHowever, despite extreme provocation, the captain of INS Kolkata âhad exercised extreme restraint by taking actions to prevent a severe accident from taking place,â the source told TOI.

headline: Senior Congress leader and former Union Minister E.M. Sudarsana Natchiappan passed away at his residence in Sivaganga on Thursday (September 17, 2026). He was 78, and is survived by his wife, daughter, two sons, and two elder brothers.
full_text:
Senior Congress leader and former Union Minister E.M. Sudarsana Natchiappan passed away at his residence in Sivaganga on Thursday (September 17, 2026). He was 78, and is survived by his wife, daughter, two sons, and two elder brothers.
Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president Manickam Tagore, a nephew of Natchiappan, said his uncle had died in his sleep. “When he did not get up in the morning, his driver went to his room, only to find he was no more,” he told The Hindu.
A Congressman since 1969, Natchiappan rose through the ranks from his early days as the Singampunari Regional Youth Congress president to become the vice-president of the TNCC in 2002. He also served as the party whip in Parliament.
Student leader
Born in Eriyur in Sivaganga district, Natchiappan was active in the Students’ Congress while studying at the Law College. “Later, he worked in the Youth Congress and became its general secretary. He was elected chairman of the Sivaganga Panchayat Union in the 1986 local body elections, which showcased a lot of talented Congress leaders in Tamil Nadu,” Mr. Tagore said.
After practising law in Sivaganga, Natchiappan shifted his practice to the Madras High Court in 1991 and to the Supreme Court in 1995.
A staunch Congress loyalist and admirer of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and Congress leader Sonia Gandhi, Natchiappan remained with the Congress when the late G.K. Moopanar launched the Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) in 1996 in protest against the Congress high command’s decision to align with the AIADMK.
Victory in 1999 LS polls
Before making his mark in national politics, he gained widespread attention in the 1999 Lok Sabha elections by winning the Sivaganga parliamentary seat against senior Congress leader P. Chidambaram when the latter was in the TMC.
After Mr. Chidambaram returned to the Congress, Natchiappan could not secure the Sivaganga Lok Sabha constituency again. He was later nominated to the Rajya Sabha by party leader Sonia Gandhi and represented the House for two terms. He served as the Congress Lok Sabha member from the Sivaganga constituency from 1999 to 2004 and as a Rajya Sabha member from 2004 to 2016.
He also served as Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry for a brief period between 2013 and 2014. He made significant contributions as chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice between 2004 and 2009.
Natchiappan, an expert in the Sri Lankan Tamils issue, fishermen’s rights, and the Katchatheevu islet, had addressed the United Nations General Assembly on two occasions.
He had been receiving medical care for his declining health in Sivaganga for the past few days, but passed away at his residence after the treatment proved unsuccessful.
Leaders condole death
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, and Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar condoled the death of Natchiappan.
Mr. Gandhi recalled Mr. Natchiappan’s commitment to public service, Tamil Nadu and the Congress party, while Mr. Birla extended condolences to his family, friends and supporters.
Mr. Shivakumar remembered his long and dedicated service to the people of Tamil Nadu and the Congress movement. Mr. Tagore recalled his association with the Youth Congress from his early years and his contributions as Sivaganga MP, Union Minister and in various organisational positions in the party. He also said Mr. Natchiappan’s death was an irreparable loss to the Congress.
Meanwhile, Congress leaders and functionaries paid floral tributes to Mr. Natchiappan’s portrait at Sathyamurthy Bhavan in Chennai. AICC general secretary and Tamil Nadu in-charge Ghulam Ahmad Mir, former Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president K.V. Thangabalu, Peter Alphonse, AICC secretary Nivedith Alva, IT and social media department head and MP Vijay Vasanth, among other State and district-level leaders, functionaries and party workers, participated.
VCK president Thol. Thirumavalavan said his demise was a great loss to Tamil Nadu. On behalf of the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi, he expressed his condolences to Mr. Natchiappan’s family and paid homage to the former Union Minister.
TVK leaders, including party spokesperson Arunraaj and C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar, also condoled the death of the senior Congress leader.
Veteran political activist and former member of the central committee of the Eelam People’s Revolutionary Liberation Front (EPRLF), Sritharan Thirunavukkarasu, also known as Sugu, recalled that when Sri Lankan government, headed by Mahinda Rajapaksa, made an attempt to dilute the 13th Amendment to its Constitution in violation of the spirit of the 1987 Indo-Lanka Accord, the Congress leader took the initiative of hosting a meeting of Tamil leaders from the island-nation in New Delhi and got a resolution adopted that any such endeavour to weaken the letter and spirit of the Amendment should be stopped and powers, intended for provincial councils in Sri Lanka, be transferred.
The Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK) general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran expressed sadness over the death of the former Union Minister.

headline: Veteran Congress leader Sudarsana Natchiappan dies at 79
full_text:
Veteran Congress leader Sudarsana Natchiappan dies at 79
He was elected to the Lok Sabha from Sivaganga in 1999 and served as a member of the House until 2004.
Veteran Congress leader and former Union Minister E M Sudarsana Natchiappan died at his residence here on Thursday following a brief illness, the party said. He was 79.
Natchiappan was elected Sivaganga union president in 1986 and served in the post until 1991.
He was elected to the Lok Sabha from Sivaganga in 1999 and served as a member of the House until 2004. He also served as Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry between 2013 and 2014.
Expressing grief over his demise, former Union Minister P Chidambaram said he had known Natchiappan since his days in the Youth Congress.
"Many praised his several facets as a vibrant youth, then a union president who served responsibly, a Member of Parliament who did not lose his party loyalty, and an outspoken Leader of the Opposition. I express my deepest condolences and sympathies to all the party comrades, his son and family, relatives and friends who are grieving his demise," Chidambaram said in a post on X.
Also Read | 'Mockery of democracy: Madras high court declines to stay bypolls to two Tamil Nadu assembly seats
Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president B Manickam Tagore said Natchiappan had served as the spokesperson of the state unit.
He joined the Youth Congress under the leadership of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and worked with great dedication for the Congress party, Tagore said.
Natchiappan became Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry in 2013 and advocated reservation rights for backward and oppressed communities, he said.
"The sudden demise of Sudarsana Natchiappan is an irreplaceable loss to the Congress movement. On behalf of the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee, I convey our deepest condolences and sympathies to the grieving family and Congress colleagues who have lost him," Tagore said in a post on X.
The last rites will be held at 3 pm on Friday in Ervadi in Sivaganga district.
Natchiappan remained with the Congress when late G K Moopanar launched the Tamil Maanila Congress in protest against the Congress high command's decision to align with the AIADMK.
He was elected to the Lok Sabha from Sivaganga in 1999, defeating senior Congress leader P Chidambaram, who was then with the TMC.
Natchiappan served as a Rajya Sabha member for two terms.
Condoling his death, Tamil Nadu Energy Resources and Law Minister R Nirmal Kumar said Natchiappan's passing was "deeply distressing".
"His long-standing contributions to politics and public life will forever be remembered. I extend my deepest condolences to his grieving family, friends, and the Congress party members. I pray to the Almighty that his soul attains eternal peace," Kumar said in a post on X.
The Congress had organised a condolence meeting at 12.30 pm on Thursday at Satyamurthy Bhavan, the party's state headquarters in Chennai, where senior leaders and cadres paid tributes to Natchiappan.
AICC general secretary and Tamil Nadu in-charge Ghulam Ahmed, former TNCC president K V Thangkabalu, party seniors including Peter Alphonse, AICC secretary Nivedith Alva and Sivaganga MP Karti Chidambaram, among others, paid floral tributes to his portrait at Satyamurthy Bhavan.
A Congressman since 1969, Natchiappan is survived by his wife, daughter, and two sons.

headline: The US House of Representatives has passed legislation allowing President Donald Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries purchasing Russian oil and gas, sending the bill to Trump's desk. The proposed measures could directly affect India, w...

The US House of Representatives has passed legislation allowing President Donald Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries purchasing Russian oil and gas, sending the bill to Trump's desk. In July, Russia supplied more crude to India than the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Venezuela, Brazil, Oman, and the United States combined. New Delhi has stated it is monitoring developments while maintaining its focus on energy security. Sourcing replacement crude from alternative markets could result in changes to shipping distances, freight charges, insurance costs, and procurement prices. The development introduces fresh complexities into bilateral trade discussions between India and the United States, raising questions about potential tariff categories and broader strategic alignments amidst shifting global partnerships.
The United States House of Representatives has passed the Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, sending legislation to President Donald Trump that enables tariffs of up to 100 percent on major buyers of Russian crude oil and natural gas, including India and China. In response, the Ministry of External Affairs affirmed India's commitment to securing energy supplies through diversified sources while communicating bilateral and market implications to US interlocutors. Amid geopolitical developments and Russian crude accounting for 51.1 percent of Indian oil imports in July 2026, Chief Economic Advisor Dr V Ananth Nageswaran and Union Minister Kiren Rijiju examined India's economic trajectory and governance roadmap toward Viksit Bharat by 2047. Discussion points included banking sector balance sheet reforms, capital expenditure expansion, the Production Linked Incentive scheme, trade agreements, and administrative strategies under Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

headline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi pitched India as a “new and trustworthy location” for electronics manufacturing, urging global chipmakers to consider the country’s potential to relieve electronics from the “weaponisation” of supply chains.
full_text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi pitched India as a “new and trustworthy location” for electronics manufacturing, urging global chipmakers to consider the country’s potential to relieve electronics from the “weaponisation” of supply chains.
Also read | PM interacts with chip industry ahead of Semicon event
“This is not a sector where you set up a factory and the job is done,” said Mr. Modi, who inaugurated the Semicon India 2026. “Wherever semiconductor ecosystems have been built in the world, the entire ecosystem has come together only after decades of hard work. But India, with your cooperation, has worked simultaneously on chip design, manufacturing, equipment manufacturing, the materials ecosystem, testing capability, and has demonstrated success.”
Mr. Modi’s address came days after the India Semiconductor Mission’s second phase, which has an outlay of ₹1.27 lakh crore, was notified.
The Prime Minister said India is the “mother of democracy”. “When such a country succeeds in a critical industry, it strengthens the supply chain of the entire world. And today, when supply chains are being weaponised, its importance becomes much greater. We should also look at this development taking place in India from this larger perspective,” he said.
Semicon India 2026 brought together semiconductor and electronics firms from India and other countries. Speaking at the event, IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the government plans to train one lakh people who will be a “global pool of talent” and can “straightaway be employed in the factories which are coming up in India”.
Mr. Vaishnaw added that the government would target at least 200 startups and companies designing chips in India under the next phase of the country’s semiconductor mission, Semicon 2.0. He said Indian chip design firms have an established presence in the global industry, as they require little in-house manufacturing capabilities.
Global industry body SEMI’s CEO Ajit Manocha estimated that the semiconductor industry would cross $1.3 trillion this year, and $2 trillion by 2030.
Chip industry
Leaders from the semiconductor industry expressed hope in India’s trajectory and its role in their global plans. Applied Materials committed to invest $5 billion over the coming five years, to expand its R&D centre and supply chain.
“Earlier this year, we began commercial production at Sanand,” Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said. “Our current production capacity already exceeds the memory required for India’s entire laptop market … The India Semiconductor Mission, and now ISM 2.0, gave this industry a foundation it did not have before.”
Infineon CEO Jochen Hanebeck called India a “market of tremendous importance”, praising the “pace of progress across the Indian ecosystem”. Pointing to his firm increasing hiring in India by 28%, Mr. Hanebeck said that “[w]e see great potential for India to strengthen its position across the global semiconductor value chain.”
“India is evolving from a major chip consumer and chip design hub into a full-stack global semiconductor powerhouse,” Merck’s electronics CEO Benjamin Hein said.
Lam Research COO Sesha Varadarajan announced that his firm would be investing ₹10,000 crore “to establish our first silicon component manufacturing facility in the country” and that “we are increasing our partnerships with suppliers across India in specialised materials, precision components, gases, chemicals, metrology and manufacturing services.”
Wayne Allan, an executive at the Dutch firm ASML, which makes extreme ultraviolet lithography machines essential to advanced chip manufacturing, said that “India will become increasingly important globally” as the chip ecosystem develops further.

headline: ‘Hindi can’t be barred from Tamil Nadu’: SC on Navodaya schools, gives state 3 months
full_text:
‘Hindi can’t be barred from Tamil Nadu’: SC on Navodaya schools, gives state 3 months
The Supreme Court refused to recall its Navodaya school order, giving Tamil Nadu 3 months to identify land in every district.
Tamil Nadu cannot take the position that Hindi will never be taught on its soil, the Supreme Court said on Thursday while refusing to recall its earlier direction requiring the state to identify land in every district for setting up Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas.
A bench of justices BV Nagarathna and AG Masih, while urging Tamil Nadu and the Centre to resolve their differences over the schools through dialogue, gave the state three months to comply with its December 15, 2025 order and identify suitable land for the proposed schools.
‘Change your mindset’
The exchange came during the hearing of Tamil Nadu’s plea against a Madras High Court direction to establish Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district. The state has resisted the schools, among other reasons, on the ground that their three-language model, including Hindi, conflicts with Tamil Nadu’s two-language policy.
Also read: Supreme Court directs ED, Delhi Police to submit details of cases against Unitech directors
“You have to change your mindset. It can’t be that Hindi will not be taught on the soil of Tamil Nadu,” observed the bench, as it also sought to dispel the state’s apprehension that accepting the central scheme would amount to surrendering its educational autonomy.
“We are saying in addition to all the good things you are doing in your state, having something in addition will not bring down your standards. Coming from Delhi will not lower the standards of Chennai. People in Chennai should not alienate Delhi and vice versa,” it said.
What Tamil Nadu said on school order
The court’s intervention came after senior advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for Tamil Nadu, argued that the state’s opposition was not merely a matter of mindset but concerned its constitutional authority to frame education policy.
Gupta said the state was not opposed to Hindi as such but objected to what he described as the insistence on Hindi as the predominant language in the Navodaya system. He also argued that the central scheme was optional and that the court could not issue a mandamus compelling a state to adopt a particular policy.
“This kind of unification is not the purport of the Constitution. There is an adamancy that Hindi must predominate,” Gupta said.
Court's response
The bench, however, maintained that the state could continue with its own educational institutions and policies while allowing another model of school to operate in Tamil Nadu. “Today it is education, tomorrow it will be something else. You have to relax this rigidity in your mind,” said the bench, stressing the need for cooperative federalism.
Also read: ‘How can there be a blanket ban?’ Delhi HC to cops over protest refusal at Jantar Mantar
The court made clear that it was not directing Tamil Nadu to immediately acquire land or committing the state to a particular expenditure. It said its December 2025 direction only required the state to identify suitable land in its government plan. “Comply with our earlier order. We are not asking you to acquire land. We are only asking to identify,” it added.
In its 2017 order, the had held that the proposed schools did not violate Tamil Nadu’s law on Tamil learning and that a blanket refusal to facilitate them deprived students of the choice of accessing the central scheme.
Tamil Nadu then approached the top court, contending that education being in the Concurrent List did not mean the state could be compelled to adopt an optional central policy, particularly when the Navodaya model followed the three-language formula.
In December last year, the Supreme Court directed the state to identify the land required for establishing the schools in every district within six weeks. Tamil Nadu subsequently sought recall of that order, citing, among other things, the change in the state government and the lack of progress in discussions with the Centre.
Three-month deadline
The bench declined to recall the direction on Thursday. At the same time, it gave the state another three months to comply and directed representatives of the Centre and state to continue discussions on the policy and its implementation.
The language question figured prominently in those discussions. The bench suggested that the state’s concerns could be addressed through negotiations and even indicated that Tamil could be accommodated in the language arrangement.
“If you want Tamil as a second language, it is a matter which can be considered,” said the bench, asking the state and Centre to engage at the level of their respective education secretaries.
Gupta said discussions had already taken place but the Centre had remained firm on Hindi. He nevertheless agreed to another round of consultations. The state also raised a financial objection, claiming that the Centre had failed to release funds under existing education schemes and that Tamil Nadu could not take on additional financial liabilities.
Additional Solicitor General KM Nataraj, appearing for the Centre, countered that the State’s primary obligation under the Navodaya scheme was to provide land, while construction and other expenditure would be borne by the Centre.
The Centre also submitted that the schools were at a nascent stage and construction would take several years, leaving sufficient time to resolve the language-related differences. The bench said the financial and language issues could be discussed separately and emphasised that the establishment of Navodaya schools would not prevent Tamil Nadu from continuing its own education system.
“Ultimately everybody must work together,” the bench said.
The state, however, maintained that cooperative federalism could not operate in only one direction and that the court should not enter the policy debate.
The bench responded that the central scheme should not be viewed as an attempt to displace Tamil Nadu’s educational model.
“We are not alienating you and we are not alienating them. Some more type of schools come in your state also which will only enhance the high standard which we are aware of. This is not going to lower your standards. It will provide more opportunity,” said the bench.
In its order, the bench recorded Tamil Nadu’s explanation that the change in government and lack of material progress in discussions with the Centre had contributed to its non-compliance with the December 2025 direction.
“Be that as it may,” said the bench, directing the state to comply with the earlier order insofar as identification of land necessary to establish a school in each district was concerned.
The matter has been posted for December 14, by when the state and Centre are expected to have had further consultations.

headline: NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday hit out at Pakistan at the UN Security Council, saying Islamabad had provided a "permissive environment" to the "architects" of the 9/11 attacks and continues to provide space and support to terror groups such as Lashkar...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday hit out at Pakistan at the UN Security Council, saying Islamabad had provided a "permissive environment" to the "architects" of the 9/11 attacks and continues to provide space and support to terror groups such as Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed.Speaking at a UN Security Council meeting, India's Permanent Representative P Harish recalled the 9/11 terror attacks in United States and said al-Qaida leaders Osama bin Laden and Khalid Sheikh Mohammed were eventually found in settled communities in Pakistan rather than "caves or badlands".âThe international community supported the global campaign to counter terrorism in the wake of 9/11. Let us not forget, however, that al-Qaida's terror ecosystem established its strategic depth beyond Afghanistan through its affiliates,â Harish said.âThe leaders of al-Qaida who conceived and directed these 9/11 attacks did not escape justice in the wilderness of some ungoverned frontier.âThe Indian envoy also listed out the names of terrorists found in Pakistan.Bin Laden, who ordered and financed the 9/11 plot, was âtracked down and killed in a fortified compound within a settled, guarded community under Operation Neptune Spearâ, he said.
Mohammed, âthe principal architect of the operation, was found sheltering in an ordinary residential house.
Ramzi Binalshibh, who coordinated the hijacker cell after being denied a visa to join them, was sheltering in an urban centre,â Harish said.Senior al-Qaida operative Walid bin Attash, who helped select and prepare several hijackers, was captured separately, while Mustafa Ahmed al-Hawsawi, a key financial and logistical facilitator of the 9/11 operation, was also captured in Pakistan, he said."In each case, these were not fugitives hiding in caves or badlands, they were men who had long evaded detection. Draining this swamp that provided an enabling environment for such monsters of humankind to prosper is important," Harish said, in a thinly veiled reference to Pakistan.Harish also drew attention to what he described as an axis involving Pakistan, al-Qaida and terrorists targeting India.
"The same permissive environment that sheltered the architects of 9/11 has, in the years since, continued to provide space, support, and impunity to affiliates of al Qaida such as Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed and their like," he said.He said these groups continue to operate under different identities to evade the Council's sanctions, while their terror-training infrastructure continues to operate with impunity.The international community must act against the continued existence of such sanctuaries, he said, "to ensure that more such individuals are not thrust upon any country or its citizens and no one loses family and loved ones".Last week, as the world marked 25 years of the September 11 terror attacks perpetrated by al-Qaida, UN Security Council members, including Pakistan, visited the 9/11 memorial in Lower Manhattan.

headline: NEW DELHI: Congress on Thursday refuted the Centre's claim that five of its members supported the government's decision to introduce a merchant discount rate of 0.4% on UPI payments above Rs 2,000, saying that no such discussion took place during the...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Congress on Thursday refuted the Centre's claim that five of its members supported the government's decision to introduce a merchant discount rate of 0.4% on UPI payments above Rs 2,000, saying that no such discussion took place during the Parliamentary Standing Committee meeting.In a social media post on X, Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi said that the department of finance did not have any specific proposal on UPI tax when it met members of the finance committee."The Parliament standing committee on finance has not discussed the UPI tax proposal that the Modi government has recently announced," Gogoi said."The department of finance did not have any specific proposal on UPI tax when they met the members of the finance committee. Questions were raised on the need for MDR but the representatives of the government did not have any specific or satisfactory answers at that point," he added.He reiterated the party's demand to roll back MDR on UPI and said, "I reiterate that the recent UPI tax policies hurt the small Indian merchants, vendors, entrepreneurs and help the major American corporations. Roll back UPI tax. Stop surrendering, PM Modi."
Another Congress MP, Manish Tewari, backed Gogoi and accused the Centre of using the privileged proceedings of the Parliamentary Standing Committee to "score brownie points.""It is unfortunate that proceedings of Parliamentary Standing Committees that are supposed to be privileged are now sought to be used by the government to score brownie points," Tewari said in a social media post."My colleague is correct; no specific proposal qua the recent Merchant Discount Rate - MDR to be levied on UPI transactions from October 15th, 2026, was ever brought before the Parliamentary standing committee of Finance - rate, quantum, amount of fee to be charged, ceiling and exemption slabs, etc.," he added.He also said that concerns were raised by the Opposition over the need and efficacy of MDR on UPI payments during various sittings of the committee."Even on the principle or conceptual basis of MDR as my colleague Gaurav Gogoi points out concerns were raised by members with regard to its need, efficacy, etc., over the course of various sittings of the committee," Tewari said."To claim that a particular measure was supported by âcertain membersâ of the committee is an inaccurate and fallacious characterisation of the confidential proceedings of a Parliamentary Committee," he added.This comes a day after a government functionary claimed that Congress MPs, including former finance minister P Chidambaram and former minister in the UPA government Manish Tewari, supported the government's decision during the parliamentary panel's proceedings.âWhy is Rahul Gandhi opposing something his own MPs, including former finance minister P Chidambaram and former minister in the UPA government Manish Tewari, supported within the parliamentary panel?â news agency PTI reported a functionary as saying.According to the report of the standing committee headed by BJP MP Bhartruhari Mahtab, the panel noted its earlier recommendation emphasising that due to the imperative of a viable revenue model, legislative-enabling provisions for a tiered MDR structure have been brought forward.However, the committee remained deeply concerned by the staggering mismatch between the Rs 2,000-crore allocation and the industry's estimated operational cost of Rs 20,700 crore.In the view of the committee, while statutory enablement now exists to permit calibrated MDR on high-value transactions, any delay in notifying and operationalising this framework leaves payment service providers heavily dependent on inadequate subsidies, thereby threatening critical investments in cybersecurity, fraud prevention and network infrastructure.
On the incentive scheme for promotion of RuPay debit cards and low-value BHIM-UPI transactions (person-to-merchant), the committee, in its report, observed and recommended: âThe Committee notes the massive Rs 2,000 crore budgetary allocation for 2026-27 designed to offset ecosystem costs caused by the zero-MDR policy on RuPay and low-value UPI transactions.âThe Committee observes that while UPI is expected to process up to 150 billion transactions per month and add 600 million new users, the current government incentive covers merely 11% of the industry's actual costs and 14% of potential MDR collections, creating a structural funding gap impacting long-term infrastructural investment.âThe committee recommended that while the proposed three-year multi-year scheme and cashback components are necessary to democratise digital payments in untapped Tier 3-6 cities, the Department of Financial Services must concurrently explore a self-reliant, tiered revenue model.

headline: On Modi's birthday, CM Omar Abdullah wishes PM would grant J&K statehood
full_text:
On Modi's birthday, CM Omar Abdullah wishes PM would grant J&K statehood
Omar Abdullah also advised the Ladakh leadership to not rely on Centre's verbal assurances regarding their struggle for constitutional safeguards.
Wishing Prime Minister Narendra Modi on his birthday, Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Thursday reiterated his demand to restore statehood, saying all they have received so far on the matter were verbal assurances.
PM Modi celebrated his 76th birthday on Thursday, September 17.
"What can I say as to what he (Modi) does… If nothing else, let him grant us statehood; what else could we want?" Abdullah said, when asked about what announcement he expected today, news agency PTI reported.
The J&K CM was in Amritsar for the inauguration of renovated heritage building of the Jammu & Kashmir House on Court Road.
“You all know what happened with us. We were told that statehood would be restored after the (J&K) elections. But nothing was given in writing; only verbal assurances were given,” he was quoted as saying, as he also advised the leadership of Ladakh not to rely on the Centre's verbal assurances regarding their struggle for constitutional safeguards with regard to land and jobs.
"Hence, I suggest to people and friends in Ladakh not to trust the Centre's words… Rather, have them in writing. We did not get anything in writing, and we are at the same place today. J&K has been a victim of the Centre's verbal assurances," Abdullah said.
Abdullah said that the Centre had outlined a three-step process – delimitation, Assembly elections and the restoration of statehood.
"Even in Parliament and in the Supreme Court, this assurance was given. While we saw delimitation and elections in J&K, in which people participated, statehood has not been restored even till now," he said.
The Centre on August 5, 2019, scrapped Article 370 of the Constitution that granted special status to the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir and bifurcated it into two Union territories – J&K and Ladakh.
In December 2023, the Supreme Court upheld the Centre's decision to revoke the special status and create the two UTs but told the government to restore J&K's statehood as soon as possible.
In July, when Abdullah announced a fresh phase of its campaign for the restoration of statehood, he had said the the National Conference had exhausted its patience and would now intensify its movement by taking the demand directly to the national capital, news agency PTI reported.
Also read: Italy's Giorgia Meloni wishes PM Modi on his 76th birthday: ‘I wish you health, energy and success’
"Enough is enough! There will be no more waiting!" Abdullah had declared before a large gathering of party workers.
Later that month, Abdullah said that statehood was an imperative or basic need for restoring Jammu and Kashmir’s special status, stressing that Article 370 restoration is meaningless without statehood.

headline: SC to hear on Sep 22 plea against Delhi SIR exercise
full_text:
SC to hear on Sep 22 plea against Delhi SIR exercise
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the plea would be taken up on September 22 along with other SIR matters already pending before the court, while giving the fresh petition precedence
The Supreme Court on Thursday agreed to urgently hear a fresh challenge to the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) of Delhi’s electoral rolls, with the petition questioning why the names of nearly 33.13 lakh voters issued notices for “logical discrepancies” or lack of mapping have not been made public and what precisely triggered such notices.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the plea would be taken up on September 22 along with other SIR matters already pending before the court, while giving the fresh petition precedence.
The petition, filed by activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri through advocate Prashant Bhushan, comes against the backdrop of the exclusion of 47.56 lakh names from Delhi’s draft electoral roll published on August 31.
Mentioning the matter before the CJI, Bhushan said the 47 lakh-plus exclusions were only one part of the exercise, with the authorities now proposing to issue notices to another 33 lakh voters whose names figure in the draft roll but have been flagged under the categories of “no papping” and “logical discrepancies”.
“They have not disclosed the names of people which is why some people get notices and some do not. They have also not disclosed the basis of putting them under the logical discrepancy category,” Bhushan contended.
The CJI said the matter would be heard on Tuesday, September 22, when other SIR-related cases are also listed, adding that the fresh plea “will certainly have precedence” as it was a new matter.
Also Read: Nearly 1.1mn Delhi voters’ names deleted from January 2025 to June 2026, before SIR began
The challenge under Article 32 alleges that the failure of the Election Commission of India and the Delhi chief electoral officer to publish the names of voters issued notices, along with the specific reasons for doing so, violates their constitutional and fundamental rights.
The petition, filed through advocates Neha Rathi and Kajal Giri, has sought publication of a consolidated and searchable list of all electors issued notices, along with their addresses and the precise reason or category for each notice. They have also sought disclosure of the criteria, definitions, algorithmic parameters and operational guidelines used to classify voters under “Logical Discrepancies”.
The issue assumes significance because the draft roll published on August 31 contains 97,53,577 electors -- around 32.8% fewer than the 1,45,10,299 names on Delhi’s rolls before the revision. Of the 47,56,722 names excluded from the draft roll, the Delhi CEO’s data shows that 57.2% were men and 42.8% women. The exclusions were made under the ASDD category -- absent, shifted, dead or duplicate.
Separate from these exclusions are 33,12,919 voters whose names have remained in the draft roll but have been flagged for possible discrepancies. Of these, 13,79,785 have been categorised as having “no mapping” with the 2002 electoral roll, while 19,33,134 have been classified under “logical discrepancies”.
The petitioners’ grievance is not merely about the existence of these categories but about the information supplied to voters facing scrutiny. They contend that the term “logical discrepancies” has not been defined and that neither the original SIR order nor the Election Commission’s subsequent communications placed on the Delhi CEO’s website specify the criteria or parameters by which a voter is placed in this category.
According to the petition, notices issued to voters contain only generic descriptions of the alleged discrepancy without identifying the underlying material that would enable the elector to understand and answer it.
Also Read:Automated system flags ‘unusual’ age gaps, family links in Delhi SIR
The plea has also relied on the Election Commission’s May 14, 2026 communication, which, according to the petition, requires electoral registration officers to issue notices where an elector could not be linked to the previous roll or where the linkage was found to contain discrepancies. The communication also requires publication of the names of persons issued such notices on the chief electoral officer’s website and display at relevant local offices, the petition states.
The Delhi exercise has already generated a sizeable second layer of scrutiny beyond the names excluded from the draft roll. Officials have said the “logical discrepancies” broadly concern inconsistencies in electoral database records, including different spellings of names in the current and 2002 rolls, while other flagged anomalies include unusually small or large age gaps between an elector and a parent and unusually short gaps between the birth dates of siblings.
The authorities have maintained that being issued a notice does not, by itself, mean that a voter has been declared ineligible. Such voters would get an opportunity to respond and furnish documents or clarifications before the final roll is prepared.
The claims and objections process is scheduled to continue until September 30, with disposal of notices expected by October 29 and publication of the final electoral roll on November 4.

headline: The Congress on Thursday (September 17, 2026) demanded that the Narendra Modi government make its position clear on the latest move in the U.S. to impose steep tariffs on countries buying Russian oil, with the party’s general secretary (organisation)...

The Congress on Thursday (September 17, 2026) demanded that the Narendra Modi government make its position clear on the latest move in the U.S. to impose steep tariffs on countries buying Russian oil, with the party’s general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal asking whether India’s foreign policy and energy security would be “controlled from Washington”.
His remarks came after the U.S. House of Representatives passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 by a vote of 262-159, clearing the way for American President Donald Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries that continue to purchase Russian oil and gas. “Will the PM find the guts to stand up to the U.S.’ latest Senate resolution? Will India’s foreign policy and energy sovereignty be controlled from Washington?” Mr. Venugopal said in a post on social media platform X.
The government has been projecting the recently concluded BRICS Summit’s joint declaration as a symbol of the world’s trust in India, but was now facing “aggressive bullying from a strategic partner”, he said.

“Given the compromised PM’s track record, we are likely to see the Centre toe the U.S.’ line and surrender to Washington. We demand that the Modi government clarify its stance on this at the earliest, and ensure India’s energy security is not sacrificed,” Mr. Venugopal said.
His colleague and party general secretary Randeep Surjewala described the U.S.’s move as an “affront to Indian sovereignty” and questioned whether the government would “speak for the nation”.
Mr. Surjewala cited remarks by Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal after the House voted that India and China should “buy their oil and gas somewhere else”.
The government had repeatedly compromised India’s interests in dealing with the U.S., the Congress leader alleged, and questioned why New Delhi should not be free to decide from whom it buys crude oil.
“Our foreign policy and sovereignty cannot be bartered at the altar of our friendship with the United States. National interests cannot be mortgaged at the altar of event management by a weak-kneed BJP govt.,” Mr. Surjewala said on social media platform X.
Congress general secretary in charge of communications Jairam Ramesh simply said: “Appeasement has never paid and will never pay.”
The Congress’s attack came as the government sought to reassure the country that it would protect its economic and energy interests. India is monitoring developments following the passage of the legislation and remained “firmly committed” to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people, the Ministry of External Affairs said.

headline: New Delhi: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has frozen the symbol and name of the All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) in an interim order passed Thursday, taking note of the rival groups in the party—one led by Mamata Banerjee and another by Ar...
full_text:
New Delhi: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has frozen the symbol and name of the All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) in an interim order passed Thursday, taking note of the rival groups in the party—one led by Mamata Banerjee and another by Arup Roy.
The decision comes less than 20 days before the bye-elections in Rejinagar and Nandigram constituencies necessitated by the resignations of Humayun Kabir and Suvendu Adhikari. The elections to the two constituencies in southern Bengal are scheduled for 6 October.
Neither of the groups can now use the party’s name or its reserved “Flowers & Grass” symbol for the upcoming bye-elections, pending a final determination of the organisational dispute.
The 14-page order, issued Thursday, says, “On due consideration of the totality of information available on record with the Commission…the Commission is of the opinion that there are two rival groups in All India Trinamool Congress, one led by Ms. Mamata Banerjee and the other led by Shri Arup Roy, and each group is now claiming to be the party and therefore the matter requires a substantive determination by the Commission under Para 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation & Allotment) Order 1968.”
Accordingly, in order to place both the rival groups on an “even keel and to protect their rights and interests, and going by the past precedence,” the Commission passed an interim order for the purpose of bye-elections.
This order will remain in effect till the dispute is settled.
Neither of the two groups are permitted to use the name ‘All India Trinamool Congress’ by itself, nor can they use the symbol ‘flowers and grass’ reserved for the Trinamool Congress.
“Both the groups shall be known by such names as they may choose for their respective groups, including, if they so desire, linkage with their parent party ‘All India Trinamool Congress’,” reads the order.
Both the groups have been directed to furnish by 11 am Friday, the names by which they may be recognised by Commission for the time being. They have to give three options in order of preference, any one of which may be approved by the Commission. The groups also have to submit names of three free symbols, in the order of their preference, to the Commission.
The Commission heard the delegations from both the factions Thursday.
In its order, it noted that the time available was not adequate to complete the proceedings under Para 15 of the Symbols Order.
“However, the Commission takes note of the urgency involved with regard to use of party symbol and party name in the ongoing by-elections,” it said.
Para 15 says that when the ECI is satisfied that there are rival sections or groups of a recognised political party each of whom claims to be that party, the Commission may decide that one such rival section or group or none of such rival sections or groups is that recognised political party. ECI can do so after taking into account all the available facts and circumstances of the case and hearing such representatives of the sections or groups and other persons who want to be heard.
The ECI’s decision shall be binding on all such rival sections or groups.
Responding to the interim order, Congress general secretary K.C. Venugopal wrote on X that freezing of the party name and symbol “after a blatantly unconstitutional hijack by the BJP—is CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s late night birthday gift to Modi ji.”
“Those who fought against the BJP, under Mamata Banerjee’s leadership, are now being given the red carpet to rebel against her and commit the unconstitutional sin of defection with the ECI’s help. The ECI has one again proven that it is nothing more than a puppet in the hands of the BJP—a tool to destroy democracy bit by bit,” he wrote.
Referring to the split in Shiv Sena and NCP, the senior Congress leader wrote that “whoever opposes the BJP is dealt a fatal blow and their entire electoral existence is snatched away from them.” Condemning the move, he demanded that the ECI must immediately restore the symbol to the faction led by Mamata Banerjee.
(Edited by Amrtansh Arora)

headline: NEW DELHI: The Union health ministry has asked states and Union territories to act against unauthorised stem cell therapy, reiterating that it can be offered as routine treatment only for disease conditions or indications approved by the ministry.In ...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: The Union health ministry has asked states and Union territories to act against unauthorised stem cell therapy, reiterating that it can be offered as routine treatment only for disease conditions or indications approved by the ministry.In an advisory issued on September 16, the ministry said stem cell therapy for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) must remain restricted to duly approved clinical trials. It must not be offered as routine, standard or commercial clinical treatment.The advisory follows the Supreme Court judgment of January 30, 2026, in which the court issued directions on the use of stem cell therapy for ASD. The ministry has asked states and UTs to circulate the directions to state and district regulatory authorities as well as government and private clinical establishments involved in stem cell research, treatment, promotion or administration.The ministry has also flagged the consequences of violations. Citing the Supreme Court's directions, it said non-compliance can attract professional misconduct, besides action under Sections 32 and 40 of the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010, including cancellation of registration and penalties.The National Medical Commission (NMC), in an advisory issued on September 5, also reiterated that stem cell therapy can be offered as standard clinical care only for approved indications.
It said unauthorised administration, prescription, promotion or advertisement of stem cell therapy beyond approved indications would constitute professional misconduct.The NMC has asked State Medical Councils to examine alleged violations and, where professional misconduct by a Registered Medical Practitioner is established after due process, take appropriate disciplinary action.
The health ministry has also reiterated that the regulatory framework governing stem cell research and therapy must be followed, including the National Guidelines for Stem Cell Research, 2017, issued jointly by the Indian Council of Medical Research and Department of Biotechnology.The latest advisory puts the focus on enforcement by state and district authorities. It directs authorities and clinical establishments to ensure that unproven stem cell interventions, including those for ASD, are not offered outside the permitted regulatory framework.

headline: Congress pays extra Rs 4 lakh for Rahul Gandhi event site in Indore
full_text:
Congress pays extra Rs 4 lakh for Rahul Gandhi event site in Indore
The Congress paid an extra Rs 4.03 lakh for the Indore site of Rahul Gandhi's September 19 event. The demand sparked a fresh BJP-Congress clash over land-use rules and political pressure.
The Congress on Thursday deposited an additional Rs 4.03 lakh with the Indore Development Authority for the temporary lease of land for its 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' event on September 19, which will be addressed by Rahul Gandhi. With this, the party's total payment for the site has gone up to Rs 14.11 lakh.
The additional payment came after the authority said the party had used part of the land before the approved lease period. The demand also triggered a political exchange, with the BJP saying the issue was about collecting the prescribed revenue for the use of government land, while the Congress alleged the administration was acting under pressure from ruling party leaders.
Officials said the Congress had first deposited Rs 10.08 lakh for the temporary lease. In a letter to City Congress Committee president Chintu Chouksey, the authority said 12,000 square metres of land had been allotted on a temporary lease for the event from September 17 to 19. However, a site inspection found that 4,800 square metres of land had been used by the party from September 14.
For this, the authority asked the party to deposit an additional Rs 4.03 lakh as a three-day lease fee. A Congress leader said the amount had been paid, taking the total to Rs 14.11 lakh.
The authority's demand came after BJP state spokesperson Rakesh Singh Yadav complained that the space was being used beyond the stipulated period, in violation of the permit terms. "This matter is not about opposing any political event, but about the collection of prescribed revenue for the use of government land," Yadav said in a statement.
Chouksey objected to the demand and said it had come due to pressure from BJP leaders. He alleged that the administration was acting as a puppet of the ruling party leaders.
The Congress had earlier sought permission on September 12 to hold Gandhi's event at the city's Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium. But Mayor Pushyamitra Bhargava said that, under an old order of the Madhya Pradesh High Court, the stadium could be used only for sports events or state-level government events. The Congress then rescheduled the programme for September 19 and applied for land opposite the Regional Park.
'Chhatron Ki Goonj' is a student-dialogue campaign launched by former Congress president Rahul Gandhi to target the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party on issues such as question paper leaks, expensive education, irregularities in government recruitment and unemployment. So far, four editions of the programme have been held under Gandhi's leadership in Kota, Dehradun, Prayagraj and Pune.
In sum, the Congress has paid the additional amount sought by the Indore Development Authority for alleged early use of the event site, even as the dispute over the charge has led to a fresh exchange between the BJP and the Congress ahead of Rahul Gandhi's September 19 programme.

headline: After a brief disruption in ties, India and Bangladesh have resumed official-level talks to firm up plans for a visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to New Delhi, diplomatic sources have confirmed.
full_text:
After a brief disruption in ties, India and Bangladesh have resumed official-level talks to firm up plans for a visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to New Delhi, diplomatic sources have confirmed.
Bilateral relations took a hit after the virtual press conference by former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in August triggered backlash in her home country. Ms. Hasina is currently living in an undisclosed location in India.
The Hindu was told that officials on both sides have continued meetings in Dhaka and are working on setting up an agenda for the visit that will include regularisation of bilateral trade that has been affected because of unstable political relations and questions over the renewal of Ganga Water Treaty among other issues.
Also Read | ‘Rahman wants to visit India, but agenda has to be set first’
Envoy’s meetings
Sources in Dhaka said Prime Minister Mr. Rahman is scheduled to travel to New York for the United Nations General Assembly this month following which he will have multiple diplomatic engagements over October and November, while efforts are underway to schedule his visit to New Delhi during a suitable window in November. Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi has held meetings with a series of officials over the last few days, including the country’s Minister of Water Resources Mohammed Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee and Adviser to the Prime Minister for Ministry of Education Mahdi Amin.
Mr. Rahman was invited to participate in the recently held BRICS Summit here in his capacity as the head of BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) but Bangladesh did not send any representation to the event with Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kobir asserting that Bangladesh is planning to “reset” ties with India and for that Dhaka will prioritise a bilateral visit at a “conducive” moment. The Hindu had earlier reported that the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) government had viewed the cancellation of a programme by supporters of Ms. Hasina’s Awami League earlier this month as a “positive sign”.
Ms. Hasina has been based in India since fleeing Dhaka on August 5, 2024 and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bangladesh had expressed “outrage” over her latest press conference where she had alleged that law and order had broken down in Bangladesh. Over the past two years, Ms. Hasina and several of her top ministers and officials have received death sentences at the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) in Dhaka for their alleged role in the crackdown against protesters in July-August 2024, which ultimately toppled her government.
Also Read | Rashtrapati Bhavan withdraws email on Bangladesh PM visit
Rahman’s emissaries
Though the fall of Ms. Hasina was seen as unexpected, sources within the current dispensation in Dhaka have said that Mr. Rahman maintained his touch with India during his years in exile in London and that he had received indication in February 2024 that New Delhi too was not expecting the Hasina government to last beyond a few months.
The Hindu was informed that Mr. Rahman’s personal contacts with Indian officials were renewed at least since February 2024 when he had sent an emissary to India to sense India’s mood following the widely criticised election of January 2024 that was boycotted by the BNP under his leadership. The engagement was in line with previous exchanges between BNP and India during the Sheikh Hasina era between 2009 and 2024 when she was in power.
Two months before the January 2024 election, current Energy Minister Iqbal Hasan Mahmud Tuku had visited New Delhi. In an interview with The Hindu, Mr. Tuku had urged India to extend “unambiguous support to the democratic aspirations” of the people of Bangladesh. In similar vein in 2018, a three-member team consisting of Abdul Awal Mintoo, Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury and Humayan Kobirhad visited New Delhi to engage with the Government of India. The Daily Star had reported that the 2018 visit was a result of Mr. Rahman’s instruction to his party to carry out course correction as “the hostile policy towards India was wrong and misguided”.
