headline: NEW DELHI: CBI has filed an FIR and launched a probe into an illegal funding network operated by US-based Christian missionary organisation, The Timothy Initiative, and its Indian leadership for allegedly using foreign funds to the tune of over 92 cr...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: CBI has filed an FIR and launched a probe into an illegal funding network operated by US-based Christian missionary organisation, The Timothy Initiative, and its Indian leadership for allegedly using foreign funds to the tune of over 92 crore between Nov 2025 to April 2026 for missionary activities in violation of Foreign Contribution Regulation Act.The agency's probe has also revealed that the cash withdrawals were deployed across India to conduct training programmes, preaching, and the targeted indoctrination of economically marginalised groups, which,CBI said, fostered left-wing extremism.CBI kicked off the probe following directions and approval from MHA. Key individuals named in the conspiracy include India operations head Jonathan S Rajan, primary financial handler Micah Mark, Ajit Verghese Mathai, along with field operatives Varghese Chacko, Bablu Kurmi, and Supreme Joy.CBI alleged the syndicate conspired to systematically channel foreign funds into India without oversight.The FIR, registered on the basis of findings shared by ED, says that the syndicate circumvented formal banking channels by distributing over 1,000 foreign debit cards issued by the US-based Truist Bank across India. Operatives systematically withdrew physical cash from ATMs in states such as Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, and Assam.
Investigators estimate that between Nov 2025 and April 2026 alone, the network illegally funnelled $9,995,240 into the country. This came in addition to an earlier illicit withdrawal of Rs 44 crore executed through identical ATM transactions between Jan 2024 and March 2026.The trail unravelled after agencies intercepted Micah Mark at Bengaluru airport on April 18, 2026. Mark was caught carrying 24 Truist Bank debit cards, all fraudulently embossed with the single alias "Santosh Kumar.""This was allegedly orchestrated on the instructions of Ajit Verghese Mathai to bypass Know Your Customer mandates and conceal the identity of the real users. Investigations revealed Mark had made multiple overseas trips to bring back such debit cards. Following the raids, TTI USA attempted to tamper with evidence by blocking domestic access to its website (ttiglobal.org) and remotely wiping cloud servers with data stored on seized laptops," the FIR says.
This amounted to destruction of evidence as it happened even as search and seizure proceedings were underway, officials said.Rajan managed training logistics, trainer selection, and venue identification while submitting financial requirements to the organisation's finance team to secure illegal overseas transfers. Field functionaries handled cash distribution after making regular ATM withdrawals.The I-T department carried out searches and seizures on the outfit earlier this year.
Raj Shekhar Jha is a journalist for the Times of India with over a decade of experience in reporting on national security, terrorism, crime and prisons.

headline: Three of the five baby orangutans rescued in Odisha are suffering from anaemia, officials said on Wednesday (September 16, 2026).
full_text:
Three of the five baby orangutans rescued in Odisha are suffering from anaemia, officials said on Wednesday (September 16, 2026).
A comprehensive health check-up of the primates, including X-rays and blood tests, was carried out after one of the juvenile orangutans developed fever, they said.
According to a health bulletin issued by the Nandankanan Zoological Park, where the orangutans have been quarantined, in-house haematology analysis found severe anaemia in one of the primates and mild anaemia in two others.
"Supportive supplementation for the said orangutan babies, as advised by the Technical Committee, has already been started," it said.
"X-rays of the chest, abdomen and skull were taken, while blood, serum and nasopharyngeal swab samples were collected from all five animals. Laboratory tests are underway," it added.
Nandankanan Zoological Park Director Sanath Kumar N. said the overall health condition of the orangutans appeared to be stable.
Four of the five animals recorded a body temperature of 98.4 degrees Fahrenheit, while a male orangutan recorded 99 degrees Fahrenheit, an official said.
"This particular male orangutan has shown a slightly higher temperature than the others since its arrival at Nandankanan Zoological Park on the night of September 8," he said.
The blood samples are also being tested for parameters such as haemoglobin and white blood cell count, while stool and urine samples are being examined, he said.
The samples will also be used for DNA testing to establish the origin of the rescued animals, which could aid the ongoing investigation into suspected wildlife smuggling, he added.
A laboratory capable of conducting the DNA test is being identified, the official said, adding that the facility would need to have standard DNA profiles of orangutans for comparison. "Such laboratories are not very common," he said.
Aditya Acharya, head of the Centre for Wildlife Health (CWH) at Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology, said the well-being of the animals was the priority. "Regarding DNA tests, zoo authorities will take the call on where and when to send the samples," he said.
The five orangutans were rescued from a forest in Balasore district on September 8.
According to a dietary chart prepared by experts, the orangutan babies are being fed milk every two hours, besides apple and banana fluids and boiled potatoes at regular intervals.
No major breakthrough in probe so far
The Odisha Police's Special Task Force (STF) and the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB), which are jointly investigating the suspected international wildlife smuggling that led to the animals being brought to the State, have made no major breakthrough in the probe so far, officials said.
Bhograi MLA Goutam Buddha Das of the BJD criticised the State government over the pace of the investigation and urged Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi to hand over the case to a central agency such as the CBI or NIA. "Since there is an element of international smuggling involved in the case, a high-level and professional probe is most essential," Das said.
BJP spokesperson Anil Biswal, however, said the Odisha Police STF was capable of resolving the case with the assistance of the WCCB. "The BJD MLA is politicising the matter out of nothing," Biswal said.
Orangutans are not native to India and are primarily found in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra, officials said.

headline: India rejects Pakistan-China boundary panel, says it has no legal standing
full_text:
India rejects Pakistan-China boundary panel, says it has no legal standing
India has dismissed the Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission, saying the body has no legal standing. New Delhi says any such move involving Pakistan-occupied Indian territory is illegal and cannot affect its sovereignty.
India on Wednesday rejected the Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission, saying the body has no legal basis to decide on arrangements related to Indian territory under illegal occupation. The response came after the commission held its first meeting in Islamabad.
The Ministry of External Affairs said India’s position on the matter remains “clear and consistent”. It said there is no boundary between Pakistan and China, and stressed that any such cooperation concerning Indian territories is unacceptable and has no bearing on India’s sovereignty.
External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, “Our position on this matter is clear and consistent. There is no boundary between Pakistan and China. We reject the so-called Joint Commission, which is without any legal basis.”
India has consistently maintained that Pakistan’s handing over of certain territories, including the Shaksgam Valley, to China in 1963 was illegal and unacceptable. New Delhi has also opposed the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, saying part of it passes through Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir.
Jaiswal said the entire Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh “have been, are and will always remain integral and inalienable parts of India”. He added, “We have never recognised the so-called ‘China-Pakistan Boundary Agreement’ of 1963 and have consistently maintained that it is illegal and invalid.”
The spokesperson said, “We resolutely oppose and reject any attempts to alter the status of these occupied territories or legitimise illegal occupation, impinging on India’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.”
He also said, “Any so-called boundary cooperation between China and Pakistan concerning Indian territories would be completely unacceptable and would have no bearing whatsoever on India’s sovereignty over these territories.”
Calling on Pakistan to “immediately vacate areas under its illegal and forcible occupation”, Jaiswal said such moves were “theatrics”. India’s response reiterated its rejection of the joint commission, the 1963 agreement, and any attempt by Pakistan and China to discuss or alter the status of territories that it regards as its own.

headline: The line-up for the Nagaon parliamentary seat byelection on October 6 is complete with the All India United Democratic Front (AIUDF) nominating its chief, Badruddin Ajmal, as its candidate on Tuesday. His entry makes it a four-way contest, with forme...
full_text:
The line-up for the Nagaon parliamentary seat byelection on October 6 is complete with the All India United Democratic Front (AIUDF) nominating its chief, Badruddin Ajmal, as its candidate on Tuesday. His entry makes it a four-way contest, with former legislator Sibamoni Bora of the Congress, former bureaucrat Devasish Sharma of the BJP and academic Abdul Salam of Trinamool Congress also in the fray.
Nagaon is the first major face-off between the principal combatants, BJP and Congress, since the former’s crushing sweep in the April Assembly election with 102 out of 126 seats for the National Democratic Alliance. The AIUDF’s last-minute candidate switch from former student leader Rejaul Karim Sarkar to its founder is a bold gambit that could radically alter Opposition politics in a foreseeable future where the ruling party holds near-absolute sway.
Even as the upper regions of Assam were still reeling from the impact of sudden floods in July, the State’s broader Opposition unity fractured on September 3 when the Congress formally severed ties with Akhil Gogoi’s Raijor Dal. Wazid Ali Choudhury, Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly, said the decision by the Congress leadership followed repeated criticism of the party by its ally. “Akhil Gogoi has constantly been criticising the Congress party and its leaders. We got tired of the fact that he was in an alliance with us and still criticising us,” he said. The erstwhile junior ally chose to train its guns on Lok Sabha MP and Assam Congress chief Gaurav Gogoi, questioning the scale of his engagement with the flood crisis.
While he opted not to put up a candidate in Nagaon in the interest of “preventing the rise of communal forces”, the Raijor Dal chief is eyeing a larger chunk of the Opposition space over the full term of the BJP-led government. The party won two seats in the April election, Mr. Akhil Gogoi defending his Sibsagar seat from 2021 and Mehboob Muktar winning Dhing LAC in Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency.
It could have added a third to its kitty, but the Congress’s veto forced Raijor Dal to drop Sherman Ali Ahmed as its candidate from Mandia; Mr. Ahmed promptly walked over to the Trinamool Congress and secured the party its sole seat.
Raijor Dal’s long game
With only one non-Muslim among the Congress’s 19 winning candidates, the Raijor Dal’s long game is clear: expand at the expense of the principal Opposition party among the Assamese Hindu voters, a prospect even Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma had predicted in February this year.
The Muslim vote isn’t a settled question either. The Congress wrested back much of this electoral constituency from the AIUDF in the last Assembly election after refusing to renew its tie-up from 2021, but dismal performances across seats with a thin minority concentration leave it vulnerable to another shift. Mr. Ajmal set the cat among the pigeons as early as August 16 when he claimed – correctly, in retrospect – that the Congress will not field a Muslim candidate in the bypoll. By fronting himself as a candidate, the AIUDF chief, currently an MLA from central Assam’s Binnakandi seat and a former three-time MP from western Assam’s Dhubri, is going all in to reclaim the party’s core constituency. The arithmetic aligns: Nagaon has four Muslim-majority Assembly segments, Dhing, Rupahihat, Lahorighat and Samaguri, and four others – Nagaon-Batadraba, Jagiroad, Morigaon and Raha; over 55% of the parliamentary constituency’s voters are minorities.
The BJP and AIUDF, with their respective Nagaon picks, have boxed the Congress in from both flanks. State BJP chief Dilip Saikia and the CM have acknowledged the odds in a ‘non-traditional’ seat. The BJP is betting on a non-Muslim consolidation for Mr. Devasish Sharma, the former Nagaon Deputy Commissioner whose transition from bureaucrat on September 3 to BJP politician five days later sparked Congress outrage. The strategy, the CM spelled out, is to maximise its advantage in the four non-minority-heavy segments and narrow deficits in the rest.
Mr. Ajmal and Mr. Salam’s candidatures ensure that every Muslim vote would be equally fought for. A Congress victory could only come about if it manages to draw support across sections of voters – essentially making its old winning formula work. The party could not afford to alienate non-minority voters with a Muslim pick, having won the Lok Sabha seat twice in succession even as it slipped elsewhere against the BJP. The Nagaon poll is thus Congress’s to lose.
“Congress will secure victory once again in the Nagaon bypoll. Consider this as an announcement,” Mr. Gaurav Gogoi had said even before the party announced its choice.
A win here would indeed signal a vital shift: a diverse electorate, bridging religious divides, voting the Congress candidate first past the post and giving the party a credible shot at taking on the BJP five years down the road. A failure would mean the fundamental factor underlying its Assembly election rout persists – an inability to appeal to the Assamese Hindu voters beyond a certain threshold.

headline: U.S. President Donald Trump on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) welcomed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s efforts to curb illicit poppy cultivation even as he identified India, China and Pakistan among 23 major drug transit and illicit drug producing cou...
full_text:
U.S. President Donald Trump on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) welcomed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s efforts to curb illicit poppy cultivation even as he identified India, China and Pakistan among 23 major drug transit and illicit drug producing countries and urged their respective leaders to address the issue.
In a Presidential Determination to the U.S. Congress, Mr. Trump said he looks forward to continued cooperation through the United States-India Drug Policy Framework.
“I welcome Prime Minister Modi and the Government of India’s efforts to address illicit opium poppy cultivation and bolster supply chain integrity," he said in the official directive that was made public on Wednesday (September 16, 2026).
Mr. Trump also made it clear that appearing on the list of major drug transit and illicit drug producing countries was not necessarily a reflection of the respective government’s current counterdrug efforts, or coordination with the U.S.
The Presidential Determination said countries are placed on the list, as required by U.S. law, due to a combination of geographic, commercial, and economic factors that allow drugs or precursor chemicals to transit or be produced, even if a government has engaged in robust and diligent narcotics control and law enforcement measures.
The other major drug transit or major illicit drug producing countries identified are Afghanistan, The Bahamas, Belize, Bolivia, Burma, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Haiti, Honduras, Jamaica, Laos, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.
Mr. Trump also highlighted the "historic progress" made by his administration in tackling drug trafficking and narcoterrorist organisations. He pointed to tighter border security, lower drug seizures and a decline in overdose deaths as evidence of the progress.
Mr. Trump claimed drug seizures along the U.S. southern border had dropped by more than half after what he called four years of "open border chaos". He also said drug overdose deaths had "plunged" and claimed that the administration had saved tens of thousands of American lives.
“After four years of open border chaos, seizures of fentanyl and other drugs being smuggled into the United States have been reduced by more than half, and drug overdose deaths have plunged,” Mr. Trump said.
He urged China to take stronger action to stem the flow of precursor chemicals used to produce fentanyl, methamphetamine and other synthetic drugs. “The PRC continues to be the world’s largest producer of many of the precursor chemicals used to illicitly produce fentanyl, methamphetamine, and other deadly synthetic drugs,” Mr. Trump said, referring to China by its official designation, the People's Republic of China.
Mr. Trump said he had raised the issue directly with Chinese President Xi Jinping and noted that Beijing had introduced licensing requirements last year for companies exporting designated precursor chemicals to North America.

headline: Chennai: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s first official overseas visit to London has triggered a political controversy, with Opposition parties calling it a “fun trip” or “pleasure tour” funded by public money. The Bharatiya Janata Party ...
full_text:
Chennai: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s first official overseas visit to London has triggered a political controversy, with Opposition parties calling it a “fun trip” or “pleasure tour” funded by public money. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) questioned the authenticity of the plan of the government to attract foreign investors during the trip.
BJP Tamil Nadu president Nainar Nagendran Wednesday described the visit as a mere “pleasure tour”.
“It is a complete lie that Chief Minister Vijay brought investments to Tamil Nadu. They are pointing out already existing companies as new industrial investments,” he said, accusing the government of misleading the public by presenting expansions of firms already operating in the state as fresh gains from the trip.
On Monday, DMK mouthpiece Murasoli mocked the London visit as a trip to watch a car race rather than attract investors, alleging that Vijay “suddenly took off on his own” without the usual preparatory discussions involving ministers and officials. The editorial also cited reports of a roughly 74.5 percent decline in new investment proposals for Tamil Nadu during the first quarter of 2026, and a drop in the state’s national ranking from sixth to 17th.
Allies of the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) haven’t kept quiet either.
P. Shanmugam, state secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), has also questioned the state government’s claim of securing more than Rs 1 lakh crore in investments and asked for the presentation of a white paper on the same. The DMK also pointed out the need for transparency of investments attracted by the government within about 100 days in office, asking why the visit was being presented as an investment-promotion exercise when the main visible programme appeared to be the Silverstone motor racing event.
Social media users also criticised the presence of Vijay’s co-actor Trisha Krishnan at the Silverstone Circuit, where he flagged off a race that saw the participation of actor-racer Ajith Kumar.
Opposition leaders, including Udhayanidhi Stalin, have also raised questions about the purpose of the multi-day trip, the composition of the delegation, noting the absence of the industries minister or senior officials from the department and asking whether government funds were used, and if there were any actual concrete outcomes.
The TVK strongly countered the criticism on Wednesday, highlighting announced investment commitments of around Rs 15,300 crore that are expected to create thousands of jobs, including a memorandum of understanding signed with EY and Samvardhana Motherson. TVK leaders, including Energy and Law Minister Nirmal Kumar, insisted that the primary purpose was investment outreach and studying sports infrastructure for a proposed motor sports city near Chennai.
In a statement on X, the TVK’s Information Technology Wing attacked the DMK over past use of public money. It stated that the previous regime used people’s tax money to go on a luxury trip outside Tamil Nadu with the entire family, including the son and daughter. Referring to former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin’s visit to Oxford University, the tweet stated that the previous regime booked a private venue in advance, and staged a photo-op under the name of “unveiling a Periyar statue,” and enacted a drama to deceive the people of Tamil Nadu.
The post contrasted this with Vijay’s visit, under which MoUs worth Rs 15,300 crore were signed, and mocked critics who complained about crowds gathering to see the chief minister in London. That event of Chief Minister Vijay was later cancelled over safety concerns.
(Edited by Nardeep Singh Dahiya)

headline: Jhiram Valley massacre: All 10 convicts get death penalty 13 years after Maoist attack in Chhattisgarh
full_text:
Jhiram Valley massacre: All 10 convicts get death penalty 13 years after Maoist attack in Chhattisgarh
The court found them guilty under multiple laws, while defense plans to appeal the verdict, citing dissatisfaction with the investigation.
A special National Investigation Agency (NIA) court in Jagdalpur in Chhattisgarh’s Bastar district on Wednesday sentenced all 10 convicts in the 2013 Jhiram Valley Maoist attack case to death, 13 years after an ambush on a Congress Parivartan Yatra convoy in Bastar killed 27 people, including senior Congress leaders, and injured more than 35.
Special judge Ajay Singh Rajput had convicted the 10 accused on September 5 and reserved the order on the quantum of punishment.
NIA counsel Dinesh Panigrahi confirmed that the court awarded the death penalty to all 10 convicts. “The court has awarded the death penalty to all 10 convicts,” Panigrahi said.
Defence lawyer Arvind Choudhary said the defence was not satisfied with the verdict and would challenge it in the high court.
Also Read | Jhiram Valley massacre: NIA court convicts all 10 accused in 2013 Maoist attack
The convicts are Pramila Modiyam, Chaitu Lekam, Sumitra Punem Modiyam, Mukka Mandavi, Kosa Kavasi, Aayata Markam, Madkami Deva, Joga Madkami, Banjami Sanna and Mahadev Nag. Pramila Modiyam and Sumitra Punem Modiyam are the two women among those convicted.
The NIA, in a statement issued on Wednesday, said the court found them guilty under various sections of the Indian Penal Code, Arms Act, Explosive Substances Act and Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.
The Maoists ambushed the Congress convoy on NH-221 in Jhiram Valley in Darbha ahead of the 2013 Chhattisgarh assembly elections. The attack began with an IED blast, followed by indiscriminate firing and grenade attacks. Twenty-four people were killed on the spot and more than 35 civilians and police personnel were injured. Three of the injured later succumbed to their injuries, taking the death toll to 27, the NIA said.
Those killed included then state Congress president Nand Kumar Patel and his son Dinesh Patel, former Leader of Opposition Mahendra Karma, former Union minister Vidya Charan Shukla and senior Congress leader and former MLA Uday Mudliyar.
The NIA said its investigation established that armed cadres of the banned CPI (Maoist), in connivance with local committees and divisions, had entered into a criminal conspiracy to target senior Congress leaders and security personnel travelling with the Parivartan Yatra as part of the outfit’s Tactical Counter Offensive Campaign (TCOC). The state police initially registered a case, but the then Raman Singh-led BJP government handed over the investigation to the NIA within two days.
The agency filed its first charge sheet against nine accused on September 25, 2014, and a supplementary charge sheet against 30 accused on September 28, 2015, naming 39 accused in all.
Eleven arrested accused were put on trial, but one died in judicial custody. The trial saw the examination of 101 prosecution witnesses and presentation of documentary evidence.
The investigation also named several senior CPI (Maoist) leaders, including Thippiri Tirupathi alias Devuji, Barse Deva and Ganesh Uikey.
Also Read | ‘He didn’t know how to shoot': Jhiram Valley attack convicts' kin dispute court judgment, claim innocence
The larger conspiracy behind the attack remains a political issue in Chhattisgarh, with the Congress repeatedly alleging that the NIA did not fully investigate it.
In January 2019, the then Bhupesh Baghel-led Congress government constituted a Special Investigation Team (SIT). A fresh FIR was registered at Darbha police station on May 25, 2020, under sections 302 (murder) and 120B (criminal conspiracy) of the IPC against unidentified persons on a complaint by Jitendra Mudliyar, son of slain Congress leader Uday Mudliyar.
The NIA later sought transfer of the fresh probe to the agency. After its plea was rejected, it moved the Supreme Court, which declined to interfere.
Commenting on the judgment, Chhattisgarh Pradesh Congress Committee president Deepak Baij said the verdict amounted to “half and incomplete justice” and that the party respected the court’s decision.
“The court has punished only those against whom evidence was placed before it. The NIA could not reach the conspirators behind the attack and its investigation was directionless from the beginning,” Baij said.
“The NIA made those who carried bags, supplied water, dug pits and showed routes accused in the case, and they have now been punished. But such a major attack could not have taken place without senior Maoist leaders,” he said.
Baij also questioned why punishment had been awarded to only 10 people if, as the agency had stated, around 200 Maoists were involved in the attack and 39 people had been named as accused.
Also Read | Top Maoist with ₹1.1 crore bounty among 6 killed
“If 200 Maoists were involved in the incident and 39 were named as accused, why have charges been proved and punishment awarded against only 10?” he asked.
The Congress had alleged that the NIA probe lost momentum after the NDA government came to power at the Centre in 2014.

He reports on Maoism, internal security, politics, mining, governance, and major developments shaping the state. Based in Raipur, he has covered Chhattisgarh since 2016, reporting extensively from the Bastar region and other conflict-affected areas. With nearly two decades of experience in journalism, Ritesh has built a reputation for ground reporting from some of India's most challenging terrains. headline: 13 years after Jhiram Valley massacre, 10 Maoist convicts get death penalty
full_text:
13 years after Jhiram Valley massacre, 10 Maoist convicts get death penalty
A special NIA court in Chhattisgarh's Jagdalpur sentenced 10 Maoist convicts to death over the 2013 Jhiram Valley massacre, which killed 27 people, including Congress leaders.
Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai on Wednesday welcomed a special NIA court's decision to award the death penalty to all 10 convicts in the 2013 Jhiram Valley Maoist attack case, calling it a "victory of justice".
Former Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel, however, termed the punishment "incomplete justice" and said those who masterminded the massacre were still free.
A special NIA court in Jagdalpur sentenced the 10 convicted Maoists, including two women, to death in the 13-year-old case in which 27 people, including senior Congress leaders, were killed. The court had convicted the accused on September 5 and reserved its order on the quantum of punishment for Wednesday.
In a post on X, Sai said the Jhiram Valley massacre was a painful chapter in Chhattisgarh's history and that memories of the tragedy would continue to cause pain. "We lost senior leaders of the state, security personnel and common citizens in this horrific communist violence," he said.
"The death sentence awarded by the Jagdalpur NIA court to the 10 Maoists found guilty in the case is a victory of justice. The NIA also deserves appreciation for taking the investigation to its logical conclusion," Sai said.
He also said Chhattisgarh had been freed from armed Maoist insurgency under Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and that Bastar, once affected by Left-Wing Extremism, was moving towards peace, trust and development.
The Chief Minister also said, "This is also a moment for introspection, especially for those who engage in politics over the bodies of tribals and who provide intellectual and ideological support to terror. 'Urban Naxals', too, must realise the consequences of sheltering or abetting terror for vested interests are invariably catastrophic for everyone. The monster of terror battles against Indian democracy, the Constitution, and respects no ideological or territorial boundaries."
He added, "I bow to the souls of all those who lost their lives in that brutal Jhiram attack. A humble tribute."
Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Sharma, who holds the Home portfolio, said the verdict showed the NIA investigation had been carried out thoroughly. Speaking to reporters in Kawardha, he said the death sentence was awarded after the court considered the evidence collected by the agency. "Today, it has become clear that the NIA conducted the investigation with great effort and sincerity," he said.
Sharma said the Congress had unnecessarily tried to politicise the issue and target some people without sufficient basis. Responding to Baghel's criticism, he said there was no basis for his dissatisfaction.
"When Baghel was the Chief Minister (2018-23), he used to say he had evidence relating to the Jhiram Ghati attack in his pocket. Why did he not bring it out?" Sharma asked. "An attempt was being made to mislead people. The investigation was still going on. If you have something to say, give your statement before the NIA. Speaking at public gatherings will not achieve anything," he said.
Asked about senior Maoist leaders who had surrendered in Telangana and were allegedly involved in the Jhiram attack, Sharma said action would be taken under the government's surrender and rehabilitation policy.
"Rehabilitation policies are decisions taken by governments according to the prevailing circumstances. Those who have surrendered will be dealt with as per the applicable procedure under the surrender policy," he said.
Baghel, in a social media post, said the punishment given to the Maoists' "foot soldiers" was neither proportionate nor justice. "Those who hatched the conspiracy and those who carried out this massacre are still roaming free," he said.
He alleged that the names of senior Maoist leaders had been removed from the NIA case earlier and that they were not even charged. "Neither the NIA nor the inquiry commission investigated the conspiracy angle," he alleged, adding that BJP leaders had repeatedly obstructed the investigation.
"The question of changing our position because of the court's verdict does not arise. We still believe that justice is incomplete because the investigation is incomplete," Baghel said.
Barsa Vetti, a close relative of convict Joga Madkami, also questioned the verdict and asked why senior Maoist leaders who had surrendered and were allegedly involved in the attack were not being questioned.
Speaking to reporters, he said he was upset over the conviction of what he called "innocent" tribals. "Joga was not a Maoist and he had also served twice as the sarpanch of Chikpal village panchayat," Vetti said.
He claimed several Maoists from Bastar's Darbha division had since surrendered and that some of those allegedly involved in the attack had either died or laid down arms. "If those who carried out the attack have surrendered and are with the government, why is the government not investigating them?" he asked.
Jagdalpur-based social activist Bela Bhatia also questioned the verdict and called it devoid of justice.
The Jhiram Valley attack took place on May 25, 2013, when Maoists ambushed a Congress Parivartan Yatra in Bastar ahead of the Chhattisgarh Assembly elections. Twenty-seven people were killed, including then state Congress chief Nand Kumar Patel and his son Dinesh, former minister Mahendra Karma, former Union minister Vidya Charan Shukla and Congress leader Uday Mudliyar.

headline: The Congress party should be in an alliance with a party that accepts party leader Rahul Gandhi as the next Prime Ministerial candidate, former Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president K. Selvaperunthagai has said.
full_text:
The Congress party should be in an alliance with a party that accepts party leader Rahul Gandhi as the next Prime Ministerial candidate, former Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president K. Selvaperunthagai has said.
Speaking at a press meet on Wednesday, Mr. Selvaperunthagai said, “The alliance partners should accept that Rahul Gandhi is the Prime Ministerial candidate. If they don’t, why should we be in the [TVK-led] alliance?”
Responding to Mr. Selvaperunthagai’s remarks, Congress Rajya Sabha member Praveen Chakravarty, while speaking to reporters at the airport asked, “Who is he [Mr. Selvaperunthagai] today? He could have been anyone in the past.”
Stating that there was no confusion, he further added, “Even recently, when we got together for a meeting to decide on the name for the alliance [headed by TVK], which I had attended, we were talking and laughing with each other…Chief Minister [C Joseph Vijay] was also there. The alliance is strong. There are no issues.”
Later in the evening, Mr. Selvaperunthagai criticised Mr. Chakravarty in a statement for his comments and charged that he was exhibiting his “elitist mindset”.
“I said why do we need an alliance with a party that doesn’t accept our leader Rahul Gandhi as the Prime Ministerial candidate. But, this intellectual says that Chief Minister was smiling and talking to him when they met. Is that the reason for continuing in the alliance? Chief Minister can state openly that Rahul Gandhi is the PM candidate just once,” he said.
Mr. Selvaperunthagai also added, “Please ask the Chief Minister why comments critical of PM Modi, Amit Shah and BJP are being removed from the Assembly records.”

headline: The government on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) questioned the rationale behind Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's criticism of the decision to levy a fee on UPI payments to merchants above ₹2,000, saying a parliamentary standing committee had backed su...
full_text:
The government on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) questioned the rationale behind Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's criticism of the decision to levy a fee on UPI payments to merchants above ₹2,000, saying a parliamentary standing committee had backed such a move and Congress members of the panel had supported it.
A senior government functionary said the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance had pressed for a tiered Merchant Discount Rate (MDR)/ revenue framework for Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and noted that it should be notified and operationalised without delay.
Also Read | Opposition MPs raise concerns over proposed UPI merchant payment fee
Five Congress MPs including P Chidambaram, Manish Tewari, Gaurav Gogoi, Kishori Lal and K Gopinath were present on August 12 when the report was adopted, with no dissent recorded in the published minutes, the functionary said.
"Why is Rahul Gandhi opposing something his own MPs, including former finance minister P.Chidambaram and former minister in the UPA government Manish Tewari supported within the parliamentary panel," the functionary asked.
Reacting to the government's decision to levy a fee on UPI payments above ₹2,000 to merchants, Mr. Gandhi alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has decided to "prostrate" before U.S. President Donald Trump and give a huge amount of money to America.
The Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha also demanded a rollback of the government's decision to levy a fee on UPI payments.
According to the report of the standing committee headed by BJP MP Bhartruhari Mahtab, the panel noted its earlier recommendation emphasising that due to the imperative of a viable revenue model, legislative-enabling provisions for a tiered MDR structure have been brought forward.
However, the committee remained deeply concerned by the staggering mismatch between the ₹2,000-crore allocation and the industry's estimated operational cost of ₹20,700 crore.
In the view of the committee, while statutory enablement now exists to permit calibrated MDR on high-value transactions, any delay in notifying and operationalising this framework leaves payment service providers heavily dependent on inadequate subsidies, thereby threatening critical investments in cybersecurity, fraud prevention and network infrastructure.
Regarding the incentive scheme for promotion of RuPay debit cards and low-value BHIM-UPI transactions (person-to-merchant), the committee, in its report, had further observed and recommended: "The Committee note the massive ₹2000 crore budgetary allocation for 2026-27 designed to offset ecosystem costs caused by the zero-MDR policy on RuPay and low-value UPI transactions.
"The Committee observe that while UPI is expected to process up to 150 billion transactions per month and add 600 million new users, the current government incentive covers merely 11 per cent of the industry's actual costs and 14 per cent of potential MDR collections, creating a structural funding gap impacting long-term infrastructural investment." The committee recommended that while the proposed three-year multi-year scheme and cashback components are necessary to democratise digital payments in untapped Tier 3-6 cities, the Department of Financial Services must concurrently explore a self-reliant, tiered revenue model.
The committee would like to emphasise that establishing a viable revenue mechanism is critical to ensuring that the UPI ecosystem achieves financial sustainability without perpetually straining the government exchequer, it said.

headline: Birthday wishes and congratulatory messages poured in for Prime Minister Narendra Modi from across political spectrum on Thursday. President Droupadi Murmu and Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan conveyed their wishes, crediting Mr. Modi as a leader f...
full_text:
Birthday wishes and congratulatory messages poured in for Prime Minister Narendra Modi from across political spectrum on Thursday. President Droupadi Murmu and Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan conveyed their wishes, crediting Mr. Modi as a leader for driving governance reforms, inclusive growth, and progress towards “Viksit Bharat” by 2047.
Also Read: Rajasthan order asking students to join PM Modi's birthday celebrations sparks controversy
Marking the occasion, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) organised events such as lighting of diyas (oil lamps) and blood donation camps across the country.
“Over the past 25 years, during your tenure as Chief Minister and Prime Minister, you have established many new benchmarks of good governance and imparted unprecedented momentum and a new direction to inclusive development,” said Ms. Murmu on X, wishing Mr. Modi good health and long life for his continued campaign of “public service and nation-building”.
The Vice-President said: “Under your steadfast and visionary leadership, Bharat is shining as a bright spot in the world and among the fastest-growing major economies. Over 25 crore Indians have come out of extreme poverty. A transformative digital revolution has empowered millions, and every sector — from space, technology, and healthcare to infrastructure and manufacturing — has witnessed remarkable growth.”
Congress president and Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge and his Lok Sabha counterpart, Rahul Gandhi, greeted Mr. Modi on his 76th birthday. “Best wishes to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji on his birthday. May he be blessed with good health and long life,” Mr. Kharge said in a post on X. Mr. Gandhi said: “Happy birthday to PM Narendra Modi ji. Wishing you good health and a long life.”
Telugu Desam Party president and Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, Keralam Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha chief and State Chief Minister Hemant Soren were among the heads of State governments who sent birthday greetings to the Prime Minister.
Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam chief and former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin said on X: “Warm birthday greetings to Hon’ble Prime Minister Thiru. @NarendraModi avl. Wishing him good health, happiness and a long life.” Biju Janata Dal president Naveen Patnaik extended his wishes, as did Bahujan Samaj Party supremo Mayawati and Samajwadi Party’s Akhilesh Yadav.

Former Bihar Chief Minister and Janata Dal (United)’s Nitish Kumar also extended his greetings. Mr. Modi’s Cabinet colleagues showered praises on him for his contributions to the country’s development over the 25 years of public service. Union Home Minister Amit Shah flagged off the Seva Yatra being undertaken on 250 motorcycles from Vadnagar in Gujarat to the Prime Minister’s parliamentary constituency in Uttar Pradesh’s Varanasi, where it will conclude on October 17.
The event is part of the “Seva Sankalp Abhiyan”, a month-long programme from September 17 to October 17, marking Mr. Modi’s birthday and 25 years since he became Gujarat Chief Minister.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh also flagged off the “Seva Sankalp Yatra” from Varanasi to Vadnagar. The programme was attended by Mr. Naidu, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and Union Minister Chirag Paswan among others.

Describing Mr. Modi as the “architect of modern India”, Mr. Nabin said the “Seva Sankalp Abhiyan” was inspired by his resolve throughout his public life to serve the country, work for public welfare, and bring positive change in the lives of those standing at the last rung of society.

headline: BJP plans month-long ‘Seva’ outreach across India, spanning party and govt
full_text:
BJP plans month-long ‘Seva’ outreach across India, spanning party and govt
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is set to turn Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday into the launch pad for a nationwide outreach campaign from September 17 to mark his 25 years in public life
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is set to turn Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday into the launch pad for a nationwide outreach campaign from September 17 to mark his 25 years in public life.
Built around the idea of “seva” (service), the campaign will run till October 17 and span nearly every rung of the party and government machinery, from booth workers to chief ministers. One of its strands, “Seva Mera Yogdan”, has drawn up a list of 25 service activities, from blood donation camps to tree plantation drives, and is asking citizens to pick at least one and participate.
The exercise is less a single event than a web of parallel programmes, each assigned to a different arm of the party and the state machinery. Party workers, government departments, schools, Anganwadi centres, digital influencers, NGOs and elected representatives have all been roped in, with nodal officers appointed at the block, district and state levels to monitor how each component is implemented.
Deep Dive
Interestingly, party circulars have asked state education departments to frame their official communication around “Viksit Bharat Sankalp” and “25 years of service work”, while avoiding any direct mention of the PM’s birthday, even as the campaign’s start date coincides with it. The instruction points to a conscious effort to present the drive as a governance initiative rather than a personality-led one, though the timing itself will hardly go unnoticed.
The first big moment comes on the evening of September 17 itself. Under “Ashirwad Ka Diya”, booth workers will visit the homes of scheme beneficiaries and ask them to light a lamp as a mark of gratitude for welfare schemes. State governments have been asked to share beneficiary lists, including those who received Covid vaccines, so the visits can be planned door to door. The lamps, once lit, are meant to travel further online under the hashtag #AshirwadKaDiya.
Schools get their own version of the campaign through “25 Crore Children’s Dreams of India”, a drawing and speech competition to be held between September 17 and October 7. States can choose any window of seven to 10 days that suits them. The best drawings will move from school to district and then state-level exhibitions, while winners will receive certificates signed by CMs.
There is a cultural push too. “Nukkad nataks” or street plays under “Namo Seva Gatha” will be staged in villages, schools and colleges nationwide, retelling 25 years of welfare schemes through music and drama, with a major push planned for October 2.
Anganwadi centres, meanwhile, will host a three-day event between September 25 and October 7 called “Aangan Ka Utsav”, where workers will be publicly felicitated and mothers briefed on nutrition and maternity schemes.
Central to the campaign is “Kahani Badlav Ki”, under which party workers will fan out to record the real stories of 2.5 million citizens whose lives, the party says, have changed through government schemes. From this pool, around 25,000 stories will be shortlisted, and roughly 250 of the strongest ones will be turned into polished videos for a national compilation.
Digital creators occupy a bigger role in the campaign this time than in past BJP drives. Under the “Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra”, between 300 and 500 influencers and content creators will be taken to sites the party sees as proof of visible change, from the changed security situation in Bastar to Gujarat’s GIFT City and innovation hubs such as iCreate. States have been asked to submit lists of such “transformative sites” within three days, and are expected to both send their own influencers and host visitors from elsewhere.
Two more journeys add a religious and symbolic layer to the month. The “Seva Jyoti Yatra” will carry a ceremonial flame through villages by foot and motorcycle, converging at fixed points for gatherings where beneficiaries speak and crowds take a collective pledge for a developed India by 2047. A separate “Jal, Jan aur Seva Sankalp Yatra” will move holy water between Vadnagar in Gujarat and Varanasi on a 500-pilgrim, 250-motorcycle relay, with 10 groups fanning out on different routes each way to cover an estimated 60 to 80 locations a day.
The month builds up to a grand finale on October 17, the “Jansevak Mahakumbh”, where around 125,000 sarpanches (village heads) and other public representatives are expected to gather across Delhi, Gurugram, Ghaziabad, Surajkund and Varanasi. The plan includes a mass rendition of all six stanzas of Vande Mataram, aimed at a Guinness World Records attempt, followed by a formal resolution and an address by the Prime Minister.
Stripped of its many names and hashtags, what emerges is essentially a coordinated public outreach exercise running for a month, bringing together party workers, beneficiaries, schools, Anganwadi centres, influencers, digital creators, local artists, NGOs, public representatives and government departments under one umbrella. Whether the numbers, particularly the 2.5 million beneficiary stories and the Guinness record bid, hold up will only become clear once the month plays out.

headline: Chicken biryani for schoolchildren CM Vijay's wish: TN minister on mid-day meal plan
full_text:
Chicken biryani for schoolchildren CM Vijay's wish: TN minister on mid-day meal plan
Tamil Nadu has reiterated its plan to offer chicken biriyani in government schools after a pilot phase. The government says hygiene, food safety and logistics will decide any wider rollout.
The Tamil Nadu government, led by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, has reiterated plans to introduce chicken biriyani for students in government schools, with School Education Minister Raj Mohan saying the proposal is a wish of the Chief Minister. The plan will be taken up after a pilot and testing phase to ensure the meal is prepared and served under hygienic conditions.
Speaking about the proposal, Raj Mohan said the government wants all school students to have the option of chicken biriyani, but stressed that it cannot be introduced immediately as arrangements must first be made to ensure hygiene and food safety.
“With all due respect, even prisoners in Puzhal prison have chicken biriyani. Can’t our students also have it?” the minister said.
He added that the government would first conduct a pilot project and assess the arrangements before expanding the initiative.
“It cannot be implemented immediately as it has to be done in hygienic conditions. There has to be a pilot and test project. In the coming days, we will make sure school students will have chicken biriyani in schools,” Raj Mohan said.
PROPOSAL UNDER CONSIDERATION SINCE JULY
The proposal was first reported in July, when the Tamil Nadu government was considering serving chicken biriyani once a week to students in government schools under the Mid-Day Meal Scheme.
Raj Mohan had said he personally proposed the idea to Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, who would take the final decision on the plan. The proposal came amid a broader discussion over introducing non-vegetarian food into school meal programmes.
The minister had argued that growing children requires adequate protein and said providing chicken biriyani should not be viewed as a political issue.
“In Tamil Nadu, the educational revolution has always gone hand in hand with a nutritional revolution,” he had said while explaining the rationale behind the proposal.
Raj Mohan had also clarified that students who prefer vegetarian food would continue to receive vegetarian meals, while those who eat non-vegetarian food could opt for chicken biriyani if the proposal is implemented.
HYGIENE AND PILOT PROJECT
The minister's latest remarks indicate that the proposal remains under consideration, with the government focusing on how the meal can be prepared and served safely on a large scale.
A pilot and testing phase is expected to help authorities assess food preparation, hygiene standards and logistics before any wider rollout across government schools.
Tamil Nadu's school nutrition programme has undergone several changes over the years, with successive governments expanding the range of meals provided to students. The state also operates a breakfast programme for government school students, alongside the midday meal initiative.
The government is also considering improvements to the school breakfast menu as part of its broader focus on nutrition and school attendance.

headline: In response to Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi’s allegations of “government theft” and “party theft” after the Trinamool Congress symbol freeze, the BJP on Friday (September 18, 2026) said the Congress’s history was replete wit...
full_text:
In response to Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi’s allegations of “government theft” and “party theft” after the Trinamool Congress symbol freeze, the BJP on Friday (September 18, 2026) said the Congress’s history was replete with instances of “betraying allies and bringing down elected governments”.
The Election Commission had barred two factions of the Trinamool from using the existing party symbol and name, and allotted them fresh symbols and names for use in the upcoming Assembly bypolls.
Responding to the development on Friday, Mr. Gandhi posted on X: “First Shiv Sena, then NCP, and now Trinamool Congress. Every time, the same pattern – BJP and the Election Commission join forces to split a party. Then its election symbol is snatched away. When an entire party can be stolen, it is hardly surprising that the votes of millions of Indians can be stolen too.”
“Vote theft. Government theft. Now party theft – these have become symbols of our democratic decline...,” he alleged.
Sudhanshu’s retort
BJP MP and spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi retorted, describing the Congress as the “Bhasmasur” of Indian politics, alleging that whoever came in contact with it was eventually destroyed.
At a press conference, he said that “the Congress, throughout its history, has betrayed its allies, brought down elected State governments in an unconstitutional manner, and repeatedly divided the party by sidelining even its own veteran leaders”, while the BJP was “a symbol of democratic values and unity”.
“Rahul Gandhi cannot even read enough to understand that the full form of NCP is ‘Nationalist Congress Party’ and that the name of the Trinamool Congress also contains the word ‘Congress’. Sharad Pawar separated from the Congress in 1999 over the issue of leadership by a person of foreign origin, while Mamata Banerjee left the party in 1997 after being distressed by the internal situation within the Congress, and later ousted the Congress itself from West Bengal,” he said.
Mr. Trivedi accused the Congress of sidelining and undermining several people, including its own leaders, over the years. “...in the 1969 Presidential election, Indira Gandhi called for votes against her own party’s candidate, Neelam Sanjiva Reddy”, said the BJP leader.
He further alleged that senior Congress leader Ashok Gehlot was recently “prevented from becoming Congress president”. “The betrayal of Chaudhary Charan Singh during the Janata Party regime, the merger of the Lok Dal in Haryana in 1980, and the absorption of Chimanbhai Patel’s Janata Dal into the Congress in 1992” were among the alleged instances he cited.
Mr. Trivedi said that after the Congress came to power at the Centre in 1980, Opposition governments in nine States were dismissed. The then Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister T. Anjaiah was “humiliated” in 1982, Karpoori Thakur’s Lok Dal split in 1982, the N. T. Rama Rao’s government in Andhra Pradesh was dismissed in 1984, the National Conference split the same year, and the then Prime Minister Chandra Shekhar’s government fell within three months in 1991, he alleged.
Mr. Trivedi also referred to the dismissal of the S.R. Bommai government in Karnataka in 1989. “Subsequently, in 1994, a nine-judge Bench of the Supreme Court ruled that a government’s majority cannot be determined by the personal opinion of a Governor or the President, but only through a floor test in the House,” he said, also mentioning the “1993-94 Jharkhand Mukti Morcha bribery” case.
He also alleged that the Union governments led by Janata Dal (Secular) chief H.D. Deve Gowda and Janata Dal’s I.K. Gujral were brought down by the Congress in the late 90s.

Karnataka grants Tulu additional official language status in 2 coastal districts
Karnataka has granted Tulu additional official language status in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi, fulfilling a long-standing demand, deputy CM D K Shivakumar said.
Karnataka has granted Tulu the status of an additional official language in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts, chief minister D K Shivakumar announced on Friday.
The decision was taken at the first Cabinet meeting held in the coastal city, at the Praja Soudha building. It fulfils a long-standing demand for formal recognition of Tulu in the region, where it is widely spoken.
“Considering the demand of the people of undivided Dakshina Kannada, we have decided to announce Tulu as an additional official language of the state. It will be treated as an additional official language in undivided Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts,” Shivakumar told reporters after the meeting.
Tulu is a Dravidian language with a history of more than 2,000 years and is spoken by nearly one crore people globally, with its principal base in the undivided Dakshina Kannada and Udupi regions and parts of Kasaragod.
Shivakumar said the government had chosen to focus on the lives and needs of people rather than revisit why previous governments had not acted on the demand.
“I am not going to question why earlier governments failed to consider Tulu as the second language. Our government considers the baduku (life) and not the bhavane (sentiments) of the people. Therefore, a region grows when a language is given recognition,” he said.
The Cabinet also discussed a proposal to rename Dakshina Kannada district as Mangaluru.
“We discussed this during the Cabinet meeting, and public opinion will be collected alongside a formal debate. A decision on this will be taken within a month,” Shivakumar said.
The language decision came as the government held its first Cabinet meeting in Mangaluru, with coastal districts having sought action on a range of long-pending demands.

headline: NIA chargesheets 9 over alleged plot to recruit youths for ISIS activities
full_text:
NIA chargesheets 9 over alleged plot to recruit youths for ISIS activities
The agency alleged that the accused were part of a wider conspiracy to support the banned terrorist organisation and establish a caliphate in India through violent jihad.
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has charge-sheeted nine alleged ISIS members and supporters for conspiring to radicalise and recruit young people for terrorist activities, officials said on Friday.
The agency alleged that the accused were part of a wider conspiracy to support the banned terrorist organisation and establish a caliphate in India through violent jihad. Social media platforms, including Instagram, were allegedly used to identify, influence and recruit young people.
The charge sheet was filed before a special court in Vijayawada against Mohammad Rehmatullah Shariff, Mohammed Danish, Mirza Sohail Baig, Lucky Ahmad, Jishan Abdul Majid, Mir Ashif Ali, Abdul Salaam, Sharuk Khan and Shaikh Faiz ur Rehman.
Eleven accused and a child in conflict with the law have so far been apprehended in the case, the NIA said.
EXPLOSIVES, WEAPONS TRAINING PLANNED: NIA
According to the agency, the accused attempted to persuade young people to join violent activities and made preparations to manufacture explosives and undergo weapons training.
“It has been established that the accused persons motivated and radicalised gullible youths to join violent terrorist activities and also planned and prepared for making explosives and undertaking weapon training,” the NIA said in a statement.
The accused also allegedly developed and tested a secure application to communicate secretly while preparing for terrorist activities.
The case was initially registered at Vijayawada II Town police station on March 23, 2026, and was later taken over by the NIA.
The accused have been charged under Sections 61(2), read with 3(5), and 152 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with Sections 13(1), 38 and 39 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.
The BNS provisions cover criminal conspiracy, common intention and acts endangering India’s sovereignty, unity and integrity. The UAPA sections relate to unlawful activities and association with or support for a terrorist organisation.

headline: Surendra Koli, acquitted in Nithari serial killing case, found dead in Haridwar
full_text:
Surendra Koli, acquitted in Nithari serial killing case, found dead in Haridwar
Surinder Koli was acquitted by the Supreme Court in the last remaining Nithari killings case in November 2025,
Surendra Koli, who was acquitted in November 2025 in the last remaining case related to the killings in Noida's Nithari, was found dead inside a tea stall in Uttarakhand's Haridwar under suspicious circumstances, police said on Friday.
Kundan Singh Rana, an Uttarakhand Police officer, said Koli had started the stall days ago. He added that Koli, who was from Mangrukhal village in Almora, had been living in Haridwar for the past few months. He worked as a security guard before renting the stall. Track all updates on Surendra Koli's death here
Rana said no suicide note was found. He added that Koli's family in Almora had been informed, and an investigation was initiated into the circumstances surrounding his death.
Koli's acquittal
In November 2025, the Supreme Court said Koli's 2011 conviction could not stand when he was acquitted in 12 identical cases based on the same evidence, confession, and flawed investigation. It said it would be a "travesty of justice" to let one conviction survive.
The court upheld the principle that the rule of law must be consistent, years after the killings surfaced when a child playing cricket spotted a human hand in a drain between two houses in Nithari. When the drain was dug up in December 2006, multiple skulls, bones, and tattered children's clothes were found.
Police claimed that Koli, who was a domestic worker at one of the houses of businessman Moninder Singh Pandher, lured children and women, murdered them, and in some cases, even indulged in cannibalism. Pandher was accused of complicity and exploitation.
By the time investigators arrived on the scene in December 2006, crowds had gathered, trampling through evidence as remains were pulled from the ground. The "recovery" of a knife from beneath a terrace tank and several other items was the backbone of the prosecution. But courts found them unreliable.
The Central Bureau of Investigation took over the probe in January 2007. The agency relied on Koli's confession recorded after weeks in custody and on dubious recoveries.
The Supreme Court pointed out that the same confession and the recoveries were rejected as unreliable in all other cases. It said it found "no principled basis" to uphold one conviction when 12 others had already fallen on identical facts.

A birthday celebration on a roadside in Jammu turned fatal after a man allegedly attacked his friend with a sharp-edged weapon following a dispute over cake being smeared on his face, police said on Friday.
The incident came to light around 9 pm on Thursday when Pawan Nair alias “Sameer” was brought to Government Medical College (GMC) Jammu by his friends John Sotra, Gaurav Singh and Sugandh Bhatti, reported news agency PTI.
Doctors declared him brought dead, following which the Police Post Government Medical College Jammu informed Police Station Janipur, a police spokesperson said.
Dispute broke out during birthday celebration
A preliminary inquiry revealed that Neeraj was celebrating his birthday on a roadside near Lower Roop Nagar, where his friends, including Nair, Sotra, Singh and Bhatti, were present. Neeraj was accompanied by his brother Rishu.

The celebration took a violent turn during the cake-cutting ceremony after Nair smeared cake on Neeraj’s face, police said.

Cops search for attack weapon
Following the incident, Police Station Janipur registered a murder case and arrested the accused, Neeraj alias “Anshu”, and his brother, Rishu, in connection with the murder, the PTI report added.

This came an hour after Mamata Banerjee said she would support the Congress candidate after her own candidate withdrew the nomination.

headline: Hours after Mamata's support, Congress claims Nandigram bypoll candidate Milan Pradhan arrested
full_text:
Hours after Mamata's support, Congress claims Nandigram bypoll candidate Milan Pradhan arrested
On Friday, Mamata Banerjee extended her support to the Congress' Nandigram candidate and said that her TMC faction would not field a candidate.
Milan Pradhan, the Congress candidate for the Nandigram bypoll in West Bengal, was arrested by the police on Friday in connection with a 2007 case hours after former Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee declared that her party would back Pradhan in the October 6 bypoll.
Banerjee’s announcement came on Friday afternoon after her party’s candidate, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew her nomination,leaving her party without a contender in a constituency that has voted chief minister Suvendu Adhikari in the last four elections. Nandigram was one of the two seats that Adhikari won in the April 2026 elections; the bypoll is necessitated because he retained Bhabanipur.
Milan Pradhan, the Congress candidate, was arrested in a murder case registered in 2007 in the Nandigram police station, a police officer said, but did not explain why the police chose to act now.
According to the affidavit submitted by Pradhan along with his nomination papers, he was named in at least six murder cases in Nandigram police station in 2007.
Subhankar Sarkar, West Bengal Congress president, said Pradhan had expressed apprehension about his safety.
“He wasn’t taking my calls. He earlier told me that he could be abducted. I was trying to make some alternative arrangements. But meanwhile, I learned that he has been arrested along with a few other people. I am yet to receive the full information,” said Sarkar.
“If there are so many cases pending against him, what were the police doing all these days? The police suddenly became active only after he filed his nomination to contest the election? It appears that they (BJP) won’t allow any political party to contest the elections. Do they not want a multi-party democracy? This aggressive attitude isn’t good for democracy,” the state Congress leader said.
The manoeuvring came a day after the Election Commission of India restrained the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress and the rebel group led by Arup Roy from using the party’s name or its "flower and grass" election symbol. On Friday, the Banerjee-led faction was temporarily allowed the name “Mamata All India Trinamool Congress” and the football symbol for the October 6 bypolls.
News that a teacher, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew from the fray just before the deadline came soon after. Banerjee said she did not blame Dey.
“She was threatened that her children would be kidnapped. What can she do? I have no grudges,” Banerjee said, declaring her party’s support for the Congress candidate.
She also spoke about the phone call that she had received from Congress leader and leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, to express solidarity with her party after the Election Commission ruling. Banerjee’s remarks were a shift in her approach, as the TMC, during its 15 years in power, had maintained it could take on the BJP on its own in Bengal.
The Trinamool Congress that she founded has been under intense pressure after it lost power to the Bharatiya Janata Party in April this year.
The BJP won 207 of 294 seats and the TMC, only 80.
But after the elections, 57 TMC legislators backed Ritabrata Banerjee, who was recognised as the leader of the opposition in the state assembly by speaker Rathindra Nath Bose. TMC leaders in parliament also switched sides.
Twenty rebel TMC parliamentarians have also merged with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India and backed the Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Alliance.
Twenty rebel TMC Lok Sabha MPs have also claimed to have merged with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India and backed the Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Alliance.
In the Rajya Sabha, the Mamata Banerjee-led TMC has been left with nine Rajya Sabha members after Sukhendu Sekhar Roy, Sushmita Dev and Prakash Chik Baraik resigned in June, joined the BJP and were reelected to the upper House on July 24. A fourth TMC Rajya Sabha member, actor Koel Mallick, also resigned from the Rajya Sabha.

headline: CM Vijay to launch one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Tamil Nadu on September 28
full_text:
CM Vijay to launch one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Tamil Nadu on September 28
Under the scheme, every child born in a government hospital from June 22 onwards will be given a one-gram gold ring.
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joseph Vijay will launch the state government’s Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram scheme on September 28, following a review meeting on its rollout and implementation at the Secretariat on Friday.
The scheme is part of the government’s Vettri Tamilagam long-term vision and aims to mark the birth of children in government hospitals while boosting public confidence in state-run healthcare services. It also draws from the Tamil cultural tradition of Thaaimaman Seer, news agency ANI reported.
One-gram gold ring for babies born in government hospitals
Under the scheme, every child born in a government hospital from June 22 onwards will be given a one-gram gold ring. The Government Order for the initiative was issued on June 23.
Also read | Vijay’s UK trip slammed as ‘pleasure tour’; BJP, AIADMK raise questions over investments
Tamil Nadu records around 7.80 lakh births every year. According to National Family Health Survey-6, 99.9% of deliveries in the state take place in institutions. Around 4.20 lakh, or 53%, of these deliveries are conducted in government hospitals.
Of the deliveries in government hospitals, 90% take place at Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (CEMONC) centres, highlighting the role of the public health system in providing safe delivery and childbirth services.
1,28,000 gold rings procured for initial rollout
The state government said each gold ring will carry a unique serial number and be distributed in tamper-proof packaging. A total of 1,28,000 gold rings have been procured for the first phase of the scheme.
Mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have registered with the Pregnancy and Child Tracking (PICME) system and obtained an RCH ID will be eligible for the benefit.
Also read | Tami Nadu bypoll: Know schedule, candidates and more in Vijay govt's first electoral test
To cover babies born between June 22 and the launch date, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across the state from September 28. Each hub will distribute rings to 100 babies per day.
From September 28, babies born in government hospitals will receive the gold ring at the time of discharge.
Government highlights focus on mother and child health
The Tamil Nadu government said mother and child health has been a key priority in the state. It cited the implementation of financial assistance for pregnant women, free delivery services, newborn care, maternity treatment, nutrition support and birth planning.
The government also highlighted the use of the Pregnancy and Child Tracking (PICME) software for monitoring and evaluation, saying these measures have contributed to significant improvement in maternal and child health indicators in the state.
According to the government, the Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram scheme is intended to increase public trust in government medical services, encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen mother and child health protection and demonstrate its commitment to child welfare.
Senior officials attend review meeting
The review meeting was chaired by Chief Minister Joseph Vijay at the Secretariat.
The meeting was attended by Medical and Medical Education and Public Health Minister Dr. Ma. Ka. Arunraj, Chief Secretary Dr. Mu. Vaikumar IAS, Director General of Police Thiru Mahesh Kumar Agarwal IPS, Health and Family Welfare Secretary Dr. Thares Ahmad IAS, National Health Mission Director Dr. Aneesh Segar IAS, Director of Municipal Administration P. Mathusoothan Reddy IAS, Tamil Nadu Health System Project Director Dr. S. Uma IAS, Greater Chennai Corporation Commissioner Dr. G.S. Sameeran IAS and other senior officials.
(With inputs from ANI)

The case was registered on March 23, 2026, at Vijayawada II Town police station and was later taken over by the NIA.

headline: India to get its first dengue vaccine Qdenga by first half of 2027
full_text:
India to get its first dengue vaccine Qdenga by first half of 2027
The Takeda vaccine, Qdenga, is likely to be introduced in India in the first half of 2027 and the price has not yet been decided
Hyderabad-based Dr Reddy’s Laboratories will promote and distribute India’s first anti-dengue vaccine by Takeda Pharmaceuticals across India’s private market for paediatric and adult vaccination, the companies announced on Friday.
The Takeda vaccine—Qdenga—is likely to be introduced in India in the first half of 2027, they added. However, the vaccine’s price has not yet been decided.
“The approval for marketing authorisation was just granted in July. Hence, the immediate priority is to complete the necessary local processes required before commercial distribution can begin. It would be premature to speculate on pricing before the remaining local processes are complete,” said Mahender Nayak, head of intercontinental markets, Takeda.
Also Read | Maharashtra reports sharp spike in vector-borne disease cases
He added that through the collaboration announced today, Takeda and Dr Reddy’s will support healthcare-professional engagement, disease awareness, promotion and distribution of Qdenga across India’s private market for paediatric and adult vaccination, in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.
“While inclusion in India’s public immunization program remains an important long-term ambition, private-market availability through Dr. Reddy’s will provide a pathway for eligible individuals to access the vaccine once it becomes available. Further details will be shared at the appropriate time,” added Nayak.
The collaboration follows the approval of Qdenga’s marketing authorisation by India’s Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) in July for individuals aged between 4 and 60 years. Dengue remains a significant and evolving public-health challenge in India. According to a nationwide dengue surveillance study conducted by the Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratory of the Indian Council of Medical Research, all four dengue virus serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4) are co-circulating across multiple regions in India, with 1 in 14 patients being infected with multiple dengue serotypes concurrently.
Also Read | Noida Sector 108 RWA seeks park fogging amid dengue concerns
With dengue cases occurring year-round across India, dengue prevention and management is an urgent public-health priority.
Qdenga is a live-attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccine, built on a DENV-2 backbone with structural proteins from DENV-1, DENV-3, and DENV-4, enabling broad immune coverage across all four dengue serotypes.

headline: NEW DELHI: Seeking to make rules to act against stubble burning cases more stringent, the Centre has proposed to mark land revenue records of erring farmers with a âred entryâ for a period of 15 months that may potentially be much more consequential ...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Seeking to make rules to act against stubble burning cases more stringent, the Centre has proposed to mark land revenue records of erring farmers with a âred entryâ for a period of 15 months that may potentially be much more consequential than just an existing fine.The rules, once finalised, will be applicable in Delhi, Punjab, Haryana and National Capital Region (NCR) of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. Stubble burning episodes in these areas lead to a substantial increase in the level of air pollution in Delhi-NCR every winter.Though the draft rules to this effect, notified by the Union environment ministry, have not spelt out the consequences of the âred entryâ mark in the land revenue record, officials hinted that they may potentially disallow farmers to sell their lands and stop them from availing benefits of govt schemes. They may even include restrictions on getting registered for selling their produce at minimum support price (MSP) at designated âmandisâ for a certain period.The proposed rules, which will be finalised after analysing stakeholdersâ comments and suggestions, have a provision to extend the âred entryâ tag for a further period of 15 months if any subsequent incident of stubble burning is found on that land or the erring farmers fail to pay environmental compensation (fine) within the first tag period.
The existing rules, framed in April 2023 and amended to increase quantum of fine in Nov 2024, have the provision for âred entryâ till the penalty by the erring farmer is made, but the draft of the new rules proposes land record-based compliance mechanism by introducing the continuation of the tag for 15 months and its further extension for the next 15 months in case of repeat incidents of stubble burning.Stakeholders are expected to send their comments and suggestions to the ministry within 60 days. The draft was published on Wednesday.The proposed new rules retain the existing quantum of penalty provisions whereby the farmers having an area of land of less than two acres will have to pay an environmental compensation (fine) of Rs 5,000 per incident; those having an area of land of two acres or more but less than five acres need to pay Rs 10,000 per incident; and the farmer having an area of land of more than five acres will have to pay Rs 30,000 per incident as a penalty.
The fine collected under the rule will be deposited in the account of the respective State Pollution Control Board or Pollution Control Committee.The draft proposes that the collected amount will be utilised for various activities including subsidising residue management technologies such as in-situ crop residue management equipment and machinery; incentivising crop diversification programmes; and supporting development and operation of biomass utilisation and storage infrastructure among others in Delhi-NCR and adjoining areas.
