headline: NEW DELHI: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Friday announced that Tulu, spoken in the state's Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts, would be recognised as an additional administrative language in the region, fulfilling a long-standing demand...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Friday announced that Tulu, spoken in the state's Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts, would be recognised as an additional administrative language in the region, fulfilling a long-standing demand."Today, we have decided to make Tulu applicable to Udupi and Dakshina Kannada districts and declare it the stateâs second additional administrative language," Shivakumar told reporters after a marathon cabinet meeting in Mangaluru.According to a cabinet note shared by the chief ministerâs office, Tulu would be Karnatakaâs "second additional administrative language" in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi.The 2011 national census recorded more than 18 lakh native Tulu speakers in Karnataka, whose population was recorded at over six crore at the time. Kannada is the state's most-widely spoken and its primary official language.
This was also the first time a cabinet meeting was held in Mangaluru and not in Bengaluru.
Eye on BJP's coastal bastion
The political significance of Shivakumar taking his cabinet to Mangaluru becomes clearer against the BJP's electoral dominance in the region.Coastal Karnataka, particularly Dakshina Kannada and Udupi, has long been one of the BJP's strongest pockets in the state.
In the 2023 Karnataka assembly election, BJP won 11 of the 13 seats across the two districts, taking all five seats in Udupi and six of the eight in Dakshina Kannada. The Congress won only two constituencies.This was despite Congress sweeping to power across Karnataka with 135 seats, against 66 for the BJP.The BJP's hold remained intact in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. It won both parliamentary seats covering the region, with Brijesh Chowta defeating Congress's Padmaraj R by over 64,000 votes in Dakshina Kannada. Kota Srinivas Poojary won Udupi-Chikkamagaluru by more than 2.5 lakh votes.The BJP responded to the Tulu announcement by alleging that Shivakumar was "peddling soft Hindutva to make a dent in the BJPâs vote bank.""Shivakumar has never made any secret of his firm belief in Hinduism and frequently visits temples, performs rituals publicly and quotes scriptures. He is now peddling soft Hindutva. This was also evident from his rendition of 'Namaste Sada Vatsale' inside the Karnataka assembly," a BJP leader told PTI, referring to an August 2025 incident in which Shivakumar sang a few lines of the RSS anthem.The RSS is the BJP's ideological mentor.But there is a political twist to the Tulu issue itself. The BJP had previously taken up the demand while in power in Karnataka.In January 2023, the then BJP government led by Basavaraj Bommai constituted a committee to examine granting Tulu the status of a second official language in the state, months before the assembly election.
More than just Tulu
Significantly, Shivakumarâs announcements went beyond granting Tulu the status of a second administrative language.The Cabinet meeting in Mangaluru marked the Shivakumar governmentâs first meeting outside Bengaluru, the state capital. Shivakumar claimed the move was intended to recognise the regionâs contribution and address its development needs.
The chief minister added that a draft notification would soon be issued to invite public feedback on renaming the Dakshina Kannada district to Mangaluru district.He also announced a host of policies for the coastal Karnataka region, introducing a dedicated tourism policy for the coastal areas to treats tourism projects as infrastructure initiatives while offering investors special incentives and extended loan repayment windows.Additionally, the government approved the Karnataka Marine Biotechnology Policy, 2026-31, which paves the way for upgrading the existing fisheries college into the Fisheries, Marine and Blue Economy University and expanding its student intake from 60 to 200 seats.Beyond these policies, the administration unveiled new urban development planning, fisheries sector incentives, and major financial allocations totaling around Rs 32,611 croreâsplit evenly between rural development and regional growth for Mangaluru, Udupi, and the coastal region.The announcements further included plans to hold decentralised Cabinet meetings across 10 to 12 locations in the state over the next 15 months and the sanctioning of a new medical college worth approximately Rs 450 crore for the region.
Karan Manral is a journalist at the Times of India. He covers politics, social issues, and international affairs, exploring stories that affect peopleâs everyday lives. He also writes explainers to make these stories easier for readers to follow.

headline: Chennai: DMK leader and Lok Sabha MP Kanimozhi Karunanidhi met former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee at her Kalighat residence in Kolkata Thursday, adding fresh momentum to speculation about a possible regional political formation outside...
full_text:
Chennai: DMK leader and Lok Sabha MP Kanimozhi Karunanidhi met former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee at her Kalighat residence in Kolkata Thursday, adding fresh momentum to speculation about a possible regional political formation outside the Congress-led INDIA bloc ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.
The meeting follows Kanimozhi’s recent meetings with other regional leaders including Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray at his Matoshree residence in Mumbai last week, where talks reportedly covered the defeated delimitation Bill, the future of the INDIA bloc, and the role of regional parties. She then held separate discussions in Delhi with NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar and his daughter, Lok Sabha MP Supriya Sule.
While the DMK has called the meetings a means to just strengthen the role of regional parties and to discuss their stance on national issues, the possibility of a third front after Congress left the Secular Progressive Alliance (SPA) is being discussed.
Kanimozhi’s meeting with Mamata was a closed-door meeting lasting over an hour with sources stating that her interaction was only a courtesy call. However, the sequence of meetings has revived discussion of a Congress-less opposition arrangement.
With DMK-Congress relations becoming further strained following this year’s Tamil Nadu assembly elections, the Dravidian party had also skipped the INDIA bloc meeting, adding to questions about its future.
While there were similar differences between the TMC and Congress in West Bengal as well—where they had decided to contest the 6 October bypolls to Nandigram and Rejinagar seats separately—Mamata Friday lent her support to the Congress nominee for Nandigram, adding that Rahul Gandhi called her and they were together in their fight against the BJP.
DMK spokesperson Saravanan Annadurai told ThePrint that the Kanimozhi-Mamata meeting was to ensure that regional parties were on the same page on national issues faced in Tamil Nadu. DMK sources said regional leaders have been focusing on greater coordination among state-based regional parties, especially on issues like delimitation that affect southern states, and the space for regional forces in national politics.
Political observers see Kanimozhi’s back-to-back meetings as an early attempt by the DMK, under chief and former CM M.K. Stalin, to test the waters for a third front and a broader platform of regional parties that could take on the BJP-led NDA while keeping Congress outside the equation.
Political analyst and academic Ramu Manivannan said the third front is one of the prospects that has emerged with the lack of trust between Congress and other regional parties.
“Even in Congress ruled states, the differences have emerged and if seat sharing talks do not go well in UP, Akhilesh Yadav can extend support and even AAP in Delhi might join the third front. It is a better prospect for them all to be able to position themselves nationally. For DMK, Congress walking away from the SPA and then not attending the INDIA alliance meeting itself paved the way for establishing a third front. They might not want to be too late in discussing this,” he told ThePrint.
The idea of a non-Congress, non-BJP “third front” is not new. It has been floated before as well, leading analysts to see the possibility of a third front as a fruitful prospect for all regional parties.
Political commentator Sri Kumar Kannan said that in some way or the other, Congress and the third front parties are making some moves and counter moves against each other.
“While Congress wants to position the next elections as BJP vs Congress, their attitude with regional parties has not strengthened their lies. The third front would be set up by bringing together minority parties because they do play a major role in state politics. The regional parties want to revive their power nationally and come united together. They want to break the bipolar system of politics of BJP and Congress at the centre,” he told ThePrint.
NCP(SP) sources described the meetings as preliminary, with the party remaining non-committal. No formal announcement of a new front has been made, and both the DMK and TMC have avoided characterising the Kolkata meeting as political alliance-building. For now, the developments remain at the level of speculation, though they underscore growing uncertainty over the cohesion of the INDIA bloc three years before the next general elections.
(Edited by Archishman Ganguly)

headline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday (September 18, 2026) received a telephone call from UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, and the two leaders exchanged views on developments in West Asia and ways to deepen the strategic partnership...
full_text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday (September 18, 2026) received a telephone call from UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, and the two leaders exchanged views on developments in West Asia and ways to deepen the strategic partnership between the two countries.
“The Prime Minister and the UAE president reaffirmed their commitment to continued cooperation and coordination in efforts to promote regional peace, security and stability,” a statement issued by the Prime Minister's Office said.
The two leaders also discussed new measures to further deepen the India-UAE Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, including in the areas of energy, defence, technology, investment and health.
"Grateful to my brother, the President of UAE, HH Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, for his call and birthday wishes. We discussed measures to further deepen our bilateral Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and exchanged views on efforts to promote regional peace, security and stability," Mr. Modi said in a post on X.
"Prime Minister Narendra Modi received a telephone call from His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of the United Arab Emirates. The UAE President conveyed warm greetings on the Prime Minister's birthday," the statement said.
The prime minister turned 76 on Thursday (September 17).
The two leaders exchanged views on developments in West Asia, and they reaffirmed their commitment to continued cooperation and coordination in efforts to promote regional peace, security and stability, the statement said.
The UAE President also congratulated the Prime Minister on India's successful BRICS Presidency.
Mr. Modi appreciated the participation of UAE Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled in the BRICS Summit and the UAE's cooperation and partnership in achieving substantive outcomes under India's presidency.

headline: The ruling Bhartiya Janata Party’s National President Nitin Nabin on Friday (September 18, 2026) donated three months of his salary as the Rajya Sabha MP to the Bihar Chief Minister’s Relief Fund toward victims of the recent floods in the State.
full_text:
The ruling Bhartiya Janata Party’s National President Nitin Nabin on Friday (September 18, 2026) donated three months of his salary as the Rajya Sabha MP to the Bihar Chief Minister’s Relief Fund toward victims of the recent floods in the State.
About 50 lakh people were affected in the floods across 15 districts of Bihar this year because of “heavy rain and flash flood in rivers originating from neighbouring country Nepal”.
Expressing deep concern over the severe flood situation, Mr. Nabin, who has been a five–time BJP MLA from Bankipur constituency in Patna district, donated his three months’ salary of ₹6.35 lakh in his capacity as a Rajya Sabha member even though “all possible assistance is being provided to the affected families through financial aid, relief camps and assessment of crop damage”.
“The entire government stands firmly with the people during this crisis”, he asserted. Mr. Nabin also said that he “stands fully committed to all flood-affected families in Bihar”.
The State government has already distributed ₹550 crore in direct financial assistance by transferring ₹7,000 to each flood affected family, Mr. Nabin said, adding that the process of assessing crop damage and providing necessary assistance to farmers are being carried out.
Union Agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan had recently visited flood- affected districts of the State along with Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary and other top State officials. “Flood in Bihar this time has made extensive damage to life, property, crop production and even to cattle and their livestock and I would talk to the central government for adequate relief to the affected population”, Mr. Chouhan told media persons while assessing the flood damage.
The State government had set up over 1,000 community kitchens, several relief camps and multiple teams of National and State Disaster Response Forces for the relief and rescue operations in the flood-affected districts. Now, much to the relief of affected people, the flood water in major rivers like Ganga, Gandak and Kosi has been receding at several places, including Patna district.
Earlier, the Bihar CM Choudhary had conducted several aerial surveys of the flood-affected areas to monitor the speedy relief and rescue operations.

headline: NEW DELHI: India's first dengue vaccine is expected to be available in the private market in the first half of 2027. Takeda Pharma and Dr Reddy's Laboratories have entered into an agreement under which the latter will promote and distribute QDENGA, t...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: India's first dengue vaccine is expected to be available in the private market in the first half of 2027. Takeda Pharma and Dr Reddy's Laboratories have entered into an agreement under which the latter will promote and distribute QDENGA, the Japanese firm's dengue vaccine, across India's private market for paediatric and adult vaccination.
The collaboration follows QDENGA's marketing authorisation by India's Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation in July for individuals aged 4 to 60 years. "While inclusion in India's public immunisation programme remains a key ambition, private-market availability will provide a pathway for eligible individuals to access the vaccine,'' a statement said. Details of the vaccine's price were not available.

headline: NEW DELHI: The Congress on Saturday said the only way to counter a âbullyâ was to âresist him forcefullyâ, after US president Donald Trump signed into law a legislation expanding sanctions on Russia and Iran and giving Washington new tariff powers ta...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: The Congress on Saturday said the only way to counter a âbullyâ was to âresist him forcefullyâ, after US president Donald Trump signed into law a legislation expanding sanctions on Russia and Iran and giving Washington new tariff powers targeting major buyers of Russian energy.AICC general secretary Jairam Ramesh made the remarks in a post on X after Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 on Friday. The White House said the law authorises and expands sanctions, tariffs and prohibitions on Russia and extends existing sanctions on Iran.âThe only way to counter a bully is to resist him forcefully,â Ramesh said.The legislation gives the US president authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from countries that meet specified criteria linked to purchases of Russian crude oil or natural gas and sanctions evasion. It also targets Russian officials, financial institutions, defence networks and the countryâs so-called âshadow fleetâ.
The measure does not automatically impose a 100 per cent tariff on any specific country, with the law giving Trump discretion over its implementation.
Earlier on Wednesday, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the threat of up to 100 per cent US tariffs on Indian goods showed the governmentâs foreign and trade policies had âmiserably failedâ.
He said, âThe threat of up to 100 per cent US tariffs on Indian goods shows how the Modi govt's foreign and trade policies have miserably failed.â Kharge also claimed the government had agreed to a trade framework expanding US access to Indian agriculture, alleging it âmortgag[ed] the interests of our farmersâ.The legislation comes as India continues to face questions over its purchases of Russian energy. The ministry of external affairs said New Delhiâs energy sourcing decisions are guided by national interest.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal earlier said meeting the requirements of Indiaâs 1.4 billion people remained an âimperativeâ.âWhen it comes to energy sourcing, it is based on our national interest. We have said that meeting the energy requirements of our 1.4 billion people is an imperative that we have to follow. And we continue to buy energy from diversified sources,â Jaiswal said.
On the new US law, Jaiswal said India had already conveyed its concerns to senior levels of the US administration.âAs we have stated, at senior levels of the US administration, we have conveyed the implications that this legislation could have on India's energy security, for international energy markets, and for the overall bilateral relationship. I don't have anything further to add at this point,â he said.The White House said Trump signed the legislation on September 18. The law extends the Iran Sanctions Act for five years and expands measures against Russiaâs energy and financial sectors.

headline: NEW DELHI: BJP chief Nitin Nabin Friday donated three months of his salary as Rajya Sabha MP to help efforts to aid flood victims in his home state Bihar, and asserted central and state govts are making every effort to deal with the crisis.
full_text:
NEW DELHI: BJP chief Nitin Nabin Friday donated three months of his salary as Rajya Sabha MP to help efforts to aid flood victims in his home state Bihar, and asserted central and state govts are making every effort to deal with the crisis.
Expressing concern over the flood situation, he said Bihar govt is taking swift action and making adequate arrangements for relief camps, community kitchens, medical facilities and fodder for livestock in the affected areas.
Nabin said Centre and state stand fully committed to supporting the flood-affected families. Every possible assistance, including financial aid, relief camps, and crop damage assessment, is being extended to them, he said. "Fulfilling his responsibility during this time of crisis, he donated Rs 6.35 lakh, three months of his salary as an RS MP, to CM's Relief Fund," a BJP statement said.

headline: 3.7 million SIR appeals pending in Bengal; ECI proposes 42 election tribunals
full_text:
3.7 million SIR appeals pending in Bengal; ECI proposes 42 election tribunals
Election Commission stated in an affidavit filed before the Supreme Court that out of 3.8 million appeals filed, 3.7 million are currently pending.
The Election Commission of India (ECI) told the Supreme Court that it requires 42 election tribunals in total in West Bengal for expeditious disposal of over 3.7 million appeals filed concerning voters deleted from the electoral roll during the special intensive revision (SIR).
With 19 tribunals currently dealing with the appeals, the poll panel stated in an affidavit filed this week before the Supreme Court that out of 3.8 million appeals filed, 3.7 million are currently pending. Over 2.2 million of these are filed by excluded voters, and about 1.6 million are cross-appeals challenging the inclusion of names in the electoral rolls following SIR.
To deal with this caseload, the ECI said that speedy disposal of these appeals requires more than the present strength of tribunals.
Also Read | The SIR exercise and the points of concern
It said, “With a view to further streamline and expedite the disposal of the pending appeals, it is proposed that the number of appellate tribunals in the state of West Bengal may be considered for increase to correspond with the number of Parliamentary constituencies in the state, so as to facilitate expeditious disposal of the pending appeals.”
West Bengal has 42 Parliamentary constituencies and the commission has suggested having as many tribunals as Lok Sabha seats in the state.
The affidavit of the poll panel came in response to an application moved by Trinamool Congress leader and Rajya Sabha MP Derek O’Brien who is one of the petitioners in the top court challenging the SIR exercise in West Bengal. The information provided by the ECI stated that of the 3.8 million appeals filed before the tribunals, the appeals against exclusion are over 57%. The affidavit further pointed out the tribunals also face 1.61 million appeals challenging inclusion of voters in the list.

headline: Japan air chief General Takehiro Morita flies Tejas, calls it 'a truly invaluable experience' | Watch
full_text:
Japan air chief General Takehiro Morita flies Tejas, calls it 'a truly invaluable experience' | Watch
The two air chiefs undertook the sortie as part of the ongoing exercise, which is being conducted at Air Force Station Jodhpur.
Japan Air Self-Defense Force (JASDF) Chief of Staff General Takehiro Morita on Sunday flew a Tejas aircraft during the ongoing India-Japan bilateral air exercise Veer Guardian in Rajasthan's Jodhpur, describing the sortie as “a truly invaluable experience”.
Morita flew the Tejas alongside an Indian Air Force pilot, while IAF Chief Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh flew a separate Tejas fighter jet during the formation sortie at Air Force Station Jodhpur.
Also Read | Tejas fighter jet suffers major damage after overshooting runway, brake failure suspected: Report
Air chiefs fly Tejas in formation
In the video, Air Chief Marshal Singh and General Morita can be seen taking off in the two Tejas jets as part of the formation sortie. The formation sortie lasted around 20-25 minutes.
The formation flew over the airfield before carrying out a peel-off manoeuvre for landing, an official said.
Morita praises Tejas Fighter
“As an aircraft born from indigenous defence capabilities, Tejas stands as a symbol of India's technological innovation and embodies the Make in India initiative,” Morita said.
Morita said flying the Tejas gave him a first-hand appreciation of the efforts of the many people, both in the military and industry, who had contributed to the aircraft's development.
He also said the experience allowed him to appreciate the training environment available to the Indian Air Force and understand the value of Exercise Veer Guardian for the JASDF.
Morita said he would remember the sortie not only as an invaluable experience but also as a symbol of the trust, confidence and friendship built between the two air forces over the years.
“Veer Guardian is the second bilateral fighter exercise between our services. More importantly, it marks the first-ever deployment of Kōkū Jieitai fighters to India,” he said.
The JASDF chief said India and Japan had steadily expanded their defence cooperation and military exercises over the years. He recalled Shinyuu Maitri, the first bilateral exercise between the two air forces, which was held in India in 2018.
Morita said the deployment of Japanese fighters to India had been a long-standing aspiration, particularly after the historic first visit of Indian Air Force fighters to Japan three years ago.
‘Symbol of trust, confidence and friendship’
He said advanced training exercises help deepen mutual understanding, strengthen trust and enhance practical cooperation between the two air forces.
“It was with this belief in mind that we finally made it a reality together, bringing our defence cooperation to a new stage,” Morita said.
The two air chiefs later addressed the media, highlighting the role of such exercises in building interoperability and strengthening the defence partnership between India and Japan. India's Tejas and Japan's F-2A fighter aircraft, parked on the runway, formed the backdrop.
The IAF is participating with a mix of frontline combat aircraft, including indigenous Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas, Su-30 MKI and Rafale, while the JASDF is taking part with its F-2A fighter aircraft.
This is the first time JASDF fighter aircraft are operating from Indian soil as part of a bilateral exercise.

headline: NEW DELHI: Is the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code emerging as a new point of contention between the Bharatiya Janata Party and one of its oldest allies, Janata Dal (United)?The question has come into focus after Union home minister Amit Shah...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Is the implementation of the Uniform Civil Code emerging as a new point of contention between the Bharatiya Janata Party and one of its oldest allies, Janata Dal (United)?The question has come into focus after Union home minister Amit Shah's assertion that UCC would be implemented in all 21 NDA-ruled states before the next Lok Sabha elections prompted differing reactions within the JD(U).The issue surfaced after Shah, during his visit to Mumbai, put a timeline on BJP's plan to implement one of its longstanding ideological objectives before the 2029 Lok Sabha polls.
"Triple talaq has been abolished, giving Muslim women equal rights. We have introduced the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in several states and I am confident that in the 21 BJP-NDA ruled states, we will introduce the UCC before 2029," Shah said.
Shah's message, however, drew a different response from some JD(U) leaders in Bihar.JD(U) general secretary and former minister Shyam Rajak said his party did not favour implementing UCC in the state."Our stand on the issue was made clear by our leader way back. He had said that although our party was supporting the UCC Bill in the Parliament, it was not in favour of implementing the same in Bihar," Rajak said."The chief minister may be of the BJP but the government is being run with the help of allies...
our stand is clear, the question of implementing UCC in Bihar does not arise," he added.
However, Bihar deputy chief minister Vijay Kumar Chaudhary, who is considered to be a close ally of former chief minister Nitish Kumar, adopted a more cautious stance and said the party would first study the legislation and would not oppose it "for no reason" if its provisions were found to be unexceptionable."As of now, we are not aware of the details of the legislation on UCC. Let it be placed before us. If we find there is nothing objectionable, why shall we oppose it without any reason? And if there are points of concern, these will be conveyed to the Union home minister," Chaudhary said.JD(U) working president Sanjay Jha has also indicated that party leaders would discuss the issue with Shah.
For now, therefore, JD(U)'s stand is not entirely clear. While some leaders have spoken against implementing UCC in Bihar, remarks by senior leaders such as Chaudhary and Jha have left scope for the party to examine the proposed provisions before taking a final position. The party has historically favoured wider consultations and consensus on the issue.
What is UCC
India already has uniform criminal laws and common civil laws covering matters such as taxation, contracts and negotiable instruments. However, when it comes to personal laws such as marriage, divorce and inheritance of property, different religious communities follow laws based on their respective traditions and practices.Article 44 under the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Constitution says that the State shall endeavour to secure a UCC for citizens throughout India."The State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India," the Constitution says.A UCC broadly seeks to provide a common legal framework for citizens in matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance and succession.
BJP's old promise
The Uniform Civil Code has been a longstanding part of the BJP's political agenda and has featured repeatedly in the party's election manifestos over the years.The party has repeatedly included the issue in its election manifestos, arguing that a common civil code would ensure equality before law and strengthen women's rights in matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance and adoption.Matters such as marriage, divorce, adoption, wills, intestacy and succession fall in the Concurrent List, allowing both the Centre and state governments to make laws on them.
In 2022, then Union law minister Kiren Rijiju also informed the Rajya Sabha that states were empowered to legislate on these subjects."Article 44 of the Constitution provides that the State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India," Rijiju had said in a written reply."Personal laws such as intestacy and succession; wills; joint family and partition; marriage and divorce, relate to Entry 5 of List-III-Concurrent List of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, and hence, the States are also empowered to legislate upon them," he had added.This has allowed BJP-ruled states to take the state route on UCC.Uttarakhand became the first state in independent India to implement a state-specific Uniform Civil Code on January 27, 2025.Since then, UCC Bills have also been passed by the assemblies of BJP-ruled Gujarat, Assam and Madhya Pradesh. As of mid-September, the Bills in these three states were awaiting the President's assent.Other NDA-ruled states are at different stages of considering or preparing their own legislation.Shah's latest remarks have now put a 2029 timeline on that process for all NDA-ruled states.
Why UCC needs careful balancing for JD(U)
For JD(U), the issue comes with both political and ideological considerations.Nitish Kumar has long maintained that a reform such as UCC should not be pushed without broad consultation and consensus, particularly given India's social and religious diversity.There is also an electoral dimension.Within the NDA in Bihar, JD(U) has traditionally sought support across a social coalition that includes Extremely Backward Classes, women and sections of minorities. While its support among Muslims has weakened over the years, the party has continued to reach out to the community.Muslims constitute around 17.7% of Bihar's population, according to the state's caste survey. Recent electoral data cited by The Indian Express suggests that only a relatively small section of Muslim voters backed the NDA in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, underlining the challenge for JD(U) in retaining support among the community while remaining part of the BJP-led alliance.In the 2025 assembly election, JD(U) fielded four Muslim candidates, but only Mohammad Zama Khan won from the Chainpur seat.The political setting has also changed since that election.The NDA won 202 of Bihar's 243 assembly seats, with the BJP emerging as the single-largest party with 89 seats and JD(U) winning 85.Nitish Kumar is also no longer chief minister, with BJP's Samrat Choudhary now heading the NDA government. JD(U), however, remains one of its two principal constituents.This makes the UCC question an important one for the alliance: BJP has put a timeline on a longstanding policy commitment, while JD(U) has traditionally stressed consultation before any such move.
When JD(U) differed with BJP
Although an ally of BJP, JD(U) has not always agreed with it on politically sensitive issues.On UCC itself, Nitish Kumar has long cautioned against hurried implementation.In January 2017, as Bihar chief minister, he returned the Law Commission's questionnaire on UCC, arguing that there was insufficient clarity about what the proposed code would contain and calling for wider consultations with affected groups.Nitish argued that diverse customs and practices had existed for centuries and that any effort towards a common code should be based on consensus rather than simply imposed.JD(U) has also differed from the BJP on issues such as the Triple Talaq Bill and the abrogation of Article 370.In 2019, JD(U) opposed the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Bill, commonly known as the Triple Talaq Bill. The party objected particularly to the provision making instant triple talaq a criminal offence, arguing that the legislation could create "a lack of trust" in society. Its MPs walked out of the Lok Sabha debate and later abstained during the Rajya Sabha proceedings.In August 2019, the party also opposed the Modi government's decision to abrogate the special status of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370 and reorganise the former state into two Union Territories. JD(U) MPs staged a walkout when the measures were introduced in Parliament.However, it struck a reconciliatory note later and said that once the law had come into force, it should be abided by all.These differences did not, by themselves, prevent the BJP and JD(U) from working together. The two allies have in the past maintained separate positions on some issues while continuing their political partnership.UCC could similarly depend on what form a proposed law for Bihar eventually takes and whether the allies are able to arrive at a common position.
Mahagathbandhan's offer to Nitish
Amid the debate over UCC, Congress and Rashtriya Janata Dal have taken the opportunity to invite Nitish Kumar to join the opposition alliance.RJD MLA Bhai Virendra asked Nitish to break ties with the BJP and form a new government with its support, saying the parties shared a socialist political tradition.The RJD MLA alleged that Nitish was surrounded by people who were "hellbent on ruining his political career" and said, "We urge Nitish Kumar ji to walk out of the NDA and form a govt with our support."Former Bihar Congress president and Rajya Sabha member Akhilesh Prasad Singh also extended an invitation to Nitish to join the Mahagathbandhan, saying Nitish had long been associated with socialist politics.
"It is the agenda of the BJP and the RSS. Several allies of the NDA may not agree with it, and Nitish certainly should not agree with it. He has always been associated with social concerns and socialism, so I do not think he can ever agree with this," Singh said."Why would Congress have any objection to that? If he leaves, Congress will always welcome him," he added.For now, however, the differing remarks on UCC do not necessarily point to a larger crisis within the Bihar NDA.
JD(U)'s final position remains open. Some of its leaders have opposed implementation in Bihar, while others have said the party should first see the proposed legislation and discuss its concerns with the BJP leadership.Shah, meanwhile, has set a clear target of introducing UCC in all NDA-ruled states before 2029.It remains to be seen whether Bihar eventually follows that roadmap and, if it does, what shape the proposed law takes after consultations between the two allies.

headline: All about ‘Yatra of Seva’: 20 teams to cover 35,500 km between Gujarat's Vadnagar to Varanasi
full_text:
All about ‘Yatra of Seva’: 20 teams to cover 35,500 km between Gujarat's Vadnagar to Varanasi
The initiative also includes distributing kits to widows, honouring ASHA workers and bringing communities together for various welfare activities.
A total of 35,500 kilometres will be covered as 20 teams travel from Vadnagar in Gujarat to Varanasi and back to Vadnagar from September 17 to October 7 as part of a first-of-its-kind motorcycle Yatra centred on 'Seva' (service).
The Yatra will pass through towns, districts, talukas and villages, taking its spirit to communities at the grassroots level.
The ‘Seva Yatris’ will stop to meet people and take part in activities based on local needs. These will include cleanliness drives at ponds, temples, schools, parks, hospitals and other public areas, along with beneficiary interactions, youth dialogues, Gram Sabha samvad, Gau Seva and tree plantation under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’.
At PM SHRI Schools, the Yatris are cleaning school campuses, spending time with students and handing out books and stationery. They are also visiting hospitals, orphanages and old-age homes to support people in need.
The initiative also includes distributing kits to widows, honouring ASHA workers and bringing communities together for various welfare activities.
The Yatra also places focus on 'sampark' (connect) and dialogue. Interactions with young people, village meetings, discussions with local leaders, women and beneficiaries of government welfare schemes are helping the teams engage directly with communities, understand their aspirations and spread awareness at the grassroots level.
Organ donation pledges promote the spirit of giving, while tributes to martyrs and freedom fighters help communities connect with the nation's history and its heroes.
The initiative brings together Seva, Sampark, youth participation, social welfare, cultural connect and community mobilisation, taking these efforts from one grassroots location to another.

headline: Congress calls SIR ‘Shah Instigated Removal’, flags ‘unusually high’ voter deletions
full_text:
Congress calls SIR ‘Shah Instigated Removal’, flags ‘unusually high’ voter deletions
The party alleged that the exercise amounted to a massive "Shah Instigated Removal" of voters and an “assault on the Constitution”.
The Congress on Sunday raised concerns over alleged large-scale voter deletions during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls being conducted by the Election Commission, pointing to the deletion and verification of millions of names across states.
Taking a swipe at Union home minister Amit Shah, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh described the exercise as a massive “Shah Instigated Removal” of voters and alleged that it amounted to an “assault on the Constitution”. The party also claimed that voters from economically and socially disadvantaged sections had been disproportionately affected by the deletions.
Also Read | The SIR exercise and the points of concern
Congress on 7.8 crore voter names
Deep Dive
Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh said the Election Commission of India (ECI) began Phase 1 of the SIR process in June 2025 in Bihar, followed by Phase 2 in November 2025 across nine states and three Union Territories (UTs).
Ramesh said 7.8 crore voter names were deleted during Phases 1 and 2, with the deletions accounting for 13% of the pre-SIR electoral roll.
Phase 3 began in 16 states and three UTs in mid-2026, he said.
Rames alleged that, according to data from 12 states and two UTs, 6.18 crore of the 36.06 crore voters covered in the ongoing phase have had their names deleted.
"The deletion rate works out to over 17% 2. An additional 5.43 crore voters have been issued notices demanding additional documentation to have their names retained on the electoral roll. The risk of deletion rate works to another 15%. This is an unusually high proportion that reflects structural flaws in the entire SIR process," Ramesh said.
He questioned how such a large number of voters could still be required to undergo verification after the deletions.
"Thus, a staggering 32% (or about one in three) of voters have had their names deleted or face risk of deletion. The state-wise picture on this measure is as follows: Delhi (53.73%). Chandigarh (52.58%), Jharkhand (39.57%), Uttarakhand (35.71%), Meghalaya (35.36%), Maharashtra (33.88%), Telangana (48.90%), Karnataka (27.6%), Haryana (37.5%), Odisha (23.67%), Andhra Pradesh (21.17%) and Punjab (15.23%). 4. The list of voters facing risk of deletion in Karnataka, Telangana and Jharkhand was made publicly available so voters can check if they are on it
"Delhi made this list available publicly only on September 19th 2026 and that too only in response to public pressure. Other BJP-ruled states as well as Punjab have not done so till now," he said.
Also Read | 3.7 million SIR appeals pending in Bengal; ECI proposes 42 election tribunals
Jairam Ramesh on impact on ‘disadvantaged sections’
Ramesh alleged that there was abundant evidence that voters from the most economically and socially disadvantaged sections had been disproportionately affected by the deletions.
He also claimed that in most major states, more women than men had been removed from the electoral rolls during the SIR process.
"With this SIR, the state has abdicated its responsibility and shifted the burden onto citizens to produce documents it may never have provided them," he said.
A test that the overwhelming majority of citizens cannot pass is just a "machine for exclusion", Ramesh said.
"SIR is actually a massive Shah Instigated Removal of voters. It is an assault on our Constitution," the Congress general secretary said, in an apparent reference to Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
Tagging his statement on X, Ramesh said, “SIR is actually a Shah Instigated Removal of voters on a massive scale. Here is a statement on this brazen assault on our Constitution itself.”
Also Read | SC to hear on Sep 22 plea against Delhi SIR exercise
Delhi SIR notices
In Delhi, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) chief Arvind Kejriwal were among more than 3.16 million voters served notices over “discrepancies” following the SIR of electoral rolls, according to officials involved in the exercise.
The Delhi chief electoral officer's (CEO) office published the list of electors served notices late on Friday, nearly three weeks after the draft electoral roll was released on August 31. Voters flagged in the exercise must now submit their responses and supporting documents to the election authorities to have their names included in the final roll.
The electors have been placed in two categories: “no mapping” — voters who could not be linked to the electoral roll from the previous revision in 2002 — and “logical discrepancies” — voters whose entries contained inconsistencies with the previous roll.
Of the 9,753,577 electors whose names were included in Delhi's draft electoral roll after the SIR, 1,379,785 were placed in the “no mapping” category, while 1,933,134 were flagged for “logical discrepancies”.

headline: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (September 20, 2026) said the Kurmi community would be kept outside the ambit of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) and announced that cases registered against members of the community during protests u...
full_text:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (September 20, 2026) said the Kurmi community would be kept outside the ambit of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) and announced that cases registered against members of the community during protests under the previous Trinamool Congress government would be withdrawn.
The Kurmis are a prominent community in the State’s Jangalmahal region. They are currently categorised as Other Backward Class and have been demanding the status of Scheduled Tribe (ST).
Members of the Kurmi community had organised road and railway blockades across parts of West Bengal during the previous Trinamool Congress government’s tenure, demanding ST status and inclusion of the Kurmali language in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution. Mr. Adhikari also promised to push for constitutional recognition of the Kurmali and Rajbanshi languages.
The West Bengal government has said it would submit a “Further Common Justification Report” to the Centre to support the inclusion of the Kurmi community in the ST list.
Committee on UCC
On the UCC, the State government has set up a committee led by former Supreme Court judge Ranjana Gopal Desai to work out the modalities for implementing the proposed code in the State. The government has already promised to keep ST out of the ambit of the UCC.
Addressing a Karam festival programme in Purulia, the Chief Minister said that many leaders of the Kurmi community had approached him seeking to keep the community out of the ambit of the UCC.
Mr. Adhikari accused the previous government of creating divisions within the Kurmi community and said his government would fulfil the promises made in its election manifesto.
“The previous government (in West Bengal) created divisions among the Kurmis... It never wanted them to stay united. We will, on the other hand, keep all promises made to the community in our ‘Sankalp Patra’ before this year’s Assembly elections,” he said.
The Chief Minister said people of the region had voted for the BJP over the past several years and assured to protect the region’s language, diversity and natural resources.
Criticising the previous administration, he alleged that it had been “selling hills” and promised that no natural resources would be auctioned under his tenure.
“It is our responsibility to protect the dignity of language, culture, tradition and rights. The previous government was even selling hills! I promised not to let anyone touch any of them. I will not let anyone touch the gifts of nature. No mountain can be auctioned,” he said. Mr. Adhikari also announced an allocation of ₹50 crore for the Kurmi Development Board and said the amount would be increased if necessary.
Several members of the Kurmi community, including prominent leader Ajit Mahato and Purulia BJP MP Jyotirmoy Singh Mahato, attended the festival.

headline: A political row erupted in Madhya Pradesh on Sunday (September 20, 2026), as BJP leaders slammed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for featuring the mimicry of Prime Minister Narendra Modi by standup comedian Pulkit Mani at a student interaction event in ...
full_text:
A political row erupted in Madhya Pradesh on Sunday (September 20, 2026), as BJP leaders slammed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for featuring the mimicry of Prime Minister Narendra Modi by standup comedian Pulkit Mani at a student interaction event in Indore.
Mr. Gandhi, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, could be seen laughing during the performance by Mr. Mani at his ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event. In the act, Mr. Mani appeared to be mimicking Mr. Modi’s interactions with foreign leaders and others. While Mr. Mani did not name the Prime Minister in his act, Mr. Gandhi said, “How are you, Modi ji?”, while hugging him.
Another part of the act, where Mr. Mani appeared to be mocking the Prime Minister for asking for a chair for an elderly woman at a rally, took the most heat. Similar performances by the comedian have previously gone viral on social media.
‘Insulting honour of mothers’
Soon after the event, Madhya Pradesh CM Mohan Yadav shared a clip of the act and said that Mr. Gandhi’s attitude was “extremely shameful”.
“This irresponsible attitude of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi is extremely shameful, condemnable, and unbecoming. By insulting the honour of our country’s culture and mothers, he has encouraged leading the youth’s future in the wrong direction,” Mr. Yadav wrote on X, late on September 19.
“Our visionary Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji, who had set an exemplary example by placing the honour of mothers above all, is being mocked in this manner, which is an insult to mothers across the country,” he said, seeking an apology from the Congress.
‘Cheap political theatre’
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal said the act amounted to “cheap political theatre”.
“Uncultured angry uncle! The irony writes itself. The need to come on stage every now and then just to drag Prime Minister Modi ji’s name into cheap political theatre never fails to amaze me. Look in the mirror, Mr. Rahul Gandhi,” Mr. Goyal said on X.
Chhattisgarh CM Vishnu Deo Sai invoked the Delhi University Student Union (DUSU) election results to take a dig at Mr. Gandhi’s event, claiming that the ABVP’s victory showed that the youth of the country was with the BJP.
PM’s previous mockery unearthed
While the Congress is yet to officially respond to the BJP’s allegations, sources say that many within the party did not “approve of it”.
However, various Congress supporters on social media shared an old clip of Mr. Modi’s interaction with students from 2019, in which he was apparently seen mocking Mr. Gandhi as a dyslexic person.
While interacting by video conference with a group of students gathered at IIT-Kharagpur, Mr. Modi had interrupted a student who was explaining how her project could help dyslexic kids and laughingly asked if it could also help “40 to 50-year-old child as well”.
As the girl said, “Yes, it can,” Mr. Modi further added, “Then the mother of such children will get very happy.” His comments, which drew laughter from the audience, were seen as potshots at Mr. Gandhi.
At his event in Indore, Mr. Gandhi had alleged that a “system” run by a handful of powerful people like Mr. Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah and a few bureaucrats and businesspersons had captured the country, harming students and the education system. He claimed that the “system” did not want students who raised questions and preferred “andhbhakts (blind followers)” instead.
Following the controversy, Mr. Mani said in an Instagram story that an upcoming show of his, scheduled to be held in Uttar Pradesh’s Noida, has been cancelled “due to unforeseen circumstances”. Gautam Budh Nagar District Magistrate Medha Roopam, under whose jurisdiction Noida falls, was not available for a comment on Sunday evening, while some other district officials said that they were not aware of the show or any decision regarding it.

headline: US law gives Trump power to impose 100% tariffs on India, China over Russian oil
full_text:
US law gives Trump power to impose 100% tariffs on India, China over Russian oil
The legislation does not automatically trigger duties, but allows the US president to decide the rate and countries targeted among the Russian energy buyers.
US President Donald Trump on Friday signed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law, acquiring congressionally backed authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods from the five largest buyers of Russian oil — a list that by current import volumes includes China and India.
New law expands Trump’s tariff powers
The law gives Trump a tariff instrument his broader trade campaign has lacked. His sweeping duties on global trade have relied on executive powers — first under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, which the Supreme Court struck down in February, and then under Section 122 of the Trade Act, which carries a 150-day expiry. The new law faces neither constraint. Once in effect, it gives the president durable, congressionally authorised power to penalise buyers of Russian energy.
India had warned on Thursday, hours after the House passed the bill, that it was determined “to take all necessary measures to protect its trade and economic interests.” The external affairs ministry said the legislation’s implications — “for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market” — had been “very clearly articulated” to US interlocutors at high levels in recent months.
To be sure, Trump has yet to announce a new tariff rate under these powers.
On Saturday, Union minister of state for external affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh reiterated India’s position. “We have our own independent foreign policy. We will not follow any country,” he told news agency ANI, adding that the government would “take every strong step for the strength and stability of our country, our population of 140 crores.”
Also read: India says Russia sanctions bill threatening 100% tariffs can impact US ties, global energy market
China echoes India’s response
China too responded on Saturday, in similar language to India’s statement on Thursday, with the ministry of commerce saying it reserved the right “to take all necessary measures” to firmly safeguard China’s interests, “as well as the legitimate and just rights and interests of Chinese companies.”
The law does not name any country. It tasks the US Trade Representative, in consultation with the Secretary of State and Secretary of Energy, to identify the five largest importers of Russian crude oil and natural gas by total volume over the preceding 12 months, with the list reassessed every 180 days. The tariff rate, up to the 100% ceiling, is at the president’s discretion; the law does not compel him to act. It also includes an exemption for countries whose Russian natural gas imports account for less than 15% of Russia’s total gas exports and that are “taking significant steps” to reduce those imports — a provision that shields several European nations but offers no protection to India or China.
But the bill’s backers have left little doubt about where the pressure is aimed. “To China and India: You better clean up your act. Buy your oil and gas somewhere else,” Senator Richard Blumenthal said after the House passed the bill on Wednesday.
Also read: US sanctions on Russian oil, 100% tariff to make reaching Ukraine deal 'harder', warns Kremlin
Bill’s 18-month journey through Congress
Trump’s signature brings to a close an 18-month legislative saga that began in April 2025, when Senators Lindsey Graham and Richard Blumenthal introduced an earlier version proposing tariffs as high as 500% on buyers of Russian energy. Graham, a close Trump ally who spearheaded the legislation, died suddenly in July; the law now bears his name. The bill was softened — the top-line tariff brought down to 100%, its scope narrowed to the five largest purchasers — but its passage through Congress was far from assured. Members of the majority Republican party unexpectedly brought it to a House vote this week after the Rules Committee removed a procedural hurdle on Monday. On Tuesday, the House narrowly voted 214-211 to schedule the final vote after two Democratic lawmakers crossed the aisle. It passed on Wednesday 262-159. The Senate had cleared it 86-11 on August 7.
The White House’s role in securing passage remains unclear. Last month, US Ambassador Sergio Gor said Trump’s support had been muted even as legislators sought to give him expanded tariff authority. But recent reports in US media indicate the administration may have helped push the bill through by persuading opposition Democratic lawmakers to vote for it.
Also read: ‘Russian oil buyers will have to pay': US senator backs bill threatening higher tariffs on India
Trump retains power to waive tariffs
The president can waive tariffs on any country by certifying to Congress that the waiver serves the national interests of the United States. To permanently lift them, he must certify that the country has stopped purchasing Russian energy and has provided “reliable assurances” it will not resume.
India’s purchases of Russian crude have been a persistent friction point in the bilateral relationship. India scaled back Russian oil imports under US pressure through much of 2025, but the widening conflict in West Asia and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz forced New Delhi to seek alternative supplies. Washington itself granted a series of general licences temporarily allowing countries including India to resume Russian purchases to cover the shortfall.
The law’s 12-month lookback period for identifying the top five purchasers would capture that surge — meaning Washington is now empowered to penalise purchases it had itself facilitated.
Also read: US-India ties, trade talks: What to watch as the Russia sanctions bill heads to Trump's desk
Exporters warn of tariff impact
Indian exporters expressed alarm. “If the US imposes high tariffs, it will completely halt our exports to the US. No importer can afford this high level of tariffs,” said SC Ralhan, president of the Federation of Indian Export Organisations, according to PTI. He noted the actual impact could be assessed only after Washington announces the tariff rate, product coverage and implementation schedule.
The textile sector, where the US is India’s largest market by a significant margin, flagged particular vulnerability. “Any additional tariffs under this Act will be very difficult to absorb for the MSME-dominated Indian textile and apparel sector already under stress due to several factors, including the continuing turmoil in West Asia,” said CITI chairman Ashwin Chandran, according to ANI.
Ajay Srivastava of the Global Trade Research Initiative said Washington could use the tariff threat to pressure India into reducing Russian oil purchases and accepting an unequal trade agreement. “India should protect its energy security and continue buying Russian crude while it remains commercially competitive,” he said.

headline: U.S. President Donald Trump has signed into law the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, 2026, which could see tariffs of up to 100% being levied on imports from India if it continues to import oil from Russia. This Act, therefore, has ...
full_text:
The story so far:
U.S. President Donald Trump has signed into law the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, 2026, which could see tariffs of up to 100% being levied on imports from India if it continues to import oil from Russia. This Act, therefore, has significant implications for India with regard to its export ambitions and energy security. The Indian government’s concerns over the tariffs have so far gone unheeded.
Why did the U.S. introduce this law?
The initial purpose of the Act — proposed by the late Senator Lindsey O. Graham and named after him — was to cut off financing for Russia so as to choke its funding of its war with Ukraine. To this end, the Act provides for sanctions to be levied on Russia’s top leadership and its biggest energy customers.
Recently, the ‘and Iran’ part of the title was added to the Act to convey that such measures are also aimed at Iran. The text was amended to say that sanctions on Iran would be levied for another five years until 2031.
What does the Act say about tariffs?
For India, the most crucial aspect of the Act is what it says about countries that import Russian oil. Thirty days after its enactment, the Act allows the U.S. to impose a 100% tariff on goods originating in a country that meets one of two broad criteria. The first is a country that was among the five largest importers, by total volume, of crude oil or natural gas from Russia during the 12 months preceding the Act’s enactment, and that continues to import oil or gas from Russia after the 30-day period.
This is the criterion that will likely impact India. China and India are the top two importers of Russian crude oil. Russian crude oil has accounted for a rising share of India’s oil imports since February 2026, when the U.S. Supreme Court struck down Mr. Trump’s tariff regime, including the 25% punitive tariff he had imposed on India for its Russian oil imports.
According to the latest data, Russia accounted for more than 51% of India's crude oil imports in July 2026. Scaling this back drastically within 30 days, at a time when passage through the Strait of Hormuz is still constrained, will likely be impossible for India.
The second criterion for imposition of tariffs is whether a country was among the top five nations “facilitating Russian oil sanctions evasion during the 12 months preceding the date of the enactment of the Act”. India runs a much lower risk of qualifying for tariffs under this criterion, as Indian oil marketing companies have repeatedly said that all their purchases have been made without violating sanctions.
Will these be the total tariffs on imports from India?
No. The law clearly states that an import tariff imposed under this Act “shall be in addition to any other duty” levied on any good. This includes tariffs imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the United States Trade Representative to investigate and retaliate against foreign trade practices that harm American commerce, and Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, which authorises the U.S. President to restrict imports or impose tariffs if an investigation finds that foreign goods threaten national security.
These two other Acts are important because India is among the countries that already face tariffs under them. That is, the U.S. Trade Representative used Section 301 to investigate American trade partners to determine whether they had done enough to stop the import of goods made using forced labour. Based on its findings, it imposed a tariff of 10% on imports from India. In addition, Mr. Trump had widened existing tariffs under Section 232 to include steel, aluminium, copper, and related derivative products, and hiked the rate to 50%. Since this applied to all countries equally, it placed India on a level playing field with its competitors.
A potential 100% tariff on top of that will severely dent India’s competitiveness in these sectors.
Will these tariffs come into force immediately?
No. A period of 30 days has to elapse before the U.S. can determine whether countries are still importing oil and gas from Russia. It is only after this period that the U.S. can levy the tariffs under the law. Further, the text of the Act says that the U.S. Trade Representative, in consultation with the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Energy would, within 180 days after the initial imposition of tariffs, again review the countries that are the five largest importers of crude oil and natural gas from Russia based on the most recent 12-month period.
What is the potential impact on India’s economy?
The impact on India’s economy has to be looked at in terms of two eventualities. The first is if India continues to buy large quantities of Russian oil and bears the tariffs. The second is if India cuts back on Russian oil imports and manages to have the potential tariffs removed.
In the event that India continues to buy Russian oil and bears the tariffs, we can look at what happened during the period when the 50% tariffs were in force, between August 2025 and February 2026, to gauge the likely impact.
The April to August 2025 period saw merchandise exports to the U.S. grow nearly 18% compared with the same period the previous year. While some of this was due to front-loaded exports in anticipation of future tariffs, it nevertheless highlighted the strong momentum of exports from India to the U.S. However, over the longer April 2025 to February 2026 period, exports to the U.S. grew at a much slower 3.8%, showing a substantial slowdown in exports after August, when the tariffs came into effect.
Conversations with exporters at the time showed that many of them were sharing the cost of the higher tariffs with their U.S. customers in order to retain them. At the rate of 50%, this was already a body blow to most of them. These exporters will not be in a position to share a 100% tariff.
Historical data, however, show that India has chosen to comply with U.S. pressure to reduce oil imports from countries such as Venezuela, Iran, and Russia. If India again cuts down on Russian oil imports, this could have serious ramifications for the supply and price of fuel within India. At a time when the Strait of Hormuz is constrained, and oil prices are again comfortably above $100 a barrel, India will likely find it very expensive to look for newer sources of oil. For Indian citizens, this could translate into more fuel price hikes. For the government, such hikes would be politically unpalatable since there are several key State elections next year.
Is there a third way out?
The Act includes a provision for a waiver of tariffs. The U.S. President can waive the tariffs once he has submitted to Congress a certification in writing that the waiver “is in the national interests of the U.S.” and a report explaining the basis for the certification.
The other way out is if Russia signs “a peace agreement that is accepted by the free and independent Government of Ukraine” and ceases “all military hostilities against and any activities to overthrow, dismantle, and subvert the Government of Ukraine”.

headline: Surendra Koli cremated, cops probe his activities since acquittal in Nithari case
full_text:
Surendra Koli cremated, cops probe his activities since acquittal in Nithari case
Nithari case accused Surendra Koli was cremated in Haridwar after he was found hanging in a tea stall. The case has raised fresh questions over whether Koli died by suicide or was murdered weeks after his acquittal.
Surendra Koli, the main accused in the 2006 Nithari serial killings, was cremated in Haridwar on Saturday in the presence of his family members, police said. His body was handed over to the family after a post-mortem examination, and the last rites were performed at the Kharkhari cremation ground.
Police are awaiting the post-mortem report and suspect that Koli may have died by suicide after he was found hanging in his tea stall in Haridwar on Friday. At the same time, they have started an investigation into his activities since he arrived in the city and the circumstances leading to his death.
Those present at the cremation included Koli's brother Harish Koli, his 20-year-old son Shivam, and former zila panchayat member Narayan Singh Rawat. Speaking to reporters after the last rites, Rawat called for an impartial police investigation and said it must be determined whether Koli died by suicide or was murdered.
Haridwar Deputy Superintendent of Police Shishupal Singh Negi told PTI that police have also begun examining Koli's movements after they found that he had been living in Haridwar under a false identity for the past four to five months.
During this period, he worked as a security guard at two or three places, but kept changing jobs because he feared his real identity would be exposed when he was asked to provide identification documents.
Negi said police are also questioning the people who employed Koli and those who helped him rent a tea stall. According to the police, Koli had rented the stall from a man named Anil Sharma only four days before his death, using the alias Sadaram.
His real identity came to light only after his death, when police found his Aadhaar card and voter ID during a search. Police have denied reports that there was any dispute between Sharma and Koli over the shop.
Dharmendra Kaushik, a local who helped Koli get the shop, claimed that the 50-year-old had spoken to his family over the phone a day before his death. He said Koli was worried about his son's birthday and had argued with family members during the call.
The Nithari case had drawn national attention in 2006 after skeletal remains, skulls and bones were found in the backyard and drainage near businessman Moninder Singh Pandher's bungalow in Sector 31, Noida, in Uttar Pradesh.
Koli had worked as a domestic help at Pandher's residence. He was the only convict in the case and was acquitted by the Supreme Court in 2025 in the last of the Nithari cases, marking his acquittal in the 13th case.

headline: After Nandigram, Rejinagar Independent candidate arrested in old election clash case

After Nandigram, Rejinagar Independent candidate arrested in old election clash case
Police arrested Independent Rejinagar bypoll candidate Saiful Islam in a 2021 election clash case. The action, alongside other detentions, has sharpened political tension before the October 6 bypolls.
An Independent candidate for the Rejinagar Assembly bypoll in West Bengal has been arrested in a five-year-old case linked to a clash between two groups during the 2021 state elections, police said. Saiful Islam, who is associated with the Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) led by Humayun Kabir, was arrested on September 19.
The arrest came a day after police arrested Congress candidate Milan Pradhan, the party's nominee for the Nandigram Assembly bypoll, in a case that is nearly two decades old and was registered during protests against land acquisition in the area. The two bypolls are scheduled for October 6.
Police said the bypolls were necessitated after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari vacated Nandigram, which he had won along with Bhabanipur, while Rejinagar fell vacant after Kabir retained Nawda after winning both seats in the 2026 Assembly polls.
"Officials from Berhampore police station arrested Saiful Islam in connection with a case dating back to the previous Assembly election, when a clash had broken out between two groups," an officer told PTI.
On Saturday, police also sent a notice to AJUP chief Humayun Kabir, asking him to appear before investigating officers on Monday in a case registered over an alleged conspiracy to create tension between two communities.
A senior officer said the case was registered on September 14 after police recently played an audio recording at a press conference in Berhampore. Police claimed the conversation suggested a possible conspiracy to instigate tension between two communities.
Meanwhile, AJUP state secretary Ashik Iqbal was arrested on Friday during vehicle checking at a police picket in Murshidabad district with a large quantity of fake currency and illegal arms, officials said.

headline: Senior journalist Payal Mehta passes away; PM Modi, Rahul Gandhi, CMs offer condolences
full_text:
Senior journalist Payal Mehta passes away; PM Modi, Rahul Gandhi, CMs offer condolences
Mehta was on a visit to Mumbai when she developed uneasiness early in the morning. She was rushed to a hospital, where she later passed away.
Senior journalist Payal Mehta passed away on Sunday. Mehta, 46, was on a visit to Mumbai when she was rushed to the hospital after sudden uneasiness.
"On a visit to Mumbai, she developed uneasiness. Around 2 am she was taken to the hospital. Before any treatment could be administered, her pulse went silent," said senior journalist Sheela Bhatt in a post on X.
"Payal was one of the standout political reporters of her generation — deeply respected, remarkably well connected and a formidable presence in Parliament. Her access was matched by her understanding of national politics, and her relentless commitment to being on the ground made her reporting stand apart," said a post by CNN-News 18, while paying tribute to the late journalist.
PM Modi, Rahul Gandhi and more offer condolences
Prime Minister Narendra Modi also condoled Mehta's death. He emphasised that beyond her work, Mehta would be remembered for the kindness and warmth with which she touched many lives.
"Payal Mehta Ji was a hardworking journalist who remained firmly connected to the ground, bringing a deep understanding of national issues to her reporting," Modi said in a post on X.
"Her sudden and untimely passing is extremely saddening. My condolences to her family, friends and colleagues. May they find strength in this difficult hour. Om Shanti," he said.
Hailing Mehta as a thorough professional committed to delivering detailed information about various issues, home minister Amit Shah remarked that the passing of such a talented journalist is an irreplaceable loss to the field of journalism.
"I extend my deepest condolences to her grieving family and friends and pray to God to give them the strength to bear this profound pain. Om Shanti," he said.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh also expressed his deep shock and sadness at the news of Mehta's passing.
"She has left us far too soon. Payal was an extremely hardworking and dedicated journalist who covered the Parliament beat with great commitment and professionalism," he said.
Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge also condoled her death, adding that Mehta was a hardworking and diligent journalist who had a keen understanding of public affairs.
"Her untimely passing is deeply distressing. My heartfelt condolences to her family, friends and colleagues. May they find strength in this difficult hour," he said.
Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also expressed sadness over Mehta's demise, saying, "My sincere condolences to her family, friends and colleagues," he said.
Meanwhile, Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla said that Mehta's passing is a profound loss to journalism. "May God grant peace to the departed soul and strength to the bereaved family," he said.
Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said he was deeply pained to know about the sudden demise of the "very hardworking" journalist. "She used to meet me whenever I was in New Delhi and always on the field. She will be remembered for her dedication towards journalism. My deepest condolences to her family and friends," he said.
Assam Chief Minister Sarma expressed his sadness upon hearing of Mehta's passing. "I have known her for a long time. She was full of life and brought an infectious energy to everything she did. Yet for all her dedication to her work, what stood out most was how deeply she valued her relationships," he said.
Conveying his deepest condolences to Mehta's family, Sarma said, "I pray they find the strength to navigate this difficult phase. Prayers for her sadgati. Om Shanti".
