headline: Indore: The Congress and BJP traded barbs on Saturday over a comedian impersonating Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Rahul Gandhi’s ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event in Indore. Standup comic Pulkit Mani took the stage during the student-focused programme and ...
full_text:
Indore: The Congress and BJP traded barbs on Saturday over a comedian impersonating Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Rahul Gandhi’s ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ event in Indore. Standup comic Pulkit Mani took the stage during the student-focused programme and mimicked Modi’s mannerisms and his way of speaking to foreign leaders.
The act included references to Modi’s foreign policy, his mother and a coin trick the prime minister had performed with children.
Mani repeatedly used the phrase “my friend”, mimicking Modi’s interactions with foreign leaders. “My friend, how are you?” he said, without explicitly naming the prime minister.
The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha responded, “I am fine, how are you Modi ji?” Mani replied, “Great harassment,” and continued using “my friend” while exaggerating Modi’s mannerisms.
The act also referred to Galgotias University and the controversy surrounding a Chinese humanoid robot showcased by the university at the India Global AI Summit.
Gandhi then said, “Very nice to meet you,” and asked Mani to “tell me more”. The comedian then referred to the prime minister’s mother, saying, “Maa ko kursi do, maa,” while laughing and impersonating Modi. He followed it with, “Setting, my friend.”
Mani also mimicked a coin trick Modi had performed during an interaction with children, placing a coin on his forehead to loud cheers from the audience.
The Congress widely shared clips of the interaction on X. Its official handle posted one with the caption, “Narendra Modi ki Foreign Policy”, while another said, “My friend!! Great Harassment!!”
My friend!! Great Harassment!! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/PqetUPxUWp
— Congress (@INCIndia) September 19, 2026
Congress Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera also shared the video, writing: “In Indore, the giggling smart one arrived, stuck a coin on the forehead, and put on a spectacular show of great harassment.”
The BJP then hit out at Gandhi and the Congress, particularly over the reference to Modi’s late mother.
Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami wrote on X: “It is extremely shameful and painful to see objectionable words spoken about the late mother of the Honorable Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji, and Rahul Gandhi laughing at it.”
“A mother is not a subject of politics. The insult to a mother cannot be acceptable in any civilised society,” he said. “Laughing at the indecent remarks made about the late mother of the Prime Minister ji exposes your own political culture. Rahul Gandhi ji, crossing all limits of propriety in political opposition is neither democracy, nor service, nor culture. The maternal power of the country is watching everything. Such insensitivity and mockery are unacceptable at any cost,” Dhami added.
Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav also slammed Gandhi saying the latter’s “irresponsible attitude is extremely shameful, condemnable, and unbecoming”. Yadav added, “By insulting the honour of our country’s culture and mothers, he has encouraged leading the youth’s future in the wrong direction.” The CM said the “insult” to the prime minister’s mother amounted to “an insult to mothers across the country” and demanded an apology from Gandhi.
This is not the first time the Congress has used a political rival’s public image for satire. At a Congress event in August, Gandhi had hugged party leader Sandeep Dikshit while taking a dig at Modi’s foreign policy.
Dikshit had joked, “You weren’t hugging me thinking I was Meloni?” Gandhi replied, “I haven’t reached that stage yet.” The BJP had criticised the exchange.
The two parties have also been engaged in a wider social media war, including over AI-generated images. Earlier this month, the Congress’ Kerala unit shared AI-generated images targeting BJP leaders, including one showing a man resembling Amit Shah sitting in a Maruti Omni and another depicting Modi at a railway station.
The BJP state units in Gujarat, Kerala and Telangana later shared a series of AI-generated images targeting Sonia Gandhi. One Telangana BJP post showed a woman in a bar with the caption, “Lusiana, Italy. Circa-1970s”, referring to Sonia Gandhi’s birthplace.
The Congress has since said it was taking legal action over some of the posts.
(Edited by Chingkheinganbi Mayengbam)

headline: LK Advani, Manish Sisodia, Kailash Gahlot among Delhi voters served SIR notices
full_text:
LK Advani, Manish Sisodia, Kailash Gahlot among Delhi voters served SIR notices
A poll official said that prominent figures who received notices will be facilitated and their documents collected
Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) veteran LK Advani, former Delhi deputy chief minister Manish Sisodia, and BJP MLA Kailash Gahlot are among those who received notices for “discrepancies” during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in the national Capital, officials said.
The office of the Delhi chief electoral officer (CEO) late on Friday published the list of electors served notices, nearly three weeks after the draft electoral roll of voters in the city was released on August 31.
Advani, his daughter Pratibha Advani, and his daughter-in-law Geetika have been issued notices for ‘no mapping’, voters who could not be linked with the electoral roll from the previous revision.
Deep Dive
Gahlot, former minister in the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government and presently a BJP MLA, was also flagged for no mapping. His wife Moushumi Mishra Gahlot and elder daughter Jahnavi Gahlot were also served notices for the same discrepancy.
Former deputy CM Manish Sisodia, a voter in the New Delhi assembly constituency, was issued a notice, but the reason was not specified. His wife, Seema, and son, Meer, are also on the list. His wife has been flagged for a self-name mismatch, while Meer has been flagged for a parent-name mismatch.
A poll official said that prominent figures who received notices will be facilitated and their documents collected.
Other prominent flagged names include Abhishek Manu Singhvi, Kapil Sibal, Subramanian Swamy, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj and former CM and AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal.
Also Read:Delhi CM Rekha Gupta, Arvind Kejriwal among 3.16 mn voters issued notices for SIR ‘discrepancies’
Reacting to the development, Swamy, in a post on X, said, “It is surprising that Election Commission officials are under pressure to delete my name from the voter list. I intend to take it up, perhaps file a case in the Supreme Court.”
Sibal, in a press conference on Sunday, warned that the issue of voter names being removed from electoral rolls could eventually reach the Supreme Court.
Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta and Kejriwal were among more than 3.16 million voters served notices for “discrepancies” .
Of the electors flagged by poll authorities, 1,379,785 were in the “no mapping” category and 1,933,134 were tagged as bearing “logical discrepancies”.
To be sure, the two categories account for 3,312,919 electors.

NEW DELHI: BJP stalwart LK Advani and former Delhi deputy chief minister Manish Sisodia are among the prominent voters whose names figure in the list of 33 lakh people being issued notices over âlogical discrepanciesâ in details furnished during the recent Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Delhi.âThe notices arose from âlogical discrepanciesâ in the details furnished in their enumeration forms. Their names will be included in the final electoral rolls after due process of verification of facts and documents to be furnished by such voters,â a senior poll officer told PTI, confirming that notices had been issued to both Advani and Sisodia.
âThe process of verification of facts and documents is underway and validation of entries is being done accordingly,â the officer added.The 98-year-old Advani, a former deputy prime minister, his daughter Pratibha and daughter-in-law Geetika also received notices after their names could not be mapped to the 2002 SIR electoral roll. His son, Jayant, however, cleared the mapping exercise.All four are registered voters in the New Delhi assembly constituency.Meanwhile, in Sisodiaâs family, his wife Seema and son Meer have also been issued notices.
While the Election Commission has not cited a specific reason for the notice issued to the AAP leader, his son Meerâs notice mentions a âdiscrepancy in his parentâs nameâ, according to officials. The notice issued to his wife, Seema, cites a âmismatch in her own nameâ.
From politicians to bureaucrats, thousands face verification over 'discrepancies' in SIR enumeration forms
Many prominent voters, including senior government functionaries, bureaucrats and politicians, have been issued notices as part of the SIR exercise in Delhi.Chief minister Rekha Gupta, AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal and former Union minister Kapil Sibal have also received notices over similar discrepancies, officials said.Guptaâs entry was validated following verification of her documents, and her name has been cleared for inclusion in the final electoral roll of the Shalimar Bagh constituency, scheduled to be published on November 4.
According to the Delhi CEOâs office, notices are being issued to voters whose names could not be linked to the electoral roll prepared during the previous SIR, or whose details showed discrepancies when matched against the earlier roll.As part of the door-to-door verification exercise conducted between June 30 and August 17, every voter was required to submit an enumeration form.Of the around 97 lakh voters included in the draft electoral rolls, 33.13 lakh have been identified for notices over discrepancies in their enumeration forms. More than 31.63 lakh notices have been served so far.Most of the notices relate to the absence of corresponding records in the electoral roll prepared during the previous SIR in 2002.Voters have been asked to submit their replies along with supporting documents to the Electoral Registration Officers of their respective Assembly constituencies by October 29.

headline: India remains the fastest draw in flood relief to Nepal: 141.5 tonnes of aid rushed after flash floods
full_text:
India remains the fastest draw in flood relief to Nepal: 141.5 tonnes of aid rushed after flash floods
India's prompt response to the disaster in Nepal has reinforced the country's "first responder" tag.
India has sent over hundreds of tonnes of emergency relief material to flood-stricken Nepal. As per data accessed by HT, New Delhi has rushed a total of 141.5tonnes of material and equipment between August 26 and September 19.
On August 26, 2026, a series of flash floods struck Nepal and Tibet in one of the worst natural disasters the country has seen. The floods killed a total of 1,411 people in the landlocked country, as per Nepal's disaster management agency, and left around 5,875 missing. In Tibet, around 43 deaths were reported, with 519 people missing.
India's prompt response reinforces the country's "first responder" tag, reflecting its growing record of delivering aid and assistance to disaster-hit countries, from Türkiye and Syria to Myanmar, Sri Lanka and Venezuela.
Based on the data accessed by HT, along with emergency relief material, India has also sent around 54 expert personnel to help with reconstruction, emergency control and rescue across Nepal.
India rushes aid to Nepal | A timeline
- August 26 - 10 tonnes of emergency aid
- August 27 - 37.5 tonnes of emergency aid
- August 28 - 3 tonnes of emergency aid, 6 member army tunnel rescue team and 5 member medical team.
- August 29 - 11 tonnes of emergency aid, 13 member tunnel rescue team, 19 member forsenics team
- September 2 - 5.5 tonnes of emergency aid, 11 member rescue team
- September 6 - Two flights of 21.5 tonnes of emergency aid
- September 8 - 35 tonnes of emergency aid
- September 19 - 11 tonnes of emergency aid

headline: Imran Masood said only Congress can take BJP on. (ANI)
full_text:
Imran Masood said only Congress can take BJP on. (ANI)
NEW DELHI: With Uttar Pradesh gearing up for the 2027 assembly elections, Congress MP Imran Masood on Monday took a swipe at AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi's alliance pitch, warning that the party's presence in the polls "would end up benefitting BJP."His remarks came a day after Owaisi said AIMIM was open to an alliance with "like-minded" parties seeking to prevent the BJP from returning to power in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term.Speaking to ANI, Masood said, "If an alliance is to be formed, it should be finalised; otherwise, we must proceed with our own preparations. The political climate, not just here, but across the entire country, is such that one cannot move forward without the Congress; the Congress is essential. A fight against the BJP can only be waged with the Congress; only the Congress can take them on."
"Rahul Gandhi's leadership is capable of overcoming them. Finalise it (alliance) immediately. I am not aware of who is in touch; I have no information regarding that so far. If it isn't finalised, the damage happens on the ground," he added.
Responding to Owaisi's proposal, Masood said defeating the BJP was the primary objective but argued that strategic voting would be important.
"Defeating the BJP is the primary objective, and Muslims alone cannot defeat the BJP. If the BJP wins and forms the government, it is the Muslims who suffer the consequences. The political atmosphere in Hyderabad is different from that in Uttar Pradesh. Owaisi Ji might win 4-5 seats, but he ends up facilitating a BJP government. What will you do with those five MLAs? If a BJP government is formed, who suffers the loss? Since the BJP would form the government, people need to act sensibly. People must make decisions wisely and astutely," he said.
Owaisi's alliance pitch
Owaisi had earlier on Sunday said that AIMIM was ready to work with parties that share its objective of keeping the BJP out of power in Uttar Pradesh."We do not want the BJP government to be formed for a third time in Uttar Pradesh. If anyone does not want the BJP to form the government, they can talk to us. We are ready to work with you to stop the BJP from coming to power. But it is important to understand that you cannot stop the BJP alone," Owaisi said.Owaisi also cited AIMIM's experience in Bihar, saying the party had sought an alliance with opposition parties and asked for six seats, but the proposal was not accepted. He said AIMIM would continue building its organisation in Uttar Pradesh irrespective of alliance talks.Earlier in the day, Owaisi, meanwhile, said AIMIM was already preparing for the Uttar Pradesh elections and was hopeful of sending its candidates to the state Assembly."We are visiting specifically in connection with election preparations. Our party is fully prepared and actively gearing up; we are hopeful that this time our candidates will be elected as MLAs and enter the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly," he said.
On the possibility of an alliance, Owaisi said, "Wait until October 2nd; we will let you know by then."
Akhilesh sets 27,000-vote target
The Congress's push for an early alliance decision also comes as the Samajwadi Party steps up its preparations for the 2027 polls. At the party's state executive meeting on Sunday, Akhilesh Yadav said the SP would work to increase its vote share by 27,000 votes in every assembly constituency."Today was our state executive meeting. In this, we have decided that in the 2027 assembly elections, we will work to increase 27,000 votes in every assembly seat. That means we will reduce 27,000 votes of the BJP," Yadav said.Masood also criticised the Election Commission over Special Intensive Revision (SIR) notices, questioning the difficulties they could create for ordinary citizens."What could be more farcical in this country than a situation where Members of Parliament, former Chief Ministers, and even the External Affairs Minister receive such notices? If they are getting notices, the Election Commission's situation couldn't be more absurd. Imagine the plight of the common man or those who are unemployed and struggling just to find a single meal a day. Are they expected to run around with documents? Look at the state the country has been reduced to, constantly standing in queues. The system has failed. The system has completely collapsed," he said.
Kanchan Yadav is a writer at The Times of India, where she covers business, politics, international affairs and social issues. Her reporting also focuses on policy, governance and economic developments, with a close lens on how decisions in corridors of power affect everyday lives and community well-being.

headline: India has served 8 times on UNSC: Why does it want a permanent seat now?
full_text:
India has served 8 times on UNSC: Why does it want a permanent seat now?
India officially put forward its candidature for a permanent seat in the Security Council during the 49th General Assembly in 1994.
It has been 81 years since the United Nations Security Council was established in 1945, in the aftermath of World War II. Since then, its permanent membership has remained unchanged; China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States hold the five permanent seats, each with veto power.
India has been pitching for a permanent seat while calling for an expansion of the UNSC to make it more representative of today’s world, with greater participation from Asia, Africa and Latin America. Apart from the five permanent members, the Council currently has 10 non-permanent, rotational members.
India officially put forward its candidature for a permanent seat in the Security Council during the 49th General Assembly in 1994. Since then, it has reiterated its candidature at all the subsequent UN General Assemblies.
At the UN Millennium Summit in New York in September 2000, then Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee had reiterated India's case for permanent membership, saying that India had “let it be known for some years” that it considered itself qualified for the responsibilities of permanent membership.
What India says
New Delhi has called for an expansion in both the permanent and non-permanent categories of Security Council membership. It has also cautioned that expanding only the non-permanent category would not fundamentally alter the Council's decision-making structure, which gives the five permanent members a special position.
It is important to note here that the composition of the UNSC has been expanded only once since its creation in 1945. An amendment to the UN Charter in 1965 increased its membership from 11 to 15 by adding four non-permanent seats. The five permanent seats remained unchanged.
India argues that the global order has changed significantly since the UN's early days and that developing countries should have greater participation in global decision-making. India has consequently maintained that reform of the Security Council can no longer be delayed.
India also points to its size, democratic system, growing economic and geopolitical weight, and contribution to UN peacekeeping as part of its case for a permanent membership.
While launching a campaign for India’s election as a non-permanent UNSC member for the 2028-29 term, external affairs minister S Jaishankar highlighted that India has contributed nearly 300,000 personnel to about 50 UN peacekeeping missions since the organisation’s inception—and currently has over 4,300 personnel serving in 10 UN peacekeeping missions.
He added that India has consistently advocated dialogue and diplomacy and has sought to give voice to the concerns of the Global South.
Who are the non-permanent members?
The 10 non-permanent members are elected by the UN General Assembly for two-year terms.
The 10 non-permanent members now and when their terms end-
2026: Denmark, Greece, Pakistan, Panama, Somalia
2027: Bahrain, Colombia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Latvia, Liberia
Australia will bid to join the United Nations Security Council from 2029, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has said, as he launched a campaign to secure one of the two non-permanent seats available to its bloc.
India as non-permanent member
India has served as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council eight times: first in 1950–51, followed by terms in 1967–68, 1972–73, 1977–78, 1984–85, 1991–92, 2011–12 and most recently in 2021–22.
Across these terms, India has participated in the Council's deliberations and decisions on international peace and security, including on issues ranging from conflicts and peacekeeping to sanctions and international cooperation.
New Delhi has officially launched its campaign for election as a non-permanent member of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) for the 2028-29 term.
Its official campaign for the two-year term is “Shanti: India for the United Nations Security Council 2028–29 — Norms, Trust, Integrity.”
Amongst the five permanent members of the Council, four have long supported India’s bid. However, China has not explicitly backed India, even though said it was in favour of it during the recent BRICS Summit and other occasions.
What is the difference between permanent and non-permanent members?
Each of the 15 members of the Security Council has one vote. However, the five permanent members – China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States – have veto power over substantive decisions. Under the UN Charter, all member states are obligated to comply with Security Council decisions.
If India gets a permanent seat on the UN Security Council, it would also gain veto power as the existing five. This would give India a more substantial say in major global issues before the Council.
But why is a veto important?
A veto is particularly significant because a substantive resolution cannot be adopted if even one of the five permanent members votes against it, provided the resolution otherwise requires the permanent members' concurrence.
In other words, a single veto from a permanent member can block a substantive resolution, regardless of how many other members support it.
When was the council formed and what does it do?
The UN Security Council was established in 1945, when the United Nations was created in the aftermath of World War II. The UN Charter, which established the Council, was signed on June 26, 1945, and came into force on October 24, 1945.
The Security Council held its first meeting on January 17, 1946, at Church House, Westminster, London.
The Security Council takes the lead in determining the existence of a threat to the peace, breach of the peace or act of aggression. It calls upon parties to a dispute to settle it by peaceful means and recommends methods of adjustment or terms of settlement. In some cases, the Security Council can impose sanctions or even authorise the use of force to maintain or restore international peace and security.
The Security Council also has a presidency, which rotates among its 15 members every month.
The decision to first review the question of Security Council restructuring was first taken at the 47th General Assembly in 1992 following which an Open Ended Working Group (OEWG) to review all aspects relating to Security Council restructuring was established in 1993.
Although the OEWG has been discussing the issue since 1993, it has not yet been possible to arrive at any agreement on the key questions of size of an expanded Council, models for expansion, or criteria for candidatures.
World leaders back India
India’s bid for a permanent seat has secured support from several major countries, strengthening its case for a greater role in the Council.
Recently, at the BRICS Summit held in New Delhi, China and Russia (two permanent UNSC members) reiterated their support for the aspirations of Brazil and India to play a greater role in the UN, including its Security Council.
The BRICS leaders also reaffirmed their commitment to reforming the UN Security Council to make it more democratic, representative, effective and efficient, with greater representation for developing countries.
American economist Jeffrey Sachs has also thrown his weight behind India, saying no other country has as strong a claim to become the sixth permanent member of the UNSC than India.
“Think of all countries in the world, there is no country other than India that has such a strong claim as the sixth permanent member of the UN Security Council,” Sachs said in an interview with news agency PTI.
Sachs also called on India and China to work together to overcome their differences and said Beijing should support New Delhi’s bid.
Back in 2002, eight years after India first bid itself for a permanent seat, nine countries had expressed support in the UN for India's candidature. These countries are Mauritius, Bhutan, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Russia, Vietnam, Laos, Cyprus and Cambodia.
Cyprus also recently reiterated its firm support for India’s permanent membership of a reformed UNSC. Palestine has also publicly backed New Delhi's long-standing aspiration for a permanent seat.

headline: Congress nominee Milan Pradhan sent to judicial custody till October 5
full_text:
Congress nominee Milan Pradhan sent to judicial custody till October 5
Congress' Nandigram bypoll nominee Milan Pradhan was on Monday remanded to judicial custody till October 5 in connection with a case registered at Khejuri Police Station 19 years ago, dealing a setback to his campaign for the October 6 assembly bypoll.Pradhan was sent to judicial custody by a Contai court in West Bengal's Purba Medinipur district, his counsel Ayan Bhattacharjee said. He added that the order would be challenged before the Calcutta high court.The development came two days after a Haldia court had remanded Pradhan to judicial custody till October 3, following his arrest on September 18 on multiple charges, including murder, linked to the 2007 Nandigram land agitation.The latest order effectively prevents Pradhan from campaigning during the final days of the bypoll campaign, which ends on October 4.The Nandigram seat was vacated by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, who resigned in May and chose to retain Bhabanipur after defeating Mamata Banerjee in the assembly election held earlier this year.Meanwhile, Banerjee's decision to support Pradhan has marked a significant political shift between the Trinamool Congress and Congress in Bengal.
Banerjee backed the Congress candidate after her faction's nominee, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew from the October 6 contest following a meeting with Adhikari in Kolkata.Announcing her support on September 18, Banerjee described Congress as a "sister party" and a "natural ally", saying the decision was taken in the larger interest of the country and to strengthen the INDIA bloc.
Banerjee also said she wanted to send a message about the future of the opposition alliance beginning from Bengal.The move follows a series of political developments involving the TMC. The Election Commission had frozen the Trinamool Congress' traditional name and âJora Ghash Phulâ symbol amid an internal party dispute, assigning separate names and symbols to Banerjee's faction and its dissidents for the upcoming bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar.The Congress-TMC relationship has previously seen periods of cooperation. The parties contested the 2001 Bengal assembly election together and later joined hands in the 2009 Lok Sabha polls. In 2011, their alliance helped end the Left Front's 34-year rule in Bengal.

With over three years of experience, she focuses on national and global developments, conflict, diplomacy and their impact on India. Her work combines breaking news with in-depth analysis, offering readers context and clarity on the stories shaping the world.

headline: MEERUT: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday launched an attack against the opposition parties, accusing them of dynastic politics and casteism.Addressing the Shakti Kendra Sanyojak Sammelan in Meerut, the CM said, "For a long time,...
full_text:
MEERUT: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday launched an attack against the opposition parties, accusing them of dynastic politics and casteism.Addressing the Shakti Kendra Sanyojak Sammelan in Meerut, the CM said, "For a long time, politics was plagued by the maladies of dynastic politics and casteism. The Congress party and its political allies long treated politics merely as a vehicle for dynastic interests and personal gain. Instead of serving as a means for public service, power became a tool for them to perpetuate dynastic rule and advance their own vested interests."CM Yogi said the very name 'Shakti Kendra' defines its work. "In BJP's organisational structure, the Shakti Kendra Sanyojak embodies the entire strength of the organisation and elections," he said."Politics came to be seen as a means to serve one's own interests. BJP has presented a different ideal before this political thinking - Rashtra Pratham. For us, politics is not just a means to attain power but a medium of national service. Our workers' goal is to keep organisation above self, society above organisation and nation above society," he said.Taking a swipe at the "mujhe kya" (what's in it for me) mindset, he termed it "Manthara-buddhi".
"Those who say 'mujhe kya' have Manthara-buddhi - meaning 'what will I get, no matter who does what, what is it to me?' This thinking not only harms the individual but the entire society. It creates an identity crisis, makes society flee from its responsibilities, and hampers development," he said.CM Yogi said this mindset had weakened the country and created an identity crisis, but the transformation was visible after 2014 when Prime Minister Narendra Modi assumed office."We saw a new India - an India which is proud of its heritage and sets its own speed for development. An India which no longer has an identity crisis, which walks with its chest high and looks the world in the eye. And when someone dares to challenge India, it also knows how to protect its security and sovereignty," he said.He said 'New India' under PM Modi was shedding the slave mentality and restoring pride in its heritage, citing the construction of Kashi Vishwanath Dham in Varanasi and the grand Ram Mandir in Ayodhya as examples of works once considered impossible."In Mathura-Vrindavan, development works are underway. We have taken up rejuvenation of Shuktirth, the Bhagwat land, and have also allocated funds for Vidur Koti," he added.He said the convention was aimed at awakening the strength of workers and channelising it for the party with the spirit of 'Nation First' to realise PM Narendra Modi's resolve to build an Atmanirbhar and Viksit Bharat.He welcomed BJP National President Nitin Nabin, who was present for the two-day tour of the western region, along with the state president, Union Minister Pankaj Chaudhary, national office bearers and regional leaders.The chief minister also said Uttar Pradesh's identity had changed since 2017. "There was a time when UP was counted among BIMARU states, youth did not get jobs, and people hesitated to reveal their identity. Today no one can call UP a BIMARU state. When big economies are discussed, UP's name is taken prominently," he said.Highlighting his government's achievements, he said nine and a half lakh government jobs were given, traditional enterprises were revived under 'One District One Product' (ODOP), providing employment to 3.25 crore youth, and Meerut's products, Agra's papad and Muzaffarnagar's jaggery were given national branding."Before 2017, UP was identified with 'katta and tamancha'. Now the 12-lane expressway, Namo Bharat rapid rail between Delhi and Meerut, India's largest airport - Noida International Airport - an hour away, UP's first sports university named after Major Dhyan Chand in Meerut, a film city, medical device park, semiconductor units are coming up. Sixty percent of electronic components and 55 percent of mobile phones made in India are now made in UP," he said.He said the state had become riot-free and curfew-free, ensuring the safety of daughters and traders.Alleging that those who indulged in appeasement and patronised mafias did not like this transformation, he cautioned workers against attempts to divide society on caste lines.
"Mahapurush do not belong to one caste; they belong to the entire society and nation. Maharana Pratap, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Guru Gobind Singh ji Maharaj are our national heroes. They cannot be tied in caste brackets," he said, adding that his government had honoured heroes of the 1857 First War of Independence.Asking workers to become 'sarathi' like Lord Krishna in the Mahabharata, he said, "History never honoured Shakuni and Manthara, but it has honoured a sarathi like Krishna for ages. Every worker should work with the feeling - my work is for Nation First."CM Yogi's attack against Congress and the opposition comes ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly election, where the BJP-led NDA eyes a third consecutive win.

headline: Google to report child abuse content directly to Indian authorities: Spokesperson
full_text:
Google to report child abuse content directly to Indian authorities: Spokesperson
Google said on Monday it has agreed to report content flagged as child sexual abuse material (CSAM) to Indian authorities.
Tech giant Google on Monday said it has proposed operationalising the sharing of information on cases involving child sex abuse material (CSAM) with the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the Ministry of Home Affairs, signalling a shift away from sole reliance on international reporting channels.
“Google is deeply committed to fighting CSAM online and preventing its platforms from being used to create, store or distribute such material. We invest significantly to detect, deter, remove, and report child sexual abuse material. As part of our ongoing discussions with the Government of India, we have respectfully proposed to operationalize the provision of relevant information to the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) in cases related to child sexual abuse material,” a Google spokesperson said on Monday in response to a query.
Also Read | Centre questions Meta's 'intermediary' status over Facebook, Instagram ads
Google considers direct reporting of CSAM cases to I4C
The Business Standard first reported the development.
This move comes days after Meta announced it would begin reporting child-safety matters directly to the Cyber Crime portal maintained by the I4C. Google’s plan, however, is still in the discussion stage.
It could not be immediately established which ministry or department Google made this proposal to.
Google currently reports CSAM through a process that involves the US-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC), similar to Meta.
According to Google, when it detects CSAM on its platforms, it removes the material and makes a CyberTipline report to NCMEC or other relevant authorities. Such reports may include the offending content, contextual information and, where relevant, information identifying the user or the child victim.
NCMEC then forwards reports to law enforcement authorities around the world, as appropriate.
In a statement to HT on September 15, a Meta spokesperson said: “Protecting children on our platforms is a priority for us and we are committed to working with the government to ensure that the perpetrators of these crimes are held responsible. To collectively strengthen our efforts to combat this harm, Meta will now report child safety matters directly to the Cyber crime portal managed by I4C.”
Centre pushes platforms to report cases to Indian agencies
Increased government scrutiny on CSAM, specifically on Meta’s platforms like Instagram and Facebook, came after a BBC Eye investigation found advertisements on Instagram containing phrases such as “rape video” and “child video”, which directed users to Telegram channels allegedly selling CSAM.
After the matter came to light, officials at the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) summoned Meta officials.
The government’s position has been that platforms should report such cases directly to Indian law enforcement agencies. A senior MeitY official told HT earlier that Meta had been reporting such cases to NCMEC, but the government wanted the company to also report them to Indian authorities.
The government has also said that online safety of children is a fundamental principle for social media platforms operating in India and is “non-negotiable”.

headline: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar has claimed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi assured him that the state would be divided into four parts, reviving a nearly two-decade-old debate over dividing the country's most populous state.Ra...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar has claimed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi assured him that the state would be divided into four parts, reviving a nearly two-decade-old debate over dividing the country's most populous state.Rajbhar, who heads BJP ally Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP), claimed that PM Modi told him Uttar Pradesh could be divided after the caste census.âWe want to assure you regarding the 27% reservation. I spoke with the prime minister about this,â he told the audience at an SBSP programme in Deoria on Sunday.âHe (PM Modi) said, âOm Prakash ji, your point is justified, but some people are opposing it.â I asked him how we could move forward, and he replied, âI will conduct a caste census, and once we have counted the castes, there will be no difficulty.â The state will be divided into four parts. And on the day the Purvanchal is formed, if the chief minister is to be from any caste, then a Rajbharâs son will become the chief minister,â he added.However, another UP minister and BJP ally, Sanjay Nishad, dismissed Rajbharâs remarks as âmisleadingâ, saying the Nishad Party was not in favour of a reorganisation.âThere had been a demand to divide UP earlier, but now the state is progressing rapidly in all spheres.
Further, special development funds have been allocated for regions like Bundelkhand and Purvanchal that needed handholding,â Nishad told PTI.Rajbhar has advocated the division of Uttar Pradesh in the past as well, saying in October 2018 that the âstate can be developed only after it is divided into four parts.â
When Mayawati proposed carving out four states from UP
With the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections due in early 2027, Rajbharâs remarks have revived the long-running political debate over dividing the state.Ahead of the 2012 UP assembly elections, then chief minister Mayawati revived the demand, with the state assembly passing a resolution to split Uttar Pradesh into Avadh Pradesh, Purvanchal, Bundelkhand and Paschim Pradesh.In 2011, her government had sent a proposal to the Congress-led Centre seeking the creation of the four states.Before that, in 2008, Mayawati had proposed dividing Uttar Pradesh into three parts.Several parties, including the Rashtriya Lok Dal and Congress, have also backed demands for dividing the state at various points. There have additionally been calls for a separate Bundelkhand comprising parts of Uttar Pradesh and neighbouring Madhya Pradesh.
Uttar Pradesh was last divided in 2000, when the BJP-led central government carved out Uttarakhand, then known as Uttaranchal.
Why Uttar Pradesh matters
With a population of around 25 crore, Uttar Pradesh is Indiaâs most populous state. If it were an independent country, its population would make it the fifth- or sixth-most populous country in the world.Geographically, Uttar Pradesh is the fourth-largest state in India.It sends 80 members to the 543-seat Lok Sabha, the highest representation of any state or Union territory. Its legislative assembly has 403 members.Six prime ministers were born in Uttar Pradesh, while several others, including Narendra Modi, have represented the state in Parliament.

headline: London a dead economy, go to Madurai instead: Annamalai mocks Vijay's UK visit
full_text:
London a dead economy, go to Madurai instead: Annamalai mocks Vijay's UK visit
Annamalai said Vijay should focus on attracting investment from Tamil Nadu and other Indian cities rather than making overseas trips, also questioning the economic value of his London visit.
Former Tamil Nadu BJP president K Annamalai has slammed Chief Minister Joseph Vijay over his recent London visit, arguing that the UK was not the right place to seek investment for Tamil Nadu. He argued that the state government should focus more on attracting investment from within India, pointing out that said India was now a USD 4.1 trillion economy while the UK was a USD 3.4 trillion economy.
"Today, India is a country with a USD 4.1 trillion economy, while the UK has a USD 3.4 trillion economy. Why go to that country with such a large delegation from here and then ask whether he met this person, whether he met that person, whether they saw him, whether they went inside? What is the point of all this?" he questioned.
Vijay undertook a six-day official visit to the UK from September 10, leading a state delegation with a stated focus on attracting investments and exploring industrial and motorsports opportunities. The Tamil Nadu government said the trip resulted in investment commitments worth nearly Rs 15,000 crore and more than 10,000 direct and indirect jobs.
'UK HAS JUST 1% GROWTH'
Annamalai claimed that the UK offered limited scope for fresh investment and described London as a "dead economy".
"I know London well. It is a dead economy. There is no money there. The UK's growth is just 1 per cent. If you go there and ask them to invest money in Tamil Nadu, what money are they going to give?" he said.
Instead, he suggested that Vijay travel to major industrial centres in Tamil Nadu and engage directly with local businesses.
"What the Chief Minister should do is, rather than taking an Emirates flight from Chennai to London, take an IndiGo flight from Chennai to Coimbatore or Madurai," Annamalai said.
He suggested that the state could offer tax incentives to companies already operating in Tamil Nadu to encourage them to expand.
"Let us sit down with the industrialists who are already here. Tell them, 'If you expand your production facility, don't pay 50 per cent of the tax; the government will bear that 50 per cent.' That will encourage them to invest," he said.
Annamalai specifically mentioned Madurai, Coimbatore and Kovilpatti, besides other major Indian cities such as Mumbai, Delhi and Bengaluru, as potential destinations for investment outreach.
"Come to Madurai and meet the Madurai Chamber of Commerce and the people involved in industry. Go to Coimbatore and encourage the textile mills, automobile industry and foundries," he said.
"Go to Bombay, go to Delhi, go to Bengaluru. Bring investment from there. You don't have to go abroad for everything," the former IPS officer added.
QUESTIONS FOCUS ON VIJAY'S LONDON ENGAGEMENTS
Annamalai also took a swipe at the attention surrounding Vijay's meetings and public appearances during the visit.
"Did he meet this person? Did he meet that person? Did they see him? I am talking about this unnecessary politics," he said.
The remarks came amid criticism of Vijay's visit, particularly after photographs of him at Silverstone alongside actor and racing driver Ajith Kumar and actress Trisha emerged.
Vijay had visited the Silverstone Motor Racing Circuit as part of follow-up work on the proposed Motor Sports City in Tamil Nadu and flagged off the 2026 Michelin Le Mans Cup race, in which Ajith participated.
BJP state president Nainar Nagendran had also criticised the trip, describing it as a "pleasure tour" and alleging that companies already operating in India were being presented as fresh investments secured through the visit.
The Tamil Nadu government and Vijay's TVK, however, released details of investment commitments announced during the trip, with the state putting the total value at around Rs 15,300 crore.
Among the announced commitments was an Rs 11,000-crore investment from Samvardhana Motherson International. Other agreements covered sectors including renewable energy, power-grid equipment and Global Capability Centres.
CHIEF MINISTER MUST TRAVEL WITHIN TAMIL NADU
Annamalai argued that the state should first tap the investment potential within Tamil Nadu and urged Vijay to visit the state's major industrial centres more frequently.
"When so many people in the local economy are ready to invest, go and encourage the local industrialists in Tamil Nadu. They have money. They are ready to invest," he said.
He also pointed to Indian companies investing in the UK as an argument for greater focus on domestic capital.
"In fact, Indian companies such as Jaguar Land Rover and Mahindra are among those investing substantial amounts of money in the UK today," he said.
Annamalai argued that overseas investment missions would have made more sense when India's economy was smaller.
"When should we have gone to London? When India was a USD 1 trillion economy, in 2008 or 2010, while London was around USD 3 trillion. At that time, if you had gone to London with a large delegation, it would have made sense," he said.
He also urged the government to move away from repeatedly publicising overseas investment trips.
“Please stop all this business of saying, ‘I am going to London, I am going to New York, I am going to Chicago, I am going to San Francisco, I am going to Singapore.’ That is old politics,” he said.
At the same time, Annamalai said the newly elected government should be given time to work.
The remarks come as Vijay's first foreign trip as Chief Minister continues to draw political scrutiny, with the Tamil Nadu government highlighting the investment commitments announced in London and critics questioning the economic value and nature of the visit.

headline: 37 lakh Bengal SIR appeals could take 12 years to clear, EC seeks more tribunals
full_text:
37 lakh Bengal SIR appeals could take 12 years to clear, EC seeks more tribunals
The Election Commission has told the Supreme Court that clearing West Bengal's SIR appeal backlog could take more than 12 years at the current pace. It has sought more tribunals, saying the present disposal rate is too slow for timely adjudication.
Clearing the more than 37 lakh appeals pending from West Bengal’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls could take nearly 12 years at the current pace, prompting the Election Commission to ask the Supreme Court to increase the number of tribunals hearing the cases.
In an affidavit, the poll panel told the Supreme Court that the tribunals have disposed of 1,26,194 appeals since they started hearing cases in mid-April. This works out to roughly 25,238 cases being cleared every month, with the calculation taking into account all seven days of the week as working days, according to a Times of India report.
As of September 16, when the affidavit was filed, 37,05,235 appeals remained pending. If the tribunals continue working seven days a week at the current pace, it would take 146 months — more than 12 years — to dispose of the entire backlog.
The Commission has therefore asked the Supreme Court to create more tribunals to speed up the process. It has proposed setting up one tribunal for each of West Bengal's 42 parliamentary constituencies.
The EC's data shows that 38.31 lakh appeals have been filed against orders relating to the SIR of electoral rolls. Of these, 22.21 lakh were filed by people whose names were deleted and who are seeking their inclusion in the electoral rolls, while 16.10 lakh appeals challenge the inclusion of names.
OVER 1 LAKH NAMES ADDED BACK
Of the 1,26,194 appeals decided by the tribunals, 1,13,943 resulted in the applicants being added back to the electoral rolls, according to the EC. This means more than 90 per cent of the appeals decided so far have resulted in names being restored.
The Commission's affidavit also disputes claims that the SIR-related deletions affected the outcome of the West Bengal Assembly elections.
The EC said claims that deletions exceeded victory margins in several constituencies ignored entries classified as "absent, shifted, dead and duplicate".
The poll panel described the comparison between the number of deletions and election victory margins as a "flawed, speculative yardstick."
It also cited constituencies won by TMC candidates where the number of deletions was greater than the winning margin.
The affidavit argues that using deletion numbers as a measure to claim that SIR affected election results would therefore be an unreliable approach.
19 TRIBUNALS CURRENTLY HEARING APPEALS
The Supreme Court had earlier directed the Election Commission to provide data on the pendency and disposal of appeals and explain what steps were being taken to streamline their disposal.
The court had also said the appeals needed to be adjudicated in a time-bound manner and asked how many additional tribunals would be required.
Later, the chief justice of the Calcutta High Court, acting on the Supreme Court's direction, set up 19 tribunals headed by former high court chief justices and judges to decide the appeals.
Around 700 judicial officers from West Bengal, Odisha and Jharkhand had also been deployed to deal with the claims and objections arising from the SIR exercise.

headline: SIR appeals pile up in WB, EC says hike number of tribunals

NEW DELHI: The innumerable voters in West Bengal who were removed from the electoral rolls after special intensive revision (SIR) may not be able to vote for more than a decade as appellate tribunals set up by Supreme Court could take more than 12 years to decide on their appeals for inclusion, going by the present pace of adjudication.An affidavit filed by Election Commission before Supreme Court says 1,26,194 applications have been decided by tribunals in the last five months since they started functioning in mid-April. So, on average, 25,238 cases are being decided by the tribunals in a month when even Saturdays and Sundays are included as working days. The total number of pending cases as of Sept 16, when the affidavit was filed, was 37,05,235. At current speed, if the tribunals work seven days a week, it would take 146 months to decide all cases.
Excessive backlog
Admitting that the present infrastructure and number of tribunals are insufficient to handle the Herculean task of adjudicating 37 lakh cases, the poll panel pleaded with the court to increase the number of tribunals in the state from 24 to 42, almost double the present strength, and allow judicial officers to work from home.
"With a view to further streamlining and expediting the disposal of the pending appeals, it is proposed that the number of appellate tribunals in the state of West Bengal may be considered for increase to correspond with the number of parliamentary constituencies in the state, so as to facilitate expeditious disposal of the pending appeals," said the affidavit, filed in response to a petition from TMC MP Derek O' Brien. Allowing judicial workers to conduct hearings and undertake other proceedings from home "would assist in expediting the disposal of pending appeals by minimising the time lost in conveyance", it said.In another affidavit filed in response to a petition on the functioning of the tribunals, the commission said they were constituted pursuant to the directives of the apex court and the standard operating procedure (SOP) governing their functioning has been formulated by the committee constituted for this purpose, comprising, inter alia, former judges of the high court at Calcutta.
"It is humbly submitted that the reliefs sought by the petitioner pertain primarily to the functioning, procedure and accessibility of the appellate mechanism and, therefore, fall within the domain of the SOP governing the functioning of the appellate tribunals and the authorities entrusted with the administration thereof. The feasibility, modalities and implementation... are matters best left to the consideration of the concerned appellate tribunal..." the affidavit said.

A bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Arun Bhardwaj also permitted Kejriwal and the other AAP leaders Manish Sisodia, Sanjay Singh, Saurabh Bharadwaj, Vinay Mishra and Durgesh Pathak, to approach the judicial registrar for copies of documents and other material that formed the basis of the contempt proceedings but had not yet been supplied to them.
The direction came after senior advocate Vikram Chaudhary, appearing for Kejriwal, along with lawyers representing the other AAP leaders, submitted that certain documents had not been provided to the accused.
“The respondents are permitted to approach the registrar. Let the replies be filed by the respondents in four weeks,” the court said in its order, while fixing November 16 as the next date of hearing.
Also Read: Delhi HC to appoint 3 senior lawyers as amicus for Kejriwal, Sisodia in excise policy case
On February 27, a trial court discharged Kejriwal and others in the excise policy case, prompting the CBI to approach the high court. On March 9, Justice Sharma stayed the trial court’s direction for departmental action against a CBI officer and deferred Enforcement Directorate (ED) proceedings.
However, Kejriwal then sought to transfer the matter from her bench, which was rejected by Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya on March 13.
On April 5, Kejriwal, Sisodia and others sought Justice Sharma’s recusal, which she dismissed on April 20. On April 27, Kejriwal informed the judge that he would boycott the proceedings.
Also Read:‘Apprehension’ of not receiving a ‘fair’ hearing in case: Kejriwal
Following this, Sisodia and Pathak also wrote similar letters. On May 5, the court decided to appoint senior advocates as amicus curiae to represent the three leaders, but the matter was deferred on three occasions.
However, on May 14, justice Sharma initiated contempt proceedings and withdrew herself, stating that the law did not permit a judge who has initiated contempt proceedings over allegedly defamatory, contemptuous and vilifying material posted against the judge on social media – in relation to a matter to continue hearing that very matter.
Following the initiation of the contempt, a lawyer Ashok Chaitanya also sought initiation of contempt proceedings against Kejriwal, Bhardwaj, Gopal Rai and a journalist for allegedly running a coordinated campaign targeting Justice Sharma.

headline: The ruling TVK on Monday (September 21, 2026) dropped the names of leaders of its alliance parties from its list of star campaigners for the upcoming Assembly bypolls to Madurantakam and Dharapuram, hours after the DMK submitted a petition to the Ele...
full_text:
The ruling TVK on Monday (September 21, 2026) dropped the names of leaders of its alliance parties from its list of star campaigners for the upcoming Assembly bypolls to Madurantakam and Dharapuram, hours after the DMK submitted a petition to the Election Commission (EC), objecting to it.
Earlier in the day, DMK organisation secretary R.S. Bharathi submitted a complaint to the EC, urging it to cancel the TVK’s list. The DMK said it went against the provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and the Model Code of Conduct.
The TVK has named Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president Manickam Tagore, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) leader Thol. Thirumavalavan, Minister Vanni Arasu (VCK), D. Ravikumar (VCK MP), senior VCK leader Sinthanai Selvan, Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (MDMK) general secretary Vaiko, the party’s MP Durai Vaiko, and Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) leader K.M. Kader Mohideen in its list of “star campaigners.”
What does DMK’s complaint say?
In his complaint to Chief Electoral Officer of Tamil Nadu Archana Patnaik, Mr. Bharathi said Section 77(1) of the Representation of the People Act used the expressions “leaders of a political party” and “of that political party” in providing for the exemption of their travel expenses from being included in the election expenditure accounts of individual candidates.
“According to these statutory provisions, a political party can designate only its own leaders and office-bearers as star campaigners. There is no provision under the law permitting a party to list leaders or office-bearers of another recognised political party as its own star campaigners,” he said.
Mr. Bharathi pointed out that, in accordance with the guidelines issued periodically by the Election Commission of India, a political party was required to list only its own leaders to campaign for its candidates. Even in the case of alliance partners, he said, declaring a leader of one party as the official “star campaigner” of another party amounted to misuse of the exemption from election expenditure.
He said recognising individuals from other parties as a party’s star campaigners created a risk of campaign expenses, including travel and accommodation, being unlawfully exempted instead of being debited to the election expenditure limits of candidates in the respective constituencies.
“This completely undermines a level playing field. Furthermore, I wish to emphasise here that this runs entirely contrary to the Election Commission’s foundational principle of conducting free and fair elections,” he said.
Mr. Bharathi also urged the Election Commission to issue directions to ensure that, if leaders of other parties campaigned for TVK candidates, all associated expenses were fully included in the individual candidates’ election expenditure accounts.

headline: New Delhi: Days after Congress student wing NSUI drew a blank in the Delhi University Students Union (DUSU) elections, an NSUI member has approached Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra with complaints against the organisation’s leadership under Ka...
full_text:
New Delhi: Days after Congress student wing NSUI drew a blank in the Delhi University Students Union (DUSU) elections, an NSUI member has approached Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra with complaints against the organisation’s leadership under Kanhaiya Kumar, ThePrint has learnt.
The complaint comes over candidate selection, the handling of aspirants and the lack of involvement of the leadership in campus elections. The member alleged that Kumar—the AICC in-charge of the party’s student wing—was not involved enough on the ground and took decisions without consulting student leaders.
“Kanhaiya wasn’t on campus, how would he know what was happening? He did not take anyone’s advice, just went and made decisions on his own. What he did with Shokeen was just one example. This has happened over the years. He was inactive during elections at all times,” the NSUI member, not wanting to be named, alleged while speaking to ThePrint.
The handling of DUSU vice-president-elect Deepanshu Shokeen—famously known as the ‘barefoot candidate’ who contested independently after being denied an NSUI ticket—is among the issues being raised. Shokeen went on to win the vice-president’s post with 30,615 votes, while NSUI’s official candidate Vir Chatrath finished third with 4,313 votes.
An NSUI functionary familiar with the process said the organisation had already finalised Chatrath’s ticket when Shokeen said he did not want to contest for president.
“When Shokeen said he did not want to fight for president, they told him he had to. Chatrath’s ticket was already fixed and we could not change it because he is the son of a senior party leader,” the functionary told ThePrint on condition of anonymity.
The NSUI functionary further said that once Shokeen decided to contest independently, nobody in the organisation tried to stop him or speak to him. “No one tried to retain him despite seeing his potential.”
Another NSUI functionary said the leadership repeatedly questioned Shokeen over the money he was spending on the election. “He doesn’t have money to splurge on an election, he doesn’t have big cars. Is it right to taunt someone over his lack of resources? We supported him from the back, but this was incorrect. Shokeen, he is the son of a DTC bus conductor, he did not have the resources that some other candidates had.”
Shokeen was not the only aspirant to contest outside NSUI after a ticket dispute. Vishesh Yadav, another aspirant, contested the joint-secretary election outside the organisation. He polled 15,778 votes, more than NSUI’s official candidate Gopal Choudhary, who secured 15,206.
NSUI went from winning one post in 2023 to two in 2024, one in 2025 and none in 2026. This year was the first time since 2015 that it failed to win any of the four central-panel posts.
ThePrint has reached out to NSUI president Vinod Jakhar via WhatsApp calls and texts, and Kanhaiya Kumar over WhatsApp texts for comment. This report will be updated if and when their responses are received.
‘More importance to optics than ground-level mgmt’
Other complaints conveyed to Rahul and Priyanka include: leadership “prioritising social media and X optics over ground-level cadre management and mobilisation”.
The members also claimed cadre-wide dissatisfaction with the working style of both the Jakhar and Kumar was evident, “compounded by their visible absence from ground campaigning following ticket distribution”.
Not just DUSU polls
The criticism is not limited to the DUSU elections. Another NSUI member who was closely involved in the elections alleged that Jakhar had not constituted the National Organising Bodies—involved in grassroots outreach—even after eight months in office.
“Regularity and involvement is really less. There is no engagement. They meet no student leaders; the national organising body hasn’t been set up too,” the member told ThePrint.
A former student president of a Delhi University college, who is still associated with NSUI, said Kumar should have been in regular touch with college-level leaders.
“As an in-charge of NSUI, Kumar should have been in touch with his leaders in college. If utilised properly, we could have been his eyes and ears, but he never spoke to us. There is a massive leadership crisis,” the former college president said.
In a now-deleted post on X, another NSUI member wrote: “We need serious reflections over our organisation and its leadership.”
(Edited by Gitanjali Das)

headline: Delhi court revives complaint against Sonia Gandhi over alleged voter list forgery
full_text:
Delhi court revives complaint against Sonia Gandhi over alleged voter list forgery
Special Judge Vishal Gogne of Rouse Avenue Court passed the order while setting aside a magistrate’s decision last year dismissing allegations against Gandhi.
A Delhi court on Monday revived a complaint against senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi, alleging voter manipulation and forgery on her part in adding her name to the electoral list in 1980, and directed a magistrate to hear the matter afresh next week by calling for a police status report.
Special Judge Vishal Gogne of Rouse Avenue Court passed the order while setting aside a magistrate’s decision last year dismissing allegations against Gandhi, observing that the judge failed to substantiate the reasons for junking the petitioner’s allegations. “The order suffers from manifest error in law on account of non-compliance of 175(3) of BNSS and on account of not hearing the submissions of the investigating officer and not calling a status report”.
Also Read I Congress calls SIR ‘Shah Instigated Removal’, flags ‘unusually high’ voter deletions
Voter roll inclusion before becoming Indian citizen
The judge was presiding over a revision petition moved by lawyer Vikas Tripathi, vice-president of the Central Delhi Court Bar Association of the Rouse Avenue courts, challenging an order passed on September 11 last year, wherein a magistrate dismissed his complaint after holding that the accusations against Gandhi lacked substance and abused the process of law.
Tripathi had filed a complaint claiming that while Gandhi took Indian citizenship on April 30, 1983, her name was enrolled as a voter in the electoral list three years before this, in 1980.
The complaint alleged that Gandhi’s name was deleted in 1982 and re-entered again on January 1, 1983.
Special Judge Gogne observed that the magistrate seems to have casually dismissed several factual allegations without delving into their veracity.
“The order suffers from non-application of mind and is liable to be set aside. The magistrate had not discussed the implications of the documents presented by the petitioner”.
Remanding the matter back to the magistrate, the court asked for a status report to be sought from the investigating officer on the allegations.
While junking the plea which sought directions for investigation, the magistrate had pointed to the lack of any cogent evidence against the Congress leader, proving she forged papers to enrol herself as a voter.
Sonia Gandhi alleges political motivations
Gandhi on her part, through senior advocate R.S. Cheema, informed the court that the complaint questioning her inclusion in the electoral roll was politically motivated and lacked documentary evidence to show any manipulation and forgery on her end.
She said that the revision plea was “wholly misconceived” and “politically motivated” and an attempt to “abuse the process of law”. She pointed out that the magistrate’s court had rightly observed that matters of citizenship fell exclusively under the central government’s domain, while electoral roll disputes were the sole prerogative of ECI.
Her reply said, “Criminal courts cannot usurp these functions by entertaining private complaints disguised under IPC/BNSS sections. This is barred by the doctrine of separation of powers and would violate Article 329 of the Constitution, which prohibits judicial interference in the electoral process”.
Also Read I 'Cordial, then rough': Inside the Penguin-Sonia Gandhi memoir fallout
Gandhi added that it was evident from the complaint that a controversy that was raised in the media more than 25 years back was being recycled.
Her counsel further said that the complainant’s assertion that Gandhi got her name re-entered in the electoral roll having a qualifying date of January 1, 1983, was incomprehensible and without any factual basis as no documents were produced to show any alleged forgery or falsification.
Gandhi pointed out that it was the statutory function of the election commission to prepare the electoral roll in accordance with the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, drawn in tune with article 324 of the Constitution of India.

Delhi court revives forgery plea against Sonia Gandhi over voter roll inclusion
The Rouse Avenue Court allowed a revision petition concerning Sonia Gandhi's alleged inclusion in the 1980 voter roll before she obtained Indian citizenship in 1983. The court set aside the magistrate's order rejecting an FIR plea, citing legal infirmities, and allowed the petitioner to approach the magistrate court again.
The Rouse Avenue Court has allowed the revision petition filed against Sonia Gandhi in connection with the alleged inclusion of her name in the electoral roll through forgery without obtaining citizenship.
The next hearing will be on September 29.
The petition filed against Sonia Gandhi states that she obtained citizenship on April 30, 1983, while her name was included in the 1980 voter list. The petition questioned how her name was included in the 1980 New Delhi voter list.

The development comes at a time when roughly 47 lakh names were dropped from Delhi’s draft electoral rolls, with notices sent to 33.1 lakh voters over unmapped records or “logical discrepancies.”
Last month, the draft roll removed 47 lakh voters from the city’s 1.45 crore-strong electorate, meaning roughly one in three voters in Delhi was removed as part of the Special Intensive Revision of the voter list.

headline: Upcoming superpower: 4 European nations back India's bid for permanent UNSC seat
full_text:
Upcoming superpower: 4 European nations back India's bid for permanent UNSC seat
India's push for a permanent seat on the UN Security Council gets fresh backing from Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and the Czech Republic. The Visegrad Four support New Delhi's bid at the 81st UN General Assembly.
India's bid for a permanent seat at the UN Security Council has won collective support from four Central European countries, adding fresh diplomatic weight to decades-old demand for reform of the global body.
Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and the Czech Republic -- the four members of the Visegrad Group -- voiced their support for India during the first V4-India meeting held on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly in New York.
"We all agree as V4 countries that India as a part of the Global South, upcoming superpower in the Indo-Pacific region, must be at the table as the permanent member of the UN Security Council," Slovak Foreign Minister Juraj Blanar said after meeting External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar.
WHY INDIA WANTS PERMANENT SEAT AT UNSC
The argument behind India's campaign is straightforward: the world has changed since the Security Council was created, but its permanent membership has not. In 1945, much of Asia and Africa was still under colonial rule. Several countries that now have major populations, economies and diplomatic influence were either not independent or did not exist as sovereign states.
India has served eight times as an elected member of the Security Council, most recently in 2021 and 2022.
Its case rests on several factors -- its population, economic weight, contribution to UN peacekeeping and growing diplomatic influence. India has also played an active role in discussions on counterterrorism, development, maritime security and international peace.
Its priorities paper for the 81st UNGA argues that the UN's inability to respond effectively to conflicts has raised questions about its "efficacy, credibility and legitimacy". For New Delhi, therefore, Security Council reform is not simply about adding India to the permanent membership.
It is about changing the structure of the world's most powerful multilateral security institution so that it better reflects the world of today.
INDIA IS NOT PUSHING ALONE
India's campaign has been supported by multiple members of the UN Security Council itself.
France has consistently supported India's claim. The United Kingdom has also backed India's inclusion in an expanded Security Council. The United States has publicly supported India's permanent membership in principle, while Russia has also backed India's bid.
India is also part of the G4 grouping with Brazil, Germany and Japan. The four countries support each other's bids for permanent membership and coordinate their positions during negotiations. The G4 has proposed increasing the size of the Security Council from its current 15 members to 25 or 26.
Under its proposed model, six new permanent seats would be created -- two for Africa, two for the Asia-Pacific region, one for Latin America and the Caribbean and one for Western Europe and Others. The proposal also includes four or five additional non-permanent seats.
THE P5 PROBLEM
The five existing permanent members -- the US, Russia, China, France and the UK -- have not agreed on a single model for expanding the Council. There are differences over how many countries should be added, which regions should receive seats, whether new permanent members should have veto powers and how the Council should function after expansion.
China is the sole permanent member of the UN Security Council withholding explicit backing for India's bid for a permanent seat. Beijing employs diplomatic ambiguity by stating it understands and respects India's aspirations while structurally blocking the bid through demands for a broader consensus.
This is why diplomatic support for India's permanent membership does not automatically mean agreement on every aspect of Security Council reform.
The ultimate hurdle is structural. Reform would require amendments to the UN Charter, meaning the process needs broad support while also navigating the interests of the existing permanent members.
THEN THERE IS THE VETO
The biggest question may be what happens to the veto.
At present, the five permanent members can block substantive Security Council decisions. Elected members do not have that power.
The African Union has argued that the veto should eventually disappear. But as long as it exists, it wants new permanent members to receive the same rights as the existing P5.
India has taken a similar position.
In an April 2026 statement, New Delhi said there could not be a separate category of permanent members in which some countries have veto rights while others do not. India has backed an "all or none" approach, under which existing and new permanent members would have the same privileges and responsibilities.
NEW DIPLOMATIC FRONT FOR INDIA
The V4 meeting itself marked a new chapter in India's engagement with the four Central European nations. Jaishankar described it as a "new historic occasion" and thanked Blanar for bringing the countries together.
"We had our first Visegrad Four and India meeting. It was, in a sense, a new historic occasion, and I would like to thank Minister Juraj (Foreign Minister of Slovakia) for convening us today. It was a very, very productive meeting," Jaishankar said.
The meeting was not solely about the Security Council. India and the V4 countries agreed to explore a wider institutional relationship, including an annual business forum and regular meetings between their foreign ministers.
"What we agreed was that since India's relationship with the European Union itself is deepening, with the V4, we would take some special initiatives to create an annual business forum. As foreign ministers, we would meet annually. That was the consensus," Jaishankar said.
Technology and innovation were also discussed, along with defence, space, connectivity and people-to-people ties. The ministers also exchanged views on major global crises, including the Ukraine conflict and developments in the Gulf.
WHAT THE V4 BACKING MEANS
The V4 endorsement does not by itself guarantee Security Council reform. The process remains tied to negotiations involving a wide range of countries and, crucially, the existing permanent members.
But it gives India another collective bloc of countries supporting its permanent membership claim.
Jaishankar was also asked whether the V4's growing importance for India had a political dimension.
"We have very good relations with the V4 countries, and we know that these are countries with very strong, very distinctive capability. They are industrial economies, economies with great innovation and technology talent. And I think how the V4 come together is for them to decide. But we certainly welcome the opportunity to work," he said.

full_text:
Cabinet Minister in the Uttar Pradeshgovernment and Suheldev Bhartiya Samaj Party (SBSP) president Om Prakash Rajbhar on Monday (September 21, 2026) claimed that U.P. will be divided into four parts soon, and the Purvanchal region will get a Chief Minister from the Rajbhar caste; the assertion brought fresh focus on demands for the division of the State.
While the BJP played down the issue, the Congress hit out at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over double-speak, as Mr. Rajbhar referred to his conversation with the PM on the division of the State.
“Once the caste census is completed, there will be no problem in carrying out the division. We will divide the State after the caste census. This is what the Prime Minister of the country said,” said Mr. Rajbhar, a partner of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Uttar Pradesh, while addressing a public meeting in Ambedkarnagar district, and referred to his dialogue with Mr. Modi and claimed that the PM told him that the division of the State could happen after the caste census.
Mr. Rajbhar further added, “The day a separate Purvanchal State is created, the first Chief Minister will be a son of the Rajbhar community. When the State is divided, there will be Purvanchal, Madhyanchal, Bundelkhand and Harit Pradesh. The Rajbhar community has the largest vote base in Purvanchal,” he said.
The claim brought fresh focus on demands for the division of the State, as many social and regional outfits pushed for creating states of Purvanchal, Bundelkhand, Harit Pradesh and Madhyanchal.
“The demand for a separate Purvanchal is long pending. We are happy that Om Prakash Rajbhar is raising the issue; the economic and social dynamics of Eastern U.P. are fundamentally different from Western U.P. We hope the demand for division will reach a logical conclusion,” said Devesh Chaubey, who is associated with Purvanchal Vikas Parishad.
Before the 2012 Assembly election, the U.P. government led by the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) passed a proposal in the state assembly to divide Uttar Pradesh into four parts, but failed to get Central government’s approval.
Congress alleged that the fresh claim by Mr. Rajbhar is aimed at remaining relevant in the politics of Purvanchal (Eastern U.P.) as his own community is drifting rapidly towards the opposition INDIA alliance.
“In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the Rajbhar social group supported the INDIA alliance. Om Prakash Rajbhar’s political stake has diminished in the last two years; such a statement is coming out of frustration amid a push to remain relevant in the region’s politics, but the Rajbhar community understands that Om Prakash Rajbhar has done nothing for the region or the community; hence they are supporting the SP-Congress alliance,” said Shahnawaz Alam, National Secretary, Congress.
The Samajwadi Party (SP) said the BJP and its alliance work on the policy of divide and rule, with the statement reflecting the same. “BJP and its allies have a history of divide and rule. Instead of speaking about what development work they have done in the last 10-years, such a statement highlights that the NDA has nothing to present in front of the public; we are fundamentally against the division of Uttar Pradesh,” said Sunil Singh Yadav ‘Sajan’, the SP spokesperson.
The BJP leaders declined to speak on Mr. Rajbhar’s comment.
